chapters.zh: 行法术的在摩西面前站立不住，因为在他们身上和一切埃及人身上都有这疮。

chapters.en: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said to Moses.
chapters.zh: 耶和华使法老的心刚硬，不听他们，正如耶和华对摩西所说的。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, confront Pharaoh and say to him, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你清早起来，站在法老面前，对他说，耶和华希伯来人的神这样说，容我的百姓去，好事奉我。

chapters.en: or this time I will send the full force of my plagues against you and against your officials and your people, so you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth.
chapters.zh: 因为这一次我要叫一切的灾殃临到你和你臣仆并你百姓的身上，叫你知道在普天下没有像我的。

chapters.en: For by now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with a plague that would have wiped you off the earth.
chapters.zh: 我若伸手用瘟疫攻击你和你的百姓，你早就从地上除灭了。

chapters.en: But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might show you my power and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
chapters.zh: 其实，我叫你存立，是特要向你显我的大能，并要使我的名传遍天下。

chapters.en: You still set yourself against my people and will not let them go.
chapters.zh: 你还向我的百姓自高，不容他们去吗？

chapters.en: Therefore, at this time tomorrow I will send the worst hailstorm that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded till now.
chapters.zh: 到明天约在这时候，我必叫重大的冰雹降下，自从埃及开国以来，没有这样的冰雹。

chapters.en: Give an order now to bring your livestock and everything you have in the field to a place of shelter, because the hail will fall on every person and animal that has not been brought in and is still out in the field, and they will die.’ ”
chapters.zh: 现在你要打发人把你的牲畜和你田间一切所有的催进来，凡在田间不收回家的，无论是人是牲畜，冰雹必降在他们身上，他们就必死。

chapters.en: Those officials of Pharaoh who feared the word of the LORD hurried to bring their slaves and their livestock inside.
chapters.zh: 法老的臣仆中，惧怕耶和华这话的，便叫他的奴仆和牲畜跑进家来。

chapters.en: But those who ignored the word of the LORD left their slaves and livestock in the field.
chapters.zh: 但那不把耶和华这话放在心上的，就将他的奴仆和牲畜留在田里。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky so that hail will fall all over Egypt—on people and animals and on everything growing in the fields of Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你向天伸杖，使埃及遍地的人身上和牲畜身上，并田间各样菜蔬上，都有冰雹。

chapters.en: When Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky, the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning flashed down to the ground. So the LORD rained hail on the land of Egypt;
chapters.zh: 摩西向天伸杖，耶和华就打雷下雹，有火闪到地上，耶和华下雹在埃及地上。

chapters.en: hail fell and lightning flashed back and forth. It was the worst storm in all the land of Egypt since it had become a nation.
chapters.zh: 那时，雹与火搀杂，甚是厉害，自从埃及成国以来，遍地没有这样的。

chapters.en: Throughout Egypt hail struck everything in the fields—both people and animals; it beat down everything growing in the fields and stripped every tree.
chapters.zh: 在埃及遍地，雹击打了田间所有的人和牲畜，并一切的菜蔬，又打坏田间一切的树木。

chapters.en: The only place it did not hail was the land of Goshen, where the Israelites were.
chapters.zh: 惟独以色列人所住的歌珊地没有冰雹。

chapters.en: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. “This time I have sinned,” he said to them. “The LORD is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong.
chapters.zh: 法老打发人召摩西，亚伦来，对他们说，这一次我犯了罪了。耶和华是公义的，我和我的百姓是邪恶的。

chapters.en: Pray to the LORD, for we have had enough thunder and hail. I will let you go; you don’t have to stay any longer.”
chapters.zh: 这雷轰和冰雹已经够了。请你们求耶和华，我就容你们去，不再留住你们。

chapters.en: Moses replied, “When I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands in prayer to the LORD. The thunder will stop and there will be no more hail, so you may know that the earth is the LORD’s.
chapters.zh: 摩西对他说，我一出城，就要向耶和华举手祷告，雷必止住，也不再有冰雹，叫你知道全地都是属耶和华的。

chapters.en: But I know that you and your officials still do not fear the LORD God.”
chapters.zh: 至于你和你的臣仆，我知道你们还是不惧怕耶和华神。

chapters.en: (The flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley had headed and the flax was in bloom.
chapters.zh: 那时，麻和大麦被雹击打，因为大麦已经吐穗，麻也开了花。

chapters.en: The wheat and spelt, however, were not destroyed, because they ripen later.)
chapters.zh: 只是小麦和粗麦没有被击打，因为还没有长成。

chapters.en: Then Moses left Pharaoh and went out of the city. He spread out his hands toward the LORD; the thunder and hail stopped, and the rain no longer poured down on the land.
chapters.zh: 摩西离了法老出城，向耶和华举手祷告，雷和雹就止住，雨也不再浇在地上了。

chapters.en: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had stopped, he sinned again: He and his officials hardened their hearts.
chapters.zh: 法老见雨和雹与雷止住，就越发犯罪，他和他的臣仆都硬着心。

chapters.en: So Pharaoh’s heart was hard and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
chapters.zh: 法老的心刚硬，不容以色列人去，正如耶和华借着摩西所说的。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials so that I may perform these signs of mine among them
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你进去见法老。我使他和他臣仆的心刚硬，为要在他们中间显我这些神迹，

chapters.en: that you may tell your children and grandchildren how I dealt harshly with the Egyptians and how I performed my signs among them, and that you may know that I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 并要叫你将我向埃及人所作的事，和在他们中间所行的神迹，传于你儿子和你孙子的耳中，好叫你们知道我是耶和华。

chapters.en: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, so that they may worship me.
chapters.zh: 摩西，亚伦就进去见法老，对他说，耶和华希伯来人的神这样说，你在我面前不肯自卑要到几时呢？容我的百姓去，好事奉我。

chapters.en: If you refuse to let them go, I will bring locusts into your country tomorrow.
chapters.zh: 你若不肯容我的百姓去，明天我要使蝗虫进入你的境内，

chapters.en: They will cover the face of the ground so that it cannot be seen. They will devour what little you have left after the hail, including every tree that is growing in your fields.
chapters.zh: 遮满地面，甚至看不见地，并且吃那冰雹所剩的和田间所长的一切树木。

chapters.en: They will fill your houses and those of all your officials and all the Egyptians—something neither your parents nor your ancestors have ever seen from the day they settled in this land till now.’ ” Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh.
chapters.zh: 你的宫殿和你众臣仆的房屋，并一切埃及人的房屋，都要被蝗虫占满了，自从你祖宗和你祖宗的祖宗在世以来，直到今日，没有见过这样的灾。摩西就转身离开法老出去。

chapters.en: Pharaoh’s officials said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt is ruined?”
chapters.zh: 法老的臣仆对法老说，这人为我们的网罗要到几时呢？容这些人去事奉耶和华他们的神吧，埃及已经败坏了，你还不知道吗？

chapters.en: Then Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go, worship the LORD your God,” he said. “But tell me who will be going.”
chapters.zh: 于是摩西，亚伦被召回来见法老，法老对他们说，你们去事奉耶和华你们的神，但那要去的是谁呢？

chapters.en: Moses answered, “We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and our daughters, and with our flocks and herds, because we are to celebrate a festival to the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 摩西说，我们要和我们老的少的，儿子女儿同去，且把羊群牛群一同带去，因为我们务要向耶和华守节。

chapters.en: Pharaoh said, “The LORD be with you—if I let you go, along with your women and children! Clearly you are bent on evil.
chapters.zh: 法老对他们说，我容你们和你们妇人孩子去的时候，耶和华与你们同在吧，你们要谨慎，因为有祸在你们眼前（或作你们存着恶意），

chapters.en: No! Have only the men go and worship the LORD, since that’s what you have been asking for.” Then Moses and Aaron were driven out of Pharaoh’s presence.
chapters.zh: 不可都去，你们这壮年人去事奉耶和华吧，因为这是你们所求的。于是把他们从法老面前撵出去。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over Egypt so that locusts swarm over the land and devour everything growing in the fields, everything left by the hail.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你向埃及地伸杖，使蝗虫到埃及地上来，吃地上一切的菜蔬，就是冰雹所剩的。

chapters.en: So Moses stretched out his staff over Egypt, and the LORD made an east wind blow across the land all that day and all that night. By morning the wind had brought the locusts;
chapters.zh: 摩西就向埃及地伸杖，那一昼一夜，耶和华使东风刮在埃及地上，到了早晨，东风把蝗虫刮了来。

chapters.en: they invaded all Egypt and settled down in every area of the country in great numbers. Never before had there been such a plague of locusts, nor will there ever be again.
chapters.zh: 蝗虫上来，落在埃及的四境，甚是厉害，以前没有这样的，以后也必没有。

chapters.en: They covered all the ground until it was black. They devoured all that was left after the hail—everything growing in the fields and the fruit on the trees. Nothing green remained on tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 因为这蝗虫遮满地面，甚至地都黑暗了，又吃地上一切的菜蔬和冰雹所剩树上的果子。埃及遍地，无论是树木，是田间的菜蔬，连一点青的也没有留下。

chapters.en: Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
chapters.zh: 于是法老急忙召了摩西，亚伦来，说，我得罪耶和华你们的神，又得罪了你们。

chapters.en: Now forgive my sin once more and pray to the LORD your God to take this deadly plague away from me.”
chapters.zh: 现在求你，只这一次，饶恕我的罪，求耶和华你们的神使我脱离这一次的死亡。

chapters.en: Moses then left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 摩西就离开法老去求耶和华。

chapters.en: And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind, which caught up the locusts and carried them into the Red Sea. Not a locust was left anywhere in Egypt.
chapters.zh: 耶和华转了极大的西风，把蝗虫刮起，吹入红海，在埃及的四境连一个也没有留下。

chapters.en: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.
chapters.zh: 但耶和华使法老的心刚硬，不容以色列人去。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky so that darkness spreads over Egypt—darkness that can be felt.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你向天伸杖，使埃及地黑暗，这黑暗似乎摸得着。

chapters.en: So Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and total darkness covered all Egypt for three days.
chapters.zh: 摩西向天伸杖，埃及遍地就乌黑了三天。

chapters.en: No one could see anyone else or move about for three days. Yet all the Israelites had light in the places where they lived.
chapters.zh: 三天之久，人不能相见，谁也不敢起来离开本处，惟有以色列人家中都有亮光。

chapters.en: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, “Go, worship the LORD. Even your women and children may go with you; only leave your flocks and herds behind.”
chapters.zh: 法老就召摩西来，说，你们去事奉耶和华，只是你们的羊群牛群要留下，你们的妇人孩子可以和你们同去。

chapters.en: But Moses said, “You must allow us to have sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.
chapters.zh: 摩西说，你总要把祭物和燔祭牲交给我们，使我们可以祭祀耶和华我们的神。

chapters.en: Our livestock too must go with us; not a hoof is to be left behind. We have to use some of them in worshiping the LORD our God, and until we get there we will not know what we are to use to worship the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 我们的牲畜也要带去，连一蹄也不留下，因为我们要从其中取出来，事奉耶和华我们的神。我们未到那里，还不知道用什么事奉耶和华。

chapters.en: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was not willing to let them go.
chapters.zh: 但耶和华使法老的心刚硬，不肯容他们去。

chapters.en: Pharaoh said to Moses, “Get out of my sight! Make sure you do not appear before me again! The day you see my face you will die.”
chapters.zh: 法老对摩西说，你离开我去吧，你要小心，不要再见我的面，因为你见我面的那日你就必死。

chapters.en: “Just as you say,” Moses replied. “I will never appear before you again.”
chapters.zh: 摩西说，你说得好，我必不再见你的面了。

chapters.en: Now the LORD had said to Moses, “I will bring one more plague on Pharaoh and on Egypt. After that, he will let you go from here, and when he does, he will drive you out completely.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，我再使一样的灾殃临到法老和埃及，然后他必容你们离开这地。他容你们去的时候，总要催逼你们都从这地出去。

chapters.en: Tell the people that men and women alike are to ask their neighbors for articles of silver and gold.”
chapters.zh: 你要传于百姓的耳中，叫他们男女各人向邻舍要金器银器。

chapters.en: (The LORD made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, and Moses himself was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh’s officials and by the people.)
chapters.zh: 耶和华叫百姓在埃及人眼前蒙恩，并且摩西在埃及地，法老臣仆，和百姓的眼中看为极大。

chapters.en: So Moses said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘About midnight I will go throughout Egypt.
chapters.zh: 摩西说，耶和华这样说，约到半夜，我必出去巡行埃及遍地。

chapters.en: Every firstborn son in Egypt will die, from the firstborn son of Pharaoh, who sits on the throne, to the firstborn son of the female slave, who is at her hand mill, and all the firstborn of the cattle as well.
chapters.zh: 凡在埃及地，从坐宝座的法老直到磨子后的婢女所有的长子，以及一切头生的牲畜，都必死。

chapters.en: There will be loud wailing throughout Egypt—worse than there has ever been or ever will be again.
chapters.zh: 埃及遍地必有大哀号，从前没有这样的，后来也必没有。

chapters.en: But among the Israelites not a dog will bark at any person or animal.’ Then you will know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.
chapters.zh: 至于以色列中，无论是人是牲畜，连狗也不敢向他们摇舌，好叫你们知道耶和华是将埃及人和以色列人分别出来。

chapters.en: All these officials of yours will come to me, bowing down before me and saying, ‘Go, you and all the people who follow you!’ After that I will leave.” Then Moses, hot with anger, left Pharaoh.
chapters.zh: 你这一切臣仆都要俯伏来见我，说，求你和跟从你的百姓都出去，然后我要出去。于是，摩西气忿忿地离开法老，出去了。

chapters.en: The LORD had said to Moses, “Pharaoh will refuse to listen to you—so that my wonders may be multiplied in Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，法老必不听你们，使我的奇事在埃及地多起来。

chapters.en: Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go out of his country.
chapters.zh: 摩西，亚伦在法老面前行了这一切奇事，耶和华使法老的心刚硬，不容以色列人出离他的地。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron in Egypt,
chapters.zh: 耶和华在埃及地晓谕摩西，亚伦说，

chapters.en: “This month is to be for you the first month, the first month of your year.
chapters.zh: 你们要以本月为正月，为一年之首。

chapters.en: Tell the whole community of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man is to take a lamb for his family, one for each household.
chapters.zh: 你们吩咐以色列全会众说，本月初十日，各人要按着父家取羊羔，一家一只。

chapters.en: If any household is too small for a whole lamb, they must share one with their nearest neighbor, having taken into account the number of people there are. You are to determine the amount of lamb needed in accordance with what each person will eat.
chapters.zh: 若是一家的人太少，吃不了一只羊羔，本人就要和他隔壁的邻舍共取一只。你们预备羊羔，要按着人数和饭量计算。

chapters.en: The animals you choose must be year-old males without defect, and you may take them from the sheep or the goats.
chapters.zh: 要无残疾，一岁的公羊羔，你们或从绵羊里取，或从山羊里取，都可以。

chapters.en: Take care of them until the fourteenth day of the month, when all the members of the community of Israel must slaughter them at twilight.
chapters.zh: 要留到本月十四日，在黄昏的时候，以色列全会众把羊羔宰了。

chapters.en: Then they are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.
chapters.zh: 各家要取点血，涂在吃羊羔的房屋左右的门框上和门楣上。

chapters.en: That same night they are to eat the meat roasted over the fire, along with bitter herbs, and bread made without yeast.
chapters.zh: 当夜要吃羊羔的肉，用火烤了，与无酵饼和苦菜同吃。

chapters.en: Do not eat the meat raw or boiled in water, but roast it over a fire—with the head, legs and internal organs.
chapters.zh: 不可吃生的，断不可吃水煮的，要带着头，腿，五脏，用火烤了吃。

chapters.en: Do not leave any of it till morning; if some is left till morning, you must burn it.
chapters.zh: 不可剩下一点留到早晨，若留到早晨，要用火烧了。

chapters.en: This is how you are to eat it: with your cloak tucked into your belt, your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. Eat it in haste; it is the LORD’s Passover.
chapters.zh: 你们吃羊羔当腰间束带，脚上穿鞋，手中拿杖，赶紧地吃，这是耶和华的逾越节。

chapters.en: “On that same night I will pass through Egypt and strike down every firstborn of both people and animals, and I will bring judgment on all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 因为那夜我要巡行埃及地，把埃及地一切头生的，无论是人是牲畜，都击杀了，又要败坏埃及一切的神。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No destructive plague will touch you when I strike Egypt.
chapters.zh: 这血要在你们所住的房屋上作记号，我一见这血，就越过你们去。我击杀埃及地头生的时候，灾殃必不临到你们身上灭你们。

chapters.en: “This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD—a lasting ordinance.
chapters.zh: 你们要记念这日，守为耶和华的节，作为你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast. On the first day remove the yeast from your houses, for whoever eats anything with yeast in it from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.
chapters.zh: 你们要吃无酵饼七日。头一日要把酵从你们各家中除去，因为从头一日起，到第七日为止，凡吃有酵之饼的，必从以色列中剪除。

chapters.en: On the first day hold a sacred assembly, and another one on the seventh day. Do no work at all on these days, except to prepare food for everyone to eat; that is all you may do.
chapters.zh: 头一日你们当有圣会，第七日也当有圣会。这两日之内，除了预备各人所要吃的以外，无论何工都不可作。

chapters.en: “Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day that I brought your divisions out of Egypt. Celebrate this day as a lasting ordinance for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 你们要守无酵节，因为我正当这日把你们的军队从埃及地领出来。所以，你们要守这日，作为世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: In the first month you are to eat bread made without yeast, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.
chapters.zh: 从正月十四日晚上，直到二十一日晚上，你们要吃无酵饼。

chapters.en: For seven days no yeast is to be found in your houses. And anyone, whether foreigner or native-born, who eats anything with yeast in it must be cut off from the community of Israel.
chapters.zh: 在你们各家中，七日之内不可有酵，因为凡吃有酵之物的，无论是寄居的，是本地的，必从以色列的会中剪除。

chapters.en: Eat nothing made with yeast. Wherever you live, you must eat unleavened bread.”
chapters.zh: 有酵的物，你们都不可吃，在你们一切住处要吃无酵饼。

chapters.en: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and said to them, “Go at once and select the animals for your families and slaughter the Passover lamb.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西召了以色列的众长老来，对他们说，你们要按着家口取出羊羔，把这逾越节的羊羔宰了。

chapters.en: Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin and put some of the blood on the top and on both sides of the doorframe. None of you shall go out of the door of your house until morning.
chapters.zh: 拿一把牛膝草，蘸盆里的血，打在门楣上和左右的门框上。你们谁也不可出自己的房门，直到早晨。

chapters.en: When the LORD goes through the land to strike down the Egyptians, he will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway, and he will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华要巡行击杀埃及人，他看见血在门楣上和左右的门框上，就必越过那门，不容灭命的进你们的房屋，击杀你们。

chapters.en: “Obey these instructions as a lasting ordinance for you and your descendants.
chapters.zh: 这例，你们要守着，作为你们和你们子孙永远的定例。

chapters.en: When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as he promised, observe this ceremony.
chapters.zh: 日后，你们到了耶和华按着所应许赐给你们的那地，就要守这礼。

chapters.en: And when your children ask you, ‘What does this ceremony mean to you?’
chapters.zh: 你们的儿女问你们说，行这礼是什么意思？

chapters.en: then tell them, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt and spared our homes when he struck down the Egyptians.’ ” Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
chapters.zh: 你们就说，这是献给耶和华逾越节的祭。当以色列人在埃及的时候，他击杀埃及人，越过以色列人的房屋，救了我们各家。于是百姓低头下拜。

chapters.en: The Israelites did just what the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron.
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样吩咐摩西，亚伦，以色列人就怎样行。

chapters.en: At midnight the LORD struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on the throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner, who was in the dungeon, and the firstborn of all the livestock as well.
chapters.zh: 到了半夜，耶和华把埃及地所有的长子，就是从坐宝座的法老，直到被掳囚在监里之人的长子，以及一切头生的牲畜，尽都杀了。

chapters.en: Pharaoh and all his officials and all the Egyptians got up during the night, and there was loud wailing in Egypt, for there was not a house without someone dead.
chapters.zh: 法老和一切臣仆，并埃及众人，夜间都起来了。在埃及有大哀号，无一家不死一个人的。

chapters.en: During the night Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Up! Leave my people, you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have requested.
chapters.zh: 夜间，法老召了摩西，亚伦来，说，起来，连你们带以色列人，从我民中出去，依你们所说的，去事奉耶和华吧。

chapters.en: Take your flocks and herds, as you have said, and go. And also bless me.”
chapters.zh: 也依你们所说的，连羊群牛群带着走吧，并要为我祝福。

chapters.en: The Egyptians urged the people to hurry and leave the country. “For otherwise,” they said, “we will all die!”
chapters.zh: 埃及人催促百姓，打发他们快快出离那地，因为埃及人说，我们都要死了。

chapters.en: So the people took their dough before the yeast was added, and carried it on their shoulders in kneading troughs wrapped in clothing.
chapters.zh: 百姓就拿着没有酵的生面，把抟面盆包在衣服中，扛在肩头上。

chapters.en: The Israelites did as Moses instructed and asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold and for clothing.
chapters.zh: 以色列人照着摩西的话行，向埃及人要金器，银器，和衣裳。

chapters.en: The LORD had made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, and they gave them what they asked for; so they plundered the Egyptians.
chapters.zh: 耶和华叫百姓在埃及人眼前蒙恩，以致埃及人给他们所要的。他们就把埃及人的财物夺去了。

chapters.en: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Sukkoth. There were about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides women and children.
chapters.zh: 以色列人从兰塞起行，往疏割去，除了妇人孩子，步行的男人约有六十万。

chapters.en: Many other people went up with them, and also large droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.
chapters.zh: 又有许多闲杂人，并有羊群牛群，和他们一同上去。

chapters.en: With the dough the Israelites had brought from Egypt, they baked loaves of unleavened bread. The dough was without yeast because they had been driven out of Egypt and did not have time to prepare food for themselves.
chapters.zh: 他们用埃及带出来的生面烤成无酵饼。这生面原没有发起，因为他们被催逼离开埃及，不能耽延，也没有为自己预备什么食物。

chapters.en: Now the length of time the Israelite people lived in Egypt was 430 years.
chapters.zh: 以色列人住在埃及共有四百三十年。

chapters.en: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD’s divisions left Egypt.
chapters.zh: 正满了四百三十年的那一天，耶和华的军队都从埃及地出来了。

chapters.en: Because the LORD kept vigil that night to bring them out of Egypt, on this night all the Israelites are to keep vigil to honor the LORD for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 这夜是耶和华的夜，因耶和华领他们出了埃及地，所以当向耶和华谨守，是以色列众人世世代代该谨守的。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “These are the regulations for the Passover meal: “No foreigner may eat it.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西，亚伦说，逾越节的例是这样，外邦人都不可吃这羊羔。

chapters.en: Any slave you have bought may eat it after you have circumcised him,
chapters.zh: 但各人用银子买的奴仆，既受了割礼就可以吃。

chapters.en: but a temporary resident or a hired worker may not eat it.
chapters.zh: 寄居的和雇工人都不可吃。

chapters.en: “It must be eaten inside the house; take none of the meat outside the house. Do not break any of the bones.
chapters.zh: 应当在一个房子里吃，不可把一点肉从房子里带到外头去。羊羔的骨头一根也不可折断。

chapters.en: The whole community of Israel must celebrate it.
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众都要守这礼。

chapters.en: “A foreigner residing among you who wants to celebrate the LORD’s Passover must have all the males in his household circumcised; then he may take part like one born in the land. No uncircumcised male may eat it.
chapters.zh: 若有外人寄居在你们中间，愿向耶和华守逾越节，他所有的男子务要受割礼，然后才容他前来遵守，他也就像本地人一样，但未受割礼的，都不可吃这羊羔。

chapters.en: The same law applies both to the native-born and to the foreigner residing among you.”
chapters.zh: 本地人和寄居在你们中间的外人同归一例。

chapters.en: All the Israelites did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样吩咐摩西，亚伦，以色列众人就怎样行了。

chapters.en: And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt by their divisions.
chapters.zh: 正当那日，耶和华将以色列人按着他们的军队，从埃及地领出来。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal.”
chapters.zh: 以色列中凡头生的，无论是人是牲畜，都是我的，要分别为圣归我。

chapters.en: Then Moses said to the people, “Commemorate this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery, because the LORD brought you out of it with a mighty hand. Eat nothing containing yeast.
chapters.zh: 摩西对百姓说，你们要记念从埃及为奴之家出来的这日，因为耶和华用大能的手将你们从这地方领出来。有酵的饼都不可吃。

chapters.en: Today, in the month of Aviv, you are leaving.
chapters.zh: 亚笔月间的这日是你们出来的日子。

chapters.en: When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites and Jebusites—the land he swore to your ancestors to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you are to observe this ceremony in this month:
chapters.zh: 将来耶和华领你进迦南人，赫人，亚摩利人，希未人，耶布斯人之地，就是他向你的祖宗起誓应许给你那流奶与蜜之地，那时你要在这月间守这礼。

chapters.en: For seven days eat bread made without yeast and on the seventh day hold a festival to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你要吃无酵饼七日，到第七日要向耶和华守节。

chapters.en: Eat unleavened bread during those seven days; nothing with yeast in it is to be seen among you, nor shall any yeast be seen anywhere within your borders.
chapters.zh: 这七日之久，要吃无酵饼，在你四境之内不可见有酵的饼，也不可见发酵的物。

chapters.en: On that day tell your son, ‘I do this because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’
chapters.zh: 当那日，你要告诉你的儿子说，这是因耶和华在我出埃及的时候为我所行的事。

chapters.en: This observance will be for you like a sign on your hand and a reminder on your forehead that this law of the LORD is to be on your lips. For the LORD brought you out of Egypt with his mighty hand.
chapters.zh: 这要在你手上作记号，在你额上作纪念，使耶和华的律法常在你口中，因为耶和华曾用大能的手将你从埃及领出来。

chapters.en: You must keep this ordinance at the appointed time year after year.
chapters.zh: 所以你每年要按着日期守这例。

chapters.en: “After the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as he promised on oath to you and your ancestors,
chapters.zh: 将来，耶和华照他向你和你祖宗所起的誓将你领进迦南人之地，把这地赐给你，

chapters.en: you are to give over to the LORD the first offspring of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 那时你要将一切头生的，并牲畜中头生的，归给耶和华，公的都要属耶和华。

chapters.en: Redeem with a lamb every firstborn donkey, but if you do not redeem it, break its neck. Redeem every firstborn among your sons.
chapters.zh: 凡头生的驴，你要用羊羔代赎，若不代赎，就要打折它的颈项。凡你儿子中头生的都要赎出来。

chapters.en: “In days to come, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ say to him, ‘With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.
chapters.zh: 日后，你的儿子问你说，这是什么意思？你就说，耶和华用大能的手将我们从埃及为奴之家领出来。

chapters.en: When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed the firstborn of both people and animals in Egypt. This is why I sacrifice to the LORD the first male offspring of every womb and redeem each of my firstborn sons.’
chapters.zh: 那时法老几乎不容我们去，耶和华就把埃及地所有头生的，无论是人是牲畜，都杀了。因此，我把一切头生的公牲畜献给耶和华为祭，但将头生的儿子都赎出来。

chapters.en: And it will be like a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead that the LORD brought us out of Egypt with his mighty hand.”
chapters.zh: 这要在你手上作记号，在你额上作经文，因为耶和华用大能的手将我们从埃及领出来。

chapters.en: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them on the road through the Philistine country, though that was shorter. For God said, “If they face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 法老容百姓去的时候，非利士地的道路虽近，神却不领他们从那里走，因为神说，恐怕百姓遇见打仗后悔，就回埃及去。

chapters.en: So God led the people around by the desert road toward the Red Sea. The Israelites went up out of Egypt ready for battle.
chapters.zh: 所以神领百姓绕道而行，走红海旷野的路。以色列人出埃及地，都带着兵器上去。

chapters.en: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the Israelites swear an oath. He had said, “God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up with you from this place.”
chapters.zh: 摩西把约瑟的骸骨一同带去，因为约瑟曾叫以色列人严严地起誓，对他们说，神必眷顾你们，你们要把我的骸骨从这里一同带上去。

chapters.en: After leaving Sukkoth they camped at Etham on the edge of the desert.
chapters.zh: 他们从疏割起行，在旷野边的以倘安营。

chapters.en: By day the LORD went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud to guide them on their way and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day or night.
chapters.zh: 日间，耶和华在云柱中领他们的路，夜间，在火柱中光照他们，使他们日夜都可以行走。

chapters.en: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place in front of the people.
chapters.zh: 日间云柱，夜间火柱，总不离开百姓的面前。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp near Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. They are to encamp by the sea, directly opposite Baal Zephon.
chapters.zh: 你吩咐以色列人转回，安营在比哈希录前，密夺和海的中间，对着巴力洗分，靠近海边安营。

chapters.en: Pharaoh will think, ‘The Israelites are wandering around the land in confusion, hemmed in by the desert.’
chapters.zh: 法老必说，以色列人在地中绕迷了，旷野把他们困住了。

chapters.en: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them. But I will gain glory for myself through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.” So the Israelites did this.
chapters.zh: 我要使法老的心刚硬，他要追赶他们，我便在法老和他全军身上得荣耀，埃及人就知道我是耶和华。于是以色列人这样行了。

chapters.en: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them and said, “What have we done? We have let the Israelites go and have lost their services!”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉埃及王说，百姓逃跑。法老和他的臣仆就向百姓变心，说，我们容以色列人去，不再服事我们，这作的是什么事呢？

chapters.en: So he had his chariot made ready and took his army with him.
chapters.zh: 法老就预备他的车辆，带领军兵同去，

chapters.en: He took six hundred of the best chariots, along with all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.
chapters.zh: 并带着六百辆特选的车和埃及所有的车，每辆都有车兵长。

chapters.en: The LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, so that he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out boldly.
chapters.zh: 耶和华使埃及王法老的心刚硬，他就追赶以色列人，因为以色列人是昂然无惧地出埃及。

chapters.en: The Egyptians—all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, horsemen and troops—pursued the Israelites and overtook them as they camped by the sea near Pi Hahiroth, opposite Baal Zephon.
chapters.zh: 埃及人追赶他们，法老一切的马匹，车辆，马兵，与军兵就在海边上，靠近比哈希录，对着巴力洗分，在他们安营的地方追上了。

chapters.en: As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up, and there were the Egyptians, marching after them. They were terrified and cried out to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 法老临近的时候，以色列人举目看见埃及人赶来，就甚惧怕，向耶和华哀求。

chapters.en: They said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us to the desert to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
chapters.zh: 他们对摩西说，难道在埃及没有坟地，你把我们带来死在旷野吗？你为什么这样待我们，将我们从埃及领出来呢？

chapters.en: Didn’t we say to you in Egypt, ‘Leave us alone; let us serve the Egyptians’? It would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the desert!”
chapters.zh: 我们在埃及岂没有对你说过，不要搅扰我们，容我们服事埃及人吗？因为服事埃及人比死在旷野还好。

chapters.en: Moses answered the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the LORD will bring you today. The Egyptians you see today you will never see again.
chapters.zh: 摩西对百姓说，不要惧怕，只管站住，看耶和华今天向你们所要施行的救恩。因为，你们今天所看见的埃及人必永远不再看见了。

chapters.en: The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华必为你们争战，你们只管静默，不要作声。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites to move on.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你为什么向我哀求呢？你吩咐以色列人往前走。

chapters.en: Raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea to divide the water so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.
chapters.zh: 你举手向海伸杖，把水分开。以色列人要下海中走干地。

chapters.en: I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. And I will gain glory through Pharaoh and all his army, through his chariots and his horsemen.
chapters.zh: 我要使埃及人的心刚硬，他们就跟着下去。我要在法老和他的全军，车辆，马兵上得荣耀。

chapters.en: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I gain glory through Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen.”
chapters.zh: 我在法老和他的车辆，马兵上得荣耀的时候，埃及人就知道我是耶和华了。

chapters.en: Then the angel of God, who had been traveling in front of Israel’s army, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from in front and stood behind them,
chapters.zh: 在以色列营前行走神的使者，转到他们后边去，云柱也从他们前边转到他们后边立住。

chapters.en: coming between the armies of Egypt and Israel. Throughout the night the cloud brought darkness to the one side and light to the other side; so neither went near the other all night long.
chapters.zh: 在埃及营和以色列营中间有云柱，一边黑暗，一边发光，终夜两下不得相近。

chapters.en: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land. The waters were divided,
chapters.zh: 摩西向海伸杖，耶和华便用大东风，使海水一夜退去，水便分开，海就成了干地。

chapters.en: and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.
chapters.zh: 以色列人下海中走干地，水在他们的左右作了墙垣。

chapters.en: The Egyptians pursued them, and all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots and horsemen followed them into the sea.
chapters.zh: 埃及人追赶他们，法老一切的马匹，车辆，和马兵都跟着下到海中。

chapters.en: During the last watch of the night the LORD looked down from the pillar of fire and cloud at the Egyptian army and threw it into confusion.
chapters.zh: 到了晨更的时候，耶和华从云火柱中向埃及的军兵观看，使埃及的军兵混乱了，

chapters.en: He jammed the wheels of their chariots so that they had difficulty driving. And the Egyptians said, “Let’s get away from the Israelites! The LORD is fighting for them against Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 又使他们的车轮脱落，难以行走，以致埃及人说，我们从以色列人面前逃跑吧，因耶和华为他们攻击我们了。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea so that the waters may flow back over the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你向海伸杖，叫水仍合在埃及人并他们的车辆，马兵身上。

chapters.en: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea went back to its place. The Egyptians were fleeing toward it, and the LORD swept them into the sea.
chapters.zh: 摩西就向海伸杖，到了天一亮，海水仍旧复原。埃及人避水逃跑的时候，耶和华把他们推翻在海中，

chapters.en: The water flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen—the entire army of Pharaoh that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
chapters.zh: 水就回流，淹没了车辆和马兵。那些跟着以色列人下海法老的全军，连一个也没有剩下。

chapters.en: But the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.
chapters.zh: 以色列人却在海中走干地，水在他们的左右作了墙垣。

chapters.en: That day the LORD saved Israel from the hands of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians lying dead on the shore.
chapters.zh: 当日，耶和华这样拯救以色列人脱离埃及人的手，以色列人看见埃及人的死尸都在海边了。

chapters.en: And when the Israelites saw the mighty hand of the LORD displayed against the Egyptians, the people feared the LORD and put their trust in him and in Moses his servant.
chapters.zh: 以色列人看见耶和华向埃及人所行的大事，就敬畏耶和华，又信服他和他的仆人摩西。

chapters.en: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: “I will sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted. Both horse and driver he has hurled into the sea.
chapters.zh: 那时，摩西和以色列人向耶和华唱歌说，我要向耶和华歌唱，因他大大战胜，将马和骑马的投在海中。

chapters.en: “The LORD is my strength and my defense ; he has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will praise him, my father’s God, and I will exalt him.
chapters.zh: 耶和华是我的力量，我的诗歌，也成了我的拯救。这是我的神，我要赞美他，是我父亲的神，我要尊崇他。

chapters.en: The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is his name.
chapters.zh: 耶和华是战士，他的名是耶和华。

chapters.en: Pharaoh’s chariots and his army he has hurled into the sea. The best of Pharaoh’s officers are drowned in the Red Sea.
chapters.zh: 法老的车辆，军兵，耶和华已抛在海中，他特选的军长都沉于红海。

chapters.en: The deep waters have covered them; they sank to the depths like a stone.
chapters.zh: 深水淹没他们，他们如同石头坠到深处。

chapters.en: Your right hand, LORD, was majestic in power. Your right hand, LORD, shattered the enemy.
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，你的右手施展能力，显出荣耀，耶和华阿，你的右手摔碎仇敌。

chapters.en: “In the greatness of your majesty you threw down those who opposed you. You unleashed your burning anger; it consumed them like stubble.
chapters.zh: 你大发威严，推翻那些起来攻击你的，你发出烈怒如火，烧灭他们像烧碎秸一样。

chapters.en: By the blast of your nostrils the waters piled up. The surging waters stood up like a wall; the deep waters congealed in the heart of the sea.
chapters.zh: 你发鼻中的气，水便聚起成堆，大水直立如垒，海中的深水凝结。

chapters.en: The enemy boasted, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake them. I will divide the spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword and my hand will destroy them.’
chapters.zh: 仇敌说，我要追赶，我要追上，我要分掳物，我要在他们身上称我的心愿。我要拔出刀来，亲手杀灭他们。

chapters.en: But you blew with your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
chapters.zh: 你叫风一吹，海就把他们淹没，他们如铅沉在大水之中。

chapters.en: Who among the gods is like you, LORD? Who is like you— majestic in holiness, awesome in glory, working wonders?
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，众神之中，谁能象你。谁能象你，至圣至荣，可颂可畏，施行奇事。

chapters.en: “You stretch out your right hand, and the earth swallows your enemies.
chapters.zh: 你伸出右手，地便吞灭他们。

chapters.en: In your unfailing love you will lead the people you have redeemed. In your strength you will guide them to your holy dwelling.
chapters.zh: 你凭慈爱，领了你所赎的百姓，你凭能力，引他们到了你的圣所。

chapters.en: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the people of Philistia.
chapters.zh: 外邦人听见就发颤，疼痛抓住非利士的居民。

chapters.en: The chiefs of Edom will be terrified, the leaders of Moab will be seized with trembling, the people of Canaan will melt away;
chapters.zh: 那时，以东的族长惊惶，摩押的英雄被战兢抓住，迦南的居民心都消化了。

chapters.en: terror and dread will fall on them. By the power of your arm they will be as still as a stone— until your people pass by, LORD, until the people you bought pass by.
chapters.zh: 惊骇恐惧临到他们。耶和华阿，因你膀臂的大能，他们如石头寂然不动，等候你的百姓过去，等候你所赎的百姓过去。

chapters.en: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance— the place, LORD, you made for your dwelling, the sanctuary, Lord, your hands established.
chapters.zh: 你要将他们领进去，栽于你产业的山上。耶和华阿，就是你为自己所造的住处，主阿，就是你手所建立的圣所。

chapters.en: “The LORD reigns for ever and ever.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华必作王，直到永永远远。

chapters.en: When Pharaoh’s horses, chariots and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them, but the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
chapters.zh: 法老的马匹，车辆，和马兵下到海中，耶和华使海水回流，淹没他们，惟有以色列人在海中走干地。

chapters.en: Then Miriam the prophet, Aaron’s sister, took a timbrel in her hand, and all the women followed her, with timbrels and dancing.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的姐姐，女先知米利暗，手里拿着鼓，众妇女也跟她出去拿鼓跳舞。

chapters.en: Miriam sang to them: “Sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted. Both horse and driver he has hurled into the sea.”
chapters.zh: 米利暗应声说，你们要歌颂耶和华，因他大大战胜，将马和骑马的投在海中。

chapters.en: Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea and they went into the Desert of Shur. For three days they traveled in the desert without finding water.
chapters.zh: 摩西领以色列人从红海往前行，到了书珥的旷野，在旷野走了三天，找不着水。

chapters.en: When they came to Marah, they could not drink its water because it was bitter. (That is why the place is called Marah. )
chapters.zh: 到了玛拉，不能喝那里的水，因为水苦，所以那地名叫玛拉。

chapters.en: So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, “What are we to drink?”
chapters.zh: 百姓就向摩西发怨言，说，我们喝什么呢？

chapters.en: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became fit to drink. There the LORD issued a ruling and instruction for them and put them to the test.
chapters.zh: 摩西呼求耶和华，耶和华指示他一棵树。他把树丢在水里，水就变甜了。耶和华在那里为他们定了律例，典章，在那里试验他们，

chapters.en: He said, “If you listen carefully to the LORD your God and do what is right in his eyes, if you pay attention to his commands and keep all his decrees, I will not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on the Egyptians, for I am the LORD, who heals you.”
chapters.zh: 又说，你若留意听耶和华你神的话，又行我眼中看为正的事，留心听我的诫命，守我一切的律例，我就不将所加与埃及人的疾病加在你身上，因为我耶和华是医治你的。

chapters.en: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there near the water.
chapters.zh: 他们到了以琳，在那里有十二股水泉，七十棵棕树，他们就在那里的水边安营。

chapters.en: The whole Israelite community set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had come out of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众从以琳起行，在出埃及后第二个月十五日到了以琳和西乃中间，汛的旷野。

chapters.en: In the desert the whole community grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众在旷野向摩西，亚伦发怨言，

chapters.en: The Israelites said to them, “If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in Egypt! There we sat around pots of meat and ate all the food we wanted, but you have brought us out into this desert to starve this entire assembly to death.”
chapters.zh: 说，巴不得我们早死在埃及地，耶和华的手下，那时我们坐在肉锅旁边，吃得饱足。你们将我们领出来，到这旷野，是要叫这全会众都饿死啊。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “I will rain down bread from heaven for you. The people are to go out each day and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test them and see whether they will follow my instructions.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，我要将粮食从天降给你们。百姓可以出去，每天收每天的分，我好试验他们遵不遵我的法度。

chapters.en: On the sixth day they are to prepare what they bring in, and that is to be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”
chapters.zh: 到第六天，他们要把所收进来的预备好了，比每天所收的多一倍。

chapters.en: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “In the evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of Egypt,
chapters.zh: 摩西，亚伦对以色列众人说，到了晚上，你们要知道是耶和华将你们从埃及地领出来的。

chapters.en: and in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we, that you should grumble against us?”
chapters.zh: 早晨，你们要看见耶和华的荣耀，因为耶和华听见你们向他所发的怨言了。我们算什么，你们竟向我们发怨言呢？

chapters.en: Moses also said, “You will know that it was the LORD when he gives you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you want in the morning, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we? You are not grumbling against us, but against the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 摩西又说，耶和华晚上必给你们肉吃，早晨必给你们食物得饱，因为你们向耶和华发的怨言，他都听见了。我们算什么，你们的怨言不是向我们发的，乃是向耶和华发的。

chapters.en: Then Moses told Aaron, “Say to the entire Israelite community, ‘Come before the LORD, for he has heard your grumbling.’ ”
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦说，你告诉以色列全会众说，你们就近耶和华面前，因为他已经听见你们的怨言了。

chapters.en: While Aaron was speaking to the whole Israelite community, they looked toward the desert, and there was the glory of the LORD appearing in the cloud.
chapters.zh: 亚伦正对以色列全会众说话的时候，他们向旷野观看，不料，耶和华的荣光在云中显现。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’ ”
chapters.zh: 我已经听见以色列人的怨言。你告诉他们说，到黄昏的时候，你们要吃肉，早晨必有食物得饱，你们就知道我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
chapters.zh: 到了晚上，有鹌鹑飞来，遮满了营，早晨在营四围的地上有露水。

chapters.en: When the dew was gone, thin flakes like frost on the ground appeared on the desert floor.
chapters.zh: 露水上升之后，不料，野地面上有如白霜的小圆物。

chapters.en: When the Israelites saw it, they said to each other, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread the LORD has given you to eat.
chapters.zh: 以色列人看见，不知道是什么，就彼此对问说，这是什么呢？摩西对他们说，这就是耶和华给你们吃的食物。

chapters.en: This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Everyone is to gather as much as they need. Take an omer for each person you have in your tent.’ ”
chapters.zh: 耶和华所吩咐的是这样，你们要按着各人的饭量，为帐棚里的人，按着人数收起来，各拿一俄梅珥。

chapters.en: The Israelites did as they were told; some gathered much, some little.
chapters.zh: 以色列人就这样行，有多收的，有少收的。

chapters.en: And when they measured it by the omer, the one who gathered much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too little. Everyone had gathered just as much as they needed.
chapters.zh: 及至用俄梅珥量一量，多收的也没有余，少收的也没有缺，各人按着自己的饭量收取。

chapters.en: Then Moses said to them, “No one is to keep any of it until morning.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对他们说，所收的，不许什么人留到早晨。

chapters.en: However, some of them paid no attention to Moses; they kept part of it until morning, but it was full of maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.
chapters.zh: 然而他们不听摩西的话，内中有留到早晨的，就生虫变臭了，摩西便向他们发怒。

chapters.en: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
chapters.zh: 他们每日早晨，按着各人的饭量收取，日头一发热，就消化了。

chapters.en: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much—two omers for each person—and the leaders of the community came and reported this to Moses.
chapters.zh: 到第六天，他们收了双倍的食物，每人两俄梅珥。会众的官长来告诉摩西，

chapters.en: He said to them, “This is what the LORD commanded: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of sabbath rest, a holy sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil. Save whatever is left and keep it until morning.’ ”
chapters.zh: 摩西对他们说，耶和华这样说，明天是圣安息日，是向耶和华守的圣安息日。你们要烤的就烤了，要煮的就煮了，所剩下的都留到早晨。

chapters.en: So they saved it until morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not stink or get maggots in it.
chapters.zh: 他们就照摩西的吩咐留到早晨，也不臭，里头也没有虫子。

chapters.en: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a sabbath to the LORD. You will not find any of it on the ground today.
chapters.zh: 摩西说，你们今天吃这个吧，因为今天是向耶和华守的安息日，你们在田野必找不着了。

chapters.en: Six days you are to gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will not be any.”
chapters.zh: 六天可以收取，第七天乃是安息日，那一天必没有了。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather it, but they found none.
chapters.zh: 第七天，百姓中有人出去收，什么也找不着。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep my commands and my instructions?
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你们不肯守我的诫命和律法，要到几时呢？

chapters.en: Bear in mind that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Everyone is to stay where they are on the seventh day; no one is to go out.”
chapters.zh: 你们看，耶和华既将安息日赐给你们，所以第六天他赐给你们两天的食物，第七天各人要住在自己的地方，不许什么人出去。

chapters.en: So the people rested on the seventh day.
chapters.zh: 于是百姓第七天安息了。

chapters.en: The people of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
chapters.zh: 这食物，以色列家叫吗哪，样子像芫荽子，颜色是白的，滋味如同搀蜜的薄饼。

chapters.en: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Take an omer of manna and keep it for the generations to come, so they can see the bread I gave you to eat in the wilderness when I brought you out of Egypt.’ ”
chapters.zh: 摩西说，耶和华所吩咐的是这样，要将一满俄梅珥吗哪留到世世代代，使后人可以看见我当日将你们领出埃及地，在旷野所给你们吃的食物。

chapters.en: So Moses said to Aaron, “Take a jar and put an omer of manna in it. Then place it before the LORD to be kept for the generations to come.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦说，你拿一个罐子，盛一满俄梅珥吗哪，存在耶和华面前，要留到世世代代。

chapters.en: As the LORD commanded Moses, Aaron put the manna with the tablets of the covenant law, so that it might be preserved.
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎么吩咐摩西，亚伦就怎么行，把吗哪放在法柜前存留。

chapters.en: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land that was settled; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
chapters.zh: 以色列人吃吗哪共四十年，直到进了有人居住之地，就是迦南的境界。

chapters.en: (An omer is one-tenth of an ephah.)
chapters.zh: （俄梅珥乃伊法十分之一）。

chapters.en: The whole Israelite community set out from the Desert of Sin, traveling from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众都遵耶和华的吩咐，按着站口从汛的旷野往前行，在利非订安营。百姓没有水喝，

chapters.en: So they quarreled with Moses and said, “Give us water to drink.” Moses replied, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you put the LORD to the test?”
chapters.zh: 所以与摩西争闹，说，给我们水喝吧。摩西对他们说，你们为什么与我争闹？为什么试探耶和华呢？

chapters.en: But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses. They said, “Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?”
chapters.zh: 百姓在那里甚渴，要喝水，就向摩西发怨言，说，你为什么将我们从埃及领出来，使我们和我们的儿女并牲畜都渴死呢？

chapters.en: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What am I to do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me.”
chapters.zh: 摩西就呼求耶和华说，我向这百姓怎样行呢？他们几乎要拿石头打死我。

chapters.en: The LORD answered Moses, “Go out in front of the people. Take with you some of the elders of Israel and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你手里拿着你先前击打河水的杖，带领以色列的几个长老，从百姓面前走过去。

chapters.en: I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink.” So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.
chapters.zh: 我必在何烈的磐石那里，站在你面前。你要击打磐石，从磐石里必有水流出来，使百姓可以喝。摩西就在以色列的长老眼前这样行了。

chapters.en: And he called the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled and because they tested the LORD saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
chapters.zh: 他给那地方起名叫玛撒（就是试探的意思），又叫米利巴（就是争闹的意思），因以色列人争闹，又因他们试探耶和华，说，耶和华是在我们中间不是。

chapters.en: The Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.
chapters.zh: 那时，亚玛力人来在利非订，和以色列人争战。

chapters.en: Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hands.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对约书亚说，你为我们选出人来，出去和亚玛力人争战。明天我手里要拿着神的杖，站在山顶上。

chapters.en: So Joshua fought the Amalekites as Moses had ordered, and Moses, Aaron and Hur went to the top of the hill.
chapters.zh: 于是约书亚照着摩西对他所说的话行，和亚玛力人争战。摩西，亚伦，与户珥都上了山顶。

chapters.en: As long as Moses held up his hands, the Israelites were winning, but whenever he lowered his hands, the Amalekites were winning.
chapters.zh: 摩西何时举手，以色列人就得胜，何时垂手，亚玛力人就得胜。

chapters.en: When Moses’ hands grew tired, they took a stone and put it under him and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held his hands up—one on one side, one on the other—so that his hands remained steady till sunset.
chapters.zh: 但摩西的手发沉，他们就搬石头来，放在他以下，他就坐在上面。亚伦与户珥扶着他的手，一个在这边，一个在那边，他的手就稳住，直到日落的时候。

chapters.en: So Joshua overcame the Amalekite army with the sword.
chapters.zh: 约书亚用刀杀了亚玛力王和他的百姓。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this on a scroll as something to be remembered and make sure that Joshua hears it, because I will completely blot out the name of Amalek from under heaven.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，我要将亚玛力的名号从天下全然涂抹了，你要将这话写在书上作纪念，又念给约书亚听。

chapters.en: Moses built an altar and called it The LORD is my Banner.
chapters.zh: 摩西筑了一座坛，起名叫耶和华尼西（就是耶和华是我旌旗的意思），

chapters.en: He said, “Because hands were lifted up against the throne of the LORD, the LORD will be at war against the Amalekites from generation to generation.”
chapters.zh: 又说，耶和华已经起了誓，必世世代代和亚玛力人争战。

chapters.en: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses, heard of everything God had done for Moses and for his people Israel, and how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父，米甸祭司叶忒罗，听见神为摩西和神的百姓以色列所行的一切事，就是耶和华将以色列从埃及领出来的事，

chapters.en: After Moses had sent away his wife Zipporah, his father-in-law Jethro received her
chapters.zh: 便带着摩西的妻子西坡拉，就是摩西从前打发回去的，

chapters.en: and her two sons. One son was named Gershom, for Moses said, “I have become a foreigner in a foreign land”;
chapters.zh: 又带着西坡拉的两个儿子，一个名叫革舜，因为摩西说，我在外邦作了寄居的，

chapters.en: and the other was named Eliezer, for he said, “My father’s God was my helper; he saved me from the sword of Pharaoh.”
chapters.zh: 一个名叫以利以谢，因为他说，我父亲的神帮助了我，救我脱离法老的刀。

chapters.en: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, together with Moses’ sons and wife, came to him in the wilderness, where he was camped near the mountain of God.
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父叶忒罗带着摩西的妻子和两个儿子来到神的山，就是摩西在旷野安营的地方。

chapters.en: Jethro had sent word to him, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons.”
chapters.zh: 他对摩西说，我是你岳父叶忒罗，带着你的妻子和两个儿子来到你这里。

chapters.en: So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down and kissed him. They greeted each other and then went into the tent.
chapters.zh: 摩西迎接他的岳父，向他下拜，与他亲嘴，彼此问安，都进了帐棚。

chapters.en: Moses told his father-in-law about everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel’s sake and about all the hardships they had met along the way and how the LORD had saved them.
chapters.zh: 摩西将耶和华为以色列的缘故向法老和埃及人所行的一切事，以及路上所遭遇的一切艰难，并耶和华怎样搭救他们，都述说与他岳父听。

chapters.en: Jethro was delighted to hear about all the good things the LORD had done for Israel in rescuing them from the hand of the Egyptians.
chapters.zh: 叶忒罗因耶和华待以色列的一切好处，就是拯救他们脱离埃及人的手，便甚欢喜。

chapters.en: He said, “Praise be to the LORD, who rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians and of Pharaoh, and who rescued the people from the hand of the Egyptians.
chapters.zh: 叶忒罗说，耶和华是应当称颂的，他救了你们脱离埃及人和法老的手，将这百姓从埃及人的手下救出来。

chapters.en: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for he did this to those who had treated Israel arrogantly.”
chapters.zh: 我现今在埃及人向这百姓发狂傲的事上得知，耶和华比万神都大。

chapters.en: Then Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and other sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat a meal with Moses’ father-in-law in the presence of God.
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父叶忒罗把燔祭和平安祭献给神。亚伦和以色列的众长老都来了，与摩西的岳父在神面前吃饭。

chapters.en: The next day Moses took his seat to serve as judge for the people, and they stood around him from morning till evening.
chapters.zh: 第二天，摩西坐着审判百姓，百姓从早到晚都站在摩西的左右。

chapters.en: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he said, “What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you alone sit as judge, while all these people stand around you from morning till evening?”
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父看见他向百姓所作的一切事，就说，你向百姓作的是什么事呢？你为什么独自坐着，众百姓从早到晚都站在你的左右呢？

chapters.en: Moses answered him, “Because the people come to me to seek God’s will.
chapters.zh: 摩西对岳父说，这是因百姓到我这里来求问神。

chapters.en: Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me, and I decide between the parties and inform them of God’s decrees and instructions.”
chapters.zh: 他们有事的时候就到我这里来，我便在两造之间施行审判，我又叫他们知道神的律例和法度。

chapters.en: Moses’ father-in-law replied, “What you are doing is not good.
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父说，你这作的不好。

chapters.en: You and these people who come to you will only wear yourselves out. The work is too heavy for you; you cannot handle it alone.
chapters.zh: 你和这些百姓必都疲惫，因为这事太重，你独自一人办理不了。

chapters.en: Listen now to me and I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the people’s representative before God and bring their disputes to him.
chapters.zh: 现在你要听我的话。我为你出个主意，愿神与你同在。你要替百姓到神面前，将案件奏告神，

chapters.en: Teach them his decrees and instructions, and show them the way they are to live and how they are to behave.
chapters.zh: 又要将律例和法度教训他们，指示他们当行的道，当作的事，

chapters.en: But select capable men from all the people—men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate dishonest gain—and appoint them as officials over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.
chapters.zh: 并要从百姓中拣选有才能的人，就是敬畏神，诚实无妄，恨不义之财的人，派他们作千夫长，百夫长，五十夫长，十夫长，管理百姓，

chapters.en: Have them serve as judges for the people at all times, but have them bring every difficult case to you; the simple cases they can decide themselves. That will make your load lighter, because they will share it with you.
chapters.zh: 叫他们随时审判百姓，大事都要呈到你这里，小事他们自己可以审判。这样，你就轻省些，他们也可以同当此任。

chapters.en: If you do this and God so commands, you will be able to stand the strain, and all these people will go home satisfied.”
chapters.zh: 你若这样行，神也这样吩咐你，你就能受得住，这百姓也都平平安安归回他们的住处。

chapters.en: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西听从他岳父的话，按着他所说的去行。

chapters.en: He chose capable men from all Israel and made them leaders of the people, officials over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.
chapters.zh: 摩西从以色列人中拣选了有才能的人，立他们为百姓的首领，作千夫长，百夫长，五十夫长，十夫长。

chapters.en: They served as judges for the people at all times. The difficult cases they brought to Moses, but the simple ones they decided themselves.
chapters.zh: 他们随时审判百姓，有难断的案件就呈到摩西那里，但各样小事他们自己审判。

chapters.en: Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro returned to his own country.
chapters.zh: 此后，摩西让他的岳父去，他就往本地去了。

chapters.en: On the first day of the third month after the Israelites left Egypt—on that very day—they came to the Desert of Sinai.
chapters.zh: 以色列人出埃及地以后，满了三个月的那一天，就来到西乃的旷野。

chapters.en: After they set out from Rephidim, they entered the Desert of Sinai, and Israel camped there in the desert in front of the mountain.
chapters.zh: 他们离了利非订，来到西乃的旷野，就在那里的山下安营。

chapters.en: Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain and said, “This is what you are to say to the descendants of Jacob and what you are to tell the people of Israel:
chapters.zh: 摩西到神那里，耶和华从山上呼唤他说，你要这样告诉雅各家，晓谕以色列人说，

chapters.en: ‘You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself.
chapters.zh: 我向埃及人所行的事，你们都看见了，且看见我如鹰将你们背在翅膀上，带来归我。

chapters.en: Now if you obey me fully and keep my covenant, then out of all nations you will be my treasured possession. Although the whole earth is mine,
chapters.zh: 如今你们若实在听从我的话，遵守我的约，就要在万民中作属我的子民，因为全地都是我的。

chapters.en: you will be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words you are to speak to the Israelites.”
chapters.zh: 你们要归我作祭司的国度，为圣洁的国民。这些话你要告诉以色列人。

chapters.en: So Moses went back and summoned the elders of the people and set before them all the words the LORD had commanded him to speak.
chapters.zh: 摩西去召了民间的长老来，将耶和华所吩咐他的话都在他们面前陈明。

chapters.en: The people all responded together, “We will do everything the LORD has said.” So Moses brought their answer back to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 百姓都同声回答说，凡耶和华所说的，我们都要遵行。摩西就将百姓的话回覆耶和华。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses, “I am going to come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people will hear me speaking with you and will always put their trust in you.” Then Moses told the LORD what the people had said.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，我要在密云中临到你那里，叫百姓在我与你说话的时候可以听见，也可以永远信你了。于是，摩西将百姓的话奏告耶和华。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. Have them wash their clothes
chapters.zh: 耶和华又对摩西说，你往百姓那里去，叫他们今天明天自洁，又叫他们洗衣服。

chapters.en: and be ready by the third day, because on that day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
chapters.zh: 到第三天要预备好了，因为第三天耶和华要在众百姓眼前降临在西乃山上。

chapters.en: Put limits for the people around the mountain and tell them, ‘Be careful that you do not approach the mountain or touch the foot of it. Whoever touches the mountain is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 你要在山的四围给百姓定界限，说，你们当谨慎，不可上山去，也不可摸山的边界，凡摸这山的，必要治死他。

chapters.en: They are to be stoned or shot with arrows; not a hand is to be laid on them. No person or animal shall be permitted to live.’ Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain.”
chapters.zh: 不可用手摸他，必用石头打死，或用箭射透，无论是人是牲畜，都不得活。到角声拖长的时候，他们才可到山根来。

chapters.en: After Moses had gone down the mountain to the people, he consecrated them, and they washed their clothes.
chapters.zh: 摩西下山往百姓那里去，叫他们自洁，他们就洗衣服。

chapters.en: Then he said to the people, “Prepare yourselves for the third day. Abstain from sexual relations.”
chapters.zh: 他对百姓说，到第三天要预备好了。不可亲近女人。

chapters.en: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, with a thick cloud over the mountain, and a very loud trumpet blast. Everyone in the camp trembled.
chapters.zh: 到了第三天早晨，在山上有雷轰，闪电，和密云，并且角声甚大，营中的百姓尽都发颤。

chapters.en: Then Moses led the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
chapters.zh: 摩西率领百姓出营迎接神，都站在山下。

chapters.en: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke, because the LORD descended on it in fire. The smoke billowed up from it like smoke from a furnace, and the whole mountain trembled violently.
chapters.zh: 西乃全山冒烟，因为耶和华在火中降于山上。山的烟气上腾，如烧窑一般，遍山大大地震动。

chapters.en: As the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and the voice of God answered him.
chapters.zh: 角声渐渐地高而又高，摩西就说话，神有声音答应他。

chapters.en: The LORD descended to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the top of the mountain. So Moses went up
chapters.zh: 耶和华降临在西乃山顶上，耶和华召摩西上山顶，摩西就上去。

chapters.en: and the LORD said to him, “Go down and warn the people so they do not force their way through to see the LORD and many of them perish.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你下去嘱咐百姓，不可闯过来到我面前观看，恐怕他们有多人死亡，

chapters.en: Even the priests, who approach the LORD, must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them.”
chapters.zh: 又叫亲近我的祭司自洁，恐怕我忽然出来击杀他们。

chapters.en: Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, because you yourself warned us, ‘Put limits around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’ ”
chapters.zh: 摩西对耶和华说，百姓不能上西乃山，因为你已经嘱咐我们说，要在山的四围定界限，叫山成圣。

chapters.en: The LORD replied, “Go down and bring Aaron up with you. But the priests and the people must not force their way through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对他说，下去吧，你要和亚伦一同上来，只是祭司和百姓不可闯过来上到我面前，恐怕我忽然出来击杀他们。

chapters.en: So Moses went down to the people and told them.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西下到百姓那里告诉他们。

chapters.en: And God spoke all these words:
chapters.zh: 神吩咐这一切的话说，

chapters.en: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery.
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华你的神，曾将你从埃及地为奴之家领出来。

chapters.en: “You shall have no other gods before me.
chapters.zh: 除了我以外，你不可有别的神。

chapters.en: “You shall not make for yourself an image in the form of anything in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the waters below.
chapters.zh: 不可为自己雕刻偶像，也不可作什么形像仿佛上天，下地，和地底下，水中的百物。

chapters.en: You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sin of the parents to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
chapters.zh: 不可跪拜那些像，也不可事奉它，因为我耶和华你的神是忌邪的神。恨我的，我必追讨他的罪，自父及子，直到三四代，

chapters.en: but showing love to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.
chapters.zh: 爱我，守我诫命的，我必向他们发慈爱，直到千代。

chapters.en: “You shall not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not hold anyone guiltless who misuses his name.
chapters.zh: 不可妄称耶和华你神的名，因为妄称耶和华名的，耶和华必不以他为无罪。

chapters.en: “Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.
chapters.zh: 当记念安息日，守为圣日。

chapters.en: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
chapters.zh: 六日要劳碌作你一切的工，

chapters.en: but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall not do any work, neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your animals, nor any foreigner residing in your towns.
chapters.zh: 但第七日是向耶和华你神当守的安息日。这一日你和你的儿女，仆婢，牲畜，并你城里寄居的客旅，无论何工都不可作，

chapters.en: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, but he rested on the seventh day. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
chapters.zh: 因为六日之内，耶和华造天，地，海，和其中的万物，第七日便安息，所以耶和华赐福与安息日，定为圣日。

chapters.en: “Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
chapters.zh: 当孝敬父母，使你的日子在耶和华你神所赐你的地上得以长久。

chapters.en: “You shall not murder.
chapters.zh: 不可杀人。

chapters.en: “You shall not commit adultery.
chapters.zh: 不可奸淫。

chapters.en: “You shall not steal.
chapters.zh: 不可偷盗。

chapters.en: “You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
chapters.zh: 不可作假见证陷害人。

chapters.en: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his male or female servant, his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”
chapters.zh: 不可贪恋人的房屋，也不可贪恋人的妻子，仆婢，牛驴，并他一切所有的。

chapters.en: When the people saw the thunder and lightning and heard the trumpet and saw the mountain in smoke, they trembled with fear. They stayed at a distance
chapters.zh: 众百姓见雷轰，闪电，角声，山上冒烟，就都发颤，远远地站立。

chapters.en: and said to Moses, “Speak to us yourself and we will listen. But do not have God speak to us or we will die.”
chapters.zh: 对摩西说，求你和我们说话，我们必听，不要神和我们说话，恐怕我们死亡。

chapters.en: Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, so that the fear of God will be with you to keep you from sinning.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对百姓说，不要惧怕，因为神降临是要试验你们，叫你们时常敬畏他，不致犯罪。

chapters.en: The people remained at a distance, while Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
chapters.zh: 于是百姓远远地站立，摩西就挨近神所在的幽暗之中。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites this: ‘You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven:
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你要向以色列人这样说，你们自己看见我从天上和你们说话了。

chapters.en: Do not make any gods to be alongside me; do not make for yourselves gods of silver or gods of gold.
chapters.zh: 你们不可作什么神像与我相配，不可为自己作金银的神像。

chapters.en: “ ‘Make an altar of earth for me and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, your sheep and goats and your cattle. Wherever I cause my name to be honored, I will come to you and bless you.
chapters.zh: 你要为我筑土坛，在上面以牛羊献为燔祭和平安祭。凡记下我名的地方，我必到那里赐福给你。

chapters.en: If you make an altar of stones for me, do not build it with dressed stones, for you will defile it if you use a tool on it.
chapters.zh: 你若为我筑一座石坛，不可用凿成的石头，因你在上头一动家具，就把坛污秽了。

chapters.en: And do not go up to my altar on steps, or your private parts may be exposed.’
chapters.zh: 你上我的坛，不可用台阶，免得露出你的下体来。

chapters.en: “These are the laws you are to set before them:
chapters.zh: 你在百姓面前所要立的典章是这样，

chapters.en: “If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free, without paying anything.
chapters.zh: 你若买希伯来人作奴仆，他必服事你六年，第七年他可以自由，白白地出去。

chapters.en: If he comes alone, he is to go free alone; but if he has a wife when he comes, she is to go with him.
chapters.zh: 他若孤身来，就可以孤身去，他若有妻，他的妻就可以同他出去。

chapters.en: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free.
chapters.zh: 他主人若给他妻子，妻子给他生了儿子或女儿，妻子和儿女要归主人，他要独自出去。

chapters.en: “But if the servant declares, ‘I love my master and my wife and children and do not want to go free,’
chapters.zh: 倘或奴仆明说，我爱我的主人和我的妻子儿女，不愿意自由出去。

chapters.en: then his master must take him before the judges. He shall take him to the door or the doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he will be his servant for life.
chapters.zh: 他的主人就要带他到审判官那里（审判官或作神下同），又要带他到门前，靠近门框，用锥子穿他的耳朵，他就永远服事主人。

chapters.en: “If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as male servants do.
chapters.zh: 人若卖女儿作婢女，婢女不可像男仆那样出去。

chapters.en: If she does not please the master who has selected her for himself, he must let her be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, because he has broken faith with her.
chapters.zh: 主人选定她归自己，若不喜欢她，就要许她赎身，主人既然用诡诈待她，就没有权柄卖给外邦人。

chapters.en: If he selects her for his son, he must grant her the rights of a daughter.
chapters.zh: 主人若选定她给自己的儿子，就当待她如同女儿。

chapters.en: If he marries another woman, he must not deprive the first one of her food, clothing and marital rights.
chapters.zh: 若另娶一个，那女子的吃食，衣服，并好合的事，仍不可减少。

chapters.en: If he does not provide her with these three things, she is to go free, without any payment of money.
chapters.zh: 若不向她行这三样，她就可以不用钱赎，白白地出去。

chapters.en: “Anyone who strikes a person with a fatal blow is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 打人以致打死的，必要把他治死。

chapters.en: However, if it is not done intentionally, but God lets it happen, they are to flee to a place I will designate.
chapters.zh: 人若不是埋伏着杀人，乃是神交在他手中，我就设下一个地方，他可以往那里逃跑。

chapters.en: But if anyone schemes and kills someone deliberately, that person is to be taken from my altar and put to death.
chapters.zh: 人若任意用诡计杀了他的邻舍，就是逃到我的坛那里，也当捉去把他治死。

chapters.en: “Anyone who attacks their father or mother is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 打父母的，必要把他治死。

chapters.en: “Anyone who kidnaps someone is to be put to death, whether the victim has been sold or is still in the kidnapper’s possession.
chapters.zh: 拐带人口，或是把人卖了，或是留在他手下，必要把他治死。

chapters.en: “Anyone who curses their father or mother is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 咒骂父母的，必要把他治死。

chapters.en: “If people quarrel and one person hits another with a stone or with their fist and the victim does not die but is confined to bed,
chapters.zh: 人若彼此相争，这个用石头或是拳头打那个，尚且不至于死，不过躺卧在床，

chapters.en: the one who struck the blow will not be held liable if the other can get up and walk around outside with a staff; however, the guilty party must pay the injured person for any loss of time and see that the victim is completely healed.
chapters.zh: 若再能起来扶杖而出，那打他的可算无罪，但要将他耽误的工夫用钱赔补，并要将他全然医好。

chapters.en: “Anyone who beats their male or female slave with a rod must be punished if the slave dies as a direct result,
chapters.zh: 人若用棍子打奴仆或婢女，立时死在他的手下，他必要受刑。

chapters.en: but they are not to be punished if the slave recovers after a day or two, since the slave is their property.
chapters.zh: 若过一两天才死，就可以不受刑，因为是用钱买的。

chapters.en: “If people are fighting and hit a pregnant woman and she gives birth prematurely but there is no serious injury, the offender must be fined whatever the woman’s husband demands and the court allows.
chapters.zh: 人若彼此争斗，伤害有孕的妇人，甚至坠胎，随后却无别害，那伤害她的，总要按妇人的丈夫所要的，照审判官所断的，受罚。

chapters.en: But if there is serious injury, you are to take life for life,
chapters.zh: 若有别害，就要以命偿命，

chapters.en: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
chapters.zh: 以眼还眼，以牙还牙，以手还手，以脚还脚，

chapters.en: burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
chapters.zh: 以烙还烙，以伤还伤，以打还打。

chapters.en: “An owner who hits a male or female slave in the eye and destroys it must let the slave go free to compensate for the eye.
chapters.zh: 人若打坏了他奴仆或是婢女的一只眼，就要因他的眼放他去得以自由。

chapters.en: And an owner who knocks out the tooth of a male or female slave must let the slave go free to compensate for the tooth.
chapters.zh: 若打掉了他奴仆或是婢女的一个牙，就要因他的牙放他去得以自由。

chapters.en: “If a bull gores a man or woman to death, the bull is to be stoned to death, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the bull will not be held responsible.
chapters.zh: 牛若触死男人或是女人，总要用石头打死那牛，却不可吃它的肉，牛的主人可算无罪。

chapters.en: If, however, the bull has had the habit of goring and the owner has been warned but has not kept it penned up and it kills a man or woman, the bull is to be stoned and its owner also is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 倘若那牛素来是触人的，有人报告了牛主，他竟不把牛拴着，以致把男人或是女人触死，就要用石头打死那牛，牛主也必治死。

chapters.en: However, if payment is demanded, the owner may redeem his life by the payment of whatever is demanded.
chapters.zh: 若罚他赎命的价银，他必照所罚的赎他的命。

chapters.en: This law also applies if the bull gores a son or daughter.
chapters.zh: 牛无论触了人的儿子或是女儿，必照这例办理。

chapters.en: If the bull gores a male or female slave, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the master of the slave, and the bull is to be stoned to death.
chapters.zh: 牛若触了奴仆或是婢女，必将银子三十舍客勒给他们的主人，也要用石头把牛打死。

chapters.en: “If anyone uncovers a pit or digs one and fails to cover it and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
chapters.zh: 人若敞着井口，或挖井不遮盖，有牛或驴掉在里头，

chapters.en: the one who opened the pit must pay the owner for the loss and take the dead animal in exchange.
chapters.zh: 井主要拿钱赔还本主人，死牲畜要归自己。

chapters.en: “If anyone’s bull injures someone else’s bull and it dies, the two parties are to sell the live one and divide both the money and the dead animal equally.
chapters.zh: 这人的牛若伤了那人的牛，以致于死，他们要卖了活牛，平分价值，也要平分死牛。

chapters.en: However, if it was known that the bull had the habit of goring, yet the owner did not keep it penned up, the owner must pay, animal for animal, and take the dead animal in exchange.
chapters.zh: 人若知道这牛素来是触人的，主人竟不把牛拴着，他必要以牛还牛，死牛要归自己。

chapters.en: “Whoever steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it must pay back five head of cattle for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
chapters.zh: 人若偷牛或羊，无论是宰了，是卖了，他就要以五牛赔一牛，四羊赔一羊。

chapters.en: “If a thief is caught breaking in at night and is struck a fatal blow, the defender is not guilty of bloodshed;
chapters.zh: 人若遇见贼挖窟窿，把贼打了，以致于死，就不能为他有流血的罪。

chapters.en: but if it happens after sunrise, the defender is guilty of bloodshed. “Anyone who steals must certainly make restitution, but if they have nothing, they must be sold to pay for their theft.
chapters.zh: 若太阳已经出来，就为他有流血的罪。贼若被拿，总要赔还。若他一无所有，就要被卖，顶他所偷的物。

chapters.en: If the stolen animal is found alive in their possession—whether ox or donkey or sheep—they must pay back double.
chapters.zh: 若他所偷的，或牛，或驴，或羊，仍在他手下存活，他就要加倍赔还。

chapters.en: “If anyone grazes their livestock in a field or vineyard and lets them stray and they graze in someone else’s field, the offender must make restitution from the best of their own field or vineyard.
chapters.zh: 人若在田间或在葡萄园里放牲畜，任凭牲畜上别人的田里去吃，就必拿自己田间上好的和葡萄园上好的赔还。

chapters.en: “If a fire breaks out and spreads into thornbushes so that it burns shocks of grain or standing grain or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make restitution.
chapters.zh: 若点火焚烧荆棘，以致将别人堆积的禾捆，站着的禾稼，或是田园，都烧尽了，那点火的必要赔还。

chapters.en: “If anyone gives a neighbor silver or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double.
chapters.zh: 人若将银钱或家具交付邻舍看守，这物从那人的家被偷去，若把贼找到了，贼要加倍赔还，

chapters.en: But if the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges, and they must determine whether the owner of the house has laid hands on the other person’s property.
chapters.zh: 若找不到贼，那家主必就近审判官，要看看他拿了原主的物件没有。

chapters.en: In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any other lost property about which somebody says, ‘This is mine,’ both parties are to bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges declare guilty must pay back double to the other.
chapters.zh: 两个人的案件，无论是为什么过犯，或是为牛，为驴，为羊，为衣裳，或是为什么失掉之物，有一人说，这是我的，两造就要将案件禀告审判官，审判官定谁有罪，谁就要加倍赔还。

chapters.en: “If anyone gives a donkey, an ox, a sheep or any other animal to their neighbor for safekeeping and it dies or is injured or is taken away while no one is looking,
chapters.zh: 人若将驴，或牛，或羊，或别的牲畜，交付邻舍看守，牲畜或死，或受伤，或被赶去，无人看见，

chapters.en: the issue between them will be settled by the taking of an oath before the LORD that the neighbor did not lay hands on the other person’s property. The owner is to accept this, and no restitution is required.
chapters.zh: 那看守的人要凭着耶和华起誓，手里未曾拿邻舍的物，本主就要罢休，看守的人不必赔还。

chapters.en: But if the animal was stolen from the neighbor, restitution must be made to the owner.
chapters.zh: 牲畜若从看守的那里被偷去，他就要赔还本主，

chapters.en: If it was torn to pieces by a wild animal, the neighbor shall bring in the remains as evidence and shall not be required to pay for the torn animal.
chapters.zh: 若被野兽撕碎，看守的要带来当作证据，所撕的不必赔还。

chapters.en: “If anyone borrows an animal from their neighbor and it is injured or dies while the owner is not present, they must make restitution.
chapters.zh: 人若向邻舍借什么，所借的或受伤，或死，本主没有同在一处，借的人总要赔还，

chapters.en: But if the owner is with the animal, the borrower will not have to pay. If the animal was hired, the money paid for the hire covers the loss.
chapters.zh: 若本主同在一处，他就不必赔还，若是雇的，也不必赔还，本是为雇价来的。

chapters.en: “If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged to be married and sleeps with her, he must pay the bride-price, and she shall be his wife.
chapters.zh: 人若引诱没有受聘的处女，与她行淫，他总要交出聘礼，娶她为妻。

chapters.en: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he must still pay the bride-price for virgins.
chapters.zh: 若女子的父亲决不肯将女子给他，他就要按处女的聘礼，交出钱来。

chapters.en: “Do not allow a sorceress to live.
chapters.zh: 行邪术的女人，不可容她存活。

chapters.en: “Anyone who has sexual relations with an animal is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 凡与兽淫合的，总要把他治死。

chapters.en: “Whoever sacrifices to any god other than the LORD must be destroyed.
chapters.zh: 祭祀别神，不单单祭祀耶和华的，那人必要灭绝。

chapters.en: “Do not mistreat or oppress a foreigner, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
chapters.zh: 不可亏负寄居的，也不可欺压他，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

chapters.en: “Do not take advantage of the widow or the fatherless.
chapters.zh: 不可苦待寡妇和孤儿，

chapters.en: If you do and they cry out to me, I will certainly hear their cry.
chapters.zh: 若是苦待他们一点，他们向我一哀求，我总要听他们的哀声，

chapters.en: My anger will be aroused, and I will kill you with the sword; your wives will become widows and your children fatherless.
chapters.zh: 并要发烈怒，用刀杀你们，使你们的妻子为寡妇，儿女为孤儿。

chapters.en: “If you lend money to one of my people among you who is needy, do not treat it like a business deal; charge no interest.
chapters.zh: 我民中有贫穷人与你同住，你若借钱给他，不可如放债的向他取利。

chapters.en: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as a pledge, return it by sunset,
chapters.zh: 你即或拿邻舍的衣服作当头，必在日落以先归还他，

chapters.en: because that cloak is the only covering your neighbor has. What else can they sleep in? When they cry out to me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
chapters.zh: 因他只有这一件当盖头，是他盖身的衣服，若是没有，他拿什么睡觉呢？他哀求我，我就应允，因为我是有恩惠的。

chapters.en: “Do not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people.
chapters.zh: 不可毁谤神，也不可毁谤你百姓的官长。

chapters.en: “Do not hold back offerings from your granaries or your vats.“You must give me the firstborn of your sons.
chapters.zh: 你要从你庄稼中的谷和酒榨中滴出来的酒拿来献上，不可迟延。你要将头生的儿子归给我。

chapters.en: Do the same with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but give them to me on the eighth day.
chapters.zh: 你牛羊头生的，也要这样，七天当跟着母，第八天要归给我。

chapters.en: “You are to be my holy people. So do not eat the meat of an animal torn by wild beasts; throw it to the dogs.
chapters.zh: 你要在我面前为圣洁的人。因此，田间被野兽撕裂牲畜的肉，你们不可吃，要丢给狗吃。

chapters.en: “Do not spread false reports. Do not help a guilty person by being a malicious witness.
chapters.zh: 不可随伙布散谣言，不可与恶人连手妄作见证。

chapters.en: “Do not follow the crowd in doing wrong. When you give testimony in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd,
chapters.zh: 不可随众行恶，不可在争讼的事上随众偏行，作见证屈枉正直，

chapters.en: and do not show favoritism to a poor person in a lawsuit.
chapters.zh: 也不可在争讼的事上偏护穷人。

chapters.en: “If you come across your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering off, be sure to return it.
chapters.zh: 若遇见你仇敌的牛或驴失迷了路，总要牵回来交给他。

chapters.en: If you see the donkey of someone who hates you fallen down under its load, do not leave it there; be sure you help them with it.
chapters.zh: 若看见恨你人的驴压卧在重驮之下，不可走开，务要和驴主一同抬开重驮。

chapters.en: “Do not deny justice to your poor people in their lawsuits.
chapters.zh: 不可在穷人争讼的事上屈枉正直。

chapters.en: Have nothing to do with a false charge and do not put an innocent or honest person to death, for I will not acquit the guilty.
chapters.zh: 当远离虚假的事。不可杀无辜和有义的人，因我必不以恶人为义。

chapters.en: “Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the innocent.
chapters.zh: 不可受贿赂，因为贿赂能叫明眼人变瞎了，又能颠倒义人的话。

chapters.en: “Do not oppress a foreigner; you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
chapters.zh: 不可欺压寄居的，因为你们在埃及地作过寄居的，知道寄居的心。

chapters.en: “For six years you are to sow your fields and harvest the crops,
chapters.zh: 六年你要耕种田地，收藏土产，

chapters.en: but during the seventh year let the land lie unplowed and unused. Then the poor among your people may get food from it, and the wild animals may eat what is left. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
chapters.zh: 只是第七年要叫地歇息，不耕不种，使你民中的穷人有吃的，他们所剩下的，野兽可以吃。你的葡萄园和橄榄园也要照样办理。

chapters.en: “Six days do your work, but on the seventh day do not work, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and so that the slave born in your household and the foreigner living among you may be refreshed.
chapters.zh: 六日你要作工，第七日要安息，使牛，驴可以歇息，并使你婢女的儿子和寄居的都可以舒畅。

chapters.en: “Be careful to do everything I have said to you. Do not invoke the names of other gods; do not let them be heard on your lips.
chapters.zh: 凡我对你们说的话，你们要谨守。别神的名，你不可提，也不可从你口中传说。

chapters.en: “Three times a year you are to celebrate a festival to me.
chapters.zh: 一年三次，你要向我守节。

chapters.en: “Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread; for seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you. Do this at the appointed time in the month of Aviv, for in that month you came out of Egypt. “No one is to appear before me empty-handed.
chapters.zh: 你要守除酵节，照我所吩咐你的，在亚笔月内所定的日期，吃无酵饼七天。谁也不可空手朝见我，因为你是这月出了埃及。

chapters.en: “Celebrate the Festival of Harvest with the firstfruits of the crops you sow in your field. “Celebrate the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in your crops from the field.
chapters.zh: 又要守收割节，所收的是你田间所种，劳碌得来初熟之物。并在年底收藏，要守收藏节。

chapters.en: “Three times a year all the men are to appear before the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 一切的男丁要一年三次朝见主耶和华。

chapters.en: “Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to me along with anything containing yeast. “The fat of my festival offerings must not be kept until morning.
chapters.zh: 不可将我祭牲的血和有酵的饼一同献上，也不可将我节上祭牲的脂油留到早晨。

chapters.en: “Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. “Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
chapters.zh: 地里首先初熟之物要送到耶和华你神的殿。不可用山羊羔母的奶煮山羊羔。

chapters.en: “See, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
chapters.zh: 看哪，我差遣使者在你前面，在路上保护你，领你到我所预备的地方去。

chapters.en: Pay attention to him and listen to what he says. Do not rebel against him; he will not forgive your rebellion, since my Name is in him.
chapters.zh: 他是奉我名来的，你们要在他面前谨慎，听从他的话，不可惹他（惹或作违背），因为他必不赦免你们的过犯。

chapters.en: If you listen carefully to what he says and do all that I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and will oppose those who oppose you.
chapters.zh: 你若实在听从他的话，照着我一切所说的去行，我就向你的仇敌作仇敌，向你的敌人作敌人。

chapters.en: My angel will go ahead of you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
