chapters.en: And they made from pure gold the articles for the table—its plates and dishes and bowls and its pitchers for the pouring out of drink offerings.
chapters.zh: 又用精金作桌子上的器皿，就是盘子，调羹，并奠酒的瓶和爵。

chapters.en: They made the lampstand of pure gold. They hammered out its base and shaft, and made its flowerlike cups, buds and blossoms of one piece with them.
chapters.zh: 他用精金作一个灯台，这灯台的座和干，与杯，球，花，都是接连一块锤出来的。

chapters.en: Six branches extended from the sides of the lampstand—three on one side and three on the other.
chapters.zh: 灯台两旁杈出六个枝子，这旁三个，那旁三个。

chapters.en: Three cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms were on one branch, three on the next branch and the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
chapters.zh: 这旁每枝上有三个杯，形状像杏花，有球有花，那旁每枝上也有三个杯，形状像杏花，有球有花。从灯台杈出来的六个枝子都是如此。

chapters.en: And on the lampstand were four cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms.
chapters.zh: 灯台上有四个杯，形状像杏花，有球有花。

chapters.en: One bud was under the first pair of branches extending from the lampstand, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair—six branches in all.
chapters.zh: 灯台每两个枝子以下有球，与枝子接连一块，灯台杈出的六个枝子都是如此。

chapters.en: The buds and the branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
chapters.zh: 球和枝子是接连一块，都是一块精金锤出来的。

chapters.en: They made its seven lamps, as well as its wick trimmers and trays, of pure gold.
chapters.zh: 用精金作灯台的七个灯盏，并灯台的蜡剪和蜡花盘。

chapters.en: They made the lampstand and all its accessories from one talent of pure gold.
chapters.zh: 他用精金一他连得作灯台和灯台的一切器具。

chapters.en: They made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, a cubit long and a cubit wide and two cubits high —its horns of one piece with it.
chapters.zh: 他用皂荚木作香坛，是四方的，长一肘，宽一肘，高二肘，坛的四角与坛接连一块，

chapters.en: They overlaid the top and all the sides and the horns with pure gold, and made a gold molding around it.
chapters.zh: 又用精金把坛的上面与坛的四面并坛的四角包裹，又在坛的四围镶上金牙边。

chapters.en: They made two gold rings below the molding—two on each of the opposite sides—to hold the poles used to carry it.
chapters.zh: 作两个金环，安在牙子边以下，在坛的两旁，两根横撑上，作为穿杠的用处，以便抬坛。

chapters.en: They made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
chapters.zh: 用皂荚木作杠，用金包裹。

chapters.en: They also made the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense—the work of a perfumer.
chapters.zh: 又按作香之法作圣膏油和馨香料的净香。

chapters.en: They built the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood, three cubits high; it was square, five cubits long and five cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 他用皂荚木作燔祭坛，是四方的，长五肘，宽五肘，高三肘，

chapters.en: They made a horn at each of the four corners, so that the horns and the altar were of one piece, and they overlaid the altar with bronze.
chapters.zh: 在坛的四拐角上作四个角，与坛接连一块，用铜把坛包裹。

chapters.en: They made all its utensils of bronze—its pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans.
chapters.zh: 他作坛上的盆，铲子，盘子，肉锸子，火鼎，这一切器具都是用铜作的。

chapters.en: They made a grating for the altar, a bronze network, to be under its ledge, halfway up the altar.
chapters.zh: 又为坛作一个铜网，安在坛四面的围腰板以下，从下达到坛的半腰。

chapters.en: They cast bronze rings to hold the poles for the four corners of the bronze grating.
chapters.zh: 为铜网的四角铸四个环子，作为穿杠的用处。

chapters.en: They made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
chapters.zh: 用皂荚木作杠，用铜包裹，

chapters.en: They inserted the poles into the rings so they would be on the sides of the altar for carrying it. They made it hollow, out of boards.
chapters.zh: 把杠穿在坛两旁的环子内，用以抬坛，并用板作坛，坛是空的。

chapters.en: They made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 他用铜作洗濯盆和盆座，是用会幕门前伺候的妇人之镜子作的。

chapters.en: Next they made the courtyard. The south side was a hundred cubits long and had curtains of finely twisted linen,
chapters.zh: 他作帐幕的院子。院子的南面用捻的细麻作帷子，宽一百肘。

chapters.en: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
chapters.zh: 帷子的柱子二十根，带卯的铜座二十个，柱子上的钩子和杆子都是用银子作的。

chapters.en: The north side was also a hundred cubits long and had twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
chapters.zh: 北面也有帷子，宽一百肘。帷子的柱子二十根，带卯的铜座二十个，柱子上的钩子和杆子都是用银子作的。

chapters.en: The west end was fifty cubits wide and had curtains, with ten posts and ten bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
chapters.zh: 院子的西面有帷子，宽五十肘。帷子的柱子十根，带卯的座十个，柱子的钩子和杆子都是用银子作的。

chapters.en: The east end, toward the sunrise, was also fifty cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 院子的东面，宽五十肘。

chapters.en: Curtains fifteen cubits long were on one side of the entrance, with three posts and three bases,
chapters.zh: 门这边的帷子十五肘，那边也是一样。帷子的柱子三根，带卯的座三个。在门的左右各有帷子十五肘，帷子的柱子三根，带卯的座三个。

chapters.en: and curtains fifteen cubits long were on the other side of the entrance to the courtyard, with three posts and three bases.
All the curtains around the courtyard were of finely twisted linen.
chapters.zh: 院子四面的帷子都是用捻的细麻作的。

chapters.en: The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver; so all the posts of the courtyard had silver bands.
chapters.zh: 柱子带卯的座是铜的，柱子上的钩子和杆子是银的，柱顶是用银子包的。院子一切的柱子都是用银杆连络的。

chapters.en: The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen—the work of an embroiderer. It was twenty cubits long and, like the curtains of the courtyard, five cubits high,
chapters.zh: 院子的门帘是以绣花的手工，用蓝色，紫色，朱红色线，和捻的细麻织的，宽二十肘，高五肘，与院子的帷子相配。

chapters.en: with four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks and bands were silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver.
chapters.zh: 帷子的柱子四根，带卯的铜座四个，柱子上的钩子和杆子是银的，柱顶是用银子包的。

chapters.en: All the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the surrounding courtyard were bronze.
chapters.zh: 帐幕一切的橛子和院子四围的橛子都是铜的。

chapters.en: These are the amounts of the materials used for the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the covenant law, which were recorded at Moses’ command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.
chapters.zh: 这是法柜的帐幕中利未人所用物件的总数，是照摩西的吩咐，经祭司亚伦的儿子以他玛的手数点的。

chapters.en: (Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD commanded Moses;
chapters.zh: 凡耶和华所吩咐摩西的都是犹大支派户珥的孙子，乌利的儿子比撒列作的。

chapters.en: with him was Oholiab son of Ahisamak, of the tribe of Dan—an engraver and designer, and an embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen.)
chapters.zh: 与他同工的有但支派中亚希撒抹的儿子亚何利亚伯，他是雕刻匠，又是巧匠，又能用蓝色，紫色，朱红色线，和细麻绣花。

chapters.en: The total amount of the gold from the wave offering used for all the work on the sanctuary was 29 talents and 730 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
chapters.zh: 为圣所一切工作使用所献的金子，按圣所的平，有二十九他连得并七百三十舍客勒。

chapters.en: The silver obtained from those of the community who were counted in the census was 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel—
chapters.zh: 会中被数的人所出的银子，按圣所的平，有一百他连得并一千七百七十五舍客勒。

chapters.en: one beka per person, that is, half a shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, from everyone who had crossed over to those counted, twenty years old or more, a total of 603,550 men.
chapters.zh: 凡过去归那些被数之人的，从二十岁以外，有六十万零三千五百五十人。按圣所的平，每人出银半舍客勒，就是一比加。

chapters.en: The 100 talents of silver were used to cast the bases for the sanctuary and for the curtain—100 bases from the 100 talents, one talent for each base.
chapters.zh: 用那一百他连得银子铸造圣所带卯的座，和幔子柱子带卯的座，一百他连得共一百带卯的座，每带卯的座用一他连得。

chapters.en: They used the 1,775 shekels to make the hooks for the posts, to overlay the tops of the posts, and to make their bands.
chapters.zh: 用那一千七百七十五舍客勒银子作柱子上的钩子，包裹柱顶并柱子上的杆子。

chapters.en: The bronze from the wave offering was 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.
chapters.zh: 所献的铜有七十他连得并二千四百舍客勒。

chapters.en: They used it to make the bases for the entrance to the tent of meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grating and all its utensils,
chapters.zh: 用这铜作会幕门带卯的座和铜坛，并坛上的铜网和坛的一切器具，

chapters.en: the bases for the surrounding courtyard and those for its entrance and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and those for the surrounding courtyard.
chapters.zh: 并院子四围带卯的座和院门带卯的座，与帐幕一切的橛子和院子四围所有的橛子。

chapters.en: From the blue, purple and scarlet yarn they made woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary. They also made sacred garments for Aaron, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 比撒列用蓝色，紫色，朱红色线作精致的衣服，在圣所用以供职，又为亚伦作圣衣，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: They made the ephod of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
chapters.zh: 他用金线和蓝色，紫色，朱红色线，并捻的细麻作以弗得，

chapters.en: They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut strands to be worked into the blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen—the work of skilled hands.
chapters.zh: 把金子锤成薄片，剪出线来，与蓝色，紫色，朱红色线，用巧匠的手工一同绣上。

chapters.en: They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, which were attached to two of its corners, so it could be fastened.
chapters.zh: 又为以弗得作两条相连的肩带，接连在以弗得的两头。

chapters.en: Its skillfully woven waistband was like it—of one piece with the ephod and made with gold, and with blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and with finely twisted linen, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 其上巧工织的带子和以弗得一样的作法，用以束上，与以弗得接连一块，是用金线和蓝色，紫色，朱红色线，并捻的细麻作的，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: They mounted the onyx stones in gold filigree settings and engraved them like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
chapters.zh: 又琢出两块红玛瑙，镶在金槽上，仿佛刻图书，按着以色列儿子的名字雕刻，

chapters.en: Then they fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 将这两块宝石安在以弗得的两条肩带上，为以色列人作纪念石，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: They fashioned the breastpiece—the work of a skilled craftsman. They made it like the ephod: of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
chapters.zh: 他用巧匠的手工作胸牌，和以弗得一样的作法，用金线与蓝色，紫色，朱红色线，并捻的细麻作的。

chapters.en: It was square—a span long and a span wide—and folded double.
chapters.zh: 胸牌是四方的，叠为两层，这两层长一虎口，宽一虎口，

chapters.en: Then they mounted four rows of precious stones on it. The first row was carnelian, chrysolite and beryl;
chapters.zh: 上面镶着宝石四行，第一行是红宝石，红璧玺，红玉，

chapters.en: the second row was turquoise, lapis lazuli and emerald;
chapters.zh: 第二行是绿宝石，蓝宝石，金钢石，

chapters.en: the third row was jacinth, agate and amethyst;
chapters.zh: 第三行是紫玛瑙，白玛瑙，紫晶，

chapters.en: the fourth row was topaz, onyx and jasper. They were mounted in gold filigree settings.
chapters.zh: 第四行是水苍玉，红玛瑙，碧玉。这都镶在金槽中。

chapters.en: There were twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
chapters.zh: 这些宝石都是按着以色列十二个儿子的名字，仿佛刻图书，刻十二个支派的名字。

chapters.en: For the breastpiece they made braided chains of pure gold, like a rope.
chapters.zh: 在胸牌上，用精金拧成如绳子的链子。

chapters.en: They made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and fastened the rings to two of the corners of the breastpiece.
chapters.zh: 又作两个金槽和两个金环，安在胸牌的两头。

chapters.en: They fastened the two gold chains to the rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
chapters.zh: 把那两条拧成的金链子穿过胸牌两头的环子，

chapters.en: and the other ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
chapters.zh: 又把链子的那两头接在两槽上，安在以弗得前面肩带上。

chapters.en: They made two gold rings and attached them to the other two corners of the breastpiece on the inside edge next to the ephod.
chapters.zh: 作两个金环，安在胸牌的两头，在以弗得里面的边上，

chapters.en: Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above the waistband of the ephod.
chapters.zh: 又作两个金环，安在以弗得前面两条肩带的下边，挨近相接之处，在以弗得巧工织的带子以上。

chapters.en: They tied the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with blue cord, connecting it to the waistband so that the breastpiece would not swing out from the ephod—as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 用一条蓝细带子把胸牌的环子和以弗得的环子系住，使胸牌贴在以弗得巧工织的带子上，不可与以弗得离缝，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth—the work of a weaver—
chapters.zh: 他用织工作以弗得的外袍，颜色全是蓝的。

chapters.en: with an opening in the center of the robe like the opening of a collar, and a band around this opening, so that it would not tear.
chapters.zh: 袍上留一领口，口的周围织出领边来，仿佛铠甲的领口，免得破裂。

chapters.en: They made pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen around the hem of the robe.
chapters.zh: 在袍子底边上，用蓝色，紫色，朱红色线，并捻的细麻作石榴，

chapters.en: And they made bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates.
chapters.zh: 又用精金作铃铛，把铃铛钉在袍子周围底边上的石榴中间，

chapters.en: The bells and pomegranates alternated around the hem of the robe to be worn for ministering, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 一个铃铛，一个石榴，一个铃铛，一个石榴，在袍子周围底边上用以供职，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: For Aaron and his sons, they made tunics of fine linen—the work of a weaver—
chapters.zh: 他用织成的细麻布为亚伦和他的儿子作内袍，

chapters.en: and the turban of fine linen, the linen caps and the undergarments of finely twisted linen.
chapters.zh: 并用细麻布作冠冕和华美的裹头巾，用捻的细麻布作裤子，

chapters.en: The sash was made of finely twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn—the work of an embroiderer—as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 又用蓝色，紫色，朱红色线，并捻的细麻，以绣花的手工作腰带，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: They made the plate, the sacred emblem, out of pure gold and engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
chapters.zh: 他用精金作圣冠上的牌，在上面按刻图书之法，刻着‘归耶和华为圣’。

chapters.en: Then they fastened a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 又用一条蓝细带子将牌系在冠冕上，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: So all the work on the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 帐幕，就是会幕，一切的工就这样作完了。凡耶和华所吩咐摩西的，以色列人都照样作了。

chapters.en: Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, frames, crossbars, posts and bases;
chapters.zh: 他们送到摩西那里，帐幕和帐幕的一切器具，就是钩子，板，闩，柱子，带卯的座，

chapters.en: the covering of ram skins dyed red and the covering of another durable leather and the shielding curtain;
chapters.zh: 染红公羊皮的盖，海狗皮的顶盖，和遮掩柜的幔子，

chapters.en: the ark of the covenant law with its poles and the atonement cover;
chapters.zh: 法柜和柜的杠并施恩座，

chapters.en: the table with all its articles and the bread of the Presence;
chapters.zh: 桌子和桌子的一切器具并陈设饼，

chapters.en: the pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its accessories, and the olive oil for the light;
chapters.zh: 精金的灯台和摆列的灯盏，与灯台的一切器具，并点灯的油，

chapters.en: the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
chapters.zh: 金坛，膏油，馨香的香料，会幕的门帘，

chapters.en: the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
chapters.zh: 铜坛和坛上的铜网，坛的杠并坛的一切器具，洗濯盆和盆座，

chapters.en: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases, and the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard; the ropes and tent pegs for the courtyard; all the furnishings for the tabernacle, the tent of meeting;
chapters.zh: 院子的帷子和柱子，并带卯的座，院子的门帘，绳子，橛子，并帐幕和会幕中一切使用的器具，

chapters.en: and the woven garments worn for ministering in the sanctuary, both the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons when serving as priests.
chapters.zh: 精工作的礼服，和祭司亚伦并他儿子在圣所用以供祭司职分的圣衣。

chapters.en: The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 这一切工作都是以色列人照耶和华所吩咐摩西作的。

chapters.en: Moses inspected the work and saw that they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样吩咐的，他们就怎样作了。摩西看见一切的工都作成了，就给他们祝福。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, on the first day of the first month.
chapters.zh: 正月初一日，你要立起帐幕，

chapters.en: Place the ark of the covenant law in it and shield the ark with the curtain.
chapters.zh: 把法柜安放在里面，用幔子将柜遮掩。

chapters.en: Bring in the table and set out what belongs on it. Then bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
chapters.zh: 把桌子搬进去，摆设上面的物。把灯台搬进去，点其上的灯。

chapters.en: Place the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the covenant law and put the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 把烧香的金坛安在法柜前，挂上帐幕的门帘。

chapters.en: “Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting;
chapters.zh: 把燔祭坛安在帐幕门前。

chapters.en: place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it.
chapters.zh: 把洗濯盆安在会幕和坛的中间，在盆里盛水。

chapters.en: Set up the courtyard around it and put the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard.
chapters.zh: 又在四围立院帷，把院子的门帘挂上。

chapters.en: “Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it will be holy.
chapters.zh: 用膏油把帐幕和其中所有的都抹上，使帐幕和一切器具成圣，就都成圣。

chapters.en: Then anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it will be most holy.
chapters.zh: 又要抹燔祭坛和一切器具，使坛成圣，就都成为至圣。

chapters.en: Anoint the basin and its stand and consecrate them.
chapters.zh: 要抹洗濯盆和盆座，使盆成圣。

chapters.en: “Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
chapters.zh: 要使亚伦和他儿子到会幕门口来，用水洗身。

chapters.en: Then dress Aaron in the sacred garments, anoint him and consecrate him so he may serve me as priest.
chapters.zh: 要给亚伦穿上圣衣，又膏他，使他成圣，可以给我供祭司的职分，

chapters.en: Bring his sons and dress them in tunics.
chapters.zh: 又要使他儿子来，给他们穿上内袍。

chapters.en: Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so they may serve me as priests. Their anointing will be to a priesthood that will continue throughout their generations.”
chapters.zh: 怎样膏他们的父亲，也要照样膏他们，使他们给我供祭司的职分。他们世世代代凡受膏的，就永远当祭司的职任。

chapters.en: Moses did everything just as the LORD commanded him.
chapters.zh: 摩西这样行，都是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month in the second year.
chapters.zh: 第二年正月初一日，帐幕就立起来。

chapters.en: When Moses set up the tabernacle, he put the bases in place, erected the frames, inserted the crossbars and set up the posts.
chapters.zh: 摩西立起帐幕，安上带卯的座，立上板，穿上闩，立起柱子。

chapters.en: Then he spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering over the tent, as the LORD commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在帐幕以上搭罩棚，把罩棚的顶盖盖在其上，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: He took the tablets of the covenant law and placed them in the ark, attached the poles to the ark and put the atonement cover over it.
chapters.zh: 又把法版放在柜里，把杠穿在柜的两旁，把施恩座安在柜上。

chapters.en: Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle and hung the shielding curtain and shielded the ark of the covenant law, as the LORD commanded him.
chapters.zh: 把柜抬进帐幕，挂上遮掩柜的幔子，把法柜遮掩了，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Moses placed the table in the tent of meeting on the north side of the tabernacle outside the curtain
chapters.zh: 又把桌子安在会幕内，在帐幕北边，在幔子外。

chapters.en: and set out the bread on it before the LORD, as the LORD commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在桌子上将饼陈设在耶和华面前，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: He placed the lampstand in the tent of meeting opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle
chapters.zh: 又把灯台安在会幕内，在帐幕南边，与桌子相对，

chapters.en: and set up the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在耶和华面前点灯，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Moses placed the gold altar in the tent of meeting in front of the curtain
chapters.zh: 把金坛安在会幕内的幔子前，

chapters.en: and burned fragrant incense on it, as the LORD commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在坛上烧了馨香料作的香，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Then he put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 又挂上帐幕的门帘。

chapters.en: He set the altar of burnt offering near the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, and offered on it burnt offerings and grain offerings, as the LORD commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在会幕的帐幕门前，安设燔祭坛，把燔祭和素祭献在其上，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: He placed the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing,
chapters.zh: 把洗濯盆安在会幕和坛的中间，盆中盛水，以便洗濯。

chapters.en: and Moses and Aaron and his sons used it to wash their hands and feet.
chapters.zh: 摩西和亚伦并亚伦的儿子在这盆里洗手洗脚。

chapters.en: They washed whenever they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 他们进会幕或就近坛的时候，便都洗濯，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Then Moses set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and altar and put up the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard. And so Moses finished the work.
chapters.zh: 在帐幕和坛的四围立了院帷，把院子的门帘挂上。这样，摩西就完了工。

chapters.en: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 当时，云彩遮盖会幕，耶和华的荣光就充满了帐幕。

chapters.en: Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 摩西不能进会幕，因为云彩停在其上，并且耶和华的荣光充满了帐幕。

chapters.en: In all the travels of the Israelites, whenever the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle, they would set out;
chapters.zh: 每逢云彩从帐幕收上去，以色列人就起程前往。

chapters.en: but if the cloud did not lift, they did not set out—until the day it lifted.
chapters.zh: 云彩若不收上去，他们就不起程，直等到云彩收上去。

chapters.en: So the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the Israelites during all their travels.
chapters.zh: 日间，耶和华的云彩是在帐幕以上。夜间，云中有火，在以色列全家的眼前，在他们所行的路上，都是这样。

chapters.en: The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting. He said,
chapters.zh: 耶和华从会幕中呼叫摩西，对他说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘When anyone among you brings an offering to the LORD, bring as your offering an animal from either the herd or the flock.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，你们中间若有人献供物给耶和华，要从牛群羊群中献牲畜为供物。

chapters.en: “ ‘If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, you are to offer a male without defect. You must present it at the entrance to the tent of meeting so that it will be acceptable to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 他的供物若以牛为燔祭，就要在会幕门口献一只没有残疾的公牛，可以在耶和华面前蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: You are to lay your hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on your behalf to make atonement for you.
chapters.zh: 他要按手在燔祭牲的头上，燔祭便蒙悦纳，为他赎罪。

chapters.en: You are to slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and then Aaron’s sons the priests shall bring the blood and splash it against the sides of the altar at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 他要在耶和华面前宰公牛，亚伦子孙作祭司的，要奉上血，把血洒在会幕门口，坛的周围。

chapters.en: You are to skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
chapters.zh: 那人要剥去燔祭牲的皮，把燔祭牲切成块子。

chapters.en: The sons of Aaron the priest are to put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
chapters.zh: 祭司亚伦的子孙要把火放在坛上，把柴摆在火上。

chapters.en: Then Aaron’s sons the priests shall arrange the pieces, including the head and the fat, on the wood that is burning on the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦子孙作祭司的，要把肉块和头并脂油摆在坛上火的柴上。

chapters.en: You are to wash the internal organs and the legs with water, and the priest is to burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 但燔祭的脏腑与腿要用水洗。祭司就要把一切全烧在坛上，当作燔祭，献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘If the offering is a burnt offering from the flock, from either the sheep or the goats, you are to offer a male without defect.
chapters.zh: 人的供物若以绵羊或山羊为燔祭，就要献上没有残疾的公羊。

chapters.en: You are to slaughter it at the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests shall splash its blood against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 要把羊宰于坛的北边，在耶和华面前，亚伦子孙作祭司的，要把羊血洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: You are to cut it into pieces, and the priest shall arrange them, including the head and the fat, on the wood that is burning on the altar.
chapters.zh: 要把燔祭牲切成块子，连头和脂油，祭司就要摆在坛上火的柴上。

chapters.en: You are to wash the internal organs and the legs with water, and the priest is to bring all of them and burn them on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 但脏腑与腿要用水洗，祭司就要全然奉献，烧在坛上。这是燔祭，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘If the offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, you are to offer a dove or a young pigeon.
chapters.zh: 人奉给耶和华的供物，若以鸟为燔祭，就要献斑鸠或是雏鸽为供物。

chapters.en: The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off the head and burn it on the altar; its blood shall be drained out on the side of the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把鸟拿到坛前，揪下头来，把鸟烧在坛上，鸟的血要流在坛的旁边。

chapters.en: He is to remove the crop and the feathers and throw them down east of the altar where the ashes are.
chapters.zh: 又要把鸟的嗉子和脏物除掉（脏物或作翎毛），丢在坛的东边倒灰的地方。

chapters.en: He shall tear it open by the wings, not dividing it completely, and then the priest shall burn it on the wood that is burning on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要拿着鸟的两个翅膀，把鸟撕开，只是不可撕断，祭司要在坛上，在火的柴上焚烧。这是燔祭，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, their offering is to be of the finest flour. They are to pour olive oil on it, put incense on it
chapters.zh: 若有人献素祭为供物给耶和华，要用细面浇上油，加上乳香，

chapters.en: and take it to Aaron’s sons the priests. The priest shall take a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense, and burn this as a memorial portion on the altar, a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 带到亚伦子孙作祭司的那里，祭司就要从细面中取出一把来，并取些油和所有的乳香，然后要把所取的这些作为纪念，烧在坛上，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 素祭所剩的要归给亚伦和他的子孙，这是献与耶和华的火祭中为至圣的。

chapters.en: “ ‘If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it is to consist of the finest flour: either thick loaves made without yeast and with olive oil mixed in or thin loaves made without yeast and brushed with olive oil.
chapters.zh: 若用炉中烤的物为素祭，就要用调油的无酵细面饼，或是抹油的无酵薄饼。

chapters.en: If your grain offering is prepared on a griddle, it is to be made of the finest flour mixed with oil, and without yeast.
chapters.zh: 若用铁鏊上作的物为素祭，就要用调油的无酵细面，

chapters.en: Crumble it and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
chapters.zh: 分成块子，浇上油，这是素祭。

chapters.en: If your grain offering is cooked in a pan, it is to be made of the finest flour and some olive oil.
chapters.zh: 若用煎盘作的物为素祭，就要用油与细面作成。

chapters.en: Bring the grain offering made of these things to the LORD; present it to the priest, who shall take it to the altar.
chapters.zh: 要把这些东西作的素祭带到耶和华面前，并奉给祭司，带到坛前。

chapters.en: He shall take out the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要从素祭中取出作为纪念的，烧在坛上，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 素祭所剩的要归给亚伦和他的子孙。这是献与耶和华的火祭中为至圣的。

chapters.en: “ ‘Every grain offering you bring to the LORD must be made without yeast, for you are not to burn any yeast or honey in a food offering presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 凡献给耶和华的素祭都不可有酵，因为你们不可烧一点酵，一点蜜当作火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of the firstfruits, but they are not to be offered on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
chapters.zh: 这些物要献给耶和华作为初熟的供物，只是不可在坛上献为馨香的祭。

chapters.en: Season all your grain offerings with salt. Do not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offerings; add salt to all your offerings.
chapters.zh: 凡献为素祭的供物都要用盐调和，在素祭上不可缺了你神立约的盐。一切的供物都要配盐而献。

chapters.en: “ ‘If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, offer crushed heads of new grain roasted in the fire.
chapters.zh: 若向耶和华献初熟之物为素祭，要献上烘了的禾穗子，就是轧了的新穗子，当作初熟之物的素祭。

chapters.en: Put oil and incense on it; it is a grain offering.
chapters.zh: 并要抹上油，加上乳香，这是素祭。

chapters.en: The priest shall burn the memorial portion of the crushed grain and the oil, together with all the incense, as a food offering presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把其中作为纪念的，就是一些轧了的禾穗子和一些油，并所有的乳香，都焚烧，是向耶和华献的火祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘If your offering is a fellowship offering, and you offer an animal from the herd, whether male or female, you are to present before the LORD an animal without defect.
chapters.zh: 人献供物为平安祭（平安或作酬恩下同），若是从牛群中献，无论是公的是母的，必用没有残疾的献在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: You are to lay your hand on the head of your offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the tent of meeting. Then Aaron’s sons the priests shall splash the blood against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 他要按手在供物的头上，宰于会幕门口。亚伦子孙作祭司的，要把血洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: From the fellowship offering you are to bring a food offering to the LORD: the internal organs and all the fat that is connected to them,
chapters.zh: 从平安祭中，将火祭献给耶和华，也要把盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which you will remove with the kidneys.
chapters.zh: 并两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，与肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下。

chapters.en: Then Aaron’s sons are to burn it on the altar on top of the burnt offering that is lying on the burning wood; it is a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的子孙要把这些烧在坛的燔祭上，就是在火的柴上，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘If you offer an animal from the flock as a fellowship offering to the LORD, you are to offer a male or female without defect.
chapters.zh: 人向耶和华献供物为平安祭，若是从羊群中献，无论是公的是母的，必用没有残疾的。

chapters.en: If you offer a lamb, you are to present it before the LORD,
chapters.zh: 若献一只羊羔为供物，必在耶和华面前献上，

chapters.en: lay your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting. Then Aaron’s sons shall splash its blood against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 并要按手在供物的头上，宰于会幕前。亚伦的子孙要把血洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: From the fellowship offering you are to bring a food offering to the LORD: its fat, the entire fat tail cut off close to the backbone, the internal organs and all the fat that is connected to them,
chapters.zh: 从平安祭中，将火祭献给耶和华，其中的脂油和整肥尾巴都要在靠近脊骨处取下，并要把盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which you will remove with the kidneys.
chapters.zh: 两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，并肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下。

chapters.en: The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要在坛上焚烧，是献给耶和华为食物的火祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘If your offering is a goat, you are to present it before the LORD,
chapters.zh: 人的供物若是山羊，必在耶和华面前献上。

chapters.en: lay your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting. Then Aaron’s sons shall splash its blood against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 要按手在山羊头上，宰于会幕前。亚伦的子孙要把血洒在坛的周围，

chapters.en: From what you offer you are to present this food offering to the LORD: the internal organs and all the fat that is connected to them,
chapters.zh: 又把盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，并肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下，献给耶和华为火祭。

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which you will remove with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering, a pleasing aroma. All the fat is the LORD’s.
chapters.zh: 祭司要在坛上焚烧，作为馨香火祭的食物。脂油都是耶和华的。

chapters.en: “ ‘This is a lasting ordinance for the generations to come, wherever you live: You must not eat any fat or any blood.’ ”
chapters.zh: 在你们一切的住处，脂油和血都不可吃，这要成为你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘When anyone sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the LORD’s commands—
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，若有人在耶和华所吩咐不可行的什么事上误犯了一件，

chapters.en: “ ‘If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, he must bring to the LORD a young bull without defect as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
chapters.zh: 或是受膏的祭司犯罪，使百姓陷在罪里，就当为他所犯的罪把没有残疾的公牛犊献给耶和华为赎罪祭。

chapters.en: He is to present the bull at the entrance to the tent of meeting before the LORD. He is to lay his hand on its head and slaughter it there before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 他要牵公牛到会幕门口，在耶和华面前按手在牛的头上，把牛宰于耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Then the anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and carry it into the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 受膏的祭司要取些公牛的血带到会幕，

chapters.en: He is to dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain of the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 把指头蘸于血中，在耶和华面前对着圣所的幔子弹血七次，

chapters.en: The priest shall then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the LORD in the tent of meeting. The rest of the bull’s blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 又要把些血抹在会幕内，耶和华面前香坛的四角上，再把公牛所有的血倒在会幕门口，燔祭坛的脚那里。

chapters.en: He shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering—all the fat that is connected to the internal organs,
chapters.zh: 要把赎罪祭公牛所有的脂油，乃是盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he will remove with the kidneys—
chapters.zh: 并两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，与肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下，

chapters.en: just as the fat is removed from the ox sacrificed as a fellowship offering. Then the priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 与平安祭公牛上所取的一样，祭司要把这些烧在燔祭的坛上。

chapters.en: But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, as well as the head and legs, the internal organs and the intestines—
chapters.zh: 公牛的皮和所有的肉，并头，腿，脏，腑，粪，

chapters.en: that is, all the rest of the bull—he must take outside the camp to a place ceremonially clean, where the ashes are thrown, and burn it there in a wood fire on the ash heap.
chapters.zh: 就是全公牛，要搬到营外洁净之地，倒灰之所，用火烧在柴上。

chapters.en: “ ‘If the whole Israelite community sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the LORD’s commands, even though the community is unaware of the matter, when they realize their guilt
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众若行了耶和华所吩咐不可行的什么事，误犯了罪，是隐而未现，会众看不出来的，

chapters.en: and the sin they committed becomes known, the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it before the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 会众一知道所犯的罪就要献一只公牛犊为赎罪祭，牵到会幕前。

chapters.en: The elders of the community are to lay their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD, and the bull shall be slaughtered before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 会中的长老就要在耶和华面前按手在牛的头上，将牛在耶和华面前宰了。

chapters.en: Then the anointed priest is to take some of the bull’s blood into the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 受膏的祭司要取些公牛的血带到会幕，

chapters.en: He shall dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle it before the LORD seven times in front of the curtain.
chapters.zh: 把指头蘸于血中，在耶和华面前对着幔子弹血七次，

chapters.en: He is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the tent of meeting. The rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 又要把些血抹在会幕内，耶和华面前坛的四角上，再把所有的血倒在会幕门口，燔祭坛的脚那里。

chapters.en: He shall remove all the fat from it and burn it on the altar,
chapters.zh: 把牛所有的脂油都取下，烧在坛上。

chapters.en: and do with this bull just as he did with the bull for the sin offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the community, and they will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 收拾这牛，与那赎罪祭的牛一样。祭司要为他们赎罪，他们必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: Then he shall take the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. This is the sin offering for the community.
chapters.zh: 他要把牛搬到营外烧了，像烧头一个牛一样，这是会众的赎罪祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘When a leader sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the commands of the LORD his God, when he realizes his guilt
chapters.zh: 官长若行了耶和华他神所吩咐不可行的什么事，误犯了罪，

chapters.en: and the sin he has committed becomes known, he must bring as his offering a male goat without defect.
chapters.zh: 所犯的罪自己知道了，就要牵一只没有残疾的公山羊为供物，

chapters.en: He is to lay his hand on the goat’s head and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 按手在羊的头上，宰于耶和华面前，宰燔祭牲的地方，这是赎罪祭。

chapters.en: Then the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要用指头蘸些赎罪祭牲的血，抹在燔祭坛的四角上，把血倒在燔祭坛的脚那里。

chapters.en: He shall burn all the fat on the altar as he burned the fat of the fellowship offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the leader’s sin, and he will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 所有的脂油，祭司都要烧在坛上，正如平安祭的脂油一样。至于他的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: “ ‘If any member of the community sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the LORD’s commands, when they realize their guilt
chapters.zh: 民中若有人行了耶和华所吩咐不可行的什么事，误犯了罪，

chapters.en: and the sin they have committed becomes known, they must bring as their offering for the sin they committed a female goat without defect.
chapters.zh: 所犯的罪自己知道了，就要为所犯的罪牵一只没有残疾的母山羊为供物，

chapters.en: They are to lay their hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 按手在赎罪祭牲的头上，在那宰燔祭牲的地方宰了。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to take some of the blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要用指头蘸些羊的血，抹在燔祭坛的四角上，所有的血都要倒在坛的脚那里。

chapters.en: They shall remove all the fat, just as the fat is removed from the fellowship offering, and the priest shall burn it on the altar as an aroma pleasing to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 又要把羊所有的脂油都取下，正如取平安祭牲的脂油一样。祭司要在坛上焚烧，在耶和华面前作为馨香的祭，为他赎罪，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: “ ‘If someone brings a lamb as their sin offering, they are to bring a female without defect.
chapters.zh: 人若牵一只绵羊羔为赎罪祭的供物，必要牵一只没有残疾的母羊，

chapters.en: They are to lay their hand on its head and slaughter it for a sin offering at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
chapters.zh: 按手在赎罪祭牲的头上，在那宰燔祭牲的地方宰了作赎罪祭。

chapters.en: Then the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要用指头蘸些赎罪祭牲的血，抹在燔祭坛的四角上，所有的血都要倒在坛的脚那里，

chapters.en: They shall remove all the fat, just as the fat is removed from the lamb of the fellowship offering, and the priest shall burn it on the altar on top of the food offerings presented to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for them for the sin they have committed, and they will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 又要把所有的脂油都取下，正如取平安祭羊羔的脂油一样。祭司要按献给耶和华火祭的条例，烧在坛上。至于所犯的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: “ ‘If anyone sins because they do not speak up when they hear a public charge to testify regarding something they have seen or learned about, they will be held responsible.
chapters.zh: 若有人听见发誓的声音（或作若有人听见叫人发誓的声音），他本是见证，却不把所看见的，所知道的说出来，这就是罪，他要担当他的罪孽。

chapters.en: “ ‘If anyone becomes aware that they are guilty—if they unwittingly touch anything ceremonially unclean (whether the carcass of an unclean animal, wild or domestic, or of any unclean creature that moves along the ground) and they are unaware that they have become unclean, but then they come to realize their guilt;
chapters.zh: 或是有人摸了不洁的物，无论是不洁的死兽，是不洁的死畜，是不洁的死虫，他却不知道，因此成了不洁，就有了罪。

chapters.en: or if they touch human uncleanness (anything that would make them unclean) even though they are unaware of it, but then they learn of it and realize their guilt;
chapters.zh: 或是他摸了别人的污秽，无论是染了什么污秽，他却不知道，一知道了就有了罪。

chapters.en: or if anyone thoughtlessly takes an oath to do anything, whether good or evil (in any matter one might carelessly swear about) even though they are unaware of it, but then they learn of it and realize their guilt—
chapters.zh: 或是有人嘴里冒失发誓，要行恶，要行善，无论人在什么事上冒失发誓，他却不知道，一知道了就要在这其中的一件上有了罪。

chapters.en: when anyone becomes aware that they are guilty in any of these matters, they must confess in what way they have sinned.
chapters.zh: 他有了罪的时候，就要承认所犯的罪，

chapters.en: As a penalty for the sin they have committed, they must bring to the LORD a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering ; and the priest shall make atonement for them for their sin.
chapters.zh: 并要因所犯的罪，把他的赎愆祭牲就是羊群中的母羊，或是一只羊羔，或是一只山羊牵到耶和华面前为赎罪祭。至于他的罪，祭司要为他赎了。

chapters.en: “ ‘Anyone who cannot afford a lamb is to bring two doves or two young pigeons to the LORD as a penalty for their sin—one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 他的力量若不够献一只羊羔，就要因所犯的罪，把两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽带到耶和华面前为赎愆祭，一只作赎罪祭，一只作燔祭。

chapters.en: They are to bring them to the priest, who shall first offer the one for the sin offering. He is to wring its head from its neck, not dividing it completely,
chapters.zh: 把这些带到祭司那里，祭司就要先把那赎罪祭献上，从鸟的颈项上揪下头来，只是不可把鸟撕断，

chapters.en: and is to splash some of the blood of the sin offering against the side of the altar; the rest of the blood must be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 也把些赎罪祭牲的血弹在坛的旁边，剩下的血要流在坛的脚那里，这是赎罪祭。

chapters.en: The priest shall then offer the other as a burnt offering in the prescribed way and make atonement for them for the sin they have committed, and they will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 他要照例献第二只为燔祭。至于他所犯的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: “ ‘If, however, they cannot afford two doves or two young pigeons, they are to bring as an offering for their sin a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour for a sin offering. They must not put olive oil or incense on it, because it is a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 他的力量若不够献两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，就要因所犯的罪带供物来，就是细面伊法十分之一为赎罪祭，不可加上油，也不可加上乳香，因为是赎罪祭。

chapters.en: They are to bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful of it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar on top of the food offerings presented to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 他要把供物带到祭司那里，祭司要取出自己的一把来作为纪念，按献给耶和华火祭的条例烧在坛上，这是赎罪祭。

chapters.en: In this way the priest will make atonement for them for any of these sins they have committed, and they will be forgiven. The rest of the offering will belong to the priest, as in the case of the grain offering.’ ”
chapters.zh: 至于他在这几件事中所犯的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。剩下的面都归与祭司，和素祭一样。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “When anyone is unfaithful to the LORD by sinning unintentionally in regard to any of the LORD’s holy things, they are to bring to the LORD as a penalty a ram from the flock, one without defect and of the proper value in silver, according to the sanctuary shekel. It is a guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 人若在耶和华的圣物上误犯了罪，有了过犯，就要照你所估的，按圣所的舍客勒拿银子，将赎愆祭牲就是羊群中一只没有残疾的公绵羊牵到耶和华面前为赎愆祭。

chapters.en: They must make restitution for what they have failed to do in regard to the holy things, pay an additional penalty of a fifth of its value and give it all to the priest. The priest will make atonement for them with the ram as a guilt offering, and they will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 并且他因在圣物上的差错要偿还，另外加五分之一，都给祭司。祭司要用赎愆祭的公绵羊为他赎罪，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: “If anyone sins and does what is forbidden in any of the LORD’s commands, even though they do not know it, they are guilty and will be held responsible.
chapters.zh: 若有人犯罪，行了耶和华所吩咐不可行的什么事，他虽然不知道，还是有了罪，就要担当他的罪孽。

chapters.en: They are to bring to the priest as a guilt offering a ram from the flock, one without defect and of the proper value. In this way the priest will make atonement for them for the wrong they have committed unintentionally, and they will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 也要照你所估定的价，从羊群中牵一只没有残疾的公绵羊来，给祭司作赎愆祭。至于他误行的那错事，祭司要为他赎罪，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: It is a guilt offering; they have been guilty of wrongdoing against the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 这是赎愆祭，因他在耶和华面前实在有了罪。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “If anyone sins and is unfaithful to the LORD by deceiving a neighbor about something entrusted to them or left in their care or about something stolen, or if they cheat their neighbor,
chapters.zh: 若有人犯罪，干犯耶和华，在邻舍交付他的物上，或是在交易上行了诡诈，或是抢夺人的财物，或是欺压邻舍，

chapters.en: or if they find lost property and lie about it, or if they swear falsely about any such sin that people may commit—
chapters.zh: 或是在捡了遗失的物上行了诡诈，说谎起誓，在这一切的事上犯了什么罪。

chapters.en: when they sin in any of these ways and realize their guilt, they must return what they have stolen or taken by extortion, or what was entrusted to them, or the lost property they found,
chapters.zh: 他既犯了罪，有了过犯，就要归还他所抢夺的，或是因欺压所得的，或是人交付他的，或是人遗失他所捡的物，

chapters.en: or whatever it was they swore falsely about. They must make restitution in full, add a fifth of the value to it and give it all to the owner on the day they present their guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 或是他因什么物起了假誓，就要如数归还，另外加上五分之一，在查出他有罪的日子要交还本主。

chapters.en: And as a penalty they must bring to the priest, that is, to the LORD, their guilt offering, a ram from the flock, one without defect and of the proper value.
chapters.zh: 也要照你所估定的价，把赎愆祭牲就是羊群中一只没有残疾的公绵羊牵到耶和华面前，给祭司为赎愆祭。

chapters.en: In this way the priest will make atonement for them before the LORD, and they will be forgiven for any of the things they did that made them guilty.”
chapters.zh: 祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪，他无论行了什么事，使他有了罪，都必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Give Aaron and his sons this command: ‘These are the regulations for the burnt offering: The burnt offering is to remain on the altar hearth throughout the night, till morning, and the fire must be kept burning on the altar.
chapters.zh: 你要吩咐亚伦和他的子孙说，燔祭的条例乃是这样，燔祭要放在坛的柴上，从晚上到天亮，坛上的火要常常烧着。

chapters.en: The priest shall then put on his linen clothes, with linen undergarments next to his body, and shall remove the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed on the altar and place them beside the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要穿上细麻布衣服，又要把细麻布裤子穿在身上，把坛上所烧的燔祭灰收起来，倒在坛的旁边。

chapters.en: Then he is to take off these clothes and put on others, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a place that is ceremonially clean.
chapters.zh: 随后要脱去这衣服，穿上别的衣服，把灰拿到营外洁净之处。

chapters.en: The fire on the altar must be kept burning; it must not go out. Every morning the priest is to add firewood and arrange the burnt offering on the fire and burn the fat of the fellowship offerings on it.
chapters.zh: 坛上的火要在其上常常烧着，不可熄灭。祭司要每日早晨在上面烧柴，并要把燔祭摆在坛上，在其上烧平安祭牲的脂油。

chapters.en: The fire must be kept burning on the altar continuously; it must not go out.
chapters.zh: 在坛上必有常常烧着的火，不可熄灭。

chapters.en: “ ‘These are the regulations for the grain offering: Aaron’s sons are to bring it before the LORD, in front of the altar.
chapters.zh: 素祭的条例乃是这样，亚伦的子孙要在坛前把这祭献在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: The priest is to take a handful of the finest flour and some olive oil, together with all the incense on the grain offering, and burn the memorial portion on the altar as an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要从其中就是从素祭的细面中取出自己的一把，又要取些油和素祭上所有的乳香，烧在坛上，奉给耶和华为馨香素祭的纪念。

chapters.en: Aaron and his sons shall eat the rest of it, but it is to be eaten without yeast in the sanctuary area; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 所剩下的，亚伦和他子孙要吃，必在圣处不带酵而吃，要在会幕的院子里吃。

chapters.en: It must not be baked with yeast; I have given it as their share of the food offerings presented to me. Like the sin offering and the guilt offering, it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 烤的时候不可搀酵。这是从所献给我的火祭中赐给他们的分，是至圣的，和赎罪祭并赎愆祭一样。

chapters.en: Any male descendant of Aaron may eat it. For all generations to come it is his perpetual share of the food offerings presented to the LORD. Whatever touches them will become holy. ’ ”
chapters.zh: 凡献给耶和华的火祭，亚伦子孙中的男丁都要吃这一分，直到万代，作他们永得的分。摸这些祭物的，都要成为圣。

chapters.en: The LORD also said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “This is the offering Aaron and his sons are to bring to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
chapters.zh: 当亚伦受膏的日子，他和他子孙所要献给耶和华的供物，就是细面伊法十分之一，为常献的素祭，早晨一半，晚上一半。

chapters.en: It must be prepared with oil on a griddle; bring it well-mixed and present the grain offering broken in pieces as an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要在铁鏊上用油调和作成，调匀了，你就拿进来，烤好了分成块子，献给耶和华为馨香的素祭。

chapters.en: The son who is to succeed him as anointed priest shall prepare it. It is the LORD’s perpetual share and is to be burned completely.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的子孙中，接续他为受膏的祭司，要把这素祭献上，要全烧给耶和华。这是永远的定例。

chapters.en: Every grain offering of a priest shall be burned completely; it must not be eaten.”
chapters.zh: 祭司的素祭都要烧了，却不可吃。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to Aaron and his sons: ‘These are the regulations for the sin offering: The sin offering is to be slaughtered before the LORD in the place the burnt offering is slaughtered; it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 你对亚伦和他的子孙说，赎罪祭的条例乃是这样，要在耶和华面前，宰燔祭牲的地方宰赎罪祭牲，这是至圣的。

chapters.en: The priest who offers it shall eat it; it is to be eaten in the sanctuary area, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 为赎罪献这祭的祭司要吃，要在圣处，就是在会幕的院子里吃。

chapters.en: Whatever touches any of the flesh will become holy, and if any of the blood is spattered on a garment, you must wash it in the sanctuary area.
chapters.zh: 凡摸这祭肉的要成为圣，这祭牲的血若弹在什么衣服上，所弹的那一件要在圣处洗净。

chapters.en: The clay pot the meat is cooked in must be broken; but if it is cooked in a bronze pot, the pot is to be scoured and rinsed with water.
chapters.zh: 惟有煮祭物的瓦器要打碎，若是煮在铜器里，这铜器要擦磨，在水中涮净。

chapters.en: Any male in a priest’s family may eat it; it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 凡祭司中的男丁都可以吃，这是至圣的。

chapters.en: But any sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place must not be eaten; it must be burned up.
chapters.zh: 凡赎罪祭，若将血带进会幕在圣所赎罪，那肉都不可吃，必用火焚烧。

chapters.en: “ ‘These are the regulations for the guilt offering, which is most holy:
chapters.zh: 赎愆祭的条例乃是如此，这祭是至圣的。

chapters.en: The guilt offering is to be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood is to be splashed against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 人在哪里宰燔祭牲，也要在哪里宰赎愆祭牲，其血，祭司要洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: All its fat shall be offered: the fat tail and the fat that covers the internal organs,
chapters.zh: 又要将肥尾巴和盖脏的脂油，

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
chapters.zh: 两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，并肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下。

chapters.en: The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering presented to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 祭司要在坛上焚烧，为献给耶和华的火祭，是赎愆祭。

chapters.en: Any male in a priest’s family may eat it, but it must be eaten in the sanctuary area; it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 祭司中的男丁都可以吃这祭物，要在圣处吃，是至圣的。

chapters.en: “ ‘The same law applies to both the sin offering and the guilt offering: They belong to the priest who makes atonement with them.
chapters.zh: 赎罪祭怎样，赎愆祭也是怎样，两个祭是一个条例。献赎愆祭赎罪的祭司要得这祭物。

chapters.en: The priest who offers a burnt offering for anyone may keep its hide for himself.
chapters.zh: 献燔祭的祭司，无论为谁奉献，要亲自得他所献那燔祭牲的皮。

chapters.en: Every grain offering baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest who offers it,
chapters.zh: 凡在炉中烤的素祭和煎盘中作的，并铁鏊上作的，都要归那献祭的祭司。

chapters.en: and every grain offering, whether mixed with olive oil or dry, belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron.
chapters.zh: 凡素祭，无论是油调和的，是干的，都要归亚伦的子孙，大家均分。

chapters.en: “ ‘These are the regulations for the fellowship offering anyone may present to the LORD:
chapters.zh: 人献与耶和华平安祭的条例乃是这样，

chapters.en: “ ‘If they offer it as an expression of thankfulness, then along with this thank offering they are to offer thick loaves made without yeast and with olive oil mixed in, thin loaves made without yeast and brushed with oil, and thick loaves of the finest flour well-kneaded and with oil mixed in.
chapters.zh: 他若为感谢献上，就要用调油的无酵饼和抹油的无酵薄饼，并用油调匀细面作的饼，与感谢祭一同献上。

chapters.en: Along with their fellowship offering of thanksgiving they are to present an offering with thick loaves of bread made with yeast.
chapters.zh: 要用有酵的饼和为感谢献的平安祭，与供物一同献上。

chapters.en: They are to bring one of each kind as an offering, a contribution to the LORD; it belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the fellowship offering against the altar.
chapters.zh: 从各样的供物中，他要把一个饼献给耶和华为举祭，是要归给洒平安祭牲血的祭司。

chapters.en: The meat of their fellowship offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day it is offered; they must leave none of it till morning.
chapters.zh: 为感谢献平安祭牲的肉，要在献的日子吃，一点不可留到早晨。

chapters.en: “ ‘If, however, their offering is the result of a vow or is a freewill offering, the sacrifice shall be eaten on the day they offer it, but anything left over may be eaten on the next day.
chapters.zh: 若所献的是为还愿，或是甘心献的，必在献祭的日子吃，所剩下的第二天也可以吃。

chapters.en: Any meat of the sacrifice left over till the third day must be burned up.
chapters.zh: 但所剩下的祭肉，到第三天要用火焚烧。

chapters.en: If any meat of the fellowship offering is eaten on the third day, the one who offered it will not be accepted. It will not be reckoned to their credit, for it has become impure; the person who eats any of it will be held responsible.
chapters.zh: 第三天若吃了平安祭的肉，这祭必不蒙悦纳，人所献的也不算为祭，反为可憎嫌的，吃这祭肉的，就必担当他的罪孽。

chapters.en: “ ‘Meat that touches anything ceremonially unclean must not be eaten; it must be burned up. As for other meat, anyone ceremonially clean may eat it.
chapters.zh: 挨了污秽物的肉就不可吃，要用火焚烧。至于平安祭的肉，凡洁净的人都要吃。

chapters.en: But if anyone who is unclean eats any meat of the fellowship offering belonging to the LORD, they must be cut off from their people.
chapters.zh: 只是献与耶和华平安祭的肉，人若不洁净而吃了，这人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: Anyone who touches something unclean—whether human uncleanness or an unclean animal or any unclean creature that moves along the ground —and then eats any of the meat of the fellowship offering belonging to the LORD must be cut off from their people.’ ”
chapters.zh: 有人摸了什么不洁净的物，或是人的不洁净，或是不洁净的牲畜，或是不洁可憎之物，吃了献与耶和华平安祭的肉，这人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘Do not eat any of the fat of cattle, sheep or goats.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，牛的脂油，绵羊的脂油，山羊的脂油，你们都不可吃。

chapters.en: The fat of an animal found dead or torn by wild animals may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
chapters.zh: 自死的和被野兽撕裂的，那脂油可以作别的使用，只是你们万不可吃。

chapters.en: Anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering may be presented to the LORD must be cut off from their people.
chapters.zh: 无论何人吃了献给耶和华当火祭牲畜的脂油，那人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: And wherever you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal.
chapters.zh: 在你们一切的住处，无论是雀鸟的血是野兽的血，你们都不可吃。

chapters.en: Anyone who eats blood must be cut off from their people.’ ”
chapters.zh: 无论是谁吃血，那人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘Anyone who brings a fellowship offering to the LORD is to bring part of it as their sacrifice to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，献平安祭给耶和华的，要从平安祭中取些来奉给耶和华。

chapters.en: With their own hands they are to present the food offering to the LORD; they are to bring the fat, together with the breast, and wave the breast before the LORD as a wave offering.
chapters.zh: 他亲手献给耶和华的火祭，就是脂油和胸，要带来，好把胸在耶和华面前作摇祭，摇一摇。

chapters.en: The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把脂油在坛上焚烧，但胸要归亚伦和他的子孙。

chapters.en: You are to give the right thigh of your fellowship offerings to the priest as a contribution.
chapters.zh: 你们要从平安祭中把右腿作举祭，奉给祭司。

chapters.en: The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the fellowship offering shall have the right thigh as his share.
chapters.zh: 亚伦子孙中，献平安祭牲血和脂油的，要得这右腿为分。

chapters.en: From the fellowship offerings of the Israelites, I have taken the breast that is waved and the thigh that is presented and have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as their perpetual share from the Israelites.’ ”
chapters.zh: 因为我从以色列人的平安祭中，取了这摇的胸和举的腿给祭司亚伦和他子孙，作他们从以色列人中所永得的分。

chapters.en: This is the portion of the food offerings presented to the LORD that were allotted to Aaron and his sons on the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.
chapters.zh: 这是从耶和华火祭中，作亚伦受膏的分和他子孙受膏的分，正在摩西（原文作他）叫他们前来给耶和华供祭司职分的日子，

chapters.en: On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded that the Israelites give this to them as their perpetual share for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 就是在摩西（原文作他）膏他们的日子，耶和华吩咐以色列人给他们的。这是他们世世代代永得的分。

chapters.en: These, then, are the regulations for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering and the fellowship offering,
chapters.zh: 这就是燔祭，素祭，赎罪祭，赎愆祭，和平安祭的条例，并承接圣职的礼，

chapters.en: which the LORD gave Moses at Mount Sinai in the Desert of Sinai on the day he commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 都是耶和华在西乃山所吩咐摩西的，就是他在西乃旷野吩咐以色列人献供物给耶和华之日所说的。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Bring Aaron and his sons, their garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams and the basket containing bread made without yeast,
chapters.zh: 你将亚伦和他儿子一同带来，并将圣衣，膏油，与赎罪祭的一只公牛，两只公绵羊，一筐无酵饼都带来，

chapters.en: and gather the entire assembly at the entrance to the tent of meeting.”
chapters.zh: 又招聚会众到会幕门口。

chapters.en: Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 摩西就照耶和华所吩咐的行了，于是会众聚集在会幕门口。

chapters.en: Moses said to the assembly, “This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.”
chapters.zh: 摩西告诉会众说，这就是耶和华所吩咐当行的事。

chapters.en: Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
chapters.zh: 摩西带了亚伦和他儿子来，用水洗了他们。

chapters.en: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe and put the ephod on him. He also fastened the ephod with a decorative waistband, which he tied around him.
chapters.zh: 给亚伦穿上内袍，束上腰带，穿上外袍，又加上以弗得，用其上巧工织的带子把以弗得系在他身上，

chapters.en: He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece.
chapters.zh: 又给他戴上胸牌，把乌陵和土明放在胸牌内，

chapters.en: Then he placed the turban on Aaron’s head and set the gold plate, the sacred emblem, on the front of it, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 把冠冕戴在他头上，在冠冕的前面钉上金牌，就是圣冠，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and so consecrated them.
chapters.zh: 摩西用膏油抹帐幕和其中所有的，使它成圣。

chapters.en: He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, anointing the altar and all its utensils and the basin with its stand, to consecrate them.
chapters.zh: 又用膏油在坛上弹了七次，又抹了坛和坛的一切器皿，并洗濯盆和盆座，使它成圣。

chapters.en: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.
chapters.zh: 又把膏油倒在亚伦的头上膏他，使他成圣。

chapters.en: Then he brought Aaron’s sons forward, put tunics on them, tied sashes around them and fastened caps on them, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 摩西带了亚伦的儿子来，给他们穿上内袍，束上腰带，包上裹头巾，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: He then presented the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
chapters.zh: 他牵了赎罪祭的公牛来，亚伦和他儿子按手在赎罪祭公牛的头上，

chapters.en: Moses slaughtered the bull and took some of the blood, and with his finger he put it on all the horns of the altar to purify the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. So he consecrated it to make atonement for it.
chapters.zh: 就宰了公牛。摩西用指头蘸血，抹在坛上四角的周围，使坛洁净，把血倒在坛的脚那里，使坛成圣，坛就洁净了。

chapters.en: Moses also took all the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and both kidneys and their fat, and burned it on the altar.
chapters.zh: 又取脏上所有的脂油和肝上的网子，并两个腰子与腰子上的脂油，都烧在坛上。

chapters.en: But the bull with its hide and its flesh and its intestines he burned up outside the camp, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 惟有公牛，连皮带肉并粪，用火烧在营外，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: He then presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
chapters.zh: 他奉上燔祭的公绵羊，亚伦和他儿子按手在羊的头上，

chapters.en: Then Moses slaughtered the ram and splashed the blood against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 就宰了公羊。摩西把血洒在坛的周围，

chapters.en: He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces and the fat.
chapters.zh: 把羊切成块子，把头和肉块并脂油都烧了。

chapters.en: He washed the internal organs and the legs with water and burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 用水洗了脏腑和腿，就把全羊烧在坛上为馨香的燔祭，是献给耶和华的火祭，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: He then presented the other ram, the ram for the ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
chapters.zh: 他又奉上第二只公绵羊，就是承接圣职之礼的羊，亚伦和他儿子按手在羊的头上，

chapters.en: Moses slaughtered the ram and took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.
chapters.zh: 就宰了羊。摩西把些血抹在亚伦的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上，

chapters.en: Moses also brought Aaron’s sons forward and put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet. Then he splashed blood against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 又带了亚伦的儿子来，把些血抹在他们的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上，又把血洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: After that, he took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, both kidneys and their fat and the right thigh.
chapters.zh: 取脂油和肥尾巴，并脏上一切的脂油与肝上的网子，两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，并右腿，

chapters.en: And from the basket of bread made without yeast, which was before the LORD, he took one thick loaf, one thick loaf with olive oil mixed in, and one thin loaf, and he put these on the fat portions and on the right thigh.
chapters.zh: 再从耶和华面前，盛无酵饼的筐子里取出一个无酵饼，一个油饼，一个薄饼，都放在脂油和右腿上，

chapters.en: He put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and they waved them before the LORD as a wave offering.
chapters.zh: 把这一切放在亚伦的手上和他儿子的手上作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇。

chapters.en: Then Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering as an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 摩西从他们的手上拿下来，烧在坛上的燔祭上，都是为承接圣职献给耶和华馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: Moses also took the breast, which was his share of the ordination ram, and waved it before the LORD as a wave offering, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 摩西拿羊的胸作为摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，是承接圣职之礼，归摩西的分，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his garments and on his sons and their garments. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments and his sons and their garments.
chapters.zh: 摩西取点膏油和坛上的血，弹在亚伦和他的衣服上，并他儿子和他儿子的衣服上，使他和他们的衣服一同成圣。

chapters.en: Moses then said to Aaron and his sons, “Cook the meat at the entrance to the tent of meeting and eat it there with the bread from the basket of ordination offerings, as I was commanded: ‘Aaron and his sons are to eat it.’
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦和他儿子说，把肉煮在会幕门口，在那里吃，又吃承接圣职筐子里的饼，按我所吩咐的说（或作按所吩咐我的说），这是亚伦和他儿子要吃的。

chapters.en: Then burn up the rest of the meat and the bread.
chapters.zh: 剩下的肉和饼，你们要用火焚烧。

chapters.en: Do not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed, for your ordination will last seven days.
chapters.zh: 你们七天不可出会幕的门，等到你们承接圣职的日子满了，因为主叫你们七天承接圣职。

chapters.en: What has been done today was commanded by the LORD to make atonement for you.
chapters.zh: 像今天所行的都是耶和华吩咐行的，为你们赎罪。

chapters.en: You must stay at the entrance to the tent of meeting day and night for seven days and do what the LORD requires, so you will not die; for that is what I have been commanded.”
chapters.zh: 七天你们要昼夜住在会幕门口，遵守耶和华的吩咐，免得你们死亡，因为所吩咐我的就是这样。

chapters.en: So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD commanded through Moses.
chapters.zh: 于是亚伦和他儿子行了耶和华借着摩西所吩咐的一切事。

chapters.en: On the eighth day Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
chapters.zh: 到了第八天，摩西召了亚伦和他儿子，并以色列的众长老来，

chapters.en: He said to Aaron, “Take a bull calf for your sin offering and a ram for your burnt offering, both without defect, and present them before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 对亚伦说，你当取牛群中的一只公牛犊作赎罪祭，一只公绵羊作燔祭，都要没有残疾的，献在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Then say to the Israelites: ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb—both a year old and without defect—for a burnt offering,
chapters.zh: 你也要对以色列人说，你们当取一只公山羊作赎罪祭，又取一只牛犊和一只绵羊羔，都要一岁，没有残疾的，作燔祭，

chapters.en: and an ox and a ram for a fellowship offering to sacrifice before the LORD, together with a grain offering mixed with olive oil. For today the LORD will appear to you.’ ”
chapters.zh: 又取一只公牛，一只公绵羊作平安祭，献在耶和华面前，并取调油的素祭，因为今天耶和华要向你们显现。

chapters.en: They took the things Moses commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the entire assembly came near and stood before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 于是他们把摩西所吩咐的，带到会幕前，全会众都近前来，站在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Then Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.”
chapters.zh: 摩西说，这是耶和华吩咐你们所当行的，耶和华的荣光就要向你们显现。

chapters.en: Moses said to Aaron, “Come to the altar and sacrifice your sin offering and your burnt offering and make atonement for yourself and the people; sacrifice the offering that is for the people and make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦说，你就近坛前，献你的赎罪祭和燔祭，为自己与百姓赎罪，又献上百姓的供物，为他们赎罪，都照耶和华所吩咐的。

chapters.en: So Aaron came to the altar and slaughtered the calf as a sin offering for himself.
chapters.zh: 于是，亚伦就近坛前，宰了为自己作赎罪祭的牛犊。

chapters.en: His sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger into the blood and put it on the horns of the altar; the rest of the blood he poured out at the base of the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的儿子把血奉给他，他就把指头蘸在血中，抹在坛的四角上，又把血倒在坛脚那里。

chapters.en: On the altar he burned the fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering, as the LORD commanded Moses;
chapters.zh: 惟有赎罪祭的脂油和腰子，并肝上取的网子，都烧在坛上，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: the flesh and the hide he burned up outside the camp.
chapters.zh: 又用火将肉和皮烧在营外。

chapters.en: Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦宰了燔祭牲，他儿子把血递给他，他就洒在坛的周围，

chapters.en: They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, including the head, and he burned them on the altar.
chapters.zh: 又把燔祭一块一块地，连头递给他，他都烧在坛上。

chapters.en: He washed the internal organs and the legs and burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
chapters.zh: 又洗了脏腑和腿，烧在坛上的燔祭上。

chapters.en: Aaron then brought the offering that was for the people. He took the goat for the people’s sin offering and slaughtered it and offered it for a sin offering as he did with the first one.
chapters.zh: 他奉上百姓的供物，把那给百姓作赎罪祭的公山羊宰了，为罪献上，和先献的一样。

chapters.en: He brought the burnt offering and offered it in the prescribed way.
chapters.zh: 也奉上燔祭，照例而献。

chapters.en: He also brought the grain offering, took a handful of it and burned it on the altar in addition to the morning’s burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 他又奉上素祭，从其中取一满把，烧在坛上，这是在早晨的燔祭以外。

chapters.en: He slaughtered the ox and the ram as the fellowship offering for the people. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦宰了那给百姓作平安祭的公牛和公绵羊。他儿子把血递给他，他就洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: But the fat portions of the ox and the ram—the fat tail, the layer of fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver—
chapters.zh: 又把公牛和公绵羊的脂油，肥尾巴，并盖脏的脂油与腰子，和肝上的网子，都递给他。

chapters.en: these they laid on the breasts, and then Aaron burned the fat on the altar.
chapters.zh: 把脂油放在胸上，他就把脂油烧在坛上。

chapters.en: Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh before the LORD as a wave offering, as Moses commanded.
chapters.zh: 胸和右腿，亚伦当作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，都是照摩西所吩咐的。

chapters.en: Then Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. And having sacrificed the sin offering, the burnt offering and the fellowship offering, he stepped down.
chapters.zh: 亚伦向百姓举手，为他们祝福。他献了赎罪祭，燔祭，平安祭就下来了。

chapters.en: Moses and Aaron then went into the tent of meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people; and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
chapters.zh: 摩西，亚伦进入会幕，又出来为百姓祝福，耶和华的荣光就向众民显现。

chapters.en: Fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. And when all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell facedown.
chapters.zh: 有火从耶和华面前出来，在坛上烧尽燔祭和脂油，众民一见，就都欢呼，俯伏在地。

chapters.en: Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu took their censers, put fire in them and added incense; and they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, contrary to his command.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的儿子拿答，亚比户各拿自己的香炉，盛上火，加上香，在耶和华面前献上凡火，是耶和华没有吩咐他们的，

chapters.en: So fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 就有火从耶和华面前出来，把他们烧灭，他们就死在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Moses then said to Aaron, “This is what the LORD spoke of when he said: “ ‘Among those who approach me I will be proved holy; in the sight of all the people I will be honored.’ ” Aaron remained silent.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西对亚伦说，这就是耶和华所说，我在亲近我的人中要显为圣，在众民面前，我要得荣耀。亚伦就默默不言。

chapters.en: Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron’s uncle Uzziel, and said to them, “Come here; carry your cousins outside the camp, away from the front of the sanctuary.”
chapters.zh: 摩西召了亚伦叔父乌薛的儿子米沙利，以利撒反来，对他们说，上前来，把你们的亲属从圣所前抬到营外。

chapters.en: So they came and carried them, still in their tunics, outside the camp, as Moses ordered.
chapters.zh: 于是二人上前来，把他们穿着袍子抬到营外，是照摩西所吩咐的。

chapters.en: Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not let your hair become unkempt and do not tear your clothes, or you will die and the LORD will be angry with the whole community. But your relatives, all the Israelites, may mourn for those the LORD has destroyed by fire.
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦和他儿子以利亚撒，以他玛说，不可蓬头散发，也不可撕裂衣裳，免得你们死亡，又免得耶和华向会众发怒，只要你们的弟兄以色列全家为耶和华所发的火哀哭。

chapters.en: Do not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting or you will die, because the LORD’s anointing oil is on you.” So they did as Moses said.
chapters.zh: 你们也不可出会幕的门，恐怕你们死亡，因为耶和华的膏油在你们的身上。他们就照摩西的话行了。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕亚伦说，

chapters.en: “You and your sons are not to drink wine or other fermented drink whenever you go into the tent of meeting, or you will die. This is a lasting ordinance for the generations to come,
chapters.zh: 你和你儿子进会幕的时候，清酒，浓酒都不可喝，免得你们死亡，这要作你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: so that you can distinguish between the holy and the common, between the unclean and the clean,
chapters.zh: 使你们可以将圣的，俗的，洁净的，不洁净的，分别出来。

chapters.en: and so you can teach the Israelites all the decrees the LORD has given them through Moses.”
chapters.zh: 又使你们可以将耶和华借摩西晓谕以色列人的一切律例教训他们。

chapters.en: Moses said to Aaron and his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take the grain offering left over from the food offerings prepared without yeast and presented to the LORD and eat it beside the altar, for it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦和他剩下的儿子以利亚撒，以他玛说，你们献给耶和华火祭中所剩的素祭，要在坛旁不带酵而吃，因为是至圣的。

chapters.en: Eat it in the sanctuary area, because it is your share and your sons’ share of the food offerings presented to the LORD; for so I have been commanded.
chapters.zh: 你们要在圣处吃，因为在献给耶和华的火祭中，这是你的分和你儿子的分，所吩咐我的本是这样。

chapters.en: But you and your sons and your daughters may eat the breast that was waved and the thigh that was presented. Eat them in a ceremonially clean place; they have been given to you and your children as your share of the Israelites’ fellowship offerings.
chapters.zh: 所摇的胸，所举的腿，你们要在洁净地方吃。你和你的儿女都要同吃，因为这些是从以色列人平安祭中给你，当你的分和你儿子的分。

chapters.en: The thigh that was presented and the breast that was waved must be brought with the fat portions of the food offerings, to be waved before the LORD as a wave offering. This will be the perpetual share for you and your children, as the LORD has commanded.”
chapters.zh: 所举的腿，所摇的胸，他们要与火祭的脂油一同带来当摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，这要归你和你儿子，当作永得的分，都是照耶和华所吩咐的。

chapters.en: When Moses inquired about the goat of the sin offering and found that it had been burned up, he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, and asked,
chapters.zh: 当下摩西急切地寻找作赎罪祭的公山羊，谁知已经焚烧了，便向亚伦剩下的儿子以利亚撒，以他玛发怒，说，

chapters.en: “Why didn’t you eat the sin offering in the sanctuary area? It is most holy; it was given to you to take away the guilt of the community by making atonement for them before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这赎罪祭既是至圣的，主又给了你们，为要你们担当会众的罪孽，在耶和华面前为他们赎罪，你们为何没有在圣所吃呢？

chapters.en: Since its blood was not taken into the Holy Place, you should have eaten the goat in the sanctuary area, as I commanded.”
chapters.zh: 看哪，这祭牲的血并没有拿到圣所里去，你们本当照我所吩咐的，在圣所里吃这祭肉。

chapters.en: Aaron replied to Moses, “Today they sacrificed their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, but such things as this have happened to me. Would the LORD have been pleased if I had eaten the sin offering today?”
chapters.zh: 亚伦对摩西说，今天他们在耶和华面前献上赎罪祭和燔祭，我又遇见这样的灾，若今天吃了赎罪祭，耶和华岂能看为美呢？

chapters.en: When Moses heard this, he was satisfied.
chapters.zh: 摩西听见这话，便以为美。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西，亚伦说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘Of all the animals that live on land, these are the ones you may eat:
chapters.zh: 你们晓谕以色列人说，在地上一切走兽中可吃的乃是这些，

chapters.en: You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof and that chews the cud.
chapters.zh: 凡蹄分两瓣，倒嚼的走兽，你们都可以吃。

chapters.en: “ ‘There are some that only chew the cud or only have a divided hoof, but you must not eat them. The camel, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is ceremonially unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 但那倒嚼或分蹄之中不可吃的乃是骆驼，因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: The hyrax, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 沙番因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: The rabbit, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 兔子因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: And the pig, though it has a divided hoof, does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 猪因为蹄分两瓣，却不倒嚼，就与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 这些兽的肉，你们不可吃，死的，你们不可摸，都与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: “ ‘Of all the creatures living in the water of the seas and the streams you may eat any that have fins and scales.
chapters.zh: 水中可吃的乃是这些，凡在水里，海里，河里，有翅有鳞的，都可以吃。

chapters.en: But all creatures in the seas or streams that do not have fins and scales—whether among all the swarming things or among all the other living creatures in the water—you are to regard as unclean.
chapters.zh: 凡在海里，河里，并一切水里游动的活物，无翅无鳞的，你们都当以为可憎。

chapters.en: And since you are to regard them as unclean, you must not eat their meat; you must regard their carcasses as unclean.
chapters.zh: 这些无翅无鳞，以为可憎的，你们不可吃它的肉，死的也当以为可憎。

chapters.en: Anything living in the water that does not have fins and scales is to be regarded as unclean by you.
chapters.zh: 凡水里无翅无鳞的，你们都当以为可憎。

chapters.en: “ ‘These are the birds you are to regard as unclean and not eat because they are unclean: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
chapters.zh: 雀鸟中你们当以为可憎，不可吃的乃是，雕，狗头雕，红头雕，

chapters.en: the red kite, any kind of black kite,
chapters.zh: 鹞鹰，小鹰与其类。

chapters.en: any kind of raven,
chapters.zh: 乌鸦与其类。

chapters.en: the horned owl, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
chapters.zh: 鸵鸟，夜鹰，鱼鹰，鹰与其类。

chapters.en: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
chapters.zh: 鸱鹗，鸬鹚，猫头鹰，

chapters.en: the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
chapters.zh: 角鸱，鹈鹕，秃雕，

chapters.en: the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.
chapters.zh: 鹳，鹭鸶与其类，戴胜与蝙蝠。

chapters.en: “ ‘All flying insects that walk on all fours are to be regarded as unclean by you.
chapters.zh: 凡有翅膀用四足爬行的物，你们都当以为可憎。

chapters.en: There are, however, some flying insects that walk on all fours that you may eat: those that have jointed legs for hopping on the ground.
chapters.zh: 只是有翅膀用四足爬行的物中，有足有腿，在地上蹦跳的，你们还可以吃。

chapters.en: Of these you may eat any kind of locust, katydid, cricket or grasshopper.
chapters.zh: 其中有蝗虫，蚂蚱，蟋蟀与其类，蚱蜢与其类，这些你们都可以吃。

chapters.en: But all other flying insects that have four legs you are to regard as unclean.
chapters.zh: 但是有翅膀有四足的爬物，你们都当以为可憎。

chapters.en: “ ‘You will make yourselves unclean by these; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 这些都能使你们不洁净。凡摸了死的，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: Whoever picks up one of their carcasses must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 凡拿了死的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。

chapters.en: “ ‘Every animal that does not have a divided hoof or that does not chew the cud is unclean for you; whoever touches the carcass of any of them will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 凡走兽分蹄不成两瓣，也不倒嚼的，是与你们不洁净，凡摸了的就不洁净。

chapters.en: Of all the animals that walk on all fours, those that walk on their paws are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 凡四足的走兽，用掌行走的，是与你们不洁净，摸其尸的，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: Anyone who picks up their carcasses must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening. These animals are unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 拿其尸的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。这些是与你们不洁净的。

chapters.en: “ ‘Of the animals that move along the ground, these are unclean for you: the weasel, the rat, any kind of great lizard,
chapters.zh: 地上爬物与你们不洁净的乃是这些，鼬鼠，鼫鼠，蜥蜴与其类。

chapters.en: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink and the chameleon.
chapters.zh: 壁虎，龙子，守宫，蛇医，蝘蜓。

chapters.en: Of all those that move along the ground, these are unclean for you. Whoever touches them when they are dead will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 这些爬物都是与你们不洁净的。在它死了以后，凡摸了的，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: When one of them dies and falls on something, that article, whatever its use, will be unclean, whether it is made of wood, cloth, hide or sackcloth. Put it in water; it will be unclean till evening, and then it will be clean.
chapters.zh: 其中死了的，掉在什么东西上，这东西就不洁净，无论是木器，衣服，皮子，口袋，不拘是作什么工用的器皿，须要放在水中，必不洁净到晚上，到晚上才洁净了。

chapters.en: If one of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will be unclean, and you must break the pot.
chapters.zh: 若有死了掉在瓦器里的，其中不拘有什么，就不洁净，你们要把这瓦器打破了。

chapters.en: Any food you are allowed to eat that has come into contact with water from any such pot is unclean, and any liquid that is drunk from such a pot is unclean.
chapters.zh: 其中一切可吃的食物，沾水的就不洁净，并且那样器皿中一切可喝的，也必不洁净。

chapters.en: Anything that one of their carcasses falls on becomes unclean; an oven or cooking pot must be broken up. They are unclean, and you are to regard them as unclean.
chapters.zh: 其中已死的，若有一点掉在什么物件上，那物件就不洁净，不拘是炉子，是锅台，就要打碎，都不洁净，也必与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: A spring, however, or a cistern for collecting water remains clean, but anyone who touches one of these carcasses is unclean.
chapters.zh: 但是泉源或是聚水的池子仍是洁净，惟挨了那死的，就不洁净。

chapters.en: If a carcass falls on any seeds that are to be planted, they remain clean.
chapters.zh: 若是死的，有一点掉在要种的子粒上，子粒仍是洁净。

chapters.en: But if water has been put on the seed and a carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 若水已经浇在子粒上，那死的有一点掉在上头，这子粒就与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: “ ‘If an animal that you are allowed to eat dies, anyone who touches its carcass will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 你们可吃的走兽若是死了，有人摸它，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: Anyone who eats some of its carcass must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening. Anyone who picks up the carcass must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 有人吃那死了的走兽，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，拿了死走兽的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。

chapters.en: “ ‘Every creature that moves along the ground is to be regarded as unclean; it is not to be eaten.
chapters.zh: 凡地上的爬物是可憎的，都不可吃。

chapters.en: You are not to eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it moves on its belly or walks on all fours or on many feet; it is unclean.
chapters.zh: 凡用肚子行走的和用四足行走的，或是有许多足的，就是一切爬在地上的，你们都不可吃，因为是可憎的。

chapters.en: Do not defile yourselves by any of these creatures. Do not make yourselves unclean by means of them or be made unclean by them.
chapters.zh: 你们不可因什么爬物使自己成为可憎的，也不可因这些使自己不洁净，以致染了污秽。

chapters.en: I am the LORD your God; consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean by any creature that moves along the ground.
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华你们的神，所以你们要成为圣洁，因为我是圣洁的。你们也不可在地上的爬物污秽自己。
