chapters.en: I am the LORD, who brought you up out of Egypt to be your God; therefore be holy, because I am holy.
chapters.zh: 我是把你们从埃及地领出来的耶和华，要作你们的神，所以你们要圣洁，因为我是圣洁的。

chapters.en: “ ‘These are the regulations concerning animals, birds, every living thing that moves about in the water and every creature that moves along the ground.
chapters.zh: 这是走兽，飞鸟，和水中游动的活物，并地上爬物的条例。

chapters.en: You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between living creatures that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten.’ ”
chapters.zh: 要把洁净的和不洁净的，可吃的与不可吃的活物，都分别出来。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘A woman who becomes pregnant and gives birth to a son will be ceremonially unclean for seven days, just as she is unclean during her monthly period.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，若有妇人怀孕生男孩，她就不洁净七天，像在月经污秽的日子不洁净一样。

chapters.en: On the eighth day the boy is to be circumcised.
chapters.zh: 第八天，要给婴孩行割礼。

chapters.en: Then the woman must wait thirty-three days to be purified from her bleeding. She must not touch anything sacred or go to the sanctuary until the days of her purification are over.
chapters.zh: 妇人在产血不洁之中，要家居三十三天。她洁净的日子未满，不可摸圣物，也不可进入圣所。

chapters.en: If she gives birth to a daughter, for two weeks the woman will be unclean, as during her period. Then she must wait sixty-six days to be purified from her bleeding.
chapters.zh: 她若生女孩，就不洁净两个七天，像污秽的时候一样，要在产血不洁之中，家居六十六天。

chapters.en: “ ‘When the days of her purification for a son or daughter are over, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a dove for a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 满了洁净的日子，无论是为男孩是为女孩，她要把一岁的羊羔为燔祭，一只雏鸽或是一只斑鸠为赎罪祭，带到会幕门口交给祭司。

chapters.en: He shall offer them before the LORD to make atonement for her, and then she will be ceremonially clean from her flow of blood. “ ‘These are the regulations for the woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.
chapters.zh: 祭司要献在耶和华面前，为她赎罪，她的血源就洁净了。这条例是为生育的妇人，无论是生男生女。

chapters.en: But if she cannot afford a lamb, she is to bring two doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.’ ”
chapters.zh: 她的力量若不够献一只羊羔，她就要取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，一只为燔祭，一只为赎罪祭。祭司要为她赎罪，她就洁净了。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西，亚伦说，

chapters.en: “When anyone has a swelling or a rash or a shiny spot on their skin that may be a defiling skin disease, they must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest.
chapters.zh: 人的肉皮上若长了疖子，或长了癣，或长了火斑，在他肉皮上成了大麻疯的灾病，就要将他带到祭司亚伦或亚伦作祭司的一个子孙面前。

chapters.en: The priest is to examine the sore on the skin, and if the hair in the sore has turned white and the sore appears to be more than skin deep, it is a defiling skin disease. When the priest examines that person, he shall pronounce them ceremonially unclean.
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看肉皮上的灾病，若灾病处的毛已经变白，灾病的现象深于肉上的皮，这便是大麻疯的灾病。祭司要察看他，定他为不洁净。

chapters.en: If the shiny spot on the skin is white but does not appear to be more than skin deep and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest is to isolate the affected person for seven days.
chapters.zh: 若火斑在他肉皮上是白的，现象不深于皮，其上的毛也没有变白，祭司就要将有灾病的人关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to examine them, and if he sees that the sore is unchanged and has not spread in the skin, he is to isolate them for another seven days.
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要察看他，若看灾病止住了，没有在皮上发散，祭司还要将他关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to examine them again, and if the sore has faded and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them clean; it is only a rash. They must wash their clothes, and they will be clean.
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要再察看他，若灾病发暗，而且没有在皮上发散，祭司要定他为洁净，原来是癣，那人就要洗衣服，得为洁净。

chapters.en: But if the rash does spread in their skin after they have shown themselves to the priest to be pronounced clean, they must appear before the priest again.
chapters.zh: 但他为得洁净，将身体给祭司察看以后，癣若在皮上发散开了，他要再将身体给祭司察看。

chapters.en: The priest is to examine that person, and if the rash has spread in the skin, he shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease.
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，癣若在皮上发散，就要定他为不洁净，是大麻疯。

chapters.en: “When anyone has a defiling skin disease, they must be brought to the priest.
chapters.zh: 人有了大麻疯的灾病，就要将他带到祭司面前。

chapters.en: The priest is to examine them, and if there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white and if there is raw flesh in the swelling,
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，皮上若长了白疖，使毛变白，在长白疖之处有了红瘀肉，

chapters.en: it is a chronic skin disease and the priest shall pronounce them unclean. He is not to isolate them, because they are already unclean.
chapters.zh: 这是肉皮上的旧大麻疯，祭司要定他为不洁净，不用将他关锁，因为他是不洁净了。

chapters.en: “If the disease breaks out all over their skin and, so far as the priest can see, it covers all the skin of the affected person from head to foot,
chapters.zh: 大麻疯若在皮上四外发散，长满了患灾病人的皮，据祭司察看，从头到脚无处不有，

chapters.en: the priest is to examine them, and if the disease has covered their whole body, he shall pronounce them clean. Since it has all turned white, they are clean.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，全身的肉若长满了大麻疯，就要定那患灾病的为洁净，全身都变为白，他乃洁净了。

chapters.en: But whenever raw flesh appears on them, they will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 但红肉几时显在他的身上就几时不洁净。

chapters.en: When the priest sees the raw flesh, he shall pronounce them unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; they have a defiling disease.
chapters.zh: 祭司一看那红肉就定他为不洁净。红肉本是不洁净，是大麻疯。

chapters.en: If the raw flesh changes and turns white, they must go to the priest.
chapters.zh: 红肉若复原，又变白了，他就要来见祭司。

chapters.en: The priest is to examine them, and if the sores have turned white, the priest shall pronounce the affected person clean; then they will be clean.
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，灾病处若变白了，祭司就要定那患灾病的为洁净，他乃洁净了。

chapters.en: “When someone has a boil on their skin and it heals,
chapters.zh: 人若在皮肉上长疮，却治好了，

chapters.en: and in the place where the boil was, a white swelling or reddish-white spot appears, they must present themselves to the priest.
chapters.zh: 在长疮之处又起了白疖，或是白中带红的火斑，就要给祭司察看。

chapters.en: The priest is to examine it, and if it appears to be more than skin deep and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce that person unclean. It is a defiling skin disease that has broken out where the boil was.
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，若现象洼于皮，其上的毛也变白了，就要定他为不洁净，是大麻疯的灾病发在疮中。

chapters.en: But if, when the priest examines it, there is no white hair in it and it is not more than skin deep and has faded, then the priest is to isolate them for seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司若察看，其上没有白毛，也没有洼于皮，乃是发暗，就要将他关锁七天。

chapters.en: If it is spreading in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling disease.
chapters.zh: 若在皮上发散开了，祭司就要定他为不洁净，是灾病。

chapters.en: But if the spot is unchanged and has not spread, it is only a scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce them clean.
chapters.zh: 火斑若在原处止住，没有发散，便是疮的痕迹，祭司就要定他为洁净。

chapters.en: “When someone has a burn on their skin and a reddish-white or white spot appears in the raw flesh of the burn,
chapters.zh: 人的皮肉上若起了火毒，火毒的瘀肉成了火斑，或是白中带红的，或是全白的，

chapters.en: the priest is to examine the spot, and if the hair in it has turned white, and it appears to be more than skin deep, it is a defiling disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，火斑中的毛若变白了，现象又深于皮，是大麻疯在火毒中发出，就要定他为不洁净，是大麻疯的灾病。

chapters.en: But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot and if it is not more than skin deep and has faded, then the priest is to isolate them for seven days.
chapters.zh: 但是祭司察看，在火斑中若没有白毛，也没有洼于皮，乃是发暗，就要将他关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to examine that person, and if it is spreading in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease.
chapters.zh: 到第七天，祭司要察看他，火斑若在皮上发散开了，就要定他为不洁净，是大麻疯的灾病。

chapters.en: If, however, the spot is unchanged and has not spread in the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest shall pronounce them clean; it is only a scar from the burn.
chapters.zh: 火斑若在原处止住，没有在皮上发散，乃是发暗，是起的火毒，祭司要定他为洁净，不过是火毒的痕迹。

chapters.en: “If a man or woman has a sore on their head or chin,
chapters.zh: 无论男女，若在头上有灾病，或是男人胡须上有灾病，

chapters.en: the priest is to examine the sore, and if it appears to be more than skin deep and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease on the head or chin.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，这灾病现象若深于皮，其间有细黄毛，就要定他为不洁净，这是头疥，是头上或是胡须上的大麻疯。

chapters.en: But if, when the priest examines the sore, it does not seem to be more than skin deep and there is no black hair in it, then the priest is to isolate the affected person for seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司若察看头疥的灾病，现象不深于皮，其间也没有黑毛，就要将长头疥灾病的关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to examine the sore, and if it has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it and it does not appear to be more than skin deep,
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要察看灾病，若头疥没有发散，其间也没有黄毛，头疥的现象不深于皮，

chapters.en: then the man or woman must shave themselves, except for the affected area, and the priest is to keep them isolated another seven days.
chapters.zh: 那人就要剃去须发，但他不可剃头疥之处。祭司要将那长头疥的，再关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to examine the sore, and if it has not spread in the skin and appears to be no more than skin deep, the priest shall pronounce them clean. They must wash their clothes, and they will be clean.
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要察看头疥，头疥若没有在皮上发散，现象也不深于皮，就要定他为洁净，他要洗衣服，便成为洁净。

chapters.en: But if the sore does spread in the skin after they are pronounced clean,
chapters.zh: 但他得洁净以后，头疥若在皮上发散开了，

chapters.en: the priest is to examine them, and if he finds that the sore has spread in the skin, he does not need to look for yellow hair; they are unclean.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看他。头疥若在皮上发散，就不必找那黄毛，他是不洁净了。

chapters.en: If, however, the sore is unchanged so far as the priest can see, and if black hair has grown in it, the affected person is healed. They are clean, and the priest shall pronounce them clean.
chapters.zh: 祭司若看头疥已经止住，其间也长了黑毛，头疥已然痊愈，那人是洁净了，就要定他为洁净。

chapters.en: “When a man or woman has white spots on the skin,
chapters.zh: 无论男女，皮肉上若起了火斑，就是白火斑，

chapters.en: the priest is to examine them, and if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; they are clean.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，他们肉皮上的火斑若白中带黑，这是皮上发出的白癣，那人是洁净了。

chapters.en: “A man who has lost his hair and is bald is clean.
chapters.zh: 人头上的发若掉了，他不过是头秃，还是洁净。

chapters.en: If he has lost his hair from the front of his scalp and has a bald forehead, he is clean.
chapters.zh: 他顶前若掉了头发，他不过是顶门秃，还是洁净。

chapters.en: But if he has a reddish-white sore on his bald head or forehead, it is a defiling disease breaking out on his head or forehead.
chapters.zh: 头秃处或是顶门秃处若有白中带红的灾病，这就是大麻疯发在他头秃处或是顶门秃处，

chapters.en: The priest is to examine him, and if the swollen sore on his head or forehead is reddish-white like a defiling skin disease,
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，他起的那灾病若在头秃处或是顶门秃处有白中带红的，像肉皮上大麻疯的现象，

chapters.en: the man is diseased and is unclean. The priest shall pronounce him unclean because of the sore on his head.
chapters.zh: 那人就是长大麻疯，不洁净的，祭司总要定他为不洁净，他的灾病是在头上。

chapters.en: “Anyone with such a defiling disease must wear torn clothes, let their hair be unkempt, cover the lower part of their face and cry out, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’
chapters.zh: 身上有长大麻疯灾病的，他的衣服要撕裂，也要蓬头散发，蒙着上唇，喊叫说，不洁净了，不洁净了。

chapters.en: As long as they have the disease they remain unclean. They must live alone; they must live outside the camp.
chapters.zh: 灾病在他身上的日子，他便是不洁净，他既是不洁净，就要独居营外。

chapters.en: “As for any fabric that is spoiled with a defiling mold—any woolen or linen clothing,
chapters.zh: 染了大麻疯灾病的衣服，无论是羊毛衣服，是麻布衣服，

chapters.en: any woven or knitted material of linen or wool, any leather or anything made of leather—
chapters.zh: 无论是在经上，在纬上，是麻布的，是羊毛的，是在皮子上，或在皮子作的什么物件上，

chapters.en: if the affected area in the fabric, the leather, the woven or knitted material, or any leather article, is greenish or reddish, it is a defiling mold and must be shown to the priest.
chapters.zh: 或在衣服上，皮子上，经上，纬上，或在皮子作的什么物件上，这灾病若是发绿，或是发红，是大麻疯的灾病，要给祭司察看。

chapters.en: The priest is to examine the affected area and isolate the article for seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看那灾病，把染了灾病的物件关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day he is to examine it, and if the mold has spread in the fabric, the woven or knitted material, or the leather, whatever its use, it is a persistent defiling mold; the article is unclean.
chapters.zh: 第七天，他要察看那灾病，灾病或在衣服上，经上，纬上，皮子上，若发散，这皮子无论当作何用，这灾病是蚕食的大麻疯，都是不洁净了。

chapters.en: He must burn the fabric, the woven or knitted material of wool or linen, or any leather article that has been spoiled; because the defiling mold is persistent, the article must be burned.
chapters.zh: 那染了灾病的衣服，或是经上，纬上，羊毛上，麻衣上，或是皮子作的什么物件上，他都要焚烧，因为这是蚕食的大麻疯，必在火中焚烧。

chapters.en: “But if, when the priest examines it, the mold has not spread in the fabric, the woven or knitted material, or the leather article,
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，若灾病在衣服上，经上，纬上，或是皮子作的什么物件上，没有发散，

chapters.en: he shall order that the spoiled article be washed. Then he is to isolate it for another seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要吩咐他们，把染了灾病的物件洗了，再关锁七天。

chapters.en: After the article has been washed, the priest is to examine it again, and if the mold has not changed its appearance, even though it has not spread, it is unclean. Burn it, no matter which side of the fabric has been spoiled.
chapters.zh: 洗过以后，祭司要察看，那物件若没有变色，灾病也没有消散，那物件就不洁净，是透重的灾病，无论正面反面，都要在火中焚烧。

chapters.en: If, when the priest examines it, the mold has faded after the article has been washed, he is to tear the spoiled part out of the fabric, the leather, or the woven or knitted material.
chapters.zh: 洗过以后，祭司要察看，若见那灾病发暗，他就要把那灾病从衣服上，皮子上，经上，纬上，都撕去。

chapters.en: But if it reappears in the fabric, in the woven or knitted material, or in the leather article, it is a spreading mold; whatever has the mold must be burned.
chapters.zh: 若仍现在衣服上，或是经上，纬上，皮子作的什么物件上，这就是灾病又发了，必用火焚烧那染灾病的物件。

chapters.en: Any fabric, woven or knitted material, or any leather article that has been washed and is rid of the mold, must be washed again. Then it will be clean.”
chapters.zh: 所洗的衣服，或是经，或是纬，或是皮子作的什么物件，若灾病离开了，要再洗，就洁净了。

chapters.en: These are the regulations concerning defiling molds in woolen or linen clothing, woven or knitted material, or any leather article, for pronouncing them clean or unclean.
chapters.zh: 这就是大麻疯灾病的条例，无论是在羊毛衣服上，麻布衣服上，经上，纬上，和皮子作的什么物件上，可以定为洁净或是不洁净。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “These are the regulations for any diseased person at the time of their ceremonial cleansing, when they are brought to the priest:
chapters.zh: 长大麻疯得洁净的日子，其例乃是这样，要带他去见祭司。

chapters.en: The priest is to go outside the camp and examine them. If they have been healed of their defiling skin disease,
chapters.zh: 祭司要出到营外察看，若见他的大麻疯痊愈了，

chapters.en: the priest shall order that two live clean birds and some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop be brought for the person to be cleansed.
chapters.zh: 就要吩咐人为那求洁净的拿两只洁净的活鸟和香柏木，朱红色线，并牛膝草来。

chapters.en: Then the priest shall order that one of the birds be killed over fresh water in a clay pot.
chapters.zh: 祭司要吩咐用瓦器盛活水，把一只鸟宰在上面。

chapters.en: He is then to take the live bird and dip it, together with the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn and the hyssop, into the blood of the bird that was killed over the fresh water.
chapters.zh: 至于那只活鸟，祭司要把它和香柏木，朱红色线并牛膝草一同蘸于宰在活水上的鸟血中，

chapters.en: Seven times he shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed of the defiling disease, and then pronounce them clean. After that, he is to release the live bird in the open fields.
chapters.zh: 用以在那长大麻疯求洁净的人身上洒七次，就定他为洁净，又把活鸟放在田野里。

chapters.en: “The person to be cleansed must wash their clothes, shave off all their hair and bathe with water; then they will be ceremonially clean. After this they may come into the camp, but they must stay outside their tent for seven days.
chapters.zh: 求洁净的人当洗衣服，剃去毛发，用水洗澡，就洁净了，然后可以进营，只是要在自己的帐棚外居住七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day they must shave off all their hair; they must shave their head, their beard, their eyebrows and the rest of their hair. They must wash their clothes and bathe themselves with water, and they will be clean.
chapters.zh: 第七天，再把头上所有的头发与胡须，眉毛，并全身的毛，都剃了，又要洗衣服，用水洗身，就洁净了。

chapters.en: “On the eighth day they must bring two male lambs and one ewe lamb a year old, each without defect, along with three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.
chapters.zh: 第八天，他要取两只没有残疾的公羊羔和一只没有残疾，一岁的母羊羔，又要把调油的细面伊法十分之三为素祭，并油一罗革，一同取来。

chapters.en: The priest who pronounces them clean shall present both the one to be cleansed and their offerings before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 行洁净之礼的祭司要将那求洁净的人和这些东西安置在会幕门口，耶和华面前。

chapters.en: “Then the priest is to take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, along with the log of oil; he shall wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.
chapters.zh: 祭司要取一只公羊羔献为赎愆祭，和那一罗革油一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇。

chapters.en: He is to slaughter the lamb in the sanctuary area where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest; it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 把公羊羔宰于圣地，就是宰赎罪祭牲和燔祭牲之地。赎愆祭要归祭司，与赎罪祭一样，是至圣的。

chapters.en: The priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot.
chapters.zh: 祭司要取些赎愆祭牲的血，抹在求洁净人的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上。

chapters.en: The priest shall then take some of the log of oil, pour it in the palm of his own left hand,
chapters.zh: 祭司要从那一罗革油中取些倒在自己的左手掌里，

chapters.en: dip his right forefinger into the oil in his palm, and with his finger sprinkle some of it before the LORD seven times.
chapters.zh: 把右手的一个指头蘸在左手的油里，在耶和华面前用指头弹七次。

chapters.en: The priest is to put some of the oil remaining in his palm on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 将手里所剩的油抹在那求洁净人的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上，就是抹在赎愆祭牲的血上。

chapters.en: The rest of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the head of the one to be cleansed and make atonement for them before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司手里所剩的油要抹在那求洁净人的头上，在耶和华面前为他赎罪。

chapters.en: “Then the priest is to sacrifice the sin offering and make atonement for the one to be cleansed from their uncleanness. After that, the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering
chapters.zh: 祭司要献赎罪祭，为那本不洁净，求洁净的人赎罪，然后要宰燔祭牲，

chapters.en: and offer it on the altar, together with the grain offering, and make atonement for them, and they will be clean.
chapters.zh: 把燔祭和素祭献在坛上，为他赎罪，他就洁净了。

chapters.en: “If, however, they are poor and cannot afford these, they must take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved to make atonement for them, together with a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, a log of oil,
chapters.zh: 他若贫穷不能预备够数，就要取一只公羊羔作赎愆祭，可以摇一摇，为他赎罪，也要把调油的细面伊法十分之一为素祭，和油一罗革一同取来。

chapters.en: and two doves or two young pigeons, such as they can afford, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 又照他的力量取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，一只作赎罪祭，一只作燔祭。

chapters.en: “On the eighth day they must bring them for their cleansing to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting, before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 第八天，要为洁净，把这些带到会幕门口，耶和华面前，交给祭司。

chapters.en: The priest is to take the lamb for the guilt offering, together with the log of oil, and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把赎愆祭的羊羔和那一罗革油一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇。

chapters.en: He shall slaughter the lamb for the guilt offering and take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot.
chapters.zh: 要宰了赎愆祭的羊羔，取些赎愆祭牲的血，抹在那求洁净人的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上。

chapters.en: The priest is to pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand,
chapters.zh: 祭司要把些油倒在自己的左手掌里，

chapters.en: and with his right forefinger sprinkle some of the oil from his palm seven times before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 把左手里的油，在耶和华面前，用右手的一个指头弹七次，

chapters.en: Some of the oil in his palm he is to put on the same places he put the blood of the guilt offering—on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot.
chapters.zh: 又把手里的油抹些在那求洁净人的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上，就是抹赎愆祭之血的原处。

chapters.en: The rest of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司手里所剩的油要抹在那求洁净人的头上，在耶和华面前为他赎罪。

chapters.en: Then he shall sacrifice the doves or the young pigeons, such as the person can afford,
chapters.zh: 那人又要照他的力量献上一只斑鸠或是一只雏鸽，

chapters.en: one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. In this way the priest will make atonement before the LORD on behalf of the one to be cleansed.”
chapters.zh: 就是他所能办的，一只为赎罪祭，一只为燔祭，与素祭一同献上，祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪。

chapters.en: These are the regulations for anyone who has a defiling skin disease and who cannot afford the regular offerings for their cleansing.
chapters.zh: 这是那有大麻疯灾病的人，不能将关乎得洁净之物预备够数的条例。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西，亚伦说，

chapters.en: “When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your possession, and I put a spreading mold in a house in that land,
chapters.zh: 你们到了我赐给你们为业的迦南地，我若使你们所得为业之地的房屋中有大麻疯的灾病，

chapters.en: the owner of the house must go and tell the priest, ‘I have seen something that looks like a defiling mold in my house.’
chapters.zh: 房主就要去告诉祭司说，据我看，房屋中似乎有灾病。

chapters.en: The priest is to order the house to be emptied before he goes in to examine the mold, so that nothing in the house will be pronounced unclean. After this the priest is to go in and inspect the house.
chapters.zh: 祭司还没有进去察看灾病以前，就要吩咐人把房子腾空，免得房子里所有的都成了不洁净，然后祭司要进去察看房子。

chapters.en: He is to examine the mold on the walls, and if it has greenish or reddish depressions that appear to be deeper than the surface of the wall,
chapters.zh: 他要察看那灾病，灾病若在房子的墙上有发绿或发红的凹斑纹，现象洼于墙，

chapters.en: the priest shall go out the doorway of the house and close it up for seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要出到房门外，把房子封锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest shall return to inspect the house. If the mold has spread on the walls,
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要再去察看，灾病若在房子的墙上发散，

chapters.en: he is to order that the contaminated stones be torn out and thrown into an unclean place outside the town.
chapters.zh: 就要吩咐人把那有灾病的石头挖出来，扔在城外不洁净之处。

chapters.en: He must have all the inside walls of the house scraped and the material that is scraped off dumped into an unclean place outside the town.
chapters.zh: 也要叫人刮房内的四围，所刮掉的灰泥要倒在城外不洁净之处。

chapters.en: Then they are to take other stones to replace these and take new clay and plaster the house.
chapters.zh: 又要用别的石头代替那挖出来的石头，要另用灰泥墁房子。

chapters.en: “If the defiling mold reappears in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house scraped and plastered,
chapters.zh: 他挖出石头，刮了房子，墁了以后，灾病若在房子里又发现，

chapters.en: the priest is to go and examine it and, if the mold has spread in the house, it is a persistent defiling mold; the house is unclean.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要进去察看，灾病若在房子里发散，这就是房内蚕食的大麻疯，是不洁净。

chapters.en: It must be torn down—its stones, timbers and all the plaster—and taken out of the town to an unclean place.
chapters.zh: 他就要拆毁房子，把石头，木头，灰泥都搬到城外不洁净之处。

chapters.en: “Anyone who goes into the house while it is closed up will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 在房子封锁的时候，进去的人必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: Anyone who sleeps or eats in the house must wash their clothes.
chapters.zh: 在房子里躺着的必洗衣服，在房子里吃饭的也必洗衣服。

chapters.en: “But if the priest comes to examine it and the mold has not spread after the house has been plastered, he shall pronounce the house clean, because the defiling mold is gone.
chapters.zh: 房子墁了以后，祭司若进去察看，见灾病在房内没有发散，就要定房子为洁净，因为灾病已经消除。

chapters.en: To purify the house he is to take two birds and some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop.
chapters.zh: 要为洁净房子取两只鸟和香柏木，朱红色线并牛膝草，

chapters.en: He shall kill one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.
chapters.zh: 用瓦器盛活水，把一只鸟宰在上面，

chapters.en: Then he is to take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn and the live bird, dip them into the blood of the dead bird and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
chapters.zh: 把香柏木，牛膝草，朱红色线，并那活鸟，都蘸在被宰的鸟血中与活水中，用以洒房子七次。

chapters.en: He shall purify the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet yarn.
chapters.zh: 要用鸟血，活水，活鸟，香柏木，牛膝草，并朱红色线，洁净那房子。

chapters.en: Then he is to release the live bird in the open fields outside the town. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.”
chapters.zh: 但要把活鸟放在城外田野里。这样洁净房子（原文作为房子赎罪），房子就洁净了。

chapters.en: These are the regulations for any defiling skin disease, for a sore,
chapters.zh: 这是为各类大麻疯的灾病和头疥，

chapters.en: for defiling molds in fabric or in a house,
chapters.zh: 并衣服与房子的大麻疯，

chapters.en: and for a swelling, a rash or a shiny spot,
chapters.zh: 以及疖子，癣，火斑所立的条例，

chapters.en: to determine when something is clean or unclean. These are the regulations for defiling skin diseases and defiling molds.
chapters.zh: 指明何时为洁净，何时为不洁净。这是大麻疯的条例。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西，亚伦说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘When any man has an unusual bodily discharge, such a discharge is unclean.
chapters.zh: 你们晓谕以色列人说，人若身患漏症，他因这漏症就不洁净了。

chapters.en: Whether it continues flowing from his body or is blocked, it will make him unclean. This is how his discharge will bring about uncleanness:
chapters.zh: 他患漏症，无论是下流的，是止住的，都是不洁净。

chapters.en: “ ‘Any bed the man with a discharge lies on will be unclean, and anything he sits on will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 他所躺的床都为不洁净，所坐的物也为不洁净。

chapters.en: Anyone who touches his bed must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸那床的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: Whoever sits on anything that the man with a discharge sat on must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 那坐患漏症人所坐之物的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: “ ‘Whoever touches the man who has a discharge must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 那摸患漏症人身体的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: “ ‘If the man with the discharge spits on anyone who is clean, they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 若患漏症人吐在洁净的人身上，那人必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: “ ‘Everything the man sits on when riding will be unclean,
chapters.zh: 患漏症人所骑的鞍子也为不洁净。

chapters.en: and whoever touches any of the things that were under him will be unclean till evening; whoever picks up those things must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸了他身下之物的，必不洁净到晚上，拿了那物的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: “ ‘Anyone the man with a discharge touches without rinsing his hands with water must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 患漏症的人没有用水涮手，无论摸了谁，谁必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: “ ‘A clay pot that the man touches must be broken, and any wooden article is to be rinsed with water.
chapters.zh: 患漏症人所摸的瓦器就必打破，所摸的一切木器也必用水涮洗。

chapters.en: “ ‘When a man is cleansed from his discharge, he is to count off seven days for his ceremonial cleansing; he must wash his clothes and bathe himself with fresh water, and he will be clean.
chapters.zh: 患漏症的人痊愈了，就要为洁净自己计算七天，也必洗衣服，用活水洗身，就洁净了。

chapters.en: On the eighth day he must take two doves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD to the entrance to the tent of meeting and give them to the priest.
chapters.zh: 第八天，要取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，来到会幕门口，耶和华面前，把鸟交给祭司。

chapters.en: The priest is to sacrifice them, the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. In this way he will make atonement before the LORD for the man because of his discharge.
chapters.zh: 祭司要献上一只为赎罪祭，一只为燔祭，因那人患的漏症，祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪。

chapters.en: “ ‘When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 人若梦遗，他必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗全身。

chapters.en: Any clothing or leather that has semen on it must be washed with water, and it will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 无论是衣服是皮子，被精所染，必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗。

chapters.en: When a man has sexual relations with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both of them must bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 若男女交合，两个人必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗澡。

chapters.en: “ ‘When a woman has her regular flow of blood, the impurity of her monthly period will last seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 女人行经，必污秽七天，凡摸她的，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: “ ‘Anything she lies on during her period will be unclean, and anything she sits on will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 女人在污秽之中，凡她所躺的物件都为不洁净，所坐的物件也都不洁净。

chapters.en: Anyone who touches her bed will be unclean; they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸她床的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: Anyone who touches anything she sits on will be unclean; they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸她所坐什么物件的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: Whether it is the bed or anything she was sitting on, when anyone touches it, they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 在女人的床上，或在她坐的物上，若有别的物件，人一摸了，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man has sexual relations with her and her monthly flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days; any bed he lies on will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 男人若与那女人同房，染了她的污秽，就要七天不洁净，所躺的床也为不洁净。

chapters.en: “ ‘When a woman has a discharge of blood for many days at a time other than her monthly period or has a discharge that continues beyond her period, she will be unclean as long as she has the discharge, just as in the days of her period.
chapters.zh: 女人若在经期以外患多日的血漏，或是经期过长，有了漏症，她就因这漏症不洁净，与她在经期不洁净一样。

chapters.en: Any bed she lies on while her discharge continues will be unclean, as is her bed during her monthly period, and anything she sits on will be unclean, as during her period.
chapters.zh: 她在患漏症的日子所躺的床，所坐的物都要看为不洁净，与她月经的时候一样。

chapters.en: Anyone who touches them will be unclean; they must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸这些物件的，就为不洁净，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: “ ‘When she is cleansed from her discharge, she must count off seven days, and after that she will be ceremonially clean.
chapters.zh: 女人的漏症若好了，就要计算七天，然后才为洁净。

chapters.en: On the eighth day she must take two doves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 第八天，要取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，带到会幕门口给祭司。

chapters.en: The priest is to sacrifice one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. In this way he will make atonement for her before the LORD for the uncleanness of her discharge.
chapters.zh: 祭司要献一只为赎罪祭，一只为燔祭，因那人血漏不洁，祭司要在耶和华面前为她赎罪。

chapters.en: “ ‘You must keep the Israelites separate from things that make them unclean, so they will not die in their uncleanness for defiling my dwelling place, which is among them.’ ”
chapters.zh: 你们要这样使以色列人与他们的污秽隔绝，免得他们玷污我的帐幕，就因自己的污秽死亡。

chapters.en: These are the regulations for a man with a discharge, for anyone made unclean by an emission of semen,
chapters.zh: 这是患漏症和梦遗而不洁净的，

chapters.en: for a woman in her monthly period, for a man or a woman with a discharge, and for a man who has sexual relations with a woman who is ceremonially unclean.
chapters.zh: 并有月经病的和患漏症的，无论男女，并人与不洁净女人同房的条例。

chapters.en: The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron who died when they approached the LORD.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的两个儿子近到耶和华面前死了。死了之后，耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses: “Tell your brother Aaron that he is not to come whenever he chooses into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain in front of the atonement cover on the ark, or else he will die. For I will appear in the cloud over the atonement cover.
chapters.zh: 要告诉你哥哥亚伦，不可随时进圣所的幔子内，到柜上的施恩座前，免得他死亡，因为我要从云中显现在施恩座上。

chapters.en: “This is how Aaron is to enter the Most Holy Place: He must first bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 亚伦进圣所，要带一只公牛犊为赎罪祭，一只公绵羊为燔祭。

chapters.en: He is to put on the sacred linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body; he is to tie the linen sash around him and put on the linen turban. These are sacred garments; so he must bathe himself with water before he puts them on.
chapters.zh: 要穿上细麻布圣内袍，把细麻布裤子穿在身上，腰束细麻布带子，头戴细麻布冠冕，这都是圣服。他要用水洗身，然后穿戴。

chapters.en: From the Israelite community he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 要从以色列会众取两只公山羊为赎罪祭，一只公绵羊为燔祭。

chapters.en: “Aaron is to offer the bull for his own sin offering to make atonement for himself and his household.
chapters.zh: 亚伦要把赎罪祭的公牛奉上，为自己和本家赎罪。

chapters.en: Then he is to take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 也要把两只公山羊安置在会幕门口，耶和华面前，

chapters.en: He is to cast lots for the two goats—one lot for the LORD and the other for the scapegoat.
chapters.zh: 为那两只羊拈阄，一阄归与耶和华，一阄归与阿撒泻勒。

chapters.en: Aaron shall bring the goat whose lot falls to the LORD and sacrifice it for a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 亚伦要把那拈阄归与耶和华的羊献为赎罪祭，

chapters.en: But the goat chosen by lot as the scapegoat shall be presented alive before the LORD to be used for making atonement by sending it into the wilderness as a scapegoat.
chapters.zh: 但那拈阄归与阿撒泻勒的羊要活着安置在耶和华面前，用以赎罪，打发人送到旷野去，归与阿撒泻勒。

chapters.en: “Aaron shall bring the bull for his own sin offering to make atonement for himself and his household, and he is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.
chapters.zh: 亚伦要把赎罪祭的公牛牵来宰了，为自己和本家赎罪。

chapters.en: He is to take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense and take them behind the curtain.
chapters.zh: 拿香炉，从耶和华面前的坛上盛满火炭，又拿一捧捣细的香料，都带入幔子内，

chapters.en: He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the smoke of the incense will conceal the atonement cover above the tablets of the covenant law, so that he will not die.
chapters.zh: 在耶和华面前，把香放在火上，使香的烟云遮掩法柜上的施恩座，免得他死亡。

chapters.en: He is to take some of the bull’s blood and with his finger sprinkle it on the front of the atonement cover; then he shall sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the atonement cover.
chapters.zh: 也要取些公牛的血，用指头弹在施恩座的东面，又在施恩座的前面弹血七次。

chapters.en: “He shall then slaughter the goat for the sin offering for the people and take its blood behind the curtain and do with it as he did with the bull’s blood: He shall sprinkle it on the atonement cover and in front of it.
chapters.zh: 随后他要宰那为百姓作赎罪祭的公山羊，把羊的血带入幔子内，弹在施恩座的上面和前面，好像弹公牛的血一样。

chapters.en: In this way he will make atonement for the Most Holy Place because of the uncleanness and rebellion of the Israelites, whatever their sins have been. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which is among them in the midst of their uncleanness.
chapters.zh: 他因以色列人诸般的污秽，过犯，就是他们一切的罪愆，当这样在圣所行赎罪之礼，并因会幕在他们污秽之中，也要照样而行。

chapters.en: No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place until he comes out, having made atonement for himself, his household and the whole community of Israel.
chapters.zh: 他进圣所赎罪的时候，会幕里不可有人，直等到他为自己和本家并以色列全会众赎了罪出来。

chapters.en: “Then he shall come out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.
chapters.zh: 他出来，要到耶和华面前的坛那里，在坛上行赎罪之礼，又要取些公牛的血和公山羊的血，抹在坛上四角的周围。

chapters.en: He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times to cleanse it and to consecrate it from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 也要用指头把血弹在坛上七次，洁净了坛，从坛上除掉以色列人诸般的污秽，使坛成圣。

chapters.en: “When Aaron has finished making atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting and the altar, he shall bring forward the live goat.
chapters.zh: 亚伦为圣所和会幕并坛献完了赎罪祭，就要把那只活着的公山羊奉上。

chapters.en: He is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the wickedness and rebellion of the Israelites—all their sins—and put them on the goat’s head. He shall send the goat away into the wilderness in the care of someone appointed for the task.
chapters.zh: 两手按在羊头上，承认以色列人诸般的罪孽过犯，就是他们一切的罪愆，把这罪都归在羊的头上，借着所派之人的手，送到旷野去。

chapters.en: The goat will carry on itself all their sins to a remote place; and the man shall release it in the wilderness.
chapters.zh: 要把这羊放在旷野，这羊要担当他们一切的罪孽，带到无人之地。

chapters.en: “Then Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting and take off the linen garments he put on before he entered the Most Holy Place, and he is to leave them there.
chapters.zh: 亚伦要进会幕，把他进圣所时所穿的细麻布衣服脱下，放在那里，

chapters.en: He shall bathe himself with water in the sanctuary area and put on his regular garments. Then he shall come out and sacrifice the burnt offering for himself and the burnt offering for the people, to make atonement for himself and for the people.
chapters.zh: 又要在圣处用水洗身，穿上衣服，出来，把自己的燔祭和百姓的燔祭献上，为自己和百姓赎罪。

chapters.en: He shall also burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
chapters.zh: 赎罪祭牲的脂油要在坛上焚烧。

chapters.en: “The man who releases the goat as a scapegoat must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may come into the camp.
chapters.zh: 那放羊归与阿撒泻勒的人要洗衣服，用水洗身，然后进营。

chapters.en: The bull and the goat for the sin offerings, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp; their hides, flesh and intestines are to be burned up.
chapters.zh: 作赎罪祭的公牛和公山羊的血既带入圣所赎罪，这牛羊就要搬到营外，将皮，肉，粪用火焚烧。

chapters.en: The man who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may come into the camp.
chapters.zh: 焚烧的人要洗衣服，用水洗身，然后进营。

chapters.en: “This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month you must deny yourselves and not do any work—whether native-born or a foreigner residing among you—
chapters.zh: 每逢七月初十日，你们要刻苦己心，无论是本地人，是寄居在你们中间的外人，什么工都不可作，这要作你们永远的定例。

chapters.en: because on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you. Then, before the LORD, you will be clean from all your sins.
chapters.zh: 因在这日要为你们赎罪，使你们洁净。你们要在耶和华面前得以洁净，脱尽一切的罪愆。

chapters.en: It is a day of sabbath rest, and you must deny yourselves; it is a lasting ordinance.
chapters.zh: 这日你们要守为圣安息日，要刻苦己心，这为永远的定例。

chapters.en: The priest who is anointed and ordained to succeed his father as high priest is to make atonement. He is to put on the sacred linen garments
chapters.zh: 那受膏，接续他父亲承接圣职的祭司要穿上细麻布的圣衣，行赎罪之礼。

chapters.en: and make atonement for the Most Holy Place, for the tent of meeting and the altar, and for the priests and all the members of the community.
chapters.zh: 他要在至圣所和会幕与坛行赎罪之礼，并要为众祭司和会众的百姓赎罪。

chapters.en: “This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: Atonement is to be made once a year for all the sins of the Israelites.” And it was done, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 这要作你们永远的定例就是因以色列人一切的罪，要一年一次为他们赎罪。于是，亚伦照耶和华所吩咐摩西的行了。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them: ‘This is what the LORD has commanded:
chapters.zh: 你晓谕亚伦和他儿子并以色列众人说，耶和华所吩咐的乃是这样，

chapters.en: Any Israelite who sacrifices an ox, a lamb or a goat in the camp or outside of it
chapters.zh: 凡以色列家中的人宰公牛，或是绵羊羔，或是山羊，不拘宰于营内营外，

chapters.en: instead of bringing it to the entrance to the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD in front of the tabernacle of the LORD—that person shall be considered guilty of bloodshed; they have shed blood and must be cut off from their people.
chapters.zh: 若未曾牵到会幕门口，耶和华的帐幕前献给耶和华为供物，流血的罪必归到那人身上。他流了血，要从民中剪除。

chapters.en: This is so the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they are now making in the open fields. They must bring them to the priest, that is, to the LORD, at the entrance to the tent of meeting and sacrifice them as fellowship offerings.
chapters.zh: 这是为要使以色列人把他们在田野里所献的祭带到会幕门口，耶和华面前，交给祭司，献与耶和华为平安祭。

chapters.en: The priest is to splash the blood against the altar of the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting and burn the fat as an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把血洒在会幕门口，耶和华的坛上，把脂油焚烧，献给耶和华为馨香的祭。

chapters.en: They must no longer offer any of their sacrifices to the goat idols to whom they prostitute themselves. This is to be a lasting ordinance for them and for the generations to come.’
chapters.zh: 他们不可再献祭给他们行邪淫所随从的鬼魔（原文作公山羊），这要作他们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: “Say to them: ‘Any Israelite or any foreigner residing among them who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice
chapters.zh: 你要晓谕他们说，凡以色列家中的人，或是寄居在他们中间的外人，献燔祭或是平安祭，

chapters.en: and does not bring it to the entrance to the tent of meeting to sacrifice it to the LORD must be cut off from the people of Israel.
chapters.zh: 若不带到会幕门口献给耶和华，那人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: “ ‘I will set my face against any Israelite or any foreigner residing among them who eats blood, and I will cut them off from the people.
chapters.zh: 凡以色列家中的人，或是寄居在他们中间的外人，若吃什么血，我必向那吃血的人变脸，把他从民中剪除。

chapters.en: For the life of a creature is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for yourselves on the altar; it is the blood that makes atonement for one’s life.
chapters.zh: 因为活物的生命是在血中。我把这血赐给你们，可以在坛上为你们的生命赎罪，因血里有生命，所以能赎罪。

chapters.en: Therefore I say to the Israelites, “None of you may eat blood, nor may any foreigner residing among you eat blood.”
chapters.zh: 因此，我对以色列人说，你们都不可吃血，寄居在你们中间的外人也不可吃血。

chapters.en: “ ‘Any Israelite or any foreigner residing among you who hunts any animal or bird that may be eaten must drain out the blood and cover it with earth,
chapters.zh: 凡以色列人，或是寄居在他们中间的外人，若打猎得了可吃的禽兽，必放出它的血来，用土掩盖。

chapters.en: because the life of every creature is its blood. That is why I have said to the Israelites, “You must not eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is its blood; anyone who eats it must be cut off.”
chapters.zh: 论到一切活物的生命，就在血中。所以我对以色列人说，无论什么活物的血，你们都不可吃，因为一切活物的血就是他的生命。凡吃了血的，必被剪除。

chapters.en: “ ‘Anyone, whether native-born or foreigner, who eats anything found dead or torn by wild animals must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be ceremonially unclean till evening; then they will be clean.
chapters.zh: 凡吃自死的，或是被野兽撕裂的，无论是本地人，是寄居的，必不洁净到晚上，都要洗衣服，用水洗身，到了晚上才为洁净。

chapters.en: But if they do not wash their clothes and bathe themselves, they will be held responsible.’ ”
chapters.zh: 但他若不洗衣服，也不洗身，就必担当他的罪孽。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: You must not do as they do in Egypt, where you used to live, and you must not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not follow their practices.
chapters.zh: 你们从前住的埃及地，那里人的行为，你们不可效法，我要领你们到的迦南地，那里人的行为也不可效法，也不可照他们的恶俗行。

chapters.en: You must obey my laws and be careful to follow my decrees. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们要遵我的典章，守我的律例，按此而行。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: Keep my decrees and laws, for the person who obeys them will live by them. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要守我的律例典章，人若遵行，就必因此活着。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘No one is to approach any close relative to have sexual relations. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你们都不可露骨肉之亲的下体，亲近他们。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not dishonor your father by having sexual relations with your mother. She is your mother; do not have relations with her.
chapters.zh: 不可露你母亲的下体，羞辱了你父亲。她是你的母亲，不可露她的下体。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with your father’s wife; that would dishonor your father.
chapters.zh: 不可露你继母的下体，这本是你父亲的下体。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with your sister, either your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether she was born in the same home or elsewhere.
chapters.zh: 你的姐妹，不拘是异母同父的，是异父同母的，无论是生在家生在外的，都不可露她们的下体。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter; that would dishonor you.
chapters.zh: 不可露你孙女或是外孙女的下体，露了她们的下体就是露了自己的下体。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with the daughter of your father’s wife, born to your father; she is your sister.
chapters.zh: 你继母从你父亲生的女儿本是你的妹妹，不可露她的下体。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.
chapters.zh: 不可露你姑母的下体，她是你父亲的骨肉之亲。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with your mother’s sister, because she is your mother’s close relative.
chapters.zh: 不可露你姨母的下体，她是你母亲的骨肉之亲。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not dishonor your father’s brother by approaching his wife to have sexual relations; she is your aunt.
chapters.zh: 不可亲近你伯叔之妻，羞辱了你伯叔，她是你的伯叔母。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law. She is your son’s wife; do not have relations with her.
chapters.zh: 不可露你儿妇的下体，她是你儿子的妻，不可露她的下体。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with your brother’s wife; that would dishonor your brother.
chapters.zh: 不可露你弟兄妻子的下体，这本是你弟兄的下体。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with both a woman and her daughter. Do not have sexual relations with either her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter; they are her close relatives. That is wickedness.
chapters.zh: 不可露了妇人的下体，又露她女儿的下体，也不可娶她孙女或是外孙女，露她们的下体，她们是骨肉之亲，这本是大恶。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not take your wife’s sister as a rival wife and have sexual relations with her while your wife is living.
chapters.zh: 你妻还在的时候，不可另娶她的姐妹作对头，露她的下体。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not approach a woman to have sexual relations during the uncleanness of her monthly period.
chapters.zh: 女人行经不洁净的时候，不可露她的下体，与她亲近。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with your neighbor’s wife and defile yourself with her.
chapters.zh: 不可与邻舍的妻行淫，玷污自己。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not give any of your children to be sacrificed to Molek, for you must not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可使你的儿女经火归与摩洛，也不可亵渎你神的名。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with a man as one does with a woman; that is detestable.
chapters.zh: 不可与男人苟合，像与女人一样，这本是可憎恶的。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with an animal and defile yourself with it. A woman must not present herself to an animal to have sexual relations with it; that is a perversion.
chapters.zh: 不可与兽淫合，玷污自己。女人也不可站在兽前，与它淫合，这本是逆性的事。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not defile yourselves in any of these ways, because this is how the nations that I am going to drive out before you became defiled.
chapters.zh: 在这一切的事上，你们都不可玷污自己，因为我在你们面前所逐出的列邦，在这一切的事上玷污了自己。

chapters.en: Even the land was defiled; so I punished it for its sin, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
chapters.zh: 连地也玷污了，所以我追讨那地的罪孽，那地也吐出它的居民。

chapters.en: But you must keep my decrees and my laws. The native-born and the foreigners residing among you must not do any of these detestable things,
chapters.zh: 故此，你们要守我的律例典章。这一切可憎恶的事，无论是本地人，是寄居在你们中间的外人，都不可行，

chapters.en: for all these things were done by the people who lived in the land before you, and the land became defiled.
chapters.zh: （在你们以先居住那地的人行了这一切可憎恶的事，地就玷污了，）

chapters.en: And if you defile the land, it will vomit you out as it vomited out the nations that were before you.
chapters.zh: 免得你们玷污那地的时候，地就把你们吐出，像吐出在你们以先的国民一样。

chapters.en: “ ‘Everyone who does any of these detestable things—such persons must be cut off from their people.
chapters.zh: 无论什么人，行了其中可憎的一件事，必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: Keep my requirements and do not follow any of the detestable customs that were practiced before you came and do not defile yourselves with them. I am the LORD your God.’ ”
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要守我所吩咐的，免得你们随从那些可憎的恶俗，就是在你们以先的人所常行的，以致玷污了自己。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the entire assembly of Israel and say to them: ‘Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列全会众说，你们要圣洁，因为我耶和华你们的神是圣洁的。

chapters.en: “ ‘Each of you must respect your mother and father, and you must observe my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们各人都当孝敬父母，也要守我的安息日。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not turn to idols or make metal gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们不可偏向虚无的神，也不可为自己铸造神像。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘When you sacrifice a fellowship offering to the LORD, sacrifice it in such a way that it will be accepted on your behalf.
chapters.zh: 你们献平安祭给耶和华的时候，要献得可蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it or on the next day; anything left over until the third day must be burned up.
chapters.zh: 这祭物要在献的那一天和第二天吃，若有剩到第三天的，就必用火焚烧。

chapters.en: If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is impure and will not be accepted.
chapters.zh: 第三天若再吃，这就为可憎恶的，必不蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: Whoever eats it will be held responsible because they have desecrated what is holy to the LORD; they must be cut off from their people.
chapters.zh: 凡吃的人必担当他的罪孽，因为他亵渎了耶和华的圣物，那人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: “ ‘When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.
chapters.zh: 在你们的地收割庄稼，不可割尽田角，也不可拾取所遗落的。

chapters.en: Do not go over your vineyard a second time or pick up the grapes that have fallen. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 不可摘尽葡萄园的果子，也不可拾取葡萄园所掉的果子，要留给穷人和寄居的。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not steal. “ ‘Do not lie. “ ‘Do not deceive one another.
chapters.zh: 你们不可偷盗，不可欺骗，也不可彼此说谎。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可指着我的名起假誓，亵渎你神的名。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not defraud or rob your neighbor. “ ‘Do not hold back the wages of a hired worker overnight.
chapters.zh: 不可欺压你的邻舍，也不可抢夺他的物。雇工人的工价，不可在你那里过夜，留到早晨。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block in front of the blind, but fear your God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可咒骂聋子，也不可将绊脚石放在瞎子面前，只要敬畏你的神。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not pervert justice; do not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the great, but judge your neighbor fairly.
chapters.zh: 你们施行审判，不可行不义，不可偏护穷人，也不可重看有势力的人，只要按着公义审判你的邻舍。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not go about spreading slander among your people. “ ‘Do not do anything that endangers your neighbor’s life. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可在民中往来搬弄是非，也不可与邻舍为敌，置之于死（原文作流他的血）。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not hate a fellow Israelite in your heart. Rebuke your neighbor frankly so you will not share in their guilt.
chapters.zh: 不可心里恨你的弟兄，总要指摘你的邻舍，免得因他担罪。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against anyone among your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可报仇，也不可埋怨你本国的子民，却要爱人如己。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Keep my decrees. “ ‘Do not mate different kinds of animals. “ ‘Do not plant your field with two kinds of seed. “ ‘Do not wear clothing woven of two kinds of material.
chapters.zh: 你们要守我的律例。不可叫你的牲畜与异类配合，不可用两样搀杂的种种你的地，也不可用两样搀杂的料作衣服穿在身上。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man sleeps with a female slave who is promised to another man but who has not been ransomed or given her freedom, there must be due punishment. Yet they are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed.
chapters.zh: 婢女许配了丈夫，还没有被赎得释放，人若与她行淫，二人要受刑罚，却不把他们治死，因为婢女还没有得自由。

chapters.en: The man, however, must bring a ram to the entrance to the tent of meeting for a guilt offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 那人要把赎愆祭，就是一只公绵羊牵到会幕门口，耶和华面前。

chapters.en: With the ram of the guilt offering the priest is to make atonement for him before the LORD for the sin he has committed, and his sin will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 祭司要用赎愆祭的羊在耶和华面前赎他所犯的罪，他的罪就必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: “ ‘When you enter the land and plant any kind of fruit tree, regard its fruit as forbidden. For three years you are to consider it forbidden ; it must not be eaten.
chapters.zh: 你们到了迦南地，栽种各样结果子的树木，就要以所结的果子如未受割礼的一样。三年之久，你们要以这些果子，如未受割礼的，是不可吃的。

chapters.en: In the fourth year all its fruit will be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 但第四年所结的果子全要成为圣，用以赞美耶和华。

chapters.en: But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit. In this way your harvest will be increased. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 第五年，你们要吃那树上的果子，好叫树给你们结果子更多。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not eat any meat with the blood still in it. “ ‘Do not practice divination or seek omens.
chapters.zh: 你们不可吃带血的物，不可用法术，也不可观兆。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not cut the hair at the sides of your head or clip off the edges of your beard.
chapters.zh: 头的周围不可剃（周围或作两鬓），胡须的周围也不可损坏。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not cut your bodies for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可为死人用刀划身，也不可在身上刺花纹。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not degrade your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with wickedness.
chapters.zh: 不可辱没你的女儿，使她为娼妓，恐怕地上的人专向淫乱，地就满了大恶。

chapters.en: “ ‘Observe my Sabbaths and have reverence for my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你们要守我的安息日，敬我的圣所。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not turn to mediums or seek out spiritists, for you will be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 不可偏向那些交鬼的和行巫术的，不可求问他们，以致被他们玷污了。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Stand up in the presence of the aged, show respect for the elderly and revere your God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 在白发的人面前，你要站起来，也要尊敬老人，又要敬畏你的神。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them.
chapters.zh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。

chapters.en: The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not use dishonest standards when measuring length, weight or quantity.
chapters.zh: 你们施行审判，不可行不义，在尺，秤，升，斗上也是如此。

chapters.en: Use honest scales and honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 要用公道天平，公道法码，公道升斗，公道秤。我是耶和华你们的神，曾把你们从埃及地领出来的。

chapters.en: “ ‘Keep all my decrees and all my laws and follow them. I am the LORD.’ ”
chapters.zh: 你们要谨守遵行我一切的律例典章。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘Any Israelite or any foreigner residing in Israel who sacrifices any of his children to Molek is to be put to death. The members of the community are to stone him.
chapters.zh: 你还要晓谕以色列人说，凡以色列人，或是在以色列中寄居的外人，把自己的儿女献给摩洛的，总要治死他，本地人要用石头把他打死。

chapters.en: I myself will set my face against him and will cut him off from his people; for by sacrificing his children to Molek, he has defiled my sanctuary and profaned my holy name.
chapters.zh: 我也要向那人变脸，把他从民中剪除，因为他把儿女献给摩洛，玷污我的圣所，亵渎我的圣名。

chapters.en: If the members of the community close their eyes when that man sacrifices one of his children to Molek and if they fail to put him to death,
chapters.zh: 那人把儿女献给摩洛，本地人若佯为不见，不把他治死，

chapters.en: I myself will set my face against him and his family and will cut them off from their people together with all who follow him in prostituting themselves to Molek.
chapters.zh: 我就要向这人和他的家变脸，把他和一切随他与摩洛行邪淫的人都从民中剪除。

chapters.en: “ ‘I will set my face against anyone who turns to mediums and spiritists to prostitute themselves by following them, and I will cut them off from their people.
chapters.zh: 人偏向交鬼的和行巫术的，随他们行邪淫，我要向那人变脸，把他从民中剪除。

chapters.en: “ ‘Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 所以你们要自洁成圣，因为我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: Keep my decrees and follow them. I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
chapters.zh: 你们要谨守遵行我的律例，我是叫你们成圣的耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘Anyone who curses their father or mother is to be put to death. Because they have cursed their father or mother, their blood will be on their own head.
chapters.zh: 凡咒骂父母的，总要治死他，他咒骂了父母，他的罪要归到他身上（罪原文作血。本章同。）。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man commits adultery with another man’s wife—with the wife of his neighbor—both the adulterer and the adulteress are to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 与邻舍之妻行淫的，奸夫淫妇都必治死。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man has sexual relations with his father’s wife, he has dishonored his father. Both the man and the woman are to be put to death; their blood will be on their own heads.
chapters.zh: 与继母行淫的，就是羞辱了他父亲，总要把他们二人治死，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man has sexual relations with his daughter-in-law, both of them are to be put to death. What they have done is a perversion; their blood will be on their own heads.
chapters.zh: 与儿妇同房的，总要把他们二人治死，他们行了逆伦的事，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man has sexual relations with a man as one does with a woman, both of them have done what is detestable. They are to be put to death; their blood will be on their own heads.
chapters.zh: 人若与男人苟合，像与女人一样，他们二人行了可憎的事，总要把他们治死，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man marries both a woman and her mother, it is wicked. Both he and they must be burned in the fire, so that no wickedness will be among you.
chapters.zh: 人若娶妻，并娶其母，便是大恶，要把这三人用火焚烧，使你们中间免去大恶。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he is to be put to death, and you must kill the animal.
chapters.zh: 人若与兽淫合，总要治死他，也要杀那兽。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a woman approaches an animal to have sexual relations with it, kill both the woman and the animal. They are to be put to death; their blood will be on their own heads.
chapters.zh: 女人若与兽亲近，与它淫合，你要杀那女人和那兽，总要把他们治死，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man marries his sister, the daughter of either his father or his mother, and they have sexual relations, it is a disgrace. They are to be publicly removed from their people. He has dishonored his sister and will be held responsible.
chapters.zh: 人若娶他的姐妹，无论是异母同父的，是异父同母的，彼此见了下体，这是可耻的事，他们必在本民的眼前被剪除。他露了姐妹的下体，必担当自己的罪孽。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man has sexual relations with a woman during her monthly period, he has exposed the source of her flow, and she has also uncovered it. Both of them are to be cut off from their people.
chapters.zh: 妇人有月经，若与她同房，露了她的下体，就是露了妇人的血源，妇人也露了自己的血源，二人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not have sexual relations with the sister of either your mother or your father, for that would dishonor a close relative; both of you would be held responsible.
chapters.zh: 不可露姨母或是姑母的下体，这是露了骨肉之亲的下体，二人必担当自己的罪孽。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man has sexual relations with his aunt, he has dishonored his uncle. They will be held responsible; they will die childless.
chapters.zh: 人若与伯叔之妻同房，就羞辱了他的伯叔，二人要担当自己的罪，必无子女而死。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a man marries his brother’s wife, it is an act of impurity; he has dishonored his brother. They will be childless.
chapters.zh: 人若娶弟兄之妻，这本是污秽的事，羞辱了他的弟兄，二人必无子女。

chapters.en: “ ‘Keep all my decrees and laws and follow them, so that the land where I am bringing you to live may not vomit you out.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要谨守遵行我一切的律例典章，免得我领你们去住的那地把你们吐出。

chapters.en: You must not live according to the customs of the nations I am going to drive out before you. Because they did all these things, I abhorred them.
chapters.zh: 我在你们面前所逐出的国民，你们不可随从他们的风俗，因为他们行了这一切的事，所以我厌恶他们。

chapters.en: But I said to you, “You will possess their land; I will give it to you as an inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey.” I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the nations.
chapters.zh: 但我对你们说过，你们要承受他们的地，就是我要赐给你们为业，流奶与蜜之地。我是耶和华你们的神，使你们与万民有分别的。

chapters.en: “ ‘You must therefore make a distinction between clean and unclean animals and between unclean and clean birds. Do not defile yourselves by any animal or bird or anything that moves along the ground—those that I have set apart as unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要把洁净和不洁净的禽兽分别出来，不可因我给你们分为不洁净的禽兽，或是滋生在地上的活物，使自己成为可憎恶的。

chapters.en: You are to be holy to me because I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the nations to be my own.
chapters.zh: 你们要归我为圣，因为我耶和华是圣的，并叫你们与万民有分别，使你们作我的民。

chapters.en: “ ‘A man or woman who is a medium or spiritist among you must be put to death. You are to stone them; their blood will be on their own heads.’ ”
chapters.zh: 无论男女，是交鬼的或行巫术的，总要治死他们。人必用石头把他们打死，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: ‘A priest must not make himself ceremonially unclean for any of his people who die,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你告诉亚伦子孙作祭司的说，祭司不可为民中的死人沾染自己，

chapters.en: except for a close relative, such as his mother or father, his son or daughter, his brother,
chapters.zh: 除非为他骨肉之亲的父母，儿女，弟兄，

chapters.en: or an unmarried sister who is dependent on him since she has no husband—for her he may make himself unclean.
chapters.zh: 和未曾出嫁，作处女的姐妹，才可以沾染自己。

chapters.en: He must not make himself unclean for people related to him by marriage, and so defile himself.
chapters.zh: 祭司既在民中为首，就不可从俗沾染自己。

chapters.en: “ ‘Priests must not shave their heads or shave off the edges of their beards or cut their bodies.
chapters.zh: 不可使头光秃，不可剃除胡须的周围，也不可用刀划身。

chapters.en: They must be holy to their God and must not profane the name of their God. Because they present the food offerings to the LORD, the food of their God, they are to be holy.
chapters.zh: 要归神为圣，不可亵渎神的名，因为耶和华的火祭，就是神的食物，是他们献的，所以他们要成为圣。

chapters.en: “ ‘They must not marry women defiled by prostitution or divorced from their husbands, because priests are holy to their God.
chapters.zh: 不可娶妓女或被污的女人为妻，也不可娶被休的妇人为妻，因为祭司是归神为圣。

chapters.en: Regard them as holy, because they offer up the food of your God. Consider them holy, because I the LORD am holy—I who make you holy.
chapters.zh: 所以你要使他成圣，因为他奉献你神的食物，你要以他为圣，因为我使你们成圣的耶和华是圣的。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a priest’s daughter defiles herself by becoming a prostitute, she disgraces her father; she must be burned in the fire.
chapters.zh: 祭司的女儿若行淫辱没自己，就辱没了父亲，必用火将她焚烧。

chapters.en: “ ‘The high priest, the one among his brothers who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and who has been ordained to wear the priestly garments, must not let his hair become unkempt or tear his clothes.
chapters.zh: 在弟兄中作大祭司，头上倒了膏油，又承接圣职，穿了圣衣的，不可蓬头散发，也不可撕裂衣服。

chapters.en: He must not enter a place where there is a dead body. He must not make himself unclean, even for his father or mother,
chapters.zh: 不可挨近死尸，也不可为父母沾染自己。

chapters.en: nor leave the sanctuary of his God or desecrate it, because he has been dedicated by the anointing oil of his God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可出圣所，也不可亵渎神的圣所，因为神膏油的冠冕在他头上。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘The woman he marries must be a virgin.
chapters.zh: 他要娶处女为妻。

chapters.en: He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman defiled by prostitution, but only a virgin from his own people,
chapters.zh: 寡妇或是被休的妇人，或是被污为妓的女人，都不可娶，只可娶本民中的处女为妻。

chapters.en: so that he will not defile his offspring among his people. I am the LORD, who makes him holy.’ ”
chapters.zh: 不可在民中辱没他的儿女，因为我是叫他成圣的耶和华。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to Aaron: ‘For the generations to come none of your descendants who has a defect may come near to offer the food of his God.
chapters.zh: 你告诉亚伦说，你世世代代的后裔，凡有残疾的，都不可近前来献他神的食物。

chapters.en: No man who has any defect may come near: no man who is blind or lame, disfigured or deformed;
chapters.zh: 因为凡有残疾的，无论是瞎眼的，瘸腿的，塌鼻子的，肢体有余的，

chapters.en: no man with a crippled foot or hand,
chapters.zh: 折脚折手的，

chapters.en: or who is a hunchback or a dwarf, or who has any eye defect, or who has festering or running sores or damaged testicles.
chapters.zh: 驼背的，矮矬的，眼睛有毛病的，长癣的，长疥的，或是损坏肾子的，都不可近前来。

chapters.en: No descendant of Aaron the priest who has any defect is to come near to present the food offerings to the LORD. He has a defect; he must not come near to offer the food of his God.
chapters.zh: 祭司亚伦的后裔，凡有残疾的，都不可近前来，将火祭献给耶和华。他有残疾，不可近前来献神的食物。

chapters.en: He may eat the most holy food of his God, as well as the holy food;
chapters.zh: 神的食物，无论是圣的，至圣的，他都可以吃。

chapters.en: yet because of his defect, he must not go near the curtain or approach the altar, and so desecrate my sanctuary. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.’ ”
chapters.zh: 但不可进到幔子前，也不可就近坛前，因为他有残疾，免得亵渎我的圣所。我是叫他成圣的耶和华。

chapters.en: So Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西晓谕亚伦和亚伦的子孙，并以色列众人。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect the sacred offerings the Israelites consecrate to me, so they will not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你吩咐亚伦和他子孙说，要远离以色列人所分别为圣，归给我的圣物，免得亵渎我的圣名。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “Say to them: ‘For the generations to come, if any of your descendants is ceremonially unclean and yet comes near the sacred offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD, that person must be cut off from my presence. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你要对他们说，你们世世代代的后裔，凡身上有污秽，亲近以色列人所分别为圣，归耶和华圣物的，那人必在我面前剪除。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a descendant of Aaron has a defiling skin disease or a bodily discharge, he may not eat the sacred offerings until he is cleansed. He will also be unclean if he touches something defiled by a corpse or by anyone who has an emission of semen,
chapters.zh: 亚伦的后裔，凡长大麻疯的，或是有漏症的，不可吃圣物，直等他洁净了。无论谁摸那因死尸不洁净的物（物或作人），或是遗精的人，

chapters.en: or if he touches any crawling thing that makes him unclean, or any person who makes him unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be.
chapters.zh: 或是摸什么使他不洁净的爬物，或是摸那使他不洁净的人（不拘那人有什么不洁净），

chapters.en: The one who touches any such thing will be unclean till evening. He must not eat any of the sacred offerings unless he has bathed himself with water.
chapters.zh: 摸了这些人，物的，必不洁净到晚上，若不用水洗身，就不可吃圣物。

chapters.en: When the sun goes down, he will be clean, and after that he may eat the sacred offerings, for they are his food.
chapters.zh: 日落的时候，他就洁净了，然后可以吃圣物，因为这是他的食物。

chapters.en: He must not eat anything found dead or torn by wild animals, and so become unclean through it. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 自死的或是被野兽撕裂的，他不可吃，因此污秽自己。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘The priests are to perform my service in such a way that they do not become guilty and die for treating it with contempt. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
chapters.zh: 所以他们要守我所吩咐的，免得轻忽了，因此担罪而死。我是叫他们成圣的耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘No one outside a priest’s family may eat the sacred offering, nor may the guest of a priest or his hired worker eat it.
chapters.zh: 凡外人不可吃圣物，寄居在祭司家的，或是雇工人，都不可吃圣物。

chapters.en: But if a priest buys a slave with money, or if slaves are born in his household, they may eat his food.
chapters.zh: 倘若祭司买人，是他的钱买的，那人就可以吃圣物，生在他家的人也可以吃。

chapters.en: If a priest’s daughter marries anyone other than a priest, she may not eat any of the sacred contributions.
chapters.zh: 祭司的女儿若嫁外人，就不可吃举祭的圣物。

chapters.en: But if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, yet has no children, and she returns to live in her father’s household as in her youth, she may eat her father’s food. No unauthorized person, however, may eat it.
chapters.zh: 但祭司的女儿若是寡妇，或是被休的，没有孩子，又归回父家，与她青年一样，就可以吃她父亲的食物，只是外人不可吃。

chapters.en: “ ‘Anyone who eats a sacred offering by mistake must make restitution to the priest for the offering and add a fifth of the value to it.
chapters.zh: 若有人误吃了圣物，要照圣物的原数加上五分之一交给祭司。

chapters.en: The priests must not desecrate the sacred offerings the Israelites present to the LORD
chapters.zh: 祭司不可亵渎以色列人所献给耶和华的圣物，

chapters.en: by allowing them to eat the sacred offerings and so bring upon them guilt requiring payment. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.’ ”
chapters.zh: 免得他们在吃圣物上自取罪孽，因为我是叫他们成圣的耶和华。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them: ‘If any of you—whether an Israelite or a foreigner residing in Israel—presents a gift for a burnt offering to the LORD, either to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering,
chapters.zh: 你晓谕亚伦和他子孙，并以色列众人说，以色列家中的人，或在以色列中寄居的，凡献供物，无论是所许的愿，是甘心献的，就是献给耶和华作燔祭的，

chapters.en: you must present a male without defect from the cattle, sheep or goats in order that it may be accepted on your behalf.
chapters.zh: 要将没有残疾的公牛，或是绵羊，或是山羊献上，如此方蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: Do not bring anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.
chapters.zh: 凡有残疾的，你们不可献上，因为这不蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: When anyone brings from the herd or flock a fellowship offering to the LORD to fulfill a special vow or as a freewill offering, it must be without defect or blemish to be acceptable.
chapters.zh: 凡从牛群或是羊群中，将平安祭献给耶和华，为要还特许的愿，或是作甘心献的，所献的必纯全无残疾的才蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: Do not offer to the LORD the blind, the injured or the maimed, or anything with warts or festering or running sores. Do not place any of these on the altar as a food offering presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 瞎眼的，折伤的，残废的，有瘤子的，长癣的，长疥的都不可献给耶和华，也不可在坛上作为火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: You may, however, present as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep that is deformed or stunted, but it will not be accepted in fulfillment of a vow.
chapters.zh: 无论是公牛是绵羊羔，若肢体有余的，或是缺少的，只可作甘心祭献上，用以还愿，却不蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: You must not offer to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn or cut. You must not do this in your own land,
chapters.zh: 肾子损伤的，或是压碎的，或是破裂的，或是骟了的，不可献给耶和华，在你们的地上也不可这样行。

chapters.en: and you must not accept such animals from the hand of a foreigner and offer them as the food of your God. They will not be accepted on your behalf, because they are deformed and have defects.’ ”
chapters.zh: 这类的物，你们从外人的手，一样也不可接受作你们神的食物献上，因为这些都有损坏，有残疾，不蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “When a calf, a lamb or a goat is born, it is to remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be acceptable as a food offering presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 才生的公牛，或是绵羊或是山羊，七天当跟着母，从第八天以后，可以当供物蒙悦纳，作为耶和华的火祭。

chapters.en: Do not slaughter a cow or a sheep and its young on the same day.
chapters.zh: 无论是母牛是母羊，不可同日宰母和子。

chapters.en: “When you sacrifice a thank offering to the LORD, sacrifice it in such a way that it will be accepted on your behalf.
chapters.zh: 你们献感谢祭给耶和华，要献得可蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: It must be eaten that same day; leave none of it till morning. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要当天吃，一点不可留到早晨。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “Keep my commands and follow them. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你们要谨守遵行我的诫命。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: Do not profane my holy name, for I must be acknowledged as holy by the Israelites. I am the LORD, who made you holy
chapters.zh: 你们不可亵渎我的圣名，我在以色列人中，却要被尊为圣。我是叫你们成圣的耶和华，

chapters.en: and who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 把你们从埃及地领出来，作你们的神。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘These are my appointed festivals, the appointed festivals of the LORD, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，耶和华的节期，你们要宣告为圣会的节期。

chapters.en: “ ‘There are six days when you may work, but the seventh day is a day of sabbath rest, a day of sacred assembly. You are not to do any work; wherever you live, it is a sabbath to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 六日要作工，第七日是圣安息日，当有圣会，你们什么工都不可作。这是在你们一切的住处向耶和华守的安息日。

chapters.en: “ ‘These are the LORD’s appointed festivals, the sacred assemblies you are to proclaim at their appointed times:
chapters.zh: 耶和华的节期，就是你们到了日期要宣告为圣会的，乃是这些。

chapters.en: The LORD’s Passover begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.
chapters.zh: 正月十四日，黄昏的时候，是耶和华的逾越节。

chapters.en: On the fifteenth day of that month the LORD’s Festival of Unleavened Bread begins; for seven days you must eat bread made without yeast.
chapters.zh: 这月十五日是向耶和华守的无酵节，你们要吃无酵饼七日。

chapters.en: On the first day hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work.
chapters.zh: 第一日当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作。

chapters.en: For seven days present a food offering to the LORD. And on the seventh day hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work.’ ”
chapters.zh: 要将火祭献给耶和华七日。第七日是圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘When you enter the land I am going to give you and you reap its harvest, bring to the priest a sheaf of the first grain you harvest.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，你们到了我赐给你们的地，收割庄稼的时候，要将初熟的庄稼一捆带给祭司。

chapters.en: He is to wave the sheaf before the LORD so it will be accepted on your behalf; the priest is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
chapters.zh: 他要把这一捆在耶和华面前摇一摇，使你们得蒙悦纳。祭司要在安息日的次日把这捆摇一摇。

chapters.en: On the day you wave the sheaf, you must sacrifice as a burnt offering to the LORD a lamb a year old without defect,
chapters.zh: 摇这捆的日子，你们要把一岁没有残疾的公绵羊羔献给耶和华为燔祭。

chapters.en: together with its grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil—a food offering presented to the LORD, a pleasing aroma—and its drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.
chapters.zh: 同献的素祭，就是调油的细面伊法十分之二，作为馨香的火祭，献给耶和华。同献的奠祭，要酒一欣四分之一。

chapters.en: You must not eat any bread, or roasted or new grain, until the very day you bring this offering to your God. This is to be a lasting ordinance for the generations to come, wherever you live.
chapters.zh: 无论是饼，是烘的子粒，是新穗子，你们都不可吃，直等到把你们献给神的供物带来的那一天才可以吃。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: “ ‘From the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, count off seven full weeks.
chapters.zh: 你们要从安息日的次日，献禾捆为摇祭的那日算起，要满了七个安息日。

chapters.en: Count off fifty days up to the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then present an offering of new grain to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 到第七个安息日的次日，共计五十天，又要将新素祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: From wherever you live, bring two loaves made of two-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour, baked with yeast, as a wave offering of firstfruits to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要从你们的住处取出细面伊法十分之二，加酵，烤成两个摇祭的饼，当作初熟之物献给耶和华。

chapters.en: Present with this bread seven male lambs, each a year old and without defect, one young bull and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings—a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 又要将一岁，没有残疾的羊羔七只，公牛犊一只，公绵羊两只，和饼一同奉上。这些与同献的素祭和奠祭要作为燔祭献给耶和华，就是作馨香的火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: Then sacrifice one male goat for a sin offering and two lambs, each a year old, for a fellowship offering.
chapters.zh: 你们要献一只公山羊为赎罪祭，两只一岁的公绵羊羔为平安祭。

chapters.en: The priest is to wave the two lambs before the LORD as a wave offering, together with the bread of the firstfruits. They are a sacred offering to the LORD for the priest.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把这些和初熟麦子作的饼一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，这是献与耶和华为圣物归给祭司的。

chapters.en: On that same day you are to proclaim a sacred assembly and do no regular work. This is to be a lasting ordinance for the generations to come, wherever you live.
chapters.zh: 当这日，你们要宣告圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: “ ‘When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and for the foreigner residing among you. I am the LORD your God.’ ”
chapters.zh: 在你们的地收割庄稼，不可割尽田角，也不可拾取所遗落的，要留给穷人和寄居的。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘On the first day of the seventh month you are to have a day of sabbath rest, a sacred assembly commemorated with trumpet blasts.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，七月初一，你们要守为圣安息日，要吹角作纪念，当有圣会。

chapters.en: Do no regular work, but present a food offering to the LORD.’ ”
chapters.zh: 什么劳碌的工都不可作，要将火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. Hold a sacred assembly and deny yourselves, and present a food offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 七月初十是赎罪日，你们要守为圣会，并要刻苦己心，也要将火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: Do not do any work on that day, because it is the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for you before the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 当这日，什么工都不可作，因为是赎罪日，要在耶和华你们的神面前赎罪。

chapters.en: Those who do not deny themselves on that day must be cut off from their people.
chapters.zh: 当这日，凡不刻苦己心的，必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: I will destroy from among their people anyone who does any work on that day.
chapters.zh: 凡这日作什么工的，我必将他从民中除灭。

chapters.en: You shall do no work at all. This is to be a lasting ordinance for the generations to come, wherever you live.
chapters.zh: 你们什么工都不可作。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: It is a day of sabbath rest for you, and you must deny yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening you are to observe your sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 你们要守这日为圣安息日，并要刻苦己心。从这月初九日晚上到次日晚上，要守为安息日。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month the LORD’s Festival of Tabernacles begins, and it lasts for seven days.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，这七月十五日是住棚节，要在耶和华面前守这节七日。

chapters.en: The first day is a sacred assembly; do no regular work.
chapters.zh: 第一日当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可作。

chapters.en: For seven days present food offerings to the LORD, and on the eighth day hold a sacred assembly and present a food offering to the LORD. It is the closing special assembly; do no regular work.
chapters.zh: 七日内要将火祭献给耶和华。第八日当守圣会，要将火祭献给耶和华。这是严肃会，什么劳碌的工都不可作。

chapters.en: (“ ‘These are the LORD’s appointed festivals, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies for bringing food offerings to the LORD—the burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings required for each day.
chapters.zh: 这是耶和华的节期，就是你们要宣告为圣会的节期，要将火祭，燔祭，素祭，祭物，并奠祭，各归各日，献给耶和华。

chapters.en: These offerings are in addition to those for the LORD’s Sabbaths and in addition to your gifts and whatever you have vowed and all the freewill offerings you give to the LORD.)
chapters.zh: 这是在耶和华的安息日以外，又在你们的供物和所许的愿，并甘心献给耶和华的以外。

chapters.en: “ ‘So beginning with the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you have gathered the crops of the land, celebrate the festival to the LORD for seven days; the first day is a day of sabbath rest, and the eighth day also is a day of sabbath rest.
chapters.zh: 你们收藏了地的出产，就从七月十五日起，要守耶和华的节七日。第一日为圣安息，第八日也为圣安息。

chapters.en: On the first day you are to take branches from luxuriant trees—from palms, willows and other leafy trees—and rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
chapters.zh: 第一日要拿美好树上的果子和棕树上的枝子，与茂密树的枝条并河旁的柳枝，在耶和华你们的神面前欢乐七日。

chapters.en: Celebrate this as a festival to the LORD for seven days each year. This is to be a lasting ordinance for the generations to come; celebrate it in the seventh month.
chapters.zh: 每年七月间，要向耶和华守这节七日。这为你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: Live in temporary shelters for seven days: All native-born Israelites are to live in such shelters
chapters.zh: 你们要住在棚里七日，凡以色列家的人都要住在棚里，

chapters.en: so your descendants will know that I had the Israelites live in temporary shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.’ ”
chapters.zh: 好叫你们世世代代知道，我领以色列人出埃及地的时候曾使他们住在棚里。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: So Moses announced to the Israelites the appointed festivals of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西将耶和华的节期传给以色列人。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil of pressed olives for the light so that the lamps may be kept burning continually.
chapters.zh: 要吩咐以色列人，把那为点灯捣成的清橄榄油拿来给你，使灯常常点着。

chapters.en: Outside the curtain that shields the ark of the covenant law in the tent of meeting, Aaron is to tend the lamps before the LORD from evening till morning, continually. This is to be a lasting ordinance for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 在会幕中法柜的幔子外，亚伦从晚上到早晨必在耶和华面前经理这灯。这要作你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: The lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD must be tended continually.
chapters.zh: 他要在耶和华面前常收拾精金灯台上的灯。
