chapters.en: “Take the finest flour and bake twelve loaves of bread, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf.
chapters.zh: 你要取细面，烤成十二个饼，每饼用面伊法十分之二。

chapters.en: Arrange them in two stacks, six in each stack, on the table of pure gold before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要把饼摆列两行（行或作摞下同），每行六个，在耶和华面前精金的桌子上。

chapters.en: By each stack put some pure incense as a memorial portion to represent the bread and to be a food offering presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 又要把净乳香放在每行饼上，作为纪念，就是作为火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: This bread is to be set out before the LORD regularly, Sabbath after Sabbath, on behalf of the Israelites, as a lasting covenant.
chapters.zh: 每安息日要常摆在耶和华面前，这为以色列人作永远的约。

chapters.en: It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in the sanctuary area, because it is a most holy part of their perpetual share of the food offerings presented to the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 这饼是要给亚伦和他子孙的，他们要在圣处吃，为永远的定例，因为在献给耶和华的火祭中是至圣的。

chapters.en: Now the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went out among the Israelites, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and an Israelite.
chapters.zh: 有一个以色列妇人的儿子，他父亲是埃及人，一日闲游在以色列人中。这以色列妇人的儿子和一个以色列人在营里争斗。

chapters.en: The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a curse; so they brought him to Moses. (His mother’s name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri the Danite.)
chapters.zh: 这以色列妇人的儿子亵渎了圣名，并且咒诅，就有人把他送到摩西那里。（他母亲名叫示罗密，是但支派底伯利的女儿）。

chapters.en: They put him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them.
chapters.zh: 他们把那人收在监里，要得耶和华所指示的话。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Take the blasphemer outside the camp. All those who heard him are to lay their hands on his head, and the entire assembly is to stone him.
chapters.zh: 把那咒诅圣名的人带到营外。叫听见的人都放手在他头上，全会众就要用石头打死他。

chapters.en: Say to the Israelites: ‘Anyone who curses their God will be held responsible;
chapters.zh: 你要晓谕以色列人说，凡咒诅神的，必担当他的罪。

chapters.en: anyone who blasphemes the name of the LORD is to be put to death. The entire assembly must stone them. Whether foreigner or native-born, when they blaspheme the Name they are to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 那亵渎耶和华名的，必被治死，全会众总要用石头打死他。不管是寄居的是本地人，他亵渎耶和华名的时候，必被治死。

chapters.en: “ ‘Anyone who takes the life of a human being is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 打死人的，必被治死。

chapters.en: Anyone who takes the life of someone’s animal must make restitution—life for life.
chapters.zh: 打死牲畜的，必赔上牲畜，以命偿命。

chapters.en: Anyone who injures their neighbor is to be injured in the same manner:
chapters.zh: 人若使他邻舍的身体有残疾，他怎样行，也要照样向他行，

chapters.en: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. The one who has inflicted the injury must suffer the same injury.
chapters.zh: 以伤还伤，以眼还眼，以牙还牙。他怎样叫人的身体有残疾，也要照样向他行。

chapters.en: Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a human being is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 打死牲畜的，必赔上牲畜，打死人的，必被治死。

chapters.en: You are to have the same law for the foreigner and the native-born. I am the LORD your God.’ ”
chapters.zh: 不管是寄居的是本地人，同归一例。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. The Israelites did as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西晓谕以色列人，他们就把那咒诅圣名的人带到营外，用石头打死。以色列人就照耶和华所吩咐摩西的行了。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses at Mount Sinai,
chapters.zh: 耶和华在西乃山对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘When you enter the land I am going to give you, the land itself must observe a sabbath to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，你们到了我所赐你们那地的时候，地就要向耶和华守安息。

chapters.en: For six years sow your fields, and for six years prune your vineyards and gather their crops.
chapters.zh: 六年要耕种田地，也要修理葡萄园，收藏地的出产。

chapters.en: But in the seventh year the land is to have a year of sabbath rest, a sabbath to the LORD. Do not sow your fields or prune your vineyards.
chapters.zh: 第七年，地要守圣安息，就是向耶和华守的安息，不可耕种田地，也不可修理葡萄园。

chapters.en: Do not reap what grows of itself or harvest the grapes of your untended vines. The land is to have a year of rest.
chapters.zh: 遗落自长的庄稼不可收割，没有修理的葡萄树也不可摘取葡萄。这年，地要守圣安息。

chapters.en: Whatever the land yields during the sabbath year will be food for you—for yourself, your male and female servants, and the hired worker and temporary resident who live among you,
chapters.zh: 地在安息年所出的，要给你和你的仆人，婢女，雇工人，并寄居的外人当食物。

chapters.en: as well as for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. Whatever the land produces may be eaten.
chapters.zh: 这年的土产也要给你的牲畜和你地上的走兽当食物。

chapters.en: “ ‘Count off seven sabbath years—seven times seven years—so that the seven sabbath years amount to a period of forty-nine years.
chapters.zh: 你要计算七个安息年，就是七七年。这便为你成了七个安息年，共是四十九年。

chapters.en: Then have the trumpet sounded everywhere on the tenth day of the seventh month; on the Day of Atonement sound the trumpet throughout your land.
chapters.zh: 当年七月初十日，你要大发角声，这日就是赎罪日，要在遍地发出角声。

chapters.en: Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan.
chapters.zh: 第五十年，你们要当作圣年，在遍地给一切的居民宣告自由。这年必为你们的禧年，各人要归自己的产业，各归本家。

chapters.en: The fiftieth year shall be a jubilee for you; do not sow and do not reap what grows of itself or harvest the untended vines.
chapters.zh: 第五十年要作为你们的禧年。这年不可耕种，地中自长的，不可收割，没有修理的葡萄树也不可摘取葡萄。

chapters.en: For it is a jubilee and is to be holy for you; eat only what is taken directly from the fields.
chapters.zh: 因为这是禧年，你们要当作圣年，吃地中自出的土产。

chapters.en: “ ‘In this Year of Jubilee everyone is to return to their own property.
chapters.zh: 这禧年，你们各人要归自己的地业。

chapters.en: “ ‘If you sell land to any of your own people or buy land from them, do not take advantage of each other.
chapters.zh: 你若卖什么给邻舍，或是从邻舍的手中买什么，彼此不可亏负。

chapters.en: You are to buy from your own people on the basis of the number of years since the Jubilee. And they are to sell to you on the basis of the number of years left for harvesting crops.
chapters.zh: 你要按禧年以后的年数向邻舍买，他也要按年数的收成卖给你。

chapters.en: When the years are many, you are to increase the price, and when the years are few, you are to decrease the price, because what is really being sold to you is the number of crops.
chapters.zh: 年岁若多，要照数加添价值，年岁若少，要照数减去价值，因为他照收成的数目卖给你。

chapters.en: Do not take advantage of each other, but fear your God. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们彼此不可亏负，只要敬畏你们的神，因为我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Follow my decrees and be careful to obey my laws, and you will live safely in the land.
chapters.zh: 我的律例，你们要遵行，我的典章，你们要谨守，就可以在那地上安然居住。

chapters.en: Then the land will yield its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live there in safety.
chapters.zh: 地必出土产，你们就要吃饱，在那地上安然居住。

chapters.en: You may ask, “What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not plant or harvest our crops?”
chapters.zh: 你们若说，这第七年我们不耕种，也不收藏土产，吃什么呢？

chapters.en: I will send you such a blessing in the sixth year that the land will yield enough for three years.
chapters.zh: 我必在第六年将我所命的福赐给你们，地便生三年的土产。

chapters.en: While you plant during the eighth year, you will eat from the old crop and will continue to eat from it until the harvest of the ninth year comes in.
chapters.zh: 第八年，你们要耕种，也要吃陈粮，等到第九年出产收来的时候，你们还吃陈粮。

chapters.en: “ ‘The land must not be sold permanently, because the land is mine and you reside in my land as foreigners and strangers.
chapters.zh: 地不可永卖，因为地是我的，你们在我面前是客旅，是寄居的。

chapters.en: Throughout the land that you hold as a possession, you must provide for the redemption of the land.
chapters.zh: 在你们所得为业的全地，也要准人将地赎回。

chapters.en: “ ‘If one of your fellow Israelites becomes poor and sells some of their property, their nearest relative is to come and redeem what they have sold.
chapters.zh: 你的弟兄（弟兄指本国人说下同）若渐渐穷乏，卖了几分地业，他至近的亲属就要来把弟兄所卖的赎回。

chapters.en: If, however, there is no one to redeem it for them but later on they prosper and acquire sufficient means to redeem it themselves,
chapters.zh: 若没有能给他赎回的，他自己渐渐富足，能够赎回，

chapters.en: they are to determine the value for the years since they sold it and refund the balance to the one to whom they sold it; they can then go back to their own property.
chapters.zh: 就要算出卖地的年数，把余剩年数的价值还那买主，自己便归回自己的地业。

chapters.en: But if they do not acquire the means to repay, what was sold will remain in the possession of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. It will be returned in the Jubilee, and they can then go back to their property.
chapters.zh: 倘若不能为自己得回所卖的，仍要存在买主的手里直到禧年，到了禧年，地业要出买主的手，自己便归回自己的地业。

chapters.en: “ ‘Anyone who sells a house in a walled city retains the right of redemption a full year after its sale. During that time the seller may redeem it.
chapters.zh: 人若卖城内的住宅，卖了以后，一年之内可以赎回，在一整年，必有赎回的权柄。

chapters.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled city shall belong permanently to the buyer and the buyer’s descendants. It is not to be returned in the Jubilee.
chapters.zh: 若在一整年之内不赎回，这城内的房屋就定准永归买主，世世代代为业，在禧年也不得出买主的手。

chapters.en: But houses in villages without walls around them are to be considered as belonging to the open country. They can be redeemed, and they are to be returned in the Jubilee.
chapters.zh: 但房屋在无城墙的村庄里，要看如乡下的田地一样，可以赎回，到了禧年，都要出买主的手。

chapters.en: “ ‘The Levites always have the right to redeem their houses in the Levitical towns, which they possess.
chapters.zh: 然而利未人所得为业的城邑，其中的房屋，利未人可以随时赎回。

chapters.en: So the property of the Levites is redeemable—that is, a house sold in any town they hold—and is to be returned in the Jubilee, because the houses in the towns of the Levites are their property among the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 若是一个利未人不将所卖的房屋赎回，是在所得为业的城内，到了禧年就要出买主的手，因为利未人城邑的房屋是他们在以色列人中的产业。

chapters.en: But the pastureland belonging to their towns must not be sold; it is their permanent possession.
chapters.zh: 只是他们各城郊野之地不可卖，因为是他们永远的产业。

chapters.en: “ ‘If any of your fellow Israelites become poor and are unable to support themselves among you, help them as you would a foreigner and stranger, so they can continue to live among you.
chapters.zh: 你的弟兄在你那里若渐渐贫穷，手中缺乏，你就要帮补他，使他与你同住，像外人和寄居的一样。

chapters.en: Do not take interest or any profit from them, but fear your God, so that they may continue to live among you.
chapters.zh: 不可向他取利，也不可向他多要，只要敬畏你的神，使你的弟兄与你同住。

chapters.en: You must not lend them money at interest or sell them food at a profit.
chapters.zh: 你借钱给他，不可向他取利，借粮给他，也不可向他多要。

chapters.en: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华你们的神，曾领你们从埃及地出来，为要把迦南地赐给你们，要作你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘If any of your fellow Israelites become poor and sell themselves to you, do not make them work as slaves.
chapters.zh: 你的弟兄若在你那里渐渐穷乏，将自己卖给你，不可叫他像奴仆服事你。

chapters.en: They are to be treated as hired workers or temporary residents among you; they are to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
chapters.zh: 他要在你那里像雇工人和寄居的一样，要服事你直到禧年。

chapters.en: Then they and their children are to be released, and they will go back to their own clans and to the property of their ancestors.
chapters.zh: 到了禧年，他和他儿女要离开你，一同出去归回本家，到他祖宗的地业那里去。

chapters.en: Because the Israelites are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt, they must not be sold as slaves.
chapters.zh: 因为他们是我的仆人，是我从埃及地领出来的，不可卖为奴仆。

chapters.en: Do not rule over them ruthlessly, but fear your God.
chapters.zh: 不可严严地辖管他，只要敬畏你的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Your male and female slaves are to come from the nations around you; from them you may buy slaves.
chapters.zh: 至于你的奴仆，婢女，可以从你四围的国中买。

chapters.en: You may also buy some of the temporary residents living among you and members of their clans born in your country, and they will become your property.
chapters.zh: 并且那寄居在你们中间的外人和他们的家属，在你们地上所生的，你们也可以从其中买人，他们要作你们的产业。

chapters.en: You can bequeath them to your children as inherited property and can make them slaves for life, but you must not rule over your fellow Israelites ruthlessly.
chapters.zh: 你们要将他们遗留给你们的子孙为产业，要永远从他们中间拣出奴仆，只是你们的弟兄以色列人，你们不可严严地辖管。

chapters.en: “ ‘If a foreigner residing among you becomes rich and any of your fellow Israelites become poor and sell themselves to the foreigner or to a member of the foreigner’s clan,
chapters.zh: 住在你那里的外人，或是寄居的，若渐渐富足，你的弟兄却渐渐穷乏，将自己卖给那外人，或是寄居的，或是外人的宗族，

chapters.en: they retain the right of redemption after they have sold themselves. One of their relatives may redeem them:
chapters.zh: 卖了以后，可以将他赎回。无论是他的弟兄，

chapters.en: An uncle or a cousin or any blood relative in their clan may redeem them. Or if they prosper, they may redeem themselves.
chapters.zh: 或伯叔，伯叔的儿子，本家的近支，都可以赎他。他自己若渐渐富足，也可以自赎。

chapters.en: They and their buyer are to count the time from the year they sold themselves up to the Year of Jubilee. The price for their release is to be based on the rate paid to a hired worker for that number of years.
chapters.zh: 他要和买主计算，从卖自己的那年起，算到禧年，所卖的价值照着年数多少，好像工人每年的工价。

chapters.en: If many years remain, they must pay for their redemption a larger share of the price paid for them.
chapters.zh: 若缺少的年数多，就要按着年数从买价中偿还他的赎价。

chapters.en: If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, they are to compute that and pay for their redemption accordingly.
chapters.zh: 若到禧年只缺少几年，就要按着年数和买主计算，偿还他的赎价。

chapters.en: They are to be treated as workers hired from year to year; you must see to it that those to whom they owe service do not rule over them ruthlessly.
chapters.zh: 他和买主同住，要像每年雇的工人，买主不可严严地辖管他。

chapters.en: “ ‘Even if someone is not redeemed in any of these ways, they and their children are to be released in the Year of Jubilee,
chapters.zh: 他若不这样被赎，到了禧年，要和他的儿女一同出去。

chapters.en: for the Israelites belong to me as servants. They are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 因为以色列人都是我的仆人，是我从埃及地领出来的。我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Do not make idols or set up an image or a sacred stone for yourselves, and do not place a carved stone in your land to bow down before it. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们不可作什么虚无的神像，不可立雕刻的偶像或是柱像，也不可在你们的地上安什么錾成的石像，向它跪拜，因为我是耶和华你们的神。

chapters.en: “ ‘Observe my Sabbaths and have reverence for my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你们要守我的安息日，敬我的圣所。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: “ ‘If you follow my decrees and are careful to obey my commands,
chapters.zh: 你们若遵行我的律例，谨守我的诫命，

chapters.en: I will send you rain in its season, and the ground will yield its crops and the trees their fruit.
chapters.zh: 我就给你们降下时雨，叫地生出土产，田野的树木结果子。

chapters.en: Your threshing will continue until grape harvest and the grape harvest will continue until planting, and you will eat all the food you want and live in safety in your land.
chapters.zh: 你们打粮食要打到摘葡萄的时候，摘葡萄要摘到撒种的时候，并且要吃得饱足，在你们的地上安然居住。

chapters.en: “ ‘I will grant peace in the land, and you will lie down and no one will make you afraid. I will remove wild beasts from the land, and the sword will not pass through your country.
chapters.zh: 我要赐平安在你们的地上，你们躺卧，无人惊吓。我要叫恶兽从你们的地上息灭，刀剑也必不经过你们的地。

chapters.en: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall by the sword before you.
chapters.zh: 你们要追赶仇敌，他们必倒在你们刀下。

chapters.en: Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand, and your enemies will fall by the sword before you.
chapters.zh: 你们五个人要追赶一百人，一百人要追赶一万人，仇敌必倒在你们刀下。

chapters.en: “ ‘I will look on you with favor and make you fruitful and increase your numbers, and I will keep my covenant with you.
chapters.zh: 我要眷顾你们，使你们生养众多，也要与你们坚定所立的约。

chapters.en: You will still be eating last year’s harvest when you will have to move it out to make room for the new.
chapters.zh: 你们要吃陈粮，又因新粮挪开陈粮。

chapters.en: I will put my dwelling place among you, and I will not abhor you.
chapters.zh: 我要在你们中间立我的帐幕，我的心也不厌恶你们。

chapters.en: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
chapters.zh: 我要在你们中间行走，我要作你们的神，你们要作我的子民。

chapters.en: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves to the Egyptians; I broke the bars of your yoke and enabled you to walk with heads held high.
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华你们的神，曾将你们从埃及地领出来，使你们不作埃及人的奴仆，我也折断你们所负的轭，叫你们挺身而走。

chapters.en: “ ‘But if you will not listen to me and carry out all these commands,
chapters.zh: 你们若不听从我，不遵行我的诫命，

chapters.en: and if you reject my decrees and abhor my laws and fail to carry out all my commands and so violate my covenant,
chapters.zh: 厌弃我的律例，厌恶我的典章，不遵行我一切的诫命，背弃我的约，

chapters.en: then I will do this to you: I will bring on you sudden terror, wasting diseases and fever that will destroy your sight and sap your strength. You will plant seed in vain, because your enemies will eat it.
chapters.zh: 我待你们就要这样，我必命定惊惶，叫眼目干瘪，精神消耗的痨病热病辖制你们。你们也要白白地撒种，因为仇敌要吃你们所种的。

chapters.en: I will set my face against you so that you will be defeated by your enemies; those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee even when no one is pursuing you.
chapters.zh: 我要向你们变脸，你们就要败在仇敌面前。恨恶你们的，必辖管你们，无人追赶，你们却要逃跑。

chapters.en: “ ‘If after all this you will not listen to me, I will punish you for your sins seven times over.
chapters.zh: 你们因这些事若还不听从我，我就要为你们的罪加七倍惩罚你们。

chapters.en: I will break down your stubborn pride and make the sky above you like iron and the ground beneath you like bronze.
chapters.zh: 我必断绝你们因势力而有的骄傲，又要使覆你们的天如铁，载你们的地如铜。

chapters.en: Your strength will be spent in vain, because your soil will not yield its crops, nor will the trees of your land yield their fruit.
chapters.zh: 你们要白白地劳力，因为你们的地不出土产，其上的树木也不结果子。

chapters.en: “ ‘If you remain hostile toward me and refuse to listen to me, I will multiply your afflictions seven times over, as your sins deserve.
chapters.zh: 你们行事若与我反对，不肯听从我，我就要按你们的罪加七倍降灾与你们。

chapters.en: I will send wild animals against you, and they will rob you of your children, destroy your cattle and make you so few in number that your roads will be deserted.
chapters.zh: 我也要打发野地的走兽到你们中间，抢吃你们的儿女，吞灭你们的牲畜，使你们的人数减少，道路荒凉。

chapters.en: “ ‘If in spite of these things you do not accept my correction but continue to be hostile toward me,
chapters.zh: 你们因这些事若仍不改正归我，行事与我反对，

chapters.en: I myself will be hostile toward you and will afflict you for your sins seven times over.
chapters.zh: 我就要行事与你们反对，因你们的罪击打你们七次。

chapters.en: And I will bring the sword on you to avenge the breaking of the covenant. When you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be given into enemy hands.
chapters.zh: 我又要使刀剑临到你们，报复你们背约的仇，聚集你们在各城内，降瘟疫在你们中间，也必将你们交在仇敌的手中。

chapters.en: When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will be able to bake your bread in one oven, and they will dole out the bread by weight. You will eat, but you will not be satisfied.
chapters.zh: 我要折断你们的杖，就是断绝你们的粮。那时，必有十个女人在一个炉子给你们烤饼，按分量秤给你们，你们要吃，也吃不饱。

chapters.en: “ ‘If in spite of this you still do not listen to me but continue to be hostile toward me,
chapters.zh: 你们因这一切的事若不听从我，却行事与我反对，

chapters.en: then in my anger I will be hostile toward you, and I myself will punish you for your sins seven times over.
chapters.zh: 我就要发烈怒，行事与你们反对，又因你们的罪惩罚你们七次。

chapters.en: You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters.
chapters.zh: 并且你们要吃儿子的肉，也要吃女儿的肉。

chapters.en: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars and pile your dead bodies on the lifeless forms of your idols, and I will abhor you.
chapters.zh: 我又要毁坏你们的丘坛，砍下你们的日像，把你们的尸首扔在你们偶像的身上，我的心也必厌恶你们。

chapters.en: I will turn your cities into ruins and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will take no delight in the pleasing aroma of your offerings.
chapters.zh: 我要使你们的城邑变为荒凉，使你们的众圣所成为荒场，我也不闻你们馨香的香气。

chapters.en: I myself will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who live there will be appalled.
chapters.zh: 我要使地成为荒场，住在其上的仇敌就因此诧异。

chapters.en: I will scatter you among the nations and will draw out my sword and pursue you. Your land will be laid waste, and your cities will lie in ruins.
chapters.zh: 我要把你们散在列邦中，我也要拔刀追赶你们。你们的地要成为荒场，你们的城邑要变为荒凉。

chapters.en: Then the land will enjoy its sabbath years all the time that it lies desolate and you are in the country of your enemies; then the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.
chapters.zh: 你们在仇敌之地居住的时候，你们的地荒凉要享受众安息，正在那时候，地要歇息，享受安息。

chapters.en: All the time that it lies desolate, the land will have the rest it did not have during the sabbaths you lived in it.
chapters.zh: 地多时为荒场，就要多时歇息，地这样歇息，是你们住在其上的安息年所不能得的。

chapters.en: “ ‘As for those of you who are left, I will make their hearts so fearful in the lands of their enemies that the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight. They will run as though fleeing from the sword, and they will fall, even though no one is pursuing them.
chapters.zh: 至于你们剩下的人，我要使他们在仇敌之地心惊胆怯。叶子被风吹的响声，要追赶他们，他们要逃避，像人逃避刀剑，无人追赶，却要跌倒。

chapters.en: They will stumble over one another as though fleeing from the sword, even though no one is pursuing them. So you will not be able to stand before your enemies.
chapters.zh: 无人追赶，他们要彼此撞跌，像在刀剑之前。你们在仇敌面前也必站立不住。

chapters.en: You will perish among the nations; the land of your enemies will devour you.
chapters.zh: 你们要在列邦中灭亡，仇敌之地要吞吃你们。

chapters.en: Those of you who are left will waste away in the lands of their enemies because of their sins; also because of their ancestors’ sins they will waste away.
chapters.zh: 你们剩下的人必因自己的罪孽和祖宗的罪孽在仇敌之地消灭。

chapters.en: “ ‘But if they will confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors—their unfaithfulness and their hostility toward me,
chapters.zh: 他们要承认自己的罪和他们祖宗的罪，就是干犯我的那罪，并且承认自己行事与我反对，

chapters.en: which made me hostile toward them so that I sent them into the land of their enemies—then when their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they pay for their sin,
chapters.zh: 我所以行事与他们反对，把他们带到仇敌之地。那时，他们未受割礼的心若谦卑了，他们也服了罪孽的刑罚，

chapters.en: I will remember my covenant with Jacob and my covenant with Isaac and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.
chapters.zh: 我就要记念我与雅各所立的约，与以撒所立的约，与亚伯拉罕所立的约，并要记念这地。

chapters.en: For the land will be deserted by them and will enjoy its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them. They will pay for their sins because they rejected my laws and abhorred my decrees.
chapters.zh: 他们离开这地，地在荒废无人的时候就要享受安息。并且他们要服罪孽的刑罚，因为他们厌弃了我的典章，心中厌恶了我的律例。

chapters.en: Yet in spite of this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them completely, breaking my covenant with them. I am the LORD their God.
chapters.zh: 虽是这样，他们在仇敌之地，我却不厌弃他们，也不厌恶他们，将他们尽行灭绝，也不背弃我与他们所立的约，因为我是耶和华他们的神。

chapters.en: But for their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors whom I brought out of Egypt in the sight of the nations to be their God. I am the LORD.’ ”
chapters.zh: 我却要为他们的缘故记念我与他们先祖所立的约。他们的先祖是我在列邦人眼前，从埃及地领出来的，为要作他们的神。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: These are the decrees, the laws and the regulations that the LORD established at Mount Sinai between himself and the Israelites through Moses.
chapters.zh: 这些律例，典章，和法度是耶和华与以色列人在西乃山借着摩西立的。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘If anyone makes a special vow to dedicate a person to the LORD by giving the equivalent value,
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，人还特许的愿，被许的人要按你所估的价值归给耶和华。

chapters.en: set the value of a male between the ages of twenty and sixty at fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel ;
chapters.zh: 你估定的，从二十岁到六十岁的男人，要按圣所的平，估定价银五十舍客勒。

chapters.en: for a female, set her value at thirty shekels ;
chapters.zh: 若是女人，你要估定三十舍客勒。

chapters.en: for a person between the ages of five and twenty, set the value of a male at twenty shekels and of a female at ten shekels ;
chapters.zh: 若是从五岁到二十岁，男子你要估定二十舍客勒，女子估定十舍客勒。

chapters.en: for a person between one month and five years, set the value of a male at five shekels of silver and that of a female at three shekels of silver;
chapters.zh: 若是从一月到五岁，男子你要估定五舍客勒，女子估定三舍客勒。

chapters.en: for a person sixty years old or more, set the value of a male at fifteen shekels and of a female at ten shekels.
chapters.zh: 若是从六十岁以上，男人你要估定十五舍客勒，女人估定十舍客勒。

chapters.en: If anyone making the vow is too poor to pay the specified amount, the person being dedicated is to be presented to the priest, who will set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.
chapters.zh: 他若贫穷，不能照你所估定的价，就要把他带到祭司面前，祭司要按许愿人的力量估定他的价。

chapters.en: “ ‘If what they vowed is an animal that is acceptable as an offering to the LORD, such an animal given to the LORD becomes holy.
chapters.zh: 所许的若是牲畜，就是人献给耶和华为供物的，凡这一类献给耶和华的，都要成为圣。

chapters.en: They must not exchange it or substitute a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one; if they should substitute one animal for another, both it and the substitute become holy.
chapters.zh: 人不可改换，也不可更换，或是好的换坏的，或是坏的换好的。若以牲畜更换牲畜，所许的与所换的都要成为圣。

chapters.en: If what they vowed is a ceremonially unclean animal—one that is not acceptable as an offering to the LORD—the animal must be presented to the priest,
chapters.zh: 若牲畜不洁净，是不可献给耶和华为供物的，就要把牲畜安置在祭司面前。

chapters.en: who will judge its quality as good or bad. Whatever value the priest then sets, that is what it will be.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要估定价值，牲畜是好是坏，祭司怎样估定，就要以怎样为是。

chapters.en: If the owner wishes to redeem the animal, a fifth must be added to its value.
chapters.zh: 他若一定要赎回，就要在你所估定的价值以外加上五分之一。

chapters.en: “ ‘If anyone dedicates their house as something holy to the LORD, the priest will judge its quality as good or bad. Whatever value the priest then sets, so it will remain.
chapters.zh: 人将房屋分别为圣，归给耶和华，祭司就要估定价值。房屋是好是坏，祭司怎样估定，就要以怎样为定。

chapters.en: If the one who dedicates their house wishes to redeem it, they must add a fifth to its value, and the house will again become theirs.
chapters.zh: 将房屋分别为圣的人，若要赎回房屋，就必在你所估定的价值以外加上五分之一，房屋仍旧归他。

chapters.en: “ ‘If anyone dedicates to the LORD part of their family land, its value is to be set according to the amount of seed required for it—fifty shekels of silver to a homer of barley seed.
chapters.zh: 人若将承受为业的几分地分别为圣，归给耶和华，你要按这地撒种多少估定价值，若撒大麦一贺梅珥，要估价五十舍客勒。

chapters.en: If they dedicate a field during the Year of Jubilee, the value that has been set remains.
chapters.zh: 他若从禧年将地分别为圣，就要以你所估定的价为定。

chapters.en: But if they dedicate a field after the Jubilee, the priest will determine the value according to the number of years that remain until the next Year of Jubilee, and its set value will be reduced.
chapters.zh: 倘若他在禧年以后将地分别为圣，祭司就要按着未到禧年所剩的年数推算价值，也要从你所估的减去价值。

chapters.en: If the one who dedicates the field wishes to redeem it, they must add a fifth to its value, and the field will again become theirs.
chapters.zh: 将地分别为圣的人若定要把地赎回，他便要在你所估的价值以外加上五分之一，地就准定归他。

chapters.en: If, however, they do not redeem the field, or if they have sold it to someone else, it can never be redeemed.
chapters.zh: 他若不赎回那地，或是将地卖给别人，就再不能赎了。

chapters.en: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the LORD; it will become priestly property.
chapters.zh: 但到了禧年，那地从买主手下出来的时候，就要归耶和华为圣，和永献的地一样，要归祭司为业。

chapters.en: “ ‘If anyone dedicates to the LORD a field they have bought, which is not part of their family land,
chapters.zh: 他若将所买的一块地，不是承受为业的，分别为圣归给耶和华，

chapters.en: the priest will determine its value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the owner must pay its value on that day as something holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要将你所估的价值给他推算到禧年。当日，他要以你所估的价银为圣，归给耶和华。

chapters.en: In the Year of Jubilee the field will revert to the person from whom it was bought, the one whose land it was.
chapters.zh: 到了禧年，那地要归卖主，就是那承受为业的原主。

chapters.en: Every value is to be set according to the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.
chapters.zh: 凡你所估定的价银都要按着圣所的平，二十季拉为一舍客勒。

chapters.en: “ ‘No one, however, may dedicate the firstborn of an animal, since the firstborn already belongs to the LORD; whether an ox or a sheep, it is the LORD’s.
chapters.zh: 惟独牲畜中头生的，无论是牛是羊，既归耶和华，谁也不可再分别为圣，因为这是耶和华的。

chapters.en: If it is one of the unclean animals, it may be bought back at its set value, adding a fifth of the value to it. If it is not redeemed, it is to be sold at its set value.
chapters.zh: 若是不洁净的牲畜生的，就要按你所估定的价值加上五分之一赎回，若不赎回，就要按你所估定的价值卖了。

chapters.en: “ ‘But nothing that a person owns and devotes to the LORD—whether a human being or an animal or family land—may be sold or redeemed; everything so devoted is most holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 但一切永献的，就是人从他所有永献给耶和华的，无论是人，是牲畜，是他承受为业的地，都不可卖，也不可赎。凡永献的是归给耶和华为至圣。

chapters.en: “ ‘No person devoted to destruction may be ransomed; they are to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 凡从人中当灭的都不可赎，必被治死。

chapters.en: “ ‘A tithe of everything from the land, whether grain from the soil or fruit from the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 地上所有的，无论是地上的种子是树上的果子，十分之一是耶和华的，是归给耶和华为圣的。

chapters.en: Whoever would redeem any of their tithe must add a fifth of the value to it.
chapters.zh: 人若要赎这十分之一的什么物，就要加上五分之一。

chapters.en: Every tithe of the herd and flock—every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd’s rod—will be holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 凡牛群羊群中，一切从杖下经过的，每第十只要归给耶和华为圣。

chapters.en: No one may pick out the good from the bad or make any substitution. If anyone does make a substitution, both the animal and its substitute become holy and cannot be redeemed.’ ”
chapters.zh: 不可问是好是坏，也不可更换，若定要更换，所更换的与本来的牲畜都要成为圣，不可赎回。

chapters.en: These are the commands the LORD gave Moses at Mount Sinai for the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 这就是耶和华在西乃山为以色列人所吩咐摩西的命令。

chapters.en: The LORD spoke to Moses in the tent of meeting in the Desert of Sinai on the first day of the second month of the second year after the Israelites came out of Egypt. He said:
chapters.zh: 以色列人出埃及地后，第二年二月初一日，耶和华在西乃的旷野，会幕中晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Take a census of the whole Israelite community by their clans and families, listing every man by name, one by one.
chapters.zh: 你要按以色列全会众的家室，宗族，人名的数目，计算所有的男丁。

chapters.en: You and Aaron are to count according to their divisions all the men in Israel who are twenty years old or more and able to serve in the army.
chapters.zh: 凡以色列中，从二十岁以外，能出去打仗的，你和亚伦要照他们的军队数点。

chapters.en: One man from each tribe, each of them the head of his family, is to help you.
chapters.zh: 每支派中，必有一人作本支派的族长，帮助你们。

chapters.en: These are the names of the men who are to assist you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
chapters.zh: 他们的名字，属流便的，有示丢珥的儿子以利蓿。

chapters.en: from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
chapters.zh: 属西缅的，有苏利沙代的儿子示路蔑。

chapters.en: from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
chapters.zh: 属犹大的，有亚米拿达的儿子拿顺。

chapters.en: from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
chapters.zh: 属以萨迦的，有苏押的儿子拿坦业。

chapters.en: from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
chapters.zh: 属西布伦的，有希伦的儿子以利押。

chapters.en: from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
chapters.zh: 约瑟子孙，属以法莲的，有亚米忽的儿子以利沙玛。属玛拿西的，有比大蓿的儿子迦玛列。

chapters.en: from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
chapters.zh: 属便雅悯的，有基多尼的儿子亚比但。

chapters.en: from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
chapters.zh: 属但的，有亚米沙代的儿子亚希以谢。

chapters.en: from Asher, Pagiel son of Okran;
chapters.zh: 属亚设的，有俄兰的儿子帕结。

chapters.en: from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
chapters.zh: 属迦得的，有丢珥的儿子以利雅萨。

chapters.en: from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.”
chapters.zh: 属拿弗他利的，有以南的儿子亚希拉。

chapters.en: These were the men appointed from the community, the leaders of their ancestral tribes. They were the heads of the clans of Israel.
chapters.zh: 这都是从会中选召的，各作本支派的首领，都是以色列军中的统领。

chapters.en: Moses and Aaron took these men whose names had been specified,
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西，亚伦带着这些按名指定的人，

chapters.en: and they called the whole community together on the first day of the second month. The people registered their ancestry by their clans and families, and the men twenty years old or more were listed by name, one by one,
chapters.zh: 当二月初一日招聚全会众。会众就照他们的家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外的，都述说自己的家谱。

chapters.en: as the LORD commanded Moses. And so he counted them in the Desert of Sinai:
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样吩咐摩西，他就怎样在西乃的旷野数点他们。

chapters.en: From the descendants of Reuben the firstborn son of Israel: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, one by one, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 以色列的长子，流便子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的男丁，共有四万六千五百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.

From the descendants of Simeon: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted and listed by name, one by one, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 西缅子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的男丁，共有五万九千三百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.
From the descendants of Gad: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 迦得子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有四万五千六百五十名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Gad was 45,650.
From the descendants of Judah: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 犹大子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有七万四千六百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Judah was 74,600.
From the descendants of Issachar: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 以萨迦子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有五万四千四百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.
From the descendants of Zebulun: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 西布伦子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有五万七千四百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.

From the sons of Joseph: From the descendants of Ephraim: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 约瑟子孙，属以法莲子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有四万零五百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.
From the descendants of Manasseh: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 玛拿西子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有三万二千二百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.
From the descendants of Benjamin: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 便雅悯子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有三万五千四百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.
From the descendants of Dan: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 但子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有六万二千七百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Dan was 62,700.
From the descendants of Asher: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 亚设子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有四万一千五百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.
From the descendants of Naphtali: All the men twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were listed by name, according to the records of their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 拿弗他利子孙的后代，照着家室，宗族，人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗，被数的，共有五万三千四百名。

chapters.en: The number from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
These were the men counted by Moses and Aaron and the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his family.
chapters.zh: 这些就是被数点的，是摩西，亚伦，和以色列中十二个首领所数点的。这十二个人各作各宗族的代表。

chapters.en: All the Israelites twenty years old or more who were able to serve in Israel’s army were counted according to their families.
chapters.zh: 这样凡以色列人中被数的，照着宗族从二十岁以外，能出去打仗，被数的，共有六十万零三千五百五十名。

chapters.en: The total number was 603,550.
The ancestral tribe of the Levites, however, was not counted along with the others.
chapters.zh: 利未人却没有按着支派数在其中，

chapters.en: The LORD had said to Moses:
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “You must not count the tribe of Levi or include them in the census of the other Israelites.
chapters.zh: 惟独利未支派你不可数点，也不可在以色列人中计算他们的总数。

chapters.en: Instead, appoint the Levites to be in charge of the tabernacle of the covenant law—over all its furnishings and everything belonging to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings; they are to take care of it and encamp around it.
chapters.zh: 只要派利未人管法柜的帐幕和其中的器具，并属乎帐幕的。他们要抬（抬或作搬运）帐幕和其中的器具，并要办理帐幕的事，在帐幕的四围安营。

chapters.en: Whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites are to take it down, and whenever the tabernacle is to be set up, the Levites shall do it. Anyone else who approaches it is to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 帐幕将往前行的时候，利未人要拆卸。将支搭的时候，利未人要竖起。近前来的外人必被治死。

chapters.en: The Israelites are to set up their tents by divisions, each of them in their own camp under their standard.
chapters.zh: 以色列人支搭帐棚，要照他们的军队，各归本营，各归本纛。

chapters.en: The Levites, however, are to set up their tents around the tabernacle of the covenant law so that my wrath will not fall on the Israelite community. The Levites are to be responsible for the care of the tabernacle of the covenant law.”
chapters.zh: 但利未人要在法柜帐幕的四围安营，免得忿怒临到以色列会众。利未人并要谨守法柜的帐幕。

chapters.en: The Israelites did all this just as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 以色列人就这样行。凡耶和华所吩咐摩西的，他们就照样行了。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西，亚伦说，

chapters.en: “The Israelites are to camp around the tent of meeting some distance from it, each of them under their standard and holding the banners of their family.”
chapters.zh: 以色列人要各归自己的纛下，在本族的旗号那里，对着会幕的四围安营。

chapters.en: On the east, toward the sunrise, the divisions of the camp of Judah are to encamp under their standard. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
chapters.zh: 在东边，向日出之地，照着军队安营的是犹大营的纛。有亚米拿达的儿子拿顺作犹大人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 74,600.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有七万四千六百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Issachar will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
chapters.zh: 挨着他安营的是以萨迦支派。有苏押的儿子拿坦业作以萨迦人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 54,400.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有五万四千四百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Zebulun will be next. The leader of the people of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
chapters.zh: 又有西布伦支派。希伦的儿子以利押作西布伦人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 57,400.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有五万七千四百名。

chapters.en: All the men assigned to the camp of Judah, according to their divisions, number 186,400. They will set out first.
chapters.zh: 凡属犹大营，按着军队被数的，共有十八万六千四百名，要作第一队往前行。

chapters.en: On the south will be the divisions of the camp of Reuben under their standard. The leader of the people of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
chapters.zh: 在南边，按着军队是流便营的纛。有示丢珥的儿子以利蓿作流便人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 46,500.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有四万六千五百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Simeon will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
chapters.zh: 挨着他安营的是西缅支派。苏利沙代的儿子示路蔑作西缅人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 59,300.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有五万九千三百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Gad will be next. The leader of the people of Gad is Eliasaph son of Deuel.
chapters.zh: 又有迦得支派。丢珥的儿子以利雅萨作迦得人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 45,650.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有四万五千六百五十名，

chapters.en: All the men assigned to the camp of Reuben, according to their divisions, number 151,450. They will set out second.
chapters.zh: 凡属流便营，按着军队被数的，共有十五万一千四百五十名，要作第二队往前行。

chapters.en: Then the tent of meeting and the camp of the Levites will set out in the middle of the camps. They will set out in the same order as they encamp, each in their own place under their standard.
chapters.zh: 随后，会幕要往前行，有利未营在诸营中间。他们怎样安营就怎样往前行，各按本位，各归本纛。

chapters.en: On the west will be the divisions of the camp of Ephraim under their standard. The leader of the people of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
chapters.zh: 在西边，按着军队是以法莲营的纛。亚米忽的儿子以利沙玛作以法莲人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 40,500.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有四万零五百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Manasseh will be next to them. The leader of the people of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
chapters.zh: 挨着他的是玛拿西支派。比大蓿的儿子迦玛列作玛拿西人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 32,200.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有三万二千二百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Benjamin will be next. The leader of the people of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
chapters.zh: 又有便雅悯支派。基多尼的儿子亚比但作便雅悯人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 35,400.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有三万五千四百名。

chapters.en: All the men assigned to the camp of Ephraim, according to their divisions, number 108,100. They will set out third.
chapters.zh: 凡属以法莲营，按着军队被数的，共有十万零八千一百名，要作第三队往前行。

chapters.en: On the north will be the divisions of the camp of Dan under their standard. The leader of the people of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
chapters.zh: 在北边，按着军队是但营的纛。亚米沙代的儿子亚希以谢作但人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 62,700.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有六万二千七百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Asher will camp next to them. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Okran.
chapters.zh: 挨着他安营的是亚设支派。俄兰的儿子帕结作亚设人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 41,500.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有四万一千五百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Naphtali will be next. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
chapters.zh: 又有拿弗他利支派。以南的儿子亚希拉作拿弗他利人的首领。

chapters.en: His division numbers 53,400.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有五万三千四百名。

chapters.en: All the men assigned to the camp of Dan number 157,600. They will set out last, under their standards.
chapters.zh: 凡但营被数的，共有十五万七千六百名，要归本纛作末队往前行。

chapters.en: These are the Israelites, counted according to their families. All the men in the camps, by their divisions, number 603,550.
chapters.zh: 这些以色列人，照他们的宗族，按他们的军队，在诸营中被数的，共有六十万零三千五百五十名。

chapters.en: The Levites, however, were not counted along with the other Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 惟独利未人没有数在以色列人中，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: So the Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses; that is the way they encamped under their standards, and that is the way they set out, each of them with their clan and family.
chapters.zh: 以色列人就这样行，各人照他们的家室，宗族归于本纛，安营起行，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: This is the account of the family of Aaron and Moses at the time the LORD spoke to Moses at Mount Sinai.
chapters.zh: 耶和华在西乃山晓谕摩西的日子，亚伦和摩西的后代如下，

chapters.en: The names of the sons of Aaron were Nadab the firstborn and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的儿子，长子名叫拿答，还有亚比户，以利亚撒，以他玛。

chapters.en: Those were the names of Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests.
chapters.zh: 这是亚伦儿子的名字，都是受膏的祭司，是摩西叫他们承接圣职供祭司职分的。

chapters.en: Nadab and Abihu, however, died before the LORD when they made an offering with unauthorized fire before him in the Desert of Sinai. They had no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron.
chapters.zh: 拿答，亚比户在西乃的旷野向耶和华献凡火的时候就死在耶和华面前了。他们也没有儿子。以利亚撒，以他玛在他们的父亲亚伦面前供祭司的职分。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Bring the tribe of Levi and present them to Aaron the priest to assist him.
chapters.zh: 你使利未支派近前来，站在祭司亚伦面前好服事他，

chapters.en: They are to perform duties for him and for the whole community at the tent of meeting by doing the work of the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 替他和会众在会幕前守所吩咐的，办理帐幕的事。

chapters.en: They are to take care of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting, fulfilling the obligations of the Israelites by doing the work of the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 又要看守会幕的器具，并守所吩咐以色列人的，办理帐幕的事。

chapters.en: Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are the Israelites who are to be given wholly to him.
chapters.zh: 你要将利未人给亚伦和他的儿子，因为他们是从以色列人中选出来给他的。

chapters.en: Appoint Aaron and his sons to serve as priests; anyone else who approaches the sanctuary is to be put to death.”
chapters.zh: 你要嘱咐亚伦和他的儿子谨守自己祭司的职任。近前来的外人必被治死。

chapters.en: The LORD also said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of the first male offspring of every Israelite woman. The Levites are mine,
chapters.zh: 我从以色列人中拣选了利未人，代替以色列人一切头生的。利未人要归我。

chapters.en: for all the firstborn are mine. When I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel, whether human or animal. They are to be mine. I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 因为凡头生的是我的。我在埃及地击杀一切头生的那日就把以色列中一切头生的，连人带牲畜都分别为圣归我。他们定要属我。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses in the Desert of Sinai,
chapters.zh: 耶和华在西乃的旷野晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Count the Levites by their families and clans. Count every male a month old or more.”
chapters.zh: 你要照利未人的宗族，家室数点他们。凡一个月以外的男子都要数点。

chapters.en: So Moses counted them, as he was commanded by the word of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西照耶和华所吩咐的数点他们。

chapters.en: These were the names of the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
chapters.zh: 利未众子的名字是革顺，哥辖，米拉利。

chapters.en: These were the names of the Gershonite clans: Libni and Shimei.
chapters.zh: 革顺的儿子，按着家室，是立尼，示每。

chapters.en: The Kohathite clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
chapters.zh: 哥辖的儿子，按着家室，是暗兰，以斯哈，希伯伦，乌薛。

chapters.en: The Merarite clans: Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans, according to their families.
chapters.zh: 米拉利的儿子，按着家室，是抹利，母示。这些按着宗族是利未人的家室。

chapters.en: To Gershon belonged the clans of the Libnites and Shimeites; these were the Gershonite clans.
chapters.zh: 属革顺的，有立尼族，示每族。这是革顺的二族。

chapters.en: The number of all the males a month old or more who were counted was 7,500.
chapters.zh: 其中被数，从一个月以外所有的男子共有七千五百名。

chapters.en: The Gershonite clans were to camp on the west, behind the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 这革顺的二族要在帐幕后西边安营。

chapters.en: The leader of the families of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
chapters.zh: 拉伊勒的儿子以利雅萨作革顺人宗族的首领。

chapters.en: At the tent of meeting the Gershonites were responsible for the care of the tabernacle and tent, its coverings, the curtain at the entrance to the tent of meeting,
chapters.zh: 革顺的子孙在会幕中所要看守的，就是帐幕和罩棚，并罩棚的盖与会幕的门帘，

chapters.en: the curtains of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and altar, and the ropes—and everything related to their use.
chapters.zh: 院子的帷子和门帘（院子是围帐幕和坛的），并一切使用的绳子。

chapters.en: To Kohath belonged the clans of the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites and Uzzielites; these were the Kohathite clans.
chapters.zh: 属哥辖的，有暗兰族，以斯哈族，希伯伦族，乌薛族。这是哥辖的诸族。

chapters.en: The number of all the males a month old or more was 8,600. The Kohathites were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 按所有男子的数目，从一个月以外看守圣所的，共有八千六百名。

chapters.en: The Kohathite clans were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 哥辖儿子的诸族要在帐幕的南边安营。

chapters.en: The leader of the families of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
chapters.zh: 乌薛的儿子以利撒反作哥辖宗族家室的首领。

chapters.en: They were responsible for the care of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the articles of the sanctuary used in ministering, the curtain, and everything related to their use.
chapters.zh: 他们所要看守的是约柜，桌子，灯台，两座坛与圣所内使用的器皿，并帘子和一切使用之物。

chapters.en: The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest. He was appointed over those who were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 祭司亚伦的儿子以利亚撒作利未人众首领的领袖，要监察那些看守圣所的人。

chapters.en: To Merari belonged the clans of the Mahlites and the Mushites; these were the Merarite clans.
chapters.zh: 属米拉利的，有抹利族，母示族。这是米拉利的二族。

chapters.en: The number of all the males a month old or more who were counted was 6,200.
chapters.zh: 他们被数的，按所有男子的数目，从一个月以外的，共有六千二百名。

chapters.en: The leader of the families of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail; they were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 亚比亥的儿子苏列作米拉利二宗族的首领。他们要在帐幕的北边安营。

chapters.en: The Merarites were appointed to take care of the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, bases, all its equipment, and everything related to their use,
chapters.zh: 米拉利子孙的职分是看守帐幕的板，闩，柱子，带卯的座，和帐幕一切所使用的器具，

chapters.en: as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs and ropes.
chapters.zh: 院子四围的柱子，带卯的座，橛子，和绳子。

chapters.en: Moses and Aaron and his sons were to camp to the east of the tabernacle, toward the sunrise, in front of the tent of meeting. They were responsible for the care of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Anyone else who approached the sanctuary was to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 在帐幕前东边，向日出之地安营的是摩西，亚伦，和亚伦的儿子。他们看守圣所，替以色列人守耶和华所吩咐的。近前来的外人，必被治死。

chapters.en: The total number of Levites counted at the LORD’s command by Moses and Aaron according to their clans, including every male a month old or more, was 22,000.
chapters.zh: 凡被数的利未人，就是摩西，亚伦照耶和华吩咐所数的，按着家室，从一个月以外的男子，共有二万二千名。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses, “Count all the firstborn Israelite males who are a month old or more and make a list of their names.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，你要从以色列人中数点一个月以外，凡头生的男子，把他们的名字记下。

chapters.en: Take the Levites for me in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites. I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华。你要拣选利未人归我，代替以色列人所有头生的，也取利未人的牲畜代替以色列所有头生的牲畜。

chapters.en: So Moses counted all the firstborn of the Israelites, as the LORD commanded him.
chapters.zh: 摩西就照耶和华所吩咐的把以色列人头生的都数点了。

chapters.en: The total number of firstborn males a month old or more, listed by name, was 22,273.
chapters.zh: 按人名的数目，从一个月以外，凡头生的男子，共有二万二千二百七十三名。

chapters.en: The LORD also said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites are to be mine. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你拣选利未人代替以色列人所有头生的，也取利未人的牲畜代替以色列人的牲畜。利未人要归我。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: To redeem the 273 firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites,
chapters.zh: 以色列人中头生的男子比利未人多二百七十三个，必当将他们赎出来。

chapters.en: collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs.
chapters.zh: 你要按人丁，照圣所的平，每人取赎银五舍客勒（一舍客勒是二十季拉），

chapters.en: Give the money for the redemption of the additional Israelites to Aaron and his sons.”
chapters.zh: 把那多余之人的赎银交给亚伦和他的儿子。

chapters.en: So Moses collected the redemption money from those who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西从那被利未人所赎以外的人取了赎银。

chapters.en: From the firstborn of the Israelites he collected silver weighing 1,365 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
chapters.zh: 从以色列人头生的所取之银，按圣所的平，有一千三百六十五舍客勒。

chapters.en: Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, as he was commanded by the word of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 摩西照耶和华的话把这赎银给亚伦和他的儿子，正如耶和华所吩咐的。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西，亚伦说，

chapters.en: “Take a census of the Kohathite branch of the Levites by their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 你从利未人中，将哥辖子孙的总数，照他们的家室，宗族，

chapters.en: Count all the men from thirty to fifty years of age who come to serve in the work at the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职，在会幕里办事的，全都计算。

chapters.en: “This is the work of the Kohathites at the tent of meeting: the care of the most holy things.
chapters.zh: 哥辖子孙在会幕搬运至圣之物，所办的事乃是这样，

chapters.en: When the camp is to move, Aaron and his sons are to go in and take down the shielding curtain and put it over the ark of the covenant law.
chapters.zh: 起营的时候，亚伦和他儿子要进去摘下遮掩柜的幔子，用以蒙盖法柜，

chapters.en: Then they are to cover the curtain with a durable leather, spread a cloth of solid blue over that and put the poles in place.
chapters.zh: 又用海狗皮盖在上头，再蒙上纯蓝色的毯子，把杠穿上。

chapters.en: “Over the table of the Presence they are to spread a blue cloth and put on it the plates, dishes and bowls, and the jars for drink offerings; the bread that is continually there is to remain on it.
chapters.zh: 又用蓝色毯子铺在陈设饼的桌子上，将盘子，调羹，奠酒的爵，和杯摆在上头。桌子上也必有常设的饼。

chapters.en: They are to spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover that with the durable leather and put the poles in place.
chapters.zh: 在其上又要蒙朱红色的毯子，再蒙上海狗皮，把杠穿上。

chapters.en: “They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand that is for light, together with its lamps, its wick trimmers and trays, and all its jars for the olive oil used to supply it.
chapters.zh: 要拿蓝色毯子，把灯台和灯台上所用的灯盏，剪子，蜡花盘，并一切盛油的器皿，全都遮盖。

chapters.en: Then they are to wrap it and all its accessories in a covering of the durable leather and put it on a carrying frame.
chapters.zh: 又要把灯台和灯台的一切器具包在海狗皮里，放在抬架上。

chapters.en: “Over the gold altar they are to spread a blue cloth and cover that with the durable leather and put the poles in place.
chapters.zh: 在金坛上要铺蓝色毯子，蒙上海狗皮，把杠穿上。

chapters.en: “They are to take all the articles used for ministering in the sanctuary, wrap them in a blue cloth, cover that with the durable leather and put them on a carrying frame.
chapters.zh: 又要把圣所用的一切器具包在蓝色毯子里，用海狗皮蒙上，放在抬架上。

chapters.en: “They are to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and spread a purple cloth over it.
chapters.zh: 要收去坛上的灰，把紫色毯子铺在坛上。

chapters.en: Then they are to place on it all the utensils used for ministering at the altar, including the firepans, meat forks, shovels and sprinkling bowls. Over it they are to spread a covering of the durable leather and put the poles in place.
chapters.zh: 又要把所用的一切器具，就是火鼎，肉锸子，铲子，盘子，一切属坛的器具都摆在坛上，又蒙上海狗皮，把杠穿上。

chapters.en: “After Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy furnishings and all the holy articles, and when the camp is ready to move, only then are the Kohathites to come and do the carrying. But they must not touch the holy things or they will die. The Kohathites are to carry those things that are in the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 将要起营的时候，亚伦和他儿子把圣所和圣所的一切器具遮盖完了，哥辖的子孙就要来抬，只是不可摸圣物，免得他们死亡。会幕里这些物件是哥辖子孙所当抬的

chapters.en: “Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, is to have charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil. He is to be in charge of the entire tabernacle and everything in it, including its holy furnishings and articles.”
chapters.zh: 祭司亚伦的儿子以利亚撒所要看守的是点灯的油与香料，并当献的素祭和膏油，也要看守全帐幕与其中所有的，并圣所和圣所的器具。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西，亚伦说，

chapters.en: “See that the Kohathite tribal clans are not destroyed from among the Levites.
chapters.zh: 你们不可将哥辖人的支派从利未人中剪除。

chapters.en: So that they may live and not die when they come near the most holy things, do this for them: Aaron and his sons are to go into the sanctuary and assign to each man his work and what he is to carry.
chapters.zh: 他们挨近至圣物的时候，亚伦和他儿子要进去派他们各人所当办的，所当抬的。这样待他们，好使他们活着，不至死亡。

chapters.en: But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die.”
chapters.zh: 只是他们连片时不可进去观看圣所，免得他们死亡。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Take a census also of the Gershonites by their families and clans.
chapters.zh: 你要将革顺子孙的总数，照着宗族，家室，

chapters.en: Count all the men from thirty to fifty years of age who come to serve in the work at the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职，在会幕里办事的，全都数点。

chapters.en: “This is the service of the Gershonite clans in their carrying and their other work:
chapters.zh: 革顺人各族所办的事，所抬的物乃是这样，

chapters.en: They are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle, that is, the tent of meeting, its covering and its outer covering of durable leather, the curtains for the entrance to the tent of meeting,
chapters.zh: 他们要抬帐幕的幔子和会幕，并会幕的盖与其上的海狗皮，和会幕的门帘，

chapters.en: the curtains of the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and altar, the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard, the ropes and all the equipment used in the service of the tent. The Gershonites are to do all that needs to be done with these things.
chapters.zh: 院子的帷子和门帘（院子是围帐幕和坛的），绳子，并所用的器具，不论是作什么用的，他们都要经理。

chapters.en: All their service, whether carrying or doing other work, is to be done under the direction of Aaron and his sons. You shall assign to them as their responsibility all they are to carry.
chapters.zh: 革顺的子孙在一切抬物办事之上都要凭亚伦和他儿子的吩咐。他们所当抬的，要派他们看守。

chapters.en: This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the tent of meeting. Their duties are to be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.
chapters.zh: 这是革顺子孙的各族在会幕里所办的事。他们所看守的，必在祭司亚伦儿子以他玛的手下。

chapters.en: “Count the Merarites by their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 至于米拉利的子孙，你要照着家室，宗族把他们数点。

chapters.en: Count all the men from thirty to fifty years of age who come to serve in the work at the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职，在会幕里办事的，你都要数点。

chapters.en: As part of all their service at the tent, they are to carry the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts and bases,
chapters.zh: 他们办理会幕的事，就是抬帐幕的板，闩，柱子，和带卯的座，

chapters.en: as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, ropes, all their equipment and everything related to their use. Assign to each man the specific things he is to carry.
chapters.zh: 院子四围的柱子和其上带卯的座，橛子，绳子，并一切使用的器具。他们所抬的器具，你们要按名指定。

chapters.en: This is the service of the Merarite clans as they work at the tent of meeting under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.”
chapters.zh: 这是米拉利子孙各族在会幕里所办的事，都在祭司亚伦儿子以他玛的手下。

chapters.en: Moses, Aaron and the leaders of the community counted the Kohathites by their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 摩西，亚伦与会众的诸首领将哥辖的子孙，照着家室，宗族，

chapters.en: All the men from thirty to fifty years of age who came to serve in the work at the tent of meeting,
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职，在会幕里办事的，都数点了。

chapters.en: counted by clans, were 2,750.
chapters.zh: 被数的共有二千七百五十名。

chapters.en: This was the total of all those in the Kohathite clans who served at the tent of meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them according to the LORD’s command through Moses.
chapters.zh: 这是哥辖各族中被数的，是在会幕里办事的，就是摩西，亚伦照耶和华借摩西所吩咐数点的。

chapters.en: The Gershonites were counted by their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 革顺子孙被数的，照着家室，宗族，

chapters.en: All the men from thirty to fifty years of age who came to serve in the work at the tent of meeting,
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职，在会幕里办事的，共有二千六百三十名。

chapters.en: counted by their clans and families, were 2,630.
This was the total of those in the Gershonite clans who served at the tent of meeting. Moses and Aaron counted them according to the LORD’s command.
chapters.zh: 这是革顺子孙各族中被数的，是在会幕里办事的，就是摩西，亚伦照耶和华借摩西所吩咐数点的。

chapters.en: The Merarites were counted by their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 米拉利子孙中各族被数的，照着家室，宗族，

chapters.en: All the men from thirty to fifty years of age who came to serve in the work at the tent of meeting,
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职，在会幕里办事的，共有三千二百名。

chapters.en: counted by their clans, were 3,200.
This was the total of those in the Merarite clans. Moses and Aaron counted them according to the LORD’s command through Moses.
chapters.zh: 这是米拉利子孙各族中被数的，就是摩西，亚伦照耶和华借摩西所吩咐数点的。

chapters.en: So Moses, Aaron and the leaders of Israel counted all the Levites by their clans and families.
chapters.zh: 凡被数的利未人，就是摩西，亚伦并以色列众首领，照着家室，宗族所数点的，

chapters.en: All the men from thirty to fifty years of age who came to do the work of serving and carrying the tent of meeting
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职，在会幕里作抬物之工的，共有八千五百八十名。

chapters.en: numbered 8,580.
At the LORD’s command through Moses, each was assigned his work and told what to carry. Thus they were counted, as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 摩西按他们所办的事，所抬的物，凭耶和华的吩咐数点他们。他们这样被摩西数点，正如耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Command the Israelites to send away from the camp anyone who has a defiling skin disease or a discharge of any kind, or who is ceremonially unclean because of a dead body.
chapters.zh: 你吩咐以色列人，使一切长大麻疯的，患漏症的，并因死尸不洁净的，都出营外去。

chapters.en: Send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them.”
chapters.zh: 无论男女都要使他们出到营外，免得污秽他们的营。这营是我所住的。

chapters.en: The Israelites did so; they sent them outside the camp. They did just as the LORD had instructed Moses.
chapters.zh: 以色列人就这样行，使他们出到营外。耶和华怎样吩咐摩西，以色列人就怎样行了。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites: ‘Any man or woman who wrongs another in any way and so is unfaithful to the LORD is guilty
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，无论男女，若犯了人所常犯的罪，以至干犯耶和华，那人就有了罪。

chapters.en: and must confess the sin they have committed. They must make full restitution for the wrong they have done, add a fifth of the value to it and give it all to the person they have wronged.
chapters.zh: 他要承认所犯的罪，将所亏负人的，如数赔还，另外加上五分之一，也归与所亏负的人。

chapters.en: But if that person has no close relative to whom restitution can be made for the wrong, the restitution belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest, along with the ram with which atonement is made for the wrongdoer.
chapters.zh: 那人若没有亲属可受所赔还的，那所赔还的就要归与服事耶和华的祭司。至于那为他赎罪的公羊是在外。

chapters.en: All the sacred contributions the Israelites bring to a priest will belong to him.
chapters.zh: 以色列人一切的圣物中，所奉给祭司的举祭都要归与祭司。

chapters.en: Sacred things belong to their owners, but what they give to the priest will belong to the priest.’ ”
chapters.zh: 各人所分别为圣的物，无论是什么，都要归给祭司。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘If a man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，人的妻若有邪行，得罪她丈夫，

chapters.en: so that another man has sexual relations with her, and this is hidden from her husband and her impurity is undetected (since there is no witness against her and she has not been caught in the act),
chapters.zh: 有人与她行淫，事情严密，瞒过她丈夫，而且她被玷污，没有作见证的人，当她行淫的时候也没有被捉住，

chapters.en: and if feelings of jealousy come over her husband and he suspects his wife and she is impure—or if he is jealous and suspects her even though she is not impure—
chapters.zh: 她丈夫生了疑恨的心，疑恨她，她是被玷污，或是她丈夫生了疑恨的心，疑恨她，她并没有被玷污，

chapters.en: then he is to take his wife to the priest. He must also take an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour on her behalf. He must not pour olive oil on it or put incense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a reminder-offering to draw attention to wrongdoing.
chapters.zh: 这人就要将妻送到祭司那里，又为她带着大麦面伊法十分之一作供物，不可浇上油，也不可加上乳香。因为这是疑恨的素祭，是思念的素祭，使人思念罪孽。

chapters.en: “ ‘The priest shall bring her and have her stand before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要使那妇人近前来，站在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Then he shall take some holy water in a clay jar and put some dust from the tabernacle floor into the water.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把圣水盛在瓦器里，又从帐幕的地上取点尘土，放在水中。

chapters.en: After the priest has had the woman stand before the LORD, he shall loosen her hair and place in her hands the reminder-offering, the grain offering for jealousy, while he himself holds the bitter water that brings a curse.
chapters.zh: 祭司要叫那妇人蓬头散发，站在耶和华面前，把思念的素祭，就是疑恨的素祭，放在她手中。祭司手里拿着致咒诅的苦水，

chapters.en: Then the priest shall put the woman under oath and say to her, “If no other man has had sexual relations with you and you have not gone astray and become impure while married to your husband, may this bitter water that brings a curse not harm you.
chapters.zh: 要叫妇人起誓，对她说，若没有人与你行淫，也未曾背着丈夫作污秽的事，你就免受这致咒诅苦水的灾。

chapters.en: But if you have gone astray while married to your husband and you have made yourself impure by having sexual relations with a man other than your husband”—
chapters.zh: 你若背着丈夫行了污秽的事，在你丈夫以外有人与你行淫，

chapters.en: here the priest is to put the woman under this curse—“may the LORD cause you to become a curse among your people when he makes your womb miscarry and your abdomen swell.
chapters.zh: （祭司叫妇人发咒起誓），愿耶和华叫你大腿消瘦，肚腹发胀，使你在你民中被人咒诅，成了誓语。

chapters.en: May this water that brings a curse enter your body so that your abdomen swells or your womb miscarries.” “ ‘Then the woman is to say, “Amen. So be it.”
chapters.zh: 并且这致咒诅的水入你的肠中，要叫你的肚腹发胀，大腿消瘦。妇人要回答说，阿们，阿们。

chapters.en: “ ‘The priest is to write these curses on a scroll and then wash them off into the bitter water.
chapters.zh: 祭司要写这咒诅的话，将所写的字抹在苦水里，

chapters.en: He shall make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and this water that brings a curse and causes bitter suffering will enter her.
chapters.zh: 又叫妇人喝这致咒诅的苦水。这水要进入她里面变苦了。

chapters.en: The priest is to take from her hands the grain offering for jealousy, wave it before the LORD and bring it to the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要从妇人的手中取那疑恨的素祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，拿到坛前。

chapters.en: The priest is then to take a handful of the grain offering as a memorial offering and burn it on the altar; after that, he is to have the woman drink the water.
chapters.zh: 又要从素祭中取出一把，作为这事的纪念，烧在坛上，然后叫妇人喝这水。

chapters.en: If she has made herself impure and been unfaithful to her husband, this will be the result: When she is made to drink the water that brings a curse and causes bitter suffering, it will enter her, her abdomen will swell and her womb will miscarry, and she will become a curse.
chapters.zh: 叫她喝了以后，她若被玷污，得罪了丈夫，这致咒诅的水必进入她里面变苦了，她的肚腹就要发胀，大腿就要消瘦，那妇人便要在他民中被人咒诅。

chapters.en: If, however, the woman has not made herself impure, but is clean, she will be cleared of guilt and will be able to have children.
chapters.zh: 若妇人没有被玷污，却是清洁的，就要免受这灾，且要怀孕。

chapters.en: “ ‘This, then, is the law of jealousy when a woman goes astray and makes herself impure while married to her husband,
chapters.zh: 妻子背着丈夫行了污秽的事，

chapters.en: or when feelings of jealousy come over a man because he suspects his wife. The priest is to have her stand before the LORD and is to apply this entire law to her.
chapters.zh: 或是人生了疑恨的心，疑恨他的妻，就有这疑恨的条例。那时他要叫妇人站在耶和华面前，祭司要在她身上照这条例而行。

chapters.en: The husband will be innocent of any wrongdoing, but the woman will bear the consequences of her sin.’ ”
chapters.zh: 男人就为无罪，妇人必担当自己的罪孽。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘If a man or woman wants to make a special vow, a vow of dedication to the LORD as a Nazirite,
chapters.zh: 你晓谕以色列人说，无论男女许了特别的愿，就是拿细耳人的愿（拿细耳就是归主的意思下同），要离俗归耶和华。

chapters.en: they must abstain from wine and other fermented drink and must not drink vinegar made from wine or other fermented drink. They must not drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins.
chapters.zh: 他就要远离清酒浓酒，也不可喝什么清酒浓酒作的醋。不可喝什么葡萄汁，也不可吃鲜葡萄和干葡萄。

chapters.en: As long as they remain under their Nazirite vow, they must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.
chapters.zh: 在一切离俗的日子，凡葡萄树上结的，自核至皮所作的物，都不可吃。

chapters.en: “ ‘During the entire period of their Nazirite vow, no razor may be used on their head. They must be holy until the period of their dedication to the LORD is over; they must let their hair grow long.
chapters.zh: 在他一切许愿离俗的日子，不可用剃头刀剃头，要由发绺长长了。他要圣洁，直到离俗归耶和华的日子满了。

chapters.en: “ ‘Throughout the period of their dedication to the LORD, the Nazirite must not go near a dead body.
chapters.zh: 在他离俗归耶和华的一切日子，不可挨近死尸。

chapters.en: Even if their own father or mother or brother or sister dies, they must not make themselves ceremonially unclean on account of them, because the symbol of their dedication to God is on their head.
chapters.zh: 他的父母或是弟兄姐妹死了的时候，他不可因他们使自己不洁净，因为那离俗归神的凭据是在他头上。

chapters.en: Throughout the period of their dedication, they are consecrated to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 在他一切离俗的日子是归耶和华为圣。

chapters.en: “ ‘If someone dies suddenly in the Nazirite’s presence, thus defiling the hair that symbolizes their dedication, they must shave their head on the seventh day—the day of their cleansing.
chapters.zh: 若在他旁边忽然有人死了，以致沾染了他离俗的头，他要在第七日，得洁净的时候，剃头。

chapters.en: Then on the eighth day they must bring two doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 第八日，他要把两只斑鸠或两只雏鸽带到会幕门口，交给祭司。

chapters.en: The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make atonement for the Nazirite because they sinned by being in the presence of the dead body. That same day they are to consecrate their head again.
chapters.zh: 祭司要献一只作赎罪祭，一只作燔祭，为他赎那因死尸而有的罪，并要当日使他的头成为圣洁。

chapters.en: They must rededicate themselves to the LORD for the same period of dedication and must bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The previous days do not count, because they became defiled during their period of dedication.
chapters.zh: 他要另选离俗归耶和华的日子，又要牵一只一岁的公羊羔来作赎愆祭。但先前的日子要归徒然，因为他在离俗之间被玷污了。

chapters.en: “ ‘Now this is the law of the Nazirite when the period of their dedication is over. They are to be brought to the entrance to the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 拿细耳人满了离俗的日子乃有这条例，人要领他到会幕门口，

chapters.en: There they are to present their offerings to the LORD: a year-old male lamb without defect for a burnt offering, a year-old ewe lamb without defect for a sin offering, a ram without defect for a fellowship offering,
chapters.zh: 他要将供物奉给耶和华，就是一只没有残疾，一岁的公羊羔作燔祭，一只没有残疾，一岁的母羊羔作赎罪祭，和一只没有残疾的公绵羊作平安祭，

chapters.en: together with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and a basket of bread made with the finest flour and without yeast—thick loaves with olive oil mixed in, and thin loaves brushed with olive oil.
chapters.zh: 并一筐子无酵调油的细面饼，与抹油的无酵薄饼，并同献的素祭和奠祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘The priest is to present all these before the LORD and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 祭司要在耶和华面前献那人的赎罪祭和燔祭。

chapters.en: He is to present the basket of unleavened bread and is to sacrifice the ram as a fellowship offering to the LORD, together with its grain offering and drink offering.
chapters.zh: 也要把那只公羊和那筐无酵饼献给耶和华作平安祭，又要将同献的素祭和奠祭献上。

chapters.en: “ ‘Then at the entrance to the tent of meeting, the Nazirite must shave off the hair that symbolizes their dedication. They are to take the hair and put it in the fire that is under the sacrifice of the fellowship offering.
chapters.zh: 拿细耳人要在会幕门口剃离俗的头，把离俗头上的发放在平安祭下的火上。

chapters.en: “ ‘After the Nazirite has shaved off the hair that symbolizes their dedication, the priest is to place in their hands a boiled shoulder of the ram, and one thick loaf and one thin loaf from the basket, both made without yeast.
chapters.zh: 他剃了以后，祭司就要取那已煮的公羊一条前腿，又从筐子里取一个无酵饼和一个无酵薄饼，都放在他手上。

chapters.en: The priest shall then wave these before the LORD as a wave offering; they are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast that was waved and the thigh that was presented. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.
chapters.zh: 祭司要拿这些作为摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇。这与所摇的胸，所举的腿同为圣物，归给祭司。然后拿细耳人可以喝酒。

chapters.en: “ ‘This is the law of the Nazirite who vows offerings to the LORD in accordance with their dedication, in addition to whatever else they can afford. They must fulfill the vows they have made, according to the law of the Nazirite.’ ”
chapters.zh: 许愿的拿细耳人为离俗所献的供物，和他以外所能得的献给耶和华，就有这条例。他怎样许愿就当照离俗的条例行。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Tell Aaron and his sons, ‘This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
chapters.zh: 你告诉亚伦和他儿子说，你们要这样为以色列人祝福，说，

chapters.en: “ ‘ “The LORD bless you and keep you;
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华赐福给你，保护你。

chapters.en: the LORD make his face shine on you and be gracious to you;
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华使他的脸光照你，赐恩给你。

chapters.en: the LORD turn his face toward you and give you peace.” ’
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华向你仰脸，赐你平安。

chapters.en: “So they will put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.”
chapters.zh: 他们要如此奉我的名为以色列人祝福。我也要赐福给他们。

chapters.en: When Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings. He also anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils.
chapters.zh: 摩西立完了帐幕，就把帐幕用膏抹了，使它成圣，又把其中的器具和坛，并坛上的器具，都抹了，使它成圣。

chapters.en: Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of families who were the tribal leaders in charge of those who were counted, made offerings.
chapters.zh: 当天，以色列的众首领，就是各族的族长，都来奉献。他们是各支派的首领，管理那些被数的人。

chapters.en: They brought as their gifts before the LORD six covered carts and twelve oxen—an ox from each leader and a cart from every two. These they presented before the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 他们把自己的供物送到耶和华面前，就是六辆篷子车和十二只公牛。每两个首领奉献一辆车，每首领奉献一只牛。他们把这些都奉到帐幕前。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Accept these from them, that they may be used in the work at the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites as each man’s work requires.”
chapters.zh: 你要收下这些，好作会幕的使用，都要照利未人所办的事交给他们。

chapters.en: So Moses took the carts and oxen and gave them to the Levites.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西收了车和牛，交给利未人，

chapters.en: He gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites, as their work required,
chapters.zh: 把两辆车，四只牛，照革顺子孙所办的事交给他们，

chapters.en: and he gave four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites, as their work required. They were all under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.
chapters.zh: 又把四辆车，八只牛，照米拉利子孙所办的事交给他们。他们都在祭司亚伦的儿子以他玛手下。

chapters.en: But Moses did not give any to the Kohathites, because they were to carry on their shoulders the holy things, for which they were responsible.
chapters.zh: 但车与牛都没有交给哥辖子孙。因为他们办的是圣所的事，在肩头上抬圣物。

chapters.en: When the altar was anointed, the leaders brought their offerings for its dedication and presented them before the altar.
chapters.zh: 用膏抹坛的日子，首领都来行奉献坛的礼，众首领就在坛前献供物。

chapters.en: For the LORD had said to Moses, “Each day one leader is to bring his offering for the dedication of the altar.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说，众首领为行奉献坛的礼，要每天一个首领来献供物。

chapters.en: The one who brought his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah.
chapters.zh: 头一日献供物的是犹大支派的亚米拿达的儿子拿顺。

chapters.en: His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;
chapters.zh: 他的供物是，一个银盘子，重一百三十舍客勒，一个银碗，重七十舍客勒，都是按圣所的平，也都盛满了调油的细面作素祭。

chapters.en: one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
chapters.zh: 一个金盂，重十舍客勒，盛满了香。

chapters.en: one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
chapters.zh: 一只公牛犊，一只公绵羊，一只一岁的公羊羔作燔祭。

chapters.en: one male goat for a sin offering ;
chapters.zh: 一只公山羊作赎罪祭。

chapters.en: and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
chapters.zh: 两只公牛，五只公绵羊，五只公山羊，五只一岁的公羊羔作平安祭。这是亚米拿达儿子拿顺的供物。

chapters.en: On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his offering.
chapters.zh: 第二日来献的是以萨迦子孙的首领，苏押的儿子拿坦业。

chapters.en: The offering he brought was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel, each filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering;

chapters.en: These were the offerings of the Israelite leaders for the dedication of the altar when it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver sprinkling bowls and twelve gold dishes.
chapters.zh: 用膏抹坛的日子，以色列的众首领为行献坛之礼所献的是，银盘子十二个，银碗十二个，金盂十二个。

chapters.en: Each silver plate weighed a hundred and thirty shekels, and each sprinkling bowl seventy shekels. Altogether, the silver dishes weighed two thousand four hundred shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
chapters.zh: 每盘子重一百三十舍客勒，每碗重七十舍客勒。一切器皿的银子，按圣所的平，共有二千四百舍客勒。

chapters.en: The twelve gold dishes filled with incense weighed ten shekels each, according to the sanctuary shekel. Altogether, the gold dishes weighed a hundred and twenty shekels.
chapters.zh: 十二个金盂盛满了香，按圣所的平，每盂重十舍客勒，所有的金子共一百二十舍客勒。

chapters.en: The total number of animals for the burnt offering came to twelve young bulls, twelve rams and twelve male lambs a year old, together with their grain offering. Twelve male goats were used for the sin offering.
chapters.zh: 作燔祭的，共有公牛十二只，公羊十二只，一岁的公羊羔十二只，并同献的素祭作赎罪祭的公山羊十二只。

chapters.en: The total number of animals for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering came to twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty male goats and sixty male lambs a year old. These were the offerings for the dedication of the altar after it was anointed.
chapters.zh: 作平安祭的，共有公牛二十四只，公绵羊六十只，公山羊六十只，一岁的公羊羔六十只。这就是用膏抹坛之后，为行奉献坛之礼所献的。

chapters.en: When Moses entered the tent of meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the atonement cover on the ark of the covenant law. In this way the LORD spoke to him.
chapters.zh: 摩西进会幕要与耶和华说话的时候，听见法柜的施恩座以上，二基路伯中间有与他说话的声音，就是耶和华与他说话。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Speak to Aaron and say to him, ‘When you set up the lamps, see that all seven light up the area in front of the lampstand.’ ”
chapters.zh: 你告诉亚伦说，点灯的时候，七盏灯都要向灯台前面发光。

chapters.en: Aaron did so; he set up the lamps so that they faced forward on the lampstand, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 亚伦便这样行。他点灯台上的灯，使灯向前发光，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: This is how the lampstand was made: It was made of hammered gold—from its base to its blossoms. The lampstand was made exactly like the pattern the LORD had shown Moses.
chapters.zh: 这灯台的作法是用金子锤出来的，连座带花都是锤出来的。摩西制造灯台，是照耶和华所指示的样式。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说，

chapters.en: “Take the Levites from among all the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.
chapters.zh: 你从以色列人中选出利未人来，洁净他们。

chapters.en: To purify them, do this: Sprinkle the water of cleansing on them; then have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes. And so they will purify themselves.
chapters.zh: 洁净他们当这样行，用除罪水弹在他们身上，又叫他们用剃头刀刮全身，洗衣服，洁净自己。

chapters.en: Have them take a young bull with its grain offering of the finest flour mixed with olive oil; then you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 然后叫他们取一只公牛犊，并同献的素祭，就是调油的细面。你要另取一只公牛犊作赎罪祭。

chapters.en: Bring the Levites to the front of the tent of meeting and assemble the whole Israelite community.
chapters.zh: 将利未人奉到会幕前，招聚以色列全会众。

chapters.en: You are to bring the Levites before the LORD, and the Israelites are to lay their hands on them.
chapters.zh: 将利未人奉到耶和华面前，以色列人要按手在他们头上。

chapters.en: Aaron is to present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the Israelites, so that they may be ready to do the work of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 亚伦也将他们奉到耶和华面前，为以色列人当作摇祭，使他们好办耶和华的事。

chapters.en: “Then the Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, using one for a sin offering to the LORD and the other for a burnt offering, to make atonement for the Levites.
chapters.zh: 利未人要按手在那两只牛的头上。你要将一只作赎罪祭，一只作燔祭，献给耶和华，为利未人赎罪。

chapters.en: Have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons and then present them as a wave offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你也要使利未人站在亚伦和他儿子面前，将他们当作摇祭奉给耶和华。

chapters.en: In this way you are to set the Levites apart from the other Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
chapters.zh: 这样，你从以色列人中将利未人分别出来，利未人便要归我。

chapters.en: “After you have purified the Levites and presented them as a wave offering, they are to come to do their work at the tent of meeting.
chapters.zh: 此后利未人要进去办会幕的事，你要洁净他们，将他们当作摇祭奉上。

chapters.en: They are the Israelites who are to be given wholly to me. I have taken them as my own in place of the firstborn, the first male offspring from every Israelite woman.
chapters.zh: 因为他们是从以色列人中全然给我的，我拣选他们归我，是代替以色列人中一切头生的。

chapters.en: Every firstborn male in Israel, whether human or animal, is mine. When I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set them apart for myself.
chapters.zh: 以色列人中一切头生的，连人带牲畜，都是我的。我在埃及地击杀一切头生的那天，将他们分别为圣归我。

chapters.en: And I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons in Israel.
chapters.zh: 我拣选利未人代替以色列人中一切头生的。

chapters.en: From among all the Israelites, I have given the Levites as gifts to Aaron and his sons to do the work at the tent of meeting on behalf of the Israelites and to make atonement for them so that no plague will strike the Israelites when they go near the sanctuary.”
chapters.zh: 我从以色列人中将利未人当作赏赐给亚伦和他的儿子，在会幕中办以色列人的事，又为以色列人赎罪，免得他们挨近圣所，有灾殃临到他们中间。

chapters.en: Moses, Aaron and the whole Israelite community did with the Levites just as the LORD commanded Moses.
