chapters.en: “Next they traveled through the wilderness, skirted the lands of Edom and Moab, passed along the eastern side of the country of Moab, and camped on the other side of the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was its border.
chapters.zh: 他们又经过旷野，绕着以东和摩押地，从摩押地的东边过来，在亚嫩河边安营，并没有入摩押的境内，因为亚嫩河是摩押的边界。

chapters.en: “Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, ‘Let us pass through your country to our own place.’
chapters.zh: 以色列人打发使者去见亚摩利王西宏，就是希实本的王，对他说，求你容我们从你的地经过，往我们自己的地方去。

chapters.en: Sihon, however, did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. He mustered all his troops and encamped at Jahaz and fought with Israel.
chapters.zh: 西宏却不信服以色列人，不容他们经过他的境界，乃招聚他的众民在雅杂安营，与以色列人争战。

chapters.en: “Then the LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and his whole army into Israel’s hands, and they defeated them. Israel took over all the land of the Amorites who lived in that country,
chapters.zh: 耶和华以色列的神将西宏和他的众民都交在以色列人手中，以色列人就击杀他们，得了亚摩利人的全地，

chapters.en: capturing all of it from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the desert to the Jordan.
chapters.zh: 从亚嫩河到雅博河，从旷野直到约旦河。

chapters.en: “Now since the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven the Amorites out before his people Israel, what right have you to take it over?
chapters.zh: 耶和华以色列的神在他百姓以色列面前赶出亚摩利人，你竟要得他们的地吗？

chapters.en: Will you not take what your god Chemosh gives you? Likewise, whatever the LORD our God has given us, we will possess.
chapters.zh: 你的神基抹所赐你的地你不是得为业吗？耶和华我们的神在我们面前所赶出的人，我们就得他的地。

chapters.en: Are you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel or fight with them?
chapters.zh: 难道你比摩押王西拨的儿子巴勒还强吗？他曾与以色列人争竞，或是与他们争战吗？

chapters.en: For three hundred years Israel occupied Heshbon, Aroer, the surrounding settlements and all the towns along the Arnon. Why didn’t you retake them during that time?
chapters.zh: 以色列人住希实本和属希实本的乡村，亚罗珥和属亚罗珥的乡村，并沿亚嫩河的一切城邑，已经有三百年了。在这三百年之内，你们为什么没有取回这些地方呢？

chapters.en: I have not wronged you, but you are doing me wrong by waging war against me. Let the LORD, the Judge, decide the dispute this day between the Israelites and the Ammonites.”
chapters.zh: 原来我没有得罪你，你却攻打我，恶待我。愿审判人的耶和华今日在以色列人和亚扪人中间判断是非。

chapters.en: The king of Ammon, however, paid no attention to the message Jephthah sent him.
chapters.zh: 但亚扪人的王不肯听耶弗他打发人说的话。

chapters.en: Then the Spirit of the LORD came on Jephthah. He crossed Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from there he advanced against the Ammonites.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵降在耶弗他身上，他就经过基列和玛拿西，来到基列的米斯巴，又从米斯巴来到亚扪人那里。

chapters.en: And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD: “If you give the Ammonites into my hands,
chapters.zh: 耶弗他就向耶和华许愿，说，你若将亚扪人交在我手中，

chapters.en: whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return in triumph from the Ammonites will be the LORD’s, and I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering.”
chapters.zh: 我从亚扪人那里平平安安回来的时候，无论什么人，先从我家门出来迎接我，就必归你，我也必将他献上为燔祭。

chapters.en: Then Jephthah went over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into his hands.
chapters.zh: 于是耶弗他往亚扪人那里去，与他们争战。耶和华将他们交在他手中，

chapters.en: He devastated twenty towns from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith, as far as Abel Keramim. Thus Israel subdued Ammon.
chapters.zh: 他就大大杀败他们，从亚罗珥到米匿，直到亚备勒基拉明，攻取了二十座城。这样亚扪人就被以色列人制伏了。

chapters.en: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, who should come out to meet him but his daughter, dancing to the sound of timbrels! She was an only child. Except for her he had neither son nor daughter.
chapters.zh: 耶弗他回米斯巴到了自己的家，不料，他女儿拿着鼓跳舞出来迎接他，是他独生的，此外无儿无女。

chapters.en: When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, “Oh no, my daughter! You have brought me down and I am devastated. I have made a vow to the LORD that I cannot break.”
chapters.zh: 耶弗他看见她，就撕裂衣服，说，哀哉。我的女儿阿，你使我甚是愁苦，叫我作难了。因为我已经向耶和华开口许愿，不能挽回。

chapters.en: “My father,” she replied, “you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me just as you promised, now that the LORD has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites.
chapters.zh: 他女儿回答说，父阿，你既向耶和华开口，就当照你口中所说的向我行，因耶和华已经在仇敌亚扪人身上为你报仇。

chapters.en: But grant me this one request,” she said. “Give me two months to roam the hills and weep with my friends, because I will never marry.”
chapters.zh: 又对父亲说，有一件事求你允准，容我去两个月，与同伴在山上，好哀哭我终为处女。

chapters.en: “You may go,” he said. And he let her go for two months. She and her friends went into the hills and wept because she would never marry.
chapters.zh: 耶弗他说，你去吧。就容她去两个月。她便和同伴去了，在山上为她终为处女哀哭。

chapters.en: After the two months, she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. And she was a virgin. From this comes the Israelite tradition
chapters.zh: 两月已满，她回到父亲那里，父亲就照所许的愿向她行了。女儿终身没有亲近男子。

chapters.en: that each year the young women of Israel go out for four days to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.
chapters.zh: 此后以色列中有个规矩，每年以色列的女子去为基列人耶弗他的女儿哀哭四天。

chapters.en: The Ephraimite forces were called out, and they crossed over to Zaphon. They said to Jephthah, “Why did you go to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We’re going to burn down your house over your head.”
chapters.zh: 以法莲人聚集，到了北方，对耶弗他说，你去与亚扪人争战，为什么没有招我们同去呢？我们必用火烧你和你的房屋。

chapters.en: Jephthah answered, “I and my people were engaged in a great struggle with the Ammonites, and although I called, you didn’t save me out of their hands.
chapters.zh: 耶弗他对他们说，我和我的民与亚扪人大大争战。我招你们来，你们竟没有来救我脱离他们的手。

chapters.en: When I saw that you wouldn’t help, I took my life in my hands and crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave me the victory over them. Now why have you come up today to fight me?”
chapters.zh: 我见你们不来救我，我就拚命前去攻击亚扪人，耶和华将他们交在我手中。你们今日为什么上我这里来攻打我呢？

chapters.en: Jephthah then called together the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. The Gileadites struck them down because the Ephraimites had said, “You Gileadites are renegades from Ephraim and Manasseh.”
chapters.zh: 于是耶弗他招聚基列人，与以法莲人争战。基列人击杀以法莲人，是因他们说，你们基列人在以法莲，玛拿西中间，不过是以法莲逃亡的人。

chapters.en: The Gileadites captured the fords of the Jordan leading to Ephraim, and whenever a survivor of Ephraim said, “Let me cross over,” the men of Gilead asked him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he replied, “No,”
chapters.zh: 基列人把守约旦河的渡口，不容以法莲人过去。以法莲逃走的人若说，容我过去。基列人就问他说，你是以法莲人不是。他若说，不是，

chapters.en: they said, “All right, say ‘Shibboleth.’ ” If he said, “Sibboleth,” because he could not pronounce the word correctly, they seized him and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand Ephraimites were killed at that time.
chapters.zh: 就对他说，你说示播列。以法莲人因为咬不真字音，便说西播列。基列人就将他拿住，杀在约旦河的渡口。那时以法莲人被杀的有四万二千人。

chapters.en: Jephthah led Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in a town in Gilead.
chapters.zh: 耶弗他作以色列的士师六年。基列人耶弗他死了，葬在基列的一座城里。

chapters.en: After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem led Israel.
chapters.zh: 耶弗他以后，有伯利恒人以比赞作以色列的士师。

chapters.en: He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He gave his daughters away in marriage to those outside his clan, and for his sons he brought in thirty young women as wives from outside his clan. Ibzan led Israel seven years.
chapters.zh: 他有三十个儿子，三十个女儿。女儿都嫁出去了。他给众子从外乡娶了三十个媳妇。他作以色列的士师七年。

chapters.en: Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
chapters.zh: 以比赞死了，葬在伯利恒。

chapters.en: After him, Elon the Zebulunite led Israel ten years.
chapters.zh: 以比赞之后，有西布伦人以伦，作以色列的士师十年。

chapters.en: Then Elon died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
chapters.zh: 西布伦人以伦死了，葬在西布伦地的亚雅仑。

chapters.en: After him, Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, led Israel.
chapters.zh: 以伦之后，有比拉顿人希列的儿子押顿作以色列的士师。

chapters.en: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He led Israel eight years.
chapters.zh: 他有四十个儿子，三十个孙子，骑着七十匹驴驹。押顿作以色列的士师八年。

chapters.en: Then Abdon son of Hillel died and was buried at Pirathon in Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
chapters.zh: 比拉顿人希列的儿子押顿死了，葬在以法莲地的比拉顿，在亚玛力人的山地。

chapters.en: Again the Israelites did evil in the eyes of the LORD, so the LORD delivered them into the hands of the Philistines for forty years.
chapters.zh: 以色列人又行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，耶和华将他们交在非利士人手中四十年。

chapters.en: A certain man of Zorah, named Manoah, from the clan of the Danites, had a wife who was childless, unable to give birth.
chapters.zh: 那时，有一个琐拉人，是属但族的，名叫玛挪亚。他的妻不怀孕，不生育。

chapters.en: The angel of the LORD appeared to her and said, “You are barren and childless, but you are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的使者向那妇人显现，对她说，向来你不怀孕，不生育，如今你必怀孕生一个儿子。

chapters.en: Now see to it that you drink no wine or other fermented drink and that you do not eat anything unclean.
chapters.zh: 所以你当谨慎，清酒浓酒都不可喝，一切不洁之物也不可吃。

chapters.en: You will become pregnant and have a son whose head is never to be touched by a razor because the boy is to be a Nazirite, dedicated to God from the womb. He will take the lead in delivering Israel from the hands of the Philistines.”
chapters.zh: 你必怀孕生一个儿子，不可用剃头刀剃他的头，因为这孩子一出胎就归神作拿细耳人。他必起首拯救以色列人脱离非利士人的手。

chapters.en: Then the woman went to her husband and told him, “A man of God came to me. He looked like an angel of God, very awesome. I didn’t ask him where he came from, and he didn’t tell me his name.
chapters.zh: 妇人就回去对丈夫说，有一个神人到我面前来，他的相貌如神使者的相貌，甚是可畏。我没有问他从哪里来，他也没有将他的名告诉我，

chapters.en: But he said to me, ‘You will become pregnant and have a son. Now then, drink no wine or other fermented drink and do not eat anything unclean, because the boy will be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day of his death.’ ”
chapters.zh: 却对我说，你要怀孕生一个儿子，所以清酒浓酒都不可喝，一切不洁之物也不可吃。因为这孩子从出胎一直到死，必归神作拿细耳人。

chapters.en: Then Manoah prayed to the LORD: “Pardon your servant, Lord. I beg you to let the man of God you sent to us come again to teach us how to bring up the boy who is to be born.”
chapters.zh: 玛挪亚就祈求耶和华说，主阿，求你再差遣那神人到我们这里来，好指教我们怎样待这将要生的孩子。

chapters.en: God heard Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was out in the field; but her husband Manoah was not with her.
chapters.zh: 神应允玛挪亚的话。妇人正坐在田间的时候，神的使者又到她那里，她丈夫玛挪亚却没有同她在一处。

chapters.en: The woman hurried to tell her husband, “He’s here! The man who appeared to me the other day!”
chapters.zh: 妇人急忙跑去告诉丈夫说，那日到我面前来的人，又向我显现。

chapters.en: Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he said, “Are you the man who talked to my wife?” “I am,” he said.
chapters.zh: 玛挪亚起来跟随他的妻来到那人面前，对他说，与这妇人说话的就是你吗？他说，是我。

chapters.en: So Manoah asked him, “When your words are fulfilled, what is to be the rule that governs the boy’s life and work?”
chapters.zh: 玛挪亚说，愿你的话应验。我们当怎样待这孩子，他后来当怎样呢？

chapters.en: The angel of the LORD answered, “Your wife must do all that I have told her.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的使者对玛挪亚说，我告诉妇人的一切事，她都当谨慎。

chapters.en: She must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, nor drink any wine or other fermented drink nor eat anything unclean. She must do everything I have commanded her.”
chapters.zh: 葡萄树所结的都不可吃，清酒浓酒都不可喝，一切不洁之物也不可吃。凡我所吩咐的，她都当遵守。

chapters.en: Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “We would like you to stay until we prepare a young goat for you.”
chapters.zh: 玛挪亚对耶和华的使者说，求你容我们款留你，好为你预备一只山羊羔。

chapters.en: The angel of the LORD replied, “Even though you detain me, I will not eat any of your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” (Manoah did not realize that it was the angel of the LORD.)
chapters.zh: 耶和华的使者对玛挪亚说，你虽然款留我，我却不吃你的食物，你若预备燔祭就当献与耶和华。原来玛挪亚不知道他是耶和华的使者。

chapters.en: Then Manoah inquired of the angel of the LORD, “What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes true?”
chapters.zh: 玛挪亚对耶和华的使者说，请将你的名告诉我，到你话应验的时候，我们好尊敬你。

chapters.en: He replied, “Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding. ”
chapters.zh: 耶和华的使者对他说，你何必问我的名，我名是奇妙的。

chapters.en: Then Manoah took a young goat, together with the grain offering, and sacrificed it on a rock to the LORD. And the LORD did an amazing thing while Manoah and his wife watched:
chapters.zh: 玛挪亚将一只山羊羔和素祭在磐石上献与耶和华，使者行奇妙的事。玛挪亚和他的妻观看，

chapters.en: As the flame blazed up from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame. Seeing this, Manoah and his wife fell with their faces to the ground.
chapters.zh: 见火焰从坛上往上升，耶和华的使者在坛上的火焰中也升上去了。玛挪亚和他的妻看见，就俯伏于地。

chapters.en: When the angel of the LORD did not show himself again to Manoah and his wife, Manoah realized that it was the angel of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的使者不再向玛挪亚和他的妻显现，玛挪亚才知道他是耶和华的使者。

chapters.en: “We are doomed to die!” he said to his wife. “We have seen God!”
chapters.zh: 玛挪亚对他的妻说，我们必要死，因为看见了神。

chapters.en: But his wife answered, “If the LORD had meant to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hands, nor shown us all these things or now told us this.”
chapters.zh: 他的妻却对他说，耶和华若要杀我们，必不从我们手里收纳燔祭和素祭，并不将这一切事指示我们，今日也不将这些话告诉我们。

chapters.en: The woman gave birth to a boy and named him Samson. He grew and the LORD blessed him,
chapters.zh: 后来妇人生了一个儿子，给他起名叫参孙。孩子长大，耶和华赐福与他。

chapters.en: and the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him while he was in Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
chapters.zh: 在玛哈尼但，就是琐拉和以实陶中间，耶和华的灵才感动他。

chapters.en: Samson went down to Timnah and saw there a young Philistine woman.
chapters.zh: 参孙下到亭拿，在那里看见一个女子，是非利士人的女儿。

chapters.en: When he returned, he said to his father and mother, “I have seen a Philistine woman in Timnah; now get her for me as my wife.”
chapters.zh: 参孙上来禀告他父母说，我在亭拿看见一个女子，是非利士人的女儿，愿你们给我娶来为妻。

chapters.en: His father and mother replied, “Isn’t there an acceptable woman among your relatives or among all our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?” But Samson said to his father, “Get her for me. She’s the right one for me.”
chapters.zh: 他父母说，在你弟兄的女儿中，或在本国的民中，岂没有一个女子，何至你去在未受割礼的非利士人中娶妻呢？参孙对他父亲说，愿你给我娶那女子，因我喜悦她。

chapters.en: (His parents did not know that this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion to confront the Philistines; for at that time they were ruling over Israel.)
chapters.zh: 他的父母却不知道这事是出于耶和华，因为他找机会攻击非利士人。那时，非利士人辖制以色列人。

chapters.en: Samson went down to Timnah together with his father and mother. As they approached the vineyards of Timnah, suddenly a young lion came roaring toward him.
chapters.zh: 参孙跟他父母下亭拿去，到了亭拿的葡萄园，见有一只少壮狮子向他吼叫。

chapters.en: The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him so that he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as he might have torn a young goat. But he told neither his father nor his mother what he had done.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵大大感动参孙，他虽然手无器械，却将狮子撕裂，如同撕裂山羊羔一样。他行这事并没有告诉父母。

chapters.en: Then he went down and talked with the woman, and he liked her.
chapters.zh: 参孙下去与女子说话，就喜悦她。

chapters.en: Some time later, when he went back to marry her, he turned aside to look at the lion’s carcass, and in it he saw a swarm of bees and some honey.
chapters.zh: 过了些日子，再下去要娶那女子，转向道旁要看死狮，见有一群蜂子和蜜在死狮之内，

chapters.en: He scooped out the honey with his hands and ate as he went along. When he rejoined his parents, he gave them some, and they too ate it. But he did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the lion’s carcass.
chapters.zh: 就用手取蜜，且吃且走。到了父母那里，给他父母，他们也吃了。只是没有告诉这蜜是从死狮之内取来的。

chapters.en: Now his father went down to see the woman. And there Samson held a feast, as was customary for young men.
chapters.zh: 他父亲下去见女子。参孙在那里设摆筵宴，因为向来少年人都有这个规矩。

chapters.en: When the people saw him, they chose thirty men to be his companions.
chapters.zh: 众人看见参孙，就请了三十个人陪伴他。

chapters.en: “Let me tell you a riddle,” Samson said to them. “If you can give me the answer within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.
chapters.zh: 参孙对他们说，我给你们出一个谜语，你们在七日筵宴之内，若能猜出意思告诉我，我就给你们三十件里衣，三十套衣裳。

chapters.en: If you can’t tell me the answer, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.” “Tell us your riddle,” they said. “Let’s hear it.”
chapters.zh: 你们若不能猜出意思告诉我，你们就给我三十件里衣，三十套衣裳。他们说，请将谜语说给我们听。

chapters.en: He replied, “Out of the eater, something to eat; out of the strong, something sweet.” For three days they could not give the answer.
chapters.zh: 参孙对他们说，吃的从吃者出来。甜的从强者出来。他们三日不能猜出谜语的意思。

chapters.en: On the fourth day, they said to Samson’s wife, “Coax your husband into explaining the riddle for us, or we will burn you and your father’s household to death. Did you invite us here to steal our property?”
chapters.zh: 到第七天，他们对参孙的妻说，你诓哄你丈夫，探出谜语的意思告诉我们，免得我们用火烧你和你父家。你们请了我们来，是要夺我们所有的吗？

chapters.en: Then Samson’s wife threw herself on him, sobbing, “You hate me! You don’t really love me. You’ve given my people a riddle, but you haven’t told me the answer.” “I haven’t even explained it to my father or mother,” he replied, “so why should I explain it to you?”
chapters.zh: 参孙的妻在丈夫面前啼哭说，你是恨我，不是爱我，你给我本国的人出谜语，却没有将意思告诉我。参孙回答说，连我父母我都没有告诉，岂可告诉你呢？

chapters.en: She cried the whole seven days of the feast. So on the seventh day he finally told her, because she continued to press him. She in turn explained the riddle to her people.
chapters.zh: 七日筵宴之内，她在丈夫面前啼哭，到第七天逼着他，他才将谜语的意思告诉他妻，他妻就告诉本国的人。

chapters.en: Before sunset on the seventh day the men of the town said to him, “What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?” Samson said to them, “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle.”
chapters.zh: 到第七天，日头未落以前，那城里的人对参孙说，有什么比蜜还甜呢？有什么比狮子还强呢？参孙对他们说，你们若非用我的母牛犊耕地，就猜不出我谜语的意思来。

chapters.en: Then the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him. He went down to Ashkelon, struck down thirty of their men, stripped them of everything and gave their clothes to those who had explained the riddle. Burning with anger, he returned to his father’s home.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵大大感动参孙，他就下到亚实基伦，击杀了三十个人，夺了他们的衣裳，将衣裳给了猜出谜语的人。参孙发怒，就上父家去了。

chapters.en: And Samson’s wife was given to one of his companions who had attended him at the feast.
chapters.zh: 参孙的妻便归了参孙的陪伴，就是作过他朋友的。

chapters.en: Later on, at the time of wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife. He said, “I’m going to my wife’s room.” But her father would not let him go in.
chapters.zh: 过了些日子，到割麦子的时候，参孙带着一只山羊羔去看他的妻，说，我要进内室见我的妻。他岳父不容他进去，

chapters.en: “I was so sure you hated her,” he said, “that I gave her to your companion. Isn’t her younger sister more attractive? Take her instead.”
chapters.zh: 说，我估定你是极其恨她，因此我将她给了你的陪伴。她的妹子不是比她还美丽吗？你可以娶来代替她吧。

chapters.en: Samson said to them, “This time I have a right to get even with the Philistines; I will really harm them.”
chapters.zh: 参孙说，这回我加害于非利士人不算有罪。

chapters.en: So he went out and caught three hundred foxes and tied them tail to tail in pairs. He then fastened a torch to every pair of tails,
chapters.zh: 于是参孙去捉了三百只狐狸（或作野狗），将狐狸尾巴一对一对地捆上，将火把捆在两条尾巴中间，

chapters.en: lit the torches and let the foxes loose in the standing grain of the Philistines. He burned up the shocks and standing grain, together with the vineyards and olive groves.
chapters.zh: 点着火把，就放狐狸进入非利士人站着的禾稼，将堆集的禾捆和未割的禾稼，并橄榄园尽都烧了。

chapters.en: When the Philistines asked, “Who did this?” they were told, “Samson, the Timnite’s son-in-law, because his wife was given to his companion.” So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.
chapters.zh: 非利士人说，这事是谁作的呢？有人说，是亭拿人的女婿参孙，因为他岳父将他的妻给了他的陪伴。于是非利士人上去，用火烧了妇人和她的父亲。

chapters.en: Samson said to them, “Since you’ve acted like this, I swear that I won’t stop until I get my revenge on you.”
chapters.zh: 参孙对非利士人说，你们既然这样行，我必向你们报仇才肯罢休。

chapters.en: He attacked them viciously and slaughtered many of them. Then he went down and stayed in a cave in the rock of Etam.
chapters.zh: 参孙就大大击杀他们，连腿带腰都砍断了。他便下去，住在以坦磐的穴内。

chapters.en: The Philistines went up and camped in Judah, spreading out near Lehi.
chapters.zh: 非利士人上去安营在犹大，布散在利希。

chapters.en: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you come to fight us?” “We have come to take Samson prisoner,” they answered, “to do to him as he did to us.”
chapters.zh: 犹大人说，你们为何上来攻击我们呢？他们说，我们上来是要捆绑参孙。他向我们怎样行，我们也要向他怎样行。

chapters.en: Then three thousand men from Judah went down to the cave in the rock of Etam and said to Samson, “Don’t you realize that the Philistines are rulers over us? What have you done to us?” He answered, “I merely did to them what they did to me.”
chapters.zh: 于是有三千犹大人下到以坦磐的穴内，对参孙说，非利士人辖制我们，你不知道吗？你向我们行的是什么事呢？他回答说，他们向我怎样行，我也要向他们怎样行。

chapters.en: They said to him, “We’ve come to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines.” Samson said, “Swear to me that you won’t kill me yourselves.”
chapters.zh: 犹大人对他说，我们下来是要捆绑你，将你交在非利士人手中。参孙说，你们要向我起誓，应承你们自己不害死我。

chapters.en: “Agreed,” they answered. “We will only tie you up and hand you over to them. We will not kill you.” So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.
chapters.zh: 他们说，我们断不杀你，只要将你捆绑交在非利士人手中。于是用两条新绳捆绑参孙，将他从以坦磐带上去。

chapters.en: As he approached Lehi, the Philistines came toward him shouting. The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him. The ropes on his arms became like charred flax, and the bindings dropped from his hands.
chapters.zh: 参孙到了利希，非利士人都迎着喧嚷。耶和华的灵大大感动参孙，他臂上的绳就像火烧的麻一样，他的绑绳都从他手上脱落下来。

chapters.en: Finding a fresh jawbone of a donkey, he grabbed it and struck down a thousand men.
chapters.zh: 他见一块未干的驴腮骨，就伸手拾起来，用以击杀一千人。

chapters.en: Then Samson said, “With a donkey’s jawbone I have made donkeys of them.With a donkey’s jawbone I have killed a thousand men.”
chapters.zh: 参孙说，我用驴腮骨杀人成堆，用驴腮骨杀了一千人。

chapters.en: When he finished speaking, he threw away the jawbone; and the place was called Ramath Lehi.
chapters.zh: 说完这话，就把那腮骨从手里抛出去了。那地便叫拉末利希。

chapters.en: Because he was very thirsty, he cried out to the LORD, “You have given your servant this great victory. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?”
chapters.zh: 参孙甚觉口渴，就求告耶和华说，你既借仆人的手施行这么大的拯救，岂可任我渴死，落在未受割礼的人手中呢？

chapters.en: Then God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it. When Samson drank, his strength returned and he revived. So the spring was called En Hakkore, and it is still there in Lehi.
chapters.zh: 神就使利希的洼处裂开，有水从其中涌出来。参孙喝了精神复原。因此那泉名叫隐哈歌利，那泉直到今日还在利希。

chapters.en: Samson led Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
chapters.zh: 当非利士人辖制以色列人的时候，参孙作以色列的士师二十年。

chapters.en: One day Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute. He went in to spend the night with her.
chapters.zh: 参孙到了迦萨，在那里看见一个妓女，就与她亲近。

chapters.en: The people of Gaza were told, “Samson is here!” So they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They made no move during the night, saying, “At dawn we’ll kill him.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉迦萨人说，参孙到这里来了。他们就把他团团围住，终夜在城门悄悄埋伏，说，等到天亮我们便杀他。

chapters.en: But Samson lay there only until the middle of the night. Then he got up and took hold of the doors of the city gate, together with the two posts, and tore them loose, bar and all. He lifted them to his shoulders and carried them to the top of the hill that faces Hebron.
chapters.zh: 参孙睡到半夜，起来，将城门的门扇，门框，门闩，一齐拆下来，扛在肩上，扛到希伯仑前的山顶上。

chapters.en: Some time later, he fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek whose name was Delilah.
chapters.zh: 后来参孙在梭烈谷喜爱一个妇人，名叫大利拉。

chapters.en: The rulers of the Philistines went to her and said, “See if you can lure him into showing you the secret of his great strength and how we can overpower him so we may tie him up and subdue him. Each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.”
chapters.zh: 非利士人的首领上去见那妇人，对她说，求你诓哄参孙，探探他因何有这么大的力气，我们用何法能胜他，捆绑克制他。我们就每人给你一千一百舍客勒银子。

chapters.en: So Delilah said to Samson, “Tell me the secret of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.”
chapters.zh: 大利拉对参孙说，求你告诉我，你因何有这么大的力气，当用何法捆绑克制你。

chapters.en: Samson answered her, “If anyone ties me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I’ll become as weak as any other man.”
chapters.zh: 参孙回答说，人若用七条未干的青绳子捆绑我，我就软弱像别人一样。

chapters.en: Then the rulers of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him with them.
chapters.zh: 于是非利士人的首领拿了七条未干的青绳子来，交给妇人，她就用绳子捆绑参孙。

chapters.en: With men hidden in the room, she called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are upon you!” But he snapped the bowstrings as easily as a piece of string snaps when it comes close to a flame. So the secret of his strength was not discovered.
chapters.zh: 有人预先埋伏在妇人的内室里。妇人说，参孙哪。非利士人拿你来了。参孙就挣断绳子，如挣断经火的麻线一般。这样，他力气的根由人还是不知道。

chapters.en: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have made a fool of me; you lied to me. Come now, tell me how you can be tied.”
chapters.zh: 大利拉对参孙说，你欺哄我，向我说谎言。现在求你告诉我当用何法捆绑你。

chapters.en: He said, “If anyone ties me securely with new ropes that have never been used, I’ll become as weak as any other man.”
chapters.zh: 参孙回答说，人若用没有使过的新绳捆绑我，我就软弱像别人一样。

chapters.en: So Delilah took new ropes and tied him with them. Then, with men hidden in the room, she called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are upon you!” But he snapped the ropes off his arms as if they were threads.
chapters.zh: 大利拉就用新绳捆绑他。对他说，参孙哪。非利士人拿你来了。有人预先埋伏在内室里。参孙将臂上的绳挣断了，如挣断一条线一样。

chapters.en: Delilah then said to Samson, “All this time you have been making a fool of me and lying to me. Tell me how you can be tied.” He replied, “If you weave the seven braids of my head into the fabric on the loom and tighten it with the pin, I’ll become as weak as any other man.” So while he was sleeping, Delilah took the seven braids of his head, wove them into the fabric
chapters.zh: 大利拉对参孙说，你到如今还是欺哄我，向我说谎言。求你告诉我，当用何法捆绑你。参孙回答说，你若将我头上的七条发绺，与纬线同织就可以了。

chapters.en: and tightened it with the pin. Again she called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are upon you!” He awoke from his sleep and pulled up the pin and the loom, with the fabric.
chapters.zh: 于是大利拉将他的发绺与纬线同织，用橛子钉住，对他说，参孙哪。非利士人拿你来了。参孙从睡中醒来，将机上的橛子和纬线一齐都拔出来了。

chapters.en: Then she said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when you won’t confide in me? This is the third time you have made a fool of me and haven’t told me the secret of your great strength.”
chapters.zh: 大利拉对参孙说，你既不与我同心，怎么说你爱我呢？你这三次欺哄我，没有告诉我，你因何有这么大的力气。

chapters.en: With such nagging she prodded him day after day until he was sick to death of it.
chapters.zh: 大利拉天天用话催逼他，甚至他心里烦闷要死。

chapters.en: So he told her everything. “No razor has ever been used on my head,” he said, “because I have been a Nazirite dedicated to God from my mother’s womb. If my head were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I would become as weak as any other man.”
chapters.zh: 参孙就把心中所藏的都告诉了她，对她说，向来人没有用剃头刀剃我的头，因为我自出母胎就归神作拿细耳人。若剃了我的头发，我的力气就离开我，我便软弱像别人一样。

chapters.en: When Delilah saw that he had told her everything, she sent word to the rulers of the Philistines, “Come back once more; he has told me everything.” So the rulers of the Philistines returned with the silver in their hands.
chapters.zh: 大利拉见他把心中所藏的都告诉了她，就打发人到非利士人的首领那里，对他们说，他已经把心中所藏的都告诉了我，请你们再上来一次。于是非利士人的首领手里拿着银子，上到妇人那里。

chapters.en: After putting him to sleep on her lap, she called for someone to shave off the seven braids of his hair, and so began to subdue him. And his strength left him.
chapters.zh: 大利拉使参孙枕着她的膝睡觉，叫了一个人来剃除他头上的七条发绺。于是大利拉克制他，他的力气就离开他了。

chapters.en: Then she called, “Samson, the Philistines are upon you!” He awoke from his sleep and thought, “I’ll go out as before and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the LORD had left him.
chapters.zh: 大利拉说，参孙哪。非利士人拿你来了。参孙从睡中醒来，心里说，我要像前几次出去活动身体。他却不知道耶和华已经离开他了。

chapters.en: Then the Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes and took him down to Gaza. Binding him with bronze shackles, they set him to grinding grain in the prison.
chapters.zh: 非利士人将他拿住，剜了他的眼睛，带他下到迦萨，用铜链拘索他。他就在监里推磨。

chapters.en: But the hair on his head began to grow again after it had been shaved.
chapters.zh: 然而他的头发被剃之后，又渐渐长起来了。

chapters.en: Now the rulers of the Philistines assembled to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to celebrate, saying, “Our god has delivered Samson, our enemy, into our hands.”
chapters.zh: 非利士人的首领聚集，要给他们的神大衮献大祭，并且欢乐，因为他们说，我们的神将我们的仇敌参孙交在我们手中了。

chapters.en: When the people saw him, they praised their god, saying, “Our god has delivered our enemy into our hands, the one who laid waste our land and multiplied our slain.”
chapters.zh: 众人看见参孙，就赞美他们的神说，我们的神将毁坏我们地，杀害我们许多人的仇敌交在我们手中了。

chapters.en: While they were in high spirits, they shouted, “Bring out Samson to entertain us.” So they called Samson out of the prison, and he performed for them. When they stood him among the pillars,
chapters.zh: 他们正宴乐的时候，就说，叫参孙来，在我们面前戏耍戏耍。于是将参孙从监里提出来，他就在众人面前戏耍。他们使他站在两柱中间。

chapters.en: Samson said to the servant who held his hand, “Put me where I can feel the pillars that support the temple, so that I may lean against them.”
chapters.zh: 参孙向拉他手的童子说，求你让我摸着托房的柱子，我要靠一靠。

chapters.en: Now the temple was crowded with men and women; all the rulers of the Philistines were there, and on the roof were about three thousand men and women watching Samson perform.
chapters.zh: 那时房内充满男女，非利士人的众首领也都在那里。房的平顶上约有三千男女，观看参孙戏耍。

chapters.en: Then Samson prayed to the LORD, “Sovereign LORD, remember me. Please, God, strengthen me just once more, and let me with one blow get revenge on the Philistines for my two eyes.”
chapters.zh: 参孙求告耶和华说，主耶和华阿，求你眷念我。神阿，求你赐我这一次的力量，使我在非利士人身上报那剜我双眼的仇。

chapters.en: Then Samson reached toward the two central pillars on which the temple stood. Bracing himself against them, his right hand on the one and his left hand on the other,
chapters.zh: 参孙就抱住托房的那两根柱子，左手抱一根，右手抱一根，

chapters.en: Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines!” Then he pushed with all his might, and down came the temple on the rulers and all the people in it. Thus he killed many more when he died than while he lived.
chapters.zh: 说，我情愿与非利士人同死。就尽力屈身，房子倒塌，压住首领和房内的众人。这样，参孙死时所杀的人，比活着所杀的还多。

chapters.en: Then his brothers and his father’s whole family went down to get him. They brought him back and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. He had led Israel twenty years.
chapters.zh: 参孙的弟兄和他父的全家，都下去取他的尸首，抬上来葬在琐拉和以实陶中间，在他父玛挪亚的坟墓里。参孙作以色列的士师二十年。

chapters.en: Now a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim
chapters.zh: 以法莲山地有一个人名叫米迦。

chapters.en: said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse—I have that silver with me; I took it.” Then his mother said, “The LORD bless you, my son!”
chapters.zh: 他对母亲说，你那一千一百舍客勒银子被人拿去，你因此咒诅，并且告诉了我。看哪。这银子在我这里，是我拿去了。他母亲说，我儿阿，愿耶和华赐福与你。

chapters.en: When he returned the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, she said, “I solemnly consecrate my silver to the LORD for my son to make an image overlaid with silver. I will give it back to you.”
chapters.zh: 米迦就把这一千一百舍客勒银子还他母亲。他母亲说，我分出这银子来为你献给耶和华，好雕刻一个像，铸成一个像。现在我还是交给你。

chapters.en: So after he returned the silver to his mother, she took two hundred shekels of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who used them to make the idol. And it was put in Micah’s house.
chapters.zh: 米迦将银子还他母亲，他母亲将二百舍客勒银子交给银匠，雕刻一个像，铸成一个像，安置在米迦的屋内。

chapters.en: Now this man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household gods and installed one of his sons as his priest.
chapters.zh: 这米迦有了神堂，又制造以弗得和家中的神像，分派他一个儿子作祭司。

chapters.en: In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit.
chapters.zh: 那时以色列中没有王，各人任意而行。

chapters.en: A young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, who had been living within the clan of Judah,
chapters.zh: 犹大伯利恒有一个少年人，是犹大族的利未人，他在那里寄居。

chapters.en: left that town in search of some other place to stay. On his way he came to Micah’s house in the hill country of Ephraim.
chapters.zh: 这人离开犹大伯利恒城，要找一个可住的地方。行路的时候，到了以法莲山地，走到米迦的家。

chapters.en: Micah asked him, “Where are you from?” “I’m a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” he said, “and I’m looking for a place to stay.”
chapters.zh: 米迦问他说，你从哪里来。他回答说，从犹大伯利恒来。我是利未人，要找一个可住的地方。

chapters.en: Then Micah said to him, “Live with me and be my father and priest, and I’ll give you ten shekels of silver a year, your clothes and your food.”
chapters.zh: 米迦说，你可以住在我这里，我以你为父，为祭司。我每年给你十舍客勒银子，一套衣服和度日的食物。利未人就进了他的家。

chapters.en: So the Levite agreed to live with him, and the young man became like one of his sons to him.
chapters.zh: 利未人情愿与那人同住。那人看这少年人如自己的儿子一样。

chapters.en: Then Micah installed the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.
chapters.zh: 米迦分派这少年的利未人作祭司，他就住在米迦的家里。

chapters.en: And Micah said, “Now I know that the LORD will be good to me, since this Levite has become my priest.”
chapters.zh: 米迦说，现在我知道耶和华必赐福与我，因我有一个利未人作祭司。

chapters.en: In those days Israel had no king. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking a place of their own where they might settle, because they had not yet come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 那时，以色列中没有王。但支派的人仍是寻地居住。因为到那日子，他们还没有在以色列支派中得地为业。

chapters.en: So the Danites sent five of their leading men from Zorah and Eshtaol to spy out the land and explore it. These men represented all the Danites. They told them, “Go, explore the land.” So they entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.
chapters.zh: 但人从琐拉和以实陶打发本族中的五个勇士，去仔细窥探那地，吩咐他们说，你们去窥探那地。他们来到以法莲山地，进了米迦的住宅，就在那里住宿。

chapters.en: When they were near Micah’s house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they turned in there and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”
chapters.zh: 他们临近米迦的住宅，听出那少年利未人的口音来，就进去问他说，谁领你到这里来。你在这里作什么。你在这里得什么。

chapters.en: He told them what Micah had done for him, and said, “He has hired me and I am his priest.”
chapters.zh: 他回答说，米迦待我如此如此，请我作祭司。

chapters.en: Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God to learn whether our journey will be successful.”
chapters.zh: 他们对他说，请你求问神，使我们知道所行的道路通达不通达。

chapters.en: The priest answered them, “Go in peace. Your journey has the LORD’s approval.”
chapters.zh: 祭司对他们说，你们可以平平安安地去，你们所行的道路是在耶和华面前的。

chapters.en: So the five men left and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living in safety, like the Sidonians, at peace and secure. And since their land lacked nothing, they were prosperous. Also, they lived a long way from the Sidonians and had no relationship with anyone else.
chapters.zh: 五人就走了，来到拉亿，见那里的民安居无虑，如同西顿人安居一样。在那地没有人掌权扰乱他们。他们离西顿人也远，与别人没有来往。

chapters.en: When they returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their fellow Danites asked them, “How did you find things?”
chapters.zh: 五人回到琐拉和以实陶，见他们的弟兄。弟兄问他们说，你们有什么话。

chapters.en: They answered, “Come on, let’s attack them! We have seen the land, and it is very good. Aren’t you going to do something? Don’t hesitate to go there and take it over.
chapters.zh: 他们回答说，起来，我们上去攻击他们吧。我们已经窥探那地，见那地甚好。你们为何静坐不动呢？要急速前往得那地为业，不可迟延。

chapters.en: When you get there, you will find an unsuspecting people and a spacious land that God has put into your hands, a land that lacks nothing whatever.”
chapters.zh: 你们到了那里，必看见安居无虑的民，地也宽阔。神已将那地交在你们手中。那地百物俱全，一无所缺。

chapters.en: Then six hundred men of the Danites, armed for battle, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.
chapters.zh: 于是但族中的六百人，各带兵器，从琐拉和以实陶前往，

chapters.en: On their way they set up camp near Kiriath Jearim in Judah. This is why the place west of Kiriath Jearim is called Mahaneh Dan to this day.
chapters.zh: 上到犹大的基列耶琳，在基列耶琳后边安营。因此那地方名叫玛哈尼但，直到今日。

chapters.en: From there they went on to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house.
chapters.zh: 他们从那里往以法莲山地去，来到米迦的住宅。

chapters.en: Then the five men who had spied out the land of Laish said to their fellow Danites, “Do you know that one of these houses has an ephod, some household gods and an image overlaid with silver? Now you know what to do.”
chapters.zh: 从前窥探拉亿地的五个人对他们的弟兄说，这宅子里有以弗得和家中的神像，并雕刻的像与铸成的像，你们知道吗？现在你们要想一想当怎样行。

chapters.en: So they turned in there and went to the house of the young Levite at Micah’s place and greeted him.
chapters.zh: 五人就进入米迦的住宅，到了那少年利未人的房内问他好。

chapters.en: The six hundred Danites, armed for battle, stood at the entrance of the gate.
chapters.zh: 那六百但人各带兵器，站在门口。

chapters.en: The five men who had spied out the land went inside and took the idol, the ephod and the household gods while the priest and the six hundred armed men stood at the entrance of the gate.
chapters.zh: 窥探地的五个人走进去，将雕刻的像，以弗得，家中的神像，并铸成的像，都拿了去。祭司和带兵器的六百人，一同站在门口。

chapters.en: When the five men went into Micah’s house and took the idol, the ephod and the household gods, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
chapters.zh: 那五个人进入米迦的住宅，拿出雕刻的像，以弗得，家中的神像，并铸成的像，祭司就问他们说，你们作什么呢？

chapters.en: They answered him, “Be quiet! Don’t say a word. Come with us, and be our father and priest. Isn’t it better that you serve a tribe and clan in Israel as priest rather than just one man’s household?”
chapters.zh: 他们回答说，不要作声，用手捂口，跟我们去吧。我们必以你为父，为祭司。你作一家的祭司好呢？还是作以色列一族一支派的祭司好呢？

chapters.en: The priest was very pleased. He took the ephod, the household gods and the idol and went along with the people.
chapters.zh: 祭司心里喜悦，便拿着以弗得和家中的神像，并雕刻的像，进入他们中间。

chapters.en: Putting their little children, their livestock and their possessions in front of them, they turned away and left.
chapters.zh: 他们就转身离开那里，妻子，儿女，牲畜，财物都在前头。

chapters.en: When they had gone some distance from Micah’s house, the men who lived near Micah were called together and overtook the Danites.
chapters.zh: 离米迦的住宅已远，米迦的近邻都聚集来，追赶但人，

chapters.en: As they shouted after them, the Danites turned and said to Micah, “What’s the matter with you that you called out your men to fight?”
chapters.zh: 呼叫但人。但人回头问米迦说，你聚集这许多人来作什么呢？

chapters.en: He replied, “You took the gods I made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you ask, ‘What’s the matter with you?’ ”
chapters.zh: 米迦说，你们将我所作的神像和祭司都带了去，我还有所剩的吗？怎么还问我说作什么呢？

chapters.en: The Danites answered, “Don’t argue with us, or some of the men may get angry and attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.”
chapters.zh: 但人对米迦说，你不要使我们听见你的声音，恐怕有性暴的人攻击你，以致你和你的全家尽都丧命。

chapters.en: So the Danites went their way, and Micah, seeing that they were too strong for him, turned around and went back home.
chapters.zh: 但人还是走他们的路。米迦见他们的势力比自己强盛，就转身回家去了。

chapters.en: Then they took what Micah had made, and his priest, and went on to Laish, against a people at peace and secure. They attacked them with the sword and burned down their city.
chapters.zh: 但人将米迦所作的神像和他的祭司都带到拉亿，见安居无虑的民，就用刀杀了那民，又放火烧了那城，

chapters.en: There was no one to rescue them because they lived a long way from Sidon and had no relationship with anyone else. The city was in a valley near Beth Rehob. The Danites rebuilt the city and settled there.
chapters.zh: 并无人搭救。因为离西顿远，他们又与别人没有来往。城在平原，那平原靠近伯利合。但人又在那里修城居住，

chapters.en: They named it Dan after their ancestor Dan, who was born to Israel—though the city used to be called Laish.
chapters.zh: 照着他们始祖以色列之子但的名字，给那城起名叫但。原先那城名叫拉亿。

chapters.en: There the Danites set up for themselves the idol, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the time of the captivity of the land.
chapters.zh: 但人就为自己设立那雕刻的像。摩西的孙子，革舜的儿子约拿单，和他的子孙作但支派的祭司，直到那地遭掳掠的日子。

chapters.en: They continued to use the idol Micah had made, all the time the house of God was in Shiloh.
chapters.zh: 神的殿在示罗多少日子，但人为自己设立米迦所雕刻的像也在但多少日子。

chapters.en: In those days Israel had no king. Now a Levite who lived in a remote area in the hill country of Ephraim took a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.
chapters.zh: 当以色列中没有王的时候，有住以法莲山地那边的一个利未人，娶了一个犹大伯利恒的女子为妾。

chapters.en: But she was unfaithful to him. She left him and went back to her parents’ home in Bethlehem, Judah. After she had been there four months,
chapters.zh: 妾行淫离开丈夫，回犹大伯利恒，到了父家，在那里住了四个月。

chapters.en: her husband went to her to persuade her to return. He had with him his servant and two donkeys. She took him into her parents’ home, and when her father saw him, he gladly welcomed him.
chapters.zh: 她丈夫起来，带着一个仆人，两匹驴去见她，用好话劝她回来。女子就引丈夫进入父家。她父见了那人，便欢欢喜喜地迎接。

chapters.en: His father-in-law, the woman’s father, prevailed on him to stay; so he remained with him three days, eating and drinking, and sleeping there.
chapters.zh: 那人的岳父，就是女子的父亲，将那人留下住了三天。于是二人一同吃喝，住宿。

chapters.en: On the fourth day they got up early and he prepared to leave, but the woman’s father said to his son-in-law, “Refresh yourself with something to eat; then you can go.”
chapters.zh: 到第四天，利未人清早起来要走，女子的父亲对女婿说，请你吃点饭，加添心力，然后可以行路。

chapters.en: So the two of them sat down to eat and drink together. Afterward the woman’s father said, “Please stay tonight and enjoy yourself.”
chapters.zh: 于是二人坐下一同吃喝。女子的父亲对那人说，请你再住一夜，畅快你的心。

chapters.en: And when the man got up to go, his father-in-law persuaded him, so he stayed there that night.
chapters.zh: 那人起来要走，他岳父强留他，他又住了一宿。

chapters.en: On the morning of the fifth day, when he rose to go, the woman’s father said, “Refresh yourself. Wait till afternoon!” So the two of them ate together.
chapters.zh: 到第五天，他清早起来要走，女子的父亲说，请你吃点饭，加添心力，等到日头偏西再走。于是二人一同吃饭。

chapters.en: Then when the man, with his concubine and his servant, got up to leave, his father-in-law, the woman’s father, said, “Now look, it’s almost evening. Spend the night here; the day is nearly over. Stay and enjoy yourself. Early tomorrow morning you can get up and be on your way home.”
chapters.zh: 那人同他的妾和仆人起来要走，他岳父，就是女子的父亲，对他说，看哪，日头偏西了，请你再住一夜。天快晚了，可以在这里住宿，畅快你的心。明天早早起行回家去。

chapters.en: But, unwilling to stay another night, the man left and went toward Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), with his two saddled donkeys and his concubine.
chapters.zh: 那人不愿再住一夜，就备上那两匹驴，带着妾起身走了，来到耶布斯的对面，耶布斯就是耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: When they were near Jebus and the day was almost gone, the servant said to his master, “Come, let’s stop at this city of the Jebusites and spend the night.”
chapters.zh: 临近耶布斯的时候，日头快要落了，仆人对主人说，我们不如进这耶布斯人的城里住宿。

chapters.en: His master replied, “No. We won’t go into any city whose people are not Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah.”
chapters.zh: 主人回答说，我们不可进不是以色列人住的外邦城，不如过到基比亚去。

chapters.en: He added, “Come, let’s try to reach Gibeah or Ramah and spend the night in one of those places.”
chapters.zh: 又对仆人说，我们可以到一个地方，或住在基比亚，或住在拉玛。

chapters.en: So they went on, and the sun set as they neared Gibeah in Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 他们就往前走。将到便雅悯的基比亚，日头已经落了。

chapters.en: There they stopped to spend the night. They went and sat in the city square, but no one took them in for the night.
chapters.zh: 他们进入基比亚要在那里住宿，就坐在城里的街上，因为无人接他们进家住宿。

chapters.en: That evening an old man from the hill country of Ephraim, who was living in Gibeah (the inhabitants of the place were Benjamites), came in from his work in the fields.
chapters.zh: 晚上，有一个老年人从田间作工回来。他原是以法莲山地的人，住在基比亚。那地方的人却是便雅悯人。

chapters.en: When he looked and saw the traveler in the city square, the old man asked, “Where are you going? Where did you come from?”
chapters.zh: 老年人举目看见客人坐在城里的街上，就问他说，你从哪里来。要往哪里去。

chapters.en: He answered, “We are on our way from Bethlehem in Judah to a remote area in the hill country of Ephraim where I live. I have been to Bethlehem in Judah and now I am going to the house of the LORD. No one has taken me in for the night.
chapters.zh: 他回答说，我们从犹大伯利恒来，要往以法莲山地那边去。我原是那里的人，到过犹大伯利恒，现在我往耶和华的殿去，在这里无人接我进他的家。

chapters.en: We have both straw and fodder for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves your servants—me, the woman and the young man with us. We don’t need anything.”
chapters.zh: 其实我有粮草可以喂驴，我与我的妾，并我的仆人，有饼有酒，并不缺少什么。

chapters.en: “You are welcome at my house,” the old man said. “Let me supply whatever you need. Only don’t spend the night in the square.”
chapters.zh: 老年人说，愿你平安。你所需用的我都给你，只是不可在街上过夜。

chapters.en: So he took him into his house and fed his donkeys. After they had washed their feet, they had something to eat and drink.
chapters.zh: 于是领他们到家里，喂上驴，他们就洗脚吃喝。

chapters.en: While they were enjoying themselves, some of the wicked men of the city surrounded the house. Pounding on the door, they shouted to the old man who owned the house, “Bring out the man who came to your house so we can have sex with him.”
chapters.zh: 他们心里正欢畅的时候，城中的匪徒围住房子，连连叩门，对房主老人说，你把那进你家的人带出来，我们要与他交合。

chapters.en: The owner of the house went outside and said to them, “No, my friends, don’t be so vile. Since this man is my guest, don’t do this outrageous thing.
chapters.zh: 那房主出来对他们说，弟兄们哪，不要这样作恶。这人既然进了我的家，你们就不要行这丑事。

chapters.en: Look, here is my virgin daughter, and his concubine. I will bring them out to you now, and you can use them and do to them whatever you wish. But as for this man, don’t do such an outrageous thing.”
chapters.zh: 我有个女儿，还是处女，并有这人的妾，我将她们领出来任凭你们玷辱她们，只是向这人不可行这样的丑事。

chapters.en: But the men would not listen to him. So the man took his concubine and sent her outside to them, and they raped her and abused her throughout the night, and at dawn they let her go.
chapters.zh: 那些人却不听从他的话。那人就把他的妾拉出去交给他们，他们便与她交合，终夜凌辱她，直到天色快亮才放她去。

chapters.en: At daybreak the woman went back to the house where her master was staying, fell down at the door and lay there until daylight.
chapters.zh: 天快亮的时候，妇人回到她主人住宿的房门前，就仆倒在地，直到天亮。

chapters.en: When her master got up in the morning and opened the door of the house and stepped out to continue on his way, there lay his concubine, fallen in the doorway of the house, with her hands on the threshold.
chapters.zh: 早晨，她的主人起来开了房门，出去要行路，不料那妇人仆倒在房门前，两手搭在门槛上。

chapters.en: He said to her, “Get up; let’s go.” But there was no answer. Then the man put her on his donkey and set out for home.
chapters.zh: 就对妇人说，起来，我们走吧。妇人却不回答。那人便将她驮在驴上，起身回本处去了。

chapters.en: When he reached home, he took a knife and cut up his concubine, limb by limb, into twelve parts and sent them into all the areas of Israel.
chapters.zh: 到了家里，用刀将妾的尸身切成十二块，使人拿着传送以色列的四境。

chapters.en: Everyone who saw it was saying to one another, “Such a thing has never been seen or done, not since the day the Israelites came up out of Egypt. Just imagine! We must do something! So speak up!”
chapters.zh: 凡看见的人都说，从以色列人出埃及地，直到今日，这样的事没有行过，也没有见过。现在应当思想，大家商议当怎样办理。

chapters.en: Then all Israel from Dan to Beersheba and from the land of Gilead came together as one and assembled before the LORD in Mizpah.
chapters.zh: 于是以色列从但到别是巴，以及住基列地的众人都出来，如同一人，聚集在米斯巴耶和华面前。

chapters.en: The leaders of all the people of the tribes of Israel took their places in the assembly of God’s people, four hundred thousand men armed with swords.
chapters.zh: 以色列民的首领，就是各支派的军长，都站在神百姓的会中。拿刀的步兵共有四十万。

chapters.en: (The Benjamites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah.) Then the Israelites said, “Tell us how this awful thing happened.”
chapters.zh: 以色列人上到米斯巴，便雅悯人都听见了。以色列人说，请你将这件恶事的情由对我们说明。

chapters.en: So the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, said, “I and my concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
chapters.zh: 那利未人，就是被害之妇人的丈夫，回答说，我和我的妾到了便雅悯的基比亚住宿。

chapters.en: During the night the men of Gibeah came after me and surrounded the house, intending to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.
chapters.zh: 基比亚人夜间起来，围了我住的房子，想要杀我，又将我的妾强奸致死。

chapters.en: I took my concubine, cut her into pieces and sent one piece to each region of Israel’s inheritance, because they committed this lewd and outrageous act in Israel.
chapters.zh: 我就把我妾的尸身切成块子，使人拿着传送以色列得为业的全地，因为基比亚人在以色列中行了凶淫丑恶的事。

chapters.en: Now, all you Israelites, speak up and tell me what you have decided to do.”
chapters.zh: 你们以色列人都当筹划商议。

chapters.en: All the men rose up together as one, saying, “None of us will go home. No, not one of us will return to his house.
chapters.zh: 众民都起来如同一人，说，我们连一人都不回自己帐棚，自己房屋去。

chapters.en: But now this is what we’ll do to Gibeah: We’ll go up against it in the order decided by casting lots.
chapters.zh: 我们向基比亚人必这样行，照所掣的签去攻击他们。

chapters.en: We’ll take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred from a thousand, and a thousand from ten thousand, to get provisions for the army. Then, when the army arrives at Gibeah in Benjamin, it can give them what they deserve for this outrageous act done in Israel.”
chapters.zh: 我们要在以色列各支派中，一百人挑取十人，一千人挑取百人，一万人挑取千人，为民运粮，等大众到了便雅悯的基比亚，就照基比亚人在以色列中所行的丑事征伐他们。

chapters.en: So all the Israelites got together and united as one against the city.
chapters.zh: 于是以色列众人彼此连合如同一人，聚集攻击那城。

chapters.en: The tribes of Israel sent messengers throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying, “What about this awful crime that was committed among you?
chapters.zh: 以色列众支派打发人去，问便雅悯支派的各家说，你们中间怎么作了这样的恶事呢？

chapters.en: Now turn those wicked men of Gibeah over to us so that we may put them to death and purge the evil from Israel.” But the Benjamites would not listen to their fellow Israelites.
chapters.zh: 现在你们要将基比亚的那些匪徒交出来，我们好治死他们，从以色列中除掉这恶。便雅悯人却不肯听从他们弟兄以色列人的话。

chapters.en: From their towns they came together at Gibeah to fight against the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人从他们的各城里出来，聚集到了基比亚，要与以色列人打仗。

chapters.en: At once the Benjamites mobilized twenty-six thousand swordsmen from their towns, in addition to seven hundred able young men from those living in Gibeah.
chapters.zh: 那时便雅悯人从各城里点出拿刀的，共有二万六千。另外还有基比亚人点出七百精兵。

chapters.en: Among all these soldiers there were seven hundred select troops who were left-handed, each of whom could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
chapters.zh: 在众军之中有拣选的七百精兵，都是左手便利的，能用机弦甩石打人，毫发不差。

chapters.en: Israel, apart from Benjamin, mustered four hundred thousand swordsmen, all of them fit for battle.
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人之外，点出以色列人拿刀的，共有四十万，都是战士。

chapters.en: The Israelites went up to Bethel and inquired of God. They said, “Who of us is to go up first to fight against the Benjamites?” The LORD replied, “Judah shall go first.”
chapters.zh: 以色列人就起来，到伯特利去求问神说，我们中间谁当首先上去与便雅悯人争战呢？耶和华说，犹大当先上去。

chapters.en: The next morning the Israelites got up and pitched camp near Gibeah.
chapters.zh: 以色列人早晨起来，对着基比亚安营。

chapters.en: The Israelites went out to fight the Benjamites and took up battle positions against them at Gibeah.
chapters.zh: 以色列人出来，要与便雅悯人打仗，就在基比亚前摆阵。

chapters.en: The Benjamites came out of Gibeah and cut down twenty-two thousand Israelites on the battlefield that day.
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人就从基比亚出来，当日杀死以色列人二万二千。

chapters.en: But the Israelites encouraged one another and again took up their positions where they had stationed themselves the first day.
chapters.zh: 以色列人彼此奋勇，仍在头一日摆阵的地方又摆阵。

chapters.en: The Israelites went up and wept before the LORD until evening, and they inquired of the LORD. They said, “Shall we go up again to fight against the Benjamites, our fellow Israelites?” The LORD answered, “Go up against them.”
chapters.zh: 未摆阵之先，以色列人上去，在耶和华面前哭号，直到晚上，求问耶和华说，我们再去与我们弟兄便雅悯人打仗可以不可以。耶和华说，可以上去攻击他们。

chapters.en: Then the Israelites drew near to Benjamin the second day.
chapters.zh: 第二日，以色列人就上前攻击便雅悯人。

chapters.en: This time, when the Benjamites came out from Gibeah to oppose them, they cut down another eighteen thousand Israelites, all of them armed with swords.
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人也在这日从基比亚出来，与以色列人接战，又杀死他们一万八千，都是拿刀的。

chapters.en: Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel, and there they sat weeping before the LORD. They fasted that day until evening and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 以色列众人就上到伯特利，坐在耶和华面前哭号，当日禁食直到晚上。又在耶和华面前献燔祭和平安祭。

chapters.en: And the Israelites inquired of the LORD. (In those days the ark of the covenant of God was there,
chapters.zh: 那时，神的约柜在那里。亚伦的孙子，以利亚撒的儿子非尼哈侍立在约柜前。以色列人问耶和华说，我们当再出去与我们弟兄便雅悯人打仗呢？还是罢兵呢？耶和华说，你们当上去，因为明日我必将他们交在你们手中。

chapters.en: with Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, ministering before it.) They asked, “Shall we go up again to fight against the Benjamites, our fellow Israelites, or not?” The LORD responded, “Go, for tomorrow I will give them into your hands.”
Then Israel set an ambush around Gibeah.
chapters.zh: 以色列人在基比亚的四围设下伏兵。

chapters.en: They went up against the Benjamites on the third day and took up positions against Gibeah as they had done before.
chapters.zh: 第三日，以色列人又上去攻击便雅悯人，在基比亚前摆阵，与前两次一样。

chapters.en: The Benjamites came out to meet them and were drawn away from the city. They began to inflict casualties on the Israelites as before, so that about thirty men fell in the open field and on the roads—the one leading to Bethel and the other to Gibeah.
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人也出来迎敌，就被引诱离城。在田间两条路上，一通伯特利，一通基比亚，像前两次，动手杀死以色列人约有三十个。

chapters.en: While the Benjamites were saying, “We are defeating them as before,” the Israelites were saying, “Let’s retreat and draw them away from the city to the roads.”
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人说，他们仍旧败在我们面前。但以色列人说，我们不如逃跑，引诱他们离开城到路上来。

chapters.en: All the men of Israel moved from their places and took up positions at Baal Tamar, and the Israelite ambush charged out of its place on the west of Gibeah.
chapters.zh: 以色列众人都起来，在巴力他玛摆阵，以色列的伏兵从马利迦巴埋伏的地方冲上前去。

chapters.en: Then ten thousand of Israel’s able young men made a frontal attack on Gibeah. The fighting was so heavy that the Benjamites did not realize how near disaster was.
chapters.zh: 有以色列人中的一万精兵，来到基比亚前接战，势派甚是凶猛。便雅悯人却不知道灾祸临近了。

chapters.en: The LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel, and on that day the Israelites struck down 25,100 Benjamites, all armed with swords.
chapters.zh: 耶和华使以色列人杀败便雅悯人。那日，以色列人杀死便雅悯人二万五千一百，都是拿刀的。

chapters.en: Then the Benjamites saw that they were beaten. Now the men of Israel had given way before Benjamin, because they relied on the ambush they had set near Gibeah.
chapters.zh: 于是便雅悯人知道自己败了。先是以色列人。因为靠着在基比亚前所设的伏兵，就在便雅悯人面前诈败。

chapters.en: Those who had been in ambush made a sudden dash into Gibeah, spread out and put the whole city to the sword.
chapters.zh: 伏兵急忙闯进基比亚，用刀杀死全城的人。

chapters.en: The Israelites had arranged with the ambush that they should send up a great cloud of smoke from the city,
chapters.zh: 以色列人预先同伏兵约定在城内放火，以烟气上腾为号。

chapters.en: and then the Israelites would counterattack. The Benjamites had begun to inflict casualties on the Israelites (about thirty), and they said, “We are defeating them as in the first battle.”
chapters.zh: 以色列人临退阵的时候，便雅悯人动手杀死以色列人，约有三十个，就说，他们仍像前次被我们杀败了。

chapters.en: But when the column of smoke began to rise from the city, the Benjamites turned and saw the whole city going up in smoke.
chapters.zh: 当烟气如柱从城中上腾的时候，便雅悯人回头观看，见全城的烟气冲天。

chapters.en: Then the Israelites counterattacked, and the Benjamites were terrified, because they realized that disaster had come on them.
chapters.zh: 以色列人又转身回来，便雅悯人就甚惊惶，因为看见灾祸临到自己了。

chapters.en: So they fled before the Israelites in the direction of the wilderness, but they could not escape the battle. And the Israelites who came out of the towns cut them down there.
chapters.zh: 他们在以色列人面前转身往旷野逃跑。以色列人在后面追杀。那从各城里出来的，也都夹攻杀灭他们。

chapters.en: They surrounded the Benjamites, chased them and easily overran them in the vicinity of Gibeah on the east.
chapters.zh: 以色列人围绕便雅悯人，追赶他们，在他们歇脚之处，对着日出之地的基比亚践踏他们。

chapters.en: Eighteen thousand Benjamites fell, all of them valiant fighters.
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人死了的有一万八千，都是勇士。

chapters.en: As they turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, the Israelites cut down five thousand men along the roads. They kept pressing after the Benjamites as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand more.
chapters.zh: 其余的人转身向旷野逃跑，往临门磐去。以色列人在道路上杀了他们五千人，如拾取遗穗一样，追到基顿又杀了他们二千人。

chapters.en: On that day twenty-five thousand Benjamite swordsmen fell, all of them valiant fighters.
chapters.zh: 那日便雅悯死了的共有二万五千人，都是拿刀的勇士。

chapters.en: But six hundred of them turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed four months.
chapters.zh: 只剩下六百人，转身向旷野逃跑，到了临门磐，就在那里住了四个月。

chapters.en: The men of Israel went back to Benjamin and put all the towns to the sword, including the animals and everything else they found. All the towns they came across they set on fire.
chapters.zh: 以色列人又转到便雅悯地，将各城的人和牲畜，并一切所遇见的，都用刀杀尽，又放火烧了一切城邑。

chapters.en: The men of Israel had taken an oath at Mizpah: “Not one of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjamite.”
chapters.zh: 以色列人在米斯巴曾起誓说，我们都不将女儿给便雅悯人为妻。

chapters.en: The people went to Bethel, where they sat before God until evening, raising their voices and weeping bitterly.
chapters.zh: 以色列人来到伯特利，坐在神面前直到晚上，放声痛哭，

chapters.en: “LORD, God of Israel,” they cried, “why has this happened to Israel? Why should one tribe be missing from Israel today?”
chapters.zh: 说，耶和华以色列的神阿，为何以色列中有这样缺了一支派的事呢？

chapters.en: Early the next day the people built an altar and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings.
chapters.zh: 次日清早，百姓起来，在那里筑了一座坛，献燔祭和平安祭。

chapters.en: Then the Israelites asked, “Who from all the tribes of Israel has failed to assemble before the LORD?” For they had taken a solemn oath that anyone who failed to assemble before the LORD at Mizpah was to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 以色列人彼此问说，以色列各支派中，谁没有同会众上到耶和华面前来呢？先是以色列人起过大誓说，凡不上米斯巴到耶和华面前来的，必将他治死。

chapters.en: Now the Israelites grieved for the tribe of Benjamin, their fellow Israelites. “Today one tribe is cut off from Israel,” they said.
chapters.zh: 以色列人为他们的弟兄便雅悯后悔，说，如今以色列中绝了一个支派了。

chapters.en: “How can we provide wives for those who are left, since we have taken an oath by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters in marriage?”
chapters.zh: 我们既在耶和华面前起誓说，必不将我们的女儿给便雅悯人为妻，现在我们当怎样办理，使他们剩下的人有妻呢？

chapters.en: Then they asked, “Which one of the tribes of Israel failed to assemble before the LORD at Mizpah?” They discovered that no one from Jabesh Gilead had come to the camp for the assembly.
chapters.zh: 又彼此问说，以色列支派中谁没有上米斯巴到耶和华面前来呢？他们就查出基列雅比没有一人进营到会众那里。

chapters.en: For when they counted the people, they found that none of the people of Jabesh Gilead were there.
chapters.zh: 因为百姓被数的时候，没有一个基列雅比人在那里。

chapters.en: So the assembly sent twelve thousand fighting men with instructions to go to Jabesh Gilead and put to the sword those living there, including the women and children.
chapters.zh: 会众就打发一万二千大勇士，吩咐他们说，你们去用刀将基列雅比人连妇女带孩子都击杀了。

chapters.en: “This is what you are to do,” they said. “Kill every male and every woman who is not a virgin.”
chapters.zh: 所当行的就是这样，要将一切男子和已嫁的女子尽行杀戮。

chapters.en: They found among the people living in Jabesh Gilead four hundred young women who had never slept with a man, and they took them to the camp at Shiloh in Canaan.
chapters.zh: 他们在基列雅比人中，遇见了四百个未嫁的处女，就带到迦南地的示罗营里。

chapters.en: Then the whole assembly sent an offer of peace to the Benjamites at the rock of Rimmon.
chapters.zh: 全会众打发人到临门磐的便雅悯人那里，向他们说和睦的话。

chapters.en: So the Benjamites returned at that time and were given the women of Jabesh Gilead who had been spared. But there were not enough for all of them.
chapters.zh: 当时便雅悯人回来了，以色列人就把所存活基列雅比的女子给他们为妻，还是不够。

chapters.en: The people grieved for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a gap in the tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 百姓为便雅悯人后悔，因为耶和华使以色列人缺了一个支派（原文作使以色列中有了破口）。

chapters.en: And the elders of the assembly said, “With the women of Benjamin destroyed, how shall we provide wives for the men who are left?
chapters.zh: 会中的长老说，便雅悯中的女子既然除灭了，我们当怎样办理，使那余剩的人有妻呢？

chapters.en: The Benjamite survivors must have heirs,” they said, “so that a tribe of Israel will not be wiped out.
chapters.zh: 又说，便雅悯逃脱的人当有地业，免得以色列中涂抹了一个支派。

chapters.en: We can’t give them our daughters as wives, since we Israelites have taken this oath: ‘Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to a Benjamite.’
chapters.zh: 只是我们不能将自己的女儿给他们为妻。因为以色列人曾起誓说，有将女儿给便雅悯人为妻的，必受咒诅。

chapters.en: But look, there is the annual festival of the LORD in Shiloh, which lies north of Bethel, east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.”
chapters.zh: 他们又说，在利波拿以南，伯特利以北，在示剑大路以东的示罗，年年有耶和华的节期。

chapters.en: So they instructed the Benjamites, saying, “Go and hide in the vineyards
chapters.zh: 就吩咐便雅悯人说，你们去，在葡萄园中埋伏。

chapters.en: and watch. When the young women of Shiloh come out to join in the dancing, rush from the vineyards and each of you seize one of them to be your wife. Then return to the land of Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 若看见示罗的女子出来跳舞，就从葡萄园出来，在示罗的女子中各抢一个为妻，回便雅悯地去。

chapters.en: When their fathers or brothers complain to us, we will say to them, ‘Do us the favor of helping them, because we did not get wives for them during the war. You will not be guilty of breaking your oath because you did not give your daughters to them.’ ”
chapters.zh: 他们的父亲或是弟兄若来与我们争竞，我们就说，求你们看我们的情面，施恩给这些人，因我们在争战的时候没有给他们留下女子为妻。这也不是你们将女子给他们的。若是你们给的，就算有罪。

chapters.en: So that is what the Benjamites did. While the young women were dancing, each man caught one and carried her off to be his wife. Then they returned to their inheritance and rebuilt the towns and settled in them.
chapters.zh: 于是便雅悯人照样而行，按着他们的数目从跳舞的女子中抢去为妻，就回自己的地业去，又重修城邑居住。

chapters.en: At that time the Israelites left that place and went home to their tribes and clans, each to his own inheritance.
chapters.zh: 当时以色列人离开那里，各归本支派，本宗族，本地业去了。

chapters.en: In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit.
chapters.zh: 那时，以色列中没有王，各人任意而行。

chapters.en: In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. So a man from Bethlehem in Judah, together with his wife and two sons, went to live for a while in the country of Moab.
chapters.zh: 当士师秉政的时候，国中遭遇饥荒，在犹大伯利恒，有一个人带着妻子和两个儿子，往摩押地去寄居。

chapters.en: The man’s name was Elimelek, his wife’s name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Kilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem, Judah. And they went to Moab and lived there.
chapters.zh: 这人名叫以利米勒，他的妻名叫拿俄米。他两个儿子，一个名叫玛伦，一个名叫基连，都是犹大伯利恒的以法他人。他们到了摩押地，就住在那里。

chapters.en: Now Elimelek, Naomi’s husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
chapters.zh: 后来拿俄米的丈夫以利米勒死了，剩下妇人和她两个儿子。

chapters.en: They married Moabite women, one named Orpah and the other Ruth. After they had lived there about ten years,
chapters.zh: 这两个儿子娶了摩押女子为妻，一个名叫俄珥巴，一个名叫路得，在那里住了约有十年。

chapters.en: both Mahlon and Kilion also died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and her husband.
chapters.zh: 玛伦和基连二人也死了，剩下拿俄米，没有丈夫，也没有儿子。

chapters.en: When Naomi heard in Moab that the LORD had come to the aid of his people by providing food for them, she and her daughters-in-law prepared to return home from there.
chapters.zh: 她就与两个儿妇起身，要从摩押地归回。因为她在摩押地，听见耶和华眷顾自己的百姓，赐粮食与他们。

chapters.en: With her two daughters-in-law she left the place where she had been living and set out on the road that would take them back to the land of Judah.
chapters.zh: 于是她和两个儿妇起行离开所住的地方，要回犹大地去。

chapters.en: Then Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you, to your mother’s home. May the LORD show you kindness, as you have shown kindness to your dead husbands and to me.
chapters.zh: 拿俄米对两个儿妇说，你们各人回娘家去吧，愿耶和华恩待你们，象你们恩待已死的人与我一样。

chapters.en: May the LORD grant that each of you will find rest in the home of another husband.” Then she kissed them goodbye and they wept aloud
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华使你们各在新夫家中得平安。于是，拿俄米与她们亲嘴。她们就放声而哭，

chapters.en: and said to her, “We will go back with you to your people.”
chapters.zh: 说，不然，我们必与你一同回你本国去。

chapters.en: But Naomi said, “Return home, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Am I going to have any more sons, who could become your husbands?
chapters.zh: 拿俄米说，我女儿们哪，回去吧，为何要跟我去呢？我还能生子作你们的丈夫吗？

chapters.en: Return home, my daughters; I am too old to have another husband. Even if I thought there was still hope for me—even if I had a husband tonight and then gave birth to sons—
chapters.zh: 我女儿们哪，回去吧，我年纪老迈，不能再有丈夫。即或说，我还有指望，今夜有丈夫可以生子。

chapters.en: would you wait until they grew up? Would you remain unmarried for them? No, my daughters. It is more bitter for me than for you, because the LORD’s hand has turned against me!”
chapters.zh: 你们岂能等着他们长大呢？你们岂能等着他们不嫁别人呢？我女儿们哪，不要这样，我为你们的缘故，甚是愁苦，因为耶和华伸手攻击我。

chapters.en: At this they wept aloud again. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.
chapters.zh: 两个儿妇又放声而哭，俄珥巴与婆婆亲嘴而别，只是路得舍不得拿俄米。

chapters.en: “Look,” said Naomi, “your sister-in-law is going back to her people and her gods. Go back with her.”
chapters.zh: 拿俄米说，看哪，你嫂子已经回她本国，和她所拜的神那里去了，你也跟着你嫂子回去吧。

chapters.en: But Ruth replied, “Don’t urge me to leave you or to turn back from you. Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay. Your people will be my people and your God my God.
chapters.zh: 路得说，不要催我回去不跟随你，你往哪里去，我也往哪里去。你在哪里住宿，我也在哪里住宿。你的国就是我的国，你的神就是我的神。

chapters.en: Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD deal with me, be it ever so severely, if even death separates you and me.”
chapters.zh: 你在哪里死，我也在哪里死，也葬在那里。除非死能使你我相离，不然，愿耶和华重重地降罚与我。

chapters.en: When Naomi realized that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.
chapters.zh: 拿俄米见路得定意要跟随自己去，就不再劝她了。

chapters.en: So the two women went on until they came to Bethlehem. When they arrived in Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred because of them, and the women exclaimed, “Can this be Naomi?”
chapters.zh: 于是二人同行，来到伯利恒。她们到了伯利恒，合城的人就都惊讶。妇女们说，这是拿俄米吗？

chapters.en: “Don’t call me Naomi, ” she told them. “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has made my life very bitter.
chapters.zh: 拿俄米对他们说，不要叫我拿俄米（拿俄米就是甜的意思），要叫我玛拉（玛拉就是苦的意思），因为全能者使我受了大苦。

chapters.en: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? The LORD has afflicted me; the Almighty has brought misfortune upon me.”
chapters.zh: 我满满的出去，耶和华使我空空的回来。耶和华降祸与我，全能者使我受苦，既是这样，你们为何还叫我拿俄米呢？

chapters.en: So Naomi returned from Moab accompanied by Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, arriving in Bethlehem as the barley harvest was beginning.
chapters.zh: 拿俄米和她儿妇摩押女子路得，从摩押地回来到伯利恒，正是动手割大麦的时候。

chapters.en: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband’s side, a man of standing from the clan of Elimelek, whose name was Boaz.
chapters.zh: 拿俄米的丈夫以利米勒的亲族中，有一个人名叫波阿斯，是个大财主。

chapters.en: And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Let me go to the fields and pick up the leftover grain behind anyone in whose eyes I find favor.” Naomi said to her, “Go ahead, my daughter.”
chapters.zh: 摩押女子路得对拿俄米说，容我往田间去，我蒙谁的恩，就在谁的身后拾取麦穗。拿俄米说，女儿阿，你只管去。

chapters.en: So she went out, entered a field and began to glean behind the harvesters. As it turned out, she was working in a field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelek.
chapters.zh: 路得就去了，来到田间，在收割的人身后拾取麦穗。她恰巧到了以利米勒本族的人，波阿斯那块田里。

chapters.en: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and greeted the harvesters, “The LORD be with you!” “The LORD bless you!” they answered.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯正从伯利恒来，对收割的人说，愿耶和华与你们同在。他们回答说，愿耶和华赐福与你。

chapters.en: Boaz asked the overseer of his harvesters, “Who does that young woman belong to?”
chapters.zh: 波阿斯问监管收割的仆人说，那是谁家的女子。

chapters.en: The overseer replied, “She is the Moabite who came back from Moab with Naomi.
chapters.zh: 监管收割的仆人回答说，是那摩押女子，跟随拿俄米从摩押地回来的。

chapters.en: She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.’ She came into the field and has remained here from morning till now, except for a short rest in the shelter.”
chapters.zh: 她说，请你容我跟着收割的人，拾取打捆剩下的麦穗，她从早晨直到如今，除了在屋子里坐一会儿，常在这里。

chapters.en: So Boaz said to Ruth, “My daughter, listen to me. Don’t go and glean in another field and don’t go away from here. Stay here with the women who work for me.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯对路得说，女儿阿，听我说，不要往别人田里拾取麦穗，也不要离开这里，要常与我使女们在一处。

chapters.en: Watch the field where the men are harvesting, and follow along after the women. I have told the men not to lay a hand on you. And whenever you are thirsty, go and get a drink from the water jars the men have filled.”
chapters.zh: 我的仆人在那块田收割，你就跟着他们去。我已经吩咐仆人不可欺负你。你若渴了，就可以到器皿那里喝仆人打来的水。

chapters.en: At this, she bowed down with her face to the ground. She asked him, “Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you notice me—a foreigner?”
chapters.zh: 路得就俯伏在地叩拜，对他说，我既是外邦人，怎么蒙你的恩，这样顾恤我呢？

chapters.en: Boaz replied, “I’ve been told all about what you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband—how you left your father and mother and your homeland and came to live with a people you did not know before.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯回答说，自从你丈夫死后，凡你向婆婆所行的，并你离开父母和本地，到素不认识的民中，这些事人全都告诉我了。

chapters.en: May the LORD repay you for what you have done. May you be richly rewarded by the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华照你所行的赏赐你。你来投靠耶和华以色列神的翅膀下，愿你满得他的赏赐。

chapters.en: “May I continue to find favor in your eyes, my lord,” she said. “You have put me at ease by speaking kindly to your servant—though I do not have the standing of one of your servants.”
chapters.zh: 路得说，我主阿，愿在你眼前蒙恩。我虽然不及你的一个使女，你还用慈爱的话安慰我的心。

chapters.en: At mealtime Boaz said to her, “Come over here. Have some bread and dip it in the wine vinegar.” When she sat down with the harvesters, he offered her some roasted grain. She ate all she wanted and had some left over.
chapters.zh: 到了吃饭的时候，波阿斯对路得说，你到这里来吃饼，将饼蘸在醋里。路得就在收割的人旁边坐下，他们把烘了的穗子递给她。她吃饱了，还有余剩的。

chapters.en: As she got up to glean, Boaz gave orders to his men, “Let her gather among the sheaves and don’t reprimand her.
chapters.zh: 她起来又拾取麦穗，波阿斯吩咐仆人说，她就是在捆中拾取麦穗，也可以容她，不可羞辱她。

chapters.en: Even pull out some stalks for her from the bundles and leave them for her to pick up, and don’t rebuke her.”
chapters.zh: 并要从捆里抽出些来，留在地下任她拾取，不可叱吓她。

chapters.en: So Ruth gleaned in the field until evening. Then she threshed the barley she had gathered, and it amounted to about an ephah.
chapters.zh: 这样，路得在田间拾取麦穗，直到晚上，将所拾取的打了，约有一伊法大麦。

chapters.en: She carried it back to town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gathered. Ruth also brought out and gave her what she had left over after she had eaten enough.
chapters.zh: 她就把所拾取的带进城去给婆婆看，又把她吃饱了所剩的给了婆婆。

chapters.en: Her mother-in-law asked her, “Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!” Then Ruth told her mother-in-law about the one at whose place she had been working. “The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz,” she said.
chapters.zh: 婆婆问她说，你今日在哪里拾取麦穗，在哪里做工呢？愿那顾恤你的得福。路得就告诉婆婆说，我今日在一个名叫波阿斯的人那里做工。

chapters.en: “The LORD bless him!” Naomi said to her daughter-in-law. “He has not stopped showing his kindness to the living and the dead.” She added, “That man is our close relative; he is one of our guardian-redeemers. ”
chapters.zh: 拿俄米对儿妇说，愿那人蒙耶和华赐福，因为他不断地恩待活人死人。拿俄米又说，那是我们本族的人，是一个至近的亲属。

chapters.en: Then Ruth the Moabite said, “He even said to me, ‘Stay with my workers until they finish harvesting all my grain.’ ”
chapters.zh: 摩押女子路得说，他对我说，你要紧随我的仆人拾取麦穗，直等他们收完了我的庄稼。

chapters.en: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It will be good for you, my daughter, to go with the women who work for him, because in someone else’s field you might be harmed.”
chapters.zh: 拿俄米对儿妇路得说，女儿阿，你跟着他的使女出去，不叫人遇见你在别人田间，这才为好。

chapters.en: So Ruth stayed close to the women of Boaz to glean until the barley and wheat harvests were finished. And she lived with her mother-in-law.
chapters.zh: 于是路得与波阿斯的使女常在一处拾取麦穗，直到收完了大麦和小麦。路得仍与婆婆同住。

chapters.en: One day Ruth’s mother-in-law Naomi said to her, “My daughter, I must find a home for you, where you will be well provided for.
chapters.zh: 路得的婆婆拿俄米对她说，女儿阿，我不当为你找个安身之处，使你享福吗？

chapters.en: Now Boaz, with whose women you have worked, is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be winnowing barley on the threshing floor.
chapters.zh: 你与波阿斯的使女常在一处，波阿斯不是我们的亲族吗？他今夜在场上簸大麦，

chapters.en: Wash, put on perfume, and get dressed in your best clothes. Then go down to the threshing floor, but don’t let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
chapters.zh: 你要沐浴抹膏，换上衣服，下到场上，却不要使那人认出你来。你等他吃喝完了，

chapters.en: When he lies down, note the place where he is lying. Then go and uncover his feet and lie down. He will tell you what to do.”
chapters.zh: 到他睡的时候，你看准他睡的地方，就进去掀开他脚上的被，躺卧在那里，他必告诉你所当做的事。

chapters.en: “I will do whatever you say,” Ruth answered.
chapters.zh: 路得说，凡你所吩咐的，我必遵行。

chapters.en: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law told her to do.
chapters.zh: 路得就下到场上，照她婆婆所吩咐她的而行。

chapters.en: When Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went over to lie down at the far end of the grain pile. Ruth approached quietly, uncovered his feet and lay down.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯吃喝完了，心里欢畅，就去睡在麦堆旁边。路得便悄悄地来掀开他脚上的被，躺卧在那里。

chapters.en: In the middle of the night something startled the man; he turned—and there was a woman lying at his feet!
chapters.zh: 到了夜半，那人忽然惊醒，翻过身来，不料有女子躺在他的脚下。

chapters.en: “Who are you?” he asked. “I am your servant Ruth,” she said. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, since you are a guardian-redeemer of our family.”
chapters.zh: 他就说，你是谁。回答说，我是你的婢女路得。求你用你的衣襟遮盖我，因为你是我一个至近的亲属。

chapters.en: “The LORD bless you, my daughter,” he replied. “This kindness is greater than that which you showed earlier: You have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯说，女儿阿，愿你蒙耶和华赐福。你末后的恩比先前更大。因为少年人无论贫富，你都没有跟从。

chapters.en: And now, my daughter, don’t be afraid. I will do for you all you ask. All the people of my town know that you are a woman of noble character.
chapters.zh: 女儿阿，现在不要惧怕，凡你所说的，我必照着行。我本城的人都知道你是个贤德的女子。

chapters.en: Although it is true that I am a guardian-redeemer of our family, there is another who is more closely related than I.
chapters.zh: 我实在是你一个至近的亲属，只是还有一个人比我更近。

chapters.en: Stay here for the night, and in the morning if he wants to do his duty as your guardian-redeemer, good; let him redeem you. But if he is not willing, as surely as the LORD lives I will do it. Lie here until morning.”
chapters.zh: 你今夜在这里住宿，明早他若肯为你尽亲属的本分。就由他吧。倘若不肯，我指着永生的耶和华起誓，我必为你尽了本分，你只管躺到天亮。

chapters.en: So she lay at his feet until morning, but got up before anyone could be recognized; and he said, “No one must know that a woman came to the threshing floor.”
chapters.zh: 路得便在他脚下躺到天快亮。人彼此不能辨认的时候就起来了。波阿斯说，不可使人知道有女子到场上来。

chapters.en: He also said, “Bring me the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” When she did so, he poured into it six measures of barley and placed the bundle on her. Then he went back to town.
chapters.zh: 又对路得说，打开你所披的外衣。她打开了，波阿斯就撮了六簸箕大麦，帮她扛在肩上，她便进城去了。

chapters.en: When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, “How did it go, my daughter?” Then she told her everything Boaz had done for her
chapters.zh: 路得回到婆婆那里，婆婆说，女儿阿，怎么样了。路得就将那人向她所行的述说了一遍。

chapters.en: and added, “He gave me these six measures of barley, saying, ‘Don’t go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’ ”
chapters.zh: 又说，那人给了我六簸箕大麦，对我说，你不可空手回去见你的婆婆。

chapters.en: Then Naomi said, “Wait, my daughter, until you find out what happens. For the man will not rest until the matter is settled today.”
chapters.zh: 婆婆说，女儿阿，你只管安坐等候，看这事怎样成就，因为那人今日不办成这事必不休息。

chapters.en: Meanwhile Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down there just as the guardian-redeemer he had mentioned came along. Boaz said, “Come over here, my friend, and sit down.” So he went over and sat down.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯到了城门，坐在那里，恰巧波阿斯所说的那至近的亲属经过。波阿斯说，某人哪，你来坐在这里。他就来坐下。

chapters.en: Boaz took ten of the elders of the town and said, “Sit here,” and they did so.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯又从本城的长老中拣选了十人，对他们说，请你们坐在这里。他们就都坐下。

chapters.en: Then he said to the guardian-redeemer, “Naomi, who has come back from Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our relative Elimelek.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯对那至近的亲属说，从摩押地回来的拿俄米，现在要卖我们族兄以利米勒的那块地。

chapters.en: I thought I should bring the matter to your attention and suggest that you buy it in the presence of these seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, do so. But if you will not, tell me, so I will know. For no one has the right to do it except you, and I am next in line.” “I will redeem it,” he said.
chapters.zh: 我想当赎那块地的是你，其次是我，以外再没有别人了。你可以在这里的人面前，和我本国的长老面前说明，你若肯赎就赎，若不肯赎就告诉我。那人回答说，我肯赎。

chapters.en: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the land from Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the dead man’s widow, in order to maintain the name of the dead with his property.”
chapters.zh: 波阿斯说，你从拿俄米手中买这地的时候，也当娶（原文作买十节同）死人的妻摩押女子路得，使死人在产业上存留他的名。

chapters.en: At this, the guardian-redeemer said, “Then I cannot redeem it because I might endanger my own estate. You redeem it yourself. I cannot do it.”
chapters.zh: 那人说，这样我就不能赎了，恐怕于我的产业有碍。你可以赎我所当赎的，我不能赎了。

chapters.en: (Now in earlier times in Israel, for the redemption and transfer of property to become final, one party took off his sandal and gave it to the other. This was the method of legalizing transactions in Israel.)
chapters.zh: 从前，在以色列中要定夺什么事，或赎回，或交易，这人就脱鞋给那人。以色列人都以此为证据。

chapters.en: So the guardian-redeemer said to Boaz, “Buy it yourself.” And he removed his sandal.
chapters.zh: 那人对波阿斯说，你自己买吧。于是将鞋脱下来了。

chapters.en: Then Boaz announced to the elders and all the people, “Today you are witnesses that I have bought from Naomi all the property of Elimelek, Kilion and Mahlon.
chapters.zh: 波阿斯对长老和众民说，你们今日作见证，凡属以利米勒和基连，玛伦的，我都从拿俄米手中置买了。

chapters.en: I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s widow, as my wife, in order to maintain the name of the dead with his property, so that his name will not disappear from among his family or from his hometown. Today you are witnesses!”
chapters.zh: 又娶了玛伦的妻摩押女子路得为妻，好在死人的产业上存留他的名，免得他的名在本族本乡灭没。你们今日可以作见证。

chapters.en: Then the elders and all the people at the gate said, “We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is coming into your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the family of Israel. May you have standing in Ephrathah and be famous in Bethlehem.
chapters.zh: 在城门坐着的众民和长老都说，我们作见证。愿耶和华使进你家的这女子，像建立以色列家的拉结，利亚二人一样。又愿你在以法他得亨通，在伯利恒得名声。

chapters.en: Through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman, may your family be like that of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah.”
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华从这少年女子赐你后裔，使你的家像他玛，从犹大所生法勒斯的家一般。

chapters.en: So Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife. When he made love to her, the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son.
chapters.zh: 于是，波阿斯娶了路得为妻，与她同房。耶和华使她怀孕生了一个儿子。

chapters.en: The women said to Naomi: “Praise be to the LORD, who this day has not left you without a guardian-redeemer. May he become famous throughout Israel!
chapters.zh: 妇人们对拿俄米说，耶和华是应当称颂的。因为今日没有撇下你使你无至近的亲属。愿这孩子在以色列中得名声。

chapters.en: He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and who is better to you than seven sons, has given him birth.”
chapters.zh: 他必提起你的精神，奉养你的老，因为是爱慕你的那儿妇所生的。有这儿妇比有七个儿子还好。

chapters.en: Then Naomi took the child in her arms and cared for him.
chapters.zh: 拿俄米就把孩子抱在怀中，作他的养母。

chapters.en: The women living there said, “Naomi has a son!” And they named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
chapters.zh: 邻舍的妇人说，拿俄米得孩子了。就给孩子起名叫俄备得。这俄备得是耶西的父，耶西是大卫的父。

chapters.en: This, then, is the family line of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron,
chapters.zh: 法勒斯的后代，记在下面。法勒斯生希斯仑。

chapters.en: Hezron the father of Ram, Ram the father of Amminadab,
chapters.zh: 希斯仑生兰，兰生亚米拿达。

chapters.en: Amminadab the father of Nahshon, Nahshon the father of Salmon,
chapters.zh: 亚米拿达生拿顺，拿顺生撒门。

chapters.en: Salmon the father of Boaz, Boaz the father of Obed,
chapters.zh: 撒门生波阿斯，波阿斯生俄备得。

chapters.en: Obed the father of Jesse, and Jesse the father of David.
chapters.zh: 俄备得生耶西，耶西生大卫。

chapters.en: There was a certain man from Ramathaim, a Zuphite from the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
chapters.zh: 以法莲山地的拉玛琐非有一个以法莲人，名叫以利加拿，是苏弗的玄孙，托户的曾孙，以利户的孙子，耶罗罕的儿子。

chapters.en: He had two wives; one was called Hannah and the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
chapters.zh: 他有两个妻，一名哈拿，一名毗尼拿。毗尼拿有儿女，哈拿没有儿女。

chapters.en: Year after year this man went up from his town to worship and sacrifice to the LORD Almighty at Shiloh, where Hophni and Phinehas, the two sons of Eli, were priests of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这人每年从本城上到示罗，敬拜祭祀万军之耶和华。在那里有以利的两个儿子何弗尼，非尼哈当耶和华的祭司。

chapters.en: Whenever the day came for Elkanah to sacrifice, he would give portions of the meat to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.
chapters.zh: 以利加拿每逢献祭的日子，将祭肉分给他的妻毗尼拿和毗尼拿所生的儿女。

chapters.en: But to Hannah he gave a double portion because he loved her, and the LORD had closed her womb.
chapters.zh: 给哈拿的却是双分，因为他爱哈拿。无奈耶和华不使哈拿生育。

chapters.en: Because the LORD had closed Hannah’s womb, her rival kept provoking her in order to irritate her.
chapters.zh: 毗尼拿见耶和华不使哈拿生育，就作她的对头，大大激动她，要使她生气。

chapters.en: This went on year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, her rival provoked her till she wept and would not eat.
chapters.zh: 每年上到耶和华殿的时候，以利加拿都以双分给哈拿。毗尼拿仍是激动她，以致她哭泣不吃饭。

chapters.en: Her husband Elkanah would say to her, “Hannah, why are you weeping? Why don’t you eat? Why are you downhearted? Don’t I mean more to you than ten sons?”
chapters.zh: 她丈夫以利加拿对她说，哈拿阿，你为何哭泣，不吃饭，心里愁闷呢？有我不比十个儿子还好吗？
