chapters.en: But Samuel said, “As your sword has made women childless, so will your mother be childless among women.” And Samuel put Agag to death before the LORD at Gilgal.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳说，你既用刀使妇人丧子，这样，你母亲在妇人中也必丧子。于是，撒母耳在吉甲耶和华面前将亚甲杀死。

chapters.en: Then Samuel left for Ramah, but Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳回了拉玛。扫罗上他所住的基比亚，回自己的家去了。

chapters.en: Until the day Samuel died, he did not go to see Saul again, though Samuel mourned for him. And the LORD regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳直到死的日子，再没有见扫罗。但撒母耳为扫罗悲伤，是因耶和华后悔立他为以色列的王。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Samuel, “How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and be on your way; I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem. I have chosen one of his sons to be king.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对撒母耳说，我既厌弃扫罗作以色列的王，你为他悲伤要到几时呢？你将膏油盛满了角，我差遣你往伯利恒人耶西那里去。因为我在他众子之内，预定一个作王的。

chapters.en: But Samuel said, “How can I go? If Saul hears about it, he will kill me.” The LORD said, “Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’
chapters.zh: 撒母耳说，我怎能去呢？扫罗若听见，必要杀我。耶和华说，你可以带一只牛犊去，就说，我来是要向耶和华献祭。

chapters.en: Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what to do. You are to anoint for me the one I indicate.”
chapters.zh: 你要请耶西来吃祭肉，我就指示你所当行的事。我所指给你的人，你要膏他。

chapters.en: Samuel did what the LORD said. When he arrived at Bethlehem, the elders of the town trembled when they met him. They asked, “Do you come in peace?”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳就照耶和华的话去行。到了伯利恒，那城里的长老都战战兢兢地出来迎接他，问他说，你是为平安来的吗？

chapters.en: Samuel replied, “Yes, in peace; I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come to the sacrifice with me.” Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
chapters.zh: 他说，为平安来的，我是给耶和华献祭。你们当自洁，来与我同吃祭肉。撒母耳就使耶西和他众子自洁，请他们来吃祭肉。

chapters.en: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and thought, “Surely the LORD’s anointed stands here before the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 他们来的时候，撒母耳看见以利押，就心里说，耶和华的受膏者必定在他面前。

chapters.en: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or his height, for I have rejected him. The LORD does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华却对撒母耳说，不要看他的外貌和他身材高大，我不拣选他。因为，耶和华不像人看人，人是看外貌。耶和华是看内心。

chapters.en: Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass in front of Samuel. But Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
chapters.zh: 耶西叫亚比拿达从撒母耳面前经过，撒母耳说，耶和华也不拣选他。

chapters.en: Jesse then had Shammah pass by, but Samuel said, “Nor has the LORD chosen this one.”
chapters.zh: 耶西又叫沙玛从撒母耳面前经过，撒母耳说，耶和华也不拣选他。

chapters.en: Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel said to him, “The LORD has not chosen these.”
chapters.zh: 耶西叫他七个儿子都从撒母耳面前经过，撒母耳说，这都不是耶和华所拣选的。

chapters.en: So he asked Jesse, “Are these all the sons you have?” “There is still the youngest,” Jesse answered. “He is tending the sheep.” Samuel said, “Send for him; we will not sit down until he arrives.”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳对耶西说，你的儿子都在这里吗？他回答说，还有个小的，现在放羊。撒母耳对耶西说，你打发人去叫他来。他若不来，我们必不坐席。

chapters.en: So he sent for him and had him brought in. He was glowing with health and had a fine appearance and handsome features. Then the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him; this is the one.”
chapters.zh: 耶西就打发人去叫了他来。他面色光红，双目清秀，容貌俊美。耶和华说，这就是他，你起来膏他。

chapters.en: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day on the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon David. Samuel then went to Ramah.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳就用角里的膏油，在他诸兄中膏了他。从这日起，耶和华的灵就大大感动大卫。撒母耳起身回拉玛去了。

chapters.en: Now the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented him.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵离开扫罗，有恶魔从耶和华那里来扰乱他。

chapters.en: Saul’s attendants said to him, “See, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的臣仆对他说，现在有恶魔从神那里来扰乱你。

chapters.en: Let our lord command his servants here to search for someone who can play the lyre. He will play when the evil spirit from God comes on you, and you will feel better.”
chapters.zh: 我们的主可以吩咐面前的臣仆，找一个善于弹琴的来，等神那里来的恶魔临到你身上的时候，使他用手弹琴，你就好了。

chapters.en: So Saul said to his attendants, “Find someone who plays well and bring him to me.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对臣仆说，你们可以为我找一个善于弹琴的，带到我这里来。

chapters.en: One of the servants answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play the lyre. He is a brave man and a warrior. He speaks well and is a fine-looking man. And the LORD is with him.”
chapters.zh: 其中有一个少年人说，我曾见伯利恒人耶西的一个儿子善于弹琴，是大有勇敢的战士，说话合宜，容貌俊美，耶和华也与他同在。

chapters.en: Then Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, “Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.”
chapters.zh: 于是扫罗差遣使者去见耶西，说，请你打发你放羊的儿子大卫到我这里来。

chapters.en: So Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat and sent them with his son David to Saul.
chapters.zh: 耶西就把几个饼和一皮袋酒，并一只山羊羔，都驮在驴上，交给他儿子大卫，送与扫罗。

chapters.en: David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul liked him very much, and David became one of his armor-bearers.
chapters.zh: 大卫到了扫罗那里，就侍立在扫罗面前。扫罗甚喜爱他，他就作了扫罗拿兵器的人。

chapters.en: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, “Allow David to remain in my service, for I am pleased with him.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗差遣人去见耶西，说，求你容大卫侍立在我面前，因为他在我眼前蒙了恩。

chapters.en: Whenever the spirit from God came on Saul, David would take up his lyre and play. Then relief would come to Saul; he would feel better, and the evil spirit would leave him.
chapters.zh: 从神那里来的恶魔临到扫罗身上的时候，大卫就拿琴，用手而弹，扫罗便舒畅爽快，恶魔离了他。

chapters.en: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for war and assembled at Sokoh in Judah. They pitched camp at Ephes Dammim, between Sokoh and Azekah.
chapters.zh: 非利士人招聚他们的军旅，要来争战。聚集在属犹大的梭哥，安营在梭哥和亚西加中间的以弗大悯。

chapters.en: Saul and the Israelites assembled and camped in the Valley of Elah and drew up their battle line to meet the Philistines.
chapters.zh: 扫罗和以色列人也聚集，在以拉谷安营，摆列队伍，要与非利士人打仗。

chapters.en: The Philistines occupied one hill and the Israelites another, with the valley between them.
chapters.zh: 非利士人站在这边山上，以色列人站在那边山上，当中有谷。

chapters.en: A champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out of the Philistine camp. His height was six cubits and a span.
chapters.zh: 从非利士营中出来一个讨战的人，名叫歌利亚，是迦特人，身高六肘零一虎口。

chapters.en: He had a bronze helmet on his head and wore a coat of scale armor of bronze weighing five thousand shekels ;
chapters.zh: 头戴铜盔，身穿铠甲，甲重五千舍客勒。

chapters.en: on his legs he wore bronze greaves, and a bronze javelin was slung on his back.
chapters.zh: 腿上有铜护膝，两肩之中背负铜戟。

chapters.en: His spear shaft was like a weaver’s rod, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. His shield bearer went ahead of him.
chapters.zh: 枪杆粗如织布的机轴，铁枪头重六百舍客勒。有一个拿盾牌的人在他前面走。

chapters.en: Goliath stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, “Why do you come out and line up for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not the servants of Saul? Choose a man and have him come down to me.
chapters.zh: 歌利亚对着以色列的军队站立，呼叫说，你们出来摆列队伍作什么呢？我不是非利士人吗？你们不是扫罗的仆人吗？可以从你们中间拣选一人，使他下到我这里来。

chapters.en: If he is able to fight and kill me, we will become your subjects; but if I overcome him and kill him, you will become our subjects and serve us.”
chapters.zh: 他若能与我战斗，将我杀死，我们就作你们的仆人。我若胜了他，将他杀死，你们就作我们的仆人，服事我们。

chapters.en: Then the Philistine said, “This day I defy the armies of Israel! Give me a man and let us fight each other.”
chapters.zh: 那非利士人又说，我今日向以色列人的军队骂阵。你们叫一个人出来，与我战斗。

chapters.en: On hearing the Philistine’s words, Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and terrified.
chapters.zh: 扫罗和以色列众人听见非利士人的这些话，就惊惶，极其害怕。

chapters.en: Now David was the son of an Ephrathite named Jesse, who was from Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons, and in Saul’s time he was very old.
chapters.zh: 大卫是犹大，伯利恒的以法他人耶西的儿子。耶西有八个儿子。当扫罗的时候，耶西已经老迈。

chapters.en: Jesse’s three oldest sons had followed Saul to the war: The firstborn was Eliab; the second, Abinadab; and the third, Shammah.
chapters.zh: 耶西的三个大儿子跟随扫罗出征。这出征的三个儿子，长子名叫以利押，次子名叫亚比拿达，三子名叫沙玛。

chapters.en: David was the youngest. The three oldest followed Saul,
chapters.zh: 大卫是最小的。那三个大儿子跟随扫罗。

chapters.en: but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.
chapters.zh: 大卫有时离开扫罗，回伯利恒放他父亲的羊。

chapters.en: For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening and took his stand.
chapters.zh: 那非利士人早晚都出来站着，如此四十日。

chapters.en: Now Jesse said to his son David, “Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread for your brothers and hurry to their camp.
chapters.zh: 一日，耶西对他儿子大卫说，你拿一伊法烘了的穗子和十个饼，速速地送到营里去，交给你哥哥们。

chapters.en: Take along these ten cheeses to the commander of their unit. See how your brothers are and bring back some assurance from them.
chapters.zh: 再拿这十块奶饼，送给他们的千夫长，且问你哥哥们好，向他们要一封信来。

chapters.en: They are with Saul and all the men of Israel in the Valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗与大卫的三个哥哥和以色列众人，在以拉谷与非利士人打仗。

chapters.en: Early in the morning David left the flock in the care of a shepherd, loaded up and set out, as Jesse had directed. He reached the camp as the army was going out to its battle positions, shouting the war cry.
chapters.zh: 大卫早晨起来，将羊交托一个看守的人，照着他父亲所吩咐的话，带着食物去了。到了辎重营，军兵刚出到战场，呐喊要战。

chapters.en: Israel and the Philistines were drawing up their lines facing each other.
chapters.zh: 以色列人和非利士人都摆列队伍，彼此相对。

chapters.en: David left his things with the keeper of supplies, ran to the battle lines and asked his brothers how they were.
chapters.zh: 大卫把他带来的食物留在看守物件人的手下，跑到战场，问他哥哥们安。

chapters.en: As he was talking with them, Goliath, the Philistine champion from Gath, stepped out from his lines and shouted his usual defiance, and David heard it.
chapters.zh: 与他们说话的时候，那讨战的，就是属迦特的非利士人歌利亚，从非利士队中出来，说从前所说的话。大卫都听见了。

chapters.en: Whenever the Israelites saw the man, they all fled from him in great fear.
chapters.zh: 以色列众人看见那人，就逃跑，极其害怕。

chapters.en: Now the Israelites had been saying, “Do you see how this man keeps coming out? He comes out to defy Israel. The king will give great wealth to the man who kills him. He will also give him his daughter in marriage and will exempt his family from taxes in Israel.”
chapters.zh: 以色列人彼此说，这上来的人你看见了吗？他上来是要向以色列人骂阵。若有能杀他的，王必赏赐他大财，将自己的女儿给他为妻，并在以色列人中免他父家纳粮当差。

chapters.en: David asked the men standing near him, “What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes this disgrace from Israel? Who is this uncircumcised Philistine that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
chapters.zh: 大卫问站在旁边的人说，有人杀这非利士人，除掉以色列人的耻辱，怎样待他呢？这未受割礼的非利士人是谁呢？竟敢向永生神的军队骂阵吗？

chapters.en: They repeated to him what they had been saying and told him, “This is what will be done for the man who kills him.”
chapters.zh: 百姓照先前的话回答他说，有人能杀这非利士人，必如此如此待他。

chapters.en: When Eliab, David’s oldest brother, heard him speaking with the men, he burned with anger at him and asked, “Why have you come down here? And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know how conceited you are and how wicked your heart is; you came down only to watch the battle.”
chapters.zh: 大卫的长兄以利押听见大卫与他们所说的话，就向他发怒，说，你下来作什么呢？在旷野的那几只羊，你交托了谁呢？我知道你的骄傲和你心里的恶意，你下来特为要看争战。

chapters.en: “Now what have I done?” said David. “Can’t I even speak?”
chapters.zh: 大卫说，我作了什么呢？我来岂没有缘故吗？

chapters.en: He then turned away to someone else and brought up the same matter, and the men answered him as before.
chapters.zh: 大卫就离开他转向别人，照先前的话而问。百姓仍照先前的话回答他。

chapters.en: What David said was overheard and reported to Saul, and Saul sent for him.
chapters.zh: 有人听见大卫所说的话，就告诉了扫罗。扫罗便打发人叫他来。

chapters.en: David said to Saul, “Let no one lose heart on account of this Philistine; your servant will go and fight him.”
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说，人都不必因那非利士人胆怯。你的仆人要去与那非利士人战斗。

chapters.en: Saul replied, “You are not able to go out against this Philistine and fight him; you are only a young man, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对大卫说，你不能去与那非利士人战斗。因为你年纪太轻，他自幼就作战士。

chapters.en: But David said to Saul, “Your servant has been keeping his father’s sheep. When a lion or a bear came and carried off a sheep from the flock,
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说，你仆人为父亲放羊，有时来了狮子，有时来了熊，从群中衔一只羊羔去。

chapters.en: I went after it, struck it and rescued the sheep from its mouth. When it turned on me, I seized it by its hair, struck it and killed it.
chapters.zh: 我就追赶它，击打它，将羊羔从它口中救出来。它起来要害我，我就揪着它的胡子，将它打死。

chapters.en: Your servant has killed both the lion and the bear; this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has defied the armies of the living God.
chapters.zh: 你仆人曾打死狮子和熊，这未受割礼的非利士人向永生神的军队骂阵，也必像狮子和熊一般。

chapters.en: The LORD who rescued me from the paw of the lion and the paw of the bear will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine.” Saul said to David, “Go, and the LORD be with you.”
chapters.zh: 大卫又说，耶和华救我脱离狮子和熊的爪，也必救我脱离这非利士人的手。扫罗对大卫说，你可以去吧。耶和华必与你同在。

chapters.en: Then Saul dressed David in his own tunic. He put a coat of armor on him and a bronze helmet on his head.
chapters.zh: 扫罗就把自己的战衣给大卫穿上，将铜盔给他戴上，又给他穿上铠甲。

chapters.en: David fastened on his sword over the tunic and tried walking around, because he was not used to them. “I cannot go in these,” he said to Saul, “because I am not used to them.” So he took them off.
chapters.zh: 大卫把刀跨在战衣外，试试能走不能走。因为素来没有穿惯，就对扫罗说，我穿戴这些不能走，因为素来没有穿惯。于是摘脱了。

chapters.en: Then he took his staff in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the stream, put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag and, with his sling in his hand, approached the Philistine.
chapters.zh: 他手中拿杖，又在溪中挑选了五块光滑石子，放在袋里，就是牧人带的囊里。手中拿着甩石的机弦，就去迎那非利士人。

chapters.en: Meanwhile, the Philistine, with his shield bearer in front of him, kept coming closer to David.
chapters.zh: 非利士人也渐渐地迎着大卫来，拿盾牌的走在前头。

chapters.en: He looked David over and saw that he was little more than a boy, glowing with health and handsome, and he despised him.
chapters.zh: 非利士人观看，见了大卫，就藐视他。因为他年轻，面色光红，容貌俊美。

chapters.en: He said to David, “Am I a dog, that you come at me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
chapters.zh: 非利士人对大卫说，你拿杖到我这里来，我岂是狗呢？非利士人就指着自己的神咒诅大卫。

chapters.en: “Come here,” he said, “and I’ll give your flesh to the birds and the wild animals!”
chapters.zh: 非利士人又对大卫说，来吧。我将你的肉给空中的飞鸟，田野的走兽吃。

chapters.en: David said to the Philistine, “You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD Almighty, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
chapters.zh: 大卫对非利士人说，你来攻击我，是靠着刀枪和铜戟。我来攻击你，是靠着万军之耶和华的名，就是你所怒骂带领以色列军队的神。

chapters.en: This day the LORD will deliver you into my hands, and I’ll strike you down and cut off your head. This very day I will give the carcasses of the Philistine army to the birds and the wild animals, and the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel.
chapters.zh: 今日耶和华必将你交在我手里。我必杀你，斩你的头，又将非利士军兵的尸首给空中的飞鸟，地上的野兽吃，使普天下的人都知道以色列中有神。

chapters.en: All those gathered here will know that it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves; for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give all of you into our hands.”
chapters.zh: 又使这众人知道耶和华使人得胜，不是用刀用枪，因为争战的胜败全在乎耶和华。他必将你们交在我们手里。

chapters.en: As the Philistine moved closer to attack him, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.
chapters.zh: 非利士人起身，迎着大卫前来。大卫急忙迎着非利士人，往战场跑去。

chapters.en: Reaching into his bag and taking out a stone, he slung it and struck the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.
chapters.zh: 大卫用手从囊中掏出一块石子来，用机弦甩去，打中非利士人的额，石子进入额内，他就仆倒，面伏于地。

chapters.en: So David triumphed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him.
chapters.zh: 这样，大卫用机弦甩石，胜了那非利士人，打死他。大卫手中却没有刀。

chapters.en: David ran and stood over him. He took hold of the Philistine’s sword and drew it from the sheath. After he killed him, he cut off his head with the sword. When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran.
chapters.zh: 大卫跑去，站在非利士人身旁，将他的刀从鞘中拔出来，杀死他，割了他的头。非利士众人看见他们讨战的勇士死了，就都逃跑。

chapters.en: Then the men of Israel and Judah surged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron. Their dead were strewn along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.
chapters.zh: 以色列人和犹大人便起身呐喊，追赶非利士人，直到迦特（或作该）和以革伦的城门。被杀的非利士人倒在沙拉音的路上，直到迦特和以革伦。

chapters.en: When the Israelites returned from chasing the Philistines, they plundered their camp.
chapters.zh: 以色列人追赶非利士人回来，就夺了他们的营盘。

chapters.en: David took the Philistine’s head and brought it to Jerusalem; he put the Philistine’s weapons in his own tent.
chapters.zh: 大卫将那非利士人的头拿到耶路撒冷，却将他军装放在自己的帐棚里。

chapters.en: As Saul watched David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, commander of the army, “Abner, whose son is that young man?” Abner replied, “As surely as you live, Your Majesty, I don’t know.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗看见大卫去攻击非利士人，就问元帅押尼珥说，押尼珥阿，那少年人是谁的儿子。押尼珥说，我敢在王面前起誓，我不知道。

chapters.en: The king said, “Find out whose son this young man is.”
chapters.zh: 王说，你可以问问那幼年人是谁的儿子。

chapters.en: As soon as David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with David still holding the Philistine’s head.
chapters.zh: 大卫打死非利士人回来，押尼珥领他到扫罗面前，他手中拿着非利士人的头。

chapters.en: “Whose son are you, young man?” Saul asked him. David said, “I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗问他说，少年人哪，你是谁的儿子。大卫说，我是你仆人伯利恒人耶西的儿子。

chapters.en: After David had finished talking with Saul, Jonathan became one in spirit with David, and he loved him as himself.
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说完了话，约拿单的心与大卫的心深相契合。约拿单爱大卫，如同爱自己的性命。

chapters.en: From that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return home to his family.
chapters.zh: 那日扫罗留住大卫，不容他再回父家。

chapters.en: And Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.
chapters.zh: 约拿单爱大卫如同爱自己的性命，就与他结盟。

chapters.en: Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, and even his sword, his bow and his belt.
chapters.zh: 约拿单从身上脱下外袍，给了大卫，又将战衣，刀，弓，腰带都给了他。

chapters.en: Whatever mission Saul sent him on, David was so successful that Saul gave him a high rank in the army. This pleased all the troops, and Saul’s officers as well.
chapters.zh: 扫罗无论差遣大卫往何处去，他都作事精明。扫罗就立他作战士长，众百姓和扫罗的臣仆无不喜悦。

chapters.en: When the men were returning home after David had killed the Philistine, the women came out from all the towns of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with joyful songs and with timbrels and lyres.
chapters.zh: 大卫打死了那非利士人，同众人回来的时候，妇女们从以色列各城里出来，欢欢喜喜，打鼓击磬，歌唱跳舞，迎接扫罗王。

chapters.en: As they danced, they sang: “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”
chapters.zh: 众妇女舞蹈唱和，说，扫罗杀死千千，大卫杀死万万。

chapters.en: Saul was very angry; this refrain displeased him greatly. “They have credited David with tens of thousands,” he thought, “but me with only thousands. What more can he get but the kingdom?”
chapters.zh: 扫罗甚发怒，不喜悦这话，就说，将万万归大卫，千千归我，只剩下王位没有给他了。

chapters.en: And from that time on Saul kept a close eye on David.
chapters.zh: 从这日起，扫罗就怒视大卫。

chapters.en: The next day an evil spirit from God came forcefully on Saul. He was prophesying in his house, while David was playing the lyre, as he usually did. Saul had a spear in his hand
chapters.zh: 次日，从神那里来的恶魔大大降在扫罗身上，他就在家中胡言乱语。大卫照常弹琴，扫罗手里拿着枪。

chapters.en: and he hurled it, saying to himself, “I’ll pin David to the wall.” But David eluded him twice.
chapters.zh: 扫罗把枪一抡，心里说，我要将大卫刺透，钉在墙上。大卫躲避他两次。

chapters.en: Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul.
chapters.zh: 扫罗惧怕大卫。因为耶和华离开自己，与大卫同在。

chapters.en: So he sent David away from him and gave him command over a thousand men, and David led the troops in their campaigns.
chapters.zh: 所以扫罗使大卫离开自己，立他为千夫长，他就领兵出入。

chapters.en: In everything he did he had great success, because the LORD was with him.
chapters.zh: 大卫作事无不精明，耶和华也与他同在。

chapters.en: When Saul saw how successful he was, he was afraid of him.
chapters.zh: 扫罗见大卫作事精明，就甚怕他。

chapters.en: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in their campaigns.
chapters.zh: 但以色列和犹大众人都爱大卫，因为他领他们出入。

chapters.en: Saul said to David, “Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage; only serve me bravely and fight the battles of the LORD.” For Saul said to himself, “I will not raise a hand against him. Let the Philistines do that!”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对大卫说，我将大女儿米拉给你为妻，只要你为我奋勇，为耶和华争战。扫罗心里说，我不好亲手害他，要借非利士人的手害他。

chapters.en: But David said to Saul, “Who am I, and what is my family or my clan in Israel, that I should become the king’s son-in-law?”
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说，我是谁？我是什么出身，我父家在以色列中是何等的家，岂敢作王的女婿呢？

chapters.en: So when the time came for Merab, Saul’s daughter, to be given to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的女儿米拉到了当给大卫的时候，扫罗却给了米何拉人亚得列为妻。

chapters.en: Now Saul’s daughter Michal was in love with David, and when they told Saul about it, he was pleased.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的次女米甲爱大卫。有人告诉扫罗，扫罗就喜悦。

chapters.en: “I will give her to him,” he thought, “so that she may be a snare to him and so that the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” So Saul said to David, “Now you have a second opportunity to become my son-in-law.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗心里说，我将这女儿给大卫，作他的网罗，好借非利士人的手害他。所以扫罗对大卫说，你今日可以第二次作我的女婿。

chapters.en: Then Saul ordered his attendants: “Speak to David privately and say, ‘Look, the king likes you, and his attendants all love you; now become his son-in-law.’ ”
chapters.zh: 扫罗吩咐臣仆说，你们暗中对大卫说，王喜悦你，王的臣仆也都喜爱你，所以你当作王的女婿。

chapters.en: They repeated these words to David. But David said, “Do you think it is a small matter to become the king’s son-in-law? I’m only a poor man and little known.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗的臣仆就照这话说给大卫听。大卫说，你们以为作王的女婿是一件小事吗？我是贫穷卑微的人。

chapters.en: When Saul’s servants told him what David had said,
chapters.zh: 扫罗的臣仆回奏说，大卫所说的如此如此。

chapters.en: Saul replied, “Say to David, ‘The king wants no other price for the bride than a hundred Philistine foreskins, to take revenge on his enemies.’ ” Saul’s plan was to have David fall by the hands of the Philistines.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说，你们要对大卫这样说，王不要什么聘礼，只要一百非利士人的阳皮，好在王的仇敌身上报仇。扫罗的意思要使大卫丧在非利士人的手里。

chapters.en: When the attendants told David these things, he was pleased to become the king’s son-in-law. So before the allotted time elapsed,
chapters.zh: 扫罗的臣仆将这话告诉大卫，大卫就欢喜作王的女婿。日期还没有到，

chapters.en: David took his men with him and went out and killed two hundred Philistines and brought back their foreskins. They counted out the full number to the king so that David might become the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal in marriage.
chapters.zh: 大卫和跟随他的人起身前往，杀了二百非利士人，将阳皮满数交给王，为要作王的女婿。于是扫罗将女儿米甲给大卫为妻。

chapters.en: When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David,
chapters.zh: 扫罗见耶和华与大卫同在，又知道女儿米甲爱大卫，

chapters.en: Saul became still more afraid of him, and he remained his enemy the rest of his days.
chapters.zh: 就更怕大卫，常作大卫的仇敌。

chapters.en: The Philistine commanders continued to go out to battle, and as often as they did, David met with more success than the rest of Saul’s officers, and his name became well known.
chapters.zh: 每逢非利士军长出来打仗，大卫比扫罗的臣仆作事精明，因此他的名被人尊重。

chapters.en: Saul told his son Jonathan and all the attendants to kill David. But Jonathan had taken a great liking to David
chapters.zh: 扫罗对他儿子约拿单和众臣仆说，要杀大卫。扫罗的儿子约拿单却甚喜爱大卫。

chapters.en: and warned him, “My father Saul is looking for a chance to kill you. Be on your guard tomorrow morning; go into hiding and stay there.
chapters.zh: 约拿单告诉大卫说，我父扫罗想要杀你，所以明日早晨你要小心，到一个僻静地方藏身。

chapters.en: I will go out and stand with my father in the field where you are. I’ll speak to him about you and will tell you what I find out.”
chapters.zh: 我就出到你所藏的田里，站在我父亲旁边与他谈论。我看他情形怎样，我必告诉你。

chapters.en: Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father and said to him, “Let not the king do wrong to his servant David; he has not wronged you, and what he has done has benefited you greatly.
chapters.zh: 约拿单向他父亲扫罗替大卫说好话，说，王不可得罪王的仆人大卫。因为他未曾得罪你，他所行的都与你大有益处。

chapters.en: He took his life in his hands when he killed the Philistine. The LORD won a great victory for all Israel, and you saw it and were glad. Why then would you do wrong to an innocent man like David by killing him for no reason?”
chapters.zh: 他拚命杀那非利士人，耶和华为以色列众人大行拯救。那时你看见，甚是欢喜，现在为何无故要杀大卫，流无辜人的血，自己取罪呢？

chapters.en: Saul listened to Jonathan and took this oath: “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗听了约拿单的话，就指着永生的耶和华起誓说，我必不杀他。

chapters.en: So Jonathan called David and told him the whole conversation. He brought him to Saul, and David was with Saul as before.
chapters.zh: 约拿单叫大卫来，把这一切事告诉他，带他去见扫罗。他就仍然侍立在扫罗面前。

chapters.en: Once more war broke out, and David went out and fought the Philistines. He struck them with such force that they fled before him.
chapters.zh: 此后又有争战的事。大卫出去与非利士人打仗，大大杀败他们，他们就在他面前逃跑。

chapters.en: But an evil spirit from the LORD came on Saul as he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand. While David was playing the lyre,
chapters.zh: 从耶和华那里来的恶魔又降在扫罗身上（扫罗手里拿枪坐在屋里），大卫就用手弹琴。

chapters.en: Saul tried to pin him to the wall with his spear, but David eluded him as Saul drove the spear into the wall. That night David made good his escape.
chapters.zh: 扫罗用枪想要刺透大卫，钉在墙上。他却躲开，扫罗的枪刺入墙内。当夜大卫逃走，躲避了。

chapters.en: Saul sent men to David’s house to watch it and to kill him in the morning. But Michal, David’s wife, warned him, “If you don’t run for your life tonight, tomorrow you’ll be killed.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗打发人到大卫的房屋那里窥探他，要等到天亮杀他。大卫的妻米甲对他说，你今夜若不逃命，明日你要被杀。

chapters.en: So Michal let David down through a window, and he fled and escaped.
chapters.zh: 于是米甲将大卫从窗户里缒下去。大卫就逃走，躲避了。

chapters.en: Then Michal took an idol and laid it on the bed, covering it with a garment and putting some goats’ hair at the head.
chapters.zh: 米甲把家中的神像放在床上，头枕在山羊毛装的枕头上，用被遮盖。

chapters.en: When Saul sent the men to capture David, Michal said, “He is ill.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗打发人去捉拿大卫，米甲说，他病了。

chapters.en: Then Saul sent the men back to see David and told them, “Bring him up to me in his bed so that I may kill him.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗又打发人去看大卫，说，当连床将他抬来，我好杀他。

chapters.en: But when the men entered, there was the idol in the bed, and at the head was some goats’ hair.
chapters.zh: 使者进去，看见床上有神像，头枕在山羊毛装的枕头上。

chapters.en: Saul said to Michal, “Why did you deceive me like this and send my enemy away so that he escaped?” Michal told him, “He said to me, ‘Let me get away. Why should I kill you?’ ”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对米甲说，你为什么这样欺哄我，放我仇敌逃走呢？米甲回答说，他对我说，你放我走，不然我要杀你。

chapters.en: When David had fled and made his escape, he went to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went to Naioth and stayed there.
chapters.zh: 大卫逃避，来到拉玛见撒母耳，将扫罗向他所行的事述说了一遍。他和撒母耳就往拿约去居住。

chapters.en: Word came to Saul: “David is in Naioth at Ramah”;
chapters.zh: 有人告诉扫罗，说大卫在拉玛的拿约。

chapters.en: so he sent men to capture him. But when they saw a group of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing there as their leader, the Spirit of God came on Saul’s men, and they also prophesied.
chapters.zh: 扫罗打发人去捉拿大卫。去的人见有一班先知都受感说话，撒母耳站在其中监管他们。打发去的人也受神的灵感动说话。

chapters.en: Saul was told about it, and he sent more men, and they prophesied too. Saul sent men a third time, and they also prophesied.
chapters.zh: 有人将这事告诉扫罗，他又打发人去，他们也受感说话。扫罗第三次打发人去，他们也受感说话。

chapters.en: Finally, he himself left for Ramah and went to the great cistern at Seku. And he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “Over in Naioth at Ramah,” they said.
chapters.zh: 然后扫罗自己往拉玛去，到了西沽的大井，问人说，撒母耳和大卫在哪里呢？有人说，在拉玛的拿约。

chapters.en: So Saul went to Naioth at Ramah. But the Spirit of God came even on him, and he walked along prophesying until he came to Naioth.
chapters.zh: 他就往拉玛的拿约去。神的灵也感动他，一面走一面说话，直到拉玛的拿约。

chapters.en: He stripped off his garments, and he too prophesied in Samuel’s presence. He lay naked all that day and all that night. This is why people say, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
chapters.zh: 他就脱了衣服，在撒母耳面前受感说话，一昼一夜露体躺卧。因此有句俗语说，扫罗也列在先知中吗？

chapters.en: Then David fled from Naioth at Ramah and went to Jonathan and asked, “What have I done? What is my crime? How have I wronged your father, that he is trying to kill me?”
chapters.zh: 大卫从拉玛的拿约逃跑，来到约拿单那里，对他说，我作了什么。有什么罪孽呢？在你父亲面前犯了什么罪，他竟寻索我的性命呢？

chapters.en: “Never!” Jonathan replied. “You are not going to die! Look, my father doesn’t do anything, great or small, without letting me know. Why would he hide this from me? It isn’t so!”
chapters.zh: 约拿单回答说，断然不是。你必不至死。我父作事，无论大小，没有不叫我知道的。怎么独有这事隐瞒我呢？决不如此。

chapters.en: But David took an oath and said, “Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said to himself, ‘Jonathan must not know this or he will be grieved.’ Yet as surely as the LORD lives and as you live, there is only a step between me and death.”
chapters.zh: 大卫又起誓说，你父亲准知我在你眼前蒙恩。他心里说，不如不叫约拿单知道，恐怕他愁烦。我指着永生的耶和华，又敢在你面前起誓，我离死不过一步。

chapters.en: Jonathan said to David, “Whatever you want me to do, I’ll do for you.”
chapters.zh: 约拿单对大卫说，你心里所求的，我必为你成就。

chapters.en: So David said, “Look, tomorrow is the New Moon feast, and I am supposed to dine with the king; but let me go and hide in the field until the evening of the day after tomorrow.
chapters.zh: 大卫对约拿单说，明日是初一，我当与王同席，求你容我去藏在田野，直到第三日晚上。

chapters.en: If your father misses me at all, tell him, ‘David earnestly asked my permission to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because an annual sacrifice is being made there for his whole clan.’
chapters.zh: 你父亲若见我不在席上，你就说，大卫切求我许他回本城伯利恒去，因为他全家在那里献年祭。

chapters.en: If he says, ‘Very well,’ then your servant is safe. But if he loses his temper, you can be sure that he is determined to harm me.
chapters.zh: 你父亲若说好，仆人就平安了。他若发怒，你就知道他决意要害我。

chapters.en: As for you, show kindness to your servant, for you have brought him into a covenant with you before the LORD. If I am guilty, then kill me yourself! Why hand me over to your father?”
chapters.zh: 求你施恩与仆人，因你在耶和华面前曾与仆人结盟。我若有罪，不如你自己杀我，何必将我交给你父亲呢？

chapters.en: “Never!” Jonathan said. “If I had the least inkling that my father was determined to harm you, wouldn’t I tell you?”
chapters.zh: 约拿单说，断无此事。我若知道我父亲决意害你，我岂不告诉你呢？

chapters.en: David asked, “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”
chapters.zh: 大卫对约拿单说，你父亲若用厉言回答你，谁来告诉我呢？

chapters.en: “Come,” Jonathan said, “let’s go out into the field.” So they went there together.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对大卫说，你我且往田野去。二人就往田野去了。

chapters.en: Then Jonathan said to David, “I swear by the LORD, the God of Israel, that I will surely sound out my father by this time the day after tomorrow! If he is favorably disposed toward you, will I not send you word and let you know?
chapters.zh: 约拿单对大卫说，愿耶和华以色列的神为证。明日约在这时候，或第三日，我探我父亲的意思，若向你有好意，我岂不打发人告诉你吗？

chapters.en: But if my father intends to harm you, may the LORD deal with Jonathan, be it ever so severely, if I do not let you know and send you away in peace. May the LORD be with you as he has been with my father.
chapters.zh: 我父亲若有意害你，我不告诉你使你平平安安地走，愿耶和华重重地降罚与我。愿耶和华与你同在，如同从前与我父亲同在一样。

chapters.en: But show me unfailing kindness like the LORD’s kindness as long as I live, so that I may not be killed,
chapters.zh: 你要照耶和华的慈爱恩待我，不但我活着的时候免我死亡，

chapters.en: and do not ever cut off your kindness from my family—not even when the LORD has cut off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”
chapters.zh: 就是我死后，耶和华从地上剪除你仇敌的时候，你也永不可向我家绝了恩惠。

chapters.en: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May the LORD call David’s enemies to account.”
chapters.zh: 于是约拿单与大卫家结盟，说，愿耶和华借大卫的仇敌追讨背约的罪。

chapters.en: And Jonathan had David reaffirm his oath out of love for him, because he loved him as he loved himself.
chapters.zh: 约拿单因爱大卫如同爱自己的性命，就使他再起誓。

chapters.en: Then Jonathan said to David, “Tomorrow is the New Moon feast. You will be missed, because your seat will be empty.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对他说，明日是初一，你的座位空设，人必理会你不在那里。

chapters.en: The day after tomorrow, toward evening, go to the place where you hid when this trouble began, and wait by the stone Ezel.
chapters.zh: 你等三日，就要速速下去，到你从前遇事所藏的地方，在以色磐石那里等候。

chapters.en: I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though I were shooting at a target.
chapters.zh: 我要向磐石旁边射三箭，如同射箭靶一样。

chapters.en: Then I will send a boy and say, ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I say to him, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them here,’ then come, because, as surely as the LORD lives, you are safe; there is no danger.
chapters.zh: 我要打发童子，说，去把箭找来。我若对童子说，箭在后头，把箭拿来，你就可以回来。我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你必平安无事。

chapters.en: But if I say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then you must go, because the LORD has sent you away.
chapters.zh: 我若对童子说，箭在前头，你就要去，因为是耶和华打发你去的。

chapters.en: And about the matter you and I discussed—remember, the LORD is witness between you and me forever.”
chapters.zh: 至于你我今日所说的话，有耶和华在你我中间为证，直到永远。

chapters.en: So David hid in the field, and when the New Moon feast came, the king sat down to eat.
chapters.zh: 大卫就去藏在田野。到了初一日，王坐席要吃饭。

chapters.en: He sat in his customary place by the wall, opposite Jonathan, and Abner sat next to Saul, but David’s place was empty.
chapters.zh: 王照常坐在靠墙的位上，约拿单侍立，押尼珥坐在扫罗旁边，大卫的座位空设。

chapters.en: Saul said nothing that day, for he thought, “Something must have happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.”
chapters.zh: 然而这日扫罗没有说什么，他想大卫遇事，偶染不洁，他必定是不洁。

chapters.en: But the next day, the second day of the month, David’s place was empty again. Then Saul said to his son Jonathan, “Why hasn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal, either yesterday or today?”
chapters.zh: 初二日大卫的座位还空设。扫罗问他儿子约拿单说，耶西的儿子为何昨日，今日没有来吃饭呢？

chapters.en: Jonathan answered, “David earnestly asked me for permission to go to Bethlehem.
chapters.zh: 约拿单回答扫罗说，大卫切求我容他往伯利恒去。

chapters.en: He said, ‘Let me go, because our family is observing a sacrifice in the town and my brother has ordered me to be there. If I have found favor in your eyes, let me get away to see my brothers.’ That is why he has not come to the king’s table.”
chapters.zh: 他说，求你容我去，因为我家在城里有献祭的事。我长兄吩咐我去。如今我若在你眼前蒙恩，求你容我去见我的弟兄。所以大卫没有赴王的席。

chapters.en: Saul’s anger flared up at Jonathan and he said to him, “You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Don’t I know that you have sided with the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the shame of the mother who bore you?
chapters.zh: 扫罗向约拿单发怒，对他说，你这顽梗背逆之妇人所生的，我岂不知道你喜悦耶西的儿子，自取羞辱，以至你母亲露体蒙羞吗？

chapters.en: As long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be established. Now send someone to bring him to me, for he must die!”
chapters.zh: 耶西的儿子若在世间活着，你和你的国位必站立不住。现在你要打发人去，将他捉拿交给我。他是该死的。

chapters.en: “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?” Jonathan asked his father.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对父亲扫罗说，他为什么该死呢？他作了什么呢？

chapters.en: But Saul hurled his spear at him to kill him. Then Jonathan knew that his father intended to kill David.
chapters.zh: 扫罗向约拿单抡枪要刺他，约拿单就知道他父亲决意要杀大卫。

chapters.en: Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger; on that second day of the feast he did not eat, because he was grieved at his father’s shameful treatment of David.
chapters.zh: 于是约拿单气忿忿地从席上起来，在这初二日没有吃饭。他因见父亲羞辱大卫，就为大卫愁烦。

chapters.en: In the morning Jonathan went out to the field for his meeting with David. He had a small boy with him,
chapters.zh: 次日早晨，约拿单按着与大卫约会的时候出到田野，有一个童子跟随。

chapters.en: and he said to the boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.” As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对童子说，你跑去，把我所射的箭找来。童子跑去，约拿单就把箭射在童子前头。

chapters.en: When the boy came to the place where Jonathan’s arrow had fallen, Jonathan called out after him, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?”
chapters.zh: 童子到了约拿单落箭之地，约拿单呼叫童子说，箭不是在你前头吗？

chapters.en: Then he shouted, “Hurry! Go quickly! Don’t stop!” The boy picked up the arrow and returned to his master.
chapters.zh: 约拿单又呼叫童子说，速速地去，不要迟延。童子就拾起箭来，回到主人那里。

chapters.en: (The boy knew nothing about all this; only Jonathan and David knew.)
chapters.zh: 童子却不知道这是什么意思，只有约拿单和大卫知道。

chapters.en: Then Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and said, “Go, carry them back to town.”
chapters.zh: 约拿单将弓箭交给童子，吩咐说，你拿到城里去。

chapters.en: After the boy had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone and bowed down before Jonathan three times, with his face to the ground. Then they kissed each other and wept together—but David wept the most.
chapters.zh: 童子一去，大卫就从磐石的南边出来，俯伏在地，拜了三拜。二人亲嘴，彼此哭泣，大卫哭得更恸。

chapters.en: Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for we have sworn friendship with each other in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘The LORD is witness between you and me, and between your descendants and my descendants forever.’ ” Then David left, and Jonathan went back to the town.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对大卫说，我们二人曾指着耶和华的名起誓说，愿耶和华在你我中间，并你我后裔中间为证，直到永远。如今你平平安安地去吧。大卫就起身走了。约拿单也回城里去了。

chapters.en: David went to Nob, to Ahimelek the priest. Ahimelek trembled when he met him, and asked, “Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?”
chapters.zh: 大卫到了挪伯祭司亚希米勒那里，亚希米勒战战兢兢地出来迎接他，问他说，你为什么独自来，没有人跟随呢？

chapters.en: David answered Ahimelek the priest, “The king sent me on a mission and said to me, ‘No one is to know anything about the mission I am sending you on.’ As for my men, I have told them to meet me at a certain place.
chapters.zh: 大卫回答祭司亚希米勒说，王吩咐我一件事说，我差遣你委托你的这件事，不要使人知道。故此我已派定少年人在某处等候我。

chapters.en: Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever you can find.”
chapters.zh: 现在你手下有什么。求你给我五个饼或是别样的食物。

chapters.en: But the priest answered David, “I don’t have any ordinary bread on hand; however, there is some consecrated bread here—provided the men have kept themselves from women.”
chapters.zh: 祭司对大卫说，我手下没有寻常的饼，只有圣饼。若少年人没有亲近妇人才可以给。

chapters.en: David replied, “Indeed women have been kept from us, as usual whenever I set out. The men’s bodies are holy even on missions that are not holy. How much more so today!”
chapters.zh: 大卫对祭司说，实在约有三日我们没有亲近妇人。我出来的时候，虽是寻常行路，少年人的器皿还是洁净的。何况今日不更是洁净吗？

chapters.en: So the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence that had been removed from before the LORD and replaced by hot bread on the day it was taken away.
chapters.zh: 祭司就拿圣饼给他。因为在那里没有别样饼，只有更换新饼，从耶和华面前撤下来的陈设饼。

chapters.en: Now one of Saul’s servants was there that day, detained before the LORD; he was Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s chief shepherd.
chapters.zh: 当日有扫罗的一个臣子留在耶和华面前。他名叫多益，是以东人，作扫罗的司牧长。

chapters.en: David asked Ahimelek, “Don’t you have a spear or a sword here? I haven’t brought my sword or any other weapon, because the king’s mission was urgent.”
chapters.zh: 大卫问亚希米勒说，你手下有枪有刀没有。因为王的事甚急，连刀剑器械我都没有带。

chapters.en: The priest replied, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here; it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want it, take it; there is no sword here but that one.” David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”
chapters.zh: 祭司说，你在以拉谷杀非利士人歌利亚的那刀在这里，裹在布中，放在以弗得后边，你要就可以拿去。除此以外，再没有别的。大卫说，这刀没有可比的。求你给我。

chapters.en: That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.
chapters.zh: 那日大卫起来，躲避扫罗，逃到迦特王亚吉那里。

chapters.en: But the servants of Achish said to him, “Isn’t this David, the king of the land? Isn’t he the one they sing about in their dances: “ ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
chapters.zh: 亚吉的臣仆对亚吉说，这不是以色列国王大卫吗？那里的妇女跳舞唱和，不是指着他说扫罗杀死千千，大卫杀死万万吗？

chapters.en: David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish king of Gath.
chapters.zh: 大卫将这话放在心里，甚惧怕迦特王亚吉，

chapters.en: So he pretended to be insane in their presence; and while he was in their hands he acted like a madman, making marks on the doors of the gate and letting saliva run down his beard.
chapters.zh: 就在众人面前改变了寻常的举动，在他们手下假装疯癫，在城门的门扇上胡写乱画，使唾沫流在胡子上。

chapters.en: Achish said to his servants, “Look at the man! He is insane! Why bring him to me?
chapters.zh: 亚吉对臣仆说，你们看，这人是疯子。为什么带他到我这里来呢？

chapters.en: Am I so short of madmen that you have to bring this fellow here to carry on like this in front of me? Must this man come into my house?”
chapters.zh: 我岂缺少疯子，你们带这人来在我面前疯癫吗？这人岂可进我的家呢？

chapters.en: David left Gath and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.
chapters.zh: 大卫就离开那里，逃到亚杜兰洞。他的弟兄和他父亲的全家听见了，就都下到他那里。

chapters.en: All those who were in distress or in debt or discontented gathered around him, and he became their commander. About four hundred men were with him.
chapters.zh: 凡受窘迫的，欠债的，心里苦恼的都聚集到大卫那里。大卫就作他们的头目，跟随他的约有四百人。

chapters.en: From there David went to Mizpah in Moab and said to the king of Moab, “Would you let my father and mother come and stay with you until I learn what God will do for me?”
chapters.zh: 大卫从那里往摩押的米斯巴去，对摩押王说，求你容我父母搬来，住在你们这里，等我知道神要为我怎样行。

chapters.en: So he left them with the king of Moab, and they stayed with him as long as David was in the stronghold.
chapters.zh: 大卫领他父母到摩押王面前。大卫住山寨多少日子，他父母也住摩押王那里多少日子。

chapters.en: But the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
chapters.zh: 先知迦得对大卫说，你不要住在山寨，要往犹大地去。大卫就离开那里，进入哈列的树林。

chapters.en: Now Saul heard that David and his men had been discovered. And Saul was seated, spear in hand, under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with all his officials standing at his side.
chapters.zh: 扫罗在基比亚的拉玛，坐在垂丝柳树下，手里拿着枪，众臣仆侍立在左右。扫罗听见大卫和跟随他的人在何处，

chapters.en: He said to them, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?
chapters.zh: 就对左右侍立的臣仆说，便雅悯人哪，你们要听我的话。耶西的儿子能将田地和葡萄园赐给你们各人吗？能立你们各人作千夫长百夫长吗？

chapters.en: Is that why you have all conspired against me? No one tells me when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse. None of you is concerned about me or tells me that my son has incited my servant to lie in wait for me, as he does today.”
chapters.zh: 你们竟都结党害我。我的儿子与耶西的儿子结盟的时候，无人告诉我。我的儿子挑唆我的臣子谋害我，就如今日的光景，也无人告诉我，为我忧虑。

chapters.en: But Doeg the Edomite, who was standing with Saul’s officials, said, “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelek son of Ahitub at Nob.
chapters.zh: 那时以东人多益站在扫罗的臣仆中，对他说，我曾看见耶西的儿子到了挪伯，亚希突的儿子亚希米勒那里。

chapters.en: Ahimelek inquired of the LORD for him; he also gave him provisions and the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
chapters.zh: 亚希米勒为他求问耶和华，又给他食物，并给他杀非利士人歌利亚的刀。

chapters.en: Then the king sent for the priest Ahimelek son of Ahitub and all the men of his family, who were the priests at Nob, and they all came to the king.
chapters.zh: 王就打发人将祭司亚希突的儿子亚希米勒和他父亲的全家，就是住挪伯的祭司都召了来。他们就来见王。

chapters.en: Saul said, “Listen now, son of Ahitub.” “Yes, my lord,” he answered.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说，亚希突的儿子，要听我的话。他回答说，主阿，我在这里。

chapters.en: Saul said to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, giving him bread and a sword and inquiring of God for him, so that he has rebelled against me and lies in wait for me, as he does today?”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对他说，你为什么与耶西的儿子结党害我，将食物和刀给他，又为他求问神，使他起来谋害我，就如今日的光景。

chapters.en: Ahimelek answered the king, “Who of all your servants is as loyal as David, the king’s son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard and highly respected in your household?
chapters.zh: 亚希米勒回答王说，王的臣仆中有谁比大卫忠心呢？他是王的女婿，又是王的参谋，并且在王家中是尊贵的。

chapters.en: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Of course not! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of his father’s family, for your servant knows nothing at all about this whole affair.”
chapters.zh: 我岂是从今日才为他求问神呢？断不是这样。王不要将罪归我和我父的全家。因为这事，无论大小，仆人都不知道。

chapters.en: But the king said, “You will surely die, Ahimelek, you and your whole family.”
chapters.zh: 王说，亚希米勒阿，你和你父的全家都是该死的。

chapters.en: Then the king ordered the guards at his side: “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too have sided with David. They knew he was fleeing, yet they did not tell me.” But the king’s officials were unwilling to raise a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 王就吩咐左右的侍卫说，你们去杀耶和华的祭司。因为他们帮助大卫，又知道大卫逃跑，竟没有告诉我。扫罗的臣子却不肯伸手杀耶和华的祭司。

chapters.en: The king then ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests.” So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck them down. That day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
chapters.zh: 王吩咐多益说，你去杀祭司吧。以东人多益就去杀祭司，那日杀了穿细麻布以弗得的八十五人。

chapters.en: He also put to the sword Nob, the town of the priests, with its men and women, its children and infants, and its cattle, donkeys and sheep.
chapters.zh: 又用刀将祭司城挪伯中的男女，孩童，吃奶的，和牛，羊，驴尽都杀灭。

chapters.en: But one son of Ahimelek son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled to join David.
chapters.zh: 亚希突的儿子亚希米勒有一个儿子，名叫亚比亚他，逃到大卫那里。

chapters.en: He told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 亚比亚他将扫罗杀耶和华祭司的事告诉大卫。

chapters.en: Then David said to Abiathar, “That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul. I am responsible for the death of your whole family.
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚比亚他说，那日我见以东人多益在那里，就知道他必告诉扫罗。你父的全家丧命，都是因我的缘故。

chapters.en: Stay with me; don’t be afraid. The man who wants to kill you is trying to kill me too. You will be safe with me.”
chapters.zh: 你可以住在我这里，不要惧怕。因为寻索你命的就是寻索我的命。你在我这里可得保全。

chapters.en: When David was told, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and are looting the threshing floors,”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉大卫说，非利士人攻击基伊拉，抢夺禾场。

chapters.en: he inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go and attack these Philistines?” The LORD answered him, “Go, attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”
chapters.zh: 所以大卫求问耶和华说，我去攻打那些非利士人可以不可以。耶和华对大卫说，你可以去攻打非利士人，拯救基伊拉。

chapters.en: But David’s men said to him, “Here in Judah we are afraid. How much more, then, if we go to Keilah against the Philistine forces!”
chapters.zh: 跟随大卫的人对他说，我们在犹大地这里尚且惧怕，何况往基伊拉去攻打非利士人的军旅呢？

chapters.en: Once again David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him, “Go down to Keilah, for I am going to give the Philistines into your hand.”
chapters.zh: 大卫又求问耶和华。耶和华回答说，你起身下基伊拉去，我必将非利士人交在你手里。

chapters.en: So David and his men went to Keilah, fought the Philistines and carried off their livestock. He inflicted heavy losses on the Philistines and saved the people of Keilah.
chapters.zh: 大卫和跟随他的人往基伊拉去，与非利士人打仗，大大杀败他们，又夺获他们的牲畜。这样，大卫救了基伊拉的居民。

chapters.en: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelek had brought the ephod down with him when he fled to David at Keilah.)
chapters.zh: 亚希米勒的儿子亚比亚他逃到基伊拉见大卫的时候，手里拿着以弗得。

chapters.en: Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, and he said, “God has delivered him into my hands, for David has imprisoned himself by entering a town with gates and bars.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉扫罗说，大卫到了基伊拉。扫罗说，他进了有门有闩的城，困闭在里头。这是神将他交在我手里了。

chapters.en: And Saul called up all his forces for battle, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.
chapters.zh: 于是扫罗招聚众民，要下去攻打基伊拉城，围困大卫和跟随他的人。

chapters.en: When David learned that Saul was plotting against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod.”
chapters.zh: 大卫知道扫罗设计谋害他，就对祭司亚比亚他说，将以弗得拿过来。

chapters.en: David said, “LORD, God of Israel, your servant has heard definitely that Saul plans to come to Keilah and destroy the town on account of me.
chapters.zh: 大卫祷告说，耶和华以色列的神阿，你仆人听真了扫罗要往基伊拉来，为我的缘故灭城。

chapters.en: Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me to him? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? LORD, God of Israel, tell your servant.” And the LORD said, “He will.”
chapters.zh: 基伊拉人将我交在扫罗手里不交。扫罗照着你仆人所听的话下来不下来。耶和华以色列的神阿，求你指示仆人。耶和华说，扫罗必下来。

chapters.en: Again David asked, “Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me and my men to Saul?” And the LORD said, “They will.”
chapters.zh: 大卫又说，基伊拉人将我和跟随我的人交在扫罗手里不交。耶和华说，必交出来。

chapters.en: So David and his men, about six hundred in number, left Keilah and kept moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he did not go there.
chapters.zh: 大卫和跟随他的约有六百人，就起身出了基伊拉，往他们所能往的地方去。有人告诉扫罗，大卫离开基伊拉逃走。于是扫罗不出来了。

chapters.en: David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hills of the Desert of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God did not give David into his hands.
chapters.zh: 大卫住在旷野的山寨里，常在西弗旷野的山地。扫罗天天寻索大卫，神却不将大卫交在他手里。

chapters.en: While David was at Horesh in the Desert of Ziph, he learned that Saul had come out to take his life.
chapters.zh: 大卫知道扫罗出来寻索他的命。那时，他住在西弗旷野的树林里。

chapters.en: And Saul’s son Jonathan went to David at Horesh and helped him find strength in God.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的儿子约拿单起身，往那树林里去见大卫，使他倚靠神得以坚固，

chapters.en: “Don’t be afraid,” he said. “My father Saul will not lay a hand on you. You will be king over Israel, and I will be second to you. Even my father Saul knows this.”
chapters.zh: 对他说，不要惧怕。我父扫罗的手必不加害于你。你必作以色列的王，我也作你的宰相。这事我父扫罗知道了。

chapters.en: The two of them made a covenant before the LORD. Then Jonathan went home, but David remained at Horesh.
chapters.zh: 于是二人在耶和华面前立约。大卫仍住在树林里，约拿单回家去了。

chapters.en: The Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hakilah, south of Jeshimon?
chapters.zh: 西弗人上到基比亚见扫罗，说，大卫不是在我们那里的树林里山寨中，旷野南边的哈基拉山藏着吗？

chapters.en: Now, Your Majesty, come down whenever it pleases you to do so, and we will be responsible for giving him into your hands.”
chapters.zh: 王阿，请你随你的心愿下来，我们必亲自将他交在王的手里。

chapters.en: Saul replied, “The LORD bless you for your concern for me.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说，愿耶和华赐福与你们，因你们顾恤我。

chapters.en: Go and get more information. Find out where David usually goes and who has seen him there. They tell me he is very crafty.
chapters.zh: 请你们回去，再确实查明他的住处和行踪，是谁看见他在那里，因为我听见人说他甚狡猾。

chapters.en: Find out about all the hiding places he uses and come back to me with definite information. Then I will go with you; if he is in the area, I will track him down among all the clans of Judah.”
chapters.zh: 所以要看准他藏匿的地方，回来据实地告诉我，我就与你们同去。他若在犹大的境内，我必从千门万户中搜出他来。

chapters.en: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Desert of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon.
chapters.zh: 西弗人就起身，在扫罗以先往西弗去。大卫和跟随他的人却在玛云旷野南边的亚拉巴。

chapters.en: Saul and his men began the search, and when David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Desert of Maon. When Saul heard this, he went into the Desert of Maon in pursuit of David.
chapters.zh: 扫罗和跟随他的人去寻找大卫。有人告诉大卫，他就下到磐石，住在玛云的旷野。扫罗听见，便在玛云的旷野追赶大卫。

chapters.en: Saul was going along one side of the mountain, and David and his men were on the other side, hurrying to get away from Saul. As Saul and his forces were closing in on David and his men to capture them,
chapters.zh: 扫罗在山这边走，大卫和跟随他的人在山那边走。大卫急忙躲避扫罗。因为扫罗和跟随他的人，四面围住大卫和跟随他的人，要拿获他们。

chapters.en: a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Come quickly! The Philistines are raiding the land.”
chapters.zh: 忽有使者来报告扫罗说，非利士人犯境抢掠，请王快快回去。

chapters.en: Then Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why they call this place Sela Hammahlekoth.
chapters.zh: 于是扫罗不追赶大卫，回去攻打非利士人。因此那地方名叫西拉哈玛希罗结。

chapters.en: And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En Gedi.
chapters.zh: 大卫从那里上去，住在隐基底的山寨里。

chapters.en: After Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the Desert of En Gedi.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗追赶非利士人回来，有人告诉他说，大卫在隐基底的旷野。

chapters.en: So Saul took three thousand able young men from all Israel and set out to look for David and his men near the Crags of the Wild Goats.
chapters.zh: 扫罗就从以色列人中挑选三千精兵，率领他们往野羊的磐石去，寻索大卫和跟随他的人。

chapters.en: He came to the sheep pens along the way; a cave was there, and Saul went in to relieve himself. David and his men were far back in the cave.
chapters.zh: 到了路旁的羊圈，在那里有洞，扫罗进去大解。大卫和跟随他的人正藏在洞里的深处。

chapters.en: The men said, “This is the day the LORD spoke of when he said to you, ‘I will give your enemy into your hands for you to deal with as you wish.’ ” Then David crept up unnoticed and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.
chapters.zh: 跟随的人对大卫说，耶和华曾应许你说，我要将你的仇敌交在你手里，你可以任意待他。如今时候到了。大卫就起来，悄悄地割下扫罗外袍的衣襟。

chapters.en: Afterward, David was conscience-stricken for having cut off a corner of his robe.
chapters.zh: 随后大卫心中自责，因为割下扫罗的衣襟。

chapters.en: He said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD’s anointed, or lay my hand on him; for he is the anointed of the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 对跟随他的人说，我的主乃是耶和华的受膏者，我在耶和华面前万不敢伸手害他，因他是耶和华的受膏者。

chapters.en: With these words David sharply rebuked his men and did not allow them to attack Saul. And Saul left the cave and went his way.
chapters.zh: 大卫用这话拦住跟随他的人，不容他们起来害扫罗。扫罗起来，从洞里出去行路。

chapters.en: Then David went out of the cave and called out to Saul, “My lord the king!” When Saul looked behind him, David bowed down and prostrated himself with his face to the ground.
chapters.zh: 随后大卫也起来，从洞里出去，呼叫扫罗说，我主，我王。扫罗回头观看，大卫就屈身，脸伏于地下拜。

chapters.en: He said to Saul, “Why do you listen when men say, ‘David is bent on harming you’?
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说，你为何听信人的谗言，说大卫想要害你呢？

chapters.en: This day you have seen with your own eyes how the LORD delivered you into my hands in the cave. Some urged me to kill you, but I spared you; I said, ‘I will not lay my hand on my lord, because he is the LORD’s anointed.’
chapters.zh: 今日你亲眼看见在洞中，耶和华将你交在我手里。有人叫我杀你，我却爱惜你，说，我不敢伸手害我的主，因为他是耶和华的受膏者。

chapters.en: See, my father, look at this piece of your robe in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe but did not kill you. See that there is nothing in my hand to indicate that I am guilty of wrongdoing or rebellion. I have not wronged you, but you are hunting me down to take my life.
chapters.zh: 我父阿，看看你外袍的衣襟在我手中。我割下你的衣襟，没有杀你。你由此可以知道我没有恶意叛逆你。你虽然猎取我的命，我却没有得罪你。

chapters.en: May the LORD judge between you and me. And may the LORD avenge the wrongs you have done to me, but my hand will not touch you.
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华在你我中间判断是非，在你身上为我伸冤，我却不亲手加害于你。

chapters.en: As the old saying goes, ‘From evildoers come evil deeds,’ so my hand will not touch you.
chapters.zh: 古人有句俗语说，恶事出于恶人。我却不亲手加害于你。

chapters.en: “Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Who are you pursuing? A dead dog? A flea?
chapters.zh: 以色列王出来要寻找谁呢？追赶谁呢？不过追赶一条死狗，一个虼蚤就是了。

chapters.en: May the LORD be our judge and decide between us. May he consider my cause and uphold it; may he vindicate me by delivering me from your hand.”
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华在你我中间施行审判，断定是非，并且鉴察，为我伸冤，救我脱离你的手。

chapters.en: When David finished saying this, Saul asked, “Is that your voice, David my son?” And he wept aloud.
chapters.zh: 大卫向扫罗说完这话，扫罗说，我儿大卫，这是你的声音吗？就放声大哭，

chapters.en: “You are more righteous than I,” he said. “You have treated me well, but I have treated you badly.
chapters.zh: 对大卫说，你比我公义。因为你以善待我，我却以恶待你。

chapters.en: You have just now told me about the good you did to me; the LORD delivered me into your hands, but you did not kill me.
chapters.zh: 你今日显明是以善待我。因为耶和华将我交在你手里，你却没有杀我。

chapters.en: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him get away unharmed? May the LORD reward you well for the way you treated me today.
chapters.zh: 人若遇见仇敌，岂肯放他平安无事地去呢？愿耶和华因你今日向我所行的，以善报你。

chapters.en: I know that you will surely be king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.
chapters.zh: 我也知道你必要作王，以色列的国必坚立在你手里。

chapters.en: Now swear to me by the LORD that you will not kill off my descendants or wipe out my name from my father’s family.”
chapters.zh: 现在你要指着耶和华向我起誓，不剪除我的后裔，在我父家不灭没我的名。

chapters.en: So David gave his oath to Saul. Then Saul returned home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫向扫罗起誓，扫罗就回家去。大卫和跟随他的人上山寨去了。

chapters.en: Now Samuel died, and all Israel assembled and mourned for him; and they buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David moved down into the Desert of Paran.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳死了，以色列众人聚集，为他哀哭，将他葬在拉玛他自己的坟墓里（坟墓原文作房屋）。大卫起身，下到巴兰的旷野。

chapters.en: A certain man in Maon, who had property there at Carmel, was very wealthy. He had a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.
chapters.zh: 在玛云有一个人，他的产业在迦密，是一个大富户，有三千绵羊，一千山羊。他正在迦密剪羊毛。

chapters.en: His name was Nabal and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband was surly and mean in his dealings—he was a Calebite.
chapters.zh: 那人名叫拿八，是迦勒族的人。他的妻名叫亚比该，是聪明俊美的妇人。拿八为人刚愎凶恶。

chapters.en: While David was in the wilderness, he heard that Nabal was shearing sheep.
chapters.zh: 大卫在旷野听见说拿八剪羊毛，

chapters.en: So he sent ten young men and said to them, “Go up to Nabal at Carmel and greet him in my name.
chapters.zh: 大卫就打发十个仆人，吩咐他们说，你们上迦密去见拿八，提我的名问他安。

chapters.en: Say to him: ‘Long life to you! Good health to you and your household! And good health to all that is yours!
chapters.zh: 要对那富户如此说，愿你平安，愿你家平安，愿你一切所有的都平安。

chapters.en: “ ‘Now I hear that it is sheep-shearing time. When your shepherds were with us, we did not mistreat them, and the whole time they were at Carmel nothing of theirs was missing.
chapters.zh: 现在我听说有人为你剪羊毛，你的牧人在迦密的时候和我们在一处，我们没有欺负他们，他们也未曾失落什么。

chapters.en: Ask your own servants and they will tell you. Therefore be favorable toward my men, since we come at a festive time. Please give your servants and your son David whatever you can find for them.’ ”
chapters.zh: 可以问你的仆人，他们必告诉你。所以愿我的仆人在你眼前蒙恩，因为是在好日子来的。求你随手取点赐与仆人和你儿子大卫。

chapters.en: When David’s men arrived, they gave Nabal this message in David’s name. Then they waited.
chapters.zh: 大卫的仆人到了，将这话提大卫的名都告诉了拿八，就住了口。

chapters.en: Nabal answered David’s servants, “Who is this David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants are breaking away from their masters these days.
chapters.zh: 拿八回答大卫的仆人说，大卫是谁。耶西的儿子是谁。近来悖逆主人奔逃的仆人甚多，

chapters.en: Why should I take my bread and water, and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men coming from who knows where?”
chapters.zh: 我岂可将饮食和为我剪羊毛人所宰的肉给我不知道从哪里来的人呢？

chapters.en: David’s men turned around and went back. When they arrived, they reported every word.
chapters.zh: 大卫的仆人就转身从原路回去，照这话告诉大卫。

chapters.en: David said to his men, “Each of you strap on your sword!” So they did, and David strapped his on as well. About four hundred men went up with David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.
chapters.zh: 大卫向跟随他的人说，你们各人都要带上刀。众人就都带上刀，大卫也带上刀。跟随大卫上去的约有四百人，留下二百人看守器具。

chapters.en: One of the servants told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, “David sent messengers from the wilderness to give our master his greetings, but he hurled insults at them.
chapters.zh: 有拿八的一个仆人告诉拿八的妻亚比该说，大卫从旷野打发使者来问我主人的安，主人却辱骂他们。

chapters.en: Yet these men were very good to us. They did not mistreat us, and the whole time we were out in the fields near them nothing was missing.
chapters.zh: 但是那些人待我们甚好。我们在田野与他们来往的时候，没有受他们的欺负，也未曾失落什么。

chapters.en: Night and day they were a wall around us the whole time we were herding our sheep near them.
chapters.zh: 我们在他们那里牧羊的时候，他们昼夜作我们的保障。

chapters.en: Now think it over and see what you can do, because disaster is hanging over our master and his whole household. He is such a wicked man that no one can talk to him.”
chapters.zh: 所以你当筹划，看怎样行才好。不然，祸患定要临到我主人和他全家。他性情凶暴，无人敢与他说话。

chapters.en: Abigail acted quickly. She took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five dressed sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred cakes of raisins and two hundred cakes of pressed figs, and loaded them on donkeys.
chapters.zh: 亚比该急忙将二百饼，两皮袋酒，五只收拾好了的羊，五细亚烘好了的穗子，一百葡萄饼，二百无花果饼，都驮在驴上，

chapters.en: Then she told her servants, “Go on ahead; I’ll follow you.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.
chapters.zh: 对仆人说，你们前头走，我随着你们去。这事她却没有告诉丈夫拿八。

chapters.en: As she came riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, there were David and his men descending toward her, and she met them.
chapters.zh: 亚比该骑着驴，正下山坡，见大卫和跟随他的人从对面下来，亚比该就迎接他们。

chapters.en: David had just said, “It’s been useless—all my watching over this fellow’s property in the wilderness so that nothing of his was missing. He has paid me back evil for good.
chapters.zh: 大卫曾说，我在旷野为那人看守所有的，以致他一样不失落，实在是徒然了。他向我以恶报善。

chapters.en: May God deal with David, be it ever so severely, if by morning I leave alive one male of all who belong to him!”
chapters.zh: 凡属拿八的男丁，我若留一个到明日早晨，愿神重重降罚与我。

chapters.en: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off her donkey and bowed down before David with her face to the ground.
chapters.zh: 亚比该见大卫，便急忙下驴，在大卫面前脸伏于地叩拜，

chapters.en: She fell at his feet and said: “Pardon your servant, my lord, and let me speak to you; hear what your servant has to say.
chapters.zh: 俯伏在大卫的脚前，说，我主阿，愿这罪归我。求你容婢女向你进言，更求你听婢女的话。

chapters.en: Please pay no attention, my lord, to that wicked man Nabal. He is just like his name—his name means Fool, and folly goes with him. And as for me, your servant, I did not see the men my lord sent.
chapters.zh: 我主不要理这坏人拿八，他的性情与他的名相称。他名叫拿八（就是愚顽的意思），他为人果然愚顽。但我主所打发的仆人，婢女并没有看见。

chapters.en: And now, my lord, as surely as the LORD your God lives and as you live, since the LORD has kept you from bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hands, may your enemies and all who are intent on harming my lord be like Nabal.
chapters.zh: 我主阿，耶和华既然阻止你亲手报仇，取流血的罪，所以我指着永生的耶和华，又敢在你面前起誓说，愿你的仇敌和谋害你的人都像拿八一样。

chapters.en: And let this gift, which your servant has brought to my lord, be given to the men who follow you.
chapters.zh: 如今求你将婢女送来的礼物给跟随你的仆人。

chapters.en: “Please forgive your servant’s presumption. The LORD your God will certainly make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because you fight the LORD’s battles, and no wrongdoing will be found in you as long as you live.
chapters.zh: 求你饶恕婢女的罪过。耶和华必为我主建立坚固的家，因我主为耶和华争战。并且在你平生的日子查不出有什么过来。

chapters.en: Even though someone is pursuing you to take your life, the life of my lord will be bound securely in the bundle of the living by the LORD your God, but the lives of your enemies he will hurl away as from the pocket of a sling.
chapters.zh: 虽有人起来追逼你，寻索你的性命，你的性命却在耶和华你的神那里蒙保护，如包裹宝器一样。你仇敌的性命，耶和华必抛去，如用机弦甩石一样。

chapters.en: When the LORD has fulfilled for my lord every good thing he promised concerning him and has appointed him ruler over Israel,
chapters.zh: 我主现在若不亲手报仇流无辜人的血，到了耶和华照所应许你的话赐福与你，立你作以色列的王，那时我主必不至心里不安，觉得良心有亏。耶和华赐福与我主的时候，求你记念婢女。

chapters.en: my lord will not have on his conscience the staggering burden of needless bloodshed or of having avenged himself. And when the LORD your God has brought my lord success, remember your servant.”
David said to Abigail, “Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel, who has sent you today to meet me.
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚比该说，耶和华以色列的神是应当称颂的，因为他今日使你来迎接我。

chapters.en: May you be blessed for your good judgment and for keeping me from bloodshed this day and from avenging myself with my own hands.
chapters.zh: 你和你的见识也当称赞。因为你今日拦阻我亲手报仇，流人的血。

chapters.en: Otherwise, as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has kept me from harming you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, not one male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by daybreak.”
chapters.zh: 我指着阻止我加害于你的耶和华以色列永生的神起誓，你若不速速地来迎接我，到明日早晨，凡属拿八的男丁必定不留一个。

chapters.en: Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him and said, “Go home in peace. I have heard your words and granted your request.”
chapters.zh: 大卫受了亚比该送来的礼物，就对她说，我听了你的话，准了你的情面，你可以平平安安地回家吧。

chapters.en: When Abigail went to Nabal, he was in the house holding a banquet like that of a king. He was in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing at all until daybreak.
chapters.zh: 亚比该到拿八那里，见他在家里设摆筵席，如同王的筵席。拿八快乐大醉。亚比该无论大小事都没有告诉他，就等到次日早晨。

chapters.en: Then in the morning, when Nabal was sober, his wife told him all these things, and his heart failed him and he became like a stone.
chapters.zh: 到了早晨，拿八醒了酒，他的妻将这些事都告诉他，他就魂不附体，身僵如石头一般。

chapters.en: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal and he died.
chapters.zh: 过了十天，耶和华击打拿八，他就死了。

chapters.en: When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, “Praise be to the LORD, who has upheld my cause against Nabal for treating me with contempt. He has kept his servant from doing wrong and has brought Nabal’s wrongdoing down on his own head.” Then David sent word to Abigail, asking her to become his wife.
chapters.zh: 大卫听见拿八死了，就说，应当称颂耶和华，因他伸了拿八羞辱我的冤，又阻止仆人行恶。也使拿八的恶归到拿八的头上。于是大卫打发人去，与亚比该说，要娶她为妻。

chapters.en: His servants went to Carmel and said to Abigail, “David has sent us to you to take you to become his wife.”
chapters.zh: 大卫的仆人到了迦密见亚比该，对她说，大卫打发我们来见你，想要娶你为妻。

chapters.en: She bowed down with her face to the ground and said, “I am your servant and am ready to serve you and wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”
chapters.zh: 亚比该就起来，俯伏在地，说，我情愿作婢女，洗我主仆人的脚。

chapters.en: Abigail quickly got on a donkey and, attended by her five female servants, went with David’s messengers and became his wife.
chapters.zh: 亚比该立刻起身，骑上驴，带着五个使女，跟从大卫的使者去了，就作了大卫的妻。

chapters.en: David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel, and they both were his wives.
chapters.zh: 大卫先娶了耶斯列人亚希暖，她们二人都作了他的妻。

chapters.en: But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Paltiel son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
chapters.zh: 扫罗已将他的女儿米甲，就是大卫的妻，给了迦琳人拉亿的儿子帕提为妻。

chapters.en: The Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding on the hill of Hakilah, which faces Jeshimon?”
chapters.zh: 西弗人到基比亚见扫罗，说，大卫不是在旷野前的哈基拉山藏着吗？

chapters.en: So Saul went down to the Desert of Ziph, with his three thousand select Israelite troops, to search there for David.
chapters.zh: 扫罗就起身，带领以色列人中挑选的三千精兵下到西弗的旷野，要在那里寻索大卫。

chapters.en: Saul made his camp beside the road on the hill of Hakilah facing Jeshimon, but David stayed in the wilderness. When he saw that Saul had followed him there,
chapters.zh: 扫罗在旷野前的哈基拉山，在道路上安营。大卫住在旷野，听说扫罗到旷野来追寻他，

chapters.en: he sent out scouts and learned that Saul had definitely arrived.
chapters.zh: 就打发人去探听，便知道扫罗果然来到。

chapters.en: Then David set out and went to the place where Saul had camped. He saw where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the commander of the army, had lain down. Saul was lying inside the camp, with the army encamped around him.
chapters.zh: 大卫起来，到扫罗安营的地方，看见扫罗和他的元帅尼珥的儿子押尼珥睡卧之处。扫罗睡在辎重营里，百姓安营在他周围。

chapters.en: David then asked Ahimelek the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, “Who will go down into the camp with me to Saul?” “I’ll go with you,” said Abishai.
chapters.zh: 大卫对赫人亚希米勒和洗鲁雅的儿子约押的兄弟亚比筛说，谁同我下到扫罗营里去。亚比筛说，我同你下去。

chapters.en: So David and Abishai went to the army by night, and there was Saul, lying asleep inside the camp with his spear stuck in the ground near his head. Abner and the soldiers were lying around him.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫和亚比筛夜间到了百姓那里，见扫罗睡在辎重营里。他的枪在头旁，插在地上。押尼珥和百姓睡在他周围。

chapters.en: Abishai said to David, “Today God has delivered your enemy into your hands. Now let me pin him to the ground with one thrust of the spear; I won’t strike him twice.”
chapters.zh: 亚比筛对大卫说，现在神将你的仇敌交在你手里，求你容我拿枪将他刺透在地，一刺就成，不用再刺。

chapters.en: But David said to Abishai, “Don’t destroy him! Who can lay a hand on the LORD’s anointed and be guiltless?
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚比筛说，不可害死他。有谁伸手害耶和华的受膏者而无罪呢？

chapters.en: As surely as the LORD lives,” he said, “the LORD himself will strike him, or his time will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and perish.
chapters.zh: 大卫又说，我指着永生的耶和华起誓，他或被耶和华击打，或是死期到了，或是出战阵亡。

chapters.en: But the LORD forbid that I should lay a hand on the LORD’s anointed. Now get the spear and water jug that are near his head, and let’s go.”
chapters.zh: 我在耶和华面前，万不敢伸手害耶和华的受膏者。现在你可以将他头旁的枪和水瓶拿来，我们就走。

chapters.en: So David took the spear and water jug near Saul’s head, and they left. No one saw or knew about it, nor did anyone wake up. They were all sleeping, because the LORD had put them into a deep sleep.
chapters.zh: 大卫从扫罗的头旁拿了枪和水瓶，二人就走了，没有人看见，没有人知道，也没有人醒起，都睡着了，因为耶和华使他们沉沉地睡了。

chapters.en: Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on top of the hill some distance away; there was a wide space between them.
chapters.zh: 大卫过到那边去，远远地站在山顶上，与他们相离甚远。

chapters.en: He called out to the army and to Abner son of Ner, “Aren’t you going to answer me, Abner?” Abner replied, “Who are you who calls to the king?”
chapters.zh: 大卫呼叫百姓和尼珥的儿子押尼珥说，押尼珥阿，你为何不答应呢？押尼珥说，你是谁。竟敢呼叫王呢？

chapters.en: David said, “You’re a man, aren’t you? And who is like you in Israel? Why didn’t you guard your lord the king? Someone came to destroy your lord the king.
chapters.zh: 大卫对押尼珥说，你不是个勇士吗？以色列中谁能比你呢？民中有人进来要害死王你的主，你为何没有保护王你的主呢？

chapters.en: What you have done is not good. As surely as the LORD lives, you and your men must die, because you did not guard your master, the LORD’s anointed. Look around you. Where are the king’s spear and water jug that were near his head?”
chapters.zh: 你这样是不好的。我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你们都是该死的。因为没有保护你们的主，就是耶和华的受膏者。现在你看看王头旁的枪和水瓶在哪里。

chapters.en: Saul recognized David’s voice and said, “Is that your voice, David my son?” David replied, “Yes it is, my lord the king.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗听出是大卫的声音，就说，我儿大卫，这是你的声音吗？大卫说，主我的王阿，是我的声音。

chapters.en: And he added, “Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done, and what wrong am I guilty of?
chapters.zh: 又说，我作了什么。我手里有什么恶事。我主竟追赶仆人呢？

chapters.en: Now let my lord the king listen to his servant’s words. If the LORD has incited you against me, then may he accept an offering. If, however, people have done it, may they be cursed before the LORD! They have driven me today from my share in the LORD’s inheritance and have said, ‘Go, serve other gods.’
chapters.zh: 求我主我王听仆人的话，若是耶和华激发你攻击我，愿耶和华收纳祭物。若是人激发你，愿他在耶和华面前受咒诅。因为他现今赶逐我，不容我在耶和华的产业上有分，说，你去事奉别神吧。

chapters.en: Now do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the LORD. The king of Israel has come out to look for a flea—as one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
chapters.zh: 现在求王不要使我的血流在离耶和华远的地方。以色列王出来是寻找一个虼蚤，如同人在山上猎取一个鹧鸪一般。

chapters.en: Then Saul said, “I have sinned. Come back, David my son. Because you considered my life precious today, I will not try to harm you again. Surely I have acted like a fool and have been terribly wrong.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗说，我有罪了。我儿大卫，你可以回来，因你今日看我的性命为宝贵。我必不再加害于你。我是糊涂人，大大错了。

chapters.en: “Here is the king’s spear,” David answered. “Let one of your young men come over and get it.
chapters.zh: 大卫说，王的枪在这里，可以吩咐一个仆人过来拿去。

chapters.en: The LORD rewards everyone for their righteousness and faithfulness. The LORD delivered you into my hands today, but I would not lay a hand on the LORD’s anointed.
chapters.zh: 今日耶和华将王交在我手里，我却不肯伸手害耶和华的受膏者。耶和华必照各人的公义诚实报应他。

chapters.en: As surely as I valued your life today, so may the LORD value my life and deliver me from all trouble.”
chapters.zh: 我今日重看你的性命，愿耶和华也重看我的性命，并且拯救我脱离一切患难。

chapters.en: Then Saul said to David, “May you be blessed, David my son; you will do great things and surely triumph.” So David went on his way, and Saul returned home.
chapters.zh: 扫罗对大卫说，我儿大卫，愿你得福。你必作大事，也必得胜。于是大卫起行，扫罗回他的本处去了。

chapters.en: But David thought to himself, “One of these days I will be destroyed by the hand of Saul. The best thing I can do is to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in Israel, and I will slip out of his hand.”
chapters.zh: 大卫心里说，必有一日我死在扫罗手里，不如逃奔非利士地去。扫罗见我不在以色列的境内，就必绝望，不再寻索我。这样我可以脱离他的手。

chapters.en: So David and the six hundred men with him left and went over to Achish son of Maok king of Gath.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫起身，和跟随他的六百人投奔迦特王玛俄的儿子亚吉去了。

chapters.en: David and his men settled in Gath with Achish. Each man had his family with him, and David had his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal.
chapters.zh: 大卫和他的两个妻，就是耶斯列人亚希暖和作过拿八妻的迦密人亚比该，并跟随他的人，连各人的眷属，都住在迦特亚吉那里。

chapters.en: When Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he no longer searched for him.
chapters.zh: 有人告诉扫罗说，大卫逃到迦特。扫罗就不再寻索他了。

chapters.en: Then David said to Achish, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be assigned to me in one of the country towns, that I may live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚吉说，我若在你眼前蒙恩，求你在京外的城邑中赐我一个地方居住。仆人何必与王同住京都呢？

chapters.en: So on that day Achish gave him Ziklag, and it has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
chapters.zh: 当日亚吉将洗革拉赐给他，因此洗革拉属犹大王，直到今日。

chapters.en: David lived in Philistine territory a year and four months.
chapters.zh: 大卫在非利士地住了一年零四个月。

chapters.en: Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. (From ancient times these peoples had lived in the land extending to Shur and Egypt.)
chapters.zh: 大卫和跟随他的人上去，侵夺基述人，基色人，亚玛力人之地。这几族历来住在那地，从书珥直到埃及。

chapters.en: Whenever David attacked an area, he did not leave a man or woman alive, but took sheep and cattle, donkeys and camels, and clothes. Then he returned to Achish.
chapters.zh: 大卫击杀那地的人，无论男女都没有留下一个，又夺获牛，羊，骆驼，驴，并衣服，回来见亚吉。

chapters.en: When Achish asked, “Where did you go raiding today?” David would say, “Against the Negev of Judah” or “Against the Negev of Jerahmeel” or “Against the Negev of the Kenites.”
chapters.zh: 亚吉说，你们今日侵夺了什么地方呢？大卫说，侵夺了犹大的南方，耶拉篾的南方，基尼的南方。

chapters.en: He did not leave a man or woman alive to be brought to Gath, for he thought, “They might inform on us and say, ‘This is what David did.’ ” And such was his practice as long as he lived in Philistine territory.
chapters.zh: 无论男女，大卫没有留下一个带到迦特来。他说，恐怕他们将我们的事告诉人，说大卫住在非利士地的时候常常这样行。

chapters.en: Achish trusted David and said to himself, “He has become so obnoxious to his people, the Israelites, that he will be my servant for life.”
chapters.zh: 亚吉信了大卫，心里说，大卫使本族以色列人憎恶他，所以他必永远作我的仆人了。

chapters.en: In those days the Philistines gathered their forces to fight against Israel. Achish said to David, “You must understand that you and your men will accompany me in the army.”
chapters.zh: 那时，非利士人聚集军旅，要与以色列人打仗。亚吉对大卫说，你当知道，你和跟随你的人都要随我出战。

chapters.en: David said, “Then you will see for yourself what your servant can do.” Achish replied, “Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life.”
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚吉说，仆人所能作的事，王必知道。亚吉对大卫说，这样，我立你永远作我的护卫长。

chapters.en: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in his own town of Ramah. Saul had expelled the mediums and spiritists from the land.
chapters.zh: 那时撒母耳已经死了，以色列众人为他哀哭，葬他在拉玛，就是在他本城里。扫罗曾在国内不容有交鬼的和行巫术的人。

chapters.en: The Philistines assembled and came and set up camp at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and set up camp at Gilboa.
chapters.zh: 非利士人聚集，来到书念安营。扫罗聚集以色列众人在基利波安营。

chapters.en: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid; terror filled his heart.
chapters.zh: 扫罗看见非利士的军旅就惧怕，心中发颤。

chapters.en: He inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets.
chapters.zh: 扫罗求问耶和华，耶和华却不借梦，或乌陵，或先知回答他。

chapters.en: Saul then said to his attendants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so I may go and inquire of her.” “There is one in Endor,” they said.
chapters.zh: 扫罗吩咐臣仆说，当为我找一个交鬼的妇人，我好去问她。臣仆说，在隐多珥有一个交鬼的妇人。

chapters.en: So Saul disguised himself, putting on other clothes, and at night he and two men went to the woman. “Consult a spirit for me,” he said, “and bring up for me the one I name.”
chapters.zh: 于是扫罗改了装，穿上别的衣服，带着两个人，夜里去见那妇人。扫罗说，求你用交鬼的法术，将我所告诉你的死人，为我招上来。

chapters.en: But the woman said to him, “Surely you know what Saul has done. He has cut off the mediums and spiritists from the land. Why have you set a trap for my life to bring about my death?”
chapters.zh: 妇人对他说，你知道扫罗从国中剪除交鬼的和行巫术的。你为何陷害我的性命，使我死呢？

chapters.en: Saul swore to her by the LORD, “As surely as the LORD lives, you will not be punished for this.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗向妇人指着耶和华起誓说，我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你必不因这事受刑。

chapters.en: Then the woman asked, “Whom shall I bring up for you?” “Bring up Samuel,” he said.
chapters.zh: 妇人说，我为你招谁上来呢？回答说，为我招撒母耳上来。

chapters.en: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out at the top of her voice and said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”
chapters.zh: 妇人看见撒母耳，就大声呼叫，对扫罗说，你是扫罗，为什么欺哄我呢？

chapters.en: The king said to her, “Don’t be afraid. What do you see?” The woman said, “I see a ghostly figure coming up out of the earth.”
chapters.zh: 王对妇人说，不要惧怕，你看见了什么呢？妇人对扫罗说，我看见有神从地里上来。

chapters.en: “What does he look like?” he asked. “An old man wearing a robe is coming up,” she said. Then Saul knew it was Samuel, and he bowed down and prostrated himself with his face to the ground.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说，他是怎样的形状。妇人说，有一个老人上来，身穿长衣。扫罗知道是撒母耳，就屈身，脸伏于地下拜。

chapters.en: Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” “I am in great distress,” Saul said. “The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has departed from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do.”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说，你为什么搅扰我，招我上来呢？扫罗回答说，我甚窘急。因为非利士人攻击我，神也离开我，不再借先知或梦回答我。因此请你上来，好指示我应当怎样行。

chapters.en: Samuel said, “Why do you consult me, now that the LORD has departed from you and become your enemy?
chapters.zh: 撒母耳说，耶和华已经离开你，且与你为敌，你何必问我呢？

chapters.en: The LORD has done what he predicted through me. The LORD has torn the kingdom out of your hands and given it to one of your neighbors—to David.
chapters.zh: 耶和华照他借我说的话，已经从你手里夺去国权，赐与别人，就是大卫。

chapters.en: Because you did not obey the LORD or carry out his fierce wrath against the Amalekites, the LORD has done this to you today.
chapters.zh: 因你没有听从耶和华的命令。他恼怒亚玛力人，你没有灭绝他们，所以今日耶和华向你这样行，

chapters.en: The LORD will deliver both Israel and you into the hands of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also give the army of Israel into the hands of the Philistines.”
chapters.zh: 并且耶和华必将你和以色列人交在非利士人的手里。明日你和你众子必与我在一处了。耶和华必将以色列的军兵交在非利士人手里。

chapters.en: Immediately Saul fell full length on the ground, filled with fear because of Samuel’s words. His strength was gone, for he had eaten nothing all that day and all that night.
chapters.zh: 扫罗猛然仆倒，挺身在地，因撒母耳的话甚是惧怕。那一昼一夜没有吃什么，就毫无气力。

chapters.en: When the woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly shaken, she said, “Look, your servant has obeyed you. I took my life in my hands and did what you told me to do.
chapters.zh: 妇人到扫罗面前，见他极其惊恐，对他说，婢女听从你的话，不顾惜自己的性命，遵从你所吩咐的。

chapters.en: Now please listen to your servant and let me give you some food so you may eat and have the strength to go on your way.”
chapters.zh: 现在求你听婢女的话，容我在你面前摆上一点食物，你吃了，可以有气力行路。

chapters.en: He refused and said, “I will not eat.” But his men joined the woman in urging him, and he listened to them. He got up from the ground and sat on the couch.
chapters.zh: 扫罗不肯，说，我不吃。但他的仆人和妇人再三劝他，他才听了他们的话，从地上起来，坐在床上。

chapters.en: The woman had a fattened calf at the house, which she butchered at once. She took some flour, kneaded it and baked bread without yeast.
chapters.zh: 妇人急忙将家里的一只肥牛犊宰了，又拿面抟成无酵饼烤了，

chapters.en: Then she set it before Saul and his men, and they ate. That same night they got up and left.
chapters.zh: 摆在扫罗和他仆人面前。他们吃完，当夜就起身走了。

chapters.en: The Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, and Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.
chapters.zh: 非利士人将他们的军旅聚到亚弗。以色列人在耶斯列的泉旁安营。

chapters.en: As the Philistine rulers marched with their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men were marching at the rear with Achish.
chapters.zh: 非利士人的首领各率军队，或百或千，挨次前进。大卫和跟随他的人同着亚吉跟在后边。

chapters.en: The commanders of the Philistines asked, “What about these Hebrews?” Achish replied, “Is this not David, who was an officer of Saul king of Israel? He has already been with me for over a year, and from the day he left Saul until now, I have found no fault in him.”
chapters.zh: 非利士人的首领说，这些希伯来人在这里作什么呢？亚吉对他们说，这不是以色列王扫罗的臣子大卫吗？他在我这里有些年日了。自从他投降我直到今日，我未曾见他有过错。

chapters.en: But the Philistine commanders were angry with Achish and said, “Send the man back, that he may return to the place you assigned him. He must not go with us into battle, or he will turn against us during the fighting. How better could he regain his master’s favor than by taking the heads of our own men?
chapters.zh: 非利士人的首领向亚吉发怒，对他说，你要叫这人回你所安置他的地方，不可叫他同我们出战，恐怕他在阵上反为我们的敌人。他用什么与他主人复和呢？岂不是用我们这些人的首级吗？

chapters.en: Isn’t this the David they sang about in their dances: “ ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
chapters.zh: 从前以色列的妇女跳舞唱和说，扫罗杀死千千，大卫杀死万万，所说的不是这个大卫吗？

chapters.en: So Achish called David and said to him, “As surely as the LORD lives, you have been reliable, and I would be pleased to have you serve with me in the army. From the day you came to me until today, I have found no fault in you, but the rulers don’t approve of you.
chapters.zh: 亚吉叫大卫来，对他说，我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你是正直人。你随我在军中出入，我看你甚好。自从你投奔我到如今，我未曾见你有什么过失。只是众首领不喜悦你。

chapters.en: Now turn back and go in peace; do nothing to displease the Philistine rulers.”
chapters.zh: 现在你可以平平安安地回去，免得非利士人的首领不欢喜你。
