chapters.en: Now the whole clan has risen up against your servant; they say, ‘Hand over the one who struck his brother down, so that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed; then we will get rid of the heir as well.’ They would put out the only burning coal I have left, leaving my husband neither name nor descendant on the face of the earth.”
chapters.zh: 现在全家的人都起来攻击婢女，说，你将那打死兄弟的交出来，我们好治死他，偿他打死兄弟的命，灭绝那承受家业的。这样，他们要将我剩下的炭火灭尽，不与我丈夫留名留后在世上。

chapters.en: The king said to the woman, “Go home, and I will issue an order in your behalf.”
chapters.zh: 王对妇人说，你回家去吧。我必为你下令。

chapters.en: But the woman from Tekoa said to him, “Let my lord the king pardon me and my family, and let the king and his throne be without guilt.”
chapters.zh: 提哥亚妇人又对王说，我主我王，愿这罪归我和我父家，与王和王的位无干。

chapters.en: The king replied, “If anyone says anything to you, bring them to me, and they will not bother you again.”
chapters.zh: 王说，凡难为你的，你就带他到我这里来，他必不再搅扰你。

chapters.en: She said, “Then let the king invoke the LORD his God to prevent the avenger of blood from adding to the destruction, so that my son will not be destroyed.” “As surely as the LORD lives,” he said, “not one hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”
chapters.zh: 妇人说，愿王记念耶和华你的神，不许报血仇的人施行灭绝，恐怕他们灭绝我的儿子。王说，我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你的儿子连一根头发也不至落在地上。

chapters.en: Then the woman said, “Let your servant speak a word to my lord the king.” “Speak,” he replied.
chapters.zh: 妇人说，求我主我王容婢女再说一句话。王说，你说吧。

chapters.en: The woman said, “Why then have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, for the king has not brought back his banished son?
chapters.zh: 妇人说，王为何也起意要害神的民呢？王不使那逃亡的人回来，王的这话就是自证己错了。

chapters.en: Like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be recovered, so we must die. But that is not what God desires; rather, he devises ways so that a banished person does not remain banished from him.
chapters.zh: 我们都是必死的，如同水泼在地上，不能收回。神并不夺取人的性命，乃设法使逃亡的人不至成为赶出回不来的。

chapters.en: “And now I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king; perhaps he will grant his servant’s request.
chapters.zh: 我来将这话告诉我主我王，是因百姓使我惧怕。婢女想，不如将这话告诉王，或者王成就婢女所求的。

chapters.en: Perhaps the king will agree to deliver his servant from the hand of the man who is trying to cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’
chapters.zh: 人要将我和我儿子从神的地业上一同除灭，王必应允救我脱离他的手。

chapters.en: “And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king secure my inheritance, for my lord the king is like an angel of God in discerning good and evil. May the LORD your God be with you.’ ”
chapters.zh: 婢女又想，我主我王的话必安慰我。因为我主我王能辨别是非，如同神的使者一样。惟愿耶和华你的神与你同在。

chapters.en: Then the king said to the woman, “Don’t keep from me the answer to what I am going to ask you.” “Let my lord the king speak,” the woman said.
chapters.zh: 王对妇人说，我要问你一句话，你一点不要瞒我。妇人说，愿我主我王说。

chapters.en: The king asked, “Isn’t the hand of Joab with you in all this?” The woman answered, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything my lord the king says. Yes, it was your servant Joab who instructed me to do this and who put all these words into the mouth of your servant.
chapters.zh: 王说，你这些话莫非是约押的主意吗？妇人说，我敢在我主我王面前起誓，王的话正对，不偏左右，是王的仆人约押吩咐我的，这些话是他教导我的。

chapters.en: Your servant Joab did this to change the present situation. My lord has wisdom like that of an angel of God—he knows everything that happens in the land.”
chapters.zh: 王的仆人约押如此行，为要挽回这事。我主的智慧却如神使者的智慧，能知世上一切事。

chapters.en: The king said to Joab, “Very well, I will do it. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.”
chapters.zh: 王对约押说，我应允你这事。你可以去，把那少年人押沙龙带回来。

chapters.en: Joab fell with his face to the ground to pay him honor, and he blessed the king. Joab said, “Today your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his servant’s request.”
chapters.zh: 约押就面伏于地叩拜，祝谢于王，又说，王既应允仆人所求的，仆人今日知道在我主我王眼前蒙恩了。

chapters.en: Then Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 于是约押起身往基述去，将押沙龙带回耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: But the king said, “He must go to his own house; he must not see my face.” So Absalom went to his own house and did not see the face of the king.
chapters.zh: 王说，使他回自己家里去，不要见我的面。押沙龙就回自己家里去，没有见王的面。

chapters.en: In all Israel there was not a man so highly praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom. From the top of his head to the sole of his foot there was no blemish in him.
chapters.zh: 以色列全地之中，无人像押沙龙那样俊美，得人的称赞，从脚底到头顶毫无瑕疵。

chapters.en: Whenever he cut the hair of his head—he used to cut his hair once a year because it became too heavy for him—he would weigh it, and its weight was two hundred shekels by the royal standard.
chapters.zh: 他的头发甚重，每到年底剪发一次。所剪下来的，按王的平称一称，重二百舍客勒。

chapters.en: Three sons and a daughter were born to Absalom. His daughter’s name was Tamar, and she became a beautiful woman.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙生了三个儿子，一个女儿。女儿名叫他玛，是个容貌俊美的女子。

chapters.en: Absalom lived two years in Jerusalem without seeing the king’s face.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙住在耶路撒冷足有二年，没有见王的面。

chapters.en: Then Absalom sent for Joab in order to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So he sent a second time, but he refused to come.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙打发人去叫约押来，要托他去见王，约押却不肯来。第二次打发人去叫他，他仍不肯来。

chapters.en: Then he said to his servants, “Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” So Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
chapters.zh: 所以押沙龙对仆人说，你们看，约押有一块田，与我的田相近，其中有大麦，你们去放火烧了。押沙龙的仆人就去放火烧了那田。

chapters.en: Then Joab did go to Absalom’s house, and he said to him, “Why have your servants set my field on fire?”
chapters.zh: 于是约押起来，到了押沙龙家里，问他说，你的仆人为何放火烧了我的田呢？

chapters.en: Absalom said to Joab, “Look, I sent word to you and said, ‘Come here so I can send you to the king to ask, “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there!” ’ Now then, I want to see the king’s face, and if I am guilty of anything, let him put me to death.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙回答约押说，我打发人去请你来，好托你去见王，替我说，我为何从基述回来呢？不如仍在那里。现在要许我见王的面。我若有罪，任凭王杀我就是了。

chapters.en: So Joab went to the king and told him this. Then the king summoned Absalom, and he came in and bowed down with his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.
chapters.zh: 于是约押去见王，将这话奏告王，王便叫押沙龙来。押沙龙来见王，在王面前俯伏于地，王就与押沙龙亲嘴。

chapters.en: In the course of time, Absalom provided himself with a chariot and horses and with fifty men to run ahead of him.
chapters.zh: 此后，押沙龙为自己预备车马，又派五十人在他前头奔走。

chapters.en: He would get up early and stand by the side of the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone came with a complaint to be placed before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out to him, “What town are you from?” He would answer, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙常常早晨起来，站在城门的道旁，凡有争讼要去求王判断的，押沙龙就叫他过来，问他说，你是哪一城的人。回答说，仆人是以色列某支派的人。

chapters.en: Then Absalom would say to him, “Look, your claims are valid and proper, but there is no representative of the king to hear you.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙对他说，你的事有情有理，无奈王没有委人听你伸诉。

chapters.en: And Absalom would add, “If only I were appointed judge in the land! Then everyone who has a complaint or case could come to me and I would see that they receive justice.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙又说，恨不得我作国中的士师。凡有争讼求审判的到我这里来，我必秉公判断。

chapters.en: Also, whenever anyone approached him to bow down before him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.
chapters.zh: 若有人近前来要拜押沙龙，押沙龙就伸手拉住他，与他亲嘴。

chapters.en: Absalom behaved in this way toward all the Israelites who came to the king asking for justice, and so he stole the hearts of the people of Israel.
chapters.zh: 以色列人中，凡去见王求判断的，押沙龙都是如此待他们。这样，押沙龙暗中得了以色列人的心。

chapters.en: At the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, “Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow I made to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 满了四十年（有作四年的），押沙龙对王说，求你准我往希伯仑去，还我向耶和华所许的愿。

chapters.en: While your servant was living at Geshur in Aram, I made this vow: ‘If the LORD takes me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron. ’ ”
chapters.zh: 因为仆人住在亚兰的基述，曾许愿说，耶和华若使我再回耶路撒冷，我必事奉他。

chapters.en: The king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he went to Hebron.
chapters.zh: 王说，你平平安安地去吧。押沙龙就起身，往希伯仑去了。

chapters.en: Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout the tribes of Israel to say, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpets, then say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron.’ ”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙打发探子走遍以色列各支派，说，你们一听见角声就说，押沙龙在希伯仑作王了。

chapters.en: Two hundred men from Jerusalem had accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and went quite innocently, knowing nothing about the matter.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙在耶路撒冷请了二百人与他同去，都是诚诚实实去的，并不知道其中的真情。

chapters.en: While Absalom was offering sacrifices, he also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from Giloh, his hometown. And so the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept on increasing.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙献祭的时候，打发人去将大卫的谋士，基罗人亚希多弗从他本城请了来。于是叛逆的势派甚大。因为随从押沙龙的人民，日渐增多。

chapters.en: A messenger came and told David, “The hearts of the people of Israel are with Absalom.”
chapters.zh: 有人报告大卫说，以色列人的心都归向押沙龙了。

chapters.en: Then David said to all his officials who were with him in Jerusalem, “Come! We must flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. We must leave immediately, or he will move quickly to overtake us and bring ruin on us and put the city to the sword.”
chapters.zh: 大卫就对耶路撒冷跟随他的臣仆说，我们要起来逃走，不然都不能躲避押沙龙了。要速速地去，恐怕他忽然来到，加害于我们，用刀杀尽合城的人。

chapters.en: The king’s officials answered him, “Your servants are ready to do whatever our lord the king chooses.”
chapters.zh: 王的臣仆对王说，我主我王所定的，仆人都愿遵行。

chapters.en: The king set out, with his entire household following him; but he left ten concubines to take care of the palace.
chapters.zh: 于是王带着全家的人出去了，但留下十个妃嫔看守宫殿。

chapters.en: So the king set out, with all the people following him, and they halted at the edge of the city.
chapters.zh: 王出去，众民都跟随他，到伯墨哈，就住下了。

chapters.en: All his men marched past him, along with all the Kerethites and Pelethites; and all the six hundred Gittites who had accompanied him from Gath marched before the king.
chapters.zh: 王的臣仆都在他面前过去。基利提人，比利提人，就是从迦特跟随王来的六百人，也都在他面前过去。

chapters.en: The king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you come along with us? Go back and stay with King Absalom. You are a foreigner, an exile from your homeland.
chapters.zh: 王对迦特人以太说，你是外邦逃来的人，为什么与我们同去呢？你可以回去与新王同住，或者回你本地去吧。

chapters.en: You came only yesterday. And today shall I make you wander about with us, when I do not know where I am going? Go back, and take your people with you. May the LORD show you kindness and faithfulness.”
chapters.zh: 你来的日子不多，我今日怎好叫你与我们一同飘流，没有一定的住处呢？你不如带你的弟兄回去吧。愿耶和华用慈爱诚实待你。

chapters.en: But Ittai replied to the king, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be.”
chapters.zh: 以太对王说，我指着永生的耶和华起誓，又敢在王面前起誓，无论生死，王在哪里，仆人也必在哪里。

chapters.en: David said to Ittai, “Go ahead, march on.” So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and the families that were with him.
chapters.zh: 大卫对以太说，你前去过河吧。于是迦特人以太带着跟随他的人和所有的妇人孩子，就都过去了。

chapters.en: The whole countryside wept aloud as all the people passed by. The king also crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people moved on toward the wilderness.
chapters.zh: 本地的人都放声大哭。众民尽都过去，王也过了汲沦溪。众民往旷野去了。

chapters.en: Zadok was there, too, and all the Levites who were with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving the city.
chapters.zh: 撒督和抬神约柜的利未人也一同来了，将神的约柜放下。亚比亚他上来，等着众民从城里出来过去。

chapters.en: Then the king said to Zadok, “Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the LORD’s eyes, he will bring me back and let me see it and his dwelling place again.
chapters.zh: 王对撒督说，你将神的约柜抬回城去。我若在耶和华眼前蒙恩，他必使我回来，再见约柜和他的居所。

chapters.en: But if he says, ‘I am not pleased with you,’ then I am ready; let him do to me whatever seems good to him.”
chapters.zh: 倘若他说，我不喜悦你，看哪，我在这里，愿他凭自己的意旨待我。

chapters.en: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Do you understand? Go back to the city with my blessing. Take your son Ahimaaz with you, and also Abiathar’s son Jonathan. You and Abiathar return with your two sons.
chapters.zh: 王又对祭司撒督说，你不是先见吗？你可以安然回城。你儿子亚希玛斯和亚比亚他的儿子约拿单都可以与你同去。

chapters.en: I will wait at the fords in the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
chapters.zh: 我在旷野的渡口那里等你们报信给我。

chapters.en: So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there.
chapters.zh: 于是撒督和亚比亚他将神的约柜抬回耶路撒冷，他们就住在那里。

chapters.en: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went; his head was covered and he was barefoot. All the people with him covered their heads too and were weeping as they went up.
chapters.zh: 大卫蒙头赤脚上橄榄山，一面上，一面哭。跟随他的人也都蒙头哭着上去。

chapters.en: Now David had been told, “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David prayed, “LORD, turn Ahithophel’s counsel into foolishness.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉大卫说，亚希多弗也在叛党之中，随从押沙龙。大卫祷告说，耶和华阿，求你使亚希多弗的计谋变为愚拙。

chapters.en: When David arrived at the summit, where people used to worship God, Hushai the Arkite was there to meet him, his robe torn and dust on his head.
chapters.zh: 大卫到了山顶，敬拜神的地方，见亚基人户筛，衣服撕裂，头蒙灰尘来迎接他。

chapters.en: David said to him, “If you go with me, you will be a burden to me.
chapters.zh: 大卫对他说，你若与我同去，必累赘我。

chapters.en: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘Your Majesty, I will be your servant; I was your father’s servant in the past, but now I will be your servant,’ then you can help me by frustrating Ahithophel’s advice.
chapters.zh: 你若回城去，对押沙龙说，王阿，我愿作你的仆人。我向来作你父亲的仆人，现在我也照样作你的仆人。这样，你就可以为我破坏亚希多弗的计谋。

chapters.en: Won’t the priests Zadok and Abiathar be there with you? Tell them anything you hear in the king’s palace.
chapters.zh: 祭司撒督和亚比亚他岂不都在那里吗？你在王宫里听见什么，就要告诉祭司撒督和亚比亚他。

chapters.en: Their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with anything you hear.”
chapters.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯，亚比亚他的儿子约拿单，也都在那里。凡你们所听见的可以托这二人来报告我。

chapters.en: So Hushai, David’s confidant, arrived at Jerusalem as Absalom was entering the city.
chapters.zh: 于是，大卫的朋友户筛进了城。押沙龙也进了耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: When David had gone a short distance beyond the summit, there was Ziba, the steward of Mephibosheth, waiting to meet him. He had a string of donkeys saddled and loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred cakes of figs and a skin of wine.
chapters.zh: 大卫刚过山顶，见米非波设的仆人洗巴拉着备好了的两匹驴，驴上驮着二百面饼，一百葡萄饼，一百个夏天的果饼，一皮袋酒来迎接他。

chapters.en: The king asked Ziba, “Why have you brought these?” Ziba answered, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on, the bread and fruit are for the men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”
chapters.zh: 王问洗巴说，你带这些来是什么意思呢？洗巴说，驴是给王的家眷骑的。面饼和夏天的果饼是给少年人吃的。酒是给在旷野疲乏人喝的。

chapters.en: The king then asked, “Where is your master’s grandson?” Ziba said to him, “He is staying in Jerusalem, because he thinks, ‘Today the Israelites will restore to me my grandfather’s kingdom.’ ”
chapters.zh: 王问说，你主人的儿子在哪里呢？洗巴回答王说，他仍在耶路撒冷，因他说，以色列人今日必将我父的国归还我。

chapters.en: Then the king said to Ziba, “All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours.” “I humbly bow,” Ziba said. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king.”
chapters.zh: 王对洗巴说，凡属米非波设的都归你了。洗巴说，我叩拜我主我王，愿我在你眼前蒙恩。

chapters.en: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the same clan as Saul’s family came out from there. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he cursed as he came out.
chapters.zh: 大卫王到了巴户琳，见有一个人出来，是扫罗族基拉的儿子，名叫示每。他一面走一面咒骂，

chapters.en: He pelted David and all the king’s officials with stones, though all the troops and the special guard were on David’s right and left.
chapters.zh: 又拿石头砍大卫王和王的臣仆。众民和勇士都在王的左右。

chapters.en: As he cursed, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you murderer, you scoundrel!
chapters.zh: 示每咒骂说，你这流人血的坏人哪，去吧去吧。

chapters.en: The LORD has repaid you for all the blood you shed in the household of Saul, in whose place you have reigned. The LORD has given the kingdom into the hands of your son Absalom. You have come to ruin because you are a murderer!”
chapters.zh: 你流扫罗全家的血，接续他作王。耶和华把这罪归在你身上，将这国交给你儿子押沙龙。现在你自取其祸，因为你是流人血的人。

chapters.en: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head.”
chapters.zh: 洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛对王说，这死狗岂可咒骂我主我王呢？求你容我过去，割下他的头来。

chapters.en: But the king said, “What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? If he is cursing because the LORD said to him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why do you do this?’ ”
chapters.zh: 王说，洗鲁雅的儿子，我与你们有何关涉呢？他咒骂是因耶和华吩咐他说，你要咒骂大卫。如此，谁敢说你为什么这样行呢？

chapters.en: David then said to Abishai and all his officials, “My son, my own flesh and blood, is trying to kill me. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone; let him curse, for the LORD has told him to.
chapters.zh: 大卫又对亚比筛和众臣仆说，我亲生的儿子尚且寻索我的性命，何况这便雅悯人呢？由他咒骂吧。因为这是耶和华吩咐他的。

chapters.en: It may be that the LORD will look upon my misery and restore to me his covenant blessing instead of his curse today.”
chapters.zh: 或者耶和华见我遭难，为我今日被这人咒骂，就施恩与我。

chapters.en: So David and his men continued along the road while Shimei was going along the hillside opposite him, cursing as he went and throwing stones at him and showering him with dirt.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫和跟随他的人往前行走。示每在大卫对面山坡，一面行走一面咒骂，又拿石头砍他，拿土扬他。

chapters.en: The king and all the people with him arrived at their destination exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.
chapters.zh: 王和跟随他的众人疲疲乏乏地到了一个地方，就在那里歇息歇息。

chapters.en: Meanwhile, Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙和以色列众人来到耶路撒冷。亚希多弗也与他同来。

chapters.en: Then Hushai the Arkite, David’s confidant, went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
chapters.zh: 大卫的朋友亚基人户筛去见押沙龙，对他说，愿王万岁。愿王万岁。

chapters.en: Absalom said to Hushai, “So this is the love you show your friend? If he’s your friend, why didn’t you go with him?”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙问户筛说，这是你恩待朋友吗？为什么不与你的朋友同去呢？

chapters.en: Hushai said to Absalom, “No, the one chosen by the LORD, by these people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and I will remain with him.
chapters.zh: 户筛对押沙龙说，不然，耶和华和这民，并以色列众人所拣选的，我必归顺他，与他同住。

chapters.en: Furthermore, whom should I serve? Should I not serve the son? Just as I served your father, so I will serve you.”
chapters.zh: 再者，我当服事谁呢？岂不是前王的儿子吗？我怎样服事你父亲，也必照样服事你。

chapters.en: Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give us your advice. What should we do?”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙对亚希多弗说，你们出个主意，我们怎样行才好。

chapters.en: Ahithophel answered, “Sleep with your father’s concubines whom he left to take care of the palace. Then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself obnoxious to your father, and the hands of everyone with you will be more resolute.”
chapters.zh: 亚希多弗对押沙龙说，你父所留下看守宫殿的妃嫔，你可以与她们亲近。以色列众人听见你父亲憎恶你，凡归顺你人的手就更坚强。

chapters.en: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
chapters.zh: 于是人为押沙龙在宫殿的平顶上支搭帐棚。押沙龙在以色列众人眼前，与他父的妃嫔亲近。

chapters.en: Now in those days the advice Ahithophel gave was like that of one who inquires of God. That was how both David and Absalom regarded all of Ahithophel’s advice.
chapters.zh: 那时亚希多弗所出的主意好像人问神的话一样。他昔日给大卫，今日给押沙龙所出的主意，都是这样。

chapters.en: Ahithophel said to Absalom, “I would choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.
chapters.zh: 亚希多弗又对押沙龙说，求你准我挑选一万二千人，今夜我就起身追赶大卫，

chapters.en: I would attack him while he is weary and weak. I would strike him with terror, and then all the people with him will flee. I would strike down only the king
chapters.zh: 趁他疲乏手软，我忽然追上他，使他惊惶。跟随他的民必都逃跑，我就单杀王一人，

chapters.en: and bring all the people back to you. The death of the man you seek will mean the return of all; all the people will be unharmed.”
chapters.zh: 使众民都归顺你。你所寻找的人既然死了，众民就如已经归顺你。这样，也都平安无事了。

chapters.en: This plan seemed good to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙和以色列的长老都以这话为美。

chapters.en: But Absalom said, “Summon also Hushai the Arkite, so we can hear what he has to say as well.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙说，要召亚基人户筛来，我们也要听他怎样说。

chapters.en: When Hushai came to him, Absalom said, “Ahithophel has given this advice. Should we do what he says? If not, give us your opinion.”
chapters.zh: 户筛到了押沙龙面前，押沙龙向他说，亚希多弗是如此如此说的，我们照着他的话行可以不可以。若不可，你就说吧。

chapters.en: Hushai replied to Absalom, “The advice Ahithophel has given is not good this time.
chapters.zh: 户筛对押沙龙说，亚希多弗这次所定的谋不善。

chapters.en: You know your father and his men; they are fighters, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Besides, your father is an experienced fighter; he will not spend the night with the troops.
chapters.zh: 户筛又说，你知道，你父亲和跟随他的人都是勇士，现在他们心里恼怒，如同田野丢崽子的母熊一般，而且你父亲是个战士，必不和民一同住宿。

chapters.en: Even now, he is hidden in a cave or some other place. If he should attack your troops first, whoever hears about it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’
chapters.zh: 他现今或藏在坑中或在别处，若有人首先被杀，凡听见的必说，跟随押沙龙的民被杀了。

chapters.en: Then even the bravest soldier, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will melt with fear, for all Israel knows that your father is a fighter and that those with him are brave.
chapters.zh: 虽有人胆大如狮子，他的心也必消化。因为以色列人都知道你父亲是英雄，跟随他的人也都是勇士。

chapters.en: “So I advise you: Let all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba—as numerous as the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, with you yourself leading them into battle.
chapters.zh: 依我之计，不如将以色列众人从但直到别是巴，如同海边的沙那样多聚集到你这里来，你也亲自率领他们出战。

chapters.en: Then we will attack him wherever he may be found, and we will fall on him as dew settles on the ground. Neither he nor any of his men will be left alive.
chapters.zh: 这样，我们在何处遇见他，就下到他那里，如同露水下在地上一般，连他带跟随他的人，一个也不留下。

chapters.en: If he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not so much as a pebble is left.”
chapters.zh: 他若进了哪一座城，以色列众人必带绳子去，将那城拉到河里，甚至连一块小石头都不剩下。

chapters.en: Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Arkite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had determined to frustrate the good advice of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙和以色列众人说，亚基人户筛的计谋比亚希多弗的计谋更好。这是因耶和华定意破坏亚希多弗的良谋，为要降祸与押沙龙。

chapters.en: Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel to do such and such, but I have advised them to do so and so.
chapters.zh: 户筛对祭司撒督和亚比亚他说，亚希多弗为押沙龙和以色列的长老所定的计谋是如此如此，我所定的计谋是如此如此。

chapters.en: Now send a message at once and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords in the wilderness; cross over without fail, or the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’ ”
chapters.zh: 现在你们要急速打发人去，告诉大卫说，今夜不可住在旷野的渡口，务要过河，免得王和跟随他的人都被吞灭。

chapters.en: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En Rogel. A female servant was to go and inform them, and they were to go and tell King David, for they could not risk being seen entering the city.
chapters.zh: 那时，约拿单和亚希玛斯在隐罗结那里等候，不敢进城，恐怕被人看见。有一个使女出来，将这话告诉他们，他们就去报信给大卫王。

chapters.en: But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them left at once and went to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
chapters.zh: 然而有一个童子看见他们，就去告诉押沙龙。他们急忙跑到巴户琳某人的家里。那人院中有一口井，他们就下到井里。

chapters.en: His wife took a covering and spread it out over the opening of the well and scattered grain over it. No one knew anything about it.
chapters.zh: 那家的妇人用盖盖上井口，又在上头铺上碎麦，事就没有泄漏。

chapters.en: When Absalom’s men came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered them, “They crossed over the brook.” The men searched but found no one, so they returned to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙的仆人来到那家，问妇人说，亚希玛斯和约拿单在哪里。妇人说，他们过了河了。仆人找他们，找不着，就回耶路撒冷去了。

chapters.en: After they had gone, the two climbed out of the well and went to inform King David. They said to him, “Set out and cross the river at once; Ahithophel has advised such and such against you.”
chapters.zh: 他们走后，二人从井里上来，去告诉大卫王说，亚希多弗如此如此定计害你，你们务要起来，快快过河。

chapters.en: So David and all the people with him set out and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, no one was left who had not crossed the Jordan.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫和跟随他的人都起来，过约旦河。到了天亮，无一人不过约旦河的。

chapters.en: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his house in order and then hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.
chapters.zh: 亚希多弗见不依从他的计谋，就备上驴，归回本城。到了家，留下遗言，便吊死了，葬在他父亲的坟墓里。

chapters.en: David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
chapters.zh: 大卫到了玛哈念，押沙龙和跟随他的以色列人也都过了约旦河。

chapters.en: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of Jether, an Ishmaelite who had married Abigail , the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙立亚玛撒作元帅，代替约押。亚玛撒是以实玛利人（又作以色列人）以特拉的儿子。以特拉曾与拿辖的女儿亚比该亲近。这亚比该与约押的母亲洗鲁雅是姐妹。

chapters.en: The Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙和以色列人都安营在基列地。

chapters.en: When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and Makir son of Ammiel from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim
chapters.zh: 大卫到了玛哈念，亚扪族的拉巴人拿辖的儿子朔比，罗底巴人亚米利的儿子玛吉，基列的罗基琳人巴西莱，

chapters.en: brought bedding and bowls and articles of pottery. They also brought wheat and barley, flour and roasted grain, beans and lentils,
chapters.zh: 带着被，褥，盆，碗，瓦器，小麦，大麦，麦面，炒谷，豆子，红豆，炒豆，

chapters.en: honey and curds, sheep, and cheese from cows’ milk for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become exhausted and hungry and thirsty in the wilderness.”
chapters.zh: 蜂蜜，奶油，绵羊，奶饼，供给大卫和跟随他的人吃。他们说，民在旷野，必饥渴困乏了。

chapters.en: David mustered the men who were with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.
chapters.zh: 大卫数点跟随他的人，立千夫长，百夫长率领他们。

chapters.en: David sent out his troops, a third under the command of Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. The king told the troops, “I myself will surely march out with you.”
chapters.zh: 大卫打发军兵出战，分为三队，一队在约押手下，一队在洗鲁雅的儿子，约押兄弟亚比筛手下，一队在迦特人以太手下。大卫对军兵说，我必与你们一同出战。

chapters.en: But the men said, “You must not go out; if we are forced to flee, they won’t care about us. Even if half of us die, they won’t care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It would be better now for you to give us support from the city.”
chapters.zh: 军兵却说，你不可出战。若是我们逃跑，敌人必不介意。我们阵亡一半，敌人也不介意。因为你一人强似我们万人，你不如在城里预备帮助我们。

chapters.en: The king answered, “I will do whatever seems best to you.” So the king stood beside the gate while all his men marched out in units of hundreds and of thousands.
chapters.zh: 王向他们说，你们以为怎样好，我就怎样行。于是王站在城门旁，军兵或百或千地挨次出去了。

chapters.en: The king commanded Joab, Abishai and Ittai, “Be gentle with the young man Absalom for my sake.” And all the troops heard the king giving orders concerning Absalom to each of the commanders.
chapters.zh: 王嘱咐约押，亚比筛，以太说，你们要为我的缘故宽待那少年人押沙龙。王为押沙龙嘱咐众将的话，兵都听见了。

chapters.en: David’s army marched out of the city to fight Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
chapters.zh: 兵就出到田野迎着以色列人，在以法莲树林里交战。

chapters.en: There Israel’s troops were routed by David’s men, and the casualties that day were great—twenty thousand men.
chapters.zh: 以色列人败在大卫的仆人面前。那日阵亡的甚多，共有二万人。

chapters.en: The battle spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest swallowed up more men that day than the sword.
chapters.zh: 因为在那里四面打仗，死于树林的比死于刀剑的更多。

chapters.en: Now Absalom happened to meet David’s men. He was riding his mule, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s hair got caught in the tree. He was left hanging in midair, while the mule he was riding kept on going.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙偶然遇见大卫的仆人。押沙龙骑着骡子，从大橡树密枝底下经过，他的头发被树枝绕住，就悬挂起来，所骑的骡子便离他去了。

chapters.en: When one of the men saw what had happened, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree.”
chapters.zh: 有个人看见，就告诉约押说，我看见押沙龙挂在橡树上了。

chapters.en: Joab said to the man who had told him this, “What! You saw him? Why didn’t you strike him to the ground right there? Then I would have had to give you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt.”
chapters.zh: 约押对报信的人说，你既看见他，为什么不将他打死落在地上呢？你若打死他，我就赏你十舍客勒银子，一条带子。

chapters.en: But the man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels were weighed out into my hands, I would not lay a hand on the king’s son. In our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake. ’
chapters.zh: 那人对约押说，我就是得你一千舍客勒银子，我也不敢伸手害王的儿子。因为我们听见王嘱咐你和亚比筛并以太说，你们要谨慎，不可害那少年人押沙龙。

chapters.en: And if I had put my life in jeopardy —and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have kept your distance from me.”
chapters.zh: 我若妄为害了他的性命，就是你自己也必与我为敌。原来无论何事都瞒不过王。

chapters.en: Joab said, “I’m not going to wait like this for you.” So he took three javelins in his hand and plunged them into Absalom’s heart while Absalom was still alive in the oak tree.
chapters.zh: 约押说，我不能与你留连。约押手拿三杆短枪，趁押沙龙在橡树上还活着，就刺透他的心。

chapters.en: And ten of Joab’s armor-bearers surrounded Absalom, struck him and killed him.
chapters.zh: 给约押拿兵器的十个少年人围绕押沙龙，将他杀死。

chapters.en: Then Joab sounded the trumpet, and the troops stopped pursuing Israel, for Joab halted them.
chapters.zh: 约押吹角，拦阻众人，他们就回来，不再追赶以色列人。

chapters.en: They took Absalom, threw him into a big pit in the forest and piled up a large heap of rocks over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled to their homes.
chapters.zh: 他们将押沙龙丢在林中一个大坑里，上头堆起一大堆石头。以色列众人都逃跑，各回各家去了。

chapters.en: During his lifetime Absalom had taken a pillar and erected it in the King’s Valley as a monument to himself, for he thought, “I have no son to carry on the memory of my name.” He named the pillar after himself, and it is called Absalom’s Monument to this day.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙活着的时候，在王谷立了一根石柱，因他说，我没有儿子为我留名。他就以自己的名称那石柱叫押沙龙柱，直到今日。

chapters.en: Now Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Let me run and take the news to the king that the LORD has vindicated him by delivering him from the hand of his enemies.”
chapters.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯说，容我跑去，将耶和华向仇敌给王报仇的信息报与王知。

chapters.en: “You are not the one to take the news today,” Joab told him. “You may take the news another time, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”
chapters.zh: 约押对他说，你今日不可去报信，改日可以报信。因为今日王的儿子死了，所以你不可去报信。

chapters.en: Then Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed down before Joab and ran off.
chapters.zh: 约押对古示人说，你去将你所看见的告诉王。古示人在约押面前下拜，就跑去了。

chapters.en: Ahimaaz son of Zadok again said to Joab, “Come what may, please let me run behind the Cushite.” But Joab replied, “My son, why do you want to go? You don’t have any news that will bring you a reward.”
chapters.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯又对约押说，无论怎样，求你容我随着古示人跑去。约押说，我儿，你报这信息，既不得赏赐，何必要跑去呢？

chapters.en: He said, “Come what may, I want to run.” So Joab said, “Run!” Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
chapters.zh: 他又说，无论怎样，我要跑去。约押说，你跑去吧。亚希玛斯就从平原往前跑，跑过古示人去了。

chapters.en: While David was sitting between the inner and outer gates, the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall. As he looked out, he saw a man running alone.
chapters.zh: 大卫正坐在城瓮里。守望的人上城门楼的顶上，举目观看，见有一个人独自跑来。

chapters.en: The watchman called out to the king and reported it. The king said, “If he is alone, he must have good news.” And the runner came closer and closer.
chapters.zh: 守望的人就大声告诉王。王说，他若独自来，必是报口信的。那人跑得渐渐近了。

chapters.en: Then the watchman saw another runner, and he called down to the gatekeeper, “Look, another man running alone!” The king said, “He must be bringing good news, too.”
chapters.zh: 守望的人又见一人跑来，就对守城门的人说，又有一人独自跑来。王说，这也必是报信的。

chapters.en: The watchman said, “It seems to me that the first one runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.” “He’s a good man,” the king said. “He comes with good news.”
chapters.zh: 守望的人说，我看前头人的跑法，好像撒督的儿子亚希玛斯的跑法一样。王说，他是个好人，必是报好信息。

chapters.en: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” He bowed down before the king with his face to the ground and said, “Praise be to the LORD your God! He has delivered up those who lifted their hands against my lord the king.”
chapters.zh: 亚希玛斯向王呼叫说，平安了。就在王面前脸伏于地叩拜，说，耶和华你的神是应当称颂的，因他已将那举手攻击我主我王的人交给王了。

chapters.en: The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom safe?” Ahimaaz answered, “I saw great confusion just as Joab was about to send the king’s servant and me, your servant, but I don’t know what it was.”
chapters.zh: 王问说，少年人押沙龙平安不平安。亚希玛斯回答说，约押打发王的仆人，那时仆人听见众民大声喧哗，却不知道是什么事。

chapters.en: The king said, “Stand aside and wait here.” So he stepped aside and stood there.
chapters.zh: 王说，你退去，站在旁边。他就退去，站在旁边。

chapters.en: Then the Cushite arrived and said, “My lord the king, hear the good news! The LORD has vindicated you today by delivering you from the hand of all who rose up against you.”
chapters.zh: 古示人也来到，说，有信息报给我主我王。耶和华今日向一切兴起攻击你的人给你报仇了。

chapters.en: The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom safe?” The Cushite replied, “May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up to harm you be like that young man.”
chapters.zh: 王问古示人说，少年人押沙龙平安不平安。古示人回答说，愿我主我王的仇敌，和一切兴起要杀害你的人，都与那少年人一样。

chapters.en: The king was shaken. He went up to the room over the gateway and wept. As he went, he said: “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you—O Absalom, my son, my son!”
chapters.zh: 王就心里伤恸，上城门楼去哀哭，一面走一面说，我儿押沙龙阿。我儿，我儿押沙龙阿。我恨不得替你死，押沙龙阿，我儿。我儿。

chapters.en: Joab was told, “The king is weeping and mourning for Absalom.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉约押说，王为押沙龙哭泣悲哀。

chapters.en: And for the whole army the victory that day was turned into mourning, because on that day the troops heard it said, “The king is grieving for his son.”
chapters.zh: 众民听说王为他儿子忧愁，他们得胜的欢乐却变成悲哀。

chapters.en: The men stole into the city that day as men steal in who are ashamed when they flee from battle.
chapters.zh: 那日众民暗暗地进城，就如败阵逃跑，惭愧的民一般。

chapters.en: The king covered his face and cried aloud, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”
chapters.zh: 王蒙着脸，大声哭号说，我儿押沙龙阿。押沙龙，我儿，我儿阿。

chapters.en: Then Joab went into the house to the king and said, “Today you have humiliated all your men, who have just saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters and the lives of your wives and concubines.
chapters.zh: 约押进去见王，说，你今日使你一切仆人脸面惭愧了。他们今日救了你的性命和你儿女妻妾的性命，

chapters.en: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it clear today that the commanders and their men mean nothing to you. I see that you would be pleased if Absalom were alive today and all of us were dead.
chapters.zh: 你却爱那恨你的人，恨那爱你的人。你今日明明地不以将帅，仆人为念。我今日看明，若押沙龙活着，我们都死亡，你就喜悦了。

chapters.en: Now go out and encourage your men. I swear by the LORD that if you don’t go out, not a man will be left with you by nightfall. This will be worse for you than all the calamities that have come on you from your youth till now.”
chapters.zh: 现在你当出去，安慰你仆人的心。我指着耶和华起誓，你若不出去，今夜必无一人与你同在一处。这祸患就比你从幼年到如今所遭的更甚。

chapters.en: So the king got up and took his seat in the gateway. When the men were told, “The king is sitting in the gateway,” they all came before him. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled to their homes.
chapters.zh: 于是王起来，坐在城门口。众民听说王坐在城门口，就都到王面前。以色列人已经逃跑，各回各家去了。

chapters.en: Throughout the tribes of Israel, all the people were arguing among themselves, saying, “The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies; he is the one who rescued us from the hand of the Philistines. But now he has fled the country to escape from Absalom;
chapters.zh: 以色列众支派的人纷纷议论说，王曾救我们脱离仇敌的手，又救我们脱离非利士人的手，现在他躲避押沙龙逃走了。

chapters.en: and Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?”
chapters.zh: 我们膏押沙龙治理我们，他已经阵亡。现在为什么不出一言请王回来呢？

chapters.en: King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Ask the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his palace, since what is being said throughout Israel has reached the king at his quarters?
chapters.zh: 大卫王差人去见祭司撒督和亚比亚他，说，你们当向犹大长老说，以色列众人已经有话请王回宫，你们为什么落在他们后头呢？

chapters.en: You are my relatives, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to bring back the king?’
chapters.zh: 你们是我的弟兄，是我的骨肉，为什么在人后头请王回来呢？

chapters.en: And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my own flesh and blood? May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if you are not the commander of my army for life in place of Joab.’ ”
chapters.zh: 也要对亚玛撒说，你不是我的骨肉吗？我若不立你替约押常作元帅，愿神重重地降罚与我。

chapters.en: He won over the hearts of the men of Judah so that they were all of one mind. They sent word to the king, “Return, you and all your men.”
chapters.zh: 如此就挽回犹大众人的心，如同一人的心。他们便打发人去见王，说，请王和王的一切臣仆回来。

chapters.en: Then the king returned and went as far as the Jordan. Now the men of Judah had come to Gilgal to go out and meet the king and bring him across the Jordan.
chapters.zh: 王就回来，到了约旦河。犹大人来到吉甲，要去迎接王，请他过约旦河。

chapters.en: Shimei son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
chapters.zh: 巴户琳的便雅悯人，基拉的儿子示每急忙与犹大人一同下去迎接大卫王。

chapters.en: With him were a thousand Benjamites, along with Ziba, the steward of Saul’s household, and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed to the Jordan, where the king was.
chapters.zh: 跟从示每的有一千便雅悯人，还有扫罗家的仆人洗巴和他十五个儿子，二十个仆人。他们都趟过约旦河迎接王。

chapters.en: They crossed at the ford to take the king’s household over and to do whatever he wished. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell prostrate before the king
chapters.zh: 有摆渡船过去，渡王的家眷，任王使用。王要过约旦河的时候，基拉的儿子示每就俯伏在王面前，

chapters.en: and said to him, “May my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember how your servant did wrong on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king put it out of his mind.
chapters.zh: 对王说，我主我王出耶路撒冷的时候，仆人行悖逆的事，现在求我主不要因此加罪与仆人，不要记念，也不要放在心上。

chapters.en: For I your servant know that I have sinned, but today I have come here as the first from the tribes of Joseph to come down and meet my lord the king.”
chapters.zh: 仆人明知自己有罪，所以约瑟全家之中，今日我首先下来迎接我主我王。

chapters.en: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed the LORD’s anointed.”
chapters.zh: 洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛说，示每既咒骂耶和华的受膏者，不应当治死他吗？

chapters.en: David replied, “What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? What right do you have to interfere? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? Don’t I know that today I am king over Israel?”
chapters.zh: 大卫说，洗鲁雅的儿子，我与你们有何关涉，使你们今日与我反对呢？今日在以色列中岂可治死人呢？我岂不知今日我作以色列的王吗？

chapters.en: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king promised him on oath.
chapters.zh: 于是王对示每说，你必不死。王就向他起誓。

chapters.en: Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, also went down to meet the king. He had not taken care of his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的孙子米非波设也下去迎接王。他自从王去的日子，直到王平平安安地回来，没有修脚，没有剃胡须，也没有洗衣服。

chapters.en: When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, “Why didn’t you go with me, Mephibosheth?”
chapters.zh: 他来到耶路撒冷迎接王的时候，王问他说，米非波设，你为什么没有与我同去呢？

chapters.en: He said, “My lord the king, since I your servant am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled and will ride on it, so I can go with the king.’ But Ziba my servant betrayed me.
chapters.zh: 他回答说，我主我王，仆人是瘸腿的。那日我想要备驴骑上，与王同去，无奈我的仆人欺哄了我，

chapters.en: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. My lord the king is like an angel of God; so do whatever you wish.
chapters.zh: 又在我主我王面前谗毁我。然而我主我王如同神的使者一般，你看怎样好，就怎样行吧。

chapters.en: All my grandfather’s descendants deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, but you gave your servant a place among those who eat at your table. So what right do I have to make any more appeals to the king?”
chapters.zh: 因为我祖全家的人，在我主我王面前都算为死人，王却使仆人在王的席上同人吃饭，我现在向王还能辨理诉冤吗？

chapters.en: The king said to him, “Why say more? I order you and Ziba to divide the land.”
chapters.zh: 王对他说，你何必再提你的事呢？我说，你与洗巴均分地土。

chapters.en: Mephibosheth said to the king, “Let him take everything, now that my lord the king has returned home safely.”
chapters.zh: 米非波设对王说，我主我王既平平安安地回宫，就任凭洗巴都取了也可以。

chapters.en: Barzillai the Gileadite also came down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and to send him on his way from there.
chapters.zh: 基列人巴西莱从罗基琳下来，要送王过约旦河，就与王一同过了约旦河。

chapters.en: Now Barzillai was very old, eighty years of age. He had provided for the king during his stay in Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.
chapters.zh: 巴西莱年纪老迈，已经八十岁了。王住在玛哈念的时候，他就拿食物来供给王。他原是大富户。

chapters.en: The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me and stay with me in Jerusalem, and I will provide for you.”
chapters.zh: 王对巴西莱说，你与我同去，我要在耶路撒冷那里养你的老。

chapters.en: But Barzillai answered the king, “How many more years will I live, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?
chapters.zh: 巴西莱对王说，我在世的年日还能有多少，使我与王同上耶路撒冷呢？

chapters.en: I am now eighty years old. Can I tell the difference between what is enjoyable and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats and drinks? Can I still hear the voices of male and female singers? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
chapters.zh: 仆人现在八十岁了，还能尝出饮食的滋味，辨别美恶吗？还能听男女歌唱的声音吗？仆人何必累赘我主我王呢？

chapters.en: Your servant will cross over the Jordan with the king for a short distance, but why should the king reward me in this way?
chapters.zh: 仆人只要送王过约旦河，王何必赐我这样的恩典呢？

chapters.en: Let your servant return, that I may die in my own town near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever you wish.”
chapters.zh: 求你准我回去，好死在我本城，葬在我父母的墓旁。这里有王的仆人金罕，让他同我主我王过去，可以随意待他。

chapters.en: The king said, “Kimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him whatever you wish. And anything you desire from me I will do for you.”
chapters.zh: 王说，金罕可以与我同去，我必照你的心愿待他。你向我求什么，我都必为你成就。

chapters.en: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and bid him farewell, and Barzillai returned to his home.
chapters.zh: 于是众民过约旦河，王也过去。王与巴西莱亲嘴，为他祝福，巴西莱就回本地去了。

chapters.en: When the king crossed over to Gilgal, Kimham crossed with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel had taken the king over.
chapters.zh: 王过去，到了吉甲，金罕也跟他过去。犹大众民和以色列民的一半也都送王过去。

chapters.en: Soon all the men of Israel were coming to the king and saying to him, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal the king away and bring him and his household across the Jordan, together with all his men?”
chapters.zh: 以色列众人来见王，对他说，我们弟兄犹大人为什么暗暗送王和王的家眷，并跟随王的人过约旦河。

chapters.en: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is closely related to us. Why are you angry about it? Have we eaten any of the king’s provisions? Have we taken anything for ourselves?”
chapters.zh: 犹大众人回答以色列人说，因为王与我们是亲属，你们为何因这事发怒呢？我们吃了王的什么呢？王赏赐了我们什么呢？

chapters.en: Then the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, “We have ten shares in the king; so we have a greater claim on David than you have. Why then do you treat us with contempt? Weren’t we the first to speak of bringing back our king?” But the men of Judah pressed their claims even more forcefully than the men of Israel.
chapters.zh: 以色列人回答犹大人说，按支派，我们与王有十分的情分。在大卫身上，我们也比你们更有情分。你们为何藐视我们，请王回来不先与我们商量呢？但犹大人的话比以色列人的话更硬。

chapters.en: Now a troublemaker named Sheba son of Bikri, a Benjamite, happened to be there. He sounded the trumpet and shouted, “We have no share in David, no part in Jesse’s son! Every man to his tent, Israel!”
chapters.zh: 在那里恰巧有一个匪徒，名叫示巴，是便雅悯人比基利的儿子。他吹角，说，我们与大卫无分，与耶西的儿子无涉。以色列人哪，你们各回各家去吧。

chapters.en: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bikri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 于是以色列人都离开大卫，跟随比基利的儿子示巴。但犹大人从约旦河直到耶路撒冷，都紧紧跟随他们的王。

chapters.en: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to take care of the palace and put them in a house under guard. He provided for them but had no sexual relations with them. They were kept in confinement till the day of their death, living as widows.
chapters.zh: 大卫王来到耶路撒冷，进了宫殿，就把从前留下看守宫殿的十个妃嫔禁闭在冷宫，养活她们，不与她们亲近。她们如同寡妇被禁，直到死的日子。

chapters.en: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”
chapters.zh: 王对亚玛撒说，你要在三日之内将犹大人招聚了来，你也回到这里来。

chapters.en: But when Amasa went to summon Judah, he took longer than the time the king had set for him.
chapters.zh: 亚玛撒就去招聚犹大人，却耽延过了王所限的日期。

chapters.en: David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba son of Bikri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your master’s men and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and escape from us.”
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚比筛说，现在恐怕比基利的儿子示巴加害于我们比押沙龙更甚。你要带领你主的仆人追赶他，免得他得了坚固城，躲避我们。

chapters.en: So Joab’s men and the Kerethites and Pelethites and all the mighty warriors went out under the command of Abishai. They marched out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bikri.
chapters.zh: 约押的人和基利提人，比利提人，并所有的勇士，都跟着亚比筛，从耶路撒冷出去追赶比基利的儿子示巴。

chapters.en: While they were at the great rock in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his military tunic, and strapped over it at his waist was a belt with a dagger in its sheath. As he stepped forward, it dropped out of its sheath.
chapters.zh: 他们到了基遍的大磐石那里，亚玛撒来迎接他们。那时约押穿着战衣，腰束佩刀的带子，刀在鞘内。约押前行，刀从鞘内掉出来。

chapters.en: Joab said to Amasa, “How are you, my brother?” Then Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.
chapters.zh: 约押左手拾起刀来，对亚玛撒说，我兄弟，你好阿。就用右手抓住亚玛撒的胡子，要与他亲嘴。

chapters.en: Amasa was not on his guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab plunged it into his belly, and his intestines spilled out on the ground. Without being stabbed again, Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bikri.
chapters.zh: 亚玛撒没有防备约押手里所拿的刀。约押用刀刺入他的肚腹，他的肠子流在地上，没有再刺他，就死了。约押和他兄弟亚比筛往前追赶比基利的儿子示巴。

chapters.en: One of Joab’s men stood beside Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”
chapters.zh: 有约押的一个少年人站在亚玛撒尸身旁边，对众人说，谁喜悦约押，谁归顺大卫，就当跟随约押去。

chapters.en: Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road, and the man saw that all the troops came to a halt there. When he realized that everyone who came up to Amasa stopped, he dragged him from the road into a field and threw a garment over him.
chapters.zh: 亚玛撒在道路上滚在自己的血里。那人见众民经过都站住，就把亚玛撒的尸身从路上挪到田间，用衣服遮盖。

chapters.en: After Amasa had been removed from the road, everyone went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bikri.
chapters.zh: 尸身从路上挪移之后，众民就都跟随约押去追赶比基利的儿子示巴。

chapters.en: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel Beth Maakah and through the entire region of the Bikrites, who gathered together and followed him.
chapters.zh: 他走遍以色列各支派，直到伯玛迦的亚比拉，并比利人的全地。那些地方的人也都聚集跟随他。

chapters.en: All the troops with Joab came and besieged Sheba in Abel Beth Maakah. They built a siege ramp up to the city, and it stood against the outer fortifications. While they were battering the wall to bring it down,
chapters.zh: 约押和跟随的人到了伯玛迦的亚比拉，围困示巴，就对着城筑垒。跟随约押的众民用锤撞城，要使城塌陷。

chapters.en: a wise woman called from the city, “Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I can speak to him.”
chapters.zh: 有一个聪明妇人从城上呼叫说，听阿，听阿，请约押近前来，我好与他说话。

chapters.en: He went toward her, and she asked, “Are you Joab?” “I am,” he answered. She said, “Listen to what your servant has to say.” “I’m listening,” he said.
chapters.zh: 约押就近前来，妇人问他说，你是约押不是。他说，我是。妇人说，求你听婢女的话。约押说，我听。

chapters.en: She continued, “Long ago they used to say, ‘Get your answer at Abel,’ and that settled it.
chapters.zh: 妇人说，古时有话说，当先在亚比拉求问，然后事就定妥。

chapters.en: We are the peaceful and faithful in Israel. You are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why do you want to swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”
chapters.zh: 我们这城的人在以色列人中是和平，忠厚的。你为何要毁坏以色列中的大城，吞灭耶和华的产业呢？

chapters.en: “Far be it from me!” Joab replied, “Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!
chapters.zh: 约押回答说，我决不吞灭毁坏，

chapters.en: That is not the case. A man named Sheba son of Bikri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Hand over this one man, and I’ll withdraw from the city.” The woman said to Joab, “His head will be thrown to you from the wall.”
chapters.zh: 乃因以法莲山地的一个人比基利的儿子示巴举手攻击大卫王，你们若将他一人交出来，我便离城而去。妇人对约押说，那人的首级必从城墙上丢给你。

chapters.en: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise advice, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bikri and threw it to Joab. So he sounded the trumpet, and his men dispersed from the city, each returning to his home. And Joab went back to the king in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 妇人就凭她的智慧去劝众人。他们便割下比基利的儿子示巴的首级，丢给约押。约押吹角，众人就离城而散，各归各家去了。约押回耶路撒冷，到王那里。

chapters.en: Joab was over Israel’s entire army; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites;
chapters.zh: 约押作以色列全军的元帅。耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅统辖基利提人和比利提人。

chapters.en: Adoniram was in charge of forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
chapters.zh: 亚多兰掌管服苦的人。亚希律的儿子约沙法作史官。

chapters.en: Sheva was secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
chapters.zh: 示法作书记。撒督和亚比亚他作祭司长。

chapters.en: and Ira the Jairite was David’s priest.
chapters.zh: 睚珥人以拉作大卫的宰相。

chapters.en: During the reign of David, there was a famine for three successive years; so David sought the face of the LORD. The LORD said, “It is on account of Saul and his blood-stained house; it is because he put the Gibeonites to death.”
chapters.zh: 大卫年间有饥荒，一连三年，大卫就求问耶和华。耶和华说，这饥荒是因扫罗和他流人血之家杀死基遍人。

chapters.en: The king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not a part of Israel but were survivors of the Amorites; the Israelites had sworn to spare them, but Saul in his zeal for Israel and Judah had tried to annihilate them.)
chapters.zh: 原来这基遍人不是以色列人，乃是亚摩利人中所剩的。以色列人曾向他们起誓，不杀灭他们，扫罗却为以色列人和犹大人发热心，想要杀灭他们。大卫王召了他们来，

chapters.en: David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How shall I make atonement so that you will bless the LORD’s inheritance?”
chapters.zh: 问他们说，我当为你们怎样行呢？可用什么赎这罪，使你们为耶和华的产业祝福呢？

chapters.en: The Gibeonites answered him, “We have no right to demand silver or gold from Saul or his family, nor do we have the right to put anyone in Israel to death.” “What do you want me to do for you?” David asked.
chapters.zh: 基遍人回答说，我们和扫罗与他家的事并不关乎金银，也不要因我们的缘故杀一个以色列人。大卫说，你们怎样说，我就为你们怎样行。

chapters.en: They answered the king, “As for the man who destroyed us and plotted against us so that we have been decimated and have no place anywhere in Israel,
chapters.zh: 他们对王说，那从前谋害我们，要灭我们，使我们不得再住以色列境内的人，

chapters.en: let seven of his male descendants be given to us to be killed and their bodies exposed before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul—the LORD’s chosen one.” So the king said, “I will give them to you.”
chapters.zh: 现在愿将他的子孙七人交给我们，我们好在耶和华面前，将他们悬挂在耶和华拣选扫罗的基比亚。王说，我必交给你们。

chapters.en: The king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
chapters.zh: 王因为曾与扫罗的儿子约拿单指着耶和华起誓结盟，就爱惜扫罗的孙子，约拿单的儿子米非波设，不交出来。

chapters.en: But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons of Aiah’s daughter Rizpah, whom she had borne to Saul, together with the five sons of Saul’s daughter Merab, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
chapters.zh: 却把爱雅的女儿利斯巴给扫罗所生的两个儿子亚摩尼，米非波设，和扫罗女儿米甲的姐姐给米何拉人巴西莱儿子亚得列所生的五个儿子

chapters.en: He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who killed them and exposed their bodies on a hill before the LORD. All seven of them fell together; they were put to death during the first days of the harvest, just as the barley harvest was beginning.
chapters.zh: 交在基遍人的手里。基遍人就把他们，在耶和华面前，悬挂在山上，这七人就一同死亡。被杀的时候正是收割的日子，就是动手割大麦的时候。

chapters.en: Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest till the rain poured down from the heavens on the bodies, she did not let the birds touch them by day or the wild animals by night.
chapters.zh: 爱雅的女儿利斯巴用麻布在磐石上搭棚，从动手收割的时候直到天降雨在尸身上的时候，日间不容空中的雀鸟落在尸身上，夜间不让田野的走兽前来糟践。

chapters.en: When David was told what Aiah’s daughter Rizpah, Saul’s concubine, had done,
chapters.zh: 有人将扫罗的妃嫔爱雅女儿利斯巴所行的这事告诉大卫。

chapters.en: he went and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead. (They had stolen their bodies from the public square at Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hung them after they struck Saul down on Gilboa.)
chapters.zh: 大卫就去，从基列雅比人那里将扫罗和他儿子约拿单的骸骨搬了来。是因非利士人从前在基利波杀扫罗，将尸身悬挂在伯珊的街市上，基列雅比人把尸身偷了去。

chapters.en: David brought the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from there, and the bones of those who had been killed and exposed were gathered up.
chapters.zh: 大卫将扫罗和他儿子约拿单的骸骨从那里搬了来，又收殓被悬挂七人的骸骨，

chapters.en: They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish, at Zela in Benjamin, and did everything the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer in behalf of the land.
chapters.zh: 将扫罗和他儿子约拿单的骸骨葬在便雅悯的洗拉，在扫罗父亲基士的坟墓里。众人行了王所吩咐的。此后神垂听国民所求的。

chapters.en: Once again there was a battle between the Philistines and Israel. David went down with his men to fight against the Philistines, and he became exhausted.
chapters.zh: 非利士人与以色列人打仗。大卫带领仆人下去，与非利士人接战，大卫就疲乏了。

chapters.en: And Ishbi-Benob, one of the descendants of Rapha, whose bronze spearhead weighed three hundred shekels and who was armed with a new sword, said he would kill David.
chapters.zh: 伟人的一个儿子以实比诺要杀大卫。他的铜枪重三百舍客勒，又佩着新刀。

chapters.en: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to David’s rescue; he struck the Philistine down and killed him. Then David’s men swore to him, saying, “Never again will you go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel will not be extinguished.”
chapters.zh: 但洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛帮助大卫，攻打非利士人，将他杀死。当日，跟随大卫的人向大卫起誓说，以后你不可再与我们一同出战，恐怕熄灭以色列的灯。

chapters.en: In the course of time, there was another battle with the Philistines, at Gob. At that time Sibbekai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the descendants of Rapha.
chapters.zh: 后来，以色列人在歌伯与非利士人打仗，户沙人西比该杀了伟人的一个儿子撒弗。

chapters.en: In another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, who had a spear with a shaft like a weaver’s rod.
chapters.zh: 又在歌伯与非利士人打仗，伯利恒人雅雷俄珥金的儿子伊勒哈难杀了迦特人歌利亚。这人的枪杆粗如织布的机轴。

chapters.en: In still another battle, which took place at Gath, there was a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He also was descended from Rapha.
chapters.zh: 又在迦特打仗，那里有一个身量高大的人，手脚都是六指，共有二十四个指头。他也是伟人的儿子。

chapters.en: When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimeah, David’s brother, killed him.
chapters.zh: 这人向以色列人骂阵，大卫的哥哥示米亚的儿子约拿单就杀了他。

chapters.en: These four were descendants of Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his men.
chapters.zh: 这四个人是迦特伟人的儿子，都死在大卫和他仆人的手下。

chapters.en: David sang to the LORD the words of this song when the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
chapters.zh: 当耶和华救大卫脱离一切仇敌和扫罗之手的日子，他向耶和华念这诗，

chapters.en: He said: “The LORD is my rock, my fortress and my deliverer;
chapters.zh: 说，耶和华是我的岩石，我的山寨，我的救主，

chapters.en: my God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation. He is my stronghold, my refuge and my savior— from violent people you save me.
chapters.zh: 我的神，我的磐石，我所投靠的。他是我的盾牌，是拯救我的角，是我的高台，是我的避难所。我的救主阿，你是救我脱离强暴的。

chapters.en: “I called to the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and have been saved from my enemies.
chapters.zh: 我要求告当赞美的耶和华，这样，我必从仇敌手中被救出来。

chapters.en: The waves of death swirled about me; the torrents of destruction overwhelmed me.
chapters.zh: 曾有死亡的波浪环绕我，匪类的急流使我惊惧，

chapters.en: The cords of the grave coiled around me; the snares of death confronted me.
chapters.zh: 阴间的绳索缠绕我，死亡的网罗临到我。

chapters.en: “In my distress I called to the LORD; I called out to my God. From his temple he heard my voice; my cry came to his ears.
chapters.zh: 我在急难中求告耶和华，向我的神呼求。他从殿中听了我的声音。我的呼求入了他的耳中。

chapters.en: The earth trembled and quaked, the foundations of the heavens shook; they trembled because he was angry.
chapters.zh: 那时因他发怒，地就摇撼战抖。天的根基也震动摇撼。

chapters.en: Smoke rose from his nostrils; consuming fire came from his mouth, burning coals blazed out of it.
chapters.zh: 从他鼻孔冒烟上腾。从他口中发火焚烧，连炭也着了。

chapters.en: He parted the heavens and came down; dark clouds were under his feet.
chapters.zh: 他又使天下垂，亲自降临。有黑云在他脚下。

chapters.en: He mounted the cherubim and flew; he soared on the wings of the wind.
chapters.zh: 他坐着基路伯飞行，在风的翅膀上显现。

chapters.en: He made darkness his canopy around him— the dark rain clouds of the sky.
chapters.zh: 他以黑暗和聚集的水，天空的厚云为他四围的行宫。

chapters.en: Out of the brightness of his presence bolts of lightning blazed forth.
chapters.zh: 因他面前的光辉炭都着了。

chapters.en: The LORD thundered from heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded.
chapters.zh: 耶和华从天上打雷。至高者发出声音。

chapters.en: He shot his arrows and scattered the enemy, with great bolts of lightning he routed them.
chapters.zh: 他射出箭来，使仇敌四散，发出闪电，使他们扰乱。

chapters.en: The valleys of the sea were exposed and the foundations of the earth laid bare at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of breath from his nostrils.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的斥责一发，鼻孔的气一出，海底就出现，大地的根基也显露。

chapters.en: “He reached down from on high and took hold of me; he drew me out of deep waters.
chapters.zh: 他从高天伸手抓住我，把我从大水中拉上来。

chapters.en: He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from my foes, who were too strong for me.
chapters.zh: 他救我脱离我的劲敌和那些恨我的人，因为他们比我强盛。

chapters.en: They confronted me in the day of my disaster, but the LORD was my support.
chapters.zh: 我遭遇灾难的日子，他们来攻击我。但耶和华是我的倚靠。

chapters.en: He brought me out into a spacious place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.
chapters.zh: 他又领我到宽阔之处。他救拔我，因他喜悦我。

chapters.en: “The LORD has dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he has rewarded me.
chapters.zh: 耶和华按着我的公义报答我，按着我手中的清洁赏赐我。

chapters.en: For I have kept the ways of the LORD; I am not guilty of turning from my God.
chapters.zh: 因为我遵守了耶和华的道，未曾作恶离开我的神。

chapters.en: All his laws are before me; I have not turned away from his decrees.
chapters.zh: 他的一切典章常在我面前。他的律例，我也未曾离弃。

chapters.en: I have been blameless before him and have kept myself from sin.
chapters.zh: 我在他面前作了完全人。我也保守自己远离我的罪孽。

chapters.en: The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in his sight.
chapters.zh: 所以耶和华按我的公义，按我在他眼前的清洁赏赐我。

chapters.en: “To the faithful you show yourself faithful, to the blameless you show yourself blameless,
chapters.zh: 慈爱的人，你以慈爱待他。完全的人，你以完全待他。

chapters.en: to the pure you show yourself pure, but to the devious you show yourself shrewd.
chapters.zh: 清洁的人，你以清洁待他。乖僻的人，你以弯曲待他。

chapters.en: You save the humble, but your eyes are on the haughty to bring them low.
chapters.zh: 困苦的百姓，你必拯救。但你的眼目察看高傲的人，使他降卑。

chapters.en: You, LORD, are my lamp; the LORD turns my darkness into light.
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，你是我的灯。耶和华必照明我的黑暗。

chapters.en: With your help I can advance against a troop ; with my God I can scale a wall.
chapters.zh: 我借着你冲入敌军，借着我的神跳过墙垣。

chapters.en: “As for God, his way is perfect: The LORD’s word is flawless; he shields all who take refuge in him.
chapters.zh: 至于神，他的道是完全的。耶和华的话是炼净的。凡投靠他的，他便作他们的盾牌。

chapters.en: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God?
chapters.zh: 除了耶和华，谁是神呢？除了我们的神，谁是磐石呢？

chapters.en: It is God who arms me with strength and keeps my way secure.
chapters.zh: 神是我坚固的保障。他引导完全人行他的路。

chapters.en: He makes my feet like the feet of a deer; he causes me to stand on the heights.
chapters.zh: 他使我的脚快如母鹿的蹄，又使我在高处安稳。

chapters.en: He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
chapters.zh: 他教导我的手能以争战，甚至我的膀臂能开铜弓。

chapters.en: You make your saving help my shield; your help has made me great.
chapters.zh: 你把你的救恩给我作盾牌。你的温和使我为大。

chapters.en: You provide a broad path for my feet, so that my ankles do not give way.
chapters.zh: 你使我脚下的地步宽阔。我的脚未曾滑跌。

chapters.en: “I pursued my enemies and crushed them; I did not turn back till they were destroyed.
chapters.zh: 我追赶我的仇敌，灭绝了他们，未灭以先，我没有归回。

chapters.en: I crushed them completely, and they could not rise; they fell beneath my feet.
chapters.zh: 我灭绝了他们，打伤了他们，使他们不能起来。他们都倒在我的脚下。

chapters.en: You armed me with strength for battle; you humbled my adversaries before me.
chapters.zh: 因为你曾以力量束我的腰，使我能争战。你也使那起来攻击我的都服在我以下。

chapters.en: You made my enemies turn their backs in flight, and I destroyed my foes.
chapters.zh: 你又使我的仇敌在我面前转背逃跑，叫我能以剪除那恨我的人。

chapters.en: They cried for help, but there was no one to save them— to the LORD, but he did not answer.
chapters.zh: 他们仰望，却无人拯救。就是呼求耶和华，他也不应允。

chapters.en: I beat them as fine as the dust of the earth; I pounded and trampled them like mud in the streets.
chapters.zh: 我捣碎他们，如同地上的灰尘，践踏他们，四散在地，如同街上的泥土。

chapters.en: “You have delivered me from the attacks of the peoples; you have preserved me as the head of nations. People I did not know now serve me,
chapters.zh: 你救我脱离我百姓的争竞，保护我作列国的元首。我素不认识的民必事奉我。

chapters.en: foreigners cower before me; as soon as they hear of me, they obey me.
chapters.zh: 外邦人要投降我，一听见我的名声就必顺从我。

chapters.en: They all lose heart; they come trembling from their strongholds.
chapters.zh: 外邦人要衰残，战战兢兢地出他们的营寨。

chapters.en: “The LORD lives! Praise be to my Rock! Exalted be my God, the Rock, my Savior!
chapters.zh: 耶和华是活神，愿我的磐石被人称颂。愿神那拯救我的磐石被人尊崇。

chapters.en: He is the God who avenges me, who puts the nations under me,
chapters.zh: 这位神就是那为我伸冤，使众民服在我以下的。

chapters.en: who sets me free from my enemies. You exalted me above my foes; from a violent man you rescued me.
chapters.zh: 你救我脱离仇敌，又把我举起，高过那些起来攻击我的。你救我脱离强暴的人。

chapters.en: Therefore I will praise you, LORD, among the nations; I will sing the praises of your name.
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，因此我要在外邦中称谢你，歌颂你的名。

chapters.en: “He gives his king great victories; he shows unfailing kindness to his anointed, to David and his descendants forever.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华赐极大的救恩给他所立的王，施慈爱给他的受膏者，就是给大卫和他的后裔，直到永远。

chapters.en: These are the last words of David: “The inspired utterance of David son of Jesse, the utterance of the man exalted by the Most High, the man anointed by the God of Jacob, the hero of Israel’s songs:
chapters.zh: 以下是大卫末了的话。耶西的儿子大卫得居高位，是雅各神所膏的，作以色列的美歌者，说，

chapters.en: “The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; his word was on my tongue.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵借着我说，他的话在我口中。

chapters.en: The God of Israel spoke, the Rock of Israel said to me: ‘When one rules over people in righteousness, when he rules in the fear of God,
chapters.zh: 以色列的神，以色列的磐石晓谕我说，那以公义治理人民的，敬畏神执掌权柄，

chapters.en: he is like the light of morning at sunrise on a cloudless morning, like the brightness after rain that brings grass from the earth.’
chapters.zh: 他必像日出的晨光，如无云的清晨，雨后的晴光，使地发生嫩草。

chapters.en: “If my house were not right with God, surely he would not have made with me an everlasting covenant, arranged and secured in every part; surely he would not bring to fruition my salvation and grant me my every desire.
chapters.zh: 我家在神面前并非如此。神却与我立永远的约。这约凡事坚稳，关乎我的一切救恩和我一切所想望的，他岂不为我成就吗？

chapters.en: But evil men are all to be cast aside like thorns, which are not gathered with the hand.
chapters.zh: 但匪类都必像荆棘被丢弃。人不敢用手拿它。

chapters.en: Whoever touches thorns uses a tool of iron or the shaft of a spear; they are burned up where they lie.”
chapters.zh: 拿它的人必带铁器和枪杆，终久它必被火焚烧。

chapters.en: These are the names of David’s mighty warriors: Josheb-Basshebeth, a Tahkemonite, was chief of the Three; he raised his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed in one encounter.
chapters.zh: 大卫勇士的名字记在下面，他革扪人约设巴设，又称伊斯尼人亚底挪，他是军长的统领，一时击杀了八百人。

chapters.en: Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodai the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty warriors, he was with David when they taunted the Philistines gathered at Pas Dammim for battle. Then the Israelites retreated,
chapters.zh: 其次是亚合人朵多的儿子以利亚撒。从前非利士人聚集要打仗，以色列人迎着上去，有跟随大卫的三个勇士向非利士人骂阵，其中有以利亚撒。

chapters.en: but Eleazar stood his ground and struck down the Philistines till his hand grew tired and froze to the sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. The troops returned to Eleazar, but only to strip the dead.
chapters.zh: 他起来击杀非利士人，直到手臂疲乏，手粘住刀把。那日耶和华使以色列人大获全胜。众民在以利亚撒后头专夺财物。

chapters.en: Next to him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines banded together at a place where there was a field full of lentils, Israel’s troops fled from them.
chapters.zh: 其次是哈拉人亚基的儿子沙玛。一日，非利士人聚集成群，在一块长满红豆的田里，众民就在非利士人面前逃跑。

chapters.en: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field. He defended it and struck the Philistines down, and the LORD brought about a great victory.
chapters.zh: 沙玛却站在那田间击杀非利士人，救护了那田。耶和华使以色列人大获全胜。

chapters.en: During harvest time, three of the thirty chief warriors came down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
chapters.zh: 收割的时候，有三十个勇士中的三个人下到亚杜兰洞见大卫。非利士的军兵在利乏音谷安营。

chapters.en: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was at Bethlehem.
chapters.zh: 那时大卫在山寨，非利士人的防营在伯利恒。

chapters.en: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”
chapters.zh: 大卫渴想，说，甚愿有人将伯利恒城门旁，井里的水打来给我喝。

chapters.en: So the three mighty warriors broke through the Philistine lines, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem and carried it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这三个勇士就闯过非利士人的营盘，从伯利恒城门旁的井里打水，拿来奉给大卫。他却不肯喝，将水奠在耶和华面前，

chapters.en: “Far be it from me, LORD, to do this!” he said. “Is it not the blood of men who went at the risk of their lives?” And David would not drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty warriors.
chapters.zh: 说，耶和华阿，这三个人冒死去打水。这水好像他们的血一般，我断不敢喝。如此，大卫不肯喝。这是三个勇士所作的事。

chapters.en: Abishai the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah was chief of the Three. He raised his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed, and so he became as famous as the Three.
chapters.zh: 洗鲁雅的儿子，约押的兄弟亚比筛是这三个勇士的首领。他举枪杀了三百人，就在三个勇士里得了名。

chapters.en: Was he not held in greater honor than the Three? He became their commander, even though he was not included among them.
chapters.zh: 他在这三个勇士里是最尊贵的，所以作他们的首领，只是不及前三个勇士。

chapters.en: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, a valiant fighter from Kabzeel, performed great exploits. He struck down Moab’s two mightiest warriors. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.
chapters.zh: 有甲薛勇士耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅行过大能的事。他杀了摩押人亚利伊勒的两个儿子，又在下雪的时候下坑里去，杀了一个狮子，

chapters.en: And he struck down a huge Egyptian. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club. He snatched the spear from the Egyptian’s hand and killed him with his own spear.
chapters.zh: 又杀了一个强壮的埃及人。埃及人手里拿着枪，比拿雅只拿着棍子下去，从埃及人手里夺过枪来，用那枪将他杀死。

chapters.en: Such were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada; he too was as famous as the three mighty warriors.
chapters.zh: 这是耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅所行的事，就在三个勇士里得了名。

chapters.en: He was held in greater honor than any of the Thirty, but he was not included among the Three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
chapters.zh: 他比那三十个勇士都尊贵，只是不及前三个勇士。大卫立他作护卫长。

chapters.en: Among the Thirty were: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,
chapters.zh: 三十个勇士里有约押的兄弟亚撒黑，伯利恒人朵多的儿子伊勒哈难，

chapters.en: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
chapters.zh: 哈律人沙玛，哈律人以利加，

chapters.en: Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa,
chapters.zh: 帕勒提人希利斯，提哥亚人益吉的儿子以拉，

chapters.en: Abiezer from Anathoth, Sibbekai the Hushathite,
chapters.zh: 亚拿突人亚比以谢，户沙人米本乃，

chapters.en: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
chapters.zh: 亚合人撒们，尼陀法人玛哈莱，

chapters.en: Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin,
chapters.zh: 尼陀法人巴拿的儿子希立，便雅悯族，基比亚人利拜的儿子以太，

chapters.en: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the ravines of Gaash,
chapters.zh: 比拉顿人比拿雅，迦实溪人希太，

chapters.en: Abi-Albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
chapters.zh: 伯亚拉巴人亚比亚本，巴鲁米人押斯玛弗，

chapters.en: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan
chapters.zh: 沙本人以利雅哈巴，雅善儿子中的约拿单，

chapters.en: son of Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
chapters.zh: 哈拉人沙玛，哈拉人沙拉的儿子亚希暗，

chapters.en: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maakathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
chapters.zh: 玛迦人亚哈拜的儿子以利法列，基罗人亚希多弗的儿子以连，

chapters.en: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
chapters.zh: 迦密人希斯莱，亚巴人帕莱，

chapters.en: Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, the son of Hagri,
chapters.zh: 琐巴人拿单的儿子以甲，迦得人巴尼，

chapters.en: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
chapters.zh: 亚扪人洗勒，比录人拿哈莱，是给洗鲁雅的儿子约押拿兵器的，

chapters.en: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite
chapters.zh: 以帖人以拉，以帖人迦立，

chapters.en: and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.
chapters.zh: 赫人乌利亚，共有三十七人。

chapters.en: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华又向以色列人发怒，就激动大卫，使他吩咐人去数点以色列人和犹大人。

chapters.en: So the king said to Joab and the army commanders with him, “Go throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and enroll the fighting men, so that I may know how many there are.”
chapters.zh: 大卫就吩咐跟随他的元帅约押说，你去走遍以色列众支派，从但直到别是巴，数点百姓，我好知道他们的数目。

chapters.en: But Joab replied to the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?”
chapters.zh: 约押对王说，无论百姓多少，愿耶和华你的神再加增百倍，使我主我王亲眼得见。我主我王何必喜悦行这事呢？

chapters.en: The king’s word, however, overruled Joab and the army commanders; so they left the presence of the king to enroll the fighting men of Israel.
chapters.zh: 但王的命令胜过约押和众军长。约押和众军长就从王面前出去，数点以色列的百姓。

chapters.en: After crossing the Jordan, they camped near Aroer, south of the town in the gorge, and then went through Gad and on to Jazer.
chapters.zh: 他们过了约旦河，在迦得谷中，城的右边亚罗珥安营，与雅谢相对，

chapters.en: They went to Gilead and the region of Tahtim Hodshi, and on to Dan Jaan and around toward Sidon.
chapters.zh: 又到了基列和他停合示地，又到了但雅安，绕到西顿，

chapters.en: Then they went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to Beersheba in the Negev of Judah.
chapters.zh: 来到推罗的保障，并希未人和迦南人的各城，又到犹大南方的别是巴。

chapters.en: After they had gone through the entire land, they came back to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
chapters.zh: 他们走遍全地，过了九个月零二十天，就回到耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: Joab reported the number of the fighting men to the king: In Israel there were eight hundred thousand able-bodied men who could handle a sword, and in Judah five hundred thousand.
chapters.zh: 约押将百姓的总数奏告于王，以色列拿刀的勇士有八十万。犹大有五十万。

chapters.en: David was conscience-stricken after he had counted the fighting men, and he said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, LORD, I beg you, take away the guilt of your servant. I have done a very foolish thing.”
chapters.zh: 大卫数点百姓以后，就心中自责，祷告耶和华说，我行这事大有罪了。耶和华阿，求你除掉仆人的罪孽，因我所行的甚是愚昧。

chapters.en: Before David got up the next morning, the word of the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer:
chapters.zh: 大卫早晨起来，耶和华的话临到先知迦得，就是大卫的先见，说，

chapters.en: “Go and tell David, ‘This is what the LORD says: I am giving you three options. Choose one of them for me to carry out against you.’ ”
chapters.zh: 你去告诉大卫，说耶和华如此说，我有三样灾，随你选择一样，我好降与你。

chapters.en: So Gad went to David and said to him, “Shall there come on you three years of famine in your land? Or three months of fleeing from your enemies while they pursue you? Or three days of plague in your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should answer the one who sent me.”
chapters.zh: 于是迦得来见大卫，对他说，你愿意国中有七年的饥荒呢？是在你敌人面前逃跑，被追赶三个月呢？是在你国中有三日的瘟疫呢？现在你要揣摩思想，我好回覆那差我来的。

chapters.en: David said to Gad, “I am in deep distress. Let us fall into the hands of the LORD, for his mercy is great; but do not let me fall into human hands.”
chapters.zh: 大卫对迦得说，我甚为难。我愿落在耶和华的手里，因为他有丰盛的怜悯。我不愿落在人的手里。

chapters.en: So the LORD sent a plague on Israel from that morning until the end of the time designated, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.
chapters.zh: 于是，耶和华降瘟疫与以色列人，自早晨到所定的时候。从但直到别是巴，民间死了七万人。

chapters.en: When the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented concerning the disaster and said to the angel who was afflicting the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand.” The angel of the LORD was then at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
chapters.zh: 天使向耶路撒冷伸手要灭城的时候，耶和华后悔，就不降这灾了，吩咐灭民的天使说，够了，住手吧。那时耶和华的使者在耶布斯人亚劳拿的禾场那里。

chapters.en: When David saw the angel who was striking down the people, he said to the LORD, “I have sinned; I, the shepherd, have done wrong. These are but sheep. What have they done? Let your hand fall on me and my family.”
chapters.zh: 大卫看见灭民的天使，就祷告耶和华说，我犯了罪，行了恶。但这群羊作了什么呢？愿你的手攻击我和我的父家。

chapters.en: On that day Gad went to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
chapters.zh: 当日，迦得来见大卫，对他说，你上去，在耶布斯人亚劳拿的禾场上为耶和华筑一座坛。

chapters.en: So David went up, as the LORD had commanded through Gad.
chapters.zh: 大卫就照着迦得奉耶和华名所说的话上去了。

chapters.en: When Araunah looked and saw the king and his officials coming toward him, he went out and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.
chapters.zh: 亚劳拿观看，见王和他臣仆前来，就迎接出去，脸伏于地，向王下拜，

chapters.en: Araunah said, “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” “To buy your threshing floor,” David answered, “so I can build an altar to the LORD, that the plague on the people may be stopped.”
chapters.zh: 说，我主我王为何来到仆人这里呢？大卫说，我要买你这禾场，为耶和华筑一座坛，使民间的瘟疫止住。

chapters.en: Araunah said to David, “Let my lord the king take whatever he wishes and offer it up. Here are oxen for the burnt offering, and here are threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.
chapters.zh: 亚劳拿对大卫说，我主我王，你喜悦用什么，就拿去献祭。看哪，这里有牛可以作燔祭，有打粮的器具和套牛的轭可以当柴烧。

chapters.en: Your Majesty, Araunah gives all this to the king.” Araunah also said to him, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
chapters.zh: 王阿，这一切，我亚劳拿都奉给你。又对王说，愿耶和华你的神悦纳你。

chapters.en: But the king replied to Araunah, “No, I insist on paying you for it. I will not sacrifice to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen and paid fifty shekels of silver for them.
chapters.zh: 王对亚劳拿说，不然。我必要按着价值向你买。我不肯用白得之物作燔祭献给耶和华我的神。大卫就用五十舍客勒银子买了那禾场与牛。

chapters.en: David built an altar to the LORD there and sacrificed burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Then the LORD answered his prayer in behalf of the land, and the plague on Israel was stopped.
chapters.zh: 大卫在那里为耶和华筑了一座坛，献燔祭和平安祭。如此，耶和华垂听国民所求的，瘟疫在以色列人中就止住了。

chapters.en: When King David was very old, he could not keep warm even when they put covers over him.
chapters.zh: 大卫王年纪老迈，虽用被遮盖，仍不觉暖。

chapters.en: So his attendants said to him, “Let us look for a young virgin to serve the king and take care of him. She can lie beside him so that our lord the king may keep warm.”
chapters.zh: 所以臣仆对他说，不如为我主我王寻找一个处女，使她伺候王，奉养王，睡在王的怀中，好叫我主我王得暖。

chapters.en: Then they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful young woman and found Abishag, a Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
chapters.zh: 于是在以色列全境寻找美貌的童女，寻得书念的一个童女亚比煞，就带到王那里。

chapters.en: The woman was very beautiful; she took care of the king and waited on him, but the king had no sexual relations with her.
chapters.zh: 这童女极其美貌，她奉养王，伺候王，王却没有与她亲近。

chapters.en: Now Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith, put himself forward and said, “I will be king.” So he got chariots and horses ready, with fifty men to run ahead of him.
chapters.zh: 那时，哈及的儿子亚多尼雅自尊，说，我必作王，就为自己预备车辆，马兵，又派五十人在他前头奔走。

chapters.en: (His father had never rebuked him by asking, “Why do you behave as you do?” He was also very handsome and was born next after Absalom.)
chapters.zh: 他父亲素来没有使他忧闷，说，你是作什么呢？他甚俊美，生在押沙龙之后。

chapters.en: Adonijah conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they gave him their support.
chapters.zh: 亚多尼雅与洗鲁雅的儿子约押，和祭司亚比亚他商议。二人就顺从他，帮助他。

chapters.en: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei and Rei and David’s special guard did not join Adonijah.
chapters.zh: 但祭司撒督，耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，先知拿单，示每，利以，并大卫的勇士都不顺从亚多尼雅。

chapters.en: Adonijah then sacrificed sheep, cattle and fattened calves at the Stone of Zoheleth near En Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the royal officials of Judah,
chapters.zh: 一日，亚多尼雅在隐罗结旁，琐希列磐石那里宰了牛羊，肥犊，请他的诸弟兄，就是王的众子，并所有作王臣仆的犹大人。

chapters.en: but he did not invite Nathan the prophet or Benaiah or the special guard or his brother Solomon.
chapters.zh: 惟独先知拿单和比拿雅并勇士，与他的兄弟所罗门，他都没有请。

chapters.en: Then Nathan asked Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, “Have you not heard that Adonijah, the son of Haggith, has become king, and our lord David knows nothing about it?
chapters.zh: 拿单对所罗门的母亲拔示巴说，哈及的儿子亚多尼雅作王了，你没有听见吗？我们的主大卫却不知道。

chapters.en: Now then, let me advise you how you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
chapters.zh: 现在我可以给你出个主意，好保全你和你儿子所罗门的性命。

chapters.en: Go in to King David and say to him, ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to me your servant: “Surely Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’
chapters.zh: 你进去见大卫王，对他说，我主我王阿，你不曾向婢女起誓说，你儿子所罗门必接续我作王，坐在我的位上吗？现在亚多尼雅怎么作了王呢？

chapters.en: While you are still there talking to the king, I will come in and add my word to what you have said.”
chapters.zh: 你还与王说话的时候，我也随后进去，证实你的话。

chapters.en: So Bathsheba went to see the aged king in his room, where Abishag the Shunammite was attending him.
chapters.zh: 拔示巴进入内室见王，王甚老迈，书念的童女亚比煞正伺候王。

chapters.en: Bathsheba bowed down, prostrating herself before the king. “What is it you want?” the king asked.
chapters.zh: 拔示巴向王屈身下拜。王说，你要什么。

chapters.en: She said to him, “My lord, you yourself swore to me your servant by the LORD your God: ‘Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he will sit on my throne.’
chapters.zh: 她说，我主阿，你曾向婢女指着耶和华你的神起誓说，你儿子所罗门必接续我作王，坐在我的位上。

chapters.en: But now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know about it.
chapters.zh: 现在亚多尼雅作王了，我主我王却不知道。

chapters.en: He has sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the king’s sons, Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army, but he has not invited Solomon your servant.
chapters.zh: 他宰了许多牛羊，肥犊，请了王的众子和祭司亚比亚他，并元帅约押。惟独王的仆人所罗门，他没有请。

chapters.en: My lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, to learn from you who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
chapters.zh: 我主我王阿，以色列众人的眼目都仰望你，等你晓谕他们，在我主我王之后谁坐你的位。

chapters.en: Otherwise, as soon as my lord the king is laid to rest with his ancestors, I and my son Solomon will be treated as criminals.”
chapters.zh: 若不然，到我主我王与列祖同睡以后，我和我儿子所罗门必算为罪人了。

chapters.en: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
chapters.zh: 拔示巴还与王说话的时候，先知拿单也进来了。

chapters.en: And the king was told, “Nathan the prophet is here.” So he went before the king and bowed with his face to the ground.
chapters.zh: 有人奏告王说，先知拿单来了。拿单进到王前，脸伏于地。

chapters.en: Nathan said, “Have you, my lord the king, declared that Adonijah shall be king after you, and that he will sit on your throne?
chapters.zh: 拿单说，我主我王果然应许亚多尼雅说你必接续我作王，坐在我的位上吗？

chapters.en: Today he has gone down and sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep. He has invited all the king’s sons, the commanders of the army and Abiathar the priest. Right now they are eating and drinking with him and saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’
chapters.zh: 他今日下去，宰了许多牛羊，肥犊，请了王的众子和军长，并祭司亚比亚他。他们正在亚多尼雅面前吃喝，说，愿亚多尼雅王万岁。

chapters.en: But me your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon he did not invite.
chapters.zh: 惟独我，就是你的仆人和祭司撒督，耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，并王的仆人所罗门，他都没有请。

chapters.en: Is this something my lord the king has done without letting his servants know who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?”
chapters.zh: 这事果然出乎我主我王吗？王却没有告诉仆人们，在我主我王之后谁坐你的位。
