chapters.en: to bring before him Queen Vashti, wearing her royal crown, in order to display her beauty to the people and nobles, for she was lovely to look at.
chapters.zh: 请王后瓦实提头戴王后的冠冕到王面前，使各等臣民看她的美貌，因为她容貌甚美。

chapters.en: But when the attendants delivered the king’s command, Queen Vashti refused to come. Then the king became furious and burned with anger.
chapters.zh: 王后瓦实提却不肯遵太监所传的王命而来，所以王甚发怒，心如火烧。

chapters.en: Since it was customary for the king to consult experts in matters of law and justice, he spoke with the wise men who understood the times
chapters.zh: 那时，在王左右常见王面，国中坐高位的，有波斯和玛代的七个大臣，就是甲示拿，示达，押玛他，他施斯，米力，玛西拿，米母干，都是达时务的明哲人。按王的常规，办事必先询问知例明法的人。王问他们说，

chapters.en: and were closest to the king—Karshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena and Memukan, the seven nobles of Persia and Media who had special access to the king and were highest in the kingdom.
“According to law, what must be done to Queen Vashti?” he asked. “She has not obeyed the command of King Xerxes that the eunuchs have taken to her.”
chapters.zh: 王后瓦实提不遵太监所传的王命，照例应当怎样办理呢？

chapters.en: Then Memukan replied in the presence of the king and the nobles, “Queen Vashti has done wrong, not only against the king but also against all the nobles and the peoples of all the provinces of King Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 米母干在王和众首领面前回答说，王后瓦实提这事，不但得罪王，并且有害于王各省的臣民。

chapters.en: For the queen’s conduct will become known to all the women, and so they will despise their husbands and say, ‘King Xerxes commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she would not come.’
chapters.zh: 因为王后这事必传到众妇人的耳中，说，亚哈随鲁王吩咐王后瓦实提到王面前，她却不来，她们就藐视自己的丈夫。

chapters.en: This very day the Persian and Median women of the nobility who have heard about the queen’s conduct will respond to all the king’s nobles in the same way. There will be no end of disrespect and discord.
chapters.zh: 今日波斯和玛代的众夫人听见王后这事，必向王的大臣照样行。从此必大开藐视和忿怒之端。

chapters.en: “Therefore, if it pleases the king, let him issue a royal decree and let it be written in the laws of Persia and Media, which cannot be repealed, that Vashti is never again to enter the presence of King Xerxes. Also let the king give her royal position to someone else who is better than she.
chapters.zh: 王若以为美，就降旨写在波斯和玛代人的例中，永不更改，不准瓦实提再到王面前，将她王后的位分赐给比她还好的人。

chapters.en: Then when the king’s edict is proclaimed throughout all his vast realm, all the women will respect their husbands, from the least to the greatest.”
chapters.zh: 所降的旨意传遍通国（国度本来广大），所有的妇人，无论丈夫贵贱都必尊敬他。

chapters.en: The king and his nobles were pleased with this advice, so the king did as Memukan proposed.
chapters.zh: 王和众首领都以米母干的话为美，王就照这话去行，

chapters.en: He sent dispatches to all parts of the kingdom, to each province in its own script and to each people in their own language, proclaiming that every man should be ruler over his own household, using his native tongue.
chapters.zh: 发诏书，用各省的文字，各族的方言通知各省，使为丈夫的在家中作主，各说本地的方言。

chapters.en: Later when King Xerxes’ fury had subsided, he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what he had decreed about her.
chapters.zh: 这事以后，亚哈随鲁王的忿怒止息，就想念瓦实提和她所行的，并怎样降旨办她。

chapters.en: Then the king’s personal attendants proposed, “Let a search be made for beautiful young virgins for the king.
chapters.zh: 于是王的侍臣对王说，不如为王寻找美貌的处女。

chapters.en: Let the king appoint commissioners in every province of his realm to bring all these beautiful young women into the harem at the citadel of Susa. Let them be placed under the care of Hegai, the king’s eunuch, who is in charge of the women; and let beauty treatments be given to them.
chapters.zh: 王可以派官在国中的各省，招聚美貌的处女到书珊城（或作宫）的女院，交给掌管女子的太监希该，给她们当用的香品。

chapters.en: Then let the young woman who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti.” This advice appealed to the king, and he followed it.
chapters.zh: 王所喜爱的女子可以立为王后，代替瓦实提。王以这事为美，就如此行。

chapters.en: Now there was in the citadel of Susa a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin, named Mordecai son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish,
chapters.zh: 书珊城有一个犹大人，名叫末底改，是便雅悯人基士的曾孙，示每的孙子，睚珥的儿子。

chapters.en: who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, among those taken captive with Jehoiachin king of Judah.
chapters.zh: 从前巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒，将犹大王耶哥尼雅（又名约雅斤）和百姓从耶路撒冷掳去，末底改也在其内。

chapters.en: Mordecai had a cousin named Hadassah, whom he had brought up because she had neither father nor mother. This young woman, who was also known as Esther, had a lovely figure and was beautiful. Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter when her father and mother died.
chapters.zh: 末底改抚养他叔叔的女儿哈大沙（后名以斯帖），因为她没有父母。这女子又容貌俊美，她父母死了，末底改就收她为自己的女儿。

chapters.en: When the king’s order and edict had been proclaimed, many young women were brought to the citadel of Susa and put under the care of Hegai. Esther also was taken to the king’s palace and entrusted to Hegai, who had charge of the harem.
chapters.zh: 王的谕旨传出，就招聚许多女子到书珊城，交给掌管女子的希该。以斯帖也送入王宫，交付希该。

chapters.en: She pleased him and won his favor. Immediately he provided her with her beauty treatments and special food. He assigned to her seven female attendants selected from the king’s palace and moved her and her attendants into the best place in the harem.
chapters.zh: 希该喜悦以斯帖，就恩待她。急忙给她需用的香品和她所当得的分，又派所当得的七个宫女服事她，使她和她的宫女搬入女院上好的房屋。

chapters.en: Esther had not revealed her nationality and family background, because Mordecai had forbidden her to do so.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖未曾将籍贯宗族告诉人，因为末底改嘱咐她不可叫人知道。

chapters.en: Every day he walked back and forth near the courtyard of the harem to find out how Esther was and what was happening to her.
chapters.zh: 末底改天天在女院前边行走，要知道以斯帖平安不平安，并后事如何。

chapters.en: Before a young woman’s turn came to go in to King Xerxes, she had to complete twelve months of beauty treatments prescribed for the women, six months with oil of myrrh and six with perfumes and cosmetics.
chapters.zh: 众女子照例先洁净身体十二个月。六个月用没药油，六个月用香料和洁身之物。满了日期，然后挨次进去见亚哈随鲁王。

chapters.en: And this is how she would go to the king: Anything she wanted was given her to take with her from the harem to the king’s palace.
chapters.zh: 女子进去见王是这样。从女院到王宫的时候，凡她所要的都必给她。

chapters.en: In the evening she would go there and in the morning return to another part of the harem to the care of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch who was in charge of the concubines. She would not return to the king unless he was pleased with her and summoned her by name.
chapters.zh: 晚上进去，次日回到女子第二院，交给掌管妃嫔的太监沙甲。除非王喜爱她，再提名召她，就不再进去见王。

chapters.en: When the turn came for Esther (the young woman Mordecai had adopted, the daughter of his uncle Abihail) to go to the king, she asked for nothing other than what Hegai, the king’s eunuch who was in charge of the harem, suggested. And Esther won the favor of everyone who saw her.
chapters.zh: 末底改叔叔亚比孩的女儿，就是末底改收为自己女儿的以斯帖，按次序当进去见王的时候，除了掌管女子的太监希该所派定给她的，她别无所求。凡看见以斯帖的都喜悦她。

chapters.en: She was taken to King Xerxes in the royal residence in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王第七年十月，就是提别月，以斯帖被引入宫见王。

chapters.en: Now the king was attracted to Esther more than to any of the other women, and she won his favor and approval more than any of the other virgins. So he set a royal crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.
chapters.zh: 王爱以斯帖过于爱众女，她在王眼前蒙宠爱比众处女更甚。王就把王后的冠冕戴在她头上，立她为王后，代替瓦实提。

chapters.en: And the king gave a great banquet, Esther’s banquet, for all his nobles and officials. He proclaimed a holiday throughout the provinces and distributed gifts with royal liberality.
chapters.zh: 王因以斯帖的缘故给众首领和臣仆设摆大筵席，又豁免各省的租税，并照王的厚意大颁赏赐。

chapters.en: When the virgins were assembled a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate.
chapters.zh: 第二次招聚处女的时候，末底改坐在朝门。

chapters.en: But Esther had kept secret her family background and nationality just as Mordecai had told her to do, for she continued to follow Mordecai’s instructions as she had done when he was bringing her up.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖照着末底改所嘱咐的，还没有将籍贯宗族告诉人。因为以斯帖遵末底改的命，如抚养她的时候一样。

chapters.en: During the time Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate, Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s officers who guarded the doorway, became angry and conspired to assassinate King Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 当那时候，末底改坐在朝门，王的太监中有两个守门的，辟探和提列，恼恨亚哈随鲁王，想要下手害他。

chapters.en: But Mordecai found out about the plot and told Queen Esther, who in turn reported it to the king, giving credit to Mordecai.
chapters.zh: 末底改知道了，就告诉王后以斯帖。以斯帖奉末底改的名，报告于王。

chapters.en: And when the report was investigated and found to be true, the two officials were impaled on poles. All this was recorded in the book of the annals in the presence of the king.
chapters.zh: 究察这事，果然是实，就把二人挂在木头上，将这事在王面前写于历史上。

chapters.en: After these events, King Xerxes honored Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, elevating him and giving him a seat of honor higher than that of all the other nobles.
chapters.zh: 这事以后，亚哈随鲁王抬举，亚甲族哈米大他的儿子哈曼，使他高升，叫他的爵位超过与他同事的一切臣宰。

chapters.en: All the royal officials at the king’s gate knelt down and paid honor to Haman, for the king had commanded this concerning him. But Mordecai would not kneel down or pay him honor.
chapters.zh: 在朝门的一切臣仆都跪拜哈曼，因为王如此吩咐。惟独末底改不跪不拜。

chapters.en: Then the royal officials at the king’s gate asked Mordecai, “Why do you disobey the king’s command?”
chapters.zh: 在朝门的臣仆问末底改说，你为何违背王的命令呢？

chapters.en: Day after day they spoke to him but he refused to comply. Therefore they told Haman about it to see whether Mordecai’s behavior would be tolerated, for he had told them he was a Jew.
chapters.zh: 他们天天劝他，他还是不听，他们就告诉哈曼，要看末底改的事站得住站不住，因他已经告诉他们自己是犹大人。

chapters.en: When Haman saw that Mordecai would not kneel down or pay him honor, he was enraged.
chapters.zh: 哈曼见末底改不跪不拜，他就怒气填胸。

chapters.en: Yet having learned who Mordecai’s people were, he scorned the idea of killing only Mordecai. Instead Haman looked for a way to destroy all Mordecai’s people, the Jews, throughout the whole kingdom of Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 他们已将末底改的本族告诉哈曼。他以为下手害末底改一人是小事，就要灭绝亚哈随鲁王通国所有的犹大人，就是末底改的本族。

chapters.en: In the twelfth year of King Xerxes, in the first month, the month of Nisan, the pur (that is, the lot) was cast in the presence of Haman to select a day and month. And the lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王十二年正月，就是尼散月，人在哈曼面前，按日日月月掣普珥，就是掣签，要定何月何日为吉，择定了十二月，就是亚达月。

chapters.en: Then Haman said to King Xerxes, “There is a certain people dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom who keep themselves separate. Their customs are different from those of all other people, and they do not obey the king’s laws; it is not in the king’s best interest to tolerate them.
chapters.zh: 哈曼对亚哈随鲁王说，有一种民，散居在王国各省的民中，他们的律例与万民的律例不同，也不守王的律例，所以容留他们与王无益。

chapters.en: If it pleases the king, let a decree be issued to destroy them, and I will give ten thousand talents of silver to the king’s administrators for the royal treasury.”
chapters.zh: 王若以为美，请下旨意灭绝他们。我就捐一万他连得银子交给掌管国帑的人，纳入王的府库。

chapters.en: So the king took his signet ring from his finger and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
chapters.zh: 于是王从自己手上摘下戒指，给犹大人的仇敌亚甲族哈米大他的儿子哈曼。

chapters.en: “Keep the money,” the king said to Haman, “and do with the people as you please.”
chapters.zh: 王对哈曼说，这银子仍赐给你，这民也交给你，你可以随意待他们。

chapters.en: Then on the thirteenth day of the first month the royal secretaries were summoned. They wrote out in the script of each province and in the language of each people all Haman’s orders to the king’s satraps, the governors of the various provinces and the nobles of the various peoples. These were written in the name of King Xerxes himself and sealed with his own ring.
chapters.zh: 正月十三日，就召了王的书记来，照着哈曼一切所吩咐的，用各省的文字，各族的方言，奉亚哈随鲁王的名写旨意，传与总督和各省的省长，并各族的首领。又用王的戒指盖印。

chapters.en: Dispatches were sent by couriers to all the king’s provinces with the order to destroy, kill and annihilate all the Jews—young and old, women and children—on a single day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their goods.
chapters.zh: 交给驿卒传到王的各省，吩咐将犹大人，无论老少妇女孩子，在一日之间，十二月，就是亚达月十三日，全然剪除，杀戮灭绝，并夺他们的财为掠物。

chapters.en: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued as law in every province and made known to the people of every nationality so they would be ready for that day.
chapters.zh: 抄录这旨意，颁行各省，宣告各族，使他们预备等候那日。

chapters.en: The couriers went out, spurred on by the king’s command, and the edict was issued in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was bewildered.
chapters.zh: 驿卒奉王命急忙起行，旨意也传遍书珊城。王同哈曼坐下饮酒，书珊城的民却都慌乱。

chapters.en: When Mordecai learned of all that had been done, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the city, wailing loudly and bitterly.
chapters.zh: 末底改知道所做的这一切事，就撕裂衣服，穿麻衣，蒙灰尘，在城中行走，痛哭哀号。

chapters.en: But he went only as far as the king’s gate, because no one clothed in sackcloth was allowed to enter it.
chapters.zh: 到了朝门前停住脚步，因为穿麻衣的不可进朝门。

chapters.en: In every province to which the edict and order of the king came, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing. Many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
chapters.zh: 王的谕旨所到的各省各处，犹大人大大悲哀，禁食哭泣哀号，穿麻衣躺在灰中的甚多。

chapters.en: When Esther’s eunuchs and female attendants came and told her about Mordecai, she was in great distress. She sent clothes for him to put on instead of his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.
chapters.zh: 王后以斯帖的宫女和太监来把这事告诉以斯帖，她甚是忧愁，就送衣服给末底改穿，要他脱下麻衣，他却不受。

chapters.en: Then Esther summoned Hathak, one of the king’s eunuchs assigned to attend her, and ordered him to find out what was troubling Mordecai and why.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖就把王所派伺候她的一个太监，名叫哈他革召来，吩咐他去见末底改，要知道这是什么事，是什么缘故。

chapters.en: So Hathak went out to Mordecai in the open square of the city in front of the king’s gate.
chapters.zh: 于是哈他革出到朝门前的宽阔处见末底改。

chapters.en: Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, including the exact amount of money Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury for the destruction of the Jews.
chapters.zh: 末底改将自己所遇的事，并哈曼为灭绝犹大人，应许捐入王库的银数都告诉了他。

chapters.en: He also gave him a copy of the text of the edict for their annihilation, which had been published in Susa, to show to Esther and explain it to her, and he told him to instruct her to go into the king’s presence to beg for mercy and plead with him for her people.
chapters.zh: 又将所抄写传遍书珊城，要灭绝犹大人的旨意交给哈他革，要给以斯帖看，又要给她说明，并嘱咐她进去见王，为本族的人在王面前恳切祈求。

chapters.en: Hathak went back and reported to Esther what Mordecai had said.
chapters.zh: 哈他革回来，将末底改的话告诉以斯帖。

chapters.en: Then she instructed him to say to Mordecai,
chapters.zh: 以斯帖就吩咐哈他革去见末底改，说，

chapters.en: “All the king’s officials and the people of the royal provinces know that for any man or woman who approaches the king in the inner court without being summoned the king has but one law: that they be put to death unless the king extends the gold scepter to them and spares their lives. But thirty days have passed since I was called to go to the king.”
chapters.zh: 王的一切臣仆和各省的人民，都知道有一个定例，若不蒙召，擅入内院见王的，无论男女必被治死。除非王向他伸出金杖，不得存活。现在我没有蒙召进去见王已经三十日了。

chapters.en: When Esther’s words were reported to Mordecai,
chapters.zh: 人就把以斯帖这话告诉末底改。

chapters.en: he sent back this answer: “Do not think that because you are in the king’s house you alone of all the Jews will escape.
chapters.zh: 末底改托人回覆以斯帖说，你莫想在王宫里强过一切犹大人，得免这祸。

chapters.en: For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance for the Jews will arise from another place, but you and your father’s family will perish. And who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?”
chapters.zh: 此时你若闭口不言，犹大人必从别处得解脱，蒙拯救，你和你父家，必至灭亡。焉知你得了王后的位分，不是为现今的机会吗？

chapters.en: Then Esther sent this reply to Mordecai:
chapters.zh: 以斯帖就吩咐人回报末底改说，

chapters.en: “Go, gather together all the Jews who are in Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my attendants will fast as you do. When this is done, I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish.”
chapters.zh: 你当去招聚书珊城所有的犹大人，为我禁食三昼三夜，不吃不喝。我和我的宫女也要这样禁食。然后我违例进去见王，我若死就死吧。

chapters.en: So Mordecai went away and carried out all of Esther’s instructions.
chapters.zh: 于是末底改照以斯帖一切所吩咐的去行。

chapters.en: On the third day Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the palace, in front of the king’s hall. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the hall, facing the entrance.
chapters.zh: 第三日，以斯帖穿上朝服，进王宫的内院，对殿站立。王在殿里坐在宝座上，对着殿门。

chapters.en: When he saw Queen Esther standing in the court, he was pleased with her and held out to her the gold scepter that was in his hand. So Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter.
chapters.zh: 王见王后以斯帖站在院内，就施恩于她，向她伸出手中的金杖，以斯帖便向前摸杖头。

chapters.en: Then the king asked, “What is it, Queen Esther? What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given you.”
chapters.zh: 王对她说，王后以斯帖阿，你要什么。你求什么，就是国的一半也必赐给你。

chapters.en: “If it pleases the king,” replied Esther, “let the king, together with Haman, come today to a banquet I have prepared for him.”
chapters.zh: 以斯帖说，王若以为美，就请王带着哈曼，今日赴我所预备的筵席。

chapters.en: “Bring Haman at once,” the king said, “so that we may do what Esther asks.” So the king and Haman went to the banquet Esther had prepared.
chapters.zh: 王说，叫哈曼速速照以斯帖的话去行。于是王带着哈曼赴以斯帖所预备的筵席。

chapters.en: As they were drinking wine, the king again asked Esther, “Now what is your petition? It will be given you. And what is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be granted.”
chapters.zh: 在酒席筵前，王又问以斯帖说，你要什么，我必赐给你。你求什么，就是国的一半也必为你成就。

chapters.en: Esther replied, “My petition and my request is this:
chapters.zh: 以斯帖回答说，我有所要，我有所求。

chapters.en: If the king regards me with favor and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request, let the king and Haman come tomorrow to the banquet I will prepare for them. Then I will answer the king’s question.”
chapters.zh: 我若在王眼前蒙恩，王若愿意赐我所要的，准我所求的，就请王带着哈曼，再赴我所要预备的筵席。明日我必照王所问的说明。

chapters.en: Haman went out that day happy and in high spirits. But when he saw Mordecai at the king’s gate and observed that he neither rose nor showed fear in his presence, he was filled with rage against Mordecai.
chapters.zh: 那日哈曼心中快乐，欢欢喜喜地出来。但见末底改在朝门不站起来，连身也不动，就满心恼怒末底改。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, Haman restrained himself and went home. Calling together his friends and Zeresh, his wife,
chapters.zh: 哈曼暂且忍耐回家，叫人请他朋友和他妻子细利斯来。

chapters.en: Haman boasted to them about his vast wealth, his many sons, and all the ways the king had honored him and how he had elevated him above the other nobles and officials.
chapters.zh: 哈曼将他富厚的荣耀，众多的儿女，和王抬举他使他超乎首领臣仆之上，都述说给他们听。

chapters.en: “And that’s not all,” Haman added. “I’m the only person Queen Esther invited to accompany the king to the banquet she gave. And she has invited me along with the king tomorrow.
chapters.zh: 哈曼又说，王后以斯帖预备筵席，除了我之外不许别人随王赴席。明日王后又请我随王赴席。

chapters.en: But all this gives me no satisfaction as long as I see that Jew Mordecai sitting at the king’s gate.”
chapters.zh: 只是我见犹大人末底改坐在朝门，虽有这一切荣耀，也与我无益。

chapters.en: His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, “Have a pole set up, reaching to a height of fifty cubits, and ask the king in the morning to have Mordecai impaled on it. Then go with the king to the banquet and enjoy yourself.” This suggestion delighted Haman, and he had the pole set up.
chapters.zh: 他的妻细利斯和他一切的朋友对他说，不如立一个五丈高的木架，明早求王将末底改挂在其上，然后你可以欢欢喜喜地随王赴席。哈曼以这话为美，就叫人做了木架。

chapters.en: That night the king could not sleep; so he ordered the book of the chronicles, the record of his reign, to be brought in and read to him.
chapters.zh: 那夜王睡不着觉，就吩咐人取历史来，念给他听。

chapters.en: It was found recorded there that Mordecai had exposed Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s officers who guarded the doorway, who had conspired to assassinate King Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 正遇见书上写着说，王的太监中有两个守门的，辟探和提列，想要下手害亚哈随鲁王，末底改将这事告诉王后。

chapters.en: “What honor and recognition has Mordecai received for this?” the king asked. “Nothing has been done for him,” his attendants answered.
chapters.zh: 王说，末底改行了这事，赐他什么尊荣爵位没有。伺候王的臣仆回答说，没有赐他什么。

chapters.en: The king said, “Who is in the court?” Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the palace to speak to the king about impaling Mordecai on the pole he had set up for him.
chapters.zh: 王说，谁在院子里。（那时哈曼正进王宫的外院，要求王将末底改挂在他所预备的木架上）

chapters.en: His attendants answered, “Haman is standing in the court.” “Bring him in,” the king ordered.
chapters.zh: 臣仆说，哈曼站在院内。王说，叫他进来。

chapters.en: When Haman entered, the king asked him, “What should be done for the man the king delights to honor?” Now Haman thought to himself, “Who is there that the king would rather honor than me?”
chapters.zh: 哈曼就进去。王问他说，王所喜悦尊荣的人，当如何待他呢？哈曼心里说，王所喜悦尊荣的，不是我是谁呢？

chapters.en: So he answered the king, “For the man the king delights to honor,
chapters.zh: 哈曼就回答说，王所喜悦尊荣的人，

chapters.en: have them bring a royal robe the king has worn and a horse the king has ridden, one with a royal crest placed on its head.
chapters.zh: 当将王常穿的朝服和戴冠的御马，

chapters.en: Then let the robe and horse be entrusted to one of the king’s most noble princes. Let them robe the man the king delights to honor, and lead him on the horse through the city streets, proclaiming before him, ‘This is what is done for the man the king delights to honor!’ ”
chapters.zh: 都交给王极尊贵的一个大臣，命他将衣服给王所喜悦尊荣的人穿上，使他骑上马，走遍城里的街市，在他面前宣告说，王所喜悦尊荣的人，就如此待他。

chapters.en: “Go at once,” the king commanded Haman. “Get the robe and the horse and do just as you have suggested for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king’s gate. Do not neglect anything you have recommended.”
chapters.zh: 王对哈曼说，你速速将这衣服和马，照你所说的，向坐在朝门的犹大人末底改去行。凡你所说的，一样不可缺。

chapters.en: So Haman got the robe and the horse. He robed Mordecai, and led him on horseback through the city streets, proclaiming before him, “This is what is done for the man the king delights to honor!”
chapters.zh: 于是哈曼将朝服给末底改穿上，使他骑上马，走遍城里的街市，在他面前宣告说，王所喜悦尊荣的人，就如此待他。

chapters.en: Afterward Mordecai returned to the king’s gate. But Haman rushed home, with his head covered in grief,
chapters.zh: 末底改仍回到朝门，哈曼却忧忧闷闷地蒙着头，急忙回家去了。

chapters.en: and told Zeresh his wife and all his friends everything that had happened to him. His advisers and his wife Zeresh said to him, “Since Mordecai, before whom your downfall has started, is of Jewish origin, you cannot stand against him—you will surely come to ruin!”
chapters.zh: 将所遇的一切事，详细说给他的妻细利斯，和他的众朋友听。他的智慧人，和他的妻细利斯对他说，你在末底改面前始而败落，他如果是犹大人，你必不能胜他，终必在他面前败落。

chapters.en: While they were still talking with him, the king’s eunuchs arrived and hurried Haman away to the banquet Esther had prepared.
chapters.zh: 他们还与哈曼说话的时候，王的太监来催哈曼，快去赴以斯帖所预备的筵席。

chapters.en: So the king and Haman went to Queen Esther’s banquet,
chapters.zh: 王带着哈曼来赴王后以斯帖的筵席。

chapters.en: and as they were drinking wine on the second day, the king again asked, “Queen Esther, what is your petition? It will be given you. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be granted.”
chapters.zh: 这第二次在酒席筵前，王又问以斯帖说，王后以斯帖阿，你要什么，我必赐给你。你求什么，就是国的一半也必为你成就。

chapters.en: Then Queen Esther answered, “If I have found favor with you, Your Majesty, and if it pleases you, grant me my life—this is my petition. And spare my people—this is my request.
chapters.zh: 王后以斯帖回答说，我若在王眼前蒙恩，王若以为美，我所愿的，是愿王将我的性命赐给我。我所求的，是求王将我的本族赐给我。

chapters.en: For I and my people have been sold to be destroyed, killed and annihilated. If we had merely been sold as male and female slaves, I would have kept quiet, because no such distress would justify disturbing the king. ”
chapters.zh: 因我和我的本族被卖了，要剪除杀戮灭绝我们。我们若被卖为奴为婢，我也闭口不言。但王的损失，敌人万不能补足。

chapters.en: King Xerxes asked Queen Esther, “Who is he? Where is he—the man who has dared to do such a thing?”
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王问王后以斯帖说，擅敢起意如此行的是谁。这人在哪里呢？

chapters.en: Esther said, “An adversary and enemy! This vile Haman!” Then Haman was terrified before the king and queen.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖说，仇人敌人就是这恶人哈曼。哈曼在王和王后面前就甚惊惶。

chapters.en: The king got up in a rage, left his wine and went out into the palace garden. But Haman, realizing that the king had already decided his fate, stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life.
chapters.zh: 王便大怒，起来离开酒席往御园去了。哈曼见王定意要加罪与他，就起来，求王后以斯帖救命。

chapters.en: Just as the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall, Haman was falling on the couch where Esther was reclining. The king exclaimed, “Will he even molest the queen while she is with me in the house?” As soon as the word left the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
chapters.zh: 王从御园回到酒席之处，见哈曼伏在以斯帖所靠的榻上。王说，他竟敢在宫内，在我面前凌辱王后吗？这话一出王口，人就蒙了哈曼的脸。

chapters.en: Then Harbona, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said, “A pole reaching to a height of fifty cubits stands by Haman’s house. He had it set up for Mordecai, who spoke up to help the king.” The king said, “Impale him on it!”
chapters.zh: 伺候王的一个太监名叫哈波拿，说，哈曼为那救王有功的末底改做了五丈高的木架，现今立在哈曼家里。王说，把哈曼挂在其上。

chapters.en: So they impaled Haman on the pole he had set up for Mordecai. Then the king’s fury subsided.
chapters.zh: 于是人将哈曼挂在他为末底改所预备的木架上。王的忿怒这才止息。

chapters.en: That same day King Xerxes gave Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai came into the presence of the king, for Esther had told how he was related to her.
chapters.zh: 当日，亚哈随鲁王把犹大人仇敌哈曼的家产，赐给王后以斯帖。末底改也来到王面前，因为以斯帖已经告诉王，末底改是她的亲属。

chapters.en: The king took off his signet ring, which he had reclaimed from Haman, and presented it to Mordecai. And Esther appointed him over Haman’s estate.
chapters.zh: 王摘下自己的戒指，就是从哈曼追回的，给了末底改。以斯帖派末底改管理哈曼的家产。

chapters.en: Esther again pleaded with the king, falling at his feet and weeping. She begged him to put an end to the evil plan of Haman the Agagite, which he had devised against the Jews.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖又俯伏在王脚前，流泪哀告，求他除掉亚甲族哈曼害犹大人的恶谋。

chapters.en: Then the king extended the gold scepter to Esther and she arose and stood before him.
chapters.zh: 王向以斯帖伸出金杖，以斯帖就起来，站在王前。

chapters.en: “If it pleases the king,” she said, “and if he regards me with favor and thinks it the right thing to do, and if he is pleased with me, let an order be written overruling the dispatches that Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, devised and wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king’s provinces.
chapters.zh: 说，亚甲族哈米大他的儿子哈曼设谋传旨，要杀灭在王各省的犹大人。现今王若愿意，我若在王眼前蒙恩，王若以为美，若喜悦我，请王另下旨意，废除哈曼所传的那旨意。

chapters.en: For how can I bear to see disaster fall on my people? How can I bear to see the destruction of my family?”
chapters.zh: 我何忍见我本族的人受害？何忍见我同宗的人被灭呢？

chapters.en: King Xerxes replied to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, “Because Haman attacked the Jews, I have given his estate to Esther, and they have impaled him on the pole he set up.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王对王后以斯帖，和犹大人末底改说，因哈曼要下手害犹大人，我已将他的家产赐给以斯帖，人也将哈曼挂在木架上。

chapters.en: Now write another decree in the king’s name in behalf of the Jews as seems best to you, and seal it with the king’s signet ring—for no document written in the king’s name and sealed with his ring can be revoked.”
chapters.zh: 现在你们可以随意，奉王的名写谕旨给犹大人，用王的戒指盖印。因为奉王名所写，用王戒指盖印的谕旨，人都不能废除。

chapters.en: At once the royal secretaries were summoned—on the twenty-third day of the third month, the month of Sivan. They wrote out all Mordecai’s orders to the Jews, and to the satraps, governors and nobles of the 127 provinces stretching from India to Cush. These orders were written in the script of each province and the language of each people and also to the Jews in their own script and language.
chapters.zh: 三月，就是西弯月二十三日，将王的书记召来。按着末底改所吩咐的，用各省的文字，各族的方言，并犹大人的文字方言写谕旨。传给那从印度直到古实一百二十七省的犹大人和总督省长首领。

chapters.en: Mordecai wrote in the name of King Xerxes, sealed the dispatches with the king’s signet ring, and sent them by mounted couriers, who rode fast horses especially bred for the king.
chapters.zh: 末底改奉亚哈随鲁王的名写谕旨，用王的戒指盖印，交给骑御马圈快马的驿卒，传到各处。

chapters.en: The king’s edict granted the Jews in every city the right to assemble and protect themselves; to destroy, kill and annihilate the armed men of any nationality or province who might attack them and their women and children, and to plunder the property of their enemies.
chapters.zh: 谕旨中，王准各省各城的犹大人在一日之间，十二月，就是亚达月十三日，聚集保护性命，剪除杀戮灭绝那要攻击犹大人的一切仇敌，和他们的妻子儿女，夺取他们的财为掠物。

chapters.en: The day appointed for the Jews to do this in all the provinces of King Xerxes was the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.

A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued as law in every province and made known to the people of every nationality so that the Jews would be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
chapters.zh: 抄录这谕旨，颁行各省，宣告各族，使犹大人预备等候那日，在仇敌身上报仇。

chapters.en: The couriers, riding the royal horses, went out, spurred on by the king’s command, and the edict was issued in the citadel of Susa.
chapters.zh: 于是骑快马的驿卒被王命催促，急忙起行。谕旨也传遍书珊城。

chapters.en: When Mordecai left the king’s presence, he was wearing royal garments of blue and white, a large crown of gold and a purple robe of fine linen. And the city of Susa held a joyous celebration.
chapters.zh: 末底改穿着蓝色白色的朝服，头戴大金冠冕，又穿紫色细麻布的外袍，从王面前出来。书珊城的人民都欢呼快乐。

chapters.en: For the Jews it was a time of happiness and joy, gladness and honor.
chapters.zh: 犹大人有光荣，欢喜快乐而得尊贵。

chapters.en: In every province and in every city to which the edict of the king came, there was joy and gladness among the Jews, with feasting and celebrating. And many people of other nationalities became Jews because fear of the Jews had seized them.
chapters.zh: 王的谕旨所到的各省各城，犹大人都欢喜快乐，设摆筵宴，以那日为吉日。那国的人民，有许多因惧怕犹大人，就入了犹大籍。

chapters.en: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, the edict commanded by the king was to be carried out. On this day the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, but now the tables were turned and the Jews got the upper hand over those who hated them.
chapters.zh: 十二月，乃亚达月十三日，王的谕旨将要举行，就是犹大人的仇敌盼望辖制他们的日子，犹大人反倒辖制恨他们的人。

chapters.en: The Jews assembled in their cities in all the provinces of King Xerxes to attack those determined to destroy them. No one could stand against them, because the people of all the other nationalities were afraid of them.
chapters.zh: 犹大人在亚哈随鲁王各省的城里聚集，下手击杀那要害他们的人。无人能敌挡他们，因为各族都惧怕他们。

chapters.en: And all the nobles of the provinces, the satraps, the governors and the king’s administrators helped the Jews, because fear of Mordecai had seized them.
chapters.zh: 各省的首领，总督，省长，和办理王事的人，因惧怕末底改，就都帮助犹大人。

chapters.en: Mordecai was prominent in the palace; his reputation spread throughout the provinces, and he became more and more powerful.
chapters.zh: 末底改在朝中为大，名声传遍各省，日渐昌盛。

chapters.en: The Jews struck down all their enemies with the sword, killing and destroying them, and they did what they pleased to those who hated them.
chapters.zh: 犹大人用刀击杀一切仇敌，任意杀灭恨他们的人。

chapters.en: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.
chapters.zh: 在书珊城，犹大人杀灭了五百人。

chapters.en: They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
chapters.zh: 又杀巴珊大他，达分，亚斯帕他，

chapters.en: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
chapters.zh: 破拉他，亚大利雅，亚利大他，

chapters.en: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai and Vaizatha,
chapters.zh: 帕玛斯他，亚利赛，亚利代，瓦耶撒他。

chapters.en: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay their hands on the plunder.
chapters.zh: 这十人都是哈米大他的孙子，犹大人仇敌哈曼的儿子。犹大人却没有下手夺取财物。

chapters.en: The number of those killed in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king that same day.
chapters.zh: 当日，将书珊城被杀的人数呈在王前。

chapters.en: The king said to Queen Esther, “The Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman in the citadel of Susa. What have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? Now what is your petition? It will be given you. What is your request? It will also be granted.”
chapters.zh: 王对王后以斯帖说，犹大人在书珊城杀灭了五百人，又杀了哈曼的十个儿子，在王的各省不知如何呢？现在你要什么，我必赐给你。你还求什么，也必为你成就。

chapters.en: “If it pleases the king,” Esther answered, “give the Jews in Susa permission to carry out this day’s edict tomorrow also, and let Haman’s ten sons be impaled on poles.”
chapters.zh: 以斯帖说，王若以为美，求你准书珊的犹大人，明日也照今日的旨意行，并将哈曼十个儿子的尸首挂在木架上。

chapters.en: So the king commanded that this be done. An edict was issued in Susa, and they impaled the ten sons of Haman.
chapters.zh: 王便允准如此行。旨意传在书珊，人就把哈曼十个儿子的尸首挂起来了。

chapters.en: The Jews in Susa came together on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, and they put to death in Susa three hundred men, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.
chapters.zh: 亚达月十四日书珊的犹大人又聚集在书珊，杀了三百人，却没有下手夺取财物。

chapters.en: Meanwhile, the remainder of the Jews who were in the king’s provinces also assembled to protect themselves and get relief from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of them but did not lay their hands on the plunder.
chapters.zh: 在王各省其余的犹大人，也都聚集保护性命，杀了恨他们的人七万五千，却没有下手夺取财物。这样，就脱离仇敌，得享平安。

chapters.en: This happened on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.
chapters.zh: 亚达月十三日，行了这事。十四日安息，以这日为设筵欢乐的日子。

chapters.en: The Jews in Susa, however, had assembled on the thirteenth and fourteenth, and then on the fifteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.
chapters.zh: 但书珊的犹大人，这十三日，十四日聚集杀戮仇敌。十五日安息，以这日为设筵欢乐的日子。

chapters.en: That is why rural Jews—those living in villages—observe the fourteenth of the month of Adar as a day of joy and feasting, a day for giving presents to each other.
chapters.zh: 所以住无城墙乡村的犹大人，如今都以亚达月十四日为设筵欢乐的吉日，彼此馈送礼物。

chapters.en: Mordecai recorded these events, and he sent letters to all the Jews throughout the provinces of King Xerxes, near and far,
chapters.zh: 末底改记录这事，写信与亚哈随鲁王各省远近所有的犹大人，

chapters.en: to have them celebrate annually the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar
chapters.zh: 嘱咐他们每年守亚达月十四，十五两日。

chapters.en: as the time when the Jews got relief from their enemies, and as the month when their sorrow was turned into joy and their mourning into a day of celebration. He wrote them to observe the days as days of feasting and joy and giving presents of food to one another and gifts to the poor.
chapters.zh: 以这月的两日为犹大人脱离仇敌得平安，转忧为喜，转悲为乐的吉日。在这两日设筵欢乐，彼此馈送礼物，周济穷人。

chapters.en: So the Jews agreed to continue the celebration they had begun, doing what Mordecai had written to them.
chapters.zh: 于是，犹大人按着末底改所写与他们的信，应承照初次所守的守为永例。

chapters.en: For Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them and had cast the pur (that is, the lot) for their ruin and destruction.
chapters.zh: 是因犹大人的仇敌，亚甲族哈米大他的儿子哈曼，设谋杀害犹大人，掣普珥，就是掣签，为要杀尽灭绝他们。

chapters.en: But when the plot came to the king’s attention, he issued written orders that the evil scheme Haman had devised against the Jews should come back onto his own head, and that he and his sons should be impaled on poles.
chapters.zh: 这事报告于王，王便降旨使哈曼谋害犹大人的恶事，归到他自己的头上，并吩咐把他和他的众子都挂在木架上。

chapters.en: (Therefore these days were called Purim, from the word pur.) Because of everything written in this letter and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them,
chapters.zh: 照着普珥的名字，犹大人就称这两日为普珥日。他们因这信上的话，又因所看见所遇见的事，

chapters.en: the Jews took it on themselves to establish the custom that they and their descendants and all who join them should without fail observe these two days every year, in the way prescribed and at the time appointed.
chapters.zh: 就应承自己与后裔，并归附他们的人，每年按时必守这两日，永远不废。

chapters.en: These days should be remembered and observed in every generation by every family, and in every province and in every city. And these days of Purim should never fail to be celebrated by the Jews—nor should the memory of these days die out among their descendants.
chapters.zh: 各省各城，家家户户，世世代代纪念遵守这两日，使这普珥日在犹大人中不可废掉，在他们后裔中也不可忘记。

chapters.en: So Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.
chapters.zh: 亚比孩的女儿王后以斯帖，和犹大人末底改以全权写第二封信，坚嘱犹大人守这普珥日。

chapters.en: And Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of Xerxes’ kingdom—words of goodwill and assurance—
chapters.zh: 用和平诚实话，写信给亚哈随鲁王国中，一百二十七省所有的犹大人，

chapters.en: to establish these days of Purim at their designated times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had decreed for them, and as they had established for themselves and their descendants in regard to their times of fasting and lamentation.
chapters.zh: 劝他们按时守这普珥日，禁食呼求，是照犹大人末底改，和王后以斯帖，所嘱咐的。也照犹大人为自己与后裔所应承的。

chapters.en: Esther’s decree confirmed these regulations about Purim, and it was written down in the records.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖命定守普珥日，这事也记录在书上。

chapters.en: King Xerxes imposed tribute throughout the empire, to its distant shores.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王使旱地，和海岛的人民都进贡。

chapters.en: And all his acts of power and might, together with a full account of the greatness of Mordecai, whom the king had promoted, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Media and Persia?
chapters.zh: 他以权柄能力所行的，并他抬举末底改使他高升的事，岂不都写在玛代，和波斯王的历史上吗？

chapters.en: Mordecai the Jew was second in rank to King Xerxes, preeminent among the Jews, and held in high esteem by his many fellow Jews, because he worked for the good of his people and spoke up for the welfare of all the Jews.
chapters.zh: 犹大人末底改作亚哈随鲁王的宰相，在犹大人中为大，得他众弟兄的喜悦，为本族的人求好处，向他们说和平的话。

chapters.en: In the land of Uz there lived a man whose name was Job. This man was blameless and upright; he feared God and shunned evil.
chapters.zh: 乌斯地有一个人名叫约伯。那人完全正直，敬畏神，远离恶事。

chapters.en: He had seven sons and three daughters,
chapters.zh: 他生了七个儿子，三个女儿。

chapters.en: and he owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred donkeys, and had a large number of servants. He was the greatest man among all the people of the East.
chapters.zh: 他的家产有七千羊，三千骆驼，五百对牛，五百母驴，并有许多仆婢。这人在东方人中就为至大。

chapters.en: His sons used to hold feasts in their homes on their birthdays, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
chapters.zh: 他的儿子，按着日子，各在自己家里设摆筵宴，就打发人去，请了他们的三个姐妹来，与他们一同吃喝，

chapters.en: When a period of feasting had run its course, Job would make arrangements for them to be purified. Early in the morning he would sacrifice a burnt offering for each of them, thinking, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” This was Job’s regular custom.
chapters.zh: 筵宴的日子过了，约伯打发人去叫他们自洁。他清早起来，按着他们众人的数目献燔祭。因为他说，恐怕我儿子犯了罪，心中弃掉神。约伯常常这样行。

chapters.en: One day the angels came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them.
chapters.zh: 有一天，神的众子，来侍立在耶和华面前，撒但也来在其中。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered the LORD, “From roaming throughout the earth, going back and forth on it.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华问撒但说，你从哪里来？撒但回答说，我从地上走来走去，往返而来。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华问撒但说，你曾用心察看我的仆人约伯没有。地上再没有人像他完全正直，敬畏神，远离恶事。

chapters.en: “Does Job fear God for nothing?” Satan replied.
chapters.zh: 撒但回答耶和华说，约伯敬畏神，岂是无故呢？

chapters.en: “Have you not put a hedge around him and his household and everything he has? You have blessed the work of his hands, so that his flocks and herds are spread throughout the land.
chapters.zh: 你岂不是四面圈上篱笆，围护他和他的家，并他一切所有的吗？他手所做的都蒙你赐福。他的家产也在地上增多。

chapters.en: But now stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face.”
chapters.zh: 你且伸手毁他一切所有的。他必当面弃掉你。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Satan, “Very well, then, everything he has is in your power, but on the man himself do not lay a finger.” Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对撒但说，凡他所有的都在你手中。只是不可伸手加害于他。于是撒但从耶和华面前退去。

chapters.en: One day when Job’s sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother’s house,
chapters.zh: 有一天，约伯的儿女正在他们长兄的家里，吃饭喝酒，

chapters.en: a messenger came to Job and said, “The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby,
chapters.zh: 有报信的来见约伯，说，牛正耕地，驴在旁边吃草。

chapters.en: and the Sabeans attacked and made off with them. They put the servants to the sword, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”
chapters.zh: 示巴人忽然闯来，把牲畜掳去，并用刀杀了仆人。惟有我一人逃脱，来报信给你。

chapters.en: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned up the sheep and the servants, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”
chapters.zh: 他还说话的时候，又有人来说，神从天上降下火来，将群羊和仆人都烧灭了。惟有我一人逃脱，来报信给你。

chapters.en: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “The Chaldeans formed three raiding parties and swept down on your camels and made off with them. They put the servants to the sword, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”
chapters.zh: 他还说话的时候，又有人来说，迦勒底人分作三队忽然闯来，把骆驼掳去，并用刀杀了仆人。惟有我一人逃脱，来报信给你。

chapters.en: While he was still speaking, yet another messenger came and said, “Your sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother’s house,
chapters.zh: 他还说话的时候，又有人来说，你的儿女正在他们长兄的家里吃饭喝酒。

chapters.en: when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on them and they are dead, and I am the only one who has escaped to tell you!”
chapters.zh: 不料，有狂风从旷野刮来，击打房屋的四角，房屋倒塌在少年人身上，他们就都死了。惟有我一人逃脱，来报信给你。

chapters.en: At this, Job got up and tore his robe and shaved his head. Then he fell to the ground in worship
chapters.zh: 约伯便起来，撕裂外袍，剃了头，伏在地上下拜。

chapters.en: and said: “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will depart.The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away; may the name of the LORD be praised.”
chapters.zh: 说，我赤身出于母胎，也必赤身归回。赏赐的是耶和华，收取的也是耶和华。耶和华的名是应当称颂的。

chapters.en: In all this, Job did not sin by charging God with wrongdoing.
chapters.zh: 在这一切的事上约伯并不犯罪，也不以神为愚妄（或作也不妄评神）。

chapters.en: On another day the angels came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them to present himself before him.
chapters.zh: 又有一天，神的众子来侍立在耶和华面前，撒但也来在其中。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered the LORD, “From roaming throughout the earth, going back and forth on it.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华问撒但说，你从哪里来？撒但回答说，我从地上走来走去，往返而来。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him; he is blameless and upright, a man who fears God and shuns evil. And he still maintains his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him without any reason.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华问撒但说，你曾用心察看我的仆人约伯没有。地上再没有人像他完全正直，敬畏神，远离恶事。你虽激动我攻击他，无故地毁灭他，他仍然持守他的纯正。

chapters.en: “Skin for skin!” Satan replied. “A man will give all he has for his own life.
chapters.zh: 撒但回答耶和华说，人以皮代皮，情愿舍去一切所有的，保全性命。

chapters.en: But now stretch out your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse you to your face.”
chapters.zh: 你且伸手伤他的骨头和他的肉，他必当面弃掉你。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Satan, “Very well, then, he is in your hands; but you must spare his life.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对撒但说，他在你手中，只要存留他的性命。

chapters.en: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and afflicted Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.
chapters.zh: 于是撒但从耶和华面前退去，击打约伯，使他从脚掌到头顶长毒疮。

chapters.en: Then Job took a piece of broken pottery and scraped himself with it as he sat among the ashes.
chapters.zh: 约伯就坐在炉灰中，拿瓦片刮身体。

chapters.en: His wife said to him, “Are you still maintaining your integrity? Curse God and die!”
chapters.zh: 他的妻子对他说，你仍然持守你的纯正吗？你弃掉神，死了吧。

chapters.en: He replied, “You are talking like a foolish woman. Shall we accept good from God, and not trouble?” In all this, Job did not sin in what he said.
chapters.zh: 约伯却对她说，你说话像愚顽的妇人一样。嗳，难道我们从神手里得福，不也受祸吗？在这一切的事上约伯并不以口犯罪。

chapters.en: When Job’s three friends, Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite, heard about all the troubles that had come upon him, they set out from their homes and met together by agreement to go and sympathize with him and comfort him.
chapters.zh: 约伯的三个朋友提幔人以利法，书亚人比勒达，拿玛人琐法，听说有这一切的灾祸临到他身上，各人就从本处约会同来，为他悲伤，安慰他。

chapters.en: When they saw him from a distance, they could hardly recognize him; they began to weep aloud, and they tore their robes and sprinkled dust on their heads.
chapters.zh: 他们远远地举目观看，认不出他来，就放声大哭。各人撕裂外袍，把尘土向天扬起来，落在自己的头上。

chapters.en: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him, because they saw how great his suffering was.
chapters.zh: 他们就同他七天七夜坐在地上，一个人也不向他说句话，因为他极其痛苦。

chapters.en: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
chapters.zh: 此后，约伯开口咒诅自己的生日，

chapters.en: He said:
chapters.zh: 说，愿我生的那日，和说怀了男胎的那夜都灭没。

chapters.en: “May the day of my birth perish, and the night that said, ‘A boy is conceived!’
That day—may it turn to darkness; may God above not care about it; may no light shine on it.
chapters.zh: 愿那日变为黑暗。愿神不从上面寻找它。愿亮光不照于其上。

chapters.en: May gloom and utter darkness claim it once more; may a cloud settle over it; may blackness overwhelm it.
chapters.zh: 愿黑暗和死荫索取那日。愿密云停在其上。愿日蚀恐吓它。

chapters.en: That night—may thick darkness seize it; may it not be included among the days of the year nor be entered in any of the months.
chapters.zh: 愿那夜被幽暗夺取，不在年中的日子同乐，也不入月中的数目。

chapters.en: May that night be barren; may no shout of joy be heard in it.
chapters.zh: 愿那夜没有生育，其间也没有欢乐的声音。

chapters.en: May those who curse days curse that day, those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.
chapters.zh: 愿那咒诅日子且能惹动鳄鱼的，咒诅那夜。

chapters.en: May its morning stars become dark; may it wait for daylight in vain and not see the first rays of dawn,
chapters.zh: 愿那夜黎明的星宿变为黑暗，盼亮却不亮，也不见早晨的光线（光线原文作眼皮）。

chapters.en: for it did not shut the doors of the womb on me to hide trouble from my eyes.
chapters.zh: 因没有把怀我胎的门关闭，也没有将患难对我的眼隐藏。

chapters.en: “Why did I not perish at birth, and die as I came from the womb?
chapters.zh: 我为何不出母胎而死。为何不出母腹绝气。

chapters.en: Why were there knees to receive me and breasts that I might be nursed?
chapters.zh: 为何有膝接收我。为何有奶哺养我。

chapters.en: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest
chapters.zh: 不然，我就早已躺卧安睡。

chapters.en: with kings and rulers of the earth, who built for themselves places now lying in ruins,
chapters.zh: 和地上为自己重造荒邱的君王，谋士。

chapters.en: with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
chapters.zh: 或与有金子，将银子装满了房屋的王子一同安息。

chapters.en: Or why was I not hidden away in the ground like a stillborn child, like an infant who never saw the light of day?
chapters.zh: 或像隐而未现，不到期而落的胎，归于无有，如同未见光的婴孩。

chapters.en: There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there the weary are at rest.
chapters.zh: 在那里恶人止息搅扰，困乏人得享安息。

chapters.en: Captives also enjoy their ease; they no longer hear the slave driver’s shout.
chapters.zh: 被囚的人同得安逸，不听见督工的声音。

chapters.en: The small and the great are there, and the slaves are freed from their owners.
chapters.zh: 大小都在那里。奴仆脱离主人的辖制。

chapters.en: “Why is light given to those in misery, and life to the bitter of soul,
chapters.zh: 受患难的人，为何有光赐给他呢？心中愁苦的人，为何有生命赐给他呢？

chapters.en: to those who long for death that does not come, who search for it more than for hidden treasure,
chapters.zh: 他们切望死，却不得死。求死，胜于求隐藏的珍宝。

chapters.en: who are filled with gladness and rejoice when they reach the grave?
chapters.zh: 他们寻见坟墓就快乐，极其欢喜。

chapters.en: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
chapters.zh: 人的道路既然遮隐，神又把他四面围困，为何有光赐给他呢？

chapters.en: For sighing has become my daily food; my groans pour out like water.
chapters.zh: 我未曾吃饭就发出叹息。我唉哼的声音涌出如水。

chapters.en: What I feared has come upon me; what I dreaded has happened to me.
chapters.zh: 因我所恐惧的临到我身，我所惧怕的迎我而来。

chapters.en: I have no peace, no quietness; I have no rest, but only turmoil.”
chapters.zh: 我不得安逸，不得平静，也不得安息，却有患难来到。

chapters.en: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
chapters.zh: 提幔人以利法回答说，

chapters.en: “If someone ventures a word with you, will you be impatient? But who can keep from speaking?
chapters.zh: 人若想与你说话，你就厌烦吗？但谁能忍住不说呢？

chapters.en: Think how you have instructed many, how you have strengthened feeble hands.
chapters.zh: 你素来教导许多的人，又坚固软弱的手。

chapters.en: Your words have supported those who stumbled; you have strengthened faltering knees.
chapters.zh: 你的言语曾扶助那将要跌倒的人。你又使软弱的膝稳固。

chapters.en: But now trouble comes to you, and you are discouraged; it strikes you, and you are dismayed.
chapters.zh: 但现在祸患临到你，你就昏迷，挨近你，你便惊惶。

chapters.en: Should not your piety be your confidence and your blameless ways your hope?
chapters.zh: 你的倚靠不是在你敬畏神吗？你的盼望不是在你行事纯正吗？

chapters.en: “Consider now: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Where were the upright ever destroyed?
chapters.zh: 请你追想，无辜的人有谁灭亡。正直的人在何处剪除。

chapters.en: As I have observed, those who plow evil and those who sow trouble reap it.
chapters.zh: 按我所见，耕罪孽，种毒害的人，都照样收割。

chapters.en: At the breath of God they perish; at the blast of his anger they are no more.
chapters.zh: 神一出气，他们就灭亡。神一发怒，他们就消没。

chapters.en: The lions may roar and growl, yet the teeth of the great lions are broken.
chapters.zh: 狮子的吼叫，和猛狮的声音，尽都止息。少壮狮子的牙齿，也都敲掉。

chapters.en: The lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
chapters.zh: 老狮子因绝食而死。母狮之子也都离散。

chapters.en: “A word was secretly brought to me, my ears caught a whisper of it.
chapters.zh: 我暗暗地得了默示。我耳朵也听其细微的声音。

chapters.en: Amid disquieting dreams in the night, when deep sleep falls on people,
chapters.zh: 在思念夜中，异象之间，世人沉睡的时候。

chapters.en: fear and trembling seized me and made all my bones shake.
chapters.zh: 恐惧，战兢临到我身，使我百骨打战。

chapters.en: A spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body stood on end.
chapters.zh: 有灵从我面前经过，我身上的毫毛直立。

chapters.en: It stopped, but I could not tell what it was. A form stood before my eyes, and I heard a hushed voice:
chapters.zh: 那灵停住，我却不能辨其形状。有影像在我眼前。我在静默中听见有声音说，

chapters.en: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can even a strong man be more pure than his Maker?
chapters.zh: 必死的人岂能比神公义吗？人岂能比造他的主洁净吗？

chapters.en: If God places no trust in his servants, if he charges his angels with error,
chapters.zh: 主不信靠他的臣仆，并且指他的使者为愚昧。

chapters.en: how much more those who live in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who are crushed more readily than a moth!
chapters.zh: 何况那住在土房，根基在尘土里，被蠹虫所毁坏的人呢？

chapters.en: Between dawn and dusk they are broken to pieces; unnoticed, they perish forever.
chapters.zh: 早晚之间，就被毁灭，永归无有，无人理会。

chapters.en: Are not the cords of their tent pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?’
chapters.zh: 他帐棚的绳索岂不从中抽出来呢？他死，且是无智慧而死。

chapters.en: “Call if you will, but who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
chapters.zh: 你且呼求，有谁答应你？诸圣者之中，你转向那一位呢？

chapters.en: Resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.
chapters.zh: 忿怒害死愚妄人，嫉妒杀死痴迷人。

chapters.en: I myself have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.
chapters.zh: 我曾见愚妄人扎下根，但我忽然咒诅他的住处。

chapters.en: His children are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.
chapters.zh: 他的儿女远离稳妥的地步，在城门口被压，并无人搭救。

chapters.en: The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from among thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.
chapters.zh: 他的庄稼有饥饿的人吃尽了，就是在荆棘里的也抢去了。他的财宝有网罗张口吞灭了。

chapters.en: For hardship does not spring from the soil, nor does trouble sprout from the ground.
chapters.zh: 祸患原不是从土中出来。患难也不是从地里发生。

chapters.en: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
chapters.zh: 人生在世必遇患难，如同火星飞腾。

chapters.en: “But if I were you, I would appeal to God; I would lay my cause before him.
chapters.zh: 至于我，我必仰望神，把我的事情托付他。

chapters.en: He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed, miracles that cannot be counted.
chapters.zh: 他行大事不可测度，行奇事不可胜数。

chapters.en: He provides rain for the earth; he sends water on the countryside.
chapters.zh: 降雨在地上，赐水于田里。

chapters.en: The lowly he sets on high, and those who mourn are lifted to safety.
chapters.zh: 将卑微的安置在高处，将哀痛的举到稳妥之地。

chapters.en: He thwarts the plans of the crafty, so that their hands achieve no success.
chapters.zh: 破坏狡猾人的计谋，使他们所谋的不得成就。

chapters.en: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and the schemes of the wily are swept away.
chapters.zh: 他叫有智慧的中了自己的诡计，使狡诈人的计谋速速灭亡。

chapters.en: Darkness comes upon them in the daytime; at noon they grope as in the night.
chapters.zh: 他们白昼遇见黑暗，午间摸索如在夜间。

chapters.en: He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth; he saves them from the clutches of the powerful.
chapters.zh: 神拯救穷乏人，脱离他们口中的刀，和强暴人的手。

chapters.en: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
chapters.zh: 这样，贫寒的人有指望，罪孽之辈必塞口无言。

chapters.en: “Blessed is the one whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 神所惩治的人是有福的。所以你不可轻看全能者的管教。

chapters.en: For he wounds, but he also binds up; he injures, but his hands also heal.
chapters.zh: 因为他打破，又缠裹。他击伤，用手医治。

chapters.en: From six calamities he will rescue you; in seven no harm will touch you.
chapters.zh: 你六次遭难，他必救你。就是七次，灾祸也无法害你。

chapters.en: In famine he will deliver you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.
chapters.zh: 在饥荒中，他必救你脱离死亡。在争战中，他必救你脱离刀剑的权力。

chapters.en: You will be protected from the lash of the tongue, and need not fear when destruction comes.
chapters.zh: 你必被隐藏，不受口舌之害。灾殃临到，你也不惧怕。

chapters.en: You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the wild animals.
chapters.zh: 你遇见灾害饥馑，就必嬉笑。地上的野兽，你也不惧怕。

chapters.en: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
chapters.zh: 因为你必与田间的石头立约，田里的野兽也必与你和好。

chapters.en: You will know that your tent is secure; you will take stock of your property and find nothing missing.
chapters.zh: 你必知道你帐棚平安，要查看你的羊圈，一无所失。

chapters.en: You will know that your children will be many, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
chapters.zh: 也必知道你的后裔将来发达，你的子孙像地上的青草。

chapters.en: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like sheaves gathered in season.
chapters.zh: 你必寿高年迈才归坟墓，好像禾捆到时收藏。

chapters.en: “We have examined this, and it is true. So hear it and apply it to yourself.”
chapters.zh: 这理，我们已经考察，本是如此。你须要听，要知道是与自己有益。

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说，

chapters.en: “If only my anguish could be weighed and all my misery be placed on the scales!
chapters.zh: 惟愿我的烦恼称一称，我一切的灾害放在天平里。

chapters.en: It would surely outweigh the sand of the seas— no wonder my words have been impetuous.
chapters.zh: 现今都比海沙更重，所以我的言语急躁。

chapters.en: The arrows of the Almighty are in me, my spirit drinks in their poison; God’s terrors are marshaled against me.
chapters.zh: 因全能者的箭射入我身，其毒，我的灵喝尽了。神的惊吓摆阵攻击我。

chapters.en: Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass, or an ox bellow when it has fodder?
chapters.zh: 野驴有草岂能叫唤，牛有料，岂能吼叫。

chapters.en: Is tasteless food eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the sap of the mallow ?
chapters.zh: 物淡而无盐岂可吃吗？蛋青有什么滋味呢？

chapters.en: I refuse to touch it; such food makes me ill.
chapters.zh: 看为可厌的食物，我心不肯挨近。

chapters.en: “Oh, that I might have my request, that God would grant what I hope for,
chapters.zh: 惟愿我得着所求的，愿神赐我所切望的。

chapters.en: that God would be willing to crush me, to let loose his hand and cut off my life!
chapters.zh: 就是愿神把我压碎，伸手将我剪除。

chapters.en: Then I would still have this consolation— my joy in unrelenting pain— that I had not denied the words of the Holy One.
chapters.zh: 我因没有违弃那圣者的言语，就仍以此为安慰，在不止息的痛苦中还可踊跃。

chapters.en: “What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What prospects, that I should be patient?
chapters.zh: 我有什么气力使我等候。我有什么结局使我忍耐。

chapters.en: Do I have the strength of stone? Is my flesh bronze?
chapters.zh: 我的气力岂是石头的气力。我的肉身岂是铜的呢？

chapters.en: Do I have any power to help myself, now that success has been driven from me?
chapters.zh: 在我岂不是毫无帮助吗？智慧岂不是从我心中赶出净尽吗？

chapters.en: “Anyone who withholds kindness from a friend forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 那将要灰心，离弃全能者，不敬畏神的人，他的朋友当以慈爱待他。

chapters.en: But my brothers are as undependable as intermittent streams, as the streams that overflow
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄诡诈，好像溪水，又像溪水流干的河道。

chapters.en: when darkened by thawing ice and swollen with melting snow,
chapters.zh: 这河因结冰发黑，有雪藏在其中。

chapters.en: but that stop flowing in the dry season, and in the heat vanish from their channels.
chapters.zh: 天气渐暖就随时消化，日头炎热便从原处干涸。

chapters.en: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go off into the wasteland and perish.
chapters.zh: 结伴的客旅离弃大道，顺河边行，到荒野之地死亡。

chapters.en: The caravans of Tema look for water, the traveling merchants of Sheba look in hope.
chapters.zh: 提玛结伴的客旅瞻望。示巴同伙的人等候。

chapters.en: They are distressed, because they had been confident; they arrive there, only to be disappointed.
chapters.zh: 他们因失了盼望就抱愧，来到那里便蒙羞。

chapters.en: Now you too have proved to be of no help; you see something dreadful and are afraid.
chapters.zh: 现在你们正是这样，看见惊吓的事便惧怕。

chapters.en: Have I ever said, ‘Give something on my behalf, pay a ransom for me from your wealth,
chapters.zh: 我岂说，请你们供给我，从你们的财物中送礼物给我。

chapters.en: deliver me from the hand of the enemy, rescue me from the clutches of the ruthless’?
chapters.zh: 岂说，拯救我脱离敌人的手吗？救赎我脱离强暴人的手吗？

chapters.en: “Teach me, and I will be quiet; show me where I have been wrong.
chapters.zh: 请你们教导我，我便不作声。使我明白在何事上有错。

chapters.en: How painful are honest words! But what do your arguments prove?
chapters.zh: 正直的言语力量何其大。但你们责备是责备什么呢？

chapters.en: Do you mean to correct what I say, and treat my desperate words as wind?
chapters.zh: 绝望人的讲论既然如风，你们还想要驳正言语吗？

chapters.en: You would even cast lots for the fatherless and barter away your friend.
chapters.zh: 你们想为孤儿拈阄，以朋友当货物。

chapters.en: “But now be so kind as to look at me. Would I lie to your face?
chapters.zh: 现在请你们看看我，我决不当面说谎。

chapters.en: Relent, do not be unjust; reconsider, for my integrity is at stake.
chapters.zh: 请你们转意，不要不公。请再转意，我的事有理。

chapters.en: Is there any wickedness on my lips? Can my mouth not discern malice?
chapters.zh: 我的舌上岂有不义吗？我的口里岂不辨奸恶吗？

chapters.en: “Do not mortals have hard service on earth? Are not their days like those of hired laborers?
chapters.zh: 人在世上岂无争战吗？他的日子不像雇工人的日子吗？

chapters.en: Like a slave longing for the evening shadows, or a hired laborer waiting to be paid,
chapters.zh: 像奴仆切慕黑影，像雇工人盼望工价。

chapters.en: so I have been allotted months of futility, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.
chapters.zh: 我也照样经过困苦的日月，夜间的疲乏为我而定。

chapters.en: When I lie down I think, ‘How long before I get up?’ The night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.
chapters.zh: 我躺卧的时候便说，我何时起来，黑夜就过去呢？我尽是反来覆去，直到天亮。

chapters.en: My body is clothed with worms and scabs, my skin is broken and festering.
chapters.zh: 我的肉体以虫子和尘土为衣。我的皮肤才收了口又重新破裂。

chapters.en: “My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.
chapters.zh: 我的日子比梭更快，都消耗在无指望之中。

chapters.en: Remember, O God, that my life is but a breath; my eyes will never see happiness again.
chapters.zh: 求你想念，我的生命不过是一口气。我的眼睛必不再见福乐。

chapters.en: The eye that now sees me will see me no longer; you will look for me, but I will be no more.
chapters.zh: 观看我的人，他的眼必不再见我。你的眼目要看我，我却不在了。

chapters.en: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so one who goes down to the grave does not return.
chapters.zh: 云彩消散而过。照样，人下阴间也不再上来。

chapters.en: He will never come to his house again; his place will know him no more.
chapters.zh: 他不再回自己的家，故土也不再认识他。

chapters.en: “Therefore I will not keep silent; I will speak out in the anguish of my spirit, I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
chapters.zh: 我不禁止我口。我灵愁苦，要发出言语。我心苦恼，要吐露哀情。

chapters.en: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that you put me under guard?
chapters.zh: 我对神说，我岂是洋海，岂是大鱼，你竟防守我呢？

chapters.en: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,
chapters.zh: 若说，我的床必安慰我，我的榻必解释我的苦情。

chapters.en: even then you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
chapters.zh: 你就用梦惊骇我，用异象恐吓我。

chapters.en: so that I prefer strangling and death, rather than this body of mine.
chapters.zh: 甚至我宁肯噎死，宁肯死亡，胜似留我这一身的骨头。

chapters.en: I despise my life; I would not live forever. Let me alone; my days have no meaning.
chapters.zh: 我厌弃性命，不愿永活。你任凭我吧，因我的日子都是虚空。

chapters.en: “What is mankind that you make so much of them, that you give them so much attention,
chapters.zh: 人算什么，你竟看他为大，将他放在心上，

chapters.en: that you examine them every morning and test them every moment?
chapters.zh: 每早鉴察他，时刻试验他。

chapters.en: Will you never look away from me, or let me alone even for an instant?
chapters.zh: 你到何时才转眼不看我，才任凭我咽下唾沫呢？

chapters.en: If I have sinned, what have I done to you, you who see everything we do? Why have you made me your target? Have I become a burden to you?
chapters.zh: 鉴察人的主阿，我若有罪，于你何妨？为何以我当你的箭靶子，使我厌弃自己的性命？

chapters.en: Why do you not pardon my offenses and forgive my sins? For I will soon lie down in the dust; you will search for me, but I will be no more.”
chapters.zh: 为何不赦免我的过犯，除掉我的罪孽。我现今要躺卧在尘土中。你要殷勤地寻找我，我却不在了。

chapters.en: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
chapters.zh: 书亚人比勒达回答说，

chapters.en: “How long will you say such things? Your words are a blustering wind.
chapters.zh: 这些话你要说到几时？口中的言语如狂风要到几时呢？

chapters.en: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?
chapters.zh: 神岂能偏离公平？全能者岂能偏离公义？

chapters.en: When your children sinned against him, he gave them over to the penalty of their sin.
chapters.zh: 或者你的儿女得罪了他，他使他们受报应。

chapters.en: But if you will seek God earnestly and plead with the Almighty,
chapters.zh: 你若殷勤地寻求神，向全能者恳求。

chapters.en: if you are pure and upright, even now he will rouse himself on your behalf and restore you to your prosperous state.
chapters.zh: 你若清洁正直，他必定为你起来，使你公义的居所兴旺。

chapters.en: Your beginnings will seem humble, so prosperous will your future be.
chapters.zh: 你起初虽然微小，终久必甚发达。

chapters.en: “Ask the former generation and find out what their ancestors learned,
chapters.zh: 请你考问前代，追念他们的列祖所查究的。

chapters.en: for we were born only yesterday and know nothing, and our days on earth are but a shadow.
chapters.zh: （我们不过从昨日才有，一无所知。我们在世的日子好像影儿。）

chapters.en: Will they not instruct you and tell you? Will they not bring forth words from their understanding?
chapters.zh: 他们岂不指教你，告诉你，从心里发出言语来呢？

chapters.en: Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh? Can reeds thrive without water?
chapters.zh: 蒲草没有泥，岂能发长？芦荻没有水，岂能生发？

chapters.en: While still growing and uncut, they wither more quickly than grass.
chapters.zh: 尚青的时候，还没有割下，比百样的草先枯槁。

chapters.en: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so perishes the hope of the godless.
chapters.zh: 凡忘记神的人，景况也是这样。不虔敬人的指望要灭没。

chapters.en: What they trust in is fragile ; what they rely on is a spider’s web.
chapters.zh: 他所仰赖的必折断，他所倚靠的是蜘蛛网。

chapters.en: They lean on the web, but it gives way; they cling to it, but it does not hold.
chapters.zh: 他要倚靠房屋，房屋却站立不住。他要抓住房屋，房屋却不能存留。

chapters.en: They are like a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden;
chapters.zh: 他在日光之下发青，蔓子爬满了园子。

chapters.en: it entwines its roots around a pile of rocks and looks for a place among the stones.
chapters.zh: 他的根盘绕石堆，扎入石地。

chapters.en: But when it is torn from its spot, that place disowns it and says, ‘I never saw you.’
chapters.zh: 他若从本地被拔出，那地就不认识他，说，我没有见过你。

chapters.en: Surely its life withers away, and from the soil other plants grow.
chapters.zh: 看哪，这就是他道中之乐。以后必另有人从地而生。

chapters.en: “Surely God does not reject one who is blameless or strengthen the hands of evildoers.
chapters.zh: 神必不丢弃完全人，也不扶助邪恶人。

chapters.en: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy.
chapters.zh: 他还要以喜笑充满你的口，以欢呼充满你的嘴。

chapters.en: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tents of the wicked will be no more.”
chapters.zh: 恨恶你的要披戴惭愧。恶人的帐棚，必归于无有。

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说，

chapters.en: “Indeed, I know that this is true. But how can mere mortals prove their innocence before God?
chapters.zh: 我真知道是这样。但人在神面前怎能成为义呢？

chapters.en: Though they wished to dispute with him, they could not answer him one time out of a thousand.
chapters.zh: 若愿意与他争辩，千中之一也不能回答。

chapters.en: His wisdom is profound, his power is vast. Who has resisted him and come out unscathed?
chapters.zh: 他心里有智慧，且大有能力。谁向神刚硬而得亨通呢？

chapters.en: He moves mountains without their knowing it and overturns them in his anger.
chapters.zh: 他发怒，把山翻倒挪移，山并不知觉。

chapters.en: He shakes the earth from its place and makes its pillars tremble.
chapters.zh: 他使地震动，离其本位，地的柱子就摇撼。

chapters.en: He speaks to the sun and it does not shine; he seals off the light of the stars.
chapters.zh: 他吩咐日头不出来，就不出来，又封闭众星。

chapters.en: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.
chapters.zh: 他独自铺张苍天，步行在海浪之上。

chapters.en: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.
chapters.zh: 他造北斗，参星，昴星，并南方的密宫。

chapters.en: He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed, miracles that cannot be counted.
chapters.zh: 他行大事，不可测度，行奇事，不可胜数。

chapters.en: When he passes me, I cannot see him; when he goes by, I cannot perceive him.
chapters.zh: 他从我旁边经过，我却不看见。他在我面前行走，我倒不知觉。

chapters.en: If he snatches away, who can stop him? Who can say to him, ‘What are you doing?’
chapters.zh: 他夺取，谁能阻挡。谁敢问他，你做什么。

chapters.en: God does not restrain his anger; even the cohorts of Rahab cowered at his feet.
chapters.zh: 神必不收回他的怒气。扶助拉哈伯的，屈身在他以下。

chapters.en: “How then can I dispute with him? How can I find words to argue with him?
chapters.zh: 既是这样，我怎敢回答他，怎敢选择言语与他辩论呢？

chapters.en: Though I were innocent, I could not answer him; I could only plead with my Judge for mercy.
chapters.zh: 我虽有义，也不回答他。只要向那审判我的恳求。

chapters.en: Even if I summoned him and he responded, I do not believe he would give me a hearing.
chapters.zh: 我若呼吁，他应允我。我仍不信他真听我的声音。

chapters.en: He would crush me with a storm and multiply my wounds for no reason.
chapters.zh: 他用暴风折断我，无故地加增我的损伤。

chapters.en: He would not let me catch my breath but would overwhelm me with misery.
chapters.zh: 我就是喘一口气，他都不容，倒使我满心苦恼。

chapters.en: If it is a matter of strength, he is mighty! And if it is a matter of justice, who can challenge him ?
chapters.zh: 若论力量，他真有能力。若论审判，他说谁能将我传来呢？

chapters.en: Even if I were innocent, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would pronounce me guilty.
chapters.zh: 我虽有义，自己的口要定我为有罪。我虽完全，我口必显我为弯曲。

chapters.en: “Although I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.
chapters.zh: 我本完全，不顾自己。我厌恶我的性命。

chapters.en: It is all the same; that is why I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’
chapters.zh: 善恶无分，都是一样。所以我说，完全人和恶人，他都灭绝。

chapters.en: When a scourge brings sudden death, he mocks the despair of the innocent.
chapters.zh: 若忽然遭杀害之祸，他必戏笑无辜的人遇难。

chapters.en: When a land falls into the hands of the wicked, he blindfolds its judges. If it is not he, then who is it?
chapters.zh: 世界交在恶人手中。蒙蔽世界审判官的脸，若不是他，是谁呢？

chapters.en: “My days are swifter than a runner; they fly away without a glimpse of joy.
chapters.zh: 我的日子比跑信的更快，急速过去，不见福乐。

chapters.en: They skim past like boats of papyrus, like eagles swooping down on their prey.
chapters.zh: 我的日子过去如快船，如急落抓食的鹰。

chapters.en: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will change my expression, and smile,’
chapters.zh: 我若说，我要忘记我的哀情，除去我的愁容，心中畅快。

chapters.en: I still dread all my sufferings, for I know you will not hold me innocent.
chapters.zh: 我因愁苦而惧怕，知道你必不以我为无辜。

chapters.en: Since I am already found guilty, why should I struggle in vain?
chapters.zh: 我必被你定为有罪，我何必徒然劳苦呢？

chapters.en: Even if I washed myself with soap and my hands with cleansing powder,
chapters.zh: 我若用雪水洗身，用碱洁净我的手。

chapters.en: you would plunge me into a slime pit so that even my clothes would detest me.
chapters.zh: 你还要扔我在坑里，我的衣服都憎恶我。

chapters.en: “He is not a mere mortal like me that I might answer him, that we might confront each other in court.
chapters.zh: 他本不像我是人，使我可以回答他，又使我们可以同听审判。

chapters.en: If only there were someone to mediate between us, someone to bring us together,
chapters.zh: 我们中间没有听讼的人，可以向我们两造按手。

chapters.en: someone to remove God’s rod from me, so that his terror would frighten me no more.
chapters.zh: 愿他把杖离开我，不使惊惶威吓我。

chapters.en: Then I would speak up without fear of him, but as it now stands with me, I cannot.
chapters.zh: 我就说话，也不惧怕他，现在我却不是那样。

chapters.en: “I loathe my very life; therefore I will give free rein to my complaint and speak out in the bitterness of my soul.
chapters.zh: 我厌烦我的性命，必由着自己述说我的哀情。因心里苦恼，我要说话。

chapters.en: I say to God: Do not declare me guilty, but tell me what charges you have against me.
chapters.zh: 对神说，不要定我有罪。要指示我，你为何与我争辩。

chapters.en: Does it please you to oppress me, to spurn the work of your hands, while you smile on the plans of the wicked?
chapters.zh: 你手所造的，你又欺压，又藐视，却光照恶人的计谋。这事你以为美吗？

chapters.en: Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?
chapters.zh: 你的眼岂是肉眼，你查看岂像人查看吗？

chapters.en: Are your days like those of a mortal or your years like those of a strong man,
chapters.zh: 你的日子岂像人的日子，你的年岁岂像人的年岁。

chapters.en: that you must search out my faults and probe after my sin—
chapters.zh: 就追问我的罪孽，寻察我的罪过吗？

chapters.en: though you know that I am not guilty and that no one can rescue me from your hand?
chapters.zh: 其实，你知道我没有罪恶，并没有能救我脱离你手的。

chapters.en: “Your hands shaped me and made me. Will you now turn and destroy me?
chapters.zh: 你的手创造我，造就我的四肢百体，你还要毁灭我。

chapters.en: Remember that you molded me like clay. Will you now turn me to dust again?
chapters.zh: 求你记念制造我如抟泥一般，你还要使我归于尘土吗？

chapters.en: Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese,
chapters.zh: 你不是倒出我来好像奶，使我凝结如同奶饼吗？

chapters.en: clothe me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews?
chapters.zh: 你以皮和肉为衣给我穿上，用骨与筋把我全体联络。

chapters.en: You gave me life and showed me kindness, and in your providence watched over my spirit.
chapters.zh: 你将生命和慈爱赐给我，你也眷顾保全我的心灵。

chapters.en: “But this is what you concealed in your heart, and I know that this was in your mind:
chapters.zh: 然而，你待我的这些事早已藏在你心里，我知道你久有此意。

chapters.en: If I sinned, you would be watching me and would not let my offense go unpunished.
chapters.zh: 我若犯罪，你就察看我，并不赦免我的罪孽。

chapters.en: If I am guilty—woe to me! Even if I am innocent, I cannot lift my head, for I am full of shame and drowned in my affliction.
chapters.zh: 我若行恶，便有了祸。我若为义，也不敢抬头。正是满心羞愧，眼见我的苦情。

chapters.en: If I hold my head high, you stalk me like a lion and again display your awesome power against me.
chapters.zh: 我若昂首自得，你就追捕我如狮子，又在我身上显出奇能。

chapters.en: You bring new witnesses against me and increase your anger toward me; your forces come against me wave upon wave.
chapters.zh: 你重立见证攻击我，向我加增恼怒，如军兵更换着攻击我。

chapters.en: “Why then did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before any eye saw me.
chapters.zh: 你为何使我出母胎呢？不如我当时气绝，无人得见我。

chapters.en: If only I had never come into being, or had been carried straight from the womb to the grave!
chapters.zh: 这样，就如没有我一般，一出母胎就被送入坟墓。

chapters.en: Are not my few days almost over? Turn away from me so I can have a moment’s joy
chapters.zh: 我的日子不是甚少吗？求你停手宽容我，叫我在往而不返之先，就是往黑暗，和死荫之地以先，可以稍得畅快。

chapters.en: before I go to the place of no return, to the land of gloom and utter darkness,
to the land of deepest night, of utter darkness and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”
chapters.zh: 那地甚是幽暗，是死荫混沌之地。那里的光好像幽暗。

chapters.en: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:
chapters.zh: 拿玛人琐法回答说，

chapters.en: “Are all these words to go unanswered? Is this talker to be vindicated?
chapters.zh: 这许多的言语岂不该回答吗？多嘴多舌的人岂可称为义吗？

chapters.en: Will your idle talk reduce others to silence? Will no one rebuke you when you mock?
chapters.zh: 你夸大的话，岂能使人不作声吗？你戏笑的时候，岂没有人叫你害羞吗？

chapters.en: You say to God, ‘My beliefs are flawless and I am pure in your sight.’
chapters.zh: 你说，我的道理纯全，我在你眼前洁净。

chapters.en: Oh, how I wish that God would speak, that he would open his lips against you
chapters.zh: 惟愿神说话，愿他开口攻击你。

chapters.en: and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know this: God has even forgotten some of your sin.
chapters.zh: 并将智慧的奥秘指示你，他有诸般的智识。所以当知道神追讨你，比你罪孽该得的还少。

chapters.en: “Can you fathom the mysteries of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
chapters.zh: 你考察，就能测透神吗？你岂能尽情测透全能者吗？

chapters.en: They are higher than the heavens above—what can you do? They are deeper than the depths below—what can you know?
chapters.zh: 他的智慧高于天，你还能做什么。深于阴间，你还能知道什么。

chapters.en: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
chapters.zh: 其量比地长，比海宽。

chapters.en: “If he comes along and confines you in prison and convenes a court, who can oppose him?
chapters.zh: 他若经过，将人拘禁，招人受审，谁能阻挡他呢？

chapters.en: Surely he recognizes deceivers; and when he sees evil, does he not take note?
chapters.zh: 他本知道虚妄的人。人的罪孽，他虽不留意，还是无所不见。

chapters.en: But the witless can no more become wise than a wild donkey’s colt can be born human.
chapters.zh: 空虚的人却毫无知识。人生在世好像野驴的驹子。

chapters.en: “Yet if you devote your heart to him and stretch out your hands to him,
chapters.zh: 你若将心安正，又向主举手。

chapters.en: if you put away the sin that is in your hand and allow no evil to dwell in your tent,
chapters.zh: 你手里若有罪孽，就当远远地除掉，也不容非义住在你帐棚之中。

chapters.en: then, free of fault, you will lift up your face; you will stand firm and without fear.
chapters.zh: 那时，你必仰起脸来毫无斑点。你也必坚固，无所惧怕。

chapters.en: You will surely forget your trouble, recalling it only as waters gone by.
chapters.zh: 你必忘记你的苦楚，就是想起也如流过去的水一样。

chapters.en: Life will be brighter than noonday, and darkness will become like morning.
chapters.zh: 你在世的日子要比正午更明，虽有黑暗仍像早晨。

chapters.en: You will be secure, because there is hope; you will look about you and take your rest in safety.
chapters.zh: 你因有指望就必稳固，也必四围巡查，坦然安息。

chapters.en: You will lie down, with no one to make you afraid, and many will court your favor.
chapters.zh: 你躺卧，无人惊吓，且有许多人向你求恩。

chapters.en: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; their hope will become a dying gasp.”
chapters.zh: 但恶人的眼目必要失明。他们无路可逃。他们的指望就是气绝。

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说，

chapters.en: “Doubtless you are the only people who matter, and wisdom will die with you!
chapters.zh: 你们真是子民哪，你们死亡，智慧也就灭没了。

chapters.en: But I have a mind as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know all these things?
chapters.zh: 但我也有聪明，与你们一样，并非不及你们。你们所说的，谁不知道呢？

chapters.en: “I have become a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God and he answered— a mere laughingstock, though righteous and blameless!
chapters.zh: 我这求告神，蒙他应允的人，竟成了朋友所讥笑的。公义完全人，竟受了人的讥笑。

chapters.en: Those who are at ease have contempt for misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.
chapters.zh: 安逸的人，心里藐视灾祸。这灾祸常常等待滑脚的人。

chapters.en: The tents of marauders are undisturbed, and those who provoke God are secure— those God has in his hand.
chapters.zh: 强盗的帐棚兴旺，惹神的人稳固，神多将财物送到他们手中。

chapters.en: “But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you;
chapters.zh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你。又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。

chapters.en: or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
chapters.zh: 或与地说话，地必指教你。海中的鱼也必向你说明。

chapters.en: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
chapters.zh: 看这一切，谁不知道是耶和华的手做成的呢？

chapters.en: In his hand is the life of every creature and the breath of all mankind.
chapters.zh: 凡活物的生命，和人类的气息，都在他手中。

chapters.en: Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes food?
chapters.zh: 耳朵岂不试验言语，正如上膛尝食物吗？

chapters.en: Is not wisdom found among the aged? Does not long life bring understanding?
chapters.zh: 年老的有智慧，寿高的有知识。

chapters.en: “To God belong wisdom and power; counsel and understanding are his.
chapters.zh: 在神有智慧和能力，他有谋略和知识。

chapters.en: What he tears down cannot be rebuilt; those he imprisons cannot be released.
chapters.zh: 他拆毁的，就不能再建造。他捆住人，便不得开释。

chapters.en: If he holds back the waters, there is drought; if he lets them loose, they devastate the land.
chapters.zh: 他把水留住，水便枯干。他再发出水来，水就翻地。

chapters.en: To him belong strength and insight; both deceived and deceiver are his.
chapters.zh: 在他有能力和智慧。被诱惑的，与诱惑人的，都是属他。

chapters.en: He leads rulers away stripped and makes fools of judges.
chapters.zh: 他把谋士剥衣掳去，又使审判官变成愚人。

chapters.en: He takes off the shackles put on by kings and ties a loincloth around their waist.
chapters.zh: 他放松君王的绑，又用带子捆他们的腰。

chapters.en: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows officials long established.
chapters.zh: 他把祭司剥衣掳去，又使有能的人倾败。

chapters.en: He silences the lips of trusted advisers and takes away the discernment of elders.
chapters.zh: 他废去忠信人的讲论，又夺去老人的聪明。

chapters.en: He pours contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.
chapters.zh: 他使君王蒙羞被辱，放松有力之人的腰带。

chapters.en: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings utter darkness into the light.
chapters.zh: 他将深奥的事从黑暗中彰显，使死荫显为光明。

chapters.en: He makes nations great, and destroys them; he enlarges nations, and disperses them.
chapters.zh: 他使邦国兴旺而又毁灭，他使邦国开广而又掳去。

chapters.en: He deprives the leaders of the earth of their reason; he makes them wander in a trackless waste.
chapters.zh: 他将地上民中首领的聪明夺去，使他们在荒废无路之地漂流。

chapters.en: They grope in darkness with no light; he makes them stagger like drunkards.
chapters.zh: 他们无光，在黑暗中摸索，又使他们东倒西歪，像醉酒的人一样。

chapters.en: “My eyes have seen all this, my ears have heard and understood it.
chapters.zh: 这一切，我眼都见过。我耳都听过，而且明白。

chapters.en: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
chapters.zh: 你们所知道的，我也知道，并非不及你们。

chapters.en: But I desire to speak to the Almighty and to argue my case with God.
chapters.zh: 我真要对全能者说话。我愿与神理论。

chapters.en: You, however, smear me with lies; you are worthless physicians, all of you!
chapters.zh: 你们是编造谎言的，都是无用的医生。

chapters.en: If only you would be altogether silent! For you, that would be wisdom.
chapters.zh: 惟愿你们全然不作声。这就算为你们的智慧。

chapters.en: Hear now my argument; listen to the pleas of my lips.
chapters.zh: 请你们听我的辩论，留心听我口中的分诉。

chapters.en: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him?
chapters.zh: 你们要为神说不义的话吗？为他说诡诈的言语吗？

chapters.en: Will you show him partiality? Will you argue the case for God?
chapters.zh: 你们要为神徇情吗？要为他争论吗？

chapters.en: Would it turn out well if he examined you? Could you deceive him as you might deceive a mortal?
chapters.zh: 他查出你们来，这岂是好吗？人欺哄人，你们也要照样欺哄他吗？

chapters.en: He would surely call you to account if you secretly showed partiality.
chapters.zh: 你们若暗中徇情，他必要责备你们。

chapters.en: Would not his splendor terrify you? Would not the dread of him fall on you?
chapters.zh: 他的尊荣岂不叫你们惧怕吗？他的惊吓岂不临到你们吗？

chapters.en: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
chapters.zh: 你们以为可记念的箴言是炉灰的箴言。你们以为可靠的坚垒是淤泥的坚垒。

chapters.en: “Keep silent and let me speak; then let come to me what may.
chapters.zh: 你们不要作声，任凭我吧。让我说话，无论如何我都承当。

chapters.en: Why do I put myself in jeopardy and take my life in my hands?
chapters.zh: 我何必把我的肉挂在牙上，将我的命放在手中。

chapters.en: Though he slay me, yet will I hope in him; I will surely defend my ways to his face.
chapters.zh: 他必杀我。我虽无指望，然而我在他面前还要辩明我所行的。

chapters.en: Indeed, this will turn out for my deliverance, for no godless person would dare come before him!
chapters.zh: 这要成为我的拯救，因为不虔诚的人，不得到他面前。

chapters.en: Listen carefully to what I say; let my words ring in your ears.
chapters.zh: 你们要细听我的言语，使我所辩论的入你们的耳中。

chapters.en: Now that I have prepared my case, I know I will be vindicated.
chapters.zh: 我已陈明我的案，知道自己有义。

chapters.en: Can anyone bring charges against me? If so, I will be silent and die.
chapters.zh: 有谁与我争论，我就情愿缄默不言，气绝而亡。

chapters.en: “Only grant me these two things, God, and then I will not hide from you:
chapters.zh: 惟有两件不要向我施行，我就不躲开你的面。

chapters.en: Withdraw your hand far from me, and stop frightening me with your terrors.
chapters.zh: 就是把你的手缩回，远离我身。又不使你的惊惶威吓我。

chapters.en: Then summon me and I will answer, or let me speak, and you reply to me.
chapters.zh: 这样，你呼叫，我就回答。或是让我说话，你回答我。

chapters.en: How many wrongs and sins have I committed? Show me my offense and my sin.
chapters.zh: 我的罪孽和罪过有多少呢？求你叫我知道我的过犯与罪愆。

chapters.en: Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?
chapters.zh: 你为何掩面，拿我当仇敌呢？

chapters.en: Will you torment a windblown leaf? Will you chase after dry chaff?
chapters.zh: 你要惊动被风吹的叶子吗？要追赶枯干的碎秸吗？

chapters.en: For you write down bitter things against me and make me reap the sins of my youth.
chapters.zh: 你按罪状刑罚我，又使我担当幼年的罪孽。

chapters.en: You fasten my feet in shackles; you keep close watch on all my paths by putting marks on the soles of my feet.
chapters.zh: 也把我的脚上了木狗，并窥察我一切的道路，为我的脚掌划定界限。
