chapters.en: “So man wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.
chapters.zh: 我已经像灭绝的烂物，像虫蛀的衣裳。

chapters.en: “Mortals, born of woman, are of few days and full of trouble.
chapters.zh: 人为妇人所生，日子短少，多有患难。

chapters.en: They spring up like flowers and wither away; like fleeting shadows, they do not endure.
chapters.zh: 出来如花，又被割下。飞去如影，不能存留。

chapters.en: Do you fix your eye on them? Will you bring them before you for judgment?
chapters.zh: 这样的人你岂睁眼看他吗？又叫我来受审吗？

chapters.en: Who can bring what is pure from the impure? No one!
chapters.zh: 谁能使洁净之物出于污秽之中呢？无论谁也不能。

chapters.en: A person’s days are determined; you have decreed the number of his months and have set limits he cannot exceed.
chapters.zh: 人的日子既然限定，他的月数在你那里，你也派定他的界限，使他不能越过。

chapters.en: So look away from him and let him alone, till he has put in his time like a hired laborer.
chapters.zh: 便求你转眼不看他，使他得歇息。直等他像雇工人完毕他的日子。

chapters.en: “At least there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its new shoots will not fail.
chapters.zh: 树若被砍下，还可指望发芽，嫩枝生长不息。

chapters.en: Its roots may grow old in the ground and its stump die in the soil,
chapters.zh: 其根虽然衰老在地里，干也死在土中。

chapters.en: yet at the scent of water it will bud and put forth shoots like a plant.
chapters.zh: 及至得了水气，还要发芽，又长枝条，像新栽的树一样。

chapters.en: But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last and is no more.
chapters.zh: 但人死亡而消灭。他气绝，竟在何处呢？

chapters.en: As the water of a lake dries up or a riverbed becomes parched and dry,
chapters.zh: 海中的水绝尽，江河消散干涸。

chapters.en: so he lies down and does not rise; till the heavens are no more, people will not awake or be roused from their sleep.
chapters.zh: 人也是如此，躺下不再起来。等到天没有了，仍不得复醒，也不得从睡中唤醒。

chapters.en: “If only you would hide me in the grave and conceal me till your anger has passed! If only you would set me a time and then remember me!
chapters.zh: 惟愿你把我藏在阴间，存于隐密处，等你的忿怒过去。愿你为我定了日期，记念我。

chapters.en: If someone dies, will they live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait for my renewal to come.
chapters.zh: 人若死了岂能再活呢？我只要在我一切争战的日子，等我被释放的时候来到（被释放或作改变）。

chapters.en: You will call and I will answer you; you will long for the creature your hands have made.
chapters.zh: 你呼叫，我便回答。你手所做的，你必羡慕。

chapters.en: Surely then you will count my steps but not keep track of my sin.
chapters.zh: 但如今你数点我的脚步，岂不窥察我的罪过吗？

chapters.en: My offenses will be sealed up in a bag; you will cover over my sin.
chapters.zh: 我的过犯被你封在囊中，也缝严了我的罪孽。

chapters.en: “But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and as a rock is moved from its place,
chapters.zh: 山崩变为无有。磐石挪开原处。

chapters.en: as water wears away stones and torrents wash away the soil, so you destroy a person’s hope.
chapters.zh: 水流消磨石头，所流溢的洗去地上的尘土。你也照样灭绝人的指望。

chapters.en: You overpower them once for all, and they are gone; you change their countenance and send them away.
chapters.zh: 你攻击人常常得胜，使他去世。你改变他的容貌，叫他往而不回。

chapters.en: If their children are honored, they do not know it; if their offspring are brought low, they do not see it.
chapters.zh: 他儿子得尊荣，他也不知道。降为卑，他也不觉得。

chapters.en: They feel but the pain of their own bodies and mourn only for themselves.”
chapters.zh: 但知身上疼痛，心中悲哀。

chapters.en: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
chapters.zh: 提幔人以利法回答说，

chapters.en: “Would a wise person answer with empty notions or fill their belly with the hot east wind?
chapters.zh: 智慧人岂可用虚空的知识回答，用东风充满肚腹呢？

chapters.en: Would they argue with useless words, with speeches that have no value?
chapters.zh: 他岂可用无益的话，和无济于事的言语，理论呢？

chapters.en: But you even undermine piety and hinder devotion to God.
chapters.zh: 你是废弃敬畏的意，在神面前阻止敬虔的心。

chapters.en: Your sin prompts your mouth; you adopt the tongue of the crafty.
chapters.zh: 你的罪孽指教你的口。你选用诡诈人的舌头。

chapters.en: Your own mouth condemns you, not mine; your own lips testify against you.
chapters.zh: 你自己的口定你有罪，并非是我。你自己的嘴，见证你的不是。

chapters.en: “Are you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
chapters.zh: 你岂是头一个被生的人吗？你受造在诸山之先吗？

chapters.en: Do you listen in on God’s council? Do you have a monopoly on wisdom?
chapters.zh: 你曾听见神的密旨吗？你还将智慧独自得尽吗？

chapters.en: What do you know that we do not know? What insights do you have that we do not have?
chapters.zh: 你知道什么是我们不知道的呢？你明白什么是我们不明白的呢？

chapters.en: The gray-haired and the aged are on our side, men even older than your father.
chapters.zh: 我们这里有白发的，和年纪老迈的，比你父亲还老。

chapters.en: Are God’s consolations not enough for you, words spoken gently to you?
chapters.zh: 神用温和的话安慰你，你以为太小吗？

chapters.en: Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash,
chapters.zh: 你的心为何将你逼去。你的眼为何冒出火星。

chapters.en: so that you vent your rage against God and pour out such words from your mouth?
chapters.zh: 使你的灵反对神，也任你的口发这言语。

chapters.en: “What are mortals, that they could be pure, or those born of woman, that they could be righteous?
chapters.zh: 人是什么，竟算为洁净呢？妇人所生的是什么，竟算为义呢？

chapters.en: If God places no trust in his holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in his eyes,
chapters.zh: 神不信靠他的众圣者。在他眼前，天也不洁净。

chapters.en: how much less mortals, who are vile and corrupt, who drink up evil like water!
chapters.zh: 何况那污秽可憎，喝罪孽如水的世人呢？

chapters.en: “Listen to me and I will explain to you; let me tell you what I have seen,
chapters.zh: 我指示你，你要听。我要述说所看见的。

chapters.en: what the wise have declared, hiding nothing received from their ancestors
chapters.zh: 就是智慧人从列祖所受，传说而不隐瞒的。

chapters.en: (to whom alone the land was given when no foreigners moved among them):
chapters.zh: （这地惟独赐给他们，并没有外人从他们中间经过）。

chapters.en: All his days the wicked man suffers torment, the ruthless man through all the years stored up for him.
chapters.zh: 恶人一生之日劬劳痛苦，强暴人一生的年数也是如此。

chapters.en: Terrifying sounds fill his ears; when all seems well, marauders attack him.
chapters.zh: 惊吓的声音常在他耳中。在平安时，抢夺的必临到他那里。

chapters.en: He despairs of escaping the realm of darkness; he is marked for the sword.
chapters.zh: 他不信自己能从黑暗中转回，他被刀剑等候。

chapters.en: He wanders about for food like a vulture; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.
chapters.zh: 他漂流在外求食，说，哪里有食物呢？他知道黑暗的日子，在他手边预备好了。

chapters.en: Distress and anguish fill him with terror; troubles overwhelm him, like a king poised to attack,
chapters.zh: 急难困苦叫他害怕，而且胜了他，好像君王预备上阵一样。

chapters.en: because he shakes his fist at God and vaunts himself against the Almighty,
chapters.zh: 他伸手攻击神，以骄傲攻击全能者。

chapters.en: defiantly charging against him with a thick, strong shield.
chapters.zh: 挺着颈项，用盾牌的厚凸面，向全能者直闯。

chapters.en: “Though his face is covered with fat and his waist bulges with flesh,
chapters.zh: 是因他的脸蒙上脂油，腰积成肥肉。

chapters.en: he will inhabit ruined towns and houses where no one lives, houses crumbling to rubble.
chapters.zh: 他曾住在荒凉城邑，无人居住，将成乱堆的房屋。

chapters.en: He will no longer be rich and his wealth will not endure, nor will his possessions spread over the land.
chapters.zh: 他不得富足，财物不得常存，产业在地上也不加增。

chapters.en: He will not escape the darkness; a flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God’s mouth will carry him away.
chapters.zh: 他不得出离黑暗。火焰要将他的枝子烧干。因神口中的气，他要灭亡（灭亡原文作走去）。

chapters.en: Let him not deceive himself by trusting what is worthless, for he will get nothing in return.
chapters.zh: 他不用倚靠虚假欺哄自己，因虚假必成为他的报应。

chapters.en: Before his time he will wither, and his branches will not flourish.
chapters.zh: 他的日期未到之先，这事必成就。他的枝子不得青绿。

chapters.en: He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree shedding its blossoms.
chapters.zh: 他必像葡萄树的葡萄，未熟而落。又像橄榄树的花，一开而谢。

chapters.en: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of those who love bribes.
chapters.zh: 原来不敬虔之辈必无生育。受贿赂之人的帐棚必被火烧。

chapters.en: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb fashions deceit.”
chapters.zh: 他们所怀的是毒害，所生的是罪孽，心里所预备的是诡诈。

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说，

chapters.en: “I have heard many things like these; you are miserable comforters, all of you!
chapters.zh: 这样的话我听了许多。你们安慰人，反叫人愁烦。

chapters.en: Will your long-winded speeches never end? What ails you that you keep on arguing?
chapters.zh: 虚空的言语有穷尽吗？有什么话惹动你回答呢？

chapters.en: I also could speak like you, if you were in my place; I could make fine speeches against you and shake my head at you.
chapters.zh: 我也能说你们那样的话。你们若处在我的境遇，我也会联络言语攻击你们，又能向你们摇头。

chapters.en: But my mouth would encourage you; comfort from my lips would bring you relief.
chapters.zh: 但我必用口坚固你们，用嘴消解你们的忧愁。

chapters.en: “Yet if I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I refrain, it does not go away.
chapters.zh: 我虽说话，忧愁仍不得消解。我虽停住不说，忧愁就离开我吗？

chapters.en: Surely, God, you have worn me out; you have devastated my entire household.
chapters.zh: 但现在神使我困倦，使亲友远离我。

chapters.en: You have shriveled me up—and it has become a witness; my gauntness rises up and testifies against me.
chapters.zh: 又抓住我，作见证攻击我。我身体的枯瘦，也当面见证我的不是。

chapters.en: God assails me and tears me in his anger and gnashes his teeth at me; my opponent fastens on me his piercing eyes.
chapters.zh: 主发怒撕裂我，逼迫我，向我切齿。我的敌人怒目看我。

chapters.en: People open their mouths to jeer at me; they strike my cheek in scorn and unite together against me.
chapters.zh: 他们向我开口，打我的脸羞辱我，聚会攻击我。

chapters.en: God has turned me over to the ungodly and thrown me into the clutches of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 神把我交给不敬虔的人，把我扔到恶人的手中。

chapters.en: All was well with me, but he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and crushed me. He has made me his target;
chapters.zh: 我素来安逸，他折断我，掐住我的颈项，把我摔碎。又立我为他的箭靶子。

chapters.en: his archers surround me. Without pity, he pierces my kidneys and spills my gall on the ground.
chapters.zh: 他的弓箭手四面围绕我。他破裂我的肺腑，并不留情，把我的胆倾倒在地上，

chapters.en: Again and again he bursts upon me; he rushes at me like a warrior.
chapters.zh: 将我破裂又破裂，如同勇士向我直闯。

chapters.en: “I have sewed sackcloth over my skin and buried my brow in the dust.
chapters.zh: 我缝麻布在我皮肤上，把我的角放在尘土中。

chapters.en: My face is red with weeping, dark shadows ring my eyes;
chapters.zh: 我的脸因哭泣发紫，在我的眼皮上有死荫。

chapters.en: yet my hands have been free of violence and my prayer is pure.
chapters.zh: 我的手中却无强暴。我的祈祷也是清洁。

chapters.en: “Earth, do not cover my blood; may my cry never be laid to rest!
chapters.zh: 地阿，不要遮盖我的血。不要阻挡我的哀求。

chapters.en: Even now my witness is in heaven; my advocate is on high.
chapters.zh: 现今，在天有我的见证，在上有我的中保。

chapters.en: My intercessor is my friend as my eyes pour out tears to God;
chapters.zh: 我的朋友讥诮我，我却向神眼泪汪汪。

chapters.en: on behalf of a man he pleads with God as one pleads for a friend.
chapters.zh: 愿人得与神辩白，如同人与朋友辩白一样。

chapters.en: “Only a few years will pass before I take the path of no return.
chapters.zh: 因为再过几年，我必走那往而不返之路。

chapters.en: My spirit is broken, my days are cut short, the grave awaits me.
chapters.zh: 我的心灵消耗，我的日子灭尽。坟墓为我预备好了。

chapters.en: Surely mockers surround me; my eyes must dwell on their hostility.
chapters.zh: 真有戏笑我的在我这里，我眼常见他们惹动我。

chapters.en: “Give me, O God, the pledge you demand. Who else will put up security for me?
chapters.zh: 愿主拿凭据给我，自己为我作保。在你以外谁肯与我击掌呢？

chapters.en: You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore you will not let them triumph.
chapters.zh: 因你使他们心不明理，所以你必不高举他们。

chapters.en: If anyone denounces their friends for reward, the eyes of their children will fail.
chapters.zh: 控告他的朋友，以朋友为可抢夺的，连他儿女的眼睛也要失明。

chapters.en: “God has made me a byword to everyone, a man in whose face people spit.
chapters.zh: 神使我作了民中的笑谈。他们也吐唾沫在我脸上。

chapters.en: My eyes have grown dim with grief; my whole frame is but a shadow.
chapters.zh: 我的眼睛因忧愁昏花。我的百体好像影儿。

chapters.en: The upright are appalled at this; the innocent are aroused against the ungodly.
chapters.zh: 正直人因此必惊奇。无辜的人，要兴起攻击不敬虔之辈。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, the righteous will hold to their ways, and those with clean hands will grow stronger.
chapters.zh: 然而，义人要持守所行的道。手洁的人要力上加力。

chapters.en: “But come on, all of you, try again! I will not find a wise man among you.
chapters.zh: 至于你们众人，可以再来辩论吧。你们中间，我找不着一个智慧人。

chapters.en: My days have passed, my plans are shattered. Yet the desires of my heart
chapters.zh: 我的日子已经过了。我的谋算，我心所想望的已经断绝。

chapters.en: turn night into day; in the face of the darkness light is near.
chapters.zh: 他们以黑夜为白昼，说，亮光近乎黑暗。

chapters.en: If the only home I hope for is the grave, if I spread out my bed in the realm of darkness,
chapters.zh: 我若盼望阴间为我的房屋，若下榻在黑暗中，

chapters.en: if I say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother’ or ‘My sister,’
chapters.zh: 若对朽坏说，你是我的父。对虫说，你是我的母亲姐妹。

chapters.en: where then is my hope— who can see any hope for me?
chapters.zh: 这样，我的指望在哪里呢？我所指望的谁能看见呢？

chapters.en: Will it go down to the gates of death? Will we descend together into the dust?”
chapters.zh: 等到安息在尘土中，这指望必下到阴间的门闩那里了。

chapters.en: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
chapters.zh: 书亚人比勒达回答说，

chapters.en: “When will you end these speeches? Be sensible, and then we can talk.
chapters.zh: 你寻索言语要到几时呢？你可以揣摩思想，然后我们就说话。

chapters.en: Why are we regarded as cattle and considered stupid in your sight?
chapters.zh: 我们为何算为畜生，在你眼中看作污秽呢？

chapters.en: You who tear yourself to pieces in your anger, is the earth to be abandoned for your sake? Or must the rocks be moved from their place?
chapters.zh: 你这恼怒将自己撕裂的，难道大地为你见弃，磐石挪开原处吗？

chapters.en: “The lamp of a wicked man is snuffed out; the flame of his fire stops burning.
chapters.zh: 恶人的亮光必要熄灭。他的火焰必不照耀。

chapters.en: The light in his tent becomes dark; the lamp beside him goes out.
chapters.zh: 他帐棚中的亮光要变为黑暗。他以上的灯也必熄灭。

chapters.en: The vigor of his step is weakened; his own schemes throw him down.
chapters.zh: 他坚强的脚步必见狭窄。自己的计谋必将他绊倒。

chapters.en: His feet thrust him into a net; he wanders into its mesh.
chapters.zh: 因为他被自己的脚陷入网中，走在缠人的网罗上。

chapters.en: A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare holds him fast.
chapters.zh: 圈套必抓住他的脚跟。机关必擒获他。

chapters.en: A noose is hidden for him on the ground; a trap lies in his path.
chapters.zh: 活扣为他藏在土内。羁绊为他藏在路上。

chapters.en: Terrors startle him on every side and dog his every step.
chapters.zh: 四面的惊吓要使他害怕，并且追赶他的脚跟。

chapters.en: Calamity is hungry for him; disaster is ready for him when he falls.
chapters.zh: 他的力量必因饥饿衰败，祸患要在他旁边等候。

chapters.en: It eats away parts of his skin; death’s firstborn devours his limbs.
chapters.zh: 他本身的肢体要被吞吃，死亡的长子要吞吃他的肢体。

chapters.en: He is torn from the security of his tent and marched off to the king of terrors.
chapters.zh: 他要从所倚靠的帐棚被拔出来，带到惊吓的王那里。

chapters.en: Fire resides in his tent; burning sulfur is scattered over his dwelling.
chapters.zh: 不属他的必住在他的帐棚里。硫磺必撒在他所住之处。

chapters.en: His roots dry up below and his branches wither above.
chapters.zh: 下边，他的根本要枯干。上边，他的枝子要剪除。

chapters.en: The memory of him perishes from the earth; he has no name in the land.
chapters.zh: 他的记念在地上必然灭亡。他的名字在街上也不存留。

chapters.en: He is driven from light into the realm of darkness and is banished from the world.
chapters.zh: 他必从光明中被撵到黑暗里，必被赶出世界。

chapters.en: He has no offspring or descendants among his people, no survivor where once he lived.
chapters.zh: 在本民中必无子无孙。在寄居之地也无一人存留。

chapters.en: People of the west are appalled at his fate; those of the east are seized with horror.
chapters.zh: 以后来的要惊奇他的日子，好像以前去的受了惊骇。

chapters.en: Surely such is the dwelling of an evil man; such is the place of one who does not know God.”
chapters.zh: 不义之人的住处总是这样。此乃不认识神之人的地步。

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说，

chapters.en: “How long will you torment me and crush me with words?
chapters.zh: 你们搅扰我的心，用言语压碎我，要到几时呢？

chapters.en: Ten times now you have reproached me; shamelessly you attack me.
chapters.zh: 你们这十次羞辱我。你们苦待我也不以为耻。

chapters.en: If it is true that I have gone astray, my error remains my concern alone.
chapters.zh: 果真我有错，这错乃是在我。

chapters.en: If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me and use my humiliation against me,
chapters.zh: 你们果然要向我夸大，以我的羞辱为证指责我。

chapters.en: then know that God has wronged me and drawn his net around me.
chapters.zh: 就该知道是神倾覆我，用网罗围绕我。

chapters.en: “Though I cry, ‘Violence!’ I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.
chapters.zh: 我因委曲呼叫，却不蒙应允。我呼求，却不得公断。

chapters.en: He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; he has shrouded my paths in darkness.
chapters.zh: 神用篱笆拦住我的道路，使我不得经过。又使我的路径黑暗。

chapters.en: He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.
chapters.zh: 他剥去我的荣光，摘去我头上的冠冕。

chapters.en: He tears me down on every side till I am gone; he uproots my hope like a tree.
chapters.zh: 他在四围攻击我，我便归于死亡，将我的指望如树拔出来。

chapters.en: His anger burns against me; he counts me among his enemies.
chapters.zh: 他的忿怒向我发作，以我为敌人。

chapters.en: His troops advance in force; they build a siege ramp against me and encamp around my tent.
chapters.zh: 他的军旅一齐上来，修筑战路攻击我。在我帐棚的四围安营。

chapters.en: “He has alienated my family from me; my acquaintances are completely estranged from me.
chapters.zh: 他把我的弟兄隔在远处，使我所认识的，全然与我生疏。

chapters.en: My relatives have gone away; my closest friends have forgotten me.
chapters.zh: 我的亲戚与我断绝。我的密友都忘记我。

chapters.en: My guests and my female servants count me a foreigner; they look on me as on a stranger.
chapters.zh: 在我家寄居的，和我的使女都以我为外人。我在他们眼中看为外邦人。

chapters.en: I summon my servant, but he does not answer, though I beg him with my own mouth.
chapters.zh: 我呼唤仆人，虽用口求他，他还是不回答。

chapters.en: My breath is offensive to my wife; I am loathsome to my own family.
chapters.zh: 我口的气味，我妻子厌恶。我的恳求，我同胞也憎嫌。

chapters.en: Even the little boys scorn me; when I appear, they ridicule me.
chapters.zh: 连小孩子也藐视我。我若起来，他们都嘲笑我。

chapters.en: All my intimate friends detest me; those I love have turned against me.
chapters.zh: 我的密友都憎恶我。我平日所爱的人向我翻脸。

chapters.en: I am nothing but skin and bones; I have escaped only by the skin of my teeth.
chapters.zh: 我的皮肉紧贴骨头。我只剩牙皮逃脱了。

chapters.en: “Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.
chapters.zh: 我朋友阿，可怜我。可怜我。因为神的手攻击我。

chapters.en: Why do you pursue me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?
chapters.zh: 你们为什么仿佛神逼迫我，吃我的肉还以为不足呢？

chapters.en: “Oh, that my words were recorded, that they were written on a scroll,
chapters.zh: 惟愿我的言语现在写上，都记录在书上。

chapters.en: that they were inscribed with an iron tool on lead, or engraved in rock forever!
chapters.zh: 用铁笔镌刻，用铅灌在磐石上，直存到永远。

chapters.en: I know that my redeemer lives, and that in the end he will stand on the earth.
chapters.zh: 我知道我的救赎主活着，末了必站立在地上。

chapters.en: And after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God;
chapters.zh: 我这皮肉灭绝之后，我必在肉体之外得见神。

chapters.en: I myself will see him with my own eyes—I, and not another. How my heart yearns within me!
chapters.zh: 我自己要见他，亲眼要看他，并不像外人。我的心肠在我里面消灭了。

chapters.en: “If you say, ‘How we will hound him, since the root of the trouble lies in him, ’
chapters.zh: 你们若说，我们逼迫他要何等地重呢？惹事的根乃在乎他。

chapters.en: you should fear the sword yourselves; for wrath will bring punishment by the sword, and then you will know that there is judgment. ”
chapters.zh: 你们就当惧怕刀剑。因为忿怒惹动刀剑的刑罚，使你们知道有报应（原文作审判）。

chapters.en: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:
chapters.zh: 拿玛人琐法回答说，

chapters.en: “My troubled thoughts prompt me to answer because I am greatly disturbed.
chapters.zh: 我心中急躁，所以我的思念叫我回答。

chapters.en: I hear a rebuke that dishonors me, and my understanding inspires me to reply.
chapters.zh: 我已听见那羞辱我，责备我的话。我的悟性叫我回答。

chapters.en: “Surely you know how it has been from of old, ever since mankind was placed on the earth,
chapters.zh: 你岂不知亘古以来，自从人生在地。

chapters.en: that the mirth of the wicked is brief, the joy of the godless lasts but a moment.
chapters.zh: 恶人夸胜是暂时的，不敬虔人的喜乐，不过转眼之间吗？

chapters.en: Though the pride of the godless person reaches to the heavens and his head touches the clouds,
chapters.zh: 他的尊荣虽达到天上，头虽顶到云中，

chapters.en: he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’
chapters.zh: 他终必灭亡，像自己的粪一样。素来见他的人要说，他在哪里呢？

chapters.en: Like a dream he flies away, no more to be found, banished like a vision of the night.
chapters.zh: 他必飞去如梦，不再寻见，速被赶去，如夜间的异象。

chapters.en: The eye that saw him will not see him again; his place will look on him no more.
chapters.zh: 亲眼见过他的，必不再见他。他的本处也再见不着他。

chapters.en: His children must make amends to the poor; his own hands must give back his wealth.
chapters.zh: 他的儿女要求穷人的恩。他的手要赔还不义之财。

chapters.en: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie with him in the dust.
chapters.zh: 他的骨头虽然有青年之力，却要和他一同躺卧在尘土中。

chapters.en: “Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,
chapters.zh: 他口内虽以恶为甘甜，藏在舌头底下。

chapters.en: though he cannot bear to let it go and lets it linger in his mouth,
chapters.zh: 爱恋不舍，含在口中。

chapters.en: yet his food will turn sour in his stomach; it will become the venom of serpents within him.
chapters.zh: 他的食物在肚里却要化为酸，在他里面成为虺蛇的恶毒。

chapters.en: He will spit out the riches he swallowed; God will make his stomach vomit them up.
chapters.zh: 他吞了财宝，还要吐出。神要从他腹中掏出来。

chapters.en: He will suck the poison of serpents; the fangs of an adder will kill him.
chapters.zh: 他必吸饮虺蛇的毒气。蝮蛇的舌头也必杀他。

chapters.en: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.
chapters.zh: 流奶与蜜之河，他不得再见。

chapters.en: What he toiled for he must give back uneaten; he will not enjoy the profit from his trading.
chapters.zh: 他劳碌得来的要赔还，不得享用（原文作吞下），不能照所得的财货欢乐。

chapters.en: For he has oppressed the poor and left them destitute; he has seized houses he did not build.
chapters.zh: 他欺压穷人，且又离弃。强取非自己所盖的房屋（或作强取房屋不得再建造）。

chapters.en: “Surely he will have no respite from his craving; he cannot save himself by his treasure.
chapters.zh: 他因贪而无厌，所喜悦的连一样也不能保守。

chapters.en: Nothing is left for him to devour; his prosperity will not endure.
chapters.zh: 其余的没有一样他不吞灭，所以他的福乐不能长久。

chapters.en: In the midst of his plenty, distress will overtake him; the full force of misery will come upon him.
chapters.zh: 他在满足有余的时候，必到狭窄的地步。凡受苦楚的人，都必加手在他身上。

chapters.en: When he has filled his belly, God will vent his burning anger against him and rain down his blows on him.
chapters.zh: 他正要充满肚腹的时候，神必将猛烈的忿怒，降在他身上。正在他吃饭的时候，要将这忿怒像雨降在他身上。

chapters.en: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow pierces him.
chapters.zh: 他要躲避铁器。铜弓的箭要将他射透。

chapters.en: He pulls it out of his back, the gleaming point out of his liver. Terrors will come over him;
chapters.zh: 他把箭一抽，就从他身上出来。发光的箭头从他胆中出来，有惊惶临在他身上。

chapters.en: total darkness lies in wait for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.
chapters.zh: 他的财宝归于黑暗。人所不吹的火要把他烧灭，要把他帐棚中所剩下的烧毁。

chapters.en: The heavens will expose his guilt; the earth will rise up against him.
chapters.zh: 天要显明他的罪孽，地要兴起攻击他。

chapters.en: A flood will carry off his house, rushing waters on the day of God’s wrath.
chapters.zh: 他的家产必然过去。神发怒的日子，他的货物都要消灭。

chapters.en: Such is the fate God allots the wicked, the heritage appointed for them by God.”
chapters.zh: 这是恶人从神所得的分，是神为他所定的产业。

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说，

chapters.en: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be the consolation you give me.
chapters.zh: 你们要细听我的言语，就算是你们安慰我。

chapters.en: Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken, mock on.
chapters.zh: 请宽容我，我又要说话。说了以后，任凭你们嗤笑吧。

chapters.en: “Is my complaint directed to a human being? Why should I not be impatient?
chapters.zh: 我岂是向人诉冤，为何不焦急呢？

chapters.en: Look at me and be appalled; clap your hand over your mouth.
chapters.zh: 你们要看着我而惊奇，用手捂口。

chapters.en: When I think about this, I am terrified; trembling seizes my body.
chapters.zh: 我每逢思想，心就惊惶，浑身战兢。

chapters.en: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?
chapters.zh: 恶人为何存活，享大寿数，势力强盛呢？

chapters.en: They see their children established around them, their offspring before their eyes.
chapters.zh: 他们眼见儿孙，和他们一同坚立。

chapters.en: Their homes are safe and free from fear; the rod of God is not on them.
chapters.zh: 他们的家宅平安无惧。神的杖也不加在他们身上。

chapters.en: Their bulls never fail to breed; their cows calve and do not miscarry.
chapters.zh: 他们的公牛孳生而不断绝。母牛下犊而不掉胎。

chapters.en: They send forth their children as a flock; their little ones dance about.
chapters.zh: 他们打发小孩子出去，多如羊群。他们的儿女踊跃跳舞。

chapters.en: They sing to the music of timbrel and lyre; they make merry to the sound of the pipe.
chapters.zh: 他们随着琴鼓歌唱，又因箫声欢喜。

chapters.en: They spend their years in prosperity and go down to the grave in peace.
chapters.zh: 他们度日诸事亨通，转眼下入阴间。

chapters.en: Yet they say to God, ‘Leave us alone! We have no desire to know your ways.
chapters.zh: 他们对神说，离开我们吧。我们不愿晓得你的道。

chapters.en: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?’
chapters.zh: 全能者是谁，我们何必事奉他呢？求告他有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: But their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stand aloof from the plans of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 看哪，他们亨通不在乎自己。恶人所谋定的离我好远。

chapters.en: “Yet how often is the lamp of the wicked snuffed out? How often does calamity come upon them, the fate God allots in his anger?
chapters.zh: 恶人的灯何尝熄灭。患难何尝临到他们呢？神何尝发怒，向他们分散灾祸呢？

chapters.en: How often are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a gale?
chapters.zh: 他们何尝像风前的碎秸，如暴风刮去的糠秕呢？

chapters.en: It is said, ‘God stores up the punishment of the wicked for their children.’ Let him repay the wicked, so that they themselves will experience it!
chapters.zh: 你们说，神为恶人的儿女积蓄罪孽。我说，不如本人受报，好使他亲自知道。

chapters.en: Let their own eyes see their destruction; let them drink the cup of the wrath of the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 愿他亲眼看见自己败亡，亲自饮全能者的忿怒。

chapters.en: For what do they care about the families they leave behind when their allotted months come to an end?
chapters.zh: 他的岁月既尽，他还顾他本家吗？

chapters.en: “Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since he judges even the highest?
chapters.zh: 神既审判那在高位的，谁能将知识教训他呢？

chapters.en: One person dies in full vigor, completely secure and at ease,
chapters.zh: 有人至死身体强壮，尽得平靖安逸。

chapters.en: well nourished in body,bones rich with marrow.
chapters.zh: 他的奶桶充满，他的骨髓滋润。

chapters.en: Another dies in bitterness of soul, never having enjoyed anything good.
chapters.zh: 有人至死心中痛苦，终身未尝福乐的滋味。

chapters.en: Side by side they lie in the dust, and worms cover them both.
chapters.zh: 他们一样躺卧在尘土中，都被虫子遮盖。

chapters.en: “I know full well what you are thinking, the schemes by which you would wrong me.
chapters.zh: 我知道你们的意思，并诬害我的计谋。

chapters.en: You say, ‘Where now is the house of the great, the tents where the wicked lived?’
chapters.zh: 你们说，霸者的房屋在哪里？恶人住过的帐棚在哪里？

chapters.en: Have you never questioned those who travel? Have you paid no regard to their accounts—
chapters.zh: 你们岂没有询问过路的人吗？不知道他们所引的证据吗？

chapters.en: that the wicked are spared from the day of calamity, that they are delivered from the day of wrath?
chapters.zh: 就是恶人在祸患的日子得存留，在发怒的日子得逃脱。

chapters.en: Who denounces their conduct to their face? Who repays them for what they have done?
chapters.zh: 他所行的，有谁当面给他说明。他所做的，有谁报应他呢？

chapters.en: They are carried to the grave, and watch is kept over their tombs.
chapters.zh: 然而他要被抬到茔地，并有人看守坟墓。

chapters.en: The soil in the valley is sweet to them; everyone follows after them, and a countless throng goes before them.
chapters.zh: 他要以谷中的土块为甘甜，在他以先去的无数，在他以后去的更多。

chapters.en: “So how can you console me with your nonsense? Nothing is left of your answers but falsehood!”
chapters.zh: 你们对答的话中既都错谬，怎么徒然安慰我呢？

chapters.en: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
chapters.zh: 提幔人以利法回答说，

chapters.en: “Can a man be of benefit to God? Can even a wise person benefit him?
chapters.zh: 人岂能使神有益呢？智慧人但能有益于己。

chapters.en: What pleasure would it give the Almighty if you were righteous? What would he gain if your ways were blameless?
chapters.zh: 你为人公义，岂叫全能者喜悦呢？你行为完全，岂能使他得利呢？

chapters.en: “Is it for your piety that he rebukes you and brings charges against you?
chapters.zh: 岂是因你敬畏他，就责备你，审判你吗？

chapters.en: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your sins endless?
chapters.zh: 你的罪恶岂不是大吗？你的罪孽也没有穷尽。

chapters.en: You demanded security from your relatives for no reason; you stripped people of their clothing, leaving them naked.
chapters.zh: 因你无故强取弟兄的物为当头，剥去贫寒人的衣服。

chapters.en: You gave no water to the weary and you withheld food from the hungry,
chapters.zh: 困乏的人，你没有给他水喝。饥饿的人，你没有给他食物。

chapters.en: though you were a powerful man, owning land— an honored man, living on it.
chapters.zh: 有能力的人就得地土。尊贵的人也住在其中。

chapters.en: And you sent widows away empty-handed and broke the strength of the fatherless.
chapters.zh: 你打发寡妇空手回去，折断孤儿的膀臂。

chapters.en: That is why snares are all around you, why sudden peril terrifies you,
chapters.zh: 因此，有网罗环绕你，有恐惧忽然使你惊惶。

chapters.en: why it is so dark you cannot see, and why a flood of water covers you.
chapters.zh: 或有黑暗蒙蔽你，并有洪水淹没你。

chapters.en: “Is not God in the heights of heaven? And see how lofty are the highest stars!
chapters.zh: 神岂不是在高天吗？你看星宿何其高呢？

chapters.en: Yet you say, ‘What does God know? Does he judge through such darkness?
chapters.zh: 你说，神知道什么？他岂能看透幽暗施行审判呢？

chapters.en: Thick clouds veil him, so he does not see us as he goes about in the vaulted heavens.’
chapters.zh: 密云将他遮盖，使他不能看见。他周游穹苍。

chapters.en: Will you keep to the old path that the wicked have trod?
chapters.zh: 你要依从上古的道吗？这道是恶人所行的。

chapters.en: They were carried off before their time, their foundations washed away by a flood.
chapters.zh: 他们未到死期，忽然除灭。根基毁坏，好像被江河冲去。

chapters.en: They said to God, ‘Leave us alone! What can the Almighty do to us?’
chapters.zh: 他们向神说，离开我们吧。又说，全能者能把我们怎么样呢？

chapters.en: Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things, so I stand aloof from the plans of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 哪知，神以美物充满他们的房屋。但恶人所谋定的离我好远。

chapters.en: The righteous see their ruin and rejoice; the innocent mock them, saying,
chapters.zh: 义人看见他们的结局就欢喜。无辜的人嗤笑他们。

chapters.en: ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire devours their wealth.’
chapters.zh: 说，那起来攻击我们的果然被剪除，其余的都被火烧灭。

chapters.en: “Submit to God and be at peace with him; in this way prosperity will come to you.
chapters.zh: 你要认识神，就得平安。福气也必临到你。

chapters.en: Accept instruction from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart.
chapters.zh: 你当领受他口中的教训，将他的言语存在心里。

chapters.en: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored: If you remove wickedness far from your tent
chapters.zh: 你若归向全能者，从你帐棚中远除不义，就必得建立。

chapters.en: and assign your nuggets to the dust, your gold of Ophir to the rocks in the ravines,
chapters.zh: 要将你的珍宝丢在尘土里，将俄斐的黄金丢在溪河石头之间。

chapters.en: then the Almighty will be your gold, the choicest silver for you.
chapters.zh: 全能者就必为你的珍宝，作你的宝银。

chapters.en: Surely then you will find delight in the Almighty and will lift up your face to God.
chapters.zh: 你就要以全能者为喜乐，向神仰起脸来。

chapters.en: You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
chapters.zh: 你要祷告他，他就听你。你也要还你的愿。

chapters.en: What you decide on will be done, and light will shine on your ways.
chapters.zh: 你定意要作何事，必然给你成就。亮光也必照耀你的路。

chapters.en: When people are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then he will save the downcast.
chapters.zh: 人使你降卑，你仍可说，必得高升。谦卑的人神必然拯救。

chapters.en: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, who will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”
chapters.zh: 人非无辜，神且要搭救他。他因你手中清洁，必蒙拯救。

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说，

chapters.en: “Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.
chapters.zh: 如今我的哀告还算为悖逆。我的责罚比我的唉哼还重。

chapters.en: If only I knew where to find him; if only I could go to his dwelling!
chapters.zh: 惟愿我能知道在哪里可以寻见神，能到他的台前。

chapters.en: I would state my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
chapters.zh: 我就在他面前将我的案件陈明，满口辩白。

chapters.en: I would find out what he would answer me, and consider what he would say to me.
chapters.zh: 我必知道他回答我的言语，明白他向我所说的话。

chapters.en: Would he vigorously oppose me? No, he would not press charges against me.
chapters.zh: 他岂用大能与我争辩吗？必不这样，他必理会我。

chapters.en: There the upright can establish their innocence before him, and there I would be delivered forever from my judge.
chapters.zh: 在他那里，正直人可以与他辩论。这样，我必永远脱离那审判我的。

chapters.en: “But if I go to the east, he is not there; if I go to the west, I do not find him.
chapters.zh: 只是，我往前行，他不在那里，往后退，也不能见他。

chapters.en: When he is at work in the north, I do not see him; when he turns to the south, I catch no glimpse of him.
chapters.zh: 他在左边行事，我却不能看见，在右边隐藏，我也不能见他。

chapters.en: But he knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
chapters.zh: 然而他知道我所行的路。他试炼我之后，我必如精金。

chapters.en: My feet have closely followed his steps; I have kept to his way without turning aside.
chapters.zh: 我脚追随他的步履。我谨守他的道，并不偏离。

chapters.en: I have not departed from the commands of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily bread.
chapters.zh: 他嘴唇的命令，我未曾背弃。我看重他口中的言语，过于我需用的饮食。

chapters.en: “But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? He does whatever he pleases.
chapters.zh: 只是他心志已定，谁能使他转意呢？他心里所愿的，就行出来。

chapters.en: He carries out his decree against me, and many such plans he still has in store.
chapters.zh: 他向我所定的，就必做成。这类的事他还有许多。

chapters.en: That is why I am terrified before him; when I think of all this, I fear him.
chapters.zh: 所以我在他面前惊惶，我思念这事，便惧怕他。

chapters.en: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
chapters.zh: 神使我丧胆，全能者使我惊惶。

chapters.en: Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.
chapters.zh: 我的恐惧，不是因为黑暗，也不是因为幽暗蒙蔽我的脸。

chapters.en: “Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment? Why must those who know him look in vain for such days?
chapters.zh: 全能者既定期罚恶，为何不使认识他的人看见那日子呢？

chapters.en: There are those who move boundary stones; they pasture flocks they have stolen.
chapters.zh: 有人挪移地界，抢夺群畜而牧养。

chapters.en: They drive away the orphan’s donkey and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
chapters.zh: 他们拉去孤儿的驴，强取寡妇的牛为当头。

chapters.en: They thrust the needy from the path and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
chapters.zh: 他们使穷人离开正道，世上的贫民尽都隐藏。

chapters.en: Like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go about their labor of foraging food; the wasteland provides food for their children.
chapters.zh: 这些贫穷人，如同野驴出到旷野，殷勤寻找食物。他们靠着野地给儿女糊口，

chapters.en: They gather fodder in the fields and glean in the vineyards of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 收割别人田间的禾稼，摘取恶人余剩的葡萄。

chapters.en: Lacking clothes, they spend the night naked; they have nothing to cover themselves in the cold.
chapters.zh: 终夜赤身无衣，天气寒冷毫无遮盖，

chapters.en: They are drenched by mountain rains and hug the rocks for lack of shelter.
chapters.zh: 在山上被大雨淋湿，因没有避身之处就挨近磐石。

chapters.en: The fatherless child is snatched from the breast; the infant of the poor is seized for a debt.
chapters.zh: 又有人从母怀中抢夺孤儿，强取穷人的衣服为当头。

chapters.en: Lacking clothes, they go about naked; they carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
chapters.zh: 使人赤身无衣，到处流行，且因饥饿扛抬禾捆，

chapters.en: They crush olives among the terraces ; they tread the winepresses, yet suffer thirst.
chapters.zh: 在那些人的围墙内造油，榨酒，自己还口渴。

chapters.en: The groans of the dying rise from the city, and the souls of the wounded cry out for help. But God charges no one with wrongdoing.
chapters.zh: 在多民的城内有人唉哼，受伤的人哀号。神却不理会那恶人的愚妄。

chapters.en: “There are those who rebel against the light, who do not know its ways or stay in its paths.
chapters.zh: 又有人背弃光明，不认识光明的道，不住在光明的路上。

chapters.en: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises up, kills the poor and needy, and in the night steals forth like a thief.
chapters.zh: 杀人的黎明起来，杀害困苦穷乏人，夜间又作盗贼。

chapters.en: The eye of the adulterer watches for dusk; he thinks, ‘No eye will see me,’ and he keeps his face concealed.
chapters.zh: 奸夫等候黄昏，说，必无眼能见我，就把脸蒙蔽。

chapters.en: In the dark, thieves break into houses, but by day they shut themselves in; they want nothing to do with the light.
chapters.zh: 盗贼黑夜挖窟窿，白日躲藏，并不认识光明。

chapters.en: For all of them, midnight is their morning; they make friends with the terrors of darkness.
chapters.zh: 他们看早晨如幽暗，因为他们晓得幽暗的惊骇。

chapters.en: “Yet they are foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one goes to the vineyards.
chapters.zh: 这些恶人犹如浮萍快快飘去。他们所得的分在世上被咒诅。他们不得再走葡萄园的路。

chapters.en: As heat and drought snatch away the melted snow, so the grave snatches away those who have sinned.
chapters.zh: 干旱炎热消没雪水，阴间也如此消没犯罪之辈。

chapters.en: The womb forgets them, the worm feasts on them; the wicked are no longer remembered but are broken like a tree.
chapters.zh: 怀他的母（原文作胎）要忘记他。虫子要吃他，觉得甘甜。他不再被人记念。不义的人必如树折断。

chapters.en: They prey on the barren and childless woman, and to the widow they show no kindness.
chapters.zh: 他恶待（或作他吞灭）不怀孕不生养的妇人，不善待寡妇。

chapters.en: But God drags away the mighty by his power; though they become established, they have no assurance of life.
chapters.zh: 然而神用能力保全有势力的人，那性命难保的人仍然兴起。

chapters.en: He may let them rest in a feeling of security, but his eyes are on their ways.
chapters.zh: 神使他们安稳，他们就有所倚靠。神的眼目也看顾他们的道路。

chapters.en: For a little while they are exalted, and then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
chapters.zh: 他们被高举，不过片时就没有了。他们降为卑，被除灭，与众人一样，又如谷穗被割。

chapters.en: “If this is not so, who can prove me false and reduce my words to nothing?”
chapters.zh: 若不是这样，谁能证实我是说谎的，将我的言语驳为虚空呢？

chapters.en: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
chapters.zh: 书亚人比勒达回答说，

chapters.en: “Dominion and awe belong to God; he establishes order in the heights of heaven.
chapters.zh: 神有治理之权，有威严可畏。他在高处施行和平。

chapters.en: Can his forces be numbered? On whom does his light not rise?
chapters.zh: 他的诸军，岂能数算？他的光亮一发，谁不蒙照呢？

chapters.en: How then can a mortal be righteous before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
chapters.zh: 这样在神面前，人怎能称义？妇人所生的怎能洁净？

chapters.en: If even the moon is not bright and the stars are not pure in his eyes,
chapters.zh: 在神眼前，月亮也无光亮，星宿也不清洁。

chapters.en: how much less a mortal, who is but a maggot— a human being, who is only a worm!”
chapters.zh: 何况如虫的人，如蛆的世人呢？

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说，

chapters.en: “How you have helped the powerless! How you have saved the arm that is feeble!
chapters.zh: 无能的人，蒙你何等的帮助。膀臂无力的人，蒙你何等的拯救。

chapters.en: What advice you have offered to one without wisdom! And what great insight you have displayed!
chapters.zh: 无智慧的人，蒙你何等的指教。你向他多显大知识。

chapters.en: Who has helped you utter these words? And whose spirit spoke from your mouth?
chapters.zh: 你向谁发出言语来。谁的灵从你而出。

chapters.en: “The dead are in deep anguish, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.
chapters.zh: 在大水，和水族以下的阴魂，战兢。

chapters.en: The realm of the dead is naked before God; Destruction lies uncovered.
chapters.zh: 在神面前，阴间显露。灭亡也不得遮掩。

chapters.en: He spreads out the northern skies over empty space; he suspends the earth over nothing.
chapters.zh: 神将北极铺在空中，将大地悬在虚空。

chapters.en: He wraps up the waters in his clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their weight.
chapters.zh: 将水包在密云中，云却不破裂。

chapters.en: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading his clouds over it.
chapters.zh: 遮蔽他的宝座，将云铺在其上。

chapters.en: He marks out the horizon on the face of the waters for a boundary between light and darkness.
chapters.zh: 在水面的周围划出界限，直到光明黑暗的交界。

chapters.en: The pillars of the heavens quake, aghast at his rebuke.
chapters.zh: 天的柱子，因他的斥责，震动惊奇。

chapters.en: By his power he churned up the sea; by his wisdom he cut Rahab to pieces.
chapters.zh: 他以能力搅动大海（搅动或作平静），他借知识打伤拉哈伯。

chapters.en: By his breath the skies became fair; his hand pierced the gliding serpent.
chapters.zh: 借他的灵使天有妆饰，他的手刺杀快蛇。

chapters.en: And these are but the outer fringe of his works; how faint the whisper we hear of him! Who then can understand the thunder of his power?”
chapters.zh: 看哪，这不过是神工作的些微。我们所听于他的，是何等细微的声音。他大能的雷声谁能明透呢？

chapters.en: And Job continued his discourse:
chapters.zh: 约伯接着说，

chapters.en: “As surely as God lives, who has denied me justice, the Almighty, who has made my life bitter,
chapters.zh: 神夺去我的理，全能者使我心中愁苦。我指着永生的神起誓。

chapters.en: as long as I have life within me, the breath of God in my nostrils,
chapters.zh: 我的生命尚在我里面，神所赐呼吸之气，仍在我的鼻孔内。

chapters.en: my lips will not say anything wicked, and my tongue will not utter lies.
chapters.zh: 我的嘴决不说非义之言，我的舌也不说诡诈之语。

chapters.en: I will never admit you are in the right; till I die, I will not deny my integrity.
chapters.zh: 我断不以你们为是，我至死必不以自己为不正。

chapters.en: I will maintain my innocence and never let go of it; my conscience will not reproach me as long as I live.
chapters.zh: 我持定我的义，必不放松。在世的日子，我心必不责备我。

chapters.en: “May my enemy be like the wicked, my adversary like the unjust!
chapters.zh: 愿我的仇敌如恶人一样。愿那起来攻击我的，如不义之人一般。

chapters.en: For what hope have the godless when they are cut off, when God takes away their life?
chapters.zh: 不敬虔的人虽然得利，神夺取其命的时候，还有什么指望呢？

chapters.en: Does God listen to their cry when distress comes upon them?
chapters.zh: 患难临到他，神岂能听他的呼求？

chapters.en: Will they find delight in the Almighty? Will they call on God at all times?
chapters.zh: 他岂以全能者为乐，随时求告神呢？

chapters.en: “I will teach you about the power of God; the ways of the Almighty I will not conceal.
chapters.zh: 神的作为，我要指教你们。全能者所行的，我也不隐瞒。

chapters.en: You have all seen this yourselves. Why then this meaningless talk?
chapters.zh: 你们自己也都见过，为何全然变为虚妄呢？

chapters.en: “Here is the fate God allots to the wicked, the heritage a ruthless man receives from the Almighty:
chapters.zh: 神为恶人所定的分，强暴人从全能者所得的报（报原文作产业）乃是这样。

chapters.en: However many his children, their fate is the sword; his offspring will never have enough to eat.
chapters.zh: 倘或他的儿女增多，还是被刀所杀。他的子孙必不得饱食。

chapters.en: The plague will bury those who survive him, and their widows will not weep for them.
chapters.zh: 他所遗留的人必死而埋葬，他的寡妇也不哀哭。

chapters.en: Though he heaps up silver like dust and clothes like piles of clay,
chapters.zh: 他虽积蓄银子如尘沙，预备衣服如泥土。

chapters.en: what he lays up the righteous will wear, and the innocent will divide his silver.
chapters.zh: 他只管预备，义人却要穿上。他的银子，无辜的人要分取。

chapters.en: The house he builds is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut made by a watchman.
chapters.zh: 他建造房屋如虫做窝，又如守望者所搭的棚。

chapters.en: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.
chapters.zh: 他虽富足躺卧，却不得收殓，转眼之间就不在了。

chapters.en: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest snatches him away in the night.
chapters.zh: 惊恐如波涛将他追上。暴风在夜间将他刮去。

chapters.en: The east wind carries him off, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
chapters.zh: 东风把他飘去，又刮他离开本处。

chapters.en: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.
chapters.zh: 神要向他射箭，并不留情。他恨不得逃脱神的手。

chapters.en: It claps its hands in derision and hisses him out of his place.”
chapters.zh: 人要向他拍掌，并要发叱声，使他离开本处。

chapters.en: There is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.
chapters.zh: 银子有矿，炼金有方。

chapters.en: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.
chapters.zh: 铁从地里挖出，铜从石中熔化。

chapters.en: Mortals put an end to the darkness; they search out the farthest recesses for ore in the blackest darkness.
chapters.zh: 人为黑暗定界限，查究幽暗阴翳的石头，直到极处。

chapters.en: Far from human dwellings they cut a shaft, in places untouched by human feet; far from other people they dangle and sway.
chapters.zh: 在无人居住之处刨开矿穴，过路的人也想不到他们。又与人远离，悬在空中摇来摇去。

chapters.en: The earth, from which food comes, is transformed below as by fire;
chapters.zh: 至于地，能出粮食，地内好像被火翻起来。

chapters.en: lapis lazuli comes from its rocks, and its dust contains nuggets of gold.
chapters.zh: 地中的石头有蓝宝石，并有金沙。

chapters.en: No bird of prey knows that hidden path, no falcon’s eye has seen it.
chapters.zh: 矿中的路鸷鸟不得知道，鹰眼也未见过。

chapters.en: Proud beasts do not set foot on it, and no lion prowls there.
chapters.zh: 狂傲的野兽未曾行过。猛烈的狮子也未曾经过。

chapters.en: People assault the flinty rock with their hands and lay bare the roots of the mountains.
chapters.zh: 人伸手凿开坚石，倾倒山根。

chapters.en: They tunnel through the rock; their eyes see all its treasures.
chapters.zh: 在磐石中凿出水道，亲眼看见各样宝物。

chapters.en: They search the sources of the rivers and bring hidden things to light.
chapters.zh: 他封闭水不得滴流，使隐藏的物显露出来。

chapters.en: But where can wisdom be found? Where does understanding dwell?
chapters.zh: 然而，智慧有何处可寻？聪明之处在哪里呢？

chapters.en: No mortal comprehends its worth; it cannot be found in the land of the living.
chapters.zh: 智慧的价值无人能知，在活人之地也无处可寻。

chapters.en: The deep says, “It is not in me”; the sea says, “It is not with me.”
chapters.zh: 深渊说，不在我内。沧海说，不在我中。

chapters.en: It cannot be bought with the finest gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.
chapters.zh: 智慧非用黄金可得，也不能平白银为它的价值。

chapters.en: It cannot be bought with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or lapis lazuli.
chapters.zh: 俄斐金，和贵重的红玛瑙，并蓝宝石，不足与较量。

chapters.en: Neither gold nor crystal can compare with it, nor can it be had for jewels of gold.
chapters.zh: 黄金，和玻璃，不足与比较。精金的器皿，不足与兑换。

chapters.en: Coral and jasper are not worthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.
chapters.zh: 珊瑚，水晶都不足论。智慧的价值胜过珍珠（或作红宝石）。

chapters.en: The topaz of Cush cannot compare with it; it cannot be bought with pure gold.
chapters.zh: 古实的红璧玺，不足与比较。精金，也不足与较量。

chapters.en: Where then does wisdom come from? Where does understanding dwell?
chapters.zh: 智慧从何处来呢？聪明之处在哪里呢？

chapters.en: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, concealed even from the birds in the sky.
chapters.zh: 是向一切有生命的眼目隐藏，向空中的飞鸟掩蔽。

chapters.en: Destruction and Death say, “Only a rumor of it has reached our ears.”
chapters.zh: 灭没和死亡说，我们风闻其名。

chapters.en: God understands the way to it and he alone knows where it dwells,
chapters.zh: 神明白智慧的道路，晓得智慧的所在。

chapters.en: for he views the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
chapters.zh: 因他鉴察直到地极，遍观普天之下。

chapters.en: When he established the force of the wind and measured out the waters,
chapters.zh: 要为风定轻重，又度量诸水。

chapters.en: when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderstorm,
chapters.zh: 他为雨露定命令，为雷电定道路。

chapters.en: then he looked at wisdom and appraised it; he confirmed it and tested it.
chapters.zh: 那时他看见智慧，而且述说。他坚定，并且查究。

chapters.en: And he said to the human race, “The fear of the Lord—that is wisdom, and to shun evil is understanding.”
chapters.zh: 他对人说，敬畏主就是智慧。远离恶便是聪明。

chapters.en: Job continued his discourse:
chapters.zh: 约伯又接着说，

chapters.en: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,
chapters.zh: 惟愿我的景况如从前的月份，如神保守我的日子。

chapters.en: when his lamp shone on my head and by his light I walked through darkness!
chapters.zh: 那时他的灯照在我头上。我借他的光行过黑暗。

chapters.en: Oh, for the days when I was in my prime, when God’s intimate friendship blessed my house,
chapters.zh: 我愿如壮年的时候，那时我在帐棚中。神待我有密友之情。

chapters.en: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,
chapters.zh: 全能者仍与我同在。我的儿女都环绕我。

chapters.en: when my path was drenched with cream and the rock poured out for me streams of olive oil.
chapters.zh: 奶多可洗我的脚。磐石为我出油成河。

chapters.en: “When I went to the gate of the city and took my seat in the public square,
chapters.zh: 我出到城门，在街上设立座位。

chapters.en: the young men saw me and stepped aside and the old men rose to their feet;
chapters.zh: 少年人见我而回避，老年人也起身站立。

chapters.en: the chief men refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands;
chapters.zh: 王子都停止说话，用手捂口。

chapters.en: the voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.
chapters.zh: 首领静默无声，舌头贴住上膛。

chapters.en: Whoever heard me spoke well of me, and those who saw me commended me,
chapters.zh: 耳朵听我的，就称我有福。眼睛看我的，便称赞我。

chapters.en: because I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had none to assist them.
chapters.zh: 因我拯救哀求的困苦人，和无人帮助的孤儿。

chapters.en: The one who was dying blessed me; I made the widow’s heart sing.
chapters.zh: 将要灭亡的为我祝福。我也使寡妇心中欢乐。

chapters.en: I put on righteousness as my clothing; justice was my robe and my turban.
chapters.zh: 我以公义为衣服，以公平为外袍和冠冕。

chapters.en: I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
chapters.zh: 我为瞎子的眼，瘸子的脚。

chapters.en: I was a father to the needy; I took up the case of the stranger.
chapters.zh: 我为穷乏人的父，素不认识的人，我查明他的案件。

chapters.en: I broke the fangs of the wicked and snatched the victims from their teeth.
chapters.zh: 我打破不义之人的牙床，从他牙齿中夺了所抢的。

chapters.en: “I thought, ‘I will die in my own house, my days as numerous as the grains of sand.
chapters.zh: 我便说，我必死在家中（原文作窝中），必增添我的日子，多如尘沙。

chapters.en: My roots will reach to the water, and the dew will lie all night on my branches.
chapters.zh: 我的根长到水边，露水终夜沾在我的枝上。

chapters.en: My glory will not fade; the bow will be ever new in my hand.’
chapters.zh: 我的荣耀在身上增新，我的弓在手中日强。

chapters.en: “People listened to me expectantly, waiting in silence for my counsel.
chapters.zh: 人听见我而仰望，静默等候我的指教。

chapters.en: After I had spoken, they spoke no more; my words fell gently on their ears.
chapters.zh: 我说话之后，他们就不再说。我的言语像雨露滴在他们身上。

chapters.en: They waited for me as for showers and drank in my words as the spring rain.
chapters.zh: 他们仰望我如仰望雨，又张开口如切慕春雨。

chapters.en: When I smiled at them, they scarcely believed it; the light of my face was precious to them.
chapters.zh: 他们不敢自信，我就向他们含笑。他们不使我脸上的光改变。

chapters.en: I chose the way for them and sat as their chief; I dwelt as a king among his troops; I was like one who comforts mourners.
chapters.zh: 我为他们选择道路，又坐首位。我如君王在军队中居住，又如吊丧的安慰伤心的人。

chapters.en: “But now they mock me, men younger than I, whose fathers I would have disdained to put with my sheep dogs.
chapters.zh: 但如今，比我年少的人戏笑我。其人之父我曾藐视，不肯安在看守我羊群的狗中。

chapters.en: Of what use was the strength of their hands to me, since their vigor had gone from them?
chapters.zh: 他们壮年的气力既已衰败，其手之力与我何益呢？

chapters.en: Haggard from want and hunger, they roamed the parched land in desolate wastelands at night.
chapters.zh: 他们因穷乏饥饿，身体枯瘦，在荒废凄凉的幽暗中啃干燥之地。

chapters.en: In the brush they gathered salt herbs, and their food was the root of the broom bush.
chapters.zh: 在草丛之中采咸草，罗腾的根为他们的食物（罗腾小树名松类）。

chapters.en: They were banished from human society, shouted at as if they were thieves.
chapters.zh: 他们从人中被赶出，人追喊他们如贼一般。

chapters.en: They were forced to live in the dry stream beds, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.
chapters.zh: 以致他们住在荒谷之间，在地洞和岩穴中。

chapters.en: They brayed among the bushes and huddled in the undergrowth.
chapters.zh: 在草丛中叫唤，在荆棘下聚集。

chapters.en: A base and nameless brood, they were driven out of the land.
chapters.zh: 这都是愚顽下贱人的儿女，他们被鞭打，赶出境外。

chapters.en: “And now those young men mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.
chapters.zh: 现在这些人以我为歌曲，以我为笑谈。

chapters.en: They detest me and keep their distance; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
chapters.zh: 他们厌恶我，躲在旁边站着，不住地吐唾沫在我脸上。

chapters.en: Now that God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they throw off restraint in my presence.
chapters.zh: 松开他们的绳索苦待我，在我面前脱去辔头。

chapters.en: On my right the tribe attacks; they lay snares for my feet, they build their siege ramps against me.
chapters.zh: 这等下流人在我右边起来，推开我的脚，筑成战路来攻击我。

chapters.en: They break up my road; they succeed in destroying me. ‘No one can help him,’ they say.
chapters.zh: 这些无人帮助的，毁坏我的道，加增我的灾。

chapters.en: They advance as through a gaping breach; amid the ruins they come rolling in.
chapters.zh: 他们来如同闯进大破口，在毁坏之间滚在我身上。

chapters.en: Terrors overwhelm me; my dignity is driven away as by the wind, my safety vanishes like a cloud.
chapters.zh: 惊恐临到我，驱逐我的尊荣如风，我的福禄如云过去。

chapters.en: “And now my life ebbs away; days of suffering grip me.
chapters.zh: 现在我心极其悲伤。困苦的日子将我抓住。

chapters.en: Night pierces my bones; my gnawing pains never rest.
chapters.zh: 夜间，我里面的骨头刺我，疼痛不止，好像龈我。

chapters.en: In his great power God becomes like clothing to me ; he binds me like the neck of my garment.
chapters.zh: 因神的大力，我的外衣污秽不堪，又如里衣的领子将我缠住。

chapters.en: He throws me into the mud, and I am reduced to dust and ashes.
chapters.zh: 神把我扔在淤泥中，我就像尘土和炉灰一般。

chapters.en: “I cry out to you, God, but you do not answer; I stand up, but you merely look at me.
chapters.zh: 主阿，我呼求你，你不应允我。我站起来，你就定睛看我。

chapters.en: You turn on me ruthlessly; with the might of your hand you attack me.
chapters.zh: 你向我变心，待我残忍，又用大能追逼我。

chapters.en: You snatch me up and drive me before the wind; you toss me about in the storm.
chapters.zh: 把我提在风中，使我驾风而行，又使我消灭在烈风中。

chapters.en: I know you will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.
chapters.zh: 我知道要使我临到死地，到那为众生所定的阴宅。

chapters.en: “Surely no one lays a hand on a broken man when he cries for help in his distress.
chapters.zh: 然而，人仆倒岂不伸手？遇灾难岂不求救呢？

chapters.en: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has not my soul grieved for the poor?
chapters.zh: 人遭难，我岂不为他哭泣呢？人穷乏，我岂不为他忧愁呢？

chapters.en: Yet when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, then came darkness.
chapters.zh: 我仰望得好处，灾祸就到了。我等待光明，黑暗便来了。

chapters.en: The churning inside me never stops; days of suffering confront me.
chapters.zh: 我心里烦扰不安，困苦的日子临到我身。

chapters.en: I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
chapters.zh: 我没有日光就哀哭行去（或作我面发黑并非因日晒）。我在会中站着求救。

chapters.en: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of owls.
chapters.zh: 我与野狗为弟兄，与鸵鸟为同伴。

chapters.en: My skin grows black and peels; my body burns with fever.
chapters.zh: 我的皮肤黑而脱落，我的骨头因热烧焦。

chapters.en: My lyre is tuned to mourning, and my pipe to the sound of wailing.
chapters.zh: 所以，我的琴音变为悲音，我的箫声变为哭声。

chapters.en: “I made a covenant with my eyes not to look lustfully at a young woman.
chapters.zh: 我与眼睛立约，怎能恋恋瞻望处女呢？

chapters.en: For what is our lot from God above, our heritage from the Almighty on high?
chapters.zh: 从至上的神所得之分，从至高全能者所得之业，是什么呢？

chapters.en: Is it not ruin for the wicked, disaster for those who do wrong?
chapters.zh: 岂不是祸患临到不义的，灾害临到作孽的呢？

chapters.en: Does he not see my ways and count my every step?
chapters.zh: 神岂不是察看我的道路，数点我的脚步呢？

chapters.en: “If I have walked with falsehood or my foot has hurried after deceit—
chapters.zh: 我若与虚谎同行，脚若追随诡诈。

chapters.en: let God weigh me in honest scales and he will know that I am blameless—
chapters.zh: 我若被公道的天平称度，使神可以知道我的纯正。

chapters.en: if my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has been led by my eyes, or if my hands have been defiled,
chapters.zh: 我的脚步若偏离正路，我的心若随着我的眼目，若有玷污粘在我手上。

chapters.en: then may others eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.
chapters.zh: 就愿我所种的有别人吃，我田所产的被拔出来。

chapters.en: “If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or if I have lurked at my neighbor’s door,
chapters.zh: 我若受迷惑，向妇人起淫念，在邻舍的门外蹲伏。

chapters.en: then may my wife grind another man’s grain, and may other men sleep with her.
chapters.zh: 就愿我的妻子给别人推磨，别人也与她同室。

chapters.en: For that would have been wicked, a sin to be judged.
chapters.zh: 因为这是大罪，是审判官当罚的罪孽。

chapters.en: It is a fire that burns to Destruction ; it would have uprooted my harvest.
chapters.zh: 这本是火焚烧，直到毁灭，必拔除我所有的家产。

chapters.en: “If I have denied justice to any of my servants, whether male or female, when they had a grievance against me,
chapters.zh: 我的仆婢与我争辩的时候，我若藐视不听他们的情节。

chapters.en: what will I do when God confronts me? What will I answer when called to account?
chapters.zh: 神兴起，我怎样行呢？他察问，我怎样回答呢？

chapters.en: Did not he who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same one form us both within our mothers?
chapters.zh: 造我在腹中的，不也是造他吗？将他与我抟在腹中的，岂不是一位吗？

chapters.en: “If I have denied the desires of the poor or let the eyes of the widow grow weary,
chapters.zh: 我若不容贫寒人得其所愿，或叫寡妇眼中失望，

chapters.en: if I have kept my bread to myself, not sharing it with the fatherless—
chapters.zh: 或独自吃我一点食物，孤儿没有与我同吃。

chapters.en: but from my youth I reared them as a father would, and from my birth I guided the widow—
chapters.zh: （从幼年时孤儿与我同长，好像父子一样。我从出母腹就扶助寡妇）。（扶助原文作引领）

chapters.en: if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or the needy without garments,
chapters.zh: 我若见人因无衣死亡，或见穷乏人身无遮盖。

chapters.en: and their hearts did not bless me for warming them with the fleece from my sheep,
chapters.zh: 我若不使他因我羊的毛得暖，为我祝福。

chapters.en: if I have raised my hand against the fatherless, knowing that I had influence in court,
chapters.zh: 我若在城门口见有帮助我的，举手攻击孤儿。

chapters.en: then let my arm fall from the shoulder, let it be broken off at the joint.
chapters.zh: 情愿我的肩头从缺盆骨脱落，我的膀臂从羊矢骨折断。

chapters.en: For I dreaded destruction from God, and for fear of his splendor I could not do such things.
chapters.zh: 因神降的灾祸使我恐惧。因他的威严，我不能妄为。

chapters.en: “If I have put my trust in gold or said to pure gold, ‘You are my security,’
chapters.zh: 我若以黄金为指望，对精金说，你是我的倚靠。

chapters.en: if I have rejoiced over my great wealth, the fortune my hands had gained,
chapters.zh: 我若因财物丰裕，因我手多得资财而欢喜。

chapters.en: if I have regarded the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,
chapters.zh: 我若见太阳发光，明月行在空中，

chapters.en: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand offered them a kiss of homage,
chapters.zh: 心就暗暗被引诱，口便亲手。

chapters.en: then these also would be sins to be judged, for I would have been unfaithful to God on high.
chapters.zh: 这也是审判官当罚的罪孽，又是我背弃在上的神。

chapters.en: “If I have rejoiced at my enemy’s misfortune or gloated over the trouble that came to him—
chapters.zh: 我若见恨我的遭报就欢喜，见他遭灾便高兴。

chapters.en: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by invoking a curse against their life—
chapters.zh: （我没有容口犯罪，咒诅他的生命）

chapters.en: if those of my household have never said, ‘Who has not been filled with Job’s meat?’—
chapters.zh: 若我帐棚的人未尝说，谁不以主人的食物吃饱呢？

chapters.en: but no stranger had to spend the night in the street, for my door was always open to the traveler—
chapters.zh: （从来我没有容客旅在街上住宿，却开门迎接行路的人）

chapters.en: if I have concealed my sin as people do,by hiding my guilt in my heart
chapters.zh: 我若像亚当（亚当或作别人）遮掩我的过犯，将罪孽藏在怀中。

chapters.en: because I so feared the crowd and so dreaded the contempt of the clans that I kept silent and would not go outside—
chapters.zh: 因惧怕大众，又因宗族藐视我使我惊恐，以致闭口无言，杜门不出。

chapters.en: (“Oh, that I had someone to hear me! I sign now my defense—let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser put his indictment in writing.
chapters.zh: 惟愿有一位肯听我。（看哪，在这里有我所划的押，愿全能者回答我）

chapters.en: Surely I would wear it on my shoulder, I would put it on like a crown.
chapters.zh: 愿那敌我者，所写的状词在我这里，我必带在肩上，又绑在头上为冠冕。

chapters.en: I would give him an account of my every step; I would present it to him as to a ruler.)—
chapters.zh: 我必向他述说我脚步的数目，必如君王进到他面前。

chapters.en: “if my land cries out against me and all its furrows are wet with tears,
chapters.zh: 我若夺取田地，这地向我喊冤，犁沟一同哭泣。

chapters.en: if I have devoured its yield without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants,
chapters.zh: 我若吃地的出产不给价值，或叫原主丧命。

chapters.en: then let briers come up instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
chapters.zh: 愿这地长蒺藜代替麦子，长恶草代替大麦。约伯的话说完了。

chapters.en: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
chapters.zh: 于是这三个人，因约伯自以为义就，不再回答他。

chapters.en: But Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became very angry with Job for justifying himself rather than God.
chapters.zh: 那时有布西人，兰族巴拉迦的儿子，以利户向约伯发怒。因约伯自以为义，不以神为义。

chapters.en: He was also angry with the three friends, because they had found no way to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.
chapters.zh: 他又向约伯的三个朋友发怒。因为他们想不出回答的话来，仍以约伯为有罪。

chapters.en: Now Elihu had waited before speaking to Job because they were older than he.
chapters.zh: 以利户要与约伯说话，就等候他们，因为他们比自己年老。

chapters.en: But when he saw that the three men had nothing more to say, his anger was aroused.
chapters.zh: 以利户见这三个人口中无话回答，就怒气发作。

chapters.en: So Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite said: “I am young in years, and you are old; that is why I was fearful, not daring to tell you what I know.
chapters.zh: 布西人，巴拉迦的儿子，以利户回答说，我年轻，你们老迈。因此我退让，不敢向你们陈说我的意见。

chapters.en: I thought, ‘Age should speak; advanced years should teach wisdom.’
chapters.zh: 我说，年老的当先说话。寿高的当以智慧教训人。

chapters.en: But it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives them understanding.
chapters.zh: 但在人里面有灵，全能者的气使人有聪明。

chapters.en: It is not only the old who are wise, not only the aged who understand what is right.
chapters.zh: 尊贵的不都有智慧。寿高的不都能明白公平。

chapters.en: “Therefore I say: Listen to me; I too will tell you what I know.
chapters.zh: 因此我说，你们要听我言，我也要陈说我的意见。

chapters.en: I waited while you spoke, I listened to your reasoning; while you were searching for words,
chapters.zh: 你们查究所要说的话。那时我等候你们的话，侧耳听你们的辩论。

chapters.en: I gave you my full attention. But not one of you has proved Job wrong; none of you has answered his arguments.
chapters.zh: 留心听你们。谁知你们中间无一人折服约伯，驳倒他的话。

chapters.en: Do not say, ‘We have found wisdom; let God, not a man, refute him.’
chapters.zh: 你们切不可说，我们寻得智慧。神能胜他，人却不能。

chapters.en: But Job has not marshaled his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
chapters.zh: 约伯没有向我争辩。我也不用你们的话回答他。

chapters.en: “They are dismayed and have no more to say; words have failed them.
chapters.zh: 他们惊奇不再回答，一言不发。

chapters.en: Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand there with no reply?
chapters.zh: 我岂因他们不说话，站住不再回答，仍旧等候呢？

chapters.en: I too will have my say; I too will tell what I know.
chapters.zh: 我也要回答我的一分话，陈说我的意见。

chapters.en: For I am full of words, and the spirit within me compels me;
chapters.zh: 因为我的言语满怀。我里面的灵激动我。

chapters.en: inside I am like bottled-up wine, like new wineskins ready to burst.
chapters.zh: 我的胸怀如盛酒之囊，没有出气之缝，又如新皮袋快要破裂。

chapters.en: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and reply.
chapters.zh: 我要说话，使我舒畅。我要开口回答。

chapters.en: I will show no partiality, nor will I flatter anyone;
chapters.zh: 我必不看人的情面，也不奉承人。

chapters.en: for if I were skilled in flattery, my Maker would soon take me away.
chapters.zh: 我不晓得奉承。若奉承，造我的主必快快除灭我。

chapters.en: “But now, Job, listen to my words; pay attention to everything I say.
chapters.zh: 约伯阿，请听我的话，留心听我一切的言语。

chapters.en: I am about to open my mouth; my words are on the tip of my tongue.
chapters.zh: 我现在开口，用舌发言。

chapters.en: My words come from an upright heart; my lips sincerely speak what I know.
chapters.zh: 我的言语要发明心中所存的正直。我所知道的，我嘴唇要诚实地说出。

chapters.en: The Spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
chapters.zh: 神的灵造我，全能者的气使我得生。

chapters.en: Answer me then, if you can; stand up and argue your case before me.
chapters.zh: 你若回答我，就站起来，在我面前陈明。

chapters.en: I am the same as you in God’s sight; I too am a piece of clay.
chapters.zh: 我在神面前与你一样，也是用土造成。

chapters.en: No fear of me should alarm you, nor should my hand be heavy on you.
chapters.zh: 我不用威严惊吓你，也不用势力重压你。

chapters.en: “But you have said in my hearing— I heard the very words—
chapters.zh: 你所说的，我听见了，也听见你的言语，说，

chapters.en: ‘I am pure, I have done no wrong; I am clean and free from sin.
chapters.zh: 我是清洁无过的，我是无辜的。在我里面也没有罪孽。

chapters.en: Yet God has found fault with me; he considers me his enemy.
chapters.zh: 神找机会攻击我，以我为仇敌，

chapters.en: He fastens my feet in shackles; he keeps close watch on all my paths.’
chapters.zh: 把我的脚上了木狗，窥察我一切的道路。

chapters.en: “But I tell you, in this you are not right, for God is greater than any mortal.
chapters.zh: 我要回答你说，你这话无理，因神比世人更大。

chapters.en: Why do you complain to him that he responds to no one’s words ?
chapters.zh: 你为何与他争论呢？因他的事都不对人解说。

chapters.en: For God does speak—now one way, now another— though no one perceives it.
chapters.zh: 神说一次，两次，世人却不理会。

chapters.en: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they slumber in their beds,
chapters.zh: 人躺在床上沉睡的时候，神就用梦，和夜间的异象，

chapters.en: he may speak in their ears and terrify them with warnings,
chapters.zh: 开通他们的耳朵，将当受的教训印在他们心上，

chapters.en: to turn them from wrongdoing and keep them from pride,
chapters.zh: 好叫人不从自己的谋算，不行骄傲的事。（原文作将骄傲向人隐藏）

chapters.en: to preserve them from the pit, their lives from perishing by the sword.
chapters.zh: 拦阻人不陷于坑里，不死在刀下。

chapters.en: “Or someone may be chastened on a bed of pain with constant distress in their bones,
chapters.zh: 人在床上被惩治，骨头中不住地疼痛。

chapters.en: so that their body finds food repulsive and their soul loathes the choicest meal.
chapters.zh: 以致他的口厌弃食物，心厌恶美味。

chapters.en: Their flesh wastes away to nothing, and their bones, once hidden, now stick out.
chapters.zh: 他的肉消瘦，不得再见。先前不见的骨头都凸出来。

chapters.en: They draw near to the pit, and their life to the messengers of death.
chapters.zh: 他的灵魂临近深坑。他的生命近于灭命的。

chapters.en: Yet if there is an angel at their side, a messenger, one out of a thousand, sent to tell them how to be upright,
chapters.zh: 一千天使中，若有一个作传话的与神同在，指示人所当行的事。

chapters.en: and he is gracious to that person and says to God, ‘Spare them from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom for them—
chapters.zh: 神就给他开恩，说，救赎他免得下坑。我已经得了赎价。

chapters.en: let their flesh be renewed like a child’s; let them be restored as in the days of their youth’—
chapters.zh: 他的肉要比孩童的肉更嫩。他就返老还童。

chapters.en: then that person can pray to God and find favor with him, they will see God’s face and shout for joy; he will restore them to full well-being.
chapters.zh: 他祷告神，神就喜悦他，使他欢呼朝见神的面。神又看他为义。

chapters.en: And they will go to others and say, ‘I have sinned, I have perverted what is right, but I did not get what I deserved.
chapters.zh: 他在人前歌唱说，我犯了罪，颠倒是非，这竟与我无益。

chapters.en: God has delivered me from going down to the pit, and I shall live to enjoy the light of life.’
chapters.zh: 神救赎我的灵魂免入深坑。我的生命也必见光。

chapters.en: “God does all these things to a person— twice, even three times—
chapters.zh: 神两次，三次，向人行这一切的事。

chapters.en: to turn them back from the pit, that the light of life may shine on them.
chapters.zh: 为要从深坑救回人的灵魂，使他被光照耀与活人一样。

chapters.en: “Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
chapters.zh: 约伯阿，你当侧耳听我的话，不要作声，等我讲说。

chapters.en: If you have anything to say, answer me; speak up, for I want to vindicate you.
chapters.zh: 你若有话说，就可以回答我。你只管说，因我愿以你为是。

chapters.en: But if not, then listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”
chapters.zh: 若不然，你就听我说。你不要作声，我便将智慧教训你。

chapters.en: Then Elihu said:
chapters.zh: 以利户又说，

chapters.en: “Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you men of learning.
chapters.zh: 你们智慧人，要听我的话。有知识的人，要留心听我说。

chapters.en: For the ear tests words as the tongue tastes food.
chapters.zh: 因为耳朵试验话语，好像上膛尝食物。

chapters.en: Let us discern for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.
chapters.zh: 我们当选择何为是，彼此知道何为善。

chapters.en: “Job says, ‘I am innocent, but God denies me justice.
chapters.zh: 约伯曾说，我是公义，神夺去我的理。

chapters.en: Although I am right, I am considered a liar; although I am guiltless, his arrow inflicts an incurable wound.’
chapters.zh: 我虽有理，还算为说谎言的。我虽无过，受的伤还不能医治。

chapters.en: Is there anyone like Job, who drinks scorn like water?
chapters.zh: 谁像约伯，喝讥诮如同喝水呢？

chapters.en: He keeps company with evildoers; he associates with the wicked.
chapters.zh: 他与作孽的结伴，和恶人同行。

chapters.en: For he says, ‘There is no profit in trying to please God.’
chapters.zh: 他说，人以神为乐，总是无益。

chapters.en: “So listen to me, you men of understanding. Far be it from God to do evil, from the Almighty to do wrong.
chapters.zh: 所以你们明理的人，要听我的话。神断不至行恶，全能者断不至作孽。

chapters.en: He repays everyone for what they have done; he brings on them what their conduct deserves.
chapters.zh: 他必按人所作的报应人，使各人照所行的得报。

chapters.en: It is unthinkable that God would do wrong, that the Almighty would pervert justice.
chapters.zh: 神必不作恶，全能者也不偏离公平。

chapters.en: Who appointed him over the earth? Who put him in charge of the whole world?
chapters.zh: 谁派他治理地，安定全世界呢？

chapters.en: If it were his intention and he withdrew his spirit and breath,
chapters.zh: 他若专心为己，将灵和气收归自己。

chapters.en: all humanity would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.
chapters.zh: 凡有血气的就必一同死亡，世人必仍归尘土。

chapters.en: “If you have understanding, hear this; listen to what I say.
chapters.zh: 你若明理，就当听我的话，留心听我言语的声音。

chapters.en: Can someone who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One?
chapters.zh: 难道恨恶公平的可以掌权吗？那有公义的，有大能的，岂可定他有罪吗？

chapters.en: Is he not the One who says to kings, ‘You are worthless,’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’
chapters.zh: 他对君王说，你是鄙陋的。对贵臣说，你是邪恶的。

chapters.en: who shows no partiality to princes and does not favor the rich over the poor, for they are all the work of his hands?
chapters.zh: 他待王子不徇情面，也不看重富足的过于贫穷的，因为都是他手所造。

chapters.en: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night; the people are shaken and they pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
chapters.zh: 在转眼之间，半夜之中，他们就死亡。百姓被震动而去世。有权力的被夺去非借人手。

chapters.en: “His eyes are on the ways of mortals; he sees their every step.
chapters.zh: 神注目观看人的道路，看明人的脚步。

chapters.en: There is no deep shadow, no utter darkness, where evildoers can hide.
chapters.zh: 没有黑暗，阴翳能给作孽的藏身。

chapters.en: God has no need to examine people further, that they should come before him for judgment.
chapters.zh: 神审判人，不必使人到他面前再三鉴察。

chapters.en: Without inquiry he shatters the mighty and sets up others in their place.
chapters.zh: 他用难测之法，打破有能力的人，设立别人代替他们。

chapters.en: Because he takes note of their deeds, he overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.
chapters.zh: 他原知道他们的行为，使他们在夜间倾倒灭亡。

chapters.en: He punishes them for their wickedness where everyone can see them,
chapters.zh: 他在众人眼前击打他们，如同击打恶人一样。

chapters.en: because they turned from following him and had no regard for any of his ways.
chapters.zh: 因为他们偏行不跟从他，也不留心他的道，

chapters.en: They caused the cry of the poor to come before him, so that he heard the cry of the needy.
chapters.zh: 甚至使贫穷人的哀声，达到他那里。他也听了困苦人的哀声。

chapters.en: But if he remains silent, who can condemn him? If he hides his face, who can see him? Yet he is over individual and nation alike,
chapters.zh: 他使人安静，谁能扰乱（或作定罪）呢？他掩面谁能见他呢？无论待一国，或一人都是如此。

chapters.en: to keep the godless from ruling, from laying snares for the people.
chapters.zh: 使不虔敬的人不得作王，免得有人牢笼百姓。

chapters.en: “Suppose someone says to God, ‘I am guilty but will offend no more.
chapters.zh: 有谁对神说，我受了责罚，不再犯罪。

chapters.en: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do so again.’
chapters.zh: 我所看不明的，求你指教我。我若作了孽，必不再作。

chapters.en: Should God then reward you on your terms, when you refuse to repent? You must decide, not I; so tell me what you know.
chapters.zh: 他施行报应，岂要随你的心愿，叫你推辞不受吗？选定的是你，不是我。你所知道的只管说吧。

chapters.en: “Men of understanding declare, wise men who hear me say to me,
chapters.zh: 明理的人，和听我话的智慧人，必对我说。

chapters.en: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’
chapters.zh: 约伯说话没有知识，言语中毫无智慧。

chapters.en: Oh, that Job might be tested to the utmost for answering like a wicked man!
chapters.zh: 愿约伯被试验到底，因他回答像恶人一样。

chapters.en: To his sin he adds rebellion; scornfully he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
chapters.zh: 他在罪上又加悖逆。在我们中间拍手，用许多言语轻慢神。

chapters.en: Then Elihu said:
chapters.zh: 以利户又说，

chapters.en: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am in the right, not God.’
chapters.zh: 你以为有理，或以为你的公义胜于神的公义，

chapters.en: Yet you ask him, ‘What profit is it to me,and what do I gain by not sinning?’
chapters.zh: 才说这与我有什么益处。我不犯罪比犯罪有什么好处呢？

chapters.en: “I would like to reply to you and to your friends with you.
chapters.zh: 我要回答你，和在你这里的朋友。

chapters.en: Look up at the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds so high above you.
chapters.zh: 你要向天观看，瞻望那高于你的穹苍。

chapters.en: If you sin, how does that affect him? If your sins are many, what does that do to him?
chapters.zh: 你若犯罪，能使神受何害呢？你的过犯加增，能使神受何损呢？

chapters.en: If you are righteous, what do you give to him, or what does he receive from your hand?
chapters.zh: 你若是公义，还能加增他什么呢？他从你手里还接受什么呢？

chapters.en: Your wickedness only affects humans like yourself, and your righteousness only other people.
chapters.zh: 你的过恶，或能害你这类的人。你的公义，或能叫世人得益处。

chapters.en: “People cry out under a load of oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the powerful.
chapters.zh: 人因多受欺压就哀求，因受能者的辖制（辖制原文作膀臂）便求救。

chapters.en: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
chapters.zh: 却无人说，造我的神在哪里？他使人夜间歌唱。

chapters.en: who teaches us more than he teaches the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds in the sky?’
chapters.zh: 教训我们胜于地上的走兽，使我们有聪明胜于空中的飞鸟。

chapters.en: He does not answer when people cry out because of the arrogance of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 他们在那里，因恶人的骄傲呼求，却无人答应。

chapters.en: Indeed, God does not listen to their empty plea; the Almighty pays no attention to it.
chapters.zh: 虚妄的呼求，神必不垂听。全能者也必不眷顾。

chapters.en: How much less, then, will he listen when you say that you do not see him, that your case is before him and you must wait for him,
chapters.zh: 何况你说，你不得见他。你的案件在他面前，你等候他吧。

chapters.en: and further, that his anger never punishes and he does not take the least notice of wickedness.
chapters.zh: 但如今因他未曾发怒降罚，也不甚理会狂傲，

chapters.en: So Job opens his mouth with empty talk; without knowledge he multiplies words.”
chapters.zh: 所以约伯开口说虚妄的话，多发无知识的言语。

chapters.en: Elihu continued:
chapters.zh: 以利户又接着说，

chapters.en: “Bear with me a little longer and I will show you that there is more to be said in God’s behalf.
chapters.zh: 你再容我片时，我就指示你，因我还有话为神说。

chapters.en: I get my knowledge from afar; I will ascribe justice to my Maker.
chapters.zh: 我要将所知道的从远处引来，将公义归给造我的主。

chapters.en: Be assured that my words are not false; one who has perfect knowledge is with you.
chapters.zh: 我的言语真不虚谎。有知识全备的与你同在。

chapters.en: “God is mighty, but despises no one; he is mighty, and firm in his purpose.
chapters.zh: 神有大能，并不藐视人。他的智慧甚广。

chapters.en: He does not keep the wicked alive but gives the afflicted their rights.
chapters.zh: 他不保护恶人的性命，却为困苦人伸冤。

chapters.en: He does not take his eyes off the righteous; he enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever.
chapters.zh: 他时常看顾义人，使他们和君王同坐宝座，永远要被高举。

chapters.en: But if people are bound in chains, held fast by cords of affliction,
chapters.zh: 他们若被锁链捆住，被苦难的绳索缠住，

chapters.en: he tells them what they have done— that they have sinned arrogantly.
chapters.zh: 他就把他们的作为，和过犯指示他们，叫他们知道有骄傲的行动。

chapters.en: He makes them listen to correction and commands them to repent of their evil.
chapters.zh: 他也开通他们的耳朵，得受教训，吩咐他们离开罪孽转回。

chapters.en: If they obey and serve him, they will spend the rest of their days in prosperity and their years in contentment.
chapters.zh: 他们若听从事奉他，就必度日亨通，历年福乐。

chapters.en: But if they do not listen, they will perish by the sword and die without knowledge.
chapters.zh: 若不听从，就要被刀杀灭，无知无识而死。

chapters.en: “The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when he fetters them, they do not cry for help.
chapters.zh: 那心中不敬虔的人积蓄怒气。神捆绑他们，他们竟不求救。

chapters.en: They die in their youth, among male prostitutes of the shrines.
chapters.zh: 必在青年时死亡，与污秽人一样丧命。

chapters.en: But those who suffer he delivers in their suffering; he speaks to them in their affliction.
chapters.zh: 神借着困苦救拔困苦人，趁他们受欺压，开通他们的耳朵。

chapters.en: “He is wooing you from the jaws of distress to a spacious place free from restriction, to the comfort of your table laden with choice food.
chapters.zh: 神也必引你出离患难，进入宽阔不狭窄之地。摆在你席上的必满有肥甘。

chapters.en: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have taken hold of you.
chapters.zh: 但你满口有恶人批评的言语。判断和刑罚抓住你。

chapters.en: Be careful that no one entices you by riches; do not let a large bribe turn you aside.
chapters.zh: 不可容忿怒触动你，使你不服责罚。也不可因赎价大就偏行。

chapters.en: Would your wealth or even all your mighty efforts sustain you so you would not be in distress?
chapters.zh: 你的呼求（呼求或作资财），或是你一切的势力，果有灵验，叫你不受患难吗？

chapters.en: Do not long for the night, to drag people away from their homes.
chapters.zh: 不要切慕黑夜，就是众民在本处被除灭的时候。

chapters.en: Beware of turning to evil, which you seem to prefer to affliction.
chapters.zh: 你要谨慎，不可重看罪孽，因你选择罪孽，过于选择苦难。

chapters.en: “God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
chapters.zh: 神行事有高大的能力。教训人的有谁像他呢？

chapters.en: Who has prescribed his ways for him, or said to him, ‘You have done wrong’?
chapters.zh: 谁派定他的道路？谁能说，你所行的不义？

chapters.en: Remember to extol his work, which people have praised in song.
chapters.zh: 你不可忘记称赞他所行的为大，就是人所歌颂的。

chapters.en: All humanity has seen it; mortals gaze on it from afar.
chapters.zh: 他所行的，万人都看见，世人也从远处观看。

chapters.en: How great is God—beyond our understanding! The number of his years is past finding out.
chapters.zh: 神为大，我们不能全知，他的年数不能测度。

chapters.en: “He draws up the drops of water, which distill as rain to the streams ;
chapters.zh: 他吸取水点，这水点从云雾中就变成雨。

chapters.en: the clouds pour down their moisture and abundant showers fall on mankind.
chapters.zh: 云彩将雨落下，沛然降与世人。

chapters.en: Who can understand how he spreads out the clouds, how he thunders from his pavilion?
chapters.zh: 谁能明白云彩如何铺张，和神行宫的雷声呢？

chapters.en: See how he scatters his lightning about him, bathing the depths of the sea.
chapters.zh: 他将亮光普照在自己的四围。他又遮覆海底。

chapters.en: This is the way he governs the nations and provides food in abundance.
chapters.zh: 他用这些审判众民，且赐丰富的粮食。

chapters.en: He fills his hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.
chapters.zh: 他以电光遮手，命闪电击中敌人（或作中了靶子）。

chapters.en: His thunder announces the coming storm; even the cattle make known its approach.
chapters.zh: 所发的雷声显明他的作为，又向牲畜指明要起暴风。

chapters.en: “At this my heart pounds and leaps from its place.
chapters.zh: 因此我心战兢，从原处移动。

chapters.en: Listen! Listen to the roar of his voice, to the rumbling that comes from his mouth.
chapters.zh: 听阿，神轰轰的声音，是他口中所发的响声。

chapters.en: He unleashes his lightning beneath the whole heaven and sends it to the ends of the earth.
chapters.zh: 他发响声震遍天下，发电光闪到地极。

chapters.en: After that comes the sound of his roar; he thunders with his majestic voice. When his voice resounds, he holds nothing back.
chapters.zh: 随后人听见有雷声轰轰，大发威严，雷电接连不断。

chapters.en: God’s voice thunders in marvelous ways; he does great things beyond our understanding.
chapters.zh: 神发出奇妙的雷声，他行大事，我们不能测透。

chapters.en: He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the rain shower, ‘Be a mighty downpour.’
chapters.zh: 他对雪说，要降在地上，对大雨和暴雨也是这样说。

chapters.en: So that everyone he has made may know his work, he stops all people from their labor.
chapters.zh: 他封住各人的手，叫所造的万人，都晓得他的作为。

chapters.en: The animals take cover; they remain in their dens.
chapters.zh: 百兽进入穴中，卧在洞内。

chapters.en: The tempest comes out from its chamber, the cold from the driving winds.
chapters.zh: 暴风出于南宫。寒冷出于北方。

chapters.en: The breath of God produces ice, and the broad waters become frozen.
chapters.zh: 神嘘气成冰。宽阔之水也都凝结。

chapters.en: He loads the clouds with moisture; he scatters his lightning through them.
chapters.zh: 他使密云盛满水气，布散电光之云。

chapters.en: At his direction they swirl around over the face of the whole earth to do whatever he commands them.
chapters.zh: 这云是借他的指引游行旋转，得以在全地面上，行他一切所吩咐的，

chapters.en: He brings the clouds to punish people, or to water his earth and show his love.
chapters.zh: 或为责罚，或为润地，或为施行慈爱。

chapters.en: “Listen to this, Job; stop and consider God’s wonders.
chapters.zh: 约伯阿，你要留心听，要站立思想神奇妙的作为。

chapters.en: Do you know how God controls the clouds and makes his lightning flash?
chapters.zh: 神如何吩咐这些，如何使云中的电光照耀，你知道吗？

chapters.en: Do you know how the clouds hang poised, those wonders of him who has perfect knowledge?
chapters.zh: 云彩如何浮于空中，那知识全备者奇妙的作为，你知道吗？

chapters.en: You who swelter in your clothes when the land lies hushed under the south wind,
chapters.zh: 南风使地寂静，你的衣服就如火热，你知道吗？

chapters.en: can you join him in spreading out the skies, hard as a mirror of cast bronze?
chapters.zh: 你岂能与神同铺穹苍吗？这穹苍坚硬，如同铸成的镜子。

chapters.en: “Tell us what we should say to him; we cannot draw up our case because of our darkness.
chapters.zh: 我们愚昧不能陈说。请你指教我们该对他说什么话。

chapters.en: Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?
chapters.zh: 人岂可说，我愿与他说话。岂有人自愿灭亡吗？

chapters.en: Now no one can look at the sun, bright as it is in the skies after the wind has swept them clean.
chapters.zh: 现在有云遮蔽，人不得见穹苍的光亮。但风吹过，天又发晴。

chapters.en: Out of the north he comes in golden splendor; God comes in awesome majesty.
chapters.zh: 金光出于北方，在神那里有可怕的威严。

chapters.en: The Almighty is beyond our reach and exalted in power; in his justice and great righteousness, he does not oppress.
chapters.zh: 论到全能者，我们不能测度。他大有能力，有公平和大义，必不苦待人。

chapters.en: Therefore, people revere him, for does he not have regard for all the wise in heart? ”
chapters.zh: 所以，人敬畏他。凡自以为心中有智慧的人，他都不顾念。

chapters.en: Then the LORD spoke to Job out of the storm. He said:
chapters.zh: 那时，耶和华从旋风中回答约伯说，

chapters.en: “Who is this that obscures my plans with words without knowledge?
chapters.zh: 谁用无知的言语，使我的旨意暗昧不明。

chapters.en: Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer me.
chapters.zh: 你要如勇士束腰。我问你，你可以指示我。
