chapters.en: People curse the one who hoards grain, but they pray God’s blessing on the one who is willing to sell.
chapters.zh: 屯粮不卖的，民必咒诅他。情愿出卖的，人必为他祝福。

chapters.en: Whoever seeks good finds favor, but evil comes to one who searches for it.
chapters.zh: 恳切求善的，就求得恩惠。惟独求恶的，恶必临到他身。

chapters.en: Those who trust in their riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like a green leaf.
chapters.zh: 倚仗自己财物的，必跌倒。义人必发旺如青叶。

chapters.en: Whoever brings ruin on their family will inherit only wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise.
chapters.zh: 扰害己家的，必承受清风。愚昧人必作慧心人的仆人。

chapters.en: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and the one who is wise saves lives.
chapters.zh: 义人所结的果子，就是生命树。有智慧的必能得人。

chapters.en: If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!
chapters.zh: 看哪，义人在世尚且受报，何况恶人和罪人呢？

chapters.en: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is stupid.
chapters.zh: 喜爱管教的，就是喜爱知识。恨恶责备的，却是畜类。

chapters.en: Good people obtain favor from the LORD, but he condemns those who devise wicked schemes.
chapters.zh: 善人必蒙耶和华的恩惠。设诡计的人，耶和华必定他的罪。

chapters.en: No one can be established through wickedness, but the righteous cannot be uprooted.
chapters.zh: 人靠恶行不能坚立。义人的根，必不动摇。

chapters.en: A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown, but a disgraceful wife is like decay in his bones.
chapters.zh: 才德的妇人，是丈夫的冠冕。贻羞的妇人，如同朽烂在她丈夫的骨中。

chapters.en: The plans of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.
chapters.zh: 义人的思念是公平。恶人的计谋是诡诈。

chapters.en: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
chapters.zh: 恶人的言论，是埋伏流人的血。正直人的口，必拯救人。

chapters.en: The wicked are overthrown and are no more, but the house of the righteous stands firm.
chapters.zh: 恶人倾覆，归于无有。义人的家，必站得住。

chapters.en: A person is praised according to their prudence, and one with a warped mind is despised.
chapters.zh: 人必按自己的智慧被称赞。心中乖谬的，必被藐视。

chapters.en: Better to be a nobody and yet have a servant than pretend to be somebody and have no food.
chapters.zh: 被人轻贱，却有仆人，强如自尊，缺少食物。

chapters.en: The righteous care for the needs of their animals, but the kindest acts of the wicked are cruel.
chapters.zh: 义人顾惜他牲畜的命。恶人的怜悯，也是残忍。

chapters.en: Those who work their land will have abundant food, but those who chase fantasies have no sense.
chapters.zh: 耕种自己田地的，必得饱食。追随虚浮的，却是无知。

chapters.en: The wicked desire the stronghold of evildoers, but the root of the righteous endures.
chapters.zh: 恶人想得坏人的网罗。义人的根，得以结实。

chapters.en: Evildoers are trapped by their sinful talk, and so the innocent escape trouble.
chapters.zh: 恶人嘴中的过错，是自己的网罗。但义人必脱离患难。

chapters.en: From the fruit of their lips people are filled with good things, and the work of their hands brings them reward.
chapters.zh: 人因口所结的果子，必饱得美福。人手所作的，必为自己的报应。

chapters.en: The way of fools seems right to them, but the wise listen to advice.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人所行的，在自己眼中看为正直。惟智慧人，肯听人的劝教。

chapters.en: Fools show their annoyance at once, but the prudent overlook an insult.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人的恼怒，立时显露。通达人能忍辱藏羞。

chapters.en: An honest witness tells the truth, but a false witness tells lies.
chapters.zh: 说出真话的，显明公义。作假见证的，显出诡诈。

chapters.en: The words of the reckless pierce like swords, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
chapters.zh: 说话浮躁的，如刀刺人。智慧人的舌头，却为医人的良药。

chapters.en: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
chapters.zh: 口吐真言，永远坚立。舌说谎话，只存片时。

chapters.en: Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil, but those who promote peace have joy.
chapters.zh: 图谋恶事的，心存诡诈。劝人和睦的，便得喜乐。

chapters.en: No harm overtakes the righteous, but the wicked have their fill of trouble.
chapters.zh: 义人不遭灾害恶人满受祸患。

chapters.en: The LORD detests lying lips, but he delights in people who are trustworthy.
chapters.zh: 说谎言的嘴，为耶和华所憎恶。行事诚实的，为他所喜悦。

chapters.en: The prudent keep their knowledge to themselves, but a fool’s heart blurts out folly.
chapters.zh: 通达人隐藏知识。愚昧人的心，彰显愚昧。

chapters.en: Diligent hands will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
chapters.zh: 殷勤人的手必掌权。懒惰的人必服苦。

chapters.en: Anxiety weighs down the heart, but a kind word cheers it up.
chapters.zh: 人心忧虑，屈而不伸。一句良言，使心欢乐。

chapters.en: The righteous choose their friends carefully, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
chapters.zh: 义人引导他的邻舍。恶人的道，叫人失迷。

chapters.en: The lazy do not roast any game, but the diligent feed on the riches of the hunt.
chapters.zh: 懒惰的人，不烤打猎所得的。殷勤的人，却得宝贵的财物。

chapters.en: In the way of righteousness there is life; along that path is immortality.
chapters.zh: 在公义的道上有生命。其路之中，并无死亡。

chapters.en: A wise son heeds his father’s instruction, but a mocker does not respond to rebukes.
chapters.zh: 智慧子听父亲的教训。亵慢人不听责备。

chapters.en: From the fruit of their lips people enjoy good things, but the unfaithful have an appetite for violence.
chapters.zh: 人因口所结的果子，必享美福。奸诈人必遭强暴。

chapters.en: Those who guard their lips preserve their lives, but those who speak rashly will come to ruin.
chapters.zh: 谨守口的，得保生命。大张嘴的，必致败亡。

chapters.en: A sluggard’s appetite is never filled, but the desires of the diligent are fully satisfied.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人羡慕，却无所得。殷勤人必得丰裕。

chapters.en: The righteous hate what is false, but the wicked make themselves a stench and bring shame on themselves.
chapters.zh: 义人恨恶谎言。恶人有臭名，且致惭愧。

chapters.en: Righteousness guards the person of integrity, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
chapters.zh: 行为正直的，有公义保守。犯罪的被邪恶倾覆。

chapters.en: One person pretends to be rich, yet has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.
chapters.zh: 假作富足的，却一无所有。装作穷乏的，却广有财物。

chapters.en: A person’s riches may ransom their life, but the poor cannot respond to threatening rebukes.
chapters.zh: 人的赀财，是他生命的赎价。穷乏人却听不见威吓的话。

chapters.en: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out.
chapters.zh: 义人的光明亮。（明亮原文作欢喜）恶人的灯要熄灭。

chapters.en: Where there is strife, there is pride, but wisdom is found in those who take advice.
chapters.zh: 骄傲只启争竞。听劝言的，却有智慧。

chapters.en: Dishonest money dwindles away, but whoever gathers money little by little makes it grow.
chapters.zh: 不劳而得之财，必然消耗。勤劳积蓄的，必见加增。

chapters.en: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but a longing fulfilled is a tree of life.
chapters.zh: 所盼望的迟延未得，令人心忧。所愿意的临到，却是生命树。

chapters.en: Whoever scorns instruction will pay for it, but whoever respects a command is rewarded.
chapters.zh: 藐视训言的，自取灭亡。敬畏诫命的，必得善报。

chapters.en: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning a person from the snares of death.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的法则，（或作指教）是生命的泉源，可以使人离开死亡的网罗。

chapters.en: Good judgment wins favor, but the way of the unfaithful leads to their destruction.
chapters.zh: 美好的聪明，使人蒙恩。奸诈人的道路，崎岖难行。

chapters.en: All who are prudent act with knowledge, but fools expose their folly.
chapters.zh: 凡通达人都凭知识行事。愚昧人张扬自己的愚昧。

chapters.en: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy envoy brings healing.
chapters.zh: 奸恶的使者，必陷在祸患里。忠信的使臣，乃医人的良药。

chapters.en: Whoever disregards discipline comes to poverty and shame, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
chapters.zh: 弃绝管教的，必致贫受辱。领受责备的，必得尊荣。

chapters.en: A longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools detest turning from evil.
chapters.zh: 所欲的成就，心觉甘甜。远离恶事，为愚昧人所憎恶。

chapters.en: Walk with the wise and become wise, for a companion of fools suffers harm.
chapters.zh: 与智慧人同行的，必得智慧。和愚昧人作伴的，必受亏损。

chapters.en: Trouble pursues the sinner, but the righteous are rewarded with good things.
chapters.zh: 祸患追赶罪人。义人必得善报。

chapters.en: A good person leaves an inheritance for their children’s children, but a sinner’s wealth is stored up for the righteous.
chapters.zh: 善人给子孙遗留产业。罪人为义人积存赀财。

chapters.en: An unplowed field produces food for the poor, but injustice sweeps it away.
chapters.zh: 穷人耕种多得粮食，但因不义有消灭的。

chapters.en: Whoever spares the rod hates their children, but the one who loves their children is careful to discipline them.
chapters.zh: 不忍用杖打儿子的，是恨恶他。疼爱儿子的，随时管教。

chapters.en: The righteous eat to their hearts’ content, but the stomach of the wicked goes hungry.
chapters.zh: 义人吃得饱足。恶人肚腹缺粮。

chapters.en: The wise woman builds her house, but with her own hands the foolish one tears hers down.
chapters.zh: 智慧妇人，建立家室。愚妄妇人，亲手拆毁。

chapters.en: Whoever fears the LORD walks uprightly, but those who despise him are devious in their ways.
chapters.zh: 行动正直的，敬畏耶和华。行事乖僻的，却藐视他。

chapters.en: A fool’s mouth lashes out with pride, but the lips of the wise protect them.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人口中骄傲，如杖责打己身。智慧人的嘴，必保守自己。

chapters.en: Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty, but from the strength of an ox come abundant harvests.
chapters.zh: 家里无牛，槽头干净。土产加多，乃凭牛力。

chapters.en: An honest witness does not deceive, but a false witness pours out lies.
chapters.zh: 诚实见证人，不说谎话。假见证人，吐出谎言。

chapters.en: The mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
chapters.zh: 亵慢人寻智慧，却寻不着。聪明人易得知识。

chapters.en: Stay away from a fool, for you will not find knowledge on their lips.
chapters.zh: 到愚昧人面前，不见他嘴中有知识。

chapters.en: The wisdom of the prudent is to give thought to their ways, but the folly of fools is deception.
chapters.zh: 通达人的智慧，在乎明白己道。愚昧人的愚妄，乃是诡诈。（或作自欺）

chapters.en: Fools mock at making amends for sin, but goodwill is found among the upright.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人犯罪，以为戏耍。（或作赎愆祭愚弄愚妄人）正直人互相喜悦。

chapters.en: Each heart knows its own bitterness, and no one else can share its joy.
chapters.zh: 心中的苦楚，自己知道。心里的喜乐，外人无干。

chapters.en: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
chapters.zh: 奸恶人的房屋必倾倒。正直人的帐棚必兴盛。

chapters.en: There is a way that appears to be right, but in the end it leads to death.
chapters.zh: 有一条路人以为正。至终成为死亡之路。

chapters.en: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and rejoicing may end in grief.
chapters.zh: 人在喜笑中，心也忧愁。快乐至极，就生愁苦。

chapters.en: The faithless will be fully repaid for their ways, and the good rewarded for theirs.
chapters.zh: 心中背道的，必满得自己的结果。善人必从自己的行为，得以知足。

chapters.en: The simple believe anything, but the prudent give thought to their steps.
chapters.zh: 愚蒙人是话都信。通达人步步谨慎。

chapters.en: The wise fear the LORD and shun evil, but a fool is hotheaded and yet feels secure.
chapters.zh: 智慧人惧怕，就远离恶事。愚妄人却狂傲自恃。

chapters.en: A quick-tempered person does foolish things, and the one who devises evil schemes is hated.
chapters.zh: 轻易发怒的，行事愚妄。设立诡计的，被人恨恶。

chapters.en: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
chapters.zh: 愚蒙人得愚昧为产业。通达人得知识为冠冕。

chapters.en: Evildoers will bow down in the presence of the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 坏人俯伏在善人面前。恶人俯伏在义人门口。

chapters.en: The poor are shunned even by their neighbors, but the rich have many friends.
chapters.zh: 贫穷人连邻舍也恨他。富足人朋友最多。

chapters.en: It is a sin to despise one’s neighbor, but blessed is the one who is kind to the needy.
chapters.zh: 藐视邻舍的，这人有罪。怜悯贫穷的，这人有福。

chapters.en: Do not those who plot evil go astray? But those who plan what is good find love and faithfulness.
chapters.zh: 谋恶的岂非走入迷途吗？谋善的必得慈爱和诚实。

chapters.en: All hard work brings a profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
chapters.zh: 诸般勤劳，都有益处。嘴上多言，乃致穷乏。

chapters.en: The wealth of the wise is their crown, but the folly of fools yields folly.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的财，为自己的冠冕。愚妄人的愚昧，终是愚昧。

chapters.en: A truthful witness saves lives, but a false witness is deceitful.
chapters.zh: 作真见证的，救人性命。吐出谎言的，施行诡诈。

chapters.en: Whoever fears the LORD has a secure fortress, and for their children it will be a refuge.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华的，大有倚靠。他的儿女，也有避难所。

chapters.en: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person from the snares of death.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华，就是生命的泉源，可以使人离开死亡的网罗。

chapters.en: A large population is a king’s glory, but without subjects a prince is ruined.
chapters.zh: 帝王荣耀在乎民多。君王衰败在乎民少。

chapters.en: Whoever is patient has great understanding, but one who is quick-tempered displays folly.
chapters.zh: 不轻易发怒的，大有聪明。性情暴躁的，大显愚妄。

chapters.en: A heart at peace gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
chapters.zh: 心中安静，是肉体的生命。嫉妒是骨中的朽烂。

chapters.en: Whoever oppresses the poor shows contempt for their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors God.
chapters.zh: 欺压贫寒的，是辱没造他的主。怜悯穷乏的，乃是尊敬主

chapters.en: When calamity comes, the wicked are brought down, but even in death the righteous seek refuge in God.
chapters.zh: 恶人在所行的恶上，必被推倒。义人临死，有所投靠。

chapters.en: Wisdom reposes in the heart of the discerning and even among fools she lets herself be known.
chapters.zh: 智慧存在聪明人心中。愚昧人心里所存的，显而易见。

chapters.en: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin condemns any people.
chapters.zh: 公义使邦国高举。罪恶是人民的羞辱。

chapters.en: A king delights in a wise servant, but a shameful servant arouses his fury.
chapters.zh: 智慧的臣子，蒙王恩惠。贻羞的仆人，遭其震怒。

chapters.en: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
chapters.zh: 回答柔和，使怒消退。言语暴戾，触动怒气。

chapters.en: The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge, but the mouth of the fool gushes folly.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的舌，善发知识。愚昧人的口，吐出愚昧。

chapters.en: The eyes of the LORD are everywhere, keeping watch on the wicked and the good.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的眼目，无处不在。恶人善人，他都鉴察。

chapters.en: The soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.
chapters.zh: 温良的舌，是生命树。乖谬的嘴，使人心碎。

chapters.en: A fool spurns a parent’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction shows prudence.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人藐视父亲的管教。领受责备的，得着见识。

chapters.en: The house of the righteous contains great treasure, but the income of the wicked brings ruin.
chapters.zh: 义人家中，多有财宝。恶人得利，反受扰害。

chapters.en: The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but the hearts of fools are not upright.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的嘴，播扬知识。愚昧人的心，并不如此。

chapters.en: The LORD detests the sacrifice of the wicked, but the prayer of the upright pleases him.
chapters.zh: 恶人献祭，为耶和华所憎恶。正直人祈祷，为他所喜悦。

chapters.en: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but he loves those who pursue righteousness.
chapters.zh: 恶人的道路，为耶和华所憎恶。追求公义的，为他所喜爱。

chapters.en: Stern discipline awaits anyone who leaves the path; the one who hates correction will die.
chapters.zh: 舍弃正路的，必受严刑。恨恶责备的，必致死亡。

chapters.en: Death and Destruction lie open before the LORD— how much more do human hearts!
chapters.zh: 阴间和灭亡，尚在耶和华眼前，何况世人的心呢？

chapters.en: Mockers resent correction, so they avoid the wise.
chapters.zh: 亵慢人不爱受责备。他也不就近智慧人。

chapters.en: A happy heart makes the face cheerful, but heartache crushes the spirit.
chapters.zh: 心中喜乐，面带笑容。心里忧愁，灵被损伤。

chapters.en: The discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.
chapters.zh: 聪明人心求知识。愚昧人口吃愚昧。

chapters.en: All the days of the oppressed are wretched, but the cheerful heart has a continual feast.
chapters.zh: 困苦人的日子，都是愁苦。心中欢畅的，常享丰筵。

chapters.en: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great wealth with turmoil.
chapters.zh: 少有财宝，敬畏耶和华，强如多有财宝，烦乱不安。

chapters.en: Better a small serving of vegetables with love than a fattened calf with hatred.
chapters.zh: 吃素菜，彼此相爱，强如吃肥牛，彼此相恨。

chapters.en: A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but the one who is patient calms a quarrel.
chapters.zh: 暴怒的人，挑启争端。忍怒的人，止息分争。

chapters.en: The way of the sluggard is blocked with thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人的道，像荆棘的篱笆。正直人的路，是平坦的大道。

chapters.en: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother.
chapters.zh: 智慧子使父亲喜乐。愚昧人藐视母亲。

chapters.en: Folly brings joy to one who has no sense, but whoever has understanding keeps a straight course.
chapters.zh: 无知的人，以愚妄为乐。聪明的人，按正直而行。

chapters.en: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
chapters.zh: 不先商议，所谋无效。谋士众多，所谋乃成。

chapters.en: A person finds joy in giving an apt reply— and how good is a timely word!
chapters.zh: 口善应对，自觉喜乐。话合其时，何等美好。

chapters.en: The path of life leads upward for the prudent to keep them from going down to the realm of the dead.
chapters.zh: 智慧人从生命的道上升，使他远离在下的阴间。

chapters.en: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but he sets the widow’s boundary stones in place.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必拆毁骄傲人的家。却要立定寡妇的地界。

chapters.en: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but gracious words are pure in his sight.
chapters.zh: 恶谋为耶和华所憎恶。良言乃为纯净。

chapters.en: The greedy bring ruin to their households, but the one who hates bribes will live.
chapters.zh: 贪恋财利的，扰害己家。恨恶贿赂的，必得存活。

chapters.en: The heart of the righteous weighs its answers, but the mouth of the wicked gushes evil.
chapters.zh: 义人的心，思量如何回答。恶人的口，吐出恶言。

chapters.en: The LORD is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 耶和华远离恶人。却听义人的祷告。

chapters.en: Light in a messenger’s eyes brings joy to the heart, and good news gives health to the bones.
chapters.zh: 眼有光使心喜乐。好信息使骨滋润。

chapters.en: Whoever heeds life-giving correction will be at home among the wise.
chapters.zh: 听从生命责备的，必常在智慧人中。

chapters.en: Those who disregard discipline despise themselves, but the one who heeds correction gains understanding.
chapters.zh: 弃绝管教的，轻看自己的生命。听从责备的，却得智慧。

chapters.en: Wisdom’s instruction is to fear the LORD, and humility comes before honor.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华，是智慧的训诲。尊荣以前，必有谦卑。

chapters.en: To humans belong the plans of the heart, but from the LORD comes the proper answer of the tongue.
chapters.zh: 心中的谋算在乎人。舌头的应对，由于耶和华。

chapters.en: All a person’s ways seem pure to them, but motives are weighed by the LORD.
chapters.zh: 人一切所行的，在自己眼中看为清洁。惟有耶和华衡量人心。

chapters.en: Commit to the LORD whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
chapters.zh: 你所作的，要交托耶和华，你所谋的，就必成立。

chapters.en: The LORD works out everything to its proper end— even the wicked for a day of disaster.
chapters.zh: 耶和华所造的，各适其用。就是恶人，也为祸患的日子所造。

chapters.en: The LORD detests all the proud of heart. Be sure of this: They will not go unpunished.
chapters.zh: 凡心里骄傲的，为耶和华所憎恶。虽然连手，他必不免受罚。

chapters.en: Through love and faithfulness sin is atoned for; through the fear of the LORD evil is avoided.
chapters.zh: 因怜悯诚实，罪孽得赎。敬畏耶和华的，远离恶事。

chapters.en: When the LORD takes pleasure in anyone’s way, he causes their enemies to make peace with them.
chapters.zh: 人所行的若蒙耶和华喜悦，耶和华也使他的仇敌与他和好。

chapters.en: Better a little with righteousness than much gain with injustice.
chapters.zh: 多有财利，行事不义，不如少有财利，行事公义。

chapters.en: In their hearts humans plan their course, but the LORD establishes their steps.
chapters.zh: 人心筹算自己的道路。惟耶和华指引他的脚步。

chapters.en: The lips of a king speak as an oracle, and his mouth does not betray justice.
chapters.zh: 王的嘴中有神语。审判之时，他的口，必不差错。

chapters.en: Honest scales and balances belong to the LORD; all the weights in the bag are of his making.
chapters.zh: 公道的天平和秤，都属耶和华。囊中一切法码，都为他所定。

chapters.en: Kings detest wrongdoing, for a throne is established through righteousness.
chapters.zh: 作恶为王所憎恶。因国位是靠公义坚立。

chapters.en: Kings take pleasure in honest lips; they value the one who speaks what is right.
chapters.zh: 公义的嘴，为王所喜悦。说正直话的，为王所喜爱。

chapters.en: A king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but the wise will appease it.
chapters.zh: 王的震怒，如杀人的使者。但智慧人能止息王怒。

chapters.en: When a king’s face brightens, it means life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.
chapters.zh: 王的脸光，使人有生命。王的恩典，好像春云时雨。

chapters.en: How much better to get wisdom than gold, to get insight rather than silver!
chapters.zh: 得智慧胜似得金子。选聪明强如选银子。

chapters.en: The highway of the upright avoids evil; those who guard their ways preserve their lives.
chapters.zh: 正直人的道，是远离恶事。谨守己路的，是保全性命。

chapters.en: Pride goes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.
chapters.zh: 骄傲在败坏以先，狂心在跌倒之前。

chapters.en: Better to be lowly in spirit along with the oppressed than to share plunder with the proud.
chapters.zh: 心里谦卑与穷乏人来往，强如将掳物与骄傲人同分。

chapters.en: Whoever gives heed to instruction prospers,and blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD.
chapters.zh: 谨守训言的，必得好处。倚靠耶和华的，便为有福。

chapters.en: The wise in heart are called discerning, and gracious words promote instruction.
chapters.zh: 心中有智慧，必称为通达人。嘴中的甜言，加增人的学问。

chapters.en: Prudence is a fountain of life to the prudent, but folly brings punishment to fools.
chapters.zh: 人有智慧就有生命的泉源。愚昧人必被愚昧惩治。

chapters.en: The hearts of the wise make their mouths prudent, and their lips promote instruction.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的心，教训他的口，又使他的嘴，增长学问。

chapters.en: Gracious words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
chapters.zh: 良言如同蜂房，使心觉甘甜，使骨得医治。

chapters.en: There is a way that appears to be right, but in the end it leads to death.
chapters.zh: 有一条路，人以为正，至终成为死亡之路。

chapters.en: The appetite of laborers works for them; their hunger drives them on.
chapters.zh: 劳力人的胃口，使他劳力，因为他的口腹催逼他。

chapters.en: A scoundrel plots evil, and on their lips it is like a scorching fire.
chapters.zh: 匪徒图谋奸恶，嘴上仿佛有烧焦的火。

chapters.en: A perverse person stirs up conflict, and a gossip separates close friends.
chapters.zh: 乖僻人播散分争。传舌的离间密友。

chapters.en: A violent person entices their neighbor and leads them down a path that is not good.
chapters.zh: 强暴人诱惑邻舍，领他走不善之道。

chapters.en: Whoever winks with their eye is plotting perversity; whoever purses their lips is bent on evil.
chapters.zh: 眼目紧合的，图谋乖僻，嘴唇紧闭的，成就邪恶。

chapters.en: Gray hair is a crown of splendor; it is attained in the way of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 白发是荣耀的冠冕。在公义的道上，必能得着。

chapters.en: Better a patient person than a warrior, one with self-control than one who takes a city.
chapters.zh: 不轻易发怒的，胜过勇士。治服己心的，强如取城。

chapters.en: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 签放在怀里。定事由耶和华。

chapters.en: Better a dry crust with peace and quiet than a house full of feasting, with strife.
chapters.zh: 设筵满屋，大家相争，不如有块干饼，大家相安。

chapters.en: A prudent servant will rule over a disgraceful son and will share the inheritance as one of the family.
chapters.zh: 仆人办事聪明，必管辖贻羞之子，又在众子中，同分产业。

chapters.en: The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests the heart.
chapters.zh: 鼎为炼银，炉为炼金。惟有耶和华熬炼人心。

chapters.en: A wicked person listens to deceitful lips; a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue.
chapters.zh: 行恶的留心听奸诈之言。说谎的侧耳听邪恶之语。

chapters.en: Whoever mocks the poor shows contempt for their Maker; whoever gloats over disaster will not go unpunished.
chapters.zh: 戏笑穷人的，是辱没造他的主。幸灾乐祸的，必不免受罚。

chapters.en: Children’s children are a crown to the aged, and parents are the pride of their children.
chapters.zh: 子孙为老人的冠冕。父亲是儿女的荣耀。

chapters.en: Eloquent lips are unsuited to a godless fool— how much worse lying lips to a ruler!
chapters.zh: 愚顽人说美言本不相宜，何况君王说谎话呢？

chapters.en: A bribe is seen as a charm by the one who gives it; they think success will come at every turn.
chapters.zh: 贿赂在馈送的人眼中，看为宝玉。随处运动，都得顺利。

chapters.en: Whoever would foster love covers over an offense, but whoever repeats the matter separates close friends.
chapters.zh: 遮掩人过的，寻求人爱。屡次挑错的，离间密友。

chapters.en: A rebuke impresses a discerning person more than a hundred lashes a fool.
chapters.zh: 一句责备话，深入聪明人的心，强如责打愚昧人一百下。

chapters.en: Evildoers foster rebellion against God; the messenger of death will be sent against them.
chapters.zh: 恶人只寻背叛，所以必有严厉的使者，奉差攻击他。

chapters.en: Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool bent on folly.
chapters.zh: 宁可遇见丢崽子的母熊，不可遇见正行愚妄的愚昧人。

chapters.en: Evil will never leave the house of one who pays back evil for good.
chapters.zh: 以恶报善的，祸患必不离他的家。

chapters.en: Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam; so drop the matter before a dispute breaks out.
chapters.zh: 分争的起头，如水放开。所以在争闹之先，必当止息争竞。

chapters.en: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent— the LORD detests them both.
chapters.zh: 定恶人为义的，定义人为恶的，这都为耶和华所憎恶。

chapters.en: Why should fools have money in hand to buy wisdom, when they are not able to understand it?
chapters.zh: 愚昧人既无聪明，为何手拿价银买智慧呢？

chapters.en: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for a time of adversity.
chapters.zh: 朋友乃时常亲爱。弟兄为患难而生。

chapters.en: One who has no sense shakes hands in pledge and puts up security for a neighbor.
chapters.zh: 在邻舍面前击掌作保，乃是无知的人。

chapters.en: Whoever loves a quarrel loves sin; whoever builds a high gate invites destruction.
chapters.zh: 喜爱争竞的，是喜爱过犯。高立家门的，乃自取败坏。

chapters.en: One whose heart is corrupt does not prosper; one whose tongue is perverse falls into trouble.
chapters.zh: 心存邪僻的，寻不着好处。舌弄是非的，陷在祸患中。

chapters.en: To have a fool for a child brings grief; there is no joy for the parent of a godless fool.
chapters.zh: 生愚昧子的，必自愁苦。愚顽人的父，毫无喜乐。

chapters.en: A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
chapters.zh: 喜乐的心，乃是良药。忧伤的灵，使骨枯干。

chapters.en: The wicked accept bribes in secret to pervert the course of justice.
chapters.zh: 恶人暗中受贿赂，为要颠倒判断。

chapters.en: A discerning person keeps wisdom in view, but a fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
chapters.zh: 明哲人眼前有智慧。愚昧人眼望地极。

chapters.en: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to the mother who bore him.
chapters.zh: 愚昧子使父亲愁烦，使母亲忧苦。

chapters.en: If imposing a fine on the innocent is not good, surely to flog honest officials is not right.
chapters.zh: 刑罚义人为不善。责打君子为不义。

chapters.en: The one who has knowledge uses words with restraint, and whoever has understanding is even-tempered.
chapters.zh: 寡少言语的有知识。性情温良的有聪明。

chapters.en: Even fools are thought wise if they keep silent, and discerning if they hold their tongues.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人若静默不言，也可算为智慧。闭口不说，也可算为聪明。

chapters.en: An unfriendly person pursues selfish ends and against all sound judgment starts quarrels.
chapters.zh: 与众寡合的，独自寻求心愿，并恼恨一切真智慧。

chapters.en: Fools find no pleasure in understanding but delight in airing their own opinions.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人不喜爱明哲，只喜爱显露心意。

chapters.en: When wickedness comes, so does contempt, and with shame comes reproach.
chapters.zh: 恶人来，藐视随来。羞耻到，辱骂同到。

chapters.en: The words of the mouth are deep waters, but the fountain of wisdom is a rushing stream.
chapters.zh: 人口中的言语，如同深水。智慧的泉源，好像涌流的河水。

chapters.en: It is not good to be partial to the wicked and so deprive the innocent of justice.
chapters.zh: 瞻徇恶人的情面，偏断义人的案件，都为不善。

chapters.en: The lips of fools bring them strife, and their mouths invite a beating.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人张嘴启争端，开口招鞭打。

chapters.en: The mouths of fools are their undoing, and their lips are a snare to their very lives.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人的口，自取败坏。他的嘴，是他生命的网罗。

chapters.en: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they go down to the inmost parts.
chapters.zh: 传舌人的言语，如同美食，深入人的心腹。

chapters.en: One who is slack in his work is brother to one who destroys.
chapters.zh: 作工懈怠的，与浪费人为弟兄。

chapters.en: The name of the LORD is a fortified tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的名，是坚固台。义人奔入，便得安稳。

chapters.en: The wealth of the rich is their fortified city; they imagine it a wall too high to scale.
chapters.zh: 富足人的财物，是他的坚城，在他心想，犹如高墙。

chapters.en: Before a downfall the heart is haughty, but humility comes before honor.
chapters.zh: 败坏之先，人心骄傲。尊荣以前，必有谦卑。

chapters.en: To answer before listening— that is folly and shame.
chapters.zh: 未曾听完先回答的，便是他的愚昧，和羞辱。

chapters.en: The human spirit can endure in sickness, but a crushed spirit who can bear?
chapters.zh: 人有疾病，心能忍耐。心灵忧伤，谁能承当呢？

chapters.en: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, for the ears of the wise seek it out.
chapters.zh: 聪明人的心得知识。智慧人的耳求知识。

chapters.en: A gift opens the way and ushers the giver into the presence of the great.
chapters.zh: 人的礼物，为他开路，引他到高位的人面前。

chapters.en: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
chapters.zh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理。但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

chapters.en: Casting the lot settles disputes and keeps strong opponents apart.
chapters.zh: 掣签能止息争竞，也能解散强胜的人。

chapters.en: A brother wronged is more unyielding than a fortified city; disputes are like the barred gates of a citadel.
chapters.zh: 弟兄结怨，劝他和好，比取坚固城还难。这样的争竞，如同坚寨的门闩。

chapters.en: From the fruit of their mouth a person’s stomach is filled; with the harvest of their lips they are satisfied.
chapters.zh: 人口中所结的果子，必充满肚腹。他嘴所出的，必使他饱足。

chapters.en: The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
chapters.zh: 生死在舌头的权下。喜爱他的，必吃他所结的果子。

chapters.en: He who finds a wife finds what is good and receives favor from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 得着贤妻的，是得着好处，也是蒙了耶和华的恩惠。

chapters.en: The poor plead for mercy, but the rich answer harshly.
chapters.zh: 贫穷人说哀求的话。富足人用威吓的话回答。

chapters.en: One who has unreliable friends soon comes to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
chapters.zh: 滥交朋友的，自取败坏。但有一朋友，比弟兄更亲密。

chapters.en: Better the poor whose walk is blameless than a fool whose lips are perverse.
chapters.zh: 行为纯正的贫穷人，胜过乖谬愚妄的富足人。

chapters.en: Desire without knowledge is not good— how much more will hasty feet miss the way!
chapters.zh: 心无知识的，乃为不善。脚步急快的难免犯罪。

chapters.en: A person’s own folly leads to their ruin, yet their heart rages against the LORD.
chapters.zh: 人的愚昧，倾败他的道。他的心也抱怨耶和华。

chapters.en: Wealth attracts many friends, but even the closest friend of the poor person deserts them.
chapters.zh: 财物使朋友增多。但穷人朋友远离。

chapters.en: A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever pours out lies will not go free.
chapters.zh: 作假见证的，必不免受罚。吐出谎言的，终不能逃脱。

chapters.en: Many curry favor with a ruler, and everyone is the friend of one who gives gifts.
chapters.zh: 好施散的，有多人求他的恩情。爱送礼的，人都为他的朋友。

chapters.en: The poor are shunned by all their relatives— how much more do their friends avoid them! Though the poor pursue them with pleading, they are nowhere to be found.
chapters.zh: 贫穷人弟兄都恨他，何况他的朋友，更远离他。他用言语追随，他们却走了。

chapters.en: The one who gets wisdom loves life; the one who cherishes understanding will soon prosper.
chapters.zh: 得着智慧的，爱惜生命，保守聪明的，必得好处。

chapters.en: A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever pours out lies will perish.
chapters.zh: 作假见证的，不免受罚。吐出谎言的，也必灭亡。

chapters.en: It is not fitting for a fool to live in luxury— how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!
chapters.zh: 愚昧人宴乐度日，是不合宜的，何况仆人管辖王子呢？

chapters.en: A person’s wisdom yields patience; it is to one’s glory to overlook an offense.
chapters.zh: 人有见识，就不轻易发怒。宽恕人的过失，便是自己的荣耀。

chapters.en: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
chapters.zh: 王的忿怒，好像狮子吼叫。他的恩典，却如草上的甘露。

chapters.en: A foolish child is a father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like the constant dripping of a leaky roof.
chapters.zh: 愚昧的儿子，是父亲的祸患。妻子的争吵，如雨连连滴漏。

chapters.en: Houses and wealth are inherited from parents, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 房屋钱财。是祖宗所遗留的。惟有贤慧的妻，是耶和华所赐的。

chapters.en: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and the shiftless go hungry.
chapters.zh: 懒惰使人沉睡。懈怠的人，必受饥饿。

chapters.en: Whoever keeps commandments keeps their life, but whoever shows contempt for their ways will die.
chapters.zh: 谨守诫命的，保全生命。轻忽己路的，必致死亡。

chapters.en: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will reward them for what they have done.
chapters.zh: 怜悯贫穷的，就是借给耶和华。他的善行，耶和华必偿还。

chapters.en: Discipline your children, for in that there is hope; do not be a willing party to their death.
chapters.zh: 趁有指望，管教你的儿子。你的心不可任他死亡。

chapters.en: A hot-tempered person must pay the penalty; rescue them, and you will have to do it again.
chapters.zh: 暴怒的人，必受刑罚。你若救他，必须再救。

chapters.en: Listen to advice and accept discipline, and at the end you will be counted among the wise.
chapters.zh: 你要听劝教，受训诲，使你终久有智慧。

chapters.en: Many are the plans in a person’s heart, but it is the LORD’s purpose that prevails.
chapters.zh: 人心多有计谋。惟有耶和华的筹算，才能立定。

chapters.en: What a person desires is unfailing love ; better to be poor than a liar.
chapters.zh: 施行仁慈的，令人爱慕。穷人强如说谎言的。

chapters.en: The fear of the LORD leads to life; then one rests content, untouched by trouble.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华的，得着生命。他必恒久知足，不遭祸患。

chapters.en: A sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth!
chapters.zh: 懒惰人放手在盘子里。就是向口撤回，他也不肯。

chapters.en: Flog a mocker, and the simple will learn prudence; rebuke the discerning, and they will gain knowledge.
chapters.zh: 鞭打亵慢人，愚蒙人必长见识。责备明哲人，他就明白知识。

chapters.en: Whoever robs their father and drives out their mother is a child who brings shame and disgrace.
chapters.zh: 虐待父亲，撵出母亲的，是贻羞致辱之子。

chapters.en: Stop listening to instruction, my son, and you will stray from the words of knowledge.
chapters.zh: 我儿，不可听了教训，而又偏离知识的言语。

chapters.en: A corrupt witness mocks at justice, and the mouth of the wicked gulps down evil.
chapters.zh: 匪徒作见证戏笑公平。恶人的口吞下罪孽。

chapters.en: Penalties are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
chapters.zh: 刑罚是为亵慢人预备的。鞭打是为愚昧人的背预备的。

chapters.en: Wine is a mocker and beer a brawler; whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
chapters.zh: 酒能使人亵慢，浓酒使人喧嚷。凡因酒错误的，就无智慧。

chapters.en: A king’s wrath strikes terror like the roar of a lion; those who anger him forfeit their lives.
chapters.zh: 王的威吓，如同狮子吼叫。惹动他怒的，是自害己命。

chapters.en: It is to one’s honor to avoid strife, but every fool is quick to quarrel.
chapters.zh: 远离分争，是人的尊荣。愚妄人都爱争闹。

chapters.en: Sluggards do not plow in season; so at harvest time they look but find nothing.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人因冬寒不肯耕种。到收割的时候，他必讨饭，而无所得。

chapters.en: The purposes of a person’s heart are deep waters, but one who has insight draws them out.
chapters.zh: 人心怀藏谋略，好像深水。惟明哲人，才能汲引出来。

chapters.en: Many claim to have unfailing love, but a faithful person who can find?
chapters.zh: 人多述说自己的仁慈。但忠信人谁能遇着呢？

chapters.en: The righteous lead blameless lives; blessed are their children after them.
chapters.zh: 行为纯正的义人，他的子孙，是有福的。

chapters.en: When a king sits on his throne to judge, he winnows out all evil with his eyes.
chapters.zh: 王坐在审判的位上，以眼目驱散诸恶。

chapters.en: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am clean and without sin”?
chapters.zh: 谁能说，我洁净了我的心。我脱净了我的罪。

chapters.en: Differing weights and differing measures— the LORD detests them both.
chapters.zh: 两样的法码，两样的升斗，都为耶和华所憎恶。

chapters.en: Even small children are known by their actions, so is their conduct really pure and upright?
chapters.zh: 孩童的动作，是清洁，是正直，都显明他的本性。

chapters.en: Ears that hear and eyes that see— the LORD has made them both.
chapters.zh: 能听的耳，能看的眼，都是耶和华所造的。

chapters.en: Do not love sleep or you will grow poor; stay awake and you will have food to spare.
chapters.zh: 不要贪睡，免致贫穷。眼要睁开，你就吃饱。

chapters.en: “It’s no good, it’s no good!” says the buyer— then goes off and boasts about the purchase.
chapters.zh: 买物的说，不好，不好。及至买去，他便自夸。

chapters.en: Gold there is, and rubies in abundance, but lips that speak knowledge are a rare jewel.
chapters.zh: 有金子，和许多珍珠。（或作红宝石）惟有知识的嘴，乃为贵重的珍宝。

chapters.en: Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge if it is done for an outsider.
chapters.zh: 谁为生人作保，就拿谁的衣服。谁为外人作保，谁就要承当。

chapters.en: Food gained by fraud tastes sweet, but one ends up with a mouth full of gravel.
chapters.zh: 以虚谎而得的食物，人觉甘甜。但后来他的口，必充满尘沙。

chapters.en: Plans are established by seeking advice; so if you wage war, obtain guidance.
chapters.zh: 计谋都凭筹算立定。打仗要凭智谋。

chapters.en: A gossip betrays a confidence; so avoid anyone who talks too much.
chapters.zh: 往来传舌的，泄漏密事。大张嘴的不可与他结交。

chapters.en: If someone curses their father or mother, their lamp will be snuffed out in pitch darkness.
chapters.zh: 咒骂父母的，他的灯必灭，变为漆黑的黑暗。

chapters.en: An inheritance claimed too soon will not be blessed at the end.
chapters.zh: 起初速得的产业，终久却不为福。

chapters.en: Do not say, “I’ll pay you back for this wrong!” Wait for the LORD, and he will avenge you.
chapters.zh: 你不要说，我要以恶报恶。要等候耶和华，他必拯救你。

chapters.en: The LORD detests differing weights, and dishonest scales do not please him.
chapters.zh: 两样的法码，为耶和华所憎恶。诡诈的天平，也为不善。

chapters.en: A person’s steps are directed by the LORD. How then can anyone understand their own way?
chapters.zh: 人的脚步，为耶和华所定。人岂能明白自己的路呢？

chapters.en: It is a trap to dedicate something rashly and only later to consider one’s vows.
chapters.zh: 人冒失说，这是圣物，许愿之后才查问，就是自陷网罗。

chapters.en: A wise king winnows out the wicked; he drives the threshing wheel over them.
chapters.zh: 智慧的王，簸散恶人，用碌碡滚轧他们。

chapters.en: The human spirit is the lamp of the LORD that sheds light on one’s inmost being.
chapters.zh: 人的灵是耶和华的灯，鉴察人的心腹。

chapters.en: Love and faithfulness keep a king safe; through love his throne is made secure.
chapters.zh: 王因仁慈和诚实，得以保全他的国位，也因仁慈立稳。

chapters.en: The glory of young men is their strength, gray hair the splendor of the old.
chapters.zh: 强壮乃少年人的荣耀。白发为老年人的尊荣。

chapters.en: Blows and wounds scrub away evil, and beatings purge the inmost being.
chapters.zh: 鞭伤除净人的罪恶。责打能入人的心腹。

chapters.en: In the LORD’s hand the king’s heart is a stream of water that he channels toward all who please him.
chapters.zh: 王的心在耶和华手中，好像陇沟的水，随意流转。

chapters.en: A person may think their own ways are right, but the LORD weighs the heart.
chapters.zh: 人所行的，在自己眼中都看为正，惟有耶和华衡量人心。

chapters.en: To do what is right and just is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
chapters.zh: 行仁义公平，比献祭更蒙耶和华悦纳。

chapters.en: Haughty eyes and a proud heart— the unplowed field of the wicked—produce sin.
chapters.zh: 恶人发达，眼高心傲，这乃是罪。（发达原文作灯）

chapters.en: The plans of the diligent lead to profit as surely as haste leads to poverty.
chapters.zh: 殷勤筹划的，足致丰裕。行事急躁的，都必缺乏。

chapters.en: A fortune made by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor and a deadly snare.
chapters.zh: 用诡诈之舌求财的，就是自己取死。所得之财，乃是吹来吹去的浮云。

chapters.en: The violence of the wicked will drag them away, for they refuse to do what is right.
chapters.zh: 恶人的强暴，必将自己扫除。因他们不肯按公平行事。

chapters.en: The way of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
chapters.zh: 负罪之人的路，甚是弯曲。至于清洁的人，他所行的乃是正直。

chapters.en: Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
chapters.zh: 宁可住在房顶的角上，不在宽阔的房屋，与争吵的妇人同住。

chapters.en: The wicked crave evil; their neighbors get no mercy from them.
chapters.zh: 恶人的心，乐人受祸。他眼并不怜恤邻舍。

chapters.en: When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; by paying attention to the wise they get knowledge.
chapters.zh: 亵慢的人受刑罚，愚蒙的人就得智慧。智慧人受训诲，便得知识。

chapters.en: The Righteous One takes note of the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.
chapters.zh: 义人思想恶人的家，知道恶人倾倒，必至灭亡。

chapters.en: Whoever shuts their ears to the cry of the poor will also cry out and not be answered.
chapters.zh: 塞耳不听穷人哀求的，他将来呼吁也不蒙应允。

chapters.en: A gift given in secret soothes anger, and a bribe concealed in the cloak pacifies great wrath.
chapters.zh: 暗中送的礼物，挽回怒气。怀中搋的贿赂，止息暴怒。

chapters.en: When justice is done, it brings joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers.
chapters.zh: 秉公行义，使义人喜乐，使作孽的人败坏。

chapters.en: Whoever strays from the path of prudence comes to rest in the company of the dead.
chapters.zh: 迷离通达道路的，必住在阴魂的会中。

chapters.en: Whoever loves pleasure will become poor; whoever loves wine and olive oil will never be rich.
chapters.zh: 爱宴乐的，必致穷乏。好酒爱膏油的，必不富足。

chapters.en: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the unfaithful for the upright.
chapters.zh: 恶人作了义人的赎价。奸诈人代替正直人。

chapters.en: Better to live in a desert than with a quarrelsome and nagging wife.
chapters.zh: 宁可住在旷野，不与争吵使气的妇人同住。

chapters.en: The wise store up choice food and olive oil, but fools gulp theirs down.
chapters.zh: 智慧人家中积蓄宝物膏油。愚昧人随得来随吞下。

chapters.en: Whoever pursues righteousness and love finds life, prosperity and honor.
chapters.zh: 追求公义仁慈的，就寻得生命，公义，和尊荣。

chapters.en: One who is wise can go up against the city of the mighty and pull down the stronghold in which they trust.
chapters.zh: 智慧人爬上勇士的城墙，倾覆他所倚靠的坚垒。

chapters.en: Those who guard their mouths and their tongues keep themselves from calamity.
chapters.zh: 谨守口与舌的，就保守自己免受灾难。

chapters.en: The proud and arrogant person—“Mocker” is his name— behaves with insolent fury.
chapters.zh: 心骄气傲的人，名叫亵慢。他行事狂妄，都出于骄傲。

chapters.en: The craving of a sluggard will be the death of him, because his hands refuse to work.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人的心愿，将他杀害，因为他手不肯作工。

chapters.en: All day long he craves for more, but the righteous give without sparing.
chapters.zh: 有终日贪得无餍的，义人施舍而不吝惜。

chapters.en: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable— how much more so when brought with evil intent!
chapters.zh: 恶人的祭物是可憎的，何况他存恶意来献呢？

chapters.en: A false witness will perish, but a careful listener will testify successfully.
chapters.zh: 作假见证的必灭亡，惟有听真情而言的，其言长存。

chapters.en: The wicked put up a bold front, but the upright give thought to their ways.
chapters.zh: 恶人脸无羞耻，正直人行事坚定。

chapters.en: There is no wisdom, no insight, no plan that can succeed against the LORD.
chapters.zh: 没有人能以智慧，聪明，谋略，敌挡耶和华。

chapters.en: The horse is made ready for the day of battle, but victory rests with the LORD.
chapters.zh: 马是为打仗之日预备的。得胜乃在乎耶和华。

chapters.en: A good name is more desirable than great riches; to be esteemed is better than silver or gold.
chapters.zh: 美名胜过大财，恩宠强如金银。

chapters.en: Rich and poor have this in common: The LORD is the Maker of them all.
chapters.zh: 富户穷人，在世相遇，都为耶和华所造。

chapters.en: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
chapters.zh: 通达人见祸藏躲。愚蒙人前往受害。

chapters.en: Humility is the fear of the LORD; its wages are riches and honor and life.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华心存谦卑，就得富有，尊荣，生命，为赏赐。

chapters.en: In the paths of the wicked are snares and pitfalls, but those who would preserve their life stay far from them.
chapters.zh: 乖僻人的路上，有荆棘和网罗。保守自己生命的。必要远离。

chapters.en: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.
chapters.zh: 教养孩童，使他走当行的道，就是到老他也不偏离。

chapters.en: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.
chapters.zh: 富户管辖穷人，欠债的是债主的仆人。

chapters.en: Whoever sows injustice reaps calamity, and the rod they wield in fury will be broken.
chapters.zh: 撒罪孽的，必收灾祸。他逞怒的杖，也必废掉。

chapters.en: The generous will themselves be blessed, for they share their food with the poor.
chapters.zh: 眼目慈善的，就必蒙福。因他将食物分给穷人。

chapters.en: Drive out the mocker, and out goes strife; quarrels and insults are ended.
chapters.zh: 赶出亵慢人，争端就消除，分争和羞辱，也必止息。

chapters.en: One who loves a pure heart and who speaks with grace will have the king for a friend.
chapters.zh: 喜爱清心的人，因他嘴上的恩言，王必与他为友。

chapters.en: The eyes of the LORD keep watch over knowledge, but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的眼目，眷顾聪明人。却倾败奸诈人的言语。

chapters.en: The sluggard says, “There’s a lion outside! I’ll be killed in the public square!”
chapters.zh: 懒惰人说，外头有狮子，我在街上，就必被杀。

chapters.en: The mouth of an adulterous woman is a deep pit; a man who is under the LORD’s wrath falls into it.
chapters.zh: 淫妇的口为深坑，耶和华所憎恶的，必陷在其中。

chapters.en: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far away.
chapters.zh: 愚蒙迷住孩童的心，用管教的杖可以远远赶除。

chapters.en: One who oppresses the poor to increase his wealth and one who gives gifts to the rich—both come to poverty.
chapters.zh: 欺压贫穷为要利己的，并送礼与富户的，都必缺乏。

chapters.en: Pay attention and turn your ear to the sayings of the wise; apply your heart to what I teach,
chapters.zh: 你须侧耳听受智慧人的言语，留心领会我的知识，

chapters.en: for it is pleasing when you keep them in your heart and have all of them ready on your lips.
chapters.zh: 你若心中存记，嘴上咬定，这便为美。

chapters.en: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I teach you today, even you.
chapters.zh: 我今日以此特特指教你，为要使你倚靠耶和华。

chapters.en: Have I not written thirty sayings for you, sayings of counsel and knowledge,
chapters.zh: 谋略和知识的美事，我岂没有写给你吗？

chapters.en: teaching you to be honest and to speak the truth, so that you bring back truthful reports to those you serve?
chapters.zh: 要使你知道真言的实理，你好将真言回覆那打发你来的人。

chapters.en: Do not exploit the poor because they are poor and do not crush the needy in court,
chapters.zh: 贫穷人，你不可因他贫穷，就抢夺他的物。也不可在城门口欺压困苦人。

chapters.en: for the LORD will take up their case and will exact life for life.
chapters.zh: 因耶和华必为他辨屈。抢夺他的，耶和华必夺取那人的命。

chapters.en: Do not make friends with a hot-tempered person, do not associate with one easily angered,
chapters.zh: 好生气的人，不可与他结交。暴怒的人，不可与他来往。

chapters.en: or you may learn their ways and get yourself ensnared.
chapters.zh: 恐怕你效法他的行为，自己就陷在网罗里。

chapters.en: Do not be one who shakes hands in pledge or puts up security for debts;
chapters.zh: 不要与人击掌，不要为欠债的作保。

chapters.en: if you lack the means to pay, your very bed will be snatched from under you.
chapters.zh: 你若没有什么偿还，何必使人夺去你睡卧的床呢？

chapters.en: Do not move an ancient boundary stone set up by your ancestors.
chapters.zh: 你先祖所立的地界，你不可挪移。

chapters.en: Do you see someone skilled in their work? They will serve before kings; they will not serve before officials of low rank.
chapters.zh: 你看见办事殷勤的人吗？他必站在君王面前，必不站在下贱人面前。

chapters.en: When you sit to dine with a ruler, note well what is before you,
chapters.zh: 你若与官长坐席，要留意在你面前的是谁。

chapters.en: and put a knife to your throat if you are given to gluttony.
chapters.zh: 你若是贪食的，就当拿刀放在喉咙上。

chapters.en: Do not crave his delicacies, for that food is deceptive.
chapters.zh: 不可贪恋他的美食，因为是哄人的食物。

chapters.en: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; do not trust your own cleverness.
chapters.zh: 不要劳碌求富。休仗自己的聪明。

chapters.en: Cast but a glance at riches, and they are gone, for they will surely sprout wings and fly off to the sky like an eagle.
chapters.zh: 你岂要定睛在虚无的钱财上吗？因钱财必长翅膀，如鹰向天飞去。

chapters.en: Do not eat the food of a begrudging host, do not crave his delicacies;
chapters.zh: 不要吃恶眼人的饭。也不要贪他的美味。

chapters.en: for he is the kind of person who is always thinking about the cost.“Eat and drink,” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
chapters.zh: 因为他心怎样思量，他为人就是怎样。他虽对你说，请吃，请喝。他的心却与你相背。

chapters.en: You will vomit up the little you have eaten and will have wasted your compliments.
chapters.zh: 你所吃的那点食物，必吐出来。你所说的甘美言语，也必落空。

chapters.en: Do not speak to fools, for they will scorn your prudent words.
chapters.zh: 你不要说话给愚昧人听。因他必藐视你智慧的言语。

chapters.en: Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
chapters.zh: 不可挪移古时的地界。也不可侵入孤儿的田地。

chapters.en: for their Defender is strong; he will take up their case against you.
chapters.zh: 因他们的救赎主，大有能力。他必向你为他们辨屈。

chapters.en: Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge.
chapters.zh: 你要留心领受训诲。侧耳听从知识的言语。

chapters.en: Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you punish them with the rod, they will not die.
chapters.zh: 不可不管教孩童，你用杖打他，他必不至于死。

chapters.en: Punish them with the rod and save them from death.
chapters.zh: 你要用杖打他，就可以救他的灵魂免下阴间。

chapters.en: My son, if your heart is wise, then my heart will be glad indeed;
chapters.zh: 我儿你心若存智慧，我的心也甚欢喜。

chapters.en: my inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
chapters.zh: 你的嘴若说正直话，我的心肠也必快乐。

chapters.en: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always be zealous for the fear of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你心中不要嫉妒罪人。只要终日敬畏耶和华。

chapters.en: There is surely a future hope for you, and your hope will not be cut off.
chapters.zh: 因为至终必有善报。你的指望也不至断绝。

chapters.en: Listen, my son, and be wise, and set your heart on the right path:
chapters.zh: 我儿，你当听，当存智慧，好在正道上引导你的心。

chapters.en: Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat,
chapters.zh: 好饮酒的，好吃肉的，不要与他们来往。

chapters.en: for drunkards and gluttons become poor, and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
chapters.zh: 因为好酒贪食的，必致贫穷。好睡觉的，必穿破烂衣服。

chapters.en: Listen to your father, who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
chapters.zh: 你要听从生你的父亲。你母亲老了，也不可藐视她。

chapters.en: Buy the truth and do not sell it— wisdom, instruction and insight as well.
chapters.zh: 你当买真理。就是智慧，训诲，和聪明，也都不可卖。

chapters.en: The father of a righteous child has great joy; a man who fathers a wise son rejoices in him.
chapters.zh: 义人的父亲，必大得快乐。人生智慧的儿子，必因他欢喜。

chapters.en: May your father and mother rejoice; may she who gave you birth be joyful!
chapters.zh: 你要使父母欢喜。使生你的快乐。

chapters.en: My son, give me your heart and let your eyes delight in my ways,
chapters.zh: 我儿，要将你的心归我。你的眼目，也要喜悦我的道路。

chapters.en: for an adulterous woman is a deep pit, and a wayward wife is a narrow well.
chapters.zh: 妓女是深坑。外女是窄阱。

chapters.en: Like a bandit she lies in wait and multiplies the unfaithful among men.
chapters.zh: 她埋伏好像强盗，她使人中多有奸诈的。

chapters.en: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?
chapters.zh: 谁有祸患，谁有忧愁，谁有争斗，谁有哀叹，（或作怨言）谁无故受伤，谁眼目红赤。

chapters.en: Those who linger over wine, who go to sample bowls of mixed wine.
chapters.zh: 就是那流连饮酒，常去寻找调和酒的人。

chapters.en: Do not gaze at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly!
chapters.zh: 酒发红，在杯中闪烁，你不可观看，虽然下咽舒畅，终久是咬你如蛇，刺你如毒蛇。

chapters.en: In the end it bites like a snake and poisons like a viper.
Your eyes will see strange sights, and your mind will imagine confusing things.
chapters.zh: 你眼必看见异怪的事。（异怪的事或作淫妇）你心必发出乖谬的话。

chapters.en: You will be like one sleeping on the high seas, lying on top of the rigging.
chapters.zh: 你必像躺在海中，或像卧在桅杆上。

chapters.en: “They hit me,” you will say, “but I’m not hurt! They beat me, but I don’t feel it! When will I wake up so I can find another drink?”
chapters.zh: 你必说，人打我，我却未受伤，人鞭打我，我竟不觉得，我几时清醒，我仍去寻酒。

chapters.en: Do not envy the wicked, do not desire their company;
chapters.zh: 你不要嫉妒恶人，也不要起意与他们相处。

chapters.en: for their hearts plot violence, and their lips talk about making trouble.
chapters.zh: 因为他们的心，图谋强暴。他们的口谈论奸恶。

chapters.en: By wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established;
chapters.zh: 房屋因智慧建造，又因聪明立稳。

chapters.en: through knowledge its rooms are filled with rare and beautiful treasures.
chapters.zh: 其中因知识充满各样美好宝贵的财物。

chapters.en: The wise prevail through great power, and those who have knowledge muster their strength.
chapters.zh: 智慧人大有能力。有知识的人，力上加力。

chapters.en: Surely you need guidance to wage war, and victory is won through many advisers.
chapters.zh: 你去打仗，要凭智谋。谋士众多，人便得胜。

chapters.en: Wisdom is too high for fools; in the assembly at the gate they must not open their mouths.
chapters.zh: 智慧极高，非愚昧人所能及，所以在城门内，不敢开口。

chapters.en: Whoever plots evil will be known as a schemer.
chapters.zh: 设计作恶的，必称为奸人。

chapters.en: The schemes of folly are sin, and people detest a mocker.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人的思念，乃是罪恶。亵慢者为人所憎恶。

chapters.en: If you falter in a time of trouble, how small is your strength!
chapters.zh: 你在患难之日若胆怯，你的力量就微小。

chapters.en: Rescue those being led away to death; hold back those staggering toward slaughter.
chapters.zh: 人被拉到死地，你要解救。人将被杀，你须拦阻。

chapters.en: If you say, “But we knew nothing about this,” does not he who weighs the heart perceive it? Does not he who guards your life know it? Will he not repay everyone according to what they have done?
chapters.zh: 你若说，这事我未曾知道。那衡量人心的，岂不明白吗？保守你命的，岂不知道吗？他岂不按各人所行的，报应各人吗？

chapters.en: Eat honey, my son, for it is good; honey from the comb is sweet to your taste.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你要吃蜜，因为是好的。吃蜂房下滴的蜜，便觉甘甜。

chapters.en: Know also that wisdom is like honey for you: If you find it, there is a future hope for you, and your hope will not be cut off.
chapters.zh: 你心得了智慧，也必觉得如此。你若找着，至终必有善报。你的指望，也不至断绝。

chapters.en: Do not lurk like a thief near the house of the righteous, do not plunder their dwelling place;
chapters.zh: 你这恶人，不要埋伏攻击义人的家。不要毁坏他安居之所。

chapters.en: for though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again, but the wicked stumble when calamity strikes.
chapters.zh: 因为义人虽七次跌倒，仍必兴起。恶人却被祸患倾倒。

chapters.en: Do not gloat when your enemy falls; when they stumble, do not let your heart rejoice,
chapters.zh: 你仇敌跌倒，你不要欢喜。他倾倒，你心不要快乐。

chapters.en: or the LORD will see and disapprove and turn his wrath away from them.
chapters.zh: 恐怕耶和华看见就不喜悦，将怒气从仇敌身上转过来。

chapters.en: Do not fret because of evildoers or be envious of the wicked,
chapters.zh: 不要为作恶的心怀不平。也不要嫉妒恶人。

chapters.en: for the evildoer has no future hope, and the lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.
chapters.zh: 因为恶人终不得善报。恶人的灯也必熄灭。

chapters.en: Fear the LORD and the king, my son, and do not join with rebellious officials,
chapters.zh: 我儿，你要敬畏耶和华与君王。不要与反覆无常的人结交。

chapters.en: for those two will send sudden destruction on them, and who knows what calamities they can bring?
chapters.zh: 因为他们的灾难，必忽然而起。耶和华与君王所施行的毁灭，谁能知道呢？

chapters.en: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judging is not good:
chapters.zh: 以下也是智慧人的箴言。审判时看人情面，是不好的。

chapters.en: Whoever says to the guilty, “You are innocent,” will be cursed by peoples and denounced by nations.
chapters.zh: 对恶人说，你是义人的，这人万民必咒诅，列邦必憎恶。

chapters.en: But it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come on them.
chapters.zh: 责备恶人的，必得喜悦。美好的福，也必临到他。

chapters.en: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
chapters.zh: 应对正直的，犹如与人亲嘴。

chapters.en: Put your outdoor work in order and get your fields ready; after that, build your house.
chapters.zh: 你要在外头预备工料，在田间办理整齐，然后建造房屋。

chapters.en: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause— would you use your lips to mislead?
chapters.zh: 不可无故作见证，陷害邻舍。也不可用嘴欺骗人。

chapters.en: Do not say, “I’ll do to them as they have done to me; I’ll pay them back for what they did.”
chapters.zh: 不可说，人怎样待我，我也怎样待他，我必照他所行的报复他。

chapters.en: I went past the field of a sluggard, past the vineyard of someone who has no sense;
chapters.zh: 我经过懒惰人的田地，无知人的葡萄园。

chapters.en: thorns had come up everywhere, the ground was covered with weeds, and the stone wall was in ruins.
chapters.zh: 荆棘长满了地皮，刺草遮盖了田面，石墙也坍塌了。

chapters.en: I applied my heart to what I observed and learned a lesson from what I saw:
chapters.zh: 我看见就留心思想，我看着就领了训诲。

chapters.en: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest—
chapters.zh: 再睡片时，打盹片时，抱着手躺卧片时，

chapters.en: and poverty will come on you like a thief and scarcity like an armed man.
chapters.zh: 你的贫穷，就必如强盗速来，你的缺乏，仿佛拿兵器的人来到。

chapters.en: These are more proverbs of Solomon, compiled by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:
chapters.zh: 以下也是所罗门的箴言。是犹大王希西家的人所誊录的。

chapters.en: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter; to search out a matter is the glory of kings.
chapters.zh: 将事隐秘，乃神的荣耀。将事察清，乃君王的荣耀。

chapters.en: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
chapters.zh: 天之高，地之厚，君王之心也测不透。

chapters.en: Remove the dross from the silver, and a silversmith can produce a vessel;
chapters.zh: 除去银子的渣滓，就有银子出来，银匠能以作器皿。

chapters.en: remove wicked officials from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established through righteousness.
chapters.zh: 除去王面前的恶人，国位就靠公义坚立。

chapters.en: Do not exalt yourself in the king’s presence, and do not claim a place among his great men;
chapters.zh: 不要在王面前妄自尊大。不要在大人的位上站立。

chapters.en: it is better for him to say to you, “Come up here,” than for him to humiliate you before his nobles. What you have seen with your eyes
chapters.zh: 宁可有人说，请你上来，强如在你觐见的王子面前，叫你退下。

chapters.en: do not bring hastily to court, for what will you do in the end if your neighbor puts you to shame?
chapters.zh: 不要冒失出去与人争竞，免得至终被他羞辱，你就不知道怎样行了。

chapters.en: If you take your neighbor to court, do not betray another’s confidence,
chapters.zh: 你与邻舍争讼，要与他一人辩论。不可泄漏人的密事。

chapters.en: or the one who hears it may shame you and the charge against you will stand.
chapters.zh: 恐怕听见的人骂你，你的臭名就难以脱离。

chapters.en: Like apples of gold in settings of silver is a ruling rightly given.
chapters.zh: 一句话说得合宜，就如金苹果在银网子里。

chapters.en: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is the rebuke of a wise judge to a listening ear.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的劝戒，在顺从的人耳中，好像金耳环，和精金的妆饰。

chapters.en: Like a snow-cooled drink at harvest time is a trustworthy messenger to the one who sends him; he refreshes the spirit of his master.
chapters.zh: 忠信的使者，叫差他的人心里舒畅，就如在收割时，有冰雪的凉气。

chapters.en: Like clouds and wind without rain is one who boasts of gifts never given.
chapters.zh: 空夸赠送礼物的，好像无雨的风云。

chapters.en: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
chapters.zh: 恒常忍耐，可以劝动君王。柔和的舌头，能折断骨头。

chapters.en: If you find honey, eat just enough— too much of it, and you will vomit.
chapters.zh: 你得了蜜吗？只可吃够而已。恐怕你过饱就呕吐出来。

chapters.en: Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house— too much of you, and they will hate you.
chapters.zh: 你的脚要少进邻舍的家，恐怕他厌烦你，恨恶你。

chapters.en: Like a club or a sword or a sharp arrow is one who gives false testimony against a neighbor.
chapters.zh: 作假见证陷害邻舍的，就是大槌，是利刀，是快箭。

chapters.en: Like a broken tooth or a lame foot is reliance on the unfaithful in a time of trouble.
chapters.zh: 患难时倚靠不忠诚的人，好像破坏的牙，错骨缝的脚。

chapters.en: Like one who takes away a garment on a cold day, or like vinegar poured on a wound, is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
chapters.zh: 对伤心的人唱歌，就如冷天脱衣服，又如碱上倒醋。

chapters.en: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
chapters.zh: 你的仇敌，若饿了就给他饭吃。若渴了就给他水喝。

chapters.en: In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
chapters.zh: 因为你这样行，就是把炭火堆在他的头上。耶和华也必赏赐你。

chapters.en: Like a north wind that brings unexpected rain is a sly tongue—which provokes a horrified look.
chapters.zh: 北风生雨，谗谤人的舌头也生怒容。

chapters.en: Better to live on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
chapters.zh: 宁可住在房顶的角上，不在宽阔的房屋与争吵的妇人同住。

chapters.en: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
chapters.zh: 有好消息从远方来，就如拿凉水给口渴的人喝。

chapters.en: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well are the righteous who give way to the wicked.
chapters.zh: 义人在恶人面前退缩，好像搅浑之泉，弄浊之井。

chapters.en: It is not good to eat too much honey, nor is it honorable to search out matters that are too deep.
chapters.zh: 吃蜜过多，是不好的。考究自己的荣耀，也是可厌的。

chapters.en: Like a city whose walls are broken through is a person who lacks self-control.
chapters.zh: 人不制伏自己的心，好像毁坏的城邑，没有墙垣。

chapters.en: Like snow in summer or rain in harvest, honor is not fitting for a fool.
chapters.zh: 夏天落雪，收割时下雨，都不相宜。愚昧人得尊荣，也是如此。

chapters.en: Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.
chapters.zh: 麻雀往来，燕子翻飞，这样，无故地咒诅，也必不临到。

chapters.en: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools!
chapters.zh: 鞭子是为打马。辔头是为勒驴。刑杖是为打愚昧人的背。

chapters.en: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will be just like him.
chapters.zh: 不要照愚昧人的愚妄话回答他，恐怕你与他一样。

chapters.en: Answer a fool according to his folly, or he will be wise in his own eyes.
chapters.zh: 要照愚昧人的愚妄话回答他，免得他自以为有智慧。

chapters.en: Sending a message by the hands of a fool is like cutting off one’s feet or drinking poison.
chapters.zh: 借愚昧人手寄信的，是砍断自己的脚，自受损害。（自受原文作喝）

chapters.en: Like the useless legs of one who is lame is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
chapters.zh: 瘸子的脚，空存无用。箴言在愚昧人的口中，也是如此。

chapters.en: Like tying a stone in a sling is the giving of honor to a fool.
chapters.zh: 将尊荣给愚昧人的，好像人把石子包在机弦里。

chapters.en: Like a thornbush in a drunkard’s hand is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
chapters.zh: 箴言在愚昧人的口中，好像荆棘刺入醉汉的手。

chapters.en: Like an archer who wounds at random is one who hires a fool or any passer-by.
chapters.zh: 雇愚昧人的，与雇过路人的，就像射伤众人的弓箭手。

chapters.en: As a dog returns to its vomit, so fools repeat their folly.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人行愚妄事，行了又行，就如狗转过来吃它所吐的。

chapters.en: Do you see a person wise in their own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for them.
chapters.zh: 你见自以为有智慧的人吗？愚昧人比他更有指望。

chapters.en: A sluggard says, “There’s a lion in the road, a fierce lion roaming the streets!”
chapters.zh: 懒惰人说，道上有猛狮，街上有壮狮。

chapters.en: As a door turns on its hinges, so a sluggard turns on his bed.
chapters.zh: 门在枢纽转动，懒惰人在床上也是如此。

chapters.en: A sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人放手在盘子里，就是向口撤回，也以为劳乏。

chapters.en: A sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven people who answer discreetly.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人看自己，比七个善于应对的人更有智慧。

chapters.en: Like one who grabs a stray dog by the ears is someone who rushes into a quarrel not their own.
chapters.zh: 过路被事激动，管理不干己的争竞，好像人揪住狗耳。

chapters.en: Like a maniac shooting flaming arrows of death
chapters.zh: 人欺凌邻舍，却说，我岂不是戏耍吗？他就像疯狂的人，抛掷火把，利箭，与杀人的兵器。（杀人的兵器原文作死亡）

chapters.en: is one who deceives their neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”
Without wood a fire goes out; without a gossip a quarrel dies down.
chapters.zh: 火缺了柴，就必熄灭。无人传舌，争竞便止息。

chapters.en: As charcoal to embers and as wood to fire, so is a quarrelsome person for kindling strife.
chapters.zh: 好争竞的人煽惑争端，就如余火加炭，火上加柴一样。

chapters.en: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; they go down to the inmost parts.
chapters.zh: 传舌人的言语，如同美食，深入人的心腹。

chapters.en: Like a coating of silver dross on earthenware are fervent lips with an evil heart.
chapters.zh: 火热的嘴，奸恶的心，好像银渣包的瓦器。

chapters.en: Enemies disguise themselves with their lips, but in their hearts they harbor deceit.
chapters.zh: 怨恨人的用嘴粉饰，心里却藏着诡诈。

chapters.en: Though their speech is charming, do not believe them, for seven abominations fill their hearts.
chapters.zh: 他用甜言蜜语，你不可信他，因为他心中有七样可憎恶的。

chapters.en: Their malice may be concealed by deception, but their wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
chapters.zh: 他虽用诡诈遮掩自己的怨恨，他的邪恶必在会中显露。

chapters.en: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it; if someone rolls a stone, it will roll back on them.
chapters.zh: 挖陷坑的，自己必掉在其中。滚石头的，石头必反滚在他身上。

chapters.en: A lying tongue hates those it hurts, and a flattering mouth works ruin.
chapters.zh: 虚谎的舌，恨他所压伤的人。谄媚的口，败坏人的事。

chapters.en: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
chapters.zh: 不要为明日自夸，因为一日要生何事，你尚且不能知道。

chapters.en: Let someone else praise you, and not your own mouth; an outsider, and not your own lips.
chapters.zh: 要别人夸奖你，不可用口自夸。等外人称赞你，不可用嘴自称。

chapters.en: Stone is heavy and sand a burden, but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
chapters.zh: 石头重，沙土沉，愚妄人的恼怒，比这两样更重。

chapters.en: Anger is cruel and fury overwhelming, but who can stand before jealousy?
chapters.zh: 忿怒为残忍，怒气为狂澜，惟有嫉妒，谁能敌得住呢？

chapters.en: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
chapters.zh: 当面的责备，强如背地的爱情。

chapters.en: Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses.
chapters.zh: 朋友加的伤痕，出于忠诚，仇敌连连亲嘴，却是多余。

chapters.en: One who is full loathes honey from the comb, but to the hungry even what is bitter tastes sweet.
chapters.zh: 人吃饱了，厌恶蜂房的蜜。人饥饿了，一切苦物都觉甘甜。

chapters.en: Like a bird that flees its nest is anyone who flees from home.
chapters.zh: 人离本处飘流，好像雀鸟离窝游飞。

chapters.en: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart, and the pleasantness of a friend springs from their heartfelt advice.
chapters.zh: 膏油与香料，使人心喜悦。朋友诚实的劝教，也是如此甘美。

chapters.en: Do not forsake your friend or a friend of your family, and do not go to your relative’s house when disaster strikes you— better a neighbor nearby than a relative far away.
chapters.zh: 你的朋友，和父亲的朋友，你都不可离弃。你遭难的日子，不要上弟兄的家去。相近的邻舍，强如远方的弟兄。

chapters.en: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart; then I can answer anyone who treats me with contempt.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你要作智慧人，好叫我的心欢喜，使我可以回答那讥诮我的人。

chapters.en: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
chapters.zh: 通达人见祸藏躲。愚蒙人前往受害。

chapters.en: Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge if it is done for an outsider.
chapters.zh: 谁为生人作保，就拿谁的衣服。谁为外女作保，谁就承当。

chapters.en: If anyone loudly blesses their neighbor early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse.
chapters.zh: 清晨起来，大声给朋友祝福的，就算是咒诅他。

chapters.en: A quarrelsome wife is like the dripping of a leaky roof in a rainstorm;
chapters.zh: 大雨之日连连滴漏，和争吵的妇人一样。

chapters.en: restraining her is like restraining the wind or grasping oil with the hand.
chapters.zh: 想拦阻她的，便是拦阻风，也是右手抓油。

chapters.en: As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.
chapters.zh: 铁磨铁，磨出刃来。朋友相感，（原文作磨朋友的脸）也是如此。

chapters.en: The one who guards a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever protects their master will be honored.
chapters.zh: 看守无花果树的，必吃树上的果子。敬奉主人的，必得尊荣。

chapters.en: As water reflects the face, so one’s life reflects the heart.
chapters.zh: 水中照脸，彼此相符。人与人，心也相对。

chapters.en: Death and Destruction are never satisfied, and neither are human eyes.
chapters.zh: 阴间和灭亡，永不满足。人的眼目，也是如此。

chapters.en: The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold, but people are tested by their praise.
chapters.zh: 鼎为炼银，炉为炼金，人的称赞也试炼人。

chapters.en: Though you grind a fool in a mortar, grinding them like grain with a pestle, you will not remove their folly from them.
chapters.zh: 你虽用杵，将愚妄人与打碎的麦子一同捣在臼中，他的愚妄还是离不了他。

chapters.en: Be sure you know the condition of your flocks, give careful attention to your herds;
chapters.zh: 你要详细知道你羊群的景况。留心料理你的牛群。

chapters.en: for riches do not endure forever, and a crown is not secure for all generations.
chapters.zh: 因为赀财不能永有。冠冕岂能存到万代。

chapters.en: When the hay is removed and new growth appears and the grass from the hills is gathered in,
chapters.zh: 干草割去，嫩草发现，山上的菜蔬，也被收敛。

chapters.en: the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.
chapters.zh: 羊羔之毛，是为你作衣服。山羊是为作田地的价值。

chapters.en: You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed your family and to nourish your female servants.
chapters.zh: 并有母山羊奶够你吃，也够你的家眷吃，且够养你的婢女。

chapters.en: The wicked flee though no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
chapters.zh: 恶人虽无人追赶也逃跑，义人却胆壮像狮子。

chapters.en: When a country is rebellious, it has many rulers, but a ruler with discernment and knowledge maintains order.
chapters.zh: 邦国因有罪过，君王就多更换。因有聪明知识的人，国必长存。

chapters.en: A ruler who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no crops.
chapters.zh: 穷人欺压贫民，好像暴雨冲没粮食。

chapters.en: Those who forsake instruction praise the wicked, but those who heed it resist them.
chapters.zh: 违弃律法的，夸奖恶人。遵守律法的，却与恶人相争。

chapters.en: Evildoers do not understand what is right, but those who seek the LORD understand it fully.
chapters.zh: 坏人不明白公义。惟有寻求耶和华的，无不明白。

chapters.en: Better the poor whose walk is blameless than the rich whose ways are perverse.
chapters.zh: 行为纯正的穷乏人，胜过行事乖僻的富足人。

chapters.en: A discerning son heeds instruction, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.
chapters.zh: 谨守律法的是智慧之子。与贪食人作伴的，却羞辱其父。

chapters.en: Whoever increases wealth by taking interest or profit from the poor amasses it for another, who will be kind to the poor.
chapters.zh: 人以厚利加增财物，是给那怜悯穷人者积蓄的。

chapters.en: If anyone turns a deaf ear to my instruction, even their prayers are detestable.
chapters.zh: 转耳不听律法的，他的祈祷也为可憎。

chapters.en: Whoever leads the upright along an evil path will fall into their own trap, but the blameless will receive a good inheritance.
chapters.zh: 诱惑正直人行恶道的，必掉在自己的坑里。惟有完全人，必承受福分。

chapters.en: The rich are wise in their own eyes; one who is poor and discerning sees how deluded they are.
chapters.zh: 富足人自以为有智慧。但聪明的贫穷人，能将他查透。

chapters.en: When the righteous triumph, there is great elation; but when the wicked rise to power, people go into hiding.
chapters.zh: 义人得志有大荣耀。恶人兴起人就躲藏。

chapters.en: Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
chapters.zh: 遮掩自己罪过的，必不亨通。承认离弃罪过的，必蒙怜恤。

chapters.en: Blessed is the one who always trembles before God, but whoever hardens their heart falls into trouble.
chapters.zh: 常存敬畏的，便为有福。心存刚硬的，必陷在祸患里。

chapters.en: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
chapters.zh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民。好像吼叫的狮子，觅食的熊。

chapters.en: A tyrannical ruler practices extortion, but one who hates ill-gotten gain will enjoy a long reign.
chapters.zh: 无知的君多行暴虐。以贪财为可恨的，必年长日久。

chapters.en: Anyone tormented by the guilt of murder will seek refuge in the grave; let no one hold them back.
chapters.zh: 背负流人血之罪的，必往坑里奔跑，谁也不可拦阻他。

chapters.en: The one whose walk is blameless is kept safe, but the one whose ways are perverse will fall into the pit.
chapters.zh: 行动正直的，必蒙拯救。行事弯曲的，立时跌倒。

chapters.en: Those who work their land will have abundant food, but those who chase fantasies will have their fill of poverty.
chapters.zh: 耕种自己田地的，必得饱食。追随虚浮的，足受穷乏。

chapters.en: A faithful person will be richly blessed, but one eager to get rich will not go unpunished.
chapters.zh: 诚实人必多得福，想要急速发财的，不免受罚。

chapters.en: To show partiality is not good— yet a person will do wrong for a piece of bread.
chapters.zh: 看人的情面，乃为不好。人因一块饼枉法，也为不好。

chapters.en: The stingy are eager to get rich and are unaware that poverty awaits them.
chapters.zh: 人有恶眼想要急速发财，却不知穷乏必临到他身。

chapters.en: Whoever rebukes a person will in the end gain favor rather than one who has a flattering tongue.
chapters.zh: 责备人的，后来蒙人喜悦，多于那用舌头谄媚人的。

chapters.en: Whoever robs their father or mother and says, “It’s not wrong,” is partner to one who destroys.
chapters.zh: 偷窃父母的，说，这不是罪。此人就是与强盗同类。

chapters.en: The greedy stir up conflict, but those who trust in the LORD will prosper.
chapters.zh: 心中贪婪的，挑起争端。倚靠耶和华的，必得丰裕。

chapters.en: Those who trust in themselves are fools, but those who walk in wisdom are kept safe.
chapters.zh: 心中自是的，便是愚昧人。凭智慧行事的，必蒙拯救。

chapters.en: Those who give to the poor will lack nothing, but those who close their eyes to them receive many curses.
chapters.zh: 周济贫穷的，不致缺乏。佯为不见的，必多受咒诅。

chapters.en: When the wicked rise to power, people go into hiding; but when the wicked perish, the righteous thrive.
chapters.zh: 恶人兴起，人就躲藏。恶人败亡，义人增多。

chapters.en: Whoever remains stiff-necked after many rebukes will suddenly be destroyed—without remedy.
chapters.zh: 人屡次受责罚，仍然硬着颈项，他必顷刻败坏，无法可治。

chapters.en: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
chapters.zh: 义人增多，民就喜乐。恶人掌权，民就叹息。

chapters.en: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
chapters.zh: 爱慕智慧的，使父亲喜乐。与妓女结交的，却浪费钱财。

chapters.en: By justice a king gives a country stability, but those who are greedy for bribes tear it down.
chapters.zh: 王借公平，使国坚定。索要贿赂，使国倾败。

chapters.en: Those who flatter their neighbors are spreading nets for their feet.
chapters.zh: 谄媚邻舍的，就是设网罗绊他的脚。

chapters.en: Evildoers are snared by their own sin, but the righteous shout for joy and are glad.
chapters.zh: 恶人犯罪，自陷网罗。惟独义人，欢呼喜乐。

chapters.en: The righteous care about justice for the poor, but the wicked have no such concern.
chapters.zh: 义人知道查明穷人的案。恶人没有聪明，就不得而知。

chapters.en: Mockers stir up a city, but the wise turn away anger.
chapters.zh: 亵慢人煽惑通城。智慧人止息众怒。

chapters.en: If a wise person goes to court with a fool, the fool rages and scoffs, and there is no peace.
chapters.zh: 智慧人与愚妄人相争，或怒，或笑，总不能使他止息。

chapters.en: The bloodthirsty hate a person of integrity and seek to kill the upright.
chapters.zh: 好流人血的，恨恶完全人。索取正直人的性命。

chapters.en: Fools give full vent to their rage, but the wise bring calm in the end.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人怒气全发。智慧人忍气含怒。

chapters.en: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials become wicked.
chapters.zh: 君王若听谎言，他一切臣仆都是奸恶。

chapters.en: The poor and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives sight to the eyes of both.
chapters.zh: 贫穷人，强暴人，在世相遇，他们的眼目，都蒙耶和华光照。

chapters.en: If a king judges the poor with fairness, his throne will be established forever.
chapters.zh: 君王凭诚实判断穷人，他的国位，必永远坚立。

chapters.en: A rod and a reprimand impart wisdom, but a child left undisciplined disgraces its mother.
chapters.zh: 杖打和责备，能加增智慧。放纵的儿子，使母亲羞愧。

chapters.en: When the wicked thrive, so does sin, but the righteous will see their downfall.
chapters.zh: 恶人加多，过犯也加多。义人必看见他们跌倒。

chapters.en: Discipline your children, and they will give you peace; they will bring you the delights you desire.
chapters.zh: 管教你的儿子，他就使你得安息，也必使你心里喜乐。

chapters.en: Where there is no revelation, people cast off restraint; but blessed is the one who heeds wisdom’s instruction.
chapters.zh: 没有异象，（或作默示）民就放肆。惟遵守律法的，便为有福。

chapters.en: Servants cannot be corrected by mere words; though they understand, they will not respond.
chapters.zh: 只用言语，仆人不肯受管教，他虽然明白，也不留意。

chapters.en: Do you see someone who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for them.
chapters.zh: 你见言语急躁的人吗？愚昧人比他更有指望。

chapters.en: A servant pampered from youth will turn out to be insolent.
chapters.zh: 人将仆人从小娇养，这仆人终久必成了他的儿子。

chapters.en: An angry person stirs up conflict, and a hot-tempered person commits many sins.
chapters.zh: 好气的人，挑启争端。暴怒的人，多多犯罪。

chapters.en: Pride brings a person low, but the lowly in spirit gain honor.
chapters.zh: 人的高傲，必使他卑下。心里谦逊的，必得尊荣。

chapters.en: The accomplices of thieves are their own enemies; they are put under oath and dare not testify.
chapters.zh: 人与盗贼分赃，是恨恶自己的性命。他听见叫人发誓的声音，却不言语。

chapters.en: Fear of man will prove to be a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe.
chapters.zh: 惧怕人的陷入网罗。惟有倚靠耶和华的，必得安稳。

chapters.en: Many seek an audience with a ruler, but it is from the LORD that one gets justice.
chapters.zh: 求王恩的人多。定人事乃在耶和华。

chapters.en: The righteous detest the dishonest; the wicked detest the upright.
chapters.zh: 为非作歹的，被义人憎嫌。行事正直的，被恶人憎恶。

chapters.en: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh—an inspired utterance. This man’s utterance to Ithiel: “I am weary, God, but I can prevail.
chapters.zh: 雅基的儿子亚古珥的言语，就是真言。这人对以铁和乌甲说，

chapters.en: Surely I am only a brute, not a man; I do not have human understanding.
chapters.zh: 我比众人更蠢笨，也没有人的聪明。

chapters.en: I have not learned wisdom, nor have I attained to the knowledge of the Holy One.
chapters.zh: 我没有学好智慧。也不认识至圣者。

chapters.en: Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Whose hands have gathered up the wind? Who has wrapped up the waters in a cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is the name of his son? Surely you know!
chapters.zh: 谁升天又降下来？谁聚风在掌握中？谁包水在衣服里？谁立定地的四极？他名叫什么？他儿子名叫什么？你知道吗？

chapters.en: “Every word of God is flawless; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
chapters.zh: 神的言语，句句都是炼净的，投靠他的，他便作他们的盾牌。

chapters.en: Do not add to his words, or he will rebuke you and prove you a liar.
chapters.zh: 他的言语，你不可加添。恐怕他责备你，你就显为说谎言的。

chapters.en: “Two things I ask of you, LORD; do not refuse me before I die:
chapters.zh: 我求你两件事，在我未死之先，不要不赐给我。

chapters.en: Keep falsehood and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches, but give me only my daily bread.
chapters.zh: 求你使虚假和谎言远离我。使我也不贫穷，也不富足，赐给我需用的饮食。

chapters.en: Otherwise, I may have too much and disown you and say, ‘Who is the LORD?’ Or I may become poor and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
chapters.zh: 恐怕我饱足不认你，说，耶和华是谁呢？又恐怕我贫穷就偷窃，以致亵渎我神的名。

chapters.en: “Do not slander a servant to their master, or they will curse you, and you will pay for it.
chapters.zh: 你不要向主人谗谤仆人。恐怕他咒诅你，你便算为有罪。

chapters.en: “There are those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers;
chapters.zh: 有一宗人，（宗原文作代下同）咒诅父亲，不给母亲祝福。

chapters.en: those who are pure in their own eyes and yet are not cleansed of their filth;
chapters.zh: 有一宗人，自以为清洁，却没有洗去自己的污秽。

chapters.en: those whose eyes are ever so haughty, whose glances are so disdainful;
chapters.zh: 有一宗人，眼目何其高傲，眼皮也是高举。

chapters.en: those whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are set with knives to devour the poor from the earth and the needy from among mankind.
chapters.zh: 有一宗人，牙如剑，齿如刀，要吞灭地上的困苦人，和世间的穷乏人。

chapters.en: “The leech has two daughters. ‘Give! Give!’ they cry. “There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, ‘Enough!’:
chapters.zh: 蚂蟥有两个女儿，常说，给呀给呀。有三样不知足的，连不说够的共有四样。

chapters.en: the grave, the barren womb, land, which is never satisfied with water, and fire, which never says, ‘Enough!’
chapters.zh: 就是阴间，和石胎，浸水不足的地，并火。

chapters.en: “The eye that mocks a father, that scorns an aged mother, will be pecked out by the ravens of the valley, will be eaten by the vultures.
chapters.zh: 戏笑父亲，藐视而不听从母亲的，他的眼睛，必为谷中的乌鸦啄出来，为鹰雏所吃。

chapters.en: “There are three things that are too amazing for me, four that I do not understand:
chapters.zh: 我所测不透的奇妙有三样，连我所不知道的共有四样。

chapters.en: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship on the high seas, and the way of a man with a young woman.
chapters.zh: 就是鹰在空中飞的道，蛇在磐石上爬的道，船在海中行的道，男与女交合的道。

chapters.en: “This is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, ‘I’ve done nothing wrong.’
chapters.zh: 淫妇的道，也是这样，她吃了把嘴一擦，就说，我没有行恶。

chapters.en: “Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
chapters.zh: 使地震动的有三样，连地担不起的共有四样。

chapters.en: a servant who becomes king, a godless fool who gets plenty to eat,
chapters.zh: 就是仆人作王。愚顽人吃饱。

chapters.en: a contemptible woman who gets married, and a servant who displaces her mistress.
chapters.zh: 丑恶的女子出嫁。婢女接续主母。

chapters.en: “Four things on earth are small, yet they are extremely wise:
chapters.zh: 地上有四样小物，却甚聪明。

chapters.en: Ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;
chapters.zh: 蚂蚁是无力之类，却在夏天预备粮食。

chapters.en: hyraxes are creatures of little power, yet they make their home in the crags;
chapters.zh: 沙番是软弱之类，却在磐石中造房。

chapters.en: locusts have no king, yet they advance together in ranks;
chapters.zh: 蝗虫没有君王，却分队而出。

chapters.en: a lizard can be caught with the hand, yet it is found in kings’ palaces.
chapters.zh: 守宫用爪抓墙，却住在王宫。

chapters.en: “There are three things that are stately in their stride, four that move with stately bearing:
chapters.zh: 步行威武的有三样，连行走威武的共有四样。

chapters.en: a lion, mighty among beasts, who retreats before nothing;
chapters.zh: 就是狮子乃百兽中最为猛烈，无所躲避的。

chapters.en: a strutting rooster, a he-goat, and a king secure against revolt.
chapters.zh: 猎狗，公山羊，和无人能敌的君王。

chapters.en: “If you play the fool and exalt yourself, or if you plan evil, clap your hand over your mouth!
chapters.zh: 你若行事愚顽，自高自傲，或是怀了恶念，就当用手捂口。

chapters.en: For as churning cream produces butter, and as twisting the nose produces blood, so stirring up anger produces strife.”
chapters.zh: 摇牛奶必成奶油。扭鼻子必出血。照样，激动怒气必起争端。

chapters.en: The sayings of King Lemuel—an inspired utterance his mother taught him.
chapters.zh: 利慕伊勒王的言语，是他母亲教训他的真言。

chapters.en: Listen, my son! Listen, son of my womb! Listen, my son, the answer to my prayers!
chapters.zh: 我的儿阿，我腹中生的儿阿，我许愿得的儿阿，我当怎样教训你呢？

chapters.en: Do not spend your strength on women, your vigor on those who ruin kings.
chapters.zh: 不要将你的精力给妇女，也不要有败坏君王的行为。

chapters.en: It is not for kings, Lemuel— it is not for kings to drink wine, not for rulers to crave beer,
chapters.zh: 利慕伊勒阿，君王喝酒，君王喝酒不相宜。王子说，浓酒在那里也不相宜。

chapters.en: lest they drink and forget what has been decreed, and deprive all the oppressed of their rights.
chapters.zh: 恐怕喝了就忘记律例，颠倒一切困苦人的是非。

chapters.en: Let beer be for those who are perishing, wine for those who are in anguish!
chapters.zh: 可以把浓酒给将亡的人喝。把清酒给苦心的人喝。

chapters.en: Let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their misery no more.
chapters.zh: 让他喝了，就忘记他的贫穷，不再记念他的苦楚。

chapters.en: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute.
chapters.zh: 你当为哑吧（或作不能自辨的）开口，为一切孤独的伸冤。

chapters.en: Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
chapters.zh: 你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

chapters.en: A wife of noble character who can find? She is worth far more than rubies.
chapters.zh: 才德的妇人，谁能得着呢？她的价值远胜过珍珠。

chapters.en: Her husband has full confidence in her and lacks nothing of value.
chapters.zh: 她丈夫心里倚靠她，必不缺少利益。

chapters.en: She brings him good, not harm, all the days of her life.
chapters.zh: 她一生使丈夫有益无损。

chapters.en: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.
chapters.zh: 她寻找羊绒和麻，甘心用手作工。

chapters.en: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.
chapters.zh: 她好像商船从远方运粮来。

chapters.en: She gets up while it is still night; she provides food for her family and portions for her female servants.
chapters.zh: 未到黎明她就起来，把食物分给家中的人。将当作的工分派婢女。

chapters.en: She considers a field and buys it; out of her earnings she plants a vineyard.
chapters.zh: 她想得田地，就买来。用手所得之利，栽种葡萄园。

chapters.en: She sets about her work vigorously; her arms are strong for her tasks.
chapters.zh: 她以能力束腰，使膀臂有力。

chapters.en: She sees that her trading is profitable, and her lamp does not go out at night.
chapters.zh: 她觉得所经营的有利，她的灯终夜不灭。

chapters.en: In her hand she holds the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.
chapters.zh: 她手拿捻线竿。手把纺线车。

chapters.en: She opens her arms to the poor and extends her hands to the needy.
chapters.zh: 她张手周济困苦人，伸手帮补穷乏人。

chapters.en: When it snows, she has no fear for her household; for all of them are clothed in scarlet.
chapters.zh: 她不因下雪为家里的人担心，因为全家都穿着朱红衣服。

chapters.en: She makes coverings for her bed; she is clothed in fine linen and purple.
chapters.zh: 她为自己制作绣花毯子，她的衣服，是细麻和紫色布作的。
