chapters.en: Her husband is respected at the city gate, where he takes his seat among the elders of the land.
chapters.zh: 她丈夫在城门口与本地的长老同坐，为众人所认识。

chapters.en: She makes linen garments and sells them, and supplies the merchants with sashes.
chapters.zh: 她作细麻布衣裳出卖。又将腰带卖与商家。

chapters.en: She is clothed with strength and dignity; she can laugh at the days to come.
chapters.zh: 能力和威仪，是她的衣服。她想到日后的景况就喜笑。

chapters.en: She speaks with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
chapters.zh: 她开口就发智慧。她舌上有仁慈的法则。

chapters.en: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
chapters.zh: 她观察家务，并不吃闲饭。

chapters.en: Her children arise and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praises her:
chapters.zh: 她的儿女起来称她有福。她的丈夫也称赞她，

chapters.en: “Many women do noble things, but you surpass them all.”
chapters.zh: 说，才德的女子很多，惟独你超过一切。

chapters.en: Charm is deceptive, and beauty is fleeting; but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
chapters.zh: 艳丽是虚假的。美容是虚浮的。惟敬畏耶和华的妇女，必得称赞。

chapters.en: Honor her for all that her hands have done, and let her works bring her praise at the city gate.
chapters.zh: 愿她享受操作所得的。愿她的工作，在城门口荣耀她。

chapters.en: The words of the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:
chapters.zh: 在耶路撒冷作王，大卫的儿子，传道者的言语。

chapters.en: “Meaningless! Meaningless!” says the Teacher. “Utterly meaningless! Everything is meaningless.”
chapters.zh: 传道者说，虚空的虚空，虚空的虚空。凡事都是虚空。

chapters.en: What do people gain from all their labors at which they toil under the sun?
chapters.zh: 人一切的劳碌，就是他在日光之下的劳碌，有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.
chapters.zh: 一代过去，一代又来。地却永远长存。

chapters.en: The sun rises and the sun sets, and hurries back to where it rises.
chapters.zh: 日头出来，日头落下，急归所出之地。

chapters.en: The wind blows to the south and turns to the north; round and round it goes, ever returning on its course.
chapters.zh: 风往南刮，又向北转，不住地旋转，而且返回转行原道。

chapters.en: All streams flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full. To the place the streams come from, there they return again.
chapters.zh: 江河都往海里流，海却不满。江河从何处流，仍归还何处。

chapters.en: All things are wearisome, more than one can say. The eye never has enough of seeing, nor the ear its fill of hearing.
chapters.zh: 万事令人厌烦。（或作万物满有困乏）人不能说尽。眼看，看不饱，耳听，听不足。

chapters.en: What has been will be again, what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
chapters.zh: 已有的事，后必再有。已行的事，后必再行。日光之下并无新事。

chapters.en: Is there anything of which one can say, “Look! This is something new”? It was here already, long ago; it was here before our time.
chapters.zh: 岂有一件事人能指着说，这是新的。哪知，在我们以前的世代，早已有了。

chapters.en: No one remembers the former generations, and even those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow them.
chapters.zh: 已过的世代，无人记念，将来的世代，后来的人也不记念。

chapters.en: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 我传道者在耶路撒冷作过以色列的王。

chapters.en: I applied my mind to study and to explore by wisdom all that is done under the heavens. What a heavy burden God has laid on mankind!
chapters.zh: 我专心用智慧寻求查究天下所作的一切事，乃知神叫世人所经练的，是极重的劳苦。

chapters.en: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun; all of them are meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下所作的一切事，都是虚空，都是捕风。

chapters.en: What is crooked cannot be straightened; what is lacking cannot be counted.
chapters.zh: 弯曲的不能变直，缺少的不能足数。

chapters.en: I said to myself, “Look, I have increased in wisdom more than anyone who has ruled over Jerusalem before me; I have experienced much of wisdom and knowledge.”
chapters.zh: 我心里议论，说，我得了大智慧，胜过我以前在耶路撒冷的众人。而且我心中多经历智慧，和知识的事。

chapters.en: Then I applied myself to the understanding of wisdom, and also of madness and folly, but I learned that this, too, is a chasing after the wind.
chapters.zh: 我又专心察明智慧，狂妄，和愚昧。乃知这也是捕风。

chapters.en: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow; the more knowledge, the more grief.
chapters.zh: 因为多有智慧，就多有愁烦。加增知识的，就加增忧伤。

chapters.en: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure to find out what is good.” But that also proved to be meaningless.
chapters.zh: 我心里说，来吧，我以喜乐试试你，你好享福。谁知，这也是虚空。

chapters.en: “Laughter,” I said, “is madness. And what does pleasure accomplish?”
chapters.zh: 我指嬉笑说，这是狂妄。论喜乐说，有何功效呢？

chapters.en: I tried cheering myself with wine, and embracing folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom. I wanted to see what was good for people to do under the heavens during the few days of their lives.
chapters.zh: 我心里察究，如何用酒使我肉体舒畅，我心却仍以智慧引导我。又如何持住愚昧，等我看明世人，在天下一生当行何事为美。

chapters.en: I undertook great projects: I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.
chapters.zh: 我为自己动大工程，建造房屋，栽种葡萄园，

chapters.en: I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
chapters.zh: 修造园囿，在其中栽种各样果木树，

chapters.en: I made reservoirs to water groves of flourishing trees.
chapters.zh: 挖造水池，用以浇灌嫩小的树木。

chapters.en: I bought male and female slaves and had other slaves who were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me.
chapters.zh: 我买了仆婢，也有生在家中的仆婢。又有许多牛群羊群，胜过以前在耶路撒冷众人所有的。

chapters.en: I amassed silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and a harem as well—the delights of a man’s heart.
chapters.zh: 我又为自己积蓄金银，和君王的财宝，并各省的财宝。又得唱歌的男女，和世人所喜爱的物，并许多的妃嫔。

chapters.en: I became greater by far than anyone in Jerusalem before me. In all this my wisdom stayed with me.
chapters.zh: 这样，我就日见昌盛，胜过以前在耶路撒冷的众人。我的智慧仍然存留。

chapters.en: I denied myself nothing my eyes desired; I refused my heart no pleasure. My heart took delight in all my labor, and this was the reward for all my toil.
chapters.zh: 凡我眼所求的，我没有留下不给他的。我心所乐的，我没有禁止不享受的。因我的心为我一切所劳碌的快乐。这就是我从劳碌中所得的分。

chapters.en: Yet when I surveyed all that my hands had done and what I had toiled to achieve, everything was meaningless, a chasing after the wind; nothing was gained under the sun.
chapters.zh: 后来我察看我手所经营的一切事，和我劳碌所成的功。谁知都是虚空，都是捕风，在日光之下毫无益处。

chapters.en: Then I turned my thoughts to consider wisdom, and also madness and folly. What more can the king’s successor do than what has already been done?
chapters.zh: 我转念观看智慧，狂妄，和愚昧。在王以后而来的人，还能作什么呢？也不过行早先所行的就是了。

chapters.en: I saw that wisdom is better than folly, just as light is better than darkness.
chapters.zh: 我便看出智慧胜过愚昧，如同光明胜过黑暗。

chapters.en: The wise have eyes in their heads, while the fool walks in the darkness; but I came to realize that the same fate overtakes them both.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的眼目光明，（光明原文作在他头上）愚昧人在黑暗里行。我却看明有一件事，这两等人都必遇见。

chapters.en: Then I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will overtake me also. What then do I gain by being wise?” I said to myself, “This too is meaningless.”
chapters.zh: 我就心里说，愚昧人所遇见的，我也必遇见。我为何更有智慧呢？我心里说，这也是虚空。

chapters.en: For the wise, like the fool, will not be long remembered; the days have already come when both have been forgotten. Like the fool, the wise too must die!
chapters.zh: 智慧人，和愚昧人一样，永远无人记念。因为日后都被忘记。可叹智慧人死亡，与愚昧人无异。

chapters.en: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. All of it is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
chapters.zh: 我所以恨恶生命，因为在日光之下所行的事我都以为烦恼。都是虚空，都是捕风。

chapters.en: I hated all the things I had toiled for under the sun, because I must leave them to the one who comes after me.
chapters.zh: 我恨恶一切的劳碌，就是我在日光之下的劳碌。因为我得来的必留给我以后的人。

chapters.en: And who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet they will have control over all the fruit of my toil into which I have poured my effort and skill under the sun. This too is meaningless.
chapters.zh: 那人是智慧，是愚昧，谁能知道。他竟要管理我劳碌所得的，就是我在日光之下用智慧所得的。这也是虚空。

chapters.en: So my heart began to despair over all my toilsome labor under the sun.
chapters.zh: 故此，我转想我在日光之下所劳碌的一切工作，心便绝望。

chapters.en: For a person may labor with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and then they must leave all they own to another who has not toiled for it. This too is meaningless and a great misfortune.
chapters.zh: 因为有人用智慧知识灵巧所劳碌得来的，却要留给未曾劳碌的人为分。这也是虚空，也是大患。

chapters.en: What do people get for all the toil and anxious striving with which they labor under the sun?
chapters.zh: 人在日光之下劳碌累心，在他一切的劳碌上得着什么呢？

chapters.en: All their days their work is grief and pain; even at night their minds do not rest. This too is meaningless.
chapters.zh: 因为他日日忧虑，他的劳苦成为愁烦。连夜间心也不安。这也是虚空。

chapters.en: A person can do nothing better than to eat and drink and find satisfaction in their own toil. This too, I see, is from the hand of God,
chapters.zh: 人莫强如吃喝，且在劳碌中享福。我看这也是出于神的手。

chapters.en: for without him, who can eat or find enjoyment?
chapters.zh: 论到吃用，享福，谁能胜过我呢？

chapters.en: To the person who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge and happiness, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and storing up wealth to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
chapters.zh: 神喜悦谁，就给谁智慧，知识，和喜乐。惟有罪人，神使他劳苦，叫他将所收聚的，所堆积的，归给神所喜悦的人。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

chapters.en: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens:
chapters.zh: 凡事都有定期，天下万务都有定时。

chapters.en: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,
chapters.zh: 生有时，死有时。栽种有时，拔出所栽种的，也有时。

chapters.en: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build,
chapters.zh: 杀戮有时，医治有时。拆毁有时，建造有时。

chapters.en: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,
chapters.zh: 哭有时，笑有时。哀恸有时，跳舞有时。

chapters.en: a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,
chapters.zh: 抛掷石头有时，堆聚石头有时。怀抱有时，不怀抱有时。

chapters.en: a time to search and a time to give up, a time to keep and a time to throw away,
chapters.zh: 寻找有时，失落有时。保守有时，舍弃有时。

chapters.en: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
chapters.zh: 撕裂有时，缝补有时。静默有时，言语有时。

chapters.en: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
chapters.zh: 喜爱有时，恨恶有时。争战有时，和好有时。

chapters.en: What do workers gain from their toil?
chapters.zh: 这样看来，作事的人在他的劳碌上有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: I have seen the burden God has laid on the human race.
chapters.zh: 我见神叫世人劳苦，使他们在其中受经练。

chapters.en: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart; yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end.
chapters.zh: 神造万物，各按其时成为美好。又将永生安置在世人心里。（永生原文作永远）然而神从始至终的作为，人不能参透。

chapters.en: I know that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do good while they live.
chapters.zh: 我知道世人，莫强如终身喜乐行善。

chapters.en: That each of them may eat and drink, and find satisfaction in all their toil—this is the gift of God.
chapters.zh: 并且人人吃喝，在他一切劳碌中享福。这也是神的恩赐。

chapters.en: I know that everything God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God does it so that people will fear him.
chapters.zh: 我知道神一切所作的，都必永存，无所增添，无所减少。神这样行，是要人在他面前存敬畏的心。

chapters.en: Whatever is has already been, and what will be has been before; and God will call the past to account.
chapters.zh: 现今的事早先就有了。将来的事早已也有了。并且神使已过的事重新再来。（或作并且神再寻回已过的事）

chapters.en: And I saw something else under the sun: In the place of judgment—wickedness was there, in the place of justice—wickedness was there.
chapters.zh: 我又见日光之下，在审判之处有奸恶。在公义之处也有奸恶。

chapters.en: I said to myself, “God will bring into judgment both the righteous and the wicked, for there will be a time for every activity, a time to judge every deed.”
chapters.zh: 我心里说，神必审判义人和恶人。因为在那里，各样事务，一切工作，都有定时。

chapters.en: I also said to myself, “As for humans, God tests them so that they may see that they are like the animals.
chapters.zh: 我心里说，这乃为世人的缘故，是神要试验他们，使他们觉得自己不过像兽一样。

chapters.en: Surely the fate of human beings is like that of the animals; the same fate awaits them both: As one dies, so dies the other. All have the same breath ; humans have no advantage over animals. Everything is meaningless.
chapters.zh: 因为世人遭遇的，兽也遭遇。所遭遇的都是一样。这个怎样死，那个也怎样死。气息都是一样。人不能强于兽。都是虚空。

chapters.en: All go to the same place; all come from dust, and to dust all return.
chapters.zh: 都归一处。都是出于尘土，也都归于尘土。

chapters.en: Who knows if the human spirit rises upward and if the spirit of the animal goes down into the earth?”
chapters.zh: 谁知道人的灵是往上升，兽的魂是下入地呢？

chapters.en: So I saw that there is nothing better for a person than to enjoy their work, because that is their lot. For who can bring them to see what will happen after them?
chapters.zh: 故此，我见人，莫强如在他经营的事上喜乐。因为这是他的分。他身后的事，谁能使他回来得见呢？

chapters.en: Again I looked and saw all the oppression that was taking place under the sun: I saw the tears of the oppressed— and they have no comforter; power was on the side of their oppressors— and they have no comforter.
chapters.zh: 我又转念，见日光之下所行的一切欺压。看哪，受欺压的流泪，且无人安慰。欺压他们的有势力，也无人安慰他们。

chapters.en: And I declared that the dead, who had already died, are happier than the living, who are still alive.
chapters.zh: 因此，我赞叹那早已死的死人，胜过那还活着的活人。

chapters.en: But better than both is the one who has never been born, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
chapters.zh: 并且我以为那未曾生的，就是未见过日光之下恶事的，比这两等人更强。

chapters.en: And I saw that all toil and all achievement spring from one person’s envy of another. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
chapters.zh: 我又见人为一切的劳碌，和各样灵巧的工作，就被邻舍嫉妒。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

chapters.en: Fools fold their hands and ruin themselves.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人抱着手，吃自己的肉。

chapters.en: Better one handful with tranquillity than two handfuls with toil and chasing after the wind.
chapters.zh: 满了一把，得享安静，强如满了两把，劳碌捕风。

chapters.en: Again I saw something meaningless under the sun:
chapters.zh: 我又转念，见日光之下有一件虚空的事。

chapters.en: There was a man all alone; he had neither son nor brother. There was no end to his toil, yet his eyes were not content with his wealth. “For whom am I toiling,” he asked, “and why am I depriving myself of enjoyment?” This too is meaningless— a miserable business!
chapters.zh: 有人孤单无二，无子，无兄，竟劳碌不息，眼目也不以钱财为足。他说，我劳劳碌碌，刻苦自己，不享福乐，到底是为谁呢？这也是虚空，是极重的劳苦。

chapters.en: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor:
chapters.zh: 两个人总比一个人好，因为二人劳碌同得美好的果效。

chapters.en: If either of them falls down, one can help the other up. But pity anyone who falls and has no one to help them up.
chapters.zh: 若是跌倒，这人可以扶起他的同伴。若是孤身跌倒，没有别人扶起他来。这人就有祸了。

chapters.en: Also, if two lie down together, they will keep warm. But how can one keep warm alone?
chapters.zh: 再者，二人同睡，就都暖和。一人独睡，怎能暖和呢？

chapters.en: Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
chapters.zh: 有人攻胜孤身一人，若有二人便能敌挡他。三股合成的绳子，不容易折断。

chapters.en: Better a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to heed a warning.
chapters.zh: 贫穷而有智慧的少年人，胜过年老不肯纳谏的愚昧王。

chapters.en: The youth may have come from prison to the kingship, or he may have been born in poverty within his kingdom.
chapters.zh: 这人是从监牢中出来作王。在他国中，生来原是贫穷的。

chapters.en: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed the youth, the king’s successor.
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下一切行动的活人，都随从那第二位，就是起来代替老王的少年人。

chapters.en: There was no end to all the people who were before them. But those who came later were not pleased with the successor. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
chapters.zh: 他所治理的众人，就是他的百姓，多得无数。在他后来的人，尚且不喜悦他。这真是虚空，也是捕风。

chapters.en: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Go near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.
chapters.zh: 你到神的殿，要谨慎脚步。因为近前听，胜过愚昧人献祭，（或作胜过献愚昧人的祭）他们本不知道所作的是恶。

chapters.en: Do not be quick with your mouth, do not be hasty in your heart to utter anything before God. God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few.
chapters.zh: 你在神面前不可冒失开口，也不可心急发言。因为神在天上，你在地下，所以你的言语要寡少。

chapters.en: A dream comes when there are many cares, and many words mark the speech of a fool.
chapters.zh: 事务多，就令人作梦，言语多，就显出愚昧。

chapters.en: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfill it. He has no pleasure in fools; fulfill your vow.
chapters.zh: 你向神许愿，偿还不可迟延。因他不喜悦愚昧人。所以你许的愿应当偿还。

chapters.en: It is better not to make a vow than to make one and not fulfill it.
chapters.zh: 你许愿不还，不如不许。

chapters.en: Do not let your mouth lead you into sin. And do not protest to the temple messenger, “My vow was a mistake.” Why should God be angry at what you say and destroy the work of your hands?
chapters.zh: 不可任你的口使肉体犯罪。也不可在祭司（原文作使者）面前说是错许了。为何使神因你的声音发怒，败坏你手所作的呢？

chapters.en: Much dreaming and many words are meaningless. Therefore fear God.
chapters.zh: 多梦和多言，其中多有虚幻。你只要敬畏神。

chapters.en: If you see the poor oppressed in a district, and justice and rights denied, do not be surprised at such things; for one official is eyed by a higher one, and over them both are others higher still.
chapters.zh: 你若在一省之中见穷人受欺压，并夺去公义公平的事，不要因此诧异。因有一位高过居高位的鉴察。在他们以上还有更高的。

chapters.en: The increase from the land is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
chapters.zh: 况且地的益处归众人。就是君王也受田地的供应。

chapters.en: Whoever loves money never has enough; whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with their income. This too is meaningless.
chapters.zh: 贪爱银子的，不因得银子知足。贪爱丰富的，也不因得利益知足。这也是虚空。

chapters.en: As goods increase, so do those who consume them. And what benefit are they to the owners except to feast their eyes on them?
chapters.zh: 货物增添，吃的人也增添。物主得什么益处呢？不过眼看而已。

chapters.en: The sleep of a laborer is sweet, whether they eat little or much, but as for the rich, their abundance permits them no sleep.
chapters.zh: 劳碌的人，不拘吃多吃少，睡得香甜。富足人的丰满，却不容他睡觉。

chapters.en: I have seen a grievous evil under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owners,
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下，有一宗大祸患，就是财主积存赀财，反害自己。

chapters.en: or wealth lost through some misfortune, so that when they have children there is nothing left for them to inherit.
chapters.zh: 因遭遇祸患，这些赀财就消灭。那人若生了儿子，手里也一无所有。

chapters.en: Everyone comes naked from their mother’s womb, and as everyone comes, so they depart. They take nothing from their toil that they can carry in their hands.
chapters.zh: 他怎样从母胎赤身而来，也必照样赤身而去。他所劳碌得来的。手中分毫不能带去。

chapters.en: This too is a grievous evil: As everyone comes, so they depart, and what do they gain, since they toil for the wind?
chapters.zh: 他来的情形怎样，他去的情形也怎样。这也是一宗大祸患。他为风劳碌有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: All their days they eat in darkness, with great frustration, affliction and anger.
chapters.zh: 并且他终身在黑暗中吃喝，多有烦恼，又有病患呕气。

chapters.en: This is what I have observed to be good: that it is appropriate for a person to eat, to drink and to find satisfaction in their toilsome labor under the sun during the few days of life God has given them—for this is their lot.
chapters.zh: 我所见为善为美的，就是人在神赐他一生的日子吃喝，享受日光之下劳碌得来的好处。因为这是他的分。

chapters.en: Moreover, when God gives someone wealth and possessions, and the ability to enjoy them, to accept their lot and be happy in their toil—this is a gift of God.
chapters.zh: 神赐人赀财丰富，使他能以吃用，能取自己的分，在他劳碌中喜乐。这乃是神的恩赐。

chapters.en: They seldom reflect on the days of their life, because God keeps them occupied with gladness of heart.
chapters.zh: 他不多思念自己一生的年日。因为神应他的心使他喜乐。

chapters.en: I have seen another evil under the sun, and it weighs heavily on mankind:
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下有一宗祸患，重压在人身上。

chapters.en: God gives some people wealth, possessions and honor, so that they lack nothing their hearts desire, but God does not grant them the ability to enjoy them, and strangers enjoy them instead. This is meaningless, a grievous evil.
chapters.zh: 就是人蒙神赐他赀财，丰富，尊荣，以致他心里所愿的一样都不缺，只是神使他不能吃用，反有外人来吃用。这是虚空，也是祸患。

chapters.en: A man may have a hundred children and live many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he cannot enjoy his prosperity and does not receive proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
chapters.zh: 人若生一百个儿子，活许多岁数，以致他的年日甚多，心里却不得满享福乐，又不得埋葬。据我说，那不到期而落的胎比他倒好。

chapters.en: It comes without meaning, it departs in darkness, and in darkness its name is shrouded.
chapters.zh: 因为虚虚而来，暗暗而去，名字被黑暗遮蔽。

chapters.en: Though it never saw the sun or knew anything, it has more rest than does that man—
chapters.zh: 并且没有见过天日，也毫无知觉。这胎，比那人倒享安息。

chapters.en: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?
chapters.zh: 那人虽然活千年，再活千年，却不享福，众人岂不都归一个地方去吗？

chapters.en: Everyone’s toil is for their mouth, yet their appetite is never satisfied.
chapters.zh: 人的劳碌都为口腹，心里却不知足。

chapters.en: What advantage have the wise over fools? What do the poor gain by knowing how to conduct themselves before others?
chapters.zh: 这样看来，智慧人比愚昧人有什么长处呢？穷人在众人面前知道如何行，有什么长处呢？

chapters.en: Better what the eye sees than the roving of the appetite. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
chapters.zh: 眼睛所看的，比心里妄想的倒好。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

chapters.en: Whatever exists has already been named, and what humanity is has been known; no one can contend with someone who is stronger.
chapters.zh: 先前所有的，早已起了名。并知道何为人。他也不能与那比自己力大的相争。

chapters.en: The more the words, the less the meaning, and how does that profit anyone?
chapters.zh: 加增虚浮的事既多，这与人有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: For who knows what is good for a person in life, during the few and meaningless days they pass through like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they are gone?
chapters.zh: 人一生虚度的日子，就如影儿经过。谁知道什么与他有益呢？谁能告诉他身后在日光之下有什么事呢？

chapters.en: A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death better than the day of birth.
chapters.zh: 名誉强如美好的膏油。人死的日子，胜过人生的日子。

chapters.en: It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for death is the destiny of everyone; the living should take this to heart.
chapters.zh: 往遭丧的家去，强如往宴乐的家去，因为死是众人的结局。活人也必将这事放在心上。

chapters.en: Frustration is better than laughter, because a sad face is good for the heart.
chapters.zh: 忧愁强如喜笑，因为面带愁容，终必使心喜乐。

chapters.en: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的心，在遭丧之家。愚昧人的心，在快乐之家。

chapters.en: It is better to heed the rebuke of a wise person than to listen to the song of fools.
chapters.zh: 听智慧人的责备，强如听愚昧人的歌唱。

chapters.en: Like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of fools. This too is meaningless.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人的笑声，好像锅下烧荆棘的爆声，这也是虚空。

chapters.en: Extortion turns a wise person into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
chapters.zh: 勒索使智慧人变为愚妄。贿赂能败坏人的慧心。

chapters.en: The end of a matter is better than its beginning, and patience is better than pride.
chapters.zh: 事情的终局，强如事情的起头。存心忍耐的，胜过居心骄傲的。

chapters.en: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger resides in the lap of fools.
chapters.zh: 你不要心里急躁恼怒，因为恼怒存在愚昧人的怀中。

chapters.en: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is not wise to ask such questions.
chapters.zh: 不要说，先前的日子强过如今的日子，是什么缘故呢？你这样问，不是出于智慧。

chapters.en: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is a good thing and benefits those who see the sun.
chapters.zh: 智慧和产业并好。而且见天日的人，得智慧更为有益。

chapters.en: Wisdom is a shelter as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is this: Wisdom preserves those who have it.
chapters.zh: 因为智慧护庇人，好像银钱护庇人一样。惟独智慧能保全智慧人的生命，这就是知识的益处。

chapters.en: Consider what God has done: Who can straighten what he has made crooked?
chapters.zh: 你要察看神的作为，因神使为曲的，谁能变为直呢？

chapters.en: When times are good, be happy; but when times are bad, consider this: God has made the one as well as the other. Therefore, no one can discover anything about their future.
chapters.zh: 遇亨通的日子，你当喜乐。遭患难的日子，你当思想。因为神使这两样并列，为的是叫人查不出身后有什么事。

chapters.en: In this meaningless life of mine I have seen both of these: the righteous perishing in their righteousness, and the wicked living long in their wickedness.
chapters.zh: 有义人行义，反致灭亡。有恶人行恶，倒享长寿。这都是我在虚度之日中所见过的。

chapters.en: Do not be overrighteous, neither be overwise— why destroy yourself?
chapters.zh: 不要行义过分。也不要过于自逞智慧。何必自取败亡呢？

chapters.en: Do not be overwicked, and do not be a fool— why die before your time?
chapters.zh: 不要行恶过分。也不要为人愚昧。何必不到期而死呢？

chapters.en: It is good to grasp the one and not let go of the other. Whoever fears God will avoid all extremes.
chapters.zh: 你持守这个为美。那个也不要松手。因为敬畏神的人，必从这两样出来。

chapters.en: Wisdom makes one wise person more powerful than ten rulers in a city.
chapters.zh: 智慧使有智慧的人，比城中十个官长更有能力。

chapters.en: Indeed, there is no one on earth who is righteous, no one who does what is right and never sins.
chapters.zh: 时常行善而不犯罪的义人，世上实在没有。

chapters.en: Do not pay attention to every word people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you—
chapters.zh: 人所说的一切话，你不要放在心上，恐怕听见你的仆人咒诅你。

chapters.en: for you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.
chapters.zh: 因为你心里知道，自己也曾屡次咒诅别人。

chapters.en: All this I tested by wisdom and I said, “I am determined to be wise”— but this was beyond me.
chapters.zh: 我曾用智慧试验这一切事。我说，要得智慧，智慧却离我远。

chapters.en: Whatever exists is far off and most profound— who can discover it?
chapters.zh: 万事之理离我甚远，而且最深，谁能测透呢？

chapters.en: So I turned my mind to understand, to investigate and to search out wisdom and the scheme of things and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the madness of folly.
chapters.zh: 我转念，一心要知道，要考察，要寻求智慧，和万事的理由。又要知道邪恶为愚昧，愚昧为狂妄。

chapters.en: I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a trap and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner she will ensnare.
chapters.zh: 我得知有等妇人，比死还苦，她的心是网罗，手是锁链。凡蒙神喜悦的人，必能躲避她。有罪的人，却被她缠住了。

chapters.en: “Look,” says the Teacher, “this is what I have discovered: “Adding one thing to another to discover the scheme of things—
chapters.zh: 传道者说，看哪，一千男子中，我找到一个正直人。但众女子中，没有找到一个。我将这事一一比较，要寻求其理，我心仍要寻找，却未曾找到。

chapters.en: while I was still searching but not finding— I found one upright man among a thousand, but not one upright woman among them all.
This only have I found: God created mankind upright, but they have gone in search of many schemes.”
chapters.zh: 我所找到的，只有一件，就是神造人原是正直，但他们寻出许多巧计。

chapters.en: Who is like the wise? Who knows the explanation of things? A person’s wisdom brightens their face and changes its hard appearance.
chapters.zh: 谁如智慧人呢？谁知道事情的解释呢？人的智慧使他的脸发光，并使他脸上的暴气改变。

chapters.en: Obey the king’s command, I say, because you took an oath before God.
chapters.zh: 我劝你遵守王的命令。既指神起誓，理当如此。

chapters.en: Do not be in a hurry to leave the king’s presence. Do not stand up for a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.
chapters.zh: 不要急躁离开王的面前。不要固执行恶。因为他凡事都随自己的心意而行。

chapters.en: Since a king’s word is supreme, who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
chapters.zh: 王的话本有权力，谁敢问他说，你作什么呢？

chapters.en: Whoever obeys his command will come to no harm, and the wise heart will know the proper time and procedure.
chapters.zh: 凡遵守命令的，必不经历祸患。智慧人的心，能辨明时候和定理。（原文作审判下节同）

chapters.en: For there is a proper time and procedure for every matter, though a person may be weighed down by misery.
chapters.zh: 各样事务成就，都有时候和定理。因为人的苦难，重压在他身上。

chapters.en: Since no one knows the future, who can tell someone else what is to come?
chapters.zh: 他不知道将来的事，因为将来如何，谁能告诉他呢？

chapters.en: As no one has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has power over the time of their death. As no one is discharged in time of war, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
chapters.zh: 无人有权力掌管生命，将生命留住。也无人有权力掌管死期。这场争战，无人能免，邪恶也不能救那好行邪恶的人。

chapters.en: All this I saw, as I applied my mind to everything done under the sun. There is a time when a man lords it over others to his own hurt.
chapters.zh: 这一切我都见过。也专心查考日光之下所作的一切事。有时这人管辖那人，令人受害。

chapters.en: Then too, I saw the wicked buried—those who used to come and go from the holy place and receive praise in the city where they did this. This too is meaningless.
chapters.zh: 我见恶人埋葬，归入坟墓。又见行正直事的，离开圣地，在城中被人忘记。这也是虚空。

chapters.en: When the sentence for a crime is not quickly carried out, people’s hearts are filled with schemes to do wrong.
chapters.zh: 因为断定罪名，不立刻施刑，所以世人满心作恶。

chapters.en: Although a wicked person who commits a hundred crimes may live a long time, I know that it will go better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him.
chapters.zh: 罪人虽然作恶百次，倒享长久的年日。然而我准知道，敬畏神的，就是在他面前敬畏的人，终久必得福乐。

chapters.en: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.
chapters.zh: 恶人却不得福乐，也不得长久的年日。这年日好像影儿，因他不敬畏神。

chapters.en: There is something else meaningless that occurs on earth: the righteous who get what the wicked deserve, and the wicked who get what the righteous deserve. This too, I say, is meaningless.
chapters.zh: 世上有一件虚空的事，就是义人所遭遇的，反照恶人所行的。又有恶人所遭遇的，反照义人所行的。我说，这也是虚空。

chapters.en: So I commend the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a person under the sun than to eat and drink and be glad. Then joy will accompany them in their toil all the days of the life God has given them under the sun.
chapters.zh: 我就称赞快乐，原来人在日光之下，莫强如吃喝快乐。因为他在日光之下，神赐他一生的年日，要从劳碌中，时常享受所得的。

chapters.en: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the labor that is done on earth—people getting no sleep day or night—
chapters.zh: 我专心求智慧，要看世上所作的事。（有昼夜不睡觉，不合眼的）。

chapters.en: then I saw all that God has done. No one can comprehend what goes on under the sun. Despite all their efforts to search it out, no one can discover its meaning. Even if the wise claim they know, they cannot really comprehend it.
chapters.zh: 我就看明神一切的作为。知道人查不出日光之下所作的事。任凭他费多少力寻查，都查不出来。就是智慧人虽想知道，也是查不出来。

chapters.en: So I reflected on all this and concluded that the righteous and the wise and what they do are in God’s hands, but no one knows whether love or hate awaits them.
chapters.zh: 我将这一切事放在心上，详细考究，就知道义人和智慧人，并他们的作为，都在神手中。或是爱，或是恨，都在他们的前面，人不能知道。

chapters.en: All share a common destiny—the righteous and the wicked, the good and the bad, the clean and the unclean, those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. As it is with the good, so with the sinful; as it is with those who take oaths, so with those who are afraid to take them.
chapters.zh: 凡临到众人的事，都是一样。义人和恶人，都遭遇一样的事。好人，洁净人和不洁净人，献祭的与不献祭的，也是一样。好人如何，罪人也如何。起誓的如何，怕起誓的也如何。

chapters.en: This is the evil in everything that happens under the sun: The same destiny overtakes all. The hearts of people, moreover, are full of evil and there is madness in their hearts while they live, and afterward they join the dead.
chapters.zh: 在日光之下所行的一切事上，有一件祸患，就是众人所遭遇的，都是一样。并且世人的心，充满了恶。活着的时候心里狂妄，后来就归死人那里去了。

chapters.en: Anyone who is among the living has hope —even a live dog is better off than a dead lion!
chapters.zh: 与一切活人相连的，那人还有指望。因为活着的狗，比死了的狮子更强。

chapters.en: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing; they have no further reward, and even their name is forgotten.
chapters.zh: 活着的人，知道必死。死了的人，毫无所知。也不再得赏赐，他们的名无人记念。

chapters.en: Their love, their hate and their jealousy have long since vanished; never again will they have a part in anything that happens under the sun.
chapters.zh: 他们的爱，他们的恨，他们的嫉妒，早都消灭了。在日光之下所行的一切事上，他们永不再有分了。

chapters.en: Go, eat your food with gladness, and drink your wine with a joyful heart, for God has already approved what you do.
chapters.zh: 你只管去欢欢喜喜吃你的饭。心中快乐喝你的酒。因为神已经悦纳你的作为。

chapters.en: Always be clothed in white, and always anoint your head with oil.
chapters.zh: 你的衣服当时常洁白。你头上也不要缺少膏油。

chapters.en: Enjoy life with your wife, whom you love, all the days of this meaningless life that God has given you under the sun—all your meaningless days. For this is your lot in life and in your toilsome labor under the sun.
chapters.zh: 在你一生虚空的年日，就是神赐你在日光之下虚空的年日，当同你所爱的妻，快活度日。因为那是你生前，在日光之下劳碌的事上所得的分。

chapters.en: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might, for in the realm of the dead, where you are going, there is neither working nor planning nor knowledge nor wisdom.
chapters.zh: 凡你手所当作的事，要尽力去作。因为在你所必去的阴间，没有工作，没有谋算，没有知识，也没有智慧。

chapters.en: I have seen something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift or the battle to the strong, nor does food come to the wise or wealth to the brilliant or favor to the learned; but time and chance happen to them all.
chapters.zh: 我又转念，见日光之下，快跑的未必能赢，力战的未必得胜，智慧的未必得粮食，明哲的未必得赀财，灵巧的未必得喜悦。所临到众人的，是在乎当时的机会。

chapters.en: Moreover, no one knows when their hour will come: As fish are caught in a cruel net, or birds are taken in a snare, so people are trapped by evil times that fall unexpectedly upon them.
chapters.zh: 原来人也不知道自己的定期。鱼被恶网圈住，鸟被网罗捉住，祸患忽然临到的时候，世人陷在其中，也是如此。

chapters.en: I also saw under the sun this example of wisdom that greatly impressed me:
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下有一样智慧，据我看乃是广大，

chapters.en: There was once a small city with only a few people in it. And a powerful king came against it, surrounded it and built huge siege works against it.
chapters.zh: 就是有一小城，其中的人数稀少，有大君王来攻击，修筑营垒，将城围困。

chapters.en: Now there lived in that city a man poor but wise, and he saved the city by his wisdom. But nobody remembered that poor man.
chapters.zh: 城中有一个贫穷的智慧人，他用智慧救了那城，却没有人记念那穷人。

chapters.en: So I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” But the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are no longer heeded.
chapters.zh: 我就说，智慧胜过勇力。然而那贫穷人的智慧，被人藐视，他的话也无人听从。

chapters.en: The quiet words of the wise are more to be heeded than the shouts of a ruler of fools.
chapters.zh: 宁可在安静之中听智慧人的言语，不听掌管愚昧人的喊声。

chapters.en: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
chapters.zh: 智慧胜过打仗的兵器。但一个罪人，能败坏许多善事。

chapters.en: As dead flies give perfume a bad smell, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
chapters.zh: 死苍蝇，使作香的膏油发出臭气。这样，一点愚昧，也能败坏智慧和尊荣。

chapters.en: The heart of the wise inclines to the right, but the heart of the fool to the left.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的心居右。愚昧人的心居左。

chapters.en: Even as fools walk along the road, they lack sense and show everyone how stupid they are.
chapters.zh: 并且愚昧人行路，显出无知。对众人说，他是愚昧人。

chapters.en: If a ruler’s anger rises against you, do not leave your post; calmness can lay great offenses to rest.
chapters.zh: 掌权者的心，若向你发怒，不要离开你的本位，因为柔和能免大过。

chapters.en: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, the sort of error that arises from a ruler:
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下，有一件祸患，似乎出于掌权的错误，

chapters.en: Fools are put in many high positions, while the rich occupy the low ones.
chapters.zh: 就是愚昧人立在高位。富足人坐在低位。

chapters.en: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.
chapters.zh: 我见过仆人骑马，王子像仆人在地上步行。

chapters.en: Whoever digs a pit may fall into it; whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
chapters.zh: 挖陷坑的，自己必掉在其中。拆墙垣的，必为蛇所咬。

chapters.en: Whoever quarries stones may be injured by them; whoever splits logs may be endangered by them.
chapters.zh: 凿开（或作挪移）石头的，必受损伤。劈开木头的，必遭危险。

chapters.en: If the ax is dull and its edge unsharpened, more strength is needed, but skill will bring success.
chapters.zh: 铁器钝了，若不将刃磨快，就必多费气力。但得智慧指教，便有益处。

chapters.en: If a snake bites before it is charmed, the charmer receives no fee.
chapters.zh: 未行法术以先，蛇若咬人，后行法术也是无益。

chapters.en: Words from the mouth of the wise are gracious, but fools are consumed by their own lips.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的口，说出恩言。愚昧人的嘴，吞灭自己。

chapters.en: At the beginning their words are folly; at the end they are wicked madness—
chapters.zh: 他口中的言语，起头是愚昧。他话的末尾，是奸恶的狂妄。

chapters.en: and fools multiply words. No one knows what is coming— who can tell someone else what will happen after them?
chapters.zh: 愚昧人多有言语，人却不知将来有什么事。他身后的事，谁能告诉他呢？

chapters.en: The toil of fools wearies them; they do not know the way to town.
chapters.zh: 凡愚昧人，他的劳碌使自己困乏。因为连进城的路他也不知道。

chapters.en: Woe to the land whose king was a servant and whose princes feast in the morning.
chapters.zh: 邦国阿，你的王若是孩童，你的群臣早晨宴乐，你就有祸了。

chapters.en: Blessed is the land whose king is of noble birth and whose princes eat at a proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.
chapters.zh: 邦国阿，你的王若是贵胄之子，你的群臣按时吃喝，为要补力，不为酒醉，你就有福了。

chapters.en: Through laziness, the rafters sag; because of idle hands, the house leaks.
chapters.zh: 因人懒惰，房顶塌下。因人手懒，房屋滴漏。

chapters.en: A feast is made for laughter, wine makes life merry, and money is the answer for everything.
chapters.zh: 设摆筵席，是为喜笑。酒能使人快活，钱能叫万事应心。

chapters.en: Do not revile the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich in your bedroom, because a bird in the sky may carry your words, and a bird on the wing may report what you say.
chapters.zh: 你不可咒诅君王，也不可心怀此念。在你卧房也不可咒诅富户。因为空中的鸟，必传扬这声音。有翅膀的，也必述说这事。

chapters.en: Ship your grain across the sea; after many days you may receive a return.
chapters.zh: 当将你的粮食撒在水面，因为日久必能得着。

chapters.en: Invest in seven ventures, yes, in eight; you do not know what disaster may come upon the land.
chapters.zh: 你要分给七人，或分给八人，因为你不知道将来有什么灾祸临到地上。

chapters.en: If clouds are full of water, they pour rain on the earth. Whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
chapters.zh: 云若满了雨，就必倾倒在地上。树若向南倒，或向北倒，树倒在何处，就存在何处。

chapters.en: Whoever watches the wind will not plant; whoever looks at the clouds will not reap.
chapters.zh: 看风的必不撒种。望云的必不收割。

chapters.en: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the body is formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
chapters.zh: 风从何道来，骨头在怀孕妇人的胎中如何长成，你尚且不得知道，这样，行万事之神的作为，你更不得知道。

chapters.en: Sow your seed in the morning, and at evening let your hands not be idle, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or whether both will do equally well.
chapters.zh: 早晨要撒你的种，晚上也不要歇你的手，因为你不知道哪一样发旺，或是早撒的，或是晚撒的，或是两样都好。

chapters.en: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
chapters.zh: 光本是佳美的，眼见日光也是可悦的。

chapters.en: However many years anyone may live, let them enjoy them all. But let them remember the days of darkness, for there will be many. Everything to come is meaningless.
chapters.zh: 人活多年，就当快乐多年。然而也当想到黑暗的日子，因为这日子必多，所要来的都是虚空。

chapters.en: You who are young, be happy while you are young, and let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth. Follow the ways of your heart and whatever your eyes see, but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
chapters.zh: 少年人哪，你在幼年时当快乐。在幼年的日子，使你的心欢畅，行你心所愿行的，看你眼所爱看的，却要知道，为这一切的事，神必审问你。

chapters.en: So then, banish anxiety from your heart and cast off the troubles of your body, for youth and vigor are meaningless.
chapters.zh: 所以你当从心中除掉愁烦。从肉体克去邪恶。因为一生的开端，和幼年之时，都是虚空的。

chapters.en: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years approach when you will say, “I find no pleasure in them”—
chapters.zh: 你趁着年幼，衰败的日子尚未来到，就是你所说，我毫无喜乐的那些年日未曾临近之先，当记念造你的主。

chapters.en: before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds return after the rain;
chapters.zh: 不要等到日头，光明，月亮，星宿，变为黑暗，雨后云彩反回，

chapters.en: when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men stoop, when the grinders cease because they are few, and those looking through the windows grow dim;
chapters.zh: 看守房屋的发颤，有力的屈身，推磨的稀少就止息，从窗户往外看的都昏暗，

chapters.en: when the doors to the street are closed and the sound of grinding fades; when people rise up at the sound of birds, but all their songs grow faint;
chapters.zh: 街门关闭，推磨的响声微小，雀鸟一叫，人就起来，歌唱的女子，也都衰微，

chapters.en: when people are afraid of heights and of dangers in the streets; when the almond tree blossoms and the grasshopper drags itself along and desire no longer is stirred. Then people go to their eternal home and mourners go about the streets.
chapters.zh: 人怕高处，路上有惊慌，杏树开花，蚱蜢成为重担，人所愿的也都废掉，因为人归他永远的家，吊丧的在街上往来，

chapters.en: Remember him—before the silver cord is severed, and the golden bowl is broken; before the pitcher is shattered at the spring, and the wheel broken at the well,
chapters.zh: 银链折断，金罐破裂，瓶子在泉旁损坏，水轮在井口破烂，

chapters.en: and the dust returns to the ground it came from, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
chapters.zh: 尘土仍归于地，灵仍归于赐灵的神。

chapters.en: “Meaningless! Meaningless!” says the Teacher.“Everything is meaningless!”
chapters.zh: 传道者说，虚空的虚空，凡事都是虚空。

chapters.en: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also imparted knowledge to the people. He pondered and searched out and set in order many proverbs.
chapters.zh: 再者，传道者因有智慧，仍将知识教训众人。又默想，又考查，又陈说许多箴言。

chapters.en: The Teacher searched to find just the right words, and what he wrote was upright and true.
chapters.zh: 传道者专心寻求可喜悦的言语，是凭正直写的诚实话。

chapters.en: The words of the wise are like goads, their collected sayings like firmly embedded nails—given by one shepherd.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的言语，好像刺棍。会中之师的言语，又像钉稳的钉子。都是一个牧者所赐的。

chapters.en: Be warned, my son, of anything in addition to them. Of making many books there is no end, and much study wearies the body.
chapters.zh: 我儿，还有一层，你当受劝戒。着书多，没有穷尽。读书多，身体疲倦。

chapters.en: Now all has been heard; here is the conclusion of the matter: Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the duty of all mankind.
chapters.zh: 这些事都已听见了。总意就是敬畏神，谨守他的诫命，这是人所当尽的本分。（或作这是众人的本分）

chapters.en: For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing, whether it is good or evil.
chapters.zh: 因为人所作的事，连一切隐藏的事，无论是善是恶，神都必审问。

chapters.en: Solomon’s Song of Songs.
chapters.zh: 所罗门的歌，是歌中的雅歌。

chapters.en: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth— for your love is more delightful than wine.
chapters.zh: 愿他用口与我亲嘴。因你的爱情比酒更美。

chapters.en: Pleasing is the fragrance of your perfumes; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the young women love you!
chapters.zh: 你的膏油馨香。你的名如同倒出来的香膏，所以众童女都爱你。

chapters.en: Take me away with you—let us hurry! Let the king bring me into his chambers. We rejoice and delight in you ; we will praise your love more than wine. How right they are to adore you!
chapters.zh: 愿你吸引我，我们就快跑跟随你。王带我进了内室，我们必因你欢喜快乐。我们要称赞你的爱情，胜似称赞美酒。他们爱你是理所当然的。

chapters.en: Dark am I, yet lovely, daughters of Jerusalem, dark like the tents of Kedar, like the tent curtains of Solomon.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子阿，我虽然黑，却是秀美，如同基达的帐棚，好像所罗门的幔子。

chapters.en: Do not stare at me because I am dark, because I am darkened by the sun. My mother’s sons were angry with me and made me take care of the vineyards; my own vineyard I had to neglect.
chapters.zh: 不要因日头把我晒黑了，就轻看我。我同母的弟兄向我发怒，他们使我看守葡萄园，我自己的葡萄园却没有看守。

chapters.en: Tell me, you whom I love, where you graze your flock and where you rest your sheep at midday. Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your friends?
chapters.zh: 我心所爱的阿，求你告诉我，你在何处牧羊，晌午在何处使羊歇卧。我何必在你同伴的羊群旁边，好像蒙着脸的人呢？

chapters.en: If you do not know, most beautiful of women, follow the tracks of the sheep and graze your young goats by the tents of the shepherds.
chapters.zh: 你这女子中极美丽的，你若不知道，只管跟随羊群的脚踪去，把你的山羊羔牧放在牧人帐棚的旁边。

chapters.en: I liken you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariot horses.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶，我将你比法老车上套的骏马。

chapters.en: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.
chapters.zh: 你的两腮因发辫而秀美，你的颈项因珠串而华丽。

chapters.en: We will make you earrings of gold, studded with silver.
chapters.zh: 我们要为你编上金辫，镶上银钉。

chapters.en: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
chapters.zh: 王正坐席的时候，我的哪哒香膏发出香味。

chapters.en: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.
chapters.zh: 我以我的良人为一袋没药，常在我怀中。

chapters.en: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.
chapters.zh: 我以我的良人为一棵凤仙花，在隐基底葡萄园中。

chapters.en: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how beautiful! Your eyes are doves.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶，你甚美丽，你甚美丽，你的眼好像鸽子眼。

chapters.en: How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how charming! And our bed is verdant.
chapters.zh: 我的良人哪，你甚美丽可爱，我们以青草为床榻，

chapters.en: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are firs.
chapters.zh: 以香柏树为房屋的栋梁，以松树为椽子。

chapters.en: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
chapters.zh: 我是沙仑的玫瑰花（或作水仙花），是谷中的百合花。

chapters.en: Like a lily among thorns is my darling among the young women.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶在女子中，好像百合花在荆棘内。

chapters.en: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
chapters.zh: 我的良人在男子中，如同苹果树在树林中。我欢欢喜喜坐在他的荫下，尝他果子的滋味，觉得甘甜。

chapters.en: Let him lead me to the banquet hall, and let his banner over me be love.
chapters.zh: 他带我入筵宴所，以爱为旗在我以上。

chapters.en: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.
chapters.zh: 求你们给我葡萄干增补我力，给我苹果畅快我心，因我思爱成病。

chapters.en: His left arm is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
chapters.zh: 他的左手在我头下，他的右手将我抱住。

chapters.en: Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you by the gazelles and by the does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子阿，我指着羚羊或田野的母鹿，嘱咐你们，不要惊动，不要叫醒我所亲爱的，等他自己情愿（不要叫醒云云或作不要激动爱情等它自发）。

chapters.en: Listen! My beloved! Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.
chapters.zh: 听阿，是我良人的声音。看哪，他蹿山越岭而来。

chapters.en: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look! There he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
chapters.zh: 我的良人好像羚羊，或像小鹿。他站在我们墙壁后，从窗户往里观看，从窗棂往里窥探。

chapters.en: My beloved spoke and said to me, “Arise, my darling, my beautiful one, come with me.
chapters.zh: 我良人对我说，我的佳偶，我的美人，起来，与我同去。

chapters.en: See! The winter is past; the rains are over and gone.
chapters.zh: 因为冬天已往。雨水止住过去了。

chapters.en: Flowers appear on the earth; the season of singing has come, the cooing of doves is heard in our land.
chapters.zh: 地上百花开放。百鸟鸣叫的时候（或作修理葡萄树的时候）已经来到，斑鸠的声音在我们境内也听见了。

chapters.en: The fig tree forms its early fruit; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come, my darling; my beautiful one, come with me.”
chapters.zh: 无花果树的果子渐渐成熟，葡萄树开花放香。我的佳偶，我的美人，起来，与我同去。

chapters.en: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places on the mountainside, show me your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
chapters.zh: 我的鸽子阿，你在磐石穴中，在陡岩的隐密处。求你容我得见你的面貌，得听你的声音。因为你的声音柔和，你的面貌秀美。

chapters.en: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, our vineyards that are in bloom.
chapters.zh: 要给我们擒拿狐狸，就是毁坏葡萄园的小狐狸。因为我们的葡萄正在开花。

chapters.en: My beloved is mine and I am his; he browses among the lilies.
chapters.zh: 良人属我，我也属他。他在百合花中牧放群羊

chapters.en: Until the day breaks and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or like a young stag on the rugged hills.
chapters.zh: 我的良人哪，求你等到天起凉风，日影飞去的时候，你要转回，好像羚羊，或像小鹿在比特山上。

chapters.en: All night long on my bed I looked for the one my heart loves; I looked for him but did not find him.
chapters.zh: 我夜间躺卧在床上，寻找我心所爱的。我寻找他，却寻不见。

chapters.en: I will get up now and go about the city, through its streets and squares; I will search for the one my heart loves. So I looked for him but did not find him.
chapters.zh: 我说，我要起来，游行城中，在街市上，在宽阔处，寻找我心所爱的。我寻找他，却寻不见。

chapters.en: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. “Have you seen the one my heart loves?”
chapters.zh: 城中巡逻看守的人遇见我。我问他们，你们看见我心所爱的没有。

chapters.en: Scarcely had I passed them when I found the one my heart loves. I held him and would not let him go till I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the room of the one who conceived me.
chapters.zh: 我刚离开他们，就遇见我心所爱的。我拉住他，不容他走，领他入我母家，到怀我者的内室。

chapters.en: Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you by the gazelles and by the does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子阿，我指着羚羊，或田野的母鹿嘱咐你们，不要惊动，不要叫醒我所亲爱的，等他自己情愿（不要叫醒云云或作不要激动爱情等它自发）。

chapters.en: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and incense made from all the spices of the merchant?
chapters.zh: 那从旷野上来，形状如烟柱，以没药和乳香并商人各样香粉薰的是谁呢？

chapters.en: Look! It is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty warriors, the noblest of Israel,
chapters.zh: 看哪，是所罗门的轿。四围有六十个勇士，都是以色列中的勇士。

chapters.en: all of them wearing the sword, all experienced in battle, each with his sword at his side, prepared for the terrors of the night.
chapters.zh: 手都持刀，善于争战，腰间佩刀，防备夜间有惊慌。

chapters.en: King Solomon made for himself the carriage; he made it of wood from Lebanon.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王用利巴嫩木，为自己制造一乘华轿。

chapters.en: Its posts he made of silver, its base of gold. Its seat was upholstered with purple, its interior inlaid with love. Daughters of Jerusalem,
chapters.zh: 轿柱是用银做的，轿底是用金做的。坐垫是紫色的，其中所铺的乃耶路撒冷众女子的爱情。

chapters.en: come out, and look, you daughters of Zion. Look on King Solomon wearing a crown, the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, the day his heart rejoiced.
chapters.zh: 锡安的众女子阿，你们出去观看所罗门王，头戴冠冕，就是在他婚筵的日子，心中喜乐的时候，他母亲给他戴上的。

chapters.en: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how beautiful! Your eyes behind your veil are doves. Your hair is like a flock of goats descending from the hills of Gilead.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶，你甚美丽，你甚美丽。你的眼在帕子内好像鸽子眼。你的头发如同山羊群卧在基列山旁。

chapters.en: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep just shorn, coming up from the washing. Each has its twin; not one of them is alone.
chapters.zh: 你的牙齿如新剪毛的一群母羊，洗净上来，个个都有双生，没有一只丧掉子的。

chapters.en: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon; your mouth is lovely. Your temples behind your veil are like the halves of a pomegranate.
chapters.zh: 你的唇好像一条朱红线，你的嘴也秀美。你的两太阳在帕子内，如同一块石榴。

chapters.en: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with courses of stone ; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.
chapters.zh: 你的颈项好像大卫建造收藏军器的高台，其上悬挂一千盾牌，都是勇士的藤牌。

chapters.en: Your breasts are like two fawns, like twin fawns of a gazelle that browse among the lilies.
chapters.zh: 你的两乳好像百合花中吃草的一对小鹿，就是母鹿双生的。

chapters.en: Until the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of incense.
chapters.zh: 我要往没药山和乳香冈去，直等到天起凉风，日影飞去的时候回来。

chapters.en: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; there is no flaw in you.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶，你全然美丽，毫无瑕疵。

chapters.en: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon. Descend from the crest of Amana, from the top of Senir, the summit of Hermon, from the lions’ dens and the mountain haunts of leopards.
chapters.zh: 我的新妇，求你与我一同离开利巴嫩，与我一同离开利巴嫩。从亚玛拿顶，从示尼珥与黑门顶，从有狮子的洞，从有豹子的山往下观看。

chapters.en: You have stolen my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
chapters.zh: 我妹子，我新妇，你夺了我的心。你用眼一看，用你项上的一条金链，夺了我的心。

chapters.en: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much more pleasing is your love than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume more than any spice!
chapters.zh: 我妹子，我新妇，你的爱情何其美。你的爱情比酒更美。你膏油的香气胜过一切香品。

chapters.en: Your lips drop sweetness as the honeycomb, my bride; milk and honey are under your tongue. The fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
chapters.zh: 我新妇，你的嘴唇滴蜜。好像蜂房滴蜜。你的舌下有蜜，有奶。你衣服的香气如利巴嫩的香气。

chapters.en: You are a garden locked up, my sister, my bride; you are a spring enclosed, a sealed fountain.
chapters.zh: 我妹子，我新妇，乃是关锁的园，禁闭的井，封闭的泉源。

chapters.en: Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates with choice fruits, with henna and nard,
chapters.zh: 你园内所种的结了石榴，有佳美的果子，并凤仙花与哪哒树。

chapters.en: nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree, with myrrh and aloes and all the finest spices.
chapters.zh: 有哪哒和番红花，菖蒲和桂树，并各样乳香木，没药，沉香，与一切上等的果品。

chapters.en: You are a garden fountain, a well of flowing water streaming down from Lebanon.
chapters.zh: 你是园中的泉，活水的井，从利巴嫩流下来的溪水。

chapters.en: Awake, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow on my garden, that its fragrance may spread everywhere. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choice fruits.
chapters.zh: 北风阿，兴起。南风阿，吹来。吹在我的园内，使其中的香气发出来。愿我的良人进入自己园里，吃他佳美的果子。

chapters.en: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb and my honey; I have drunk my wine and my milk. Eat, friends, and drink; drink your fill of love.
chapters.zh: 我妹子，我新妇，我进了我的园中，采了我的没药和香料，吃了我的蜜房和蜂蜜。喝了我的酒和奶。我的朋友们，请吃，我所亲爱的，请喝，且多多地喝。

chapters.en: I slept but my heart was awake. Listen! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”
chapters.zh: 我身睡卧，我心却醒。这是我良人的声音。他敲门，说，我的妹子，我的佳偶，我的鸽子，我的完全人，求你给我开门，因我的头满了露水，我的头发被夜露滴湿。

chapters.en: I have taken off my robe— must I put it on again? I have washed my feet— must I soil them again?
chapters.zh: 我回答说，我脱了衣裳，怎能再穿上呢？我洗了脚，怎能再玷污呢？

chapters.en: My beloved thrust his hand through the latch-opening; my heart began to pound for him.
chapters.zh: 我的良人从门孔里伸进手来，我便因他动了心。

chapters.en: I arose to open for my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, on the handles of the bolt.
chapters.zh: 我起来，要给我良人开门。我的两手滴下没药，我的指头有没药汁滴在门闩上。

chapters.en: I opened for my beloved, but my beloved had left; he was gone. My heart sank at his departure.I looked for him but did not find him. I called him but he did not answer.
chapters.zh: 我给我的良人开了门。我的良人却已转身走了。他说话的时候，我神不守舍。我寻找他，竟寻不见。我呼叫他，他却不回答。

chapters.en: The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. They beat me, they bruised me; they took away my cloak, those watchmen of the walls!
chapters.zh: 城中巡逻看守的人遇见我，打了我，伤了我。看守城墙的人夺去我的披肩。

chapters.en: Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you— if you find my beloved, what will you tell him? Tell him I am faint with love.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子阿，我嘱咐你们。若遇见我的良人，要告诉他，我因思爱成病。

chapters.en: How is your beloved better than others, most beautiful of women? How is your beloved better than others, that you so charge us?
chapters.zh: 你这女子中极美丽的，你的良人，比别人的良人有何强处。你的良人，比别人的良人有何强处，你就这样嘱咐我们。

chapters.en: My beloved is radiant and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
chapters.zh: 我的良人，白而且红，超乎万人之上。

chapters.en: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.
chapters.zh: 他的头像至精的金子。他的头发厚密累垂，黑如乌鸦。

chapters.en: His eyes are like doves by the water streams, washed in milk, mounted like jewels.
chapters.zh: 他的眼如溪水旁的鸽子眼，用奶洗净，安得合式。

chapters.en: His cheeks are like beds of spice yielding perfume. His lips are like lilies dripping with myrrh.
chapters.zh: 他的两腮如香花畦，如香草台。他的嘴唇像百合花，且滴下没药汁。

chapters.en: His arms are rods of gold set with topaz. His body is like polished ivory decorated with lapis lazuli.
chapters.zh: 他的两手好像金管，镶嵌水苍玉。他的身体如同雕刻的象牙，周围镶嵌蓝宝石。

chapters.en: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as its cedars.
chapters.zh: 他的腿好像白玉石柱，安在精金座上。他的形状如利巴嫩，且佳美如香柏树。

chapters.en: His mouth is sweetness itself; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 他的口极其甘甜。他全然可爱。耶路撒冷的众女子阿，这是我的良人，这是我的朋友。

chapters.en: Where has your beloved gone, most beautiful of women? Which way did your beloved turn, that we may look for him with you?
chapters.zh: 你这女子中极美丽的，你的良人往何处去了。你的良人转向何处去了，我们好与你同去寻找他。

chapters.en: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to browse in the gardens and to gather lilies.
chapters.zh: 我的良人下入自己园中，到香花畦，在园内牧放群羊，采百合花。

chapters.en: I am my beloved’s and my beloved is mine; he browses among the lilies.
chapters.zh: 我属我的良人，我的良人也属我。他在百合花中牧放群羊。

chapters.en: You are as beautiful as Tirzah, my darling, as lovely as Jerusalem, as majestic as troops with banners.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶阿，你美丽如得撒，秀美如耶路撒冷，威武如展开旌旗的军队。

chapters.en: Turn your eyes from me; they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats descending from Gilead.
chapters.zh: 求你掉转眼目不看我，因你的眼目使我惊乱。你的头发如同山羊群卧在基列山旁。

chapters.en: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing. Each has its twin, not one of them is missing.
chapters.zh: 你的牙齿如一群母羊，洗净上来。个个都有双生，没有一只丧掉子的。

chapters.en: Your temples behind your veil are like the halves of a pomegranate.
chapters.zh: 你的两太阳在帕子内，如同一块石榴。

chapters.en: Sixty queens there may be, and eighty concubines, and virgins beyond number;
chapters.zh: 有六十王后八十妃嫔，并有无数的童女。

chapters.en: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the only daughter of her mother, the favorite of the one who bore her. The young women saw her and called her blessed; the queens and concubines praised her.
chapters.zh: 我的鸽子，我的完全人，只有这一个是她母亲独生的。是生养她者所宝爱的。众女子见了，就称她有福。王后妃嫔见了，也赞美她。

chapters.en: Who is this that appears like the dawn, fair as the moon, bright as the sun, majestic as the stars in procession?
chapters.zh: 那向外观看，如晨光发现，美丽如月亮，皎洁如日头，威武如展开旌旗军队的是谁呢？

chapters.en: I went down to the grove of nut trees to look at the new growth in the valley, to see if the vines had budded or the pomegranates were in bloom.
chapters.zh: 我下入核桃园，要看谷中青绿的植物，要看葡萄发芽没有，石榴开花没有。

chapters.en: Before I realized it, my desire set me among the royal chariots of my people.
chapters.zh: 不知不觉，我的心将我安置在我尊长的车中。

chapters.en: Come back, come back, O Shulammite; come back, come back, that we may gaze on you! Why would you gaze on the Shulammite as on the dance of Mahanaim?
chapters.zh: 回来，回来，书拉密女。你回来，你回来，使我们得观看你。你们为何要观看书拉密女，像观看玛哈念跳舞的呢？

chapters.en: How beautiful your sandaled feet, O prince’s daughter! Your graceful legs are like jewels, the work of an artist’s hands.
chapters.zh: 王女阿，你的脚在鞋中何其美好。你的大腿圆润，好像美玉，是巧匠的手做成的。

chapters.en: Your navel is a rounded goblet that never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by lilies.
chapters.zh: 你的肚脐如圆杯，不缺调和的酒。你的腰如一堆麦子，周围有百合花。

chapters.en: Your breasts are like two fawns, like twin fawns of a gazelle.
chapters.zh: 你的两乳好像一对小鹿，就是母鹿双生的。

chapters.en: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath Rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon looking toward Damascus.
chapters.zh: 你的颈项如象牙台。你的眼目像希实本，巴特拉并门旁的水池。你的鼻子仿佛朝大马色的利巴嫩塔。

chapters.en: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel. Your hair is like royal tapestry; the king is held captive by its tresses.
chapters.zh: 你的头在你身上好像迦密山。你头上的发是紫黑色。王的心因这下垂的发绺系住了。

chapters.en: How beautiful you are and how pleasing, my love, with your delights!
chapters.zh: 我所爱的，你何其美好。何其可悦，使人欢畅喜乐。

chapters.en: Your stature is like that of the palm, and your breasts like clusters of fruit.
chapters.zh: 你的身量好像棕树。你的两乳如同其上的果子，累累下垂。

chapters.en: I said, “I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of grapes on the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,
chapters.zh: 我说，我要上这棕树，抓住枝子。愿你的两乳好像葡萄累累下垂，你鼻子的气味香如苹果。

chapters.en: and your mouth like the best wine. May the wine go straight to my beloved, flowing gently over lips and teeth.
chapters.zh: 你的口如上好的酒，女子说，为我的良人下咽舒畅，流入睡觉人的嘴中。

chapters.en: I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.
chapters.zh: 我属我的良人，他也恋慕我。

chapters.en: Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside, let us spend the night in the villages.
chapters.zh: 我的良人，来吧，你我可以往田间去。你我可以在村庄住宿。

chapters.en: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vines have budded, if their blossoms have opened, and if the pomegranates are in bloom— there I will give you my love.
chapters.zh: 我们早晨起来往葡萄园去，看看葡萄发芽开花没有，石榴放蕊没有。我在那里要将我的爱情给你。

chapters.en: The mandrakes send out their fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, both new and old, that I have stored up for you, my beloved.
chapters.zh: 风茄放香，在我们的门内有各样新陈佳美的果子。我的良人，这都是我为你存留的。

chapters.en: If only you were to me like a brother, who was nursed at my mother’s breasts! Then, if I found you outside, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.
chapters.zh: 巴不得你像我的兄弟，像吃我母亲奶的兄弟。我在外头遇见你就与你亲嘴，谁也不轻看我。

chapters.en: I would lead you and bring you to my mother’s house— she who has taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranates.
chapters.zh: 我必引导你，领你进我母亲的家。我可以领受教训，也就使你喝石榴汁酿的香酒。

chapters.en: His left arm is under my head and his right arm embraces me.
chapters.zh: 他的左手必在我头下，他的右手必将我抱住。

chapters.en: Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you: Do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子阿，我嘱咐你们，不要惊动，不要叫醒我所亲爱的，等他自己情愿（不要叫醒云云或作不要激动爱情等它自发）。

chapters.en: Who is this coming up from the wilderness leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I roused you; there your mother conceived you, there she who was in labor gave you birth.
chapters.zh: 那靠着良人从旷野上来的，是谁呢？我在苹果树下叫醒你。你母亲在那里为你劬劳，生养你的在那里为你劬劳。

chapters.en: Place me like a seal over your heart, like a seal on your arm; for love is as strong as death, its jealousy unyielding as the grave. It burns like blazing fire, like a mighty flame.
chapters.zh: 求你将我放在你心上如印记，带在你臂上如戳记。因为爱情如死之坚强。嫉恨如阴间之残忍。所发的电光，是火焰的电光，是耶和华的烈焰。

chapters.en: Many waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If one were to give all the wealth of one’s house for love, it would be utterly scorned.
chapters.zh: 爱情众水不能息灭，大水也不能淹没。若有人拿家中所有的财宝要换爱情，就全被藐视。

chapters.en: We have a little sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
chapters.zh: 我们有一小妹，她的两乳尚未长成。人来提亲的日子，我们当为她怎样办理。

chapters.en: If she is a wall, we will build towers of silver on her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar.
chapters.zh: 她若是墙，我们要在其上建造银塔。她若是门，我们要用香柏木板围护她。

chapters.en: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. Thus I have become in his eyes like one bringing contentment.
chapters.zh: 我是墙，我两乳像其上的楼。那时，我在他眼中像得平安的人。

chapters.en: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal Hamon; he let out his vineyard to tenants. Each was to bring for its fruit a thousand shekels of silver.
chapters.zh: 所罗门在巴力哈们有一葡萄园。他将这葡萄园交给看守的人，为其中的果子，必交一千舍客勒银子。

chapters.en: But my own vineyard is mine to give; the thousand shekels are for you, Solomon, and two hundred are for those who tend its fruit.
chapters.zh: 我自己的葡萄园在我面前。所罗门哪，一千舍客勒归你，二百舍客勒归看守果子的人。

chapters.en: You who dwell in the gardens with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice!
chapters.zh: 你这住在园中的，同伴都要听你的声音，求你使我也得听见。

chapters.en: Come away, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or like a young stag on the spice-laden mountains.
chapters.zh: 我的良人哪，求你快来。如羚羊或小鹿在香草山上。

chapters.en: The vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
chapters.zh: 当乌西雅，约坦，亚哈斯，希西家，作犹大王的时候，亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚得默示，论到犹大和耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: Hear me, you heavens! Listen, earth! For the LORD has spoken: “I reared children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against me.
chapters.zh: 天哪，要听，地阿，侧耳而听。因为耶和华说，我养育儿女，将他们养大，他们竟悖逆我。

chapters.en: The ox knows its master, the donkey its owner’s manger, but Israel does not know, my people do not understand.”
chapters.zh: 牛认识主人，驴认识主人的槽。以色列却不认识，我的民却不留意。

chapters.en: Woe to the sinful nation, a people whose guilt is great, a brood of evildoers, children given to corruption! They have forsaken the LORD; they have spurned the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on him.
chapters.zh: 嗐，犯罪的国民，担着罪孽的百姓，行恶的种类，败坏的儿女。他们离弃耶和华，藐视以色列的圣者，与他生疏，往后退步。

chapters.en: Why should you be beaten anymore? Why do you persist in rebellion? Your whole head is injured, your whole heart afflicted.
chapters.zh: 你们为什么屡次悖逆，还要受责打吗？你们已经满头疼痛，全心发昏。

chapters.en: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head there is no soundness— only wounds and welts and open sores, not cleansed or bandaged or soothed with olive oil.
chapters.zh: 从脚掌到头顶，没有一处完全的。尽是伤口，青肿，与新打的伤痕。都没有收口，没有缠裹，也没有用膏滋润。

chapters.en: Your country is desolate, your cities burned with fire; your fields are being stripped by foreigners right before you, laid waste as when overthrown by strangers.
chapters.zh: 你们的地土已经荒凉。你们的城邑被火焚毁。你们的田地，在你们眼前为外邦人所侵吞，既被外邦人倾覆，就成为荒凉。

chapters.en: Daughter Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege.
chapters.zh: 仅存锡安城（城原文作女子），好像葡萄园的草棚，瓜田的茅屋，被围困的城邑。

chapters.en: Unless the LORD Almighty had left us some survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have been like Gomorrah.
chapters.zh: 若不是万军之耶和华给我们稍留余种，我们早已像所多玛，蛾摩拉的样子了。

chapters.en: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
chapters.zh: 你们这所多玛的官长阿，要听耶和华的话。你们这蛾摩拉的百姓阿，要侧耳听我们神的训诲。

chapters.en: “The multitude of your sacrifices— what are they to me?” says the LORD. “I have more than enough of burnt offerings, of rams and the fat of fattened animals; I have no pleasure in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，你们所献的许多祭物，与我何益呢？公绵羊的燔祭，和肥畜的脂油，我已经够了。公牛的血，羊羔的血，公山羊的血，我都不喜悦。

chapters.en: When you come to appear before me, who has asked this of you, this trampling of my courts?
chapters.zh: 你们来朝见我，谁向你们讨这些，使你们践踏我的院宇呢？

chapters.en: Stop bringing meaningless offerings! Your incense is detestable to me. New Moons, Sabbaths and convocations— I cannot bear your worthless assemblies.
chapters.zh: 你们不要再献虚浮的供物。香品是我所憎恶的。月朔，和安息日，并宣召的大会，也是我所憎恶的。作罪孽，又守严肃会，我也不能容忍。

chapters.en: Your New Moon feasts and your appointed festivals I hate with all my being. They have become a burden to me; I am weary of bearing them.
chapters.zh: 你们的月朔，和节期，我心里恨恶，我都以为麻烦。我担当，便不耐烦。

chapters.en: When you spread out your hands in prayer, I hide my eyes from you; even when you offer many prayers, I am not listening. Your hands are full of blood!
chapters.zh: 你们举手祷告，我必遮眼不看。就是你们多多地祈祷，我也不听。你们的手都满了杀人的血。

chapters.en: Wash and make yourselves clean. Take your evil deeds out of my sight; stop doing wrong.
chapters.zh: 你们要洗濯，自洁。从我眼前除掉你们的恶行。要止住作恶，

chapters.en: Learn to do right; seek justice. Defend the oppressed.Take up the cause of the fatherless; plead the case of the widow.
chapters.zh: 学习行善。寻求公平，解救受欺压的，给孤儿伸冤，为寡妇辨屈。

chapters.en: “Come now, let us settle the matter,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red as crimson, they shall be like wool.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，你们来，我们彼此辩论。你们的罪虽像朱红，必变成雪白。虽红如丹颜，必白如羊毛。

chapters.en: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good things of the land;
chapters.zh: 你们若甘心听从，必吃地上的美物。

chapters.en: but if you resist and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
chapters.zh: 若不听从，反倒悖逆，必被刀剑吞灭。这是耶和华亲口说的。

chapters.en: See how the faithful city has become a prostitute! She once was full of justice; righteousness used to dwell in her— but now murderers!
chapters.zh: 可叹忠信的城，变为妓女。从前充满了公平，公义居在其中，现今却有凶手居住。

chapters.en: Your silver has become dross, your choice wine is diluted with water.
chapters.zh: 你的银子，变为渣滓，你的酒，用水搀对。

chapters.en: Your rulers are rebels, partners with thieves; they all love bribes and chase after gifts. They do not defend the cause of the fatherless; the widow’s case does not come before them.
chapters.zh: 你的官长居心悖逆，与盗贼作伴。各都喜爱贿赂，追求赃私。他们不为孤儿伸冤，寡妇的案件，也不得呈到他们面前。

chapters.en: Therefore the Lord, the LORD Almighty, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah! I will vent my wrath on my foes and avenge myself on my enemies.
chapters.zh: 因此主万军之耶和华以色列的大能者说，哎，我要向我的对头雪恨，向我的敌人报仇。

chapters.en: I will turn my hand against you;I will thoroughly purge away your dross and remove all your impurities.
chapters.zh: 我必反手加在你身上，炼尽你的渣滓，除净你的杂质。

chapters.en: I will restore your leaders as in days of old, your rulers as at the beginning. Afterward you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.”
chapters.zh: 我也必复还你的审判官，像起初一样，复还你的谋士，像起先一般。然后你必称为公义之城，忠信之邑。

chapters.en: Zion will be delivered with justice, her penitent ones with righteousness.
chapters.zh: 锡安必因公平得蒙救赎，其中归正的人，必因公义得蒙救赎。

chapters.en: But rebels and sinners will both be broken, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
chapters.zh: 但悖逆的，和犯罪的，必一同败亡，离弃耶和华的，必致消灭。

chapters.en: “You will be ashamed because of the sacred oaks in which you have delighted; you will be disgraced because of the gardens that you have chosen.
chapters.zh: 那等人必因你们所喜爱的橡树抱愧，你们必因所选择的园子蒙羞。

chapters.en: You will be like an oak with fading leaves, like a garden without water.
chapters.zh: 因为你们必如叶子枯干的橡树，好像无水浇灌的园子。

chapters.en: The mighty man will become tinder and his work a spark; both will burn together, with no one to quench the fire.”
chapters.zh: 有权势的必如麻瓤，他的工作，好像火星，都要一同焚毁，无人扑灭。

chapters.en: This is what Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:
chapters.zh: 亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚得默示，论到犹大和耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: In the last days the mountain of the LORD’s temple will be established as the highest of the mountains; it will be exalted above the hills, and all nations will stream to it.
chapters.zh: 末后的日子，耶和华殿的山必坚立，超乎诸山，高举过于万岭。万民都要流归这山。

chapters.en: Many peoples will come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the temple of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways, so that we may walk in his paths.” The law will go out from Zion, the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 必有许多国的民前往，说，来吧，我们登耶和华的山。奔雅各神的殿。主必将他的道教训我们，我们也要行他的路。因为训诲必出于锡安，耶和华的言语，必出于耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: He will judge between the nations and will settle disputes for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not take up sword against nation, nor will they train for war anymore.
chapters.zh: 他必在列国中施行审判，为许多国民断定是非。他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。这国不举刀攻击那国，他们也不再学习战事。

chapters.en: Come, descendants of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 雅各家阿，来吧，我们在耶和华的光明中行走。

chapters.en: You, LORD, have abandoned your people, the descendants of Jacob. They are full of superstitions from the East; they practice divination like the Philistines and embrace pagan customs.
chapters.zh: 耶和华，你离弃了你百姓雅各家，是因他们充满了东方的风俗，作观兆的，像非利士人一样，并与外邦人击掌。

chapters.en: Their land is full of silver and gold; there is no end to their treasures. Their land is full of horses; there is no end to their chariots.
chapters.zh: 他们的国满了金银，财宝也无穷，他们的地满了马匹，车辆也无数。

chapters.en: Their land is full of idols; they bow down to the work of their hands, to what their fingers have made.
chapters.zh: 他们的地满了偶像。他们跪拜自己手所造的，就是自己指头所作的。

chapters.en: So people will be brought low and everyone humbled— do not forgive them.
chapters.zh: 卑贱人屈膝，尊贵人下跪。所以不可饶恕他们。

chapters.en: Go into the rocks, hide in the ground from the fearful presence of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty!
chapters.zh: 你当进入岩穴，藏在土中，躲避耶和华的惊吓，和他威严的荣光。

chapters.en: The eyes of the arrogant will be humbled and human pride brought low; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
chapters.zh: 到那日，眼目高傲的必降为卑，性情狂傲的都必屈膝。惟独耶和华被尊崇。

chapters.en: The LORD Almighty has a day in store for all the proud and lofty, for all that is exalted (and they will be humbled),
chapters.zh: 必有万军耶和华降罚的一个日子，要临到骄傲狂妄的，一切自高的，都必降为卑。

chapters.en: for all the cedars of Lebanon, tall and lofty, and all the oaks of Bashan,
chapters.zh: 又临到利巴嫩高大的香柏树，和巴珊的橡树。

chapters.en: for all the towering mountains and all the high hills,
chapters.zh: 又临到一切高山的峻岭。

chapters.en: for every lofty tower and every fortified wall,
chapters.zh: 又临到高台和坚固城墙。

chapters.en: for every trading ship and every stately vessel.
chapters.zh: 又临到他施的船只，并一切可爱的美物。

chapters.en: The arrogance of man will be brought low and human pride humbled; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day,
chapters.zh: 骄傲的必屈膝，狂妄的必降卑。在那日，惟独耶和华被尊崇。

chapters.en: and the idols will totally disappear.
chapters.zh: 偶像必全然废弃

chapters.en: People will flee to caves in the rocks and to holes in the ground from the fearful presence of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth.
chapters.zh: 耶和华兴起使地大震动的时候，人就进入石洞，进入土穴，躲避耶和华的惊吓，和他威严的荣光。

chapters.en: In that day people will throw away to the moles and bats their idols of silver and idols of gold, which they made to worship.
chapters.zh: 到那日，人必将为拜而造的金偶像，银偶像，抛给田鼠和蝙蝠。

chapters.en: They will flee to caverns in the rocks and to the overhanging crags from the fearful presence of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth.
chapters.zh: 到耶和华兴起使地大震动的时候，人好进入磐石洞中，和岩石穴里，躲避耶和华的惊吓，和他威严的荣光。

chapters.en: Stop trusting in mere humans, who have but a breath in their nostrils. Why hold them in esteem?
chapters.zh: 你们休要倚靠世人，他鼻孔里不过有气息。他在一切事上可算什么呢？

chapters.en: See now, the Lord, the LORD Almighty, is about to take from Jerusalem and Judah both supply and support: all supplies of food and all supplies of water,
chapters.zh: 主万军之耶和华，从耶路撒冷和犹大，除掉众人所倚靠的，所仗赖的，就是所倚靠的粮，所仗赖的水。

chapters.en: the hero and the warrior, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
chapters.zh: 除掉勇士，和战士，审判官，和先知，占卜的，和长老。

chapters.en: the captain of fifty and the man of rank, the counselor, skilled craftsman and clever enchanter.
chapters.zh: 五十夫长，和尊贵人。谋士，和有巧艺的，以及妙行法术的。

chapters.en: “I will make mere youths their officials; children will rule over them.”
chapters.zh: 主说，我必使孩童作他们的首领，使婴孩辖管他们。

chapters.en: People will oppress each other— man against man, neighbor against neighbor. The young will rise up against the old, the nobody against the honored.
chapters.zh: 百姓要彼此欺压，各人受邻舍的欺压。少年人必侮慢老年人，卑贱人必侮慢尊贵人。

chapters.en: A man will seize one of his brothers in his father’s house, and say, “You have a cloak, you be our leader; take charge of this heap of ruins!”
chapters.zh: 人在父家拉住弟兄，说，你有衣服，可以作我们的官长，这败落的事归在你手下吧。

chapters.en: But in that day he will cry out, “I have no remedy. I have no food or clothing in my house; do not make me the leader of the people.”
chapters.zh: 那时他必扬声说，我不作医治你们的人。因我家中没有粮食，也没有衣服。你们不可立我作百姓的官长。

chapters.en: Jerusalem staggers, Judah is falling; their words and deeds are against the LORD, defying his glorious presence.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷败落，犹大倾倒。因为他们的舌头，和行为，与耶和华反对，惹了他荣光的眼目。

chapters.en: The look on their faces testifies against them; they parade their sin like Sodom; they do not hide it. Woe to them! They have brought disaster upon themselves.
chapters.zh: 他们的面色证明自己的不正。他们述说自己的罪恶，并不隐瞒，好像所多玛一样。他们有祸了。因为作恶自害。

chapters.en: Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their deeds.
chapters.zh: 你们要论义人说，他必享福乐。因为要吃自己行为所结的果子。

chapters.en: Woe to the wicked! Disaster is upon them! They will be paid back for what their hands have done.
chapters.zh: 恶人有祸了。他必遭灾难。因为要照自己手所行的受报应。

chapters.en: Youths oppress my people, women rule over them. My people, your guides lead you astray; they turn you from the path.
chapters.zh: 至于我的百姓，孩童欺压他们，妇女辖管他们。我的百姓阿，引导你的，使你走错，并毁坏你所行的道路。

chapters.en: The LORD takes his place in court; he rises to judge the people.
chapters.zh: 耶和华起来辩论，站着审判众民。

chapters.en: The LORD enters into judgment against the elders and leaders of his people: “It is you who have ruined my vineyard; the plunder from the poor is in your houses.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必审问他民中的长老，和首领，说，吃尽葡萄园果子的，就是你们。向贫穷人所夺的，都在你们家中。

chapters.en: What do you mean by crushing my people and grinding the faces of the poor?” declares the Lord, the LORD Almighty.
chapters.zh: 主万军之耶和华说，你们为何压制我的百姓，搓磨贫穷人的脸呢？

chapters.en: The LORD says, “The women of Zion are haughty, walking along with outstretched necks, flirting with their eyes, strutting along with swaying hips, with ornaments jingling on their ankles.
chapters.zh: 耶和华又说，因为锡安的女子狂傲，行走挺项，卖弄眼目，俏步徐行，脚下玎铛。

chapters.en: Therefore the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the women of Zion; the LORD will make their scalps bald.”
chapters.zh: 所以主必使锡安的女子头长秃疮，耶和华又使她们赤露下体。

chapters.en: In that day the Lord will snatch away their finery: the bangles and headbands and crescent necklaces,
chapters.zh: 到那日，主必除掉她们华美的脚钏，发网，月牙圈。

chapters.en: the earrings and bracelets and veils,
chapters.zh: 耳环，手镯，蒙脸的帕子。

chapters.en: the headdresses and anklets and sashes, the perfume bottles and charms,
chapters.zh: 华冠，足链，华带，香盒，符囊。

chapters.en: the signet rings and nose rings,
chapters.zh: 戒指，鼻环。

chapters.en: the fine robes and the capes and cloaks, the purses
chapters.zh: 吉服，外套，云肩，荷包。

chapters.en: and mirrors, and the linen garments and tiaras and shawls.
chapters.zh: 手镜，细麻衣，裹头巾，蒙身的帕子。

chapters.en: Instead of fragrance there will be a stench; instead of a sash, a rope; instead of well-dressed hair, baldness; instead of fine clothing, sackcloth; instead of beauty, branding.
chapters.zh: 必有臭烂代替馨香，绳子代替腰带，光秃代替美发，麻衣系腰代替华服，烙伤代替美容。

chapters.en: Your men will fall by the sword, your warriors in battle.
chapters.zh: 你的男丁，必倒在刀下，你的勇士，必死在阵上。

chapters.en: The gates of Zion will lament and mourn; destitute, she will sit on the ground.
chapters.zh: 锡安（原文作他）的城门必悲伤，哀号。他必荒凉坐在地上。

chapters.en: In that day seven women will take hold of one man and say, “We will eat our own food and provide our own clothes; only let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace!”
chapters.zh: 在那日，七个女人必拉住一个男人，说，我们吃自己的食物，穿自己的衣服。但求你许我们归你名下。求你除掉我们的羞耻。

chapters.en: In that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and glory of the survivors in Israel.
chapters.zh: 到那日，耶和华发生的苗，必华美尊荣，地的出产，必为以色列逃脱的人显为荣华茂盛。

chapters.en: Those who are left in Zion, who remain in Jerusalem, will be called holy, all who are recorded among the living in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 主以公义的灵，和焚烧的灵，将锡安女子的污秽洗去，又将耶路撒冷中杀人的血除净，那时，剩在锡安留在耶路撒冷的，就是一切住耶路撒冷，在生命册上记名的，必称为圣。

chapters.en: The Lord will wash away the filth of the women of Zion; he will cleanse the bloodstains from Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.
Then the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion and over those who assemble there a cloud of smoke by day and a glow of flaming fire by night; over everything the glory will be a canopy.
chapters.zh: 耶和华也必在锡安全山，并各会众以上，使白日有烟云，黑夜有火焰的光。因为在全荣耀之上必有遮蔽。

chapters.en: It will be a shelter and shade from the heat of the day, and a refuge and hiding place from the storm and rain.
chapters.zh: 必有亭子，白日可以得荫避暑，也可以作为藏身之处，躲避狂风暴雨。

chapters.en: I will sing for the one I love a song about his vineyard: My loved one had a vineyard on a fertile hillside.
chapters.zh: 我要为我所亲爱的唱歌，是我所爱者的歌，论他葡萄园的事。我所亲爱的有葡萄园，在肥美的山冈上。

chapters.en: He dug it up and cleared it of stones and planted it with the choicest vines. He built a watchtower in it and cut out a winepress as well. Then he looked for a crop of good grapes, but it yielded only bad fruit.
chapters.zh: 他刨挖园子，捡去石头，栽种上等的葡萄树，在园中盖了一座楼，又凿出压酒池。指望结好葡萄，反倒结了野葡萄。

chapters.en: “Now you dwellers in Jerusalem and people of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的居民，和犹大人哪，请你们现今在我与我的葡萄园中断定是非。

chapters.en: What more could have been done for my vineyard than I have done for it? When I looked for good grapes, why did it yield only bad?
chapters.zh: 我为我葡萄园所作之外，还有什么可作的呢？我指望结好葡萄，怎么倒结了野葡萄呢？

chapters.en: Now I will tell you what I am going to do to my vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be destroyed; I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
chapters.zh: 现在我告诉你们，我要向我葡萄园怎样行。我必撤去篱笆，使它被吞灭，拆毁墙垣，使它被践踏。

chapters.en: I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated, and briers and thorns will grow there. I will command the clouds not to rain on it.”
chapters.zh: 我必使它荒废，不再修理，不再锄刨。荆棘蒺藜倒要生长。我也必命云不降雨在其上。

chapters.en: The vineyard of the LORD Almighty is the nation of Israel, and the people of Judah are the vines he delighted in. And he looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard cries of distress.
chapters.zh: 万军之耶和华的葡萄园，就是以色列家，他所喜爱的树，就是犹大人。他指望的是公平，谁知倒有暴虐（或作倒流人血）。指望的是公义，谁知倒有冤声。

chapters.en: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field till no space is left and you live alone in the land.
chapters.zh: 祸哉，那些以房接房，以地连地，以致不留余地的，只顾自己独居境内。

chapters.en: The LORD Almighty has declared in my hearing: “Surely the great houses will become desolate, the fine mansions left without occupants.
chapters.zh: 我耳闻万军之耶和华说，必有许多又大又美的房屋，成为荒凉，无人居住。

chapters.en: A ten-acre vineyard will produce only a bath of wine; a homer of seed will yield only an ephah of grain.”
chapters.zh: 三十亩葡萄园只出一吧特酒，一贺梅珥谷种只结一伊法粮食。

chapters.en: Woe to those who rise early in the morning to run after their drinks, who stay up late at night till they are inflamed with wine.
chapters.zh: 祸哉，那些清早起来，追求浓酒，留连到夜深，甚至因酒发烧的人。

chapters.en: They have harps and lyres at their banquets, pipes and timbrels and wine, but they have no regard for the deeds of the LORD, no respect for the work of his hands.
chapters.zh: 他们在筵席上弹琴，鼓瑟，击鼓，吹笛，饮酒，却不顾念耶和华的作为，也不留心他手所作的。

chapters.en: Therefore my people will go into exile for lack of understanding; those of high rank will die of hunger and the common people will be parched with thirst.
chapters.zh: 所以我的百姓，因无知就被掳去。他们的尊贵人甚是饥饿，群众极其干渴。

chapters.en: Therefore Death expands its jaws, opening wide its mouth; into it will descend their nobles and masses with all their brawlers and revelers.
chapters.zh: 故此，阴间扩张其欲，开了无限量的口。他们的荣耀，群众，繁华，并快乐的人，都落在其中。

chapters.en: So people will be brought low and everyone humbled, the eyes of the arrogant humbled.
chapters.zh: 卑贱人被压服，尊贵人降为卑，眼目高傲的人也降为卑。

chapters.en: But the LORD Almighty will be exalted by his justice, and the holy God will be proved holy by his righteous acts.
chapters.zh: 惟有万军之耶和华，因公平而崇高，圣者神，因公义显为圣。
