chapters.zh: 所以雅各的罪孽得赦免，他的罪过得除掉的果效，全在乎此。就是他叫祭坛的石头，变为打碎的灰石，以致木偶和日像，不再立起。

chapters.en: The fortified city stands desolate, an abandoned settlement, forsaken like the wilderness; there the calves graze, there they lie down; they strip its branches bare.
chapters.zh: 因为坚固城变为凄凉，成了撇下离弃的居所，像旷野一样，牛犊必在那里吃草，在那里躺卧，并吃尽其中的树枝。

chapters.en: When its twigs are dry, they are broken off and women come and make fires with them. For this is a people without understanding; so their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shows them no favor.
chapters.zh: 枝条枯干，必被折断。妇女要来，点火烧着，因为这百姓蒙昧无知，所以创造他们的，必不怜恤他们，造成他们的，也不施恩与他们。

chapters.en: In that day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, Israel, will be gathered up one by one.
chapters.zh: 以色列人哪，到那日，耶和华必从大河，直到埃及小河，将你们一一地收集，如同人打树拾果一样。

chapters.en: And in that day a great trumpet will sound. Those who were perishing in Assyria and those who were exiled in Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 当那日，必大发角声。在亚述地将要灭亡的，并在埃及地被赶散的，都要来。他们就在耶路撒冷圣山上敬拜耶和华。

chapters.en: Woe to that wreath, the pride of Ephraim’s drunkards, to the fading flower, his glorious beauty, set on the head of a fertile valley— to that city, the pride of those laid low by wine!
chapters.zh: 祸哉，以法莲的酒徒，住在肥美谷的山上，他们心里高傲，以所夸的为冠冕，犹如将残之花。

chapters.en: See, the Lord has one who is powerful and strong. Like a hailstorm and a destructive wind, like a driving rain and a flooding downpour, he will throw it forcefully to the ground.
chapters.zh: 看哪，主有一大能大力者，像一阵冰雹，像毁灭的暴风，像涨溢的大水，他必用手将冠冕摔落于地。

chapters.en: That wreath, the pride of Ephraim’s drunkards, will be trampled underfoot.
chapters.zh: 以法莲高傲的酒徒，他的冠冕，必被踏在脚下。

chapters.en: That fading flower, his glorious beauty, set on the head of a fertile valley, will be like figs ripe before harvest— as soon as people see them and take them in hand, they swallow them.
chapters.zh: 那荣美将残之花，就是在肥美谷山上的，必像夏令以前初熟的无花果。看见这果的就注意，一到手中就吞吃了。

chapters.en: In that day the LORD Almighty will be a glorious crown, a beautiful wreath for the remnant of his people.
chapters.zh: 到那日，万军之耶和华必作他余剩之民的荣冠华冕。

chapters.en: He will be a spirit of justice to the one who sits in judgment, a source of strength to those who turn back the battle at the gate.
chapters.zh: 也作了在位上行审判者公平之灵，并城门口打退仇敌者的力量。

chapters.en: And these also stagger from wine and reel from beer: Priests and prophets stagger from beer and are befuddled with wine; they reel from beer, they stagger when seeing visions, they stumble when rendering decisions.
chapters.zh: 就是这地的人，也因酒摇摇晃晃，因浓酒东倒西歪。祭司和先知因浓酒摇摇晃晃，被酒所困，因浓酒东倒西歪。他们错解默示，谬行审判。

chapters.en: All the tables are covered with vomit and there is not a spot without filth.
chapters.zh: 因为各席上满了呕吐的污秽，无一处干净。

chapters.en: “Who is it he is trying to teach? To whom is he explaining his message? To children weaned from their milk, to those just taken from the breast?
chapters.zh: 讥诮先知的说，他要将知识指教谁呢？要使谁明白传言呢？是那刚断奶离怀的吗？

chapters.en: For it is: Do this, do that, a rule for this, a rule for that ; a little here, a little there.”
chapters.zh: 他竟命上加命，令上加令，律上加律，例上加例，这里一点，那里一点。

chapters.en: Very well then, with foreign lips and strange tongues God will speak to this people,
chapters.zh: 先知说，不然，主要借异邦人的嘴唇，和外邦人的舌头，对这百姓说话。

chapters.en: to whom he said, “This is the resting place, let the weary rest”; and, “This is the place of repose”— but they would not listen.
chapters.zh: 他曾对他们说，你们要使疲乏人得安息。这样才得安息，才得舒畅。他们却不肯听。

chapters.en: So then, the word of the LORD to them will become: Do this, do that, a rule for this, a rule for that; a little here, a little there— so that as they go they will fall backward; they will be injured and snared and captured.
chapters.zh: 所以耶和华向他们说的话，是命上加命，令上加令，律上加律，例上加例，这里一点，那里一点，以致他们前行仰面跌倒，而且跌碎，并陷入网罗，被缠住。

chapters.en: Therefore hear the word of the LORD, you scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 所以你们这些亵慢的人，就是辖管住在耶路撒冷这百姓的，要听耶和华的话。

chapters.en: You boast, “We have entered into a covenant with death, with the realm of the dead we have made an agreement. When an overwhelming scourge sweeps by, it cannot touch us, for we have made a lie our refuge and falsehood our hiding place.”
chapters.zh: 你们曾说，我们与死亡立约，与阴间结盟。敌军（原文作鞭子）如水涨漫经过的时候，必不临到我们。因我们以谎言为避所，在虚假以下藏身。

chapters.en: So this is what the Sovereign LORD says: “See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone for a sure foundation; the one who relies on it will never be stricken with panic.
chapters.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说，看哪，我在锡安放一块石头，作为根基，是试验过的石头，是稳固根基，宝贵的房角石，信靠的人必不着急。

chapters.en: I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line; hail will sweep away your refuge, the lie, and water will overflow your hiding place.
chapters.zh: 我必以公平为准绳，以公义为线铊。冰雹必冲去谎言的避所，大水必漫过藏身之处。

chapters.en: Your covenant with death will be annulled; your agreement with the realm of the dead will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge sweeps by, you will be beaten down by it.
chapters.zh: 你们与死亡所立的约，必然废掉，与阴间所结的盟，必立不住。敌军（原文作鞭子）如水涨漫经过的时候，你们必被他践踏。

chapters.en: As often as it comes it will carry you away; morning after morning, by day and by night, it will sweep through.” The understanding of this message will bring sheer terror.
chapters.zh: 每逢经过必将你们掳去。因为每早晨他必经过，白昼黑夜都必如此。明白传言的，必受惊恐。

chapters.en: The bed is too short to stretch out on, the blanket too narrow to wrap around you.
chapters.zh: 原来床榻短，使人不能舒身。被窝窄，使人不能遮体。

chapters.en: The LORD will rise up as he did at Mount Perazim, he will rouse himself as in the Valley of Gibeon— to do his work, his strange work, and perform his task, his alien task.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必兴起，像在毗拉心山，他必发怒，像在基遍谷，好作成他的工，就是非常的工，成就他的事，就是奇异的事。

chapters.en: Now stop your mocking, or your chains will become heavier; the Lord, the LORD Almighty, has told me of the destruction decreed against the whole land.
chapters.zh: 现在你们不可亵慢，恐怕捆你们的绑索更结实了。因为我从主万军之耶和华那里听见已经决定，在全地上施行灭绝的事。

chapters.en: Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear what I say.
chapters.zh: 你们当侧耳听我的声音，留心听我的言语。

chapters.en: When a farmer plows for planting, does he plow continually? Does he keep on breaking up and working the soil?
chapters.zh: 那耕地为要撒种的，岂是常常耕地呢？岂是常常开垦耙地呢？

chapters.en: When he has leveled the surface, does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin? Does he not plant wheat in its place,barley in its plot,and spelt in its field?
chapters.zh: 他拉平了地面，岂不就撒种小茴香，播种大茴香，按行列种小麦，在定处种大麦，在田边种粗麦呢？

chapters.en: His God instructs him and teaches him the right way.
chapters.zh: 因为他的神教导他务农相宜，并且指教他。

chapters.en: Caraway is not threshed with a sledge, nor is the wheel of a cart rolled over cumin; caraway is beaten out with a rod, and cumin with a stick.
chapters.zh: 原来打小茴香，不用尖利的器具，轧大茴香，也不用碌碡。（原文作车轮下同）但用杖打小茴香，用棍打大茴香。

chapters.en: Grain must be ground to make bread; so one does not go on threshing it forever. The wheels of a threshing cart may be rolled over it, but one does not use horses to grind grain.
chapters.zh: 作饼的粮食是用磨磨碎，因它不必常打。虽用碌碡和马打散，却不磨它。

chapters.en: All this also comes from the LORD Almighty, whose plan is wonderful, whose wisdom is magnificent.
chapters.zh: 这也是出于万军之耶和华。他的谋略奇妙，他的智慧广大。

chapters.en: Woe to you, Ariel, Ariel, the city where David settled! Add year to year and let your cycle of festivals go on.
chapters.zh: 唉，亚利伊勒，亚利伊勒，大卫安营的城。任凭你年上加年，节期照常周流。

chapters.en: Yet I will besiege Ariel; she will mourn and lament, she will be to me like an altar hearth.
chapters.zh: 我终必使亚利伊勒困难。他必悲伤哀号，我却仍以他为亚利伊勒。

chapters.en: I will encamp against you on all sides; I will encircle you with towers and set up my siege works against you.
chapters.zh: 我必四围安营攻击你，屯兵围困你，筑垒攻击你。

chapters.en: Brought low, you will speak from the ground; your speech will mumble out of the dust. Your voice will come ghostlike from the earth; out of the dust your speech will whisper.
chapters.zh: 你必败落，从地中说话。你的言语必微细出于尘埃。你的声音必像那交鬼者的声音出于地。你的言语低低微微出于尘埃。

chapters.en: But your many enemies will become like fine dust, the ruthless hordes like blown chaff. Suddenly, in an instant,
chapters.zh: 你仇敌的群众，却要像细尘，强暴人的群众，也要像飞糠。这事必顷刻之间忽然临到。

chapters.en: the LORD Almighty will come with thunder and earthquake and great noise, with windstorm and tempest and flames of a devouring fire.
chapters.zh: 万军之耶和华必用雷轰，地震，大声，旋风，暴风，并吞灭的火焰，向他讨罪。

chapters.en: Then the hordes of all the nations that fight against Ariel, that attack her and her fortress and besiege her, will be as it is with a dream, with a vision in the night—
chapters.zh: 那时，攻击亚利伊勒列国的群众，就是一切攻击亚利伊勒和他的保障，并使他困难的，必如梦景，如夜间的异象。

chapters.en: as when a hungry person dreams of eating, but awakens hungry still; as when a thirsty person dreams of drinking, but awakens faint and thirsty still. So will it be with the hordes of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion.
chapters.zh: 又必像饥饿的人，梦中吃饭，醒了仍觉腹空。或像口渴的人，梦中喝水，醒了仍觉发昏，心里想喝。攻击锡安山列国的群众，也必如此。

chapters.en: Be stunned and amazed, blind yourselves and be sightless; be drunk, but not from wine, stagger, but not from beer.
chapters.zh: 你们等候惊奇吧。你们宴乐昏迷吧。他们醉了，却非因酒。他们东倒西歪，却非因浓酒。

chapters.en: The LORD has brought over you a deep sleep: He has sealed your eyes (the prophets); he has covered your heads (the seers).
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华将沉睡的灵，浇灌你们，封闭你们的眼，蒙盖你们的头。你们的眼，就是先知。你们的头，就是先见。

chapters.en: For you this whole vision is nothing but words sealed in a scroll. And if you give the scroll to someone who can read, and say, “Read this, please,” they will answer, “I can’t; it is sealed.”
chapters.zh: 所有的默示你们看如封住的书卷。人将这书卷交给识字的，说，请念吧。他说，我不能念，因为是封住了。

chapters.en: Or if you give the scroll to someone who cannot read, and say, “Read this, please,” they will answer, “I don’t know how to read.”
chapters.zh: 又将这书卷交给不识字的人，说，请念吧。他说，我不识字。

chapters.en: The Lord says: “These people come near to me with their mouth and honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me. Their worship of me is based on merely human rules they have been taught.
chapters.zh: 主说，因为这百姓亲近我，用嘴唇尊敬我，心却远离我。他们敬畏我，不过是领受人的吩咐。

chapters.en: Therefore once more I will astound these people with wonder upon wonder; the wisdom of the wise will perish, the intelligence of the intelligent will vanish.”
chapters.zh: 所以我在这百姓中要行奇妙的事，就是奇妙又奇妙的事。他们智慧人的智慧，必然消灭，聪明人的聪明，必然隐藏。

chapters.en: Woe to those who go to great depths to hide their plans from the LORD, who do their work in darkness and think, “Who sees us? Who will know?”
chapters.zh: 祸哉，那些向耶和华深藏谋略的，又在暗中行事，说，谁看见我们呢？谁知道我们呢？

chapters.en: You turn things upside down, as if the potter were thought to be like the clay! Shall what is formed say to the one who formed it, “You did not make me”? Can the pot say to the potter, “You know nothing”?
chapters.zh: 你们把事颠倒了，岂可看窑匠如泥吗？被制作的物，岂可论制作物的说，他没有制作我。或是被创造的物论造物的说，他没有聪明？

chapters.en: In a very short time, will not Lebanon be turned into a fertile field and the fertile field seem like a forest?
chapters.zh: 利巴嫩变为肥田，肥田看如树林，不是只有一点点时候吗？

chapters.en: In that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
chapters.zh: 那时，聋子必听见这书上的话。瞎子的眼，必从迷蒙黑暗中得以看见。

chapters.en: Once more the humble will rejoice in the LORD; the needy will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
chapters.zh: 谦卑人，必因耶和华增添欢喜。人间贫穷的，必因以色列的圣者快乐。

chapters.en: The ruthless will vanish, the mockers will disappear, and all who have an eye for evil will be cut down—
chapters.zh: 因为强暴人已归无有。亵慢人已经灭绝。一切找机会作孽的，都被剪除。

chapters.en: those who with a word make someone out to be guilty, who ensnare the defender in court and with false testimony deprive the innocent of justice.
chapters.zh: 他们在争讼的事上，定无罪的为有罪，为城门口责备人的，设下网罗，用虚无的事，屈枉义人。

chapters.en: Therefore this is what the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says to the descendants of Jacob: “No longer will Jacob be ashamed; no longer will their faces grow pale.
chapters.zh: 所以救赎亚伯拉罕的耶和华，论雅各家如此说，雅各必不再羞愧，面容也不至变色。

chapters.en: When they see among them their children, the work of my hands, they will keep my name holy; they will acknowledge the holiness of the Holy One of Jacob, and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
chapters.zh: 但他看见他的众子，就是我手的工作，在他那里，他们必尊我的名为圣，必尊雅各的圣者为圣，必敬畏以色列的神。

chapters.en: Those who are wayward in spirit will gain understanding; those who complain will accept instruction.”
chapters.zh: 心中迷糊的，必得明白，发怨言的，必受训诲。

chapters.en: “Woe to the obstinate children,” declares the LORD, “to those who carry out plans that are not mine, forming an alliance, but not by my Spirit, heaping sin upon sin;
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，祸哉，这悖逆的儿女。他们同谋，却不由于我，结盟，却不由于我的灵，以至罪上加罪。

chapters.en: who go down to Egypt without consulting me; who look for help to Pharaoh’s protection, to Egypt’s shade for refuge.
chapters.zh: 起身下埃及去，并没有求问我。要靠法老的力量，加添自己的力量，并投在埃及的荫下。

chapters.en: But Pharaoh’s protection will be to your shame, Egypt’s shade will bring you disgrace.
chapters.zh: 所以法老的力量，必作你们的羞辱，投在埃及的荫下，要为你们的惭愧。

chapters.en: Though they have officials in Zoan and their envoys have arrived in Hanes,
chapters.zh: 他们的首领已在琐安，他们的使臣到了哈内斯。

chapters.en: everyone will be put to shame because of a people useless to them, who bring neither help nor advantage, but only shame and disgrace.”
chapters.zh: 他们必因那不利于他们的民蒙羞。那民并非帮助，也非利益，只作羞耻凌辱。

chapters.en: A prophecy concerning the animals of the Negev: Through a land of hardship and distress, of lions and lionesses, of adders and darting snakes, the envoys carry their riches on donkeys’ backs, their treasures on the humps of camels, to that unprofitable nation,
chapters.zh: 论南方牲畜的默示。他们把财物驮在驴驹的脊背上，将宝物驮在骆驼的肉鞍上，经过艰难困苦之地，就是公狮，母狮，蝮蛇，火焰的飞龙之地，往那不利于他们的民那里去。

chapters.en: to Egypt, whose help is utterly useless. Therefore I call her Rahab the Do-Nothing.
chapters.zh: 埃及的帮助是徒然无益的。所以我称他为坐而不动的拉哈伯。

chapters.en: Go now, write it on a tablet for them, inscribe it on a scroll, that for the days to come it may be an everlasting witness.
chapters.zh: 现今你去，在他们面前将这话刻在版上，写在书上，以便传留后世，直到永永远远。

chapters.en: For these are rebellious people, deceitful children, children unwilling to listen to the LORD’s instruction.
chapters.zh: 因为他们是悖逆的百姓，说谎的儿女，不肯听从耶和华训诲的儿女。

chapters.en: They say to the seers, “See no more visions!” and to the prophets, “Give us no more visions of what is right! Tell us pleasant things, prophesy illusions.
chapters.zh: 他们对先见说，不要望见不吉利的事，对先知说，不要向我们讲正直的话，要向我们说柔和的话，言虚幻的事。

chapters.en: Leave this way, get off this path, and stop confronting us with the Holy One of Israel!”
chapters.zh: 你们要离弃正道，偏离直路。不要在我们面前，再提说以色列的圣者。

chapters.en: Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: “Because you have rejected this message, relied on oppression and depended on deceit,
chapters.zh: 所以以色列的圣者如此说，因为你们藐视这训诲的话，倚赖欺压和乖僻，以此为可靠的。

chapters.en: this sin will become for you like a high wall, cracked and bulging, that collapses suddenly, in an instant.
chapters.zh: 故此，这罪孽在你们身上，好像将要破裂凸出来的高墙，顷刻之间，忽然坍塌。

chapters.en: It will break in pieces like pottery, shattered so mercilessly that among its pieces not a fragment will be found for taking coals from a hearth or scooping water out of a cistern.”
chapters.zh: 要被打碎，好像把窑匠的瓦器打碎，毫不顾惜，甚至碎块中找不到一片，可用以从炉内取火，从池中舀水。

chapters.en: This is what the Sovereign LORD, the Holy One of Israel, says: “In repentance and rest is your salvation, in quietness and trust is your strength, but you would have none of it.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华以色列的圣者曾如此说，你们得救在乎归回安息。你们得力在乎平静安稳。你们竟自不肯。

chapters.en: You said, ‘No, we will flee on horses.’ Therefore you will flee! You said, ‘We will ride off on swift horses.’ Therefore your pursuers will be swift!
chapters.zh: 你们却说，不然，我们要骑马奔走。所以你们必然奔走。又说，我们要骑飞快的牲口。所以追赶你们的，也必飞快。

chapters.en: A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will all flee away, till you are left like a flagstaff on a mountaintop, like a banner on a hill.”
chapters.zh: 一人叱喝，必令千人逃跑。五人叱喝，你们都必逃跑。以致剩下的，好像山顶的旗杆，冈上的大旗。

chapters.en: Yet the LORD longs to be gracious to you; therefore he will rise up to show you compassion. For the LORD is a God of justice. Blessed are all who wait for him!
chapters.zh: 耶和华必然等候，要施恩给你们。必然兴起，好怜悯你们。因为耶和华是公平的神。凡等候他的，都是有福的。

chapters.en: People of Zion, who live in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. How gracious he will be when you cry for help! As soon as he hears, he will answer you.
chapters.zh: 百姓必在锡安在耶路撒冷居住。你不再哭泣。主必因你哀求的声音施恩给你。他听见的时候，就必应允你。

chapters.en: Although the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your teachers will be hidden no more; with your own eyes you will see them.
chapters.zh: 主虽然以艰难给你当饼，以困苦给你当水，你的教师却不再隐藏，你眼必看见你的教师。

chapters.en: Whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it.”
chapters.zh: 你或向左，或向右，你必听见后边有声音说，这是正路，要行在其间。

chapters.en: Then you will desecrate your idols overlaid with silver and your images covered with gold; you will throw them away like a menstrual cloth and say to them, “Away with you!”
chapters.zh: 你雕刻偶像所包的银子，和铸造偶像所镀的金子，你要玷污，要抛弃，好像污秽之物，对偶像说，去吧。

chapters.en: He will also send you rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the food that comes from the land will be rich and plentiful. In that day your cattle will graze in broad meadows.
chapters.zh: 你将种子撒在地里，主必降雨在其上。并使地所出的粮肥美丰盛。到那时你的牲畜，必在宽阔的草场吃草。

chapters.en: The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat fodder and mash, spread out with fork and shovel.
chapters.zh: 耕地的牛和驴驹，必吃加盐的料。这料是用木锨和杈子扬净的。

chapters.en: In the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall, streams of water will flow on every high mountain and every lofty hill.
chapters.zh: 在大行杀戮的日子，高台倒塌的时候，各高山冈陵，必有川流河涌。

chapters.en: The moon will shine like the sun, and the sunlight will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven full days, when the LORD binds up the bruises of his people and heals the wounds he inflicted.
chapters.zh: 当耶和华缠裹他百姓的损处，医治他民鞭伤的日子，月光必像日光，日光必加七倍，像七日的光一样。

chapters.en: See, the Name of the LORD comes from afar, with burning anger and dense clouds of smoke; his lips are full of wrath, and his tongue is a consuming fire.
chapters.zh: 看哪，耶和华的名从远方来，怒气烧起，密烟上腾。他的嘴唇满有忿恨，他的舌头像吞灭的火。

chapters.en: His breath is like a rushing torrent, rising up to the neck. He shakes the nations in the sieve of destruction; he places in the jaws of the peoples a bit that leads them astray.
chapters.zh: 他的气如涨溢的河水，直涨到颈项，要用毁灭的筛箩，筛净列国。并且在众民的口中，必有使人错行的嚼环。

chapters.en: And you will sing as on the night you celebrate a holy festival; your hearts will rejoice as when people playing pipes go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
chapters.zh: 你们必唱歌，像守圣节的夜间一样。并且心中喜乐，像人吹笛，上耶和华的山，到以色列的磐石那里。

chapters.en: The LORD will cause people to hear his majestic voice and will make them see his arm coming down with raging anger and consuming fire, with cloudburst, thunderstorm and hail.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必使人听他威严的声音，又显他降罚的膀臂，和他怒中的忿恨，并吞灭的火焰，与霹雷，暴风，冰雹。

chapters.en: The voice of the LORD will shatter Assyria; with his rod he will strike them down.
chapters.zh: 亚述人必因耶和华的声音惊惶。耶和华必用杖击打他。

chapters.en: Every stroke the LORD lays on them with his punishing club will be to the music of timbrels and harps, as he fights them in battle with the blows of his arm.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必将命定的杖，加在他身上，每打一下，人必击鼓弹琴。打仗的时候，耶和华必抡起手来，与他交战。

chapters.en: Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king. Its fire pit has been made deep and wide, with an abundance of fire and wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.
chapters.zh: 原来陀斐特又深又宽，早已为王预备好了，其中堆的是火，与许多木柴。耶和华的气如一股硫磺火，使它着起来。

chapters.en: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in the multitude of their chariots and in the great strength of their horsemen, but do not look to the Holy One of Israel, or seek help from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祸哉，那些下埃及求帮助的，是因仗赖马匹，倚靠甚多的车辆，并倚靠强壮的马兵，却不仰望以色列的圣者，也不求问耶和华。

chapters.en: Yet he too is wise and can bring disaster; he does not take back his words. He will rise up against that wicked nation, against those who help evildoers.
chapters.zh: 其实耶和华有智慧。他必降灾祸，并不反悔自己的话，却要兴起攻击那作恶之家，又攻击那作孽帮助人的。

chapters.en: But the Egyptians are mere mortals and not God; their horses are flesh and not spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, those who help will stumble, those who are helped will fall; all will perish together.
chapters.zh: 埃及人不过是人，并不是神。他们的马不过是血肉，并不是灵。耶和华一伸手，那帮助人的必绊跌，那受帮助的也必跌倒，都一同灭亡。

chapters.en: This is what the LORD says to me: “As a lion growls, a great lion over its prey— and though a whole band of shepherds is called together against it, it is not frightened by their shouts or disturbed by their clamor— so the LORD Almighty will come down to do battle on Mount Zion and on its heights.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对我如此说，狮子和少壮狮子，获食咆哮，就是喊许多牧人来攻击它，它总不因他们的声音惊惶，也不因他们的喧哗缩伏。如此万军之耶和华，也必降临在锡安山冈上争战。

chapters.en: Like birds hovering overhead, the LORD Almighty will shield Jerusalem; he will shield it and deliver it, he will ‘pass over’ it and will rescue it.”
chapters.zh: 雀鸟怎样扇翅覆雏，万军之耶和华也要照样保护耶路撒冷，他必保护拯救，要越门保守。

chapters.en: Return, you Israelites, to the One you have so greatly revolted against.
chapters.zh: 以色列人哪，你们深深的悖逆耶和华，现今要归向他。

chapters.en: For in that day every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold your sinful hands have made.
chapters.zh: 到那日各人必将他金偶像，银偶像，就是亲手所造陷自己在罪中的，都抛弃了。

chapters.en: “Assyria will fall by no human sword; a sword, not of mortals, will devour them. They will flee before the sword and their young men will be put to forced labor.
chapters.zh: 亚述人必倒在刀下，并非人的刀。有刀要将他吞灭，并非人的刀。他必逃避这刀，他的少年人，必成为服苦的。

chapters.en: Their stronghold will fall because of terror; at the sight of the battle standard their commanders will panic,” declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 他的磐石，必因惊吓挪去，他的首领，必因大旗惊惶。这是那有火在锡安，有炉在耶路撒冷的耶和华说的。

chapters.en: See, a king will reign in righteousness and rulers will rule with justice.
chapters.zh: 看哪，必有一王凭公义行政。必有首领借公平掌权。

chapters.en: Each one will be like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in the desert and the shadow of a great rock in a thirsty land.
chapters.zh: 必有一人像避风所，和避暴雨的隐密处，又像河流在干旱之地，像大磐石的影子在疲乏之地。

chapters.en: Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
chapters.zh: 那能看的人，眼不再昏迷，能听的人，耳必得听闻。

chapters.en: The fearful heart will know and understand, and the stammering tongue will be fluent and clear.
chapters.zh: 冒失人的心，必明白知识，结吧人的舌，必说话通快。

chapters.en: No longer will the fool be called noble nor the scoundrel be highly respected.
chapters.zh: 愚顽人不再称为高明，吝啬人不再称为大方。

chapters.en: For fools speak folly, their hearts are bent on evil: They practice ungodliness and spread error concerning the LORD; the hungry they leave empty and from the thirsty they withhold water.
chapters.zh: 因为愚顽人，必说愚顽话，心里想作罪孽，惯行亵渎的事，说错谬的话，攻击耶和华，使饥饿的人，无食可吃，使口渴的人，无水可喝。

chapters.en: Scoundrels use wicked methods, they make up evil schemes to destroy the poor with lies, even when the plea of the needy is just.
chapters.zh: 吝啬人所用的法子是恶的。他图谋恶计，用谎言毁灭谦卑人。穷乏人讲公理的时候，他也是这样行。

chapters.en: But the noble make noble plans, and by noble deeds they stand.
chapters.zh: 高明人却谋高明事，在高明事上，也必永存。

chapters.en: You women who are so complacent, rise up and listen to me; you daughters who feel secure, hear what I have to say!
chapters.zh: 安逸的妇女阿，起来听我的声音。无虑的女子阿，侧耳听我的言语。

chapters.en: In little more than a year you who feel secure will tremble; the grape harvest will fail, and the harvest of fruit will not come.
chapters.zh: 无虑的女子阿，再过一年多，必受骚扰。因为无葡萄可摘，无果子（或作禾稼）可收。

chapters.en: Tremble, you complacent women; shudder, you daughters who feel secure! Strip off your fine clothes and wrap yourselves in rags.
chapters.zh: 安逸的妇女阿，要战兢。无虑的女子阿，要受骚扰。脱去衣服，赤着身体，腰束麻布。

chapters.en: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vines
chapters.zh: 她们必为美好的田地，和多结果的葡萄树，捶胸哀哭。

chapters.en: and for the land of my people, a land overgrown with thorns and briers— yes, mourn for all houses of merriment and for this city of revelry.
chapters.zh: 荆棘蒺藜必长在我百姓的地上，又长在欢乐的城中，和一切快乐的房屋上。

chapters.en: The fortress will be abandoned, the noisy city deserted; citadel and watchtower will become a wasteland forever, the delight of donkeys, a pasture for flocks,
chapters.zh: 因为宫殿必被撇下。多民的城必被离弃。山冈望楼永为洞穴，作野驴所喜乐的，为羊群的草场。

chapters.en: till the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the desert becomes a fertile field, and the fertile field seems like a forest.
chapters.zh: 等到圣灵从上浇灌我们，旷野就变为肥田，肥田看如树林。

chapters.en: The LORD’s justice will dwell in the desert, his righteousness live in the fertile field.
chapters.zh: 那时，公平要居在旷野，公义要居在肥田。

chapters.en: The fruit of that righteousness will be peace; its effect will be quietness and confidence forever.
chapters.zh: 公义的果效，必是平安。公义的效验，必是平稳，直到永远。

chapters.en: My people will live in peaceful dwelling places, in secure homes, in undisturbed places of rest.
chapters.zh: 我的百姓，必住在平安的居所，安稳的住处，平静的安歇所。

chapters.en: Though hail flattens the forest and the city is leveled completely,
chapters.zh: 但要降冰雹打倒树林。城必全然拆平。

chapters.en: how blessed you will be, sowing your seed by every stream, and letting your cattle and donkeys range free.
chapters.zh: 你们在各水边撒种牧放牛驴的有福了。

chapters.en: Woe to you, destroyer, you who have not been destroyed! Woe to you, betrayer, you who have not been betrayed! When you stop destroying, you will be destroyed; when you stop betraying, you will be betrayed.
chapters.zh: 祸哉，你这毁灭人的，自己倒不被毁灭。行事诡诈的，人倒不以诡诈待你。你毁灭罢休了，自己必被毁灭。你行完了诡诈，人必以诡诈待你。

chapters.en: LORD, be gracious to us; we long for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation in time of distress.
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，求你施恩于我们。我们等候你。求你每早晨作我们的膀臂。遭难的时候，为我们的拯救。

chapters.en: At the uproar of your army, the peoples flee; when you rise up, the nations scatter.
chapters.zh: 喧嚷的响声一发，众民奔逃。你一兴起，列国四散。

chapters.en: Your plunder, O nations, is harvested as by young locusts; like a swarm of locusts people pounce on it.
chapters.zh: 你们所掳的，必被敛尽，好像蚂蚱吃（原文作敛）尽禾稼。人要蹦在其上，好像蝗虫一样。

chapters.en: The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high; he will fill Zion with his justice and righteousness.
chapters.zh: 耶和华被尊崇，因他居在高处。他以公平公义充满锡安。

chapters.en: He will be the sure foundation for your times, a rich store of salvation and wisdom and knowledge; the fear of the LORD is the key to this treasure.
chapters.zh: 你一生一世必得安稳，有丰盛的救恩，并智慧，和知识。你以敬畏耶和华为至宝。

chapters.en: Look, their brave men cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
chapters.zh: 看哪，他们的豪杰在外头哀号。求和的使臣，痛痛哭泣。

chapters.en: The highways are deserted, no travelers are on the roads. The treaty is broken, its witnesses are despised, no one is respected.
chapters.zh: 大路荒凉，行人止息。敌人背约，藐视城邑，不顾人民。

chapters.en: The land dries up and wastes away, Lebanon is ashamed and withers; Sharon is like the Arabah, and Bashan and Carmel drop their leaves.
chapters.zh: 地上悲哀衰残。利巴嫩羞愧枯干。沙仑像旷野。巴珊和迦密的树林凋残。

chapters.en: “Now will I arise,” says the LORD. “Now will I be exalted; now will I be lifted up.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，现在我要起来。我要兴起。我要勃然而兴。

chapters.en: You conceive chaff, you give birth to straw; your breath is a fire that consumes you.
chapters.zh: 你们要怀的是糠秕。要生的是碎秸。你们的气就是吞灭自己的火。

chapters.en: The peoples will be burned to ashes; like cut thornbushes they will be set ablaze.”
chapters.zh: 列邦必像已烧的石灰，像已割的荆棘，在火中焚烧。

chapters.en: You who are far away, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge my power!
chapters.zh: 你们远方的人，当听我所行的，你们近处的人，当承认我的大能。

chapters.en: The sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling grips the godless: “Who of us can dwell with the consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting burning?”
chapters.zh: 锡安中的罪人都惧怕。不敬虔的人被战兢抓住。我们中间谁能与吞灭的火同住？我们中间谁能与永火同住呢？

chapters.en: Those who walk righteously and speak what is right, who reject gain from extortion and keep their hands from accepting bribes, who stop their ears against plots of murder and shut their eyes against contemplating evil—
chapters.zh: 行事公义，说话正直，憎恶欺压的财利，摆手不受贿赂，塞耳不听流血的话，闭眼不看邪恶事的，

chapters.en: they are the ones who will dwell on the heights, whose refuge will be the mountain fortress. Their bread will be supplied, and water will not fail them.
chapters.zh: 他必居高处。他的保障是磐石的坚垒。他的粮必不缺乏，（原文作赐给）他的水必不断绝。

chapters.en: Your eyes will see the king in his beauty and view a land that stretches afar.
chapters.zh: 你的眼必见王的荣美，必见辽阔之地。

chapters.en: In your thoughts you will ponder the former terror: “Where is that chief officer? Where is the one who took the revenue? Where is the officer in charge of the towers?”
chapters.zh: 你的心必思想那惊吓的事，自问说，记数目的在哪里呢？平贡银的在哪里呢？数戍楼的在哪里呢？

chapters.en: You will see those arrogant people no more, people whose speech is obscure, whose language is strange and incomprehensible.
chapters.zh: 你必不见那强暴的民，就是说话深奥，你不能明白，言语呢喃，你不能懂得的。

chapters.en: Look on Zion, the city of our festivals; your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful abode, a tent that will not be moved; its stakes will never be pulled up, nor any of its ropes broken.
chapters.zh: 你要看锡安我们守圣节的城。你的眼必见耶路撒冷为安静的居所，为不挪移的帐幕，橛子永不拔出，绳索一根也不折断。

chapters.en: There the LORD will be our Mighty One. It will be like a place of broad rivers and streams. No galley with oars will ride them, no mighty ship will sail them.
chapters.zh: 在那里耶和华必显威严与我们同在，当作江河宽阔之地。其中必没有荡桨摇橹的船来往，也没有威武的船经过。

chapters.en: For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; it is he who will save us.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华是审判我们的，耶和华是给我们设律法的，耶和华是我们的王。他必拯救我们。

chapters.en: Your rigging hangs loose: The mast is not held secure, the sail is not spread. Then an abundance of spoils will be divided and even the lame will carry off plunder.
chapters.zh: 你的绳索松开不能栽稳桅杆，也不能扬起篷来，那时许多掳来的物被分了。瘸腿的把掠物夺去了。

chapters.en: No one living in Zion will say, “I am ill”; and the sins of those who dwell there will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 城内居民必不说，我病了。其中居住的百姓，罪孽都赦免了。

chapters.en: Come near, you nations, and listen; pay attention, you peoples! Let the earth hear, and all that is in it, the world, and all that comes out of it!
chapters.zh: 列国阿，要近前来听。众民哪，要侧耳而听。地和其上所充满的，世界和其中一切所出的，都应当听。

chapters.en: The LORD is angry with all nations; his wrath is on all their armies. He will totally destroy them, he will give them over to slaughter.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华向万国发忿恨，向他们的全军发烈怒，将他们灭尽，交出他们受杀戮。

chapters.en: Their slain will be thrown out, their dead bodies will stink; the mountains will be soaked with their blood.
chapters.zh: 被杀的必然抛弃，尸首臭气上腾。诸山被他们的血融化。

chapters.en: All the stars in the sky will be dissolved and the heavens rolled up like a scroll; all the starry host will fall like withered leaves from the vine, like shriveled figs from the fig tree.
chapters.zh: 天上的万象都要消没，天被卷起，好像书卷。其上的万象要残败，像葡萄树的叶子残败，又像无花果树的叶子残败一样

chapters.en: My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens; see, it descends in judgment on Edom, the people I have totally destroyed.
chapters.zh: 因为我的刀在天上已经喝足。这刀必临到以东，和我所咒诅的民，要施行审判。

chapters.en: The sword of the LORD is bathed in blood, it is covered with fat— the blood of lambs and goats, fat from the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的刀满了血，用脂油和羊羔公山羊的血，并公绵羊腰子的脂油滋润的。因为耶和华在波斯拉有献祭的事，在以东地大行杀戮。

chapters.en: And the wild oxen will fall with them, the bull calves and the great bulls. Their land will be drenched with blood, and the dust will be soaked with fat.
chapters.zh: 野牛，牛犊，和公牛，要一同下来。他们的地喝醉了血，他们的尘土因脂油肥润。

chapters.en: For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of retribution, to uphold Zion’s cause.
chapters.zh: 因耶和华有报仇之日，为锡安的争辩，有报应之年。

chapters.en: Edom’s streams will be turned into pitch, her dust into burning sulfur; her land will become blazing pitch!
chapters.zh: 以东的河水要变为石油，尘埃要变为硫磺，地土成为烧着的石油。

chapters.en: It will not be quenched night or day; its smoke will rise forever. From generation to generation it will lie desolate; no one will ever pass through it again.
chapters.zh: 昼夜总不熄灭，烟气永远上腾，必世世代代成为荒废，永永远远无人经过。

chapters.en: The desert owl and screech owl will possess it; the great owl and the raven will nest there. God will stretch out over Edom the measuring line of chaos and the plumb line of desolation.
chapters.zh: 鹈鹕，箭猪，却要得为业。猫头鹰，乌鸦，要住在其间。耶和华必将空虚的准绳，混沌的线铊，拉在其上。

chapters.en: Her nobles will have nothing there to be called a kingdom, all her princes will vanish away.
chapters.zh: 以东人要召贵胄来治国，那里却无一个。首领也都归于无有。

chapters.en: Thorns will overrun her citadels, nettles and brambles her strongholds. She will become a haunt for jackals, a home for owls.
chapters.zh: 以东的宫殿要长荆棘，保障要长蒺藜和刺草。要作野狗的住处，鸵鸟的居所。

chapters.en: Desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and wild goats will bleat to each other; there the night creatures will also lie down and find for themselves places of rest.
chapters.zh: 旷野的走兽，要和豺狼相遇。野山羊，要与伴偶对叫。夜间的怪物，必在那里栖身，自找安歇之处。

chapters.en: The owl will nest there and lay eggs, she will hatch them, and care for her young under the shadow of her wings; there also the falcons will gather, each with its mate.
chapters.zh: 箭蛇要在那里作窝，下蛋，抱蛋，生子，聚子在其影下。鹞鹰，各与伴偶聚集在那里。

chapters.en: Look in the scroll of the LORD and read: None of these will be missing, not one will lack her mate. For it is his mouth that has given the order, and his Spirit will gather them together.
chapters.zh: 你们要查考宣读耶和华的书。这都无一缺少，无一没有伴偶，因为我的口已经吩咐，他的灵将他们聚集。

chapters.en: He allots their portions; his hand distributes them by measure. They will possess it forever and dwell there from generation to generation.
chapters.zh: 他也为他们拈阄，又亲手用准绳给他们分地，他们必永得为业，世世代代住在其间。

chapters.en: The desert and the parched land will be glad; the wilderness will rejoice and blossom. Like the crocus,
chapters.zh: 旷野和干旱之地，必然欢喜。沙漠也必快乐。又像玫瑰开花。

chapters.en: it will burst into bloom; it will rejoice greatly and shout for joy. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon; they will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
chapters.zh: 必开花繁盛，乐上加乐，而且欢呼。利巴嫩的荣耀，并迦密与沙仑的华美，必赐给他。人必看见耶和华的荣耀，我们神的华美。

chapters.en: Strengthen the feeble hands, steady the knees that give way;
chapters.zh: 你们要使软弱的手坚壮，无力的膝稳固。

chapters.en: say to those with fearful hearts, “Be strong, do not fear; your God will come, he will come with vengeance; with divine retribution he will come to save you.”
chapters.zh: 对胆怯的人说，你们要刚强，不要惧怕。看哪，你们的神必来报仇，必来施行极大的报应，他必来拯救你们。

chapters.en: Then will the eyes of the blind be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
chapters.zh: 那时瞎子的眼必睁开，聋子的耳必开通。

chapters.en: Then will the lame leap like a deer, and the mute tongue shout for joy. Water will gush forth in the wilderness and streams in the desert.
chapters.zh: 那时瘸子必跳跃像鹿，哑吧的舌头必能歌唱。在旷野必有水发出，在沙漠必有河涌流。

chapters.en: The burning sand will become a pool, the thirsty ground bubbling springs. In the haunts where jackals once lay, grass and reeds and papyrus will grow.
chapters.zh: 发光的沙，（或作蜃楼）要变为水池，干渴之地，要变为泉源。在野狗躺卧之处，必有青草，芦苇，和蒲草。

chapters.en: And a highway will be there; it will be called the Way of Holiness; it will be for those who walk on that Way. The unclean will not journey on it; wicked fools will not go about on it.
chapters.zh: 在那里必有一条大道，称为圣路。污秽人不得经过，必专为赎民行走，行路的人虽愚昧，也不至失迷。

chapters.en: No lion will be there, nor any ravenous beast; they will not be found there. But only the redeemed will walk there,
chapters.zh: 在那里必没有狮子，猛兽也不登这路，在那里都遇不见。只有赎民在那里行走。

chapters.en: and those the LORD has rescued will return. They will enter Zion with singing; everlasting joy will crown their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
chapters.zh: 并且耶和华救赎的民必归回，歌唱来到锡安。永乐必归到他们的头上，他们必得着欢喜快乐，忧愁叹息尽都逃避。

chapters.en: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
chapters.zh: 希西家王十四年，亚述王西拿基立，上来攻击犹大的一切坚固城，将城攻取。

chapters.en: Then the king of Assyria sent his field commander with a large army from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. When the commander stopped at the aqueduct of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field,
chapters.zh: 亚述王从拉吉差遣拉伯沙基，率领大军，往耶路撒冷到希西家王那里去。他就站在上池的水沟旁，在漂布地的大路上。

chapters.en: Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder went out to him.
chapters.zh: 于是希勒家的儿子家宰以利亚敬，并书记舍伯那，和亚萨的儿子史官约亚，出来见拉伯沙基。

chapters.en: The field commander said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: “ ‘This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: On what are you basing this confidence of yours?
chapters.zh: 拉伯沙基对他们说，你们去告诉希西家说，亚述大王如此说，你所倚靠的有什么可仗赖的呢？

chapters.en: You say you have counsel and might for war—but you speak only empty words. On whom are you depending, that you rebel against me?
chapters.zh: 你说，有打仗的计谋和能力。我看不过是虚话，你到底倚靠谁，才背叛我呢？

chapters.en: Look, I know you are depending on Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff, which pierces the hand of anyone who leans on it! Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who depend on him.
chapters.zh: 看哪，你所倚靠的埃及，是那压伤的苇杖，人若靠这杖，就必刺透他的手。埃及王法老向一切倚靠他的人，也是这样。

chapters.en: But if you say to me, “We are depending on the LORD our God”—isn’t he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, “You must worship before this altar”?
chapters.zh: 你若对我说，我们倚靠耶和华我们的神。希西家岂不是将神的丘坛，和祭坛废去，且对犹大和耶路撒冷的人说，你们当在这坛前敬拜吗？

chapters.en: “ ‘Come now, make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!
chapters.zh: 现在你把当头给我主亚述王，我给你二千匹马，看你这一面骑马的人够不够。

chapters.en: How then can you repulse one officer of the least of my master’s officials, even though you are depending on Egypt for chariots and horsemen ?
chapters.zh: 若不然，怎能打败我主臣仆中最小的军长呢？你竟倚靠埃及的战车马兵吗？

chapters.en: Furthermore, have I come to attack and destroy this land without the LORD? The LORD himself told me to march against this country and destroy it.’ ”
chapters.zh: 现在我上来攻击毁灭这地，岂没有耶和华的意思吗？耶和华吩咐我说，你上去攻击毁灭这地吧。

chapters.en: Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to the field commander, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, since we understand it. Don’t speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall.”
chapters.zh: 以利亚敬，舍伯那，约亚，对拉伯沙基说，求你用亚兰言语和仆人说话，因为我们懂得，不要用犹大言语和我们说话达到城上百姓的耳中。

chapters.en: But the commander replied, “Was it only to your master and you that my master sent me to say these things, and not to the people sitting on the wall—who, like you, will have to eat their own excrement and drink their own urine?”
chapters.zh: 拉伯沙基说，我主差遣我来，岂是单对你和你的主说这些话吗？不也是对这些坐在城上，要与你们一同吃自己粪喝自己尿的人说吗？

chapters.en: Then the commander stood and called out in Hebrew, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
chapters.zh: 于是拉伯沙基站着，用犹大言语，大声喊着说，你们当听亚述大王的话。

chapters.en: This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you. He cannot deliver you!
chapters.zh: 王如此说，你们不要被希西家欺哄了，因他不能拯救你们。

chapters.en: Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD when he says, ‘The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.’
chapters.zh: 也不要听希西家使你们倚靠耶和华说，耶和华必要拯救我们，这城必不交在亚述王的手中。

chapters.en: “Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat fruit from your own vine and fig tree and drink water from your own cistern,
chapters.zh: 不要听希西家的话，因亚述王如此说，你们要与我和好，出来投降我，各人就可以吃自己葡萄树和无花果树的果子，喝自己井里的水。

chapters.en: until I come and take you to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
chapters.zh: 等我来领你们到一个地方，与你们本地一样，就是有五谷和新酒之地，有粮食和葡萄园之地。

chapters.en: “Do not let Hezekiah mislead you when he says, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’ Have the gods of any nations ever delivered their lands from the hand of the king of Assyria?
chapters.zh: 你们要谨防，恐怕希西家劝导你们说，耶和华必拯救我们。列国的神有哪一个救他本国脱离亚述王的手呢？

chapters.en: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
chapters.zh: 哈马和亚珥拔的神在哪里呢？西法瓦音的神在哪里呢？他们曾救撒玛利亚脱离我的手吗？

chapters.en: Who of all the gods of these countries have been able to save their lands from me? How then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”
chapters.zh: 这些国的神，有谁曾救自己的国脱离我的手呢？难道耶和华能救耶路撒冷脱离我的手吗？

chapters.en: But the people remained silent and said nothing in reply, because the king had commanded, “Do not answer him.”
chapters.zh: 百姓静默不言，并不回答一句，因为王曾吩咐说，不要回答他。

chapters.en: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder went to Hezekiah, with their clothes torn, and told him what the field commander had said.
chapters.zh: 当下希勒家的儿子家宰以利亚敬，和书记舍伯那，并亚萨的儿子史官约亚，都撕裂衣服，来到希西家那里，将拉伯沙基的话告诉了他。

chapters.en: When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and went into the temple of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 希西家王听见，就撕裂衣服，披上麻布，进了耶和华的殿。

chapters.en: He sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
chapters.zh: 使家宰以利亚敬，和书记舍伯那，并祭司中的长老，都披上麻布，去见亚摩斯的儿子先知以赛亚。

chapters.en: They told him, “This is what Hezekiah says: This day is a day of distress and rebuke and disgrace, as when children come to the moment of birth and there is no strength to deliver them.
chapters.zh: 对他说，希西家如此说，今日是急难，责罚，凌辱的日子，就如妇人将要生产婴孩，却没有力量生产。

chapters.en: It may be that the LORD your God will hear the words of the field commander, whom his master, the king of Assyria, has sent to ridicule the living God, and that he will rebuke him for the words the LORD your God has heard. Therefore pray for the remnant that still survives.”
chapters.zh: 或者耶和华你的神，听见拉伯沙基的话，就是他主人亚述王打发他来辱骂永生神的话。耶和华你的神，听见这话就发斥责，故此求你为余剩的民，扬声祷告。

chapters.en: When King Hezekiah’s officials came to Isaiah,
chapters.zh: 希西家王的臣仆，就去见以赛亚，

chapters.en: Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master, ‘This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of what you have heard—those words with which the underlings of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
chapters.zh: 以赛亚对他们说，要这样对你们的主人说，耶和华如此说，你听见亚述王的仆人亵渎我的话，不要惧怕。

chapters.en: Listen! When he hears a certain report, I will make him want to return to his own country, and there I will have him cut down with the sword.’ ”
chapters.zh: 我必惊动（原文作使灵进入）他的心，他要听见风声就归回本地，我必使他在那里倒在刀下。

chapters.en: When the field commander heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.
chapters.zh: 拉伯沙基回去，正遇见亚述王攻打立拿。原来他早听见亚述王拔营离开拉吉。

chapters.en: Now Sennacherib received a report that Tirhakah, the king of Cush, was marching out to fight against him. When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah with this word:
chapters.zh: 亚述王听见人论古实王特哈加说，他出来要与你争战。亚述王一听见，就打发使者去见希西家，吩咐他们说。

chapters.en: “Say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let the god you depend on deceive you when he says, ‘Jerusalem will not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.’
chapters.zh: 你们对犹大王希西家如此说，不要听你所倚靠的神欺哄你，说，耶路撒冷必不交在亚述王的手中。

chapters.en: Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the countries, destroying them completely. And will you be delivered?
chapters.zh: 你总听说亚述诸王向列国所行的，乃是尽行灭绝，难道你还能得救吗？

chapters.en: Did the gods of the nations that were destroyed by my predecessors deliver them—the gods of Gozan, Harran, Rezeph and the people of Eden who were in Tel Assar?
chapters.zh: 我列祖所毁灭的，就是歌散，哈兰，利色，和属提拉撒的伊甸人。这些国的神，何曾拯救这些国呢？

chapters.en: Where is the king of Hamath or the king of Arpad? Where are the kings of Lair, Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah?”
chapters.zh: 哈马的王，亚珥拔的王，西法瓦音城的王，希拿和以瓦的王，都在哪里呢？

chapters.en: Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the temple of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 希西家从使者手里接过书信来，看完了，就上耶和华的殿，将书信在耶和华面前展开。

chapters.en: And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
chapters.zh: 希西家向耶和华祷告说，

chapters.en: “LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, enthroned between the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.
chapters.zh: 坐在二基路伯上万军之耶和华以色列的神阿，你，惟有你，是天下万国的神。你曾创造天地。

chapters.en: Give ear, LORD, and hear; open your eyes, LORD, and see; listen to all the words Sennacherib has sent to ridicule the living God.
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，求你侧耳而听。耶和华阿，求你睁眼而看。要听西拿基立的一切话，他是打发使者来辱骂永生神的。

chapters.en: “It is true, LORD, that the Assyrian kings have laid waste all these peoples and their lands.
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，亚述诸王果然使列国，和列国之地变为荒凉。

chapters.en: They have thrown their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods but only wood and stone, fashioned by human hands.
chapters.zh: 将列国的神像都扔在火里，因为它本不是神，乃是人手所造的，是木头，石头的，所以灭绝它。

chapters.en: Now, LORD our God, deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, LORD, are the only God. ”
chapters.zh: 耶和华我们的神阿，现在求你救我们脱离亚述王的手，使天下万国都知道惟有你是耶和华。

chapters.en: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,
chapters.zh: 亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚，就打发人去见希西家说，耶和华以色列的神如此说，你既然求我攻击亚述王西拿基立，

chapters.en: this is the word the LORD has spoken against him: “Virgin Daughter Zion despises and mocks you. Daughter Jerusalem tosses her head as you flee.
chapters.zh: 所以耶和华论他这样说，锡安的处女藐视你，嗤笑你，耶路撒冷的女子向你摇头。

chapters.en: Who is it you have ridiculed and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!
chapters.zh: 你辱骂谁？亵渎谁？扬起声来，高举眼目攻击谁呢？乃是攻击以色列的圣者。

chapters.en: By your messengers you have ridiculed the Lord. And you have said, ‘With my many chariots I have ascended the heights of the mountains, the utmost heights of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, the choicest of its junipers. I have reached its remotest heights, the finest of its forests.
chapters.zh: 你借你的臣仆辱骂主，说，我率领许多战车上山顶，到利巴嫩极深之处，我要砍伐其中高大的香柏树，和佳美的松树，我必上极高之处，进入肥田的树林。

chapters.en: I have dug wells in foreign lands and drunk the water there. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.’
chapters.zh: 我已经挖井喝水，我必用脚掌踏干埃及的一切河。

chapters.en: “Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it. In days of old I planned it; now I have brought it to pass, that you have turned fortified cities into piles of stone.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，你岂没有听见我早先所作的古时所立的吗？现在借你使坚固城荒废，变为乱堆。

chapters.en: Their people, drained of power, are dismayed and put to shame. They are like plants in the field, like tender green shoots, like grass sprouting on the roof, scorched before it grows up.
chapters.zh: 所以其中的居民力量甚小，惊惶羞愧。他们像野草，像青菜，如房顶上的草，又如田间未长成的禾稼。

chapters.en: “But I know where you are and when you come and go and how you rage against me.
chapters.zh: 你坐下，你出去，你进来，你向我发烈怒，我都知道。

chapters.en: Because you rage against me and because your insolence has reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will make you return by the way you came.
chapters.zh: 因你向我发烈怒，又因你狂傲的话达到我耳中，我就要用钩子钩上你的鼻子，把嚼环放在你口里，使你从原路转回去。

chapters.en: “This will be the sign for you, Hezekiah: “This year you will eat what grows by itself, and the second year what springs from that. But in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
chapters.zh: 以色列人哪，我赐你们一个证据，你们今年要吃自生的，明年也要吃自长的，至于后年，你们要耕种收割，栽植葡萄园，吃其中的果子。

chapters.en: Once more a remnant of the kingdom of Judah will take root below and bear fruit above.
chapters.zh: 犹大家所逃脱余剩的，仍要往下扎根，向上结果。

chapters.en: For out of Jerusalem will come a remnant, and out of Mount Zion a band of survivors. The zeal of the LORD Almighty will accomplish this.
chapters.zh: 必有余剩的民，从耶路撒冷而出，必有逃脱的人，从锡安山而来。万军之耶和华的热心必成就这事。

chapters.en: “Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria: “He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow here. He will not come before it with shield or build a siege ramp against it.
chapters.zh: 所以耶和华论亚述王如此说，他必不得来到这城，也不在这里射箭，不得拿盾牌到城前，也不筑垒攻城。

chapters.en: By the way that he came he will return; he will not enter this city,” declares the LORD.
chapters.zh: 他从那条路来，必从那条路回去，必不得来到这城。这是耶和华说的。

chapters.en: “I will defend this city and save it, for my sake and for the sake of David my servant!”
chapters.zh: 因我为自己的缘故，又为我仆人大卫的缘故，必保护拯救这城。

chapters.en: Then the angel of the LORD went out and put to death a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up the next morning—there were all the dead bodies!
chapters.zh: 耶和华的使者出去，在亚述营中杀了十八万五千人。清早有人起来一看，都是死尸了。

chapters.en: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.
chapters.zh: 亚述王西拿基立，就拔营回去，住在尼尼微。

chapters.en: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisrok, his sons Adrammelek and Sharezer killed him with the sword, and they escaped to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son succeeded him as king.
chapters.zh: 一日在他的神，尼斯洛庙里叩拜，他儿子亚得米勒，和沙利色，用刀杀了他，就逃到亚拉腊地。他儿子以撒哈顿接续他作王。

chapters.en: In those days Hezekiah became ill and was at the point of death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz went to him and said, “This is what the LORD says: Put your house in order, because you are going to die; you will not recover.”
chapters.zh: 那时希西家病得要死，亚摩斯的儿子先知以赛亚去见他，对他说，耶和华如此说，你当留遗命与你的家，因为你必死不能活了。

chapters.en: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
chapters.zh: 希西家就转脸朝墙，祷告耶和华说，

chapters.en: “Remember, LORD, how I have walked before you faithfully and with wholehearted devotion and have done what is good in your eyes.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，求你记念我在你面前怎样存完全的心，按诚实行事，又作你眼中所看为善的。希西家就痛哭了。

chapters.en: Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
chapters.zh: 耶和华的话临到以赛亚说，

chapters.en: “Go and tell Hezekiah, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears; I will add fifteen years to your life.
chapters.zh: 你去告诉希西家说，耶和华你祖大卫的神如此说，我听见了你的祷告，看见了你的眼泪，我必加增你十五年的寿数。

chapters.en: And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.
chapters.zh: 并且我要救你和这城脱离亚述王的手，也要保护这城。

chapters.en: “ ‘This is the LORD’s sign to you that the LORD will do what he has promised:
chapters.zh: 我耶和华必成就我所说的，我先给你一个兆头。

chapters.en: I will make the shadow cast by the sun go back the ten steps it has gone down on the stairway of Ahaz.’ ” So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had gone down.
chapters.zh: 就是叫亚哈斯的日晷，向前进的日影往后退十度。于是前进的日影，果然在日晷上往后退了十度。

chapters.en: A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah after his illness and recovery:
chapters.zh: 犹大王希西家患病，已经痊愈，就作诗说，

chapters.en: I said, “In the prime of my life must I go through the gates of death and be robbed of the rest of my years?”
chapters.zh: 我说，正在我中年（或作晌午）之日，必进入阴间的门。我余剩的年岁不得享受。

chapters.en: I said, “I will not again see the LORD himself in the land of the living; no longer will I look on my fellow man, or be with those who now dwell in this world.
chapters.zh: 我说，我必不得见耶和华，就是在活人之地不见耶和华。我与世上的居民不再见面。

chapters.en: Like a shepherd’s tent my house has been pulled down and taken from me. Like a weaver I have rolled up my life, and he has cut me off from the loom; day and night you made an end of me.
chapters.zh: 我的住处被迁去离开我，好像牧人的帐棚一样。我将性命卷起，像织布的卷布一样。耶和华必将我从机头剪断，从早到晚，他要使我完结。

chapters.en: I waited patiently till dawn, but like a lion he broke all my bones; day and night you made an end of me.
chapters.zh: 我使自己安静直到天亮。他像狮子折断我一切的骨头，从早到晚，他要使我完结。

chapters.en: I cried like a swift or thrush, I moaned like a mourning dove. My eyes grew weak as I looked to the heavens. I am being threatened; Lord, come to my aid!”
chapters.zh: 我像燕子呢喃。像白鹤鸣叫。又像鸽子哀鸣。我因仰观，眼睛困倦。耶和华阿，我受欺压。求你为我作保。

chapters.en: But what can I say? He has spoken to me, and he himself has done this. I will walk humbly all my years because of this anguish of my soul.
chapters.zh: 我可说什么呢？他应许我的，也给我成就了。我因心里的苦楚，在一生的年日，必悄悄而行。

chapters.en: Lord, by such things people live; and my spirit finds life in them too. You restored me to health and let me live.
chapters.zh: 主阿，人得存活，乃在乎此。我灵存活，也全在此。所以求你使我痊愈，仍然存活。

chapters.en: Surely it was for my benefit that I suffered such anguish. In your love you kept me from the pit of destruction; you have put all my sins behind your back.
chapters.zh: 看哪，我受大苦，本为使我得平安，你因爱我的灵魂，（或作生命）便救我脱离败坏的坑。因为你将我一切的罪，扔在你的背后。

chapters.en: For the grave cannot praise you, death cannot sing your praise; those who go down to the pit cannot hope for your faithfulness.
chapters.zh: 原来阴间不能称谢你，死亡不能颂扬你，下坑的人不能盼望你的诚实。

chapters.en: The living, the living—they praise you, as I am doing today; parents tell their children about your faithfulness.
chapters.zh: 只有活人，活人必称谢你，像我今日称谢你一样。为父的，必使儿女知道你的诚实。

chapters.en: The LORD will save me, and we will sing with stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the temple of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 耶和华肯救我，所以我们要一生一世，在耶和华殿中用丝弦的乐器，唱我的诗歌。

chapters.en: Isaiah had said, “Prepare a poultice of figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover.”
chapters.zh: 以赛亚说，当取一块无花果饼来，贴在疮上，王必痊愈。

chapters.en: Hezekiah had asked, “What will be the sign that I will go up to the temple of the LORD?”
chapters.zh: 希西家问说，我能上耶和华的殿，有什么兆头呢？

chapters.en: At that time Marduk-Baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent Hezekiah letters and a gift, because he had heard of his illness and recovery.
chapters.zh: 那时巴比伦王巴拉但的儿子米罗达巴拉但，听见希西家病而痊愈，就送书信和礼物给他。

chapters.en: Hezekiah received the envoys gladly and showed them what was in his storehouses—the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine olive oil—his entire armory and everything found among his treasures. There was nothing in his palace or in all his kingdom that Hezekiah did not show them.
chapters.zh: 希西家喜欢见使者，就把自己宝库的金子，银子，香料，贵重的膏油，和他武库的一切军器，并所有的财宝都给他们看。他家中和全国之内，希西家没有一样不给他们看的。

chapters.en: Then Isaiah the prophet went to King Hezekiah and asked, “What did those men say, and where did they come from?” “From a distant land,” Hezekiah replied. “They came to me from Babylon.”
chapters.zh: 于是先知以赛亚来见希西家王，问他说，这些人说什么？他们从哪里来见你？希西家说，他们从远方的巴比伦来见我。

chapters.en: The prophet asked, “What did they see in your palace?” “They saw everything in my palace,” Hezekiah said. “There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them.”
chapters.zh: 以赛亚说，他们在你家里看见了什么？希西家说，凡我家中所有的，他们都看见了，我财宝中没有一样不给他们看的。

chapters.en: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD Almighty:
chapters.zh: 以赛亚对希西家说，你要听万军之耶和华的话。

chapters.en: The time will surely come when everything in your palace, and all that your predecessors have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
chapters.zh: 日子必到，凡你家里所有的，并你列祖积蓄到如今的，都要被掳到巴比伦去，不留下一样，这是耶和华说的。

chapters.en: And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood who will be born to you, will be taken away, and they will become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
chapters.zh: 并且从你本身所生的众子，其中必有被掳去，在巴比伦王宫里当太监的。

chapters.en: “The word of the LORD you have spoken is good,” Hezekiah replied. For he thought, “There will be peace and security in my lifetime.”
chapters.zh: 希西家对以赛亚说，你所说耶和华的话甚好，因为在我的年日中，必有太平和稳固的景况。

chapters.en: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
chapters.zh: 你们的神说，你们要安慰，安慰我的百姓。

chapters.en: Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and proclaim to her that her hard service has been completed, that her sin has been paid for, that she has received from the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.
chapters.zh: 要对耶路撒冷说安慰的话，又向他宣告说，他争战的日子已满了，他的罪孽赦免了，他为自己的一切罪，从耶和华手中加倍受罚。

chapters.en: A voice of one calling: “In the wilderness prepare the way for the LORD ; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
chapters.zh: 有人声喊着说，在旷野预备耶和华的路，（或作在旷野有人声喊着说，当预备耶和华的路），在沙漠地修平我们神的道。

chapters.en: Every valley shall be raised up, every mountain and hill made low; the rough ground shall become level, the rugged places a plain.
chapters.zh: 一切山洼都要填满，大小山冈都要削平，高高低低的要改为平坦，崎崎岖岖的必成为平原。

chapters.en: And the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all people will see it together. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华的荣耀必然显现，凡有血气的，必一同看见，因为这是耶和华亲口说的。

chapters.en: A voice says, “Cry out.” And I said, “What shall I cry?” “All people are like grass, and all their faithfulness is like the flowers of the field.
chapters.zh: 有人声说，你喊叫吧。有一个说，我喊叫什么呢？说，凡有血气的，尽都如草，他的美容，都像野地的花。

chapters.en: The grass withers and the flowers fall, because the breath of the LORD blows on them. Surely the people are grass.
chapters.zh: 草必枯干，花必凋残，因为耶和华的气吹在其上。百姓诚然是草。

chapters.en: The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God endures forever.”
chapters.zh: 草必枯干，花必凋残，惟有我们神的话，必永远立定。

chapters.en: You who bring good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who bring good news to Jerusalem,lift up your voice with a shout, lift it up, do not be afraid; say to the towns of Judah, “Here is your God!”
chapters.zh: 报好信息给锡安的阿，你要登高山。报好信息给耶路撒冷的阿，你要极力扬声。扬声不要惧怕，对犹大的城邑说，看哪，你们的神。

chapters.en: See, the Sovereign LORD comes with power, and he rules with a mighty arm. See, his reward is with him, and his recompense accompanies him.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华必像大能者临到，他的膀臂必为他掌权。他的赏赐在他那里，他的报应在他面前。

chapters.en: He tends his flock like a shepherd: He gathers the lambs in his arms and carries them close to his heart; he gently leads those that have young.
chapters.zh: 他必像牧人牧养自己的羊群，用膀臂聚集羊羔抱在怀中，慢慢引导那乳养小羊的。

chapters.en: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or with the breadth of his hand marked off the heavens? Who has held the dust of the earth in a basket, or weighed the mountains on the scales and the hills in a balance?
chapters.zh: 谁曾用手心量诸水，用手虎口量苍天，用升斗盛大地的尘土，用秤称山岭，用天平平岗陵呢？

chapters.en: Who can fathom the Spirit of the LORD, or instruct the LORD as his counselor?
chapters.zh: 谁曾测度耶和华的心（或作谁曾指示耶和华的灵），或作他的谋士指教他呢？

chapters.en: Whom did the LORD consult to enlighten him, and who taught him the right way? Who was it that taught him knowledge, or showed him the path of understanding?
chapters.zh: 他与谁商议，谁教导他，谁将公平的路指示他，又将知识教训他，将通达的道指教他呢？

chapters.en: Surely the nations are like a drop in a bucket; they are regarded as dust on the scales; he weighs the islands as though they were fine dust.
chapters.zh: 看哪，万民都像水桶的一滴，又算如天平上的微尘。他举起众海岛，好像极微之物。

chapters.en: Lebanon is not sufficient for altar fires, nor its animals enough for burnt offerings.
chapters.zh: 利巴嫩的树林不够当柴烧，其中的走兽也不够作燔祭。

chapters.en: Before him all the nations are as nothing; they are regarded by him as worthless and less than nothing.
chapters.zh: 万民在他面前好像虚无，被他看为不及虚无，乃为虚空。

chapters.en: With whom, then, will you compare God? To what image will you liken him?
chapters.zh: 你们究竟将谁比神，用什么形像与神比较呢？

chapters.en: As for an idol, a metalworker casts it, and a goldsmith overlays it with gold and fashions silver chains for it.
chapters.zh: 偶像是匠人铸造，银匠用金包裹，为它铸造银链。

chapters.en: A person too poor to present such an offering selects wood that will not rot; they look for a skilled worker to set up an idol that will not topple.
chapters.zh: 穷乏献不起这样供物的，就拣选不能朽坏的树木，为自己寻找巧匠，立起不能摇动的偶像。

chapters.en: Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the earth was founded?
chapters.zh: 你们岂不曾知道吗？你们岂不曾听见吗？从起初岂没有人告诉你们吗？自从立地的根基，你们岂没有明白吗？

chapters.en: He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its people are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a canopy, and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
chapters.zh: 神坐在地球大圈之上，地上的居民好像蝗虫。他铺张穹苍如幔子，展开诸天如可住的帐棚。

chapters.en: He brings princes to naught and reduces the rulers of this world to nothing.
chapters.zh: 他使君王归于虚无，使地上的审判官成为虚空。

chapters.en: No sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, no sooner do they take root in the ground, than he blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like chaff.
chapters.zh: 他们是刚才栽上，（刚才或作不曾下同）刚才种上，根也刚才扎在地里，他一吹在其上，便都枯干，旋风将他们吹去，像碎秸一样。

chapters.en: “To whom will you compare me? Or who is my equal?” says the Holy One.
chapters.zh: 那圣者说，你们将谁比我，叫他与我相等呢？

chapters.en: Lift up your eyes and look to the heavens: Who created all these? He who brings out the starry host one by one and calls forth each of them by name. Because of his great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing.
chapters.zh: 你们向上举目，看谁创造这万象，按数目领出，他一一称其名。因他的权能，又因他的大能大力，连一个都不缺。

chapters.en: Why do you complain, Jacob? Why do you say, Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD; my cause is disregarded by my God”?
chapters.zh: 雅各阿，你为何说，我的道路向耶和华隐藏？以色列阿，你为何言，我的冤屈神并不查问？

chapters.en: Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary, and his understanding no one can fathom.
chapters.zh: 你岂不曾知道吗？你岂不曾听见吗？永在的神耶和华，创造地极的主，并不疲乏，也不困倦。他的智慧无法测度。

chapters.en: He gives strength to the weary and increases the power of the weak.
chapters.zh: 疲乏的，他赐能力。软弱的，他加力量。

chapters.en: Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall;
chapters.zh: 就是少年人也要疲乏困倦，强壮的也必全然跌倒。

chapters.en: but those who hope in the LORD will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint.
chapters.zh: 但那等候耶和华的，必从新得力，他们必如鹰展翅上腾，他们奔跑却不困倦，行走却不疲乏。

chapters.en: “Be silent before me, you islands! Let the nations renew their strength! Let them come forward and speak; let us meet together at the place of judgment.
chapters.zh: 众海岛阿，当在我面前静默，众民当从新得力，都要近前来才可以说话。我们可以彼此辩论。

chapters.en: “Who has stirred up one from the east, calling him in righteousness to his service ? He hands nations over to him and subdues kings before him. He turns them to dust with his sword, to windblown chaff with his bow.
chapters.zh: 谁从东方兴起一人，凭公义召他来到脚前呢？耶和华将列国交给他，使他管辖君王，把他们如灰尘交与他的刀，如风吹的碎秸交与他的弓。

chapters.en: He pursues them and moves on unscathed, by a path his feet have not traveled before.
chapters.zh: 他追赶他们，走他所未走的道，坦然前行。

chapters.en: Who has done this and carried it through, calling forth the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD—with the first of them and with the last—I am he.”
chapters.zh: 谁行作成就这事，从起初宣召历代呢？就是我耶和华，我是首先的。也与末后的同在。

chapters.en: The islands have seen it and fear; the ends of the earth tremble. They approach and come forward;
chapters.zh: 海岛看见就都害怕，地极也都战兢，就近前来。

chapters.en: they help each other and say to their companions, “Be strong!”
chapters.zh: 他们各人帮助邻舍，各人对弟兄说，壮胆吧。

chapters.en: The metalworker encourages the goldsmith, and the one who smooths with the hammer spurs on the one who strikes the anvil. One says of the welding, “It is good.” The other nails down the idol so it will not topple.
chapters.zh: 木匠勉励银匠，用锤打光的勉励打砧的，论焊工说，焊得好。又用钉子钉稳，免得偶像动摇。

chapters.en: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, you descendants of Abraham my friend,
chapters.zh: 惟你以色列我的仆人，雅各我所拣选的，我朋友亚伯拉罕的后裔，

chapters.en: I took you from the ends of the earth, from its farthest corners I called you. I said, ‘You are my servant’; I have chosen you and have not rejected you.
chapters.zh: 你是我从地极所领（原文作抓）来的，从地角所召来的，且对你说，你是我的仆人，我拣选你并不弃绝你。

chapters.en: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you and help you; I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.
chapters.zh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在。不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。我必坚固你，我必帮助你，我必用我公义的右手扶持你。

chapters.en: “All who rage against you will surely be ashamed and disgraced; those who oppose you will be as nothing and perish.
chapters.zh: 凡向你发怒的，必都抱愧蒙羞。与你相争的，必如无有，并要灭亡。

chapters.en: Though you search for your enemies, you will not find them. Those who wage war against you will be as nothing at all.
chapters.zh: 与你争竞的，你要找他们也找不着。与你争战的，必如无有，成为虚无。

chapters.en: For I am the LORD your God who takes hold of your right hand and says to you, Do not fear; I will help you.
chapters.zh: 因为我耶和华你的神，必搀扶你的右手，对你说，不要害怕，我必帮助你。

chapters.en: Do not be afraid, you worm Jacob, little Israel, do not fear, for I myself will help you,” declares the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
chapters.zh: 你这虫雅各，和你们以色列人，不要害怕。耶和华说，我必帮助你。你的救赎主，就是以色列的圣者。

chapters.en: “See, I will make you into a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and reduce the hills to chaff.
chapters.zh: 看哪，我已使你成为有快齿打粮的新器具，你要把山岭打得粉碎，使冈陵如同糠秕。

chapters.en: You will winnow them, the wind will pick them up, and a gale will blow them away. But you will rejoice in the LORD and glory in the Holy One of Israel.
chapters.zh: 你要把他簸扬风要吹去，旋风要把他刮散。你倒要以耶和华为喜乐，以以色列的圣者为夸耀。

chapters.en: “The poor and needy search for water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. But I the LORD will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
chapters.zh: 困苦穷乏人寻求水却没有，他们因口渴，舌头干燥。我耶和华必应允他们，我以色列的神必不离弃他们。

chapters.en: I will make rivers flow on barren heights, and springs within the valleys. I will turn the desert into pools of water, and the parched ground into springs.
chapters.zh: 我要在净光的高处开江河，在谷中开泉源，我要使沙漠变为水池，使干地变为涌泉。

chapters.en: I will put in the desert the cedar and the acacia, the myrtle and the olive. I will set junipers in the wasteland, the fir and the cypress together,
chapters.zh: 我要在旷野种上香柏树，皂荚树，番石榴树，和野橄榄树。我在沙漠要把松树，杉树，并黄杨树，一同栽植。

chapters.en: so that people may see and know, may consider and understand, that the hand of the LORD has done this, that the Holy One of Israel has created it.
chapters.zh: 好叫人看见，知道，思想，明白，这是耶和华的手所作的，是以色列的圣者所造的。

chapters.en: “Present your case,” says the LORD. “Set forth your arguments,” says Jacob’s King.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对假神说，你们要呈上你们的案件，雅各的君说，你们要声明你们确实的理由。

chapters.en: “Tell us, you idols, what is going to happen. Tell us what the former things were, so that we may consider them and know their final outcome. Or declare to us the things to come,
chapters.zh: 可以声明，指示我们将来必遇的事，说明先前的是什么事，好叫我们思索，得知事的结局，或者把将来的事指示我们。

chapters.en: tell us what the future holds, so we may know that you are gods. Do something, whether good or bad, so that we will be dismayed and filled with fear.
chapters.zh: 要说明后来的事，好叫我们知道你们是神，你们或降福，或降祸，使我们惊奇，一同观看。

chapters.en: But you are less than nothing and your works are utterly worthless; whoever chooses you is detestable.
chapters.zh: 看哪，你们属乎虚无，你们的作为也属乎虚空。那选择你们的是可憎恶的。

chapters.en: “I have stirred up one from the north, and he comes— one from the rising sun who calls on my name. He treads on rulers as if they were mortar, as if he were a potter treading the clay.
chapters.zh: 我从北方兴起一人，他是求告我名的，从日出之地而来。他必临到掌权的，好像临到灰泥，仿佛窑匠踹泥一样。

chapters.en: Who told of this from the beginning, so we could know, or beforehand, so we could say, ‘He was right’? No one told of this, no one foretold it, no one heard any words from you.
chapters.zh: 谁从起初指明这事，使我们知道呢？谁从先前说明，使我们说，他不错呢？谁也没有指明，谁也没有说明。谁也没有听见你们的话。

chapters.en: I was the first to tell Zion, ‘Look, here they are!’ I gave to Jerusalem a messenger of good news.
chapters.zh: 我首先对锡安说，看哪，我要将一位报好信息的赐给耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: I look but there is no one— no one among the gods to give counsel, no one to give answer when I ask them.
chapters.zh: 我看的时候并没有人，我问的时候他们中间也没有谋士，可以回答一句。

chapters.en: See, they are all false! Their deeds amount to nothing; their images are but wind and confusion.
chapters.zh: 看哪，他们和他们的工作，都是虚空，且是虚无。他们所铸的偶像都是风，都是虚的。

chapters.en: “Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom I delight; I will put my Spirit on him, and he will bring justice to the nations.
chapters.zh: 看哪，我的仆人，我所扶持，所拣选，心里所喜悦的，我已将我的灵赐给他，他必将公理传给外邦。

chapters.en: He will not shout or cry out, or raise his voice in the streets.
chapters.zh: 他不喧嚷，不扬声，也不使街上听见他的声音。

chapters.en: A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out. In faithfulness he will bring forth justice;
chapters.zh: 压伤的芦苇，他不折断。将残的灯火，他不吹灭。他凭真实将公理传开。

chapters.en: he will not falter or be discouraged till he establishes justice on earth. In his teaching the islands will put their hope.”
chapters.zh: 他不灰心，也不丧胆，直到他在地上设立公理。海岛都等候他的训诲。

chapters.en: This is what God the LORD says— the Creator of the heavens, who stretches them out, who spreads out the earth with all that springs from it, who gives breath to its people, and life to those who walk on it:
chapters.zh: 创造诸天，铺张穹苍，将地和地所出的一并铺开，赐气息给地上的众人，又赐灵性给行在其上之人的神耶和华，他如此说，

chapters.en: “I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness; I will take hold of your hand. I will keep you and will make you to be a covenant for the people and a light for the Gentiles,
chapters.zh: 我耶和华凭公义召你，必搀扶你的手，保守你，使你作众民的中保，（中保原文作约）作外邦人的光，

chapters.en: to open eyes that are blind, to free captives from prison and to release from the dungeon those who sit in darkness.
chapters.zh: 开瞎子的眼，领被囚的出牢狱，领坐黑暗的出监牢。

chapters.en: “I am the LORD; that is my name! I will not yield my glory to another or my praise to idols.
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华，这是我的名。我必不将我的荣耀归给假神，也不将我的称赞归给雕刻的偶像。

chapters.en: See, the former things have taken place, and new things I declare; before they spring into being I announce them to you.”
chapters.zh: 看哪，先前的事已经成就，现在我将新事说明，这事未发以先，我就说给你们听。

chapters.en: Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, you islands, and all who live in them.
chapters.zh: 航海的，和海中所有的，海岛，和其上的居民，都当向耶和华唱新歌，从地极赞美他。

chapters.en: Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices; let the settlements where Kedar lives rejoice. Let the people of Sela sing for joy; let them shout from the mountaintops.
chapters.zh: 旷野和其中的城邑，并基达人居住的村庄，都当扬声。西拉的居民当欢呼，在山顶上呐喊。

chapters.en: Let them give glory to the LORD and proclaim his praise in the islands.
chapters.zh: 他们当将荣耀归给耶和华，在海岛中传扬他的颂赞。

chapters.en: The LORD will march out like a champion, like a warrior he will stir up his zeal; with a shout he will raise the battle cry and will triumph over his enemies.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必像勇士出去，必像战士激动热心，要喊叫，大声呐喊，要用大力攻击仇敌。

chapters.en: “For a long time I have kept silent, I have been quiet and held myself back. But now, like a woman in childbirth, I cry out, I gasp and pant.
chapters.zh: 我许久闭口不言，静默不语，现在我要喊叫像产难的妇人，我要急气而喘哮。

chapters.en: I will lay waste the mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation; I will turn rivers into islands and dry up the pools.
chapters.zh: 我要使大山小冈变为荒场，使其上的花草都枯干，我要使江河变为洲岛，使水池都干涸。

chapters.en: I will lead the blind by ways they have not known, along unfamiliar paths I will guide them; I will turn the darkness into light before them and make the rough places smooth. These are the things I will do; I will not forsake them.
chapters.zh: 我要引瞎子行不认识的道，领他们走不知道的路。在他们面前使黑暗变为光明，使弯曲变为平直。这些事我都要行，并不离弃他们。

chapters.en: But those who trust in idols, who say to images, ‘You are our gods,’ will be turned back in utter shame.
chapters.zh: 倚靠雕刻的偶像，对铸造的偶像说，你是我们的神，这等人要退后，全然蒙羞。

chapters.en: “Hear, you deaf; look, you blind, and see!
chapters.zh: 你们这耳聋的听吧。你们这眼瞎的看吧。使你们能看见。

chapters.en: Who is blind but my servant, and deaf like the messenger I send? Who is blind like the one in covenant with me, blind like the servant of the LORD?
chapters.zh: 谁比我的仆人眼瞎呢？谁比我差遣的使者耳聋呢？谁瞎眼像那与我和好的，谁瞎眼像耶和华的仆人呢？

chapters.en: You have seen many things, but you pay no attention; your ears are open, but you do not listen.”
chapters.zh: 你看见许多事却不领会。耳朵开通却不听见。

chapters.en: It pleased the LORD for the sake of his righteousness to make his law great and glorious.
chapters.zh: 耶和华因自己公义的缘故，喜欢使律法（或作训诲）为大，为尊。

chapters.en: But this is a people plundered and looted, all of them trapped in pits or hidden away in prisons. They have become plunder, with no one to rescue them; they have been made loot, with no one to say, “Send them back.”
chapters.zh: 但这百姓是被抢被夺的，都牢笼在坑中，隐藏在狱里，他们作掠物，无人拯救，作掳物，无人说交还。

chapters.en: Which of you will listen to this or pay close attention in time to come?
chapters.zh: 你们中间谁肯侧耳听此，谁肯留心而听，以防将来呢？

chapters.en: Who handed Jacob over to become loot, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? For they would not follow his ways; they did not obey his law.
chapters.zh: 谁将雅各交出当作掳物，将以色列交给抢夺的呢？岂不是耶和华吗？就是我们所得罪的那位。他们不肯遵行他的道，也不听从他的训诲。

chapters.en: So he poured out on them his burning anger, the violence of war. It enveloped them in flames, yet they did not understand; it consumed them, but they did not take it to heart.
chapters.zh: 所以他将猛烈的怒气，和争战的勇力，倾倒在以色列的身上。在他四围如火着起，他还不知道，烧着他，他也不介意。

chapters.en: But now, this is what the LORD says— he who created you, Jacob, he who formed you, Israel: “Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have summoned you by name; you are mine.
chapters.zh: 雅各阿，创造你的耶和华，以色列阿，造成你的那位，现在如此说，你不要害怕，因为我救赎了你。我曾提你的名召你，你是属我的。

chapters.en: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and when you pass through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned; the flames will not set you ablaze.
chapters.zh: 你从水中经过，我必与你同在。你趟过江河，水必不漫过你。你从火中行过，必不被烧，火焰也不着在你身上。

chapters.en: For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I give Egypt for your ransom, Cush and Seba in your stead.
chapters.zh: 因为我是耶和华你的神，是以色列的圣者你的救主。我已经使埃及作你的赎价，使古实和西巴代替你。

chapters.en: Since you are precious and honored in my sight, and because I love you, I will give people in exchange for you, nations in exchange for your life.
chapters.zh: 因我看你为宝为尊，又因我爱你，所以我使人代替你，使列邦人替换你的生命。

chapters.en: Do not be afraid, for I am with you; I will bring your children from the east and gather you from the west.
chapters.zh: 不要害怕，因我与你同在。我必领你的后裔从东方来，又从西方招聚你。

chapters.en: I will say to the north, ‘Give them up!’ and to the south, ‘Do not hold them back.’ Bring my sons from afar and my daughters from the ends of the earth—
chapters.zh: 我要对北方说，交出来。对南方说，不要拘留。将我的众子从远方带来，将我的众女从地极领回，

chapters.en: everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed and made.”
chapters.zh: 就是凡称为我名下的人，是我为自己的荣耀创造的，是我所作成，所造作的。

chapters.en: Lead out those who have eyes but are blind, who have ears but are deaf.
chapters.zh: 你要将有眼而瞎，有耳而聋的民都带出来。

chapters.en: All the nations gather together and the peoples assemble. Which of their gods foretold this and proclaimed to us the former things? Let them bring in their witnesses to prove they were right, so that others may hear and say, “It is true.”
chapters.zh: 任凭万国聚集，任凭众民会合，其中谁能将此声明，并将先前的事说给我们听呢？他们可以带出见证来，自显为是，或者他们听见便说，这是真的。

chapters.en: “You are my witnesses,” declares the LORD, “and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, nor will there be one after me.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，你们是我的见证，我所拣选的仆人。既是这样，便可以知道，且信服我，又明白我就是耶和华，在我以前没有真神，（真原文作造作的）在我以后也必没有。

chapters.en: I, even I, am the LORD, and apart from me there is no savior.
chapters.zh: 惟有我是耶和华，除我以外没有救主。

chapters.en: I have revealed and saved and proclaimed— I, and not some foreign god among you. You are my witnesses,” declares the LORD, “that I am God.
chapters.zh: 我曾指示，我曾拯救，我曾说明。并且在你们中间没有别神，所以耶和华说，你们是我的见证，我也是神。

chapters.en: Yes, and from ancient days I am he. No one can deliver out of my hand. When I act, who can reverse it?”
chapters.zh: 自从有日子以来，我就是神。谁也不能救人脱离我手，我要行事，谁能阻止呢？

chapters.en: This is what the LORD says— your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “For your sake I will send to Babylon and bring down as fugitives all the Babylonians,in the ships in which they took pride.
chapters.zh: 耶和华你们的救赎主，以色列的圣者如此说，因你们的缘故，我已经打发人到巴比伦去，并且我要使迦勒底人如逃民，都坐自己喜乐的船下来。

chapters.en: I am the LORD, your Holy One, Israel’s Creator, your King.”
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华你们的圣者，是创造以色列的，是你们的君王。

chapters.en: This is what the LORD says— he who made a way through the sea, a path through the mighty waters,
chapters.zh: 耶和华在沧海中开道，在大水中开路。

chapters.en: who drew out the chariots and horses, the army and reinforcements together, and they lay there, never to rise again, extinguished, snuffed out like a wick:
chapters.zh: 使车辆，马匹，军兵，勇士都出来，一同躺下不再起来，他们灭没好像熄灭的灯火。

chapters.en: “Forget the former things; do not dwell on the past.
chapters.zh: 耶和华如此说，你们不要记念从前的事，也不要思想古时的事。

chapters.en: See, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it? I am making a way in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland.
chapters.zh: 看哪，我要做一件新事，如今要发现，你们岂不知道吗？我必在旷野开道路，在沙漠开江河。

chapters.en: The wild animals honor me, the jackals and the owls, because I provide water in the wilderness and streams in the wasteland, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
chapters.zh: 野地的走兽必尊重我，野狗和鸵鸟也必如此，因我使旷野有水，使沙漠有河，好赐给我的百姓我的选民喝。

chapters.en: the people I formed for myself that they may proclaim my praise.
chapters.zh: 这百姓是我为自己所造的，好述说我的美德。

chapters.en: “Yet you have not called on me, Jacob, you have not wearied yourselves for me, Israel.
chapters.zh: 雅各阿，你并没有求告我。以色列阿，你倒厌烦我。

chapters.en: You have not brought me sheep for burnt offerings, nor honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with grain offerings nor wearied you with demands for incense.
chapters.zh: 你没有将你的羊带来给我作燔祭，也没有用祭物尊敬我。我没有因供物使你服劳，也没有因乳香使你厌烦。

chapters.en: You have not bought any fragrant calamus for me, or lavished on me the fat of your sacrifices. But you have burdened me with your sins and wearied me with your offenses.
chapters.zh: 你没有用银子为我买菖蒲，也没有用祭物的脂油使我饱足，倒使我因你的罪恶服劳，使我因你的罪孽厌烦。

chapters.en: “I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions, for my own sake, and remembers your sins no more.
chapters.zh: 惟有我为自己的缘故涂抹你的过犯，我也不记念你的罪恶。

chapters.en: Review the past for me, let us argue the matter together; state the case for your innocence.
chapters.zh: 你要提醒我，你我可以一同辩论，你可以将你的理陈明，自显为义。

chapters.en: Your first father sinned; those I sent to teach you rebelled against me.
chapters.zh: 你的始祖犯罪，你的师傅违背我。

chapters.en: So I disgraced the dignitaries of your temple; I consigned Jacob to destruction and Israel to scorn.
chapters.zh: 所以我要辱没圣所的首领，使雅各成为咒诅，使以色列成为辱骂。

chapters.en: “But now listen, Jacob, my servant, Israel, whom I have chosen.
chapters.zh: 我的仆人雅各，我所拣选的以色列阿，现在你当听。

chapters.en: This is what the LORD says— he who made you, who formed you in the womb, and who will help you: Do not be afraid, Jacob, my servant, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
chapters.zh: 造作你，又从你出胎造就你，并要帮助你的耶和华如此说，我的仆人雅各，我所拣选的耶书仑哪，不要害怕。

chapters.en: For I will pour water on the thirsty land, and streams on the dry ground; I will pour out my Spirit on your offspring, and my blessing on your descendants.
chapters.zh: 因为我要将水浇灌口渴的人，将河浇灌干旱之地。我要将我的灵浇灌你的后裔，将我的福浇灌你的子孙。

chapters.en: They will spring up like grass in a meadow, like poplar trees by flowing streams.
chapters.zh: 他们要发生在草中，像溪水旁的柳树。

chapters.en: Some will say, ‘I belong to the LORD’; others will call themselves by the name of Jacob; still others will write on their hand, ‘The LORD’s,’ and will take the name Israel.
chapters.zh: 这个要说，我是属耶和华的。那个要以雅各的名自称。又一个要亲手写归耶和华的（或作在手上写归耶和华）并自称为以色列。

chapters.en: “This is what the LORD says— Israel’s King and Redeemer, the LORD Almighty: I am the first and I am the last; apart from me there is no God.
chapters.zh: 耶和华以色列的君，以色列的救赎主万军之耶和华如此说，我是首先的，我是末后的，除我以外，再没有真神。

chapters.en: Who then is like me? Let him proclaim it. Let him declare and lay out before me what has happened since I established my ancient people, and what is yet to come— yes, let them foretell what will come.
chapters.zh: 自从我设立古时的民，谁能像我宣告，并且指明，又为自己陈说呢？让他将未来的事，和必成的事说明。

chapters.en: Do not tremble, do not be afraid. Did I not proclaim this and foretell it long ago? You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me? No, there is no other Rock; I know not one.”
chapters.zh: 你们不要恐惧，也不要害怕。我岂不是从上古就说明指示你们吗？并且你们是我的见证，除我以外，岂有真神吗？诚然没有磐石，我不知道一个。

chapters.en: All who make idols are nothing, and the things they treasure are worthless. Those who would speak up for them are blind; they are ignorant, to their own shame.
chapters.zh: 制造雕刻偶像的，尽都虚空。他们所喜悦的，都无益处。他们的见证，无所看见，无所知晓，他们便觉羞愧。

chapters.en: Who shapes a god and casts an idol, which can profit nothing?
chapters.zh: 谁制造神像，铸造无益的偶像？

chapters.en: People who do that will be put to shame; such craftsmen are only human beings. Let them all come together and take their stand; they will be brought down to terror and shame.
chapters.zh: 看哪，他的同伴都必羞愧，工匠也不过是人。任他们聚会，任他们站立，都必惧怕，一同羞愧。

chapters.en: The blacksmith takes a tool and works with it in the coals; he shapes an idol with hammers, he forges it with the might of his arm. He gets hungry and loses his strength; he drinks no water and grows faint.
chapters.zh: 铁匠把铁在火炭中烧热，用锤打铁器，用他有力的臂膀锤成。他饥饿而无力，不喝水而发倦。

chapters.en: The carpenter measures with a line and makes an outline with a marker; he roughs it out with chisels and marks it with compasses. He shapes it in human form, human form in all its glory, that it may dwell in a shrine.
chapters.zh: 木匠拉线，用笔划出样子。用刨子刨成形状，用圆尺划了模样，仿照人的体态，作成人形，好住在房屋中。

chapters.en: He cut down cedars, or perhaps took a cypress or oak. He let it grow among the trees of the forest, or planted a pine, and the rain made it grow.
chapters.zh: 他砍伐香柏树，又取柞（或作青桐）树和橡树，在树林中选定了一棵。他栽种松树得雨长养，

chapters.en: It is used as fuel for burning; some of it he takes and warms himself, he kindles a fire and bakes bread. But he also fashions a god and worships it; he makes an idol and bows down to it.
chapters.zh: 这树，人可用以烧火，他自己取些烤火，又烧着烤饼。而且作神像跪拜，作雕刻的偶像向它叩拜。
