chapters.en: Then he measured the court: It was square—a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide. And the altar was in front of the temple.
chapters.zh: 他又量内院，长一百肘，宽一百肘，是见方的。祭坛在殿前。

chapters.en: He brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the jambs of the portico; they were five cubits wide on either side. The width of the entrance was fourteen cubits and its projecting walls were three cubits wide on either side.
chapters.zh: 于是他带我到殿前的廊子，量廊子的墙柱。这面厚五肘，那面厚五肘。门两旁，这边三肘，那边三肘。

chapters.en: The portico was twenty cubits wide, and twelve cubits from front to back. It was reached by a flight of stairs, and there were pillars on each side of the jambs.
chapters.zh: 廊子长二十肘，宽十一肘。上廊子有台阶。靠近墙柱又有柱子，这边一根，那边一根。

chapters.en: Then the man brought me to the main hall and measured the jambs; the width of the jambs was six cubits on each side.
chapters.zh: 他带我到殿那里量墙柱，这面厚六肘，那面厚六肘，宽窄与会幕相同。

chapters.en: The entrance was ten cubits wide, and the projecting walls on each side of it were five cubits wide. He also measured the main hall; it was forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 门口宽十肘。门两旁，这边五肘，那边五肘。他量殿长四十肘，宽二十肘。

chapters.en: Then he went into the inner sanctuary and measured the jambs of the entrance; each was two cubits wide. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the projecting walls on each side of it were seven cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 他到内殿量墙柱，各厚二肘。门口宽六肘，门两旁各宽七肘。

chapters.en: And he measured the length of the inner sanctuary; it was twenty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits across the end of the main hall. He said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
chapters.zh: 他量内殿，长二十肘，宽二十肘。他对我说，这是至圣所。

chapters.en: Then he measured the wall of the temple; it was six cubits thick, and each side room around the temple was four cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 他又量殿墙，厚六肘。围着殿有旁屋，各宽四肘。

chapters.en: The side rooms were on three levels, one above another, thirty on each level. There were ledges all around the wall of the temple to serve as supports for the side rooms, so that the supports were not inserted into the wall of the temple.
chapters.zh: 旁屋有三层，层叠而上，每层排列三十间。旁屋的梁木搁在殿墙坎上，免得插入殿墙。

chapters.en: The side rooms all around the temple were wider at each successive level. The structure surrounding the temple was built in ascending stages, so that the rooms widened as one went upward. A stairway went up from the lowest floor to the top floor through the middle floor.
chapters.zh: 这围殿的旁屋越高越宽。因旁屋围殿悬叠而上，所以越上越宽，从下一层，由中一层，到上一层。

chapters.en: I saw that the temple had a raised base all around it, forming the foundation of the side rooms. It was the length of the rod, six long cubits.
chapters.zh: 我又见围着殿有高月台。旁屋的根基，高足一竿，就是六大肘。

chapters.en: The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick. The open area between the side rooms of the temple
chapters.zh: 旁屋的外墙厚五肘。旁屋之外还有余地。

chapters.en: and the priests’ rooms was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
chapters.zh: 在旁屋与对面的房屋中间有空地，宽二十肘。

chapters.en: There were entrances to the side rooms from the open area, one on the north and another on the south; and the base adjoining the open area was five cubits wide all around.
chapters.zh: 旁屋的门都向余地，一门向北，一门向南。周围的余地宽五肘。

chapters.en: The building facing the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
chapters.zh: 在西面空地之后有房子，宽七十肘，长九十肘，墙四围厚五肘。

chapters.en: Then he measured the temple; it was a hundred cubits long, and the temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long.
chapters.zh: 这样，他量殿，长一百肘，又量空地和那房子并墙，共长一百肘。

chapters.en: The width of the temple courtyard on the east, including the front of the temple, was a hundred cubits.
chapters.zh: 殿的前面和两旁的空地，宽一百肘。

chapters.en: Then he measured the length of the building facing the courtyard at the rear of the temple, including its galleries on each side; it was a hundred cubits. The main hall, the inner sanctuary and the portico facing the court,
chapters.zh: 他量空地后面的那房子，并两旁的楼廊，共长一百肘。

chapters.en: as well as the thresholds and the narrow windows and galleries around the three of them—everything beyond and including the threshold was covered with wood. The floor, the wall up to the windows, and the windows were covered.
chapters.zh: 内殿，院廊，门槛，严紧的窗棂，并对着门槛的三层楼廊，从地到窗棂（窗棂都有蔽子），

chapters.en: In the space above the outside of the entrance to the inner sanctuary and on the walls at regular intervals all around the inner and outer sanctuary
chapters.zh: 直到门以上，就是到内殿和外殿内外四围墙壁，都按尺寸用木板遮蔽。

chapters.en: were carved cherubim and palm trees. Palm trees alternated with cherubim. Each cherub had two faces:
chapters.zh: 墙上雕刻基路伯和棕树。每二基路伯中间有一棵棕树，每基路伯有二脸。

chapters.en: the face of a human being toward the palm tree on one side and the face of a lion toward the palm tree on the other. They were carved all around the whole temple.
chapters.zh: 这边有人脸向着棕树，那边有狮子脸向着棕树，殿内周围都是如此。

chapters.en: From the floor to the area above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the main hall.
chapters.zh: 从地至门以上，都有基路伯和棕树。殿墙就是这样。

chapters.en: The main hall had a rectangular doorframe, and the one at the front of the Most Holy Place was similar.
chapters.zh: 殿的门柱是方的。至圣所的前面，形状和殿的形状一样。

chapters.en: There was a wooden altar three cubits high and two cubits square ; its corners, its base and its sides were of wood. The man said to me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 坛是木头作的，高三肘，长二肘。坛角和坛面，并四旁，都是木头作的。他对我说，这是耶和华面前的桌子。

chapters.en: Both the main hall and the Most Holy Place had double doors.
chapters.zh: 殿和至圣所的门各有两扇。

chapters.en: Each door had two leaves—two hinged leaves for each door.
chapters.zh: 每扇分两扇，这两扇是摺叠的。这边门分两扇，那边门也分两扇。

chapters.en: And on the doors of the main hall were carved cherubim and palm trees like those carved on the walls, and there was a wooden overhang on the front of the portico.
chapters.zh: 殿的门扇上雕刻基路伯和棕树，与刻在墙上的一般。在外头廊前有木槛。

chapters.en: On the sidewalls of the portico were narrow windows with palm trees carved on each side. The side rooms of the temple also had overhangs.
chapters.zh: 廊这边那边都有严紧的窗棂和棕树。殿的旁屋和槛就是这样。

chapters.en: Then the man led me northward into the outer court and brought me to the rooms opposite the temple courtyard and opposite the outer wall on the north side.
chapters.zh: 他带我出来向北，到外院，又带我进入圣屋。这圣屋一排顺着空地，一排与北边铺石地之屋相对。

chapters.en: The building whose door faced north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 这圣屋长一百肘，宽五十肘，有向北的门。

chapters.en: Both in the section twenty cubits from the inner court and in the section opposite the pavement of the outer court, gallery faced gallery at the three levels.
chapters.zh: 对着内院那二十肘宽之空地，又对着外院的铺石地，在第三层楼上有楼廊对着楼廊。

chapters.en: In front of the rooms was an inner passageway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long. Their doors were on the north.
chapters.zh: 在圣屋前有一条夹道，宽十肘，长一百肘。房门都向北。

chapters.en: Now the upper rooms were narrower, for the galleries took more space from them than from the rooms on the lower and middle floors of the building.
chapters.zh: 圣屋因为楼廊占去些地方，所以上层比中下两层窄些。

chapters.en: The rooms on the top floor had no pillars, as the courts had; so they were smaller in floor space than those on the lower and middle floors.
chapters.zh: 圣屋有三层，却无柱子，不像外院的屋子有柱子。所以上层比中下两层更窄。

chapters.en: There was an outer wall parallel to the rooms and the outer court; it extended in front of the rooms for fifty cubits.
chapters.zh: 圣屋外，东边有墙，靠着外院，长五十肘。

chapters.en: While the row of rooms on the side next to the outer court was fifty cubits long, the row on the side nearest the sanctuary was a hundred cubits long.
chapters.zh: 靠着外院的圣屋长五十肘。殿北面的圣屋长一百肘。

chapters.en: The lower rooms had an entrance on the east side as one enters them from the outer court.
chapters.zh: 在圣屋以下，东头有进入之处，就是从外院进入之处。

chapters.en: On the south side along the length of the wall of the outer court, adjoining the temple courtyard and opposite the outer wall, were rooms
chapters.zh: 向南（原文作东）在内院墙里有圣屋，一排与铺石地之屋相对，一排顺着空地。

chapters.en: with a passageway in front of them. These were like the rooms on the north; they had the same length and width, with similar exits and dimensions. Similar to the doorways on the north
chapters.zh: 这圣屋前的夹道与北边圣屋的夹道长宽一样。出入之处与北屋门的样式相同。

chapters.en: were the doorways of the rooms on the south. There was a doorway at the beginning of the passageway that was parallel to the corresponding wall extending eastward, by which one enters the rooms.
chapters.zh: 正在墙前，夹道的东头，有门可以进入，与向南圣屋的门一样。

chapters.en: Then he said to me, “The north and south rooms facing the temple courtyard are the priests’ rooms, where the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will put the most holy offerings—the grain offerings, the sin offerings and the guilt offerings—for the place is holy.
chapters.zh: 他对我说，顺着空地的南屋北屋，都是圣屋。亲近耶和华的祭司当在那里吃至圣的物，也当在那里放至圣的物，就是素祭，赎罪祭，和赎愆祭，因此处为圣。

chapters.en: Once the priests enter the holy precincts, they are not to go into the outer court until they leave behind the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They are to put on other clothes before they go near the places that are for the people.”
chapters.zh: 祭司进去出了圣所的时候，不可直到外院，但要在圣屋放下他们供职的衣服，因为是圣衣。要穿上别的衣服才可以到属民的外院。

chapters.en: When he had finished measuring what was inside the temple area, he led me out by the east gate and measured the area all around:
chapters.zh: 他量完了内殿，就带我出朝东的门，量院的四围。

chapters.en: He measured the east side with the measuring rod; it was five hundred cubits.
chapters.zh: 他用量度的竿量四围，量东面五百肘（原文作竿本章下同），

chapters.en: He measured the north side; it was five hundred cubits by the measuring rod.
chapters.zh: 用竿量北面五百肘，

chapters.en: He measured the south side; it was five hundred cubits by the measuring rod.
chapters.zh: 用竿量南面五百肘，

chapters.en: Then he turned to the west side and measured; it was five hundred cubits by the measuring rod.
chapters.zh: 又转到西面，用竿量五百肘。

chapters.en: So he measured the area on all four sides. It had a wall around it, five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, to separate the holy from the common.
chapters.zh: 他量四面，四围有墙，长五百肘，宽五百肘，为要分别圣地与俗地。

chapters.en: Then the man brought me to the gate facing east,
chapters.zh: 以后，他带我到一座门，就是朝东的门。

chapters.en: and I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of rushing waters, and the land was radiant with his glory.
chapters.zh: 以色列神的荣光从东而来。他的声音如同多水的声音。地就因他的荣耀发光。

chapters.en: The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when he came to destroy the city and like the visions I had seen by the Kebar River, and I fell facedown.
chapters.zh: 其状如从前他来灭城的时候我所见的异象，那异象如我在迦巴鲁河边所见的异象，我就俯伏在地。

chapters.en: The glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的荣光从朝东的门照入殿中。

chapters.en: Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
chapters.zh: 灵将我举起，带入内院，不料，耶和华的荣光充满了殿。

chapters.en: While the man was standing beside me, I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple.
chapters.zh: 我听见有一位从殿中对我说话。有一人站在我旁边。

chapters.en: He said: “Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet. This is where I will live among the Israelites forever. The people of Israel will never again defile my holy name—neither they nor their kings—by their prostitution and the funeral offerings for their kings at their death.
chapters.zh: 他对我说，人子阿，这是我宝座之地，是我脚掌所踏之地。我要在这里住，在以色列人中直到永远。以色列家和他们的君王必不再玷污我的圣名，就是行邪淫，在锡安的高处葬埋他们君王的尸首，

chapters.en: When they placed their threshold next to my threshold and their doorposts beside my doorposts, with only a wall between me and them, they defiled my holy name by their detestable practices. So I destroyed them in my anger.
chapters.zh: 使他们的门槛挨近我的门槛，他们的门框挨近我的门框。他们与我中间仅隔一墙，并且行可憎的事，玷污了我的圣名，所以我发怒灭绝他们。

chapters.en: Now let them put away from me their prostitution and the funeral offerings for their kings, and I will live among them forever.
chapters.zh: 现在他们当从我面前远除邪淫和他们君王的尸首，我就住在他们中间直到永远。

chapters.en: “Son of man, describe the temple to the people of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their sins. Let them consider its perfection,
chapters.zh: 人子阿，你要将这殿指示以色列家，使他们因自己的罪孽惭愧，也要他们量殿的尺寸。

chapters.en: and if they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the temple—its arrangement, its exits and entrances—its whole design and all its regulations and laws. Write these down before them so that they may be faithful to its design and follow all its regulations.
chapters.zh: 他们若因自己所行的一切事惭愧，你就将殿的规模，样式，出入之处，和一切形状，典章，礼仪，法则指示他们，在他们眼前写上，使他们遵照殿的一切规模典章去作。

chapters.en: “This is the law of the temple: All the surrounding area on top of the mountain will be most holy. Such is the law of the temple.
chapters.zh: 殿的法则乃是如此，殿在山顶上，四围的全界要称为至圣。这就是殿的法则。

chapters.en: “These are the measurements of the altar in long cubits, that cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: Its gutter is a cubit deep and a cubit wide, with a rim of one span around the edge. And this is the height of the altar:
chapters.zh: 以下量祭坛，是以肘为度（这肘是一肘零一掌）。底座高一肘，边宽一肘，四围起边高一掌，这是坛的座。

chapters.en: From the gutter on the ground up to the lower ledge that goes around the altar it is two cubits high, and the ledge is a cubit wide. From this lower ledge to the upper ledge that goes around the altar it is four cubits high, and that ledge is also a cubit wide.
chapters.zh: 从底座到下层磴台，高二肘，边宽一肘。从小磴台到大磴台，高四肘，边宽一肘。

chapters.en: Above that, the altar hearth is four cubits high, and four horns project upward from the hearth.
chapters.zh: 坛上的供台，高四肘。供台的四拐角上都有角。

chapters.en: The altar hearth is square, twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 供台长十二肘，宽十二肘，四面见方。

chapters.en: The upper ledge also is square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide. All around the altar is a gutter of one cubit with a rim of half a cubit. The steps of the altar face east.”
chapters.zh: 磴台长十四肘，宽十四肘，四面见方。四围起边高半肘，底座四围的边宽一肘。台阶朝东。

chapters.en: Then he said to me, “Son of man, this is what the Sovereign LORD says: These will be the regulations for sacrificing burnt offerings and splashing blood against the altar when it is built:
chapters.zh: 他对我说，人子阿，主耶和华如此说，建造祭坛，为要在其上献燔祭洒血，造成的时候典章如下，

chapters.en: You are to give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levitical priests of the family of Zadok, who come near to minister before me, declares the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华说，你要将一只公牛犊作为赎罪祭，给祭司利未人撒督的后裔，就是那亲近我，事奉我的。

chapters.en: You are to take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar and on the four corners of the upper ledge and all around the rim, and so purify the altar and make atonement for it.
chapters.zh: 你要取些公牛的血，抹在坛的四角和磴台的四拐角，并四围所起的边上。你这样洁净坛，坛就洁净了。

chapters.en: You are to take the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the designated part of the temple area outside the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 你又要将那作赎罪祭的公牛犊烧在殿外，圣地之外预定之处。

chapters.en: “On the second day you are to offer a male goat without defect for a sin offering, and the altar is to be purified as it was purified with the bull.
chapters.zh: 次日，要将无残疾的公山羊献为赎罪祭。要洁净坛，像用公牛犊洁净的一样。

chapters.en: When you have finished purifying it, you are to offer a young bull and a ram from the flock, both without defect.
chapters.zh: 洁净了坛，就要将一只无残疾的公牛犊和羊群中一只无残疾的公绵羊

chapters.en: You are to offer them before the LORD, and the priests are to sprinkle salt on them and sacrifice them as a burnt offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 奉到耶和华前。祭司要撒盐在其上，献与耶和华为燔祭。

chapters.en: “For seven days you are to provide a male goat daily for a sin offering; you are also to provide a young bull and a ram from the flock, both without defect.
chapters.zh: 七日内，每日要预备一只公山羊为赎罪祭，也要预备一只公牛犊和羊群中的一只公绵羊，都要没有残疾的。

chapters.en: For seven days they are to make atonement for the altar and cleanse it; thus they will dedicate it.
chapters.zh: 七日祭司洁净坛，坛就洁净了。要这样把坛分别为圣。

chapters.en: At the end of these days, from the eighth day on, the priests are to present your burnt offerings and fellowship offerings on the altar. Then I will accept you, declares the Sovereign LORD.”
chapters.zh: 满了七日，自八日以后，祭司要在坛上献你们的燔祭和平安祭。我必悦纳你们。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: Then the man brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east, and it was shut.
chapters.zh: 他又带我回到圣地朝东的外门。那门关闭了。

chapters.en: The LORD said to me, “This gate is to remain shut. It must not be opened; no one may enter through it. It is to remain shut because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对我说，这门必须关闭，不可敞开，谁也不可由其中进入。因为耶和华以色列的神已经由其中进入，所以必须关闭。

chapters.en: The prince himself is the only one who may sit inside the gateway to eat in the presence of the LORD. He is to enter by way of the portico of the gateway and go out the same way.”
chapters.zh: 至于王，他必按王的位分，坐在其内，在耶和华面前吃饼。他必由这门的廊而入，也必由此而出。

chapters.en: Then the man brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked and saw the glory of the LORD filling the temple of the LORD, and I fell facedown.
chapters.zh: 他又带我由北门来到殿前。我观看，见耶和华的荣光充满耶和华的殿，我就俯伏在地。

chapters.en: The LORD said to me, “Son of man, look carefully, listen closely and give attention to everything I tell you concerning all the regulations and instructions regarding the temple of the LORD. Give attention to the entrance to the temple and all the exits of the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对我说，人子阿，我对你所说耶和华殿中的一切典章法则，你要放在心上，用眼看，用耳听，并要留心殿宇和圣地一切出入之处。

chapters.en: Say to rebellious Israel, ‘This is what the Sovereign LORD says: Enough of your detestable practices, people of Israel!
chapters.zh: 你要对那悖逆的以色列家说，主耶和华如此说，以色列家阿，你们行一切可憎的事，当够了吧。

chapters.en: In addition to all your other detestable practices, you brought foreigners uncircumcised in heart and flesh into my sanctuary, desecrating my temple while you offered me food, fat and blood, and you broke my covenant.
chapters.zh: 你们把我的食物，就是脂油和血献上的时候，将身心未受割礼的外邦人领进我的圣地，玷污了我的殿。又背了我的约，在你们一切可憎的事上，加上这一层。

chapters.en: Instead of carrying out your duty in regard to my holy things, you put others in charge of my sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 你们也没有看守我的圣物，却派别人在圣地替你们看守我所吩咐你们的。

chapters.en: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh is to enter my sanctuary, not even the foreigners who live among the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说，以色列中的外邦人，就是身心未受割礼的，都不可入我的圣地。

chapters.en: “ ‘The Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray and who wandered from me after their idols must bear the consequences of their sin.
chapters.zh: 当以色列人走迷的时候，有利未人远离我，就是走迷离开我，随从他们的偶像，他们必担当自己的罪孽。

chapters.en: They may serve in my sanctuary, having charge of the gates of the temple and serving in it; they may slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people and stand before the people and serve them.
chapters.zh: 然而他们必在我的圣地当仆役，照管殿门，在殿中供职。必为民宰杀燔祭牲和平安祭牲，必站在民前伺候他们。

chapters.en: But because they served them in the presence of their idols and made the people of Israel fall into sin, therefore I have sworn with uplifted hand that they must bear the consequences of their sin, declares the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 因为这些利未人曾在偶像前伺候这民，成了以色列家罪孽的绊脚石，所以我向他们起誓，他们必担当自己的罪孽。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: They are not to come near to serve me as priests or come near any of my holy things or my most holy offerings; they must bear the shame of their detestable practices.
chapters.zh: 他们不可亲近我，给我供祭司的职分，也不可挨近我的一件圣物，就是至圣的物。他们却要担当自己的羞辱和所行可憎之事的报应。

chapters.en: And I will appoint them to guard the temple for all the work that is to be done in it.
chapters.zh: 然而我要使他们看守殿宇，办理其中的一切事，并作其内一切当作之工。

chapters.en: “ ‘But the Levitical priests, who are descendants of Zadok and who guarded my sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from me, are to come near to minister before me; they are to stand before me to offer sacrifices of fat and blood, declares the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 以色列人走迷离开我的时候，祭司利未人撒督的子孙仍看守我的圣所。他们必亲近我，事奉我，并且侍立在我面前，将脂油与血献给我。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: They alone are to enter my sanctuary; they alone are to come near my table to minister before me and serve me as guards.
chapters.zh: 他们必进入我的圣所，就近我的桌前事奉我，守我所吩咐的。

chapters.en: “ ‘When they enter the gates of the inner court, they are to wear linen clothes; they must not wear any woolen garment while ministering at the gates of the inner court or inside the temple.
chapters.zh: 他们进内院门必穿细麻衣。在内院门和殿内供职的时候不可穿羊毛衣服。

chapters.en: They are to wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They must not wear anything that makes them perspire.
chapters.zh: 他们头上要戴细麻布裹头巾，腰穿细麻布裤子。不可穿使身体出汗的衣服。

chapters.en: When they go out into the outer court where the people are, they are to take off the clothes they have been ministering in and are to leave them in the sacred rooms, and put on other clothes, so that the people are not consecrated through contact with their garments.
chapters.zh: 他们出到外院的民那里，当脱下供职的衣服，放在圣屋内，穿上别的衣服，免得因圣衣使民成圣。

chapters.en: “ ‘They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long, but they are to keep the hair of their heads trimmed.
chapters.zh: 不可剃头，也不可容发绺长长，只可剪发。

chapters.en: No priest is to drink wine when he enters the inner court.
chapters.zh: 祭司进内院的时候都不可喝酒。

chapters.en: They must not marry widows or divorced women; they may marry only virgins of Israelite descent or widows of priests.
chapters.zh: 不可娶寡妇和被休的妇人为妻，只可娶以色列后裔中的处女，或是祭司遗留的寡妇。

chapters.en: They are to teach my people the difference between the holy and the common and show them how to distinguish between the unclean and the clean.
chapters.zh: 他们要使我的民知道圣俗的分别，又使他们分辨洁净的和不洁净的。

chapters.en: “ ‘In any dispute, the priests are to serve as judges and decide it according to my ordinances. They are to keep my laws and my decrees for all my appointed festivals, and they are to keep my Sabbaths holy.
chapters.zh: 有争讼的事，他们应当站立判断，要按我的典章判断。在我一切的节期必守我的律法，条例，也必以我的安息日为圣日。

chapters.en: “ ‘A priest must not defile himself by going near a dead person; however, if the dead person was his father or mother, son or daughter, brother or unmarried sister, then he may defile himself.
chapters.zh: 他们不可挨近死尸沾染自己，只可为父亲，母亲，儿子，女儿，弟兄，和未嫁人的姐妹沾染自己。

chapters.en: After he is cleansed, he must wait seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司洁净之后，必再计算七日。

chapters.en: On the day he goes into the inner court of the sanctuary to minister in the sanctuary, he is to offer a sin offering for himself, declares the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 当他进内院，进圣所，在圣所中事奉的日子，要为自己献赎罪祭。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: “ ‘I am to be the only inheritance the priests have. You are to give them no possession in Israel; I will be their possession.
chapters.zh: 祭司必有产业，我是他们的产业。不可在以色列中给他们基业。我是他们的基业。

chapters.en: They will eat the grain offerings, the sin offerings and the guilt offerings; and everything in Israel devoted to the LORD will belong to them.
chapters.zh: 素祭，赎罪祭，和赎愆祭他们都可以吃，以色列中一切永献的物都要归他们。

chapters.en: The best of all the firstfruits and of all your special gifts will belong to the priests. You are to give them the first portion of your ground meal so that a blessing may rest on your household.
chapters.zh: 首先初熟之物和一切所献的供物都要归给祭司。你们也要用初熟的麦子磨面给祭司。这样，福气就必临到你们的家了。

chapters.en: The priests must not eat anything, whether bird or animal, found dead or torn by wild animals.
chapters.zh: 无论是鸟是兽，凡自死的，或是撕裂的，祭司都不可吃。

chapters.en: “ ‘When you allot the land as an inheritance, you are to present to the LORD a portion of the land as a sacred district, 25,000 cubits long and 20,000 cubits wide; the entire area will be holy.
chapters.zh: 你们拈阄分地为业，要献上一分给耶和华为圣供地，长二万五千肘，宽一万肘。这分以内，四围都为圣地。

chapters.en: Of this, a section 500 cubits square is to be for the sanctuary, with 50 cubits around it for open land.
chapters.zh: 其中有作为圣所之地，长五百肘，宽五百肘，四面见方。四围再有五十肘为郊野之地。

chapters.en: In the sacred district, measure off a section 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. In it will be the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
chapters.zh: 要以肘为度量地，长二万五千肘，宽一万肘。其中有圣所，是至圣的。

chapters.en: It will be the sacred portion of the land for the priests, who minister in the sanctuary and who draw near to minister before the LORD. It will be a place for their houses as well as a holy place for the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 这是全地的一分圣地，要归与供圣所职事的祭司，就是亲近事奉耶和华的，作为他们房屋之地与圣所之圣地。

chapters.en: An area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide will belong to the Levites, who serve in the temple, as their possession for towns to live in.
chapters.zh: 又有一分，长二万五千肘，宽一万肘，要归与在殿中供职的利未人，作为二十间房屋之业。

chapters.en: “ ‘You are to give the city as its property an area 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, adjoining the sacred portion; it will belong to all Israel.
chapters.zh: 也要分定属城的地业，宽五千肘，长二万五千肘，挨着那分圣供地，要归以色列全家。

chapters.en: “ ‘The prince will have the land bordering each side of the area formed by the sacred district and the property of the city. It will extend westward from the west side and eastward from the east side, running lengthwise from the western to the eastern border parallel to one of the tribal portions.
chapters.zh: 归王之地要在圣供地和属城之地的两旁，就是圣供地和属城之地的旁边，西至西头，东至东头，从西到东，其长与每支派的分一样。

chapters.en: This land will be his possession in Israel. And my princes will no longer oppress my people but will allow the people of Israel to possess the land according to their tribes.
chapters.zh: 这地在以色列中必归王为业。我所立的王必不再欺压我的民，却要按支派将地分给以色列家。

chapters.en: “ ‘This is what the Sovereign LORD says: You have gone far enough, princes of Israel! Give up your violence and oppression and do what is just and right. Stop dispossessing my people, declares the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说，以色列的王阿，你们应当知足，要除掉强暴和抢夺的事，施行公平和公义，不再勒索我的民。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: You are to use accurate scales, an accurate ephah and an accurate bath.
chapters.zh: 你们要用公道天平，公道伊法，公道吧特。

chapters.en: The ephah and the bath are to be the same size, the bath containing a tenth of a homer and the ephah a tenth of a homer; the homer is to be the standard measure for both.
chapters.zh: 伊法与吧特大小要一样。吧特可盛贺梅珥十分之一，伊法也可盛贺梅珥十分之一，都以贺梅珥的大小为准。

chapters.en: The shekel is to consist of twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels equal one mina.
chapters.zh: 舍客勒是二十季拉。二十舍客勒，二十五舍客勒，十五舍客勒，为你们的弥那。

chapters.en: “ ‘This is the special gift you are to offer: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
chapters.zh: 你们当献的供物乃是这样，一贺梅珥麦子要献伊法六分之一。一贺梅珥大麦要献伊法六分之一。

chapters.en: The prescribed portion of olive oil, measured by the bath, is a tenth of a bath from each cor (which consists of ten baths or one homer, for ten baths are equivalent to a homer).
chapters.zh: 你们献所分定的油，按油的吧特，一柯珥油要献吧特十分之一。原来十吧特就是一贺梅珥。

chapters.en: Also one sheep is to be taken from every flock of two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel. These will be used for the grain offerings, burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to make atonement for the people, declares the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 从以色列滋润的草场上每二百羊中，要献一只羊羔。这都可作素祭，燔祭，平安祭，为民赎罪。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: All the people of the land will be required to give this special offering to the prince in Israel.
chapters.zh: 此地的民都要奉上这供物给以色列中的王。

chapters.en: It will be the duty of the prince to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings and drink offerings at the festivals, the New Moons and the Sabbaths—at all the appointed festivals of Israel. He will provide the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to make atonement for the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 王的本分是在节期，月朔，安息日，就是以色列家一切的节期，奉上燔祭，素祭，奠祭。他要预备赎罪祭，素祭，燔祭，和平安祭，为以色列家赎罪。

chapters.en: “ ‘This is what the Sovereign LORD says: In the first month on the first day you are to take a young bull without defect and purify the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说，正月初一日，你要取无残疾的公牛犊，洁净圣所。

chapters.en: The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the upper ledge of the altar and on the gateposts of the inner court.
chapters.zh: 祭司要取些赎罪祭牲的血，抹在殿的门柱上和坛磴台的四角上，并内院的门框上。

chapters.en: You are to do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins unintentionally or through ignorance; so you are to make atonement for the temple.
chapters.zh: 本月初七日（七十经作七月初一日）也要为误犯罪的，和愚蒙犯罪的如此行，为殿赎罪。

chapters.en: “ ‘In the first month on the fourteenth day you are to observe the Passover, a festival lasting seven days, during which you shall eat bread made without yeast.
chapters.zh: 正月十四日，你们要守逾越节，守节七日，要吃无酵饼。

chapters.en: On that day the prince is to provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
chapters.zh: 当日，王要为自己和国内的众民预备一只公牛作赎罪祭。

chapters.en: Every day during the seven days of the festival he is to provide seven bulls and seven rams without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD, and a male goat for a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 这节的七日，每日他要为耶和华预备无残疾的公牛七只，公绵羊七只为燔祭。每日又要预备公山羊一只为赎罪祭。

chapters.en: He is to provide as a grain offering an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, along with a hin of olive oil for each ephah.
chapters.zh: 他也要预备素祭，就是为一只公牛同献一伊法细面，为一只公绵羊同献一伊法细面，每一伊法细面加油一欣。

chapters.en: “ ‘During the seven days of the festival, which begins in the seventh month on the fifteenth day, he is to make the same provision for sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings and oil.
chapters.zh: 七月十五日守节的时候，七日他都要如此行，照逾越节的赎罪祭，燔祭，素祭，和油的条例一样。

chapters.en: “ ‘This is what the Sovereign LORD says: The gate of the inner court facing east is to be shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon it is to be opened.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说，内院朝东的门，在办理事务的六日内必须关闭。惟有安息日和月朔必须敞开。

chapters.en: The prince is to enter from the outside through the portico of the gateway and stand by the gatepost. The priests are to sacrifice his burnt offering and his fellowship offerings. He is to bow down in worship at the threshold of the gateway and then go out, but the gate will not be shut until evening.
chapters.zh: 王要从这门的廊进入，站在门框旁边。祭司要为他预备燔祭和平安祭，他就要在门槛那里敬拜，然后出去。这门直到晚上不可关闭。

chapters.en: On the Sabbaths and New Moons the people of the land are to worship in the presence of the LORD at the entrance of that gateway.
chapters.zh: 在安息日和月朔，国内的居民要在这门口，耶和华面前敬拜。

chapters.en: The burnt offering the prince brings to the LORD on the Sabbath day is to be six male lambs and a ram, all without defect.
chapters.zh: 安息日，王所献与耶和华的燔祭要用无残疾的羊羔六只，无残疾的公绵羊一只。

chapters.en: The grain offering given with the ram is to be an ephah, and the grain offering with the lambs is to be as much as he pleases, along with a hin of olive oil for each ephah.
chapters.zh: 同献的素祭要为公绵羊献一伊法细面，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法细面加油一欣。

chapters.en: On the day of the New Moon he is to offer a young bull, six lambs and a ram, all without defect.
chapters.zh: 当月朔，要献无残疾的公牛犊一只，羊羔六只，公绵羊一只，都要无残疾的。

chapters.en: He is to provide as a grain offering one ephah with the bull, one ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he wants to give, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
chapters.zh: 他也要预备素祭，为公牛献一伊法细面，为公绵羊献一伊法细面，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法细面加油一欣。

chapters.en: When the prince enters, he is to go in through the portico of the gateway, and he is to come out the same way.
chapters.zh: 王进入的时候必由这门的廊而入，也必由此而出。

chapters.en: “ ‘When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to worship is to go out the south gate; and whoever enters by the south gate is to go out the north gate. No one is to return through the gate by which they entered, but each is to go out the opposite gate.
chapters.zh: 在各节期，国内居民朝见耶和华的时候，从北门进入敬拜的，必由南门而出。从南门进入的，必由北门而出。不可从所入的门而出，必要直往前行，由对门而出。

chapters.en: The prince is to be among them, going in when they go in and going out when they go out.
chapters.zh: 民进入，王也要在民中进入。民出去，王也要一同出去。

chapters.en: At the feasts and the appointed festivals, the grain offering is to be an ephah with a bull, an ephah with a ram, and with the lambs as much as he pleases, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
chapters.zh: 在节期和圣会的日子同献的素祭，要为一只公牛献一伊法细面，为一只公绵羊献一伊法细面，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法细面加油一欣。

chapters.en: “ ‘When the prince provides a freewill offering to the LORD—whether a burnt offering or fellowship offerings—the gate facing east is to be opened for him. He shall offer his burnt offering or his fellowship offerings as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and after he has gone out, the gate will be shut.
chapters.zh: 王预备甘心献的燔祭或平安祭，就是向耶和华甘心献的，当有人为他开朝东的门。他就预备燔祭和平安祭，与安息日预备的一样，献毕就出去。他出去之后，当有人将门关闭。

chapters.en: “ ‘Every day you are to provide a year-old lamb without defect for a burnt offering to the LORD; morning by morning you shall provide it.
chapters.zh: 每日，你要预备无残疾一岁的羊羔一只，献与耶和华为燔祭。要每早晨预备。

chapters.en: You are also to provide with it morning by morning a grain offering, consisting of a sixth of an ephah with a third of a hin of oil to moisten the flour. The presenting of this grain offering to the LORD is a lasting ordinance.
chapters.zh: 每早晨也要预备同献的素祭，细面一伊法六分之一，并油一欣三分之一，调和细面。这素祭要常献与耶和华为永远的定例。

chapters.en: So the lamb and the grain offering and the oil shall be provided morning by morning for a regular burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 每早晨要这样预备羊羔，素祭，并油为常献的燔祭。

chapters.en: “ ‘This is what the Sovereign LORD says: If the prince makes a gift from his inheritance to one of his sons, it will also belong to his descendants; it is to be their property by inheritance.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说，王若将产业赐给他的儿子，就成了他儿子的产业，那是他们承受为业的。

chapters.en: If, however, he makes a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, the servant may keep it until the year of freedom; then it will revert to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons only; it is theirs.
chapters.zh: 倘若王将一分产业赐给他的臣仆，就成了他臣仆的产业。到自由之年仍要归与王。至于王的产业，必归与他的儿子。

chapters.en: The prince must not take any of the inheritance of the people, driving them off their property. He is to give his sons their inheritance out of his own property, so that not one of my people will be separated from their property.’ ”
chapters.zh: 王不可夺取民的产业，以致驱逐他们离开所承受的。他要从自己的地业中，将产业赐给他儿子，免得我的民分散，各人离开所承受的。

chapters.en: Then the man brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate to the sacred rooms facing north, which belonged to the priests, and showed me a place at the western end.
chapters.zh: 那带我的，将我从门旁进入之处，领进为祭司预备的圣屋，是朝北的，见后头西边有一块地。

chapters.en: He said to me, “This is the place where the priests are to cook the guilt offering and the sin offering and bake the grain offering, to avoid bringing them into the outer court and consecrating the people.”
chapters.zh: 他对我说，这是祭司煮赎愆祭，赎罪祭，烤素祭之地，免得带到外院，使民成圣。

chapters.en: He then brought me to the outer court and led me around to its four corners, and I saw in each corner another court.
chapters.zh: 他又带我到外院，使我经过院子的四拐角，见每拐角各有一个院子。

chapters.en: In the four corners of the outer court were enclosed courts, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide; each of the courts in the four corners was the same size.
chapters.zh: 院子四拐角的院子，周围有墙，每院长四十肘，宽三十肘。四拐角院子的尺寸都是一样，

chapters.en: Around the inside of each of the four courts was a ledge of stone, with places for fire built all around under the ledge.
chapters.zh: 其中周围有一排房子，房子内有煮肉的地方。

chapters.en: He said to me, “These are the kitchens where those who minister at the temple are to cook the sacrifices of the people.”
chapters.zh: 他对我说，这都是煮肉的房子，殿内的仆役要在这里煮民的祭物。

chapters.en: The man brought me back to the entrance to the temple, and I saw water coming out from under the threshold of the temple toward the east (for the temple faced east). The water was coming down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
chapters.zh: 他带我回到殿门，见殿的门槛下有水往东流出（原来殿面朝东）。这水从槛下，由殿的右边，在祭坛的南边往下流。

chapters.en: He then brought me out through the north gate and led me around the outside to the outer gate facing east, and the water was trickling from the south side.
chapters.zh: 他带我出北门，又领我从外边转到朝东的外门，见水从右边流出。

chapters.en: As the man went eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and then led me through water that was ankle-deep.
chapters.zh: 他手拿准绳往东出去的时候，量了一千肘，使我趟过水，水到踝子骨。

chapters.en: He measured off another thousand cubits and led me through water that was knee-deep. He measured off another thousand and led me through water that was up to the waist.
chapters.zh: 他又量了一千肘，使我趟过水，水就到膝。再量了一千肘，使我趟过水，水便到腰。

chapters.en: He measured off another thousand, but now it was a river that I could not cross, because the water had risen and was deep enough to swim in—a river that no one could cross.
chapters.zh: 又量了一千肘，水便成了河，使我不能趟过。因为水势涨起，成了可供游泳的水，不可趟的河。

chapters.en: He asked me, “Son of man, do you see this?” Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
chapters.zh: 他对我说，人子阿，你看见了什么。他就带我回到河边。

chapters.en: When I arrived there, I saw a great number of trees on each side of the river.
chapters.zh: 我回到河边的时候，见在河这边与那边的岸上有极多的树木。

chapters.en: He said to me, “This water flows toward the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah, where it enters the Dead Sea. When it empties into the sea, the salty water there becomes fresh.
chapters.zh: 他对我说，这水往东方流去，必下到亚拉巴，直到海。所发出来的水必流入盐海，使水变甜（原文作得医治下同）。

chapters.en: Swarms of living creatures will live wherever the river flows. There will be large numbers of fish, because this water flows there and makes the salt water fresh; so where the river flows everything will live.
chapters.zh: 这河水所到之处，凡滋生的动物都必生活，并且因这流来的水必有极多的鱼，海水也变甜了。这河水所到之处，百物都必生活。

chapters.en: Fishermen will stand along the shore; from En Gedi to En Eglaim there will be places for spreading nets. The fish will be of many kinds—like the fish of the Mediterranean Sea.
chapters.zh: 必有渔夫站在河边，从隐基底直到隐以革莲，都作晒（或作张）网之处。那鱼各从其类，好像大海的鱼甚多。

chapters.en: But the swamps and marshes will not become fresh; they will be left for salt.
chapters.zh: 只是泥泞之地与洼湿之处不得治好，必为盐地。

chapters.en: Fruit trees of all kinds will grow on both banks of the river. Their leaves will not wither, nor will their fruit fail. Every month they will bear fruit, because the water from the sanctuary flows to them. Their fruit will serve for food and their leaves for healing.”
chapters.zh: 在河这边与那边的岸上必生长各类的树木。其果可作食物，叶子不枯干，果子不断绝。每月必结新果子，因为这水是从圣所流出来的。树上的果子必作食物，叶子乃为治病。

chapters.en: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: “These are the boundaries of the land that you will divide among the twelve tribes of Israel as their inheritance, with two portions for Joseph.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说，你们要照地的境界，按以色列十二支派分地为业。约瑟必得两分。

chapters.en: You are to divide it equally among them. Because I swore with uplifted hand to give it to your ancestors, this land will become your inheritance.
chapters.zh: 你们承受这地为业，要彼此均分。因为我曾起誓应许将这地赐与你们的列祖。这地必归你们为业。

chapters.en: “This is to be the boundary of the land: “On the north side it will run from the Mediterranean Sea by the Hethlon road past Lebo Hamath to Zedad,
chapters.zh: 地的四界乃是如此，北界从大海往希特伦，直到西达达口。

chapters.en: Berothah and Sibraim (which lies on the border between Damascus and Hamath), as far as Hazer Hattikon, which is on the border of Hauran.
chapters.zh: 又往哈马，比罗他，西伯莲（西伯莲在大马色与哈马两界中间），到浩兰边界的哈撒哈提干。

chapters.en: The boundary will extend from the sea to Hazar Enan, along the northern border of Damascus, with the border of Hamath to the north. This will be the northern boundary.
chapters.zh: 这样，境界从海边往大马色地界上的哈萨以难，北边以哈马地为界。这是北界。

chapters.en: “On the east side the boundary will run between Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the Dead Sea and as far as Tamar. This will be the eastern boundary.
chapters.zh: 东界在浩兰，大马色，基列，和以色列地的中间，就是约旦河。你们要从北界量到东海。这是东界。

chapters.en: “On the south side it will run from Tamar as far as the waters of Meribah Kadesh, then along the Wadi of Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea. This will be the southern boundary.
chapters.zh: 南界是从他玛到米利巴加低斯的水，延到埃及小河，直到大海。这是南界。

chapters.en: “On the west side, the Mediterranean Sea will be the boundary to a point opposite Lebo Hamath. This will be the western boundary.
chapters.zh: 西界就是大海，从南界直到哈马口对面之地。这是西界。

chapters.en: “You are to distribute this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 你们要按着以色列的支派彼此分这地。

chapters.en: You are to allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners residing among you and who have children. You are to consider them as native-born Israelites; along with you they are to be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 要拈阄分这地为业，归与自己和你们中间寄居的外人，就是在你们中间生养儿女的外人。你们要看他们如同以色列人中所生的一样。他们在以色列支派中要与你们同得地业

chapters.en: In whatever tribe a foreigner resides, there you are to give them their inheritance,” declares the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 外人寄居在哪支派中，你们就在那里分给他地业。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: “These are the tribes, listed by name: At the northern frontier, Dan will have one portion; it will follow the Hethlon road to Lebo Hamath; Hazar Enan and the northern border of Damascus next to Hamath will be part of its border from the east side to the west side.
chapters.zh: 众支派按名所得之地记在下面，从北头，由希特伦往哈马口，到大马色地界上的哈萨以难。北边靠着哈马地（各支派的地都有东西的边界），是但的一分。

chapters.en: “Asher will have one portion; it will border the territory of Dan from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着但的地界，从东到西，是亚设的一分。

chapters.en: “Naphtali will have one portion; it will border the territory of Asher from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着亚设的地界，从东到西，是拿弗他利的一分。

chapters.en: “Manasseh will have one portion; it will border the territory of Naphtali from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着拿弗他利的地界，从东到西，是玛拿西的一分。

chapters.en: “Ephraim will have one portion; it will border the territory of Manasseh from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着玛拿西的地界，从东到西，是以法莲的一分。

chapters.en: “Reuben will have one portion; it will border the territory of Ephraim from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着以法莲的地界，从东到西，是流便的一分。

chapters.en: “Judah will have one portion; it will border the territory of Reuben from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着流便的地界，从东到西，是犹大的一分。

chapters.en: “Bordering the territory of Judah from east to west will be the portion you are to present as a special gift. It will be 25,000 cubits wide, and its length from east to west will equal one of the tribal portions; the sanctuary will be in the center of it.
chapters.zh: 挨着犹大的地界，从东到西，必有你们所当献的供地，宽二万五千肘。从东界到西界，长短与各分之地相同，圣地当在其中。

chapters.en: “The special portion you are to offer to the LORD will be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 你们献与耶和华的供地要长二万五千肘，宽一万肘。

chapters.en: This will be the sacred portion for the priests. It will be 25,000 cubits long on the north side, 10,000 cubits wide on the west side, 10,000 cubits wide on the east side and 25,000 cubits long on the south side. In the center of it will be the sanctuary of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这圣供地要归与祭司，北长二万五千肘，西宽一万肘，东宽一万肘，南长二万五千肘。耶和华的圣地当在其中。

chapters.en: This will be for the consecrated priests, the Zadokites, who were faithful in serving me and did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray.
chapters.zh: 这地要归与撒督的子孙中成为圣的祭司，就是那守我所吩咐的。当以色列人走迷的时候，他们不像那些利未人走迷了。

chapters.en: It will be a special gift to them from the sacred portion of the land, a most holy portion, bordering the territory of the Levites.
chapters.zh: 这要归与他们为供地，是全地中至圣的。供地挨着利未人的地界。

chapters.en: “Alongside the territory of the priests, the Levites will have an allotment 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. Its total length will be 25,000 cubits and its width 10,000 cubits.
chapters.zh: 利未人所得的地要长二万五千肘，宽一万肘，与祭司的地界相等，都长二万五千肘，宽一万肘。

chapters.en: They must not sell or exchange any of it. This is the best of the land and must not pass into other hands, because it is holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这地不可卖，不可换，初熟之物也不可归与别人，因为是归耶和华为圣的。

chapters.en: “The remaining area, 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, will be for the common use of the city, for houses and for pastureland. The city will be in the center of it
chapters.zh: 这二万五千肘前面所剩下五千肘宽之地要作俗用，作为造城盖房郊野之地。城要在当中。

chapters.en: and will have these measurements: the north side 4,500 cubits, the south side 4,500 cubits, the east side 4,500 cubits, and the west side 4,500 cubits.
chapters.zh: 城的尺寸乃是如此，北面四千五百肘，南面四千五百肘，东面四千五百肘，西面四千五百肘。

chapters.en: The pastureland for the city will be 250 cubits on the north, 250 cubits on the south, 250 cubits on the east, and 250 cubits on the west.
chapters.zh: 城必有郊野，向北二百五十肘，向南二百五十肘，向东二百五十肘，向西二百五十肘。

chapters.en: What remains of the area, bordering on the sacred portion and running the length of it, will be 10,000 cubits on the east side and 10,000 cubits on the west side. Its produce will supply food for the workers of the city.
chapters.zh: 靠着圣供地的余地，东长一万肘，西长一万肘，要与圣供地相等。其中的土产要作城内工人的食物。

chapters.en: The workers from the city who farm it will come from all the tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 所有以色列支派中，在城内作工的，都要耕种这地。

chapters.en: The entire portion will be a square, 25,000 cubits on each side. As a special gift you will set aside the sacred portion, along with the property of the city.
chapters.zh: 你们所献的圣供地连归城之地，是四方的，长二万五千肘，宽二万五千肘。

chapters.en: “What remains on both sides of the area formed by the sacred portion and the property of the city will belong to the prince. It will extend eastward from the 25,000 cubits of the sacred portion to the eastern border, and westward from the 25,000 cubits to the western border. Both these areas running the length of the tribal portions will belong to the prince, and the sacred portion with the temple sanctuary will be in the center of them.
chapters.zh: 圣供地连归城之地，两边的余地要归与王。供地东边，南北二万五千肘，东至东界，西边南北二万五千肘，西至西界，与各分之地相同，都要归王。圣供地和殿的圣地要在其中，

chapters.en: So the property of the Levites and the property of the city will lie in the center of the area that belongs to the prince. The area belonging to the prince will lie between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 并且利未人之地，与归城之地的东西两边延长之地（这两地在王地中间），就是在犹大和便雅悯两界中间，要归与王。

chapters.en: “As for the rest of the tribes: Benjamin will have one portion; it will extend from the east side to the west side.
chapters.zh: 论到其余的支派，从东到西，是便雅悯的一分。

chapters.en: “Simeon will have one portion; it will border the territory of Benjamin from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着便雅悯的地界，从东到西，是西缅的一分。

chapters.en: “Issachar will have one portion; it will border the territory of Simeon from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着西缅的地界，从东到西，是以萨迦的一分。

chapters.en: “Zebulun will have one portion; it will border the territory of Issachar from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着以萨迦的地界，从东到西，是西布伦的一分。

chapters.en: “Gad will have one portion; it will border the territory of Zebulun from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着西布伦的地界，从东到西，是迦得的一分。

chapters.en: “The southern boundary of Gad will run south from Tamar to the waters of Meribah Kadesh, then along the Wadi of Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea.
chapters.zh: 迦得地的南界是从他玛到米利巴加低斯的水，延到埃及小河，直到大海。

chapters.en: “This is the land you are to allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these will be their portions,” declares the Sovereign LORD.
chapters.zh: 这就是你们要拈阄分给以色列支派为业之地，乃是他们各支派所得之分。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: “These will be the exits of the city: Beginning on the north side, which is 4,500 cubits long,
chapters.zh: 城的北面四千五百肘。出城之处如下。

chapters.en: the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel. The three gates on the north side will be the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah and the gate of Levi.
chapters.zh: 城的各门要按以色列支派的名字。北面有三门，一为流便门，一为犹大门，一为利未门。

chapters.en: “On the east side, which is 4,500 cubits long, will be three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin and the gate of Dan.
chapters.zh: 东面四千五百肘，有三门，一为约瑟门，一为便雅悯门，一为但门。

chapters.en: “On the south side, which measures 4,500 cubits, will be three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar and the gate of Zebulun.
chapters.zh: 南面四千五百肘，有三门，一为西缅门，一为以萨迦门，一为西布伦门。

chapters.en: “On the west side, which is 4,500 cubits long, will be three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher and the gate of Naphtali.
chapters.zh: 西面四千五百肘，有三门，一为迦得门，一为亚设门，一为拿弗他利门。

chapters.en: “The distance all around will be 18,000 cubits.“And the name of the city from that time on will be: THE LORD IS THERE.”
chapters.zh: 城四围共一万八千肘。从此以后，这城的名字必称为耶和华的所在。

chapters.en: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
chapters.zh: 犹大王约雅敬在位第三年，巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒来到耶路撒冷，将城围困。

chapters.en: And the Lord delivered Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the articles from the temple of God. These he carried off to the temple of his god in Babylonia and put in the treasure house of his god.
chapters.zh: 主将犹大王约雅敬，并神殿中器皿的几分交付他手。他就把这器皿带到示拿地，收入他神的庙里，放在他神的库中。

chapters.en: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, chief of his court officials, to bring into the king’s service some of the Israelites from the royal family and the nobility—
chapters.zh: 王吩咐太监长亚施毗拿，从以色列人的宗室和贵胄中带进几个人来，

chapters.en: young men without any physical defect, handsome, showing aptitude for every kind of learning, well informed, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace. He was to teach them the language and literature of the Babylonians.
chapters.zh: 就是年少没有残疾，相貌俊美，通达各样学问，知识聪明俱备，足能侍立在王宫里的，要教他们迦勒底的文字言语。

chapters.en: The king assigned them a daily amount of food and wine from the king’s table. They were to be trained for three years, and after that they were to enter the king’s service.
chapters.zh: 王派定将自己所用的膳和所饮的酒，每日赐他们一分，养他们三年。满了三年，好叫他们在王面前侍立。

chapters.en: Among those who were chosen were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.
chapters.zh: 他们中间有犹大族的人，但以理，哈拿尼雅，米沙利，亚撒利雅。

chapters.en: The chief official gave them new names: to Daniel, the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
chapters.zh: 太监长给他们起名，称但以理为伯提沙撒，称哈拿尼雅为沙得拉，称米沙利为米煞，称亚撒利雅为亚伯尼歌。

chapters.en: But Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the royal food and wine, and he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself this way.
chapters.zh: 但以理却立志不以王的膳和王所饮的酒玷污自己，所以求太监长容他不玷污自己。

chapters.en: Now God had caused the official to show favor and compassion to Daniel,
chapters.zh: 神使但以理在太监长眼前蒙恩惠，受怜悯。

chapters.en: but the official told Daniel, “I am afraid of my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the other young men your age? The king would then have my head because of you.”
chapters.zh: 太监长对但以理说，我惧怕我主我王，他已经派定你们的饮食。倘若他见你们的面貌比你们同岁的少年人肌瘦，怎么好呢？这样，你们就使我的头在王那里难保。

chapters.en: Daniel then said to the guard whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah,
chapters.zh: 但以理对太监长所派管理但以理，哈拿尼雅，米沙利，亚撒利雅的委办说，

chapters.en: “Please test your servants for ten days: Give us nothing but vegetables to eat and water to drink.
chapters.zh: 求你试试仆人们十天，给我们素菜吃，白水喝，

chapters.en: Then compare our appearance with that of the young men who eat the royal food, and treat your servants in accordance with what you see.”
chapters.zh: 然后看看我们的面貌和用王膳那少年人的面貌，就照你所看的待仆人吧。

chapters.en: So he agreed to this and tested them for ten days.
chapters.zh: 委办便允准他们这件事，试看他们十天。

chapters.en: At the end of the ten days they looked healthier and better nourished than any of the young men who ate the royal food.
chapters.zh: 过了十天，见他们的面貌比用王膳的一切少年人更加俊美肥胖。

chapters.en: So the guard took away their choice food and the wine they were to drink and gave them vegetables instead.
chapters.zh: 于是委办撤去派他们用的膳，饮的酒，给他们素菜吃。

chapters.en: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding of all kinds of literature and learning. And Daniel could understand visions and dreams of all kinds.
chapters.zh: 这四个少年人，神在各样文字学问上（学问原文作智慧），赐给他们聪明知识。但以理又明白各样的异象和梦兆。

chapters.en: At the end of the time set by the king to bring them into his service, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王预定带进少年人来的日期满了，太监长就把他们带到王面前。

chapters.en: The king talked with them, and he found none equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah; so they entered the king’s service.
chapters.zh: 王与他们谈论，见少年人中无一人能比但以理，哈拿尼雅，米沙利，亚撒利雅，所以留他们在王面前侍立。

chapters.en: In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his whole kingdom.
chapters.zh: 王考问他们一切事，就见他们的智慧聪明比通国的术士和用法术的胜过十倍。

chapters.en: And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
chapters.zh: 到古列王元年，但以理还在。

chapters.en: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams; his mind was troubled and he could not sleep.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒在位第二年，他作了梦，心里烦乱，不能睡觉。

chapters.en: So the king summoned the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers and astrologers to tell him what he had dreamed. When they came in and stood before the king,
chapters.zh: 王吩咐人将术士，用法术的，行邪术的，和迦勒底人召来，要他们将王的梦告诉王，他们就来站在王前。

chapters.en: he said to them, “I have had a dream that troubles me and I want to know what it means. ”
chapters.zh: 王对他们说，我作了一梦，心里烦乱，要知道这是什么梦。

chapters.en: Then the astrologers answered the king, “May the king live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will interpret it.”
chapters.zh: 迦勒底人用亚兰的言语对王说，愿王万岁。请将那梦告诉仆人，仆人就可以讲解。

chapters.en: The king replied to the astrologers, “This is what I have firmly decided: If you do not tell me what my dream was and interpret it, I will have you cut into pieces and your houses turned into piles of rubble.
chapters.zh: 王回答迦勒底人说，梦我已经忘了（或作我已定命八节同），你们若不将梦和梦的讲解告诉我，就必被凌迟，你们的房屋必成为粪堆。

chapters.en: But if you tell me the dream and explain it, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and interpret it for me.”
chapters.zh: 你们若将梦和梦的讲解告诉我，就必从我这里得赠品和赏赐，并大尊荣。现在你们要将梦和梦的讲解告诉我。

chapters.en: Once more they replied, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will interpret it.”
chapters.zh: 他们第二次对王说，请王将梦告诉仆人，仆人就可以讲解。

chapters.en: Then the king answered, “I am certain that you are trying to gain time, because you realize that this is what I have firmly decided:
chapters.zh: 王回答说，我准知道你们是故意迟延，因为你们知道那梦我已经忘了。

chapters.en: If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one penalty for you. You have conspired to tell me misleading and wicked things, hoping the situation will change. So then, tell me the dream, and I will know that you can interpret it for me.”
chapters.zh: 你们若不将梦告诉我，只有一法待你们。因为你们预备了谎言乱语向我说，要等候时势改变。现在你们要将梦告诉我，因我知道你们能将梦的讲解告诉我。

chapters.en: The astrologers answered the king, “There is no one on earth who can do what the king asks! No king, however great and mighty, has ever asked such a thing of any magician or enchanter or astrologer.
chapters.zh: 迦勒底人在王面前回答说，世上没有人能将王所问的事说出来。因为没有君王，大臣，掌权的向术士，或用法术的，或迦勒底人问过这样的事。

chapters.en: What the king asks is too difficult. No one can reveal it to the king except the gods, and they do not live among humans.”
chapters.zh: 王所问的事甚难。除了不与世人同居的神明，没有人在王面前能说出来。

chapters.en: This made the king so angry and furious that he ordered the execution of all the wise men of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 因此，王气忿忿地大发烈怒，吩咐灭绝巴比伦所有的哲士。

chapters.en: So the decree was issued to put the wise men to death, and men were sent to look for Daniel and his friends to put them to death.
chapters.zh: 于是命令发出，哲士将要见杀，人就寻找但以理和他的同伴，要杀他们。

chapters.en: When Arioch, the commander of the king’s guard, had gone out to put to death the wise men of Babylon, Daniel spoke to him with wisdom and tact.
chapters.zh: 王的护卫长亚略出来，要杀巴比伦的哲士，但以理就用婉言回答他，

chapters.en: He asked the king’s officer, “Why did the king issue such a harsh decree?” Arioch then explained the matter to Daniel.
chapters.zh: 向王的护卫长亚略说，王的命令为何这样紧急呢？亚略就将情节告诉但以理。

chapters.en: At this, Daniel went in to the king and asked for time, so that he might interpret the dream for him.
chapters.zh: 但以理遂进去求王宽限，就可以将梦的讲解告诉王。

chapters.en: Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.
chapters.zh: 但以理回到他的居所，将这事告诉他的同伴哈拿尼雅，米沙利，亚撒利雅，

chapters.en: He urged them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that he and his friends might not be executed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 要他们祈求天上的神施怜悯，将这奥秘的事指明，免得但以理和他的同伴与巴比伦其余的哲士一同灭亡。

chapters.en: During the night the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision. Then Daniel praised the God of heaven
chapters.zh: 这奥秘的事就在夜间异象中给但以理显明，但以理便称颂天上的神。

chapters.en: and said: “Praise be to the name of God for ever and ever; wisdom and power are his.
chapters.zh: 但以理说，神的名是应当称颂的。从亘古直到永远，因为智慧能力都属乎他。

chapters.en: He changes times and seasons; he deposes kings and raises up others. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning.
chapters.zh: 他改变时候，日期，废王，立王，将智慧赐与智慧人，将知识赐与聪明人。

chapters.en: He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with him.
chapters.zh: 他显明深奥隐秘的事，知道暗中所有的，光明也与他同居。

chapters.en: I thank and praise you, God of my ancestors: You have given me wisdom and power, you have made known to me what we asked of you, you have made known to us the dream of the king.”
chapters.zh: 我列祖的神阿，我感谢你，赞美你，因你将智慧才能赐给我，允准我们所求的，把王的事给我们指明。

chapters.en: Then Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to execute the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, “Do not execute the wise men of Babylon. Take me to the king, and I will interpret his dream for him.”
chapters.zh: 于是，但以理进去见亚略，就是王所派灭绝巴比伦哲士的，对他说，不要灭绝巴比伦的哲士，求你领我到王面前，我要将梦的讲解告诉王。

chapters.en: Arioch took Daniel to the king at once and said, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can tell the king what his dream means.”
chapters.zh: 亚略就急忙将但以理领到王面前，对王说，我在被掳的犹大人中遇见一人，他能将梦的讲解告诉王。

chapters.en: The king asked Daniel (also called Belteshazzar), “Are you able to tell me what I saw in my dream and interpret it?”
chapters.zh: 王问称为伯提沙撒的但以理说，你能将我所作的梦和梦的讲解告诉我吗？

chapters.en: Daniel replied, “No wise man, enchanter, magician or diviner can explain to the king the mystery he has asked about,
chapters.zh: 但以理在王面前回答说，王所问的那奥秘事，哲士，用法术的，术士，观兆的都不能告诉王。

chapters.en: but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries. He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in days to come. Your dream and the visions that passed through your mind as you were lying in bed are these:
chapters.zh: 只有一位在天上的神能显明奥秘的事。他已将日后必有的事指示尼布甲尼撒王。你的梦和你在床上脑中的异象是这样，

chapters.en: “As Your Majesty was lying there, your mind turned to things to come, and the revealer of mysteries showed you what is going to happen.
chapters.zh: 王阿，你在床上想到后来的事，那显明奥秘事的主把将来必有的事指示你。

chapters.en: As for me, this mystery has been revealed to me, not because I have greater wisdom than anyone else alive, but so that Your Majesty may know the interpretation and that you may understand what went through your mind.
chapters.zh: 至于那奥秘的事显明给我，并非因我的智慧胜过一切活人，乃为使王知道梦的讲解和心里的思念。

chapters.en: “Your Majesty looked, and there before you stood a large statue—an enormous, dazzling statue, awesome in appearance.
chapters.zh: 王阿，你梦见一个大像，这像甚高，极其光耀，站在你面前，形状甚是可怕。

chapters.en: The head of the statue was made of pure gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,
chapters.zh: 这像的头是精金的，胸膛和膀臂是银的，肚腹和腰是铜的，

chapters.en: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of baked clay.
chapters.zh: 腿是铁的，脚是半铁半泥的。

chapters.en: While you were watching, a rock was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and smashed them.
chapters.zh: 你观看，见有一块非人手凿出来的石头打在这像半铁半泥的脚上，把脚砸碎。

chapters.en: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were all broken to pieces and became like chaff on a threshing floor in the summer. The wind swept them away without leaving a trace. But the rock that struck the statue became a huge mountain and filled the whole earth.
chapters.zh: 于是金，银，铜，铁，泥都一同砸得粉碎，成如夏天禾场上的糠秕，被风吹散，无处可寻。打碎这像的石头变成一座大山，充满天下。

chapters.en: “This was the dream, and now we will interpret it to the king.
chapters.zh: 这就是那梦。我们在王面前要讲解那梦。

chapters.en: Your Majesty, you are the king of kings. The God of heaven has given you dominion and power and might and glory;
chapters.zh: 王阿，你是诸王之王。天上的神已将国度，权柄，能力，尊荣都赐给你。

chapters.en: in your hands he has placed all mankind and the beasts of the field and the birds in the sky. Wherever they live, he has made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold.
chapters.zh: 凡世人所住之地的走兽，并天空的飞鸟，他都交付你手，使你掌管这一切。你就是那金头。

chapters.en: “After you, another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours. Next, a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule over the whole earth.
chapters.zh: 在你以后必另兴一国，不及于你。又有第三国，就是铜的，必掌管天下。

chapters.en: Finally, there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron—for iron breaks and smashes everything—and as iron breaks things to pieces, so it will crush and break all the others.
chapters.zh: 第四国，必坚壮如铁，铁能打碎克制百物，又能压碎一切，那国也必打碎压制列国。

chapters.en: Just as you saw that the feet and toes were partly of baked clay and partly of iron, so this will be a divided kingdom; yet it will have some of the strength of iron in it, even as you saw iron mixed with clay.
chapters.zh: 你既见像的脚和脚指头，一半是窑匠的泥，一半是铁，那国将来也必分开。你既见铁与泥搀杂，那国也必有铁的力量。

chapters.en: As the toes were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
chapters.zh: 那脚指头，既是半铁半泥，那国也必半强半弱。

chapters.en: And just as you saw the iron mixed with baked clay, so the people will be a mixture and will not remain united, any more than iron mixes with clay.
chapters.zh: 你既见铁与泥搀杂，那国民也必与各种人搀杂，却不能彼此相合，正如铁与泥不能相合一样。

chapters.en: “In the time of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will crush all those kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will itself endure forever.
chapters.zh: 当那列王在位的时候，天上的神必另立一国，永不败坏，也不归别国的人，却要打碎灭绝那一切国，这国必存到永远。

chapters.en: This is the meaning of the vision of the rock cut out of a mountain, but not by human hands—a rock that broke the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold to pieces. “The great God has shown the king what will take place in the future. The dream is true and its interpretation is trustworthy.”
chapters.zh: 你既看见非人手凿出来的一块石头从山而出，打碎金，银，铜，铁，泥，那就是至大的神把后来必有的事给王指明。这梦准是这样，这讲解也是确实的。

chapters.en: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell prostrate before Daniel and paid him honor and ordered that an offering and incense be presented to him.
chapters.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒王俯伏在地，向但以理下拜，并且吩咐人给他奉上供物和香品。

chapters.en: The king said to Daniel, “Surely your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, for you were able to reveal this mystery.”
chapters.zh: 王对但以理说，你既能显明这奥秘的事，你们的神诚然是万神之神，万王之主，又是显明奥秘事的。

chapters.en: Then the king placed Daniel in a high position and lavished many gifts on him. He made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and placed him in charge of all its wise men.
chapters.zh: 于是王高抬但以理，赏赐他许多上等礼物，派他管理巴比伦全省，又立他为总理，掌管巴比伦的一切哲士。

chapters.en: Moreover, at Daniel’s request the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego administrators over the province of Babylon, while Daniel himself remained at the royal court.
chapters.zh: 但以理求王，王就派沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌管理巴比伦省的事务，只是但以理常在朝中侍立。

chapters.en: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王造了一个金像，高六十肘，宽六肘，立在巴比伦省杜拉平原。

chapters.en: He then summoned the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates and all the other provincial officials to come to the dedication of the image he had set up.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王差人将总督，钦差，巡抚，臬司，藩司，谋士，法官，和各省的官员都召了来，为尼布甲尼撒王所立的像行开光之礼。

chapters.en: So the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates and all the other provincial officials assembled for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before it.
chapters.zh: 于是总督，钦差，巡抚，臬司，藩司，谋士，法官，和各省的官员都聚集了来，要为尼布甲尼撒王所立的像行开光之礼，就站在尼布甲尼撒所立的像前。

chapters.en: Then the herald loudly proclaimed, “Nations and peoples of every language, this is what you are commanded to do:
chapters.zh: 那时传令的大声呼叫说，各方，各国，各族的人哪（族原文作舌下同），有令传与你们，

chapters.en: As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
chapters.zh: 你们一听见角，笛，琵琶，琴，瑟，笙，和各样乐器的声音，就当俯伏敬拜尼布甲尼撒王所立的金像。

chapters.en: Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace.”
chapters.zh: 凡不俯伏敬拜的，必立时扔在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en: Therefore, as soon as they heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp and all kinds of music, all the nations and peoples of every language fell down and worshiped the image of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
chapters.zh: 因此各方，各国，各族的人民一听见角，笛，琵琶，琴，瑟，和各样乐器的声音，就都俯伏敬拜尼布甲尼撒王所立的金像。

chapters.en: At this time some astrologers came forward and denounced the Jews.
chapters.zh: 那时，有几个迦勒底人进前来控告犹大人。

chapters.en: They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, “May the king live forever!
chapters.zh: 他们对尼布甲尼撒王说，愿王万岁。

chapters.en: Your Majesty has issued a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe and all kinds of music must fall down and worship the image of gold,
chapters.zh: 王阿，你曾降旨说，凡听见角，笛，琵琶，琴，瑟，笙，和各样乐器声音的都当俯伏敬拜金像。

chapters.en: and that whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into a blazing furnace.
chapters.zh: 凡不俯伏敬拜的，必扔在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en: But there are some Jews whom you have set over the affairs of the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego—who pay no attention to you, Your Majesty. They neither serve your gods nor worship the image of gold you have set up.”
chapters.zh: 现在有几个犹大人，就是王所派管理巴比伦省事务的沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌。王阿，这些人不理你，不事奉你的神，也不敬拜你所立的金像。

chapters.en: Furious with rage, Nebuchadnezzar summoned Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. So these men were brought before the king,
chapters.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒冲冲大怒，吩咐人把沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌带过来，他们就把那些人带到王面前。

chapters.en: and Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the image of gold I have set up?
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒问他们说，沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌，你们不事奉我的神，也不敬拜我所立的金像，是故意的吗？

chapters.en: Now when you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe and all kinds of music, if you are ready to fall down and worship the image I made, very good. But if you do not worship it, you will be thrown immediately into a blazing furnace. Then what god will be able to rescue you from my hand?”
chapters.zh: 你们再听见角，笛，琵琶，琴，瑟，笙，和各样乐器的声音，若俯伏敬拜我所造的像，却还可以。若不敬拜，必立时扔在烈火的窑中，有何神能救你们脱离我手呢？

chapters.en: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego replied to him, “King Nebuchadnezzar, we do not need to defend ourselves before you in this matter.
chapters.zh: 沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌对王说，尼布甲尼撒阿，这件事我们不必回答你。

chapters.en: If we are thrown into the blazing furnace, the God we serve is able to deliver us from it, and he will deliver us from Your Majesty’s hand.
chapters.zh: 即便如此，我们所事奉的神能将我们从烈火的窑中救出来。王阿，他也必救我们脱离你的手。

chapters.en: But even if he does not, we want you to know, Your Majesty, that we will not serve your gods or worship the image of gold you have set up.”
chapters.zh: 即或不然，王阿，你当知道我们决不事奉你的神，也不敬拜你所立的金像。

chapters.en: Then Nebuchadnezzar was furious with Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, and his attitude toward them changed. He ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual
chapters.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒怒气填胸，向沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌变了脸色，吩咐人把窑烧热，比寻常更加七倍。

chapters.en: and commanded some of the strongest soldiers in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego and throw them into the blazing furnace.
chapters.zh: 又吩咐他军中的几个壮士，将沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌捆起来，扔在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en: So these men, wearing their robes, trousers, turbans and other clothes, were bound and thrown into the blazing furnace.
chapters.zh: 这三人穿着裤子，内袍，外衣，和别的衣服，被捆起来扔在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en: The king’s command was so urgent and the furnace so hot that the flames of the fire killed the soldiers who took up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego,
chapters.zh: 因为王命紧急，窑又甚热，那抬沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌的人都被火焰烧死。

chapters.en: and these three men, firmly tied, fell into the blazing furnace.
chapters.zh: 沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌这三个人都被捆着落在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en: Then King Nebuchadnezzar leaped to his feet in amazement and asked his advisers, “Weren’t there three men that we tied up and threw into the fire?” They replied, “Certainly, Your Majesty.”
chapters.zh: 那时，尼布甲尼撒王惊奇，急忙起来，对谋士说，我捆起来扔在火里的不是三个人吗？他们回答王说，王阿，是。

chapters.en: He said, “Look! I see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods.”
chapters.zh: 王说，看哪，我见有四个人，并没有捆绑，在火中游行，也没有受伤。那第四个的相貌好像神子。

chapters.en: Nebuchadnezzar then approached the opening of the blazing furnace and shouted, “Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!” So Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego came out of the fire,
chapters.zh: 于是，尼布甲尼撒就近烈火窑门，说，至高神的仆人沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌出来，上这里来吧。沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌就从火中出来了。

chapters.en: and the satraps, prefects, governors and royal advisers crowded around them. They saw that the fire had not harmed their bodies, nor was a hair of their heads singed; their robes were not scorched, and there was no smell of fire on them.
chapters.zh: 那些总督，钦差，巡抚，和王的谋士一同聚集看这三个人，见火无力伤他们的身体，头发也没有烧焦，衣裳也没有变色，并没有火燎的气味。

chapters.en: Then Nebuchadnezzar said, “Praise be to the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, who has sent his angel and rescued his servants! They trusted in him and defied the king’s command and were willing to give up their lives rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒说，沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌的神是应当称颂的。他差遣使者救护倚靠他的仆人，他们不遵王命，舍去己身，在他们神以外不肯事奉敬拜别神。

chapters.en: Therefore I decree that the people of any nation or language who say anything against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego be cut into pieces and their houses be turned into piles of rubble, for no other god can save in this way.”
chapters.zh: 现在我降旨，无论何方，何国，何族的人，凡有人毁谤沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌之神的，必被凌迟，他的房屋必成粪堆，因为没有别神能这样施行拯救。

chapters.en: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 那时王在巴比伦省，高升了沙得拉，米煞，亚伯尼歌。

chapters.en: King Nebuchadnezzar, To the nations and peoples of every language, who live in all the earth: May you prosper greatly!
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王晓谕住在全地各方，各国，各族的人说，愿你们大享平安。

chapters.en: It is my pleasure to tell you about the miraculous signs and wonders that the Most High God has performed for me.
chapters.zh: 我乐意将至高的神向我所行的神迹奇事宣扬出来。

chapters.en: How great are his signs, how mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an eternal kingdom; his dominion endures from generation to generation.
chapters.zh: 他的神迹何其大。他的奇事何其盛。他的国是永远的。他的权柄存到万代。

chapters.en: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at home in my palace, contented and prosperous.
chapters.zh: 我尼布甲尼撒安居在宫中，平顺在殿内。

chapters.en: I had a dream that made me afraid. As I was lying in bed, the images and visions that passed through my mind terrified me.
chapters.zh: 我作了一梦，使我惧怕。我在床上的思念，并脑中的异象，使我惊惶。

chapters.en: So I commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be brought before me to interpret the dream for me.
chapters.zh: 所以我降旨召巴比伦的一切哲士到我面前，叫他们把梦的讲解告诉我。

chapters.en: When the magicians, enchanters, astrologers and diviners came, I told them the dream, but they could not interpret it for me.
chapters.zh: 于是那些术士，用法术的，迦勒底人，观兆的都进来，我将那梦告诉了他们，他们却不能把梦的讲解告诉我。

chapters.en: Finally, Daniel came into my presence and I told him the dream. (He is called Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and the spirit of the holy gods is in him.)
chapters.zh: 末后那照我神的名，称为伯提沙撒的但以理来到我面前，他里头有圣神的灵，我将梦告诉他说，

chapters.en: I said, “Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no mystery is too difficult for you. Here is my dream; interpret it for me.
chapters.zh: 术士的领袖伯提沙撒阿，因我知道你里头有圣神的灵，什么奥秘的事都不能使你为难。现在要把我梦中所见的异象和梦的讲解告诉我。

chapters.en: These are the visions I saw while lying in bed: I looked, and there before me stood a tree in the middle of the land. Its height was enormous.
chapters.zh: 我在床上脑中的异象是这样，我看见地当中有一棵树，极其高大。

chapters.en: The tree grew large and strong and its top touched the sky; it was visible to the ends of the earth.
chapters.zh: 那树渐长，而且坚固，高得顶天，从地极都能看见，

chapters.en: Its leaves were beautiful, its fruit abundant, and on it was food for all. Under it the wild animals found shelter, and the birds lived in its branches; from it every creature was fed.
chapters.zh: 叶子华美，果子甚多，可作众生的食物。田野的走兽卧在荫下，天空的飞鸟宿在枝上。凡有血气的都从这树得食。

chapters.en: “In the visions I saw while lying in bed, I looked, and there before me was a holy one, a messenger, coming down from heaven.
chapters.zh: 我在床上脑中的异象，见有一位守望的圣者从天而降。

chapters.en: He called in a loud voice: ‘Cut down the tree and trim off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it and the birds from its branches.
chapters.zh: 大声呼叫说，伐倒这树。砍下枝子。摇掉叶子。抛散果子。使走兽离开树下，飞鸟躲开树枝。

chapters.en: But let the stump and its roots, bound with iron and bronze, remain in the ground, in the grass of the field. “ ‘Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let him live with the animals among the plants of the earth.
chapters.zh: 树墩却要留在地内，用铁圈和铜圈箍住，在田野的青草中让天露滴湿，使他与地上的兽一同吃草，

chapters.en: Let his mind be changed from that of a man and let him be given the mind of an animal, till seven times pass by for him.
chapters.zh: 使他的心改变，不如人心。给他一个兽心，使他经过七期（期或作年。本章同）。

chapters.en: “ ‘The decision is announced by messengers, the holy ones declare the verdict, so that the living may know that the Most High is sovereign over all kingdoms on earth and gives them to anyone he wishes and sets over them the lowliest of people.’
chapters.zh: 这是守望者所发的命，圣者所出的令，好叫世人知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁，或立极卑微的人执掌国权。

chapters.en: “This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, had. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means, for none of the wise men in my kingdom can interpret it for me. But you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
chapters.zh: 这是我尼布甲尼撒王所作的梦。伯提沙撒阿，你要说明这梦的讲解。因为我国中的一切哲士都不能将梦的讲解告诉我，惟独你能，因你里头有圣神的灵。

chapters.en: Then Daniel (also called Belteshazzar) was greatly perplexed for a time, and his thoughts terrified him. So the king said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning alarm you.” Belteshazzar answered, “My lord, if only the dream applied to your enemies and its meaning to your adversaries!
chapters.zh: 于是称为伯提沙撒的但以理惊讶片时，心意惊惶。王说，伯提沙撒阿，不要因梦和梦的讲解惊惶。伯提沙撒回答说，我主阿，愿这梦归与恨恶你的人，讲解归与你的敌人。

chapters.en: The tree you saw, which grew large and strong, with its top touching the sky, visible to the whole earth,
chapters.zh: 你所见的树渐长，而且坚固，高得顶天，从地极都能看见。

chapters.en: with beautiful leaves and abundant fruit, providing food for all, giving shelter to the wild animals, and having nesting places in its branches for the birds—
chapters.zh: 叶子华美，果子甚多，可作众生的食物。田野的走兽住在其下。天空的飞鸟宿在枝上。

chapters.en: Your Majesty, you are that tree! You have become great and strong; your greatness has grown until it reaches the sky, and your dominion extends to distant parts of the earth.
chapters.zh: 王阿，这渐长又坚固的树就是你。你的威势渐长及天，你的权柄管到地极。

chapters.en: “Your Majesty saw a holy one, a messenger, coming down from heaven and saying, ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump, bound with iron and bronze, in the grass of the field, while its roots remain in the ground. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven; let him live with the wild animals, until seven times pass by for him.’
chapters.zh: 王既看见一位守望的圣者从天而降，说，将这树砍伐毁坏，树墩却要留在地内，用铁圈和铜圈箍住。在田野的青草中，让天露滴湿，使他与地上的兽一同吃草，直到经过七期。

chapters.en: “This is the interpretation, Your Majesty, and this is the decree the Most High has issued against my lord the king:
chapters.zh: 王阿，讲解就是这样，临到我主我王的事是出于至高者的命。

chapters.en: You will be driven away from people and will live with the wild animals; you will eat grass like the ox and be drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven times will pass by for you until you acknowledge that the Most High is sovereign over all kingdoms on earth and gives them to anyone he wishes.
chapters.zh: 你必被赶出离开世人，与野地的兽同居，吃草如牛，被天露滴湿，且要经过七期。等你知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁。

chapters.en: The command to leave the stump of the tree with its roots means that your kingdom will be restored to you when you acknowledge that Heaven rules.
chapters.zh: 守望者既吩咐存留树墩，等你知道诸天掌权，以后你的国必定归你。

chapters.en: Therefore, Your Majesty, be pleased to accept my advice: Renounce your sins by doing what is right, and your wickedness by being kind to the oppressed. It may be that then your prosperity will continue.”
chapters.zh: 王阿，求你悦纳我的谏言，以施行公义断绝罪过，以怜悯穷人除掉罪孽，或者你的平安可以延长。

chapters.en: All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
chapters.zh: 这事都临到尼布甲尼撒王。

chapters.en: Twelve months later, as the king was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon,
chapters.zh: 过了十二个月，他游行在巴比伦王宫里（原文作上）。

chapters.en: he said, “Is not this the great Babylon I have built as the royal residence, by my mighty power and for the glory of my majesty?”
chapters.zh: 他说，这大巴比伦不是我用大能大力建为京都，要显我威严的荣耀吗？

chapters.en: Even as the words were on his lips, a voice came from heaven, “This is what is decreed for you, King Nebuchadnezzar: Your royal authority has been taken from you.
chapters.zh: 这话在王口中尚未说完，有声音从天降下，说，尼布甲尼撒王阿，有话对你说，你的国位离开你了。

chapters.en: You will be driven away from people and will live with the wild animals; you will eat grass like the ox. Seven times will pass by for you until you acknowledge that the Most High is sovereign over all kingdoms on earth and gives them to anyone he wishes.”
chapters.zh: 你必被赶出离开世人，与野地的兽同居，吃草如牛，且要经过七期。等你知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁。

chapters.en: Immediately what had been said about Nebuchadnezzar was fulfilled. He was driven away from people and ate grass like the ox. His body was drenched with the dew of heaven until his hair grew like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird.
chapters.zh: 当时这话就应验在尼布甲尼撒的身上，他被赶出离开世人，吃草如牛，身被天露滴湿，头发长长，好像鹰毛。指甲长长，如同鸟爪。

chapters.en: At the end of that time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, raised my eyes toward heaven, and my sanity was restored. Then I praised the Most High; I honored and glorified him who lives forever. His dominion is an eternal dominion; his kingdom endures from generation to generation.
chapters.zh: 日子满足，我尼布甲尼撒举目望天，我的聪明复归于我，我便称颂至高者，赞美尊敬活到永远的神。他的权柄是永有的。他的国存到万代。

chapters.en: All the peoples of the earth are regarded as nothing. He does as he pleases with the powers of heaven and the peoples of the earth. No one can hold back his hand or say to him: “What have you done?”
chapters.zh: 世上所有的居民都算为虚无。在天上的万军和世上的居民中，他都凭自己的意旨行事。无人能拦住他手，或问他说，你做什么呢？

chapters.en: At the same time that my sanity was restored, my honor and splendor were returned to me for the glory of my kingdom. My advisers and nobles sought me out, and I was restored to my throne and became even greater than before.
chapters.zh: 那时，我的聪明复归于我，为我国的荣耀，威严，和光耀也都复归于我。并且我的谋士和大臣也来朝见我。我又得坚立在国位上，至大的权柄加增于我。

chapters.en: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, because everything he does is right and all his ways are just. And those who walk in pride he is able to humble.
chapters.zh: 现在我尼布甲尼撒赞美，尊崇，恭敬天上的王。因为他所作的全都诚实，他所行的也都公平。那行动骄傲的，他能降为卑。

chapters.en: King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his nobles and drank wine with them.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒王为他的一千大臣设摆盛筵，与这一千人对面饮酒。

chapters.en: While Belshazzar was drinking his wine, he gave orders to bring in the gold and silver goblets that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines might drink from them.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒欢饮之间，吩咐人将他父（父或作祖下同）尼布甲尼撒从耶路撒冷殿中所掠的金银器皿拿来，王与大臣，皇后，妃嫔好用这器皿饮酒。

chapters.en: So they brought in the gold goblets that had been taken from the temple of God in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.
chapters.zh: 于是他们把耶路撒冷神殿库房中所掠的金器皿拿来，王和大臣，皇后，妃嫔就用这器皿饮酒。

chapters.en: As they drank the wine, they praised the gods of gold and silver, of bronze, iron, wood and stone.
chapters.zh: 他们饮酒，赞美金，银，铜，铁，木，石所造的神。

chapters.en: Suddenly the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. The king watched the hand as it wrote.
chapters.zh: 当时，忽有人的指头显出，在王宫与灯台相对的粉墙上写字。王看见写字的指头，

chapters.en: His face turned pale and he was so frightened that his legs became weak and his knees were knocking.
chapters.zh: 就变了脸色，心意惊惶，腰骨好像脱节，双膝彼此相碰，

chapters.en: The king summoned the enchanters, astrologers and diviners. Then he said to these wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing and tells me what it means will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around his neck, and he will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”
chapters.zh: 大声吩咐将用法术的和迦勒底人并观兆的领进来，对巴比伦的哲士说，谁能读这文字，把讲解告诉我，他必身穿紫袍，项带金链，在我国中位列第三。
