chapters.en: Then all the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or tell the king what it meant.
chapters.zh: 于是王的一切哲士都进来，却不能读那文字，也不能把讲解告诉王。

chapters.en: So King Belshazzar became even more terrified and his face grew more pale. His nobles were baffled.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒王就甚惊惶，脸色改变，他的大臣也都惊奇。

chapters.en: The queen, hearing the voices of the king and his nobles, came into the banquet hall. “May the king live forever!” she said. “Don’t be alarmed! Don’t look so pale!
chapters.zh: 太后（或作皇后下同）因王和他大臣所说的话，就进入宴宫，说，愿王万岁。你心意不要惊惶，脸面不要变色。

chapters.en: There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In the time of your father he was found to have insight and intelligence and wisdom like that of the gods. Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, astrologers and diviners.
chapters.zh: 在你国中有一人，他里头有圣神的灵，你父在世的日子，这人心中光明，又有聪明智慧，好像神的智慧。你父尼布甲尼撒王，就是王的父，立他为术士，用法术的，和迦勒底人，并观兆的领袖。

chapters.en: He did this because Daniel, whom the king called Belteshazzar, was found to have a keen mind and knowledge and understanding, and also the ability to interpret dreams, explain riddles and solve difficult problems. Call for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means.”
chapters.zh: 在他里头有美好的灵性，又有知识聪明，能圆梦，释谜语，解疑惑。这人名叫但以理，尼布甲尼撒王又称他为伯提沙撒，现在可以召他来，他必解明这意思。

chapters.en: So Daniel was brought before the king, and the king said to him, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles my father the king brought from Judah?
chapters.zh: 但以理就被领到王前。王问但以理说，你是被掳之犹大人中的但以理吗？就是我父王从犹大掳来的吗？

chapters.en: I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you and that you have insight, intelligence and outstanding wisdom.
chapters.zh: 我听说你里头有神的灵，心中光明，又有聪明和美好的智慧。

chapters.en: The wise men and enchanters were brought before me to read this writing and tell me what it means, but they could not explain it.
chapters.zh: 现在哲士和用法术的都领到我面前，为叫他们读这文字，把讲解告诉我，无奈他们都不能把讲解说出来。

chapters.en: Now I have heard that you are able to give interpretations and to solve difficult problems. If you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around your neck, and you will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”
chapters.zh: 我听说你善于讲解，能解疑惑。现在你若能读这文字，把讲解告诉我，就必身穿紫袍，项戴金链，在我国中位列第三。

chapters.en: Then Daniel answered the king, “You may keep your gifts for yourself and give your rewards to someone else. Nevertheless, I will read the writing for the king and tell him what it means.
chapters.zh: 但以理在王面前回答说，你的赠品可以归你自己，你的赏赐可以归给别人。我却要为王读这文字，把讲解告诉王。

chapters.en: “Your Majesty, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar sovereignty and greatness and glory and splendor.
chapters.zh: 王阿，至高的神曾将国位，大权，荣耀，威严赐与你父尼布甲尼撒。

chapters.en: Because of the high position he gave him, all the nations and peoples of every language dreaded and feared him. Those the king wanted to put to death, he put to death; those he wanted to spare, he spared; those he wanted to promote, he promoted; and those he wanted to humble, he humbled.
chapters.zh: 因神所赐他的大权，各方，各国，各族的人都在他面前战兢恐惧。他可以随意生杀，随意升降。

chapters.en: But when his heart became arrogant and hardened with pride, he was deposed from his royal throne and stripped of his glory.
chapters.zh: 但他心高气傲，灵也刚愎，甚至行事狂傲，就被革去王位，夺去荣耀。

chapters.en: He was driven away from people and given the mind of an animal; he lived with the wild donkeys and ate grass like the ox; and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he acknowledged that the Most High God is sovereign over all kingdoms on earth and sets over them anyone he wishes.
chapters.zh: 他被赶出离开世人，他的心变如兽心，与野驴同居，吃草如牛，身被天露滴湿，等他知道至高的神在人的国中掌权，凭自己的意旨立人治国。

chapters.en: “But you, Belshazzar, his son, have not humbled yourself, though you knew all this.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒阿，你是他的儿子（或作孙子），你虽知道这一切，你心仍不自卑，

chapters.en: Instead, you have set yourself up against the Lord of heaven. You had the goblets from his temple brought to you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or understand. But you did not honor the God who holds in his hand your life and all your ways.
chapters.zh: 竟向天上的主自高，使人将他殿中的器皿拿到你面前，你和大臣，皇后，妃嫔用这器皿饮酒。你又赞美那不能看，不能听，无知无识，金，银，铜，铁，木，石所造的神，却没有将荣耀归与那手中有你气息，管理你一切行动的神。

chapters.en: Therefore he sent the hand that wrote the inscription.
chapters.zh: 因此从神那里显出指头来写这文字。

chapters.en: “This is the inscription that was written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN
chapters.zh: 所写的文字是，弥尼，弥尼，提客勒，乌法珥新。

chapters.en: “Here is what these words mean: Mene : God has numbered the days of your reign and brought it to an end.
chapters.zh: 讲解是这样，弥尼，就是神已经数算你国的年日到此完毕。

chapters.en: Tekel : You have been weighed on the scales and found wanting.
chapters.zh: 提客勒，就是你被称在天平里，显出你的亏欠。

chapters.en: Peres : Your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.”
chapters.zh: 毗勒斯（与乌法珥新同义），就是你的国分裂，归与玛代人和波斯人。

chapters.en: Then at Belshazzar’s command, Daniel was clothed in purple, a gold chain was placed around his neck, and he was proclaimed the third highest ruler in the kingdom.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒下令，人就把紫袍给但以理穿上，把金链给他戴在颈项上，又传令使他在国中位列第三。

chapters.en: That very night Belshazzar, king of the Babylonians, was slain,
chapters.zh: 当夜，迦勒底王伯沙撒被杀。

chapters.en: and Darius the Mede took over the kingdom, at the age of sixty-two.
chapters.zh: 玛代人大利乌年六十二岁，取了迦勒底国。

chapters.en: It pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps to rule throughout the kingdom,
chapters.zh: 大利乌随心所愿，立一百二十个总督，治理通国。

chapters.en: with three administrators over them, one of whom was Daniel. The satraps were made accountable to them so that the king might not suffer loss.
chapters.zh: 又在他们以上立总长三人（但以理在其中），使总督在他们三人面前回覆事务，免得王受亏损。

chapters.en: Now Daniel so distinguished himself among the administrators and the satraps by his exceptional qualities that the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.
chapters.zh: 因这但以理有美好的灵性，所以显然超乎其余的总长和总督，王又想立他治理通国。

chapters.en: At this, the administrators and the satraps tried to find grounds for charges against Daniel in his conduct of government affairs, but they were unable to do so. They could find no corruption in him, because he was trustworthy and neither corrupt nor negligent.
chapters.zh: 那时，总长和总督寻找但以理误国的把柄，为要参他。只是找不着他的错误过失，因他忠心办事，毫无错误过失。

chapters.en: Finally these men said, “We will never find any basis for charges against this man Daniel unless it has something to do with the law of his God.”
chapters.zh: 那些人便说，我们要找参这但以理的把柄，除非在他神的律法中就寻不着。

chapters.en: So these administrators and satraps went as a group to the king and said: “May King Darius live forever!
chapters.zh: 于是，总长和总督纷纷聚集来见王，说，愿大利乌王万岁。

chapters.en: The royal administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers and governors have all agreed that the king should issue an edict and enforce the decree that anyone who prays to any god or human being during the next thirty days, except to you, Your Majesty, shall be thrown into the lions’ den.
chapters.zh: 国中的总长，钦差，总督，谋士，和巡抚彼此商议，要立一条坚定的禁令（或作求王下旨要立一条云云），三十日内，不拘何人，若在王以外，或向神或向人求什么，就必扔在狮子坑中。

chapters.en: Now, Your Majesty, issue the decree and put it in writing so that it cannot be altered—in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed.”
chapters.zh: 王阿，现在求你立这禁令，加盖玉玺，使禁令决不更改。照玛代和波斯人的例是不可更改的。

chapters.en: So King Darius put the decree in writing.
chapters.zh: 于是大利乌王立这禁令，加盖玉玺。

chapters.en: Now when Daniel learned that the decree had been published, he went home to his upstairs room where the windows opened toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to his God, just as he had done before.
chapters.zh: 但以理知道这禁令盖了玉玺，就到自己家里（他楼上的窗户开向耶路撒冷），一日三次，双膝跪在他神面前，祷告感谢，与素常一样。

chapters.en: Then these men went as a group and found Daniel praying and asking God for help.
chapters.zh: 那些人就纷纷聚集，见但以理在他神面前祈祷恳求。

chapters.en: So they went to the king and spoke to him about his royal decree: “Did you not publish a decree that during the next thirty days anyone who prays to any god or human being except to you, Your Majesty, would be thrown into the lions’ den?” The king answered, “The decree stands—in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed.”
chapters.zh: 他们便进到王前，提王的禁令，说，王阿，三十日内不拘何人，若在王以外，或向神或向人求什么，必被扔在狮子坑中。王不是在这禁令上盖了玉玺吗？王回答说，实有这事，照玛代和波斯人的例，是不可更改的。

chapters.en: Then they said to the king, “Daniel, who is one of the exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, Your Majesty, or to the decree you put in writing. He still prays three times a day.”
chapters.zh: 他们对王说，王阿，那被掳之犹大人中的但以理不理你，也不遵你盖了玉玺的禁令，他竟一日三次祈祷。

chapters.en: When the king heard this, he was greatly distressed; he was determined to rescue Daniel and made every effort until sundown to save him.
chapters.zh: 王听见这话，就甚愁烦，一心要救但以理，筹划解救他，直到日落的时候。

chapters.en: Then the men went as a group to King Darius and said to him, “Remember, Your Majesty, that according to the law of the Medes and Persians no decree or edict that the king issues can be changed.”
chapters.zh: 那些人就纷纷聚集来见王，说，王阿，当知道玛代人和波斯人有例，凡王所立的禁令和律例都不可更改。

chapters.en: So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the lions’ den. The king said to Daniel, “May your God, whom you serve continually, rescue you!”
chapters.zh: 王下令，人就把但以理带来，扔在狮子坑中。王对但以理说，你所常事奉的神，他必救你。

chapters.en: A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that Daniel’s situation might not be changed.
chapters.zh: 有人搬石头放在坑口，王用自己的玺和大臣的印，封闭那坑，使惩办但以理的事毫无更改。

chapters.en: Then the king returned to his palace and spent the night without eating and without any entertainment being brought to him. And he could not sleep.
chapters.zh: 王回宫，终夜禁食，无人拿乐器到他面前，并且睡不着觉。

chapters.en: At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the lions’ den.
chapters.zh: 次日黎明，王就起来，急忙往狮子坑那里去。

chapters.en: When he came near the den, he called to Daniel in an anguished voice, “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?”
chapters.zh: 临近坑边，哀声呼叫但以理，对但以理说，永生神的仆人但以理阿，你所常事奉的神能救你脱离狮子吗？

chapters.en: Daniel answered, “May the king live forever!
chapters.zh: 但以理对王说，愿王万岁。

chapters.en: My God sent his angel, and he shut the mouths of the lions. They have not hurt me, because I was found innocent in his sight. Nor have I ever done any wrong before you, Your Majesty.”
chapters.zh: 我的神差遣使者，封住狮子的口，叫狮子不伤我。因我在神面前无辜，我在王面前也没有行过亏损的事。

chapters.en: The king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift Daniel out of the den. And when Daniel was lifted from the den, no wound was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
chapters.zh: 王就甚喜乐，吩咐人将但以理从坑里系上来。于是但以理从坑里被系上来，身上毫无伤损，因为信靠他的神。

chapters.en: At the king’s command, the men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought in and thrown into the lions’ den, along with their wives and children. And before they reached the floor of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
chapters.zh: 王下令，人就把那些控告但以理的人，连他们的妻子儿女都带来，扔在狮子坑中。他们还没有到坑底，狮子就抓住他们（抓住原文作胜了），咬碎他们的骨头。

chapters.en: Then King Darius wrote to all the nations and peoples of every language in all the earth: “May you prosper greatly!
chapters.zh: 那时，大利乌王传旨，晓谕住在全地各方，各国，各族的人说，愿你们大享平安。

chapters.en: “I issue a decree that in every part of my kingdom people must fear and reverence the God of Daniel. “For he is the living God and he endures forever; his kingdom will not be destroyed, his dominion will never end.
chapters.zh: 现在我降旨晓谕我所统辖的全国人民，要在但以理的神面前，战兢恐惧。因为他是永远长存的活神，他的国永不败坏。他的权柄永存无极。

chapters.en: He rescues and he saves; he performs signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth. He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions.”
chapters.zh: 他护庇人，搭救人，在天上地下施行神迹奇事，救了但以理脱离狮子的口。

chapters.en: So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
chapters.zh: 如此，这但以理当大利乌王在位的时候，和波斯王古列在位的时候，大享亨通。

chapters.en: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream, and visions passed through his mind as he was lying in bed. He wrote down the substance of his dream.
chapters.zh: 巴比伦王伯沙撒元年，但以理在床上作梦，见了脑中的异象，就记录这梦，述说其中的大意。

chapters.en: Daniel said: “In my vision at night I looked, and there before me were the four winds of heaven churning up the great sea.
chapters.zh: 但以理说，我夜里见异象，看见天的四风陡起，刮在大海之上。

chapters.en: Four great beasts, each different from the others, came up out of the sea.
chapters.zh: 有四个大兽从海中上来，形状各有不同，

chapters.en: “The first was like a lion, and it had the wings of an eagle. I watched until its wings were torn off and it was lifted from the ground so that it stood on two feet like a human being, and the mind of a human was given to it.
chapters.zh: 头一个像狮子，有鹰的翅膀。我正观看的时候，兽的翅膀被拔去，兽从地上得立起来，用两脚站立，像人一样，又得了人心。

chapters.en: “And there before me was a second beast, which looked like a bear. It was raised up on one of its sides, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. It was told, ‘Get up and eat your fill of flesh!’
chapters.zh: 又有一兽如熊，就是第二兽，旁跨而坐，口齿内衔着三根肋骨。有吩咐这兽的说，起来吞吃多肉。

chapters.en: “After that, I looked, and there before me was another beast, one that looked like a leopard. And on its back it had four wings like those of a bird. This beast had four heads, and it was given authority to rule.
chapters.zh: 此后我观看，又有一兽如豹，背上有鸟的四个翅膀。这兽有四个头，又得了权柄。

chapters.en: “After that, in my vision at night I looked, and there before me was a fourth beast—terrifying and frightening and very powerful. It had large iron teeth; it crushed and devoured its victims and trampled underfoot whatever was left. It was different from all the former beasts, and it had ten horns.
chapters.zh: 其后我在夜间的异象中观看，见第四兽甚是可怕，极其强壮，大有力量，有大铁牙，吞吃嚼碎，所剩下的用脚践踏。这兽与前三兽大不相同，头有十角。

chapters.en: “While I was thinking about the horns, there before me was another horn, a little one, which came up among them; and three of the first horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like the eyes of a human being and a mouth that spoke boastfully.
chapters.zh: 我正观看这些角，见其中又长起一个小角。先前的角中有三角在这角前，连根被它拔出来。这角有眼，像人的眼，有口说夸大的话。

chapters.en: “As I looked, “thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was as white as snow; the hair of his head was white like wool. His throne was flaming with fire, and its wheels were all ablaze.
chapters.zh: 我观看，见有宝座设立，上头坐着亘古常在者。他的衣服洁白如雪，头发如纯净的羊毛。宝座乃火焰，其轮乃烈火。

chapters.en: A river of fire was flowing, coming out from before him. Thousands upon thousands attended him; ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court was seated, and the books were opened.
chapters.zh: 从他面前有火，像河发出。事奉他的有千千，在他面前侍立的有万万。他坐着要行审判，案卷都展开了。

chapters.en: “Then I continued to watch because of the boastful words the horn was speaking. I kept looking until the beast was slain and its body destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.
chapters.zh: 那时我观看，见那兽因小角说夸大话的声音被杀，身体损坏，扔在火中焚烧。

chapters.en: (The other beasts had been stripped of their authority, but were allowed to live for a period of time.)
chapters.zh: 其余的兽，权柄都被夺去，生命却仍存留，直到所定的时候和日期。

chapters.en: “In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence.
chapters.zh: 我在夜间的异象中观看，见有一位像人子的，驾着天云而来，被领到亘古常在者面前，

chapters.en: He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshiped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
chapters.zh: 得了权柄，荣耀，国度，使各方，各国，各族的人都事奉他。他的权柄是永远的，不能废去。他的国必不败坏。

chapters.en: “I, Daniel, was troubled in spirit, and the visions that passed through my mind disturbed me.
chapters.zh: 至于我但以理，我的灵在我里面愁烦，我脑中的异象使我惊惶。

chapters.en: I approached one of those standing there and asked him the meaning of all this. “So he told me and gave me the interpretation of these things:
chapters.zh: 我就近一位侍立者，问他这一切的真情。他就告诉我，将那事的讲解给我说明。

chapters.en: ‘The four great beasts are four kings that will rise from the earth.
chapters.zh: 这四个大兽就是四王将要在世上兴起。

chapters.en: But the holy people of the Most High will receive the kingdom and will possess it forever—yes, for ever and ever.’
chapters.zh: 然而，至高者的圣民，必要得国享受，直到永永远远。

chapters.en: “Then I wanted to know the meaning of the fourth beast, which was different from all the others and most terrifying, with its iron teeth and bronze claws—the beast that crushed and devoured its victims and trampled underfoot whatever was left.
chapters.zh: 那时我愿知道第四兽的真情，它为何与那三兽的真情大不相同，甚是可怕，有铁牙铜爪，吞吃嚼碎，所剩下的用脚践踏。

chapters.en: I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head and about the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell—the horn that looked more imposing than the others and that had eyes and a mouth that spoke boastfully.
chapters.zh: 头有十角和那另长的一角，在这角前有三角被它打落。这角有眼，有说夸大话的口，形状强横，过于它的同类。

chapters.en: As I watched, this horn was waging war against the holy people and defeating them,
chapters.zh: 我观看，见这角与圣民争战，胜了他们。

chapters.en: until the Ancient of Days came and pronounced judgment in favor of the holy people of the Most High, and the time came when they possessed the kingdom.
chapters.zh: 直到亘古常在者来给至高者的圣民伸冤，圣民得国的时候就到了。

chapters.en: “He gave me this explanation: ‘The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on earth. It will be different from all the other kingdoms and will devour the whole earth, trampling it down and crushing it.
chapters.zh: 那侍立者这样说，第四兽就是世上必有的第四国，与一切国大不相同，必吞吃全地，并且践踏嚼碎。

chapters.en: The ten horns are ten kings who will come from this kingdom. After them another king will arise, different from the earlier ones; he will subdue three kings.
chapters.zh: 至于那十角，就是从这国中必兴起的十王，后来又兴起一王，与先前的不同。他必制伏三王。

chapters.en: He will speak against the Most High and oppress his holy people and try to change the set times and the laws. The holy people will be delivered into his hands for a time, times and half a time.
chapters.zh: 他必向至高者说夸大的话，必折磨至高者的圣民，必想改变节期和律法。圣民必交付他手一载，二载，半载。

chapters.en: “ ‘But the court will sit, and his power will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.
chapters.zh: 然而，审判者必坐着行审判。他的权柄必被夺去，毁坏，灭绝，一直到底。

chapters.en: Then the sovereignty, power and greatness of all the kingdoms under heaven will be handed over to the holy people of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will worship and obey him.’
chapters.zh: 国度，权柄，和天下诸国的大权必赐给至高者的圣民。他的国是永远的。一切掌权的都必事奉他，顺从他。

chapters.en: “This is the end of the matter. I, Daniel, was deeply troubled by my thoughts, and my face turned pale, but I kept the matter to myself.”
chapters.zh: 那事至此完毕。至于我但以理，心中甚是惊惶，脸色也改变了，却将那事存记在心。

chapters.en: In the third year of King Belshazzar’s reign, I, Daniel, had a vision, after the one that had already appeared to me.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒王在位第三年，有异象现与我但以理，是在先前所见的异象之后。

chapters.en: In my vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa in the province of Elam; in the vision I was beside the Ulai Canal.
chapters.zh: 我见了异象的时候，我以为在以拦省书珊城中（城或作宫）。我见异象又如在乌莱河边。

chapters.en: I looked up, and there before me was a ram with two horns, standing beside the canal, and the horns were long. One of the horns was longer than the other but grew up later.
chapters.zh: 我举目观看，见有双角的公绵羊站在河边，两角都高。这角高过那角，更高的是后长的。

chapters.en: I watched the ram as it charged toward the west and the north and the south. No animal could stand against it, and none could rescue from its power. It did as it pleased and became great.
chapters.zh: 我见那公绵羊往西，往北，往南抵触。兽在它面前都站立不住，也没有能救护脱离它手的。但它任意而行，自高自大。

chapters.en: As I was thinking about this, suddenly a goat with a prominent horn between its eyes came from the west, crossing the whole earth without touching the ground.
chapters.zh: 我正思想的时候，见有一只公山羊从西而来，遍行全地，脚不沾尘。这山羊两眼当中有一非常的角。

chapters.en: It came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and charged at it in great rage.
chapters.zh: 它往我所看见，站在河边有双角的公绵羊那里去，大发忿怒，向它直闯。

chapters.en: I saw it attack the ram furiously, striking the ram and shattering its two horns. The ram was powerless to stand against it; the goat knocked it to the ground and trampled on it, and none could rescue the ram from its power.
chapters.zh: 我见公山羊就近公绵羊，向它发烈怒，抵触它，折断它的两角。绵羊在它面前站立不住。它将绵羊触倒在地，用脚践踏，没有能救绵羊脱离它手的。

chapters.en: The goat became very great, but at the height of its power the large horn was broken off, and in its place four prominent horns grew up toward the four winds of heaven.
chapters.zh: 这山羊极其自高自大，正强盛的时候，那大角折断了，又在角根上向天的四方（方原文作风）长出四个非常的角来。

chapters.en: Out of one of them came another horn, which started small but grew in power to the south and to the east and toward the Beautiful Land.
chapters.zh: 四角之中有一角长出一个小角，向南，向东，向荣美之地，渐渐成为强大。

chapters.en: It grew until it reached the host of the heavens, and it threw some of the starry host down to the earth and trampled on them.
chapters.zh: 它渐渐强大，高及天象，将些天象和星宿抛落在地，用脚践踏。

chapters.en: It set itself up to be as great as the commander of the army of the LORD; it took away the daily sacrifice from the LORD, and his sanctuary was thrown down.
chapters.zh: 并且它自高自大，以为高及天象之君。除掉常献给君的燔祭，毁坏君的圣所。

chapters.en: Because of rebellion, the LORD’s people and the daily sacrifice were given over to it. It prospered in everything it did, and truth was thrown to the ground.
chapters.zh: 因罪过的缘故，有军旅和常献的燔祭交付它。它将真理抛在地上，任意而行，无不顺利。

chapters.en: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, “How long will it take for the vision to be fulfilled—the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, the surrender of the sanctuary and the trampling underfoot of the LORD’s people?”
chapters.zh: 我听见有一位圣者说话，又有一位圣者问那说话的圣者说，这除掉常献的燔祭和施行毁坏的罪过，将圣所与军旅践踏的异象（军旅或作以色列的军），要到几时才应验呢？

chapters.en: He said to me, “It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be reconsecrated.”
chapters.zh: 他对我说，到二千三百日，圣所就必洁净。

chapters.en: While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there before me stood one who looked like a man.
chapters.zh: 我但以理见了这异象，愿意明白其中的意思。忽有一位形状像人的站在我面前。

chapters.en: And I heard a man’s voice from the Ulai calling, “Gabriel, tell this man the meaning of the vision.”
chapters.zh: 我又听见乌莱河两岸中有人声呼叫说，加百列阿，要使此人明白这异象。

chapters.en: As he came near the place where I was standing, I was terrified and fell prostrate. “Son of man,” he said to me, “understand that the vision concerns the time of the end.”
chapters.zh: 他便来到我所站的地方。他一来，我就惊慌俯伏在地。他对我说，人子阿，你要明白，因为这是关乎末后的异象。

chapters.en: While he was speaking to me, I was in a deep sleep, with my face to the ground. Then he touched me and raised me to my feet.
chapters.zh: 他与我说话的时候，我面伏在地沉睡。他就摸我，扶我站起来，

chapters.en: He said: “I am going to tell you what will happen later in the time of wrath, because the vision concerns the appointed time of the end.
chapters.zh: 说，我要指示你恼怒临完必有的事，因为这是关乎末后的定期。

chapters.en: The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.
chapters.zh: 你所看见双角的公绵羊，就是玛代和波斯王。

chapters.en: The shaggy goat is the king of Greece, and the large horn between its eyes is the first king.
chapters.zh: 那公山羊就是希腊王（希腊原文作雅完下同）。两眼当中的大角就是头一王。

chapters.en: The four horns that replaced the one that was broken off represent four kingdoms that will emerge from his nation but will not have the same power.
chapters.zh: 至于那折断了的角，在其根上又长出四角，这四角就是四国，必从这国里兴起来，只是权势都不及他。

chapters.en: “In the latter part of their reign, when rebels have become completely wicked, a fierce-looking king, a master of intrigue, will arise.
chapters.zh: 这四国末时，犯法的人罪恶满盈，必有一王兴起，面貌凶恶，能用双关的诈语。

chapters.en: He will become very strong, but not by his own power. He will cause astounding devastation and will succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy those who are mighty, the holy people.
chapters.zh: 他的权柄必大，却不是因自己的能力。他必行非常的毁灭，事情顺利，任意而行。又必毁灭有能力的和圣民。

chapters.en: He will cause deceit to prosper, and he will consider himself superior. When they feel secure, he will destroy many and take his stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be destroyed, but not by human power.
chapters.zh: 他用权术成就手中的诡计，心里自高自大，在人坦然无备的时候，毁灭多人。又要站起来攻击万君之君，至终却非因人手而灭亡。

chapters.en: “The vision of the evenings and mornings that has been given you is true, but seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.”
chapters.zh: 所说二千三百日的异象是真的，但你要将这异象封住，因为关乎后来许多的日子。

chapters.en: I, Daniel, was worn out. I lay exhausted for several days. Then I got up and went about the king’s business. I was appalled by the vision; it was beyond understanding.
chapters.zh: 于是我但以理昏迷不醒，病了数日，然后起来办理王的事务。我因这异象惊奇，却无人能明白其中的意思。

chapters.en: In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes (a Mede by descent), who was made ruler over the Babylonian kingdom—
chapters.zh: 玛代族亚哈随鲁的儿子大利乌立为迦勒底国的王元年，

chapters.en: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the Scriptures, according to the word of the LORD given to Jeremiah the prophet, that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.
chapters.zh: 就是他在位第一年，我但以理从书上得知耶和华的话临到先知耶利米，论耶路撒冷荒凉的年数，七十年为满。

chapters.en: So I turned to the Lord God and pleaded with him in prayer and petition, in fasting, and in sackcloth and ashes.
chapters.zh: 我便禁食，披麻蒙灰，定意向主神祈祷恳求。

chapters.en: I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed: “Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps his covenant of love with those who love him and keep his commandments,
chapters.zh: 我向耶和华我的神祈祷，认罪，说，主阿，大而可畏的神，向爱主，守主诫命的人守约施慈爱。

chapters.en: we have sinned and done wrong. We have been wicked and have rebelled; we have turned away from your commands and laws.
chapters.zh: 我们犯罪作孽，行恶叛逆，偏离你的诫命典章，

chapters.en: We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes and our ancestors, and to all the people of the land.
chapters.zh: 没有听从你仆人众先知奉你名向我们君王，首领，列祖，和国中一切百姓所说的话。

chapters.en: “Lord, you are righteous, but this day we are covered with shame—the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and all Israel, both near and far, in all the countries where you have scattered us because of our unfaithfulness to you.
chapters.zh: 主阿，你是公义的，我们是脸上蒙羞的。因我们犹大人和耶路撒冷的居民，并以色列众人，或在近处，或在远处，被你赶到各国的人，都得罪了你，正如今日一样。

chapters.en: We and our kings, our princes and our ancestors are covered with shame, LORD, because we have sinned against you.
chapters.zh: 主阿，我们和我们的君王，首领，列祖因得罪了你，就都脸上蒙羞。

chapters.en: The Lord our God is merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against him;
chapters.zh: 主我们的神是怜悯饶恕人的，我们却违背了他，

chapters.en: we have not obeyed the LORD our God or kept the laws he gave us through his servants the prophets.
chapters.zh: 也没有听从耶和华我们神的话，没有遵行他借仆人众先知向我们所陈明的律法。

chapters.en: All Israel has transgressed your law and turned away, refusing to obey you. “Therefore the curses and sworn judgments written in the Law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out on us, because we have sinned against you.
chapters.zh: 以色列众人都犯了你的律法，偏行，不听从你的话。因此，在你仆人摩西律法上所写的咒诅和誓言都倾在我们身上，因我们得罪了神。

chapters.en: You have fulfilled the words spoken against us and against our rulers by bringing on us great disaster. Under the whole heaven nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 他使大灾祸临到我们，成就了警戒我们和审判我们官长的话。原来在普天之下未曾行过像在耶路撒冷所行的。

chapters.en: Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come on us, yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our sins and giving attention to your truth.
chapters.zh: 这一切灾祸临到我们身上是照摩西律法上所写的，我们却没有求耶和华我们神的恩典，使我们回头离开罪孽，明白你的真理。

chapters.en: The LORD did not hesitate to bring the disaster on us, for the LORD our God is righteous in everything he does; yet we have not obeyed him.
chapters.zh: 所以耶和华留意使这灾祸临到我们身上，因为耶和华我们的神在他所行的事上都是公义。我们并没有听从他的话。

chapters.en: “Now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of Egypt with a mighty hand and who made for yourself a name that endures to this day, we have sinned, we have done wrong.
chapters.zh: 主我们的神阿，你曾用大能的手领你的子民出埃及地，使自己得了名，正如今日一样。我们犯了罪，作了恶。

chapters.en: Lord, in keeping with all your righteous acts, turn away your anger and your wrath from Jerusalem, your city, your holy hill. Our sins and the iniquities of our ancestors have made Jerusalem and your people an object of scorn to all those around us.
chapters.zh: 主阿，求你按你的大仁大义，使你的怒气和忿怒转离你的城耶路撒冷，就是你的圣山。耶路撒冷和你的子民，因我们的罪恶和我们列祖的罪孽被四围的人羞辱。

chapters.en: “Now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of your servant. For your sake, Lord, look with favor on your desolate sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 我们的神阿，现在求你垂听仆人的祈祷恳求，为自己使脸光照你荒凉的圣所。

chapters.en: Give ear, our God, and hear; open your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears your Name. We do not make requests of you because we are righteous, but because of your great mercy.
chapters.zh: 我的神阿，求你侧耳而听，睁眼而看，眷顾我们荒凉之地和称为你名下的城。我们在你面前恳求，原不是因自己的义，乃因你的大怜悯。

chapters.en: Lord, listen! Lord, forgive! Lord, hear and act! For your sake, my God, do not delay, because your city and your people bear your Name.”
chapters.zh: 求主垂听，求主赦免，求主应允而行，为你自己不要迟延。我的神阿，因这城和这民都是称为你名下的。

chapters.en: While I was speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel and making my request to the LORD my God for his holy hill—
chapters.zh: 我说话，祷告，承认我的罪和本国之民以色列的罪，为我神的圣山，在耶和华我神面前恳求。

chapters.en: while I was still in prayer, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.
chapters.zh: 我正祷告的时候，先前在异象中所见的那位加百列，奉命迅速飞来，约在献晚祭的时候，按手在我身上。

chapters.en: He instructed me and said to me, “Daniel, I have now come to give you insight and understanding.
chapters.zh: 他指教我说，但以理阿，现在我出来要使你有智慧，有聪明。

chapters.en: As soon as you began to pray, a word went out, which I have come to tell you, for you are highly esteemed. Therefore, consider the word and understand the vision:
chapters.zh: 你初恳求的时候，就发出命令，我来告诉你，因你大蒙眷爱。所以你要思想明白这以下的事和异象。

chapters.en: “Seventy ‘sevens’ are decreed for your people and your holy city to finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for wickedness, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy and to anoint the Most Holy Place.
chapters.zh: 为你本国之民和你圣城，已经定了七十个七。要止住罪过，除净罪恶，赎尽罪孽，引进（或作彰显）永义，封住异象和预言，并膏至圣者（者或作所）。

chapters.en: “Know and understand this: From the time the word goes out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the ruler, comes, there will be seven ‘sevens,’ and sixty-two ‘sevens.’ It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of trouble.
chapters.zh: 你当知道，当明白，从出令重新建造耶路撒冷，直到有受膏君的时候，必有七个七和六十二个七。正在艰难的时候，耶路撒冷城连街带濠都必重新建造。

chapters.en: After the sixty-two ‘sevens,’ the Anointed One will be put to death and will have nothing. The people of the ruler who will come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. The end will come like a flood: War will continue until the end, and desolations have been decreed.
chapters.zh: 过了六十二个七，那受膏者（那或作有）必被剪除，一无所有。必有一王的民来毁灭这城和圣所，至终必如洪水冲没。必有争战，一直到底，荒凉的事已经定了。

chapters.en: He will confirm a covenant with many for one ‘seven.’ In the middle of the ‘seven’ he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And at the temple he will set up an abomination that causes desolation, until the end that is decreed is poured out on him. ”
chapters.zh: 一七之内，他必与许多人坚定盟约。一七之半，他必使祭祀与供献止息。那行毁坏可憎的（或作使地荒凉的）如飞而来，并且有忿怒倾在那行毁坏的身上（或作倾在那荒凉之地），直到所定的结局。

chapters.en: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a revelation was given to Daniel (who was called Belteshazzar). Its message was true and it concerned a great war. The understanding of the message came to him in a vision.
chapters.zh: 波斯王古列第三年，有事显给称为伯提沙撒的但以理。这事是真的，是指着大争战。但以理通达这事，明白这异象。

chapters.en: At that time I, Daniel, mourned for three weeks.
chapters.zh: 当那时，我但以理悲伤了三个七日。

chapters.en: I ate no choice food; no meat or wine touched my lips; and I used no lotions at all until the three weeks were over.
chapters.zh: 美味我没有吃，酒肉没有入我的口，也没有用油抹我的身，直到满了三个七日。

chapters.en: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,
chapters.zh: 正月二十四日，我在希底结大河边，

chapters.en: I looked up and there before me was a man dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz around his waist.
chapters.zh: 举目观看，见有一人身穿细麻衣，腰束乌法精金带。

chapters.en: His body was like topaz, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of burnished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.
chapters.zh: 他身体如水苍玉，面貌如闪电，眼目如火把，手和脚如光明的铜，说话的声音如大众的声音。

chapters.en: I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision; those who were with me did not see it, but such terror overwhelmed them that they fled and hid themselves.
chapters.zh: 这异象惟有我但以理一人看见，同着我的人没有看见。他们却大大战兢，逃跑隐藏，

chapters.en: So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision; I had no strength left, my face turned deathly pale and I was helpless.
chapters.zh: 只剩下我一人。我见了这大异象便浑身无力，面貌失色，毫无气力。

chapters.en: Then I heard him speaking, and as I listened to him, I fell into a deep sleep, my face to the ground.
chapters.zh: 我却听见他说话的声音，一听见就面伏在地沉睡了。

chapters.en: A hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.
chapters.zh: 忽然，有一手按在我身上，使我用膝和手掌支持微起。

chapters.en: He said, “Daniel, you who are highly esteemed, consider carefully the words I am about to speak to you, and stand up, for I have now been sent to you.” And when he said this to me, I stood up trembling.
chapters.zh: 他对我说，大蒙眷爱的但以理阿，要明白我与你所说的话，只管站起来，因为我现在奉差遣来到你这里。他对我说这话，我便战战兢兢地立起来。

chapters.en: Then he continued, “Do not be afraid, Daniel. Since the first day that you set your mind to gain understanding and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.
chapters.zh: 他就说，但以理阿，不要惧怕。因为从你第一日专心求明白将来的事，又在你神面前刻苦己心，你的言语已蒙应允。我是因你的言语而来。

chapters.en: But the prince of the Persian kingdom resisted me twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, because I was detained there with the king of Persia.
chapters.zh: 但波斯国的魔君拦阻我二十一日。忽然有大君（就是天使长。二十一节同）中的一位米迦勒来帮助我，我就停留在波斯诸王那里。

chapters.en: Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the future, for the vision concerns a time yet to come.”
chapters.zh: 现在我来，要使你明白本国之民日后必遭遇的事，因为这异象关乎后来许多的日子。

chapters.en: While he was saying this to me, I bowed with my face toward the ground and was speechless.
chapters.zh: 他向我这样说，我就脸面朝地，哑口无声。

chapters.en: Then one who looked like a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and began to speak. I said to the one standing before me, “I am overcome with anguish because of the vision, my lord, and I feel very weak.
chapters.zh: 不料，有一位像人的，摸我的嘴唇，我便开口向那站在我面前的说，我主阿，因见这异象，我大大愁苦，毫无气力。

chapters.en: How can I, your servant, talk with you, my lord? My strength is gone and I can hardly breathe.”
chapters.zh: 我主的仆人怎能与我主说话呢？我一见异象就浑身无力，毫无气息。

chapters.en: Again the one who looked like a man touched me and gave me strength.
chapters.zh: 有一位形状像人的又摸我，使我有力量。

chapters.en: “Do not be afraid, you who are highly esteemed,” he said. “Peace! Be strong now; be strong.” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened and said, “Speak, my lord, since you have given me strength.”
chapters.zh: 他说，大蒙眷爱的人哪，不要惧怕，愿你平安。你总要坚强。他一向我说话，我便觉得有力量，说，我主请说，因你使我有力量。

chapters.en: So he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Soon I will return to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I go, the prince of Greece will come;
chapters.zh: 他就说，你知道我为何来见你吗？现在我要回去与波斯的魔君争战，我去后，希腊（原文作雅完）的魔君必来。

chapters.en: but first I will tell you what is written in the Book of Truth. (No one supports me against them except Michael, your prince.
chapters.zh: 但我要将那录在真确书上的事告诉你。除了你们的大君米迦勒之外，没有帮助我抵挡这两魔君的。

chapters.en: And in the first year of Darius the Mede, I took my stand to support and protect him.)
chapters.zh: 又说，当玛代王大利乌元年，我曾起来扶助米迦勒，使他坚强。

chapters.en: “Now then, I tell you the truth: Three more kings will arise in Persia, and then a fourth, who will be far richer than all the others. When he has gained power by his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
chapters.zh: 现在我将真事指示你，波斯还有三王兴起，第四王必富足远胜诸王。他因富足成为强盛，就必激动大众攻击希腊国。

chapters.en: Then a mighty king will arise, who will rule with great power and do as he pleases.
chapters.zh: 必有一个勇敢的王兴起，执掌大权，随意而行。

chapters.en: After he has arisen, his empire will be broken up and parceled out toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, nor will it have the power he exercised, because his empire will be uprooted and given to others.
chapters.zh: 他兴起的时候，他的国必破裂，向天的四方（方原文作风）分开，却不归他的后裔，治国的权势也都不及他。因为他的国必被拔出，归与他后裔之外的人。

chapters.en: “The king of the South will become strong, but one of his commanders will become even stronger than he and will rule his own kingdom with great power.
chapters.zh: 南方的王必强盛，他将帅中必有一个比他更强盛，执掌权柄，他的权柄甚大。

chapters.en: After some years, they will become allies. The daughter of the king of the South will go to the king of the North to make an alliance, but she will not retain her power, and he and his power will not last. In those days she will be betrayed, together with her royal escort and her father and the one who supported her.
chapters.zh: 过些年后，他们必互相连合，南方王的女儿必就了北方王来立约。但这女子帮助之力存立不住，王和他所倚靠之力也不能存立。这女子和引导她来的，并生她的，以及当时扶助她的，都必交与死地。

chapters.en: “One from her family line will arise to take her place. He will attack the forces of the king of the North and enter his fortress; he will fight against them and be victorious.
chapters.zh: 但这女子的本家（本家原文作根）必另生一子（子原文作枝）继续王位，他必率领军队进入北方王的保障，攻击他们，而且得胜。

chapters.en: He will also seize their gods, their metal images and their valuable articles of silver and gold and carry them off to Egypt. For some years he will leave the king of the North alone.
chapters.zh: 并将他们的神像和铸成的偶像，与金银的宝器掠到埃及去。数年之内，他不去攻击北方的王。

chapters.en: Then the king of the North will invade the realm of the king of the South but will retreat to his own country.
chapters.zh: 北方的王（原文作他）必入南方王的国，却要仍回本地。

chapters.en: His sons will prepare for war and assemble a great army, which will sweep on like an irresistible flood and carry the battle as far as his fortress.
chapters.zh: 北方王（原文作他）的二子必动干戈，招聚许多军兵。这军兵前去，如洪水泛滥，又必再去争战，直到南方王的保障。

chapters.en: “Then the king of the South will march out in a rage and fight against the king of the North, who will raise a large army, but it will be defeated.
chapters.zh: 南方王必发烈怒，出来与北方王争战，摆列大军。北方王的军兵必交付他手。

chapters.en: When the army is carried off, the king of the South will be filled with pride and will slaughter many thousands, yet he will not remain triumphant.
chapters.zh: 他的众军高傲，他的心也必自高。他虽使数万人仆倒，却不得常胜。

chapters.en: For the king of the North will muster another army, larger than the first; and after several years, he will advance with a huge army fully equipped.
chapters.zh: 北方王必回来摆列大军，比先前的更多。满了所定的年数，他必率领大军，带极多的军装来。

chapters.en: “In those times many will rise against the king of the South. Those who are violent among your own people will rebel in fulfillment of the vision, but without success.
chapters.zh: 那时，必有许多人起来攻击南方王，并且你本国的强暴人必兴起，要应验那异象，他们却要败亡。

chapters.en: Then the king of the North will come and build up siege ramps and will capture a fortified city. The forces of the South will be powerless to resist; even their best troops will not have the strength to stand.
chapters.zh: 北方王必来筑垒攻取坚固城。南方的军兵必站立不住，就是选择的精兵（精兵原文作民）也无力站住。

chapters.en: The invader will do as he pleases; no one will be able to stand against him. He will establish himself in the Beautiful Land and will have the power to destroy it.
chapters.zh: 来攻击他的，必任意而行，无人在北方王（原文作他）面前站立得住。他必站在那荣美之地，用手施行毁灭。

chapters.en: He will determine to come with the might of his entire kingdom and will make an alliance with the king of the South. And he will give him a daughter in marriage in order to overthrow the kingdom, but his plans will not succeed or help him.
chapters.zh: 他必定意用全国之力而来，立公正的约，照约而行，将自己的女儿给南方王为妻，想要败坏他（或作埃及），这计却不得成就，与自己毫无益处。

chapters.en: Then he will turn his attention to the coastlands and will take many of them, but a commander will put an end to his insolence and will turn his insolence back on him.
chapters.zh: 其后他必转回夺取了许多海岛。但有一大帅，除掉他令人受的羞辱，并且使这羞辱归他本身。

chapters.en: After this, he will turn back toward the fortresses of his own country but will stumble and fall, to be seen no more.
chapters.zh: 他就必转向本地的保障，却要绊跌仆倒，归于无有。

chapters.en: “His successor will send out a tax collector to maintain the royal splendor. In a few years, however, he will be destroyed, yet not in anger or in battle.
chapters.zh: 那时，必有一人兴起接续他为王，使横征暴敛的人通行国中的荣美地。这王不多日就必灭亡，却不因忿怒，也不因争战。

chapters.en: “He will be succeeded by a contemptible person who has not been given the honor of royalty. He will invade the kingdom when its people feel secure, and he will seize it through intrigue.
chapters.zh: 必有一个卑鄙的人兴起接续为王，人未曾将国的尊荣给他，他却趁人坦然无备的时候，用谄媚的话得国。

chapters.en: Then an overwhelming army will be swept away before him; both it and a prince of the covenant will be destroyed.
chapters.zh: 必有无数的军兵势如洪水，在他面前冲没败坏。同盟的君也必如此。

chapters.en: After coming to an agreement with him, he will act deceitfully, and with only a few people he will rise to power.
chapters.zh: 与那君结盟之后，他必行诡诈，因为他必上来以微小的军（原文作民）成为强盛。

chapters.en: When the richest provinces feel secure, he will invade them and will achieve what neither his fathers nor his forefathers did. He will distribute plunder, loot and wealth among his followers. He will plot the overthrow of fortresses—but only for a time.
chapters.zh: 趁人坦然无备的时候，他必来到国中极肥美之地，行他列祖和他列祖之祖所未曾行的，将掳物，掠物，和财宝散给众人，又要设计攻打保障，然而这都是暂时的。

chapters.en: “With a large army he will stir up his strength and courage against the king of the South. The king of the South will wage war with a large and very powerful army, but he will not be able to stand because of the plots devised against him.
chapters.zh: 他必奋勇向前，率领大军攻击南方王。南方王也必以极大极强的军兵与他争战，却站立不住，因为有人设计谋害南方王。

chapters.en: Those who eat from the king’s provisions will try to destroy him; his army will be swept away, and many will fall in battle.
chapters.zh: 吃王膳的，必败坏他。他的军队必被冲没，而且被杀的甚多。

chapters.en: The two kings, with their hearts bent on evil, will sit at the same table and lie to each other, but to no avail, because an end will still come at the appointed time.
chapters.zh: 至于这二王，他们心怀恶计，同席说谎，计谋却不成就。因为到了定期，事就了结。

chapters.en: The king of the North will return to his own country with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant. He will take action against it and then return to his own country.
chapters.zh: 北方王（原文作他）必带许多财宝回往本国，他的心反对圣约，任意而行，回到本地。

chapters.en: “At the appointed time he will invade the South again, but this time the outcome will be different from what it was before.
chapters.zh: 到了定期，他必返回，来到南方。后一次却不如前一次，

chapters.en: Ships of the western coastlands will oppose him, and he will lose heart. Then he will turn back and vent his fury against the holy covenant. He will return and show favor to those who forsake the holy covenant.
chapters.zh: 因为基提战船必来攻击他，他就丧胆而回，又要恼恨圣约，任意而行。他必回来联络背弃圣约的人。

chapters.en: “His armed forces will rise up to desecrate the temple fortress and will abolish the daily sacrifice. Then they will set up the abomination that causes desolation.
chapters.zh: 他必兴兵，这兵必亵渎圣地，就是保障，除掉常献的燔祭，设立那行毁坏可憎的。

chapters.en: With flattery he will corrupt those who have violated the covenant, but the people who know their God will firmly resist him.
chapters.zh: 作恶违背圣约的人，他必用巧言勾引。惟独认识神的子民必刚强行事。

chapters.en: “Those who are wise will instruct many, though for a time they will fall by the sword or be burned or captured or plundered.
chapters.zh: 民间的智慧人必训诲多人。然而他们多日必倒在刀下，或被火烧，或被掳掠抢夺。

chapters.en: When they fall, they will receive a little help, and many who are not sincere will join them.
chapters.zh: 他们仆倒的时候，稍得扶助，却有许多人用谄媚的话亲近他们。

chapters.en: Some of the wise will stumble, so that they may be refined, purified and made spotless until the time of the end, for it will still come at the appointed time.
chapters.zh: 智慧人中有些仆倒的，为要熬炼其余的人，使他们清净洁白，直到末了。因为到了定期，事就了结。

chapters.en: “The king will do as he pleases. He will exalt and magnify himself above every god and will say unheard-of things against the God of gods. He will be successful until the time of wrath is completed, for what has been determined must take place.
chapters.zh: 王必任意而行，自高自大，超过所有的神，又用奇异的话攻击万神之神。他必行事亨通，直到主的忿怒完毕，因为所定的事必然成就。

chapters.en: He will show no regard for the gods of his ancestors or for the one desired by women, nor will he regard any god, but will exalt himself above them all.
chapters.zh: 他必不顾他列祖的神，也不顾妇女所羡慕的神，无论何神他都不顾。因为他必自大，高过一切。

chapters.en: Instead of them, he will honor a god of fortresses; a god unknown to his ancestors he will honor with gold and silver, with precious stones and costly gifts.
chapters.zh: 他倒要敬拜保障的神，用金，银，宝石和可爱之物敬奉他列祖所不认识的神。

chapters.en: He will attack the mightiest fortresses with the help of a foreign god and will greatly honor those who acknowledge him. He will make them rulers over many people and will distribute the land at a price.
chapters.zh: 他必靠外邦神的帮助，攻破最坚固的保障。凡承认他的，他必将荣耀加给他们，使他们管辖许多人，又为贿赂分地与他们。

chapters.en: “At the time of the end the king of the South will engage him in battle, and the king of the North will storm out against him with chariots and cavalry and a great fleet of ships. He will invade many countries and sweep through them like a flood.
chapters.zh: 到末了，南方王要与他交战。北方王必用战车，马兵，和许多战船，势如暴风来攻击他，也必进入列国，如洪水泛滥。

chapters.en: He will also invade the Beautiful Land. Many countries will fall, but Edom, Moab and the leaders of Ammon will be delivered from his hand.
chapters.zh: 又必进入那荣美之地，有许多国就被倾覆，但以东人，摩押人，和一大半亚扪人必脱离他的手。

chapters.en: He will extend his power over many countries; Egypt will not escape.
chapters.zh: 他必伸手攻击列国。埃及地也不得脱离。

chapters.en: He will gain control of the treasures of gold and silver and all the riches of Egypt, with the Libyans and Cushites in submission.
chapters.zh: 他必把持埃及的金银财宝和各样的宝物。吕彼亚人和古实人都必跟从他。

chapters.en: But reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will set out in a great rage to destroy and annihilate many.
chapters.zh: 但从东方和北方必有消息扰乱他，他就大发烈怒出去，要将多人杀灭净尽。

chapters.en: He will pitch his royal tents between the seas at the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.
chapters.zh: 他必在海和荣美的圣山中间设立他如宫殿的帐幕。然而到了他的结局，必无人能帮助他。

chapters.en: “At that time Michael, the great prince who protects your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress such as has not happened from the beginning of nations until then. But at that time your people—everyone whose name is found written in the book—will be delivered.
chapters.zh: 那时，保佑你本国之民的天使长（原文作大君）米迦勒必站起来，并且有大艰难，从有国以来直到此时，没有这样的。你本国的民中，凡名录在册上的，必得拯救。

chapters.en: Multitudes who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake: some to everlasting life, others to shame and everlasting contempt.
chapters.zh: 睡在尘埃中的，必有多人复醒。其中有得永生的，有受羞辱永远被憎恶的。

chapters.en: Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars for ever and ever.
chapters.zh: 智慧人必发光如同天上的光。那使多人归义的，必发光如星，直到永永远远。

chapters.en: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.”
chapters.zh: 但以理阿，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑（或作切心研究），知识就必增长。

chapters.en: Then I, Daniel, looked, and there before me stood two others, one on this bank of the river and one on the opposite bank.
chapters.zh: 我但以理观看，见另有两个人站立，一个在河这边，一个在河那边。

chapters.en: One of them said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, “How long will it be before these astonishing things are fulfilled?”
chapters.zh: 有一个问那站在河水以上，穿细麻衣的说，这奇异的事到几时才应验呢？

chapters.en: The man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, lifted his right hand and his left hand toward heaven, and I heard him swear by him who lives forever, saying, “It will be for a time, times and half a time. When the power of the holy people has been finally broken, all these things will be completed.”
chapters.zh: 我听见那站在河水以上，穿细麻衣的，向天举起左右手，指着活到永远的主起誓说，要到一载，二载，半载，打破圣民权力的时候，这一切事就都应验了。

chapters.en: I heard, but I did not understand. So I asked, “My lord, what will the outcome of all this be?”
chapters.zh: 我听见这话，却不明白，就说，我主阿，这些事的结局是怎样呢？

chapters.en: He replied, “Go your way, Daniel, because the words are rolled up and sealed until the time of the end.
chapters.zh: 他说，但以理阿，你只管去。因为这话已经隐藏封闭，直到末时。

chapters.en: Many will be purified, made spotless and refined, but the wicked will continue to be wicked. None of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.
chapters.zh: 必有许多人使自己清净洁白，且被熬炼。但恶人仍必行恶，一切恶人都不明白，惟独智慧人能明白。

chapters.en: “From the time that the daily sacrifice is abolished and the abomination that causes desolation is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
chapters.zh: 从除掉常献的燔祭，并设立那行毁坏可憎之物的时候，必有一千二百九十日。

chapters.en: Blessed is the one who waits for and reaches the end of the 1,335 days.
chapters.zh: 等到一千三百三十五日的，那人便为有福。

chapters.en: “As for you, go your way till the end. You will rest, and then at the end of the days you will rise to receive your allotted inheritance.”
chapters.zh: 你且去等候结局，因为你必安歇。到了末期，你必起来，享受你的福分。

chapters.en: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Jehoash king of Israel:
chapters.zh: 当乌西雅，约坦，亚哈斯，希西家作犹大王，约阿施的儿子耶罗波安，作以色列王的时候，耶和华的话临到备利的儿子何西阿。

chapters.en: When the LORD began to speak through Hosea, the LORD said to him, “Go, marry a promiscuous woman and have children with her, for like an adulterous wife this land is guilty of unfaithfulness to the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华初次与何西阿说话，对他说，你去娶淫妇为妻，也收那从淫乱所生的儿女，因为这地大行淫乱，离弃耶和华。

chapters.en: So he married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
chapters.zh: 于是，何西阿去娶了滴拉音的女儿歌篾。这妇人怀孕，给他生了一个儿子。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Hosea, “Call him Jezreel, because I will soon punish the house of Jehu for the massacre at Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对何西阿说，给他起名叫耶斯列，因为再过片时，我必讨耶户家在耶斯列杀人流血的罪，也必使以色列家的国灭绝。

chapters.en: In that day I will break Israel’s bow in the Valley of Jezreel.”
chapters.zh: 到那日，我必在耶斯列平原折断以色列的弓。

chapters.en: Gomer conceived again and gave birth to a daughter. Then the LORD said to Hosea, “Call her Lo-Ruhamah (which means “not loved”), for I will no longer show love to Israel, that I should at all forgive them.
chapters.zh: 歌篾又怀孕生了一个女儿，耶和华对何西阿说，给她起名叫罗路哈玛（就是不蒙怜悯的意思），因为我必不再怜悯以色列家，决不赦免他们。

chapters.en: Yet I will show love to Judah; and I will save them—not by bow, sword or battle, or by horses and horsemen, but I, the LORD their God, will save them.”
chapters.zh: 我却要怜悯犹大家，使他们靠耶和华他们的神得救，不使他们靠弓，刀，争战，马匹，与马兵得救。

chapters.en: After she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, Gomer had another son.
chapters.zh: 歌篾给罗路哈玛断奶以后，又怀孕生了一个儿子。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said, “Call him Lo-Ammi (which means “not my people”), for you are not my people, and I am not your God.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，给他起名叫罗阿米（就是非我民的意思），因为你们不作我的子民，我也不作你们的神。

chapters.en: “Yet the Israelites will be like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘children of the living God.’
chapters.zh: 然而，以色列的人数必如海沙，不可量，不可数。从前在什么地方对他们说，你们不是我的子民，将来在那里必对他们说，你们是永生神的儿子。

chapters.en: The people of Judah and the people of Israel will come together; they will appoint one leader and will come up out of the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.
chapters.zh: 犹大人和以色列人，必一同聚集，为自己立一个首领，从这地上去（或作从被掳之地上来），因为耶斯列的日子必为大日。

chapters.en: “Say of your brothers, ‘My people,’ and of your sisters, ‘My loved one.’
chapters.zh: 你们要称你们的弟兄为阿米（就是我民的意思），称你们的姐妹为路哈玛（就是蒙怜悯的意思）。

chapters.en: “Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the adulterous look from her face and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.
chapters.zh: 你们要与你们的母亲大大争辩，因为她不是我的妻子，我也不是她的丈夫。叫她除掉脸上的淫像，和胸间的淫态。

chapters.en: Otherwise I will strip her naked and make her as bare as on the day she was born; I will make her like a desert, turn her into a parched land, and slay her with thirst.
chapters.zh: 免得我剥她的衣服，使她赤体，与才生的时候一样，使她如旷野，如干旱之地，因渴而死。

chapters.en: I will not show my love to her children, because they are the children of adultery.
chapters.zh: 我必不怜悯她的儿女，因为他们是从淫乱而生的。

chapters.en: Their mother has been unfaithful and has conceived them in disgrace. She said, ‘I will go after my lovers, who give me my food and my water, my wool and my linen, my olive oil and my drink.’
chapters.zh: 他们的母亲行了淫乱，怀他们的母做了可羞耻的事，因为她说，我要随从所爱的，我的饼，水，羊毛，麻，油，酒都是他们给的。

chapters.en: Therefore I will block her path with thornbushes; I will wall her in so that she cannot find her way.
chapters.zh: 因此，我必用荆棘堵塞她的道，筑墙挡住她，使她找不着路。

chapters.en: She will chase after her lovers but not catch them; she will look for them but not find them. Then she will say, ‘I will go back to my husband as at first, for then I was better off than now.’
chapters.zh: 她必追随所爱的，却追不上，她必寻找他们，却寻不见，便说，我要归回前夫，因我那时的光景比如今还好。

chapters.en: She has not acknowledged that I was the one who gave her the grain, the new wine and oil, who lavished on her the silver and gold— which they used for Baal.
chapters.zh: 她不知道是我给她五谷，新酒，和油，又加增她的金银。她却以此供奉（或作制造）巴力。

chapters.en: “Therefore I will take away my grain when it ripens, and my new wine when it is ready. I will take back my wool and my linen, intended to cover her naked body.
chapters.zh: 因此，到了收割的日子，出酒的时候，我必将我的五谷新酒收回，也必将她应当遮体的羊毛和麻，夺回来。

chapters.en: So now I will expose her lewdness before the eyes of her lovers; no one will take her out of my hands.
chapters.zh: 如今我必在她所爱的眼前，显露她的丑态，必无人能救她脱离我的手。

chapters.en: I will stop all her celebrations: her yearly festivals, her New Moons, her Sabbath days—all her appointed festivals.
chapters.zh: 我也必使她的宴乐，节期，月朔，安息日，并她的一切大会，都止息了。

chapters.en: I will ruin her vines and her fig trees, which she said were her pay from her lovers; I will make them a thicket, and wild animals will devour them.
chapters.zh: 我也必毁坏她的葡萄树，和无花果树，就是她说，这是我所爱的给我为赏赐的，我必使这些树变为荒林，为田野的走兽所吃。

chapters.en: I will punish her for the days she burned incense to the Baals; she decked herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers, but me she forgot,” declares the LORD.
chapters.zh: 我必追讨她素日给诸巴力烧香的罪，那时她佩带耳环，和别样妆饰，随从她所爱的，却忘记我。这是耶和华说的。

chapters.en: “Therefore I am now going to allure her; I will lead her into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her.
chapters.zh: 后来我必劝导她，领她到旷野，对她说安慰的话。

chapters.en: There I will give her back her vineyards, and will make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will respond as in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 她从那里出来。我必赐她葡萄园，又赐她亚割谷作为指望的门，她必在那里应声（或作歌唱），与幼年的日子一样，与从埃及地上来的时候相同。

chapters.en: “In that day,” declares the LORD, “you will call me ‘my husband’; you will no longer call me ‘my master. ’
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，那日你必称呼我伊施（就是我夫的意思），不再称呼我巴力（就是我主的意思）。

chapters.en: I will remove the names of the Baals from her lips; no longer will their names be invoked.
chapters.zh: 因为我必从我民的口中除掉诸巴力的名号，这名号不再提起。

chapters.en: In that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, the birds in the sky and the creatures that move along the ground. Bow and sword and battle I will abolish from the land, so that all may lie down in safety.
chapters.zh: 当那日，我必为我的民，与田野的走兽，和空中的飞鸟，并地上的昆虫立约。又必在国中折断弓刀，止息争战，使他们安然躺卧。

chapters.en: I will betroth you to me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in love and compassion.
chapters.zh: 我必聘你永远归我为妻，以仁义，公平，慈爱，怜悯聘你归我。

chapters.en: I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will acknowledge the LORD.
chapters.zh: 也以诚实聘你归我，你就必认识我耶和华。

chapters.en: “In that day I will respond,” declares the LORD— “I will respond to the skies, and they will respond to the earth;
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，那日我必应允，我必应允天，天必应允地。

chapters.en: and the earth will respond to the grain, the new wine and the olive oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.
chapters.zh: 地必应允五谷，新酒，和油，这些必应允耶斯列民（耶斯列就是神栽种的意思）。

chapters.en: I will plant her for myself in the land; I will show my love to the one I called ‘Not my loved one. ’ I will say to those called ‘Not my people, ’ ‘You are my people’; and they will say, ‘You are my God.’ ”
chapters.zh: 我必将她种在这地，素不蒙怜悯的，我必怜悯，本非我民的，我必对他说，你是我的民，他必说，你是我的神。

chapters.en: The LORD said to me, “Go, show your love to your wife again, though she is loved by another man and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love the sacred raisin cakes.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对我说，你再去爱一个淫妇，就是她情人所爱的，好像以色列人。虽然偏向别神，喜爱葡萄饼，耶和华还是爱他们。

chapters.en: So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and about a homer and a lethek of barley.
chapters.zh: 我便用银子十五舍客勒，大麦一贺梅珥半，买她归我。

chapters.en: Then I told her, “You are to live with me many days; you must not be a prostitute or be intimate with any man, and I will behave the same way toward you.”
chapters.zh: 我对她说，你当多日为我独居，不可行淫，不可归别人为妻，我向你也必这样。

chapters.en: For the Israelites will live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred stones, without ephod or household gods.
chapters.zh: 以色列人也必多日独居，无君王，无首领，无祭祀，无柱像，无以弗得，无家中的神像。

chapters.en: Afterward the Israelites will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to his blessings in the last days.
chapters.zh: 后来以色列人必归回（或作回心转意），寻求他们的神耶和华，和他们的王大卫。在末后的日子，必以敬畏的心归向耶和华，领受他的恩惠。

chapters.en: Hear the word of the LORD, you Israelites, because the LORD has a charge to bring against you who live in the land: “There is no faithfulness, no love, no acknowledgment of God in the land.
chapters.zh: 以色列人哪，你们当听耶和华的话。耶和华与这地的居民争辩，因这地上无诚实，无良善，无人认识神。

chapters.en: There is only cursing, lying and murder, stealing and adultery; they break all bounds, and bloodshed follows bloodshed.
chapters.zh: 但起假誓，不践前言，杀害，偷盗，奸淫，行强暴，杀人流血，接连不断。

chapters.en: Because of this the land dries up, and all who live in it waste away; the beasts of the field, the birds in the sky and the fish in the sea are swept away.
chapters.zh: 因此，这地悲哀，其上的民，田野的兽，空中的鸟，必都衰微，海中的鱼也必消灭。

chapters.en: “But let no one bring a charge, let no one accuse another, for your people are like those who bring charges against a priest.
chapters.zh: 然而，人都不必争辩，也不必指责，因为这民与抗拒祭司的人一样。

chapters.en: You stumble day and night, and the prophets stumble with you. So I will destroy your mother—
chapters.zh: 你这祭司必日间跌倒，先知也必夜间与你一同跌倒。我必灭绝你的母亲。

chapters.en: my people are destroyed from lack of knowledge. “Because you have rejected knowledge, I also reject you as my priests; because you have ignored the law of your God, I also will ignore your children.
chapters.zh: 我的民因无知识而灭亡。你弃掉知识，我也必弃掉你，使你不再给我作祭司。你既忘了你神的律法，我也必忘记你的儿女。

chapters.en: The more priests there were, the more they sinned against me; they exchanged their glorious God for something disgraceful.
chapters.zh: 祭司越发增多，就越发得罪我。我必使他们的荣耀变为羞辱。

chapters.en: They feed on the sins of my people and relish their wickedness.
chapters.zh: 他们吃我民的赎罪祭，满心愿意我民犯罪。

chapters.en: And it will be: Like people, like priests. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
chapters.zh: 将来民如何，祭司也必如何，我必因他们所行的惩罚他们，照他们所做的报应他们。

chapters.en: “They will eat but not have enough; they will engage in prostitution but not flourish, because they have deserted the LORD to give themselves
chapters.zh: 他们吃，却不得饱。行淫，而不得立后。因为他们离弃耶和华，不遵他的命。

chapters.en: to prostitution; old wine and new wine take away their understanding.
chapters.zh: 奸淫和酒，并新酒，夺去人的心。

chapters.en: My people consult a wooden idol, and a diviner’s rod speaks to them. A spirit of prostitution leads them astray; they are unfaithful to their God.
chapters.zh: 我的民求问木偶，以为木杖能指示他们，因为他们的淫心使他们失迷，他们就行淫离弃神，不守约束。

chapters.en: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar and terebinth, where the shade is pleasant. Therefore your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law to adultery.
chapters.zh: 在各山顶，各高冈的橡树，杨树，栗树之下，献祭烧香，因为树影美好。所以，你们的女儿淫乱，你们的新妇（或作儿妇下同）行淫。

chapters.en: “I will not punish your daughters when they turn to prostitution, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because the men themselves consort with harlots and sacrifice with shrine prostitutes— a people without understanding will come to ruin!
chapters.zh: 你们的女儿淫乱，你们的新妇行淫，我却不惩罚她们，因为你们自己离群与娼妓同居，与妓女一同献祭。这无知的民必致倾倒。

chapters.en: “Though you, Israel, commit adultery, do not let Judah become guilty. “Do not go to Gilgal; do not go up to Beth Aven.And do not swear, ‘As surely as the LORD lives!’
chapters.zh: 以色列阿，你虽然行淫，犹大却不可犯罪。不要往吉甲去，不要上到伯亚文，也不要指着永生的耶和华起誓。

chapters.en: The Israelites are stubborn, like a stubborn heifer. How then can the LORD pasture them like lambs in a meadow?
chapters.zh: 以色列倔强，犹如倔强的母牛。现在耶和华要放他们，如同放羊羔在宽阔之地。

chapters.en: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!
chapters.zh: 以法莲亲近偶像，任凭他吧。

chapters.en: Even when their drinks are gone, they continue their prostitution; their rulers dearly love shameful ways.
chapters.zh: 他们所喝的已经发酸。他们时常行淫，他们的官长最爱羞耻的事。

chapters.en: A whirlwind will sweep them away, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.
chapters.zh: 风把他们裹在翅膀里。他们因所献的祭必致蒙羞。

chapters.en: “Hear this, you priests! Pay attention, you Israelites! Listen, royal house! This judgment is against you: You have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.
chapters.zh: 众祭司阿，要听我的话，以色列家阿，要留心听。王家阿，要侧耳而听。审判要临到你们，因你们在米斯巴如网罗，在他泊山如铺张的网。

chapters.en: The rebels are knee-deep in slaughter. I will discipline all of them.
chapters.zh: 这些悖逆的人，肆行杀戮，罪孽极深。我却斥责他们众人。

chapters.en: I know all about Ephraim; Israel is not hidden from me. Ephraim, you have now turned to prostitution; Israel is corrupt.
chapters.zh: 以法莲为我所知，以色列不能向我隐藏。以法莲哪，现在你行淫了，以色列被玷污了。

chapters.en: “Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God. A spirit of prostitution is in their heart; they do not acknowledge the LORD.
chapters.zh: 他们所行的使他们不能归向神，因有淫心在他们里面，他们也不认识耶和华。

chapters.en: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them; the Israelites, even Ephraim, stumble in their sin; Judah also stumbles with them.
chapters.zh: 以色列的骄傲当面见证自己。故此，以色列和以法莲必因自己的罪孽跌倒，犹大也必与他们一同跌倒。

chapters.en: When they go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, they will not find him; he has withdrawn himself from them.
chapters.zh: 他们必牵着牛羊去寻求耶和华，却寻不见，他已经转去离开他们。

chapters.en: They are unfaithful to the LORD; they give birth to illegitimate children. When they celebrate their New Moon feasts, he will devour their fields.
chapters.zh: 他们向耶和华行事诡诈，生了私子。到了月朔，他们与他们的地业必被吞灭。

chapters.en: “Sound the trumpet in Gibeah, the horn in Ramah. Raise the battle cry in Beth Aven ; lead on, Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 你们当在基比亚吹角，在拉玛吹号，在伯亚文吹出大声，说，便雅悯哪，有仇敌在你后头。

chapters.en: Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of reckoning. Among the tribes of Israel I proclaim what is certain.
chapters.zh: 在责罚的日子，以法莲必变为荒场。我在以色列支派中。指示将来必成的事。

chapters.en: Judah’s leaders are like those who move boundary stones. I will pour out my wrath on them like a flood of water.
chapters.zh: 犹大的首领如同挪移地界的人，我必将忿怒倒在他们身上，如水一般。

chapters.en: Ephraim is oppressed, trampled in judgment, intent on pursuing idols.
chapters.zh: 以法莲因乐从人的命令，就受欺压，被审判压碎。

chapters.en: I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the people of Judah.
chapters.zh: 我使以法莲如虫蛀之物，使犹大家如朽烂之木。

chapters.en: “When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his sores, then Ephraim turned to Assyria, and sent to the great king for help. But he is not able to cure you, not able to heal your sores.
chapters.zh: 以法莲见自己有病，犹大见自己有伤，他们就打发人往亚述去见耶雷布王，他却不能医治你们，不能治好你们的伤。

chapters.en: For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, like a great lion to Judah. I will tear them to pieces and go away; I will carry them off, with no one to rescue them.
chapters.zh: 我必向以法莲如狮子，向犹大家如少壮狮子。我必撕裂而去，我要夺去，无人搭救。

chapters.en: Then I will return to my lair until they have borne their guilt and seek my face— in their misery they will earnestly seek me.”
chapters.zh: 我要回到原处，等他们自觉有罪（或作承认己罪），寻求我面，他们在急难的时候，必切切寻求我。

chapters.en: “Come, let us return to the LORD. He has torn us to pieces but he will heal us; he has injured us but he will bind up our wounds.
chapters.zh: 来吧，我们归向耶和华。他撕裂我们，也必医治。他打伤我们，也必缠裹。

chapters.en: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will restore us, that we may live in his presence.
chapters.zh: 过两天他必使我们苏醒，第三天他必使我们兴起，我们就在他面前得以存活。

chapters.en: Let us acknowledge the LORD; let us press on to acknowledge him. As surely as the sun rises, he will appear; he will come to us like the winter rains, like the spring rains that water the earth.”
chapters.zh: 我们务要认识耶和华，竭力追求认识他。他出现确如晨光，他必临到我们像甘雨，像滋润田地的春雨。

chapters.en: “What can I do with you, Ephraim? What can I do with you, Judah? Your love is like the morning mist, like the early dew that disappears.
chapters.zh: 主说，以法莲哪，我可向你怎样行呢？犹大阿，我可向你怎样做呢？因为你们的良善，如同早晨的云雾，又如速散的甘露。

chapters.en: Therefore I cut you in pieces with my prophets, I killed you with the words of my mouth— then my judgments go forth like the sun.
chapters.zh: 因此，我借先知砍伐他们，以我口中的话杀戮他们，我施行的审判如光发出。

chapters.en: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and acknowledgment of God rather than burnt offerings.
chapters.zh: 我喜爱良善（或作怜恤），不喜爱祭祀，喜爱认识神，胜于燔祭。

chapters.en: As at Adam, they have broken the covenant; they were unfaithful to me there.
chapters.zh: 他们却如亚当背约，在境内向我行事诡诈。

chapters.en: Gilead is a city of evildoers, stained with footprints of blood.
chapters.zh: 基列是作孽之人的城。被血沾染。

chapters.en: As marauders lie in ambush for a victim, so do bands of priests; they murder on the road to Shechem, carrying out their wicked schemes.
chapters.zh: 强盗成群，怎样埋伏杀人。祭司结党，也照样在示剑的路上杀戮，行了邪恶。

chapters.en: I have seen a horrible thing in Israel: There Ephraim is given to prostitution, Israel is defiled.
chapters.zh: 在以色列家，我见了可憎的事。在以法莲那里有淫行，以色列被玷污。

chapters.en: “Also for you, Judah, a harvest is appointed. “Whenever I would restore the fortunes of my people,
chapters.zh: 犹大阿，我使被掳之民归回的时候，必有为你所命定的收场。

chapters.en: whenever I would heal Israel, the sins of Ephraim are exposed and the crimes of Samaria revealed. They practice deceit, thieves break into houses, bandits rob in the streets;
chapters.zh: 我想医治以色列的时候，以法莲的罪孽，和撒玛利亚的罪恶，就显露出来。他们行事虚谎，内有贼人入室偷窃，外有强盗成群骚扰。

chapters.en: but they do not realize that I remember all their evil deeds. Their sins engulf them; they are always before me.
chapters.zh: 他们心里并不思想我记念他们的一切恶，他们所行的现在缠绕他们，都在我面前。

chapters.en: “They delight the king with their wickedness, the princes with their lies.
chapters.zh: 他们行恶使君王欢喜，说谎使首领喜乐。

chapters.en: They are all adulterers, burning like an oven whose fire the baker need not stir from the kneading of the dough till it rises.
chapters.zh: 他们都是行淫的，像火炉被烤饼的烧热，从抟面到发面的时候，暂不使火着旺。

chapters.en: On the day of the festival of our king the princes become inflamed with wine, and he joins hands with the mockers.
chapters.zh: 在我们王宴乐的日子，首领因酒的烈性成病。王与亵慢人拉手。

chapters.en: Their hearts are like an oven; they approach him with intrigue. Their passion smolders all night; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
chapters.zh: 首领埋伏的时候，心中热如火炉，就如烤饼的整夜睡卧，到了早晨火气炎炎。

chapters.en: All of them are hot as an oven; they devour their rulers. All their kings fall, and none of them calls on me.
chapters.zh: 众民也热如火炉，烧灭他们的官长。他们的君王都仆倒而死。他们中间无一人求告我。

chapters.en: “Ephraim mixes with the nations; Ephraim is a flat loaf not turned over.
chapters.zh: 以法莲与列邦人搀杂。以法莲是没有翻过的饼。

chapters.en: Foreigners sap his strength, but he does not realize it. His hair is sprinkled with gray, but he does not notice.
chapters.zh: 外邦人吞吃他劳力得来的，他却不知道，头发斑白，他也不觉得。

chapters.en: Israel’s arrogance testifies against him, but despite all this he does not return to the LORD his God or search for him.
chapters.zh: 以色列的骄傲当面见证自己，虽遭遇这一切，他们仍不归向耶和华他们的神，也不寻求他。

chapters.en: “Ephraim is like a dove, easily deceived and senseless— now calling to Egypt, now turning to Assyria.
chapters.zh: 以法莲好像鸽子愚蠢无知。他们求告埃及，投奔亚述。

chapters.en: When they go, I will throw my net over them; I will pull them down like the birds in the sky. When I hear them flocking together, I will catch them.
chapters.zh: 他们去的时候，我必将我的网撒在他们身上，我要打下他们，如同空中的鸟。我必按他们会众所听见的惩罚他们。

chapters.en: Woe to them, because they have strayed from me! Destruction to them, because they have rebelled against me! I long to redeem them but they speak about me falsely.
chapters.zh: 他们因离弃我，必定有祸，因违背我，必被毁灭。我虽要救赎他们，他们却向我说谎。

chapters.en: They do not cry out to me from their hearts but wail on their beds. They slash themselves, appealing to their gods for grain and new wine, but they turn away from me.
chapters.zh: 他们并不诚心哀求我，乃在床上呼号。他们为求五谷新酒聚集，仍然悖逆我。

chapters.en: I trained them and strengthened their arms, but they plot evil against me.
chapters.zh: 我虽教导他们，坚固他们的膀臂，他们竟图谋抗拒我。

chapters.en: They do not turn to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword because of their insolent words. For this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 他们归向，却不归向至上者。他们如同翻背的弓。他们的首领必因舌头的狂傲倒在刀下，这在埃及地必作人的讥笑。

chapters.en: “Put the trumpet to your lips! An eagle is over the house of the LORD because the people have broken my covenant and rebelled against my law.
chapters.zh: 你用口吹角吧。敌人如鹰来攻打耶和华的家，因为这民违背我的约，干犯我的律法。

chapters.en: Israel cries out to me, ‘Our God, we acknowledge you!’
chapters.zh: 他们必呼叫我说，我的神阿，我们以色列认识你了。

chapters.en: But Israel has rejected what is good; an enemy will pursue him.
chapters.zh: 以色列丢弃良善（或作福分），仇敌必追逼他。

chapters.en: They set up kings without my consent; they choose princes without my approval. With their silver and gold they make idols for themselves to their own destruction.
chapters.zh: 他们立君王，却不由我，他们立首领，我却不认。他们用金银为自己制造偶像，以致被剪除。

chapters.en: Samaria, throw out your calf-idol! My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of purity?
chapters.zh: 撒玛利亚阿，耶和华已经丢弃你的牛犊。我的怒气向拜牛犊的人发作。他们到几时方能无罪呢？

chapters.en: They are from Israel! This calf—a metalworker has made it; it is not God. It will be broken in pieces, that calf of Samaria.
chapters.zh: 这牛犊出于以色列，是匠人所造的，并不是神。撒玛利亚的牛犊必被打碎。

chapters.en: “They sow the wind and reap the whirlwind. The stalk has no head; it will produce no flour. Were it to yield grain, foreigners would swallow it up.
chapters.zh: 他们所种的是风，所收的是暴风，所种的不成禾稼，就是发苗也不结实。即便结实，外邦人必吞吃。

chapters.en: Israel is swallowed up; now she is among the nations like something no one wants.
chapters.zh: 以色列被吞吃，现今在列国中，好像人不喜悦的器皿。

chapters.en: For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has sold herself to lovers.
chapters.zh: 他们投奔亚述，如同独行的野驴。以法莲贿买朋党。

chapters.en: Although they have sold themselves among the nations, I will now gather them together. They will begin to waste away under the oppression of the mighty king.
chapters.zh: 他们虽在列邦中贿买人，现在我却要聚集惩罚他们。他们因君王和首领所加的重担，日渐衰微。

chapters.en: “Though Ephraim built many altars for sin offerings, these have become altars for sinning.
chapters.zh: 以法莲增添祭坛取罪，因此，祭坛使他犯罪。

chapters.en: I wrote for them the many things of my law, but they regarded them as something foreign.
chapters.zh: 我为他写了律法万条，他却以为与他毫无关涉。

chapters.en: Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to me, and though they eat the meat, the LORD is not pleased with them. Now he will remember their wickedness and punish their sins: They will return to Egypt.
chapters.zh: 至于献给我的祭物，他们自食其肉，耶和华却不悦纳他们。现在必记念他们的罪孽，追讨他们的罪恶，他们必归回埃及。

chapters.en: Israel has forgotten their Maker and built palaces; Judah has fortified many towns. But I will send fire on their cities that will consume their fortresses.”
chapters.zh: 以色列忘记造他的主，建造宫殿。犹大多造坚固城，我却要降火焚烧他的城邑，烧灭其中的宫殿。

chapters.en: Do not rejoice, Israel; do not be jubilant like the other nations. For you have been unfaithful to your God; you love the wages of a prostitute at every threshing floor.
chapters.zh: 以色列阿，不要像外邦人欢喜快乐，因为你行邪淫离弃你的神，在各谷场上如妓女喜爱赏赐。

chapters.en: Threshing floors and winepresses will not feed the people; the new wine will fail them.
chapters.zh: 谷场和酒榨，都不够以色列人使用，新酒也必缺乏。

chapters.en: They will not remain in the LORD’s land; Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria.
chapters.zh: 他们必不得住耶和华的地，以法莲却要归回埃及，必在亚述吃不洁净的食物。

chapters.en: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, nor will their sacrifices please him. Such sacrifices will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat them will be unclean. This food will be for themselves; it will not come into the temple of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 他们必不得向耶和华奠酒，即便奠酒也不蒙悦纳。他们的祭物，必如居丧者的食物，凡吃的必被玷污，因他们的食物，只为自己的口腹，必不奉入耶和华的殿。

chapters.en: What will you do on the day of your appointed festivals, on the feast days of the LORD?
chapters.zh: 在大会的日子，到耶和华的节期，你们怎样行呢？

chapters.en: Even if they escape from destruction, Egypt will gather them, and Memphis will bury them. Their treasures of silver will be taken over by briers, and thorns will overrun their tents.
chapters.zh: 看哪，他们逃避灾难，埃及人必收殓他们的尸首，摩弗人必葬埋他们的骸骨。他们用银子做的美物上必长蒺藜，他们的帐棚中必生荆棘。

chapters.en: The days of punishment are coming, the days of reckoning are at hand. Let Israel know this. Because your sins are so many and your hostility so great, the prophet is considered a fool, the inspired person a maniac.
chapters.zh: 以色列人必知道降罚的日子临近，报应的时候来到。（民说，作先知的是愚昧，受灵感的是狂妄皆因他们多多作孽，大怀怨恨。

chapters.en: The prophet, along with my God, is the watchman over Ephraim,yet snares await him on all his paths, and hostility in the house of his God.
chapters.zh: 以法莲曾作我神守望的，至于先知，在他一切的道上作为捕鸟人的网罗，在他神的家中怀怨恨。

chapters.en: They have sunk deep into corruption, as in the days of Gibeah. God will remember their wickedness and punish them for their sins.
chapters.zh: 以法莲深深地败坏，如在基比亚的日子一样，耶和华必记念他们的罪孽，追讨他们的罪恶。

chapters.en: “When I found Israel, it was like finding grapes in the desert; when I saw your ancestors, it was like seeing the early fruit on the fig tree. But when they came to Baal Peor, they consecrated themselves to that shameful idol and became as vile as the thing they loved.
chapters.zh: 主说，我遇见以色列如葡萄在旷野，我看见你们的列祖如无花果树上春季初熟的果子。他们却来到巴力毗珥专拜那可羞耻的，就成为可憎恶的，与他们所爱的一样。

chapters.en: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird— no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
chapters.zh: 至于以法莲人，他们的荣耀必如鸟飞去，必不生产，不怀胎，不成孕。

chapters.en: Even if they rear children, I will bereave them of every one. Woe to them when I turn away from them!
chapters.zh: 纵然养大儿女，我却必使他们丧子，甚至不留一个。我离弃他们，他们就有祸了。

chapters.en: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place. But Ephraim will bring out their children to the slayer.”
chapters.zh: 我看以法莲如推罗栽于美地。以法莲却要将自己的儿女带出来，交与行杀戮的人。

chapters.en: Give them, LORD— what will you give them? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that are dry.
chapters.zh: 耶和华阿，求你加给他们加什么呢？要使他们胎坠乳干。

chapters.en: “Because of all their wickedness in Gilgal, I hated them there. Because of their sinful deeds, I will drive them out of my house. I will no longer love them; all their leaders are rebellious.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说，他们一切的恶事都在吉甲，我在那里憎恶他们，因他们所行的恶，我必从我地上赶出他们去，不再怜爱他们，他们的首领都是悖逆的。

chapters.en: Ephraim is blighted, their root is withered, they yield no fruit. Even if they bear children, I will slay their cherished offspring.”
chapters.zh: 以法莲受责罚，根本枯干，必不能结果，即或生产，我必杀他们所生的爱子。

chapters.en: My God will reject them because they have not obeyed him; they will be wanderers among the nations.
chapters.zh: 我的神必弃绝他们，因为他们不听从他，他们也必飘流在列国中。

chapters.en: Israel was a spreading vine; he brought forth fruit for himself. As his fruit increased, he built more altars; as his land prospered, he adorned his sacred stones.
chapters.zh: 以色列是茂盛的葡萄树，结果繁多，果子越多，就越增添祭坛。地土越肥美，就越造美丽的柱像。

chapters.en: Their heart is deceitful, and now they must bear their guilt. The LORD will demolish their altars and destroy their sacred stones.
chapters.zh: 他们心怀二意，现今要定为有罪。耶和华必拆毁他们的祭坛，毁坏他们的柱像。

chapters.en: Then they will say, “We have no king because we did not revere the LORD. But even if we had a king, what could he do for us?”
chapters.zh: 他们必说，我们没有王，因为我们不敬畏耶和华。王能为我们做什么呢？

chapters.en: They make many promises, take false oaths and make agreements; therefore lawsuits spring up like poisonous weeds in a plowed field.
chapters.zh: 他们为立约说谎言，起假誓，因此，灾罚如苦菜滋生在田间的犁沟中。

chapters.en: The people who live in Samaria fear for the calf-idol of Beth Aven.Its people will mourn over it, and so will its idolatrous priests, those who had rejoiced over its splendor, because it is taken from them into exile.
chapters.zh: 撒玛利亚的居民，必因伯亚文的牛犊惊恐，崇拜牛犊的民，和喜爱牛犊的祭司，都必因荣耀离开他，为他悲哀。

chapters.en: It will be carried to Assyria as tribute for the great king. Ephraim will be disgraced; Israel will be ashamed of its foreign alliances.
chapters.zh: 人必将牛犊带到亚述当作礼物，献给耶雷布王。以法莲必蒙羞，以色列必因自己的计谋惭愧。

chapters.en: Samaria’s king will be destroyed, swept away like a twig on the surface of the waters.
chapters.zh: 至于撒玛利亚，她的王必灭没，如水面的沫子一样。

chapters.en: The high places of wickedness will be destroyed— it is the sin of Israel. Thorns and thistles will grow up and cover their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall on us!”
chapters.zh: 伯亚文的丘坛就是以色列取罪的地方，必被毁灭，荆棘和蒺藜必长在他们的祭坛上，他们必对大山说，遮盖我们，对小山说，倒在我们身上。

chapters.en: “Since the days of Gibeah, you have sinned, Israel, and there you have remained.Will not war again overtake the evildoers in Gibeah?
chapters.zh: 以色列阿，你从基比亚的日子以来，时常犯罪。你们的先人曾站在那里，现今住基比亚的人以为攻击罪孽之辈的战事临不到自己。

chapters.en: When I please, I will punish them; nations will be gathered against them to put them in bonds for their double sin.
chapters.zh: 我必随意惩罚他们。他们为两样的罪所缠，列邦的民必聚集攻击他们。

chapters.en: Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh; so I will put a yoke on her fair neck. I will drive Ephraim, Judah must plow, and Jacob must break up the ground.
chapters.zh: 以法莲是驯良的母牛犊，喜爱踹谷，我却将轭加在它肥美的颈项上，我要使以法莲拉套（或作被骑）。犹大必耕田，雅各必耙地。

chapters.en: Sow righteousness for yourselves, reap the fruit of unfailing love, and break up your unplowed ground; for it is time to seek the LORD, until he comes and showers his righteousness on you.
chapters.zh: 你们要为自己栽种公义，就能收割慈爱。现今正是寻求耶和华的时候，你们要开垦荒地，等他临到，使公义如雨降在你们身上。

chapters.en: But you have planted wickedness, you have reaped evil, you have eaten the fruit of deception. Because you have depended on your own strength and on your many warriors,
chapters.zh: 你们耕种的是奸恶，收割的是罪孽，吃的是谎话的果子。因你倚靠自己的行为，仰赖勇士众多。

chapters.en: the roar of battle will rise against your people, so that all your fortresses will be devastated— as Shalman devastated Beth Arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to the ground with their children.
chapters.zh: 所以在这民中必有哄嚷之声，你一切的保障必被拆毁，就如沙勒幔在争战的日子拆毁伯亚比勒，将其中的母子一同摔死。

chapters.en: So will it happen to you, Bethel, because your wickedness is great. When that day dawns, the king of Israel will be completely destroyed.
chapters.zh: 因他们的大恶，伯特利必使你们遭遇如此。到了黎明，以色列的王必全然灭绝。

chapters.en: “When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
chapters.zh: 以色列年幼的时候，我爱他，就从埃及召出我的儿子来。

chapters.en: But the more they were called, the more they went away from me.They sacrificed to the Baals and they burned incense to images.
chapters.zh: 先知越发招呼他们，他们越发走开，向诸巴力献祭，给雕刻的偶像烧香。

chapters.en: It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms; but they did not realize it was I who healed them.
chapters.zh: 我原教导以法莲行走，用膀臂抱着他们，他们却不知道是我医治他们。

chapters.en: I led them with cords of human kindness, with ties of love. To them I was like one who lifts a little child to the cheek, and I bent down to feed them.
chapters.zh: 我用慈绳（慈原文是人的）爱索牵引他们，我待他们如人放松牛的两腮夹板，把粮食放在他们面前。

chapters.en: “Will they not return to Egypt and will not Assyria rule over them because they refuse to repent?
chapters.zh: 他们必不归回埃及地，亚述人却要作他们的王，因他们不肯归向我。

chapters.en: A sword will flash in their cities; it will devour their false prophets and put an end to their plans.
chapters.zh: 刀剑必临到他们的城邑，毁坏门闩，把人吞灭，都因他们随从自己的计谋。

chapters.en: My people are determined to turn from me. Even though they call me God Most High, I will by no means exalt them.
chapters.zh: 我的民偏要背道离开我，众先知虽然招呼他们归向至上的主，却无人尊崇主。

chapters.en: “How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I treat you like Admah? How can I make you like Zeboyim? My heart is changed within me; all my compassion is aroused.
chapters.zh: 以法莲哪，我怎能舍弃你，以色列阿，我怎能弃绝你，我怎能使你如押玛，怎能使你如洗扁，我回心转意，我的怜爱大大发动。

chapters.en: I will not carry out my fierce anger, nor will I devastate Ephraim again. For I am God, and not a man— the Holy One among you. I will not come against their cities.
chapters.zh: 我必不发猛烈的怒气，也不再毁灭以法莲，因我是神，并非世人，是你们中间的圣者，我必不在怒中临到你们。

chapters.en: They will follow the LORD; he will roar like a lion. When he roars, his children will come trembling from the west.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必如狮子吼叫，子民必跟随他。他一吼叫，他们就从西方急速而来。
