chapters.en: “To what can I compare this generation? They are like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling out to others:
chapters.zh: 我可用什么比这世代呢？好像孩童坐在街市上，招呼同伴，说，

chapters.en: “ ‘We played the pipe for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn.’
chapters.zh: 我们向你们吹笛，你们不跳舞。我们向你们举哀，你们不捶胸。

chapters.en: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’
chapters.zh: 约翰来了，也不吃，也不喝，人就说他是被鬼附着的。

chapters.en: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Here is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’ But wisdom is proved right by her deeds.”
chapters.zh: 人子来了，也吃，也喝，人又说他是贪食好酒的人，是税吏和罪人的朋友。但智慧之子，总以智慧为是。（有古卷作但智慧在行为上就显为是）

chapters.en: Then Jesus began to denounce the towns in which most of his miracles had been performed, because they did not repent.
chapters.zh: 耶稣在诸城中行了许多异能，那些城的人终不悔改，就在那时候责备他们说，

chapters.en: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
chapters.zh: 哥拉汛哪，你有祸了，伯赛大啊，你有祸了，因为在你们中间所行的异能，若行在推罗西顿，他们早已披麻蒙灰悔改了。

chapters.en: But I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
chapters.zh: 但我告诉你们，当审判的日子，推罗、西顿所受的，比你们还容易受呢。

chapters.en: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted to the heavens? No, you will go down to Hades.For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.
chapters.zh: 迦百农阿，你已经升到天上。（或作你将要升到天上吗）将来必坠落阴间。因为在你那里所行的异能，若行在所多玛，它还可以存到今日。

chapters.en: But I tell you that it will be more bearable for Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”
chapters.zh: 但我告诉你们，当审判的日子，所多玛所受的，比你还容易受呢。

chapters.en: At that time Jesus said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.
chapters.zh: 那时，耶稣说，父阿，天地的主，我感谢你，因为你将这些事，向聪明通达人，就藏起来，向婴孩，就显出来。

chapters.en: Yes, Father, for this is what you were pleased to do.
chapters.zh: 父阿，是的，因为你的美意本是如此。

chapters.en: “All things have been committed to me by my Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
chapters.zh: 一切所有的，都是我父交付我的。除了父，没有人知道子。除了子和子所愿意指示的，没有人知道父。

chapters.en: “Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
chapters.zh: 凡劳苦担重担的人，可以到我这里来，我就使你们得安息。

chapters.en: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
chapters.zh: 我心里柔和谦卑，你们当负我的轭，学我的样式，这样，你们心里就必得享安息。

chapters.en: For my yoke is easy and my burden is light.”
chapters.zh: 因为我的轭是容易的，我的担子是轻省的。

chapters.en: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began to pick some heads of grain and eat them.
chapters.zh: 那时，耶稣在安息日，从麦地经过。他的门徒饿了，就掐起麦穗来吃。

chapters.en: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, “Look! Your disciples are doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 法利赛人看见，就对耶稣说，看哪，你的门徒作安息日不可作的事了。

chapters.en: He answered, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说，经上记着大卫和跟从他的人饥饿之时所作的事，你们没有念过吗？

chapters.en: He entered the house of God, and he and his companions ate the consecrated bread—which was not lawful for them to do, but only for the priests.
chapters.zh: 他怎么进了神的殿，吃了陈设饼，这饼不是他和跟从他的人可以吃得，惟独祭司才可以吃。

chapters.en: Or haven’t you read in the Law that the priests on Sabbath duty in the temple desecrate the Sabbath and yet are innocent?
chapters.zh: 再者，律法上所记的，当安息日，祭司在殿里犯了安息日，还是没有罪，你们没有念过吗？

chapters.en: I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
chapters.zh: 但我告诉你们，在这里有一人比殿更大。

chapters.en: If you had known what these words mean, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice,’you would not have condemned the innocent.
chapters.zh: 我喜爱怜恤，不喜爱祭祀。你们若明白这话的意思，就不将无罪的，当作有罪的了。

chapters.en: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 因为人子是安息日的主。

chapters.en: Going on from that place, he went into their synagogue,
chapters.zh: 耶稣离开那地方，进了一个会堂。

chapters.en: and a man with a shriveled hand was there. Looking for a reason to bring charges against Jesus, they asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
chapters.zh: 那里有一个人，枯干了一只手。有人问耶稣说，安息日治病，可以不可以。意思是要控告他。

chapters.en: He said to them, “If any of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will you not take hold of it and lift it out?
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们中间谁有一只羊，当安息日掉在坑里，不把他抓住拉上来呢？

chapters.en: How much more valuable is a person than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 人比羊何等贵重呢。所以在安息日作善事是可以的。

chapters.en: Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out and it was completely restored, just as sound as the other.
chapters.zh: 于是对那人说，伸出手来。他把手一伸，手就复了原，和那只手一样。

chapters.en: But the Pharisees went out and plotted how they might kill Jesus.
chapters.zh: 法利赛人出去，商议怎样可以除灭耶稣。

chapters.en: Aware of this, Jesus withdrew from that place. A large crowd followed him, and he healed all who were ill.
chapters.zh: 耶稣知道了，就离开那里，有许多人跟着他，他把其中有病的人都治好了。

chapters.en: He warned them not to tell others about him.
chapters.zh: 又嘱咐他们，不要给他传名。

chapters.en: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:
chapters.zh: 这是要应验先知以赛亚的话，说，

chapters.en: “Here is my servant whom I have chosen, the one I love, in whom I delight; I will put my Spirit on him, and he will proclaim justice to the nations.
chapters.zh: 看哪，我的仆人，我所拣选，所亲爱，心里所喜悦的，我要将我的灵赐给他，他必将公理传给外邦。

chapters.en: He will not quarrel or cry out; no one will hear his voice in the streets.
chapters.zh: 他不争竞，不喧嚷。街上也没有人听见他的声音。

chapters.en: A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out, till he has brought justice through to victory.
chapters.zh: 压伤的芦苇，他不折断。将残的灯火，他不吹灭。等他施行公理，叫公理得胜。

chapters.en: In his name the nations will put their hope.”
chapters.zh: 外邦人都要仰望他的名。

chapters.en: Then they brought him a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute, and Jesus healed him, so that he could both talk and see.
chapters.zh: 当下有人将一个被鬼附着，又瞎又哑的人，带到耶稣那里。耶稣就医治他，甚至那哑吧又能说话，又能看见。

chapters.en: All the people were astonished and said, “Could this be the Son of David?”
chapters.zh: 众人都惊奇，说，这不是大卫的子孙吗？

chapters.en: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “It is only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, that this fellow drives out demons.”
chapters.zh: 但法利赛人听见，就说，这个人赶鬼，无非是靠着鬼王别西卜啊。

chapters.en: Jesus knew their thoughts and said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be ruined, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.
chapters.zh: 耶稣知道他们的意念，就对他们说，凡一国自相分争，就成为荒场，一城一家自相分争，必站立不住。

chapters.en: If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then can his kingdom stand?
chapters.zh: 若撒但赶逐撒但，就是自相分争，他的国怎能站得住呢？

chapters.en: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your people drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
chapters.zh: 我若靠着别西卜赶鬼，你们的子弟赶鬼，又靠着谁呢？这样，他们就要断定你们的是非。

chapters.en: But if it is by the Spirit of God that I drive out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
chapters.zh: 我若靠着神的灵赶鬼，这就是神的国临到你们了。

chapters.en: “Or again, how can anyone enter a strong man’s house and carry off his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can plunder his house.
chapters.zh: 人怎能进壮士家里，抢夺他的家具呢？除非先捆住那壮士，才可以抢夺他的家财。

chapters.en: “Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
chapters.zh: 不与我相合的，就是敌我的，不同我收聚的，就是分散的。

chapters.en: And so I tell you, every kind of sin and slander can be forgiven, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 所以我告诉你们，人一切的罪，和亵渎的话，都可得赦免。惟独亵渎圣灵，总不得赦免。

chapters.en: Anyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come.
chapters.zh: 凡说话干犯人子的，还可得赦免。惟独说话干犯圣灵的，今世来世总不得赦免。

chapters.en: “Make a tree good and its fruit will be good, or make a tree bad and its fruit will be bad, for a tree is recognized by its fruit.
chapters.zh: 你们或以为树好，果子也好。树坏，果子也坏。因为看果子，就可以知道树。

chapters.en: You brood of vipers, how can you who are evil say anything good? For the mouth speaks what the heart is full of.
chapters.zh: 毒蛇的种类，你们既是恶人，怎能说出好话来呢？因为心里所充满的，口里就说出来。

chapters.en: A good man brings good things out of the good stored up in him, and an evil man brings evil things out of the evil stored up in him.
chapters.zh: 善人从他心里所存的善，就发出善来。恶人从他心里所存的恶，就发出恶来。

chapters.en: But I tell you that everyone will have to give account on the day of judgment for every empty word they have spoken.
chapters.zh: 我又告诉你们，凡人所说的闲话，当审判的日子，必要句句供出来。

chapters.en: For by your words you will be acquitted, and by your words you will be condemned.”
chapters.zh: 因为要凭你的话定你为义，也要凭你的话，定你有罪。

chapters.en: Then some of the Pharisees and teachers of the law said to him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
chapters.zh: 当时有几个文士和法利赛人，对耶稣说，夫子，我们愿意你显个神迹给我们看。

chapters.en: He answered, “A wicked and adulterous generation asks for a sign! But none will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，一个邪恶淫乱的世代求看神迹。除了先知约拿的神迹以外，再没有神迹给他们看。

chapters.en: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of a huge fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
chapters.zh: 约拿三日三夜在大鱼肚腹中，人子也要这样三日三夜在地里头。

chapters.en: The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now something greater than Jonah is here.
chapters.zh: 当审判的时候，尼尼微人，要起来定这世代的罪，因为尼尼微人听了约拿所传的，就悔改了。看哪，在这里有一人比约拿更大。

chapters.en: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, and now something greater than Solomon is here.
chapters.zh: 当审判的时候，南方的女王，要起来定这世代的罪，因为她从地极而来，要听所罗门的智慧话。看哪，在这里有一人比所罗门更大。

chapters.en: “When an impure spirit comes out of a person, it goes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it.
chapters.zh: 污鬼离了人身，就在无水之地，过来过去，寻求安歇之处，却寻不着。

chapters.en: Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’ When it arrives, it finds the house unoccupied, swept clean and put in order.
chapters.zh: 于是说，我要回到我所出来的屋里去。到了，就看见里面空闲，打扫干净，修饰好了。

chapters.en: Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and live there. And the final condition of that person is worse than the first. That is how it will be with this wicked generation.”
chapters.zh: 便去另带了七个比自己更恶的鬼来，都进去住在那里。那人末后的景况，比先前更不好了。这邪恶的世代，也要如此。

chapters.en: While Jesus was still talking to the crowd, his mother and brothers stood outside, wanting to speak to him.
chapters.zh: 耶稣还对众人说话的时候，不料，他母亲和他弟兄站在外边，要与他说话。

chapters.en: Someone told him, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak to you.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉他说，看哪，你母亲和你弟兄站在外边，要与你说话。

chapters.en: He replied to him, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”
chapters.zh: 他却回答那人说，谁是我的母亲。谁是我的弟兄。

chapters.en: Pointing to his disciples, he said, “Here are my mother and my brothers.
chapters.zh: 就伸手指着门徒说，看哪，我的母亲，我的弟兄。

chapters.en: For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.”
chapters.zh: 凡遵行我天父旨意的人，就是我的弟兄姐妹和母亲了。

chapters.en: That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the lake.
chapters.zh: 当那一天，耶稣从房子里出来，坐在海边。

chapters.en: Such large crowds gathered around him that he got into a boat and sat in it, while all the people stood on the shore.
chapters.zh: 有许多人到他那里聚集，他只得上船坐下。众人都站在岸上。

chapters.en: Then he told them many things in parables, saying: “A farmer went out to sow his seed.
chapters.zh: 他用比喻对他们讲许多道理，说，有一个撒种的出去撒种。

chapters.en: As he was scattering the seed, some fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.
chapters.zh: 撒的时候，有落在路旁的，飞鸟来吃尽了。

chapters.en: Some fell on rocky places, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly, because the soil was shallow.
chapters.zh: 有落在土浅石头地上的。土既不深，发苗最快。

chapters.en: But when the sun came up, the plants were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.
chapters.zh: 日头出来一晒，因为没有根，就枯干了。

chapters.en: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the plants.
chapters.zh: 有落在荆棘里的。荆棘长起来，把它挤住了。

chapters.en: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it produced a crop—a hundred, sixty or thirty times what was sown.
chapters.zh: 又有落在好土里的，就结实，有一百倍的，有六十倍的，有三十倍的。

chapters.en: Whoever has ears, let them hear.”
chapters.zh: 有耳可听的，就应当听。

chapters.en: The disciples came to him and asked, “Why do you speak to the people in parables?”
chapters.zh: 门徒进前来，问耶稣说，对众人讲话，为什么用比喻呢？

chapters.en: He replied, “Because the knowledge of the secrets of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，因为天国的奥秘，只叫你们知道，不叫他们知道。

chapters.en: Whoever has will be given more, and they will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken from them.
chapters.zh: 凡有的，还要加给他，叫他有余。凡没有的，连他所有的，也要夺去。

chapters.en: This is why I speak to them in parables: “Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.
chapters.zh: 所以我用比喻对他们讲，是因他们看也看不见，听也听不见，也不明白。

chapters.en: In them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah: “ ‘You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.
chapters.zh: 在他们身上，正应了以赛亚的预言说，你们听是要听见，却不明白。看是要看见，却不晓得。

chapters.en: For this people’s heart has become calloused; they hardly hear with their ears,and they have closed their eyes.Otherwise they might see with their eyes,hear with their ears,understand with their hearts and turn, and I would heal them.’
chapters.zh: 因为这百姓油蒙了心，耳朵发沉，眼睛闭着。恐怕眼睛看见，耳朵听见，心里明白，回转过来，我就医治他们。

chapters.en: But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.
chapters.zh: 但你们的眼睛是有福的，因为看见了。你们的耳朵也是有福的，因为听见了。

chapters.en: For truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
chapters.zh: 我实在告诉你们，从前有许多先知和义人，要看你们所看的，却没有看见。要听你们所听的，却没有听见。

chapters.en: “Listen then to what the parable of the sower means:
chapters.zh: 所以你们当听这撒种的比喻。

chapters.en: When anyone hears the message about the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in their heart. This is the seed sown along the path.
chapters.zh: 凡听见天国道理不明白的，那恶者就来，把所撒在他心里的夺了去。这就是撒在路旁的了。

chapters.en: The seed falling on rocky ground refers to someone who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.
chapters.zh: 撒在石头地上的，就是人听了道，当下欢喜领受。

chapters.en: But since they have no root, they last only a short time. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.
chapters.zh: 只因心里没有根，不过是暂时的。及至为道遭了患难，或是受了逼迫，立刻就跌倒了。

chapters.en: The seed falling among the thorns refers to someone who hears the word, but the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, making it unfruitful.
chapters.zh: 撒在荆棘里的，就是人听了道，后来有世上的思虑，钱财的迷惑，把道挤住了，不能结实。

chapters.en: But the seed falling on good soil refers to someone who hears the word and understands it. This is the one who produces a crop, yielding a hundred, sixty or thirty times what was sown.”
chapters.zh: 撒在好地上的，就是人听道明白了，后来结实，有一百倍的，有六十倍的，有三十倍的。

chapters.en: Jesus told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又设个比喻对他们说，天国好像人撒好种在田里。

chapters.en: But while everyone was sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and went away.
chapters.zh: 及至人睡觉的时候，有仇敌来，将稗子撒在麦子里，就走了。

chapters.en: When the wheat sprouted and formed heads, then the weeds also appeared.
chapters.zh: 到长苗吐穗的时候，稗子也显出来。

chapters.en: “The owner’s servants came to him and said, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?’
chapters.zh: 田主的仆人来告诉他说，主阿，你不是撒好种在田里吗？从哪里来的稗子呢？

chapters.en: “ ‘An enemy did this,’ he replied. “The servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and pull them up?’
chapters.zh: 主人说，这是仇敌作的。仆人说，你要我们去薅出来吗？

chapters.en: “ ‘No,’ he answered, ‘because while you are pulling the weeds, you may uproot the wheat with them.
chapters.zh: 主人说，不必，恐怕薅稗子，连麦子也拔出来。

chapters.en: Let both grow together until the harvest. At that time I will tell the harvesters: First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat and bring it into my barn.’ ”
chapters.zh: 容这两样一齐长，等着收割。当收割的时候，我要对收割的人说，先将稗子薅出来，捆成捆，留着烧。惟有麦子，要收在仓里。

chapters.en: He told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man took and planted in his field.
chapters.zh: 他又设个比喻对他们说，天国好像一粒芥菜种，有人拿去种在田里。

chapters.en: Though it is the smallest of all seeds, yet when it grows, it is the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds come and perch in its branches.”
chapters.zh: 这原是百种里最小的。等到长起来，却比各样的菜都大，且成了树。天上的飞鸟来宿在他的枝上。

chapters.en: He told them still another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took and mixed into about sixty poundsof flour until it worked all through the dough.”
chapters.zh: 他又对他们讲个比喻说，天国好像面酵，有妇人拿来，藏在三斗面里，直等全团都发起来。

chapters.en: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowd in parables; he did not say anything to them without using a parable.
chapters.zh: 这都是耶稣用比喻对众人说的话。若不用比喻，就不对他们说什么。

chapters.en: So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet: “I will open my mouth in parables, I will utter things hidden since the creation of the world.”
chapters.zh: 这是要应验先知的话说，我要开口用比喻，把创世以来所隐藏的事发明出来。

chapters.en: Then he left the crowd and went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”
chapters.zh: 当下耶稣离开众人，进了房子。他的门徒进前来说，请把田间稗子的比喻，讲给我们听。

chapters.en: He answered, “The one who sowed the good seed is the Son of Man.
chapters.zh: 他回答说，那撒好种的，就是人子。

chapters.en: The field is the world, and the good seed stands for the people of the kingdom. The weeds are the people of the evil one,
chapters.zh: 田地，就是世界。好种，就是天国之子。稗子，就是那恶者之子。

chapters.en: and the enemy who sows them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the harvesters are angels.
chapters.zh: 撒稗子的仇敌，就是魔鬼。收割的时候，就是世界的末了。收割的人，就是天使。

chapters.en: “As the weeds are pulled up and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of the age.
chapters.zh: 将稗子薅出来，用火焚烧。世界的末了，也要如此。

chapters.en: The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will weed out of his kingdom everything that causes sin and all who do evil.
chapters.zh: 人子要差遣使者，把一切叫人跌倒的，和作恶的，从他国里挑出来，

chapters.en: They will throw them into the blazing furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
chapters.zh: 丢在火炉里。在那里必要哀哭切齿了。

chapters.en: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears, let them hear.
chapters.zh: 那时义人在他们父的国里，要发出光来，像太阳一样。有耳可听的，就应当听。

chapters.en: “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again, and then in his joy went and sold all he had and bought that field.
chapters.zh: 天国好像宝贝藏在地里。人遇见了，就把它藏起来。欢欢喜喜地去变卖一切所有的买这块地。

chapters.en: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant looking for fine pearls.
chapters.zh: 天国又好像买卖人，寻找好珠子。

chapters.en: When he found one of great value, he went away and sold everything he had and bought it.
chapters.zh: 遇见一颗重价的珠子，就去变卖他一切所有的，买了这颗珠子。

chapters.en: “Once again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was let down into the lake and caught all kinds of fish.
chapters.zh: 天国又好像网撒在海里，聚拢各样水族。

chapters.en: When it was full, the fishermen pulled it up on the shore. Then they sat down and collected the good fish in baskets, but threw the bad away.
chapters.zh: 网既满了，人就拉上岸来。坐下，拣好的收在器具里，将不好的丢弃了。

chapters.en: This is how it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous
chapters.zh: 世界的末了，也要这样。天使要出来，从义人中，把恶人分别出来，

chapters.en: and throw them into the blazing furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
chapters.zh: 丢在火炉里。在那里必要哀哭切齿了。

chapters.en: “Have you understood all these things?” Jesus asked. “Yes,” they replied.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，这一切的话，你们都明白了吗？他们说，我们明白了。

chapters.en: He said to them, “Therefore every teacher of the law who has become a disciple in the kingdom of heaven is like the owner of a house who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old.”
chapters.zh: 他说，凡文士受教作天国的门徒，就像一个家主，从他库里拿出新旧的东西来。

chapters.en: When Jesus had finished these parables, he moved on from there.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说完了这些比喻，就离开那里，

chapters.en: Coming to his hometown, he began teaching the people in their synagogue, and they were amazed. “Where did this man get this wisdom and these miraculous powers?” they asked.
chapters.zh: 来到自己的家乡，在会堂里教训人，甚至他们都希奇说，这人从哪里有这等智慧，和异能呢？

chapters.en: “Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother’s name Mary, and aren’t his brothers James, Joseph, Simon and Judas?
chapters.zh: 这不是木匠的儿子吗？他母亲不是叫马利亚吗？他弟兄们不是叫雅各，约西，（有古卷作约瑟），西门，犹大吗？

chapters.en: Aren’t all his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all these things?”
chapters.zh: 他妹妹们不是都在我们这里吗？这人从哪里有这一切的事呢？

chapters.en: And they took offense at him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his own town and in his own home.”
chapters.zh: 他们就厌弃他。（厌弃他原文作因他跌倒）耶稣对他们说，大凡先知，除了本地本家之外，没有不被人尊敬的。

chapters.en: And he did not do many miracles there because of their lack of faith.
chapters.zh: 耶稣因为他们不信，就在那里不多行异能了。

chapters.en: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus,
chapters.zh: 那时，分封的王希律听见耶稣的名声，

chapters.en: and he said to his attendants, “This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
chapters.zh: 就对臣仆说，这是施洗的约翰从死里复活，所以这些异能从他里面发出来。

chapters.en: Now Herod had arrested John and bound him and put him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife,
chapters.zh: 起先希律为他兄弟腓力的妻子希罗底的缘故，把约翰拿住锁在监里。

chapters.en: for John had been saying to him: “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
chapters.zh: 因为约翰曾对他说，你娶这妇人是不合理的。

chapters.en: Herod wanted to kill John, but he was afraid of the people, because they considered John a prophet.
chapters.zh: 希律就想要杀他，只是怕百姓。因为他们以约翰为先知。

chapters.en: On Herod’s birthday the daughter of Herodias danced for the guests and pleased Herod so much
chapters.zh: 到了希律的生日，希罗底的女儿，在众人面前跳舞，使希律欢喜。

chapters.en: that he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.
chapters.zh: 希律就起誓，应许随她所求的给她。

chapters.en: Prompted by her mother, she said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”
chapters.zh: 女儿被母亲所使，就说，请把施洗约翰的头，放在盘子里拿来给我。

chapters.en: The king was distressed, but because of his oaths and his dinner guests, he ordered that her request be granted
chapters.zh: 王便忧愁，但因他所起的誓，又因同席的人，就吩咐给她。

chapters.en: and had John beheaded in the prison.
chapters.zh: 于是打发人去，在监里斩了约翰。

chapters.en: His head was brought in on a platter and given to the girl, who carried it to her mother.
chapters.zh: 把头放在盘子里，拿来给了女子。女子拿去给她母亲。

chapters.en: John’s disciples came and took his body and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
chapters.zh: 约翰的门徒来，把尸首领去，埋葬了。就去告诉耶稣。

chapters.en: When Jesus heard what had happened, he withdrew by boat privately to a solitary place. Hearing of this, the crowds followed him on foot from the towns.
chapters.zh: 耶稣听见了，就上船从那里独自退到野地里去。众人听见，就从各城里步行跟随他。

chapters.en: When Jesus landed and saw a large crowd, he had compassion on them and healed their sick.
chapters.zh: 耶稣出来，见有许多的人，就怜悯他们，治好了他们的病人。

chapters.en: As evening approached, the disciples came to him and said, “This is a remote place, and it’s already getting late. Send the crowds away, so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food.”
chapters.zh: 天将晚的时候，门徒进前来说，这是野地，时候已经过了。请叫众人散开，他们好往村子里去，自己买吃的。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，不用他们去，你们给他们吃吧。

chapters.en: “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered.
chapters.zh: 门徒说，我们这里只有五个饼，两条鱼。

chapters.en: “Bring them here to me,” he said.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，拿过来给我。

chapters.en: And he directed the people to sit down on the grass. Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, he gave thanks and broke the loaves. Then he gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.
chapters.zh: 于是吩咐众人坐在草地上。就拿着这五个饼，两条鱼，望着天，祝福，掰开饼，递给门徒。门徒又递给众人。

chapters.en: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
chapters.zh: 他们都吃，并且吃饱了。把剩下的零碎收拾起来，装满了十二个篮子。

chapters.en: The number of those who ate was about five thousand men, besides women and children.
chapters.zh: 吃的人，除了妇女孩子，约有五千。

chapters.en: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of him to the other side, while he dismissed the crowd.
chapters.zh: 耶稣随即催门徒上船，先渡到那边去，等他叫众人散开。

chapters.en: After he had dismissed them, he went up on a mountainside by himself to pray. Later that night, he was there alone,
chapters.zh: 散了众人以后，他就独自上山去祷告。到了晚上，只有他一人在那里。

chapters.en: and the boat was already a considerable distance from land, buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it.
chapters.zh: 那时船在海中，因风不顺，被浪摇撼。

chapters.en: Shortly before dawn Jesus went out to them, walking on the lake.
chapters.zh: 夜里四更天，耶稣在海面上走，往门徒那里去。

chapters.en: When the disciples saw him walking on the lake, they were terrified. “It’s a ghost,” they said, and cried out in fear.
chapters.zh: 门徒看见他在海面上走，就惊慌了，说，是个鬼怪。便害怕，喊叫起来。

chapters.en: But Jesus immediately said to them: “Take courage! It is I. Don’t be afraid.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣连忙对他们说，你们放心。是我，不要怕。

chapters.en: “Lord, if it’s you,” Peter replied, “tell me to come to you on the water.”
chapters.zh: 彼得说，主，如果是你，请叫我从水面上走到你那里去。

chapters.en: “Come,” he said. Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water and came toward Jesus.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你来吧。彼得就从船上下去，在水面上走，要到耶稣那里去。

chapters.en: But when he saw the wind, he was afraid and, beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!”
chapters.zh: 只因见风甚大，就害怕。将要沉下去，便喊着说，主阿，救我。

chapters.en: Immediately Jesus reached out his hand and caught him. “You of little faith,” he said, “why did you doubt?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣赶紧伸手拉住他，说，你这小信的人哪，为什么疑惑呢？

chapters.en: And when they climbed into the boat, the wind died down.
chapters.zh: 他们上了船，风就住了。

chapters.en: Then those who were in the boat worshiped him, saying, “Truly you are the Son of God.”
chapters.zh: 在船上的人都拜他说，你真是神的儿子了。

chapters.en: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret.
chapters.zh: 他们过了海，来到革尼撒勒地方。

chapters.en: And when the men of that place recognized Jesus, they sent word to all the surrounding country. People brought all their sick to him
chapters.zh: 那里的人，一认出是耶稣，就打发人到周围地方去，把所有的病人，带到他那里。

chapters.en: and begged him to let the sick just touch the edge of his cloak, and all who touched it were healed.
chapters.zh: 只求耶稣准他们摸他的衣裳穗子，摸着的人，就都好了。

chapters.en: Then some Pharisees and teachers of the law came to Jesus from Jerusalem and asked,
chapters.zh: 那时有法利赛人和文士，从耶路撒冷来见耶稣说，

chapters.en: “Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? They don’t wash their hands before they eat!”
chapters.zh: 你的门徒为什么犯古人的遗传呢？因为吃饭的时候，他们不洗手。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “And why do you break the command of God for the sake of your tradition?
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，你们为什么因着你们的遗传，犯神的诫命呢？

chapters.en: For God said, ‘Honor your father and mother’and ‘Anyone who curses their father or mother is to be put to death.’
chapters.zh: 神说，当孝敬父母。又说，咒骂父母的，必治死他。

chapters.en: But you say that if anyone declares that what might have been used to help their father or mother is ‘devoted to God,’
chapters.zh: 你们倒说，无论何人对父母说，我所当奉给你的，已经作了供献。

chapters.en: they are not to ‘honor their father or mother’ with it. Thus you nullify the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
chapters.zh: 他就可以不孝敬父母。这就是你们借着遗传，废了神的诫命。

chapters.en: You hypocrites! Isaiah was right when he prophesied about you:
chapters.zh: 假冒为善的人哪，以赛亚指着你们说的预言，是不错的。他说，

chapters.en: “ ‘These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
chapters.zh: 这百姓用嘴唇尊敬我，心却远离我。

chapters.en: They worship me in vain; their teachings are merely human rules.’”
chapters.zh: 他们将人的吩咐，当作道理教导人，所以拜我也是枉然。

chapters.en: Jesus called the crowd to him and said, “Listen and understand.
chapters.zh: 耶稣就叫了众人来，对他们说，你们要听，也要明白。

chapters.en: What goes into someone’s mouth does not defile them, but what comes out of their mouth, that is what defiles them.”
chapters.zh: 入口的不能污秽人，出口的乃能污秽人。

chapters.en: Then the disciples came to him and asked, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?”
chapters.zh: 当时，门徒进前来对他说，法利赛人听见这话，不服，你知道吗？（不服原文作跌倒）

chapters.en: He replied, “Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by the roots.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，凡栽种的物，若不是我天父栽种的，必要拔出来。

chapters.en: Leave them; they are blind guides.If the blind lead the blind, both will fall into a pit.”
chapters.zh: 任凭他们吧。他们是瞎眼领路的。若是瞎子领瞎子，两个人都要掉在坑里。

chapters.en: Peter said, “Explain the parable to us.”
chapters.zh: 彼得对耶稣说，请将这比喻讲给我们听。

chapters.en: “Are you still so dull?” Jesus asked them.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们到如今还不明白吗？

chapters.en: “Don’t you see that whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and then out of the body?
chapters.zh: 岂不知凡入口的，是运到肚子里，又落在茅厕里吗？

chapters.en: But the things that come out of a person’s mouth come from the heart, and these defile them.
chapters.zh: 惟独出口的，是从心里发出来的，这才污秽人。

chapters.en: For out of the heart come evil thoughts—murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, slander.
chapters.zh: 因为从心里发出来的，有恶念，凶杀，奸淫，苟合，偷盗，妄证，毁谤。

chapters.en: These are what defile a person; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile them.”
chapters.zh: 这都是污秽人的。至于不洗手吃饭，那却不污秽人。

chapters.en: Leaving that place, Jesus withdrew to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
chapters.zh: 耶稣离开那里，退到推罗西顿的境内去。

chapters.en: A Canaanite woman from that vicinity came to him, crying out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter is demon-possessed and suffering terribly.”
chapters.zh: 有一个迦南妇人，从那地方出来，喊着说，主啊，大卫的子孙，可怜我。我女儿被鬼附得甚苦。

chapters.en: Jesus did not answer a word. So his disciples came to him and urged him, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣却一言不答。门徒进前来，求他说，这妇人在我们后头喊叫。请打发她走吧。

chapters.en: He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，我奉差遣，不过是到以色列家迷失的羊那里去。

chapters.en: The woman came and knelt before him. “Lord, help me!” she said.
chapters.zh: 那妇人来拜他，说，主啊，帮助我。

chapters.en: He replied, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
chapters.zh: 他回答说，不好拿儿女的饼，丢给狗吃。

chapters.en: “Yes it is, Lord,” she said. “Even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.”
chapters.zh: 妇人说，主啊，不错。但是狗也吃它主人桌子上掉下来的碎渣儿。

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to her, “Woman, you have great faith! Your request is granted.” And her daughter was healed at that moment.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，妇人，你的信心是大的。照你所要的，给你成全了吧。从那时候，她女儿就好了。

chapters.en: Jesus left there and went along the Sea of Galilee. Then he went up on a mountainside and sat down.
chapters.zh: 耶稣离开那地方，来到靠近加利利的海边，就上山坐下。

chapters.en: Great crowds came to him, bringing the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute and many others, and laid them at his feet; and he healed them.
chapters.zh: 有许多人到他那里，带着瘸子，瞎子，哑吧，有残疾的，和好些别的病人，都放在他脚前。他就治好了他们。

chapters.en: The people were amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled made well, the lame walking and the blind seeing. And they praised the God of Israel.
chapters.zh: 甚至众人都希奇。因为看见哑吧说话，残疾的痊愈，瘸子行走，瞎子看见，他们就归荣耀给以色列的神。

chapters.en: Jesus called his disciples to him and said, “I have compassion for these people; they have already been with me three days and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may collapse on the way.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣叫门徒来说，我怜悯这众人，因为他们同我在这里已经三天，也没有吃的了。我不愿意叫他们饿着回去，恐怕在路上困乏。

chapters.en: His disciples answered, “Where could we get enough bread in this remote place to feed such a crowd?”
chapters.zh: 门徒说，我们在这野地，哪里有这么多的饼，叫这许多人吃饱呢？

chapters.en: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied, “and a few small fish.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们有多少饼？他们说，有七个，还有几条小鱼。

chapters.en: He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
chapters.zh: 他就吩咐众人坐在地上。

chapters.en: Then he took the seven loaves and the fish, and when he had given thanks, he broke them and gave them to the disciples, and they in turn to the people.
chapters.zh: 拿着这七个饼和几条鱼，祝谢了，掰开，递给门徒。门徒又递给众人。

chapters.en: They all ate and were satisfied. Afterward the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
chapters.zh: 众人都吃并且吃饱了。收拾剩下的零碎，装满了七个筐子。

chapters.en: The number of those who ate was four thousand men, besides women and children.
chapters.zh: 吃的人，除了妇女孩子，共有四千。

chapters.en: After Jesus had sent the crowd away, he got into the boat and went to the vicinity of Magadan.
chapters.zh: 耶稣叫众人散去，就上船，来到马加丹的境界。

chapters.en: The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus and tested him by asking him to show them a sign from heaven.
chapters.zh: 法利赛人和撒都该人，来试探耶稣，请他从天上显个神迹给他们看。

chapters.en: He replied, “When evening comes, you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is red,’
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，晚上天发红，你们就说，天必要晴。

chapters.en: and in the morning, ‘Today it will be stormy, for the sky is red and overcast.’ You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but you cannot interpret the signs of the times.
chapters.zh: 早晨天发红，又发黑，你们就说，今日必有风雨。你们知道分辨天上的气色，倒不能分辨这时候的神迹。

chapters.en: A wicked and adulterous generation looks for a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.” Jesus then left them and went away.
chapters.zh: 一个邪恶淫乱的世代求神迹，除了约拿的神迹以外，再没有神迹给他看。耶稣就离开他们去了。

chapters.en: When they went across the lake, the disciples forgot to take bread.
chapters.zh: 门徒渡到那边去，忘了带饼。

chapters.en: “Be careful,” Jesus said to them. “Be on your guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说，你们要谨慎，防备法利赛人和撒都该人的酵。

chapters.en: They discussed this among themselves and said, “It is because we didn’t bring any bread.”
chapters.zh: 门徒彼此议论说，这是因为我们没有带饼吧。

chapters.en: Aware of their discussion, Jesus asked, “You of little faith, why are you talking among yourselves about having no bread?
chapters.zh: 耶稣看出来，就说，你们这小信的人，为什么因为没有饼彼此议论呢？

chapters.en: Do you still not understand? Don’t you remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?
chapters.zh: 你们还不明白吗？不记得那五个饼，分给五千人，又收拾了多少篮子的零碎吗？

chapters.en: Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?
chapters.zh: 也不记得那七个饼，分给四千人，又收拾了多少筐子的零碎吗？

chapters.en: How is it you don’t understand that I was not talking to you about bread? But be on your guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
chapters.zh: 我对你们说，要防备法利赛人和撒都该人的酵，这话不是指着饼说的。你们怎么不明白呢？

chapters.en: Then they understood that he was not telling them to guard against the yeast used in bread, but against the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
chapters.zh: 门徒这才晓得他说的，不是叫他们防备饼的酵，乃是防备法利赛人和撒都该人的教训。

chapters.en: When Jesus came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣到了该撒利亚腓立比的境内，就问门徒说，人说我人子是谁。（有古卷无我字）

chapters.en: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
chapters.zh: 他们说，有人说是施洗的约翰。有人说是以利亚。又有人说是耶利米，或是先知里的一位。

chapters.en: “But what about you?” he asked. “Who do you say I am?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们说我是谁。

chapters.en: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
chapters.zh: 西门彼得回答说，你是基督，是永生神的儿子。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, for this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by my Father in heaven.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他说，西门巴约拿，你是有福的。因为这不是属血肉的指示你的，乃是我在天上的父指示的。

chapters.en: And I tell you that you are Peter,and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hadeswill not overcome it.
chapters.zh: 我还告诉你，你是彼得，我要把我的教会建造在这磐石上，阴间的权柄，不能胜过他。（权柄原文作门）

chapters.en: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will beloosed in heaven.”
chapters.zh: 我要把天国的钥匙给你。凡你在地上所捆绑的，在天上也要捆绑。凡你在地上所释放的，在天上也要释放。

chapters.en: Then he ordered his disciples not to tell anyone that he was the Messiah.
chapters.zh: 当下，耶稣嘱咐门徒，不可对人说他是基督。

chapters.en: From that time on Jesus began to explain to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, the chief priests and the teachers of the law, and that he must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.
chapters.zh: 从此耶稣才指示门徒，他必须上耶路撒冷去，受长老祭司长文士许多的苦，并且被杀，第三日复活。

chapters.en: Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him. “Never, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to you!”
chapters.zh: 彼得就拉着他，劝他说，主阿，万不可如此，这事必不临到你身上。

chapters.en: Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me; you do not have in mind the concerns of God, but merely human concerns.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣转过来，对彼得说，撒但退我后边去吧。你是绊我脚的。因为你不体贴神的意思，只体贴人的意思。

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.
chapters.zh: 于是耶稣对门徒说，若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，背起他的十字架，来跟从我。

chapters.en: For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will find it.
chapters.zh: 因为凡要救自己生命的，（生命或作灵魂下同）必丧掉生命。凡为我丧掉生命的，必得着生命。

chapters.en: What good will it be for someone to gain the whole world, yet forfeit their soul? Or what can anyone give in exchange for their soul?
chapters.zh: 人若赚得全世界，赔上自己的生命，有什么益处呢？人还能拿什么换生命呢？

chapters.en: For the Son of Man is going to come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he will reward each person according to what they have done.
chapters.zh: 人子要在他父的荣耀里，同着众使者降临。那时候，他要照各人的行为报应各人。

chapters.en: “Truly I tell you, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.”
chapters.zh: 我实在告诉你们，站在这里的，有人在没尝死味以前，必看见人子降临在他的国里。

chapters.en: After six days Jesus took with him Peter, James and John the brother of James, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.
chapters.zh: 过了六天，耶稣带着彼得，雅各，和雅各的兄弟约翰，暗暗地上了高山。

chapters.en: There he was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as white as the light.
chapters.zh: 就在他们面前变了形像。脸面明亮如日头，衣裳洁白如光。

chapters.en: Just then there appeared before them Moses and Elijah, talking with Jesus.
chapters.zh: 忽然有摩西，以利亚，向他们显现，同耶稣说话。

chapters.en: Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you wish, I will put up three shelters—one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah.”
chapters.zh: 彼得对耶稣说，主阿，我们在这里真好。你若愿意，我就在这里搭三座棚，一座为你，一座为摩西，一座为以利亚。

chapters.en: While he was still speaking, a bright cloud covered them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased. Listen to him!”
chapters.zh: 说话之间，忽然有一朵光明的云彩遮盖他们。且有声音从云彩里出来说，这是我的爱子，我所喜悦的。你们要听他。

chapters.en: When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown to the ground, terrified.
chapters.zh: 门徒听见，就俯伏在地，极其害怕。

chapters.en: But Jesus came and touched them. “Get up,” he said. “Don’t be afraid.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣进前来，摸他们说，起来，不要害怕。

chapters.en: When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
chapters.zh: 他们举目不见一人，只见耶稣在那里。

chapters.en: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus instructed them, “Don’t tell anyone what you have seen, until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”
chapters.zh: 下山的时候，耶稣吩咐他们说，人子还没有从死里复活，你们不要将所看见的告诉人。

chapters.en: The disciples asked him, “Why then do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come first?”
chapters.zh: 门徒问耶稣说，文士为什么说，以利亚必须先来。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “To be sure, Elijah comes and will restore all things.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，以利亚固然先来，并要复兴万事。

chapters.en: But I tell you, Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but have done to him everything they wished. In the same way the Son of Man is going to suffer at their hands.”
chapters.zh: 只是我告诉你们，以利亚已经来了，人却不认识他，竟任意待他。人子也将要这样受他们的害。

chapters.en: Then the disciples understood that he was talking to them about John the Baptist.
chapters.zh: 门徒这才明白耶稣所说的，是指着施洗的约翰。

chapters.en: When they came to the crowd, a man approached Jesus and knelt before him.
chapters.zh: 耶稣和门徒到了众人那里，有一个人来见耶稣，跪下，说，

chapters.en: “Lord, have mercy on my son,” he said. “He has seizures and is suffering greatly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.
chapters.zh: 主阿，怜悯我的儿子。他害癫痫的病很苦，屡次跌在火里，屡次跌在水里。

chapters.en: I brought him to your disciples, but they could not heal him.”
chapters.zh: 我带他到你门徒那里，他们却不能医治他。

chapters.en: “You unbelieving and perverse generation,” Jesus replied, “how long shall I stay with you? How long shall I put up with you? Bring the boy here to me.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，嗳，这又不信又悖谬的世代阿，我在你们这里要到几时呢？我忍耐你们要到几时呢？把他带到我这里来吧。

chapters.en: Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, and he was healed at that moment.
chapters.zh: 耶稣斥责那鬼，鬼就出来。从此孩子就痊愈了。

chapters.en: Then the disciples came to Jesus in private and asked, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
chapters.zh: 门徒暗暗地到耶稣跟前说，我们为什么不能赶出那鬼呢？

chapters.en: He replied, “Because you have so little faith. Truly I tell you, if you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain,‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，是因你们的信心小。我实在告诉你们，你们若有信心像一粒芥菜种，就是对这座山说，你从这边挪到那边，它也必挪去。并且你们没有一件不能作的事了。

chapters.en: But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting.
chapters.zh: 至于这一类的鬼，若不祷告禁食，他就不出来。（或作不能赶他出来）

chapters.en: When they came together in Galilee, he said to them, “The Son of Man is going to be delivered into the hands of men.
chapters.zh: 他们还住在加利利的时候，耶稣对门徒说，人子将要被交在人手里。

chapters.en: They will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised to life.” And the disciples were filled with grief.
chapters.zh: 他们要杀害他，第三日他要复活。门徒就大大地忧愁。

chapters.en: After Jesus and his disciples arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma temple tax came to Peter and asked, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the temple tax?”
chapters.zh: 到了迦百农，有收丁税的人来见彼得说，你们的先生不纳丁税吗？（丁税约有半块钱）

chapters.en: “Yes, he does,” he replied. When Peter came into the house, Jesus was the first to speak. “What do you think, Simon?” he asked. “From whom do the kings of the earth collect duty and taxes—from their own children or from others?”
chapters.zh: 彼得说，纳。他进了屋子，耶稣先向他说，西门，你的意思如何。世上的君王，向谁征收关税丁税。是向自己的儿子呢？是向外人呢？

chapters.en: “From others,” Peter answered. “Then the children are exempt,” Jesus said to him.
chapters.zh: 彼得说，是向外人。耶稣说，既然如此，儿子就可以免税了。

chapters.en: “But so that we may not cause offense, go to the lake and throw out your line. Take the first fish you catch; open its mouth and you will find a four-drachma coin. Take it and give it to them for my tax and yours.”
chapters.zh: 但恐怕触犯他们，（触犯原文作绊倒）你且往海边去钓鱼，把先钓上来的鱼拿起来，开了它的口，必得一块钱，可以拿去给他们，作你我的税银。

chapters.en: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who, then, is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
chapters.zh: 当时门徒进前来，问耶稣说，天国里谁是最大的。

chapters.en: He called a little child to him, and placed the child among them.
chapters.zh: 耶稣便叫一个小孩子来，使他站在他们当中，

chapters.en: And he said: “Truly I tell you, unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
chapters.zh: 说，我实在告诉你们，你们若不回转，变成小孩子的样式，断不得进天国。

chapters.en: Therefore, whoever takes the lowly position of this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
chapters.zh: 所以凡自己谦卑像这小孩子的，他在天国里就是最大的。

chapters.en: And whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.
chapters.zh: 凡为我的名，接待一个像这小孩子的，就是接待我。

chapters.en: “If anyone causes one of these little ones—those who believe in me—to stumble, it would be better for them to have a large millstone hung around their neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
chapters.zh: 凡使这信我的一个小子跌倒的，倒不如把大磨石拴在这人的颈项上，沉在深海里。

chapters.en: Woe to the world because of the things that cause people to stumble! Such things must come, but woe to the person through whom they come!
chapters.zh: 这世界有祸了，因为将人绊倒。绊倒人的事是免不了的，但那绊倒人的有祸了。

chapters.en: If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life maimed or crippled than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into eternal fire.
chapters.zh: 倘若你一只手，或是一只脚，叫你跌倒，就砍下来丢掉。你缺一只手，或是一只脚，进入永生，强如有两手两脚，被丢在永火里。

chapters.en: And if your eye causes you to stumble, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
chapters.zh: 倘若你一只眼叫你跌倒，就把它剜出来丢掉。你只有一只眼进入永生，强如有两只眼被丢在地狱的火里。

chapters.en: “See that you do not despise one of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father in heaven.
chapters.zh: 你们要小心，不可轻看这小子里的一个。我告诉你们，他们的使者在天上，常见我天父的面。（有古卷在此有

chapters.en: The Son of Man came to save what was lost.
chapters.zh: 人子来为要拯救失丧的人）

chapters.en: “What do you think? If a man owns a hundred sheep, and one of them wanders away, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go to look for the one that wandered off?
chapters.zh: 一个人若有一百只羊，一只走迷了路，你们的意思如何。他岂不撇下这九十九只，往山里去找那只迷路的羊吗？

chapters.en: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he is happier about that one sheep than about the ninety-nine that did not wander off.
chapters.zh: 若是找着了，我实在告诉你们，他为这一只羊欢喜，比为那没有迷路的九十九只欢喜还大呢。

chapters.en: In the same way your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.
chapters.zh: 你们在天上的父，也是这样不愿意这小子里失丧一个。

chapters.en: “If your brother or sister sins, go and point out their fault, just between the two of you. If they listen to you, you have won them over.
chapters.zh: 倘若你的弟兄得罪你，你就去趁着只有他和你在一处的时候，指出他的错来。他若听你，你便得了你的弟兄。

chapters.en: But if they will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
chapters.zh: 他若不听，你就另外带一两个人同去，要凭两三个人的口作见证，句句都可定准。

chapters.en: If they still refuse to listen, tell it to the church; and if they refuse to listen even to the church, treat them as you would a pagan or a tax collector.
chapters.zh: 若是不听他们，就告诉教会。若是不听教会，就看他像外邦人和税吏一样。

chapters.en: “Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will beloosed in heaven.
chapters.zh: 我实在告诉你们，凡你们在地上所捆绑的，在天上也要捆绑。凡你们在地上所释放的，在天上也要释放。

chapters.en: “Again, truly I tell you that if two of you on earth agree about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven.
chapters.zh: 我又告诉你们，若是你们中间有两个人在地上，同心合意地求什么事，我在天上的父，必为他们成全。

chapters.en: For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them.”
chapters.zh: 因为无论在哪里，有两三个人奉我的名聚会，那里就有我在他们中间。

chapters.en: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother or sister who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
chapters.zh: 那时彼得进前来，对耶稣说，主阿，我弟兄得罪我，我当饶恕他几次呢？到七次可以吗？

chapters.en: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，我对你说，不是到七次，乃是到七十个七次。

chapters.en: “Therefore, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
chapters.zh: 天国好像一个王，要和他仆人算账。

chapters.en: As he began the settlement, a man who owed him ten thousand bags of gold was brought to him.
chapters.zh: 才算的时候，有人带了一个欠一千万银子的来。

chapters.en: Since he was not able to pay, the master ordered that he and his wife and his children and all that he had be sold to repay the debt.
chapters.zh: 因为他没有什么偿还之物，主人吩咐把他和他妻子儿女，并一切所有的都卖了偿还。

chapters.en: “At this the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Be patient with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’
chapters.zh: 那仆人就俯伏拜他说，主阿，宽容我，将来我都要还清。

chapters.en: The servant’s master took pity on him, canceled the debt and let him go.
chapters.zh: 那仆人的主人，就动了慈心，把他释放了，并且免了他的债。

chapters.en: “But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred silver coins.He grabbed him and began to choke him. ‘Pay back what you owe me!’ he demanded.
chapters.zh: 那仆人出来，遇见他的一个同伴，欠他十两银子，便揪着他，掐住他的喉咙，说，你把所欠的还我。

chapters.en: “His fellow servant fell to his knees and begged him, ‘Be patient with me, and I will pay it back.’
chapters.zh: 他的同伴就俯伏央求他，说，宽容我吧，将来我必还清。

chapters.en: “But he refused. Instead, he went off and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay the debt.
chapters.zh: 他不肯，竟去把他下在监里，等他还了所欠的债。

chapters.en: When the other servants saw what had happened, they were outraged and went and told their master everything that had happened.
chapters.zh: 众同伴看见他所作的事，就甚忧愁，去把这事都告诉了主人。

chapters.en: “Then the master called the servant in. ‘You wicked servant,’ he said, ‘I canceled all that debt of yours because you begged me to.
chapters.zh: 于是主人叫了他来，对他说，你这恶奴才，你央求我，我就把你所欠的都免了。

chapters.en: Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you?’
chapters.zh: 你不应当怜恤你的同伴像我怜恤你吗？

chapters.en: In anger his master handed him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should pay back all he owed.
chapters.zh: 主人就大怒，把他交给掌刑的，等他还清了所欠的债。

chapters.en: “This is how my heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother or sister from your heart.”
chapters.zh: 你们各人若不从心里饶恕你的弟兄，我天父也要这样待你们了。

chapters.en: When Jesus had finished saying these things, he left Galilee and went into the region of Judea to the other side of the Jordan.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说完了这些话，就离开加利利，来到犹太的境界，约但河外。

chapters.en: Large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
chapters.zh: 有许多人跟着他。他就在那里把他们的病人治好了。

chapters.en: Some Pharisees came to him to test him. They asked, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any and every reason?”
chapters.zh: 有法利赛人来试探耶稣说，人无论什么缘故，都可以休妻吗？

chapters.en: “Haven’t you read,” he replied, “that at the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，那起初造人的，是造男造女，

chapters.en: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?
chapters.zh: 并且说，因此，人要离开父母，与妻子连合，二人成为一体。这经你们没有念过吗？

chapters.en: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.”
chapters.zh: 既然如此，夫妻不再是两个人，乃是一体的了。所以神配合的，人不可分开。

chapters.en: “Why then,” they asked, “did Moses command that a man give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away?”
chapters.zh: 法利赛人说，这样，摩西为什么吩咐给妻子休书，就可以休她呢？

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because your hearts were hard. But it was not this way from the beginning.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，摩西因为你们的心硬，所以许你们休妻。但起初并不是这样。

chapters.en: I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，凡休妻另娶的，若不是为淫乱的缘故，就是犯奸淫了，有人娶那被休的妇人，也是犯奸淫了。

chapters.en: The disciples said to him, “If this is the situation between a husband and wife, it is better not to marry.”
chapters.zh: 门徒对耶稣说，人和妻子既是这样，倒不如不娶。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “Not everyone can accept this word, but only those to whom it has been given.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，这话不是人都能领受的。惟独赐给谁，谁才能领受。

chapters.en: For there are eunuchs who were born that way, and there are eunuchs who have been made eunuchs by others—and there are those who choose to live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.”
chapters.zh: 因为有生来是阉人，也有被人阉的，并有为天国的缘故自阉的。这话谁能领受，就可以领受。

chapters.en: Then people brought little children to Jesus for him to place his hands on them and pray for them. But the disciples rebuked them.
chapters.zh: 那时有人带着小孩子来见耶稣，要耶稣给他们按手祷告。门徒就责备那些人。

chapters.en: Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，让小孩子到我这里来，不要禁止他们。因为在天国的，正是这样的人。

chapters.en: When he had placed his hands on them, he went on from there.
chapters.zh: 耶稣给他们按手，就离开那地方去了。

chapters.en: Just then a man came up to Jesus and asked, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to get eternal life?”
chapters.zh: 有一个人来见耶稣说，夫子，（有古卷作良善的夫子）我该作什么善事，才能得永生。

chapters.en: “Why do you ask me about what is good?” Jesus replied. “There is only One who is good. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他说，你为什么以善事问我呢？只有一位是善的，（有古卷作你为什么称我是良善的，除了神以外，没有一个良善的）你若要进入永生，就当遵守诫命。

chapters.en: “Which ones?” he inquired. Jesus replied, “ ‘You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not give false testimony,
chapters.zh: 他说，什么诫命。耶稣说，就是不可杀人，不可奸淫，不可偷盗，不可作假见证，

chapters.en: honor your father and mother,’and ‘love your neighbor as yourself.’”
chapters.zh: 当孝敬父母。又当爱人如己。

chapters.en: “All these I have kept,” the young man said. “What do I still lack?”
chapters.zh: 那少年人说，这一切我都遵守了。还缺少什么呢？

chapters.en: Jesus answered, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你若愿意作完全人，可去变卖你所有的，分给穷人，就必有财宝在天上，你还要来跟从我。

chapters.en: When the young man heard this, he went away sad, because he had great wealth.
chapters.zh: 那少年人听见这话，就忧忧愁愁地走了。因为他的产业很多。

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Truly I tell you, it is hard for someone who is rich to enter the kingdom of heaven.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对门徒说，我实在告诉你们，财主进天国是难的。

chapters.en: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for someone who is rich to enter the kingdom of God.”
chapters.zh: 我又告诉你们，骆驼穿过针的眼，比财主进神的国还容易呢。

chapters.en: When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and asked, “Who then can be saved?”
chapters.zh: 门徒听见这话，就希奇得很，说，这样谁能得救呢？

chapters.en: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣看着他们说，在人这是不能的。在神凡事都能。

chapters.en: Peter answered him, “We have left everything to follow you! What then will there be for us?”
chapters.zh: 彼得就对他说，看哪，我们已经撇下所有的跟从你，将来我们要得什么呢？

chapters.en: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, at the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，我实在告诉你们，你们这跟从我的人，到复兴的时候，人子坐在他荣耀的宝座上，你们也要坐在十二个宝座上，审判以色列十二个支派。

chapters.en: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for my sake will receive a hundred times as much and will inherit eternal life.
chapters.zh: 凡为我的名撇下房屋，或是弟兄，姐妹，父亲，母亲，（有古卷添妻子），儿女，田地的，必要得着百倍，并且承受永生。

chapters.en: But many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first.
chapters.zh: 然而有许多在前的将要在后，在后的将要在前。

chapters.en: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
chapters.zh: 因为天国好像家主，清早去雇人，进他的葡萄园作工。

chapters.en: He agreed to pay them a denariusfor the day and sent them into his vineyard.
chapters.zh: 和工人讲定一天一钱银子，就打发他们进葡萄园去。

chapters.en: “About nine in the morning he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.
chapters.zh: 约在巳初出去，看见市上还有闲站的人。

chapters.en: He told them, ‘You also go and work in my vineyard, and I will pay you whatever is right.’
chapters.zh: 就对他们说，你们也进葡萄园去，所当给的，我必给你们。他们也进去了。

chapters.en: So they went. “He went out again about noon and about three in the afternoon and did the same thing.
chapters.zh: 约在午正和申初又出去，也是这样行。

chapters.en: About five in the afternoon he went out and found still others standing around. He asked them, ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’
chapters.zh: 约在酉初出去，看见还有人站在那里。就问他们说，你们为什么整天在这里闲站呢？

chapters.en: “ ‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered. “He said to them, ‘You also go and work in my vineyard.’
chapters.zh: 他们说，因为没有人雇我们。他说，你们也进葡萄园去。

chapters.en: “When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, beginning with the last ones hired and going on to the first.’
chapters.zh: 到了晚上，园主对管事的说，叫工人都来，给他们工钱，从后来的起，到先来的为止。

chapters.en: “The workers who were hired about five in the afternoon came and each received a denarius.
chapters.zh: 约在酉初雇的人来了，各人得了一钱银子。

chapters.en: So when those came who were hired first, they expected to receive more. But each one of them also received a denarius.
chapters.zh: 及至那先雇的来了，他们以为必要多得。谁知也是各得一钱。

chapters.en: When they received it, they began to grumble against the landowner.
chapters.zh: 他们得了，就埋怨家主说，

chapters.en: ‘These who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the work and the heat of the day.’
chapters.zh: 我们整天劳苦受热，那后来的只做了一小时，你竟叫他们和我们一样吗？

chapters.en: “But he answered one of them, ‘I am not being unfair to you, friend. Didn’t you agree to work for a denarius?
chapters.zh: 家主回答其中的一人说，朋友，我不亏负你。你与我讲定的，不是一钱银子吗？

chapters.en: Take your pay and go. I want to give the one who was hired last the same as I gave you.
chapters.zh: 拿你的走吧。我给那后来的和给你一样，这是我愿意的。

chapters.en: Don’t I have the right to do what I want with my own money? Or are you envious because I am generous?’
chapters.zh: 我的东西难道不可随我的意思用吗？因为我作好人，你就红了眼吗？

chapters.en: “So the last will be first, and the first will be last.”
chapters.zh: 这样，那在后的将要在前，在前的将要在后了。（有古卷在此有因为被召的人多，选上的人少）

chapters.en: Now Jesus was going up to Jerusalem. On the way, he took the Twelve aside and said to them,
chapters.zh: 耶稣上耶路撒冷去的时候，在路上把十二个门徒带到一边对他们说，

chapters.en: “We are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. They will condemn him to death
chapters.zh: 看哪，我们上耶路撒冷去，人子要被交给祭司长和文士。他们要定他死罪。

chapters.en: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified. On the third day he will be raised to life!”
chapters.zh: 又交给外邦人，将他戏弄，鞭打，钉在十字架上。第三日他要复活。

chapters.en: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and, kneeling down, asked a favor of him.
chapters.zh: 那时，西庇太儿子的母亲，同她两个儿子上前来拜耶稣，求他一件事。

chapters.en: “What is it you want?” he asked. She said, “Grant that one of these two sons of mine may sit at your right and the other at your left in your kingdom.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你要什么呢？她说，愿你叫我这两个儿子在你国里，一个坐在你右边，一个坐在你左边。

chapters.en: “You don’t know what you are asking,” Jesus said to them. “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?”“We can,” they answered.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，你们不知道所求的是什么。我将要喝的杯，你们能喝吗？他们说，我们能。

chapters.en: Jesus said to them, “You will indeed drink from my cup, but to sit at my right or left is not for me to grant. These places belong to those for whom they have been prepared by my Father.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，我所喝的杯，你们必要喝。只是坐在我的左右，不是我可以赐的，乃是我父为谁预备的，就赐给谁。

chapters.en: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.
chapters.zh: 那十个门徒听见，就恼怒他们弟兄二人。

chapters.en: Jesus called them together and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their high officials exercise authority over them.
chapters.zh: 耶稣叫了他们来，说，你们知道外邦人有君王为主治理他们，有大臣操权管束他们。

chapters.en: Not so with you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,
chapters.zh: 只是在你们中间不可这样。你们中间谁愿为大，就必作你们的用人。

chapters.en: and whoever wants to be first must be your slave—
chapters.zh: 谁愿为首，就必作你们的仆人。

chapters.en: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
chapters.zh: 正如人子来，不是要受人的服事，乃是要服事人。并且要舍命，作多人的赎价。

chapters.en: As Jesus and his disciples were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
chapters.zh: 他们出耶利哥的时候，有极多的人跟随他，

chapters.en: Two blind men were sitting by the roadside, and when they heard that Jesus was going by, they shouted, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
chapters.zh: 有两个瞎子坐在路旁，听说是耶稣经过，就喊着说，主阿，大卫的子孙，可怜我们吧。

chapters.en: The crowd rebuked them and told them to be quiet, but they shouted all the louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
chapters.zh: 众人责备他们，不许他们作声。他们却越发喊着说，主阿，大卫的子孙，可怜我们吧。

chapters.en: Jesus stopped and called them. “What do you want me to do for you?” he asked.
chapters.zh: 耶稣就站住，叫他们来，说，要我为你们作什么。

chapters.en: “Lord,” they answered, “we want our sight.”
chapters.zh: 他们说，主阿，要我们的眼睛能看见。

chapters.en: Jesus had compassion on them and touched their eyes. Immediately they received their sight and followed him.
chapters.zh: 耶稣就动了慈心，把他们的眼睛一摸，他们立刻看见，就跟从了耶稣。

chapters.en: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,
chapters.zh: 耶稣和门徒将近耶路撒冷，到了伯法其在橄榄山那里。

chapters.en: saying to them, “Go to the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt by her. Untie them and bring them to me.
chapters.zh: 耶稣就打发两个门徒，对他们说，你们往对面村子里去，必看见一匹驴拴在那里，还有驴驹同在一处。你们解开牵到我这里来。

chapters.en: If anyone says anything to you, say that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.”
chapters.zh: 若有人对你们说什么，你们就说，主要用它。那人必立时让你们牵来。

chapters.en: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet:
chapters.zh: 这事成就，是要应验先知的话，说，

chapters.en: “Say to Daughter Zion, ‘See, your king comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, and on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’ ”
chapters.zh: 要对锡安的居民（原文作女子）说，看哪，你的王来到你这里，是温柔的，又骑着驴，就是骑着驴驹子。

chapters.en: The disciples went and did as Jesus had instructed them.
chapters.zh: 门徒就照耶稣所吩咐的去行，

chapters.en: They brought the donkey and the colt and placed their cloaks on them for Jesus to sit on.
chapters.zh: 牵了驴和驴驹来，把自己的衣服搭在上面，耶稣就骑上。

chapters.en: A very large crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
chapters.zh: 众人多半把衣服铺在路上。还有人砍下树枝来铺在路上。

chapters.en: The crowds that went ahead of him and those that followed shouted, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!”“Hosanna in the highest heaven!”
chapters.zh: 前行后随的众人，喊着说，和散那归于大卫的子孙，（和散那原有求救的意思，在此乃称颂的话）奉主名来的，是应当称颂的。高高在上和散那。

chapters.en: When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked, “Who is this?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣既进了耶路撒冷，合城都惊动了，说，这是谁。

chapters.en: The crowds answered, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.”
chapters.zh: 众人说，这是加利利拿撒勒的先知耶稣。

chapters.en: Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves.
chapters.zh: 耶稣进了神的殿，赶出殿里一切作买卖的人，推倒兑换银钱之人的桌子，和卖鸽子之人的凳子。

chapters.en: “It is written,” he said to them, “ ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’but you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’”
chapters.zh: 对他们说，经上记着说，我的殿必称为祷告的殿。你们倒使它成为贼窝了。

chapters.en: The blind and the lame came to him at the temple, and he healed them.
chapters.zh: 在殿里有瞎子瘸子，到耶稣跟前。他就治好了他们。

chapters.en: But when the chief priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things he did and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David,” they were indignant.
chapters.zh: 祭司长和文士，看见耶稣所行的奇事，又见小孩子在殿里喊着说，和散那归于大卫的子孙。就甚恼怒，

chapters.en: “Do you hear what these children are saying?” they asked him. “Yes,” replied Jesus, “have you never read, “ ‘From the lips of children and infants you, Lord, have called forth your praise’?”
chapters.zh: 对他说，这些人所说的，你听见了吗？耶稣说，是的，经上说，你从婴孩和吃奶的口中，完全了赞美的话。你们没有念过吗？

chapters.en: And he left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where he spent the night.
chapters.zh: 于是离开他们出城到伯大尼去，在那里住宿。

chapters.en: Early in the morning, as Jesus was on his way back to the city, he was hungry.
chapters.zh: 早晨回城的时候，他饿了。

chapters.en: Seeing a fig tree by the road, he went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. Then he said to it, “May you never bear fruit again!” Immediately the tree withered.
chapters.zh: 看见路旁有一棵无花果树，就走到跟前，在树上找不着什么，不过有叶子。就对树说，从今以后，你永不结果子。那无花果树就立刻枯干了。

chapters.en: When the disciples saw this, they were amazed. “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?” they asked.
chapters.zh: 门徒看见了，便希奇说，无花果树怎么立刻枯干了呢？

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, not only can you do what was done to the fig tree, but also you can say to this mountain, ‘Go, throw yourself into the sea,’ and it will be done.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，我实在告诉你们，你们若有信心，不疑惑，不但能行无花果树上所行的事，就是对这座山说，你挪开此地，投在海里，也必成就。

chapters.en: If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.”
chapters.zh: 你们祷告，无论求什么，只要信，就必得着。

chapters.en: Jesus entered the temple courts, and, while he was teaching, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him. “By what authority are you doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave you this authority?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣进了殿，正教训人的时候，祭司长和民间的长老来问他说，你仗着什么权柄作这些事？给你这权柄的是谁呢？

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “I will also ask you one question. If you answer me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，我也要问你们一句话，你们若告诉我，我就告诉你们我仗着什么权柄作这些事。

chapters.en: John’s baptism—where did it come from? Was it from heaven, or of human origin?”They discussed it among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask, ‘Then why didn’t you believe him?’
chapters.zh: 约翰的洗礼是从哪里来的？是从天上来的？是从人间来的呢？他们彼此商议说，我们若说从天上来，他必对我们说，这样，你们为什么不信他呢？

chapters.en: But if we say, ‘Of human origin’—we are afraid of the people, for they all hold that John was a prophet.”
chapters.zh: 若说从人间来，我们又怕百姓。因为他们都以约翰为先知。

chapters.en: So they answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Then he said, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
chapters.zh: 于是回答耶稣说，我们不知道。耶稣说，我也不告诉你们我仗着什么权柄作这些事。

chapters.en: “What do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’
chapters.zh: 又说，一个人有两个儿子，他来对大儿子说，我儿，你今天到葡萄园里去作工。

chapters.en: “ ‘I will not,’ he answered, but later he changed his mind and went.
chapters.zh: 他回答说，我不去。以后自己懊悔就去了。

chapters.en: “Then the father went to the other son and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I will, sir,’ but he did not go.
chapters.zh: 又来对小儿子也是这样说，他回答说，父阿，我去。他却不去。

chapters.en: “Which of the two did what his father wanted?”“The first,” they answered. Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God ahead of you.
chapters.zh: 你们想这两个儿子，是那一个遵行父命呢？他们说，大儿子。耶稣说，我实在告诉你们，税吏和娼妓，倒比你们先进神的国。

chapters.en: For John came to you to show you the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him.
chapters.zh: 因为约翰遵着义路到你们这里来，你们却不信他。税吏和娼妓倒信他。你们看见了，后来还是不懊悔去信他。

chapters.en: “Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it and built a watchtower. Then he rented the vineyard to some farmers and moved to another place.
chapters.zh: 你们再听一个比喻。有个家主，栽了一个葡萄园，周围圈上篱笆，里面挖了一个压酒池，盖了一座楼，租给园户，就往外国去了。

chapters.en: When the harvest time approached, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his fruit.
chapters.zh: 收果子的时候近了，就打发仆人，到园户那里去收果子。

chapters.en: “The tenants seized his servants; they beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.
chapters.zh: 园户拿住仆人。打了一个，杀了一个，用石头打死一个。

chapters.en: Then he sent other servants to them, more than the first time, and the tenants treated them the same way.
chapters.zh: 主人又打发别的仆人去，比先前更多。园户还是照样待他们。

chapters.en: Last of all, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
chapters.zh: 后来打发他的儿子到他们那里去，意思说，他们必尊敬我的儿子。

chapters.en: “But when the tenants saw the son, they said to each other, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him and take his inheritance.’
chapters.zh: 不料，园户看见他儿子，就彼此说，这是承受产业的。来吧，我们杀他，占他的产业。

chapters.en: So they took him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
chapters.zh: 他们就拿住他，推出葡萄园外杀了。

chapters.en: “Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?”
chapters.zh: 园主来的时候，要怎样处治这些园户呢？

chapters.en: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and he will rent the vineyard to other tenants, who will give him his share of the crop at harvest time.”
chapters.zh: 他们说，要下毒手除灭那些恶人，将葡萄园另租给那按着时候交果子的园户。

chapters.en: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: “ ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; the Lord has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，经上写着，匠人所弃的石头，已作了房角的头块石头。这是主所作的，在我们眼中看为希奇。这经你们没有念过吗？

chapters.en: “Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.
chapters.zh: 所以我告诉你们，神的国，必从你们夺去。赐给那能结果子的百姓。

chapters.en: Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; anyone on whom it falls will be crushed.”
chapters.zh: 谁掉在这石头上，必要跌碎。这石头掉在谁的身上，就要把谁砸得稀烂。

chapters.en: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard Jesus’ parables, they knew he was talking about them.
chapters.zh: 祭司长和法利赛人，听见他的比喻，就看出他是指着他们说的。

chapters.en: They looked for a way to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowd because the people held that he was a prophet.
chapters.zh: 他们想要捉拿他，只是怕众人，因为众人以他为先知。

chapters.en: Jesus spoke to them again in parables, saying:
chapters.zh: 耶稣又用比喻对他们说，

chapters.en: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
chapters.zh: 天国好比一个王，为他儿子摆设娶亲的筵席。

chapters.en: He sent his servants to those who had been invited to the banquet to tell them to come, but they refused to come.
chapters.zh: 就打发仆人去请那些被召的人来赴席。他们却不肯来。

chapters.en: “Then he sent some more servants and said, ‘Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner: My oxen and fattened cattle have been butchered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.’
chapters.zh: 王又打发别的仆人说，你们告诉那被召的人，我的筵席已经预备好了，牛和肥畜已经宰了，各样都齐备。请你们来赴席。

chapters.en: “But they paid no attention and went off—one to his field, another to his business.
chapters.zh: 那些人不理就走了。一个到自己田里去。一个作买卖去。

chapters.en: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them and killed them.
chapters.zh: 其余的拿住仆人，凌辱他们，把他们杀了。

chapters.en: The king was enraged. He sent his army and destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
chapters.zh: 王就大怒，发兵除灭那些凶手，烧毁他们的城。

chapters.en: “Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited did not deserve to come.
chapters.zh: 于是对仆人说，喜筵已经齐备，只是所召的人不配。

chapters.en: So go to the street corners and invite to the banquet anyone you find.’
chapters.zh: 所以你们要往岔路口上去，凡遇见的，都召来赴席。

chapters.en: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered all the people they could find, the bad as well as the good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
chapters.zh: 那些仆人就出去到大路上，凡遇见的，不论善恶都召聚了来。筵席上就坐满了客。

chapters.en: “But when the king came in to see the guests, he noticed a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes.
chapters.zh: 王进来观看宾客，见那里有一个没有穿礼服的。

chapters.en: He asked, ‘How did you get in here without wedding clothes, friend?’ The man was speechless.
chapters.zh: 就对他说，朋友，你到这里来，怎么不穿礼服呢？那人无言可答。

chapters.en: “Then the king told the attendants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him outside, into the darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
chapters.zh: 于是王对使唤的人说，捆起他的手脚来，把他丢在外边的黑暗里。在那里必要哀哭切齿了。

chapters.en: “For many are invited, but few are chosen.”
chapters.zh: 因为被召的人多，选上的人少。

chapters.en: Then the Pharisees went out and laid plans to trap him in his words.
chapters.zh: 当时，法利赛人出去商议，怎样就着耶稣的话陷害他。

chapters.en: They sent their disciples to him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that you are a man of integrity and that you teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You aren’t swayed by others, because you pay no attention to who they are.
chapters.zh: 就打发他们的门徒，同希律党的人，去见耶稣说，夫子，我们知道你是诚实人，并且诚诚实实传神的道，什么人你都不徇情面，因为你不看人的外貌。

chapters.en: Tell us then, what is your opinion? Is it right to pay the imperial tax to Caesar or not?”
chapters.zh: 请告诉我们，你的意见如何。纳税给该撒，可以不可以。

chapters.en: But Jesus, knowing their evil intent, said, “You hypocrites, why are you trying to trap me?
chapters.zh: 耶稣看出他们的恶意，就说，假冒为善的人哪，为什么试探我。

chapters.en: Show me the coin used for paying the tax.” They brought him a denarius,
chapters.zh: 拿一个上税的钱给我看。他们就拿一个银钱来给他。

chapters.en: and he asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，这像和这号是谁的。

chapters.en: “Caesar’s,” they replied. Then he said to them, “So give back to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
chapters.zh: 他们说，是该撒的。耶稣说，这样，该撒的物当归给该撒，神的物当归给神。

chapters.en: When they heard this, they were amazed. So they left him and went away.
chapters.zh: 他们听见就希奇，离开他走了。

chapters.en: That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him with a question.
chapters.zh: 撒都该人常说没有复活的事。那天，他们来问耶稣说，

chapters.en: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses told us that if a man dies without having children, his brother must marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.
chapters.zh: 夫子，摩西说，人若死了，没有孩子，他兄弟当娶他的妻，为哥哥生子立后。

chapters.en: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died, and since he had no children, he left his wife to his brother.
chapters.zh: 从前在我们这里，有弟兄七人。第一个娶了妻，死了，没有孩子，撇下妻子给兄弟。

chapters.en: The same thing happened to the second and third brother, right on down to the seventh.
chapters.zh: 第二第三直到第七个，都是如此。

chapters.en: Finally, the woman died.
chapters.zh: 末后，妇人也死了。

chapters.en: Now then, at the resurrection, whose wife will she be of the seven, since all of them were married to her?”
chapters.zh: 这样当复活的时候，她是七个人中，那一个的妻子呢？因为他们都娶过她。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “You are in error because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，你们错了。因为不明白圣经，也不晓得神的大能。

chapters.en: At the resurrection people will neither marry nor be given in marriage; they will be like the angels in heaven.
chapters.zh: 当复活的时候，人也不娶也不嫁，乃像天上的使者一样。

chapters.en: But about the resurrection of the dead—have you not read what God said to you,
chapters.zh: 论到死人复活，神在经上向你们所说的，你们没有念过吗？

chapters.en: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead but of the living.”
chapters.zh: 他说，我是亚伯拉罕的神，以撒的神，雅各的神。神不是死人的神，乃是活人的神。

chapters.en: When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at his teaching.
chapters.zh: 众人听见这话，就希奇他的教训。

chapters.en: Hearing that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, the Pharisees got together.
chapters.zh: 法利赛人听见耶稣堵住了撒都该人的口，他们就聚集。

chapters.en: One of them, an expert in the law, tested him with this question:
chapters.zh: 内中有一个人是律法师，要试探耶稣，就问他说，

chapters.en: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the Law?”
chapters.zh: 夫子，律法上的诫命，那一条是最大的呢？

chapters.en: Jesus replied: “ ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他说，你要尽心，尽性，尽意，爱主你的神。

chapters.en: This is the first and greatest commandment.
chapters.zh: 这是诫命中的第一，且是最大的。

chapters.en: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
chapters.zh: 其次也相仿，就是要爱人如己。

chapters.en: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”
chapters.zh: 这两条诫命，是律法和先知一切道理的总纲。

chapters.en: While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them,
chapters.zh: 法利赛人聚集的时候，耶稣问他们说，

chapters.en: “What do you think about the Messiah? Whose son is he?”“The son of David,” they replied.
chapters.zh: 论到基督，你们的意见如何？他是谁的子孙呢？他们回答说，是大卫的子孙。

chapters.en: He said to them, “How is it then that David, speaking by the Spirit, calls him ‘Lord’? For he says,
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，这样，大卫被圣灵感动，怎么还称他为主。说，

chapters.en: “ ‘The Lord said to my Lord:“Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.” ’
chapters.zh: 主对我主说，你坐在我的右边，等我把你仇敌，放在你的脚下。

chapters.en: If then David calls him ‘Lord,’ how can he be his son?”
chapters.zh: 大卫既称他为主，他怎么又是大卫的子孙呢？

chapters.en: No one could say a word in reply, and from that day on no one dared to ask him any more questions.
chapters.zh: 他们没有一个人能回答一言。从那日以后，也没有人敢再问他什么。

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to the crowds and to his disciples:
chapters.zh: 那时，耶稣对众人和门徒讲论，

chapters.en: “The teachers of the law and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
chapters.zh: 说，文士和法利赛人，坐在摩西的位上。

chapters.en: So you must be careful to do everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.
chapters.zh: 凡他们所吩咐你们的，你们都要谨守，遵行。但不要效法他们的行为。因为他们能说不能行。

chapters.en: They tie up heavy, cumbersome loads and put them on other people’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
chapters.zh: 他们把难担的重担，捆起来搁在人的肩上。但自己一个指头也不肯动。

chapters.en: “Everything they do is done for people to see: They make their phylacterieswide and the tassels on their garments long;
chapters.zh: 他们一切所作的事，都是要叫人看见。所以将佩戴的经文做宽了，衣裳的繸子做长了

chapters.en: they love the place of honor at banquets and the most important seats in the synagogues;
chapters.zh: 喜爱筵席上的首座，会堂里的高位。

chapters.en: they love to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces and to be called ‘Rabbi’ by others.
chapters.zh: 又喜爱人在街市上问他安，称呼他拉比。（拉比就是夫子）

chapters.en: “But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
chapters.zh: 但你们不要受拉比的称呼。因为只有一位是你们的夫子。你们都是弟兄。

chapters.en: And do not call anyone on earth ‘father,’ for you have one Father, and he is in heaven.
chapters.zh: 也不要称呼地上的人为父。因为只有一位是你们的父，就是在天上的父。

chapters.en: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Messiah.
chapters.zh: 也不要受师尊的称呼。因为只有一位是你们的师尊，就是基督。

chapters.en: The greatest among you will be your servant.
chapters.zh: 你们中间谁为大，谁就要作你们的用人。

chapters.en: For those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.
chapters.zh: 凡自高的必降为卑，自卑的必升为高。

chapters.en: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the door of the kingdom of heaven in people’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let those enter who are trying to.
chapters.zh: 你们这假冒为善的文士和法利赛人有祸了。因为你们正当人前把天国的门关了。自己不进去，正要进去的人，你们也不容他们进去。（有古卷在此有

chapters.en: Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You devour windows' houses and for a show make lengthy prayers. Therefore you will be punished more severely.
chapters.zh: 你们这假冒为善的文士和法利赛人有祸了，因为你们侵吞寡妇的家产，假意作很长的祷告，所以要受更重的刑罚）

chapters.en: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You travel over land and sea to win a single convert, and when you have succeeded, you make them twice as much a child of hell as you are.
chapters.zh: 你们这假冒为善的文士和法利赛人有祸了。因为你们走遍洋海陆地，勾引一个人入教。既入了教，却使他作地狱之子，比你们还加倍。

chapters.en: “Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but anyone who swears by the gold of the temple is bound by that oath.’
chapters.zh: 你们这瞎眼领路的有祸了。你们说，凡指着殿起誓的，这算不得什么。只是凡指着殿中金子起誓的，他就该谨守。

chapters.en: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes the gold sacred?
chapters.zh: 你们这无知瞎眼的人哪，什么是大的？是金子呢？还是叫金子成圣的殿呢？

chapters.en: You also say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but anyone who swears by the gift on the altar is bound by that oath.’
chapters.zh: 你们又说，凡指着坛起誓的，这算不得什么。只是凡指着坛上礼物起誓的，他就该谨守。

chapters.en: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes the gift sacred?
chapters.zh: 你们这瞎眼的人哪，什么是大的？是礼物呢？还是叫礼物成圣的坛呢？

chapters.en: Therefore, anyone who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
chapters.zh: 所以人指着坛起誓，就是指着坛和坛上一切所有的起誓。

chapters.en: And anyone who swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it.
chapters.zh: 人指着殿起誓，就是指着殿和那住在殿里的起誓。

chapters.en: And anyone who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the one who sits on it.
chapters.zh: 人指着天起誓，就是指着神的宝座和那坐在上面的起誓。

chapters.en: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You give a tenth of your spices—mint, dill and cumin. But you have neglected the more important matters of the law—justice, mercy and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.
chapters.zh: 你们这假冒为善的文士和法利赛人有祸了。因为你们将薄荷，茴香，芹菜，献上十分之一。那律法上更重的事，就是公义，怜悯，信实，反倒不行了。这更重的是你们当行的；那也是不可不行的。

chapters.en: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.
chapters.zh: 你们这瞎眼领路的，蠓虫你们就滤出来，骆驼你们倒吞下去。

chapters.en: “Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
