chapters.en: If someone who promotes peace is there, your peace will rest on them; if not, it will return to you.
chapters.zh: 那里若有当得平安的人，当得平安的人原文作平安之子你们所求的平安就必临到那家，不然，就归与你们了。

chapters.en: Stay there, eating and drinking whatever they give you, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move around from house to house.
chapters.zh: 你们要住在那家，吃喝他们所供给的。因为工人得工价，是应当的。不要从这家搬到那家。

chapters.en: “When you enter a town and are welcomed, eat what is offered to you.
chapters.zh: 无论进那一城，人若接待你们，给你们摆上什么，你们就吃什么。

chapters.en: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’
chapters.zh: 要医治那城里的病人，对他们说，神的国临近你们了。

chapters.en: But when you enter a town and are not welcomed, go into its streets and say,
chapters.zh: 无论进那一城，人若不接待你们，你们就到街上去，

chapters.en: ‘Even the dust of your town we wipe from our feet as a warning to you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God has come near.’
chapters.zh: 说，就是你们城里的尘土，粘在我们的脚上，我们也当着你们擦去。虽然如此，你们该知道神的国临近了。

chapters.en: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，当审判的日子，所多玛所受的，比那城还容易受呢。

chapters.en: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
chapters.zh: 哥拉汛哪，你有祸了。伯赛大阿，你有祸了。因为在你们中间所行的异能，若行在推罗西顿，他们早已披麻蒙灰坐在地上悔改了。

chapters.en: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
chapters.zh: 当审判的日子，推罗西顿所受的，比你们还容易受呢。

chapters.en: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted to the heavens? No, you will go down to Hades.
chapters.zh: 迦百农阿，你已经升到天上。（或作你将要升到天上吗？）将来必推下阴间。

chapters.en: “Whoever listens to you listens to me; whoever rejects you rejects me; but whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”
chapters.zh: 又对门徒说，听从你们的，就是听从我，弃绝你们的，就是弃绝我，弃绝我的，就是弃绝那差我来的。

chapters.en: The seventy-two returned with joy and said, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name.”
chapters.zh: 那七十个人欢欢喜喜地回来说，主阿，因你的名，就是鬼也服了我们。

chapters.en: He replied, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说，我曾看见撒但从天上坠落，像闪电一样。

chapters.en: I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions and to overcome all the power of the enemy; nothing will harm you.
chapters.zh: 我已经给你们权柄，可以践踏蛇和蝎子，又胜过仇敌一切的能力，断没有什么能害你们。

chapters.en: However, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
chapters.zh: 然而不要因鬼服了你们就欢喜，要因你们的名记录在天上欢喜。

chapters.en: At that time Jesus, full of joy through the Holy Spirit, said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this is what you were pleased to do.
chapters.zh: 正当那时，耶稣被圣灵感动就欢乐，说，父阿，天地的主，我感谢你，因为你将这些事，向聪明通达人就藏起来，向婴孩就显出来。父阿，是的，因为你的美意本是如此。

chapters.en: “All things have been committed to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.”
chapters.zh: 一切所有的，都是我父交付我的。除了父，没有人知道子是谁。除了子和子所愿意指示的，没有人知道父是谁。

chapters.en: Then he turned to his disciples and said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
chapters.zh: 耶稣转身暗暗地对门徒说。看见你们所看见的，那眼睛就有福了。

chapters.en: For I tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，从前有许多先知和君王，要看你们所看的，却没有看见。要听你们所听的，却没有听见。

chapters.en: On one occasion an expert in the law stood up to test Jesus. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
chapters.zh: 有一个律法师，起来试探耶稣说，夫子，我该作什么才可以承受永生。

chapters.en: “What is written in the Law?” he replied. “How do you read it?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他说，律法上写的是什么？你念的是怎样呢？

chapters.en: He answered, “ ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ ; and, ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
chapters.zh: 他回答说，你要尽心，尽性，尽力，尽意，爱主你的神。又要爱邻舍如同自己。

chapters.en: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus replied. “Do this and you will live.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你回答的是。你这样行，就必得永生。

chapters.en: But he wanted to justify himself, so he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
chapters.zh: 那人要显明自己有理，就对耶稣说，谁是我的邻舍呢？

chapters.en: In reply Jesus said: “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, when he was attacked by robbers. They stripped him of his clothes, beat him and went away, leaving him half dead.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，有一个人从耶路撒冷下耶利哥去，落在强盗手中，他们剥去他的衣裳，把他打个半死，就丢下他走了。

chapters.en: A priest happened to be going down the same road, and when he saw the man, he passed by on the other side.
chapters.zh: 偶然有一个祭司，从这条路下来。看见他就从那边过去了。

chapters.en: So too, a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.
chapters.zh: 又有一个利未人，来到这地方，看见他，也照样从那边过去了。

chapters.en: But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came where the man was; and when he saw him, he took pity on him.
chapters.zh: 惟有一个撒玛利亚人，行路来到那里。看见他就动了慈心，

chapters.en: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put the man on his own donkey, brought him to an inn and took care of him.
chapters.zh: 上前用油和酒倒在他的伤处，包裹好了，扶他骑上自己的牲口，带到店里去照应他。

chapters.en: The next day he took out two denariiand gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Look after him,’ he said, ‘and when I return, I will reimburse you for any extra expense you may have.’
chapters.zh: 第二天拿出二钱银子来，交给店主说，你且照应他。此外所费用的，我回来必还你。

chapters.en: “Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”
chapters.zh: 你想这三个人，那一个是落在强盗手中的邻舍呢？

chapters.en: The expert in the law replied, “The one who had mercy on him.” Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”
chapters.zh: 他说，是怜悯他的。耶稣说，你去照样行吧。

chapters.en: As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him.
chapters.zh: 他们走路的时候，耶稣进了一个村庄。有一个女人名叫马大，接他到自己家里。

chapters.en: She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said.
chapters.zh: 她有一个妹子名叫马利亚，在耶稣脚前坐着听他的道。

chapters.en: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!”
chapters.zh: 马大伺候的事多，心里忙乱，就进前来说，主阿，我的妹子留下我一个人伺候，你不在意吗？请吩咐她来帮助我。

chapters.en: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things,
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，马大，马大，你为许多的事，思虑烦扰。

chapters.en: but few things are needed—or indeed only one.Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.”
chapters.zh: 但是不可少的只有一件。马利亚已经选择那上好的福分，是不能夺去的。

chapters.en: One day Jesus was praying in a certain place. When he finished, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣在一个地方祷告。祷告完了，有个门徒对他说，求主教导我们祷告，像约翰教导他的门徒。

chapters.en: He said to them, “When you pray, say: “ ‘Father,hallowed be your name, your kingdom come.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们祷告的时候，要说，我们在天上的父，有古卷只作父阿愿人都尊你的名为圣。愿你的国降临。愿你的旨意行在地上，如同行在天上。有古卷无愿你的旨意云云

chapters.en: Give us each day our daily bread.
chapters.zh: 我们日用的饮食，天天赐给我们。

chapters.en: Forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us.And lead us not into temptation.’ ”
chapters.zh: 赦免我们的罪，因为我们也赦免凡亏欠我们的人。不叫我们遇见试探。救我们脱离凶恶。有古卷无末句

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to them, “Suppose you have a friend, and you go to him at midnight and say, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread;
chapters.zh: 耶稣又说，你们中间谁有一个朋友，半夜到他那里去说，朋友，请借给我三个饼。

chapters.en: a friend of mine on a journey has come to me, and I have no food to offer him.’
chapters.zh: 因为我有一个朋友行路，来到我这里，我没有什么给他摆上。

chapters.en: And suppose the one inside answers, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is already locked, and my children and I are in bed. I can’t get up and give you anything.’
chapters.zh: 那人在里面回答说，不要搅扰我。门已经关闭，孩子们也同我在床上了。我不能起来给你。

chapters.en: I tell you, even though he will not get up and give you the bread because of friendship, yet because of your shameless audacityhe will surely get up and give you as much as you need.
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，虽不因他是朋友起来给他，但因他情词迫切的直求，就必起来照他所需用的给他。

chapters.en: “So I say to you: Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you.
chapters.zh: 我又告诉你们，你们祈求就给你们。寻找就寻见。叩门就给你们开门。

chapters.en: For everyone who asks receives; the one who seeks finds; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
chapters.zh: 因为凡祈求的就得着。寻找的就寻见。叩门的就给他开门。

chapters.en: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks fora fish, will give him a snake instead?
chapters.zh: 你们中间作父亲的，谁有儿子求饼，反给他石头呢？求鱼，反拿蛇当鱼给他呢？

chapters.en: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
chapters.zh: 求鸡蛋，反给他蝎子呢？

chapters.en: If you then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!”
chapters.zh: 你们虽然不好，尚且知道拿好东西给儿女。何况天父，岂不更将圣灵给求他的人吗？

chapters.en: Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. When the demon left, the man who had been mute spoke, and the crowd was amazed.
chapters.zh: 耶稣赶出一个叫人哑吧的鬼。鬼出去了，哑吧就说出话来众人都希奇。

chapters.en: But some of them said, “By Beelzebul, the prince of demons, he is driving out demons.”
chapters.zh: 内中却有人说，他是靠着鬼王别西卜赶鬼。

chapters.en: Others tested him by asking for a sign from heaven.
chapters.zh: 又有人试探耶稣，向他求从天上来的神迹。

chapters.en: Jesus knew their thoughts and said to them: “Any kingdom divided against itself will be ruined, and a house divided against itself will fall.
chapters.zh: 他晓得他们的意念，便对他们说，凡一国自相分争，就成为荒场。凡一家自相分争，就必败落。

chapters.en: If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? I say this because you claim that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
chapters.zh: 若撒但自相分争，他的国怎能站得住呢？因为你们说我是靠着别西卜赶鬼。

chapters.en: Now if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your followers drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
chapters.zh: 我若靠着别西卜赶鬼，你们的子弟赶鬼，又靠着谁呢？这样，他们就要断定你们的是非。

chapters.en: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
chapters.zh: 我若靠着神的能力赶鬼，这就是神的国临到你们了。

chapters.en: “When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own house, his possessions are safe.
chapters.zh: 壮士披挂整齐，看守自己的住宅，他所有的都平安无事。

chapters.en: But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted and divides up his plunder.
chapters.zh: 但有一个比他更壮的来，胜过他，就夺去他所倚靠的盔甲兵器，又分了他的赃。

chapters.en: “Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
chapters.zh: 不与我相合的，就是敌我的。不同我收聚的，就是分散的。

chapters.en: “When an impure spirit comes out of a person, it goes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’
chapters.zh: 污鬼离了人身，就在无水之地，过来过去，寻求安歇之处。既寻不着，便说，我要回到我所出来的屋里去。

chapters.en: When it arrives, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.
chapters.zh: 到了，就看见里面打扫干净，修饰好了。

chapters.en: Then it goes and takes seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and live there. And the final condition of that person is worse than the first.”
chapters.zh: 便去另带了七个比自己更恶的鬼来，都进去住在那里。那人末后的景况，比先前更不好了。

chapters.en: As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd called out, “Blessed is the mother who gave you birth and nursed you.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣正说这话的时候，众人中间，有一个女人大声说，怀你胎的和乳养你的有福了。

chapters.en: He replied, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，是却还不如听神之道而遵守的人有福。

chapters.en: As the crowds increased, Jesus said, “This is a wicked generation. It asks for a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.
chapters.zh: 当众人聚集的时候，耶稣开讲说，这世代是一个邪恶的世代。他们求看神迹，除了约拿的神迹以外，再没有神迹给他们看。

chapters.en: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so also will the Son of Man be to this generation.
chapters.zh: 约拿怎样为尼尼微人成了神迹，人子也要照样为这世代的人成了神迹。

chapters.en: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the people of this generation and condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to listen to Solomon’s wisdom; and now something greater than Solomon is here.
chapters.zh: 当审判的时候，南方的女王，要起来定这世代的罪。因为她从地极而来，要听所罗门的智慧话。看哪，在这里有一人比所罗门更大。

chapters.en: The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and now something greater than Jonah is here.
chapters.zh: 当审判的时候，尼尼微人，要起来定这世代的罪。因为尼尼微人听了约拿所传的，就悔改了。看哪，在这里有一人比约拿更大。

chapters.en: “No one lights a lamp and puts it in a place where it will be hidden, or under a bowl. Instead they put it on its stand, so that those who come in may see the light.
chapters.zh: 没有人点灯放在地窨子里，或是斗底下，总是放在灯台上，使进来的人得见亮光。

chapters.en: Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are healthy,your whole body also is full of light. But when they are unhealthy,your body also is full of darkness.
chapters.zh: 你眼睛就是身上的灯，你的眼睛若了亮，全身就光明。眼睛若昏花，全身就黑暗。

chapters.en: See to it, then, that the light within you is not darkness.
chapters.zh: 所以你要省察，恐怕你里头的光，或者黑暗了。

chapters.en: Therefore, if your whole body is full of light, and no part of it dark, it will be just as full of light as when a lamp shines its light on you.”
chapters.zh: 若是你全身光明，毫无黑暗，就必全然光明，如同灯的明光照亮你。

chapters.en: When Jesus had finished speaking, a Pharisee invited him to eat with him; so he went in and reclined at the table.
chapters.zh: 说话的时候，有一个法利赛人请耶稣同他吃饭。耶稣就进去坐席。

chapters.en: But the Pharisee was surprised when he noticed that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.
chapters.zh: 这法利赛人看见耶稣饭前不洗手，便诧异。

chapters.en: Then the Lord said to him, “Now then, you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
chapters.zh: 主对他说，如今你们法利赛人洗净杯盘的外面。你们里面却满了勒索和邪恶。

chapters.en: You foolish people! Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?
chapters.zh: 无知的人哪，造外面的，不也造里面吗？

chapters.en: But now as for what is inside you—be generous to the poor, and everything will be clean for you.
chapters.zh: 只要把里面的施舍给人，凡物于你们就都洁净了。

chapters.en: “Woe to you Pharisees, because you give God a tenth of your mint, rue and all other kinds of garden herbs, but you neglect justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without leaving the former undone.
chapters.zh: 你们法利赛人有祸了。因为你们将薄荷芸香，并各样菜蔬，献上十分之一，那公义和爱神的事，反倒不行了。这原是你们当行的，那也是不可不行的。

chapters.en: “Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the most important seats in the synagogues and respectful greetings in the marketplaces.
chapters.zh: 你们法利赛人有祸了。因为你们喜爱会堂里的首位，又喜爱人在街市上问你们的安。

chapters.en: “Woe to you, because you are like unmarked graves, which people walk over without knowing it.”
chapters.zh: 你们有祸了。因为你们如同不显露的坟墓，走在上面的人并不知道。

chapters.en: One of the experts in the law answered him, “Teacher, when you say these things, you insult us also.”
chapters.zh: 律法师中有一个回答耶稣说，夫子，你这样说，也把我们糟蹋了。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “And you experts in the law, woe to you, because you load people down with burdens they can hardly carry, and you yourselves will not lift one finger to help them.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们律法师也有祸了。因为你们把难担的担子，放在人身上，自己一个指头却不肯动。

chapters.en: “Woe to you, because you build tombs for the prophets, and it was your ancestors who killed them.
chapters.zh: 你们有祸了。因为你们修造先知的坟墓，那先知正是你们的祖宗所杀的。

chapters.en: So you testify that you approve of what your ancestors did; they killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
chapters.zh: 可见你们祖宗所作的事，你们又证明又喜欢。因为他们杀了先知，你们修造先知的坟墓。

chapters.en: Because of this, God in his wisdom said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles, some of whom they will kill and others they will persecute.’
chapters.zh: 所以神用智慧曾说，用智慧或作的智者我要差遣先知和使徒，到他们那里去。有的他们要杀害，有的他们要逼迫。

chapters.en: Therefore this generation will be held responsible for the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the beginning of the world,
chapters.zh: 使创世以来，所流众先知血的罪，都要问在这世代的人身上。

chapters.en: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be held responsible for it all.
chapters.zh: 就是从亚伯的血起，直到被杀在坛和殿中间撒迦利亚的血为止。我实在告诉你们，这都要问在这世代的人身上。

chapters.en: “Woe to you experts in the law, because you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering.”
chapters.zh: 你们律法师有祸了。因为你们把知识的钥匙夺了去。自己不进去，正要进去的人，你们也阻挡他们。

chapters.en: When Jesus went outside, the Pharisees and the teachers of the law began to oppose him fiercely and to besiege him with questions,
chapters.zh: 耶稣从那里出来，文士和法利赛人，就极力地催逼他，引动他多说话。

chapters.en: waiting to catch him in something he might say.
chapters.zh: 私下窥听，要拿他的话柄。

chapters.en: Meanwhile, when a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling on one another, Jesus began to speak first to his disciples, saying: “Beon your guard against the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
chapters.zh: 这时，有几万人聚集，甚至彼此践踏，耶稣开讲，先对门徒说，你们要防备法利赛人的酵，就是假冒为善。

chapters.en: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, or hidden that will not be made known.
chapters.zh: 掩盖的事，没有不露出来的。隐藏的事，没有不被人知道的。

chapters.en: What you have said in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the roofs.
chapters.zh: 因此你们在暗中所说的，将要在明处被人听见。在内室附耳所说的，将要在房上被人宣扬。

chapters.en: “I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
chapters.zh: 我的朋友，我对你们说，那杀身体以后，不能再作什么的，不要怕他们。

chapters.en: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear him who, after your body has been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
chapters.zh: 我要指示你们当怕的是谁。当怕那杀了以后，又有权柄丢在地狱里的。我实在告诉你们，正要怕他。

chapters.en: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
chapters.zh: 五个麻雀，不是卖二分银子吗？但在神面前，一个也不忘记。

chapters.en: Indeed, the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Don’t be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
chapters.zh: 就是你们的头发也都被数过了。不要惧怕，你们比许多麻雀还贵重。

chapters.en: “I tell you, whoever publicly acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
chapters.zh: 我又告诉你们，凡在人面前认我的，人子在神的使者面前也必认他。

chapters.en: But whoever disowns me before others will be disowned before the angels of God.
chapters.zh: 在人面前不认我的，人子在神的使者面前也必不认他。

chapters.en: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but anyone who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 凡说话干犯人子的，还可得赦免，惟独亵渎圣灵的，总不得赦免。

chapters.en: “When you are brought before synagogues, rulers and authorities, do not worry about how you will defend yourselves or what you will say,
chapters.zh: 人带你们到会堂，并官府，和有权柄的人面前，不要思虑怎么分诉，说什么话。

chapters.en: for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that time what you should say.”
chapters.zh: 因为正在那时候，圣灵要指教你们当说的话。

chapters.en: Someone in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
chapters.zh: 众人中有一个人对耶稣说，夫子，请你吩咐我的兄长和我分开家业。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed me a judge or an arbiter between you?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你这个人，谁立我作你们断事的官，给你们分家业呢？

chapters.en: Then he said to them, “Watch out! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; life does not consist in an abundance of possessions.”
chapters.zh: 于是对众人说，你们要谨慎自守，免去一切的贪心。因为人的生命，不在乎家道丰富。

chapters.en: And he told them this parable: “The ground of a certain rich man yielded an abundant harvest.
chapters.zh: 就用比喻对他们说，有一个财主，田产丰盛。

chapters.en: He thought to himself, ‘What shall I do? I have no place to store my crops.’
chapters.zh: 自己心里思想说，我的出产没有地方收藏，怎么办呢？

chapters.en: “Then he said, ‘This is what I’ll do. I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones, and there I will store my surplus grain.
chapters.zh: 又说，我要这么办。要把我的仓房拆了，另盖更大的。在那里好收藏我一切的粮食和财物。

chapters.en: And I’ll say to myself, “You have plenty of grain laid up for many years. Take life easy; eat, drink and be merry.” ’
chapters.zh: 然后要对我的灵魂说，灵魂哪，你有许多财物积存，可作多年的费用。只管安安逸逸的吃喝快乐吧。

chapters.en: “But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be demanded from you. Then who will get what you have prepared for yourself?’
chapters.zh: 神却对他说，无知的人哪，今夜必要你的灵魂。你所预备的，要归谁呢？

chapters.en: “This is how it will be with whoever stores up things for themselves but is not rich toward God.”
chapters.zh: 凡为自己积财，在神面前却不富足的，也是这样。

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to his disciples: “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat; or about your body, what you will wear.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又对门徒说，所以我告诉你们，不要为生命忧虑吃什么。为身体忧虑穿什么。

chapters.en: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.
chapters.zh: 因为生命胜于饮食，身体胜于衣裳。

chapters.en: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storeroom or barn; yet God feeds them. And how much more valuable you are than birds!
chapters.zh: 你想乌鸦，也不种，也不收。又没有仓，又没有库，神尚且养活它。你们比飞鸟是何等的贵重呢。

chapters.en: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to your life?
chapters.zh: 你们那一个能用思虑，使寿数多加一刻呢？（或作使身量多加一肘呢？）

chapters.en: Since you cannot do this very little thing, why do you worry about the rest?
chapters.zh: 这最小的事，你们尚且不能作，为什么还忧虑其余的事呢？

chapters.en: “Consider how the wild flowers grow. They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his splendor was dressed like one of these.
chapters.zh: 你想百合花，怎么长起来。它也不劳苦，也不纺线。然而我告诉你们，就是所罗门极荣华的时候，他所穿戴的，还不如这花一朵呢。

chapters.en: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today, and tomorrow is thrown into the fire, how much more will he clothe you—you of little faith!
chapters.zh: 你们这小信的人哪，野地里的草，今天还在，明天就丢在炉里，神还给它这样的妆饰，何况你们呢。

chapters.en: And do not set your heart on what you will eat or drink; do not worry about it.
chapters.zh: 你们不要求吃什么，喝什么，也不要挂心。

chapters.en: For the pagan world runs after all such things, and your Father knows that you need them.
chapters.zh: 这都是外邦人所求的，你们必须用这些东西，你们的父是知道的。

chapters.en: But seek his kingdom, and these things will be given to you as well.
chapters.zh: 你们只要求他的国，这些东西就必加给你们了。

chapters.en: “Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.
chapters.zh: 你们这小群，不要惧怕，因为你们的父，乐意把国赐给你们。

chapters.en: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide purses for yourselves that will not wear out, a treasure in heaven that will never fail, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
chapters.zh: 你们要变卖所有的，周济人。为自己预备永不坏的钱囊，用不尽的财宝在天上，就是贼不能近，虫不能蛀的地方。

chapters.en: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
chapters.zh: 因为你们的财宝在哪里，你们的心也在哪里。

chapters.en: “Be dressed ready for service and keep your lamps burning,
chapters.zh: 你们腰里要束上带，灯也要点着。

chapters.en: like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks they can immediately open the door for him.
chapters.zh: 自己好像仆人等候主人，从婚姻的筵席上回来。他来到叩门，就立刻给他开门。

chapters.en: It will be good for those servants whose master finds them watching when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve, will have them recline at the table and will come and wait on them.
chapters.zh: 主人来了，看见仆人儆醒，那仆人就有福了。我实在告诉你们，主人必叫他们坐席，自己束上带，进前伺候他们。

chapters.en: It will be good for those servants whose master finds them ready, even if he comes in the middle of the night or toward daybreak.
chapters.zh: 或是二更天来，或是三更天来，看见仆人这样，那仆人就有福了。

chapters.en: But understand this: If the owner of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
chapters.zh: 家主若知道贼什么时候来，就必儆醒，不容贼挖透房屋，这是你们所知道的。

chapters.en: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.”
chapters.zh: 你们也要预备。因为你们想不到的时候，人子就来了。

chapters.en: Peter asked, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everyone?”
chapters.zh: 彼得说，主阿，这比喻是为我们说的呢？还是为众人呢？

chapters.en: The Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their food allowance at the proper time?
chapters.zh: 主说，谁是那忠心有见识的管家，主人派他管理家里的人，按时分粮给他们呢？

chapters.en: It will be good for that servant whom the master finds doing so when he returns.
chapters.zh: 主人来到，看见仆人这样行，那仆人就有福了。

chapters.en: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
chapters.zh: 我实在告诉你们，主人要派他管理一切所有的。

chapters.en: But suppose the servant says to himself, ‘My master is taking a long time in coming,’ and he then begins to beat the other servants, both men and women, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
chapters.zh: 那仆人若心里说，我的主人必来得迟。就动手打仆人和使女，并且吃喝醉酒。

chapters.en: The master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he is not aware of. He will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.
chapters.zh: 在他想不到的日子，不知道的时辰，那仆人的主人要来，重重地处治他（或作把他腰斩了），定他和不忠心的人同罪。

chapters.en: “The servant who knows the master’s will and does not get ready or does not do what the master wants will be beaten with many blows.
chapters.zh: 仆人知道主人的意思，却不预备，又不顺他的意思行，那仆人必多受责打。

chapters.en: But the one who does not know and does things deserving punishment will be beaten with few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be demanded; and from the one who has been entrusted with much, much more will be asked.
chapters.zh: 惟有那不知道的，作了当受责打的事，必少受责打因为多给谁，就向谁多取。多托谁，就向谁多要。

chapters.en: “I have come to bring fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
chapters.zh: 我来要把火丢在地上。倘若已经着起来，不也是我所愿意的吗？

chapters.en: But I have a baptism to undergo, and what constraint I am under until it is completed!
chapters.zh: 我有当受的洗。还没有成就，我是何等的迫切呢。

chapters.en: Do you think I came to bring peace on earth? No, I tell you, but division.
chapters.zh: 你们以为我来，是叫地上太平吗？我告诉你们，不是，乃是叫人分争。

chapters.en: From now on there will be five in one family divided against each other, three against two and two against three.
chapters.zh: 从今以后，一家五个人将要分争，三个人和两个人相争，两个人和三个人相争。

chapters.en: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”
chapters.zh: 父亲和儿子相争，儿子和父亲相争。母亲和女儿相争，女儿和母亲相争。婆婆和媳妇相争，媳妇和婆婆相争。

chapters.en: He said to the crowd: “When you see a cloud rising in the west, immediately you say, ‘It’s going to rain,’ and it does.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又对众人说，你们看见西边起了云彩，就说，要下一阵雨。果然就有。

chapters.en: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It’s going to be hot,’ and it is.
chapters.zh: 起了南风，就说，将要燥热。也就有了。

chapters.en: Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky. How is it that you don’t know how to interpret this present time?
chapters.zh: 假冒为善的人哪，你们知道分辨天地的气色。怎么不知道分辨这时候呢？

chapters.en: “Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
chapters.zh: 你们又为何不自己审量，什么是合理的呢？

chapters.en: As you are going with your adversary to the magistrate, try hard to be reconciled on the way, or your adversary may drag you off to the judge, and the judge turn you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
chapters.zh: 你同告你的对头去见官，还在路上，务要尽力的和他了结。恐怕他拉你到官面前，官交付差役，差役把你下在监里

chapters.en: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你，若有半文钱没有还清，你断不能从那里出来。

chapters.en: Now there were some present at that time who told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
chapters.zh: 正当那时，有人将彼拉多使加利利人的血搀杂在他们祭物中的事，告诉耶稣。

chapters.en: Jesus answered, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered this way?
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们以为这些加利利人比众加利利人更有罪，所以受这害吗？

chapters.en: I tell you, no! But unless you repent, you too will all perish.
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，不是的。你们若不悔改，都要如此灭亡。

chapters.en: Or those eighteen who died when the tower in Siloam fell on them—do you think they were more guilty than all the others living in Jerusalem?
chapters.zh: 从前西罗亚楼倒塌了，压死十八个人，你们以为那些人比一切住在耶路撒冷的人更有罪吗？

chapters.en: I tell you, no! But unless you repent, you too will all perish.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，不是的。你们若不悔改，都要如此灭亡。

chapters.en: Then he told this parable: “A man had a fig tree growing in his vineyard, and he went to look for fruit on it but did not find any.
chapters.zh: 于是用比喻说，一个人有一棵无花果树，栽在葡萄园里。他来到树前找果子，却找不着。

chapters.en: So he said to the man who took care of the vineyard, ‘For three years now I’ve been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’
chapters.zh: 就对管园的说，看哪，我这三年，来到这无花果树前找果子，竟找不着，把它砍了吧。何必白占地土呢？

chapters.en: “ ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone for one more year, and I’ll dig around it and fertilize it.
chapters.zh: 管园的说，主阿，今年且留着，等我周围掘开土，加上粪。

chapters.en: If it bears fruit next year, fine! If not, then cut it down.’ ”
chapters.zh: 以后若结果子便吧。不然再把它砍了。

chapters.en: On a Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,
chapters.zh: 安息日，耶稣在会堂里教训人。

chapters.en: and a woman was there who had been crippled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
chapters.zh: 有一个女人，被鬼附着病了十八年。腰弯得一点直不起来。

chapters.en: When Jesus saw her, he called her forward and said to her, “Woman, you are set free from your infirmity.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣看见，便叫过她来，对她说，女人，你脱离这病了。

chapters.en: Then he put his hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and praised God.
chapters.zh: 于是用两只手按着她。她立刻直起腰来，就归荣耀与神。

chapters.en: Indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, the synagogue leader said to the people, “There are six days for work. So come and be healed on those days, not on the Sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 管会堂的，因为耶稣在安息日治病，就气忿忿地对众人说，有六日应当作工。那六日之内，可以来求医，在安息日却不可。

chapters.en: The Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Doesn’t each of you on the Sabbath untie your ox or donkey from the stall and lead it out to give it water?
chapters.zh: 主说，假冒为善的人哪，难道你们各人在安息日不解开槽上的牛驴，牵去饮吗？

chapters.en: Then should not this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be set free on the Sabbath day from what bound her?”
chapters.zh: 况且这女人本是亚伯拉罕的后裔，被撒但捆绑了这十八年，不当在安息日解开她的绑吗？

chapters.en: When he said this, all his opponents were humiliated, but the people were delighted with all the wonderful things he was doing.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说这话，他的敌人都惭愧了。众人因他所行一切荣耀的事，就都欢喜了。

chapters.en: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? What shall I compare it to?
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，神的国，好像什么？我拿什么来比较呢？

chapters.en: It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds perched in its branches.”
chapters.zh: 好像一粒芥菜种，有人拿去种在园子里。长大成树，天上的飞鸟，宿在它的枝上。

chapters.en: Again he asked, “What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?
chapters.zh: 又说，我拿什么来比神的国呢？

chapters.en: It is like yeast that a woman took and mixed into about sixty poundsof flour until it worked all through the dough.”
chapters.zh: 好比面酵，有妇人拿来藏在三斗面里，直等全团都发起来。

chapters.en: Then Jesus went through the towns and villages, teaching as he made his way to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 耶稣往耶路撒冷去，在所经过的各城各乡教训人。

chapters.en: Someone asked him, “Lord, are only a few people going to be saved?” He said to them,
chapters.zh: 有一个人问他说，主阿，得救的人少吗？

chapters.en: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able to.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对众人说，你们要努力进窄门。我告诉你们，将来有许多人想要进去，却是不能。

chapters.en: Once the owner of the house gets up and closes the door, you will stand outside knocking and pleading, ‘Sir, open the door for us.’ “But he will answer, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
chapters.zh: 及至家主起来关了门，你们站在外面叩门，说，主阿，给我们开门，他就回答说，我不认识你们，不晓得你们是哪里来的。

chapters.en: “Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
chapters.zh: 那时，你们要说，我们在你面前吃过喝过，你也在我们的街上教训过人。

chapters.en: “But he will reply, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from. Away from me, all you evildoers!’
chapters.zh: 他要说，我告诉你们，我不晓得你们是哪里来的。你们这一切作恶的人，离开我去吧。

chapters.en: “There will be weeping there, and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves thrown out.
chapters.zh: 你们要看见亚伯拉罕，以撒，雅各，和众先知，都在神的国里，你们却被赶到外面。在那里必要哀哭切齿了。

chapters.en: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will take their places at the feast in the kingdom of God.
chapters.zh: 从东，从西，从南，从北，将有人来，在神的国里坐席。

chapters.en: Indeed there are those who are last who will be first, and first who will be last.”
chapters.zh: 只是有在后的将要在前，有在前的将要在后。

chapters.en: At that time some Pharisees came to Jesus and said to him, “Leave this place and go somewhere else. Herod wants to kill you.”
chapters.zh: 正当那时，有几个法利赛人来对耶稣说，离开这里去吧。因为希律想要杀你。

chapters.en: He replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘I will keep on driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach my goal.’
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们去告诉那个狐狸说，今天明天我赶鬼治病，第三天我的事就成全了。

chapters.en: In any case, I must press on today and tomorrow and the next day—for surely no prophet can die outside Jerusalem!
chapters.zh: 虽然这样，今天明天后天我必须前行。因为先知在耶路撒冷之外丧命是不能的。

chapters.en: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷阿，耶路撒冷阿，你常杀害先知，又用石头打死那奉差遣到你这里来的人。我多次愿意聚集你的儿女，好像母鸡把小鸡聚集在翅膀底下，只是你们不愿意。

chapters.en: Look, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
chapters.zh: 看哪，你们的家成为荒场留给你们。我告诉你们，从今以后你们不得再见我，直等到你们说，奉主名来的是应当称颂的。

chapters.en: One Sabbath, when Jesus went to eat in the house of a prominent Pharisee, he was being carefully watched.
chapters.zh: 安息日，耶稣到一个法利赛人的首领家里去吃饭，他们就窥探他。

chapters.en: There in front of him was a man suffering from abnormal swelling of his body.
chapters.zh: 在他面前有一个患水臌的人。

chapters.en: Jesus asked the Pharisees and experts in the law, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对律法师和法利赛人说，安息日治病，可以不可以。

chapters.en: But they remained silent. So taking hold of the man, he healed him and sent him on his way.
chapters.zh: 他们却不言语。耶稣就治好那人，叫他走了。

chapters.en: Then he asked them, “If one of you has a child or an ox that falls into a well on the Sabbath day, will you not immediately pull it out?”
chapters.zh: 便对他们说，你们中间谁有驴或有牛，在安息日掉在井里，不立时拉他上来呢？

chapters.en: And they had nothing to say.
chapters.zh: 他们不能对答这话。

chapters.en: When he noticed how the guests picked the places of honor at the table, he told them this parable:
chapters.zh: 耶稣见所请的客拣择首位，就用比喻对他们说，

chapters.en: “When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not take the place of honor, for a person more distinguished than you may have been invited.
chapters.zh: 你被人请去赴婚姻的筵席，不要坐在首位上。恐怕有比你尊贵的客，被他请来。

chapters.en: If so, the host who invited both of you will come and say to you, ‘Give this person your seat.’ Then, humiliated, you will have to take the least important place.
chapters.zh: 那请你们的人前来对你说，让座给这一位吧。你就羞羞惭惭的退到末位上去了。

chapters.en: But when you are invited, take the lowest place, so that when your host comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all the other guests.
chapters.zh: 你被请的时候，就去坐在末位上，好叫那请你的人来，对你说，朋友，请上坐，那时你在同席的人面前，就有光彩了。

chapters.en: For all those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.”
chapters.zh: 因为凡自高的必降为卑。自卑的必升为高。

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to his host, “When you give a luncheon or dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers or sisters, your relatives, or your rich neighbors; if you do, they may invite you back and so you will be repaid.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又对请他的人说，你摆设午饭，或晚饭，不要请你的朋友，弟兄，亲属，和富足的邻舍。恐怕他们也请你，你就得了报答。

chapters.en: But when you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind,
chapters.zh: 你摆设筵席，倒要请那贫穷的，残废的，瘸腿的，瞎眼的，你就有福了。

chapters.en: and you will be blessed. Although they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
chapters.zh: 因为他们没有什么可报答你。到义人复活的时候，你要得着报答。

chapters.en: When one of those at the table with him heard this, he said to Jesus, “Blessed is the one who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”
chapters.zh: 同席的有一人听见这话，就对耶稣说，在神国里吃饭的有福了。

chapters.en: Jesus replied: “A certain man was preparing a great banquet and invited many guests.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他说，有一人摆设大筵席，请了许多客。

chapters.en: At the time of the banquet he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
chapters.zh: 到了坐席的时候，打发仆人去对所请的人说，请来吧。样样都齐备了。

chapters.en: “But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said, ‘I have just bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please excuse me.’
chapters.zh: 众人一口同音的推辞。头一个说，我买了一块地，必须去看看。请你准我辞了。

chapters.en: “Another said, ‘I have just bought five yoke of oxen, and I’m on my way to try them out. Please excuse me.’
chapters.zh: 又有一个说，我买了五对牛，要去试一试。请你准我辞了。

chapters.en: “Still another said, ‘I just got married, so I can’t come.’
chapters.zh: 又有一个说，我才娶了妻，所以不能去。

chapters.en: “The servant came back and reported this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and ordered his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the town and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame.’
chapters.zh: 那仆人回来，把这事都告诉了主人。家主就动怒，对仆人说，快出去到城里大街小巷，领那贫穷的，残废的，瞎眼的，瘸腿的来。

chapters.en: “ ‘Sir,’ the servant said, ‘what you ordered has been done, but there is still room.’
chapters.zh: 仆人说，主阿，你所吩咐的已经办了，还有空座。

chapters.en: “Then the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the roads and country lanes and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.
chapters.zh: 主人对仆人说，你出去到路上和篱笆那里，勉强人进来，坐满我的屋子。

chapters.en: I tell you, not one of those who were invited will get a taste of my banquet.’ ”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，先前所请的人，没有一个得尝我的筵席。

chapters.en: Large crowds were traveling with Jesus, and turning to them he said:
chapters.zh: 有极多的人和耶稣同行。他转过来对他们说，

chapters.en: “If anyone comes to me and does not hate father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters—yes, even their own life—such a person cannot be my disciple.
chapters.zh: 人到我这里来，若不爱我胜过爱自己的父母，妻子，儿女，弟兄，姐妹，和自己的性命，就不能作我的门徒。爱我胜过爱原文作恨

chapters.en: And whoever does not carry their cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
chapters.zh: 凡不背着自己十字架跟从我的，也不能作我的门徒。

chapters.en: “Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. Won’t you first sit down and estimate the cost to see if you have enough money to complete it?
chapters.zh: 你们那一个要盖一座楼，不先坐下算计花费，能盖成不能呢？

chapters.en: For if you lay the foundation and are not able to finish it, everyone who sees it will ridicule you,
chapters.zh: 恐怕安了地基，不能成功，看见的人都笑话他，

chapters.en: saying, ‘This person began to build and wasn’t able to finish.’
chapters.zh: 说，这个人开了工，却不能完工。

chapters.en: “Or suppose a king is about to go to war against another king. Won’t he first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand men to oppose the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
chapters.zh: 或是一个王，出去和别的王打仗，岂不先坐下酌量，能用一万兵，去敌那领二万兵来攻打他的吗？

chapters.en: If he is not able, he will send a delegation while the other is still a long way off and will ask for terms of peace.
chapters.zh: 若是不能，就趁敌人还远的时候，派使者去求和息的条款。

chapters.en: In the same way, those of you who do not give up everything you have cannot be my disciples.
chapters.zh: 这样，你们无论什么人，若不撇下一切所有的，就不能作我的门徒。

chapters.en: “Salt is good, but if it loses its saltiness, how can it be made salty again?
chapters.zh: 盐本是好的，盐若失了味，可用什么叫它再咸呢？

chapters.en: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; it is thrown out. “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.”
chapters.zh: 或用在田里，或堆在粪里，都不合式。只好丢在外面。有耳可听的，就应当听。

chapters.en: Now the tax collectors and sinners were all gathering around to hear Jesus.
chapters.zh: 众税吏和罪人，都挨近耶稣要听他讲道。

chapters.en: But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law muttered, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
chapters.zh: 法利赛人和文士，私下议论说，这个人接待罪人，又同他们吃饭。

chapters.en: Then Jesus told them this parable:
chapters.zh: 耶稣就用比喻，说，

chapters.en: “Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one of them. Doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost sheep until he finds it?
chapters.zh: 你们中间谁有一百只羊，失去一只，不把这九十九只撇在旷野，去找那失去的羊直到找着呢？

chapters.en: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders
chapters.zh: 找着了，就欢欢喜喜地扛在肩上，回到家里。

chapters.en: and goes home. Then he calls his friends and neighbors together and says, ‘Rejoice with me; I have found my lost sheep.’
chapters.zh: 就请朋友邻舍来，对他们说，我失去的羊已经找着了，你们和我一同欢喜吧。

chapters.en: I tell you that in the same way there will be more rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need to repent.
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，一个罪人悔改，在天上也要这样为他欢喜，较比为九十九个不用悔改的义人，欢喜更大。

chapters.en: “Or suppose a woman has ten silver coinsand loses one. Doesn’t she light a lamp, sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
chapters.zh: 或是一个妇人，有十块钱，若失落一块，岂不点上灯，打扫屋子，细细的找，直到找着吗？

chapters.en: And when she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors together and says, ‘Rejoice with me; I have found my lost coin.’
chapters.zh: 找着了，就请朋友邻舍来，对他们说，我失落的那块钱已经找着了，你们和我一同欢喜吧。

chapters.en: In the same way, I tell you, there is rejoicing in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，一个罪人悔改，在神的使者面前，也是这样为他欢喜。

chapters.en: Jesus continued: “There was a man who had two sons.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又说，一个人有两个儿子。

chapters.en: The younger one said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.
chapters.zh: 小儿子对父亲说，父亲，请你把我应得的家业分给我。他父亲就把产业分给他们。

chapters.en: “Not long after that, the younger son got together all he had, set off for a distant country and there squandered his wealth in wild living.
chapters.zh: 过了不多几日，小儿子就把他一切所有的，都收拾起来，往远方去了。在那里任意放荡，浪费赀财。

chapters.en: After he had spent everything, there was a severe famine in that whole country, and he began to be in need.
chapters.zh: 既耗尽了一切所有的，又遇着那地方大遭饥荒，就穷苦起来。

chapters.en: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him to his fields to feed pigs.
chapters.zh: 于是去投靠那地方的一个人，那人打发他到田里去放猪。

chapters.en: He longed to fill his stomach with the pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
chapters.zh: 他恨不得拿猪所吃的豆荚充饥。也没有人给他。

chapters.en: “When he came to his senses, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have food to spare, and here I am starving to death!
chapters.zh: 他醒悟过来，就说，我父亲有多少的雇工，口粮有余，我倒在这里饿死吗？

chapters.en: I will set out and go back to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
chapters.zh: 我要起来，到我父亲那里去，向他说，父亲，我得罪了天，又得罪了你。

chapters.en: I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired servants.’
chapters.zh: 从今以后，我不配称为你的儿子，把我当作一个雇工吧。

chapters.en: So he got up and went to his father. “But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion for him; he ran to his son, threw his arms around him and kissed him.
chapters.zh: 于是起来往他父亲那里去。相离还远，他父亲看见，就动了慈心，跑去抱着他的颈项，连连与他亲嘴。

chapters.en: “The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
chapters.zh: 儿子说，父亲，我得罪了天，又得罪了你，从今以后，我不配称为你的儿子。

chapters.en: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
chapters.zh: 父亲却吩咐仆人说，把那上好的袍子快拿出来给他穿。把戒指戴在他指头上。把鞋穿在他脚上。

chapters.en: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let’s have a feast and celebrate.
chapters.zh: 把那肥牛犊牵来宰了，我们可以吃喝快乐。

chapters.en: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’ So they began to celebrate.
chapters.zh: 因为我这个儿子，是死而复活，失而又得的。他们就快乐起来。

chapters.en: “Meanwhile, the older son was in the field. When he came near the house, he heard music and dancing.
chapters.zh: 那时，大儿子正在田里。他回来离家不远，听见作乐跳舞的声音。

chapters.en: So he called one of the servants and asked him what was going on.
chapters.zh: 便叫过一个仆人来，问是什么事。

chapters.en: ‘Your brother has come,’ he replied, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has him back safe and sound.’
chapters.zh: 仆人说，你兄弟来了。你父亲，因为得他无灾无病地回来，把肥牛犊宰了。

chapters.en: “The older brother became angry and refused to go in. So his father went out and pleaded with him.
chapters.zh: 大儿子却生气，不肯进去。他父亲就出来劝他。

chapters.en: But he answered his father, ‘Look! All these years I’ve been slaving for you and never disobeyed your orders. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
chapters.zh: 他对父亲说，我服事你这多年，从来没有违背过你的命。你并没有给我一只山羊羔，叫我和朋友，一同快乐。

chapters.en: But when this son of yours who has squandered your property with prostitutes comes home, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
chapters.zh: 但你这个儿子，和娼妓吞尽了你的产业，他一来了，你倒为他宰了肥牛犊。

chapters.en: “ ‘My son,’ the father said, ‘you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.
chapters.zh: 父亲对他说，儿阿，你常和我同在，我一切所有的，都是你的。

chapters.en: But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’ ”
chapters.zh: 只是你这个兄弟是死而复活，失而又得的，所以我们理当欢喜快乐。

chapters.en: Jesus told his disciples: “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又对门徒说，有一个财主的管家。别人向他主人告他浪费主人的财物。

chapters.en: So he called him in and asked him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your management, because you cannot be manager any longer.’
chapters.zh: 主人叫他来，对他说，我听见你这事怎么样呢？把你所经管的交代明白。因你不能再作我的管家。

chapters.en: “The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do now? My master is taking away my job. I’m not strong enough to dig, and I’m ashamed to beg—
chapters.zh: 那管家心里说，主人辞我，不用我再作管家，我将来作什么？锄地呢？无力。讨饭呢？怕羞。

chapters.en: I know what I’ll do so that, when I lose my job here, people will welcome me into their houses.’
chapters.zh: 我知道怎么行，好叫人在我不作管家之后，接我到他们家里去。

chapters.en: “So he called in each one of his master’s debtors. He asked the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
chapters.zh: 于是把欠他主人债的，一个一个地叫了来，问头一个说，你欠我主人多少。

chapters.en: “ ‘Nine hundred gallonsof olive oil,’ he replied. “The manager told him, ‘Take your bill, sit down quickly, and make it four hundred and fifty.’
chapters.zh: 他说，一百篓油。每篓约五十斤管家说，拿你的账快坐下写五十。

chapters.en: “Then he asked the second, ‘And how much do you owe?’ “ ‘A thousand bushelsof wheat,’ he replied. “He told him, ‘Take your bill and make it eight hundred.’
chapters.zh: 又问一个说，你欠多少。他说，一百石麦子。管家说，拿你的账写八十。

chapters.en: “The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the people of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the people of the light.
chapters.zh: 主人就夸奖这不义的管家作事聪明。因为今世之子，在世事之上，较比光明之子，更加聪明。

chapters.en: I tell you, use worldly wealth to gain friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, you will be welcomed into eternal dwellings.
chapters.zh: 我又告诉你们，要借着那不义的钱财，结交朋友。到了钱财无用的时候，他们可以接你们到永存的帐幕里去。

chapters.en: “Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
chapters.zh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心。在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

chapters.en: So if you have not been trustworthy in handling worldly wealth, who will trust you with true riches?
chapters.zh: 倘若你们在不义的钱财上不忠心，谁还把那真实的钱财托付你们呢？

chapters.en: And if you have not been trustworthy with someone else’s property, who will give you property of your own?
chapters.zh: 倘若你们在别人的东西上不忠心，谁还把你们自己的东西给你们呢？

chapters.en: “No one can serve two masters. Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
chapters.zh: 一个仆人不能事奉两个主。不是恶这个爱那个，就是重这个轻那个。你们不能又事奉神，又事奉玛门。

chapters.en: The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and were sneering at Jesus.
chapters.zh: 法利赛人是贪爱钱财的，他们听见这一切话，就嗤笑耶稣。

chapters.en: He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves in the eyes of others, but God knows your hearts. What people value highly is detestable in God’s sight.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说，你们是在人面前自称为义的。你们的心，神却知道。因为人所尊贵的是神看为可憎恶的。

chapters.en: “The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the good news of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing their way into it.
chapters.zh: 律法和先知，到约翰为止。从此神国的福音传开了，人人努力要进去。

chapters.en: It is easier for heaven and earth to disappear than for the least stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.
chapters.zh: 天地废去，较比律法的一点一画落空还容易。

chapters.en: “Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and the man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
chapters.zh: 凡休妻另娶的，就是犯奸淫。娶被休之妻的，也是犯奸淫。

chapters.en: “There was a rich man who was dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in luxury every day.
chapters.zh: 有一个财主，穿着紫色袍和细麻布衣服，天天奢华宴乐。

chapters.en: At his gate was laid a beggar named Lazarus, covered with sores
chapters.zh: 又有一个讨饭的，名叫拉撒路，浑身生疮，被人放在财主门口，

chapters.en: and longing to eat what fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
chapters.zh: 要得财主桌子上掉下来的零碎充饥。并且狗来舔他的疮。

chapters.en: “The time came when the beggar died and the angels carried him to Abraham’s side. The rich man also died and was buried.
chapters.zh: 后来那讨饭的死了，被天使带去放在亚伯拉罕的怀里。财主也死了，并且埋葬了。

chapters.en: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus by his side.
chapters.zh: 他在阴间受痛苦，举目远远地望见亚伯拉罕，又望见拉撒路在他怀里。

chapters.en: So he called to him, ‘Father Abraham, have pity on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in agony in this fire.’
chapters.zh: 就喊着说，我祖亚伯拉罕哪，可怜我吧，打发拉撒路来，用指头尖蘸点水，凉凉我的舌头。因为我在这火焰里，极其痛苦。

chapters.en: “But Abraham replied, ‘Son, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things, but now he is comforted here and you are in agony.
chapters.zh: 亚伯拉罕说，儿阿，你该回想你生前享过福，拉撒路也受过苦。如今他在这里得安慰，你倒受痛苦。

chapters.en: And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been set in place, so that those who want to go from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross over from there to us.’
chapters.zh: 不但这样，并且在你我之间，有深渊限定，以致人要从这边过到你们那边，是不能的，要从那边过到我们这边，也是不能的。

chapters.en: “He answered, ‘Then I beg you, father, send Lazarus to my family,
chapters.zh: 财主说，我祖阿，既是这样，求你打发拉撒路到我父家去。

chapters.en: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also come to this place of torment.’
chapters.zh: 因为我还有五个弟兄。他可以对他们作见证，免得他们也来到这痛苦的地方。

chapters.en: “Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them.’
chapters.zh: 亚伯拉罕说，他们有摩西和先知的话，可以听从。

chapters.en: “ ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.’
chapters.zh: 他说，我祖亚伯拉罕哪，不是的。若有一个从死里复活的，到他们那里去的，他们必要悔改。

chapters.en: “He said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.’ ”
chapters.zh: 亚伯拉罕说，若不听从摩西和先知的话，就是有一个从死里复活的，他们也是不听劝。

chapters.en: Jesus said to his disciples: “Things that cause people to stumble are bound to come, but woe to anyone through whom they come.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又对门徒说，绊倒人的事是免不了的。但那绊倒人的有祸了。

chapters.en: It would be better for them to be thrown into the sea with a millstone tied around their neck than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
chapters.zh: 就是把磨石拴在这人的颈项上，丢在海里，还强如他把这小子里的一个绊倒了。

chapters.en: So watch yourselves. “If your brother or sister sins against you, rebuke them; and if they repent, forgive them.
chapters.zh: 你们要谨慎。若是你的弟兄得罪你，就劝戒他。他若懊悔，就饶恕他。

chapters.en: Even if they sin against you seven times in a day and seven times come back to you saying ‘I repent,’ you must forgive them.”
chapters.zh: 倘若他一天七次得罪你，又七次回转说，我懊悔了，你总要饶恕他。

chapters.en: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”
chapters.zh: 使徒对主说，求主加增我们的信心。

chapters.en: He replied, “If you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
chapters.zh: 主说，你们若有信心像一粒芥菜种，就是对这棵桑树说，你要拔起根来栽在海里，他也必听从你们。

chapters.en: “Suppose one of you has a servant plowing or looking after the sheep. Will he say to the servant when he comes in from the field, ‘Come along now and sit down to eat’?
chapters.zh: 你们谁有仆人耕地，或是放羊，从田里回来，就对他说，你快来坐下吃饭呢？

chapters.en: Won’t he rather say, ‘Prepare my supper, get yourself ready and wait on me while I eat and drink; after that you may eat and drink’?
chapters.zh: 岂不对他说，你给我预备晚饭，束上带子伺候我，等我吃喝完了，你才可以吃喝吗？

chapters.en: Will he thank the servant because he did what he was told to do?
chapters.zh: 仆人照所吩咐的去作，主人还谢谢他吗？

chapters.en: So you also, when you have done everything you were told to do, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’ ”
chapters.zh: 这样，你们作完了一切所吩咐的，只当说，我们是无用的仆人。所作的本是我们应分作的。

chapters.en: Now on his way to Jerusalem, Jesus traveled along the border between Samaria and Galilee.
chapters.zh: 耶稣往耶路撒冷去，经过撒玛利亚和加利利。

chapters.en: As he was going into a village, ten men who had leprosy met him. They stood at a distance
chapters.zh: 进入一个村子，有十个长大麻疯的迎面而来，远远地站着。

chapters.en: and called out in a loud voice, “Jesus, Master, have pity on us!”
chapters.zh: 高声说，耶稣，夫子，可怜我们吧。

chapters.en: When he saw them, he said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they went, they were cleansed.
chapters.zh: 耶稣看见，就对他们说，你们去把身体给祭司察看。他们去的时候就洁净了。

chapters.en: One of them, when he saw he was healed, came back, praising God in a loud voice.
chapters.zh: 内中有一个见自己已经好了，就回来大声归荣耀与神。

chapters.en: He threw himself at Jesus’ feet and thanked him—and he was a Samaritan.
chapters.zh: 又俯伏在耶稣脚前感谢他。这人是撒玛利亚人。

chapters.en: Jesus asked, “Were not all ten cleansed? Where are the other nine?
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，洁净了的不是十个人吗？那九个在哪里呢？

chapters.en: Has no one returned to give praise to God except this foreigner?”
chapters.zh: 除了这外族人，再没有别人回来归荣耀与神吗？

chapters.en: Then he said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well.”
chapters.zh: 就对那人说，起来走吧。你的信救了你了。

chapters.en: Once, on being asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, Jesus replied, “The coming of the kingdom of God is not something that can be observed,
chapters.zh: 法利赛人问神的国几时来到。耶稣回答说，神的国来到，不是眼所能见的。

chapters.en: nor will people say, ‘Here it is,’ or ‘There it is,’ because the kingdom of God is in your midst.”
chapters.zh: 人也不得说，看哪，在这里。看哪，在那里。因为神的国就在你们心里。心里或作中间

chapters.en: Then he said to his disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
chapters.zh: 他又对门徒说，日子将到，你们巴不得看见人子的一个日子，却不得看见。

chapters.en: People will tell you, ‘There he is!’ or ‘Here he is!’ Do not go running off after them.
chapters.zh: 人将要对你们说，看哪，在那里，看哪，在这里。你们不要出去，也不要跟随他们。

chapters.en: For the Son of Man in his day will be like the lightning, which flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other.
chapters.zh: 因为人子在他降临的日子，好像闪电，从天这边一闪，直照到天那边。

chapters.en: But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
chapters.zh: 只是他必须先受许多苦，又被这世代弃绝。

chapters.en: “Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man.
chapters.zh: 挪亚的日子怎样，人子的日子也要怎样。

chapters.en: People were eating, drinking, marrying and being given in marriage up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
chapters.zh: 那时候的人又吃又喝，又娶又嫁，到挪亚进方舟的那日，洪水就来，把他们全都灭了。

chapters.en: “It was the same in the days of Lot. People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
chapters.zh: 又好像罗得的日子。人又吃又喝，又买又卖，又耕种，又盖造。

chapters.en: But the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
chapters.zh: 到罗得出所多玛的那日，就有火与硫磺从天上降下来，把他们全都灭了。

chapters.en: “It will be just like this on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
chapters.zh: 人子显现的日子，也要这样。

chapters.en: On that day no one who is on the housetop, with possessions inside, should go down to get them. Likewise, no one in the field should go back for anything.
chapters.zh: 当那日，人在房上，器具在屋里，不要下来拿。人在田里，也不要回家。

chapters.en: Remember Lot’s wife!
chapters.zh: 你们要回想罗得的妻子。

chapters.en: Whoever tries to keep their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life will preserve it.
chapters.zh: 凡想要保全生命的，必丧掉生命。凡丧掉生命的，必救活生命。

chapters.en: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed; one will be taken and the other left.
chapters.zh: 我对你们说，当那一夜，两个人在一个床上。要取去一个，撇下一个。

chapters.en: Two women will be grinding grain together;
chapters.zh: 两个女人一同推磨。要取去一个，撇下一个。有古卷在此有

chapters.en: one will be taken and the other left.”
chapters.zh: 两个人在田里要取去一个撇下一个

chapters.en: “Where, Lord?” they asked. He replied, “Where there is a dead body, there the vultures will gather.”
chapters.zh: 门徒说，主阿，在哪里有这事呢？耶稣说，尸首在哪里，鹰也必聚在哪里。

chapters.en: Then Jesus told his disciples a parable to show them that they should always pray and not give up.
chapters.zh: 耶稣设一个比喻，是要人常常祷告，不可灰心。

chapters.en: He said: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor cared what people thought.
chapters.zh: 说，某城里有一个官，不惧怕神，也不尊重世人。

chapters.en: And there was a widow in that town who kept coming to him with the plea, ‘Grant me justice against my adversary.’
chapters.zh: 那城里有个寡妇，常到他那里，说，我有一个对头，求你给我伸冤。

chapters.en: “For some time he refused. But finally he said to himself, ‘Even though I don’t fear God or care what people think,
chapters.zh: 他多日不准。后来心里说，我虽不惧怕神，也不尊重世人。

chapters.en: yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will see that she gets justice, so that she won’t eventually come and attack me!’ ”
chapters.zh: 只因这寡妇烦扰我，我就给她伸冤吧。免得她常来缠磨我。

chapters.en: And the Lord said, “Listen to what the unjust judge says.
chapters.zh: 主说，你们听这不义之官所说的话。

chapters.en: And will not God bring about justice for his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night? Will he keep putting them off?
chapters.zh: 神的选民，昼夜呼吁他，他纵然为他们忍了多时，岂不终久给他们伸冤吗？

chapters.en: I tell you, he will see that they get justice, and quickly. However, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，要快快地给他们伸冤了，然而人子来的时候，遇得见世上有信德吗？

chapters.en: To some who were confident of their own righteousness and looked down on everyone else, Jesus told this parable:
chapters.zh: 耶稣向那些仗着自己是义人，藐视别人的，设一个比喻，

chapters.en: “Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
chapters.zh: 说，有两个人上殿里去祷告。一个是法利赛人，一个是税吏。

chapters.en: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like other people—robbers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
chapters.zh: 法利赛人站着，自言自语的祷告说，神阿，我感谢你，我不像别人，勒索，不义，奸淫，也不像这个税吏。

chapters.en: I fast twice a week and give a tenth of all I get.’
chapters.zh: 我一个礼拜禁食两次，凡我所得的，都捐上十分之一。

chapters.en: “But the tax collector stood at a distance. He would not even look up to heaven, but beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner.’
chapters.zh: 那税吏远远地站着，连举目望天也不敢，只捶着胸说，神阿，开恩可怜我这个罪人。

chapters.en: “I tell you that this man, rather than the other, went home justified before God. For all those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，这人回家去，比那人倒算为义了，因为凡自高的，必降为卑，自卑的，必升为高。

chapters.en: People were also bringing babies to Jesus for him to place his hands on them. When the disciples saw this, they rebuked them.
chapters.zh: 有人抱着自己的婴孩，来见耶稣，要他摸他们，门徒看见就责备那些人。

chapters.en: But Jesus called the children to him and said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
chapters.zh: 耶稣却叫他们来，说，让小孩子到我这里来，不要禁止他们，因为在神国的，正是这样的人

chapters.en: Truly I tell you, anyone who will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
chapters.zh: 我实在告诉你们，凡要承受神国的，若不像小孩子，断不能进去。

chapters.en: A certain ruler asked him, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
chapters.zh: 有一个官问耶稣说，良善的夫子，我该作什么事，才可以承受永生。

chapters.en: “Why do you call me good?” Jesus answered. “No one is good—except God alone.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他说，你为什么称我是良善的，除了神一位之外，再没有良善的。

chapters.en: You know the commandments: ‘You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not give false testimony, honor your father and mother.’”
chapters.zh: 诫命你是晓得的，不可奸淫，不可杀人，不可偷盗，不可作假见证，当孝敬父母。

chapters.en: “All these I have kept since I was a boy,” he said.
chapters.zh: 那人说，这一切我从小都遵守了。

chapters.en: When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “You still lack one thing. Sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣听见了，就说，你还缺少一件，要变卖你一切所有的，分给穷人，就必有财宝在天上。你还要来跟从我。

chapters.en: When he heard this, he became very sad, because he was very wealthy.
chapters.zh: 他听见这话，就甚忧愁，因为他很富足。

chapters.en: Jesus looked at him and said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!
chapters.zh: 耶稣看见他就说，有钱财的人进神的国，是何等的难哪。

chapters.en: Indeed, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for someone who is rich to enter the kingdom of God.”
chapters.zh: 骆驼穿过针的眼，比财主进神的国，还容易呢。

chapters.en: Those who heard this asked, “Who then can be saved?”
chapters.zh: 听见的人说，这样，谁能得救呢？

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，在人所不能的事，在神却能。

chapters.en: Peter said to him, “We have left all we had to follow you!”
chapters.zh: 彼得说，看哪，我们已经撇下自己所有的跟从你了。

chapters.en: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus said to them, “no one who has left home or wife or brothers or sisters or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，我实在告诉你们，人为神的国，撇下房屋，或是妻子，弟兄，父母，儿女，

chapters.en: will fail to receive many times as much in this age, and in the age to come eternal life.”
chapters.zh: 没有在今世不得百倍，在来世不得永生的。

chapters.en: Jesus took the Twelve aside and told them, “We are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that is written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
chapters.zh: 耶稣带着十二个门徒，对他们说，看哪，我们上耶路撒冷去，先知所写的一切事，都要成就在人子身上。

chapters.en: He will be delivered over to the Gentiles. They will mock him, insult him and spit on him;
chapters.zh: 他将要被交给外邦人，他们要戏弄他，凌辱他，吐唾沫在他脸上。

chapters.en: they will flog him and kill him. On the third day he will rise again.”
chapters.zh: 并要鞭打他，杀害他，第三日他要复活。

chapters.en: The disciples did not understand any of this. Its meaning was hidden from them, and they did not know what he was talking about.
chapters.zh: 这些事门徒一样也不懂得，意思乃是隐藏的，他们不晓得所说的是什么。

chapters.en: As Jesus approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the roadside begging.
chapters.zh: 耶稣将近耶利哥的时候，有一个瞎子坐在路旁讨饭。

chapters.en: When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
chapters.zh: 听见许多人经过，就问是什么事。

chapters.en: They told him, “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.”
chapters.zh: 他们告诉他，是拿撒勒人耶稣经过。

chapters.en: He called out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
chapters.zh: 他就呼叫说，大卫的子孙耶稣阿，可怜我吧。

chapters.en: Those who led the way rebuked him and told him to be quiet, but he shouted all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
chapters.zh: 在前头走的人，就责备他，不许他作声。他却越发喊叫说，大卫的子孙，可怜我吧。

chapters.en: Jesus stopped and ordered the man to be brought to him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
chapters.zh: 耶稣站住，吩咐把他领过来。到了跟前，就问他说，

chapters.en: “What do you want me to do for you?”“Lord, I want to see,” he replied.
chapters.zh: 你要我为你作什么。他说，主阿，我要能看见。

chapters.en: Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight; your faith has healed you.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你可以看见。你的信救了你了。

chapters.en: Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, praising God. When all the people saw it, they also praised God.
chapters.zh: 瞎子立刻看见了，就跟随耶稣，一路归荣耀与神。众人看见这事，也赞美神。

chapters.en: Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.
chapters.zh: 耶稣进了耶利哥，正经过的时候，

chapters.en: A man was there by the name of Zacchaeus; he was a chief tax collector and was wealthy.
chapters.zh: 有一个人名叫撒该，作税吏长，是个财主。

chapters.en: He wanted to see who Jesus was, but because he was short he could not see over the crowd.
chapters.zh: 他要看看耶稣是怎样的人。只因人多，他的身量又矮，所以不得看见。

chapters.en: So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree to see him, since Jesus was coming that way.
chapters.zh: 就跑到前头，爬上桑树，要看耶稣，因为耶稣必从那里经过。

chapters.en: When Jesus reached the spot, he looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, come down immediately. I must stay at your house today.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣到了那里，抬头一看，对他说，撒该，快下来，今天我必住在你家里。

chapters.en: So he came down at once and welcomed him gladly.
chapters.zh: 他就急忙下来，欢欢喜喜地接待耶稣。

chapters.en: All the people saw this and began to mutter, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinner.”
chapters.zh: 众人看见，都私下议论说，他竟到罪人家里去住宿。

chapters.en: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord! Here and now I give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have cheated anybody out of anything, I will pay back four times the amount.”
chapters.zh: 撒该站着，对主说，主阿，我把所有的一半给穷人。我若讹诈了谁，就还他四倍。

chapters.en: Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man, too, is a son of Abraham.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，今天救恩到了这家，因为他也是亚伯拉罕的子孙。

chapters.en: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
chapters.zh: 人子来，为要寻找拯救失丧的人。

chapters.en: While they were listening to this, he went on to tell them a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and the people thought that the kingdom of God was going to appear at once.
chapters.zh: 众人正在听见这些话的时候，耶稣因为将近耶路撒冷，又因他们以为神的国快要显出来，就另设一个比喻说，

chapters.en: He said: “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to have himself appointed king and then to return.
chapters.zh: 有一个贵胄往远方去，要得国回来。

chapters.en: So he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas.‘Put this money to work,’ he said, ‘until I come back.’
chapters.zh: 便叫了他的十个仆人来，交给他们十锭银子（锭原文作弥拿，一弥拿约银十两），说，你们去作生意，直等我回来。

chapters.en: “But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We don’t want this man to be our king.’
chapters.zh: 他本国的人却恨他，打发使者随后去说，我们不愿意这个人作我们的王。

chapters.en: “He was made king, however, and returned home. Then he sent for the servants to whom he had given the money, in order to find out what they had gained with it.
chapters.zh: 他既得国回来，就吩咐叫那领银子的仆人来，要知道他们作生意赚了多少。

chapters.en: “The first one came and said, ‘Sir, your mina has earned ten more.’
chapters.zh: 头一个上来说，主阿，你的一锭银子，已经赚了十锭。

chapters.en: “ ‘Well done, my good servant!’ his master replied. ‘Because you have been trustworthy in a very small matter, take charge of ten cities.’
chapters.zh: 主人说，好良善的仆人。你既在最小的事上有忠心，可以有权柄管十座城。

chapters.en: “The second came and said, ‘Sir, your mina has earned five more.’
chapters.zh: 第二个来说，主阿，你的一锭银子，已经赚了五锭。

chapters.en: “His master answered, ‘You take charge of five cities.’
chapters.zh: 主人说，你也可以管五座城。

chapters.en: “Then another servant came and said, ‘Sir, here is your mina; I have kept it laid away in a piece of cloth.
chapters.zh: 又有一个来说，主阿，看哪，你的一锭银子在这里，我把他包在手巾里存着。

chapters.en: I was afraid of you, because you are a hard man. You take out what you did not put in and reap what you did not sow.’
chapters.zh: 我原是怕你，因为你是严厉的人。没有放下的还要去拿，没有种下的还要去收。

chapters.en: “His master replied, ‘I will judge you by your own words, you wicked servant! You knew, did you, that I am a hard man, taking out what I did not put in, and reaping what I did not sow?
chapters.zh: 主人对他说，你这恶仆，我要凭你的口，定你的罪。你既知道我是严厉的人，没有放下的还要去拿，没有种下的还要去收。

chapters.en: Why then didn’t you put my money on deposit, so that when I came back, I could have collected it with interest?’
chapters.zh: 为什么不把我的银子交给银行，等我来的时候，连本带利都可以要回来呢？

chapters.en: “Then he said to those standing by, ‘Take his mina away from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’
chapters.zh: 就对旁边站着的人说，夺过他这一锭来，给那有十锭的。

chapters.en: “ ‘Sir,’ they said, ‘he already has ten!’
chapters.zh: 他们说，主阿，他已经有十锭了。

chapters.en: “He replied, ‘I tell you that to everyone who has, more will be given, but as for the one who has nothing, even what they have will be taken away.
chapters.zh: 主人说，我告诉你们，凡有的，还要加给他。没有的，连他所有的，也要夺过来。

chapters.en: But those enemies of mine who did not want me to be king over them—bring them here and kill them in front of me.’ ”
chapters.zh: 至于我那些仇敌不要我作他们王的，把他们拉来，在我面前杀了吧。

chapters.en: After Jesus had said this, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说完了这话，就在前面走，上耶路撒冷去。

chapters.en: As he approached Bethphage and Bethany at the hill called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples, saying to them,
chapters.zh: 将近伯法其和伯大尼，在一座山名叫橄榄山那里。就打发两个门徒，说，

chapters.en: “Go to the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, which no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
chapters.zh: 你们往对面村子里去。进去的时候，必看见一匹驴驹拴在那里，是从来没有人骑过的。可以解开牵来。

chapters.en: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say, ‘The Lord needs it.’ ”
chapters.zh: 若有人问为什么解它，你们就说，主要用它。

chapters.en: Those who were sent ahead went and found it just as he had told them.
chapters.zh: 打发的人去了，所遇见的，正如耶稣所说的。

chapters.en: As they were untying the colt, its owners asked them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
chapters.zh: 他们解驴驹的时候，主人问他们说，解驴驹作什么？

chapters.en: They replied, “The Lord needs it.”
chapters.zh: 他们说，主要用它。

chapters.en: They brought it to Jesus, threw their cloaks on the colt and put Jesus on it.
chapters.zh: 他们牵到耶稣那里，把自己的衣服搭在上面，扶着耶稣骑上。

chapters.en: As he went along, people spread their cloaks on the road.
chapters.zh: 走的时候，众人把衣服铺在路上。

chapters.en: When he came near the place where the road goes down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples began joyfully to praise God in loud voices for all the miracles they had seen:
chapters.zh: 将近耶路撒冷，正下橄榄山的时候，众门徒因所见过的一切异能，都欢乐起来，大声赞美神，

chapters.en: “Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord!”“Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
chapters.zh: 说，奉主名来的王，是应当称颂的。在天上有和平，在至高之处有荣光。

chapters.en: Some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”
chapters.zh: 众人中有几个法利赛人对耶稣说，夫子，责备你的门徒吧。

chapters.en: “I tell you,” he replied, “if they keep quiet, the stones will cry out.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，我告诉你们，若是他们闭口不说，这些石头必要呼叫起来。

chapters.en: As he approached Jerusalem and saw the city, he wept over it
chapters.zh: 耶稣快到耶路撒冷看见城，就为他哀哭，

chapters.en: and said, “If you, even you, had only known on this day what would bring you peace—but now it is hidden from your eyes.
chapters.zh: 说，巴不得你在这日子，知道关系你平安的事。无奈这事现在是隐藏的，叫你的眼看不出来。

chapters.en: The days will come upon you when your enemies will build an embankment against you and encircle you and hem you in on every side.
chapters.zh: 因为日子将到，你的仇敌必筑起土垒，周围环绕你，四面困住你，

chapters.en: They will dash you to the ground, you and the children within your walls. They will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognize the time of God’s coming to you.”
chapters.zh: 并要扫灭你，和你里头的儿女，连一块石头也不留在石头上。因你不知道眷顾你的时候。

chapters.en: When Jesus entered the temple courts, he began to drive out those who were selling.
chapters.zh: 耶稣进了殿，赶出里头作买卖的人，

chapters.en: “It is written,” he said to them, “ ‘My house will be a house of prayer’; but you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”
chapters.zh: 对他们说，经上说，我的殿，必作祷告的殿。你们倒使它成为贼窝了。

chapters.en: Every day he was teaching at the temple. But the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the leaders among the people were trying to kill him.
chapters.zh: 耶稣天天在殿里教训人。祭司长，和文士，与百姓的尊长，都想要杀他。

chapters.en: Yet they could not find any way to do it, because all the people hung on his words.
chapters.zh: 但寻不出法子来，因为百姓都侧耳听他。

chapters.en: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the good news, the chief priests and the teachers of the law, together with the elders, came up to him.
chapters.zh: 有一天耶稣在殿里教训百姓，讲福音的时候，祭司长和文士并长老上前来，

chapters.en: “Tell us by what authority you are doing these things,” they said. “Who gave you this authority?”
chapters.zh: 问他说，你告诉我们，你仗着什么权柄作这些事？给你这权柄的是谁呢？

chapters.en: He replied, “I will also ask you a question. Tell me:
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说，我也要问你们一句话。你们且告诉我。

chapters.en: John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or of human origin?”
chapters.zh: 约翰的洗礼，是从天上来的？是从人间来的呢？

chapters.en: They discussed it among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask, ‘Why didn’t you believe him?’
chapters.zh: 他们彼此商议说，我们若说从天上来，他必说你们为什么不信他呢？

chapters.en: But if we say, ‘Of human origin,’ all the people will stone us, because they are persuaded that John was a prophet.”
chapters.zh: 若说从人间来，百姓都要用石头打死我们。因为他们信约翰是先知。

chapters.en: So they answered, “We don’t know where it was from.”
chapters.zh: 于是回答说，不知道是从哪里来的。

chapters.en: Jesus said, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，我也不告诉你们，我仗着什么权柄作这些事。

chapters.en: He went on to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it to some farmers and went away for a long time.
chapters.zh: 耶稣就设比喻，对百姓说，有人栽了一个葡萄园，租给园户，就往外国去住了许久。

chapters.en: At harvest time he sent a servant to the tenants so they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
chapters.zh: 到了时候，打发一个仆人到园户那里去，叫他们把园中当纳的果子交给他。园户竟打了他，叫他空手回去。

chapters.en: He sent another servant, but that one also they beat and treated shamefully and sent away empty-handed.
chapters.zh: 又打发一个仆人去。他们也打了他，并且凌辱他，叫他空手回去。

chapters.en: He sent still a third, and they wounded him and threw him out.
chapters.zh: 又打发第三个仆人去。他们也打伤了他，把他推出去了。

chapters.en: “Then the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my son, whom I love; perhaps they will respect him.’
chapters.zh: 园主说，我怎么办呢？我要打发我的爱子去。或者他们尊敬他。

chapters.en: “But when the tenants saw him, they talked the matter over. ‘This is the heir,’ they said. ‘Let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
chapters.zh: 不料，园户看见他，就彼此商量说，这是承受产业的。我们杀他吧，使产业归于我们。

chapters.en: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. “What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
chapters.zh: 于是把他推出葡萄园外杀了。这样，葡萄园的主人，要怎样处治他们呢？

chapters.en: He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.”When the people heard this, they said, “God forbid!”
chapters.zh: 他要来除灭这些园户，将葡萄园转给别人。听见的人说，这是万不可的。

chapters.en: Jesus looked directly at them and asked, “Then what is the meaning of that which is written: “ ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’?
chapters.zh: 耶稣看着他们说，经上记着，匠人所弃的石头，已作了房角的头块石头。这是什么意思呢？

chapters.en: Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces; anyone on whom it falls will be crushed.”
chapters.zh: 凡掉在那石头上的，必要跌碎。那石头掉在谁的身上，就要把谁砸得稀烂。

chapters.en: The teachers of the law and the chief priests looked for a way to arrest him immediately, because they knew he had spoken this parable against them. But they were afraid of the people.
chapters.zh: 文士和祭司长，看出这比喻是指着他们说的，当时就想要下手拿他。只是惧怕百姓。

chapters.en: Keeping a close watch on him, they sent spies, who pretended to be sincere. They hoped to catch Jesus in something he said, so that they might hand him over to the power and authority of the governor.
chapters.zh: 于是窥探耶稣，打发奸细装作好人，要在他的话上得把柄，好将他交在巡抚的政权之下。

chapters.en: So the spies questioned him: “Teacher, we know that you speak and teach what is right, and that you do not show partiality but teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.
chapters.zh: 奸细就问耶稣说，夫子，我们晓得你所讲所传都是正道，也不取人的外貌，乃是诚诚实实传神的道。

chapters.en: Is it right for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
chapters.zh: 我们纳税给该撒，可以不可以。

chapters.en: He saw through their duplicity and said to them,
chapters.zh: 耶稣看出他们的诡诈，就对他们说，

chapters.en: “Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?”“Caesar’s,” they replied.
chapters.zh: 拿一个银钱来给我看。这像和这号是谁的。他们说，是该撒的。

chapters.en: He said to them, “Then give back to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，这样，该撒的物当归给该撒，神的物当归给神。

chapters.en: They were unable to trap him in what he had said there in public. And astonished by his answer, they became silent.
chapters.zh: 他们当着百姓，在这话上得不着把柄。又希奇他的应对，就闭口无言了。

chapters.en: Some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus with a question.
chapters.zh: 撒都该人常说没有复活的事。有几个来问耶稣说，

chapters.en: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man must marry the widow and raise up offspring for his brother.
chapters.zh: 夫子，摩西为我们写着说，人若有妻无子就死了，他兄弟当娶他的妻，为哥哥生子立后。

chapters.en: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married a woman and died childless.
chapters.zh: 有弟兄七人。第一个娶了妻，没有孩子死了。

chapters.en: The second
chapters.zh: 第二个，第三个，也娶过她。

chapters.en: and then the third married her, and in the same way the seven died, leaving no children.
chapters.zh: 那七个人，都娶过她，没有留下孩子就死了。

chapters.en: Finally, the woman died too.
chapters.zh: 后来妇人也死了。

chapters.en: Now then, at the resurrection whose wife will she be, since the seven were married to her?”
chapters.zh: 这样当复活的时候，她是哪一个的妻子呢？因为他们七个人都娶过她。

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “The people of this age marry and are given in marriage.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，这世界的人，有娶有嫁。

chapters.en: But those who are considered worthy of taking part in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage,
chapters.zh: 惟有算为配得那世界，与从死里复活的人，也不娶也不嫁。

chapters.en: and they can no longer die; for they are like the angels. They are God’s children, since they are children of the resurrection.
chapters.zh: 因为他们不能再死。和天使一样。既是复活的人，就为神的儿子。

chapters.en: But in the account of the burning bush, even Moses showed that the dead rise, for he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
chapters.zh: 至于死人复活，摩西在荆棘篇上，称主是亚伯拉罕的神，以撒的神，雅各的神，就指示明白了。

chapters.en: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to him all are alive.”
chapters.zh: 神原不是死人的神，乃是活人的神。因为在他那里，人都是活的。（那里或作看来）

chapters.en: Some of the teachers of the law responded, “Well said, teacher!”
chapters.zh: 有几个文士说，夫子，你说得好。

chapters.en: And no one dared to ask him any more questions.
chapters.zh: 以后他们不敢再问他什么。

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to them, “Why is it said that the Messiah is the son of David?
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说，人怎么说基督是大卫的子孙呢？

chapters.en: David himself declares in the Book of Psalms: “ ‘The Lord said to my Lord: “Sit at my right hand
chapters.zh: 诗篇上，大卫自己说，主对我主说，你坐在我的右边，

chapters.en: until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.” ’
chapters.zh: 等我使你仇敌作你的脚凳。

chapters.en: David calls him ‘Lord.’ How then can he be his son?”
chapters.zh: 大卫既称他为主，他怎么又是大卫的子孙呢？

chapters.en: While all the people were listening, Jesus said to his disciples,
chapters.zh: 众百姓听的时候，耶稣对门徒说，

chapters.en: “Beware of the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in flowing robes and love to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces and have the most important seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.
chapters.zh: 你们要防备文士。他们好穿长衣游行，喜爱人在街市上问他们安，又喜爱会堂里的高位，筵席上的首座。

chapters.en: They devour widows’ houses and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will be punished most severely.”
chapters.zh: 他们侵吞寡妇的家产，假意作很长的祷告。这些人要受更重的刑罚。

chapters.en: As Jesus looked up, he saw the rich putting their gifts into the temple treasury.
chapters.zh: 耶稣抬头观看，见财主把捐项投在库里。

chapters.en: He also saw a poor widow put in two very small copper coins.
chapters.zh: 又见一个穷寡妇，投了两个小钱。

chapters.en: “Truly I tell you,” he said, “this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
chapters.zh: 就说，我实在告诉你们。这穷寡妇，所投的比众人还多。

chapters.en: All these people gave their gifts out of their wealth; but she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on.”
chapters.zh: 因为众人都是自己有余，拿出来投在捐项里。但这寡妇是自己不足，把他一切养生的都投上了。

chapters.en: Some of his disciples were remarking about how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and with gifts dedicated to God. But Jesus said,
chapters.zh: 有人谈论圣殿，是用美石和供物妆饰的。

chapters.en: “As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another; every one of them will be thrown down.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣就说，论到你们所看见的这一切，将来日子到了，在这里没有一块石头留在石头上，不被拆毁了。

chapters.en: “Teacher,” they asked, “when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?”
chapters.zh: 他们问他说，夫子，什么时候有这事呢？这事将到的时候，有什么预兆呢？

chapters.en: He replied: “Watch out that you are not deceived. For many will come in my name, claiming, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Do not follow them.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说，你们要谨慎，不要受迷惑，因为将来有好些人冒我的名来，说，我是基督，又说，时候近了，你们不要跟从他们。

chapters.en: When you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be frightened. These things must happen first, but the end will not come right away.”
chapters.zh: 你们听见打仗和扰乱的事，不要惊惶，因为这些事必须先有，只是末期不能立时就到。

chapters.en: Then he said to them: “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
