chapters.zh: 这话是因他们曾看见以弗所人特罗非摩，同保罗在城里，以为保罗带他进了殿。

chapters.en: The whole city was aroused, and the people came running from all directions. Seizing Paul, they dragged him from the temple, and immediately the gates were shut.
chapters.zh: 合城都震动，百姓一齐跑来，拿住保罗，拉他出殿，殿门立刻都关了。

chapters.en: While they were trying to kill him, news reached the commander of the Roman troops that the whole city of Jerusalem was in an uproar.
chapters.zh: 他们正想要杀他，有人报信给营里的千夫长说，耶路撒冷合城都乱了。

chapters.en: He at once took some officers and soldiers and ran down to the crowd. When the rioters saw the commander and his soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
chapters.zh: 千夫长立时带着兵丁，和几个百夫长，跑下去到他们那里。他们见了千夫长和兵丁，就止住不打保罗。

chapters.en: The commander came up and arrested him and ordered him to be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.
chapters.zh: 于是千夫长上前拿住他，吩咐用两条铁链捆锁。又问他是什么人，作的是什么事。

chapters.en: Some in the crowd shouted one thing and some another, and since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be taken into the barracks.
chapters.zh: 众人有喊叫这个的，有喊叫那个的。千夫长因为这样乱嚷，得不着实情，就吩咐人将保罗带进营楼去。

chapters.en: When Paul reached the steps, the violence of the mob was so great he had to be carried by the soldiers.
chapters.zh: 到了台阶上，众人挤得凶猛，兵丁只得将保罗抬起来。

chapters.en: The crowd that followed kept shouting, “Get rid of him!”
chapters.zh: 众人跟在后面，喊着说，除掉他。

chapters.en: As the soldiers were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, “May I say something to you?” “Do you speak Greek?” he replied.
chapters.zh: 将要带他进营楼，保罗对千夫长说，我对你说句话，可以不可以？他说，你懂得希利尼话吗？

chapters.en: “Aren’t you the Egyptian who started a revolt and led four thousand terrorists out into the wilderness some time ago?”
chapters.zh: 你莫非是从前作乱，带领四千凶徒，往旷野去的那埃及人吗？

chapters.en: Paul answered, “I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Please let me speak to the people.”
chapters.zh: 保罗说，我本是犹太人，生在基利家的大数，并不是无名小城的人，求你准我对百姓说话。

chapters.en: After receiving the commander’s permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. When they were all silent, he said to them in Aramaic :
chapters.zh: 千夫长准了，保罗就站在台阶上，向百姓摆手，他们都静默无声，保罗便用希伯来话对他们说。

chapters.en: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense.”
chapters.zh: 诸位父兄请听，我现在对你们分诉。

chapters.en: When they heard him speak to them in Aramaic, they became very quiet. Then Paul said:
chapters.zh: 众人听他说的是希伯来话，就更加安静了。

chapters.en: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city. I studied under Gamaliel and was thoroughly trained in the law of our ancestors. I was just as zealous for God as any of you are today.
chapters.zh: 保罗说，我原是犹太人，生在基利家的大数，长在这城里，在迦玛列门下，按着我们祖宗严紧的律法受教，热心事奉神，象你们众人今日一样。

chapters.en: I persecuted the followers of this Way to their death, arresting both men and women and throwing them into prison,
chapters.zh: 我也曾逼迫奉这道的人，直到死地，无论男女都锁拿下监。

chapters.en: as the high priest and all the Council can themselves testify. I even obtained letters from them to their associates in Damascus, and went there to bring these people as prisoners to Jerusalem to be punished.
chapters.zh: 这是大祭司和众长老都可以给我作见证的。我又领了他们达与弟兄的书信，往大马色去，要把在那里奉这道的人锁拿，带到耶路撒冷受刑。

chapters.en: “About noon as I came near Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.
chapters.zh: 我将到大马色，正走的时候，约在晌午，忽然从天上发大光，四面照着我。

chapters.en: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul! Saul! Why do you persecute me?’
chapters.zh: 我就仆倒在地，听见有声音对我说，扫罗，扫罗，你为什么逼迫我。

chapters.en: “ ‘Who are you, Lord?’ I asked. “ ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ he replied.
chapters.zh: 我回答说，主阿，你是谁？他说，我就是你所逼迫的拿撒勒人耶稣。

chapters.en: My companions saw the light, but they did not understand the voice of him who was speaking to me.
chapters.zh: 与我同行的人，看见了那光，却没有听明那位对我说话的声音。

chapters.en: “ ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ I asked. “ ‘Get up,’ the Lord said, ‘and go into Damascus. There you will be told all that you have been assigned to do.’
chapters.zh: 我说，主阿，我当作什么。主说，起来，进大马色去，在那里要将所派你作的一切事，告诉你。

chapters.en: My companions led me by the hand into Damascus, because the brilliance of the light had blinded me.
chapters.zh: 我因那光的荣耀，不能看见，同行的人，就拉着我手进了大马色。

chapters.en: “A man named Ananias came to see me. He was a devout observer of the law and highly respected by all the Jews living there.
chapters.zh: 那里有一个人，名叫亚拿尼亚，按着律法是虔诚人，为一切住在那里的犹太人所称赞。

chapters.en: He stood beside me and said, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ And at that very moment I was able to see him.
chapters.zh: 他来见我，站在旁边，对我说，兄弟扫罗，你可以看见。我当时往上一看，就看见了他。

chapters.en: “Then he said: ‘The God of our ancestors has chosen you to know his will and to see the Righteous One and to hear words from his mouth.
chapters.zh: 他又说，我们祖宗的神，拣选了你，叫你明白他的旨意，又得见那义者，听他口中所出的声音。

chapters.en: You will be his witness to all people of what you have seen and heard.
chapters.zh: 因为你要将所看见的，所听见的，对着万人为他作见证。

chapters.en: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized and wash your sins away, calling on his name.’
chapters.zh: 现在你为什么耽延呢？起来，求告他的名受洗，洗去你的罪。

chapters.en: “When I returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance
chapters.zh: 后来我回到耶路撒冷，在殿里祷告的时候，魂游象外，

chapters.en: and saw the Lord speaking to me. ‘Quick!’ he said. ‘Leave Jerusalem immediately, because the people here will not accept your testimony about me.’
chapters.zh: 看见主向我说，你赶紧的离开耶路撒冷，不可迟延，因你为我作的见证，这里的人，必不领受。

chapters.en: “ ‘Lord,’ I replied, ‘these people know that I went from one synagogue to another to imprison and beat those who believe in you.
chapters.zh: 我就说，主阿，他们知道我从前把信你的人，收在监里，又在各会堂里鞭打他们。

chapters.en: And when the blood of your martyr Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and guarding the clothes of those who were killing him.’
chapters.zh: 并且你的见证人司提反，被害流血的时候，我也站在旁边欢喜。又看守害死他之人的衣裳。

chapters.en: “Then the Lord said to me, ‘Go; I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’ ”
chapters.zh: 主向我说，你去吧。我要差你远远地往外邦人那里去。

chapters.en: The crowd listened to Paul until he said this. Then they raised their voices and shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He’s not fit to live!”
chapters.zh: 众人听他说到这句话，就高声说，这样的人，从世上除掉他吧。他是不当活着的。

chapters.en: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and flinging dust into the air,
chapters.zh: 众人喧嚷，摔掉衣裳，把尘土向空中扬起来。

chapters.en: the commander ordered that Paul be taken into the barracks. He directed that he be flogged and interrogated in order to find out why the people were shouting at him like this.
chapters.zh: 千夫长就吩咐将保罗带进营楼去，叫人用鞭子拷问他，要知道他们向他这样喧嚷，是为什么缘故。

chapters.en: As they stretched him out to flog him, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it legal for you to flog a Roman citizen who hasn’t even been found guilty?”
chapters.zh: 刚用皮条捆上，保罗对旁边站着的百夫长说，人是罗马人，又没有定罪，你们就鞭打他，有这个例吗？

chapters.en: When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and reported it. “What are you going to do?” he asked. “This man is a Roman citizen.”
chapters.zh: 百夫长听见这话，就去见千夫长，告诉他说，你要作什么？这人是罗马人。

chapters.en: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
chapters.zh: 千夫长就来问保罗说，你告诉我，你是罗马人吗？保罗说，是。

chapters.en: Then the commander said, “I had to pay a lot of money for my citizenship.” “But I was born a citizen,” Paul replied.
chapters.zh: 千夫长说，我用许多银子，才入了罗马的民籍。保罗说，我生来就是。

chapters.en: Those who were about to interrogate him withdrew immediately. The commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put Paul, a Roman citizen, in chains.
chapters.zh: 于是那些要拷问保罗的人，就离开他去了。千夫长既知道他是罗马人，又因为捆绑了他，也害怕了。

chapters.en: The commander wanted to find out exactly why Paul was being accused by the Jews. So the next day he released him and ordered the chief priests and all the members of the Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul and had him stand before them.
chapters.zh: 第二天，千夫长为要知道犹太人控告保罗的实情，便解开他，吩咐祭司长和全公会的人，都聚集，将保罗带下来，叫他站在他们面前。

chapters.en: Paul looked straight at the Sanhedrin and said, “My brothers, I have fulfilled my duty to God in all good conscience to this day.”
chapters.zh: 保罗定睛看着公会的人，说，弟兄们，我在神面前行事为人，都是凭着良心，直到今日。

chapters.en: At this the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.
chapters.zh: 大祭司亚拿尼亚，就吩咐旁边站着的人打他的嘴。

chapters.en: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit there to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck!”
chapters.zh: 保罗对他说，你这粉饰的墙。神要打你。你坐堂为的是按律法审问我，你竟违背律法，吩咐人打我吗？

chapters.en: Those who were standing near Paul said, “How dare you insult God’s high priest!”
chapters.zh: 站在旁边的人说，你辱骂神的大祭司吗？

chapters.en: Paul replied, “Brothers, I did not realize that he was the high priest; for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’ ”
chapters.zh: 保罗说，弟兄们，我不晓得他是大祭司。经上记着说，不可毁谤你百姓的官长。

chapters.en: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and the others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, “My brothers, I am a Pharisee, descended from Pharisees. I stand on trial because of the hope of the resurrection of the dead.”
chapters.zh: 保罗看出大众，一半是撒都该人，一半是法利赛人，就在公会中大声说，弟兄们，我是法利赛人，也是法利赛人的子孙。我现在受审问，是为盼望死人复活。

chapters.en: When he said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
chapters.zh: 说了这话，法利赛人和撒都该人，就争论起来，会众分为两党。

chapters.en: (The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, and that there are neither angels nor spirits, but the Pharisees believe all these things.)
chapters.zh: 因为撒都该人说，没有复活，也没有天使，和鬼魂，法利赛人却说，两样都有。

chapters.en: There was a great uproar, and some of the teachers of the law who were Pharisees stood up and argued vigorously. “We find nothing wrong with this man,” they said. “What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”
chapters.zh: 于是大大地喧嚷起来。有几个法利赛党的文士站起来，争辩说，我们看不出这人有什么恶处，倘若有鬼魂，或是天使，对他说过话，怎么样呢？

chapters.en: The dispute became so violent that the commander was afraid Paul would be torn to pieces by them. He ordered the troops to go down and take him away from them by force and bring him into the barracks.
chapters.zh: 那时大起争吵，千夫长恐怕保罗被他们扯碎了，就吩咐兵丁下去，把他从众人当中抢出来，带进营楼去。

chapters.en: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Take courage! As you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome.”
chapters.zh: 当夜，主站在保罗旁边说，放心吧，你怎样在耶路撒冷为我作见证，也必怎样在罗马为我作见证。

chapters.en: The next morning some Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
chapters.zh: 到了天亮，犹太人同谋起誓，说，若不先杀保罗，就不吃不喝。

chapters.en: More than forty men were involved in this plot.
chapters.zh: 这样同心起誓的，有四十多人。

chapters.en: They went to the chief priests and the elders and said, “We have taken a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.
chapters.zh: 他们来见祭司长和长老说，我们已经起了一个大誓，若不先杀保罗，就不吃什么。

chapters.en: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him before you on the pretext of wanting more accurate information about his case. We are ready to kill him before he gets here.”
chapters.zh: 现在你们和公会要知会千夫长，叫他带下保罗到你们这里来，假作要详细察考他的事。我们已经预备好了，不等他来到跟前就杀他。

chapters.en: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard of this plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.
chapters.zh: 保罗的外甥，听见他们设下埋伏，就来到营楼里告诉保罗。

chapters.en: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”
chapters.zh: 保罗请一个百夫长来，说，你领这少年人去见千夫长，他有事告诉他。

chapters.en: So he took him to the commander. The centurion said, “Paul, the prisoner, sent for me and asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you.”
chapters.zh: 于是把他领去见千夫长说，被囚的保罗请我到他那里，求我领这少年人来见你。他有事告诉你。

chapters.en: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside and asked, “What is it you want to tell me?”
chapters.zh: 千夫长就拉着他的手，走到一旁，私下问他说，你有什么事告诉我呢？

chapters.en: He said: “Some Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul before the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of wanting more accurate information about him.
chapters.zh: 他说，犹太人已经约定，要求你明天带下保罗到公会里去，假作要详细查问他的事。

chapters.en: Don’t give in to them, because more than forty of them are waiting in ambush for him. They have taken an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him. They are ready now, waiting for your consent to their request.”
chapters.zh: 你切不要随从他们，因为他们有四十多人埋伏，已经起誓，说，若不先杀保罗，就不吃不喝。现在预备好了，只等你应允。

chapters.en: The commander dismissed the young man with this warning: “Don’t tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”
chapters.zh: 于是千夫长打发少年人走，嘱咐他说，不要告诉人你将这事报给我了。

chapters.en: Then he called two of his centurions and ordered them, “Get ready a detachment of two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea at nine tonight.
chapters.zh: 千夫长便叫了两个百夫长来，说，预备步兵二百，马兵七十，长枪手二百，今夜亥初往该撒利亚去。

chapters.en: Provide horses for Paul so that he may be taken safely to Governor Felix.”
chapters.zh: 也要预备牲口叫保罗骑上，护送到巡抚腓力斯那里去。

chapters.en: He wrote a letter as follows:
chapters.zh: 千夫长又写了文书，

chapters.en: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.
chapters.zh: 大略说，革老丢吕西亚，请巡抚腓力斯大人安。

chapters.en: This man was seized by the Jews and they were about to kill him, but I came with my troops and rescued him, for I had learned that he is a Roman citizen.
chapters.zh: 这人被犹太人拿住，将要杀害，我得知他是罗马人，就带兵丁下去救他出来。

chapters.en: I wanted to know why they were accusing him, so I brought him to their Sanhedrin.
chapters.zh: 因要知道他们告他的缘故，我就带他下到他们的公会去。

chapters.en: I found that the accusation had to do with questions about their law, but there was no charge against him that deserved death or imprisonment.
chapters.zh: 便查知他被告，是因他们律法的辩论，并没有什么该死该绑的罪名。

chapters.en: When I was informed of a plot to be carried out against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also ordered his accusers to present to you their case against him.
chapters.zh: 后来有人把要害他的计谋告诉我，我就立时解他到你那里去，又吩咐告他的人，在你面前告他。（有古卷在此有愿你平安）

chapters.en: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul with them during the night and brought him as far as Antipatris.
chapters.zh: 于是兵丁照所吩咐他们的，将保罗夜里带到安提帕底。

chapters.en: The next day they let the cavalry go on with him, while they returned to the barracks.
chapters.zh: 第二天，让马兵护送，他们就回营楼去。

chapters.en: When the cavalry arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
chapters.zh: 马兵来到该撒利亚，把文书呈给巡抚，便叫保罗站在他面前。

chapters.en: The governor read the letter and asked what province he was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,
chapters.zh: 巡抚看了文书，问保罗是那省的人，既晓得他是基利家人，

chapters.en: he said, “I will hear your case when your accusers get here.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s palace.
chapters.zh: 就说，等告你的人来到，我要细听你的事，便吩咐人把他看守在希律的衙门里。

chapters.en: Five days later the high priest Ananias went down to Caesarea with some of the elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, and they brought their charges against Paul before the governor.
chapters.zh: 过了五天，大祭司亚拿尼亚，同几个长老，和一个辩士帖土罗，下来，向巡抚控告保罗。

chapters.en: When Paul was called in, Tertullus presented his case before Felix: “We have enjoyed a long period of peace under you, and your foresight has brought about reforms in this nation.
chapters.zh: 保罗被提了来，帖土罗就告他说，

chapters.en: Everywhere and in every way, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with profound gratitude.
chapters.zh: 腓力斯大人，我们因你得以大享太平，并且这一国的弊病，因着你的先见，得以更正了。我们随时随地，满心感谢不尽。

chapters.en: But in order not to weary you further, I would request that you be kind enough to hear us briefly.
chapters.zh: 惟恐多说，你嫌烦絮，只求你宽容听我们说几句话。

chapters.en: “We have found this man to be a troublemaker, stirring up riots among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the Nazarene sect
chapters.zh: 我们看这个人，如同瘟疫一般，是鼓动普天下众犹太人生乱的，又是拿撒勒教党里的一个头目。

chapters.en: and even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.By
chapters.zh: 连圣殿他也想要污秽。我们把他捉住了。（有古卷在此有要按我们的律法审问。

chapters.en: But the commander, Lysias, came and with the use of much force snatched him from our hands and ordered his accusers to come before you.
chapters.zh: 不料千夫长吕西亚前来甚是强横从我们手中把他夺去，吩咐告他的人到你这里来）。

chapters.en: examining him yourself you will be able to learn the truth about all these charges we are bringing against him.”
chapters.zh: 你自己究问他，就可以知道我们告他的一切事了。

chapters.en: The other Jews joined in the accusation, asserting that these things were true.
chapters.zh: 众犹太人也随着告他说，事情诚然是这样。

chapters.en: When the governor motioned for him to speak, Paul replied: “I know that for a number of years you have been a judge over this nation; so I gladly make my defense.
chapters.zh: 巡抚点头叫保罗说话，他就说，我知道你在这国里断事多年，所以我乐意为自己分诉。

chapters.en: You can easily verify that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
chapters.zh: 你查问就可以知道，从我上耶路撒冷礼拜，到今日，不过有十二天。

chapters.en: My accusers did not find me arguing with anyone at the temple, or stirring up a crowd in the synagogues or anywhere else in the city.
chapters.zh: 他们并没有看见我在殿里，或是在会堂里，或是在城里，和人辩论，耸动众人。

chapters.en: And they cannot prove to you the charges they are now making against me.
chapters.zh: 他们现在所告我的事，并不能对你证实了。

chapters.en: However, I admit that I worship the God of our ancestors as a follower of the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that is in accordance with the Law and that is written in the Prophets,
chapters.zh: 但有一件事，我向你承认，就是他们所称为异端的道，我正按着那道事奉我祖宗的神，又信合乎律法的，和先知书上一切所记载的。

chapters.en: and I have the same hope in God as these men themselves have, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
chapters.zh: 并且靠着神，盼望死人，无论善恶，都要复活，就是他们自己也有这个盼望。

chapters.en: So I strive always to keep my conscience clear before God and man.
chapters.zh: 我因此自己勉励，对神，对人，常存无亏的良心。

chapters.en: “After an absence of several years, I came to Jerusalem to bring my people gifts for the poor and to present offerings.
chapters.zh: 过了几年，我带着周济本国的捐项和供献的物上去。

chapters.en: I was ceremonially clean when they found me in the temple courts doing this. There was no crowd with me, nor was I involved in any disturbance.
chapters.zh: 正献的时候，他们看见我在殿里已经洁净了，并没有聚众，也没有吵嚷。惟有几个从亚西亚来的犹太人。

chapters.en: But there are some Jews from the province of Asia, who ought to be here before you and bring charges if they have anything against me.
chapters.zh: 他们若有告我的事，就应当到你面前来告我。

chapters.en: Or these who are here should state what crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin—
chapters.zh: 即或不然，这些人，若看出我站在公会前，有妄为的地方，他们自己也可以说明。

chapters.en: unless it was this one thing I shouted as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’ ”
chapters.zh: 纵然有，也不过一句话，就是我站在他们中间大声说，我今日在你们面前受审，是为死人复活的道理

chapters.en: Then Felix, who was well acquainted with the Way, adjourned the proceedings. “When Lysias the commander comes,” he said, “I will decide your case.”
chapters.zh: 腓力斯本是详细晓得这道，就支吾他们说，且等千夫长吕西亚下来，我要审断你们的事。

chapters.en: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard but to give him some freedom and permit his friends to take care of his needs.
chapters.zh: 于是吩咐百夫长看守保罗并且宽待他，也不拦阻他的亲友来供给他。

chapters.en: Several days later Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He sent for Paul and listened to him as he spoke about faith in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 过了几天，腓力斯和他夫人犹太的女子土西拉，一同来到，就叫了保罗来，听他讲论信基督耶稣的道。

chapters.en: As Paul talked about righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and said, “That’s enough for now! You may leave. When I find it convenient, I will send for you.”
chapters.zh: 保罗讲论公义，节制，和将来的审判，腓力斯甚觉恐惧，说，你暂且去吧，等我得便再叫你来。

chapters.en: At the same time he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe, so he sent for him frequently and talked with him.
chapters.zh: 腓力斯又指望保罗送他银钱，所以屡次叫他来，和他谈论。

chapters.en: When two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, but because Felix wanted to grant a favor to the Jews, he left Paul in prison.
chapters.zh: 过了两年，波求非斯都接了腓力斯的任，腓力斯要讨犹太人的喜欢，就留保罗在监里。

chapters.en: Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,
chapters.zh: 非斯都到了任，过了三天，就从该撒利亚上耶路撒冷去。

chapters.en: where the chief priests and the Jewish leaders appeared before him and presented the charges against Paul.
chapters.zh: 祭司长，和犹太人的首领，向他控告保罗，

chapters.en: They requested Festus, as a favor to them, to have Paul transferred to Jerusalem, for they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.
chapters.zh: 又央告他，求他的情，将保罗提到耶路撒冷来。他们要在路上埋伏杀害他。

chapters.en: Festus answered, “Paul is being held at Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.
chapters.zh: 非斯都却回答说，保罗押在该撒利亚，我自己快要往那里去。

chapters.en: Let some of your leaders come with me, and if the man has done anything wrong, they can press charges against him there.”
chapters.zh: 又说，你们中间有权势的人，与我一同下去，那人若有什么不是，就可以告他。

chapters.en: After spending eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he convened the court and ordered that Paul be brought before him.
chapters.zh: 非斯都在他们那里，住了不过十天八天，就下该撒利亚去。第二天坐堂，吩咐将保罗提上来。

chapters.en: When Paul came in, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him. They brought many serious charges against him, but they could not prove them.
chapters.zh: 保罗来了，那些从耶路撒冷下来的犹太人，周围站着，将许多重大的事控告他，都是不能证实的。

chapters.en: Then Paul made his defense: “I have done nothing wrong against the Jewish law or against the temple or against Caesar.”
chapters.zh: 保罗分诉说，无论犹太人的律法，或是圣殿，或是该撒，我都没有干犯。

chapters.en: Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and stand trial before me there on these charges?”
chapters.zh: 但非斯都要讨犹太人的喜欢，就问保罗说，你愿意上耶路撒冷去，在那里听我审断这事吗？

chapters.en: Paul answered: “I am now standing before Caesar’s court, where I ought to be tried. I have not done any wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
chapters.zh: 保罗说，我站在该撒的堂前，这就是我应当受审的地方。我向犹太人并没有行过什么不义的事，这也是你明明知道的。

chapters.en: If, however, I am guilty of doing anything deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if the charges brought against me by these Jews are not true, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
chapters.zh: 我若行了不义的事，犯了什么该死的罪，就是死，我也不辞。他们所告我的事若都不实，就没有人可以把我交给他们。我要上告于该撒。

chapters.en: After Festus had conferred with his council, he declared: “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!”
chapters.zh: 非斯都和议会商量了，就说，你既上告于该撒，可以往该撒那里去。

chapters.en: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.
chapters.zh: 过了些日子，亚基帕王，和百尼基氏，来到该撒利亚，问非斯都安。

chapters.en: Since they were spending many days there, Festus discussed Paul’s case with the king. He said: “There is a man here whom Felix left as a prisoner.
chapters.zh: 在那里住了多日，非斯都将保罗的事告诉王，说，这里有一个人，是腓力斯留在监里的。

chapters.en: When I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought charges against him and asked that he be condemned.
chapters.zh: 我在耶路撒冷的时候，祭司长和犹太的长老，将他的事禀报了我，求我定他的罪。

chapters.en: “I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand over anyone before they have faced their accusers and have had an opportunity to defend themselves against the charges.
chapters.zh: 我对他们说，无论什么人，被告还没有和原告对质，未得机会分诉所告他的事，就先定他的罪，这不是罗马人的条例。

chapters.en: When they came here with me, I did not delay the case, but convened the court the next day and ordered the man to be brought in.
chapters.zh: 及至他们都来到这里，我就不耽延，第二天便坐堂，吩咐把那人提上来。

chapters.en: When his accusers got up to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.
chapters.zh: 告他的人站着告他。所告的，并没有我所逆料的那等恶事。

chapters.en: Instead, they had some points of dispute with him about their own religion and about a dead man named Jesus who Paul claimed was alive.
chapters.zh: 不过是有几样辩论，为他们自己敬鬼神的事，又为一个人名叫耶稣，是已经死了，保罗却说他是活着的。

chapters.en: I was at a loss how to investigate such matters; so I asked if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial there on these charges.
chapters.zh: 这些事当怎样究问，我心里作难。所以问他说，你愿意上耶路撒冷去，在那里为这些事听审吗？

chapters.en: But when Paul made his appeal to be held over for the Emperor’s decision, I ordered him held until I could send him to Caesar.”
chapters.zh: 但保罗求我留下，他要听皇上审断，我就吩咐把他留下，等我解他到该撒那里去。

chapters.en: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.” He replied, “Tomorrow you will hear him.”
chapters.zh: 亚基帕对非斯都说，我自己也愿听这人辩论。非斯都说，明天你可以听。

chapters.en: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience room with the high-ranking military officers and the prominent men of the city. At the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.
chapters.zh: 第二天，亚基帕和百尼基大张威势而来，同着众千夫长，和城里的尊贵人，进了公厅。非斯都吩咐一声，就有人将保罗带进来。

chapters.en: Festus said: “King Agrippa, and all who are present with us, you see this man! The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him in Jerusalem and here in Caesarea, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
chapters.zh: 非斯都说，亚基帕王，和在这里的诸位阿，你们看这人，就是一切犹太人在耶路撒冷，和这里，曾向我恳求，呼叫说，不可容他再活着。

chapters.en: I found he had done nothing deserving of death, but because he made his appeal to the Emperor I decided to send him to Rome.
chapters.zh: 但我查明他没有犯什么该死的罪。并且他自己上告于皇帝，所以我定意把他解去

chapters.en: But I have nothing definite to write to His Majesty about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that as a result of this investigation I may have something to write.
chapters.zh: 论到这人，我没有确实的事，可以奏明主上。因此我带他到你们面前，也特意带他到你亚基帕王面前，为要在查问之后，有所陈奏。

chapters.en: For I think it is unreasonable to send a prisoner on to Rome without specifying the charges against him.”
chapters.zh: 据我看来，解送囚犯，不指明他的罪案，是不合理的。

chapters.en: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” So Paul motioned with his hand and began his defense:
chapters.zh: 亚基帕对保罗说，准你为自己辩明。于是保罗伸手分诉说，

chapters.en: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today as I make my defense against all the accusations of the Jews,
chapters.zh: 亚基帕王阿，犹太人所告我的一切事，今日得在你面前分诉，实为万幸。

chapters.en: and especially so because you are well acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. Therefore, I beg you to listen to me patiently.
chapters.zh: 更可幸的，是你熟悉犹太人的规矩，和他们的辩论。所以求你耐心听我。

chapters.en: “The Jewish people all know the way I have lived ever since I was a child, from the beginning of my life in my own country, and also in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 我从起初在本国的民中，并在耶路撒冷，自幼为人如何，犹太人都知道。

chapters.en: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I conformed to the strictest sect of our religion, living as a Pharisee.
chapters.zh: 他们若肯作见证，就晓得我从起初，是按着我们教中最严紧的教门，作了法利赛人。

chapters.en: And now it is because of my hope in what God has promised our ancestors that I am on trial today.
chapters.zh: 现在我站在这里受审，是因为指望神向我们祖宗所应许的。

chapters.en: This is the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. King Agrippa, it is because of this hope that these Jews are accusing me.
chapters.zh: 这应许，我们十二个支派昼夜切切地事奉神，都指望得着。王阿，我被犹太人控告，就是因这指望。

chapters.en: Why should any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
chapters.zh: 神叫死人复活，你们为什么看作不可信的呢？

chapters.en: “I too was convinced that I ought to do all that was possible to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
chapters.zh: 从前我自己以为应当多方攻击拿撒勒人耶稣的名。

chapters.en: And that is just what I did in Jerusalem. On the authority of the chief priests I put many of the Lord’s people in prison, and when they were put to death, I cast my vote against them.
chapters.zh: 我在耶路撒冷也曾这样行了。既从祭司长得了权柄，我就把许多圣徒囚在监里。他们被杀，我也出名定案。

chapters.en: Many a time I went from one synagogue to another to have them punished, and I tried to force them to blaspheme. I was so obsessed with persecuting them that I even hunted them down in foreign cities.
chapters.zh: 在各会堂，我屡次用刑，强逼他们说亵渎的话。又分外恼恨他们，甚至追逼他们直到外邦的城邑。

chapters.en: “On one of these journeys I was going to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
chapters.zh: 那时，我领了祭司长的权柄和命令，往大马色去。

chapters.en: About noon, King Agrippa, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, blazing around me and my companions.
chapters.zh: 王阿，我在路上，晌午的时候，看见从天发光，比日头还亮，四面照着我，并与我同行的人。

chapters.en: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me in Aramaic,‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
chapters.zh: 我们都仆倒在地，我就听见有声音，用希伯来话，向我说，扫罗，扫罗，为什么逼迫我。你用脚踢刺是难的。

chapters.en: “Then I asked, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ “ ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.
chapters.zh: 我说，主阿，你是谁。主说，我就是你所逼迫的耶稣。

chapters.en: ‘Now get up and stand on your feet. I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen and will see of me.
chapters.zh: 你起来站着，我特意向你显现，要派你作执事作见证，将你所看见的事，和我将要指示你的事，证明出来。

chapters.en: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them
chapters.zh: 我也要救你脱离百姓和外邦人的手。

chapters.en: to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’
chapters.zh: 我差你到他们那里去，要叫他们的眼睛得开，从黑暗中归向光明，从撒但权下归向神。又因信我，得蒙赦罪，和一切成圣的人同得基业。

chapters.en: “So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the vision from heaven.
chapters.zh: 亚基帕王阿，我故此没有违背那从天上来的异象。

chapters.en: First to those in Damascus, then to those in Jerusalem and in all Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I preached that they should repent and turn to God and demonstrate their repentance by their deeds.
chapters.zh: 先在大马色，后在耶路撒冷，和犹太全地，以及外邦，劝勉他们应当悔改归向神，行事与悔改的心相称。

chapters.en: That is why some Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
chapters.zh: 因此，犹太人在殿里拿住我，想要杀我。

chapters.en: But God has helped me to this very day; so I stand here and testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen—
chapters.zh: 然而我蒙神的帮助，直到今日还站得住，对着尊贵卑贱老幼作见证。所讲的，并不外乎众先知和摩西所说，将来必成的事。

chapters.en: that the Messiah would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, would bring the message of light to his own people and to the Gentiles.”
chapters.zh: 就是基督必须受害，并且因从死里复活，要首先把光明的道，传给百姓和外邦人。

chapters.en: At this point Festus interrupted Paul’s defense. “You are out of your mind, Paul!” he shouted. “Your great learning is driving you insane.”
chapters.zh: 保罗这样分诉，非斯都大声说，保罗，你癫狂了吧。你的学问太大，反叫你癫狂了。

chapters.en: “I am not insane, most excellent Festus,” Paul replied. “What I am saying is true and reasonable.
chapters.zh: 保罗说，非斯都大人，我不是癫狂，我说的乃是真实明白话。

chapters.en: The king is familiar with these things, and I can speak freely to him. I am convinced that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.
chapters.zh: 王也晓得这些事，所以我向王放胆直言，我深信这些事没有一件向王隐藏的。因都不是在背地里作的。

chapters.en: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
chapters.zh: 亚基帕王阿，你信先知吗？我知道你是信的。

chapters.en: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Do you think that in such a short time you can persuade me to be a Christian?”
chapters.zh: 亚基帕对保罗说，你想少微一劝，便叫我作基督徒阿。（或作你这样劝我几乎叫我作基督徒了）。

chapters.en: Paul replied, “Short time or long—I pray to God that not only you but all who are listening to me today may become what I am, except for these chains.”
chapters.zh: 保罗说，无论是少劝，是多劝，我向神所求的，不但你一个人，就是今天一切听我的，都要像我一样，只是不要像我有这些锁链。

chapters.en: The king rose, and with him the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them.
chapters.zh: 于是王，和巡抚，并百尼基，与同坐的人，都起来，

chapters.en: After they left the room, they began saying to one another, “This man is not doing anything that deserves death or imprisonment.”
chapters.zh: 退到里面，彼此谈论说，这人并没有犯什么该死该绑的罪。

chapters.en: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
chapters.zh: 亚基帕又对非斯都说，这人若没有上告于该撒，就可以释放了。

chapters.en: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
chapters.zh: 非斯都既然定规了，叫我们坐船往义大利去，便将保罗，和别的囚犯，交给御营里的一个百夫长，名叫犹流。

chapters.en: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium about to sail for ports along the coast of the province of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
chapters.zh: 有一只亚大米田的船，要沿着亚西亚一带地方的海边走，我们就上了那船开行，有马其顿的帖撒罗尼迦人，亚里达古，和我们同去。

chapters.en: The next day we landed at Sidon; and Julius, in kindness to Paul, allowed him to go to his friends so they might provide for his needs.
chapters.zh: 第二天，到了西顿。犹流宽待保罗，准他往朋友那里去，受他们的照应。

chapters.en: From there we put out to sea again and passed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
chapters.zh: 从那里又开船，因为风不顺，就贴着居比路背风岸行去。

chapters.en: When we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.
chapters.zh: 过了基利家旁非利亚前面的海，就到了吕家的每拉。

chapters.en: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
chapters.zh: 在那里百夫长遇见一只亚力山太的船，要往义大利去，便叫我们上了那船。

chapters.en: We made slow headway for many days and had difficulty arriving off Cnidus. When the wind did not allow us to hold our course, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
chapters.zh: 一连多日，船行得慢，仅仅来到革尼土的对面。因为被风拦阻，就贴着革哩底背风岸，从撒摩尼对面行过。

chapters.en: We moved along the coast with difficulty and came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
chapters.zh: 我们沿岸行走，仅仅来到一个地方，名叫佳澳。离那里不远，有拉西亚城。

chapters.en: Much time had been lost, and sailing had already become dangerous because by now it was after the Day of Atonement. So Paul warned them,
chapters.zh: 走的日子多了，已经过了禁食的节期，行船又危险，保罗就劝众人说，

chapters.en: “Men, I can see that our voyage is going to be disastrous and bring great loss to ship and cargo, and to our own lives also.”
chapters.zh: 众位，我看这次行船，不但货物和船要受伤损，大遭破坏，连我们的性命也难保。

chapters.en: But the centurion, instead of listening to what Paul said, followed the advice of the pilot and of the owner of the ship.
chapters.zh: 但百夫长信从掌船的和船主，不信从保罗所说的。

chapters.en: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided that we should sail on, hoping to reach Phoenix and winter there. This was a harbor in Crete, facing both southwest and northwest.
chapters.zh: 且因在这海口过冬不便，船上的人，就多半说，不如开船离开这地方，或者能到非尼基过冬。非尼基是革哩底的一个海口，一面朝东北，一面朝东南。

chapters.en: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they saw their opportunity; so they weighed anchor and sailed along the shore of Crete.
chapters.zh: 这时微微起了南风，他们以为得意，就起了锚，贴近革哩底行去。

chapters.en: Before very long, a wind of hurricane force, called the Northeaster, swept down from the island.
chapters.zh: 不多几时，狂风从岛上扑下来，那风名叫友拉革罗。

chapters.en: The ship was caught by the storm and could not head into the wind; so we gave way to it and were driven along.
chapters.zh: 船被风抓住，敌不住风，我们就任风刮去。

chapters.en: As we passed to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were hardly able to make the lifeboat secure,
chapters.zh: 贴着一个小岛的背风岸奔行，那岛名叫高大，在那里仅仅收住了小船。

chapters.en: so the men hoisted it aboard. Then they passed ropes under the ship itself to hold it together. Because they were afraid they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and let the ship be driven along.
chapters.zh: 既然把小船拉上来，就用缆索捆绑船底。又恐怕在赛耳底沙滩上搁了浅，就落下篷来，任船飘去。

chapters.en: We took such a violent battering from the storm that the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard.
chapters.zh: 我们被风浪逼得甚急，第二天众人就把货物抛在海里。

chapters.en: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
chapters.zh: 到第三天，他们又亲手把船上的器具抛弃了。

chapters.en: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the storm continued raging, we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
chapters.zh: 太阳和星辰多日不显露，又有狂风大浪催逼，我们得救的指望就都绝了。

chapters.en: After they had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up before them and said: “Men, you should have taken my advice not to sail from Crete; then you would have spared yourselves this damage and loss.
chapters.zh: 众人多日没有吃什么，保罗就出来站在他们中间说，众位，你们本该听我的话，不离开革哩底，免得遭这样的伤损破坏。

chapters.en: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed.
chapters.zh: 现在我还劝你们放心。你们的性命，一个也不失丧，惟独失丧这船。

chapters.en: Last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me
chapters.zh: 因我所属所事奉的神，他的使者昨夜站在我旁边说，

chapters.en: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand trial before Caesar; and God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you.’
chapters.zh: 保罗，不要害怕，你必定站在该撒面前。并且与你同船的人，神都赐给你了。

chapters.en: So keep up your courage, men, for I have faith in God that it will happen just as he told me.
chapters.zh: 所以众位可以放心，我信神，他怎样对我说，事情也要怎样成就。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, we must run aground on some island.”
chapters.zh: 只是我们必要撞在一个岛上。

chapters.en: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea, when about midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
chapters.zh: 到了第十四天夜间，船在亚底亚海，飘来飘去，约到半夜，水手以为渐近旱地，

chapters.en: They took soundings and found that the water was a hundred and twenty feet deep. A short time later they took soundings again and found it was ninety feet deep.
chapters.zh: 就探深浅，探得有十二丈，稍往前行，又探深浅，探得有九丈。

chapters.en: Fearing that we would be dashed against the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight.
chapters.zh: 恐怕撞在石头上，就从船尾抛下四个锚，盼望天亮。

chapters.en: In an attempt to escape from the ship, the sailors let the lifeboat down into the sea, pretending they were going to lower some anchors from the bow.
chapters.zh: 水手想要逃出船去，把小船放在海里，假作要从船头抛锚的样子。

chapters.en: Then Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men stay with the ship, you cannot be saved.”
chapters.zh: 保罗对百夫长和兵丁说，这些人若不等在船上，你们必不能得救。

chapters.en: So the soldiers cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it drift away.
chapters.zh: 于是兵丁砍断小船的绳子，由它飘去。

chapters.en: Just before dawn Paul urged them all to eat. “For the last fourteen days,” he said, “you have been in constant suspense and have gone without food—you haven’t eaten anything.
chapters.zh: 天渐亮的时候保罗劝众人都吃饭，说，你们悬望忍饿不吃什么，已经十四天了。

chapters.en: Now I urge you to take some food. You need it to survive. Not one of you will lose a single hair from his head.”
chapters.zh: 所以我劝你们吃饭，这是关乎你们救命的事。因为你们各人连一根头发，也不至于损坏。

chapters.en: After he said this, he took some bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
chapters.zh: 保罗说了这话，就拿着饼，在众人面前祝谢了神，掰开吃。

chapters.en: They were all encouraged and ate some food themselves.
chapters.zh: 于是他们都放下心，也就吃了。

chapters.en: Altogether there were 276 of us on board.
chapters.zh: 我们在船上的，共有二百七十六个人

chapters.en: When they had eaten as much as they wanted, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
chapters.zh: 他们吃饱了，就把船上的麦子，抛在海里，为要叫船轻一点。

chapters.en: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they saw a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
chapters.zh: 到了天亮，他们不认识那地方，但见一个海湾，有岸可登，就商议能把船拢进去不能。

chapters.en: Cutting loose the anchors, they left them in the sea and at the same time untied the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
chapters.zh: 于是砍断缆索，弃锚在海里，同时也松开舵绳，拉起头篷，顺着风向岸行去。

chapters.en: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was broken to pieces by the pounding of the surf.
chapters.zh: 但遇着两水夹流的地方，就把船搁了浅。船头胶住不动，船尾被浪的猛力冲坏。

chapters.en: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent any of them from swimming away and escaping.
chapters.zh: 兵丁的意思，要把囚犯杀了，恐怕有游水脱逃的。

chapters.en: But the centurion wanted to spare Paul’s life and kept them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
chapters.zh: 但百夫长要救保罗，不准他们任意而行，就吩咐会游水的，跳下水去先上岸。

chapters.en: The rest were to get there on planks or on other pieces of the ship. In this way everyone reached land safely.
chapters.zh: 其余的人，可以用板子，或船上的零碎东西上岸。这样众人都得了救上了岸。

chapters.en: Once safely on shore, we found out that the island was called Malta.
chapters.zh: 我们既已得救，才知道那岛名叫米利大。

chapters.en: The islanders showed us unusual kindness. They built a fire and welcomed us all because it was raining and cold.
chapters.zh: 土人看待我们，有非常的情分，因为当时下雨，天气又冷，就生火，接待我们众人。

chapters.en: Paul gathered a pile of brushwood and, as he put it on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself on his hand.
chapters.zh: 那时保罗拾起一捆柴，放在火上，有一条毒蛇，因为热了出来，咬住他的手。

chapters.en: When the islanders saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer; for though he escaped from the sea, the goddess Justice has not allowed him to live.”
chapters.zh: 土人看见那毒蛇，悬在他手上，就彼此说，这人必是个凶手，虽然从海里救上来，天理还不容他活着。

chapters.en: But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
chapters.zh: 保罗竟把那毒蛇，甩在火里，并没有受伤。

chapters.en: The people expected him to swell up or suddenly fall dead; but after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
chapters.zh: 土人想他必要肿起来，或是忽然仆倒死了。看了多时，见他无害，就转念说，他是个神。

chapters.en: There was an estate nearby that belonged to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us to his home and showed us generous hospitality for three days.
chapters.zh: 离那地方不远，有田产是岛长部百流的。他接纳我们，尽情款待三日。

chapters.en: His father was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him and, after prayer, placed his hands on him and healed him.
chapters.zh: 当时，部百流的父亲，患热病和痢疾躺着。保罗进去，为他祷告，按手在他身上，治好了他。

chapters.en: When this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured.
chapters.zh: 从此，岛上其余的病人，也来得了医治。

chapters.en: They honored us in many ways; and when we were ready to sail, they furnished us with the supplies we needed.
chapters.zh: 他们又多方的尊敬我们。到了开船的时候，也把我们所需用的送到船上。

chapters.en: After three months we put out to sea in a ship that had wintered in the island—it was an Alexandrian ship with the figurehead of the twin gods Castor and Pollux.
chapters.zh: 过了三个月，我们上了亚力山太的船，往前行。这船以丢斯双子为记，是在那海岛过了冬的。

chapters.en: We put in at Syracuse and stayed there three days.
chapters.zh: 到了叙拉古，我们停泊三日。

chapters.en: From there we set sail and arrived at Rhegium. The next day the south wind came up, and on the following day we reached Puteoli.
chapters.zh: 又从那里绕行，来到利基翁。过了一天，起了南风，第二天就来到部丢利。

chapters.en: There we found some brothers and sisters who invited us to spend a week with them. And so we came to Rome.
chapters.zh: 在那里遇见弟兄们，请我们与他们同住了七天。这样我们来到罗马。

chapters.en: The brothers and sisters there had heard that we were coming, and they traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. At the sight of these people Paul thanked God and was encouraged.
chapters.zh: 那里的弟兄们，一听见我们的信息，就出来到亚比乌市，和三馆地方迎接我们。保罗见了他们，就感谢神，放心壮胆。

chapters.en: When we got to Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
chapters.zh: 进了罗马城，（有古卷在此有百夫长把众囚犯交给御营的统领惟有）保罗蒙准，和一个看守他的兵，另住在一处。

chapters.en: Three days later he called together the local Jewish leaders. When they had assembled, Paul said to them: “My brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or against the customs of our ancestors, I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
chapters.zh: 过了三天，保罗请犹太人的首领来。他们来了，就对他们说，弟兄们，我虽没有作什么事干犯本国的百姓，和我们祖宗的规条，却被锁绑，从耶路撒冷解在罗马人的手里。

chapters.en: They examined me and wanted to release me, because I was not guilty of any crime deserving death.
chapters.zh: 他们审问了我，就愿意释放我。因为在我身上，并没有该死的罪。

chapters.en: The Jews objected, so I was compelled to make an appeal to Caesar. I certainly did not intend to bring any charge against my own people.
chapters.zh: 无奈犹太人不服，我不得已，只好上告于该撒。并非有什么事，要控告我本国的百姓。

chapters.en: For this reason I have asked to see you and talk with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
chapters.zh: 因此，我请你们来见面说话。我原为以色列人所指望的，被这链子捆锁。

chapters.en: They replied, “We have not received any letters from Judea concerning you, and none of our people who have come from there has reported or said anything bad about you.
chapters.zh: 他们说，我们并没有接着从犹太来论你的信，也没有弟兄到这里来，报给我们说，你有什么不好处。

chapters.en: But we want to hear what your views are, for we know that people everywhere are talking against this sect.”
chapters.zh: 但我们愿意听你的意见如何。因为这教门，我们晓得是到处被毁谤的。

chapters.en: They arranged to meet Paul on a certain day, and came in even larger numbers to the place where he was staying. He witnessed to them from morning till evening, explaining about the kingdom of God, and from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets he tried to persuade them about Jesus.
chapters.zh: 他们和保罗约定了日子，就有许多人到他的寓处来，保罗从早到晚，对他们讲论这事，证明神国的道，引摩西的律法和先知的书，以耶稣的事，劝勉他们。

chapters.en: Some were convinced by what he said, but others would not believe.
chapters.zh: 他所说的话，有信的，有不信的。

chapters.en: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit spoke the truth to your ancestors when he said through Isaiah the prophet:
chapters.zh: 他们彼此不合，就散了。未散以先，保罗说了一句话，说，圣灵借先知以赛亚，向你们祖宗所说的话，是不错的。

chapters.en: “ ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”
chapters.zh: 他说，你去告诉这百姓说，你们听是要听见，却不明白。看是要看见，却不晓得。

chapters.en: For this people’s heart has become calloused; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts and turn, and I would heal them.’
chapters.zh: 因为这百姓，油蒙了心，耳朵发沉，眼睛闭着。恐怕眼睛看见，耳朵听见，心里明白，回转过来，我就医治他们。

chapters.en: “Therefore I want you to know that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
chapters.zh: 所以你们当知道，神这救恩，如今传给外邦人，他们也必听受。（有古卷在此有，

chapters.en: After he said this, the jews left, arguing vigorously among themselves.
chapters.zh: 保罗说了这话犹太人议论纷纷的就走了）。

chapters.en: For two whole years Paul stayed there in his own rented house and welcomed all who came to see him.
chapters.zh: 保罗在自己所租的房子里，住了足足两年。凡来见他的人，他全都接待，

chapters.en: He proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ—with all boldness and without hindrance!
chapters.zh: 放胆传讲神国的道，将主耶稣基督的事教导人，并没有人禁止。

chapters.en: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle and set apart for the gospel of God—
chapters.zh: 耶稣基督的仆人保罗，奉召为使徒，特派传神的福音。

chapters.en: the gospel he promised beforehand through his prophets in the Holy Scriptures
chapters.zh: 这福音是神从前借众先知，在圣经上所应许的。

chapters.en: regarding his Son, who as to his earthly life was a descendant of David,
chapters.zh: 论到他儿子，我主耶稣基督。按肉体说，是从大卫后裔生的。

chapters.en: and who through the Spirit of holiness was appointed the Son of God in power by his resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
chapters.zh: 按圣善的灵说，因从死里复活，以大能显明是神的儿子。

chapters.en: Through him we received grace and apostleship to call all the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith for his name’s sake.
chapters.zh: 我们从他受了恩惠，并使徒的职分，在万国之中叫人为他的名信服真道。

chapters.en: And you also are among those Gentiles who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 其中也有你们这蒙召属耶稣基督的人。

chapters.en: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be his holy people: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 我写信给你们在罗马为神所爱，奉召作圣徒的众人。愿恩惠平安，从我们的父神，并主耶稣基督，归与你们。

chapters.en: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being reported all over the world.
chapters.zh: 第一，我靠着耶稣基督，为你们众人感谢我的神。因你们的信德传遍了天下。

chapters.en: God, whom I serve in my spirit in preaching the gospel of his Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you
chapters.zh: 我在他儿子福音上，用心灵所事奉的神，可以见证我怎样不住地提到你们，

chapters.en: in my prayers at all times; and I pray that now at last by God’s will the way may be opened for me to come to you.
chapters.zh: 在祷告之间，常常恳求，或者照神的旨意，终能得平坦的道路往你们那里去。

chapters.en: I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to make you strong—
chapters.zh: 因为我切切地想见你们，要把些属灵的恩赐分给你们，使你们可以坚固。

chapters.en: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
chapters.zh: 这样我在你们中间，因你与我彼此的信心，就可以同得安慰。

chapters.en: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that I planned many times to come to you (but have been prevented from doing so until now) in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我不愿意你们不知道，我屡次定意往你们那里去，要在你们中间得些果子，如同在其余的外邦人中一样。只是到如今仍有阻隔。

chapters.en: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.
chapters.zh: 无论是希利尼人，化外人，聪明人，愚拙人，我都欠他们的债。

chapters.en: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
chapters.zh: 所以情愿尽我的力量，将福音也传给你们在罗马的人。

chapters.en: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes: first to the Jew, then to the Gentile.
chapters.zh: 我不以福音为耻。这福音本是神的大能，要救一切相信的，先是犹太人，后是希利尼人。

chapters.en: For in the gospel the righteousness of God is revealed—a righteousness that is by faith from first to last, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”
chapters.zh: 因为神的义，正在这福音上显明出来。这义是本于信以致于信。如经上所记，义人必因信得生。

chapters.en: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness,
chapters.zh: 原来神的忿怒，从天上显明在一切不虔不义的人身上，就是那些行不义阻挡真理的人。

chapters.en: since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
chapters.zh: 神的事情，人所能知道的，原显明在人心里。因为神已经给他们显明。

chapters.en: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse.
chapters.zh: 自从造天地以来，神的永能和神性是明明可知的，虽是眼不能见，但借着所造之物，就可以晓得，叫人无可推诿。

chapters.en: For although they knew God, they neither glorified him as God nor gave thanks to him, but their thinking became futile and their foolish hearts were darkened.
chapters.zh: 因为他们虽然知道神，却不当作神荣耀他，也不感谢他。他们的思念变为虚妄，无知的心就昏暗了。

chapters.en: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools
chapters.zh: 自称为聪明，反成了愚拙，

chapters.en: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images made to look like a mortal human being and birds and animals and reptiles.
chapters.zh: 将不能朽坏之神的荣耀变为偶像，仿佛必朽坏的人，和飞禽走兽昆虫的样式。

chapters.en: Therefore God gave them over in the sinful desires of their hearts to sexual impurity for the degrading of their bodies with one another.
chapters.zh: 所以神任凭他们，逞着心里的情欲行污秽的事，以致彼此玷辱自己的身体。

chapters.en: They exchanged the truth about God for a lie, and worshiped and served created things rather than the Creator—who is forever praised. Amen.
chapters.zh: 他们将神的真实变为虚谎，去敬拜事奉受造之物，不敬奉那造物的主。主乃是可称颂的，直到永远。阿们。

chapters.en: Because of this, God gave them over to shameful lusts. Even their women exchanged natural sexual relations for unnatural ones.
chapters.zh: 因此神任凭他们放纵可羞耻的情欲。他们的女人，把顺性的用处，变为逆性的用处。

chapters.en: In the same way the men also abandoned natural relations with women and were inflamed with lust for one another. Men committed shameful acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.
chapters.zh: 男人也是如此，弃了女人顺性的用处，欲火攻心，彼此贪恋，男和男行可羞耻的事，就在自己身上受这妄为当得的报应。

chapters.en: Furthermore, just as they did not think it worthwhile to retain the knowledge of God, so God gave them over to a depraved mind, so that they do what ought not to be done.
chapters.zh: 他们既然故意不认识神，神就任凭他们存邪僻的心行那些不合理的事，

chapters.en: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit and malice. They are gossips,
chapters.zh: 装满了各样不义，邪恶，贪婪，恶毒（或作阴毒）。满心是嫉妒，凶杀，争竞，诡诈，毒恨。

chapters.en: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant and boastful; they invent ways of doing evil; they disobey their parents;
chapters.zh: 又是谗毁的，背后说人的，怨恨神的（或作被神所憎恶的），侮慢人的，狂傲的，自夸的，捏造恶事的，违背父母的，

chapters.en: they have no understanding, no fidelity, no love, no mercy.
chapters.zh: 无知的，背约的，无亲情的，不怜悯人的。

chapters.en: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things deserve death, they not only continue to do these very things but also approve of those who practice them.
chapters.zh: 他们虽知道神判定，行这样事的人是当死的，然而他们不但自己去行，还喜欢别人去行。

chapters.en: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on someone else, for at whatever point you judge another, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
chapters.zh: 你这论断人的，无论你是谁，也无可推诿，你在什么事上论断人，就在什么事上定自己的罪。因你这论断人的，自己所行却和别人一样。

chapters.en: Now we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.
chapters.zh: 我们知道这样行的人，神必照真理审判他。

chapters.en: So when you, a mere human being, pass judgment on them and yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
chapters.zh: 你这人哪，你论断行这样事的人，自己所行的却和别人一样，你以为能逃脱神的审判吗？

chapters.en: Or do you show contempt for the riches of his kindness, forbearance and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness is intended to lead you to repentance?
chapters.zh: 还是你藐视他丰富的恩慈，宽容，忍耐，不晓得他的恩慈是领你悔改呢？

chapters.en: But because of your stubbornness and your unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of God’s wrath, when his righteous judgment will be revealed.
chapters.zh: 你竟任着你刚硬不悔改的心，为自己积蓄忿怒，以致神震怒，显他公义审判的日子来到。

chapters.en: God “will repay each person according to what they have done.”
chapters.zh: 他必照各人的行为报应各人。

chapters.en: To those who by persistence in doing good seek glory, honor and immortality, he will give eternal life.
chapters.zh: 凡恒心行善寻求荣耀尊贵，和不能朽坏之福的，就以永生报应他们。

chapters.en: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow evil, there will be wrath and anger.
chapters.zh: 惟有结党不顺从真理，反顺从不义的，就以忿怒恼恨报应他们。

chapters.en: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil: first for the Jew, then for the Gentile;
chapters.zh: 将患难，困苦，加给一切作恶的人，先是犹太人，后是希利尼人。

chapters.en: but glory, honor and peace for everyone who does good: first for the Jew, then for the Gentile.
chapters.zh: 却将荣耀，尊贵，平安，加给一切行善的人，先是犹太人，后是希利尼人。

chapters.en: For God does not show favoritism.
chapters.zh: 因为神不偏待人。

chapters.en: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
chapters.zh: 凡没有律法犯了罪的，也必不按律法灭亡。凡在律法以下犯了罪的，也必按律法受审判，

chapters.en: For it is not those who hear the law who are righteous in God’s sight, but it is those who obey the law who will be declared righteous.
chapters.zh: （原来在神面前，不是听律法的为义，乃是行律法的称义。

chapters.en: (Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature things required by the law, they are a law for themselves, even though they do not have the law.
chapters.zh: 没有律法的外邦人，若顺着本性行律法上的事，他们虽然没有律法，自己就是自己的律法。

chapters.en: They show that the requirements of the law are written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts sometimes accusing them and at other times even defending them.)
chapters.zh: 这是显出律法的功用刻在他们心里，他们是非之心同作见证，并且他们的思念互相较量，或以为是，或以为非。）

chapters.en: This will take place on the day when God judges people’s secrets through Jesus Christ, as my gospel declares.
chapters.zh: 就在神借耶稣基督审判人隐秘事的日子，照着我的福音所言。

chapters.en: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;
chapters.zh: 你称为犹太人，又倚靠律法，且指着神夸口。

chapters.en: if you know his will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;
chapters.zh: 既从律法中受了教训，就晓得神的旨意，也能分别是非（或作也喜爱那美好的事）

chapters.en: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those who are in the dark,
chapters.zh: 又深信自己是给瞎子领路的，是黑暗中人的光，

chapters.en: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of little children, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—
chapters.zh: 是蠢笨人的师傅，是小孩子的先生，在律法上有知识和真理的模范。

chapters.en: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
chapters.zh: 你既是教导别人，还不教导自己吗？你讲说人不可偷窃，自己还偷窃吗？

chapters.en: You who say that people should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
chapters.zh: 你说人不可奸淫，自己还奸淫吗？你厌恶偶像，自己还偷窃庙中之物吗？

chapters.en: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
chapters.zh: 你指着律法夸口，自己倒犯律法，玷辱神吗？

chapters.en: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
chapters.zh: 神的名在外邦人中，因你们受了亵渎，正如经上所记的。

chapters.en: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, you have become as though you had not been circumcised.
chapters.zh: 你若是行律法的割礼固然于你有益。若是犯律法的，你的割礼就算不得割礼。

chapters.en: So then, if those who are not circumcised keep the law’s requirements, will they not be regarded as though they were circumcised?
chapters.zh: 所以那未受割礼的，若遵守律法的条例，他虽然未受割礼，岂不算是有割礼吗？

chapters.en: The one who is not circumcised physically and yet obeys the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
chapters.zh: 而且那本来未受割礼的，若能全守律法，岂不是要审判你这有仪文和割礼竟犯律法的人吗？

chapters.en: A person is not a Jew who is one only outwardly, nor is circumcision merely outward and physical.
chapters.zh: 因为外面作犹太人的，不是真犹太人，外面肉身的割礼，也不是真割礼。

chapters.en: No, a person is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is circumcision of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a person’s praise is not from other people, but from God.
chapters.zh: 惟有里面作的，才是真犹太人。真割礼也是心里的，在乎灵，不在乎仪文。这人的称赞不是从人来的，乃是从神来的。

chapters.en: What advantage, then, is there in being a Jew, or what value is there in circumcision?
chapters.zh: 这样说来，犹太人有什么长处？割礼有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: Much in every way! First of all, the Jews have been entrusted with the very words of God.
chapters.zh: 凡事大有好处。第一是神的圣言交托他们。

chapters.en: What if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness nullify God’s faithfulness?
chapters.zh: 即便有不信的，这有何妨呢？难道他们的不信，就废掉神的信吗？

chapters.en: Not at all! Let God be true, and every human being a liar. As it is written: “So that you may be proved right when you speak and prevail when you judge.”
chapters.zh: 断乎不能。不如说，神是真实的，人都是虚谎的。如经上所记，你责备人的时候，显为公义。被人议论的时候，可以得胜。

chapters.en: But if our unrighteousness brings out God’s righteousness more clearly, what shall we say? That God is unjust in bringing his wrath on us? (I am using a human argument.)
chapters.zh: 我且照着人的常话说，我们的不义，若显出神的义来，我们可以怎么说呢？神降怒，是他不义吗？

chapters.en: Certainly not! If that were so, how could God judge the world?
chapters.zh: 断乎不是。若是这样，神怎能审判世界呢？

chapters.en: Someone might argue, “If my falsehood enhances God’s truthfulness and so increases his glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?”
chapters.zh: 若神的真实，因我的虚谎，越发显出他的荣耀，为什么我还受审判，好像罪人呢？

chapters.en: Why not say—as some slanderously claim that we say—“Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is just!
chapters.zh: 为什么不说，我们可以作恶以成善呢？这是毁谤我们的人，说我们有这话。这等人定罪，是该当的。

chapters.en: What shall we conclude then? Do we have any advantage? Not at all! For we have already made the charge that Jews and Gentiles alike are all under the power of sin.
chapters.zh: 这却怎么样呢？我们比他们强吗？决不是的。因我们已经证明，犹太人和希利尼人都在罪恶之下。

chapters.en: As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one;
chapters.zh: 就如经上所记，没有义人，连一个也没有。

chapters.en: there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God.
chapters.zh: 没有明白的，没有寻求神的。

chapters.en: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”
chapters.zh: 都是偏离正路，一同变为无用。没有行善的，连一个也没有。

chapters.en: “Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.”“The poison of vipers is on their lips.”
chapters.zh: 他们的喉咙是敞开的坟墓。他们用舌头弄诡诈。嘴唇里有虺蛇的毒气。

chapters.en: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
chapters.zh: 满口是咒骂苦毒。

chapters.en: “Their feet are swift to shed blood;
chapters.zh: 杀人流血他们的脚飞跑。

chapters.en: ruin and misery mark their ways,
chapters.zh: 所经过的路，便行残害暴虐的事。

chapters.en: and the way of peace they do not know.”
chapters.zh: 平安的路，他们未曾知道。

chapters.en: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
chapters.zh: 他们眼中不怕神。

chapters.en: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
chapters.zh: 我们晓得律法上的话，都是对律法以下之人说的，好塞住各人的口，叫普世的人都伏在神审判之下。

chapters.en: Therefore no one will be declared righteous in God’s sight by the works of the law; rather, through the law we become conscious of our sin.
chapters.zh: 所以凡有血气的没有一个，因行律法，能在神面前称义。因为律法本是叫人知罪。

chapters.en: But now apart from the law the righteousness of God has been made known, to which the Law and the Prophets testify.
chapters.zh: 但如今神的义在律法以外已经显明出来，有律法和先知为证。

chapters.en: This righteousness is given through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no difference between Jew and Gentile,
chapters.zh: 就是神的义，因信耶稣基督，加给一切相信的人，并没有分别。

chapters.en: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
chapters.zh: 因为世人都犯了罪，亏缺了神的荣耀。

chapters.en: and all are justified freely by his grace through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 如今却蒙神的恩典，因基督耶稣的救赎，就白白地称义。

chapters.en: God presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement, through the shedding of his blood—to be received by faith. He did this to demonstrate his righteousness, because in his forbearance he had left the sins committed beforehand unpunished—
chapters.zh: 神设立耶稣作挽回祭，是凭着耶稣的血，借着人的信，要显明神的义。因为他用忍耐的心，宽容人先时所犯的罪。

chapters.en: he did it to demonstrate his righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and the one who justifies those who have faith in Jesus.
chapters.zh: 好在今时显明他的义，使人知道他自己为义，也称信耶稣的人为义。

chapters.en: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. Because of what law? The law that requires works? No, because of the law that requires faith.
chapters.zh: 既是这样，哪里能夸口呢？没有可夸的了。用何法没有的呢？是用立功之法吗？不是，乃用信主之法。

chapters.en: For we maintain that a person is justified by faith apart from the works of the law.
chapters.zh: 所以（有古卷作因为）我们看定了，人称义是因着信，不在乎遵行律法。

chapters.en: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is he not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,
chapters.zh: 难道神只作犹太人的神吗？不也是作外邦人的神吗？是的，也作外邦人的神。

chapters.en: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
chapters.zh: 神既是一位他就要因信称那受割礼的为义，也要因信称那未受割礼的为义。

chapters.en: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Not at all! Rather, we uphold the law.
chapters.zh: 这样，我们因信废了律法吗？断乎不是，更是坚固律法。

chapters.en: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, discovered in this matter?
chapters.zh: 如此说来，我们的祖宗亚伯拉罕，凭着肉体得了什么呢？

chapters.en: If, in fact, Abraham was justified by works, he had something to boast about—but not before God.
chapters.zh: 倘若亚伯拉罕是因行为称义，就有可夸的。只是在神面前并无可夸。

chapters.en: What does Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
chapters.zh: 经上说什么呢？说，亚伯拉罕信神，这就算为他的义。

chapters.en: Now to the one who works, wages are not credited as a gift but as an obligation.
chapters.zh: 作工的得工价，不算恩典，乃是该得的，

chapters.en: However, to the one who does not work but trusts God who justifies the ungodly, their faith is credited as righteousness.
chapters.zh: 惟有不作工的，只信称罪人为义的神，他的信就算为义。

chapters.en: David says the same thing when he speaks of the blessedness of the one to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
chapters.zh: 正如大卫称那在行为以外，蒙神算为义的人是有福的。

chapters.en: “Blessed are those whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
chapters.zh: 他说，得赦免其过，遮盖其罪的，这人是有福的。

chapters.en: Blessed is the one whose sin the Lord will never count against them.”
chapters.zh: 主不算为有罪的，这人是有福的。

chapters.en: Is this blessedness only for the circumcised, or also for the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.
chapters.zh: 如此看来，这福是单加给那受割礼的人吗？不也是加给那未受割礼的人吗？因我们所说，亚伯拉罕的信，就算为他的义。

chapters.en: Under what circumstances was it credited? Was it after he was circumcised, or before? It was not after, but before!
chapters.zh: 是怎么算的呢？是在他受割礼的时候呢？是在他未受割礼的时候呢？不是在受割礼的时候，乃是在未受割礼的时候。

chapters.en: And he received circumcision as a sign, a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but have not been circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.
chapters.zh: 并且他受了割礼的记号，作他未受割礼的时候因信称义的印证，叫他作一切未受割礼而信之人的父，使他们也算为义。

chapters.en: And he is then also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised but who also follow in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
chapters.zh: 又作受割礼之人的父，就是那些不但受割礼，并且按我们的祖宗亚伯拉罕，未受割礼而信之踪迹去行的人。

chapters.en: It was not through the law that Abraham and his offspring received the promise that he would be heir of the world, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
chapters.zh: 因为神应许亚伯拉罕和他后裔，必得承受世界，不是因律法，乃是因信而得的义。

chapters.en: For if those who depend on the law are heirs, faith means nothing and the promise is worthless,
chapters.zh: 若是属乎律法的人，才得为后嗣，信就归于虚空，应许也就废弃了。

chapters.en: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law there is no transgression.
chapters.zh: 因为律法是惹动忿怒的。（或作叫人受刑的）哪里没有律法，哪里就没有过犯。

chapters.en: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may be by grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law but also to those who have the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
chapters.zh: 所以人得为后嗣是本乎信。因此就属乎恩。叫应许定然归给一切后裔。不但归给那属乎律法的，也归给那效法亚伯拉罕之信的。

chapters.en: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the sight of God, in whom he believed—the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being things that were not.
chapters.zh: 亚伯拉罕所信的，是那叫死人复活使无变为有的神，他在主面前作我们世人的父。如经上所记，我已经立你作多国的父。

chapters.en: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as it had been said to him, “So shall your offspring be.”
chapters.zh: 他在无可指望的时候，因信仍有指望，就得以作多国的父，正如先前所说，你的后裔将要如此。

chapters.en: Without weakening in his faith, he faced the fact that his body was as good as dead—since he was about a hundred years old—and that Sarah’s womb was also dead.
chapters.zh: 他将近百岁的时候，虽然想到自己的身体如同已死，撒拉的生育已经断绝，他的信心还是不软弱。

chapters.en: Yet he did not waver through unbelief regarding the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,
chapters.zh: 并且仰望神的应许，总没有因不信，心里起疑惑。反倒因信，心里得坚固，将荣耀归给神。

chapters.en: being fully persuaded that God had power to do what he had promised.
chapters.zh: 且满心相信，神所应许的必能作成。

chapters.en: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”
chapters.zh: 所以这就算为他的义。

chapters.en: The words “it was credited to him” were written not for him alone,
chapters.zh: 算为他义的这句话，不是单为他写的，

chapters.en: but also for us, to whom God will credit righteousness—for us who believe in him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
chapters.zh: 也是为我们将来得算为义之人写的。就是我们这信神使我们的主耶稣从死里复活的人。

chapters.en: He was delivered over to death for our sins and was raised to life for our justification.
chapters.zh: 耶稣被交给人，是为我们的过犯，复活是为叫我们称义。（或作耶稣是为我们的过犯交付了是为我们称义复活了）

chapters.en: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
chapters.zh: 我们既因信称义，就借着我们的主耶稣基督，得与神相和。

chapters.en: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we now stand. And we boast in the hope of the glory of God.
chapters.zh: 我们又借着他，因信得进入现在所站的这恩典中，并且欢欢喜喜盼望神的荣耀。

chapters.en: Not only so, but we also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;
chapters.zh: 不但如此，就是在患难中，也是欢欢喜喜的。因为知道患难生忍耐。

chapters.en: perseverance, character; and character, hope.
chapters.zh: 忍耐生老练。老练生盼望。

chapters.en: And hope does not put us to shame, because God’s love has been poured out into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.
chapters.zh: 盼望不至于羞耻，因为所赐给我们的圣灵将神的爱浇灌在我们心里。

chapters.en: You see, at just the right time, when we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.
chapters.zh: 因我们还软弱的时候，基督就按所定的日期为罪人死。

chapters.en: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous person, though for a good person someone might possibly dare to die.
chapters.zh: 为义人死，是少有的，为仁人死，或者有敢作的。

chapters.en: But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
chapters.zh: 惟有基督在我们还作罪人的时候为我们死，神的爱就在此向我们显明了。

chapters.en: Since we have now been justified by his blood, how much more shall we be saved from God’s wrath through him!
chapters.zh: 现在我们既靠着他的血称义，就更要借着他免去神的忿怒。

chapters.en: For if, while we were God’s enemies, we were reconciled to him through the death of his Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through his life!
chapters.zh: 因为我们作仇敌的时候，且借着神儿子的死，得与神和好，既已和好，就更要因他的生得救了。

chapters.en: Not only is this so, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
chapters.zh: 不但如此，我们既借着我主耶稣基督，得与神和好，也就借着他，以神为乐。

chapters.en: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, and in this way death came to all people, because all sinned—
chapters.zh: 这就如罪是从一人入了世界，死又是从罪来的，于是死就临到众人，因为众人都犯了罪。

chapters.en: To be sure, sin was in the world before the law was given, but sin is not charged against anyone’s account where there is no law.
chapters.zh: 没有律法之先，罪已经在世上。但没有律法，罪也不算罪。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, death reigned from the time of Adam to the time of Moses, even over those who did not sin by breaking a command, as did Adam, who is a pattern of the one to come.
chapters.zh: 然而从亚当到摩西，死就作了王，连那些不与亚当犯一样罪过的，也在他的权下。亚当乃是那以后要来之人的预像。

chapters.en: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, overflow to the many!
chapters.zh: 只是过犯不如恩赐。若因一人的过犯，众人都死了，何况神的恩典，与那因耶稣基督一人恩典中的赏赐，岂不更加倍地临到众人吗？

chapters.en: Nor can the gift of God be compared with the result of one man’s sin: The judgment followed one sin and brought condemnation, but the gift followed many trespasses and brought justification.
chapters.zh: 因一人犯罪就定罪，也不如恩赐。原来审判是由一人而定罪，恩赐乃是由许多过犯而称义。

chapters.en: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive God’s abundant provision of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!
chapters.zh: 若因一人的过犯，死就因这一人作了王，何况那些受洪恩又蒙所赐之义的，岂不更要因耶稣基督一人在生命中作王吗？

chapters.en: Consequently, just as one trespass resulted in condemnation for all people, so also one righteous act resulted in justification and life for all people.
chapters.zh: 如此说来，因一次的过犯，众人都被定罪，照样，因一次的义行，众人也就被称义得生命了。

chapters.en: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
chapters.zh: 因一人的悖逆，众人成为罪人，照样，因一人的顺从，众人也成为义了。

chapters.en: The law was brought in so that the trespass might increase. But where sin increased, grace increased all the more,
chapters.zh: 律法本是外添的，叫过犯显多。只是罪在哪里显多，恩典就更显多了。

chapters.en: so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
chapters.zh: 就如罪作王叫人死，照样恩典也借着义作王，叫人因我们的主耶稣基督得永生。

chapters.en: What shall we say, then? Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase?
chapters.zh: 这样，怎么说呢？我们可以仍在罪中，叫恩典显多吗？

chapters.en: By no means! We are those who have died to sin; how can we live in it any longer?
chapters.zh: 断乎不可。我们在罪上死了的人，岂可仍在罪中活着呢？

chapters.en: Or don’t you know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
chapters.zh: 岂不知我们这受洗归入基督耶稣的人，是受洗归入他的死吗？

chapters.en: We were therefore buried with him through baptism into death in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may live a new life.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们借着洗礼归入死，和他一同埋葬，原是叫我们一举一动有新生的样式，像基督借着父的荣耀从死里复活一样。

chapters.en: For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we will certainly also be united with him in a resurrection like his.
chapters.zh: 我们若在他死的形状上与他联合，也要在他复活的形状上与他联合。

chapters.en: For we know that our old self was crucified with him so that the body ruled by sin might be done away with, that we should no longer be slaves to sin—
chapters.zh: 因为知道我们的旧人和他同钉十字架，使罪身灭绝，叫我们不再作罪的奴仆。

chapters.en: because anyone who has died has been set free from sin.
chapters.zh: 因为已死的人，是脱离了罪。

chapters.en: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him.
chapters.zh: 我们若是与基督同死，就信必与他同活。

chapters.en: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, he cannot die again; death no longer has mastery over him.
chapters.zh: 因为知道基督既从死里复活，就不再死，死也不再作他的主了。

chapters.en: The death he died, he died to sin once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God.
chapters.zh: 他死是向罪死了，只有一次。他活是向神活着。

chapters.en: In the same way, count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 这样，你们向罪也当看自己是死的。向神在基督耶稣里却当看自己是活的。

chapters.en: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its evil desires.
chapters.zh: 所以不要容罪在你们必死的身上作王，使你们顺从身子的私欲。

chapters.en: Do not offer any part of yourself to sin as an instrument of wickedness, but rather offer yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and offer every part of yourself to him as an instrument of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 也不要将你们的肢体献给罪作不义的器具。倒要像从死里复活的人，将自己献给神。并将肢体作义的器具献给神。

chapters.en: For sin shall no longer be your master, because you are not under the law, but under grace.
chapters.zh: 罪必不能作你们的主。因你们不在律法之下，乃在恩典之下。

chapters.en: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under the law but under grace? By no means!
chapters.zh: 这却怎么样呢？我们在恩典之下，不在律法之下，就可以犯罪吗？断乎不可。

chapters.en: Don’t you know that when you offer yourselves to someone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one you obey—whether you are slaves to sin, which leads to death, or to obedience, which leads to righteousness?
chapters.zh: 岂不晓得你们献上自己作奴仆，顺从谁，就作谁的奴仆吗？或作罪的奴仆，以至于死。或作顺命的奴仆，以至成义。

chapters.en: But thanks be to God that, though you used to be slaves to sin, you have come to obey from your heart the pattern of teaching that has now claimed your allegiance.
chapters.zh: 感谢神，因为你们从前虽然作罪的奴仆，现今却从心里顺服了所传给你们道理的模范。

chapters.en: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.
chapters.zh: 你们既从罪里得了释放，就作了义的奴仆。

chapters.en: I am using an example from everyday life because of your human limitations. Just as you used to offer yourselves as slaves to impurity and to ever-increasing wickedness, so now offer yourselves as slaves to righteousness leading to holiness.
chapters.zh: 我因你们肉体的软弱，就照人的常话对你们说，你们从前怎样将肢体献给不洁不法作奴仆，以至于不法。现今也要照样将肢体献给义作奴仆，以至于成圣。

chapters.en: When you were slaves to sin, you were free from the control of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 因为你们作罪之奴仆的时候，就不被义约束了。

chapters.en: What benefit did you reap at that time from the things you are now ashamed of? Those things result in death!
chapters.zh: 你们现今所看为羞耻的事，当日有什么果子呢？那些事的结局就是死。

chapters.en: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the benefit you reap leads to holiness, and the result is eternal life.
chapters.zh: 但现今你们既从罪里得了释放，作了神的奴仆，就有成圣的果子，那结局就是永生。

chapters.en: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
chapters.zh: 因为罪的工价乃是死。惟有神的恩赐，在我们的主基督耶稣里乃是永生。

chapters.en: Do you not know, brothers and sisters—for I am speaking to those who know the law—that the law has authority over someone only as long as that person lives?
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我现在对明白律法的人说，你们岂不晓得律法管人是在活着的时候吗？

chapters.en: For example, by law a married woman is bound to her husband as long as he is alive, but if her husband dies, she is released from the law that binds her to him.
chapters.zh: 就如女人有了丈夫，丈夫还活着，就被律法约束。丈夫若死了，就脱离了丈夫的律法。

chapters.en: So then, if she has sexual relations with another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is released from that law and is not an adulteress if she marries another man.
chapters.zh: 所以丈夫活着，她若归于别人，便叫淫妇。丈夫若死了，她就脱离了丈夫的律法，虽然归于别人，也不是淫妇。

chapters.en: So, my brothers and sisters, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit for God.
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，这样说来，你们借着基督的身体，在律法上也是死了。叫你们归于别人，就是归于那从死里复活的，叫我们结果子给神。

chapters.en: For when we were in the realm of the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in us, so that we bore fruit for death.
chapters.zh: 因为我们属肉体的时候，那因律法而生的恶欲，就在我们肢体中发动，以致结成死亡的果子。

chapters.en: But now, by dying to what once bound us, we have been released from the law so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.
chapters.zh: 但我们既然在捆我们的律法上死了，现今就脱离了律法，叫我们服事主，要按着心灵的新样，不按着仪文的旧样（心灵或作圣灵）。

chapters.en: What shall we say, then? Is the law sinful? Certainly not! Nevertheless, I would not have known what sin was had it not been for the law. For I would not have known what coveting really was if the law had not said, “You shall not covet.”
chapters.zh: 这样，我们可说什么呢？律法是罪吗？断乎不是。只是非因律法，我就不知何为罪。非律法说，不可起贪心。我就不知何为贪心。

chapters.en: But sin, seizing the opportunity afforded by the commandment, produced in me every kind of coveting. For apart from the law, sin was dead.
chapters.zh: 然而罪趁着机会，就借着诫命叫诸般的贪心在我里头发动。因为没有律法罪是死的。

chapters.en: Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.
chapters.zh: 我以前没有律法是活着的，但是诫命来到，罪又活了，我就死了。

chapters.en: I found that the very commandment that was intended to bring life actually brought death.
chapters.zh: 那本来叫人活的诫命，反倒叫我死。

chapters.en: For sin, seizing the opportunity afforded by the commandment, deceived me, and through the commandment put me to death.
chapters.zh: 因为罪趁着机会，就借着诫命引诱我，并且杀了我。

chapters.en: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous and good.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，律法是圣洁的，诫命也是圣洁，公义，良善的。

chapters.en: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? By no means! Nevertheless, in order that sin might be recognized as sin, it used what is good to bring about my death, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.
chapters.zh: 既然如此，那良善的是叫我死吗？断乎不是。叫我死的乃是罪。但罪借着那良善的叫我死，就显出真是罪。叫罪因着诫命更显出是恶极了。

chapters.en: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.
chapters.zh: 我们原晓得律法是属乎灵的，但我是属乎肉体的，是已经卖给罪了。

chapters.en: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do I do not do, but what I hate I do.
chapters.zh: 因为我所作的，我自己不明白。我所愿意的，我并不作。我所恨恶的，我倒去作。

chapters.en: And if I do what I do not want to do, I agree that the law is good.
chapters.zh: 若我所作的，是我所不愿意的，我就应承律法是善的。

chapters.en: As it is, it is no longer I myself who do it, but it is sin living in me.
chapters.zh: 既是这样，就不是我作的，乃是住在我里头的罪作的。

chapters.en: For I know that good itself does not dwell in me, that is, in my sinful nature. For I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.
chapters.zh: 我也知道，在我里头，就是我肉体之中，没有良善。因为立志为善由得我，只是行出来由不得我。

chapters.en: For I do not do the good I want to do, but the evil I do not want to do—this I keep on doing.
chapters.zh: 故此，我所愿意的善，我反不作。我所不愿意的恶，我倒去作。

chapters.en: Now if I do what I do not want to do, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.
chapters.zh: 若我去作所不愿意作的，就不是我作的，乃是住在我里头的罪作的。

chapters.en: So I find this law at work: Although I want to do good, evil is right there with me.
chapters.zh: 我觉得有个律，就是我愿意为善的时候，便有恶与我同在。

chapters.en: For in my inner being I delight in God’s law;
chapters.zh: 因为按着我里面的意思。（原文作人）我是喜欢神的律。

chapters.en: but I see another law at work in me, waging war against the law of my mind and making me a prisoner of the law of sin at work within me.
chapters.zh: 但我觉得肢体中另有个律，和我心中的律交战，把我掳去叫我附从那肢体中犯罪的律。

chapters.en: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body that is subject to death?
chapters.zh: 我真是苦阿，谁能救我脱离这取死的身体呢？

chapters.en: Thanks be to God, who delivers me through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself in my mind am a slave to God’s law, but in my sinful nature a slave to the law of sin.
chapters.zh: 感谢神，靠着我们的主耶稣基督就能脱离了这样看来，我以内心顺服神的律。我肉体却顺服罪的律了。

chapters.en: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus,
chapters.zh: 如今那些在基督耶稣里的，就不定罪了。

chapters.en: because through Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit who gives life has set you free from the law of sin and death.
chapters.zh: 因为赐生命圣灵的律，在基督耶稣里释放了我，使我脱离罪和死的律了。
