chapters.en: For what the law was powerless to do because it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh to be a sin offering. And so he condemned sin in the flesh,
chapters.zh: 律法既因肉体软弱，有所不能行的，神就差遣自己的儿子，成为罪身的形状，作了赎罪祭，在肉体中定了罪案，

chapters.en: in order that the righteous requirement of the law might be fully met in us, who do not live according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 使律法的义成就在我们这不随从肉体，只随从圣灵的人身上。

chapters.en: Those who live according to the flesh have their minds set on what the flesh desires; but those who live in accordance with the Spirit have their minds set on what the Spirit desires.
chapters.zh: 因为随从肉体的人体贴肉体的事，随从圣灵的人体贴圣灵的事。

chapters.en: The mind governed by the flesh is death, but the mind governed by the Spirit is life and peace.
chapters.zh: 体贴肉体的，就是死，体贴圣灵的，乃是生命，平安。

chapters.en: The mind governed by the flesh is hostile to God; it does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.
chapters.zh: 原来体贴肉体的，就是与神为仇。因为不服神的律法，也是不能服。

chapters.en: Those who are in the realm of the flesh cannot please God.
chapters.zh: 而且属肉体的人，不能得神的喜欢。

chapters.en: You, however, are not in the realm of the flesh but are in the realm of the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, they do not belong to Christ.
chapters.zh: 如果神的灵住在你们心里，你们就不属肉体，乃属圣灵了。人若没有基督的灵，就不是属基督的。

chapters.en: But if Christ is in you, then even though your body is subject to death because of sin, the Spirit gives life because of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 基督若在你们心里，身体就因罪而死，心灵却因义而活。

chapters.en: And if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies because of his Spirit who lives in you.
chapters.zh: 然而叫耶稣从死里复活者的灵，若住在你们心里，那叫基督耶稣从死里复活的，也必借着住在你们心里的圣灵，使你们必死的身体又活过来。

chapters.en: Therefore, brothers and sisters, we have an obligation—but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，这样看来，我们并不是欠肉体的债，去顺从肉体活着。

chapters.en: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the misdeeds of the body, you will live.
chapters.zh: 你们若顺从肉体活着必要死。若靠着圣灵治死身体的恶行必要活着。

chapters.en: For those who are led by the Spirit of God are the children of God.
chapters.zh: 因为凡被神的灵引导的，都是神的儿子。

chapters.en: The Spirit you received does not make you slaves, so that you live in fear again; rather, the Spirit you received brought about your adoption to sonship. And by him we cry, “Abba, Father.”
chapters.zh: 你们所受的不是奴仆的心，仍旧害怕。所受的乃是儿子的心，因此我们呼叫阿爸，父。

chapters.en: The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.
chapters.zh: 圣灵与我们的心同证我们是神的儿女。

chapters.en: Now if we are children, then we are heirs—heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ, if indeed we share in his sufferings in order that we may also share in his glory.
chapters.zh: 既是儿女，便是后嗣，就是神的后嗣，和基督同作后嗣。如果我们和他一同受苦，也必和他一同得荣耀。

chapters.en: I consider that our present sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory that will be revealed in us.
chapters.zh: 我想现在的苦楚，若比起将来要显于我们的荣耀，就不足介意了。

chapters.en: For the creation waits in eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed.
chapters.zh: 受造之物，切望等候神的众子显出来。

chapters.en: For the creation was subjected to frustration, not by its own choice, but by the will of the one who subjected it, in hope
chapters.zh: 因为受造之物服在虚空之下，不是自己愿意，乃是因那叫他如此的。

chapters.en: that the creation itself will be liberated from its bondage to decay and brought into the freedom and glory of the children of God.
chapters.zh: 但受造之物仍然指望脱离败坏的辖制，得享神儿女自由的荣耀。（享原文作入）

chapters.en: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
chapters.zh: 我们知道一切受造之物，一同叹息劳苦，直到如今。

chapters.en: Not only so, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption to sonship, the redemption of our bodies.
chapters.zh: 不但如此，就是我们这有圣灵初结果子的，也是自己心里叹息，等候得着儿子的名分，乃是我们的身体得赎。

chapters.en: For in this hope we were saved. But hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what they already have?
chapters.zh: 我们得救是在乎盼望。只是所见的盼望不是盼望。谁还盼望他所见的呢？（有古卷作人所看见的何必再盼望呢）

chapters.en: But if we hope for what we do not yet have, we wait for it patiently.
chapters.zh: 但我们若盼望那所不见的，就必忍耐等候。

chapters.en: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. We do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us through wordless groans.
chapters.zh: 况且我们的软弱有圣灵帮助，我们本不晓得当怎样祷告，只是圣灵亲自用说不出来的叹息，替我们祷告。

chapters.en: And he who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for God’s people in accordance with the will of God.
chapters.zh: 鉴察人心的，晓得圣灵的意思因为圣灵照着神的旨意替圣徒祈求。

chapters.en: And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.
chapters.zh: 我们晓得万事都互相效力，叫爱神的人得益处，就是按他旨意被召的人。

chapters.en: For those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters.
chapters.zh: 因为他预先所知道的人，就预先定下效法他儿子的模样，使他儿子在许多弟兄中作长子。

chapters.en: And those he predestined, he also called; those he called, he also justified; those he justified, he also glorified.
chapters.zh: 预先所定下的人又召他们来。所召来的人，又称他们为义。所称为义的人，又叫他们得荣耀。

chapters.en: What, then, shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
chapters.zh: 既是这样，还有什么说的呢？神若帮助我们，谁能敌挡我们呢？

chapters.en: He who did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all—how will he not also, along with him, graciously give us all things?
chapters.zh: 神既不爱惜自己的儿子为我们众人舍了，岂不也把万物和他一同白白地赐给我们吗？

chapters.en: Who will bring any charge against those whom God has chosen? It is God who justifies.
chapters.zh: 谁能控告神所拣选的人呢？有神称他们为义了。（或作是称他们为义的神吗？）

chapters.en: Who then is the one who condemns? No one. Christ Jesus who died—more than that, who was raised to life—is at the right hand of God and is also interceding for us.
chapters.zh: 谁能定他们的罪呢？有基督耶稣已经死了，而且从死里复活，现今在神的右边，也替我们祈求。（有基督云云或作是已经死了而且从死里复活现今在神的右边也替我们祈求的基督耶稣吗）

chapters.en: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or hardship or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?
chapters.zh: 谁能使我们与基督的爱隔绝呢？难道是患难吗？是困苦吗？是逼迫吗？是饥饿吗？是赤身露体吗？是危险吗？是刀剑吗？

chapters.en: As it is written: “For your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”
chapters.zh: 如经上所记，我们为你的缘故，终日被杀。人看我们如将宰的羊

chapters.en: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
chapters.zh: 然而靠着爱我们的主，在这一切的事上，已经得胜有余了。

chapters.en: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor demons, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,
chapters.zh: 因为我深信无论是死，是生，是天使，是掌权的，是有能的，是现在的事，是将来的事，

chapters.en: neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
chapters.zh: 是高处的，是低处的，是别的受造之物，都不能叫我们与神的爱隔绝。这爱是在我们的主基督耶稣里的。

chapters.en: I speak the truth in Christ—I am not lying, my conscience confirms it through the Holy Spirit—
chapters.zh: 我在基督里说真话，并不谎言，有我良心被圣灵感动，给我作见证。

chapters.en: I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
chapters.zh: 我是大有忧愁，心里时常伤痛。

chapters.en: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my people, those of my own race,
chapters.zh: 为我弟兄，我骨肉之亲，就是自己被咒诅，与基督分离，我也愿意。

chapters.en: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption to sonship; theirs the divine glory, the covenants, the receiving of the law, the temple worship and the promises.
chapters.zh: 他们是以色列人。那儿子的名分，荣耀，诸约，律法，礼仪，应许，都是他们的。

chapters.en: Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them is traced the human ancestry of the Messiah, who is God over all, forever praised! Amen.
chapters.zh: 列祖就是他们的祖宗，按肉体说，基督也是从他们出来的，他是在万有之上，永远可称颂的神。阿们。

chapters.en: It is not as though God’s word had failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
chapters.zh: 这不是说神的话落了空。因为从以色列生的，不都是以色列人。

chapters.en: Nor because they are his descendants are they all Abraham’s children. On the contrary, “It is through Isaac that your offspring will be reckoned.”
chapters.zh: 也不因为是亚伯拉罕的后裔，就都作他的儿女。惟独从以撒生的，才要称为你的后裔。

chapters.en: In other words, it is not the children by physical descent who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as Abraham’s offspring.
chapters.zh: 这就是说，肉身所生的儿女，不是神的儿女。惟独那应许的儿女，才算是后裔。

chapters.en: For this was how the promise was stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”
chapters.zh: 因为所应许的话是这样说，到明年这时候我要来，撒拉必生一个儿子。

chapters.en: Not only that, but Rebekah’s children were conceived at the same time by our father Isaac.
chapters.zh: 不但如此，还有利百加，既从一个人，就是从我们的祖宗以撒怀了孕。

chapters.en: Yet, before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad—in order that God’s purpose in election might stand:
chapters.zh: （双子还没有生下来，善恶还没有作出来，只因要显明神拣选人的旨意，不在乎人的行为，乃在乎召人的主）。

chapters.en: not by works but by him who calls—she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”
chapters.zh: 神就对利百加说，将来大的要服事小的。

chapters.en: Just as it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”
chapters.zh: 正如经上所记，雅各是我所爱的，以扫是我所恶的。

chapters.en: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Not at all!
chapters.zh: 这样，我们可说什么呢？难道神有什么不公平吗？断乎没有。

chapters.en: For he says to Moses, “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
chapters.zh: 因他对摩西说，我要怜悯谁，就怜悯谁，要恩待谁，就恩待谁。

chapters.en: It does not, therefore, depend on human desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.
chapters.zh: 据此看来，这不在乎那定意的，也不在乎那奔跑的，只在乎发怜悯的神。

chapters.en: For Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display my power in you and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
chapters.zh: 因为经上有话向法老说，我将你兴起来，特要在你身上彰显我的权能，并要使我的名传遍天下。

chapters.en: Therefore God has mercy on whom he wants to have mercy, and he hardens whom he wants to harden.
chapters.zh: 如此看来，神要怜悯谁，就怜悯谁，要叫谁刚硬，就叫谁刚硬。

chapters.en: One of you will say to me: “Then why does God still blame us? For who is able to resist his will?”
chapters.zh: 这样，你必对我说，他为什么还指责人呢？有谁抗拒他的旨意呢？

chapters.en: But who are you, a human being, to talk back to God? “Shall what is formed say to the one who formed it, ‘Why did you make me like this?’ ”
chapters.zh: 你这个人哪，你是谁，竟敢向神强嘴呢？受造之物岂能对造他的说，你为什么这样造我呢？

chapters.en: Does not the potter have the right to make out of the same lump of clay some pottery for special purposes and some for common use?
chapters.zh: 窑匠难道没有权柄，从一团泥里拿一块作成贵重的器皿，又拿一块作成卑贱的器皿吗？

chapters.en: What if God, although choosing to show his wrath and make his power known, bore with great patience the objects of his wrath—prepared for destruction?
chapters.zh: 倘若神要显明他的忿怒，彰显他的权能，就多多忍耐宽容那可怒预备遭毁灭的器皿。

chapters.en: What if he did this to make the riches of his glory known to the objects of his mercy, whom he prepared in advance for glory—
chapters.zh: 又要将他丰盛的荣耀，彰显在那蒙怜悯早预备得荣耀的器皿上。

chapters.en: even us, whom he also called, not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles?
chapters.zh: 这器皿就是我们被神所召的，不但是从犹太人中，也是从外邦人中，这有什么不可呢？

chapters.en: As he says in Hosea: “I will call them ‘my people’ who are not my people; and I will call her ‘my loved one’ who is not my loved one,”
chapters.zh: 就像神在何西阿书上说，那本来不是我子民的，我要称为我的子民。本来不是蒙爱的，我要称为蒙爱的。

chapters.en: and, “In the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ there they will be called ‘children of the living God.’ ”
chapters.zh: 从前在什么地方对他们说，你们不是我的子民，将来就在那里称他们为永生神的儿子。

chapters.en: Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the Israelites be like the sand by the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
chapters.zh: 以赛亚指着以色列人喊着说，以色列人虽多如海沙，得救的不过是剩下的余数。

chapters.en: For the Lord will carry out his sentence on earth with speed and finality.”
chapters.zh: 因为主要在世上施行他的话，叫他的话都成全，速速地完结。

chapters.en: It is just as Isaiah said previously: “Unless the Lord Almighty had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have been like Gomorrah.”
chapters.zh: 又如以赛亚先前说过，若不是万军之主给我们存留余种，我们早已像所多玛，蛾摩拉的样子了。

chapters.en: What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;
chapters.zh: 这样，我们可说什么呢？那本来不追求义的外邦人，反得了义，就是因信而得的义。

chapters.en: but the people of Israel, who pursued the law as the way of righteousness, have not attained their goal.
chapters.zh: 但以色列人追求律法的义，反得不着律法的义。

chapters.en: Why not? Because they pursued it not by faith but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone.
chapters.zh: 这是什么缘故呢？是因为他们不凭着信心求，只凭着行为求。他们正跌在那绊脚石上。

chapters.en: As it is written: “See, I lay in Zion a stone that causes people to stumble and a rock that makes them fall, and the one who believes in him will never be put to shame.”
chapters.zh: 就如经上所记，我在锡安放一块绊脚的石头，跌人的磐石。信靠他的人必不至于羞愧。

chapters.en: Brothers and sisters, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is that they may be saved.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我心里所愿的，向神所求的，是要以色列人得救。

chapters.en: For I can testify about them that they are zealous for God, but their zeal is not based on knowledge.
chapters.zh: 我可以证明他们向神有热心，但不是按着真知识。

chapters.en: Since they did not know the righteousness of God and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.
chapters.zh: 因为不知道神的义，想要立自己的义，就不服神的义了。

chapters.en: Christ is the culmination of the law so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes.
chapters.zh: 律法的总结就是基督，使凡信他的都得着义。

chapters.en: Moses writes this about the righteousness that is by the law: “The person who does these things will live by them.”
chapters.zh: 摩西写着说，人若行那出于律法的义，就必因此活着。

chapters.en: But the righteousness that is by faith says: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ ” (that is, to bring Christ down)
chapters.zh: 惟有出于信心的义如此说，你不要心里说，谁要升到天上去呢？就是要领下基督来。

chapters.en: “or ‘Who will descend into the deep?’ ” (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).
chapters.zh: 谁要下到阴间去呢？就是要领基督从死里上来。

chapters.en: But what does it say? “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,” that is, the message concerning faith that we proclaim:
chapters.zh: 他到底怎么说呢？他说，这道离你不远，正在你口里，在你心里。就是我们所传信主的道。

chapters.en: If you declare with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
chapters.zh: 你若口里认耶稣为主，心里信神叫他从死里复活，就必得救。

chapters.en: For it is with your heart that you believe and are justified, and it is with your mouth that you profess your faith and are saved.
chapters.zh: 因为人心里相信，就可以称义。口里承认，就可以得救。

chapters.en: As Scripture says, “Anyone who believes in him will never be put to shame.”
chapters.zh: 经上说，凡信他的人，必不至于羞愧。

chapters.en: For there is no difference between Jew and Gentile—the same Lord is Lord of all and richly blesses all who call on him,
chapters.zh: 犹太人和希利尼人，并没有分别。因为众人同有一位主，他也厚待一切求告他的人。

chapters.en: for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
chapters.zh: 因为凡求告主名的，就必得救。

chapters.en: How, then, can they call on the one they have not believed in? And how can they believe in the one of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone preaching to them?
chapters.zh: 然而人未曾信他，怎能求他呢？未曾听见他，怎能信他呢？没有传道的，怎能听见呢？

chapters.en: And how can anyone preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
chapters.zh: 若没有奉差遣，怎能传道呢？如经上所记，报福音传喜信的人，他们的脚踪何等佳美，

chapters.en: But not all the Israelites accepted the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
chapters.zh: 只是人没有都听从福音。因为以赛亚说，主阿，我们所传的有谁信呢？

chapters.en: Consequently, faith comes from hearing the message, and the message is heard through the word about Christ.
chapters.zh: 可见信道是从听道来的，听道是从基督的话来的。

chapters.en: But I ask: Did they not hear? Of course they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”
chapters.zh: 但我说，人没有听见吗？诚然听见了。他们的声音传遍天下，他们的言语传到地极。

chapters.en: Again I ask: Did Israel not understand? First, Moses says, “I will make you envious by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation that has no understanding.”
chapters.zh: 我再说，以色列人不知道吗？先有摩西说，我要用那不成子民的，惹动你们的愤恨。我要用那无知的民，触动你们的怒气。

chapters.en: And Isaiah boldly says, “I was found by those who did not seek me; I revealed myself to those who did not ask for me.”
chapters.zh: 又有以赛亚放胆说，没有寻找我的，我叫他们遇见。没有访问我的，我向他们显现。

chapters.en: But concerning Israel he says, “All day long I have held out my hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.”
chapters.zh: 至于以色列人，他说，我整天伸手招呼那悖逆顶嘴的百姓。

chapters.en: I ask then: Did God reject his people? By no means! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 我且说，神弃绝了他的百姓吗？断乎没有。因为我也是以色列人，亚伯拉罕的后裔，属便雅悯支派的。

chapters.en: God did not reject his people, whom he foreknew. Don’t you know what Scripture says in the passage about Elijah—how he appealed to God against Israel:
chapters.zh: 神并没有弃绝他预先所知道的百姓。你们岂不晓得经上论到以利亚是怎么说的呢？他在神面前怎样控告以色列人，说，

chapters.en: “Lord, they have killed your prophets and torn down your altars; I am the only one left, and they are trying to kill me” ?
chapters.zh: 主阿，他们杀了你的先知，拆了你的祭坛，只剩下我一个人，他们还要寻索我的命。

chapters.en: And what was God’s answer to him? “I have reserved for myself seven thousand who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
chapters.zh: 神的回话是怎么说的呢？他说，我为自己留下七千人，是未曾向巴力屈膝的。

chapters.en: So too, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
chapters.zh: 如今也是这样，照着拣选的恩典还有所留的余数。

chapters.en: And if by grace, then it cannot be based on works; if it were, grace would no longer be grace.
chapters.zh: 既是出于恩典，就不在乎行为。不然，恩典就不是恩典了。

chapters.en: What then? What the people of Israel sought so earnestly they did not obtain. The elect among them did, but the others were hardened,
chapters.zh: 这是怎么样呢？以色列人所求的，他们没有得着。惟有蒙拣选的人得着了，其余的就成了顽梗不化的。

chapters.en: as it is written: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see and ears that could not hear, to this very day.”
chapters.zh: 如经上所记，神给他们昏迷的心，眼睛不能看见，耳朵不能听见，直到今日。

chapters.en: And David says: “May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution for them.
chapters.zh: 大卫也说，愿他们的筵席变为网罗，变为机槛，变为绊脚石，作他们的报应。

chapters.en: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.”
chapters.zh: 愿他们的眼睛昏蒙，不得看见。愿你时常弯下他们的腰。

chapters.en: Again I ask: Did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Not at all! Rather, because of their transgression, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel envious.
chapters.zh: 我且说，他们失脚是要他们跌倒吗？断乎不是。反倒因他们的过失，救恩便临到外邦人，要激动他们发愤。

chapters.en: But if their transgression means riches for the world, and their loss means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches will their full inclusion bring!
chapters.zh: 若他们的过失，为天下的富足，他们的缺乏，为外邦人的富足。何况他们的丰满呢？

chapters.en: I am talking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the Gentiles, I take pride in my ministry
chapters.zh: 我对你们外邦人说这话。因我是外邦人的使徒，所以敬重我的职分。（敬重原文作荣耀）

chapters.en: in the hope that I may somehow arouse my own people to envy and save some of them.
chapters.zh: 或者可以激动我骨肉之亲发愤，好救他们一些人。

chapters.en: For if their rejection brought reconciliation to the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
chapters.zh: 若他们被丢弃，天下就得与神和好，他们被收纳，岂不是死而复生吗？

chapters.en: If the part of the dough offered as firstfruits is holy, then the whole batch is holy; if the root is holy, so are the branches.
chapters.zh: 所献的新面，若是圣洁，全团也就圣洁了。树根若是圣洁，树枝也就圣洁了。

chapters.en: If some of the branches have been broken off, and you, though a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others and now share in the nourishing sap from the olive root,
chapters.zh: 若有几根枝子被折下来，你这野橄榄得接在其中，一同得着橄榄根的肥汁。

chapters.en: do not consider yourself to be superior to those other branches. If you do, consider this: You do not support the root, but the root supports you.
chapters.zh: 你就不可向旧枝子夸口，若是夸口，当知道不是你托着根，乃是根托着你。

chapters.en: You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”
chapters.zh: 你若说，那枝子被折下来，是特为叫我接上。

chapters.en: Granted. But they were broken off because of unbelief, and you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but tremble.
chapters.zh: 不错。他们因为不信，所以被折下来。你因为信，所以立得住。你不可自高，反要惧怕。

chapters.en: For if God did not spare the natural branches, he will not spare you either.
chapters.zh: 神既不爱惜原来的枝子，也必不爱惜你。

chapters.en: Consider therefore the kindness and sternness of God: sternness to those who fell, but kindness to you, provided that you continue in his kindness. Otherwise, you also will be cut off.
chapters.zh: 可见神的恩慈，和严厉。向那跌倒的人，是严厉的。向你是有恩慈的，只要你长久在他的恩慈里。不然，你也要被砍下来。

chapters.en: And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
chapters.zh: 而且他们若不是长久不信，仍要被接上。因为神能够把他们从新接上。

chapters.en: After all, if you were cut out of an olive tree that is wild by nature, and contrary to nature were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!
chapters.zh: 你是从那天生的野橄榄上砍下来的，尚且逆着性得接在好橄榄上，何况这本树的枝子，要接在本树上呢。

chapters.en: I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers and sisters, so that you may not be conceited: Israel has experienced a hardening in part until the full number of the Gentiles has come in,
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我不愿意你们不知道这奥秘，（恐怕你们自以为聪明）就是以色列人有几分是硬心的，等到外邦人的数目添满了。

chapters.en: and in this way all Israel will be saved. As it is written: “The deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn godlessness away from Jacob.
chapters.zh: 于是以色列全家都要得救，如经上所记，必有一位救主，从锡安出来，要消除雅各家的一切罪恶。

chapters.en: And this is my covenant with them when I take away their sins.”
chapters.zh: 又说，我除去他们罪的时候，这就是我与他们所立的约。

chapters.en: As far as the gospel is concerned, they are enemies for your sake; but as far as election is concerned, they are loved on account of the patriarchs,
chapters.zh: 就着福音说，他们为你们的缘故是仇敌。就着拣选说，他们为列祖的缘故是蒙爱的。

chapters.en: for God’s gifts and his call are irrevocable.
chapters.zh: 因为神的恩赐和选召，是没有后悔的。

chapters.en: Just as you who were at one time disobedient to God have now received mercy as a result of their disobedience,
chapters.zh: 你们从前不顺服神，如今因他们的不顺服，你们倒蒙了怜恤。

chapters.en: so they too have now become disobedient in order that they too may now receive mercy as a result of God’s mercy to you.
chapters.zh: 这样，他们也是不顺服，叫他们因着施给你们的怜恤，现在也就蒙怜恤。

chapters.en: For God has bound everyone over to disobedience so that he may have mercy on them all.
chapters.zh: 因为神将众人都圈在不顺服之中，特意要怜恤众人。

chapters.en: Oh, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable his judgments, and his paths beyond tracing out!
chapters.zh: 深哉，神丰富的智慧和知识。他的判断，何其难测，他的踪迹，何其难寻，

chapters.en: “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?”
chapters.zh: 谁知道主的心？谁作过他的谋士呢？

chapters.en: “Who has ever given to God, that God should repay them?”
chapters.zh: 谁是先给了他，使他后来偿还呢？

chapters.en: For from him and through him and for him are all things. To him be the glory forever! Amen.
chapters.zh: 因为万有都是本于他，倚靠他，归于他。愿荣耀归给他，直到永远。阿们。

chapters.en: Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—this is your true and proper worship.
chapters.zh: 所以弟兄们，我以神的慈悲劝你们，将身体献上，当作活祭，是圣洁的，是神所喜悦的。你们如此事奉，乃是理所当然的。

chapters.en: Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will.
chapters.zh: 不要效法这个世界。只要心意更新而变化，叫你们察验何为神的善良，纯全可喜悦的旨意。

chapters.en: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but rather think of yourself with sober judgment, in accordance with the faith God has distributed to each of you.
chapters.zh: 我凭着所赐我的恩，对你们各人说，不要看自己过于所当看的。要照着神所分给各人信心的大小，看得合乎中道。

chapters.en: For just as each of us has one body with many members, and these members do not all have the same function,
chapters.zh: 正如我们一个身子上有好些肢体，肢体也不都是一样的用处。

chapters.en: so in Christ we, though many, form one body, and each member belongs to all the others.
chapters.zh: 我们这许多人，在基督里成为一身，互相联络作肢体，也是如此。

chapters.en: We have different gifts, according to the grace given to each of us. If your gift is prophesying, then prophesy in accordance with your faith;
chapters.zh: 按我们所得的恩赐，各有不同。或说预言，就当照着信心的程度说预言

chapters.en: if it is serving, then serve; if it is teaching, then teach;
chapters.zh: 或作执事，就当专一执事。或作教导的，就当专一教导。

chapters.en: if it is to encourage, then give encouragement; if it is giving, then give generously; if it is to lead, do it diligently; if it is to show mercy, do it cheerfully.
chapters.zh: 或作劝化的，就当专一劝化。施舍的就当诚实。治理的，就当殷勤。怜悯人的，就当甘心。

chapters.en: Love must be sincere. Hate what is evil; cling to what is good.
chapters.zh: 爱人不可虚假，恶要厌恶，善要亲近。

chapters.en: Be devoted to one another in love. Honor one another above yourselves.
chapters.zh: 爱弟兄，要彼此亲热。恭敬人，要彼此推让。

chapters.en: Never be lacking in zeal, but keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
chapters.zh: 殷勤不可懒惰。要心里火热。常常服事主。

chapters.en: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer.
chapters.zh: 在指望中要喜乐。在患难中要忍耐。祷告要恒切。

chapters.en: Share with the Lord’s people who are in need. Practice hospitality.
chapters.zh: 圣徒缺乏要帮补。客要一味地款待。

chapters.en: Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.
chapters.zh: 逼迫你们的，要给他们祝福。只要祝福，不可咒诅。

chapters.en: Rejoice with those who rejoice; mourn with those who mourn.
chapters.zh: 与喜乐的人要同乐。与哀哭的人要同哭。

chapters.en: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but be willing to associate with people of low position. Do not be conceited.
chapters.zh: 要彼此同心。不要志气高大，倒要俯就卑微的人。（人或作事）不要自以为聪明。

chapters.en: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Be careful to do what is right in the eyes of everyone.
chapters.zh: 不要以恶报恶，众人以为美的事，要留心去作。

chapters.en: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
chapters.zh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

chapters.en: Do not take revenge, my dear friends, but leave room for God’s wrath, for it is written: “It is mine to avenge; I will repay,” says the Lord.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的弟兄，不要自己伸冤，宁可让步，听凭主怒。（或作让人发怒）因为经上记着，主说，伸冤在我。我必报应。

chapters.en: On the contrary: “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink. In doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head.”
chapters.zh: 所以，你的仇敌若饿了，就给他吃。若渴了，就给他喝。因为你这样行，就是把炭火堆在他的头上。

chapters.en: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
chapters.zh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

chapters.en: Let everyone be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which God has established. The authorities that exist have been established by God.
chapters.zh: 在上有权柄的，人人当顺服他。因为没有权柄不是出于神的。凡掌权的都是神所命的。

chapters.en: Consequently, whoever rebels against the authority is rebelling against what God has instituted, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.
chapters.zh: 所以抗拒掌权的，就是抗拒神的命。抗拒的必自取刑罚

chapters.en: For rulers hold no terror for those who do right, but for those who do wrong. Do you want to be free from fear of the one in authority? Then do what is right and you will be commended.
chapters.zh: 作官的原不是叫行善的惧怕，乃是叫作恶的惧怕。你愿意不惧怕掌权的吗？你只要行善，就可得他的称赞。

chapters.en: For the one in authority is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for rulers do not bear the sword for no reason. They are God’s servants, agents of wrath to bring punishment on the wrongdoer.
chapters.zh: 因为他是神的用人，是与你有益的。你若作恶，却当惧怕。因为他不是空空的佩剑。他是神的用人，是伸冤的，刑罚那作恶的。

chapters.en: Therefore, it is necessary to submit to the authorities, not only because of possible punishment but also as a matter of conscience.
chapters.zh: 所以你们必须顺服，不但是因为刑罚，也是因为良心。

chapters.en: This is also why you pay taxes, for the authorities are God’s servants, who give their full time to governing.
chapters.zh: 你们纳粮，也为这个缘故。因他们是神的差役，常常特管这事。

chapters.en: Give to everyone what you owe them: If you owe taxes, pay taxes; if revenue, then revenue; if respect, then respect; if honor, then honor.
chapters.zh: 凡人所当得的，就给他。当得粮的，给他纳粮。当得税的，给他上税。当惧怕的，惧怕他。当恭敬的，恭敬他。

chapters.en: Let no debt remain outstanding, except the continuing debt to love one another, for whoever loves others has fulfilled the law.
chapters.zh: 凡事都不可亏欠人，惟有彼此相爱，要常以为亏欠。因为爱人的就完全了律法。

chapters.en: The commandments, “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not covet,” and whatever other command there may be, are summed up in this one command: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
chapters.zh: 像那不可奸淫，不可杀人，不可偷盗，不可贪婪，或有别的诫命，都包在爱人如己这一句话之内了。

chapters.en: Love does no harm to a neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
chapters.zh: 爱是不加害与人的，所以爱就完全了律法。

chapters.en: And do this, understanding the present time: The hour has already come for you to wake up from your slumber, because our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
chapters.zh: 再者，你们晓得现今就是该趁早睡醒的时候，因为我们得救，现今比初信的时候更近了。

chapters.en: The night is nearly over; the day is almost here. So let us put aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
chapters.zh: 黑夜已深，白昼将近。我们就当脱去暗昧的行为，带上光明的兵器。

chapters.en: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
chapters.zh: 行事为人要端正，好像行在白昼。不可荒宴醉酒。不可好色邪荡。不可争竞嫉妒。

chapters.en: Rather, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not think about how to gratify the desires of the flesh.
chapters.zh: 总要披戴主耶稣基督，不要为肉体安排，去放纵私欲。

chapters.en: Accept the one whose faith is weak, without quarreling over disputable matters.
chapters.zh: 信心软弱的，你们要接纳，但不要辩论所疑惑的事。

chapters.en: One person’s faith allows them to eat anything, but another, whose faith is weak, eats only vegetables.
chapters.zh: 有人信百物都可吃。但那软弱的，只吃蔬菜。

chapters.en: The one who eats everything must not treat with contempt the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted them.
chapters.zh: 吃的人不可轻看不吃的人。不吃的人不可论断吃的人。因为神已经收纳他了。

chapters.en: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To their own master, servants stand or fall. And they will stand, for the Lord is able to make them stand.
chapters.zh: 你是谁，竟论断别人的仆人呢？他或站住，或跌倒，自有他的主人在。而且他也必要站住。因为主能使他站住。

chapters.en: One person considers one day more sacred than another; another considers every day alike. Each of them should be fully convinced in their own mind.
chapters.zh: 有人看这日比那日强，有人看日日都是一样。只是各人心里要意见坚定。

chapters.en: Whoever regards one day as special does so to the Lord. Whoever eats meat does so to the Lord, for they give thanks to God; and whoever abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
chapters.zh: 守日的人，是为主守的。吃的人，是为主吃的，因他感谢神。不吃的人，是为主不吃的，也感谢神。

chapters.en: For none of us lives for ourselves alone, and none of us dies for ourselves alone.
chapters.zh: 我们没有一个人为自己活，也没有一个人为自己死。

chapters.en: If we live, we live for the Lord; and if we die, we die for the Lord. So, whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我们若活着，是为主而活。若死了，是为主而死。所以我们或活或死，总是主的人。

chapters.en: For this very reason, Christ died and returned to life so that he might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
chapters.zh: 因此基督死了，又活了，为要作死人并活人的主。

chapters.en: You, then, why do you judge your brother or sister ? Or why do you treat them with contempt? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.
chapters.zh: 你这个人，为什么论断弟兄呢？又为什么轻看弟兄呢？因我们都要站在神的台前。

chapters.en: It is written: “ ‘As surely as I live,’ says the Lord, ‘every knee will bow before me; every tongue will acknowledge God.’ ”
chapters.zh: 经上写着，主说，我凭着我的永生起誓，万膝必向我跪拜，万口必向我承认。

chapters.en: So then, each of us will give an account of ourselves to God.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，我们各人必要将自己的事，在神面前说明。

chapters.en: Therefore let us stop passing judgment on one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in the way of a brother or sister.
chapters.zh: 所以我们不可再彼此论断。宁可定意谁也不给弟兄放下绊脚跌人之物。

chapters.en: I am convinced, being fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for that person it is unclean.
chapters.zh: 我凭着主耶稣确知深信，凡物本来没有不洁净的。惟独人以为不洁净的，在他就不洁净了。

chapters.en: If your brother or sister is distressed because of what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy someone for whom Christ died.
chapters.zh: 你若因食物叫弟兄忧愁，就不是按着爱人的道理行。基督已经替他死，你不可因你的食物叫他败坏。

chapters.en: Therefore do not let what you know is good be spoken of as evil.
chapters.zh: 不可叫你的善被人毁谤。

chapters.en: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit,
chapters.zh: 因为神的国，不在乎吃喝，只在乎公义，和平，并圣灵中的喜乐。

chapters.en: because anyone who serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and receives human approval.
chapters.zh: 在这几样上服事基督的，就为神所喜悦，又为人所称许。

chapters.en: Let us therefore make every effort to do what leads to peace and to mutual edification.
chapters.zh: 所以我们务要追求和睦的事，与彼此建立德行的事。

chapters.en: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a person to eat anything that causes someone else to stumble.
chapters.zh: 不可因食物毁坏神的工程。凡物固然洁净，但有人因食物叫人跌倒，就是他的罪了。

chapters.en: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything else that will cause your brother or sister to fall.
chapters.zh: 无论是吃肉，是喝酒，是什么别的事，叫弟兄跌倒，一概不作才好。

chapters.en: So whatever you believe about these things keep between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
chapters.zh: 你有信心，就当在神面前守着。人在自己以为可行的事上，能不自责，就有福了。

chapters.en: But whoever has doubts is condemned if they eat, because their eating is not from faith; and everything that does not come from faith is sin.
chapters.zh: 若有疑心而吃的，就必有罪。因为他吃，不是出于信心。凡不出于信心的都是罪。

chapters.en: We who are strong ought to bear with the failings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
chapters.zh: 我们坚固的人，应该担代不坚固人的软弱，不求自己的喜悦。

chapters.en: Each of us should please our neighbors for their good, to build them up.
chapters.zh: 我们各人务要叫邻舍喜悦，使他得益处，建立德行

chapters.en: For even Christ did not please himself but, as it is written: “The insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.”
chapters.zh: 因为基督也不求自己的喜悦，如经上所记，辱骂你人的辱骂，都落在我身上。

chapters.en: For everything that was written in the past was written to teach us, so that through the endurance taught in the Scriptures and the encouragement they provide we might have hope.
chapters.zh: 从前所写的圣经都是为教训我们写的，叫我们因圣经所生的忍耐和安慰，可以得着盼望。

chapters.en: May the God who gives endurance and encouragement give you the same attitude of mind toward each other that Christ Jesus had,
chapters.zh: 但愿赐忍耐安慰的神，叫你们彼此同心，效法基督耶稣。

chapters.en: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 一心一口，荣耀神，我们主耶稣基督的父。

chapters.en: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring praise to God.
chapters.zh: 所以你们要彼此接纳，如同基督接纳你们一样，使荣耀归与神。

chapters.en: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the Jews on behalf of God’s truth, so that the promises made to the patriarchs might be confirmed
chapters.zh: 我说，基督是为神真理作了受割礼人的执事，要证实所应许列祖的话。

chapters.en: and, moreover, that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. As it is written: “Therefore I will praise you among the Gentiles; I will sing the praises of your name.”
chapters.zh: 并叫外邦人，因他的怜悯，荣耀神。如经上所记，因此我要在外邦中称赞你，歌颂你的名。

chapters.en: Again, it says, “Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people.”
chapters.zh: 又说，你们外邦人，当与主的百姓一同欢乐。

chapters.en: And again, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles; let all the peoples extol him.”
chapters.zh: 又说，外邦阿，你们当赞美主。万民哪，你们都当颂赞他。

chapters.en: And again, Isaiah says, “The Root of Jesse will spring up, one who will arise to rule over the nations; in him the Gentiles will hope.”
chapters.zh: 又有以赛亚说，将来有耶西的根，就是那兴起来要治理外邦的。外邦人要仰望他。

chapters.en: May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust in him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 但愿使人有盼望的神，因信将诸般的喜乐平安，充满你们的心，使你们借着圣灵的能力，大有盼望。

chapters.en: I myself am convinced, my brothers and sisters, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with knowledge and competent to instruct one another.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我自己也深信你们是满有良善，充足了诸般的知识，也能彼此劝戒。

chapters.en: Yet I have written you quite boldly on some points to remind you of them again, because of the grace God gave me
chapters.zh: 但我稍微放胆写信给你们，是要提醒你们的记性，特因神所给我的恩典，

chapters.en: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles. He gave me the priestly duty of proclaiming the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 使我为外邦人作基督耶稣的仆役，作神福音的祭司，叫所献上的外邦人，因着圣灵，成为圣洁，可蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: Therefore I glory in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
chapters.zh: 所以论到神的事我在基督耶稣里有可夸的。

chapters.en: I will not venture to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obey God by what I have said and done—
chapters.zh: 除了基督借我作的那些事，我什么都不敢提。只提他借我言语作为，用神迹奇事的能力，并圣灵的能力，使外邦人顺服。

chapters.en: by the power of signs and wonders, through the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
chapters.zh: 甚至我从耶路撒冷，直转到以利哩古，到处传了基督的福音。

chapters.en: It has always been my ambition to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.
chapters.zh: 我立了志向，不在基督的名被称过的地方传福音，免得建造在别人的根基上。

chapters.en: Rather, as it is written: “Those who were not told about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
chapters.zh: 就如经上所记，未曾闻知他信息的，将要看见。未曾听过的，将要明白。

chapters.en: This is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.
chapters.zh: 我因多次被拦阻，总不得到你们那里去。

chapters.en: But now that there is no more place for me to work in these regions, and since I have been longing for many years to visit you,
chapters.zh: 但如今在这里再没有可传的地方，而且这好几年，我切心想望到士班雅去的时候，可以到你们那里。

chapters.en: I plan to do so when I go to Spain. I hope to see you while passing through and to have you assist me on my journey there, after I have enjoyed your company for a while.
chapters.zh: 盼望从你们那里经过，得见你们，先与你们彼此交往，心里稍微满足，然后蒙你们送行。

chapters.en: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem in the service of the Lord’s people there.
chapters.zh: 但现在我往耶路撒冷去，供给圣徒。

chapters.en: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the Lord’s people in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 因为马其顿，和亚该亚人乐意凑出捐项，给耶路撒冷圣徒中的穷人。

chapters.en: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in the Jews’ spiritual blessings, they owe it to the Jews to share with them their material blessings.
chapters.zh: 这固然是他们乐意的。其实也算是所欠的债。因外邦人，既然在他们属灵的好处上有分，就当把养身之物供给他们。

chapters.en: So after I have completed this task and have made sure that they have received this contribution, I will go to Spain and visit you on the way.
chapters.zh: 等我办完了这事，把这善果向他们交付明白，我就要路过你们那里，往士班雅去。

chapters.en: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the full measure of the blessing of Christ.
chapters.zh: 我也晓得去的时候，必带着基督丰盛的恩典而去。

chapters.en: I urge you, brothers and sisters, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我借着我们主耶稣基督，又借着圣灵的爱，劝你们与我一同竭力，为我祈求神。

chapters.en: Pray that I may be kept safe from the unbelievers in Judea and that the contribution I take to Jerusalem may be favorably received by the Lord’s people there,
chapters.zh: 叫我脱离在犹太不顺从的人，也叫我为耶路撒冷所办的捐项，可蒙圣徒悦纳。

chapters.en: so that I may come to you with joy, by God’s will, and in your company be refreshed.
chapters.zh: 并叫我顺着神的旨意，欢欢喜喜地到你们那里，与你们同得安息。

chapters.en: The God of peace be with you all. Amen.
chapters.zh: 愿赐平安的神，常和你们众人同在，阿们。

chapters.en: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a deacon of the church in Cenchreae.
chapters.zh: 我对你们举荐我们的姊妹非比，她是坚革哩教会中的女执事。

chapters.en: I ask you to receive her in the Lord in a way worthy of his people and to give her any help she may need from you, for she has been the benefactor of many people, including me.
chapters.zh: 请你们为主接待她，合乎圣徒的体统。她在何事上，要你们帮助，你们就帮助她。因她素来帮助许多人，也帮助了我。

chapters.en: Greet Priscilla and Aquila, my co-workers in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 问百基拉和亚居拉安。他们在基督耶稣里与我同工，

chapters.en: They risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.
chapters.zh: 也为我的命，将自己的颈项，置之度外。不但我感谢他们，就是外邦的众教会，也感谢他们。

chapters.en: Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my dear friend Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.
chapters.zh: 又问在他们家中的教会安。问我所亲爱的以拜尼土安。他在亚西亚是归基督初结的果子。

chapters.en: Greet Mary, who worked very hard for you.
chapters.zh: 又问马利亚安。她为你们多受劳苦。

chapters.en: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow Jews who have been in prison with me. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.
chapters.zh: 又问我亲属与我一同坐监的安多尼古和犹尼亚安。他们在使徒中是有名望的，也是比我先在基督里。

chapters.en: Greet Ampliatus, my dear friend in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 又问我在主里面所亲爱的暗伯利安。

chapters.en: Greet Urbanus, our co-worker in Christ, and my dear friend Stachys.
chapters.zh: 又问在基督里与我们同工的耳巴奴，并我所亲爱的士大古安。

chapters.en: Greet Apelles, whose fidelity to Christ has stood the test. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
chapters.zh: 又问在基督里经过试验的亚比利安。问亚利多布家里的人安。

chapters.en: Greet Herodion, my fellow Jew. Greet those in the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 又问我亲属希罗天安。问拿其数家在主里的人安。

chapters.en: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, those women who work hard in the Lord. Greet my dear friend Persis, another woman who has worked very hard in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 又问为主劳苦的土非拿氏和土富撒氏安。问可亲爱为主多受劳苦的彼息氏安。

chapters.en: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me, too.
chapters.zh: 又问在主蒙拣选的鲁孚和他母亲安。他的母亲就是我的母亲。

chapters.en: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas and the other brothers and sisters with them.
chapters.zh: 又问亚逊其土，弗勒干，黑米，八罗巴，黑马，并与他们在一处的弟兄们安。

chapters.en: Greet Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the Lord’s people who are with them.
chapters.zh: 又问非罗罗古，和犹利亚，尼利亚，和他姊妹，同阿林巴，并与他们在一处的众圣徒安。

chapters.en: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send greetings.
chapters.zh: 你们亲嘴问安，彼此务要圣洁。基督的众教会都问你们安。

chapters.en: I urge you, brothers and sisters, to watch out for those who cause divisions and put obstacles in your way that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Keep away from them.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，那些离间你们，叫你们跌倒，背乎所学之道的人，我劝你们要留意躲避他们。

chapters.en: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the minds of naive people.
chapters.zh: 因为这样的人不服事我们的主基督，只服事自己的肚腹。用花言巧语，诱惑那些老实人的心。

chapters.en: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice because of you; but I want you to be wise about what is good, and innocent about what is evil.
chapters.zh: 你们的顺服，已经传于众人，所以我为你们欢喜。但我愿意你们在善上聪明，在恶上愚拙。

chapters.en: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
chapters.zh: 赐平安的神，快要将撒但践踏在你们脚下。愿我主耶稣基督的恩，常和你们同在。

chapters.en: Timothy, my co-worker, sends his greetings to you, as do Lucius, Jason and Sosipater, my fellow Jews.
chapters.zh: 与我同工的提摩太，和我的亲属路求，耶孙，所西巴德，问你们安。

chapters.en: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我这代笔写信的德丢，在主里面问你们安。

chapters.en: Gaius, whose hospitality I and the whole church here enjoy, sends you his greetings. Erastus, who is the city’s director of public works, and our brother Quartus send you their greetings.
chapters.zh: 那接待我，也接待全教会的该犹，问你们安。

chapters.en: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.
chapters.zh: 城内管银库的以拉都，和兄弟括土，问你们安。

chapters.en: Now to him who is able to establish you in accordance with my gospel, the message I proclaim about Jesus Christ, in keeping with the revelation of the mystery hidden for long ages past,
chapters.zh: 惟有神能照我所传的福音，和所讲的耶稣基督，并照永古隐藏不言的奥秘，坚固你们的心。

chapters.en: but now revealed and made known through the prophetic writings by the command of the eternal God, so that all the Gentiles might come to the obedience that comes from faith—
chapters.zh: 这奥秘如今显明出来，而且按着永生神的命，借众先知的书指示万国的民，使他们信服真道。

chapters.en: to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.
chapters.zh: 愿荣耀因耶稣基督归与独一全智的神，直到永远。阿们。

chapters.en: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,
chapters.zh: 奉神旨意，蒙召作耶稣基督使徒的保罗，同兄弟所提尼，

chapters.en: To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be his holy people, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ—their Lord and ours:
chapters.zh: 写信给在哥林多神的教会，就是在基督耶稣里成圣，蒙召作圣徒的，以及所有在各处求告我主耶稣基督之名的人。基督是他们的主，也是我们的主。

chapters.en: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠平安，从神我们的父，并主耶稣基督，归与你们。

chapters.en: I always thank my God for you because of his grace given you in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 我常为你们感谢我的神，因神在基督耶稣里所赐给你们的恩惠。

chapters.en: For in him you have been enriched in every way—with all kinds of speech and with all knowledge—
chapters.zh: 又因你们在他里面凡事富足，口才知识都全备。

chapters.en: God thus confirming our testimony about Christ among you.
chapters.zh: 正如我为基督作的见证，在你们心里得以坚固。

chapters.en: Therefore you do not lack any spiritual gift as you eagerly wait for our Lord Jesus Christ to be revealed.
chapters.zh: 以致你们在恩赐上没有一样不及人的。等候我们的主耶稣基督显现。

chapters.en: He will also keep you firm to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 他也必坚固你们到底，叫你们在我们主耶稣基督的日子，无可责备。

chapters.en: God is faithful, who has called you into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
chapters.zh: 神是信实的，你们原是被他所召，好与他儿子，我们的主耶稣基督，一同得分。

chapters.en: I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree with one another in what you say and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly united in mind and thought.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我借我们主耶稣基督的名，劝你们都说一样的话。你们中间也不可分党。只要一心一意彼此相合。

chapters.en: My brothers and sisters, some from Chloe’s household have informed me that there are quarrels among you.
chapters.zh: 因为革来氏家里的人，曾对我提起弟兄们来，说你们中间有分争。

chapters.en: What I mean is this: One of you says, “I follow Paul”; another, “I follow Apollos”; another, “I follow Cephas ”; still another, “I follow Christ.”
chapters.zh: 我的意思就是你们各人说，我是属保罗的。我是属亚波罗的。我是属矶法的。我是属基督的。

chapters.en: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized in the name of Paul?
chapters.zh: 基督是分开的吗？保罗为你们钉了十字架吗？你们是奉保罗的名受了洗吗？

chapters.en: I thank God that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,
chapters.zh: 我感谢神，除了基利司布并该犹以外，我没有给你们一个人施洗。

chapters.en: so no one can say that you were baptized in my name.
chapters.zh: 免得有人说，你们是奉我的名受洗。

chapters.en: (Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I don’t remember if I baptized anyone else.)
chapters.zh: 我也给司提反家施过洗。此外给别人施洗没有，我却记不清。

chapters.en: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel—not with wisdom and eloquence, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.
chapters.zh: 基督差遣我，原不是为施洗，乃是为传福音。并不用智慧的言语，免得基督的十字架落了空。

chapters.en: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
chapters.zh: 因为十字架的道理，在那灭亡的人为愚拙。在我们得救的人却为神的大能。

chapters.en: For it is written: “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the intelligence of the intelligent I will frustrate.”
chapters.zh: 就如经上所记，我要灭绝智慧人的智慧，废弃聪明人的聪明。

chapters.en: Where is the wise person? Where is the teacher of the law? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?
chapters.zh: 智慧人在哪里？文士在哪里？这世上的辩士在哪里？神岂不是叫这世上的智慧变成愚拙吗？

chapters.en: For since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not know him, God was pleased through the foolishness of what was preached to save those who believe.
chapters.zh: 世人凭自己的智慧，既不认识神，神就乐意用人所当作愚拙的道理，拯救那些信的人。这就是神的智慧了。

chapters.en: Jews demand signs and Greeks look for wisdom,
chapters.zh: 犹太人是要神迹，希利尼人是求智慧。

chapters.en: but we preach Christ crucified: a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
chapters.zh: 我们却是传钉十字架的基督，在犹太人为绊脚石，在外邦人为愚拙。

chapters.en: but to those whom God has called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
chapters.zh: 但在那蒙召的无论是犹太人，希利尼人，基督总为神的能力，神的智慧。

chapters.en: For the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.
chapters.zh: 因神的愚拙总比人智慧。神的软弱总比人强壮。

chapters.en: Brothers and sisters, think of what you were when you were called. Not many of you were wise by human standards; not many were influential; not many were of noble birth.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们哪，可见你们蒙召的，按着肉体有智慧的不多，有能力的不多，有尊贵的也不多。

chapters.en: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
chapters.zh: 神却拣选了世上愚拙的，叫有智慧的羞愧。又拣选了世上软弱的，叫那强壮的羞愧。

chapters.en: God chose the lowly things of this world and the despised things—and the things that are not—to nullify the things that are,
chapters.zh: 神也拣选了世上卑贱的，被人厌恶的，以及那无有的，为要废掉那有的。

chapters.en: so that no one may boast before him.
chapters.zh: 使一切有血气的，在神面前一个也不能自夸。

chapters.en: It is because of him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God—that is, our righteousness, holiness and redemption.
chapters.zh: 但你们得在基督耶稣里，是本乎神，神又使他成为我们的智慧，公义，圣洁，救赎。

chapters.en: Therefore, as it is written: “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”
chapters.zh: 如经上所记，夸口的当指着主夸口。

chapters.en: And so it was with me, brothers and sisters. When I came to you, I did not come with eloquence or human wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，从前我到你们那里去，并没有用高言大智对你们宣传神的奥秘。

chapters.en: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and him crucified.
chapters.zh: 因为我曾定了主意，在你们中间不知道别的，只知道耶稣基督，并他钉十字架。

chapters.en: I came to you in weakness with great fear and trembling.
chapters.zh: 我在你们那里，又软弱，又惧怕，又甚战兢。

chapters.en: My message and my preaching were not with wise and persuasive words, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,
chapters.zh: 我说的话，讲的道，不是用智慧委婉的言语，乃是用圣灵和大能的明证。

chapters.en: so that your faith might not rest on human wisdom, but on God’s power.
chapters.zh: 叫你们的信不在乎人的智慧，只在乎神的大能。

chapters.en: We do, however, speak a message of wisdom among the mature, but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.
chapters.zh: 然而在完全的人中，我们也讲智慧。但不是这世上的智慧，也不是这世上有权有位将要败亡之人的智慧。

chapters.en: No, we declare God’s wisdom, a mystery that has been hidden and that God destined for our glory before time began.
chapters.zh: 我们讲的，乃是从前所隐藏，神奥秘的智慧，就是神在万世以前预定使我们得荣耀的。

chapters.en: None of the rulers of this age understood it, for if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
chapters.zh: 这智慧世上有权有位的人没有一个知道的。他们若知道，就不把荣耀的主钉在十字架上了。

chapters.en: However, as it is written: “What no eye has seen, what no ear has heard, and what no human mind has conceived” — the things God has prepared for those who love him—
chapters.zh: 如经上所记，神为爱他的人所预备的，是眼睛未曾看见，耳朵未曾听见，人心也未曾想到的。

chapters.en: these are the things God has revealed to us by his Spirit. The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
chapters.zh: 只有神借着圣灵向我们显明了。因为圣灵参透万事，就是神深奥的事也参透了。

chapters.en: For who knows a person’s thoughts except their own spirit within them? In the same way no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.
chapters.zh: 除了在人里头的灵，谁知道人的事。像这样，除了神的灵，也没有人知道神的事。

chapters.en: What we have received is not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may understand what God has freely given us.
chapters.zh: 我们所领受的，并不是世上的灵，乃是从神来的灵，叫我们能知道神开恩赐给我们的事。

chapters.en: This is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom but in words taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual realities with Spirit-taught words.
chapters.zh: 并且我们讲说这些事，不是用人智慧所指教的言语，乃是用圣灵所指教的言语，将属灵的话，解释属灵的事。（或作将属灵的事讲与属灵的人）

chapters.en: The person without the Spirit does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God but considers them foolishness, and cannot understand them because they are discerned only through the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 然而属血气的人不领会神圣灵的事，反倒以为愚拙。并且不能知道，因为这些事惟有属灵的人才能看透。

chapters.en: The person with the Spirit makes judgments about all things, but such a person is not subject to merely human judgments,
chapters.zh: 属灵的人能看透万事，却没有一人能看透了他。

chapters.en: for, “Who has known the mind of the Lord so as to instruct him?”But we have the mind of Christ.
chapters.zh: 谁曾知道主的心去教导他呢？但我们是有基督的心了。

chapters.en: Brothers and sisters, I could not address you as people who live by the Spirit but as people who are still worldly—mere infants in Christ.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我从前对你们说话，不能把你们当作属灵的，只得把你们当作属肉体，在基督里为婴孩的。

chapters.en: I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for it. Indeed, you are still not ready.
chapters.zh: 我是用奶喂你们，没有用饭喂你们。那时你们不能吃，就是如今还是不能。

chapters.en: You are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and quarreling among you, are you not worldly? Are you not acting like mere humans?
chapters.zh: 你们仍是属肉体的。因为在你们中间有嫉妒分争，这岂不是属乎肉体，照着世人的样子行吗？

chapters.en: For when one says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” are you not mere human beings?
chapters.zh: 有说，我是属保罗的。有说，我是属亚波罗的。这岂不是你们和世人一样吗？

chapters.en: What, after all, is Apollos? And what is Paul? Only servants, through whom you came to believe—as the Lord has assigned to each his task.
chapters.zh: 亚波罗算什么。保罗算什么。无非是执事，照主所赐给他们各人的，引导你们相信。

chapters.en: I planted the seed, Apollos watered it, but God has been making it grow.
chapters.zh: 我栽种了，亚波罗浇灌了。惟有神叫他生长。

chapters.en: So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.
chapters.zh: 可见栽种的算不得什么，浇灌的也算不得什么。只在那叫他生长的神。

chapters.en: The one who plants and the one who waters have one purpose, and they will each be rewarded according to their own labor.
chapters.zh: 栽种的和浇灌的都是一样。但将来各人要照自己的工夫，得自己的赏赐。

chapters.en: For we are co-workers in God’s service; you are God’s field, God’s building.
chapters.zh: 因为我们是与神同工的。你们是神所耕种的田地，所建造的房屋。

chapters.en: By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as a wise builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one should build with care.
chapters.zh: 我照神所给我的恩，好像一个聪明的工头，立好了根基，有别人在上面建造。只是各人要谨慎怎样在上面建造。

chapters.en: For no one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 因为那已经立好的根基，就是耶稣基督，此外没有人能立别的根基。

chapters.en: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay or straw,
chapters.zh: 若有人用金，银，宝石，草木，禾楷，在这根基上建造。

chapters.en: their work will be shown for what it is, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will test the quality of each person’s work.
chapters.zh: 各人的工程必然显露。因为那日子要将它表明出来，有火发现。这火要试验各人的工程怎样。

chapters.en: If what has been built survives, the builder will receive a reward.
chapters.zh: 人在那根基上所建造的工程，若存得住，他就要得赏赐。

chapters.en: If it is burned up, the builder will suffer loss but yet will be saved—even though only as one escaping through the flames.
chapters.zh: 人的工程若被烧了，他就要受亏损。自己却要得救。虽然得救乃像从火里经过的一样。

chapters.en: Don’t you know that you yourselves are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in your midst?
chapters.zh: 岂不知你们是神的殿，神的灵住在你们里头吗？

chapters.en: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person; for God’s temple is sacred, and you together are that temple.
chapters.zh: 若有人毁坏神的殿，神必要毁坏那人。因为神的殿是圣的，这殿就是你们。

chapters.en: Do not deceive yourselves. If any of you think you are wise by the standards of this age, you should become “fools” so that you may become wise.
chapters.zh: 人不可自欺。你们中间若有人，在这世界自以为有智慧，倒不如变作愚拙，好成为有智慧的。

chapters.en: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness” ;
chapters.zh: 因这世界的智慧，在神看是愚拙。如经上记着说，主叫有智慧的中了自己的诡计。

chapters.en: and again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”
chapters.zh: 又说，主知道智慧人的意念是虚妄的。

chapters.en: So then, no more boasting about human leaders! All things are yours,
chapters.zh: 所以无论谁，都不可拿人夸口。因为万有全是你们的。

chapters.en: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future—all are yours,
chapters.zh: 或保罗，或亚波罗，或矶法，或世界，或生，或死，或现今的事，或将来的事，全是你们的。

chapters.en: and you are of Christ, and Christ is of God.
chapters.zh: 并且你们是属基督的。基督又是属神的。

chapters.en: This, then, is how you ought to regard us: as servants of Christ and as those entrusted with the mysteries God has revealed.
chapters.zh: 人应当以我们为基督的执事，为神奥秘事的管家。

chapters.en: Now it is required that those who have been given a trust must prove faithful.
chapters.zh: 所求于管家的，是要他有忠心。

chapters.en: I care very little if I am judged by you or by any human court; indeed, I do not even judge myself.
chapters.zh: 我被你们论断，或被别人论断，我都以为极小的事。连我自己也不论断自己。

chapters.en: My conscience is clear, but that does not make me innocent. It is the Lord who judges me.
chapters.zh: 我虽不觉得自己有错，却也不能因此得以称义。但判断我的乃是主。

chapters.en: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of the heart. At that time each will receive their praise from God.
chapters.zh: 所以时候未到，什么都不要论断，只等主来，他要照出暗中的隐情，显明人心的意念。那时各人要从神那里得着称赞。

chapters.en: Now, brothers and sisters, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us the meaning of the saying, “Do not go beyond what is written.” Then you will not be puffed up in being a follower of one of us over against the other.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我为你们的缘故，拿这些事转比自己和亚波罗。叫你们效法我们不可过于圣经所记。免得你们自高自大，贵重这个，轻看那个。

chapters.en: For who makes you different from anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?
chapters.zh: 使你与人不同的是谁呢？你有什么不是领受的呢？若是领受的，为何自夸，仿佛不是领受的呢？

chapters.en: Already you have all you want! Already you have become rich! You have begun to reign—and that without us! How I wish that you really had begun to reign so that we also might reign with you!
chapters.zh: 你们已经饱足了，已经丰富了，不用我们，自己就作王了。我愿意你们果真作王，叫我们也得与你们一同作王。

chapters.en: For it seems to me that God has put us apostles on display at the end of the procession, like those condemned to die in the arena. We have been made a spectacle to the whole universe, to angels as well as to human beings.
chapters.zh: 我想神把我们使徒明明列在末后，好像定死罪的囚犯。因为我们成了一台戏，给世人和天使观看。

chapters.en: We are fools for Christ, but you are so wise in Christ! We are weak, but you are strong! You are honored, we are dishonored!
chapters.zh: 我们为基督的缘故算是愚拙的，你们在基督里倒是聪明的，我们软弱，你们倒强壮。你们有荣耀，我们倒被藐视。

chapters.en: To this very hour we go hungry and thirsty, we are in rags, we are brutally treated, we are homeless.
chapters.zh: 直到如今，我们还是又饥又渴，又赤身露体，又挨打，又没有一定的住处。

chapters.en: We work hard with our own hands. When we are cursed, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;
chapters.zh: 并且劳苦，亲手作工，被人咒骂，我们就祝福。被人逼迫，我们就忍受。

chapters.en: when we are slandered, we answer kindly. We have become the scum of the earth, the garbage of the world—right up to this moment.
chapters.zh: 被人毁谤，我们就善劝。直到如今，人还把我们看作世界上的污秽，万物中的渣滓。

chapters.en: I am writing this not to shame you but to warn you as my dear children.
chapters.zh: 我写这话，不是叫你们羞愧，乃是警戒你们，好像我所亲爱的儿女一样。

chapters.en: Even if you had ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
chapters.zh: 你们学基督的，师傅虽有一万，为父的却是不多，因我在基督耶稣里用福音生了你们。

chapters.en: Therefore I urge you to imitate me.
chapters.zh: 所以我求你们效法我。

chapters.en: For this reason I have sent to you Timothy, my son whom I love, who is faithful in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which agrees with what I teach everywhere in every church.
chapters.zh: 因此我已打发提摩太到你们那里去。他在主里面，是我所亲爱有忠心的儿子。他必提醒你们，记念我在基督里怎样行事，在各处各教会中怎样教导人。

chapters.en: Some of you have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you.
chapters.zh: 有些人自高自大，以为我不到你们那里去。

chapters.en: But I will come to you very soon, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only how these arrogant people are talking, but what power they have.
chapters.zh: 然而主若许我，我必快到你们那里去。并且我所要知道的，不是那些自高自大之人的言语，乃是他们的权能。

chapters.en: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.
chapters.zh: 因为神的国不在乎言语，乃在乎权能。

chapters.en: What do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod of discipline, or shall I come in love and with a gentle spirit?
chapters.zh: 你们愿意怎么样呢？是愿意我带着刑杖到你们那里去呢？还是要我存慈爱温柔的心呢？

chapters.en: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that even pagans do not tolerate: A man is sleeping with his father’s wife.
chapters.zh: 风闻在你们中间有淫乱的事。这样的淫乱，连外邦人中也没有，就是有人收了他的继母。

chapters.en: And you are proud! Shouldn’t you rather have gone into mourning and have put out of your fellowship the man who has been doing this?
chapters.zh: 你们还是自高自大，并不哀痛，把行这事的人从你们中间赶出去。

chapters.en: For my part, even though I am not physically present, I am with you in spirit. As one who is present with you in this way, I have already passed judgment in the name of our Lord Jesus on the one who has been doing this.
chapters.zh: 我身子虽不在你们那里，心却在你们那里，好像我亲自与你们同在，已经判断了行这事的人，

chapters.en: So when you are assembled and I am with you in spirit, and the power of our Lord Jesus is present,
chapters.zh: 就是你们聚会的时候，我的心也同在，奉我们主耶稣的名，并用我们主耶稣的权能，

chapters.en: hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 要把这样的人交给撒但，败坏他的肉体，使他的灵魂在主耶稣的日子可以得救。

chapters.en: Your boasting is not good. Don’t you know that a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough?
chapters.zh: 你们这自夸是不好的。岂不知一点面酵能使全团发起来吗？

chapters.en: Get rid of the old yeast, so that you may be a new unleavened batch—as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
chapters.zh: 你们既是无酵的面，应当把旧酵除净，好使你们成为新团。因为我们逾越节的羔羊基督已经被杀献祭了。

chapters.en: Therefore let us keep the Festival, not with the old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们守这节不可用旧酵，也不可用恶毒（或作阴毒），邪恶的酵，只用诚实真正的无酵饼。

chapters.en: I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people—
chapters.zh: 我先前写信给你们说，不可与淫乱的人相交。

chapters.en: not at all meaning the people of this world who are immoral, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters. In that case you would have to leave this world.
chapters.zh: 此话不是指这世上一概行淫乱的，或贪婪的，勒索的，或拜偶像的，若是这样，你们除非离开世界方可。

chapters.en: But now I am writing to you that you must not associate with anyone who claims to be a brother or sister but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or slanderer, a drunkard or swindler. Do not even eat with such people.
chapters.zh: 但如今我写信给你们说，若有称为弟兄，是行淫乱的，或贪婪的，或拜偶像的，或辱骂的，或醉酒的，或勒索的。这样的人不可与他相交。就是与他吃饭都不可。

chapters.en: What business is it of mine to judge those outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside?
chapters.zh: 因为审判教外的人与我何干。教内的人岂不是你们审判的吗？

chapters.en: God will judge those outside. “Expel the wicked person from among you.”
chapters.zh: 至于外人有神审判他们。你们应当把那恶人从你们中间赶出去。

chapters.en: If any of you has a dispute with another, do you dare to take it before the ungodly for judgment instead of before the Lord’s people?
chapters.zh: 你们中间有彼此相争的事，怎敢在不义的人面前求审，不在圣徒面前求审呢？

chapters.en: Or do you not know that the Lord’s people will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases?
chapters.zh: 岂不知圣徒要审判世界吗？若世界为你们所审，难道你们不配审判这最小的事吗？

chapters.en: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life!
chapters.zh: 岂不知我们要审判天使吗？何况今生的事呢？

chapters.en: Therefore, if you have disputes about such matters, do you ask for a ruling from those whose way of life is scorned in the church?
chapters.zh: 既是这样，你们若有今生的事当审判，是派教会所轻看的人审判吗？

chapters.en: I say this to shame you. Is it possible that there is nobody among you wise enough to judge a dispute between believers?
chapters.zh: 我说这话，是要叫你们羞耻。难道你们中间没有一个智慧人，能审断弟兄们的事吗？

chapters.en: But instead, one brother takes another to court—and this in front of unbelievers!
chapters.zh: 你们竟是弟兄与弟兄告状，而且告在不信主的人面前。

chapters.en: The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means you have been completely defeated already. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?
chapters.zh: 你们彼此告状，这已经是你们的大错了。为什么不情愿受欺呢？为什么不情愿吃亏呢？

chapters.en: Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, and you do this to your brothers and sisters.
chapters.zh: 你们倒是欺压人，亏负人，况且所欺压，所亏负的就是弟兄。

chapters.en: Or do you not know that wrongdoers will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral nor idolaters nor adulterers nor men who have sex with men
chapters.zh: 你们岂不知不义的人不能承受神的国吗？不要自欺。无论是淫乱的，拜偶像的，奸淫的，作娈童的，亲男色的，

chapters.en: nor thieves nor the greedy nor drunkards nor slanderers nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.
chapters.zh: 偷窃的，贪婪的，醉酒的，辱骂的，勒索的，都不能承受神的国。

chapters.en: And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
chapters.zh: 你们中间也有人从前是这样。但如今你们奉主耶稣基督的名，并借着我们神的灵，已经洗净，成圣称义了。

chapters.en: “I have the right to do anything,” you say—but not everything is beneficial. “I have the right to do anything”—but I will not be mastered by anything.
chapters.zh: 凡事我都可行。但不都有益处。凡事我都可行，但无论那一件，我总不受他的辖制。

chapters.en: You say, “Food for the stomach and the stomach for food, and God will destroy them both.” The body, however, is not meant for sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
chapters.zh: 食物是为肚腹，肚腹是为食物。但神要叫这两样都废坏。身子不是为淫乱，乃是为主。主也是为身子。

chapters.en: By his power God raised the Lord from the dead, and he will raise us also.
chapters.zh: 并且神已经叫主复活，也要用自己的能力叫我们复活。

chapters.en: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ himself? Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Never!
chapters.zh: 岂不知你们的身子是基督的肢体吗？我可以将基督的肢体作为娼妓的肢体吗？断乎不可。

chapters.en: Do you not know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is said, “The two will become one flesh.”
chapters.zh: 岂不知与娼妓联合的，便是与她成为一体吗？因为主说，二人要成为一体。

chapters.en: But whoever is united with the Lord is one with him in spirit.
chapters.zh: 但与主联合的，便是与主成为一灵。

chapters.en: Flee from sexual immorality. All other sins a person commits are outside the body, but whoever sins sexually, sins against their own body.
chapters.zh: 你们要逃避淫行。人所犯的，无论什么罪，都在身子以外。惟有行淫的，是得罪自己的身子。

chapters.en: Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;
chapters.zh: 岂不知你们的身子就是圣灵的殿吗？这圣灵是从神而来，住在你们里头的。并且你们不是自己的人。

chapters.en: you were bought at a price. Therefore honor God with your bodies.
chapters.zh: 因为你们是重价买来的。所以要在你们的身子上荣耀神。

chapters.en: Now for the matters you wrote about: “It is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman.”
chapters.zh: 论到你们信上所提的事，我说男不近女倒好。

chapters.en: But since sexual immorality is occurring, each man should have sexual relations with his own wife, and each woman with her own husband.
chapters.zh: 但要免淫乱的事，男子当各有自己的妻子，女子也当各有自己的丈夫。

chapters.en: The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.
chapters.zh: 丈夫当用合宜之分待妻子，妻子待丈夫也要如此。

chapters.en: The wife does not have authority over her own body but yields it to her husband. In the same way, the husband does not have authority over his own body but yields it to his wife.
chapters.zh: 妻子没有权柄主张自己的身子，乃在丈夫。丈夫也没有权柄主张自己的身子，乃在妻子。

chapters.en: Do not deprive each other except perhaps by mutual consent and for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again so that Satan will not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
chapters.zh: 夫妻不可彼此亏负，除非两相情愿，暂时分房，为要专心祷告方可，以后仍要同房，免得撒但趁着你们情不自禁，引诱你们。

chapters.en: I say this as a concession, not as a command.
chapters.zh: 我说这话，原是准你们的，不是命你们的。

chapters.en: I wish that all of you were as I am. But each of you has your own gift from God; one has this gift, another has that.
chapters.zh: 我愿意众人像我一样。只是各人领受神的恩赐，一个是这样，一个是那样。

chapters.en: Now to the unmarried and the widows I say: It is good for them to stay unmarried, as I do.
chapters.zh: 我对着没有嫁娶的和寡妇说，若他们常像我就好。

chapters.en: But if they cannot control themselves, they should marry, for it is better to marry than to burn with passion.
chapters.zh: 倘若自己禁止不住，就可以嫁娶。与其欲火攻心，倒不如嫁娶为妙。

chapters.en: To the married I give this command (not I, but the Lord): A wife must not separate from her husband.
chapters.zh: 至于那已经嫁娶的，我吩咐他们，其实不是我吩咐，乃是主吩咐，说，妻子不可离开丈夫。

chapters.en: But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.
chapters.zh: 若是离开了，不可再嫁。或是仍同丈夫和好。丈夫也不可离弃妻子。

chapters.en: To the rest I say this (I, not the Lord): If any brother has a wife who is not a believer and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.
chapters.zh: 我对其余的人说，不是主说，倘若某弟兄有不信的妻子，妻子也情愿和他同住，他就不要离弃妻子。

chapters.en: And if a woman has a husband who is not a believer and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce him.
chapters.zh: 妻子有不信的丈夫，丈夫也情愿和她同住，她就不要离弃丈夫。

chapters.en: For the unbelieving husband has been sanctified through his wife, and the unbelieving wife has been sanctified through her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but as it is, they are holy.
chapters.zh: 因为不信的丈夫，就因着妻子成了圣洁。并且不信的妻子，就因着丈夫成了圣洁。（丈夫原文作弟兄）不然，你们的儿女就不洁净。但如今他们是圣洁的了。

chapters.en: But if the unbeliever leaves, let it be so. The brother or the sister is not bound in such circumstances; God has called us to live in peace.
chapters.zh: 倘若那不信的人要离去，就由他离去吧。无论是弟兄，是姐妹，遇着这样的事，都不必拘束。神召我们原是要我们和睦。

chapters.en: How do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or, how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
chapters.zh: 你这作妻子的，怎么知道不能救你的丈夫呢？你这作丈夫的，怎么知道不能救你的妻子呢？

chapters.en: Nevertheless, each person should live as a believer in whatever situation the Lord has assigned to them, just as God has called them. This is the rule I lay down in all the churches.
chapters.zh: 只要照主所分给各人的，和神所召各人的而行。我吩咐各教会都是这样。

chapters.en: Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man uncircumcised when he was called? He should not be circumcised.
chapters.zh: 有人已受割礼蒙召呢，就不要废割礼。有人未受割礼蒙召呢，就不要受割礼。

chapters.en: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commands is what counts.
chapters.zh: 受割礼算不得什么，不受割礼也算不得什么。只要守神的诫命就是了。

chapters.en: Each person should remain in the situation they were in when God called them.
chapters.zh: 各人蒙召的时候是什么身分，仍要守住这身分。

chapters.en: Were you a slave when you were called? Don’t let it trouble you—although if you can gain your freedom, do so.
chapters.zh: 你是作奴隶蒙召的吗？不要因此忧虑。若能以自由，就求自由更好。

chapters.en: For the one who was a slave when called to faith in the Lord is the Lord’s freed person; similarly, the one who was free when called is Christ’s slave.
chapters.zh: 因为作奴仆蒙召于主的，就是主所释放的人。作自由之人蒙召的，就是基督的奴仆。

chapters.en: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of human beings.
chapters.zh: 你们是重价买来的。不要作人的奴仆。

chapters.en: Brothers and sisters, each person, as responsible to God, should remain in the situation they were in when God called them.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们各人蒙召的时候是什么身分，仍要在神面前守住这身分。

chapters.en: Now about virgins: I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.
chapters.zh: 论到童身的人，我没有主的命令，但我既蒙主怜恤，能作忠心的人，就把自己的意见告诉你们。

chapters.en: Because of the present crisis, I think that it is good for a man to remain as he is.
chapters.zh: 因现今的艰难，据我看来，人不如守素安常才好。

chapters.en: Are you pledged to a woman? Do not seek to be released. Are you free from such a commitment? Do not look for a wife.
chapters.zh: 你有妻子缠着呢，就不要求脱离。你没有妻子缠着呢，就不要求妻子。

chapters.en: But if you do marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will face many troubles in this life, and I want to spare you this.
chapters.zh: 你若娶妻，并不是犯罪。处女若出嫁，也不是犯罪。然而这等人肉身必受苦难。我却愿意你们免这苦难。

chapters.en: What I mean, brothers and sisters, is that the time is short. From now on those who have wives should live as if they do not;
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我对你们说，时候减少了。从此以后，那有妻子的，要像没有妻子。

chapters.en: those who mourn, as if they did not; those who are happy, as if they were not; those who buy something, as if it were not theirs to keep;
chapters.zh: 哀哭的，要像不哀哭。快乐的，要像不快乐。置买的，要像无有所得。

chapters.en: those who use the things of the world, as if not engrossed in them. For this world in its present form is passing away.
chapters.zh: 用世物的，要像不用世物。因为这世界的样子将要过去了。

chapters.en: I would like you to be free from concern. An unmarried man is concerned about the Lord’s affairs—how he can please the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我愿你们无所挂虑。没有娶妻的，是为主的事挂虑，想怎样叫主喜悦。

chapters.en: But a married man is concerned about the affairs of this world—how he can please his wife—
chapters.zh: 娶了妻的，是为世上的事挂虑，想怎样叫妻子喜悦。

chapters.en: and his interests are divided. An unmarried woman or virgin is concerned about the Lord’s affairs: Her aim is to be devoted to the Lord in both body and spirit. But a married woman is concerned about the affairs of this world—how she can please her husband.
chapters.zh: 妇人和处女也有分别。没有出嫁的，是为主的事挂虑，要身体灵魂都圣洁。已经出嫁的，是为世上的事挂虑，想怎样叫丈夫喜悦。

chapters.en: I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but that you may live in a right way in undivided devotion to the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我说这话，是为你们的益处。不是要牢笼你们，乃是要叫你们行合宜的事，得以殷勤服事主，没有分心的事。

chapters.en: If anyone is worried that he might not be acting honorably toward the virgin he is engaged to, and if his passions are too strong and he feels he ought to marry, he should do as he wants. He is not sinning. They should get married.
chapters.zh: 若有人以为自己待他的女儿不合宜，女儿也过了年岁，事又当行，他就可随意办理，不算有罪，叫二人成亲就是了。

chapters.en: But the man who has settled the matter in his own mind, who is under no compulsion but has control over his own will, and who has made up his mind not to marry the virgin—this man also does the right thing.
chapters.zh: 倘若人心里坚定，没有不得已的事，并且由得自己作主，心里又决定了留下女儿不出嫁，如此行也好。

chapters.en: So then, he who marries the virgin does right, but he who does not marry her does better.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，叫自己的女儿出嫁是好。不叫她出嫁更是好。

chapters.en: A woman is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, but he must belong to the Lord.
chapters.zh: 丈夫活着的时候，妻子是被约束的。丈夫若死了，妻子就可以自由，随意再嫁。只是要嫁这在主里面的人。

chapters.en: In my judgment, she is happier if she stays as she is—and I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
chapters.zh: 然而按我的意见，若常守节更有福气。我也想自己是被神的灵感动了。

chapters.en: Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that “We all possess knowledge.” But knowledge puffs up while love builds up.
chapters.zh: 论到祭偶像之物，我们晓得我们都有知识。但知识是叫人自高自大，惟有爱心能造就人。

chapters.en: Those who think they know something do not yet know as they ought to know.
chapters.zh: 若有人以为自己知道什么，按他所当知道的，他仍是不知道。

chapters.en: But whoever loves God is known by God.
chapters.zh: 若有人爱神，这人乃是神所知道的。

chapters.en: So then, about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that “An idol is nothing at all in the world” and that “There is no God but one.”
chapters.zh: 论到吃祭偶像之物，我们知道偶像在世上算不得什么。也知道神只有一位，再没有别的神。

chapters.en: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as indeed there are many “gods” and many “lords”),
chapters.zh: 虽有称为神的，或在天，或在地。就如那许多的神，许多的主。

chapters.en: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we live; and there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we live.
chapters.zh: 然而我们只有一位神，就是父，万物都本于他，我们也归于他。并有一位主，就是耶稣基督，万物都是借着他有的，我们也是借着他有的。

chapters.en: But not everyone possesses this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that when they eat sacrificial food they think of it as having been sacrificed to a god, and since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.
chapters.zh: 但人不都有这等知识。有人到如今因拜惯了偶像，就以为所吃的是祭偶像之物。他们的良心既然软弱，也就污秽了。

chapters.en: But food does not bring us near to God; we are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.
chapters.zh: 其实食物不能叫神看中我们。因为我们不吃也无损，吃也无益。

chapters.en: Be careful, however, that the exercise of your rights does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
chapters.zh: 只是你们要谨慎，恐怕你们这自由，竟成了那软弱人的绊脚石。

chapters.en: For if someone with a weak conscience sees you, with all your knowledge, eating in an idol’s temple, won’t that person be emboldened to eat what is sacrificed to idols?
chapters.zh: 若有人见你这有知识的，在偶像的庙里坐席，这人的良心若是软弱，岂不放胆去吃那祭偶像之物吗？

chapters.en: So this weak brother or sister, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
chapters.zh: 因此，基督为他死的那软弱弟兄，也就因你的知识沉沦了。

chapters.en: When you sin against them in this way and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们这样得罪弟兄们，伤了他们软弱的良心，就是得罪基督。

chapters.en: Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother or sister to fall into sin, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause them to fall.
chapters.zh: 所以食物若叫我弟兄跌倒，我就永远不吃肉，免得叫我弟兄跌倒了。

chapters.en: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not the result of my work in the Lord?
chapters.zh: 我不是自由的吗？我不是使徒吗？我不是见过我们的主耶稣吗？你们不是我在主里面所作之工吗？

chapters.en: Even though I may not be an apostle to others, surely I am to you! For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 假若在别人我不是使徒，在你们我总是使徒。因为你们在主里正是我作使徒的印证。

chapters.en: This is my defense to those who sit in judgment on me.
chapters.zh: 我对那盘问我的人，就是这样分诉。

chapters.en: Don’t we have the right to food and drink?
chapters.zh: 难道我们没有权柄靠福音吃喝吗？

chapters.en: Don’t we have the right to take a believing wife along with us, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas ?
chapters.zh: 难道我们没有权柄娶信主的姊妹为妻，带着一同往来，仿佛其余的使徒，和主的弟兄，并矶法一样吗？

chapters.en: Or is it only I and Barnabas who lack the right to not work for a living?
chapters.zh: 独有我与巴拿巴没有权柄不作工吗？

chapters.en: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its grapes? Who tends a flock and does not drink the milk?
chapters.zh: 有谁当兵，自备粮饷呢？有谁栽葡萄园，不吃园里的果子呢？有谁牧养牛羊，不吃牛羊的奶呢？

chapters.en: Do I say this merely on human authority? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?
chapters.zh: 我说这话，岂是照人的意见。律法不也是这样说吗？

chapters.en: For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
chapters.zh: 就如摩西的律法记着说，牛在场上踹谷的时候，不可笼住它的嘴。难道神所挂念的是牛吗？

chapters.en: Surely he says this for us, doesn’t he? Yes, this was written for us, because whoever plows and threshes should be able to do so in the hope of sharing in the harvest.
chapters.zh: 不全是为我们说的吗？分明是为我们说的。因为耕种的当存着指望去耕种。打场的也当存得粮的指望去打场。

chapters.en: If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much if we reap a material harvest from you?
chapters.zh: 我们若把属灵的种子撒在你们中间，就是从你们收割奉养肉身之物，这还算大事吗？

chapters.en: If others have this right of support from you, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not use this right. On the contrary, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.
chapters.zh: 若别人在你们身上有这权柄，何况我们呢？然而我们没有用过这权柄，倒凡事忍受，免得基督的福音被阻隔。

chapters.en: Don’t you know that those who serve in the temple get their food from the temple, and that those who serve at the altar share in what is offered on the altar?
chapters.zh: 你们岂不知为圣事劳碌的，就吃殿中的物吗？伺候祭坛的，就分领坛上的物吗？

chapters.en: In the same way, the Lord has commanded that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.
chapters.zh: 主也是这样命定，叫传福音的靠着福音养生。

chapters.en: But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this in the hope that you will do such things for me, for I would rather die than allow anyone to deprive me of this boast.
chapters.zh: 但这权柄我全没有用过。我写这话，并非要你们这样待我。因为我宁可死，也不叫人使我所夸的落了空。
