chapters.en: For when I preach the gospel, I cannot boast, since I am compelled to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
chapters.zh: 我传福音原没有可夸的。因为我是不得已的。若不传福音，我便有祸了。

chapters.en: If I preach voluntarily, I have a reward; if not voluntarily, I am simply discharging the trust committed to me.
chapters.zh: 我若甘心作这事，就有赏赐。若不甘心，责任却已经托付我了。

chapters.en: What then is my reward? Just this: that in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not make full use of my rights as a preacher of the gospel.
chapters.zh: 既是这样，我的赏赐是什么呢？就是我传福音的时候，叫人不花钱得福音，免得用尽我传福音的权柄。

chapters.en: Though I am free and belong to no one, I have made myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.
chapters.zh: 我虽是自由的，无人辖管，然而我甘心作了众人的仆人，为要多得人。

chapters.en: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), so as to win those under the law.
chapters.zh: 向犹太人，我就作犹太人，为要得犹太人。向律法以下的人，我虽不在律法以下，还是作律法以下的人，为要得律法以下的人。

chapters.en: To those not having the law I became like one not having the law (though I am not free from God’s law but am under Christ’s law), so as to win those not having the law.
chapters.zh: 向没有律法的人，我就作没有律法的人，为要得没有律法的人。其实我在神面前，不是没有律法，在基督面前，正在律法之下。

chapters.en: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.
chapters.zh: 向软弱的人，我就作软弱的人，为要得软弱的人。向什么样的人，我就作什么样的人。无论如何，总要救些人。

chapters.en: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, that I may share in its blessings.
chapters.zh: 凡我所行的，都是为福音的缘故，为要与人同得这福音的好处。

chapters.en: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? Run in such a way as to get the prize.
chapters.zh: 岂不知在场上赛跑的都跑，但得奖赏的只有一人。你们也当这样跑，好叫你们得着奖赏。

chapters.en: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
chapters.zh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制。他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕。我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

chapters.en: Therefore I do not run like someone running aimlessly; I do not fight like a boxer beating the air.
chapters.zh: 所以我奔跑，不像无定向的。我斗拳，不像打空气的。

chapters.en: No, I strike a blow to my body and make it my slave so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified for the prize.
chapters.zh: 我是攻克己身，叫身服我。恐怕我传福音给别人，自己反被弃绝了。

chapters.en: For I do not want you to be ignorant of the fact, brothers and sisters, that our ancestors were all under the cloud and that they all passed through the sea.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我不愿意你们不晓得，我们的祖宗从前都在云下，都从海中经过。

chapters.en: They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
chapters.zh: 都在云里海里受洗归了摩西。

chapters.en: They all ate the same spiritual food
chapters.zh: 并且都吃了一样的灵食。

chapters.en: and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.
chapters.zh: 也都喝了一样的灵水。所喝的是出于随着他们的灵磐石。那磐石就是基督。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them; their bodies were scattered in the wilderness.
chapters.zh: 但他们中间，多半是神不喜欢的人。所以在旷野倒毙。

chapters.en: Now these things occurred as examples to keep us from setting our hearts on evil things as they did.
chapters.zh: 这些事都是我们的鉴戒，叫我们不要贪恋恶事，像他们那样贪恋的。

chapters.en: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were; as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.”
chapters.zh: 也不要拜偶像，像他们有人拜的。如经上所记，百姓坐下吃喝，起来玩耍。

chapters.en: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did—and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.
chapters.zh: 我们也不要行奸淫，像他们有人行的，一天就倒毙了二万三千人。

chapters.en: We should not test Christ, as some of them did—and were killed by snakes.
chapters.zh: 也不要试探主，（主有古卷作基督）像他们有人试探的，就被蛇所灭。

chapters.en: And do not grumble, as some of them did—and were killed by the destroying angel.
chapters.zh: 你们也不要发怨言，像他们有发怨言的，就被灭命的所灭。

chapters.en: These things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the culmination of the ages has come.
chapters.zh: 他们遭遇这些事，都要作为鉴戒。并且写在经上，正是警戒我们这末世的人。

chapters.en: So, if you think you are standing firm, be careful that you don’t fall!
chapters.zh: 所以自己以为站得稳的，须要谨慎，免得跌倒。

chapters.en: No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind. And God is faithful; he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, he will also provide a way out so that you can endure it.
chapters.zh: 你们所遇见的试探，无非是人所能受的。神是信实的，必不叫你们受试探过于所能受的。在受试探的时候，总要给你们开一条出路，叫你们能忍受得住。

chapters.en: Therefore, my dear friends, flee from idolatry.
chapters.zh: 我所亲爱的弟兄阿，你们要逃避拜偶像的事。

chapters.en: I speak to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.
chapters.zh: 我好像对明白人说的，你们要审察我的话。

chapters.en: Is not the cup of thanksgiving for which we give thanks a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?
chapters.zh: 我们所祝福的杯，岂不是同领基督的血吗？我们所掰开的饼，岂不是同领基督的身体吗？

chapters.en: Because there is one loaf, we, who are many, are one body, for we all share the one loaf.
chapters.zh: 我们虽多，仍是一个饼，一个身体。因为我们都是分受这一个饼。

chapters.en: Consider the people of Israel: Do not those who eat the sacrifices participate in the altar?
chapters.zh: 你们看属肉体的以色列人。那吃祭物的，岂不是在祭坛上有分吗？

chapters.en: Do I mean then that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
chapters.zh: 我是怎么说呢？岂是说祭偶像之物算得什么呢？或说偶像算得什么呢？

chapters.en: No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God, and I do not want you to be participants with demons.
chapters.zh: 我乃是说，外邦人所献的祭，是祭鬼，不是祭神。我不愿意你们与鬼相交。

chapters.en: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot have a part in both the Lord’s table and the table of demons.
chapters.zh: 你们不能喝主的杯，又喝鬼的杯。不能吃主的筵席，又吃鬼的筵席。

chapters.en: Are we trying to arouse the Lord’s jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
chapters.zh: 我们可惹主的愤恨吗？我们比他还有能力吗？

chapters.en: “I have the right to do anything,” you say—but not everything is beneficial. “I have the right to do anything”—but not everything is constructive.
chapters.zh: 凡事都可行。但不都有益处。凡事都可行。但不都造就人。

chapters.en: No one should seek their own good, but the good of others.
chapters.zh: 无论何人，不要求自己的益处，乃要求别人的益处。

chapters.en: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,
chapters.zh: 凡市上所卖的，你们只管吃，不要为良心的缘故问什么话。

chapters.en: for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and everything in it.”
chapters.zh: 因为地和其中所充满的，都属乎主。

chapters.en: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat whatever is put before you without raising questions of conscience.
chapters.zh: 倘有一个不信的人请你们赴席，你们若愿意去，凡摆在你们面前的，只管吃，不要为良心的缘故问什么话。

chapters.en: But if someone says to you, “This has been offered in sacrifice,” then do not eat it, both for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience.
chapters.zh: 若有人对你们说，这是献过祭的物，就要为那告诉你们的人，并为良心的缘故，不吃。

chapters.en: I am referring to the other person’s conscience, not yours. For why is my freedom being judged by another’s conscience?
chapters.zh: 我说的良心，不是你的，乃是他的。我这自由，为什么被别人的良心论断呢？

chapters.en: If I take part in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of something I thank God for?
chapters.zh: 我若谢恩而吃，为什么因我谢恩的物被人毁谤呢？

chapters.en: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God.
chapters.zh: 所以你们或吃或喝，无论作什么，都要为荣耀神而行。

chapters.en: Do not cause anyone to stumble, whether Jews, Greeks or the church of God—
chapters.zh: 不拘是犹太人，是希利尼人，是神的教会，你们都不要使他跌倒。

chapters.en: even as I try to please everyone in every way. For I am not seeking my own good but the good of many, so that they may be saved.
chapters.zh: 就好像我凡事都叫众人喜欢，不求自己的益处，只求众人的益处，叫他们得救。

chapters.en: Follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们该效法我，像我效法基督一样。

chapters.en: I praise you for remembering me in everything and for holding to the traditions just as I passed them on to you.
chapters.zh: 我称赞你们，因你们凡事记念我，又坚守我所传给你们的。

chapters.en: But I want you to realize that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
chapters.zh: 我愿意你们知道，基督是各人的头。男人是女人的头，神是基督的头。

chapters.en: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
chapters.zh: 凡男人祷告或是讲道（讲道或作说预言下同），若蒙着头，就羞辱自己的头。

chapters.en: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head—it is the same as having her head shaved.
chapters.zh: 凡女人祷告或是讲道，若不蒙着头，就羞辱自己的头。因为这就如同剃了头发一样。

chapters.en: For if a woman does not cover her head, she might as well have her hair cut off; but if it is a disgrace for a woman to have her hair cut off or her head shaved, then she should cover her head.
chapters.zh: 女人若不蒙着头，就该剪了头发。女人若以剪发剃发为羞愧，就该蒙着头。

chapters.en: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man.
chapters.zh: 男人本不该蒙着头，因为他是神的形像和荣耀，但女人是男人的荣耀。

chapters.en: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man;
chapters.zh: 起初，男人不是由女人而出。女人乃是由男人而出。

chapters.en: neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.
chapters.zh: 并且男人不是为女人造的。女人乃是为男人造的。

chapters.en: It is for this reason that a woman ought to have authority over her own head, because of the angels.
chapters.zh: 因此，女人为天使的缘故，应当在头上有服权柄的记号。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.
chapters.zh: 然而照主的安排，女也不是无男，男也不是无女。

chapters.en: For as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.
chapters.zh: 因为女人原是由男人而出，男人也是由女人而出。但万有都是出乎神。

chapters.en: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
chapters.zh: 你们自己审察，女人祷告神，不蒙着头，是合宜的吗？

chapters.en: Does not the very nature of things teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,
chapters.zh: 你们的本性不也指示你们，男人若有长头发，便是他的羞辱吗？

chapters.en: but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.
chapters.zh: 但女人有长头发，乃是她的荣耀。因为这头发是给她作盖头的。

chapters.en: If anyone wants to be contentious about this, we have no other practice—nor do the churches of God.
chapters.zh: 若有人想要辩驳，我们却没有这样的规矩，神的众教会也是没有的。

chapters.en: In the following directives I have no praise for you, for your meetings do more harm than good.
chapters.zh: 我现今吩咐你们的话，不是称赞你们。因为你们聚会不是受益，乃是招损。

chapters.en: In the first place, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and to some extent I believe it.
chapters.zh: 第一，我听说你们聚会的时候，彼此分门别类。我也稍微的信这话。

chapters.en: No doubt there have to be differences among you to show which of you have God’s approval.
chapters.zh: 在你们中间不免有分门结党的事，好叫那些有经验的人，显明出来。

chapters.en: So then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat,
chapters.zh: 你们聚会的时候，算不得吃主的晚餐。

chapters.en: for when you are eating, some of you go ahead with your own private suppers. As a result, one person remains hungry and another gets drunk.
chapters.zh: 因为吃的时候，各人先吃自己的饭，甚至这个饥饿，那个酒醉。

chapters.en: Don’t you have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God by humiliating those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? Certainly not in this matter!
chapters.zh: 你们要吃喝，难道没有家吗？还是藐视神的教会，叫那没有的羞愧呢？我向你们可怎么说呢？可因此称赞你们吗？我不称赞。

chapters.en: For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night he was betrayed, took bread,
chapters.zh: 我当日传给你们的，原是从主领受的，就是主耶稣被卖的那一夜，拿起饼来，

chapters.en: and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of me.”
chapters.zh: 祝谢了，就掰开，说，这是我的身体，为你们舍的（舍有古卷作掰开）。你们应当如此行，为的是记念我。

chapters.en: In the same way, after supper he took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, whenever you drink it, in remembrance of me.”
chapters.zh: 饭后，也照样拿起杯来，说，这杯是用我的血所立的新约。你们每逢喝的时候，要如此行，为的是记念我。

chapters.en: For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
chapters.zh: 你们每逢吃这饼，喝这杯，是表明主的死，直等到他来。

chapters.en: So then, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 所以无论何人，不按理吃主的饼，喝主的杯，就是干犯主的身主的血了。

chapters.en: Everyone ought to examine themselves before they eat of the bread and drink from the cup.
chapters.zh: 人应当自己省察，然后吃这饼，喝这杯。

chapters.en: For those who eat and drink without discerning the body of Christ eat and drink judgment on themselves.
chapters.zh: 因为人吃喝，若不分辨是主的身体，就是吃喝自己的罪了。

chapters.en: That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep.
chapters.zh: 因此，在你们中间有好些软弱的，与患病的，死的也不少（死原文作睡）。

chapters.en: But if we were more discerning with regard to ourselves, we would not come under such judgment.
chapters.zh: 我们若是先分辨自己，就不至于受审。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, when we are judged in this way by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be finally condemned with the world.
chapters.zh: 我们受审的时候，乃是被主惩治。免得我们和世人一同定罪。

chapters.en: So then, my brothers and sisters, when you gather to eat, you should all eat together.
chapters.zh: 所以我弟兄们，你们聚会吃的时候，要彼此等待。

chapters.en: Anyone who is hungry should eat something at home, so that when you meet together it may not result in judgment. And when I come I will give further directions.
chapters.zh: 若有人饥饿，可以在家里先吃。免得你们聚会自己取罪。其余的事，我来的时候再安排。

chapters.en: Now about the gifts of the Spirit, brothers and sisters, I do not want you to be uninformed.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，论到属灵的恩赐，我不愿意你们不明白。

chapters.en: You know that when you were pagans, somehow or other you were influenced and led astray to mute idols.
chapters.zh: 你们作外邦人的时候，随事被牵引受迷惑，去服事那哑吧偶像。这是你们知道的。

chapters.en: Therefore I want you to know that no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 所以我告诉你们，被神的灵感动的，没有说耶稣是可咒诅的。若不是被圣灵感动的，也没有能说耶稣是主的。

chapters.en: There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit distributes them.
chapters.zh: 恩赐原有分别，圣灵却是一位。

chapters.en: There are different kinds of service, but the same Lord.
chapters.zh: 职事也有分别，主却是一位。

chapters.en: There are different kinds of working, but in all of them and in everyone it is the same God at work.
chapters.zh: 功用也有分别，神却是一位，在众人里面运行一切的事。

chapters.en: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.
chapters.zh: 圣灵显在各人身上，是叫人得益处。

chapters.en: To one there is given through the Spirit a message of wisdom, to another a message of knowledge by means of the same Spirit,
chapters.zh: 这人蒙圣灵赐他智慧的言语。那人也蒙这位圣灵赐他知识的言语。

chapters.en: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,
chapters.zh: 又有一人蒙这位圣灵赐他信心。还有一人蒙这位圣灵赐他医病的恩赐。

chapters.en: to another miraculous powers, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in different kinds of tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.
chapters.zh: 又叫一人能行异能。又叫一人能作先知。又叫一人能辨别诸灵。又叫一人能说方言。又叫一人能翻方言。

chapters.en: All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, and he distributes them to each one, just as he determines.
chapters.zh: 这一切都是这位圣灵所运行，随己意分给各人的。

chapters.en: Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ.
chapters.zh: 就如身子是一个，却有许多肢体。而且肢体虽多，仍是一个身子。基督也是这样。

chapters.en: For we were all baptized by one Spirit so as to form one body—whether Jews or Gentiles, slave or free—and we were all given the one Spirit to drink.
chapters.zh: 我们不拘是犹太人，是希利尼人，是为奴的，是自主的，都从一位圣灵受洗，成了一个身体。饮于一位圣灵。

chapters.en: Even so the body is not made up of one part but of many.
chapters.zh: 身子原不是一个肢体，乃是许多肢体。

chapters.en: Now if the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body.
chapters.zh: 设若脚说，我不是手，所以不属乎身子。它不能因此就不属乎身子。

chapters.en: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” it would not for that reason stop being part of the body.
chapters.zh: 设若耳说，我不是眼，所以不属乎身子。它也不能因此就不属乎身子。

chapters.en: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?
chapters.zh: 若全身是眼，从哪里听声呢？若全身是耳，从哪里闻味呢？

chapters.en: But in fact God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be.
chapters.zh: 但如今神随自己的意思，把肢体俱各安排在身上了。

chapters.en: If they were all one part, where would the body be?
chapters.zh: 若都是一个肢体，身子在哪里呢？

chapters.en: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
chapters.zh: 但如今肢体是多的，身子却是一个。

chapters.en: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I don’t need you!” And the head cannot say to the feet, “I don’t need you!”
chapters.zh: 眼不能对手说，我用不着你。头也不能对脚说，我用不着你。

chapters.en: On the contrary, those parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,
chapters.zh: 不但如此，身上肢体人以为软弱的，更是不可少的。

chapters.en: and the parts that we think are less honorable we treat with special honor. And the parts that are unpresentable are treated with special modesty,
chapters.zh: 身上肢体，我们看为不体面的，越发给它加上体面。不俊美的，越发得着俊美。

chapters.en: while our presentable parts need no special treatment. But God has put the body together, giving greater honor to the parts that lacked it,
chapters.zh: 我们俊美的肢体，自然用不着装饰。但神配搭这身子，把加倍的体面给那有缺欠的肢体。

chapters.en: so that there should be no division in the body, but that its parts should have equal concern for each other.
chapters.zh: 免得身上分门别类。总要肢体彼此相顾。

chapters.en: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.
chapters.zh: 若一个肢体受苦，所有的肢体就一同受苦。若一个肢体得荣耀，所有的肢体就一同快乐。

chapters.en: Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
chapters.zh: 你们就是基督的身子，并且各自作肢体。

chapters.en: And God has placed in the church first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, of helping, of guidance, and of different kinds of tongues.
chapters.zh: 神在教会所设立的，第一是使徒。第二是先知，第三是教师。其次是行异能的。再次是得恩赐医病的。帮助人的。治理事的。说方言的。

chapters.en: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
chapters.zh: 岂都是使徒吗？岂都是先知吗？岂都是教师吗？岂都是行异能的吗？

chapters.en: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues ? Do all interpret?
chapters.zh: 岂都是得恩赐医病的吗？岂都是说方言的吗？岂都是翻方言的吗？

chapters.en: Now eagerly desire the greater gifts. And yet I will show you the most excellent way.
chapters.zh: 你们要切切地求那更大的恩赐，我现今把最妙的道指示你们。

chapters.en: If I speak in the tongues of men or of angels, but do not have love, I am only a resounding gong or a clanging cymbal.
chapters.zh: 我若能说万人的方言，并天使的话语却没有爱，我就成了鸣的锣，响的钹一般。

chapters.en: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have a faith that can move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
chapters.zh: 我若有先知讲道之能，也明白各样的奥秘，各样的知识。而且有全备的信，叫我能够移山，却没有爱，我就算不得什么。

chapters.en: If I give all I possess to the poor and give over my body to hardship that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
chapters.zh: 我若将所有的周济穷人，又舍己身叫人焚烧，却没有爱，仍然与我无益。

chapters.en: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
chapters.zh: 爱是恒久忍耐，又有恩慈。爱是不嫉妒。爱是不自夸。不张狂。

chapters.en: It does not dishonor others, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrongs.
chapters.zh: 不作害羞的事。不求自己的益处。不轻易发怒。不计算人的恶。

chapters.en: Love does not delight in evil but rejoices with the truth.
chapters.zh: 不喜欢不义。只喜欢真理。

chapters.en: It always protects, always trusts, always hopes, always perseveres.
chapters.zh: 凡事包容。凡事相信。凡事盼望。凡事忍耐。

chapters.en: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be stilled; where there is knowledge, it will pass away.
chapters.zh: 爱是永不止息。先知讲道之能，终必归于无有。说方言之能，终必停止，知识也终必归于无有。

chapters.en: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
chapters.zh: 我们现在所知道的有限，先知所讲的也有限。

chapters.en: but when completeness comes, what is in part disappears.
chapters.zh: 等那完全的来到，这有限的必归于无有了。

chapters.en: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I put the ways of childhood behind me.
chapters.zh: 我作孩子的时候，话语像孩子，心思像孩子，意念像孩子。既成了人，就把孩子的事丢弃了。

chapters.en: For now we see only a reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.
chapters.zh: 我们如今仿佛对着镜子观看，模糊不清（模糊不清原文作如同猜谜）。到那时，就要面对面了。我如今所知道的有限。到那时就全知道，如同主知道我一样。

chapters.en: And now these three remain: faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love.
chapters.zh: 如今常存的有信，有望，有爱，这三样，其中最大的是爱。

chapters.en: Follow the way of love and eagerly desire gifts of the Spirit, especially prophecy.
chapters.zh: 你们要追求爱，也要切慕属灵的恩赐，其中更要羡慕的，是作先知讲道。（原文作是说预言下同）

chapters.en: For anyone who speaks in a tongue does not speak to people but to God. Indeed, no one understands them; they utter mysteries by the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 那说方言的，原不是对人说，乃是对神说。因为没有人听出来。然而他在心灵里，却是讲说各样的奥秘。

chapters.en: But the one who prophesies speaks to people for their strengthening, encouraging and comfort.
chapters.zh: 但作先知讲道的，是对人说，要造就，安慰，劝勉人。

chapters.en: Anyone who speaks in a tongue edifies themselves, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.
chapters.zh: 说方言的，是造就自己。作先知讲道的，乃是造就教会。

chapters.en: I would like every one of you to speak in tongues, but I would rather have you prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless someone interprets, so that the church may be edified.
chapters.zh: 我愿意你们都说方言。更愿意你们作先知讲道。因为说方言的，若不翻出来，使教会被造就，那作先知讲道的，就比他强了。

chapters.en: Now, brothers and sisters, if I come to you and speak in tongues, what good will I be to you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or word of instruction?
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我到你们那里去，若只说方言，不用启示，或知识，或预言，或教训，给你们讲解，我与你们有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: Even in the case of lifeless things that make sounds, such as the pipe or harp, how will anyone know what tune is being played unless there is a distinction in the notes?
chapters.zh: 就是那有声无气的物，或箫，或琴，若发出来的声音，没有分别，怎能知道所吹所弹的是什么呢？

chapters.en: Again, if the trumpet does not sound a clear call, who will get ready for battle?
chapters.zh: 若吹无定的号声，谁能预备打仗呢？

chapters.en: So it is with you. Unless you speak intelligible words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.
chapters.zh: 你们也是如此，舌头若不说容易明白的话，怎能知道所说的是什么呢？这就是向空说话了。

chapters.en: Undoubtedly there are all sorts of languages in the world, yet none of them is without meaning.
chapters.zh: 世上的声音，或者甚多，却没有一样是无意思的。

chapters.en: If then I do not grasp the meaning of what someone is saying, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker is a foreigner to me.
chapters.zh: 我若不明白那声音的意思，这说话的人必以我为化外之人，我也以他为化外之人。

chapters.en: So it is with you. Since you are eager for gifts of the Spirit, try to excel in those that build up the church.
chapters.zh: 你们也是如此。既是切慕属灵的恩赐，就当求多得造就教会的恩赐。

chapters.en: For this reason the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that they may interpret what they say.
chapters.zh: 所以那说方言的，就当求着能翻出来。

chapters.en: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
chapters.zh: 我若用方言祷告，是我的灵祷告。但我的悟性没有果效。

chapters.en: So what shall I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my understanding; I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my understanding.
chapters.zh: 这却怎么样呢？我要用灵祷告，也要用悟性祷告。我要用灵歌唱，也要用悟性歌唱。

chapters.en: Otherwise when you are praising God in the Spirit, how can someone else, who is now put in the position of an inquirer, say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since they do not know what you are saying?
chapters.zh: 不然，你用灵祝谢，那在座不通方言的人，既然不明白你的话，怎能在你感谢的时候说阿们呢？

chapters.en: You are giving thanks well enough, but no one else is edified.
chapters.zh: 你感谢的固然是好，无奈不能造就别人。

chapters.en: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
chapters.zh: 我感谢神，我说方言比你们众人还多。

chapters.en: But in the church I would rather speak five intelligible words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.
chapters.zh: 但在教会中，宁可用悟性说五句教导人的话，强如说万句方言。

chapters.en: Brothers and sisters, stop thinking like children. In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be adults.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，在心志上不要作小孩子。然而在恶事上要作婴孩。在心志上总要作大人。

chapters.en: In the Law it is written: “With other tongues and through the lips of foreigners I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.”
chapters.zh: 律法上记着，主说，我要用外邦人的舌头，和外邦人的嘴唇，向这百姓说话。虽然如此，他们还是不听从我。

chapters.en: Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers but for unbelievers; prophecy, however, is not for unbelievers but for believers.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，说方言，不是为信的人作证据，乃是为不信的人。作先知讲道，不是为不信的人作证据，乃是为信的人。

chapters.en: So if the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and inquirers or unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your mind?
chapters.zh: 所以全教会聚在一处的时候，若都说方言，偶然有不通方言的，或是不信的人进来，岂不说你们癫狂了吗？

chapters.en: But if an unbeliever or an inquirer comes in while everyone is prophesying, they are convicted of sin and are brought under judgment by all,
chapters.zh: 若都作先知讲道，偶然有不信的，或是不通方言的人进来，就被众人劝醒，被众人审明。

chapters.en: as the secrets of their hearts are laid bare. So they will fall down and worship God, exclaiming, “God is really among you!”
chapters.zh: 他心里的隐情显露出来，就必将脸伏地，敬拜神，说神真是在你们中间了。

chapters.en: What then shall we say, brothers and sisters? When you come together, each of you has a hymn, or a word of instruction, a revelation, a tongue or an interpretation. Everything must be done so that the church may be built up.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，这却怎么样呢？你们聚会的时候，各人或有诗歌，或有教训，或有启示，或有方言，或有翻出来的话。凡事都当造就人。

chapters.en: If anyone speaks in a tongue, two—or at the most three—should speak, one at a time, and someone must interpret.
chapters.zh: 若有说方言的，只好两个人，至多三个人，且要轮流着说，也要一个人翻出来。

chapters.en: If there is no interpreter, the speaker should keep quiet in the church and speak to himself and to God.
chapters.zh: 若没有人翻，就当在会中闭口。只对自己和神说，就是了。

chapters.en: Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.
chapters.zh: 至于作先知讲道的，只好两个人，或是三个人，其余的就当慎思明辨。

chapters.en: And if a revelation comes to someone who is sitting down, the first speaker should stop.
chapters.zh: 若旁边坐着的得了启示，那先说话的就当闭口不言。

chapters.en: For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.
chapters.zh: 因为你们都可以一个一个地作先知讲道，叫众人学道理，叫众人得劝勉。

chapters.en: The spirits of prophets are subject to the control of prophets.
chapters.zh: 先知的灵，原是顺服先知的。

chapters.en: For God is not a God of disorder but of peace—as in all the congregations of the Lord’s people.
chapters.zh: 因为神不是叫人混乱，乃是叫人安静。

chapters.en: Women should remain silent in the churches. They are not allowed to speak, but must be in submission, as the law says.
chapters.zh: 妇女在会中要闭口不言，像在圣徒的众教会一样。因为不准她们说话。她们总要顺服，正如律法所说的。

chapters.en: If they want to inquire about something, they should ask their own husbands at home; for it is disgraceful for a woman to speak in the church.
chapters.zh: 她们若要学什么，可以在家里问自己的丈夫。因为妇女在会中说话原是可耻的。

chapters.en: Or did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only people it has reached?
chapters.zh: 神的道理，岂是从你们出來么．岂是单临到你们么。

chapters.en: If anyone thinks they are a prophet or otherwise gifted by the Spirit, let them acknowledge that what I am writing to you is the Lord’s command.
chapters.zh: 若有人以为自己是先知或是属灵的，就该知道，我所写给你们的是主的命令。

chapters.en: But if anyone ignores this, they will themselves be ignored.
chapters.zh: 若有不知道的，就由他不知道吧。

chapters.en: Therefore, my brothers and sisters, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
chapters.zh: 所以我弟兄们，你们要切慕作先知讲道，也不要禁止说方言。

chapters.en: But everything should be done in a fitting and orderly way.
chapters.zh: 凡事都要规规矩矩的按着次序行。

chapters.en: Now, brothers and sisters, I want to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, which you received and on which you have taken your stand.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我如今把先前所传给你们的福音，告诉你们知道，这福音你们也领受了，又靠着站立得住。

chapters.en: By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.
chapters.zh: 并且你们若不是徒然相信，能以持守我所传给你们的，就必因这福音得救。

chapters.en: For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance : that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
chapters.zh: 我当日所领受又传给你们的，第一，就是基督照圣经所说，为我们的罪死了。

chapters.en: that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
chapters.zh: 而且埋葬了。又照圣经所说，第三天复活了。

chapters.en: and that he appeared to Cephas, and then to the Twelve.
chapters.zh: 并且显给矶法看。然后显给十二使徒看。

chapters.en: After that, he appeared to more than five hundred of the brothers and sisters at the same time, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.
chapters.zh: 后来一时显给五百多弟兄看，其中一大半到如今还在，却也有已经睡了的。

chapters.en: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,
chapters.zh: 以后显给雅各看。再显给众使徒看。

chapters.en: and last of all he appeared to me also, as to one abnormally born.
chapters.zh: 末了也显给我看。我如同未到产期而生的人一般。

chapters.en: For I am the least of the apostles and do not even deserve to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
chapters.zh: 我原是使徒中最小的，不配称为使徒，因为我从前逼迫神的教会。

chapters.en: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace to me was not without effect. No, I worked harder than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.
chapters.zh: 然而我今日成了何等人，是蒙神的恩才成的。并且他所赐我的恩，不是徒然的。我比众使徒格外劳苦。这原不是我，乃是神的恩与我同在。

chapters.en: Whether, then, it is I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
chapters.zh: 不拘是我是众使徒，我们如此传，你们也如此信了。

chapters.en: But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
chapters.zh: 既传基督是从死里复活了，怎么在你们中间，有人说没有死人复活的事呢？

chapters.en: If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.
chapters.zh: 若没有死人复活的事，基督也就没有复活了。

chapters.en: And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is useless and so is your faith.
chapters.zh: 若基督没有复活，我们所传的便是枉然，你们所信的也是枉然。

chapters.en: More than that, we are then found to be false witnesses about God, for we have testified about God that he raised Christ from the dead. But he did not raise him if in fact the dead are not raised.
chapters.zh: 并且明显我们是为神妄作见证的。因我们见证神是叫基督复活了。若死人真不复活，神也就没有叫基督复活了。

chapters.en: For if the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either.
chapters.zh: 因为死人若不复活，基督也就没有复活了。

chapters.en: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
chapters.zh: 基督若没有复活，你们的信便是徒然。你们仍在罪里。

chapters.en: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ are lost.
chapters.zh: 就是在基督里睡了的人也灭亡了。

chapters.en: If only for this life we have hope in Christ, we are of all people most to be pitied.
chapters.zh: 我们若靠基督，只在今生有指望，就算比众人更可怜。

chapters.en: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
chapters.zh: 但基督已经从死里复活，成为睡了之人初熟的果子。

chapters.en: For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.
chapters.zh: 死既是因一人而来，死人复活也是因一人而来。

chapters.en: For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.
chapters.zh: 在亚当里众人都死了。照样，在基督里众人也都要复活。

chapters.en: But each in turn: Christ, the firstfruits; then, when he comes, those who belong to him.
chapters.zh: 但各人是按着自己的次序复活。初熟的果子是基督。以后在他来的时候，是那些属基督的。

chapters.en: Then the end will come, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father after he has destroyed all dominion, authority and power.
chapters.zh: 再后末期到了，那时，基督既将一切执政的，掌权的，有能的，都毁灭了，就把国交与父神。

chapters.en: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
chapters.zh: 因为基督必要作王，等神把一切仇敌，都放在他的脚下。

chapters.en: The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
chapters.zh: 尽末了所毁灭的仇敌，就是死。

chapters.en: For he “has put everything under his feet.” Now when it says that “everything” has been put under him, it is clear that this does not include God himself, who put everything under Christ.
chapters.zh: 因为经上说，神叫万物都服在他的脚下。既说万物都服了他，明显那叫万物服他的不在其内了。

chapters.en: When he has done this, then the Son himself will be made subject to him who put everything under him, so that God may be all in all.
chapters.zh: 万物既服了他，那时，子也要自己服那叫万物服他的，叫神在万物之上，为万物之主。

chapters.en: Now if there is no resurrection, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?
chapters.zh: 不然那些为死人受洗的，将来怎样呢？若死人总不复活，因何为他们受洗呢？

chapters.en: And as for us, why do we endanger ourselves every hour?
chapters.zh: 我们又因何时刻冒险呢？

chapters.en: I face death every day—yes, just as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我在我主基督耶稣里，指着你们所夸的口，极力地说，我是天天冒死。

chapters.en: If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus with no more than human hopes, what have I gained? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
chapters.zh: 我若当日像寻常人，在以弗所同野兽战斗，那于我有什么益处呢？若死人不复活，我们就吃吃喝喝吧。因为明天要死了。

chapters.en: Do not be misled: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
chapters.zh: 你们不要自欺。滥交是败坏善行。

chapters.en: Come back to your senses as you ought, and stop sinning; for there are some who are ignorant of God—I say this to your shame.
chapters.zh: 你们要醒悟为善，不要犯罪。因为有人不认识神。我说这话，是要叫你们羞愧。

chapters.en: But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?”
chapters.zh: 或有人问，死人怎样复活。带着什么身体来呢？

chapters.en: How foolish! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
chapters.zh: 无知的人哪，你所种的，若不死就不能生。

chapters.en: When you sow, you do not plant the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or of something else.
chapters.zh: 并且你所种的，不是那将来的形体，不过是子粒，即如麦子，或是别样的谷。

chapters.en: But God gives it a body as he has determined, and to each kind of seed he gives its own body.
chapters.zh: 但神随自己的意思，给它一个形体，并叫各等子粒，各有自己的形体。

chapters.en: Not all flesh is the same: People have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another and fish another.
chapters.zh: 凡肉体各有不同。人是一样，兽又是一样，鸟又是一样，鱼又是一样。

chapters.en: There are also heavenly bodies and there are earthly bodies; but the splendor of the heavenly bodies is one kind, and the splendor of the earthly bodies is another.
chapters.zh: 有天上的形体，也有地上的形体。但天上形体的荣光是一样，地上形体的荣光又是一样。

chapters.en: The sun has one kind of splendor, the moon another and the stars another; and star differs from star in splendor.
chapters.zh: 日有日的荣光，月有月的荣光，星有星的荣光。这星和那星的荣光，也有分别。

chapters.en: So will it be with the resurrection of the dead. The body that is sown is perishable, it is raised imperishable;
chapters.zh: 死人复活也是这样。所种的是必朽坏的，复活的是不朽坏的。

chapters.en: it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power;
chapters.zh: 所种的是羞辱的，复活的是荣耀的。所种的是软弱的，复活的是强壮的。

chapters.en: it is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
chapters.zh: 所种的是血气的身体，复活的是灵性的身体。若有血气的身体，也必有灵性的身体。

chapters.en: So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living being” ; the last Adam, a life-giving spirit.
chapters.zh: 经上也是这样记着说，首先的人亚当，成了有灵的活人。（灵或作血气）末后的亚当，成了叫人活的灵。

chapters.en: The spiritual did not come first, but the natural, and after that the spiritual.
chapters.zh: 但属灵的不在先，属血气的在先。以后才有属灵的。

chapters.en: The first man was of the dust of the earth; the second man is of heaven.
chapters.zh: 头一个人是出于地，乃属土。第二个人是出于天。

chapters.en: As was the earthly man, so are those who are of the earth; and as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are of heaven.
chapters.zh: 那属土的怎样，凡属土的也就怎样。属天的怎样，凡属天的也就怎样。

chapters.en: And just as we have borne the image of the earthly man, so shall we bear the image of the heavenly man.
chapters.zh: 我们既有属土的形状，将来也必有属天的形状。

chapters.en: I declare to you, brothers and sisters, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我告诉你们说，血肉之体，不能承受神的国。必朽坏的，不能承受不朽坏的。

chapters.en: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed—
chapters.zh: 我如今把一件奥秘的事告诉你们。我们不是都要睡觉，乃是都要改变，

chapters.en: in a flash, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
chapters.zh: 就在一霎时，眨眼之间，号筒末次吹响的时候。因号筒要响，死人要复活成为不朽坏的，我们也要改变。

chapters.en: For the perishable must clothe itself with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.
chapters.zh: 这必朽坏的，总要变成不朽坏的。（变成原文作穿下同）这必死的，总要变成不死的。

chapters.en: When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come true: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
chapters.zh: 这必朽坏的既变成不朽坏的。这必死的既变成不死的。那时经上所记，死被得胜吞灭的话就应验了。

chapters.en: “Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?”
chapters.zh: 死啊，你得胜的权势在哪里？死啊，你的毒钩在哪里？

chapters.en: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
chapters.zh: 死的毒钩就是罪。罪的权势就是律法。

chapters.en: But thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 感谢神，使我们借着我们的主耶稣基督得胜。

chapters.en: Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
chapters.zh: 所以我亲爱的弟兄们，你们务要坚固不可摇动，常常竭力多作主工，因为知道你们的劳苦，在主里面不是徒然的。

chapters.en: Now about the collection for the Lord’s people: Do what I told the Galatian churches to do.
chapters.zh: 论到为圣徒捐钱，我从前怎样吩咐加拉太的众教会，你们也当怎样行。

chapters.en: On the first day of every week, each one of you should set aside a sum of money in keeping with your income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will have to be made.
chapters.zh: 每逢七日的第一日，各人要照自己的进项抽出来留着。免得我来的时候现凑。

chapters.en: Then, when I arrive, I will give letters of introduction to the men you approve and send them with your gift to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 及至我来到了，你们写信举荐谁，我就打发他们，把你们的捐资送到耶路撒冷去。

chapters.en: If it seems advisable for me to go also, they will accompany me.
chapters.zh: 若我也该去，他们可以和我同去。

chapters.en: After I go through Macedonia, I will come to you—for I will be going through Macedonia.
chapters.zh: 我要从马其顿经过。既经过了，就要到你们那里去。

chapters.en: Perhaps I will stay with you for a while, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.
chapters.zh: 或者和你们同住几时，或者也过冬。无论我往哪里去，你们就可以给我送行。

chapters.en: For I do not want to see you now and make only a passing visit; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
chapters.zh: 我如今不愿意路过见你们。主若许我，我就指望和你们同住几时。

chapters.en: But I will stay on at Ephesus until Pentecost,
chapters.zh: 但我要仍旧住在以弗所，直等到五旬节。

chapters.en: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, and there are many who oppose me.
chapters.zh: 因为有宽大又有功效的门，为我开了，并且反对的人也多。

chapters.en: When Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is carrying on the work of the Lord, just as I am.
chapters.zh: 若是提摩太来到，你们要留心，叫他在你们那里无所惧怕。因为他劳力作主的工，像我一样。

chapters.en: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he may return to me. I am expecting him along with the brothers.
chapters.zh: 所以无论谁，都不可藐视他。只要送他平安前行，叫他到我这里来。因我指望他和弟兄们同来。

chapters.en: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was quite unwilling to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.
chapters.zh: 至于兄弟亚波罗，我再三地劝他，同弟兄们到你们那里去。但这时他决不愿意去。几时有了机会他必去。

chapters.en: Be on your guard; stand firm in the faith; be courageous; be strong.
chapters.zh: 你们务要儆醒，在真道上站立得稳，要作大丈夫，要刚强。

chapters.en: Do everything in love.
chapters.zh: 凡你们所作的，都要凭爱心而作。

chapters.en: You know that the household of Stephanas were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the Lord’s people. I urge you, brothers and sisters,
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们晓得司提反一家，是亚该亚初结的果子。并且他们专以服事圣徒为念。

chapters.en: to submit to such people and to everyone who joins in the work and labors at it.
chapters.zh: 我劝你们顺服这样的人，并一切同工同劳的人。

chapters.en: I was glad when Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.
chapters.zh: 司提反，和福徒拿都，并亚该古，到这里来，我很喜欢。因为你们待我有不及之处，他们补上了。

chapters.en: For they refreshed my spirit and yours also. Such men deserve recognition.
chapters.zh: 他们叫我和你们心里都快活。这样的人，你们务要敬重。

chapters.en: The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.
chapters.zh: 亚西亚的众教会问你们安。亚居拉和百基拉，并在他们家里的教会，因主多多地问你们安。

chapters.en: All the brothers and sisters here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
chapters.zh: 众弟兄都问你们安。你们要亲嘴问安，彼此务要圣洁。

chapters.en: I, Paul, write this greeting in my own hand.
chapters.zh: 我保罗亲笔问安。

chapters.en: If anyone does not love the Lord, let that person be cursed! Come, Lord !
chapters.zh: 若有人不爱主，这人可诅可咒。主必要来。

chapters.en: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
chapters.zh: 愿主耶稣基督的恩，常与你们众人同在。

chapters.en: My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
chapters.zh: 我在基督耶稣里的爱与你们众人同在。阿们。

chapters.en: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, To the church of God in Corinth, together with all his holy people throughout Achaia:
chapters.zh: 奉神旨意，作基督耶稣使徒的保罗，和兄弟提摩太，写信给在哥林多神的教会，并亚该亚遍处的众圣徒。

chapters.en: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠平安，从神我们的父和主耶稣基督归与你们。

chapters.en: Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort,
chapters.zh: 愿颂赞归与我们的主耶稣基督的父神，就是发慈悲的父，赐各样安慰的神。

chapters.en: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves receive from God.
chapters.zh: 我们在一切患难中，他就安慰我们，叫我们能用神所赐的安慰，去安慰那遭各样患难的人。

chapters.en: For just as we share abundantly in the sufferings of Christ, so also our comfort abounds through Christ.
chapters.zh: 我们既多受基督的苦楚，就靠基督多得安慰。

chapters.en: If we are distressed, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which produces in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we suffer.
chapters.zh: 我们受患难呢，是为叫你们得安慰得拯救。我们得安慰呢，也是为叫你们得安慰。这安慰能叫你们忍受我们所受的那样苦楚。

chapters.en: And our hope for you is firm, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you share in our comfort.
chapters.zh: 我们为你们所存的盼望是确定的。因为知道你们既是同受苦楚，也必同得安慰。

chapters.en: We do not want you to be uninformed, brothers and sisters, about the troubles we experienced in the province of Asia. We were under great pressure, far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired of life itself.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我们不要你们不晓得，我们从前在亚西亚遭遇苦难，被压太重，力不能胜，甚至连活命的指望都绝了。

chapters.en: Indeed, we felt we had received the sentence of death. But this happened that we might not rely on ourselves but on God, who raises the dead.
chapters.zh: 自己心里也断定是必死的，叫我们不靠自己，只靠叫死人复活的神。

chapters.en: He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and he will deliver us again. On him we have set our hope that he will continue to deliver us,
chapters.zh: 他曾救我们脱离那极大的死亡，现在仍要救我们，并且我们指望他将来还要救我们。

chapters.en: as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the gracious favor granted us in answer to the prayers of many.
chapters.zh: 你们以祈祷帮助我们，好叫许多人为我们谢恩，就是为我们因许多人所得的恩。

chapters.en: Now this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially in our relations with you, with integrity and godly sincerity. We have done so, relying not on worldly wisdom but on God’s grace.
chapters.zh: 我们所夸的，是自己的良心，见证我们凭着神的圣洁和诚实，在世为人，不靠人的聪明，乃靠神的恩惠，向你们更是这样。

chapters.en: For we do not write you anything you cannot read or understand. And I hope that,
chapters.zh: 我们现在写给你们的话，并不外乎你们所念的，所认识的，我也盼望你们到底还是要认识。

chapters.en: as you have understood us in part, you will come to understand fully that you can boast of us just as we will boast of you in the day of the Lord Jesus.
chapters.zh: 正如你们已经有几分认识我们。以我们夸口，好像我们在我们主耶稣的日子，以你们夸口一样。

chapters.en: Because I was confident of this, I wanted to visit you first so that you might benefit twice.
chapters.zh: 我既然这样深信，就早有意到你们那里去，叫你们再得益处。

chapters.en: I wanted to visit you on my way to Macedonia and to come back to you from Macedonia, and then to have you send me on my way to Judea.
chapters.zh: 也要从你们那里经过，往马其顿去，再从马其顿回到你们那里，叫你们给我送行往犹太去。

chapters.en: Was I fickle when I intended to do this? Or do I make my plans in a worldly manner so that in the same breath I say both “Yes, yes” and “No, no”?
chapters.zh: 我有此意，岂是反复不定吗？我所起的意，岂是从情欲起的，叫我忽是忽非吗？

chapters.en: But as surely as God is faithful, our message to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
chapters.zh: 我指着信实的神说，我们向你们所传的道，并没有是而又非的。

chapters.en: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us—by me and Silas and Timothy—was not “Yes” and “No,” but in him it has always been “Yes.”
chapters.zh: 因为我和西拉，并提摩太，在你们中间所传神的儿子耶稣基督，总没有是而又非的，在他只有一是。

chapters.en: For no matter how many promises God has made, they are “Yes” in Christ. And so through him the “Amen” is spoken by us to the glory of God.
chapters.zh: 神的应许，不论有多少，在基督都是是的，所以借着他也都是实在的，（实在原文作阿们）叫神因我们得荣耀。

chapters.en: Now it is God who makes both us and you stand firm in Christ. He anointed us,
chapters.zh: 那在基督里坚固我们和你们，并且膏我们的，就是神。

chapters.en: set his seal of ownership on us, and put his Spirit in our hearts as a deposit, guaranteeing what is to come.
chapters.zh: 他又用印印了我们，并赐圣灵在我们心里作凭据。（原文作质）。

chapters.en: I call God as my witness—and I stake my life on it—that it was in order to spare you that I did not return to Corinth.
chapters.zh: 我呼吁神给我的心作见证，我没有往哥林多去，是为要宽容你们。

chapters.en: Not that we lord it over your faith, but we work with you for your joy, because it is by faith you stand firm.
chapters.zh: 我们并不是辖管你们的信心，乃是帮助你们的快乐。因为你们凭信才站立得住。

chapters.en: So I made up my mind that I would not make another painful visit to you.
chapters.zh: 我自己定了主意，再到你们那里去，必须大家没有忧愁。

chapters.en: For if I grieve you, who is left to make me glad but you whom I have grieved?
chapters.zh: 倘若我叫你们忧愁，除了我叫那忧愁的人以外，谁能叫我快乐呢？

chapters.en: I wrote as I did, so that when I came I would not be distressed by those who should have made me rejoice. I had confidence in all of you, that you would all share my joy.
chapters.zh: 我曾把这事写给你们，恐怕我到的时候，应该叫我快乐的那些人，反倒叫我忧愁。我也深信，你们众人都以我的快乐为自己的快乐。

chapters.en: For I wrote you out of great distress and anguish of heart and with many tears, not to grieve you but to let you know the depth of my love for you.
chapters.zh: 我先前心里难过痛苦，多多地流泪，写信给你们。不是叫你们忧愁，乃是叫你们知道我格外的疼爱你们。

chapters.en: If anyone has caused grief, he has not so much grieved me as he has grieved all of you to some extent—not to put it too severely.
chapters.zh: 若有叫人忧愁的，他不但叫我忧愁，也是叫你们众人有几分忧愁，我说几分，恐怕说得太重。

chapters.en: The punishment inflicted on him by the majority is sufficient.
chapters.zh: 这样的人，受了众人的责罚，也就够了。

chapters.en: Now instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
chapters.zh: 倒不如赦免他，安慰他，免得他忧愁太过，甚至沉沦了。

chapters.en: I urge you, therefore, to reaffirm your love for him.
chapters.zh: 所以我劝你们，要向他显出坚定不移的爱心来。

chapters.en: Another reason I wrote you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.
chapters.zh: 为此我先前也写信给你们，要试验你们，看你们凡事顺从不顺从。

chapters.en: Anyone you forgive, I also forgive. And what I have forgiven—if there was anything to forgive—I have forgiven in the sight of Christ for your sake,
chapters.zh: 你们赦免谁，我也赦免谁，我若有所赦免的，是在基督面前为你们赦免的。

chapters.en: in order that Satan might not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.
chapters.zh: 免得撒但趁着机会胜过我们。因我们并非不晓得他的诡计。

chapters.en: Now when I went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ and found that the Lord had opened a door for me,
chapters.zh: 我从前为基督的福音到了特罗亚，主也给我开了门。

chapters.en: I still had no peace of mind, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
chapters.zh: 那时因为没有遇见兄弟提多，我心里不安，便辞别那里的人往马其顿去了。

chapters.en: But thanks be to God, who always leads us as captives in Christ’s triumphal procession and uses us to spread the aroma of the knowledge of him everywhere.
chapters.zh: 感谢神，常帅领我们在基督里夸胜，并借着我们在各处显扬那因认识基督而有的香气。

chapters.en: For we are to God the pleasing aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are perishing.
chapters.zh: 因为我们在神面前，无论在得救的人身上，或灭亡的人身上，都有基督馨香之气。

chapters.en: To the one we are an aroma that brings death; to the other, an aroma that brings life. And who is equal to such a task?
chapters.zh: 在这等人，就作了死的香气叫他死。在那等人，就作了活的香气叫他活。这事谁能当得起呢？

chapters.en: Unlike so many, we do not peddle the word of God for profit. On the contrary, in Christ we speak before God with sincerity, as those sent from God.
chapters.zh: 我们不像那许多人，为利混乱神的道。乃是由于诚实，由于神，在神面前凭着基督讲道。

chapters.en: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
chapters.zh: 我们岂是又举荐自己吗？岂像别人，用人的荐信给你们，或用你们的荐信给人吗？

chapters.en: You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
chapters.zh: 你们就是我们的荐信，写在我们的心里，被众人所知道所念诵的。

chapters.en: You show that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
chapters.zh: 你们明显是基督的信，借着我们修成的。不是用墨写的，乃是用永生神的灵写的。不是写在石版上，乃是写在心版上。

chapters.en: Such confidence we have through Christ before God.
chapters.zh: 我们因基督所以在神面前才有这样的信心，

chapters.en: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim anything for ourselves, but our competence comes from God.
chapters.zh: 并不是我们凭自己能承担什么事，我们所能承担的，乃是出于神。

chapters.en: He has made us competent as ministers of a new covenant—not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
chapters.zh: 他叫我们能承当这新约的执事。不是凭着字句，乃是凭着精意。因为那字句是叫人死，精意是叫人活。（精意或作圣灵）。

chapters.en: Now if the ministry that brought death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with glory, so that the Israelites could not look steadily at the face of Moses because of its glory, transitory though it was,
chapters.zh: 那用字刻在石头上属死的职事，尚且有荣光，甚至以色列人因摩西面上的荣光，不能定睛看他的脸。这荣光原是渐渐退去的。

chapters.en: will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?
chapters.zh: 何况那属灵的职事，岂不更有荣光吗？

chapters.en: If the ministry that brought condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry that brings righteousness!
chapters.zh: 若是定罪的职事有荣光，那称义的职事，荣光就越发大了。

chapters.en: For what was glorious has no glory now in comparison with the surpassing glory.
chapters.zh: 那从前有荣光的，因这极大的荣光，就算不得有荣光了。

chapters.en: And if what was transitory came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which lasts!
chapters.zh: 若那废掉的有荣光，这长存的就更有荣光了。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.
chapters.zh: 我们既有这样的盼望，就大胆讲说，

chapters.en: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to prevent the Israelites from seeing the end of what was passing away.
chapters.zh: 不像摩西将帕子蒙在脸上，叫以色列人不能定睛看到那将废者的结局。

chapters.en: But their minds were made dull, for to this day the same veil remains when the old covenant is read. It has not been removed, because only in Christ is it taken away.
chapters.zh: 但他们的心地刚硬。直到今日诵读旧约的时候，这帕子还没有揭去。这帕子在基督里已经废去了。

chapters.en: Even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
chapters.zh: 然而直到今日，每逢诵读摩西书的时候，帕子还在他们心上。

chapters.en: But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
chapters.zh: 但他们的心几时归向主，帕子就几时除去了。

chapters.en: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
chapters.zh: 主就是那灵。主的灵在哪里，哪里就得以自由。

chapters.en: And we all, who with unveiled faces contemplate the Lord’s glory, are being transformed into his image with ever-increasing glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 我们众人既然敞着脸，得以看见主的荣光，好像从镜子里返照，就变成主的形状，荣上加荣，如同从主的灵变成的。

chapters.en: Therefore, since through God’s mercy we have this ministry, we do not lose heart.
chapters.zh: 我们既然蒙怜悯，受了这职分，就不丧胆。

chapters.en: Rather, we have renounced secret and shameful ways; we do not use deception, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by setting forth the truth plainly we commend ourselves to everyone’s conscience in the sight of God.
chapters.zh: 乃将那些暗昧可耻的事弃绝了，不行诡诈，不谬讲神的道理。只将真理表明出来，好在神面前把自己荐与各人的良心。

chapters.en: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.
chapters.zh: 如果我们的福音蒙蔽，就是蒙蔽在灭亡的人身上。

chapters.en: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so that they cannot see the light of the gospel that displays the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
chapters.zh: 此等不信之人，被这世界的神弄瞎了心眼，不叫基督荣耀福音的光照着他们。基督本是神的像。

chapters.en: For what we preach is not ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.
chapters.zh: 我们原不是传自己，乃是传基督耶稣为主，并且自己因耶稣作你们的仆人。

chapters.en: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made his light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of God’s glory displayed in the face of Christ.
chapters.zh: 那吩咐光从黑暗里照出来的神，已经照在我们心里，叫我们得知神荣耀的光，显在耶稣基督的面上。

chapters.en: But we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us.
chapters.zh: 我们有这宝贝放在瓦器里，要显明这莫大的能力，是出于神，不是出于我们。

chapters.en: We are hard pressed on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;
chapters.zh: 我们四面受敌，却不被困住。心里作难，却不至失望。

chapters.en: persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed.
chapters.zh: 遭逼迫，却不被丢弃。打倒了，却不至死亡。

chapters.en: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
chapters.zh: 身上常带着耶稣的死，使耶稣的生，也显明在我们身上。

chapters.en: For we who are alive are always being given over to death for Jesus’ sake, so that his life may also be revealed in our mortal body.
chapters.zh: 因为我们这活着的人，是常为耶稣被交于死地，使耶稣的生，在我们这必死的身上显明出来，

chapters.en: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，死是在我们身上发动，生却在你们身上发动。

chapters.en: It is written: “I believed; therefore I have spoken.” Since we have that same spirit of faith, we also believe and therefore speak,
chapters.zh: 但我们既有信心，正如经上记着说，我因信，所以如此说话。我们也信，所以也说话。

chapters.en: because we know that the one who raised the Lord Jesus from the dead will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you to himself.
chapters.zh: 自己知道，那叫主耶稣复活的，也必叫我们与耶稣一同复活，并且叫我们与你们一同站在他面前。

chapters.en: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is reaching more and more people may cause thanksgiving to overflow to the glory of God.
chapters.zh: 凡事都是为你们，好叫恩惠因人多越发加增，感谢格外显多，以致荣耀归与神。

chapters.en: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though outwardly we are wasting away, yet inwardly we are being renewed day by day.
chapters.zh: 所以我们不丧胆。外体虽然毁坏，内心却一天新似一天。

chapters.en: For our light and momentary troubles are achieving for us an eternal glory that far outweighs them all.
chapters.zh: 我们这至暂至轻的苦楚，要为我们成就极重无比永远的荣耀。

chapters.en: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen, since what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
chapters.zh: 原来我们不是顾念所见的，乃是顾念所不见的。因为所见的是暂时的，所不见的是永远的。

chapters.en: For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is destroyed, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.
chapters.zh: 我们原知道，我们这地上的帐棚若拆毁了，必得神所造，不是人手所造，在天上永存的房屋。

chapters.en: Meanwhile we groan, longing to be clothed instead with our heavenly dwelling,
chapters.zh: 我们在这帐棚里叹息，深想得那从天上来的房屋，好像穿上衣服。

chapters.en: because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.
chapters.zh: 倘若穿上，被遇见的时候就不至于赤身了。

chapters.en: For while we are in this tent, we groan and are burdened, because we do not wish to be unclothed but to be clothed instead with our heavenly dwelling, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
chapters.zh: 我们在这帐棚里，叹息劳苦，并非愿意脱下这个，乃是愿意穿上那个，好叫这必死的被生命吞灭了。

chapters.en: Now the one who has fashioned us for this very purpose is God, who has given us the Spirit as a deposit, guaranteeing what is to come.
chapters.zh: 为此培植我们的就是神，他又赐给我们圣灵作凭据。（原文作质）。

chapters.en: Therefore we are always confident and know that as long as we are at home in the body we are away from the Lord.
chapters.zh: 所以我们时常坦然无惧，并且晓得我们住在身内，便与主相离。

chapters.en: For we live by faith, not by sight.
chapters.zh: 因我们行事为人，是凭着信心，不是凭着眼见。

chapters.en: We are confident, I say, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我们坦然无惧，是更愿意离开身体与主同住。

chapters.en: So we make it our goal to please him, whether we are at home in the body or away from it.
chapters.zh: 所以无论是住在身内，离开身外，我们立了志向，要得主的喜悦。

chapters.en: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each of us may receive what is due us for the things done while in the body, whether good or bad.
chapters.zh: 因为我们众人，必要在基督台前显露出来，叫各人按着本身所行的，或善或恶受报。

chapters.en: Since, then, we know what it is to fear the Lord, we try to persuade others. What we are is plain to God, and I hope it is also plain to your conscience.
chapters.zh: 我们既知道主是可畏的，所以劝人，但我们在神面前是显明的，盼望在你们的良心里，也是显明的。

chapters.en: We are not trying to commend ourselves to you again, but are giving you an opportunity to take pride in us, so that you can answer those who take pride in what is seen rather than in what is in the heart.
chapters.zh: 我们不是向你们再举荐自己，乃是叫你们因我们有可夸之处，好对那凭外貌不凭内心夸口的人，有言可答。

chapters.en: If we are “out of our mind,” as some say, it is for God; if we are in our right mind, it is for you.
chapters.zh: 我们若果颠狂，是为神。若果谨守，是为你们。

chapters.en: For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that one died for all, and therefore all died.
chapters.zh: 原来基督的爱激励我们。因我们想一人既替众人死，众人就都死了。

chapters.en: And he died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves but for him who died for them and was raised again.
chapters.zh: 并且他替众人死，是叫那些活着的人，不再为自己活，乃为替他们死而复活的主活。

chapters.en: So from now on we regard no one from a worldly point of view. Though we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.
chapters.zh: 所以我们从今以后，不凭着外貌（原文作肉体本节同）认人了。虽然凭着外貌认过基督，如今却不再这样认他了。

chapters.en: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
chapters.zh: 若有人在基督里，他就是新造的人。旧事已过，都变成新的了。

chapters.en: All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
chapters.zh: 一切都是出于神，他借着基督使我们与他和好，又将劝人与他和好的职分赐给我们。

chapters.en: that God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ, not counting people’s sins against them. And he has committed to us the message of reconciliation.
chapters.zh: 这就是神在基督里叫世人与自己和好，不将他们的过犯归到他们身上。并且将这和好的道理托付了我们。

chapters.en: We are therefore Christ’s ambassadors, as though God were making his appeal through us. We implore you on Christ’s behalf: Be reconciled to God.
chapters.zh: 所以我们作基督的使者，就好像神借我们劝你们一般。我们替基督求你们与神和好。

chapters.en: God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
chapters.zh: 神使那无罪的（无罪原文作不知罪），替我们成为罪。好叫我们在他里面成为神的义。

chapters.en: As God’s co-workers we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.
chapters.zh: 我们与神同工的，也劝你们，不可徒受他的恩典。

chapters.en: For he says, “In the time of my favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.”I tell you, now is the time of God’s favor, now is the day of salvation.
chapters.zh: 因为他说，在悦纳的时候，我应允了你。在拯救的日子，我搭救了你。看哪，现在正是悦纳的时候，现在正是拯救的日子。

chapters.en: We put no stumbling block in anyone’s path, so that our ministry will not be discredited.
chapters.zh: 我们凡事都不叫人有妨碍，免得这职分被人毁谤。

chapters.en: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships and distresses;
chapters.zh: 反倒在各样的事上，表明自己是神的用人，就如在许多的忍耐，患难，穷乏，困苦，

chapters.en: in beatings, imprisonments and riots; in hard work, sleepless nights and hunger;
chapters.zh: 鞭打，监禁，扰乱，勤劳，儆醒，不食，

chapters.en: in purity, understanding, patience and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;
chapters.zh: 廉洁，知识，恒忍，恩慈，圣灵的感化，无伪的爱心，

chapters.en: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;
chapters.zh: 真实的道理，神的大能。仁义的兵器在左在右。

chapters.en: through glory and dishonor, bad report and good report; genuine, yet regarded as impostors;
chapters.zh: 荣耀羞辱，恶名美名。似乎是诱惑人的，却是诚实的。

chapters.en: known, yet regarded as unknown; dying, and yet we live on; beaten, and yet not killed;
chapters.zh: 似乎不为人所知，却是人所共知的。似乎要死却是活着的。似乎受责罚，却是不至丧命的。

chapters.en: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
chapters.zh: 似乎忧愁，却是常常快乐的。似乎贫穷，却是叫许多人富足的。似乎一无所有，却是样样都有的。

chapters.en: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians, and opened wide our hearts to you.
chapters.zh: 哥林多人哪，我们向你们，口是张开的，心是宽宏的。

chapters.en: We are not withholding our affection from you, but you are withholding yours from us.
chapters.zh: 你们狭窄，原不在乎我们，是在乎自己的心肠狭窄。

chapters.en: As a fair exchange—I speak as to my children—open wide your hearts also.
chapters.zh: 你们也要照样用宽宏的心报答我。我这话正像对自己的孩子说的。

chapters.en: Do not be yoked together with unbelievers. For what do righteousness and wickedness have in common? Or what fellowship can light have with darkness?
chapters.zh: 你们和不信的原不相配，不要同负一轭。义和不义有什么相交呢？光明和黑暗有什么相通呢？

chapters.en: What harmony is there between Christ and Belial ? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?
chapters.zh: 基督和彼列（彼列就是撒但的别名）有什么相和呢？信主的和不信主的有什么相干呢？

chapters.en: What agreement is there between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will live with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people.”
chapters.zh: 神的殿和偶像有什么相同呢？因为我们是永生神的殿。就如神曾说，我要在他们中间居住，在他们中间来往。我要作他们的神，他们要作我的子民。

chapters.en: Therefore, “Come out from them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
chapters.zh: 又说，你们务要从他们中间出来，与他们分别，不要沾不洁净的物，我就收纳你们。

chapters.en: And, “I will be a Father to you, and you will be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”
chapters.zh: 我要作你们的父，你们要作我的儿女。这是全能的主说的。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we have these promises, dear friends, let us purify ourselves from everything that contaminates body and spirit, perfecting holiness out of reverence for God.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的弟兄阿，我们既有这等应许，就当洁净自己，除去身体灵魂一切的污秽，敬畏神，得以成圣。

chapters.en: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.
chapters.zh: 你们要心地宽大收纳我们。我们未曾亏负谁，未曾败坏谁，未曾占谁的便宜。

chapters.en: I do not say this to condemn you; I have said before that you have such a place in our hearts that we would live or die with you.
chapters.zh: 我说这话，不是要定你们的罪。我已经说过，你们常在我们心里，情愿与你们同生同死。

chapters.en: I have spoken to you with great frankness; I take great pride in you. I am greatly encouraged; in all our troubles my joy knows no bounds.
chapters.zh: 我大大地放胆向你们说话。我因你们多多夸口，满得安慰。我们在一切患难中分外的快乐。

chapters.en: For when we came into Macedonia, we had no rest, but we were harassed at every turn—conflicts on the outside, fears within.
chapters.zh: 我们从前就是到了马其顿的时候，身体也不得安宁，周围遭患难，外有争战，内有惧怕。

chapters.en: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the coming of Titus,
chapters.zh: 但那安慰丧气之人的神，借着提多来安慰了我们。

chapters.en: and not only by his coming but also by the comfort you had given him. He told us about your longing for me, your deep sorrow, your ardent concern for me, so that my joy was greater than ever.
chapters.zh: 不但借着他来，也借着他从你们所得的安慰，安慰了我们。因他把你们的想念，哀恸，和向我的热心，都告诉了我，叫我更加欢喜。

chapters.en: Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Though I did regret it—I see that my letter hurt you, but only for a little while—
chapters.zh: 我先前写信叫你们忧愁。我后来虽然懊悔，如今却不懊悔。因我知道那信叫你们忧愁，不过是暂时的。

chapters.en: yet now I am happy, not because you were made sorry, but because your sorrow led you to repentance. For you became sorrowful as God intended and so were not harmed in any way by us.
chapters.zh: 如今我欢喜，不是因你们忧愁，是因你们从忧愁中生出懊悔来。你们依着神的意思忧愁，凡事就不至于因我们受亏损了。

chapters.en: Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation and leaves no regret, but worldly sorrow brings death.
chapters.zh: 因为依着神的意思忧愁，就生出没有后悔的懊悔来，以致得救。但世俗的忧愁，是叫人死。

chapters.en: See what this godly sorrow has produced in you: what earnestness, what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what concern, what readiness to see justice done. At every point you have proved yourselves to be innocent in this matter.
chapters.zh: 你看，你们依着神的意思忧愁，从此就生出何等的殷勤，自诉，自恨，恐惧，想念，热心，责罚（或作自责），在这一切事上你们都表明自己是洁净的。

chapters.en: So even though I wrote to you, it was neither on account of the one who did the wrong nor on account of the injured party, but rather that before God you could see for yourselves how devoted to us you are.
chapters.zh: 我虽然从前写信给你们却不是为那亏负人的，也不是为那受人亏负的，乃要在神面前，把你们顾念我们的热心，表明出来。

chapters.en: By all this we are encouraged. In addition to our own encouragement, we were especially delighted to see how happy Titus was, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
chapters.zh: 故此我们得了安慰，并且在安慰之中，因你们众人使提多心里畅快欢喜，我们就更加欢喜了。

chapters.en: I had boasted to him about you, and you have not embarrassed me. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting about you to Titus has proved to be true as well.
chapters.zh: 我若对提多夸奖了你们什么，也觉得没有惭愧。因我对提多夸奖你们的话，成了真的。正如我对你们所说的话，也都是真的。

chapters.en: And his affection for you is all the greater when he remembers that you were all obedient, receiving him with fear and trembling.
chapters.zh: 并且提多想起你们众人的顺服，是怎样恐惧战兢地接待他，他爱你们的心肠就越发热了。

chapters.en: I am glad I can have complete confidence in you.
chapters.zh: 我如今欢喜，能在凡事上为你们放心。

chapters.en: And now, brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the Macedonian churches.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我把神赐给马其顿众教会的恩告诉你们。

chapters.en: In the midst of a very severe trial, their overflowing joy and their extreme poverty welled up in rich generosity.
chapters.zh: 就是他们在患难中受大试炼的时候，仍有满足的快乐，在极穷之间，还格外显出他们乐捐的厚恩。

chapters.en: For I testify that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond their ability. Entirely on their own,
chapters.zh: 我可以证明他们是按着力量，而且也过了力量，自己甘心乐意的捐助。

chapters.en: they urgently pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the Lord’s people.
chapters.zh: 再三地求我们，准他们在这供给圣徒的恩情上有分。

chapters.en: And they exceeded our expectations: They gave themselves first of all to the Lord, and then by the will of God also to us.
chapters.zh: 并且他们所作的，不但照我们所想望的，更照神的旨意，先把自己献给主，又归附了我们。

chapters.en: So we urged Titus, just as he had earlier made a beginning, to bring also to completion this act of grace on your part.
chapters.zh: 因此我劝提多，既然在你们中间开办这慈惠的事，就当办成了。

chapters.en: But since you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness and in the love we have kindled in you —see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
chapters.zh: 你们既然在信心，口才，知识，热心，和待我们的爱心上，都格外显出满足来，就当在这慈惠的事上，也格外显出满足来。

chapters.en: I am not commanding you, but I want to test the sincerity of your love by comparing it with the earnestness of others.
chapters.zh: 我说这话，不是吩咐你们，乃是借着别人的热心，试验你们爱心的实在。

chapters.en: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich.
chapters.zh: 你们知道我们主耶稣基督的恩典。他本来富足，却为你们成了贫穷，叫你们因他的贫穷，可以成为富足。

chapters.en: And here is my judgment about what is best for you in this matter. Last year you were the first not only to give but also to have the desire to do so.
chapters.zh: 我在这事上把我的意见告诉你们，是与你们有益。因为你们下手办这事，而且起此心意，已经有一年了。

chapters.en: Now finish the work, so that your eager willingness to do it may be matched by your completion of it, according to your means.
chapters.zh: 如今就当办成这事。既有愿作的心，也当照你们所有的去办成。

chapters.en: For if the willingness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
chapters.zh: 因为人若有愿作的心，必蒙悦纳，乃是照他所有的，并不是照他所无的。

chapters.en: Our desire is not that others might be relieved while you are hard pressed, but that there might be equality.
chapters.zh: 我原不是要别人轻省，你们受累，

chapters.en: At the present time your plenty will supply what they need, so that in turn their plenty will supply what you need. The goal is equality,
chapters.zh: 乃要均平。就是要你们的富余，现在可以补他们的不足，使他们的富余，将来也可以补你们的不足，这就均平了。

chapters.en: as it is written: “The one who gathered much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too little.”
chapters.zh: 如经上所记，多收的也没有余，少收的也没有缺。

chapters.en: Thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same concern I have for you.
chapters.zh: 多谢神，感动提多的心，叫他待你们殷勤，像我一样。

chapters.en: For Titus not only welcomed our appeal, but he is coming to you with much enthusiasm and on his own initiative.
chapters.zh: 他固然是听了我的劝。但自己更是热心，情愿往你们那里去。

chapters.en: And we are sending along with him the brother who is praised by all the churches for his service to the gospel.
chapters.zh: 我们还打发一位兄弟和他同去。这人在福音上得了众教会的称赞。

chapters.en: What is more, he was chosen by the churches to accompany us as we carry the offering, which we administer in order to honor the Lord himself and to show our eagerness to help.
chapters.zh: 不但这样，他也被众教会挑选，和我们同行，把所托与我们的这捐赀送到了，可以荣耀主，又表明我们乐意的心。

chapters.en: We want to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this liberal gift.
chapters.zh: 这就免得有人因我们收的捐银很多，就挑我们的不是。

chapters.en: For we are taking pains to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord but also in the eyes of man.
chapters.zh: 我们留心行光明的事，不但在主面前，就在人面前，也是这样。

chapters.en: In addition, we are sending with them our brother who has often proved to us in many ways that he is zealous, and now even more so because of his great confidence in you.
chapters.zh: 我们又打发一位兄弟同去。这人的热心，我们在许多事上，屡次试验过，现在他因为深信你们，就更加热心了。

chapters.en: As for Titus, he is my partner and co-worker among you; as for our brothers, they are representatives of the churches and an honor to Christ.
chapters.zh: 论到提多，他是我的同伴，一同为你们劳碌的。论到那两位兄弟，他们是众教会的使者，是基督的荣耀。

chapters.en: Therefore show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our pride in you, so that the churches can see it.
chapters.zh: 所以你们务要在众教会面前，显明你们爱心的凭据，并我所夸奖你们的凭据。

chapters.en: There is no need for me to write to you about this service to the Lord’s people.
chapters.zh: 论到供给圣徒的事，我不必写信给你们。

chapters.en: For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting about it to the Macedonians, telling them that since last year you in Achaia were ready to give; and your enthusiasm has stirred most of them to action.
chapters.zh: 因为我知道你们乐意的心，常对马其顿人夸奖你们，说亚该亚人预备好了，已经有一年了。并且你们的热心激动了许多人。

chapters.en: But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove hollow, but that you may be ready, as I said you would be.
chapters.zh: 但我打发那几位弟兄去，要叫你们照我的话预备妥当。免得我们在这事上夸奖你们的话落了空。

chapters.en: For if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—not to say anything about you—would be ashamed of having been so confident.
chapters.zh: 万一有马其顿人与我同去，见你们没有预备，就叫我们所确信的，反成了羞愧。你们羞愧，更不用说了。

chapters.en: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you in advance and finish the arrangements for the generous gift you had promised. Then it will be ready as a generous gift, not as one grudgingly given.
chapters.zh: 因此我想不得不求那几位弟兄，先到你们那里去，把从前所应许的捐赀，预备妥当，就显出你们所捐的，是出于乐意，不是出于勉强。

chapters.en: Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
chapters.zh: 少种的少收，多种的多收。这话是真的。

chapters.en: Each of you should give what you have decided in your heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
chapters.zh: 各人要随本心所酌定的。不要作难，不要勉强，因为捐得乐意的人，是神所喜爱的。

chapters.en: And God is able to bless you abundantly, so that in all things at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.
chapters.zh: 神能将各样的恩惠，多多地加给你们。使你们凡事常常充足，能多行各样善事。

chapters.en: As it is written: “They have freely scattered their gifts to the poor; their righteousness endures forever.”
chapters.zh: 如经上所记，他施舍钱财，周济贫穷。他的仁义存到永远。

chapters.en: Now he who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will also supply and increase your store of seed and will enlarge the harvest of your righteousness.
chapters.zh: 那赐种给撒种的，赐粮给人吃的，必多多加给你们种地的种子，又增添你们仁义的果子。

chapters.en: You will be enriched in every way so that you can be generous on every occasion, and through us your generosity will result in thanksgiving to God.
chapters.zh: 叫你们凡事富足，可以多多施舍，就借着我们使感谢归于神。

chapters.en: This service that you perform is not only supplying the needs of the Lord’s people but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanks to God.
chapters.zh: 因为办这供给的事，不但补圣徒的缺乏，而且叫许多人越发感谢神。

chapters.en: Because of the service by which you have proved yourselves, others will praise God for the obedience that accompanies your confession of the gospel of Christ, and for your generosity in sharing with them and with everyone else.
chapters.zh: 他们从这供给的事上得了凭据，知道你们承认基督顺服他的福音，多多地捐钱给他们和众人，便将荣耀归与神。

chapters.en: And in their prayers for you their hearts will go out to you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.
chapters.zh: 他们也因神极大的恩赐，显在你们心里，就切切地想念你们，为你们祈祷。

chapters.en: Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!
chapters.zh: 感谢神，因他有说不尽的恩赐。

chapters.en: By the humility and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you—I, Paul, who am “timid” when face to face with you, but “bold” toward you when away!
chapters.zh: 我保罗就是与你们见面的时候是谦卑的，不在你们那里的时候向你们是勇敢的，如今亲自借着基督的温柔和平，劝你们。

chapters.en: I beg you that when I come I may not have to be as bold as I expect to be toward some people who think that we live by the standards of this world.
chapters.zh: 有人以为我是凭着血气行事，我也以为必须用勇敢待这等人，求你们不要叫我在你们那里的时候，有这样的勇敢。

chapters.en: For though we live in the world, we do not wage war as the world does.
chapters.zh: 因为我们虽然在血气中行事，却不凭着血气争战。

chapters.en: The weapons we fight with are not the weapons of the world. On the contrary, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.
chapters.zh: 我们争战的兵器，本不是属血气的，乃是在神面前有能力可以攻破坚固的营垒，

chapters.en: We demolish arguments and every pretension that sets itself up against the knowledge of God, and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
chapters.zh: 将各样的计谋，各样拦阻人认识神的那些自高之事，一概攻破了，又将人所有的心意夺回，使他都顺服基督。

chapters.en: And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, once your obedience is complete.
chapters.zh: 并且我已经预备好了，等你们十分顺服的时候，要责罚那一切不顺服的人。

chapters.en: You are judging by appearances. If anyone is confident that they belong to Christ, they should consider again that we belong to Christ just as much as they do.
chapters.zh: 你们是看眼前的吗？倘若有人自信是属基督的，他要再想想，他如何属基督，我们也是如何属基督的。

chapters.en: So even if I boast somewhat freely about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed of it.
chapters.zh: 主赐给我们权柄是要造就你们，并不是要败坏你们。我就是为这权柄稍微夸口，也不至于惭愧。

chapters.en: I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you with my letters.
chapters.zh: 我说这话免得你们以为我写信是要威吓你们。

chapters.en: For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but in person he is unimpressive and his speaking amounts to nothing.”
chapters.zh: 因为有人说，他的信，又沉重，又利害。及至见面，却是气貌不扬，言语粗俗的。

chapters.en: Such people should realize that what we are in our letters when we are absent, we will be in our actions when we are present.
chapters.zh: 这等人当想，我们不在那里的时候，信上的言语如何，见面的时候，行事也必如何。

chapters.en: We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they are not wise.
chapters.zh: 因为我们不敢将自己和那自荐的人同列相比。他们用自己度量自己，用自己比较自己，乃是不通达的。

chapters.en: We, however, will not boast beyond proper limits, but will confine our boasting to the sphere of service God himself has assigned to us, a sphere that also includes you.
chapters.zh: 我们不愿意分外夸口，只要照神所量给我们的界限，构到你们那里。

chapters.en: We are not going too far in our boasting, as would be the case if we had not come to you, for we did get as far as you with the gospel of Christ.
chapters.zh: 我们并非过了自己的界限，好像构不到你们那里。因为我们早到你们那里，传了基督的福音。

chapters.en: Neither do we go beyond our limits by boasting of work done by others. Our hope is that, as your faith continues to grow, our sphere of activity among you will greatly expand,
chapters.zh: 我们不仗着别人所劳碌的，分外夸口。但指望你们信心增长的时候，所量给我们的界限，就可以因着你们更加开展，

chapters.en: so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. For we do not want to boast about work already done in someone else’s territory.
chapters.zh: 得以将福音传到你们以外的地方，并不是在别人界限之内，借着他现成的事夸口。

chapters.en: But, “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”
chapters.zh: 但夸口的当指着主夸口。

chapters.en: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
chapters.zh: 因为蒙悦纳的，不是自己称许的，乃是主所称许的。

chapters.en: I hope you will put up with me in a little foolishness. Yes, please put up with me!
chapters.zh: 但愿你们宽容我这一点愚妄。其实你们原是宽容我的。

chapters.en: I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. I promised you to one husband, to Christ, so that I might present you as a pure virgin to him.
chapters.zh: 我为你们起的愤恨，原是神那样的愤恨。因为我曾把你们许配一个丈夫，要把你们如同贞洁的童女，献给基督。

chapters.en: But I am afraid that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may somehow be led astray from your sincere and pure devotion to Christ.
chapters.zh: 我只怕你们的心或偏于邪，失去那向基督所存纯一清洁的心，就像蛇用诡诈诱惑了夏娃一样。

chapters.en: For if someone comes to you and preaches a Jesus other than the Jesus we preached, or if you receive a different spirit from the Spirit you received, or a different gospel from the one you accepted, you put up with it easily enough.
chapters.zh: 假如有人来，另传一个耶稣，不是我们所传过的。或者你们另受一个灵，不是你们所受过的。或者另得一个福音，不是你们所得过的。你们容让他也就罢了。

chapters.en: I do not think I am in the least inferior to those “super-apostles.”
chapters.zh: 但我想，我一点不在那些最大的使徒以下。

chapters.en: I may indeed be untrained as a speaker, but I do have knowledge. We have made this perfectly clear to you in every way.
chapters.zh: 我的言语虽然粗俗，我的知识却不粗俗。这是我们在凡事上，向你们众人显明出来的。

chapters.en: Was it a sin for me to lower myself in order to elevate you by preaching the gospel of God to you free of charge?
chapters.zh: 我因为白白传神的福音给你们，就自居卑微，叫你们高升，这算是我犯罪吗？

chapters.en: I robbed other churches by receiving support from them so as to serve you.
chapters.zh: 我亏负了别的教会，向他们取了工价来，给你们效力。

chapters.en: And when I was with you and needed something, I was not a burden to anyone, for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied what I needed. I have kept myself from being a burden to you in any way, and will continue to do so.
chapters.zh: 我在你们那里缺乏的时候，并没有累着你们一个人。因我所缺乏的，那从马其顿来的弟兄们都补足了。我向来凡事谨守，后来也必谨守，总不至于累着你们。

chapters.en: As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, nobody in the regions of Achaia will stop this boasting of mine.
chapters.zh: 既有基督的诚实在我里面，就无人能在亚该亚一带地方阻挡我这自夸。

chapters.en: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
chapters.zh: 为什么呢？是因我不爱你们吗？这有神知道。

chapters.en: And I will keep on doing what I am doing in order to cut the ground from under those who want an opportunity to be considered equal with us in the things they boast about.
chapters.zh: 我现在所作的，后来还要作，为要断绝那些寻机会人的机会，使他们在所夸的事上，也不过与我们一样。

chapters.en: For such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.
chapters.zh: 那等人是假使徒，行事诡诈，装作基督使徒的模样。

chapters.en: And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.
chapters.zh: 这也不足为怪。因为连撒但也装作光明的天使。

chapters.en: It is not surprising, then, if his servants also masquerade as servants of righteousness. Their end will be what their actions deserve.
chapters.zh: 所以他的差役，若装作仁义的差役，也不算希奇。他们的结局，必然照着他们的行为。

chapters.en: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then tolerate me just as you would a fool, so that I may do a little boasting.
chapters.zh: 我再说，人不可把我看作愚妄的。纵然如此，也要把我当作愚妄人接纳，叫我可以略略自夸。

chapters.en: In this self-confident boasting I am not talking as the Lord would, but as a fool.
chapters.zh: 我说的话，不是奉主命说的，乃是像愚妄人放胆自夸。

chapters.en: Since many are boasting in the way the world does, I too will boast.
chapters.zh: 既有好些人凭着血气自夸，我也要自夸了。

chapters.en: You gladly put up with fools since you are so wise!
chapters.zh: 你们既是精明人，就能甘心忍耐愚妄人。

chapters.en: In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or puts on airs or slaps you in the face.
chapters.zh: 假若有人强你们作奴仆，或侵吞你们，或掳掠你们，或悔慢你们，或打你们的脸，你们都能忍耐他。
